# Periya Tirumoli

## First Centum

## 1.1 Vadinen vadi

## 1.1.1. Vadinen vadi

*vādinēn vādi varundinēn manattāl perunduyar idumbaiyil piṟandu kūdinēn kūdi iḷaiyavar tammōdu avar tarum kalaviyē karudi ōdinēn ōdi uyvadōr poruḷāl uṇarvenum perumpadam terindu nādinēn nādi nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam*

**Пословный перевод:**

perum tuyar – being the recipient of great sorrow; idumbaiyil – in the body which is the cause for all sorrows; piṟandu – being born; kūdinēn – being unable to distinguish between body and soul, and remained closely together; kūdi – having remained in this manner for a long time; iḷaiyavar – young women; tarum – giving; kalaviyē – union only; karudi – thinking about; avar tammōdu – following their foot steps; ōdinēn – ran behind them; ōdi – in this manner, not remaining in any place, running around many matters seeking joy; manattāl – with the intellect which was following the worldly pleasures; varundinēn – experienced sorrow; further; vādinēn – suffered (like a support-less creeper); vādi – having suffered; uyvadu – for being uplifted; ōr poruḷāl – a nice principle (sarvēśvaran’s mercy); uṇarvu enum – jñānam (knowledge); perum – big; padam – state; terindu nādinēn – understood as it is, analysed “bhagavat viśayam (matters relating to bhagavān) is good and samsāram (bondage in material world) is bad”; nādi – having analysed; nān – I, who am unqualified to recite the divine name; nārāyaṇā ennum – nārāyaṇa; nāmam – the divine name; kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – got to see

**Перевод:**

**Just as nammāḻvār did not realise the full impact of the benediction he received after visualising emperumān and thought about his previous state and contemplated in tiruviruttam 1 “inninṟa nīrmai ini yāmuṟāmai” (I cannot tolerate these lowly aspects anymore), tirumangai āḻvār too, after being accepted by bhagavān, contemplated his previous states and says “vādinēn” (I suffered).**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being the recipient of great sorrow, being born in the body which is the cause for all sorrows, being unable to distinguish between body and soul, I remained closely together with the body; having remained in this manner for a long time, only thinking about the union given by young women, ran behind them, following their footsteps; in this manner, not remaining in any place, running around many matters seeking joy, with the intellect which was following the worldly pleasures, I experienced sorrow; further, I suffered like a support-less creeper; having suffered, I understood as it is, the great state of jñānam with the help of a nice principle (sarvēśvaran’s mercy) which leads to being uplifted, and analysed “bhagavat viśayam (matters relating to bhagavān) is good and samsāram (bondage in material world) is bad”; having analysed, I, who am unqualified to recite the divine name, got to see the divine name, nārāyaṇa.

- *vādinēn* – Like a shoot which lost its supporting stem; since the ātmā cannot be destroyed, ātmā is suffering (without being fully destroyed). If emperumān decided to protect, there is qualification in the ātmā to be protected. As every ātmā is having the apt qualification to remain with bhagavān as sītā pirātti said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.6 “*ananyā rāghavēṇāham*” (I always remain united with śrī rāma), once āḻvār realised such relationship, there is nothing wrong in saying “vādinēn” for having lost such enjoyment thus far. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 17.4 “*yaśca rāmam na paśyat tu*” is explained here.
   - *rāmam* – The apt target for the eyes; one who is not seeing such śrī rāma. *ya:* – However great he may be. *tu* – Even if this (seeing śrī rāma) is lost. It is specifically highlighted \[with *tu*\], to say that the loss of not being seen by śrī rāma is much greater.
   - *yanca rāmō napaśyati* – Even the most inferior person will not be missed by śrī rāma’s merciful glance.
   - *yam* – However inferior he may be. The most inferior person will be seen by śrī rāma \[to be blessed by him\]. [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-4-yarumor-nilaimaiyan/) “*yārum ōr nilaimaiyan ena aṟivaraiya emperumān* *yārum ōr nilaimaiyan ena aṟiveḷiya emperumān*” (Such [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) is having a state that is not understandable by those who are not devoted to him and is understandable by those devotees even though they may be very ignorant) – he will be beyond the knowledge of brahmā et al and will be under the auspices of covherd girl (yaśōdā and others) and hunter (śrī guhap perumāḷ and others). Irrespective of one’s greatness, if he did not have the darśan of namperumāḷ’s procession at least one day, he is not great; even the most inferior person will not be missed by his glance; those who are not seen by such emperumān, will not even be considered on a par with acit (matter). He will be counted among those who are discarded – everyone will look down upon such a person. When asked “Will he be despised only by a few like vasiśta et al?”
   - *ninditas sa vasēl lōkē* – *lōkē – nindita:* There is none who does not despise such person. Those who are immersed in worldly pleasures, will be blamed now and will also go to hell in next life, yet he will think “I am doing something good”; will such a person \[who was not seen by śrī rāma\] think like that?
   - *svātmāpyēnam vigarhatē* – He will despise himself as well. When one misses out on the tirukkaittala sēvai (namperumāḷ being carried by arcakas in their hands), one will think “I who missed to witness today’s procession can live through death if I get camphor and lemon (as prasādam from emperumān\]”; if these are the words of those who lost just one puṟappādu (procession) of namperumāḷ, the one who lost bhagavān forever cannot say anything other than “*vādinēn*“.
- *vādinēn* – What state of āḻvār does this word represent? When he was enjoying worldly pleasures, since he remained joyfully at that state, there is no suffering then; after starting to enjoy bhagavān, there is no suffering; hence this is the state where āḻvār had acquired knowledge about the true nature of the self and then contemplated about his previous situation. Only while attaining the ultimate result, will the previous situations not be remembered anymore; such previous remembrance will not occur as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm); since āḻvār acquired true knowledge, his previous situations appear to him in front of his eyes.
- *vādi* – The repetition of this word can be combined with both the previous and subsequent words; it appears to be implying that this loss has been occurring forever and is also causing subsequent disaster; it appears to be implying that this attachment to worldly pleasures was not just occasional, but would redeem oneself after atoning, but was occurring forever; and not stopping with that, it appears to be hinting at the further disaster it is causing.

When asked “What is the subsequent disaster?”, āḻvār says,

- *varundinēn manattāl* – I experienced suffering in the mind too. Senses will be attached to worldly pleasures, and while trying to enjoy them, they will fail, and even if they succeed, there is no real enjoyment in these pleasures; I suffered in my mind also; since I was unable to divert the mind which is the root of all senses, to focus internally, I suffered in my mind. With this, it is explained that  being engaged in worldly pleasures like śabda (sound) etc \[sparśa (touch), rūpa (form), rasa (taste) and ganda (fragrance)\], I was unable to think about the divine feet of emperumān.
- *perum tuyar idumbaiyil piṟandu* – \[This body, i.e. matter\] caused taste in worldly pleasures, created impressions, increased desire and hatred, and due to the ignorance and virtuous/vicious acts being the cause for the occurrence of \[another, repeated\] body, I took birth. Both tuyar and idumbai mean sorrow; with this, the body is both the abode of sorrow and the cause for sorrow. Being capable of being both the abode of sorrow and the cause for subsequent countless sorrows.

Why did āḻvār say “*vādinēn*” first instead of saying “*perum tuyar idumbaiyil piṟandu kūdi, vādinēn*“? As the relationship with karma is beginning-less and connection with acit (matter) is also pravāha rūpēṇa nityam (it is eternal in a continuous stream of births), āḻvār is just picking something in the middle and is starting with that.

- *piṟandu* – Though ātmā has no birth and death, he is said to be born and dead, in prevalent terms as spoken by everyone. \[It is really, acquiring body and relinquishing the same\]
- *kūdinēn* – ātmā who is eternal, in a singular form and is identified by his knowledge and bliss, and is subservient to bhagavān, is said as celestial being, human being and so on.
- *kūdinēn* – ātmā remained so closely united with the body, that one thinks that the ātmā cannot exist without the body.
- *kūdinēn* – By saying kūdinēn – it appears that, this \[material body\] is not natural for the ātmā, is acquired due to a reason and is extraneous. When Iron is heated, the fire sparks subtly enter the iron and due to the close connection, iron acquires the heat and colour of the fire. Similarly, this ātmā too, due to being together with acit, has become like acit to be called as acit. Just as the iron loses the colour but remains hot for a long time, even after fire sparks leave the iron, ātmā considers self to body for sometime even after acquiring knowledge.
- *kūdi* – Remaining together to be unable to tolerate the separation from body. After acquiring knowledge, one will pray hard to have the body removed. In this “*kūdi*“, it appears that the togetherness of ātmā and acit is forever and so is the subsequent disaster which occurred.

When asked “What is the subsequent disaster?”, āḻvār says,

- *iḷaiyavar tammōdu avar tarum kalaviyē karudi ōdinēn* – *iḷaiyavar* (youth) – To be unable to analyse that attachment towards worldly pleasures is disaster, and to be unable to understand the greatness of bhagavat viśayam and engage in it, the young girls will show their youth and attract.
- *tammōdu* – Whatever is said in mūla samhitā “*cāyāvā satvam anugaccēt*” (like a shadow following its owner), is all observed towards these young women; when they find a nice garland, instead of decorating themselves with that or considering themselves as respectable, they will offer it to the women. Whatever is said in parama samhitā “*yēna yēna dātā gaccati tēna tēna saha gaccati*” (wherever the lord goes, the servitor follows), is observed towards these young women.
- *avar tarum kalavi* – While initially being approached, they will speak sweet words, but once the person is trapped, they will move away, to increase the longing in the person.
- *kalaviyē karudi* – Here the usage of the word “karudi” (contemplating) is significant. Only if they could enjoy, could that be highlighted. Here, only the man is desiring for such union. Since the man has committed sins, he can only desire and the enjoyment will not occur. When there is no scope for enjoyment, the man should withdraw from the efforts. But as they keep moving away, the man’s desires will increase further considering “there is some enjoyment”. This is due to his own sins.

When the man understands that there is nothing enjoyable in a woman, he should withdraw from further efforts to get her. Instead of doing that, the man will seek the next woman and keep on doing the same thing.

- *ōdinēn* – This worldly enjoyment is not of a nature to retain the enjoyer for more than a fraction of a moment; union with woman is such that, one will have to carry the tools for enjoyment with her, and after enjoyment, one should bathe to purify oneself. Knowing well the defects of such union, to cover it up, one carries perfumes and so on and tries to enjoy with her. Even what is perceivable by the senses (i.e. the defects) are unable to help \[in stopping from the indulgence\]. Though one does not need śāstram to understand the defects of these aspects and can perceive directly with one’s own senses, they remain irresistible! Attachment for worldly pleasures is similar to a snake with open hoods. While it is waiting to swallow the prey, the prey will go and hide under the shade of its hoods. The joy acquired in this worldly pleasures is similar to a person who is about to be hanged, but feeling thirsty, becomes satisfied on quenching his thirst. One is perceiving that among the many sorrows, a particular aspect is joyful. The real bliss is explained in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.59 “*sukhabhāvaika lakśaṇā*” (bhagavat viśayam is the real bliss).
- *ōdi* – It appears that even though this has been the routine forever, somehow, it has led to some goodness. I ran away escaping the helping hands of sarvēśvaran himself who comes saying “I will protect”.
- *uyvadu ōr poruḷāl* – When I ran behind the worldly pleasures being immersed in them and fell down out of fatigue, emperumān protected me due to his mercy having that as the reason saying “Now, he will not be able to withdraw from this on his own”. With the good principle which leads to being uplifted. Good principle is bhagavat krupai. Due to respect, āḻvār is indicating it in a concealed manner; in the fourth pāsuram, he will explicitly identify it as “*āḻiyān aruḷ*” (mercy of one who carries sudarśana chakra). nammāḻvār, being unable to wait any further, explicitly mentioned in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*mayarvaṟa madi nalam aruḷinan*” (emperumān granted me knowledge which is well-matured as devotion). I got an opportunity for being uplifted while I was engaged in sinful activities which lead to self-destruction as said in periya tirumoḻi 1.9.2 “*nānē nānāvida naragam pugum pāvam seydēn*” (I committed many sins which will lead me to many hell) and tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9 “*pala nī kāttip paduppāyō*” (Will you keep me in this samsāram, showing many of these worldly aspects?). While I remained as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva bhavati*” (he is as good as non-existing), a good principle to make me as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*santamēnam tatōvidu:*” (he is known to be existing), occurred.
- *uṇarvenum perum padam* – jitantē stōtram 1-11 “*vijñānam yadidam*” (this great knowledge). Just as flood enters the place where one is sleeping on a mat \[unexpectedly\].
- *perum padam* – The greatness of this is such that we can say “Even he is not required, knowledge about him is sufficient”.
- *tirindu* – Since worldly pleasures are with boundary, I returned after realising that there is nothing to enjoy in them.
- *terindu* – Alternative for tirindu. In this case, once knowledge dawned, everything was understood clearly. It appears that hence, previous situations were considered as darkness.
- *nādinēn* – As the knowledge dawned, I started analysing “What did I go through previously? What am I going to suffer in future?”
- *nādi* – In the worldly pleasures, even when I consciously tried to get them, since it only leads to disaster, there is no result; but when I set out to engage in bhagavat viśayam, it leads to result.
- *nān* – I who said “*ōdinēn*“. Just as the one (śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān) who ate the remnants of rāvaṇa in his palace for a long time, became part of rāma gōśti (śrīrāma’s team), even without taking a bath. vēlvetti nambiyār (A śrīvaiṣṇava), once on a tirukkārtigai day, sent a message through a person to nampiḷḷai who was mercifully stationed in a village which was located east of śrīrangam. The message read “If I asked this question to anyone, they will think that I am ignorant and that there is none who can clarify this doubt; you should clarify this doubt”. The question is “When perumāḷ (śrī rāma) surrendered to the ocean,he followed proper rules such as facing east etc and surrendered; is this prapatti (surrender) also having prerequisites, like rest of the upāyams (means)?” nampiḷḷai mercifully explained – this is not a prerequisite for prapatti, this happened due to the nature of those who pursued the means; as the rākśasa clan is lowly and unqualified, śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān who is one among the clan advised śrī rāma as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.31 “*samudram rāghavō rājā śaraṇam gandumarhati*” (śrī rāma should surrender to the king of ocean); we did not see śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān following any rules and we saw śrī rāma following the rules”. With this, it is explained that, for prapatti, an unqualified person need not earn qualification and a qualified person need not give up his qualification. Everyone is qualified as (s)he is. That is, this prapatti can be pursued by everyone.
- *kaṇḍu koṇḍēn* – āḻvār says so since it feels as if a wealth-less person is acquiring wealth and as if that wealth is hereditary.
- *nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn* – Feels as if the one who lost it himself found it.
- *nārāyaṇā* – Since there is no praṇavam, nama: and caturti (to make it complete aśtākśaram), just accepting that we are part of his wealth (which is indicated by the divine name, nārāyaṇa) is sufficient; implies that, to acquire the result, the limbs of the mantram are not required.
- *ennum nāmam* – “*ennum*” highlights the renowned nature of this divine name which is revealed in nārāyaṇa anuvākam (sūktam)  which does not speak about anyone else. “*nāmam*” implies that it is desirable as it is, the right time is when the person acquires desire and the person who sets out to recite the name is the qualified person. nanjīyar asked parāśara bhattar “Should one be pure while reciting tirumantram or is that not required?” bhattar mercifully explained “Not required. When one goes to take sacred bath in gangā, should he first take bath in a water-body before? When it is ready to bestow great benefits now, will it also not bestow the qualifications which are required?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 1.1.2. Aviye amude

*āviyē! amudē! ena ninaindurugi avaravar paṇaimulai tuṇaiyā pāviyēn uṇarādu ettanai pagalum paḻudu pōyoḻindana nāḷgaḷ tūvisēr annam tuṇaiyodum puṇarum sūḻpunal kudaintaiyē toḻudu en nāvināl uyya nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam*

**Пословный перевод:**

āviyē – Oh my life!; amudē – Oh one who is enjoyable for me like nectar!; ena – saying these many praises; ninaindu – thinking about the insignificant pleasures they give; urugi – melting like ice; avaravar – of those women; paṇai – large; mulai – bosoms; tuṇaiyā – having as protection; pāviyēn – I who am a sinner; uṇarādu – without knowing “sarvēśvaran is the rakśaka (protector)”; ettanai pagalum – forever; nāḷgaḷum – everyday; paḻudupōy oḻindana – was wasted; tūvi – with wings; sēr – matching; annam – swan; tuṇaiyodum – with its female counterpart; puṇarum – living together; punal – with water; sūḻ – surrounded; kudandai – ārāvamudāḻvār in tirukkudandai; toḻudu – vorśipped; nān – I who was immersed in worldly pleasures; uyya – to get uplifted; nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam – the divine name “nārāyaṇa”; en nāvināl – with my tongue; kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – praised and realised

**Перевод:**

**Previously āḻvār said “vādinēn” and “iḷaiyavar kalaviyē karudi ōdinēn“, without realising that there is bhagavān, until then and with deep attachment towards worldly pleasures. Now, āḻvār is explaining how he enjoyed those pleasures, how he wasted the time all along and how he realised the divine name to even redeem the lost time.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Thinking about the insignificant pleasures the women give, saying these many praises such as “Oh my life! Oh one who is enjoyable for me like nectar!”, melting like ice, considering their large bosoms as protection, without knowing “sarvēśvaran is the rakśaka (protector)”, I who am a sinner, wasted everyday forever. Swan with matching wings, is living together with its female counterpart in the water surrounding tirukkudandai. To get uplifted, I who was immersed in worldly pleasures vorśipped ārāvamudāḻvār in such tirukkudandai by praising the divine name “nārāyaṇa” with my tongue and realised the divine name.

- *āviyē amudē* – Whatever is to be said in bhagavat viśayam as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/01/thiruvaimozhi-8-1-1-dhevimar-avar/) “*āviyē! amudē! alai kadal kadainda appanē!*” (you are my life; you are the most enjoyable nectar; oh great benefactor who performed difficult tasks and helped others!) and [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-7-aviye-aramudhe/) “*āviyē! āramudē! ennai āḷudait*  
   *tūvi am puḷ udaiyāy!*” (Oh one who is my prāṇa, one who is fully and eternally enjoyable, one who has beautifully winged periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) as your vehicle to enslave me). Whatever is to be said towards the apt lord, I said those towards inapt persons. Both dārakatva (being the support) and bhōjñatai (enjoyability) are fully present without any shortcoming only in bhagavat viśayam. These words were spoken towards those who are unfavourable rather than being a support and are disgusting rather than being enjoyable. I told as in uttara rāma caritam 3.26 “*tvam jīvitam tvamasi mē hrudayam madīyam*” (You are my life and heart).
- *ena ninaindu* – nanjīyar would mercifully explain “this is thought about in several ways in this manner”. nampiḷḷai humbly asked nanjīyar “Can we say āḻvār was thinking as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/08/thiruvaimozhi-9-6-2-ninaidhorum/) “*ninaidoṟum sollum toṟum nenjidindugum*” (every time I think about him, every time I speak/hear about him, my heart becomes broken)?” nanjīyar mercifully responded “You are explaining this even better than āḻvār”.
- *ena ninaindu urugi* – They will contemplate in this manner and remain like melted ice in an unconscious state.

When asked “How long did they remain in worldly pleasures in this manner?” āḻvār says,

- *avaravar* – Time is eternal, ātmā has been there forever, the bodies ātmā acquired were countless and the aspects enjoyed in each of the body are also countless; ātmā remained immersed in all of those aspects. Hence, it is said as “avaravar” (respective).
- *paṇai mulai* – Those \[bosoms\] are unlike bhagavān who feels for the suffering ātmās as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 10.9 “*hrīrēśāhi mamātulā*” (I am feeling immensely ashamed), and śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 8.3 “*natyajēyam”* (I will not abandon even if he has faults). They will grow multi-fold having the torment of the men who became attracted as the fertilizer thinking “we have trapped a lowly/helpless person; all his possessions belong to us now”. They don’t have the compassion to let the person enjoy them thinking “he is melting to get us”!
- *paṇai mulai tuṇaiyā* – Desiring for a lump which is made of skin, flesh, fatty matter and bone, one remains as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.6.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-6-8-thuyarame-tharu/) “*tayaradaṟku magan tannai anṟi maṟṟilēn tanjam āgavē*” (other than such śrī rāma, who appeared as the son of daśarata cakravarti, I will not have anyone, even another form of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), as my refuge). Having great attachment towards them, not just with the thought of “we are having bodily attachment towards them now” but thinking “these will grant us even what is to be attained in after-life”. This is because, the person has forgotten about after-life. One who should have emperumān as protection as said in tirunedundāṇḍagam 16 “*tunnu kuḻal karu niṟattu en tuṇaiyē*” (Oh my protection who is having very dark complexion of dense hair!)
- *pāviyēn* – This is the insult attained by ātmā who is eternal, singular in form, identified by jñānam (knowledge) and ānandam (bliss) and is similar to śrī kauśtubam (the crown jewel on emperumān’s chest) for īśvara.
- *uṇarādu* – Not realising that emperumān has the ātmā to be engaged in his service only.
- *ettanai pagalum paḻudu pōy oḻindana nāḷgaḷ* – We have wasted all the time thus far. We have wasted forever – just as water which had overflovn the dam and reached the ocean for no benefit. As perumāḷ felt sorrow for having lost his time with sītā as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.5 “*na mē dukkam … vayōsyā hyativartatē*” (My biggest sorrow is … sītā’s age is passing by without being enjoyed \[by me (śrī rāma)\])
- *paḻudu pōy oḻindana nāḷgaḷ* – The time which should have been spent as done by iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) in serving sītāp pirātti and śrī rāma, was simply wasted. The time which should have been spent with kainkaryam in a precious manner, was wasted.
- *tūvi sēr …* – Such ātmā who was going down in this manner, redeemed with the divyadēśams which are present in this world.  tūvi – wing. The abode where swan which has the beauty acquired by its wings, lives together with his spouse. The abode which is the refuge for all creatures. Since hamsa is fully comparable to bhagavān, it can be said that ārāvamudāḻvār (bhagavān) joyfully lives in tirukkudandai along with periya pirāttiyār. The abode where bhagavān who is śaraṇya (refuge) lives without any shortcoming. There is no shortcoming in this abode since pirātti who pacifies bhagavān when he shows anger and bhagavān who becomes pacified \[and accepts ātmās\] are residing.
- *sūḻ punal* – Even the insentient water (river) will go around the divyadēśam on approaching it. The abode which eliminates the fatigue for those who are suffering.
- *kudandaiyē toḻudu* – As said in mahābhāratam sabhā parvam 75 “*avaśā: pratibēdirē*” (They honoured kriṣṇa without even realising), āḻvār saw himself vorśipping bhagavān, though he did not have any real intention to do so.
- *en nāvināl* – With my tongue which said “*āviyē! amudē!*“. Just as saying “I attained fame by begetting this child” \[āḻvār feels happy for having the tongue\]. Though the physical tongue is different in this birth now in comparison to previous births, as the sense of speech \[subtle aspect in tongue\] is carried across different bodies, there is nothing wrong in āḻvār saying “My tongue”.

With the body, which praised worldly people,

- *uyya nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn* – I who said in periya tirumoḻi 6.2.2 “*maṟanda madiyin manattāl iṟandēn ettanaiyum*” (Due to forgetting you forever and not having intelligence, I lost you all along), realised myself for my being uplifted.
- *kaṇḍu koṇḍēn* – Just as meditating upon tirumantram’s meanings matches the true nature of the self, reciting it also matches the true nature of the self. āḻvar is saying that he realised what is apt and what was lost all along.
- *nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam* – That which is said in [mudal tiruvandādi 95](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-95/) “*nā vāyil uṇḍē*“. \[pāsuram is explained here\]
   - nā vāyil uṇḍē – One need not search for a tongue.
   - *namō nārāyāṇā enṟu ōvādu uraikkum urai uṇḍē* – ōvādu does not mean “without break”; since there are only eight syllables, one can recite this without becoming tired. This is unlike sahasrākśarī māla mantram (a thousand syllabled mantram) which makes one think “Instead of learning and reciting this, hell seems to be a better option”
- *ennum nāmam* – I saw (realised) the divine name, to make the previously wasted time to become purposeful. [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 17](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/munram-thiruvandhadhi-17/) “*senṟa nāḷ sellāda sengaṇmāl engaḷmāl enṟanāḷ ennāḷum nāḷāgum*” – The day when we realise that reddish-eyed bhagavān is our lord, occurs; *senṟa nāḷ – ennāḷum nāḷāgum* – Due to facilitating in the progress towards reciting tirumantram, even the past times will feel auspicious and the present times will be good. By reciting tirumantram, it can be guaranteed that there will be no disaster in the future.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.3. Semame vendi

*sēmamē vēṇḍit tīvinai perukkit terivaimār uruvamē maruvi ūmanār kaṇḍa kanavilum paḻudāy oḻindana kaḻinda annāḷgaḷ kāmanār tādai nammudai adigaḷ tammadaindār manattiruppār nāmam nān uyya nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam*

**Пословный перевод:**

sēmamē – well-being only; vēṇḍi – desiring (but without not performing virtuous duties which are required for that); tīvinai – sins; perukki – increasing; terivaimār – of women; uruvamē – physical beauty only; maruvi – thinking about; kaḻinda – wasted; annāḷgaḷ – those times; ūmanār – mute persons; kaṇḍa – saw; kanavilum – more than the dream; paḻudāy – being useless; oḻindana – lost; hence; kāmanār – for cupid; tādai – being the father; nammudai – for all of us; adigaḷ – being the lord; tam – him; adaindār – for those who hold as refuge; manattu – in the heart; iruppār – sarvēśvaran who firmly remains; nāmam – word; nārāyaṇā ennum – nārāyaṇa; nāmam – divine name; nān – I who was running behind worldly pleasures; uyya – to be uplifted; nān – who is too lost for redemption; kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – realised

**Перевод:**

**Desiring only for the well-being, but increasing the sins, only thinking about the physical beauty of women, all those times were wasted and were more useless than the dream seen by mute persons; hence, I who was running behind worldly pleasures, got the word nārāyaṇa which is the divine name of sarvēśvaran who is the father of cupid, who is the lord for all of us and who firmly remains in the heart of those who hold him as refuge; I who am too lost for redemption, realised such divine name for me to be uplifted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

- *sēmamē vēṇḍi* – One will be thinking in the heart “There should be no troubles from enemies, kings et al for us; we should be protected by all”.
- *tīvinai perukki* – When one looks out for the well-being, one should also engage in suitable righteous activities which lead to such well-being; but one will accumulate sins only.
- *teirvaimār uruvamē maruvi* – One will only reap the results of the sinful activities, if one does not engage in righteous activities; the sins committed will lead to engagement in worldly pleasures.
- *uruvamē maruvi* – When one sees deep inside the hearts of such women, one can easily give them up. Their hearts will be poisonous with selfish motives; if one engages in the heart, one can see the ignoble qualities, one can retract; it will be easy to hide the defects in the form.
- *maruvi* – Such forms will be meditated upon as śubśrayam (auspicious abode).
- *ūmanār kaṇḍa kanavilum paḻudāy* – ūmanār – mute persons. A mute person won’t be able to reveal the dream he saw – he can only think about it; even unlike that, enjoying these worldly pleasures for a long time, one will not even be able to recollect what one enjoyed. Alternative explanation – while a mute person cannot speak about his dream, he can at least think about it; but the enjoyment of these worldly pleasures cannot even be thought about since that will only cause fear (for the repurcussions). There is nothing worthy to recollect and even if there is, that will only cause fear.
- *oḻindana kaḻinda annāḷgaḷ* – śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.5 “*na mē dukkam priyā dūrē* *na mē dukkam hrutēti vā \| ētadēvānusōcāmi vayōsyā hyativarttatē \|\|”* (I am not feeling distressed that the one who is dear to my heart is at a far away place or that she has been abducted. I am only feeling sad that she is ageing) – I am not upset that my dear wife is far away from me, that can be remedied by traveling there; I am not upset she was abducted by a powerful demon, that can be remedied by severing his head; my only sorrow is this – “*vayōsyā hyativarttatē*” – I cannot get back the lost time with my arrow!

When asked “Are these defects not present in the entity (bhagavān) you are holding on to?” āḻvār says,

- *kāmanār tādai* – His form itself is attractive; his physical beauty will add to the greatness. He is the creator of cupid who bewilders the world with his beautiful form. He goes through the same emotions on seeing emperumān, which are observed by the world on seeing him. śrī bhāgavatam 10.32.2 “*sākśān manmata manmata:*” (For the covherd girls, kriṣṇa appeared like a cupid of cupids).
- *nammudai adigaḷ* – Not just that he is free from the defects which are present in worldly aspects, the worldly aspects are inapt while he is apt.
- *nammudai adigaḷ* – sarvasvāmi (lord of all).
- *tammadaindār manattiruppār* – Unlike those women who would showcase their forms and attract the men, take away everything possessed by the men, not presenting themselves to the men and driving the men away, emperumān will firmly remain in the heart of those who have even the slightest attachment towards him. He will even abandon his grand assembly in paramapadam and have the hearts of such devotees as his abode.
- *tammadaindār manattiruppār nāmam* – The divine name which spells out all the aforementioned aspects. Having beautiful physical form, being the lord of all, easy approacability and motherly forbearance are revealed in this name.
- *nān uyya nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn* – I, who was getting destroyed as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (as good as matter), realised him to be uplifted.
- *nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn* – I who had reached the stage to think “Is there no vision?” acquired the desired benefit. I who had thought as “I won’t exist anymore, there is no possibility of vision” got uplifted and also saw emperumān’s divine name.
- *nān uyya nān* – “*nān*” (I) is repeated twice as an outlet for the joy acquired.
- *nārāyaṇa ennum nāmam* – I got to recite the divine name which is to be recited by those who have control over internal and external senses as said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat 6.4.23 “*śāntō dānta uparatas titikśus samāhitō bhūtvā ātmanyēvātmānam paśyēt*” (One who has control over internal and external senses, who has no attachment towards activities (in the context of getting the fruits), who has patience and who has undisturbed mind can see the bhagavān who is present within the self). I who was having ignoble qualities as said in “*sēmamē vēṇḍit tīvinai perukkit terivaimār uruvamē maruvi*“, acquired the result which is acquired by those who are having noble qualities.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.4. Venriye vendi

*venṟiyē vēṇḍi vīḻporutkirangi vēṟkaṇār kalaviyē karudi ninṟavā nillā nenjinai udaiyēn enseygēn? neduvisumbaṇavum panṟiyāy anṟu pāragangīṇḍa pāḻiyān āḻiyān aruḷē nanṟu nānuyya nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam*

**Пословный перевод:**

venṟiyē – Victory only; vēṇḍi – desired; vīḻ – that which will be destroyed; porutku – for wealth; irangi – worrying; vēl kaṇār – with the women whose eyes resemble spear; kalaviyē – union only; karudi – considered; ninṟavā nillā – not being firm on anything; nenjinai – heart; udaiyēn – I who am having; en seygēn – what will I do; (not having the means to reach you, I am unable to do anything); anṟu – on the day when earth was engulfed by deluge; nedu – tall; visumbu – sky; aṇavum – growing to touch; panṟiyāy – having the form of varāha (wild boar); pāragam – earth; kīṇḍa – uplifted; pāḻiyān – the strong one; āḻiyān – sarvēśvaran’s; aruḷē – by mercy only; nān – I who was attached to worldly pleasures; nanṟu – properly; uyya – to be uplifted; nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam – the divine name nārāyaṇa; nān – I who was prideful; kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – realised

**Перевод:**

**Desiring for victory only and worrying for the wealth which will be destroyed, only considering the union with the women whose eyes resemble spear, what will I, who am having the heart which is not firm on anything, do? The strong sarvēśvaran having the form of varāha who grew up to the tall sky, on that day the earth was engulfed by deluge, uplifted the earth. To be properly uplifted by such sarvēśvaran’s mercy only, I who was attached to worldly pleasures and was prideful, realised the divine name nārāyaṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

- *venṟiyē vēṇḍi* – He only desires for victory even over father or teacher. He always tries to push-down everyone else and become prominent. He is even desiring to win over aspects where he should remain subservient.
- *vīḻ porutku irangi* – Only due to having a little bit of wealth, one disrespects others. But since it is impermanent, he will lose and will cry out for that. On top of trying to win over respectable persons instead of being subservient to them, he will also remain crying due to having attachment for wealth which should not be cared for. Alternative explanation – having dēhātmābimānam (considering body as self), not just considering oneself to be greater than all, but also will think about the impermanent body to remain forever and worry for that.
- *vēl kaṇār kalaviyē karudi* – While having wealth, he will let his wife wear saffron clothes and let her go. But on losing the wealth, if he calls out for her, just as others, his wife will also look sharply with her spear like eyes and question him. At that time, he will think “I should have made ornaments with my wealth and decorated her with them”. He will try to decorate his wife with the lost wealth.
- *ninṟavā nillā nenjinai udaiyēn en seygēn* – When the whole world is engaged in the means for ūrvasī sālōkyam (to remain in heaven where ūrvasi lives), arjuna with great detachment, vorśipped her \[considering her as his mother\], when she approached him and tried to seduce him; such arjuna said that even the wind blowing from the opposite direction can be controlled but the heart/mind cannot be controlled as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 6.34](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/6-34/) “*cancalam hi mana: kriṣṇa pramāti balavad drudam \|tasyāham nigraham manyē vāyōr iva suduśkaram \|\|*” (Because , mind is (naturally) wavering, strong and hence bewildering and firm (in pulling us towards worldly pleasures). I think that it is very difficult to restrain it, like controlling a fierce storm). How can I engage my mind in a means which is apt to attain you, when my heart cannot focus on any matter for more than a fraction of a moment? It will only facilitate my loss of you.
- *en seygēn* – arjuna became sorrowful after hearing from bhagavān about many upāyams (means) in eighteen chapters of śrī bhagavat gītā, which are impossible to practice. For āḻvār, everything is causing fear \[even without getting instructed like that\].

When asked “If you remain like this, what would you consider as the means for the goal?” āḻvār says “When the world which was engulfed by deluge, was incapable to save itself, there was the one who protected it. Such emperumān will be my means”

- *nedu visumbu aṇavum panṟiyāy anṟu pār agam kīṇḍa pāḻiyān āḻiyān aruḷē* – Only when world which was engulfed by deluge could engage in protecting itself, I who am having heart which is engulfed by worldly pleasures can contemplate about my well-being. One who grew out of the space in sky, eagerly assumed a form which is much larger than what is to be protected. When the world was engulfed in the deluge and was about to be destroyed, bhagavān assumed the form of mahāvarāham (great wild boar) which will not withdraw seeing water and mud. He assumed the form which will grow on seeing abundance of water. [nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/05/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-11-simple/) “*māsudambil nīr vārā mānamilāp panṟiyām*” is explained here. While seeing his divine consort (bhūmippirātti) where her body is not cared and is immersed in the deluge as in “*pāsi tūrttu*” (having moss all over), bhagavān who is her beloved husband, not caring for his own body, acquired a divine form which had dirt on it. *mānamilā* – Being free from the pride of being sarvēśvara. When the demon mārīca \[rāvaṇa’s uncle\] assumed the form of a mystical deer, other deer came by, smelled him, realised that he is not a real deer and ran away from him. Unlike that, what is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 120.11 “*ātmānam mānuśam manyē*” (I consider myself as a human being) is felt by him here also \[to feel one among the wild boars\].
- *pār agam kīṇḍa* – As the whole world was resting on the wall of the oval shaped universe, emperumān freed the world and brought it out.
- *pāḻiyān* – One who has great strength.
- *āḻiyān* – While protecting he does not need any tool \[as in the case of rescuing the world\]; but if he needs a tool, he has the sudarśana chakra weapon in his hand.
- *aruḷē* – Considering me to be totally lost due to having pride where one should not have, worrying for that which is not worthy of worrying, desiring to enjoy worldly matters which will lead to hell and having wavering mind, due to his mercy, sarvēśvaran thought “He will never be able to uplift himself” and having that only as the reason, tried to uplift me. Both aruḷē or aruḷālē, are acceptable.
- *nanṟu nān uyya* – I became similar to nityasūris who are known as aspruśta samsāra gandar (those who are untouched by defects of samsāra), instead of being known as one who remained as said in “*venṟiyē vēṇḍi vīḻ porutkirangi vēṟkaṇār kalaviyē karudi*“, has become pure.
- *nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam* – āḻvār spoke about himself as having pride and greed as in “*venṟiyē vēṇḍi vīḻ porutkirangi*“; I who was like this acquired the result which is acquired by those who are having noble qualities such as *amānitvam* (being free of pride) etc.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.5. Kalvanen anen

*kaḷvanēn ānēn padiṟu seidiruppēnkaṇḍavā tiritandēnēlumteḷḷiyēn ānēn selgadikkamaindēncikkenat tiruvaruḷ peṟṟēnuḷḷelām urugik kural taḻuttoḻindēnudambelām kaṇṇanīr sōranaḷḷiruḷ aḷavum pagalum nān aḻaippannārāyaṇā ennum nāmam*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaḷvanēn ānēn – (Previously, bhagavān’s possession ātmā) I stole; padiṟu – very evil acts; seydu iruppēn – I kept doing; kaṇḍa A – any aspects seen; tiritandēnēlum – even after engaging; tiru aruḷ – (his) merciful glance; sikkena – firmly; peṟṟēn – I got; teḷḷiyēn ānēn – I acquired clarity (about his lordship and my servitude); sel – to travel in (arcirādi mārgam, the path leading to paramapadam); gadikku – to paramapadam; amaindēn – became complete, to go; uḷ elām – all that which are inside (i.e., bones, nerves) my body; urugi – melting; kural – tone; taḻuttu oḻindēn – stuttered; udambu elām – everywhere on my body; kaṇṇa nīr sōra – to have tears of happiness flow over; naḷ – dense; iruḷ aḷavum – throughout the night; pagal aḷavum – throughout the day; nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam – the divine name, nārāyaṇa; nān – I, the servitor; aḻaippan – got to call out

**Перевод:**

**Previously I stole this ātmā which is owned by bhagavān; I kept doing very evil acts; I firmly received his merciful glance even after engaging in worldly aspects which were seen; I acquired clarity about his lordship and my servitude; I became complete and ready to travel to parampadam; all that which are inside my body are melting and my tone stuttered; throughout the dense night and day, I, the servitor, got to call out the divine name, nārāyaṇa to have tears of happiness flow over my body. kaṇḍavāṟu is written as kaṇḍavā and ellām is written as elām.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

- *kaḷvanēn ānēn* – In comparison with someone who stole firewood, the one who stole precious gems, will acquire more sins; in comparison to someone who stole the wealth of śūdra, the one who stole the wealth of brāhmaṇa, will acquire more sins; I stole the best entity, that is ātmā; I claimed ownership of a belonging of sarvēśvaran; \[hence, I accumulated great sin, from both the object which is stolen and from whom it is stolen\].
- *padiṟu seydiruppēn* – If it itches inside the neck/throat, one cannot scratch to eliminate the itch. In this manner, I became a great thief who accumulated great sin. Not only did I consider my body to be self, but when I saw āśtikas (faithful ones) who think “this ātmā is a servitor of īśvara”, I would ask them “How can there be an ātmā which is different from body? How can there be an īśvara?” and steal bhagavān’s possession in this manner.
- *kaṇḍavā tiritandēnēlum* – I was simply following on a bodily platform without knowing the truth instead of withdrawing from the aspects which are forbidden by śāstram. As said in stōtra ratnam 58 “*nrupaśu:*” (animal in a human body), I would seek out the pleasures which are attained from others, from own mother as well.
- *teḷḷiyēn ānēn* – While I was like this, \[suddenly\] like those who understand the difference between essence and extraneous aspects, and engage in what is allowed and avoid what is forbidden \[in śāstram\], I became knowledgeable.
- *sel gadikku amaindēn* – I became to be thought and said by emperumān as in “He is acting in a manner to remain in samsāram forever; from now onvards, he does not belong in this samsāram, he belongs in paramapadam”. There is an abode which should be reached – that is, paramapadam. I became complete, to belong there.

When asked “You first said ‘*kaṇḍavā tiritandēn*‘ and then said ‘*teḷḷiyēn ānēn*‘. This seems contradictory!” āḻvār says,

- *sikkenat tiruvaruḷ peṟṟēn* – I got his grace, to not have to look back ever.

When asked “What benefit did you get?” āḻvār says,

- *uḷ elām urugik kural taḻuttu oḻindēn* – The bones and nerves inside the body melted and that is shown in my stuttering tone.
- *udambelām kaṇṇa nīr sōra* – śrīviṣṇu tatvam “*āhlāda śīta nētrāmbu: pulakī kruta gātravān*” (One who is having cool happy tears due to blissful experience of bhagavān etc – the purpose of everyone is to see such persons). All over the body, tears overflow as necklace with five layers and necklace with three layers.
- *naḷ iruḷ aḷavum pagalum nān aḻaippan nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam* –  Both the night when worldly pleasures are enjoyed and the day when wealth for future enjoyment is earned, are fully spent in reciting the divine name by me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.6. Empiran endai

*empirān endai ennudaic cuṟṟam enakkarasu ennudai vāṇāḷ ambināl arakkar verukkoḷa nerukki avaruyir segutta em aṇṇal vambulānjōlai māmadiḷ tanjai māmaṇik kōyilē vaṇangi nambigāḷ! uyya nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn  nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam*

**Пословный перевод:**

nambigāḷ! – Oh those who are complete (with enjoying bhagavān’s qualities)!; em pirān – being my benefactor; endai – being my father; ennudaic cuṟṟam – being all my relationships; enakku arasu – being my ruler; ennudai vāḻ nāḷ – being my life-span; arakkar – rākśasas (demoniac people); verukkoḷa – to be scared; ambināl – with arrows; nerukki – suffocating them; avar uyir – their lives; segutta – destroyed; em aṇṇal – the eternal abode of sarvēśvaran, who is my lord; vambu – fragrance; ulām – blowing; sōlai – garden; mā – lengthy; madiḷ – having fort; tanjai mā maṇik kōyilē – tanjai mā maṇik kōyil only; vaṇangi – vorśipped; nān uyya – to be uplifted (like all of you); nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam – the divine name, nārāyaṇa; kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – I got to realise

**Перевод:**

**Oh those who are complete (with enjoying bhagavān’s qualities)! sarvēśvaran, being my benefactor, father, all my relationships, ruler and life-span, created fear in the rākśasas by suffocating them with arrows and destroyed their lives. I only vorśipped such sarvēśvaran, who is my lord who is residing in tanjai mā maṇik kōyil which is having garden with blowing fragrance and lengthy fort. To be uplifted, I got to realise the divine name, nārāyaṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*When asked “You are greatly celebrating this divine name. What is the meaning for it?” āḻvār explains in this pāsuram. Instead of chanting the divine name \[as part of tirumantram\] and getting a result out of it, and making it ancillary for karma yōgam (jñāna yōgam and bhakti yōgam), since āḻvār is of the opinion that the result is attained by meditating upon the meanings of it, he is explaining the meanings. nammāḻvār too, while speaking about tirumantram \[especially the divine name, nārāyaṇa\], will explain about the meaning either before or after, to emphasise on the meaning, since it is said in śāstram “jñānān mōkśam” (True knowledge leads to liberation).*

- *empirān* – My benefactor.
- *endai* – My father.
- *ennudaic cuṟṟam* – One who remains all types of relationships starting with the mother who gives birth.
- *enakku arasu* – One who eliminated my vices and ruled over me.
- *ennudai vāḻ nāḷ* – My life-span.
- *ambināl arakkar verukkoḷa nerukki avaruyir segutta em aṇṇal* – My lord who destroyed the rākśasas by causing fear in them by suffocating them with his arrows instead of destroying them with his sankalpa (will). Thus he concludes with saying “emperumān is my svāmi (lord)”. With this, what is explained in subāla upaniśat “*mātā pitā bhrātā nivāsaś śaraṇam suhrudgatirnārāyaṇa:*” ([śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is mother, father, brother, abode, refuge, friend, goal), is elaborated here.

When asked “How did you get all of these?” āḻvār says,

- *vambulānjōlai māmadiḷ tanjai māmaṇik kōyilē vaṇangi* – I kept vorśipping tanjai māmaṇik kōyil only, which is having eternally blooming garden and lengthy fort. As I meditated upon emperumān’s saulabhyam (easy approacability) where he is present announcing “I am all types of relationships for you”, I received all these.
- *nambigāḷ* – āḻvār could be addressing either those who are caring only for the body holding on to matters other than bhagavān or those who are complete due to enjoying bhagavān’s qualities.
- *uyya nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn* – āḻvār is saying either “I got to see emperumān to be uplifted, while you are suffering due to worldly attachments” or “I too reached the shore as you did knowing the ways to be uplifted”.
- *nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam* – I got to realise the divine name which explains that emperumān is all types of relationships.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.7. Irpirappu

*iṟpiṟappaṟiyīr ivaravar ennīr innadōr tanmaiyenṟu uṇareer kaṟpagam pulavar kaḷaikaṇ enṟulagil kaṇḍavā toṇḍaraip pādum soṟporuḷāḷeer sollugēn vammin sūḻpunal kudandaiyē toḻumin naṟporuḷ kāṇmin pādi nīr uymmin nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam*

**Пословный перевод:**

ulagil – for the residents of this earth; toṇḍarai – those who roam around doing menial services; il – greatness of (their) household life; piṟappu – greatness of (their) birth; aṟiyīr – not knowing; ivar – those who are wealthy now; avar – were previously in poverty; eṇṇīr – without knowing; tanmai – their nature; innadu enṟu – is in this particular manner; uṇarīr – not knowing; kaṟpagam! – Oh generous ones who resemble desire fulfilling kalpaka tree!; pulavar – for learned persons; kaḷaigaṇ – Oh protector!; enṟu – saying in this manner; kaṇḍavā – as thought in the heart; pādum – praising; sol – for words; poruḷ – and meanings; āḷīr – you who are experts; vammin – come over; sollugēn – I am informing you (so that you don’t lose the apt goal); nīr – you who are like me; punal – by water; sūḻ – surrounded; kudandai – ārāvamudan emperumān who is mercifully residing in tirukkudandai; toḻumin – worship; nārāyaṇā ennum – the word which explains “I am all kinds of relationship”; nāmam – divine name; pādi – speaking fully; uymmin – be uplifted; nal poruḷ kāṇmin – see, this is the ultimate principle

**Перевод:**

**In this pāsuram, āḻvār is saying “Those who are ignorant may lose emperumān, but how are you who are intelligent and poets like me, losing him?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh poets who are experts in words and meanings, who roam around doing menial services to the residents of this world without knowing the greatness of their household life and birth, and without knowing that those who are wealthy now were in poverty previously, and without knowing that “their nature is in this particular manner”, who tell them “Oh generous ones who resemble desire fulfilling kalpaka tree! Oh protector of learned persons!” and praise them as thought in your hearts! Come over. I am informing you. You who are like me should worship ārāvamudan emperumān who is mercifully residing in tirukkudandai which is surrounded by water; be uplifted by speaking the divine name which explains “I am all kinds of relationship”; see, this is the ultimate principle.

- *il piṟappu aṟiyīr* – Know about how they are placed in their gārhastyam (household life) and their birth.
- *ivar avar ennīr* – When a person who was previously suffering due to poverty become rich now, without knowing “This must not have been acquired by his ability; he must have been blessed by sarvēśvaran”, you are thinking that such person is like śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi) who is wealthy from birth. Alternatively,
- *ivaravarennīr* – if seen as a single word, it means “you are unable to see the difference between any two persons”.
- *innadōr tanmai enṟu uṇarīr* – You cannot know the knowledge/ability of such person.
- *kaṟpagam* – You are saying “he will grant without thinking about any aspects”.
- *pulavar kaḷaigaṇ enṟu* – Such a person will hide when knowledgeable poets come to him seeking wealth. These poets will call such a person as “Our lord”.
- *ulagil kaṇḍavā toṇḍaraip pādum* – In this world, superficially praising those who are roaming around with lowly conduct.
- *sol poruḷ āḷīr* – You who are experts in words and their meanings. There is none who can beat you in word-play and there is none who is as good as you in understanding the principles.
- *sollugēn vammin* – As I show you the entity which matches your expertise in words and meanings, you come over.
- *sūḻ punal kudandaiyē toḻumin* – You need a river and a capital city – for you to praise someone in your poems. When you praise someone, you need someone who owns rivers, mountains and cities.
- *nal poruḷ kāṇmin* – You realise this ultimate principle. That is, emperumān is the goal as well as the means.
- *pādi nīr uymmin nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam* – I showed you the entity (bhagavān) which is the best amongst the principles which are known by words. Now you sing the divine names of such entity and be uplifted – says āḻvār. The short form of tirumantram, that is akāram (syllable “a”), is explained in  nārāyaṇa anuvākam “*ya: parassa mahēśvara:*“ (nārāyaṇa, the lord of lords). Among the words, akāram is the best. Among the principles which are explained through the words, ārāvamudan emperumān is the greatest.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.8. Karrilen kalaigal

*kaṟṟilēn kalaigaḷ aimpulan karudum karuttuḷē tiruttinēn manattai peṟṟilēn adanāl pēdaiyēn nanmai perunilattāruyirkkellām seṟṟamē vēṇḍit tiritaruvēn tavirndēn selgadikkuyyumāṟeṇṇi naltuṇaiyāgap paṟṟinēn adiyēn nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam*

**Пословный перевод:**

kalaigaḷ – śāstrams; kaṟṟilēn – I have not learned (from an ācārya); aim pulan – five senses; karudum – sought out; karuttuḷ – in matters; manattai – mind; tiruttinēn – intentionally engaged; adanāl – due to this; pēdaiyēn – I who am ignorant; nanmai – good thoughts; peṟṟilēn – did not have; peru – vast; nilattu – earth; Ar – filled; uyirkku ellām – for all creatures; seṟṟamē – ways to harm; vēṇḍi – thinking; tiritaruvēn – roaming around; tavirndēn – I was freed from all of that; selgadikku – to go to paramapadam which is the apt destination (through arcirādi mārgam); uyyum āṟu – path to be uplifted; eṇṇi – considering; adiyēn – I who am a servitor; nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam – the divine name, nārāyaṇa; nal tuṇaiyāga – as good help; paṟṟinēn – held on

**Перевод:**

**The poets who were invited in previous pāsuram asked “If you look at our previous conduct, how can we become experts in the principle you are explaining?” āḻvār responds “What an ignorance! I who was worse than you have now become qualified to advice you in this subject; hence is there anyone who is unqualified for this?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I have not learned śāstrams. I intentionally engaged in the matters which are sought out by the five senses. Due to this, I, who am ignorant, did not have any good thoughts. I was roaming around the vast earth which is filled with creatures thinking about ways to harm them. I was freed from all of that. Considering to go to paramapadam which is the apt destination, as the path to be uplifted, I, who am a servitor, held on to the divine name, nārāyaṇa as good help.

- *kaṟṟilēn kalaigaḷ* – Since I did not follow an ācārya and learn from him by repeating the words he uttered, I have not acquired knowledge in śāstram.
- *aim pulan karudum karuttuḷē – tiruttinēn manattai* – Had I focussed my mind on emperumān and withdrawn the senses which were attached to worldly pleasures, from those pleasures at least sometimes, and made them focus internally, that would have led to pursuing a noble path; as the senses such as hearing etc were engaged in worldly pleasures and took me in the path which were pleasing to them, I facilitated the mind to follow them.
- *tiruttinēn manattai* – Those who are attached to worldly pleasures, will take up medication to increase the pleasure. Similarly, I forcefully engaged my mind in worldly pleasures.
- *peṟṟilēn adanāl pēdaiyēn nanmai* – Due to lacking knowledge in śāstram and being engaged in worldly pleasures, I became ignorant and did not think about my \[real\] well-being.
- *peru nilattu Ar uyirkku ellām seṟṟamē vēṇḍit tiritaruvēn* – Not only was I not doing anything good for the self, but was also constantly thinking about ways to harm others. I was looking for ways to harm all others and survive happily. nanjīyar would frequently say “One can know whether one has bhagavat sambandam (relationship with bhagavān) oneself”. When one sees someone suffering, if one feels compassionate and says “Alas!”, one can understand “We have bhagavat sambandam”; if one thinks “he should suffer more”, then one can understand “We don’t have bhagavat sambandam”. This can be split as “*peru nilattu Ar uyirkku ellām*” (for the creatures who are filling this vast world) or “*perunilattār uyirkku ellām*” (for the life of all the people of this world).
- *tavirndēn* – I don’t know the reason. I just observed that I am freed from all of the aforementioned aspects. He himself said previously in 1st pāsuram “*uyvadōr poruḷ*” (the principle which helped me to be uplifted), 5th pāsuram “*āḻiyān aruḷ*” (the mercy of sarvēśvaran, who has the chakra) and 5th pāsuram “*sikkenat tiruvaruḷ peṟṟēn*” (firmly got his divine mercy).
- *sel gadikku uyyum āṟu eṇṇi* – There is a destination to be reached – paramapadam. Contemplating the travel to that abode and being uplifted there.
- *nal tuṇaiyāgap paṟṟinēn adiyēn* – Unlike tying oneself to a rock and jumping into a river, holding on to what is said in garuda purāṇam 220.16 “*pādēyam puṇḍarikākśa nāma sankīrtanāmrutam*” (Chanting of the divine names of the lotus-eyed lord is the food/pastime during the journey), I held on to the one which will help us reach the shore.
- *nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam* – The divine name of the entity who helps us reach the shore. It is said in varāha carama ślōkam “*nayāmi paramām gatim*” (I carry my devotees to the highest abode).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.9. Kulandarum

*kulandarum selvam tandidum adiyār padu tuyar āyinavellām nilandaram seyyum nīḷ visumbaruḷum aruḷodu perunilam aḷikkum valandarum maṟṟum tandidum peṟṟa tāyinum āyina seyyum nalandarum sollai nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam*

**Пословный перевод:**

nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam – the divine name, nārāyaṇa; kulam – (for those who meditate upon it) birth in great family; tarum – will grant; selvam – wealth; tarum – will grant; adiyār – servitors; padu – the sins to be experienced and exhausted; tuyar āyina ellām – everything which is known as du:kham (sorrow); nilam taram seyyum – will completely flatten; nīḷ visumbu – paramapadam; aruḷum – will grant; aruḷodu – with mercy; peru nilam – the great position of kainkaryam; aḷikkum – will grant; valam – strength (to enjoy him); tarum – will grant; maṟṟum – all other aspects of well-being; tandidum – will facilitate; peṟṟa tāyinum – more than the mother who gave the body; āyina – expansion of true knowledge which is good; seyyum – will cause; nalam tarum – giving kainkaryaśrī (wealth of servitude); sollai – divine name; nān – I who had no knowledge about the existence of such wealth; kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – got to realise

**Перевод:**

**In the first pāsuram, āḻvār explained “I was engaged in worldly pleasures since time immemorial, and was facing away from bhagavat viśayam; when I realised the limit of worldly pleasures, I retracted and sarvēśvaran due to his mercy accepted me by saying ‘uyvadōr poruḷāl’ “. In the second pāsuram, he explained that he wasted the whole time in worldly pleasures. In the third pāsuram, he explained “I, who desired protection, engaged in sinful actions which are contrary to such result, and wasted my time in a useless manner by engaging in worldly pleasures, got to see sarvēśvaran who is enjoyable and apt, and the divine name which indicates him”. In the fourth pāsuram, he explained “Being prideful, worrying for the aspects which are not worthy to be worried for, being attached to worldly pleasures, I, who am filled with ignoble qualities, got the result which is attained by those who have noble qualities such as amānitvam (without feeling proud)”. In the fifth pāsuram, he explained “I had stolen my ātmā which is owned by bhagavān in a day-light robbery, and on seeing those who speak about the existence of bhagavān, I convinced them to think otherwise by my superficial arguments; but I got the result which is attained by those who are fully surrendered and are engaged in him always”. In the sixth pāsuram, when asked “What is the meaning for this divine name? How did you get it?” he explained its meaning and said “while the samsāris (worldly people) are suffering like this, I got this benefit”. In the seventh pāsuram, he said “Let others lose emperumān; you who are intelligent poets like me who are singing and roaming around, don’t lose such emperumān”. In the eighth pāsuram, when asked “Can we become experts in this principle?” he said “Oh ignorant one! Have I not become an expert and advising you now? In such case, no one is barred from become bhagavān’s servitor”. In this pāsuram, when asked “you are greatly celebrating the divine name; what fruits can it bestow?” he is explaining the benefits granted by tirunāmam \[divine name\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divine name, nārāyaṇa will grant birth in a great clan; will grant wealth; will completely flatten everything which is known as sorrow and the sins which are to be experienced and exhausted for the servitors; will grant paramapadam and the great position of kainkaryam; will grant strength; will facilitate all other aspects of well-being; more than the mother who gave the body, the divine name will cause the expansion of true knowledge which is good; I who had no knowledge about the existence of kainkaryaśrī (wealth of servitude), got to realise the divine name which gives such wealth of servitude.

- *kulam tarum* – emperumān’s greatness is such that when a person who has low birth and inferior conduct, acquires bhagavat sambandam \[through this divine name\], another person who has high birth and superior conduct, will not dare to think “the other person is inferior to me and I am superior to him”. Still, they don’t marry within such families, due to birth based restrictions \[ordained in śāstram\]. The greatness is due to the quality \[of being a devotee\]; it is said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.131 “*sa ślājñas saguṇī danya: sa kuleena:*”  (He is best; he is filled with good qualities; he has good conduct; he is born in noble family). darmaputra (yudiśtira) who analyses every aspect to confirm if it is righteous or not, before engaging in it, performed brahmamēda samskāram (final rites) for vidura based on vidura’s close friendship with kriṣṇa and based on the divine command from aśarīrī (voice from the formless entity); riśis (sages) would wait outside the meat shop of darmavyāda (meat seller) until he completes his duty and then would get their doubts clarified. If this (greatness based on being bhāgavatas) is not true, these incidents would not have been documented in mahābhārata which is known as pancama vēda (fifth vēdam). As seen in the kaiśika purāṇa history, a distinguished brāhmaṇa who became a demon due to mistakes committed in his yāgams, was freed from his curse by a pāduvān (singer) who has true knowledge about bhagavān. When śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān advised rāvaṇan “surrender unto perumāḷ (śrī rāma)”, rāvaṇan said to him that he was not fit to be in the rākśasa clan as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 16.15 “*tvām tu dik kulapāmsanam*” (you are an outcast from our rākśasa clan). When advising rāvaṇan, he said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 16.26 “*niśācara*“, implying that rāvaṇan is a demon while he (vibhīśaṇāḻvān) is not. perumāḷ too said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.7 “*rākśasānām balābalam*” (You tell me about the strengths and weaknesses of rākśasas). Hence, bhagavat sambandam is like a sparśavēdi (touchstone).
- *selvam tandidum* – When the relationship with rāvaṇa was severed,  as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 16.17 “*antarikśagata: śrīmān*” (vibhīśaṇa, who went through the path of sky and who is wealthy), attained the wealth due to rāma sambandam (relationship with śrī rāma). Alternatively – it could mean the wealth of lankā itself. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.5 “*parityaktā mayā lankā*” (wealth of lankā has been given up by me), though he gave up, as the relationship with rāvaṇa was severed, due to the relationship with śrī rāma, he attained the wealth of lankā and the throne. It is said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 5.9 “*ninnaiyē tān vēṇḍi nīḷ selvam vēṇḍādān tannaiyē tān vēṇḍum selvam*” (for those who are desiring for you only and not desiring for the permanent wealth, the wealth will come to them). kulaśēkarāḻvār is saying – when one is desirous towards you only and not desiring for the impermanent wealth \[the “nīḷ – permanent” in the pāsuram, is sarcasm\], the wealth will not abandon such person. Alternative explanation – when one desires for you even ignoring the permanent wealth \[of mōkśam – liberation\], mōkśam will not abandon such a person.
- *adiyār padu tuyar āyina ellām* – adiyār – those who fully exist for him; padu tuyar – the sufferings they go through as said in brahma vaivairtam prakruti kāṇḍam 26.70 “*avaśyam anubhōktavyam*” (must be experienced), the fruits of actions which need to be experienced to exhaust them; all of those,
- *nilam taram seyyum* – Will totally flatten/eradicate them. Alternatively – nilam indicates the abode of the person who is having the sins, taram – a variation of taraṇam which means elimination; the divine name will make the sins run away from the person thinking “this is not my abode”. nāradīya purāṇam 1.20 “*yatra aśtākśara samsiddō mahābhāgō mahīyatē \| na tatra sancariśyanti vyādi durbhikśa taskarā: \|\|*” (Where the person who learnt aśtākśaram and lives by that, is praised, there will be no disease, famine and robbery). periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.3 “*summenādē kaivittōdit tūṟugaḷ pāyndanavē*” (ran away being unable to breathe and went hiding into the bushes). periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.4 “*kōlādi kuṟugappeṟā*” (he cannot come close to where I rule) . Another explanation – nilam indicates the body which originated from panca bhūtams (five elements) starting with prutivī (earth), all the sins will end with this body. For bhaktimān (bhakti yōga practitioner), liberation will be at the end of prārabda karma; for the one who has become prapanna by meditating upon the meanings of the divine name, liberation will be at the end of this (present) body.
- *nīḷ visumbu aruḷum* – virōdi nivrutti (elimination of hurdles) is ending of this body. Not stopping with that, divine name will grant paramapadam also.
- *aruḷodu peru nilam aḷikkum* – The great position – kainkaryam. The divine name will grant that.
- *varam tarum* – It will grant the kainkaryam which is prayed by the individual as said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1 “*oḻivil kālam*” (without any break, I should serve).
- *valam tarum* – Also means the same as in *varam tarum*. Alternatively,
- *valam tarum* – valam means balam (strength). As said in kriṣṇa yajur 7.5.36 “*ya ātmadā baladā:*” (one who gives himself and the strength to enjoy him), the divine name will grant itself and the strength to enjoy itself. For the one who has been nitya samsāri (have been in samsāram until now), it will grant the strength of the nityasūris (eternal associates of emperumān) who enjoy him eternally. Alternatively,
- *aruḷodu peru nilam aḷikkum valam tarum* – Not stopping with those who pursued the divine name, it will shower the mercy to make them grant paramapadam even for those who are related to them.
- *maṟṟum tandidum* – Whatever is good for the individual, even if he does not know about that, the divine name will grant on its own; it will grant thinking “does he know what is good for him? I should do it for him”. When gōvindasvāmi saw emperumān, he said “I will come with you”; emperumān knew his heart and said “You remain here enjoying worldly pleasures for sometime and then come to me” and left \[this incident is explained in periya tirumoḻi 5.8.5\].
- *peṟṟa tāyinum āyina seyyum* – The mother gives birth to the body only; ācāryan (through the tirumantram) is the one who will grant true knowledge for the ātmā. As said in āpastam dharma sūtram 1.1.6 “*śarīram Eva mātā pitarau janayata:*” (the body is given by the mother and the father), the parents create the body which is a hurdle; but ācāryan grants jñānam (knowledge) as said in the same sūtram “*sa hi vidyāta: tam janayati tat śrēśtam janma*” (ācārya is the one who gives true knowledge and gives him real birth).
- *nalam tarum sollai* – The recitation of the word itself (even without meditation on the meaning) will grant bhakti; altenatively, nalam – activity; it will grant kainkaryam. Thus, it will grant the ruci (taste) for kainkaryam or kainkaryam itself.
- *nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn* – I who had no prior knowledge about this, got to realise it.
- *nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam* – That which is said in brahma purāṇam 57.24 – nāradīya kalpam – aśtākśara brahma vidyā “*namō nārāyaṇāyēti mantra: savārta sādaka:*” (This single aśtākśara mantram itself can grant all benefits).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.10. Manjulam solai

*manjulām sōlai vaṇḍaṟai mānīr mangaiyār vāḷ kalikanṟi senjolāl edutta deyva nal mālai ivaikoṇḍu cikkenat toṇḍīr! tunjumbōdu aḻaimin tuyarvaril ninaimin tuyarileer sollilum nanṟām nanjudān kaṇḍīr nammudai vinaikku nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam*

**Пословный перевод:**

manju – clouds; ulām – moving around; sōlai – garden; vaṇḍu – beetles; aṟai – humming; mā nīr – have abundant water; mangaiyār – protection for the residents of tirumangai region; vāḷ – having sword; kalikanṟi – āḻvār who eliminated the defects of kali; sem solāl – with beautiful words; edutta – mercifully spoken to be known by all; deyvam – divine; nal – distinguished; mālai – garland of words; ivai koṇḍu – with this tirumoḻi (decad); tunjumbōdu – at the end of the body; aḻaimin – call out; tuyar varil – when afflicted with sorrows; ninaimin – meditate upon this only; tuyarileer – Oh you who have no sorrows; sollilum – even if you recited; nanṟām – will lead to goodness; nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam – the divine name, nārāyaṇa; nammudai – our; vinaikku – for sins; nanjudān kaṇḍīr – is poison!

**Перевод:**

**tirumangai āḻvār, who eliminated the defects of kali and is having the sword as protection for the residents of tirumangai region which is having gardens where clouds are moving around, beetles are humming and is having abundant water, mercifully spoke these beautiful words to be known by all, in the form of a divine, distinguished garland of words. At the end of your body, you call out with this decad; when afflicted with sorrows, meditate upon this decad only; oh you who have no sorrows, even if you recited, this will lead to goodness; the divine name, nārāyaṇa, is the poison (antidote) for our sins.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

- *manju ulām sōlai* – The garden which is tall to have clouds moving around inside it.
- *vaṇḍu aṟai* – Humming beetles can be an adjective to the garden; or for the abundant water. Due to the tasty water, tamiḻ poets would praise the flowing rivers saying “Flies and beetles are swarming the water”.
- *mangaiyār vāḷ kalikanṟi* – Just as those who have realised their relationship will consider such bhagavān’s strength as their own, those who are in tirumangai consider āḻvār’s sword as their strength.
- *sem solāl edutta* – The meanings which were explained in a way that only qualified persons can learn, in samskrutam and in unfamiliar words, are revealed in an easy/beautiful manner to be known by all.
- *deyva nal mālai* – Divine, garland of words, which are enjoyed by nityasūris as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.11 “*kēttārār vānavargaḷ*” (nityasūris will never satiate hearing tiruvāimoḻi – would hear it repeatedly).
- *ivai koṇḍu sikkenat toṇḍīr tunjumbōdu aḻaimin* – At the end of your body, without fearing to be controlled by yama, recite this divine name.
- *tuyar varil ninaimin* – Even when you are afflicted with sorrows here, recite this name only.
- *tuyarileer sollilum nanṟām* – The recital of divine name is done as svayam prayōjanam (no other expectation than recital itself) for those ananyaprayōjanar (those who have no expectation other than kainkaryam) who don’t care about such sorrows and would say “when we are in this world with a body, it is natural to be afflicted with sorrows”.
- *nanjudān kaṇḍīr nammudai vinaikku* – For our sins, this is the intolerable poison.
- *nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam* – The divine name which is sweet for us as said in periya tiumoḻi 6.10.6 “*enakku enṟum tēnum pālum amudumāya tirumāl tirunāmam nānum sonnēn namarum uraimin namō nārāyaṇamē*” (The divine name of śrīman nārāyaṇa is honey, milk and nectar for me always; as I have recited this name, all of you who are related to me should also recite this name ‘*namō nārāyaṇa*‘). Other names will lead to deep rooted stay in samsāram (material world). Should everyone not understand that the meditation upon the meaning of this divine name itself will sever the ties with this samsāram?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
