## 1.3.8. Isi pomin

*īsi pōmin īngu irēnmin irumiyiḷaittīr uḷḷam kūsiyittīr enṟu pēsum kuvaḷaiyam kaṇṇiyarpāl nāsamāna pāsam vittu nanneṟi nōkkaluṟil vāsam malgu taṇḍuḻāyān vadari vaṇangudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pōmin – Go away; īsi – “cī! cī!” (tamiḻ phrase to show disgust); īngu – here; irēnmin – don’t stay; irumi – due to cough; iḷaittīr – have a weakened body (hearing our words); uḷḷam kūsi ittīr – felt shameful in your heart; enṟu pēsum – those who speak this way; kuvaḷai – like a kuvaḷai flower; am – beautiful; kaṇṇiyarpāl – towards women who have eyes; nāsamāna pāsam – attachment which will lead to destruction; vittu – giving up; nal neṟi nōkkal uṟil – while looking out for the noble path; vāsam malgu – filled with fragrance; taṇ – cool; tuḻāyān – where sarvēśvaran who is adorning tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) is permanently residing; vadari – śrī badari; vaṇangudum – let us worship

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Let us worship śrī badari where sarvēśvaran who is adorning fragrant, cool tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) is permanently residing, while looking out for the noble path after giving up attachment which will lead to destruction, towards women who have beautiful eyes which resemble kuvaḷai flower say “Go away! cī cī! (disgusting) Don’t stay here. Your body has weakened due to cough and you feel ashamed in your heart”.

- *īsi pōmin* – Saying “Go away! cī cī!”
- *pōmin* – The women will say “Go away!” The man will think otherwise due to past impressions \[previously, they would say playfully “Go away!” indicating her intent to have him there\], and remain there.
- *īngu irēlmin* – They will say “Do you know where you are? You have no connection with this place. Hence, you must go”.

At that time, he will say “Why so? Why should I go?” They will respond,

- *irumi iḷaittīr – uḷḷam kūsi ittīr* – You have become weak due to cough. You know about yourself. Thinking about our presence, you will think “Why am I being insulted in front of everyone in this manner” and will feel ashamed. Those women who say in this manner.
- *kuvaḷai am kaṇṇiyarpāl* – They will see the way he is insulted, very eagerly. He will think – whether very strong poison or very sweet nectar, it is a fortune to be seen by them. This way their glance will stir up his emotions towards them.
- *nāsamāna pāsam vittu* … – This attachment will lead to his destruction in any situation. Attachment in lowly matters will naturally lead to destruction. Giving it up, while looking out for noble path, one should worship śrī badari where emperumān is adorning a tuḷasi garland to support those who surrender unto him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.3.9. Pulangal naiya

*pulangaḷ naiya meyyil mūttup pōndirunduḷḷam eḷgi kalanga aikkaḷ pōda vundik  kaṇḍa pidaṟṟā mun alangalāya taṇḍuḻāy koṇḍu āyira nāmam solli valangoḷ toṇḍar pādi ādum vadari vaṇangudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

meyyil – in the body; pulangaḷ – senses; naiya – to become weak; mūttu – having become old; pōndu – going to a secluded place; irundu – remaining (there); uḷḷam eḷgi – having the heart worried; kalanga – as imbalance (in vāda, pitta and ślēśma) occurs (due to that); aikkaḷ – kapam (mucus); pōda undi – getting pushed out greatly; kaṇḍa – as things are seen; pidaṟṟā mun – before blabbering; valam koḷ – (performing favourable actions such as) circumambulating etc; toṇḍar – śrīvaiṣṇavas who are servitors; alangalāya – in the form of a garland; taṇ tuḻāy – cool tiruttuḻāy; koṇḍu – holding in hand; āyiram nāmam – (his) thousand divine names; solli – recite; pādi – sing; ādum – dancing; vadari – sarvēśvaran who is residing in śrī badari; vaṇangudum – let us worship

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Let us worship sarvēśvaran who is residing in śrī badari where śrīvaiṣṇavas who are servitors are performing favourable actions such as circumambulating etc, holding cool tiruttuḻāy garland in their hands and reciting his divine names, singing and dancing; let us do this before becoming old to have the senses in the body weakening, going to a secluded place and remaining there with a worried heart, having imbalance in vāta, pitta and ślēśma, the mucus getting pushed out greatly and blabbering as things are seen.

- *pulan* … – While the senses remain in the body, they would be unable to enjoy their respective objects and become very old to have weakened senses.
- *pōndirundu* – Unlike others, being unable to see and hear properly, going to a secluded place and remaining there.
- *uḷḷam eḷgi* – Heart becoming worried “Why are we suffering!”
- *kalanga …* – As three types of defects (vāta, pitta, kapa) rise, the mucus gets pushed out.
- *kaṇḍa pidaṟṟāmun* – Before blabbering about the hurdles.
- *alangalāya* – Carrying the tiruttuḻāy garland which is having the greatness to be offered to emperumān.
- *āyira nāmam solli* – Instead of blabbering gibberish, reciting the thousand divine names which are apt for the senses, as said in [mudal tiruvandādi 95](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-95/) “*nāvāyiluṇḍē* …”.
- *valam koḷ* – śrīvaiṣṇavas who perform favourable actions (kainkaryams), carrying garlands which qualify to be adorned by him, reciting his divine names, and would sing and dance; let us enter that assembly and become one amongst them.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.3.10. Vandu tanden

*vaṇḍu taṇ tēn uṇḍu vāḻum vadari nedumālaik kaṇḍal vēli mangai vēndan kaliyan oli mālai koṇḍu toṇḍar pādi ādak  kūdidil nīḷ visumbil aṇḍam allāl maṟṟavarkku  ōrātci aṟiyōmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu – beetles; taṇ tēn – cool honey; uṇḍu – drink; vāḻum – living joyfully; vadari – mercifully residing in śrī badari; nedumālai – on the supreme lord; kaṇḍal – tāḻai (a type of plant); vēli – as protective fence; mangai – for tirumangai; vēndan – king; kaliyan – mercifully spoken by āḻvār; oli mālai koṇḍu – with this decad which is having a garland of words; toṇḍar – servitors; pādi – sing; ādak kūdidil – if they can dance; nīḷ visumbil allāl – other than in paramapadam; maṟṟu – any other; ōr aṇḍam – a world; avarkku – for them; ātci aṟiyōm – won’t rule

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The supreme lord is mercifully residing in śrī badari where beetles are drinking the cool honey and living joyfully; āḻvār is the king of tirumangai region which is having tāḻai plants as protective fence; those servitors who sing and dance with this decad which is having a garland of words, will not rule any world other than paramapadam.

- *vaṇḍu taṇ tēn …* – This śrī badari is the abode where every sentient entity will live joyfully having attained its desires. āḻvār glorified sarvēśvaran who has arrived and is residing in such śrī badari, through these pāsurams.
- *kaṇḍal vēli* – kaṇḍal = tāḻai. Since the ocean is in close proximity, tāḻai plants will be there. The garland of words composed by āḻvār who is the king of tirumangi region which is having blossomed tāḻai plants as fence.
- *koṇḍu toṇḍar pādi ādak kūdidil* – Having these pāsurams, if the devotees who determined to serve as in tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1 “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍum*” (would like to serve without any break) gathered to sing and dance.
- *nīḷ visumbu* – Collection of the higher worlds; among those,
- *aṇḍam allāl* – Other than aṇḍam (paramapadam), they won’t rule any other place; alternative explanation – nīḷ visumbu – paramapadam, other than that they won’t rule any other world. In the prakruti (primordial matter) and prākrutam (worldly matters), the defects he mercifully explained are very clearly experienced by us; similarly, his instructions in bhagavat viśayam will also be truthful; hence, it is apt for cētanas (sentient beings), to abandon what āḻvār highlights to be abandoned and pursue what he highlights to be pursued.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4 Enamunagi

## 1.4.1. Enamunagi

*ēnamunāgi irunilam idandu anṟu iṇaiyadi imaiyavar vaṇangat tānavanāgam taraṇiyil puraḷat tadanjilai kunitta en talaivan tēnamar sōlaik kaṟpagam payanda deyva nal naṟumalar koṇarndu vānavar vaṇangum gangaiyin karaimēl vadariyāccirāmattuḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – long ago (when earth was consumed by deluge); imaiyavar – brahmā et al; iṇai adi – divine feet which are beautiful together; vaṇanga – to worship; mun – in the beginning of varāha kalpa (one day of brahmā); ēnamāgi – assuming the form of a wild-boar; iru nilam – vast earth; idandu – dug it out; tānavan – rāvaṇa who was born in danu clan, his; āgam – body; taraṇiyil – on earth; puraḷa – to roll; tadam – big; silai – bow; kunitta – mercifully bent; en talaivan – nārāyaṇa, my lord; tēn amar – having abundance of honey; sōlai – spread out like an orchard; kaṟpagam – kalpaka tree; payanda – created; deyvam – divine; nal – distinguished; naṟu – fragrant; malar – flowers; vānavar – dēvatās; koṇarndu – brought (and submitted); vaṇangum – to worship; gangaiyin karai mēl – on the banks of gangā; vadari āccirāmattu – in badarikāśramam; uḷḷān – is mercifully residing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Long ago, my lord, nārāyaṇan, assuming the form of a wild-boar, dug out the vast earth from the ocean of deluge in the beginning of varāha kalpa, to have his divine feet vorśipped by brahmā et al; he mercifully bent his big bow to make the body of rāvaṇa who is a descendant of danu clan, roll on the earth. Such emperumān is mercifully residing in badarikāśramam which is on the banks of gangā, to be vorśipped by dēvatās who bring along divine, distinguished, fragrant flowers which were created by kalpa tree which is spread out like an orchard and is having abundance of honey.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *mun ēnam āgi* – In the beginning of varāha kalpa (one of the days of brahmā), went up to the wall of the oval shaped universe, and dug out the vast earth; having a strong form of mahāvarāha (great wild-boar) to dig out the earth.
- *anṟu iṇai adi imaiyavar vaṇanga* – At that time, to be surrendered by those brahmā et al who were hiding in emperumān’s mane (hair on his head).  It is said in “*sukavikata satā sankatai:*” (the dēvatās who are present in the mane which is praised by poets).
- *tānavan …* – Here rāvaṇa is called as dānava. It is said in periya tirumoḻi 2.2.2 “*taiyalāḷ mēl kādal seyda tānavan vaḷ arakkan*” (rāvaṇa, the demon who has the sword gifted by rudra and who showed his inappropriate love towards pirātti). Since he is a descendant of danu, he is known as dānavan. ōr, he is known as dānava due to his demoniac qualities. To have the body of rāvaṇa, which was nourished by boons etc, to be hit with the arrow and roll on the ground.
- *tadam silai …* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 99.12 “*mahad danu:*” (the great bow), one who bent the bow which has great power.
- *en talaivan* – My lord who is the foremost in valour.
- *tēn amar …* – Due to rāvaṇa’s power, dēvatās will serve him with the flowers of kalpaka tree; on having his head severed, they will offer those flowers to the apt lord.  The kalpaka tree which is in the form of an orchard with abundance of honey, created divine, distinguished, fresh flowers. To be vorśipped by dēvatās with such flowers, emperumān arrived at śrī badarikāśramam on the banks of gangā.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4.2. Kanidai uruvai

*kānidai uruvaic cudu saram turandu kaṇḍumun kodundoḻil uravōn ūnudai agalattu adukaṇai kuḷippa ūyir kavarndu uganda em oruvan tēnudaik kamalattayanodu dēvar senṟu senṟu iṟainjida perugu vānidai mudunīrk kangaiyin karaimēl vadariyāccirāmattuḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kānidai – in the forest; uruvai – the illusory deer; kaṇḍu – saw; sudu saram – arrow which will burn; turandu – shooting (at it); mun – on the day when surgrīva surrendered; kodum toḻil – cruel activity; uravōn – on vāli who is strong as well; Un udai – filled with flesh; agalattu – on the chest; adu kaṇai – the killer arrow; kuḷippa – to pierce; uyir – (his) life; kavarndu – took away; uganda – and became pleased; em oruvan – my lord who has matchless strength; tēn udai – having honey; kamalattu – born in the lotus flower in emperumān’s divine navel; ayanodu – with brahmā; dēvar – dēvatās; senṟu senṟu – pushing each other and entered; iṟainjida – to bathe \[and purify oneself\] before surrendering; vānidai – on the sky; mudu nīr – the ancient water; perugu – flowing greatly; gangaiyin karai mēl – on the banks of gangā; vadariyācciramattu uḷḷān – is mercifully residing in śrī badarīkāśramam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My lord who has matchless strength shot the arrow which will burn when he saw the illusory deer in the forest; he took away the life of vāli who has cruel activity and strength, by shooting the killer arrow to pierce his chest which is filled with flesh, when sugrīva took refuge, and became pleased; such emperumān is mercifully residing in śrī badarīkāśramam on the banks of gangā where the ancient water is greatly flowing from the sky, as brahmā who was born in the honey-filled lotus flower in emperumān’s divine navel, entered along with other dēvatās pushing each other, to bathe before surrendering to emperumān.

- *kān …* – The illusory deer which was roaming around in the forest which was its natural habitat. Seeing that,
- *sudu saram turandu* – Seeing the deer which was hiding and appearing in front of others, shooting the arrow which cannot be tolerated; this was previously.
- *kodum toḻil …* – He made the killer arrow pierce the fleshy, vast chest of vāli who had cruel activity, and took away his life in that manner and became pleased thinking “We eliminated the enemy of sugrīva mahārājar”. Such emperumān with matchless strength.
- *tēn …* – Along with dēvatās, brahmā who has emperumān’s divine navel lotus as the birth place, pushed each other and entered, and as they started bathing to surrender to emperumān, the ancient water which remains still, started overflowing. Just as kāviri river originates from sahyam (mountai), here bhagavān’s lotus feet are the origin for gangā.
- *vānidai munnīr* – The ancient water flowing down from sky.

## 1.4.3. Ilangaiyum kadalum

*ilangaiyum kadalum adalarum tuppil irunidikkiṟaivanum arakkar kulangaḷum kedamun kodundoḻil purinda koṟṟavan koḻunjudar suḻanṟa vilangalil urinji mēl ninṟa visumbil veṇḍhugil kodiyena virindu valandaru maṇinīrk kangaiyin karai mēl vadariyāccirāmattuḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ilangaiyum – lankā; kadalum – ocean; adal arum – invincible (by anyone); tuppil – having strength; irunidikku iṟaivanum – rāvaṇa who is the lord of Sanka nidi and padma nidi; arakkar kulangaḷum – the demoniac clan; keda – to be destroyed; mun – during rāmāvatāram; kodu – cruel; toḻil – acts; purinda – performed; koṟṟavan – sarvēśvaran, the king; koḻu – shining; sudar – sun; suḻanṟa – circumambulate; vilangalil – on mēru mountain; urinji – hit; mēl ninṟa – atop; visumbil – on the sky; veḷ – having whitish colour; kodit tugil ena – like a cloth hoisted on a flag-post; virindu – vastly spread; valam tarum – being strong (due to its force); maṇi – clear; nīr – filled with water; gangaiyin karai mēl – on the banks of gangā; vadariyāccirāmattu uḷḷān – is eternally residing in śrī badarīkāśramam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, the king, performed cruel acts during rāmāvatāram to destroy lankā, ocean, invincibly strong rāvaṇa who is the lord of Sanka nidi and padma nidi, and the demoniac clan; gangā hits the mēru mountain which is circumambulated by the shining sun, and flowing on the sky which is atop, like a vastly spread whitish cloth hoisted on a flag-post, is filled with strong and clear water; such sarvēśvaran is eternally residing in śrī badarīkāśramam which is on the banks of such gangā.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *ilangaiyum …* – sarvēśvaran, the king, who previously performed cruel acts to destroy lankā which cannot be destroyed by anyone, the ocean which is like a protective layer for such lankā, rāvaṇa who has the ability to resist anyone’s efforts to win over him and who is the owner of Sanka nidi and padma nidi which were taken away from vaiśravaṇa (kubēra) after defeating him and the demoniac clan which is rāvaṇa’s strength, and make them all bite the dust. It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 18.6 “*ikśvākūṇām iyam bhūmi: saśaila vanakānanā*” (The kings of ikśvāku dynasty are the rulers of this earth which has mountains, small and big forests).
- *koḻum sudar …* – Hitting mēru mountain which is circumambulated by sun, on the sky which is atop, the gangā falls with clear water just as a white cloth was spread on a flag-post.
- *valam taru maṇi nīr* – Water being very clear due to the strength derived from its force.

## 1.4.4. Tunivini

*tuṇivini unakkuc colluvan manamē! toḻudeḻu toṇḍargaḷ tamakkup piṇiyoḻittu amarar peruvisumbu aruḷum pēraruḷāḷan emperumān aṇimalarkkuḻalār arambaiyar tugilum āramum vāri vandu aṇinīr maṇi koḻittiḻinda gangaiyin karaimēl vadariyāccirāmattuḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

manamē – Oh mind!; ini – now; unakku – to you who don’t know the greatness of bhagavān; tuṇivu – a firm advise; solluvan – I am giving; toṇḍargaḷ tamakku – for the devotees; piṇi – hurdles; pōkki – eliminate; amarar – nityasūris’; peru visumbu – paramapadamn \[śrīvaikuṇṭam\]; aruḷum – mercifully granting; pēr aruḷāḷan – very merciful; emperumān – sarvēśvaran; aṇi nīr – beautiful water; malar – with flowers; aṇi – decorated; kuḻalār – having hair; arambaiyar – the celestial girls’; tugilum – clothes; āramum – ornaments; vāri vandu – gathering those; maṇi – precious gems; koḻittu – pushing; iḻinda – coming; gangaiyin karai mēl – on the banks of gangā; vadariyāccirāmattu – in śrī badarīkāśramam; uḷḷān – mercifully residing (him); toḻudu – worship; eḻu – try to be uplifted

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh mind! Now, I am giving a firm advice to you who don’t know the greatness of bhagavān. The very merciful sarvēśvaran who eliminates the hurdles of his devotees and grants nityasūris’ paramapadam to such devotees, is mercifully residing in śrī badarīkāśramam on the banks of gangā, where the water gathers garments, ornaments of the celestial girls who are having hair which is decorated with flowers, and the precious gems are being pushed along. You worship such sarvēśvaran and try to be uplifted.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *tuṇivini unakkuc colluvan manamē toḻudu eḻu* – Oh mind! Now, I am firmly giving you a good advice. Listen to me; you worship him and try to be uplifted, so that my advice does not go in vain.

When asked “If you firmly advise, will he eliminate our hurdles?” āḻvār says,

- *piṇi …* – He will eliminate our hurdles and will grant paramapadam too. He is the greatly merciful sarvēśvaran, who will eliminate the hurdles on surrendering unto him and will also grant us the same position of nityasūris.
- *aṇi …* – The strength of the water matches kriṣṇa’s strength. Gathering the garments and ornaments of the celestial girls whose hair are decorated flowers. *aṇi nīr* – The water which decorates the banks; beautiful water. Gathering them, the beautiful water, brings precious gems along and flowing into śrī badarīkāśramam. emperumān who is residing in there; toḻudeḻu (worship and be uplifted) is the verb for the whole decad.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4.5. Peyidaikkirundu

*pēyidaikkirundu vanda maṟṟavaḷ tan perumulai suvaittidap peṟṟa tāyidaikkiruttal anjuvanenṟu taḷarndida vaḷarnda en talaivan sēymugattucci aṇḍamum sumanda semponsey vilangalil ilangu vāy mugattiḻinda gangaiyin karaimēl vadariyāccirāmattuḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vanda – one who arrived like mother; pēy – pūtanā’s; idaikku irundu – staying on her lap; maṟṟu – further; avaḷ than – her; peru mulai – large bosoms; suvaittida – consumed; peṟṟa tāy – yaśōdāp pirātti who is his real mother; idaikku – on (pūtanā’s) lap; iruttal – staying firmly; anjuvan – I am scared; enṟu – saying in this manner; taḷarndida – feeling ashamed; vaḷarnda – one who mercifully grew; en talaivan – my lord; sēy mugadu – tall peak’s; ucci – atop; aṇḍam – oval shaped universe; sumanda – holding; sem pon sey vilangalil – on the mēru mountain which is made of reddish gold; ilangu – shining; vāy – spacious; mugadu – from the peak; iḻindu – falling down; gangaiyin karaimēl – on the banks of gangā; vadariyāccirāmattu uḷḷānē – one who is residing in śrī badarikāśramam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān stayed on pūtanā’s lap and further consumed from the large bosoms of pūtanā who arrived like his mother; seeing that he is staying firmly on pūtanā’s lap, yaśōdāp pirātti, who is his real mother, felt ashamed and said “I am scared”; my lord mercifully, who grew up in this manner, is residing in śrī badarikāśramam on the banks of gangā which is falling down from the spacious, shining peak on the mēru mountain which is made of reddish gold, which is holding the oval shaped universe atop its tall peak.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *pēy …* – *vanda pēyidaikku irundu* – Staying on the lap of pūtanā who arrived in the form of yaśōdāp pirātti, and further consuming from her large bosoms.
- *peṟṟa tāy …* – yaśōdāp pirātti who saw that and felt ashamed thinking “kriṣṇa who is used to consuming milk from my bosoms, is sitting on the lap of an unknown, dangerous person who assumed my form now and is trying to consume from her bosoms” and raised kriṣṇa carefully. My lord who grew up in such manner.
- *sēy …* – emperumān has arrived and is present in śrī badarīkāśramam which is on the banks of gangā, which is falling from the shining, spacious peak of mēru, which is made of reddish gold and which holds the oval shaped universe atop its tall peak.

## 1.4.7. Vendiral kalirum

*vendiṟal kaḷiṟum vēlai vāy amudum viṇṇodu viṇṇavarkkarasum indiraṟkaruḷi emakkum īndaruḷum endai emmadigaḷ emperumān andarattu amarar adiyiṇai vaṇanga āyiramugattināl aruḷi mandarattiḻinda gangaiyin karaimēl vadariyāccirāmattuḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vem tiṟal – having great strength; kaḷiṟum – the elephant named airāvatam; vēlai vāy – came out of tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean); amudam – amrutam (nectar); viṇṇodu – with svargam (heaven); viṇṇavarkku arasum – being the king of dēvatās; indiraṟku – for indra; aruḷi – bestowed; emakkum – for us (who are ananyaprayōjanar (without any expectations)); īnda aruḷum – one who gives (himself); endai – being my father; em adigaḷ – being our lord; emperumān – being my master; andarattu – in svargam; amarar – dēvatās; adi iṇai – divine feet; vaṇanga – to worship; āyiram mugattināl aruḷi – as mercifully desired by the divine heart of sarvēśvaran to flow in thousand tributaries; mandarattu – from mantara mountain; iḻinda – fell down; gangaiyin karai mēl – on the banks of gangā; vadariyāccirāmattuḷḷānē – is residing in śrī badarīkāśramam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān bestowed the very strong elephant named airāvatam, the nectar which came out of tiruppāṟkadal, the heaven and the position of being the king to dēvatās to indra and mercifully gave himself to us who are ananyaprayōjanar; he is my father, our lord and master; such sarvēśvaran mercifully desired in his  divine heart, to have gangā flow in thousand tributaries from mantara mountain and fall down; he is residing in śrī badarīkāśramam on the banks of gangā to have his divine feet vorśipped by the dēvatās of heaven.

- *vendiṟal …* – emperumān mercifully bestowed airāvatam, the nectar from the milk ocean, heaven, and the position of being the king of dēvatās to indra and mercifully granted himself to me.
- *endai …* – My father, lord and who enslaved me by manifesting such relationships and actions.
- *andarattu amarar …* – sarvēśvaran thought “if all the dēvatās of heaven come to surrender at my divine feet, at once, tiruppāṟkadal will not be sufficient” and divinely ordered gangā “split up yourself into thousand tributaries and reach earth”, gangā fell down from mantara mountain in that manner. Alternative explanation – as dēvatās prayed to gangā, it split itself into thousand tributaries and fell down.
- *āyiram mugattināl* – As gangā passes through mēru mountain, mantara mountain and himavān (Himalaya) mountain, that could also be identified as thousand tributaries (ways), here.

## 1.4.8. Man munindu

*mān munindu oru kāl vari silai vaḷaitta mannavan ponniṟattu uravōn ūn munindu avanadudal irupiḷavā ugir nudi maduttu ayan aranait tān muninditta vendiṟal sābam tavirttavan tavam purinduyarnda māmunikoṇarnda gangaiyin karaimēl vadariyāccirāmattuḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oru kāl – while remaining in pancavati; mān – mārīca who came in the form of a deer; munindu – showing anger on; vari – beautiful; silai – bow; vaḷaitta – aimed (at him) by bending; mannavan – being the king; pon niṟam – having golden hue; uravōn – strong hiraṇya’s; Un – flesh; munindu – showing anger; avanadu – his; udal – body; iru piḷavā – to split into two parts; ugir nudi – the edge of his nails; maduttu – made to enter; avan tān – brahmā himself; aranai – rudra; munindu – showing anger; itta – gave; vem tiṟal – very cruel; sābam – curse; tavirttavan – sarvēśvaran who eliminated; tavam purindu – performing penance; uyarnda – became brahmariśi (due to that); māmuni – viśvāmitran; koṇarnda – (perumāḷ and iḷaiyaperumāḷ) brought along; gangaiyin karai mēl – on the banks of gangā; vadariyācciramattuḷḷānē – is residing in śrī badarīkāśramam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Showing anger on mārīca who came in the form of a deer, emperumān while remaining in pancavati, being the king, aimed his beautiful bow at him by bending it; showing anger on the strong hiraṇya, who was having a golden hue, made the edge of his nails enter his body to split it into two parts; sarvēśvaran eliminated the very cruel curse of brahmā who showed anger on rudra and cursed him; such sarvēśvaran is residing in śrī badarīkāśramam on the banks of gangā where viśvāmitran who became brahmariśi by performing penance, brought along śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa.

- *mān munindu …* – sītāp pirātti mercifully requested perumāḷ (śrī rāma) “Please catch and bring this deer to me”, and perumāḷ chased the deer. Since the deer was an illusory one (mārīcā came in disguise), it kept evading perumāḷ, and hence perumāḷ became angry on it and he, the strong one, aimed at the deer and bent his beautiful bow.
- *ponniṟattu uravōn …* – One who was known as hiraṇya, who had a golden hue and great strength; emperumān showed anger on his bodily flesh which grew based on his evil pride, and placed the edge of his divine nails on his body which is abode for such flesh.
- *ayan …* – emperumān favoured the child, prahlāda \[who has much less love compared to pirātti towards him\], the same way he did for pirātti; and he favoured the same way towards rudra who is prideful. brahmā who could not tolerate the prideful attitude of rudra, thought “we should make him commit a mistake and punish him”, and allowed rudra to sever his head saying “you sever my head if you have the courage to do so” and then cursed him for that same reason as said in mātsya purāṇam “*kapāleetvam bhaviśyasi*” (you will have my skull attached to your hand). When one’s own father becomes an enemy, it is bhagavān who remains even closer and helps such persons.
- *tavam …* – viśvāmitra is identified as the one who became great by his penance and brought perumāḷ and iḷaiya pertumāḷ Though he was a kśatriya he became a brahmariśi by the strength of his penance. Since he brought perumāḷ and iḷaiya perumāḷ along the banks of gangā, āḻvār could be talking about that. One who became great by performing tapas – viśvāmitran. Here, śrī parānguśa dāsar asks nampiḷḷai “jīyā (Oh great personality)! Instead of *māmuni koṇarnda*, can we not change it to *māmuni puganṟa* (the great sage spoke about) as an alternate text, and explain it as viśvāmitran explaining the greatness of gangā to perumāḷ and iḷaiya perumāḷ. āḻvār could be speaking about that”. nampiḷḷai mercifully responds “We don’t have the strength/ability to do so” \[i.e. We don’t have the ability to change āḻvār’s pāsurams\]. Alternatively, māmuni could mean bhagīrata himself \[as he also did a great penance\] and explain it as gangā which was brought down to earth by bhagīrata.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4.9. Kondal marudangal

*koṇḍal mārudangaḷ kulavarai togunīrk kuraikadal ulagudan anaittum uṇḍa māvayiṟṟōn oṇsudar ēynda umbarum ūḻiyum ānān aṇḍam ūdaṟuttu anṟu andarattu iḻindu angu avaniyāḷ alamara perugum maṇḍu māmaṇinīrk kangaiyin karaimēl vadariyāccirāmattuḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

koṇḍal – clouds; mārudangaḷ – groups of winds; kula varai – anchoring mountains; togu nīr – having abundance of water; kurai – making sound; kadal – oceans; ulagu udan – with earth; anaittum – and all other objects; uṇḍa – being the one who mercifully consumed; mā – huge; vayiṟṟōn – one who has a stomach; oḷ – shining; sudar – candra (moon) and sūrya (sun); ēynda – having; umbarum – higher worlds; ūḻiyum – kalpas (time – brahmā’s days); ānān – sarvēśvaran who is having as prakāram (form); anṟu – when bhagīrata was bringing gangā down; aṇḍam – brahma lōkam (abode of brahmā); ūdu aṟuttu – finding a way through; andarattu – from sky; iḻindu – coming down; avaniyāḷ – śrī bhūmip pirātti; alamara – to cause anguish (being unable to bear); perugum – flowing; maṇḍu – being dense; mā – being abundant; maṇi – clear; nīr – having water; gangaiyin karai mēl – on the banks of gangā; vadariyāccirāmattuḷḷānē – is residing in śrī badarīkāśramam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran mercifully consumed clouds, groups of winds, anchoring mountains, oceans which make sound  and having abundant water, the earth and all other objects, and placed them in his huge stomach; he is having the higher worlds which have candra and sūrya, and time as his form; such emperumān is residing in śrī badarīkāśramam on the banks of gangā which is having dense, abundant and clear water which is flowing down to cause anguish to śrī bhūmip pirātti when bhagīrata was bringing it down finding a way through brahmalōkam and while falling down on earth.

- *koṇḍal mārudangaḷ* – Clouds, group of winds, anchoring mountains, ocean which is having abundance of water and making sound, earth along with all the objects, were placed in …
- *mā vayiṟṟōn* – Even after placing all of these in his stomach, the stomach had so much more space left. He is known as said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.2.7 “*val vayiṟṟup perumān*” (the lord who has very strong stomach).
- *oṇ sudar …* – He had the higher worlds which have moon and sun and the deluge which is an aspect of time, as his forms, to be identified directly as him. They were the forms and he was the substratum.
- *aṇḍam …* – aṇḍam – brahmalōkam. Finding a way in there,  falling into the sky which is beneath brahmalōkam, and came down with great force to cause anguish even to śrī bhūmip pirātti who can bear anything.
- *maṇḍu mā maṇi nīr* – On the banks of gangā which has vast and clear water.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4.10. Varum tirai

*varundirai maṇinīrk kangaiyin karaimēl vadariyāccirāmattuḷḷānai karungadal munnīr vaṇṇanai eṇṇik kaliyan vāy oli seyda panuval varanjeyda aindum aindum vallārgaḷ vānavar ulagudan maruvi irungadal ulagamāṇḍu veṇkudaik kīḻ imaiyavar āguvartāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

varum – coming with great speed; tirai – having waves; maṇi – clear; nīr – having water; gangaiyin karai mēl – present on the banks of gangā; vadari āccirāmattu – in śrī badarīkāśramam; uḷḷānai – one who is eternally residing; karu – being dark; munnīr – having three types of water; kadal vaṇṇanai – sarvēśvaran, who is having the divine complexion of ocean; eṇṇi – meditating upon; kaliyan – āḻvār; vāy – mercifully spoke with his divine words; oli seyda – in the form of a garland of words; panuval – being the songs; varam seyda – compiled with the mercy of bhagavān; aindum aindum – these ten pāsurams; vallārgaḷ – those who are able to recite along with their meanings; iru – vast; kadal – surrounded by ocean; ulagam – this earth; veḷ – whitish; kudaik kīḻ – remaining on the shades of umbrella; āṇḍu – ruling over with a sceptre (further); vānavar – brahmā who is the leader of dēvatās starting with indra, his; ulagu udan – satya lōkam; maruvi – reaching (and enjoying there); imaiyavar āguvar – will become a part of nityasūris

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is eternally residing in śrī badarīkāśramam which is present on the banks of gangā having clear water with waves which are coming with great speed; he is having the divine dark complexion of ocean which is having three types of water; meditating upon such sarvēśvaran, tirumangai āḻvār mercifully spoke with his divine words in the form of songs which are garlands of words and compiled these ten pāsurams with the mercy of bhagavān; those who are able to recite these pāsurams along with their meanings will remain under the shades of a whitish umbreall and rule over with a sceptre this earth which is surrounded by vast ocean, reach satya lōkam which is the abode of brahmā who is the leader of dēvatās starting with indra and enjoy there and will eventually become a part of nityasūris.

- *varum … –* āḻvār sang and praised sarvēśvaran who is residing in śrī badarīkāśramam which is present on the banks of gangā which is having clear water and waves which are coming at great speed.
- *karum kadal munnīr* – The dark ocean which has three types of water namely river water, ground water and rain water. āḻvār meditated upon such emperumān who has the complexion of the dark ocean.
- *varam seyda* – Those who are experts in these ten pāsurams which are sung by the mercy of bhagavān. Alternatively, this can be explained as the ten pāsurams which are praiseworthy.
- *vānavar …* – After singularly ruling over the earth which is surrounded by the vast ocean, attaining brahmā’s position and ruling over from there, subsequently will reach paramapadam and become part of nityasūris. With this, it is explained that these ten pāsurams will fulfil all desires.

nanjīyar asked bhattar – Why is āḻvār who is very detached from worldly pleasures as he said in periya tirumoḻi 6.1.1 “*vēṇḍēn manai vāḻkkai*” (I don’t desire materiliastic married life) and in periya tirumoḻi 6.3.4 “*pōndēn*” (reached your divine feet), explaining these worldly wealth \[of ruling over earth etc\] as the result, while wise people abandon such worldly wealth? bhattar mercifully responded – after tirumangai āḻvār’s divine birth, even worldly wealth which is to be given up, has become part of the ultimate goal. īsn’t āḻvār with the principle that whether it is īśvaran himself or nityasūris or kings, all wealth are desirable, if they can be grabbed and used for the sake of bhāgavatas?

## 1.5 Kalaiyum kariyum

## 1.5.1. Kalaiyum kariyum

*kalaiyum kariyum parimāvum tiriyum kānam kadandu pōy silaiyum kaṇaiyum tuṇaiyāgac cenṟān venṟic ceṟuk kaḷattu malai koṇḍu alaineer aṇaikatti madiḷ nīr ilangai vāḷarakkar talaivan talai pattu aṟuttugandān  sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē*

**Пословный перевод:**

silaiyum – bow; kaṇaiyum – arrows; tuṇaiyāga – having as his help; kalaiyum – deer; kariyum – elephants; parimāvum – horses; tiriyum – roaming around; kānam – forest; kadandu – crossing; pōy – going very far; venṟi – causing battle which will lead to victory; seruk kaḷattu – in the battle-field; senṟān – entered; alai – having waves; nīr – ocean; malai koṇḍu – rocks; aṇai katti – building bridge; madiḷ – fort; nīr – having ocean as moat; ilangai – having lankā as his capital; vāḷ – having sword; arakkar talaivan – rāvaṇa, the leader of rākśasas, his; talai pattu – ten heads; aṟuttu – severed; ugandān – sarvēśvaran became joyful; the eternal abode of such sarvēśvaran; sāḷakkirāmam – śrī sāḷagrāmam; nenjē – Oh mind!; adai – try to reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran was having his bow and arrows as help and crossed over the forest where deer, elephants and horses roam around, went very far and entered the battle-field where battles which lead to victory are caused, after building a bridge with rocks over the ocean having waves, and severed the ten heads of rāvaṇa who was the leader of rākśasas, having lankā which is having the ocean as a moat, as his capital, and became joyful. Oh mind! Try to reach śrī sāḷagrāmam which is the eternal abode of such sarvēśvaran.

- *kalai …* – Crossing over the forest which only has deer etc.
- *silaiyum kaṇaiyum tuṇaiyāgac cenṟān venṟic cerukkaḷattu* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.30 “*tē vanēna vanam gatvā*” (they entered one forest after another), instead of going from city to forest, he travelled through forests only; similarly, after crossing over the forest where evil beasts live, he entered the battle-field. After crossing over the forest which has deer, elephants and horses, he entered the victorious battle-field.

When asked “Who is the companion while entering there?” āḻvār says

- *silaiyum kaṇaiyum tuṇaiyāga* – He went there having the bow and arrows as help. When asked “What about lakśmaṇa et al?” \[commentator says\] āḻvār is implying that emperumān considers all of those associates as his limbs and not as separate assistants. All the great devotees remained fully subservient to perumāḷ (śrī rāma). śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 25.33 “*rāma lakśmaṇa guptāsāsugrīvēṇa ca vāhinī*” (sugrīva along with his army was protected by śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa).
- *venṟic cerukkaḷattu* – After crossing over the forest where the animals do not have the intent to harm, keep roaming, he ended up in the battle-field. He entered the battle-field where victorious battle is caused.

Subsequently, āḻvār explains the activities after reaching the battle-field.

- *malai …* – On the greatly agitated ocean, perumāḷ built a bridge with rocks which will usually submerge in the water; rāvaṇa had his residence in lankā which is surrounded by a fort and by a moat in the form of the ocean; he considered a sword which he got by praying to a dēvatā (rudra) as his protection; perumāḷ severed the ten heads of such rāvaṇa who was the controller of all evil people and became joyful thinking “dēvatās regained their abodes and riśis (sages) got to perform their penances by remaining in their hermitages”. āḻvār is saying “Oh mind! Try to reach śrī sāḷagrāmam where such emperumān who eliminated the enemies, is residing to help those who are of subsequent times”.

## 1.5.2. Kadam sul pariyum

*kadam sūḻ kariyum parimāvum olimāndērum kālāḷum udan sūḻndeḻunda kadiyilangai podiyāvadivāyc caram turandān idam sūḻndu engum iruvisumbil imaiyōr vaṇanga maṇam kamaḻum tadam sūḻndu engum aḻagāya sāḷakkirāmam adainenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kadam sūḻ – having the liquid that comes out during periods of exultation; kariyum – elephants; parimāvum – horses; oli – resounding; māttērum – great chariots; kālāḷum – foot soldiers; udan sūḻndu – gathering together; eḻunda – appearing in a rousing manner; kadi – fortified; ilangai – evil forces in lankā; podiyā – to become dust; vadi – sharp; vāy – having mouth; saram – arrows; turandān – cakravarti tirumagan (divine son of daśarata) who shot; iru – vast; visumbil – residing in svarga (heaven); imaiyōr – dēvatās; idam engum – on the vast earth; sūḻndu – spread; vaṇanga – to be vorśipped; maṇam – fragrance (of flowers such as sengaḻunīr); kamaḻum – blowing; tadam – by ponds; sūḻndu – being surrounded; engum – in all directions; aḻagāya – having beauty; sāḷakkirāmam – śrī sāḷagrāmam; adai nenjē – Oh mind! Try to reach

**Перевод:**

**In the first pāsuram, āḻvār spoke about how rāvaṇa was killed; in this pāsuram āḻvār speaks about the rising army on day one of the battle.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In lankā, rāvaṇa had gathered together elephants having the liquid that comes out during periods of exultation, horses, resounding great chariots, foot soldiers, and they appeared in a rousing manner; cakravarti tirumagan shot arrows having sharp mouth, at such fortified lankā to become dust; such emperumān to be vorśipped by dēvatās who are residing in the vast svarga, and who are now spread everywhere in vast earth, is present in śrī sāḷagrāmam which is being surrounded by beautiful ponds which are spreading in all directions. Oh mind! Try to reach such śrī sāḷagrāmam.

- *kadam sūḻ* – āḻvār is narrating the battle ground situation as described by the riśi (vālmeeki). The elephant group where the elephants are having exultation liquid and which appear like walking mountains, subsequently horses, resounding great chariots, foot soldiers – lankā where all these armies gathered together and appeared in a rousing manner. To make it become dust as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 26.22 “*smaśāna sadruśī bhavēt*” (This lankā will become like graveyard), he conducted the arrows which had sharp mouth.
- *idam …* – Having spread everywhere on earth, he remained in śrī sāḷagrāmam which has abundantly fragrant ponds and is fully beautiful, to be approachable for dēvatās who are residing in the vast svargam. You try to reach such śrī sāḷagrāmam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.3. Ulavu tiraiyum

*ulavu tiraiyum kulavaraiyum  ūḻi mudalā eṇḍhikkum nilavum sudarum iruḷumāy ninṟān venṟi viṟal āḻi valavan vānōr tam perumān maruvā arakkarkku enjñānṟum salavan salam sūḻndu aḻagāya sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ulavu – roaming; tiraiyum – ocean having waves; kula varaiyum – seven anchoring mountains (such as mēru); ūḻi mudalā – time etc; eṇ dikkum – entities in eight directions; nilavum – candra (moon); sudarum – sūrya (sun); iruḷum – darkness, for all these; āy – being prakāri (substratum); ninṟān – one who remained; venṟi – victory; viṟal – and having strength; āḻi – tiruvāḻi (divine sudarśana chakra); valavan – one who holds in his right hand; vānōr tam – for brahmā et al; perumān – being the lord; enjñānṟum – at all times; maruvā – those who don’t surrender (unto him); arakkarkku – for the rākśasas; salavan – sarvēśvaran who is the enemy and who is eternally residing; salam – by water; sūḻndu – being surrounded; aḻagāya – beautiful; sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē – Oh mind! Try to reach śrī sāḷagrāmam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran remained the prakāri (substratum) for ocean having waves which are roaming, seven anchoring mountains, time etc, entities in eight directions, moon and sun, and darkness; being the one who holds the divine sudarśana chakra in his right hand which is having victory and strength, being the lord of brahmā et al and being the enemy of rākśasas who don’t surrender unto him, at all times, is eternally residing in the beautiful śrī sāḷagrāmam which is surrounded by water. Oh mind! Try to reach there.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *ulavu* … – Starting with the ocean which is having waves which are roaming and making loud noise, and mountains.
- *ūḻi mudalā eṇ dikkum* – For all entities in eight directions which are revealed by time, candra and sūrya who remain for a limited period of time, darkness which is opposite to them, are all present as prakāra (forms) of emperumān in a manner that they can be identified directly as him. With this, bhagavān’s universal form was explained; further emperumān having distinguished, divine form is explained.
- *venṟi …* – One who has the tiruvāḻi in his right hand for the protection of his devotees.
- *vānōr tam perumān* – One who is the refuge for brahmā et al.
- *maruvā* – The demoniac clan which does not agree with emperumān even while he is resting. As said in tirunedundāṇḍakam 6 “*avuṇarkkenṟum salam purindu*” (having enmity towards demons always), one who has enmity \[towards the evil people\]; śrī sāḷagrāmam is the beautiful, divine abode which has abundance of water and where such emperumān has arrived and is showing his presence.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.4. Uran kudandai

*ūrān kudandai uttaman orukāl irukāl silai vaḷaiya tērā arakkar tēr veḷḷam seṟṟān vaṟṟā varu punal sūḻ pērān pērāyiram udaiyān piṟangu siṟai vaṇḍu aṟaiginṟa tārān tārā vayal sūḻnda sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ūrān – one who is having tiruvūragam as his abode; kudandai – one who is mercifully resting in tirukkudandai; uttaman – being puruśōttama; orukāl – when karan et al came to fight; silai – bow’s; irukāl – both ends; vaḷaiya – bent (to show his strength); tērā – cannot analyse and understand (that he cannot be won by us); arakkar – rākśasas’; tēr veḷḷam – groups of chariots; seṟṟān – destroyed them to become pieces; vaṟṟā – not becoming dry; varu – overflowing continuously; punal – with water; sūḻ – surrounded by; pērān – one who is eternally residing in tiruppēr nagar; āyiram pēr udaiyān – one who has countless divine names; piṟangu – dense; siṟai – having wings; vaṇḍu – beetles; aṟaiginṟa – singing with tune; tārān – sarvēśvaran who is adorning tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland and mercifully residing; tārā – filled with birds named tārā; vayal – by fertile fields; sūḻnda – surrounded by; sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē – Oh mind! Try to reach śrī sāḷagrāmam

**Перевод:**

**In this pāsuram, vanquishing of kara which happened previously \[to vanquishing of rāvaṇa\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who is having tiruvūragam as his abode, who is mercifully resting as puruśōttama in tirukkudandai, bent both the ends of his bows and destroyed the groups of chariots of rākśasas, who cannot analyse and understand that he cannot be won over by them, to become pieces. He is eternally residing in tiruppēr nagar which is surrounded by perennial water. He is having countless divine names and is adorning tuḷasi garland which is having beetles with dense wings, singing with tune. He is mercifully residing in śrī sāḷagrāmam which is surrounded by fertile fields which are filled with birds named tārā. Oh mind! Try to reach there.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *ūrān* – One who is having tiruvūragam as his abode.
- *kudandai uttaman* – One who is having the greatness of voluntarily going to tirukkudandai and mercifully reclining there while none of the residents prayed for his arrival there.

Alternatively, it can be said as

- *tirukkudandai – ūrān – uttaman* – The best lord who is residing in the town of tirukkudandai.
- *orukāl* – Once.
- *irukāl silai vaḷaiya* – To bend both the ends of the bow. Since rāvaṇa did not bend (bow down), śrī rāma bent his bow.
- *tērā arakkar …* – śrī rāma destroyed the flood of chariots of rāvaṇa who could not show respect thinking “The divine son of emperor daśarata has come as enemy to fight”.
- *vaṟṟā …* – On top of the water not drying, water is flowing more and more – having such tiruppēr nagar as his abode.
- *pēr āyiram udaiyān* – One who is having countless divine names which reveal his qualities and activities. āḻvār is speaking about the divine forms which are enjoyed through those divine names.
- *piṟangu …* – Wearing garlands which are having beetles which are having dense wings, drinking the honey and singing.
- *tārā …* – śrī sāḷagrāmam is surrounded with fields which are filled with tārā birds just as a town will be filled with humans. Oh mind! Reach there.

## 1.5.5. Aduttarttelundal

*aduttārtteḻundāḷ pilavāy vittalaṟa  avaḷ mūkku ayil vāḷāl viduttān viḷangu sudar āḻi viṇṇōr perumān naṇṇārmun kaduttārttu eḻunda perumaḻaiyaik kallonṟu ēndi inaniraikkāt taduttān tadam sūḻndu aḻagāya sāḷakkirāmam adainenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

aduttu – approached; ārttu – making noise; eḻundāḷ – sūrpaṇakā who came with zeal; pilam – like a cave; vāy vittu – opening her mouth; alaṟa – to cry out; avaḷ – her; mūkku – nose; ayil – sharp; vāḷāl – with a sword; viduttān – one who severed (with the help of iḷaiya perumāḷ); viḷangu – very shining; sudar – have radiance; āḻi – one who is having tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); viṇṇōr – for nityasūris; perumān – being the lord; kaduttu – with great speed; eḻunda – appeared; peru maḻaiyai – great rain; naṇṇār mun – in front of indra et al who opposed; inam – herd; niraikkā – to protect the cows; kal onṟu – mountain named gōvardan; ēndi – held; taduttān – stopped, the abode where he is eternally residing; tadam sūḻndu – surrounded by ponds; aḻagāya – beautiful; sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē – Oh mind! Reach such śrī sāḷagrāmam

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is speaking about destruction of sūrpaṇakā which happened even before destruction of kara et al.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān severed the sharp nose of sūrpaṇakā who approached making noise and came with zeal, opening her cave like mouth, with a sword, to make her cry out. The lord of nityasūris who is having the radiant tiruvāḻi which is very shining, held the mountain named gōvardan and stopped the great rain which was appearing with great speed and noise, in front of indra et al who opposed, to protect the herd of cows. Such sarvēśvaran is eternally residing in the beautiful śrī sāḷagrāmam which is surrounded by ponds. Oh mind! Reach such śrī sāḷagrāmam.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *aduttu* – Pursued eagerly.
- *ārttu eḻundāḷ* – Making noise, she came zealously, calling out; her nose.
- *ayil* – Sharp. He \[through iḷaiya perumāḷ) pulled out the divine dagger and severed her nose.
- *viḷāngu …* – By manifesting the beautiful combination of his hand and divine chakra, he conducts the life of nityasūris.
- *naṇṇār …* – In front of the enemies. As the great rain was triggered by indra’s intent, it poured down heavily with great force. He stopped such rain by holding the gōvardana mountain to protect the cows which can neither realise the favour done by emperumān nor have any means to protect themselves.
- *tadam …* – He is residing in the beautiful śrī sāḷagrāmam which is surrounded by ponds.\[Oh mind! Try to reach there\]

## 1.5.6. Tayay vanda

*tāyāy vanda pēy uyirum tayirum viḻudum udanuṇḍa vāyān tūyavariyuruviṟkuṟaḷāyc cenṟu māvaliyai ēyān irappa mūvadi maṇ inṟē tāvenṟu ulagēḻum tāyān kāyā malar vaṇṇan sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāyāy vanda – one came in the disguise of mother; pēy – pūtanā’s; uyirum – life; tayirum – curd; viḻudum – butter; udan uṇḍa – mercifully consumed them in the same manner; vāyān – having divine mouth; ēyān – one who does not deserve to beg; tūya – being very pure; vari – beautiful; uruvin – having form; kuṟaḷāy – as vāmana; māvaliyai – from mahābali; senṟu – going there; inṟē – right now; mūvadi maṇ tā enṟu – saying “you should give three steps of land”; irappa – as he begged (and as mahābali poured the water); ulagu ēḻum – seven worlds; tāyān – one who jumped and measured; kāyā malar vaṇṇan – the eternal abode of sarvēśvaran who has the complexion of a kāyām flower; sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē – Oh mind! Reach such śrī sāḷagrāmam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, who is having divine mouth, mercifully consumed the life of pūtanā who came in the disguise of his mother, curd and better in the same manner; he who does not deserve to beg, went to mahābali in a very pure, beautiful vāmana form and begged, saying “you should give three steps of land, right now” and jumped and measured the seven worlds. Oh mind! Reach such śrī sāḷagrāmam which is the eternal abode of sarvēśvaran who has the complexion of a kāyām flower.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *tāyāy …* – One who is having the divine mouth which consumed the life of pūtanā, who came in the disguise of his mother, as well as yaśōdāp pirātti’s curd and butter, in the same manner. He considered the materials which came in contact with favourable people and the lives of unfavourable persons, as equivalent to each other, to sustain him.
- *tūya …* – Having the vāmana \[dwarf\] form which has no shortcoming/failing. He went with the vāmana form where he can attract those who cannot be won over by arrows, with his beauty.
- *ēyān irappa* – śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21-7 “*gōsahasrapradātāram*” (one who gives away a thousand cows). He who does not deserve to beg as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 33.25 “*dadyān na prati gruṇhīyāt*” (śrī rāma is a grantor, not someone who accepts), went and begged.
- *māvaliyai ēyān irappa* – emperumān vowed to beg from mahābali who was determined not to give. Alternative explanation – after praying to him to grant the 3 steps of land immediately, as he allowed to do so, grew and measured the seven worlds, before his mind changed.
- *tāyān* – One who jumped.
- *kāyā malar vaṇṇan* – He measured the earth with such beautiful form.

## 1.5.7. Enor anja

*ēnōr anja venjamattuḷ ariyāyp pariya iraṇiyanai ūnār agalam piḷavedutta oruvan tānē iru sudarāy vānāyt tīyāy mārudamāy malaiyāy alai nīr ulaganaittum tānāy tānumānān tan sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēnōr – demons, who are enemies; anja – to fear; vem – cruel; samattuḷ – in the battle; ariyāy – being narasimha; pariya – one who is having big body; iraṇiyanai – hiraṇya’s; Un Ar – filled with flesh; agalam – chest; piḷavu edutta – tore down; oruvan – having incomparable strength; tānē – such sarvēśvaran; iru sudarāy – being candra and sūrya; vānāy – being sky; tīyāy – being fire; malaiyāy – being mountains; alai nīr – surrounded by ocean with waves; ulagu anaittum – all worlds; tānāy – remained to be directly identified as him; tānum ānān than – the merciful abode of sarvēśvaran who is also having distinguished form; sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē – Oh mind! Reach such śrī sāḷagrāmam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, being narasimha, in the cruel battle, to cause fear in the demons who are enemies, tore down the chest of hiraṇya who was having a big body and whose chest was filled with flesh; such sarvēśvaran who is having incomparable strength, remained as moon and sun, sky, fire, mountains and all worlds surrounded by ocean with waves, to be directly identified as him, is also having a distinguished form in the merciful abode of śrī sāḷagrāmam. Oh mind! Reach such śrī sāḷagrāmam.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *ēnōr* … – To have the demons, who are enemies, become frightened in the battle, as narasimha.
- *pariya iraṇiyanai* – hiraṇya who has grown due to his ego. His body is not like a devotee’s body which is usually thin and tender due to thinking “there is someone higher than body as soul; there is another one (God) who owns the soul; we should reach him”; the unique one who tore down the chest which is filled with flesh; such sarvēśvaran entered in to moon and sun as antarātmā (indvelling super-soul) and remained to be identified as him, and remained as sky, fire, air, and mountain among the effectual entities, and remained as all worlds which are surrounded by ocean, to be identified as “him” in the universal form; this is being explained by āḻvār.
- *tānum ānān* – One who is having distinguished divine form.

## 1.5.8. Vendar enbum

*vendār enbum sudu nīṟum meyyil pūsik kaiyagattu ōr sandār talai koṇḍu ulagēḻum tiriyum periyōn tān senṟu en ēndāy! sābam tīrenna ilangu amudu nīr tirumārbil tandān sandār poḻil sūḻnda sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vendār – those who were cremated; enbum – bone; sudu nīṟum – the ashes which resulted from those burnt bodies; meyyil – on his body; pūsi – applied; sandu Ar – having holes; ōr – which cannot be filled by anyone; talai – brahma kapālam (skull of brahmā); kai agattu – in his hand; koṇḍu – carrying; ulagēḻum – in seven worlds; tiriyum – one who roams around; periyōn tān – rudra who is considering himself to be great; senṟu – went (to sarvēśvaran); en endāy – oh my well-wisher!; sābam – this curse; tīr – “kindly eliminate”; enna – as he prayed; ilangu – shining; tirumārvil – from his divine chest; amudu nīr – nectarean water \[sweat\]; tandān – eternal abode of one who sprinkled and mercifully freed him of such curse; sandu – sandalwood trees; Ar – filled; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻnda – surrounded; sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē – Oh mind! Reach such śrī sāḷagrāmam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

rudra who considers himself to be great, applied on his body, the bones of those who were cremated and the ashes which resulted from those burnt bodies and carried the brahma kapālam which was having holes and cannot be filled by anyone and roamed around the seven worlds; such rudra went to sarvēśvaran and as he prayed “Oh my well-wisher! Kindly eliminate this curse”, emperumān who is having śrī sāḷagrāmam which is surrounded with gardens filled with sandalwood trees, sprinkled the divine sweat from his shining, divine chest and mercifully freed rudra of such curse. Oh mind! Reach there.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *vendār embum* – Applying the bone and ashes of those who were cremated, having the skull which has many holes, in his hand. Since he severed the head at the spot where all nerves from the body connect into the head, the skull had many holes.
- *ulagil …* – Just as one who ruled a town would be paraded with shackles \[due to committing mistakes\], rudra is helplessly roaming around with the skull in his hand, where he ruled the place considering himself to be the lord. Such prideful rudra went to śrī sāḷagrāmam and prayed to sarvēśvaran “Oh my lord! You should free me from this curse”.
- *tirumārvil – ilangu amudu nīr – tandān* – From the shining, divine chest, he gave \[sprinkled\] the sweat which resembles divine nectar and freed rudra from the curse.
- *sandu Ar poḻil* – Surrounded with gardens filled with sandalwood trees.

## 1.5.9. Tondam inamum

*toṇḍām inamum imaiyōrum tuṇai nūl mārvin andaṇarum aṇḍā! emakkē aruḷāy enṟu aṇaiyum kōyil arugellām vaṇḍār poḻilin paḻanattu vayalin ayalē kayal pāyat taṇḍhāmaraigaḷ mugamalarttum sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

toṇḍām inamum – group of śrīvaiṣṇavas who are totally serving emperumān; imaiyōrum – nityasūris (eternal associates of bhagavān in paramapadam); tuṇai nūl – wearing two yajñōpavītams; mārvin – having chest; andaṇarum – brāhmaṇas; aṇḍā – Oh controller of all oval shaped universes!; emakku – in our matters; aruḷāy – show your mercy; enṟu – saying so; aṇaiyum – approaching; kōyil – temple’s; arugu ellām – nearby places; vaṇḍu – beetles; Ar – being filled with; poḻilin – present in the garden; paḻanattu ayal – in the surroundings of the water-bodies; vayalin – from the fertile fields; kayal – fishes; pāya – as they jump (into the water-bodies); taṇ – cool; tāmaraigaḷ – lotus buds; mugam alarttum – becoming blossomed and shining due to that; sāḷakkirāmam adai nenjē – Oh mind! Reach such śrī sāḷagrāmam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Group of śrīvaiṣṇavas who are totally serving emperumān, nityasūris, brāhmaṇas who are having chest adorned with two yajñōpavītams are all saying “Oh controller of all oval shaped universes! Show your mercy in our matters” and approaching the temple which is having surroundings which have gardens filled with beetles, which are having water-bodies which are, in turn, surrounded by fertile fields. The fishes from the fertile fields are jumping into the water-bodies. The lotus buds in those water-bodies are blossoming and shining. Oh mind! Reach such śrī sāḷagrāmam.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *toṇḍām inamum* – The group of śrīvaiṣṇavas who remain as said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1 “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍu nām*” (we would like to serve continuously), nityasūris and those who are just brāhmaṇas. bhāśyakārar (śrī rāmānuja) split the phrase in [śrī bhagavat gītā 5-18](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/5-18/) as “*vidya vinaya sampannē – brāhmaṇē*” (learned, humble brāhmaṇas and those who are just brāhmaṇas without real qualification).
- *aṇḍā* – Saying individually “Oh lord! Oh our refuge! You should shower your mercy upon us” and reaching the temple. On the surroundings of such temple,
- *vaṇḍār …* – In the garden which is filled with beetles, paḻanam – water-bodies. In the surroundings of such water-bodies, the fishes from fertile fields would jump into those water-bodies.
- *taṇ tāmaraigaḷ mugam alarttum* – Just as when the dancers make their dance steps, the audience will reveal their joy in their faces to celebrate the same, the lotus flowers revealed their shine by blossoming on seeing the fishes jump around.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.10. Taravarum

*tārāvārum vayal sūḻnda sāḷakkirāmattu adigaḷaik kārār puṟavin mangai vēndan kaliyan oli sey tamiḻ mālai ārār ulagattaṟivudaiyār amarar nal nāttarasāḷa pērāyiramum ōdumingaḷ anṟi ivaiyē pidaṟṟuminē.*

**Пословный перевод:**

ulagattu – in this world; aṟivudaiyār ārār – all the wise people; amarar – nityasūris’; nal nādu – distinguished paramapadam; arasāḷa – to rule; pēr āyiramum – his thousand divine names; ōdumingaḷ – try to recite; anṟi – if you are unable to recite; tārā – tārā birds; ārum – filled; vayal – by fertile fields; sūḻnda – surrounded; sāḷākkirāmattu – arrived in śrī sāḷagrāmam; adigaḷai – on the lord of all; kār Ar – filled with clouds; puṟavin – having surroundings; mangai – for tirumangai region; vēndan – king; kaliyan – āḻvār; oli – having tune; sey – mercifully composed; tamiḻ mālai ivaiyē – these ten pāsurams which are in the form of a garland of tamiḻ words; pidaṟṟumin – try to recite incoherently

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh all wise people in this world! Try to recite his thousand divine names to rule the distinguished paramapadam which is ruled by nityasūris; if you are unable to do so, incoherently recite these ten pāsurams which are in the form of a garland of tamiḻ words, having tune and were mercifully composed by tirumangai āḻvār who is the king of tirumangai region which is having surroundings filled with clouds; these ten pāsurams were sung on the lord of all who has arrived in śrī sāḷagrāmam which is surrounded by fertile fields filled with tārā birds.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *tārā …* – āḻvār praised the lord of all, who has arrived in śrī sāḷagrāmam which is surrounded by fertile fields which are filled with tārā birds.
- *kārār …* – Garland of words with tune, sung by tirumangai āḻvār who is the king of tirumangai region which is surrounded by places which have constant presence and movement of clouds.
- *ārār ulagattu aṟivudaiyār* – Those who are wise in this world; the divine abode of nityasūris – paramapadam. To rule them as they please as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-9-6-velviyul-maduththalum/) “*āṇmingaḷ vānagam*” (rule over these abodes such as svarga (heaven) etc), try to recite the thousand divine names with your mouth; if that is not possible,
- *ivaiyē pidaṟṟuminē* – You recite this decad incoherently. “*sankīrtayēt jagannātam vēdam vāpi samīrayēt*” (Either sing the glories of jagannātan, the lord of the universe, or recite vēdam).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6 Vanila muruval

## 1.6.1. Vanila muruval

*vāṇilā muṟuval siṟu nudal perundōḷ mādarār vana mulaip payanē  pēṇinēn adanaip piḻai enak karudip pēdaiyēn piṟavi nōy aṟuppān ēṇilēn irundēn eṇṇinēn eṇṇi iḷaiyavar kalaviyin tiṟattai nāṇinēn vandu un tiruvadi adaindēn naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

naimisāraṇiyattuḷ – mercifully residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam; endāy – Oh my lord!; vāḷ nilā – radiant; muṟuval – gentle smile; siṟu nudal – small forehead; peru – wide; tōḷ – having shoulders; mādarār – women’s; vanam – beautiful; mulaiyē – bosoms only; payan – as ultimate goal; pēṇinēn – I desired; pēdaiyēn – I who am foolish; adanai – that; piḻaiyena – as mistake; karudi – considered; piṟavi nōy – the disease of samsāram (cycle of birth/death); aṟuppān – to eliminate; ēṇilēn irundēn – did not think about; eṇṇinēn – I analysed my previous state; eṇṇi – thinking in this manner; iḷaiyavar – the young women’s; kalaviyin tiṟattai – the matter of union with them; nāṇinēn – I felt ashamed; nāṇi – feeling ashamed; un – your; tiruvadi – divine feet; vandu – approached; adaindēn – surrendered

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh my lord mercifully residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam! I desired the beautiful bosoms of women who are having radiant, gentle smile, small forehead and wide shoulders, as my ultimate goal; considering that as a mistake, I who am foolish did not think about eliminating the disease of samsāram (cycle of birth/death); I analysed my previous state; I felt ashamed for thinking in this manner on the matter of union with such young women; feeling ashamed, I approached your divine feet and surrendered unto you.

- *vāṇilā muṟuval siṟu nudal perundōḷ mādarār vana mulaip payanē pēṇinēn* – āḻvār is explaining that this is how he was in the past. To reach emperumān, those who obey the ordained activities and conduct with noble qualities, are only qualified. But this is what I did in the past – says āḻvār.
- *vāṇilā muṟuval* – Gentle smile which has radiance; alternatively – the radiance of gentle smile which remains in the hearts of those who became target of it. nudal – forehead; remaining small; if not, it will appear masculine.
- *perum tōḷ* – The enjoyment of wide shoulders which is beyond the capacity of the enjoyers.
- *mādarār …* – Women who have radiant, gentle smile, small forehead and very enjoyable shoulders. I considered their well-appearing lump of flesh as the goal.
- *payanē pēṇinēn* – I considered that as the invisible goal as well \[not just the visible goal\]. I considered the lump of flesh of these women who captivate a man by showing their beauty, rob everything he has and after realising that he was captured, not give what the man desired, as my goal in bewilderment and showed great attachment towards that. There is no real enjoyment in that! There is only bewilderment in him \[cētana, sentient entity\] which makes him think that there is enjoyment in that.
- *adanaip piḻai enak karudi* – In this manner, the aspect which was the target of my desire is understood to be a mistake only today; a person who is attached to worldly pleasures will not give up the attachment when told “give them up”; now, for āḻvār to give up these worldly aspects, these worldly aspects themselves remain the teacher.  That is – on thinking about their evil qualities, one can easily give up the desires towards them and move away. What is realised as mistake and abandoned today, was thought about as the goal, all along.
- *pēdaiyēn* – When asked “what is the reason for having attachment all along on the aspect which is abandoned after realising it as mistake?” āḻvār says “*pēdaiyēn*” – it is my foolishness which led to that.
- *piṟavi …* – Since I was foolish, I did not have the desire of “samsāram (worldly life) is insignificant, impermanent and cause for sorrow; hence I should avoid it”.
- *ēṇilēn* – He is saying that he did not have the greatness to eliminate such attachment.
- *irundēn* – āḻvār who thought these worldly aspects to be good, gave them up thinking that they are bad; immediately, he did not reach the ultimate destination of paramapadam. He is saying “this is my situation where I am neither there nor here”. āḻvār who said in periya tirumoḻi 1.1.1 “*ōdinēn*” (I ran), does not have the mindset to remain here. This is similar to what is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.2 “*kasta ēvatyatiśtata*” (śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān remained on the sky firmly).
- *eṇṇinēn* – I started analysing “What have I been doing? Who am I? What should I do now?”
- *eṇṇi* – thinking this way.
- *iḷaiyavar kalaviyin tiṟattai nāṇinēn* – I felt ashamed about the union with those women who hide the inferior nature of such enjoyment with their youth. Seeking pleasure from worldly aspects based on śabda etc (sound, touch, form, taste and smell) is similar to a man chasing a eunuch thinking that person to be a woman. Once knowledge is acquired, one will feel ashamed and withdraw – I was attached to such aspects all along.
- *vandu un tiruvadi adaindēn* – I surrendered unto your divine feet which will remain the refuge forever unlike these worldly aspects which can be desired for a long time, only to become ashamed one day after realising their true nature.
- *naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy* – emperumān is unlike those women who will take away the man’s wealth and abandon him as well. Unlike them, he remains a natural relative, having all auspicious qualities, the natural lord and who would mercifully caress the face of the one who surrenders saying “I am here to take care of that; why are you worrying?”, if that person feels anguished for the lost time.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.2. Silambadi uruvil

*silambadi uruvil karunedungaṇṇār tiṟattanāy aṟattaiyē maṟandu pulambadinduṇṇum bōgamē perukkip pōkkinēn poḻudinai vāḷā alamburi tadakkai āyanē! māyā! vānavarkkarasanē! vānōr nalamburindiṟainjum tiruvadi adaindēn naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

naimisāraṇiyattuḷ – mercifully residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam; endāy – Oh my lord!; silambu – wearing an anklet; uruvil – being beautiful; adi – feet; karu nedu – dark and wide; kaṇṇār tiṟattanāy – being attached towards women who have such (dark and wide) eyes; aṟattai – you who are the embodiment of dharma; maṟandē – without thinking about even a little bit (about you); pulan – senses; padindu – remaining firmly; uṇṇum – experience; bōgamē – pleasures; perukki – increased further; poḻudinai – time; vāḷā – in a useless manner; pōkkinēn – have spent; alam puri – Carrying the weapon, plough; tadam – huge; kai – having divine hands; āyanē – oh one who incarnated in the covherd clan!; māyā – Oh one who has amazing activities!; vānavarkku – for dēvatās; arasanē – Oh king!; vānōr – nityasūris; nalam purindu – with love; iṟainjum – vorśipping; tiruvadi – divine feet (of your highness); adaindēn – I approached as the refuge

**Перевод:**

**As āḻvār surrendered unto the divine feet of emperumān, he got reminded about all his evil deeds; due to that he says “All along, I wasted my time”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh my lord, mercifully residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam! Being attached to women who are having beautiful feet decorated with anklets and who have dark and wide eyes, without thinking even a little bit about you who are an embodiment of dharma, remaining fully on my senses, increasing my pleasures further, I have spent my time in a useless manner. Oh one who incarnated in the covherd clan, having huge divine hands which are carrying the weapon, plough! Oh one who has amazing activities! Oh king of dēvatās! I approached your divine feet which are vorśipped by nityasūris with love, as my refuge.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *silambu adi* – The feet having anklets.
- *uruvil* – To attract him (a man), they will apply reddish paste.
- *karu nedum kaṇṇār* – They will glance at him with their dark, wide eyes; being captivated by such women, he will remain at their feet; subsequently, since he will not be able to easily attain them, he will remain firmly at places where they are discussed.
- *aṟattaiyē maṟandu* – He will not forget to even rob others to offer things to them. But he will try hard to forget what will uplift him.
- *pulan …* – To start with, his senses will be very attached to worldly pleasures like a cow which gazes everywhere; further, remaining where there is scope for enjoyment, creating interest in the senses towards those enjoyable objects, and increasing the pleasures, to fall head over heels, to enjoy them.
- *pōkkinēn* – In this manner, I spent the time, which is priceless when spent on bhagavat viśayam (matters related to bhagavān), in a useless way.
- *alam puri tadakkai āyānē* – Instead of taking away everything he has, emperumān is of the nature to grant everything he can have to his fullest satisfaction. Having a huge hand which can grant as much as required for the recipient to say “stop”. alam can also be considered as the tamiḻ version of halam (plough), indicating “one who is having the divine hand which carries a plough”.
- *māyā* – Oh one who is having amazing qualities and activities, who manifests those to make anyone to forget his/her huge loss of time when the person falls at the divine feet once!
- *vānavarkku arasanē* – Oh one who is the refuge for brahmā et al!
- *vānōr …* – nityasūris who are enjoying emperumān forever, would love him as if they are seeing him for the first time and surrender unto his divine feet. I surrendered unto such divine feet.
- *naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy* – You who are giving your audience to nityasūris, being enjoyable to them in paramapadam, have presented yourself in śrī naimiśāraṇyam to be surrendered by me, and hence I surrendered unto you.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.3. Sudinaip perukki

*sūdinaip perukki kaḷavinait tuṇindu suri kuḻal madandaiyar tiṟattuk kādalē miguttuk kaṇḍavā tirinda toṇḍanēn naman tamar seyyum vēdanaikku odungi nadunginēn vēlai veṇ tirai alamarak kadainda nādanē! vandu un tiruvadi adaindēn naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

veḷ – Whitish; tirai – having waves; vēlai – tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi – milk ocean); alamara – to agitate; kadainda – one who churned; nādanē – Oh lord!; naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy! – the benefactor who arrived in śrī naimiśāraṇyam; sūdinaip perukki – spending a lot of time gambling; kaḷavinait tuṇindu – having firm faith in robbing; suri – curly; kuḻal – having hair; madandaiyar tiṟattu – towards the women; kādal miguttu – having increased love; kaṇḍa A – in the matters visible to eyes; tirinda – following as desired; toṇḍanēn – I who served them; naman tamar – servitors of yama; seyyum – doing; vēdanaikku – thinking about the torture; odungi – having the limbs weakened; nadunginēn – one who was shivering; un tiruvadi – at your highness’ divine feet; vandu adaindēn – came and surrendered

**Перевод:**

**In the previous pāsuram āḻvār said “I wasted my time”; he should have done something to pass his time; when asked “How did you spend your time?” he is identifying that.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh lord who churned the milk ocean which is having whitish waves, to agitate it! Oh benefactor who arrived in śrī naimiśāraṇyam! I was spending a lot of time gambling and having firm faith in robbing; I was having increased love towards women who were having curly hair, following matters visible to eyes as desired, served them. I who was shivering, thinking about the torture done by servitors of yama, having my limbs weakened, came and surrendered at your highness’ divine feet.

- *sūdinaip perukkik kaḷavinait tuṇindu* – As I would gamble in the day and observed that the loser was giving a lot of wealth, thought “since he has a lot of wealth, he is giving out like this” and would firmly plan to rob that wealthy loser in the night. Thus, I would grab his money with and without his knowledge. Since these are forbidden acts, āḻvār could be speaking about these aspects. Alternative explanation – when an āstika (person who believes in śāstram) says “Fool! There is someone called īśvara (lord)”, being a nāstika (not believing in śāstram), I would rob \[of īśvara’s supremacy\] in front of his eyes asking “Who is that īśvara?” \[like gambling\]. Further I would consider myself as independent and hence rob myself from bhagavān too \[like robbing\].
- *suri kuḻal …* – After earning wealth in this manner, the way it is spent is further explained. If a woman does not tie her hair as said in [tirumālai 33](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thirumalai-33/) “*viri kuḻalāril pattu*” (being caught in the net of women with well spread locks of hair), he would become attracted in her; if a woman had her locks tied, he would \[still\] become attracted in her. Whatever may be their posture, he will be attracted to them. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.2 “*ennai un seygai naivikkum*” (as long as they are your acts, I will be attracted towards them).
- *kaṇḍavā tirinda* – As said in stōtra ratnam 58 “*nrupaśu:*” (animal in human body), whatever is caught in the eyes, I would not withdraw myself thinking śāstram has forbidden these acts. I roamed around as I pleased.
- *toṇḍanēn* – toṇḍan – paratantran – dependent. When such dependency is seen in inapt aspects, that leads to lowliness; when it occurs in apt aspects, it will lead to greatness.
- *naman tamar …* – Since I am conducting myself in this improper manner, I would fear for the tortures done by the servitors of yama. Further, all the limbs in my body will become weakened and will shiver.
- *vēlai …* – Your relationship with ātmā (self) is such that you will churn the ocean for the sake of prayōjanāntaraparars (those who have ulterior desires while vorśipping bhagavān).
- *vandu …* – Just as you mercifully reclined in kśīrābdi to hear the cries of brahmā et al being their refuge, you arrived here and made your presence to be surrendered to, by me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
