## 1.6.4. Vambulam kundal

*vambulām kūndal manaiviyait tuṟandu piṟar poruḷ tāram enṟivaṟṟai nambinār iṟandāl naman tamar paṟṟi  eṟṟi vaittu eri eḻuginṟa sembināl iyanṟa pāvaiyaip pāvī! taḻuvena moḻivadaṟku anji nambanē! vandu un tiruvadi adaindēn naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy – Oh my lord who is residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam!; nambanē – Oh trustworthy one!; vambu ulām – fragrant; kūndal – having hair; manaiviyai – (one’s) wife; tuṟandu – abandoned; piṟar poruḷ – others’ wealth; piṟar dāram – others’ wives; enṟu ivaṟṟai – these; nambinār – those who desired; iṟandāl – when they die; naman tamar – servitors of yama; paṟṟi – catch them; eṟṟi – torture them; vaittu – keeping them in a place; sembināl – with copper; iyanṟa – made; eri eḻuginṟa – very hot with fiery sparks; pāvaiyai – a woman’s statue (placing in front); pāvī! – Oh sinner!; taḻuvu – embrace (this); ena moḻivadaṟku – for the words \[which they will\] speak; anji – fearing that; un tiruvadi vandu adaindēn – came and surrendered at your divine feet

**Перевод:**

**When asked “Is that all? Have you done anything more?” āḻvār says “Yes. There is a lot more”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh my lord who is residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam! Oh trustworthy one! Some desire others’ wealth and wives, abandoning their own wives who have fragrant hair. When such persons die, the servitors of yama will catch them, torture them, keep them in a place and showing a woman’s statue, which is made of copper and is very hot with fiery sparks, tell them “Oh sinner! Embrace this”. Fearing that, I came and surrendered at your divine feet.

- *vambu …* – vambulām kūndal – Wife who has ever-beautiful hair or very fragrant hair. \[Due to desire for other women\] One will abandon the wife whom he accepted in front of the sacred fire. Such persons will desire for worldly pleasures; in such matters, one will not bother for one’s own beautiful wife. One will desire for others’ wives only. When such persons who desire for others’ wives and wealth, die.
- *naman …* – sarvēśvaran has given as much powers as himself to yama to analyse neutrally and punish others; yama would send his servitors who are as powerful as him; a thousand such persons will come and grab each of such sinners; then they will torture the body of such sinner; after becoming tired, they will leave him for sometime; they will then say “Will this person be able to remain without women for such a long time! Bring her here!” He would then think “Though they have tortured us so far, now they are bringing the woman dear to me! Let me see!” and eagerly look in that direction;
- *eri …* – They will bring a statue which is made of copper and is emitting fiery sparks and say “Oh sinner! Embrace it!” They will say “At least when such women drove you out, had you atoned for your acts and surrendered at the divine abodes of emperumān, we would have been saved from such tiring act of punishing you”.
- *moḻivadaṟku anji* – We can even tolerate their torture but cannot tolerate their cruel words.
- *nambanē vandu un tiruvadi adaindēn* – Since you, who are a refuge for even those who roam around doing whatever they like, have presented yourself, I have surrendered unto your divine feet.
- *naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy* – You thought “he (āḻvār) becomes attached to the aspects which are visible to eyes; similarly, if I make myself visible to him, he will become attached to me” and presented yourself to be seen by me. While there are rules forbidding inapt aspects, one engages with them since they are visible to eyes; you presented yourself to be seen by me thinking “If I, who am apt and am ordained in śāstram, present myself, will he not like me?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.5. Idumbaiyal adarppundu

*idumbaiyāl adarppuṇḍu, iduminō tuṟṟenṟu irandavarkku illai enṟu nedunjolāl marutta nīsanēn andō!  ninaikkilēn vinaip payan tannaik kadunjolār kadiyār kālanār tamarāl paduvadōr kodumiṟaikku anji nadungi nān vandu un tiruvadi adaindēn naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

naimisāraṇiyattuḷ – mercifully residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam; endāy – Oh my lord!; idumbaiyāl – by poverty; adarppu uṇḍu – being tormented; tuṟṟu – handful (of food at least); idumin – give; O enṟu – Crying out “Oh” revealing their poverty; irandavarkku – for those who begged; illaiyē enṟu – not having (anything to give you); nedum solāl – with harsh words; maṟutta – refused; nīsanēn – very lowly; nān – I, the servitor; andō – alas!; vinaip payan tannai – the result of the sins (which were committed previously); ninaikkilēn – not thinking about; kadum – cruel; solār – having words; kadiyār – having cruel acts; kālanār tamarāl – by the servitors of yama; paduvadu – experienced; ōr kodu – very cruel; miṟaikku – thinking about the torture; anji – fearing; nadungi – shivering; un tiruvadi – at your highness’ divine feet; vandu adaindēn – came and surrendered

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh my lord who is mercifully residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam! Alas! For those who begged due to being tormented by poverty, requesting for a handful of food crying out “Oh” revealing their poverty, I, the very lowly servitor, refused with harsh words saying “I have nothing to give”. Thinking about the very cruel torture to be experienced by me by the cruel servitors of yama for speaking and acting cruelly without thinking about the sins, I came and surrendered at your highness’ divine feet, fearing for that and shivering.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *idumbaiyā adarppuṇḍu* – Being tormented by poverty.
- *iduminō tuṟṟenṟu irandavarkku* – When someone cries out saying “All I need is a mouthful of food. Can anyone give that?” as nammāḻvār cried out in tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.1 “*muniyē!*” (Oh lord!). tuṟṟu – a handful of food which is placed in mouth.
- *tuṟṟenṟu irandavarkku* – For those who fell at the feet in this pitiful manner.
- *illaiyē …* – āḻvār is expressing the way he harshly refused to give food to the one who cried out in such a helpless manner. That person would forever be hurt and think “Due to my helpless situation I asked him for food. But the way he harshly refused is so hurtful that if I survive such harsh words I will get some poison and kill myself”.
- *andō* – āḻvār is saying “Alas!” thinking about the suffering he will go through in future.
- *ninaikkilēn vinaip payan tannai* – If my cruel acts of the past are so harsh to even think about, how can I think about the  result of such acts?
- *kadum solār …* – Thinking about the cruel punishments of the servitors of yama, who are having very harsh words.
- *nadungi nān vandu un tiruvadi adaindēn* – I surrendered unto the divine feet of your highness.
- *naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy* – For me who refused to help those who begged, have you not come to help without my even praying for that? With this, āḻvār is explaining that “Previously I freely acted according to my will, became frightened on hearing the result of such acts and as I did not find any other refuge, I surrendered unto the divine feet of your highness”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.6. Kodiya manattal

*kōdiya manattāl sinattoḻil purindu tirindu nāyinattodum tiḷaittittu ōdiyum uḻanṟum uyirgaḷē konṟēn uṇarvilēn ādalāl namanār pādiyaip peridum parisaḻittittēn paramanē! pāṟkadal kidandāy! nādi nān vandu un tiruvadi adaindēn naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

paramanē – Oh greater than all!; pāṟkadal kidandāy – On one who is mercifully resting in kśīrābdi (milk ocean)!; naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy – Oh my lord who is residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam!; kōdiya – not engaging in good aspects; manattāl – having mind; sinam – causing anger in others; toḻil – acts; purindu – having performed; nāy inattodu – with dogs etc; tirindu – hunting; tiḷaittittu – having enjoyed; ōdiyum – running (far to hurt others); uḻanṟum – anguishing; uyirgaḷ – creatures; konṟēn – having killed; uṇarvilēn – having become ignorant; adiyēn – I, the servitor; nādi – analysed; un tiruvadi vandu adaindēn – I came and surrendered at your divine feet; ādalāl – Due to that; namanār pādiyai – hell, which is the town of yama; parisu – presence; peridum – very much; aḻittu ittēn – destroyed

**Перевод:**

**When asked “Is that all? Have you done anything else?” āḻvār says “I have killed with my hands”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh greater than all! On one who is mercifully resting in kśīrābdi (milk ocean)! Oh my lord who is residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam! Having mind which is not engaging in good aspects, having performed acts which cause anger in others, having enjoyed hunting with dogs etc, running far, anguishing, having killed creatures, I, the servitor, analysed and came and surrendered at your divine feet. Due to that, the presence of hell, which is the town of yama is very much destroyed.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *kōdiya manattāl* – Mind is detached even from those who are favourable.
- *sinat toḻil purindu* – Doing cruel acts.
- *tirindu nāy inattodum tiḷaittittu* – āḻvār is speaking about hunting along with predators; or he is speaking about playing with lowly people.
- *ōdiyum* – When told “If we go several miles, we can harm someone”, without hesitating for a moment, running all that distance.
- *uḻanṟum* – When told “You to try very hard to harm someone”, I will do so.
- *uyirgaḷē konṟēn* – I ensured that many lost their lives; I did not just steal their clothes \[but completely destroyed them\]
- *uṇarvilēn* – When I did not understand this simple sentence “There is sarvēśvaran”, is there any evil deed that I did not do?
- *ādalāl namanār pādiyaip peridum parisu aḻittittēn* – This implies the goal, that is, surrendering unto the divine feet; alternatively, this is also explained along with earlier words \[that is, I have even harmed yama\]. \[First explanation\] I won over yama’s orders so that they don’t have any power – implying “I have won over yama’s town”. \[Second explanation\] When read along with earlier words, āḻvār is saying “I have been committing so many sins that will make emperumān think ‘This current yama is not sufficient to punish him; I need to create a new hell and a new leader for that hell'”
- *paramanē* – Oh one who is greater than everyone with respect to helping others without any reason.
- *pāṟkadal kidandāy* – For that purpose \[helping others\], oh one who has descended to a nearby place, that is, kśīrābdi and is mercifully reclining there!
- *nādi nān vandu un tiruvadi adaindēn* – After roaming around fully harming others, on hearing about the result of the same, I analysed the refuge for me and surrendered at your divine feet.
- *naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy* – I thought I reached out to you, but you have reached to me even before by arriving in śrī naimiśāraṇyam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.7. Nenjinal ninaindum

*nenjināl ninaindum vāyināl moḻindum nīdi allādana seydum tunjinār sellum tol neṟi kēttē  tuḷanginēn viḷangani munindāy! vanjanēn adiyēn nenjinil piriyā  vānavā! tānavarkku enṟum nanjanē! vandu un tiruvadi adaindēn  naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

viḷangani – demon kapittāsura who came in the form of a wood apple; munindāy – oh one who showed your anger and destroyed!; vanjanēn adiyēn – I, who am deceitful, my; nenjinil – (entering) in heart; piriyā – not leaving; vānavā – Oh controller of nityasūris!; enṟum – always; tānavarkku – for demons; nanjanē – Oh death!; naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy – Oh my lord who is residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam!; nīdi allādana – What is forbidden by śāstrams; nenjināl – by mind; ninaindum – thought; vāyināl – by mouth; moḻindum – spoke; seyhdum – practiced; tunjninār – those who perished; sellum – to go; tol – ancient; neṟi – path to hell; kēttē – immediately on hearing; tuḷanginēn – having shivers; un tiruvadi vandu adaindēn – surrendered unto your divine feet

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who showed your anger on the demon kapittāsura who came in the form of a wood apple and destroyed him! Oh, the controller of nityasūris who is not leaving the heart of me who is deceitful! Oh one who is always death for demons! Oh my lord who is residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam! Immediately on hearing that those who thought in mind, spoke with mouth and practiced what is forbidden in śāstrams, perished and went in the ancient path of hell, I shivered and surrendered unto your divine feet.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *nenjināl* … – “*nīdi allādana – nenjināl ninaindum, vāyināl moḻindum, seydum*” – In the previous pāsurams, he enlisted his own mistakes; here he is collectively identifying those.
- *nīdi allādana* – For those who always engaged with mind, speech and body in those forbidden acts, after death, there is hellish path to travel. I heard that and started shivering.
- *tol neṟi* – This path to hell is as ancient as the path to paramapadam as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 8.26 “… *jagata: śāśvatē matē*” (These two paths namely arcirādi gati and dūmādi gati are permanently ordained (in śruti/vēdam) for jñānis and pious persons respectively). But the difference here is, the path to hell will have continuous flow of ātmās unlike the path to paramapadam which rarely sees ātmās travelling there.
- *kēttē tuḷānginēn* – I shivered just on hearing about it, not experiencing it.

When asked “Don’t you have to experience the result of those sins?” āḻvār says,

- *viḷangani …* – The way he (emperumān) shot the fruit and brought it down tells us that we need not experience the results of our sins \[after surrendering unto him\].
- *viḷangani munindāy* – Oh one who destroyed the demon in the form of the fruit! āḻvār says “You, who have the quality of eliminating the hurdles, should eliminate my hurdles too”.
- *vanjanēn adiyēn nenjinil piriyā vānavā* – As I said “*adiyēn*” (I, the servitor) without feeling it in the heart, you accepted it as if I said it whole-heartedly, and you, who allow nityasūris to enjoy you, have entered my heart and are not leaving.
- *tānavarkku …* – Oh one who is always poison to demons! I surrendered unto your divine feet.
- *naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy* – You came close to us to show us the good path. You are thinking to take us in the path to paramapadam which is opposite to the ancient path to hell.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.8. Evinar kaliyar

*ēvinār kaliyār naligavenṟu en mēl enganē vāḻumāṟu? aivar kōvinār seyyum kodumaiyai madittēn kuṟungudi nedungadal vaṇṇā! pāvinār insol panmalar koṇḍu un pādamē paravi nān paṇindu en nāvināl vandu un tiruvadi adaindēn naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuṟungudi – one who mercifully resides in tirukkuṟungudi; nedu – vast and deep; kadal – the ocean’s; vaṇṇā – having beautiful form with such complexion!; naimisāriṇayattul endāy – Oh my lord, who is residing in śrī naimaiśāraṇiyam!; kaliyār – age of kali; naliga enṟu – saying “torment him”; en mēl – on me; aivar – the five senses; ēvinār – sent; vāḻum āṟu enganē – How will those senses survive?; kōvinār seyyum – to be done by those popular five senses; kodumaiyai – cruel acts; madittēn – driving away; en nāvināl – with my tongue; pā – with good meters; Ar – filled; in sol – sweet words; pal malar – many flowers; koṇḍu – earned; paravi – hailed; un pādamē paṇindu – falling at your highness’ divine feet; un tiruvadi nān adaindēn – I surrendered at your divine feet

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who mercifully resides in tirukkuṟungudi and is having beautiful form with the complexion of the vast and deep ocean! Oh my lord, who is residing in śrī naimaiśāraṇiyam! The age of kali sent the senses on me saying “torment him”. How will those senses survive? I earned \[made\] the flowers of sweet words filled with good meters and hailed and surrendered at your divine feet falling at those divine feet, and drove away the cruel acts to be done by those popular senses.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *ēvinār kaliyār* – Since āḻvār is fearful of kali yuga he is calling it “kaliyār” in a respectful way. kaliyār sent the five senses saying “torment him”.
- *enganē vāḻumāṟu* – How will those survive now?

When asked “What will happen when they are sent to torment you?” āḻvār says,

- *aivar …* – Senses are subservient to mind and should follow mind’s orders; instead the senses started dominating the mind; I eliminated the cruel acts of those senses.

When asked “With whose help did you eliminate those senses?” āḻvār says,

- *kuṟungudi nedum kadal vaṇṇā* – Since you arrived in tirukkuṟungudi with your rejuvenating divine form.
- *pāvinār …* – With beautiful words in the form of many flowers, filled with good tunes, I incoherently praised and fell at your divine feet.
- *en nāvināl* – With my tongue which \[previously\] spoke that which will lead to disaster only.
- *naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy* – You who are to be praised, arrived in śrī naimiśāraṇyam to be the object of my praises.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.9. Unidaic cuvar vaittu

*ūnidaic cuvar vaittu enbu tūṇ nātti urōmam vēyndu onbadu vāsal tānudaik kurambaip piriyumbōdu undan saraṇamē saraṇam enṟirundēn tēnudaik kamalat tiruvinukkarasē!  tiraikoḷ mā nedungadal kidandāy! nānudait tavattāl tiruvadi adaindēn naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēn – honey; udai – having; kamalam – having lotus flower as abode; tiruvinukku – for periya pirāttiyār; arasē – oh beloved one!; tirai koḷ – Having waves; mā nedu – vast, deep; kadal – in tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean); kidandāy – oh one who is mercifully reclining!; naimisāraṇiyattuḷ – mercifully residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam; endāy – oh great benefactor!; Un – flesh; idai – in between; suvar vaittu – placed as wall; enbu – bone; tūṇ nātti – planted as pillar; urōmam – with hair; mēyndu – covered; onbadu vāsal – nine entrances; udai – having; kurambai – this body which is a house; piriyumbōdu – while leaving; unṟan – your highness’; saraṇamē – divine feet only; saraṇam enṟu – to have as refuge; irundēn – I considered; nānudai – (now) my; tavattāl – by your highness, the penance; tiruvadi – your highness’ divine feet; adaindēn – I reached

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh beloved one of periya pirāttiyār who is having honey-filled lotus flower as her abode! Oh one who is mercifully reclining on the vast and deep milk ocean which is having waves! Oh great benefactor who is mercifully residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam! While leaving this body which is a house where flesh is placed in between as wall, bone is planted as pillar, being covered with hair, and having nine entrances, I considered to have your highness’ divine feet only as refuge. By your highness who are my penance, I reached your highness’ divine feet.

- *ūnidaic cuvar vaittu* – Placing flesh as wall in between; alternatively – placing the flesh filled body as the wall; planting the bone as pillar and covering it with hair.
- *onbadu vāsal tānudaik kurambai* – As said in śvētaśvatara upaniśat 3.18 “*nava dvāra purē*” (city with nine entrances), this body is such that, one can enter and exit through any of the entrances. Just as a prince takes shelter of a hut, ātmā who is eternal, identified by knowledge and bliss, in a singular form, became captive in the body which shrinks the knowledge, due to his karma.
- *piriyumbōdu* – Just as he has karma to enter the body, he will also have karma to give up the body; at that time, I firmly believed that your divine feet are my refuge.

When asked “What is the hold for you to think in this manner?” āḻvār says,

- *tēnudaik kamalat tiruvinukku arasē* – Since he is always embracing periya pirāttiyār who is the puruśakārabhūtā (one who recommends and unites ātmā and paramātmā), he will not act in anger. By the strength of puruśakāram.
- *tirai …* – One who has arrived and is mercifully reclining on the rejuvenating milk ocean.
- *mā nedum kadal* – Great in vastness and depth.
- *nānudai …* – He has already explained his conduct; hence, when he says “my penance”, it is bhagavān only. I surrendered unto you by my penance.
- *naimisāraṇiyattuḷ endāy* – He creates good deed \[such as penance, for the ātmā\] by creating the universe, incarnating and making his presence in divine abodes which are dear to him.

## 1.6.10. Edam vandanuga

*ēdam vandaṇugā vaṇṇam nām eṇṇi eḻuminō toḻudum enṟu imaiyōr nādan vandirainjum naimisāraṇiyatu endaiyaic cindaiyuḷ vaittuk kādalē migutta kaliyan vāy oli sey mālaidān kaṟṟu vallārgaḷ ōda nīr vaiyagam āṇḍu veṇkudaik kīḻ umbarum āguvar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēdam vandu – sorrows approaching; aṇugā vaṇṇam – not to reach; nām eṇṇi – thinking in our mind; toḻudum – let us surrender (unto him); eḻumin enṟu – saying “arise”; imaiyōr – dēvatās; nādan – their lord, indra; vandu irainjum – coming and surrendering; naimisāraṇiyattu endaiyai – my lord who is mercifully residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam; sindaiyuḷ vaittu – placing him in the heart; kādal migutta – one who is having great love (towards bhagavat viśayam); kaliyan – āḻvār; vāy – mercifully composed; oli sey mālai – the garland of words; kaṟṟu vallārgaḷ – those who can learn with meaning; nīr – having abundant water; ōdam – surrounded by the ocean; vaiyagam – this world; veḷ – whitish; kudaikkīḻ – under the shade of the umbrella; āṇḍu – ruling with sceptre; umbarum āguvar – will become united with nityasūris as well

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

dēvatās along with their lord indra, saying “To not have the sorrows approach and reach us, let us think in our mind and surrender unto him. Arise!” come and surrender unto my lord who is mercifully residing in śrī naimiśāraṇyam. Placing such lord in my heart, I (āḻvār) who am having great love, mercifully composed this garland of words. Those who can learn this decad with its meanings, will rule this world which is surrounded by the ocean, with a sceptre, remaining under the shade of the whitish umbrella \[symbol of royalty\] and will become united with nityasūris as well.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *ēdam …* – Placing the lord who came and resided in śrī naimiśāraṇyam to be surrendered by dēvatās along with their lord indra “Thinking about sorrows not reaching us, let us worship and be uplifted! Arise!” Alternatively – the abode where nityasūris come along with their leader śrī sēnāpati āḻvār (viśvaksēnar) and surrender unto him.
- *kādalē migutta* … – Those who can learn the garland of words along with their meanings, which were mercifully composed by āḻvār whose love keeps increasing in bhagavat viśayam. āḻvār gave the shade of his love to emperumān who is residing in his heart.
- *ōda nīr vaiyagam āṇḍu* … – The ultimate goal is to become part of the assembly of nityasūris. If anyone desires, they can rule over worldly wealth and then attain the abode of nityasūris.

## 1.7 Angan jnalam

## 1.7.1. Angan jnalam

*angaṇ jñālam anja angu ōr āḷariyāy avuṇan ponga āgam vaḷḷugirāl pōḻnda punidanidam paingaṇ ānaik kombu koṇḍu pattimaiyāl adikkīḻc cengaṇ āḷi ittiṟainjum singavēḷ kunṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

angu – In that place where prahlāda vowed; am – beautiful; kaṇ – spacious; jñālam – whole world; anja – to fear; ōr – novel; āḷ ariyāy – in the form of narasimha (as he appeared, seeing that); avuṇan – hiraṇya, the demon; ponga – to arouse; āgam – (his) body; vaḷ ugirāl – with sharp, divine nail; pōḻnda – split and thrown; punidan – the pure sarvēśvaran (residing); idam – the abode is; sem kaṇ – having reddish eyes; āḷi – lions; pai – greenish; kaṇ – having eyes; ānai – elephants’; kombu – tusks; koṇḍu – grabbing; pattimaiyāl – due to bhagavat bhakti; adik kīḻ – at the divine feet; ittu – offering; iṟainjum – surrendering; singavēḷ kunṟam – singavēḷ kunṟam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In that place itself where prahlāda vowed, the pure sarvēśvaran appeared in the novel form of narasimha to make the beautiful, spacious, whole world fear and to arouse hiraṇya, the demon, and to split his body with his sharp, divine nail and throw it down; the divine abode of such sarvēśvaran is singavēḷ kunṟam where due to bhagavat bhakti, lions, having reddish eyes, grab the tusks of the elephants, which are having greenish eyes, and offer those at the divine feet of sarvēśvaran and surrender unto him.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *angaṇ jñālam anja* – To make the whole world which has beautiful places, become fearful. Though narasimha avatāram is for the protection of the world, since the people were unable to comprehend the action of emperumān, the whole world trembled.  The world thought “How is this going to end?”
- *angu* – In the same place where prahlāda vowed (the presence of bhagavān).
- *ōr āḷ ariyāy* – In the form of a narasimha which was never seen anywhere previously.
- *avuṇan ponga* – The demoniac hiraṇya became aroused in anger, on seeing narasimha. Since hiraṇya has never seen anyone coming to him saying “I am your enemy”, he became aroused in anger just on seeing narasimha. emperumān tore the body of such hiraṇya to split into two parts, by his sharp, divine nail. Just as one will tear some insentient objects, emperumān tore hiraṇya.
- *pōḻnda punidanidam* – For creation of the world etc, emperumān will accomplish that through brahmā et al; unlike that, here the purity of killing hiraṇya with his own hands is explained. In this manner, the divine abode where emperumān is residing to help the people of subsequent times.
- *paingaṇ …* – Just as the anger of narasimha on seeing hiraṇya will never diminish, the anger of the lions on seeing the elephants will remain the same.
- *paingaṇ* – The greenish eyes which are natural for the elephant species will be seen in these elephants.
- *kombu koṇḍu* – The lion will tear the head of the elephant and snatch the tusk and offer the same to bhagavān out of devotion and surrender unto him. It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 103.30 “*yadanna: puruśa: bhavati tadannās tasya dēvatā:*” (One should offer the food which is consumable by oneself, first to bhagavān). The reddish-eyed lion will bring the tusk of the greenish-eyed elephant, offer it to bhagavān with devotion and surrender unto him.
- *sengaṇ āḷi* – Though the lions have anger on elephants, their devotion towards bhagavān remains constant. Anger is incidental while their devotion is natural.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.2. Alaitta pelvay

*alaitta pēḻ vāy vāḷ eyiṟṟōr kōḷ ariyāy avuṇan kolaik kaiyāḷan nenjidanda kūrugirāḷanidam malaitta selsātteṟinda pūsal vantudivāy kaduppac cilaik kai vēdar teḻippaṟāda singavēḷ kunṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

alaitta – (due to anger) with swaying tongue; pēḻ vāy – huge mouth; vāḷ – radiant; eyiṟu – teeth; ōr – matchless; kōḷ – strong; ariyāy – being a lion; kolai – killing others as nature; kaiyāḷan – having hand; avuṇan – hiraṇyan’s; nenju – chest; idanda – one who split and threw; kūr ugirāḷan – sarvēśvaran who is having sharp divine nail and is eternally residing; idam – abode; malaitta – stopped (by hunters); sel – those who are going on holy pilgrimage; sāttu – group; eṟinda – fought; pūsal – in the battle; val – making heavy noise; vāy – having mouth; tudi – hourglass shaped drum; kaduppa – to make noise; silai – bow; kai – having in hand; vēdar – hunters’; teḻippu – noise; aṟāda – going on continuously; singavēḷ kunṟam – singavēḷ kunṟam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being a matchless, strong lion having huge month with swaying tongue and radiant teeth, sarvēśvaran who is having sharp divine nail which by nature is killing others, split the chest of hiraṇyan who has the hand which kills others as its nature and threw him down. The abode where he is residing is singavēḷ kunṟam where group of people who are going on holy pilgrimage are fought in battle by hunters who are having hourglass shaped drums which are making heavy noise and a bow in their hands and where the noise of such hunters is going on continuously.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *alaitta* – Being a matchless, strong lion who is having a huge mouth in which the tongue is swaying in anger and touching the teeth and who is having radiant teeth.
- *avuṇan kolaik kaiyāḷan* – Worldly people will harm others for the sake of protecting their own children; but for him, instead of that, he ended up harming his own child. hiraṇyan had acquired boons from dēvatās to harm others and having such act as his routine; the divine abode of sarvēśvaran who split the chest of such hiraṇyan with his sharp, divine nail.
- *malaitta …* – People will go for holy pilgrimage in many groups; to rob them, the hunters will stop them and attack them; these pilgrims will fight those hunters.
- *eṟinda pūsal* – eṟidal – idudal – engaging in fight; the battle where the hunters rob the pilgrims.
- *val tudi vāy kaduppa* – As the hourglass shaped drum makes tumultuous noise which will kill those who heard it.
- *silaik kai* – The abode where the noise of the hunters who are armed with bow in their hands, will never stop; the fearsome drum in their hands and the tumultuous noise will go on forever. For tirumangai āḻvār, since these are in the divine abodes which are dear to emperumān, everything such as the noise of the hunters’ drum or the noise of their robbery, is desirable. For āḻvār, there is no difference between the anger of narasimha, the anger of the hunters and their act of robbery.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.3. Eynda pelvay

*ēynda pēḻvāy vāḷeyiṟṟōr kōlariyāy avuṇan vāynda āgam vaḷḷugirāl vagirnda ammānadidam ōynda māvum udainda kunṟum anṟiyum ninṟaḻalāl tēynda vēyum alladillac cingavēḷ kunṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēynda – matching his form; pēḻ – huge; vāy – mouth; vāḷ – sword like; eyiṟu – teeth; ōr – matchless; kōḷ – strong; ariyāy – being narasimha; avuṇan – hiraṇya, who is demoniac; vāynda – grown to match narasimha’s form; āgam – body; vaḷ ugirāl – with sharp divine nail; vagirnda – easily tore and threw; ammānadu – sarvēśvaran’s; idam – abode; ōynda – tired (due to roaming around in barren lands); māvum – animals; udainda – broken (by heat); kunṟum – small hills; anṟiyum – further; ninṟu – having within; aḻalāl – by fire; tēynda – remaining as half burnt; vēyum – bamboo; alladu – other than those; illā – nothing else is present; singavēḷ kunṟam – singavēḷ kunṟam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being a matchless strong narasimha having huge mouth and sword like teeth which match his form, sarvēśvaran easily tore the demoniac hiraṇya’s body which had grown to match his \[emperumān’s\] form and threw it; the divine abode of such sarvēśvaran is singavēḷ kunṟam where tired animals, small broken hills, and further the bamboo which has fire within and remains as half burnt are only present and nothing else is present.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *ēynda …* – Having huge mouth \[and teeth\] matching his great divine form; sword like teeth; alternatively – radiant teeth.
- *ōr kōḷariyāy* – Strong, matchless narasimha. avuṇan’s – the demoniac one’s; vāynda āgam – the body which had grown matching narasimha’s form; the divine abode of sarvēśvaran who tore such body with his sharp divine nail.
- *ōynda māvum* – Due to roaming around the barren lands, the animals which live in that region will also be tired.
- *udainda kunṟum* – The small hills which are broken due to the heat, and will break further on coming in contact with anything. Further, the bamboo which has fire inside and is half-burnt due to that. singavēḷ kunṟam has nothing other than these. The bamboos which are burnt due to the fire within. \[Still\] For āḻvār, this abode appears similar to śrīrangam which is described in [tirumālai 14](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thirumalai-14/) “*vaṇḍinamuralum sōlai*” (gardens where the swarm of bees keep humming). It is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thiruvaimozhi-5-10-2-vadhuvai-varththaiyul/) “*adu idu udu ennal āvana valla*” (without distinguishing between that activity, this activity or the other activity, everything related to you is desirable). Desiring something implies, what is seen as fault in that by others, will be seen as desirable in the same thing by us.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.4. Evvam vevvel

*evvam vevvēl pon peyarōn ēdalan innuyirai vavvi āgam vaḷḷugirāl vagirnda ammānadidam kavvu nāyum kaḻugum uccip pōdodu kāl suḻanṟu deyvam allāl sella oṇṇāc cingavēḷ kunṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

evvam – causing sorrow; vem – cruel; vēl – having spear; ēdalan – enemy; pon peyarōn – hiraṇya’s; in uyirai – good life; vavvi – snatched; āgam – (his) body; vaḷ ugirāl vagirnda ammānadidam – the abode of the lord who tore with his strong divine nail; kavvum – biting (those who are seen); nāyum – dogs; kaḻugum – (similar) eagles; uchip pōdodu – with sun; kāl suḻanṟu – to have the feet hobble; deyvam allāl – except for the devotees who worship him with love; sella oṇṇā – not possible to go and reach; singavēḷ kunṟam – singavēḷ kunṟam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

hiraṇya, the enemy, is having cruel spear which causes sorrow; the abode of the lord who tore such hiraṇya’s body with his strong divine nail and snatched his good life, is singavēḷ kunṟam where the dogs and eagles are biting, the sun will make the feet hobble, and which is not possible to reach except for the devotees who worship him with love.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *evvam vevvēl pon peyarōn* – Just on seeing his form where he holds the spear in his hand, one will feel the pain of such spear piercing through the body. One who has the cruel spear which causes sorrow; his name – hiraṇya. evvam – sorrow. ēdalan – enemy. When he became an enemy to the child prahlāda, he automatically becomes an enemy to emperumān as well. kriṣṇa said “We cannot consume food in enemy’s home”. When duryōdana became inimical towards pāṇḍavas, he became an enemy to kriṣṇa too. His dear life. vavvi – snatching. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.19.24 “*papau janārdana: krudda:*” (janārdana who was angry, swallowed).
- *kavvu nāyum* – The dog which bites anyone it sees, and the eagles which are similar.
- *uccip pōdodu kāl suḻanṟu* – Even the sun will hobble in that abode. Alternative explanation. uccip pōdu – sun; along with the sun, the dog and eagle which bite, will all hobble. Another explanation – in the noon time when the sun is at the top, kāl – wind, wind will come twirling. Here, the heat of the land is explained. āḻvār who desires to go to and reach that abode is saying “none other than devotees can reach” because there is no one who can see the beauty of narasimha and cast an evil eye on him. āḻvārs are of the nature of singing pallāṇḍu as said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruppallandu-6-enthai-thanthai/) “*andiyam pōdil ari uruvāgi ariyai aḻittavanaip pandanai tīrap pallāṇḍu”* (I seek long life for emperumān who assumed the form of narasimha at sunset and destroyed the enemy, to eliminate his fatigue). The abode cannot be reached by non-devotees. Those who are similar to hiraṇya cannot reach there.

## 1.7.5. Menra pelvay

*menṟa pēḻ vāy vāḷ eyiṟṟōr kōḷariyāy avuṇan ponṟa āgam vaḷḷugirāl pōḻnda punidanidam ninṟa sendī moṇḍu sūṟai nīḷ visumbu ūdiriya senṟu kāṇḍaṟkariya kōyil singavēḷ kunṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

menṟa – (due to anger) chewing; pēḻ vāy – huge mouth; vāḷ – sword like; eyiṟu – teeth; kōḷ – strong; ōr ariyāy – as matchless narasimha; ponṟa – became destroyed (just on seeing that form); avuṇan – hiraṇya, the demon, his; āgam – body; vaḷ ugirāl – with sharp, divine nail; pōḻnda – split into two parts; punidan – sarvēśvaran who has pure mind, where he is residing; idam – abode; ninṟa – without any shortcoming; sem tī – reddish fire; sūṟai – tornado; moṇḍu – scooping it; nīḷ visumbu ūdu – in the vast sky; iriya – since it is moving in a scattered manner; senṟu – going to its vicinity; kāṇḍaṟku – to see; ariya – difficult for everyone; kōyil – divine abode; singavēḷ kunṟamē – singavēḷ kunṟam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Chewing his huge mouth with sword like teeth, as a strong, matchless narasimha, to destroy hiraṇya, the demon, sarvēśvaran who has pure mind, split his \[hiraṇya’s\] body into two parts with sharp, divine nail; the divine abode where such sarvēśvaran is residing is singavēḷ kunṟam which is difficult for everyone to go and see, as the tornado scoops the reddish fire without any shortcoming, in the vast sky and is moving there in a scattered manner.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *menṟa …* – Being the strong, matchless narasimha whose huge mouth is puckered due to anger, having sword like teeth.
- *avuṇan ponṟa* – hiraṇya became dead at the sight of narasimha.
- *āgam …* – Since emperumān’s anger did not subdue still, he tore the dead body of hiraṇya.
- *punidanidam* – The purity of emperumān who killed hiraṇya considering hiraṇya to be his own enemy instead of killing him considering to be enemy of others \[his devotees\], is thought about here.
- *ninṟa …* – Fire will be present without any shortcoming, scooping it, the tornado will spread it in the vast sky. iriya – spread, making tumultuous noise. If recited as *eriya*, to make the sky as a stove and have the fire blazing there.
- *senṟu* – Due to this situation, it is impossible for anyone to reach there. āḻvār is becoming joyful thinking that just as paramapadam, we need not fear for this abode as well \[i.e. very safe for emperumān\]

## 1.7.6. Erinda paingan

*erinda paingaṇ ilangu pēḻvāy eyiṟṟodu idu evvuruvenṟu irindu vānōr kalangiyōda irunda ammānadidam nerinda vēyin muḻaiyuḷ ninṟu nīḷ neṟivāy uḻuvai tirinda ānaic cuvadu pārkkum singavēḷ kunṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

erinda – burning due to anger; pai – greenish; kaṇ – eyes; ilangu – radiant; pēḻ vāy – having huge mouth; eyiṟṟodu – with teeth (looking at such a form); idu evvuru – what kind of a form is this?; enṟu anji – fearing in such manner; vānōr – dēvatās; irindu – becoming scattered here and there; kalangi – hobbled; ōda – to run away; irunda – mercifully seated; ammānadu – sarvēśvaran’s; idam – abode is; nerinda – joined together; vēyin – bamboo’s; muḻaiyuḷ ninṟu – through the gap; uḻuvai – tigers; nīḷ neṟivāy – in the vast path; tirinda – roaming around; ānai – elephants (which travelled); suvadu – footprints; pārkkum – seeing (by observing the smell); singavēḷ kunṟamē – singavēḷ kunṟam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

dēvatās on seeing sarvēśvaran having greenish eyes which are burning, radiant huge mouth with teeth, feared, thinking “What kind of a form is this?”, becoming scattered here and there, hobbled and ran away. The abode of such sarvēśvaran where he is mercifully seated is singavēḷ kunṟam where the tigers are seeing through the gaps in bamboos, which are joined together, at the footprints of the elephants which are roaming around in the vast path.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *erinda …* – Seeing sarvēśvaran’s form which is having eyes which are greenish matching the species, and are burning due to anger, radiant, huge mouth and teeth.
- *idu evvuru enṟu* – dēvatās feared thinking “We have not seen such a form previously. What kind of form is this?” made huge noise, became scattered, hobbled and ran away in such a manner that one \[dēvatā\] does not enter another person’s space. Such sarvēśvaran’s abode.
- *nerinda …* – Due to the dense presence of bamboos, they remained joined together. Through the gaps between such bamboos. uḻuvai – tiger. nīḷ neṟivāy – In the vast path. Roaming around there …
- *ānaic cuvadu pārkkum* – To hit the elephants on their head and to consume their flesh, blood etc, the tigers will follow their footprints in the vast path. Just as narasimha will follow the footprints of the demoniac persons to kill them.

## 1.7.7. Munaitta sirram

*munaitta sīṟṟam viṇ sudappōy mūvulagum piṟavum anaittum anja āḷariyāy irunda ammānadidam kanaitta tīyum kallumallā villudai vēdarumāyt tinaittanaiyum sella voṇṇāc  cingavēḷ kunṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

munaitta sīṟṟam – great anger; pōy – leaving here; viṇ suda – reaching the sky and heating it up; mū ulagum – residents of all three worlds; piṟavum – and; anaittum – residents of brahma lōkam etc; anja – to fear; āḷ ariyāy – having narasimha form; irunda – mercifully seated; ammānadu – lord of all, his; idam – abode is; kanaitta – making noise (while burning); tīyum – fire; kallum – rocks (which are burning by that fire); allā – more cruel than that; vil – bow; udai – having in hand; vēdarumāy – having hunters; tinaittanaiyum – even for a moment (for non-devotees); sella oṇṇā – unreachable; singavēḷ kunṟamē – singavēḷ kunṟam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The lord of all, having narasimha form,  mercifully seated while his great anger left here and reached the sky, heating it up, to cause fear for all the residents of the three worlds and brahma lōkam etc; his abode is singavēḷ kunṟam, where the fire is making noise and where there are rocks and hunters having bow in their hands, who are more cruel than those fire and rocks, and which is unreachable even for a moment (for non-devotees).

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *munaitta …* – The great anger reached up to the sky and heated it.
- *mū ulagum .*.. – The three worlds (bhū:, bhuva: and svarga) and the abodes of brahmā et al became frightened fully; āḷ ari – masculine lion; or āḻvār is speaking about the mix of human and lion traits.
- *kanaitta* … – Fire which is making noise; while burning, the fire makes a cracking noise and the rocks which are burning in that fire like hay.
- *allā …* – Even one can step on such fire and rocks; but cannot face the hunters of that abode; such is their cruelty.
- *tinaittanaiyum …* – The abode which cannot be reached by non-devotees to go and cast evil eye upon him.

## 1.7.8. Nattalumba nanmuganum

*nāttaḻumba nānmuganum īsanumāy muraiyāl ētta angōrāḷariyāy irunda ammānadidam kāytta vāgai neṟṟolippak kalladar vēyngaḻai pōy tēytta tīyāl viṇ sivakkum singavēḷ kunṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nā – tongue; taḻumba – to have scars; nānmuganum – brahmā who has four faces; īsanum – rudran; āy – to not lose their position; muṟaiyāl – in proper manner (that emperumān is lord and we are servitors); ētta – as they praise; angu – there (remaining to be praised by them); ōr āḷariyāy irunda ammānadidam – the abode where he is mercifully present as matchless narasimha; kāytta – filled with unripe fruits; vāgai – vāgai (lebbeck) trees’; neṟṟu – nuts; olippa – to make noise; kal adar – branching through rocks; vēyngaḻai – tube shaped bamboo; pōy – growing to reach up to the sky; tēytta – due to rubbing with each other; tīyāl – by the fire; viṇ – sky; sivakkum – become reddish; singavēḷ kunṟamē – singavēḷ kunṟam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

brahmā who has four faces and rudran praised the matchless narasimha in proper manner, to have scars on their tongue and to not lose their position; the abode where such narasimha is present is singavēḷ kunṟam where the nuts of the lebbeck trees which are filled with unripe fruits, are making noise, and the tube shaped bamboos are branching through rocks, growing to reach up to the sky and turning the sky to be red due to the fire caused by the rubbing of those bamboos with each other.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

- *nā …* – To have scars on the tongue, the four-faced brahmā and rudran who is the head of dēvatās, who were roaming around in human disguise during the rein of hiraṇyan, once such hiraṇyan died, to not lose their position, came and praised emperumān due to his natural lordship; the abode of such sarvēśvara where he remains to be praised by them and is present in the form of narasimha which was previously unseen.
- *kāytta …* – As the nuts make noise in the lebbeck tree which has many unripe fruits. These trees belong in desert lands and are highlighted.
- *kal adar vēyngaḻai pōy* – kaḻai – mūngil – bamboo. adar – vaḻi – path. There are bamboos which grow through rocks – tube shaped bamboos. Those bamboos grew up to the sky, and caused fire rubbing with each other. Just as the sky will appear dark due to presence of clouds, here due to this fire, the sky appears reddish. With this, it is explained that – inside the abode, the praises of brahmā et al are heard; outside, the sound of the nuts of lebbeck trees is heard.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.9. Nallai nenje

*nallai nenjē! nām toḻudum nammudai namperumān alli mādar pulga ninṟa āyirantōḷanidam nelli malgik kalludaippap pullilaiyārttu adarvāyc cillu cillenṟollaṟāda singavēḷ kunṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nammudai – being our refuge; namperumān – being our lord; alli mādar – periya pirāttiyār who has lotus flower as her residence; pulgu – to embrace; ninṟa – one who mercifully resides; āyiram tōḷan – sarvēśvaran who is having thousand divine shoulders, his; idam – abode is; nelli – gooseberry trees; malgi – filled; kal – rocks; udaippa – to break; pul ilai – palm leaf; ārttu – to make noise; adarvāy – in the path; silli – birds named “silveedu”; sil enṟu ol aṟāda – to not let up on making noise which sounds in the tone “sil”; singavēḷ kunṟam – singavēḷ kunṟam; nallai nenjē – Oh mind who is agreeing with me!; nām toḻudum – We will (go there) and be uplifted by worshiping him

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who is having thousand divine shoulders, who is our refuge and lord, mercifully resides in singavēḷ kunṟam, to be embraced by periya pirāttiyār who has lotus flower as her residence; this abode is filled with gooseberry trees which will break the rocks, palm leaves make noise and birds named “silveedu” in the path do not let up on making noise sounds in the tone “sil”. Oh mind who is agreeing with me! We will (go there) and be uplifted by worshiping him.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*nallai nenjē* – Oh mind who agrees with me! ōr, āḻvār calls “Oh mind!” and says “I got the fortune to have you in line with my thoughts now!”

*nān toḻudōm* – We will worship and be uplifted. This is the verb/action for the whole decad.

*nammudai namperumān* – sarvēśvaran who is presenting himself to us as refuge, just as he is enjoyable for nityasūris.

*alli …* – As brahmā et al surrender unto him and as dēvatās become scared and try to run away, periya pirāttiyār will come and embrace him to reduce his anger thinking “His incarnation which is meant to destroy the enemies has ended up causing fear in the minds of devotees as well”.

*āyiram tōḷan* – When she embraces him, he will acquire thousand shoulder to embrace her.

*nelli …* – The gooseberry trees will grow abundantly and break the rocks. As the roots of the gooseberry trees spread, the rocks will break.

*pul ilai ārttu* – As the bamboos make noise. ōr, as the palm leaves make noise.

*adarvāy …* – In the path. silli – silveedu bird. It will constantly make a sound “sil” – will repeat such sound. ollaṟāda – non-stop noise.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.10. Senganali ittirainjum

*sengaṇāḷi ittiṟainjum singavēḷ kunṟudaiya engaḷ īsan empirānai irundamiḻ nūṟpulavan mangaiyāḷan mannu tol sīr vaṇḍaṟai tārkkaliyan sengaiyāḷan senjol mālai vallavar tīdilarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem – reddish; kaṇ – having eyes; āḷi – lions; ittu – offered (the objects for worship at the divine feet); iṟainjum – surrendering; singavēḷ kunṟu – singavēḷ kunṟam (hill); udaiya – having as his abode; engaḷ – even for us who are samsāris (materialistic people); īsan – being the lord; empirānai – on sarvēśvaran who is my benefactor; iru – great; tamiḻ nūl – in tamiḻ śāstram; pulavan – being an expert; mangai āḷan – being the king of tirumangai region; tol mannu – eternally remaining; sīr – wealth; vaṇḍu – beetles; aṟai – making noise; tār – garland; sem kai āḷan – being very generous; kaliyan – mercifully spoken by tirumangai āḻvār; sem sol mālai – garland of honest words; vallavar – those who can learn; tīdu ilar – will be free from evil aspects

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who is my benefactor is having singavēḷ kunṟam as his abode, where lions having reddish eyes offered objects for worship and surrendered unto him; he is the lord even for us who are samsāris (materialistic people); on such sarvēśvaran, tirumangai āḻvār who is an expert in great tamiḻ śāstram and is the king of tirumangai region, who is having eternally remaining wealth and wearing garland where beetles remain and make noise, who is very generous, mercifully spoke this decad which is a garland of honest words; those who can learn this decad will be free from evil aspects.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

sem kaṇ … – Lions who have reddish eyes due to their vīraśrī (wealth of valour), will kill the animals which are inimical towards them, offer them as part of their worship and surrender unto sarvēśvaran. śrī gaṇṭākarṇāḻvān (a demon named gaṇṭā karṇa, who became a devotee of emperumān), killed a riśi and offered that body to kriṣṇa saying “This is the meat of a brāhmaṇa body; hence, it is the best; it is very fresh”. emperumān has singavēḷ kunṟam as his abode. The benefactor who presented himself so that even samsāris like us can go and surrender unto him.

*irum tamiḻ nūl pulavan* – One who has so much knowledge to see the end of the tamiḻ śāstram (scriptures) which are boundless and are difficult to comprehend for anyone.

*mangai āḷan* – The leader of tirumangai region.

*mannu tol sīr* … – One who has the eternal wealth of pāratantryam (total dependence on bhagavān). śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.28 “*lakśmaṇō lakśmī sampanna:*” (lakśmaṇa who is endowed with wealth of kainkaryam). āḻvār who is wearing garland which is having beetles having drunk honey, keep humming.

*sem kai āḷan* – Greatly generous. One who blessed this prabandam to be enjoyed by all.

*sem sol mālai vallavar* – Those who are well learned in this decad which is a garland of honest words which reveal very complicated principles.

*tīdu ilarē* – Since narasimhan emperumān will eliminate the hurdles, they will not be affected by any evil aspects.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8 Kongalarnda

## 1.8.1. Kongalarnda

*kongalarnda malark kurundam ositta kōvalan empirān sangu tangu tadangadal tuyil koṇḍa tāmaraik kaṇṇinan pongu puḷḷinai vāy piḷanda purāṇar tammidam pongunīrc cengayal tiḷaikkum sunait tiruvēngadam adainenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

sangu – conces; tangu – present; tadam – vast; kadal – tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi); tuyil koṇḍa – mercifully resting; tāmaraik kaṇṇinan – having lotus flower like divine eyes; kōvalan – being kriṣṇa; kongu – fragrance; alarnda – spreading; malar – filled with flowers; kurundam – kurukkatti tree (which is possessed by a demon); ositta – one who destroyed; pongu – who came fiercely; puḷḷinai – bakāsuran’s; vāy – mouth; piḷanda – one who tore and threw down; em pirān – being my benefactor; purāṇar tam – sarvēśvaran who is popular through purāṇams, his; idam – abode; pongu nīr – having abundance of water; sem – reddish; kayal – fish; tiḷaikkum – joyfully living; tiruvēngadam – tiruvēngadam tirumalā; nenjamē – Oh mind!; adai – try to reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is mercifully resting in the vast tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi) where conces are present; he is having lotus flower like divine eyes; being kriṣṇa he destroyed the kurukkatti tree which is filled with fragrant flowers; he tore and threw down bakāsuran’s mouth; the abode of such sarvēśvaran who is popular through purāṇams and who is my benefactor, is tiruvēngadam (tirumalā) which is having abundance of water where reddish fish are joyfully living. Oh mind! Try to reach there.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*kongu alarnda* – Having fragrant flowers.

*kurundu ositta* – From the bottom to top, the tree was having blossomed flowers which made it look beautiful; being possessed with a demon, it was trying to harm him. He thought “This looks beautiful \[tricky\]; let me destroy it and finish the task” and destroyed it.

*kōvalan empirān* – Just as he incarnated as kriṣṇa and destroyed the kurunda tree, he eliminated my hurdles and favoured me. Unlike the demon in the tree, destroying the demon based on the demon’s thoughts, in my case, he looked out for my well-being and favoured me.

*sangu …* – His arrival at kśīrābdi for the purpose of this kriṣṇāvatāram is highlighted by āḻvār here. Everything identified as conch is gathered in there and it is also quite vast for his comfortable rest. He is mercifully resting there.

*pongu …* – Tearing the mouth of bakāsura who came to fight kriṣṇa very fiercely; the abode of such sarvēśvaran who is eliminating the enemies since time immemorial.

*pongu …* – The fertility of the land is the reason for the joy of the fish. āḻvār is saying “Oh mind! Try to reach tirumalā which has ponds where fish which are reddish due to their youth, are joyfully living”.

## 1.8.2. Palliyavadu parkadal

*paḷḷiyāvadu pāṟkadal arangam iranga van pēy mulai piḷḷaiyāy uyiruṇḍa endai pirānavan perugumidam veḷḷiyān kariyān maṇiniṟa vaṇṇanenṟeṇṇi nāḷdoṟum teḷḷiyār vaṇangum malait tiruvēngadam adainenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

val – one who is having hard heart; pēy – pūtanā’s; mulai – bosoms; iranga – to secrete milk naturally; uyir – her life; uṇḍa – mercifully consumed; endai – my lord; pirān avan – sarvēśvaran who is the benefactor; paḷḷiyāvadu – mattress (resting place, where he mercifully rests); pāṟkadal – tirukkāṟkdal (kśīrābdi); arangam – and śrīrangam; perugum – growing; idam – abode is; teḷḷiyār – ananyaprayōjanar (those who don’t expect anything but kainkaryam); veḷḷiyān – one who has white complexion (in kruta yugam); kariyān – one who has black complexion (in kali yugam); maṇi niṟa vaṇṇan – one who has blue jewel like complexion (in dvāpara yugam); enṟu eṇṇi – meditating (repeatedly on these forms) in this manner; nādoṟum – everyday; vaṇangum – surrendering; malai – hill; tiruvēngadam – tirumalā; nenjamē adai – Oh mind! Reach there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The resting places of my benefactor, sarvēśvaran, who mercifully consumed the life of the hard-hearted pūtanā as milk which naturally secreted from her bosoms, are kśīrābdi and śrīrangam; the abode where he grows is tirumalā hill where those who don’t expect anything but kainkaryam are meditating upon his various forms such as the one in white complexion (in kruta yugam), black complexion (in kali yugam) and blue jewel like complexion (in dvāpara yugam), and surrendering everyday. Oh mind! Reach there.

*paḷḷiyāvadu pāṟkadal arangam* – kśīrābdi is where he mercifully rests to be surrendered to by brahmā et al; for those samsāris who cannot go as far as kśīrābdi, he is mercifully resting in kōyil (śrīrangam).

*iranga …* – As he touched her bosoms, they started secreting milk; or, to make her scream. Just being a child he consumed the milk from the bosoms of the hard-hearted pūtanā. Due to his infancy, he could not differentiate between her life and her milk.

*endai pirān avan perugum idam* – The abode where my lord and benefactor grows. His being nurtured is highlighted.

*veḷḷiyān …* – All forms assumed by him are desirable for āḻvār purely because they are his forms. Meditating upon his whitish form in kruta yugam, blackish form in kali yugam and bluish form in dvāpara yugam; teḷḷiyār – ananyaprayōjanar. They will visit everyday and worship him. Those who eternally enjoy as done by nityasūris.

## 1.8.3. Ninra mamarudu

*ninṟa māmarudu iṟṟuvīḻa nadanda ninmalan nēmiyān enṟum vānavar kai toḻum iṇait tāmarai adi empirān kanṟi māri poḻindidak kadidāniraikku idar nīkkuvān senṟu kunṟam eduttavan tiruvēngadam adai nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ninṟa – standing firm (due to being possessed by demon); mā marudu – the big maruda tree; iṟṟu vīḻa – to break and fall down; nadanda – going through; ninmalan – one who has very pure heart; nēmiyān – one who is having divine chakra (in his divine hand); vānavar – nityasūris; enṟum – always; kaitoḻum – vorśipping; tāmarai – lotus flower like; iṇai adi – having a pair of divine feet; em pirān – being benefactor; kanṟi – (indra) being angry; māri – heavy rain; poḻindida – poured; A – cows’; niraikku – for their herds; idar – sorrow; nīkkuvān – to eliminate and protect them; kadidu – quickly; senṟu – went; kunṟam – gōvardana hill; eduttavan – the abode, where sarvēśvaran who lifted and held as umbrella, is mercifully residing; tiruvēngadam – tirumalā; nenjamē – Oh mind!; adai – reach there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My benefactor who went through the maruda tree which was standing firm to break it and push it down, who has pure heart, who is having divine chakra (in his divine hand), whom the nityasūris are always vorśipping, quickly went and lifted the gōvardana hill and held as umbrella, to eliminate the sorrow of the cow herds and protect them, when indra poured down heavy rain in anger; tirumalā is the abode where such sarvēśvaran is mercifully residing. Oh mind! Reach there.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*ninṟa* – māmarudu, huge maruda tree, being possessed by demon, standing firm; the event would make one fear “the one which fell the other side, what would have happened to kriṣṇa had it fallen this side!” To have it break and fall down. One who has purity to stroll through it to break it and push down, without having such intention.

*nēmiyān* – He need not use his hand to do these acts; he has the weapon to eliminate the enemies without his presence; still, he was caught in the situation.

*enṟum …* – One who is cared by all the nityasūris in parampadam, came alone and was caught in the situation.

*kanṟi …* – indra, having great anger, sent the clouds, and understanding his mind, they poured down the rain heavily.

*āniraikku idar nīkkuvān kadidu senṟu kunṟam eduttavan* – One who lifted gōvardana hill by rushing there before a drop falls on those cows \[and covherd men and women\] who have no means to protect themselves.

*tiruvēngadam adai nenjamē* – One who lifted a hill and eliminated the sorrows, is standing on a hill and looking to protect \[everyone\]. āḻvār says “Oh mind! See that you reach him”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8.4. Parttarkay anru

*pārttaṟkāy anṟu bāradam kai seydittu venṟa paranjudar kōttu angāyartam pādiyil kuravai piṇainda em kōvalan ēttuvārtam manattuḷḷān idavendai mēviya empirān tīrtta nīrt tadanjōlai sūḻ tiruvēngadam adai nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – towards the end of dvāpara yugam; bāradam – in the bhārata yuddam (mahābhārata battle); pārttaṟkāy – for arjuna; kai seydittu – personally organising the army; venṟa – won over (duryōdana et al, and due to that); param sudar – one who is very radiant; āyar tam pādiyil – in tiruvāyppādi (śrī gōkulam); em kōvalan – taking birth in the covherd clan; angu – in such śrī gōkulam; kuravai – in rāsa krīdā; kōttup piṇainda – holding hands and danced; ēttuvār tam – those who praise, their; manattu – in mind; uḷḷān – present eternally; idavendai – in tiruvidavendai; mēviya – is firmly present; em pirān – my lord’s; tīrttam – pure; nīr – having water; tadam – by ponds; sōlai – gardens; sūḻ – surrounded by; tiruvēngadam adai nenjamē – Oh mind! Reach tirumalā

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is very radiant due to personally organising the battle for arjuna in the mahābhārata battle towards the end of dvāpara yugam to ensure his victory; he was born in the covherd clan in śrī gōkulam and danced with the gōpikās, holding their hands in rāsa krīdā with them; he is eternally present in the minds of those who praise him; he is firmly present in tiruvidavendai; tiruvēngadam, tirumalā is the abode of such emperumān, which is surrounded ponds which have pure water and gardens. Oh mind! Reach there.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*pārtaṟkāy* – For arjuna.

*anṟu bāradam kaiseydittu* – In the mahābhārata war, he personally arranged the army.

*venṟu param sudar* – He showed such partiality to have the loss on the heads of duryōdana et al and victory on his head \[i.e. pāṇḍavas who were so inseparable from him\].

*param sudar* – The radiance acquired after placing the crown on the head of darmaputra and after having draupadi knot her hair. śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.85 “*rākśasēndram vibhīśaṇam krutakrutyā:*” (After crowning vibhīśaṇa as the king of demons, śrī rāma felt he has fulfilled his responsibility).

*kōttu …* – Stringing himself amidst the gōpikās during rāsakrīdā in tiruvāyppādi.

*kuravai piṇainda em kōvalan* – He performed the same dance in the main junction of the town and gave complete enjoyment for the devotees.

*ēttuvār tam manattuḷḷān* – One who eternally resides in the hearts of those who meditate upon such dance, be immersed in that and praise that.

*idavendai* – Just as he arrived at tiruvidavendai for periya pirāttiyār and stayed there forever, he will remain in the hearts of those who praise him.

*tīrtta nīr …* – Being surrounded by abundance of water which will lead to all wealth and rejuvenating gardens.

## 1.8.5. Vankaiyan avunarkku

*vaṇkaiyān avuṇarkku nāyagan vēḷviyil senṟu māṇiyāy maṇ kaiyāl irandān marāmaram ēḻum eyda valattinān eṇkaiyān imayattuḷḷān irunjōlai mēviya empirān tiṇkaimmā tuyar tīrttavan tiruvēngadam adai nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇ kaiyān – being the one with a generous hand; avuṇarkku – for the demons; nāyagan – mahābali, the leader, his; vēḷviyil – in the sacrificial arena; māṇiyāy – being a celibate boy; senṟu – went; maṇ – earth; kaiyāl – with his hand; irandān – being the one who begged; marāmaram ēḻum – the seven ebony trees; eyda – (in rāmāvatāram) shot them down; valattinān – being the strong one; eṇ kaiyān – being the one with many divine hands; imayattu uḷḷān – being the one who is mercifully residing in himavān (in tiruppiridi in the himalayas); irunjōlai – in tirumālirunjōlai which is known as southern tirumalā; mēviya – one who is eternally residing; em pirān – being the lord of all; tiṇ – strong; kai – having trunk; mā – śrī gajēndrāḻvān’s; tuyar – sorrow; tīrttavan – sarvēśvaran who eliminated, is present in; tiruvēngadam – tirumalā; adai nenjamē – Oh mind! Reach there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, as the celibate boy, went to the sacrificial arena of mahābali, the leader of demons and the one who has a generous hand, and begged the earth with his hand; being the strong one in rāmāvatāram, he shot down the seven ebony trees; being the one with many hands, being the one who is mercifully residing in himavān, being the one who is eternally residing in tirumālirunjōlai which is known as southern tirumalā, being the lord of all, sarvēśvaran who eliminated the sorrow of śrī gajēndrāḻvān who is having a strong trunk, is present in tirumalā. Oh mind! Reach there.

*vaṇ kaiyān …* – He was generous. Though he was the leader of the demons, since he had a noble quality named generosity, he could not be killed by arrow. He was happy to give; hence, emperumān made himself an alms-seeker and accepted the worlds through the act which gave mahābali happiness.

*māṇiyāy maṇ kaiyāl irandān* – emperumān went to mahābali’s sacrificial arena, with a form which is well established in begging and accepted the earth which went through many transformations under his control just as cotton goes through twelve stages of development.

*marāmaram* … – One who would carry out acts to bring in faith in his devotees.

*valattinān* – Strong one.

*eṇkaiyān* – One who has many hands to hold many different weapons to cause destruction to the enemies of his devotees. Alternatively, āḻvār could be speaking about emperumān in tiruvattabhuyakaram divyadēśam.

*imayattuḷḷān* – One who is present in tiruppiridi in himavān.

*irunjōlai …* – One who arrived and resided in tirumalai of southern direction which is mlēcca bhūmi \[Very long ago, the southern portion of bhārata dēśam was considered as an inferior place inhabited by uncultured persons\].

*tiṇ kai mā tuyar tīrttavan* – When śrī gajēndrāḻvān was caught by the crocodile and was in a helpless state, emperumān arrived there, eliminated his sorrow and protected him.

*tiṇ kai* – One who would torment others with his strong trunk, was tormented by the crocodile and emperumān eliminated such suffering.

*tiruvēngadam* – To have the shortcoming of arriving late to help śrī gajēndrāḻvān after he could not protect himself anymore, emperumān arrived in tiruvēngadam to help the devotees before they get into trouble.

## 1.8.6. En disaigalum

*eṇ disaigaḷum ēḻulagamum vāngip ponvayiṟṟil peydu paṇḍu ōr ālilaip paḷḷi koṇḍavan pānmadikkidar tīrttavan oṇṭhiṟal avuṇan urattugir vaittavan oḷḷeyiṟṟodu tiṇ tiṟal ariāyavan tiruvēngadam adai nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

eṇ disaigaḷum – eight directions; ēḻu ulagamum – seven worlds; paṇḍu – during mahāpraḷayam (great deluge); vāngi – consumed; pon – praiseworthy; vayiṟṟil – in (his) divine stomach; peydu – placed; ōr Al ilai – on a banyan leaf; paḷḷi koṇḍavan – being the one who was mercifully resting; pāl – (shining) like milk; madikku – occurred for the moon; idar – decay; tīrttavan – one who eliminated; oṇ tiṟal – very strong; avuṇan – hiraṇya, the demon, his; urattu – in the chest; ugir vaittavan – being the one who placed the divine nail and tore; oḷ – radiant; eyiṟṟodu – with teeth; tiṇ – firm; tiṟal – having strength; ariyāy avan – eternal abode of the one who appeared in the form of narasimha; tiruvēngadam – tirumalā; adai nenjamē – Oh mind! Reach there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is the one who consumed eight directions and seven worlds during mahāpraḷayam and placed them in his praiseworthy stomach and was mercifully resting on a banyan leaf; he eliminated the decay occurred for the milk like moon; having appeared in the form of narasimha who is having radiant teeth and firm strength, he placed the divine nail and tore the chest of hiraṇya, the very strong demon; Oh mind! Reach tiruvēngadam which is the abode of such sarvēśvaran.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*eṇ disaigaḷum …* – Previously, taking the seven worlds which are having eight directions, and placing them in his praiseworthy stomach, mercifully resting on a freshly sprouted banyan leaf; one who is having such agaditagatanā sāmartyam (ability to unite those aspects which are not possible to be united).

*pāl madikku idar tīrttavan* – pāl madi – candran – moon; when he got into a trouble which was about to destroy his existence, emperumān was the one who saved him from getting destroyed.

*oṇ tiṟal …* – One who placed his divine nail on the chest of hiraṇya, who had great strength; one who became narasimha with beautiful divine teeth and firm strength.

The one who helped prahlāda who recited tirumantram (aśtākśaram), has arrived in tirumalā to eliminate the existence in samsāra of those who recite his divine names. Oh mind! Try to reach such tirumalā.

## 1.8.7. Parum nir

*pārum nīr eri kāṟṟinōdu āgāsamum ivai āyinān pērum āyiram pēsa ninṟa piṟappili perugum idam kārum vār pani nīḷ visumbidaic cōrumāmugil tōytara sērum vār poḻil sūḻ eḻil tiruvēngadam adai nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pārum – earth; nīr – water; eri – fire; kāṟṟinōdu – with air; āgāyamum – ether; ivai – these five elements; āyinān – one who remains as; āyiram pērum – thousand divine names; pēsa – to recite and surrender; ninṟa – being the one who is eternally residing; piṟappili – sarvēśvaran who is without a birth; perugum – growing; idam – abode is; kārum – clouds; vār pani – lot of mist; nīḷ visumbu idai – in the great sky; sōrum – to pour; māmugil – huge clouds; tōy tara – to rest; sēru – matching; vār – lengthy; poḻil – by garden; sūḻ – being surrounded; eḻil – beautiful; tiruvēngadam – tirumalā; adai nenjamē – Oh mind! Reach there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who is without a birth, who remains as the five elements namely earth, water, fire, air and ether, is eternally residing \[for devotees\] to recite the thousand names and to surrender unto him; the beautiful tirumalā is the abode where he grows, where clouds and lot of mist are pouring in the great sky and which is surrounded by lengthy gardens where clouds can rest. Oh mind! Reach there.

*pār …* – Since āḻvār speaks about the panca bhūtams (five elements), he implies bhagavān’s universal form where he has the entire universe as his form. One who stands to be surrendered to by everyone, by reciting his divine names with the body he has bestowed.

*piṟappili perugum idam* – The abode of sarvēśvaran who is not bound by karma, distinguished from everyone else, not limited to the universal form.

*kār …* – As the clouds and lot of mist are pouring in the sky, the lengthy gardens are able to have the huge clouds resting on them; tiruvēngadam being surrounded by such gardens. Alternative explanation – the clouds which have abundant water are pouring in the sky.

When recited as *sērum,* it means “reaching to touch”.  Being surrounded by such beautiful gardens which are touched by the clouds. kārum – growing. vār – abundance.

## 1.8.8. Ambaram anal

*ambaram anal kāl nilam salamāgi ninṟa amarar kōn vambulām alar mēl mali mada mangai tan koḻunan avan kombin anna idai madak kuṟa mādar nīḷ idaṇandoṟum sembunam avai kāval koḷ tiruvēngadam adai nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ambaram – ether; anal – fire; kāl – air; nilam – earth; salam – water, these five elements; āgi ninṟa – one who remained as; amarar – for nityasūris; kōn – being the lord; vambu – fragrance; ulām – blowing; malar mēl – on the lotus flower; mali – remaining firm; madam – being full with the quality of humility; mangai than – for periya pirātti; koḻunan avan – sarvēśvaran, who is the divine consort, where he eternally resides; kombu anna – like a creeper; idai – waist; madam – having humility; kuṟa mādar – the women of the hilly region; nīḷ – tall; idaṇamdoṟum – from every watch-tower; sem – reddish; punam avai – dry lands; kāval koḷ – protecting; tiruvēngadam – tirumalā; adai nenjamē – Oh mind! Reach there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being the five elements namely ether, fire, air, earth and water, being the lord of nityasūris, being the divine consort of periya pirātti who remains firmly on the fragrant lotus flower and who is full with the quality of humility, sarvēśvaran eternally resides in tirumalā where the humble women of the hilly region who have creeper like waist, remain in every watch tower and protect the reddish dry lands. Oh mind! Reach there.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*ambaram …* – āḻvār is speaking about emperumān having the universe as his body.

*amararkōn* – With this, emperumān having a distinguished form and being the lord of nityasūris who are devoid of any blemish, is explained.

*vambulā* – āḻvār is speaking about emperumān and pirātti granting their divine audience to nityasūris, in paramapadam. One who is very dear to the periya pirāttiyār who has the ever-fresh lotus flower as her residence.

*kombu …* – The women of hilly region who have creeper like waist and noble qualities. They stay in the tall watch-towers.

*sem punam …* – Since it is dry land, sem implies the reddish colour which is the natural aspect of this land. tirumalā where the grains will become ripe and fall down and they need to be protected from parrots and pigeons.

## 1.8.9. Pesumin tirunamam

*pēsumin tirunāmam etteḻuttum solli ninṟu, pinnarum pēsuvār tammai uyya vāngip piṟappaṟukkum pirān idam vāsa mā malar nāṟuvār poḻil sūḻ tarum ulagukkellām tēsamāyt tigaḻum malait tiruvēngadam adai nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pēsum – recited (by all); in – sweet (for the tongue); tirunāmam – divine name; ettu eḻuttum – the eight divine syllables; solli ninṟu – reciting once; pinnarum – further; pēsuvār tammai – those who keep reciting; uyya – to be uplifted; vāngi – accepted; piṟappu – (their) connection in this samsāram; aṟukkum – one who mercifully eliminates; pirān – the act of the great benefactor; idam – abode is; vāsam – fragrant; mā – best; malar – flowers; nāṟu – spreading the fragrance; vār – vast; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ tarum – being surrounded; ulagukku ellām – for all worlds; tēsamāy – giving radiance; tigaḻum – shining; malai – hill; tiruvēngadam – tirumalā; adai nenjamē – Oh mind! Reach there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran accepts those who recite the divine name which is recited by all and is containing eight divine syllables, once and repeat them further, to have them uplifted after eliminating their connection with samsāram; the divine abode of such great benefactor is tirumalā, the hill which is surrounded by  vast gardens which have fragrant, best flowers and which is shining to cause radiance to all worlds. Oh mind! Reach there.

*pēsum in …* – āḻvār is saying “*pēsuvār tammai uyya vāngip piṟappaṟukkum pirānidam – pēsumin tirunāmam etteḻuttum solli ninṟu*” these as parōpadēśam (instruction to others) and is saying “*vāsa mā malar nāṟuvār poḻil sūḻ tarum ulagukkellām tēsamāyt tigaḻum malait tiruvēngadam adai nenjamē!*” as svagatam (for self). ōr, it is said that he is saying this (second part) towards his divine heart.

*pēsum in …* – One need not earn qualification to recite the name of one’s mother; similarly reciting the sweet, divine name which has eight syllables and is recited by everyone when they get into trouble.

Instead of stopping  after being satisfied with just one recital ,

*pinnarum* – reciting again. For those who recite the divine name with their mouth, he will ensure that their existence is not affected, by accepting to uplift them and further eliminating their connection with samsāram which is a hurdle for them. The abode of such benefactor. It is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/07/thiruvaimozhi-9-3-8-inrip-poga/) “*ākkai pugāmai uyyak koḷvān ninṟa vēngadam*” (will make the ātmās not enter bodies of dēva (celestial) etc which are attached with acit, to be not seen separately; such emperumān who enslaves and uplifts everyone, is standing to act \[as necessary\] in tirumalā).

*vāsam …* – Being surrounded by the vast garden which is having the beautiful fragrance of the flowers.

*ulagukku ellām tēsamāyt tigaḻum malai* – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/07/thiruvaimozhi-9-3-8-inrip-poga/) “*nīḷ nilattuḷḷadu*” (is present in this praiseworthy earth), since the greatness of paramapadam is present for tirumalā, this samsāram remains desirable. It is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-10-1-ulagam-unda/) “*tiladam ulkagukkāy*” (like a tilak which is applied on the forehead in the form of ūrdvapuṇḍram (upward-pointing symbol) for the whole world). A tamiḻ poet has also sung “*nilamagaḷ than neṟṟikkut tiladamāy ninṟa*” (The abode which remains as the tilak for the forehead of mother earth).

## 1.8.10. Sengayal tilaikkum

*sengayal tiḷaikkum sunait tiruvēngadattu uṟai selvanai mangaiyar talaivan kali kanṟi vaṇ tamiḻc cenjol mālaigal sangaiyinṟit tarittu uraikka vallārgaḷ tanjamadāgavē vangamā kadalvaiyam kāvalarāgi vānulagāḷvarē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem – reddish (due to youth); kayal – fish; tiḷaikkum – joyfully living; sunai – having ponds; tiruvēngadattu – in tirumalā; uṟai – eternally residing; selvanai – on śriya:pati (divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi); mangaiyar – for the people of tirumangai region; talaivan – being the king; kali kanṟi – āḻvār who rid the defects of kali; vaṇ – beautiful; tamiḻ – with tamiḻ language; sol – mercifully sang; sem – honest; mālaigaḷ – garland of words; darittu – holding in the heart; uraikka vallārgaḷ – those who can recite; tanjamadāga – firmly; vangam – filled with ships; mā – vast; kadal – surrounded by ocean; vaiyam – for earth; kāvalar āgi – being the protector; vān ulagu – paramapadam; āḷvar – will get to rule; sangai inṟi – Remain without a doubt

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

āḻvār who rid the defects of kali, being the king of the people of tirumangai region, mercifully sang the garland of honest words in the beautiful tamiḻ language on śriya:pati who is eternally residing in tirumalā which is having ponds where reddish fish are joyfully living. Those who can firmly hold this decad in the heart and recite it will be the protector for earth which is surrounded by vast ocean which is filled with ships and will get to rule paramapadam as well. Remain without a doubt on this principle.

*sem kayal …* – Just as muktātmās (liberated souls) will always remain twenty five years old and remain joyful enjoying bhagavān, fish which are reddish due to their radiant youth will remain joyful with each other in the ponds of tirumalā where śriya:pati is eternally residing. On such śriya:pati.

*mangaiyar talaivan …* – āḻvār who is the leader of tirumangai region, mercifully sang this decad in the form of a garland in beautiful tamiḻ with honest words. Those who can firmly hold and recite this decad, will certainly be the protector of the earth which is surrounded by ocean, and will subsequently have nityavibhūti (paramapadam) also at their disposal.

Will this occur?

*sangai inṟi* – No need to doubt this principle.
