## 1.9 Taye tandai

## 1.9.1. Taye tandai

*tāyē tandai enṟum tāramē kiḷai makkaḷ enṟum nōyē pattoḻindēn unnaik kāṇbadōr āsaiyināl vēyēy pūmboḻil sūḻ viraiyār tiruvēngadavā! nāyēn vandadaindēn nalgi āḷ ennaik koṇḍaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēy – bamboos; ēy – being dense; pū – blossomed; virai Ar – very fragrant; poḻil sūḻ – surrounded by garden; tiruvēngadavā – oh one who is identified by śrī vēnkatādri!; tāyē enṟum – (one who is not the real mother) as mother; tandai enṟum – (one who is not the real father) as father; tāramē enṟum – (one who is not the real wife) as wife; kiḷaiyē enṟum – (those who are not real relatives) as relatives; makkaḷē enṟum – (those who are not real children) as children; nōy pattu oḻindēn – experienced disaster; nāyēn – I who am very lowly as a dog; unnai – your highness who are the natural relative; kāṇbadu – to see; ōr āsaiyināl – with the desire; vandu – arriving at your highness’ divine feet; adaindēn – I surrendered; ennai – I who am a servitor; nalgi – showing mercy; āḷ koṇḍa aruḷ – kindly accept my service

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is identified by śrī vēnkatādri which is surrounded by very fragrant and blossomed garden having dense bamboos! I considered unreal ones as mother, father, wife, relatives and children and experienced disaster; I who am very lowly as a dog, with the desire to see your highness who are the natural relative, arrived at your highness’ divine feet and surrendered; Showing mercy, kindly accept the service of mine, a servitor.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*tāyē …* – āḻvār says – As said in subhāla upaniśat 6 “*mātā pitā bhrātā*” (Mother, father, brother), śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 58.31 “*bhrātā bhartā ca*” (brother, lord etc) and ahirbudnya samhitā 20 “*ēkaika pala lābhāya*” (bhagavān kēśava is present to bestow all results given by various relatives), while your highness remains as all types of relatives, being relatives due to a particular reason (karma), until there is benefit from him, the relatives will get his help and when he needs some help, they will move away and even harm him. I thought of such relatives as real ones and experienced disaster. Alternative explanation – considering the children and friends as mother, father and wife.

*nōyē pattu* – Since they accept help from him whenever possible and when they have to help him, they will cause harm and go away from him. If we think about such persons as relatives, when they don’t fulfil their responsibility as relatives, that will only result in sorrow. He thinks about them as relatives, but they don’t reciprocate that. They will themselves lead to sorrow, instead of having to do something to cause sorrow.

*pattoḻindēn* – Experienced. Alternative explanation \[*pattu oḻindēn*\] – experienced the suffering and gave up those relatives. To know that bhagavān’s qualities are desirable, one needs the instructions of a true ācārya and śāstram; but to know that samsāram is to be given up, real life experience is sufficient. These practical experience remained the teacher here.

*unnaik kāṇbadu ōr āsaiyināl* – As I was bewildered in considering these incidental relatives as real relatives, I expected them to help when in need but they did not help; hence that aspect \[of them abandoning us\] caused the desire in me to see you who are the natural relative.

*vēy …* – Unlike those who abandoned me when help is needed for me after accepting my help when it was available, you remained away all along but favoured me when help was needed. The abode where bamboos are densely present.

*pūm poḻil …* – It appears that the entity who is praised in cāndōjña upaniśat as “*sarva ganda:*” (the origin of all fragrance), is present inside; I arrived here tracing such fragrance.

*vēngadavā* – His relationship and desire \[towards us\] is visible to our eyes. emperumān, not being bound by karma, who gives his divine audience to nityasūris in paramapadam, arrived in this samsāram where the cētanas are suffering for their protection just as a mother would jump into the well to save a child who fell into that well.

*nāyēn* – If we look at my previous conduct, I am neither qualified to stay outside (away from you) nor to exist for your highness. If I go out, they will pelt stones at me and if I enter your abode, it will become impure just as anything which contacts a dog becomes impure.

*vandu adaindēn* – Due to ananyagatitvam (not having any other refuge), I came and surrendered unto your divine feet.

emperumān asks “If you caused your own lowliness, what do you expect me to do?” āḻvār replies,

*nalgi* – A prince would have liking towards a lowly dog \[similarly, you accept me desirously\].

*āḷ ennaik koṇḍu aruḷē* – Considering yourself as all types of relatives, you should accept all kinds of services from me as performed by nityasūris and as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25  “*bhavāmstu saha vaidēhyā girisānuśu ramsyatē –* ***aham sarvam kariśyāmi*** *jāgrata svapataścatē*” (While you enjoy with sītā in the foothills of the mountain, I will serve you both in all the ways whether you are sleeping or awake).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.2. Maney kan madavar

*mānēykaṇ madavār mayakkil pattu mānilattu nānē nānāvida naragam pugum pāvam seydēn tēnēy pūmpoḻil sūḻ tiruvēngada māmalai en ānāy! vandadaindēn adiyēnai ātkoṇḍaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēn – beetles; ēy – filled; pū – having flowers; poḻil – by garden; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruvēngada mā malai – being the one who is having tirumalā as abode; en ānāy – oh one who forbears my faults just as an elephant would do!; mān ēy – like that of a deer; kaṇ – eyes; madavār – women who are having humility as well, their; mayakkil – in their glance; pattu – being captivated; mā nilattu – in the vast earth; nānāvida naragam – in many types of narakam (hell); pugum – to enter; pāvam – sin; nānē – I have individually; seydēn – having performed; vandu – came; adaindēn – I held your highness’ divine feet as refuge; adiyēnai – I, the servitor; āḷ koṇḍu aruḷē – Kindly accept my service

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who forbears my faults just as an elephant would do and is having tirumalā as abode, which is surrounded by garden having flowers filled with beetles! Being captivated in the glance of the eyes of humble women, which resemble eyes of deer, I have individually performed sin to enter many types of hell in the vast earth. I have come and am holding your highness’ divine feet as refuge; kindly accept service of mine, the servitor.

*mānēy …* – Having glance which resembles that of a deer. Though the heart is filled with poison, they will glance at the man as if they cannot survive without him. He won’t have the ability to analyse and understand their heart; though they are glancing at him with selfish purpose, he will think that they are looking at him with pure love and become captivated in them.

*madavār* – In shyness, fear and humility, these women have humility. By this, it is implied that, due to having this one good quality, they consider themselves to be at par with bhagavān who has all auspicious qualities.

*mā nilattil nānā vida naragam nānē pugum pāvam seydēn* – There is no boundary to the number of cētanas in this world; to make them experience the results of their sins, in each world, there will be many hellish regions; I have individually performed sin to remain in all of those hellish regions, without any opportunity for others. Now, if he has to send other cētanas to hellish regions and conduct the worlds, he needs to create new such places. In śrī rāmāyaṇam, kaikēyi was asked “Which hell will you enter?” As nampiḷḷai was reading that section, nampiḷḷai asked “Perhaps, it is implied that the existing hellish regions are not sufficient for her \[mistake of banishing śrī rāma to the forest\]” nanjīyar mercifully said “You have beautifully explained”.

*tēn …* – tēn also implies beetles \[in addition to honey\].

*en ānāy* – Elephant usually lives in a hill. It is sufficient if anything living in that hill where the elephant is present, is shown. Elephants usually ignore even great mistakes done by others and are always pleasing to the eyes \[similar to bhagavān\].

*vandu …* – I who said “*nānā vida naragam pugum pāvam seydēn*” have arrived now. You should kindly accept me in kainkaryam which is fully blissful unlike the sorrow in the hellish experience. Just as a person who is very lusty will desire the embrace of woman, kainkaryam (service) is for a śēśabhūta (servitor). śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.32 “*ramamāṇā:*” (lived delightfully in the forest).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.3. Konren palluyirai

*konṟēn palluyiraik kuṟikkōḷ onṟilāmaiyināl enṟēnum irandārkku inidāga uraittaṟiyēn kunṟēy mēgamadir kuḷir māmalai vēngadavā! anṟē vandadaindēn adiyēnai ātkoṇḍaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kunṟu – on the peaks; ēy – resting; mēgam – clouds; adir – making loud noise; kuḷir – being cool; mā – great; malai vēngadavā – oh one who has śrī vēnkatācalam as your identity!; kuṟikkōḷ – knowledge such as discrimination between body and self; onṟu – none; ilāmaiyināl – due to not having; pal uyirai – many creatures; konṟēn – tormented; irandārkku – for those who begged; inidāga – with good words; enṟēnum – ever; uraittaṟiyēn – I, the servitor, who did not say; anṟē – right then; vandu adaindēn – I came and surrendered; adiyēnai At koṇḍu aruḷ – kindly accept my service

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who has the great, cool śrī vēnkatācalam which has clouds resting on the peaks making loud noise, as your identity! I tormented many creatures due to not having any knowledge such as discrimination between body and self; I, the servitor, never said any good words to those who begged; right then, I came and surrendered; kindly accept my service.

*konṟēn* – I will not leave him after checking his wallet; had he carried some wealth, I will chase him, grab his wealth and kill him too; if he was empty handed, I will kill him saying “What will I take along with me to my dear woman, if you come empty handed like this?”

*pal uyirai* – I never repented; I do not qualify to perform atonement too. Had I atoned, I would have stopped with one or two murders; only then, one qualifies to atone.

When asked “Back then, why did you, who are identifying these as faults, do those killings?” āḻvār says,

*kuṟikkōḷ onṟu ilāmaiyināl* – Because I did not know that there is something \[self\] beyond the body; if I engaged in sinful acts, I cannot escape punishments in hell. Alternative explanation – I did not know that there is an owner for this self; he is very kind-hearted towards all; this act of mine will not be bearable for him. Due to not analysing about bhagavān and not analysing about the position of self. Even if one of these aspects is known, one will not engage in harming others.

When asked “When you earned wealth for your woman, if you harmed others without thinking about anything, subsequently you would have earned wealth, married that woman and would have enjoyed together. At that time, when you saw a suffering person, did you feel pity for such person?” āḻvār says,

*enṟēnum …* – I never gave anything to anyone – not even for the charity to be done during kārtigai month, or to help him or due to my pride \[to acquire fame\]. Here āḻvār is not saying “I did not give” but saying “Even such thought of helping others did not come across in my mind”.

*inidāga …* – When some one comes begging, if he was told “I am unable to give anything to your satisfaction”, he would leave with satisfaction thinking “What can he do? He is not giving due to his inability”; unlike that I will refuse him in such a way that he will remain hurt forever thinking “Instead of just suffering with my poverty, why did I come and get scolded by this person?”

*kunṟēy mēgam adir* – Cloud – on the peak; or like a peak. When the cloud has absorbed a lot of water, it will first rest somewhere and then only pour down as rain \[hence it is resting on the peak\].

*adir* – The noise it makes resembles the sweet words of those who offer something even when not begged.

*anṟē vandu adaindēn* – Instead of coming there after repenting or after atoning for the sins, I came and surrendered without even washing the hands after killing. You should mercifully accept my service looking at my true nature instead of looking at my act.

When asked “If we look at your previous acts, you have constantly harmed others; now you are speaking as if you have performed sādanānuśtānam (upāsanam etc)” He is speaking, looking at bhagavān only and not him. If we look at him, he is as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.28 “*ari: prāṇān parityajya*” (One has to give up lives, to protect even an enemy who was given refuge). Here it is not said “*prāṇānapi*” (even lives) since giving up life is not considered as such a great act. āḻvār is the one who thinks “Is protecting a person who comes and surrenders at his divine feet, without looking at the previous enmity, a great quality, looking at emperumān’s greatness?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.4. Kulandan ettanaiyum

*kulandān ettanaiyum piṟandē iṟandu eyttoḻindēn nalandān onṟumilēn nalladōr aṟam seydumilēn nilam tōy nīḷmugilsēr neṟiyār tiruvēngadavā! alandēn vandadaindēn adiyēnai ātkoṇḍaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nilam – on earth; tōy – resting; nīḷ mugil – huge clouds; sēr – roaming; neṟi – path; Ar – having; tiruvēngadavā – Oh leader of śrī vēnkatādri!; ettanai kulamum – In every clan; piṟandu iṟandu – taking birth and dying; eyttu oḻindēn – having weakened; oru nalamum ilēn – not having any goodness; nalladu – having goodness (in getting the result); ōr aṟamum – performance of any sādanam (means); seydilēn – not having done; alandēn – I, the servitor, who suffered (in every birth); vandu adaindēn – I came and surrendered; adiyēnai At koṇḍu aruḷ – kindly accept my service

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh leader of śrī vēnkatādri which is having the path where huge clouds which are resting on earth, are roaming! Taking birth in every clan and dying, having weakened, not having any goodness, not having performed any good sādanam (means), I, the servitor, who suffered in every birth, came and surrendered unto you; kindly accept my service.

*kulam tān …* – I took birth in every clan and roamed. There is no end to my birth under anulōma (born as the child of a woman of lower varṇa and man of higher varṇa) and pratilōma (born as the child of a woman of higher varṇa and man of lower varṇa) situations. Having born in every clan and subsequently dying, I have weakened so much that I cannot take any more birth though I still have the karma to take birth.

*nalam tān onṟum ilēn* – Though I was born and dead in many births, I did not acquire any good deed or knowledge which is the result of such good deed.

*nalladu ōr aṟam seydum ilēn* – When asked “Though there is no good deed which will reap good results now, are you engaging in any sādanam now to reap good results in future?” āḻvār says “Even now, I am not engaging in any sādanam which will reap good results in future”.

*nilam …* – The huge clouds which were resting on the earth would leave their traces visibly. The clouds which have absorbed water fully, due to the weight of the water absorbed, will not be able to move swiftly and hence will move slowly, leaving some droplets and leaving the trace of their movement.

*alandēn vandu adaindēn* – I suffered in the lengthy sequence of births.

*adiyēnai* – You should engage me in your service where I don’t have to fear for next birth.

## 1.9.5. Eppavam palavum

*eppāvam palavum ivaiyē seydu iḷaittoḻindēn tuppā! ninnadiyē todarndēttavum kiṟkinṟilēn seppār tiṇvarai sūḻ tiruvēngada māmalai en appā! vandadaindēn adiyēnai ātkoṇḍaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

seppu Ar – like copper which is protective; tiṇ – firm; varai – by hills; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruvēngada mā malai – being the one who is having tirumalā as his abode; en – for followers like me; appā – Oh benefactor!; tuppā – Oh one who is capable!; eppāvam palavum ivaiyē – these many types of sins; seydu – performed; iḷaittoḻindēn – became sorrowful (on hearing about the results of such sins); nin adi – your highness’ divine feet; tudarndu – followed; ēttavum – to surrender with bhakti; kiṟkinṟilēn – being incapable; vandu adaindēn – I came and surrendered; adiyēnai At koṇḍu aruḷ – kindly accept my service

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh benefactor for followers like me who is having tirumalā surrounded by firm hills which are protective like copper, as your abode! Oh one who is capable! Having performed these many types of sins, I became sorrowful and have become incapable to follow and surrender unto your highness’ divine feet; \[still\] I have come and surrendered; kindly accept my service.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*eppāvam …* – After performing five types of sins such as atipātakam, upapātakam, mahāpātakam etc, I felt sorrowful thinking about the results of those sins. emperumān says – though one engages in such great sins, in between due to a good deed, if you acquired taste towards me, you could remain faithful as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.31](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-31/) “*na mē bhakta: praṇaśyati*” (my devotee never perishes). It is said in śāstram that even if one has committed great sins, if he acquired puruśōttama vidyā, he will be freed from such sins.

*tuppā* – Oh one who has the ability to eliminate such sins of those who surrender unto you and protect them.

*nin adiyē* – I am incapable to firmly surrender unto your divine feet, with devotion.

*seppār …* – Oh natural relative who is having tirumalā which is surrounded by firm hills which act like a fort around it, as your abode!

*adiyēnai* – You should engage me in kainkaryam based on my natural relationship with you instead of engaging me according to my sins.

## 1.9.6. Mannay nir

*maṇṇāy nīr eri kāl manjulāvum āgāsamumām puṇṇār ākkai tannuḷ pulambit taḷarndu eyttoḻindēn viṇṇār neeḷ sigara viraiyār tiruvēngadavā! aṇṇā! vandadaindēn adiyēnai ātkoṇḍaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇ – sky; Ar – to touch; nīḷ – tall; sigaram – peaks; virai – fragrance; Ar – having; tiruvēngadavā – Oh one who has tirumalā as your abode!; aṇṇā – Oh one has all types of relationships!; maṇṇāy – being earth; nīrāy – being water; eriyāy – being fire; kālāy – being air; manju – clouds; ulāvum – roaming; ākāsamumām – being sky, hence, being made of the five great elements; puṇ Ar – resembling a wound; ākkai tannuḷ – (being held captive) in the body; pulambi – calling out; taḷarndu – becoming weakened; eyttu oḻindēn – I who have become very tired; vandu adaindēn – I came and surrendered; adiyēnai At koṇḍu aruḷ – kindly accept my service

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who has tirumalā which has tall peaks reaching sky and fragrance, as your abode! Oh one has all types of relationships! Being held captive in the body which is made of five great elements namely earth, water, fire, air and sky which has clouds roaming in it, resembling a wound, I called out and became weakened. I who have become very tired, came and surrendered. Kindly accept my service.

*maṇṇāy* … – Just as a prince who becomes \[accidentally\] associated with a hunter \[and raised by him\], starts thinking himself to be a hunter, ātmā who is eternal, identified by knowledge and bliss, singular and subordinate to īśvara, became united with matter (body) due to karma. ātmā which is singular in nature, became captivated in body which keeps changing.

*puṇ Ar ākkai* … – Placed in the body as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.1.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/05/thiruvaimozhi-5-1-5-kanna-piranai/) “*puṇṇai maṟaiya varindu*” (concealing the external faults, and surrounding me forever). Wise people will identify this body as a wound as said in “*śarīram vraṇavat paśyēt*” (let him see the body as a wound). Having entered the body and becoming captivated in it, subsequently remained there and called out, and became weak being unable to even do that, finally became very tired.

*viṇ Ar …* – Having fragrant tirumalā which is having huge peaks which have grown so tall to reach and fill the sky, to be praised by nityasūris as in śrīvaikuṇṭam, as his abode and standing there.

*aṇṇā* – Previously he said “*appā*” (father); here he is saying “*aṇṇā*” (elder brother); he considers that emperumān to be all types of relationships which he abandoned saying in [periya tirumoḻi 1.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/06/periya-thirumozhi-1-9-1/) “*tāyē tandai enṟum tāramē kiḷai makkaḷ enṟum*” (I considered unreal ones as mother, father, wife, relatives and children and experienced disaster).

*adiyēnai* – When the worthless body is eliminated, my relationship with you is similar to that of nityasūris with you; hence, you should accept service from me, just as you accept from them.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.7. Teriyen palaganay

*teriyēn pālaganāyp pala tīmaigaḷ seydumittēn periyēn āyina pin pirarkkē uḻaittu ēḻaiy ānēn kari sēr pūmpoḻil sūḻ kanamāmalai vēngadavā! ariyē! vandadaindēn adiyēnai ātkoṇḍaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kari – elephants; sēr – present in abundance; pū – filled with flowers; poḻil – by garden; sūḻ – surrounded; kanam – firm; mā malai – huge mountain; vēngadavā – Oh one who is having tirumalā as your residence!; ariyē – Oh lion!; pālaganāy – while being a child; teiryēn – being ignorant; pala tīmaigaḷ – (further) many cruel acts; seydumittēn – having performed; periyēn āyina pin – after becoming a youth; piṟarkkē – needed for others; uḻaittu – searched and gave; ēḻai ānēn – I, the servitor, lost my ability (now); vandu adaindēn – I came and surrendered; adiyēnai At koṇḍu aruḷ – kindly accept my service

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is having tirumalā which is a firm, huge mountain surrounded by garden filled with flowers and having abundant elephants, as your residence! Oh lion! While being a child, I was ignorant and performed many cruel acts; after becoming a youth, I, the servitor, searched what is needed for others and gave them, and have lost my ability; I came and surrendered; kindly accept my service.

*teriyēn …* – *pālaganāy – teriyēn* – For some time, I was an infant and remained without knowing what is to be done and what is not to be done. After acquiring a little bit of knowledge, I roamed around doing all evil deeds as desired.

*periyēn …* – After becoming a youth, when I saw a good flower, instead of decorating my head with it, being subservient to women, I searched what is needed for them, became sorrowful, lost my ability and became a laughable stock.

*kari …* – Oh one who is having the firm tirumalā which is surrounded by garden which is well blossomed and where elephants gather for their sport, as residence!

*ariyē* – Oh one who has the ability to remain victorious against everyone, to eliminate my hurdles!

*ātkoṇḍaruḷē* – Instead of letting me work for others, you should kindly accept my kainkaryam in the apt aspects.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.8. Norren palpiravi

*nōṟṟēn palpiṟavi unnaik kāṇbadōr āsaiyināl ēṟṟēn ippiṟappē idar uṟṟanan emperumān! kōltēn pāyndoḻugum kuḷirsōlai sūḻ vēngadavā! āṟṟēn vandadaindēn adiyēnai ātkoṇḍaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōl – from poles; tēn – honey; pāyndu – overflowing; oḻugum – flooding; kuḷir – cool; sōlai sūḻ – surrounded by gardens; vēngadavā – Oh one who is having tirumalā as residence!; em – for us, devotees; perumān – Oh great benefactor!; pal piṟavi – to take many births; nōṟṟēn – I, the servitor, who performed sādanānuśtānam (other upāyams such as bhakti yōgam); ēṟṟēn – I became qualified (to receive your highness’ merciful glance); (due to that); unnai – your highness; kāṇbadu – to see; ōr – a; āsaiyināl – with the desire; ippiṟappē – in this birth itself; idar uṟṟanan – I became worried; āṟṟēn – being unable to tolerate (the repetitive births); vandu adaindēn – I came and surrendered; adiyēnai At koṇḍu aruḷ – kindly accept my service

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is having tirumalā which is surrounded by cool gardens which are flooded with overflowing honey from poles, as residence! Oh great benefactor for us, devotees! I, the servitor, who performed sādanānuśtānam, to be born in many births, became qualified to receive your merciful glance. With the desire to see your highness in this birth itself, I became worried. Being unable to tolerate the repetitive births, I came and surrendered; kindly accept my service.

*nōṟṟēn pal piṟavi* – I performed sādanānuśtānam in many births. I pursued these upāyams, to cause many births for me. While taking births in this manner, in between, an incidental good deed occurred; due to that I acquired the desire to see you, and became qualified to remain for your highness.

When asked “How did you know that you have become qualified?” āḻvār says,

*ippiṟappē idar uṟṟanan* – In this birth itself, I felt in my heart that my situation is very bad.

*kōl tēn …* – The honey which was stored in poles, started overflowing and flooded to cause coolness in the gardens; oh one who is having tirumalā which is surrounded by such cool gardens, as residence!

*āṟṟēn* – I came and surrendered at your divine feet, being unable tolerate the many births.

*adiyēnai …* – Why should I even have to pray saying “Please grant me kainkaryam which matches my true nature?” to you who cannot tolerate my suffering from the beginning? I am unable to bear the suffering; you stand waiting for the time when I acquire such unbearability!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.9. Parrel onrumilen

*paṟṟēl onṟumilēn pāvamē seydu pāviyānēn maṟṟēl onṟariyēn māyanē! engaḷ mādavanē! kaltēn pāyndoḻugum kamalac cunaivēngadavā! aṟṟēn vandadaindēn adiyēnai ātkoṇḍaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māyanē – Oh one who has amazing qualities and activities!; engaḷ – (makes you tolerate) our (mistakes); mādavanē – Oh one who is dear to periya pirātti!; kal tēn – honey placed in the cave in mountain; pāyndu oḻugum – greatly flooding; kamalam – filled with lotus flowers; sunai – having waterfalls; vēngadavā – Oh eternal resident of tirumalā!; onṟu paṟṟu – any foundation (such as good deed); ilēn – not having; pāvamē seydu – performing sins only (due to that); pāviyānēn – being sinner; maṟṟu – other upāyams; onṟum – even a little bit; aṟiyēn – I, the servitor, who do not know; aṟṟēn – became completely existing for your highness; vandu adaindēn – I came and surrendered; adiyēnai At koṇḍu aruḷ – kindly accept my service

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who has amazing qualities and activities! Oh one who is dear to our periya pirātti! Oh eternal resident of tirumalā which is having waterfalls filled with lotus flowers where honey placed in the mountain caves are greatly flooding! Not having any foundation, being a sinner who is performing sins only, not knowing even a little bit in any other upāyams, I, the servitor, became completely existing for your highness. I came and surrendered; kindly accept my service.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*paṟṟēl onṟum ilēn* – For ātmā who ran away from bhagavān severing the connection, there is no good deed matching the result of attaining bhagavān. Due to that, performing sins only, I became identified with sins only rather than being identified by jñānam (knowledge), ānandam (bliss) etc.

*maṟṟēl onṟaṟiyēn* – I don’t have knowledge about upāyams which lead to bhagavān. ahirbudnya samhitā 37.30 and 37.31 “*aham asmi aparādānām ālaya: …*” (“I am the abode of all faults; I have no means \[to protect myself\]. I have no refuge other than you. Let you be my means” – the thought with this prayer is called śaraṇāgati. Let this be done towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/))

*māyanē* – Oh one who has amazing abilities to protect even such persons!

*engaḷ mādavanē* – Oh one who is the refuge for all due to having pirātti who will make you forgive the mistakes of even such persons!

*kal tēn …* – As the honey which was placed in the caves will overflow, ooze out into the ponds and the lotus flowers will blossom there.

*aṟṟēn* – I have become settled at your divine feet.

*adiyēnai āḷ koṇḍu aruḷē* – I told that I have no other refuge; you who are my refuge, are dear laksmīpati (consort of śrī mahālakśmi); thus, you should accept kainkaryam which matches my svarūpam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.10. Kannay elulagukku

*kaṇṇāy ēḻulagukku uyirāya engār vaṇṇanai viṇṇōr tām paravum poḻil vēngada vēdiyanai tiṇṇār mādangaḷ sūḻ tirumangaiyarkōn kaliyan paṇṇār pādal pattum payilvārku illai pāvangaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēḻ ulagukku – for the seven worlds; kaṇṇāy – like eyes; uyirāy – being like prāṇan (vital air); em – to give enjoyment for us, the devotees; kār – cloud like; vaṇṇan – having divine complexion; viṇṇōr tām – even nityasūris; paravum – praise; poḻil – having gardens; vēngadam – being the resident of tirumalā; vēdiyanai – on sarvēśvaran, who is spoken by vēdam; tiṇ Ar – firm; mādangaḷ sūḻ – surrounded by mansions; tirumangaiyar – for the residents of tirumangai region; kōn – the king; kaliyan – mercifully spoken by āḻvār; paṇ Ar – having tune; pattup pādalum – ten pāsurams; payilvārkku – those who learn and practice; pāvangaḷ – hurdles; illai – will be destroyed

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being the eyes for the seven worlds and the vital air, being the one who is having cloud like divine complexion to give enjoyment for us, the devotees, sarvēśvaran is the resident of tirumalā which is having gardens and is praised even by nityasūris. On such sarvēśvaran, āḻvār, the king of the residents of tirumangai region which is surrounded by firm mansions, composed these ten pāsurams having tune; those who learn and practice them, will have their hurdles destroyed.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*kaṇṇāy …* – Being the vision of all the seven worlds and being the vital air which sustains those worlds, further, having a cloud like rejuvenating form to let me enjoy him, sarvēśvaran who is praised by nityasūris who enter and remain in a corner of tirumalā just as the people of this world do, who is revealed fully by vēdam, is praised here.

*tiṇ Ar* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 124.4 “*sarvanca kuśalam gruhē*” (Everyone is safe at home).

*paṇ Ar pādal …* – Tune is abundant in these pāsurams; for those who practice these pāsurams, sins won’t come near them. All the hurdles for reaching bhagavān will run away. After āḻvār said “*pāvamē seydu pāviyānēn*” (I committed sins only and became a sinner), and after īśvaran forgave them, he won’t have any sins left. When śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān was told in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.29 “*vadyatām*” (He must be killed along with his associates), it included those who accompanied him as well; but when he was accepted by śrī rāma, they also became accepted and were spared from punishment. Similarly, if we remain āḻvār’s servitors and learn his prabandam, our  sins will also be eliminated. What is the intention of first informing his lowly conduct to īśvara and saying “I surrendered”? When we highlight the lowly conduct, that will trigger his mercy and such mercy will lead to our kainkaryam matching the true nature of the self.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10 Kannar kadal

## 1.10.1. Kannar kadal

*kaṇṇār kadal sūḻ ilangaikku iṟaivantantiṇṇāgam piḷakkac caram sela uyttāy!viṇṇōr toḻum vēngada māmalai mēyaaṇṇā! adiyēn idaraik kaḷaiyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇ Ar – Vast; kadal sūḻ – being surrounded by ocean; ilangaikku – for lankā; iṟaivan than – the leader, rāvaṇa’s; tiṇ – firm; āgam – body; piḷakka – to split \[into two\]; saram – arrows; sela – to be shot; uyttāy – the one who directed; viṇṇōr – dēvatās such as brahmā et al; toḻum – to surrender; mā – great; vēngada malai – in tirumalā; mēya – residing eternally; aṇṇā – oh one who is all types of relationship!; adiyēn – the servitor, my; idarai – sorrow; kaḷaiyāy – kindly eliminate

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

You directed the arrows to shoot them on the body of rāvaṇa, the leader of lankā which is surrounded by vast ocean, and split it. Oh one who is all types of relationship,  who is eternally residing in the great tirumalā to be surrendered by dēvatās such as brahmā et al! Kindly eliminate my sorrow.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*kaṇṇār kadal* – kaṇ – space. The ocean which is having a lot of space. The entities living in the ocean will be considered greater than those living on the land; they will have abundant space. Alternatively – the ocean is so beautiful that one cannot take one’s eyes off it. Due to having such ocean as the protective layer, lankā is well fortified, being headed by rāvaṇa, who is prideful about it.

*tiṇ āgam …* – You shot the arrows to split the strong body which effortlessly faced brahmāstram (greatest weapon) etc due to the boons of dēvatās.

*viṇṇōr …* – Those dēvatās who had lost their residences due to rāvaṇa, now come and surrender. Oh one who is having the nature to be vorśipped by brahmā et al and the natural relative who is present in tirumalā having it as residence!

*adiyēn …* – After I have realised that my presence in this world is sorrowful, you should eliminate my hurdles for your kainkaryam (service).

## 1.10.2. Ilangaip padikku

*ilangaip padikku enṟu iṟaiyāya arakkar kulam kettu avar māḷak kodippuḷ tirittāy! vilangal kudumit hiruvēngadam mēya alangal tuḷaba mudiyāy! aruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ilangaip padikku – for the city of lankā; enṟu – always; iṟaiyāya – being kings; arakkar kulam – demoniac clan; avar – those demons such as māli etc; kettu – having their state damaged; māḷa – to die; kodi – being the flag; puḷ – (climbing) periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); tirittāy – one who made to roam around; vilangal – (candra (moon) and sūrya (sun)) move away from their paths; kudumi – having tall peaks; tiruvēngadam – on tirumalā which is known as tiruvēngadam; mēya – being the one who eternally resides; tuḷabam – made with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); alangal – decorated with garland; mudiyāy – oh one who is having divine crown!; aruḷāy – You should mercifully protect me

**Перевод:**

**Thus, in the previous pāsuram and this pāsuram, by highlighting emperumān’s ability to eliminate the enemies, āḻvār prays to emperumān for the removal of his hurdles.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān made periya tiruvadi who is the flag, to roam around, to damage the state of the demons such as māli et al who are always the kings of the demoniac clan of the lankā city and kill them; he is eternally residing on tirumalā which is known as tiruvēngadam, which is having tall peak which make moon and sun move from their paths. Oh such emperumān who is having divine crown decorated with garland made with tuḷasi! You should mercifully protect me.

*ilangaip padikku …* – Here āḻvār is speaking about emperumān’s annihilation of māli et al who were living in lankā. Just as an anthill will always have evil snakes living there, lankā always remained the abode demons.

*kulam kettu avar māḷa* – Oh one who made garudāḻvār, the flag, roam around to destroy even those who hide in the under-worlds! śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 44-7 “*kīrtibhūtām patākām yō lōkē bhramayati prabhū: kinnāma durlabhām tasya*” (what is it which cannot be attained by śri rāma who let fly his flag called fame!).

*vilangal …* – \[Generally, vilangal means mountain. Here, vilangal is explained as moving away\] Since tirumalā is known as tiruvēngadam, the second meaning (moving away) is considered; not letting the moon and sun travel straight over the divine hill, it is having tall peaks which make them move away while crossing over.

*alangal …* – Since you who are decorated with garland and divine crown for the purpose of my protection, there is nothing like separately eliminating my hurdles \[it will be naturally taken care of\]. You should mercifully shower your mercy towards me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.3. Nirar kadalum

*nīrār kadalum nilanum muḻudu uṇḍu ērālam iḷandaḷirmēl tuyilendāy! sīrār tiruvēngada māmalai mēya ārāvamudē! adiyēṟku aruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīr Ar – filled with water; kadalum – ocean; nilanum – earth; muḻudu – and all other objects; uṇḍu – consumed; ēr – beautiful; iḷam – very tender; ālam taḷir mēl – on the banyan leaf; tuyil – mercifully resting; endāy – Oh one who is the protector for those who are like me!; sīr Ar – Having abundant wealth; mā – great; tiruvēngada malai – on tirumalā; mēya – residing eternally; ārā – not satiating (even if enjoyed forever); amudē – Oh one who is enjoyable like nectar!; adiyēṟku – for me, the servitor; aruḷāy – show your mercy

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is talking about emperumān being the protector of all and the controller of earth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is the protector for those who are like me, who is mercifully resting on the beautiful and very tender banyan leaf, after consuming the ocean filled with water, earth and all other objects! Oh one who is enjoyable like unsatiating nectar who is eternally residing on the great tirumalā which is having abundant wealth! Show your mercy to me, the servitor.

*nīrār …* – Ocean which has creatures which use it as their habitat, the earth which is within the oceanic boundary, and all other objects are placed within his stomach.

*ēr …* – Mercifully resting on the young sprout of the banyan flower which is beautiful enough to hold emperumān, and oh one who showed that agaditagatanā sāmartyam (ability to join contradictory aspects) and made me exist for you!

*sīrār …* – It appears that there is more wealth in tirumalā than in paramapadam.

*ārā amudē* – This amrutam (emperumān, the nectar) is not seen in svargam (heaven).

adiyēṟku – You should mercifully give this enjoyment to me who considers only this to be enjoyable.

## 1.10.4. Unday urimel

*uṇḍāy uṟimēl naṟuney amudāga koṇḍāy kuṟaḷāy nilam īradiyālē viṇṭhōy sigarat tiruvēngadam mēya aṇḍā! adiyēnukku aruḷ puriyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṟi mēl – placed on the ropes hanging down from ceiling; naṟu ney – pure ghee; amudāga – as nectar; uṇḍāy – Oh one who mercifully ate!; kuṟaḷāy – mercifully incarnating as vāmana; nilam – earth; īradiyālē – with two steps; koṇḍāy – Oh one who measured and accepted!; viṇ tōy – tall to reach up to paramapadam; sigaram – having peak; tiruvēngadam – in tirumalā; mēya – one who remains firmly; aṇḍā – Oh controller of dēvas who live inside the oval shaped world!; adiyēnukku – for me, the servitor; aruḷ puriyāy – mercifully grant the opportunity to serve you

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who mercifully ate the pure ghee which is placed on the ropes hanging down from ceiling! Oh one who measured and accepted earth with two steps mercifully incarnating as vāmana! Oh controller of dēvas who live inside the oval shaped world, firmly remaining in tirumalā having tall peak which reaches up to paramapadam! Mercifully grant me, the servitor, the opportunity to serve you.

*uṇḍāy …* – āḻvār is speaking about emperumān being unable to sustain himself without the food (ghee) which is in contact with his devotees, the act of helping them without caring for himself. You ate the pure ghee which was safely placed in the rope hanging down from the ceiling, considering it to be nectar.

*koṇḍāy …* – You who are the supreme lord, assuming the form of vāmana, accepted the vast earth with your two steps.

*viṇ tōy …* – Oh one who is firmly residing on tirumalā where the peak reaches up to paramapadam!

*aṇḍā* – Oh covherd boy! Alternatively – oh one who is the controller of those who live inside the oval shaped world!

*adiyēnukku …* – You should give me the opportunity to do my kainkaryam to you, which does not match the kainkaryam of yaśōdāp pirātti and indra.

## 1.10.5. Tunay adanudu

*tūṇāy adanūdu ariyāy vandu tōnṟi pēṇā avuṇan udalam piḷandittāy! sēṇār tiruvēngada māmalai mēya kōṇāgaṇaiyāy! kuṟikkoḷ enai nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tūṇāy – being a mere pillar; adanūdu – inside it; ariyāy – being narasimha; vandu tōnṟi – came and incarnated; pēṇā – one who did not respect; avuṇan – hiraṇya’s; udalam – chest; piḷandittāy – oh one who split it into two and threw it down!; sēṇ Ar – being very tall; mā – having great glory; tiruvēngada malai – on tirumalā; mēya – residing firmly; kōḷ – strong; nāgam – tiruvanandāḻvān (ādiśēśa); aṇaiyāy – Oh one who has as divine mattress!; enai – me, the servitor; I – your highness; kuṟikkoḷ – should consider in your divine heart

**Перевод:**

**Now, in two pāsurams, āḻvār explains how emperumān has set out to help him. āḻvār explains emperumān’s arrival on tirumalā \[in this pāsuram\] and subsequently entering āḻvār’s divine heart \[in the next pāsuram\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh narasimha, who stayed inside the pillar and incarnated by coming out of it and split the chest of hiraṇya who did not respect you, into two and threw it down! Oh one who has the strong ādiśēśa as his divine mattress, residing firmly on the very tall and greatly glorious tirumalā! Your highness should consider me, the servitor, in your divine heart.

*tūṇāy* – It cannot be said that narasimha was created and placed inside the pillar. periyāḻvār said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.6.9 “*aḷanditta tūṇai avan tatta*” (hiraṇya knocked the pillar which was measured and built by him).

*adanūdu* – Arriving inside it as a narasimha.

*pēṇā avuṇan* … – Not respecting sarvēśvaran implies tormenting his devotees. kriṣṇa himself said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 89.31 “*mama prāṇāhi pāṇḍavā:*” (āren’t pāṇḍavas my life?) One who is standing on the tall tirumalā.

*kōḷ …* – Oh one who is having the strong ādiśēśa as your divine mattress! stōtra ratnam 39 “*prakruśta vijñāna balaika dāmani*” (One who is the abode of great knowledge and strength).

*kuṟikkoḷ …* – Since prāpti (apt relationship) is the same \[for both ādiśēśa and me\], you should consider in your divine heart for me to get the same result as that of ādiśēśa.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.6. Manna immanisap

*mannā immanisap piṟaviyai nīkkit tannākkit tan in aruḷ seyyum talaivan minnār mugilsēr tiruvēngadam mēya ennānai ennappan en nenjiluḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mannā – impermanent; i – this; manisap piṟaviyai – human birth; nīkki – eliminating; than – for him; ākki – having as a servitor; than – his; in aruḷ – great mercy; seyyum – showering; talaivan – having leadership; min – by lightning; Ar – filled with; mugil – clouds; sēr – have gathered and are residing; tiruvēngadam – on tirumalā; mēya – firmly residing; en – to give enjoyment to me; ānai – having a beautiful form like an elephant; en – for me; appan – being great benefactor; en – my; nenjilē – in heart; uḷān – is eternally residing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Eliminating this impermanent human birth, having me as a servitor, showering his great mercy, having leadership, to give enjoyment to me, emperumān is firmly residing on tirumalā where clouds filled with lightning have gathered and are residing. Having a beautiful form like an elephant, being a great benefactor for me, he is eternally residing in my heart.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*mannā …* – Relieving me from this impermanent human birth.

*tannākki* – Making me at par with him; alternatively – making me exist for him. muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.2.3 “*niranjana: paramam sāmyamupaiti*” (after attaining him, they (jīvātmās) get his qualities in the same measure).

*than in aruḷ …* – One who has the leadership to do everything and still feel that he has not done much and hence will shower his mercy as if he is doing it for his sake.

*min Ar …* – The combination of cloud and lightning resembles the combination of pirātti \[bright in complexion\] and him \[dark in complexion\].

*en ānai* – One who is always vatcable.

*en appan* – One who is great benefactor for me.

When asked “What favour was done to you?” āḻvār says,

*en nenjil uḷānē* – After having entered my heart, he is not leaving from there.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.7. Maney madanokki

*mānēy madanōkki tiṟattu edir vanda ānēḻ vidai ceṟṟa aṇivarait tōḷā! tēnē! tiruvēngada māmalai mēya kōnē! en manam kudi koṇḍirundāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mān – deer’s eyes; ēy – matching; madam – beautiful; nōkki tiṟattu – on nappinnaip pirātti who is having divine eyes; edir vanda – came as hurdle; An – (roaming) amidst cows; ēḻ vidai – the seven bulls; seṟṟa – one who killed; aṇi – very beautiful; varai – firm like mountain; tōḷā – oh one who is having divine shoulders!; tēnē – Oh one who is sweet like honey for me!; mā – glorious; tiruvēngadamalai – on tirumalā; mēya – being the one who permanently resides; kōnē – Oh one who enslaved me!; en – my; manam – mind; kudi koṇḍu – having as abode; irundāy – you remained firmly

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is having mountain like firm, very beautiful, divine shoulders, who killed the bulls which were roaming amidst cows and which came as hurdle for nappinnaip pirātti who is having beautiful, divine eyes matching deer’s eyes! Oh one who is sweet like honey for me! Oh one who enslaved me, being the one who permanently resides on the glorious tirumalā! You remained firmly in my mind, having it as your abode.

*mānēy …* – To become dear to nappinnaip pirātti who is having eyes which resemble those of a deer. Having youthful eyes resembling those of a deer, and not only that, they would also be very tender.

*edir vanda* – One who destroyed the seven bulls which came to fight him.

*aṇi varait tōḷ* – Oh one who is having shoulders which are dear to nappinnaip pirātti, yet are too strong to be destroyed by the seven bulls!

*tēnē* – It is pleasing to the heart when we meditate upon the activity of jumping upon the seven bulls to destroy them for the sake of nappinnaip pirātti, without caring about himself.

*tiruvēngada malai …* – This is the abode where such honey is residing.

*kōnē* – Oh one who arrived on tirumalā to enslave me and who manifested your great enjoyability and made me exist for you!

*en …* – After destroying the seven bulls, he married nappinnaip pirātti, and arrived along with her in my heart as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.2.10 “*aravattamaḷiyinōdum*” (with the serpent bed), and remained there as if he is never going to leave.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.8. Seyan aniyan

*sēyan aṇiyan ena sindaiyuḷ ninṟa māyan maṇi vāḷ oḷi veṇ taraḷangaḷ vēy viṇḍu udir vēngada māmalai mēya āyan adiyalladu maṟṟu aṟaiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sēyan – being unreachable (for those who do not surrender); aṇiyan – being easily reachable (for those who surrender); ena – my; sindai uḷ – in mind; ninṟa – one who is eternally residing; māyan – amazing; vēy – bamboos; viṇḍu – split; udir – remaining scattered on the ground; oḷi – radiance; veṇ – having whiteness; taraḷangaḷ – pearls; vāḷ – radiant; maṇi – having precious gems; mā – very glorious; vēngada malai – on tirumalā; mēya – being the one who is firmly residing; āyan – kriṣṇa, the covherd’s; adi alladu – other than the divine feet; maṟṟu – anything else; aṟiyēn – I don’t consider as an entity

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is saying “After you killed the bulls and married nappinnaip pirātti, you have entered my heart. In such case, I don’t know anything other than serving your such family life”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa, the covherd, is both unreachable and easily reachable. He is the amazing one who is eternally residing in my mind. He is firmly residing in the very glorious tirumalā which is having bamboos which are split and \[from those bamboos\] radiant white pearls and radiant precious gems are scattered on the ground. I don’t consider anything other than such kriṣṇa’s divine feet as an entity.

*sēyan aṇiyan* – He remains very far away \[unreachable\] for those who don’t surrender unto him and remains very close \[easily reachable\] for those who surrender. These two aspects can be observed in the case of pāṇḍavas and duryōdana et al.

When asked “How are you saying that emperumān will remain subservient to those who desire him?” āzvār responds,

*ena sindai uḷ ninṟa māyan* – The amazing personality who came to my heart, entered there and eternally resided, though I did not pray for that.

*maṇi …* – vāḷ = oḷi = radiance.

When asked “What do these pearls and gems do?” āḻvār responds,

*maṇi vāḷ oḷi veṇ taraḷangaḷ* – Radiant gems and radiant, white pearls. The bamboos will split open and spill these on the ground. Having such tirumalā as residence.

*āyan* – This indicates that he is dear to nappinnaip pirātti.

*adi …* – When bhagavān who has no expectation from anyone enters me without having any other refuge, will I, who am expecting \[protection from him\], leave him?

## 1.10.9. Vanday en manam

*vandāy en manam pugundāy manni ninṟāy! nandāda koḻunjudarē! engaḷ nambī! sindā maṇiyē! tiruvēngadam mēya endāy! ini yān unnai yenṟum vidēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nandāda – continuous; koḻu – abundant; sudarē – Oh one who is having radiance!; engaḷ – being able to eliminate shortcomings of ours, we being incomplete; nambī – Oh complete one!; sindā – (cintā) just on thinking; maṇiyē – Oh precious gem (which will fulfil all desires)!; tiruvēngadam – On vēnkatācalam; mēya – firmly residing; endāy – oh my relative!; vandāy – You arrived (where I am residing); en manam – in my heart; pugundāy – you entered; manni ninṟāy – you firmly remained (in my heart); ini – now onvards; yān – I; unnai – you who are the benefactor in this manner; enṟum – ever; vidēn – will not leave

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is continuously having abundant radiance! Oh complete one who is able to eliminate shortcomings of ours, we being incomplete! Oh precious gem which will fulfil all desires just on thinking! Oh my relative who is eternally residing on vēnkatācalam! You have arrived in my heart; you have entered there and firmly remained there; now onvards, I will never leave you, who are the benefactor in this manner.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*vandāy* – While emperumān was having śrīvaikuṇṭam as his grand abode, and while āḻvār was not praying for him to come, he came and entered considering “As we tried to enter āḻvār’s heart, he did not stop us \[so, let us enter his heart\]”

*manni ninṟāy* – Previously emperumān did not enter āḻvār’s heart, not because of lack of relationship, but due to the lack of acceptance in āḻvār; but now, he remains firmly in āḻvār’s heart thinking “if we left now, it will be difficult to enter again”. While remaining in āḻvār’s heart in this manner, instead of being anguished thinking “We who have śrīvaikuṇṭam as our grand abode, have become imprisoned in āḻvār’s heart”, emperumān considered this residing in āḻvār’s heart to be an unattainable goal which is accomplished now and remains radiant that he has acquired some wealth which he did not have.

*nandāda koḻum sudarē* – Oh one who is having radiance without any break!

*engaḷ nambī* – You are filling me, this deep pit.

*sindā maṇiyē* – emperumān thinks “when a cētana thinks about something to be belonging to me, that is the reason for me to give the same to him”. The precious gem which cannot be given up even after acquiring true knowledge \[worldly gem will be given up after acquiring true knowledge\].

*tiruvēngadam mēya endāy* – Oh one who entered tirumalā, manifested your lordship and made me exclusively exist for you!

*ini …* – You will not give up your presence for me \[in divine abodes\]; that being the case, how can I give up my attachment to you which made me exist for you?

*enṟum* … – With this, it is implied that āḻvār reached up to the state of parabhakti. parabhakti is the stage of devotion where one cannot remain separated from bhagavān even for a fraction of a moment; āḻvār reached a state where he cannot survive in separation

## 1.10.10. Villar mali

*villār mali vēngada māmalai mēya mallār tiraḷ tōḷ maṇivaṇṇan ammānaik kallār tiraḷ tōḷ kaliyan sonna mālai vallār avar vānavar āguvar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

villār – the divine hunters who always carry bow; mali – abundant; vēngada mā malai – on tirumalā; mēya – one who is residing firmly; mal Ar – very strong; tiraḷ – well rounded; tōḷ – shoulders; maṇi – like a blue gem; vaṇṇan – having divine complexion; ammānai – on sarvēśvaran; kal – rock; Ar – matching; tiraḷ – well rounded; tōḷ – having shoulders; kaliyan – āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; mālai – this decad which is in the form of a garland; vallār avar tām – those who can learn with meanings; vānavar āguvar – will get to perform kainkaryam like nityasūris

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is firmly residing on tirumalā which has abundance of divine hunters who always carry bow; he is having very strong with well-rounded shoulders and blue gem like divine complexion; āḻvār who is having rock like well-rounded shoulders, mercifully spoke this decad which is in the form of a garland on such sarvēśvaran; those who can learn it with meanings will get to perform kainkaryam like nityasūris.

*villār …* – bhagavān, who is served in paramapadam by nityasūris who care for him very much, unnecessarily doubting his safety, has arrived in this samsāram and is present here; since this is samsāram, doubt for his safety will be natural and necessary; hence, the divine hunters of tirumalā will be alert with their bows and cautiously care for bhagavān, just as śrī guhapperumāḷ remained awake and cared for śrī rāma.

*mal Ar …* – In this manner, they are cautiously protecting the den of a lion. sarvēśvaran who is having very strong shoulders and a beautiful form.

*kal Ar …* – tirumangai āḻvār’s strong shoulders assure safety of both bhagavān in tirumalā and those divine hunters who are caring for bhagavān.

*vallār …* – Those who are able to learn these pāsurams, will attain the kainkaryam which is done by nityasūris to bhagavān, as their routine.

## Second Centum

## 2.1 Vanavar tangal

## 2.1.1. Vanavar tangal

*vānavar tangaḷ sindai pōla en nenjamē! inidu vandu mādava mānavar tangaḷ sindai amarndu uṟaiginṟa endai kānavaridu kāragiṟpugai ōngu vēngadam mēvi māṇ kuṟaḷ āna andaṇaṟku inṟu adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en nenjamē – Oh favourable mind!; mā – great; tavam – having tapas (penance); mānavar tangaḷ – men, their; sindai – in the heart; amarndu – firmly remaining; uṟaiginṟa – one who is eternally residing; endai – being my lord; kānavar – hunters; kār – dark (due to being very strong); agil – (cutting down) agil (āquilaria agalloca) trees; idu – due to placing them (in fire); pugai – smoke (to reach and spread); ōngu – tall; vēngadam – on tirumalā; mēvi – one who is eternally residing; māṇ – beautiful; kuṟaḷāna – assuming the form of vāmana \[dwarf\]; andaṇaṟku – for my lord, who is a brāhmaṇa; vānavar tangaḷ – nityasūris’; sindai pōla – like in their heart; inidu – sweetly; uvandu – arriving joyfully; inṟu – today; adimait toḻil – in doing kainkaryam; pūṇḍāyē – you are engaged!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is my lord who is firmly remaining and eternally residing in the heart of those men who have great penance; he is eternally residing on the tall tirumalā where the smoke from the agil trees which are placed in fire by the hunters, has reached and spread out; he is my lord who has assumed the form of vāmana, a brāhmaṇa. Oh favourable mind! Today, you are engaged in doing kainkaryam to such lord who has joyfully and sweetly arrived in my heart just as he is in the heart of nityasūris.

*vānavar …* – Present in my heart just as he is present in the heart of nityasūris.

*mādava mānavar tangaḷ sindai amarndu uṟaiginṟa endai –* The lord who is eternally residing without any expectation in the hearts of those men who have great penance.

*kānavar …* – kānavar – the divine hunters of tirumalā; they will cut the trees in their lands and burn those trees; since those trees are agil trees, their smoke will reach the sky and fill it; emperumān is eternally residing in such tirumalā which is having such height.

*māṇ kuṟaḷāya andaṇaṟku* – One who assumed the form of an alms-seeker to get his own belonging. andaṇa – brāhmaṇa. He assumed a very humble form, where mahābali cannot refuse \[whatever he asks\].

*māṇ kuṟaḷāya andaṇaṟku, vānavar tangaḷ sindai pōla en nenjamē! inidu vandu, adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē –* \[Oh mind!\] Just as nityasūris’ hearts will be immersed in bhagavat kainkaryam, you are joyfully engaged in his divine feet!

*māṇ …* – As he has arrived to beg and accept our service, you are also following his thoughts! \[How great!\]

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.2. Uravu surram

*uṟavu suṟṟam enṟu onṟilā oruvan ugandavar tammai maṇmisaip piṟaviyē keduppān adu kaṇḍu en nenjam enbāy! kuṟavar mādargaḷōdu vaṇḍu kuṟinji maruḷ isai pādum vēngadattu aṟava nāyagaṟku inṟu adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṟavu – relatives (based on karma); suṟṟam – paternal relatives; enṟu – being in this manner; onṟu – a connection; ilā – one who is not having; oruvan – being matchless; ugandavar tammai – for those who are dear to him; maṇ misai – on the earth; piṟavi – birth; keduppān – one who eliminates; kuṟavar mādargaḷōdu – with nomadic ladies; vaṇḍu – beetles; kuṟinji maruḷ – tune named kuṟinji; isai pādum – singing with music; vēngadattu – one who is eternally residing on śrī vēnkatādri; aṟavan – most magnanimous; nāyagaṟku – for sarvēśvaran; adu kaṇḍu – meditating upon his nature; en nenjam enbāy – You who are my mind; inṟu – now; adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē – You are engaged in serving him!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is not having (general) relatives and paternal relatives and is matchless; he eliminates the birth on earth, for those who are dear to him; he is eternally residing on śrī vēnkatādri where nomadic ladies and beetles sing with music, the tune named kuṟinji; mediating upon such most magnanimous sarvēśvaran’s nature, you who are my mind, are engaged in serving him now!

*uṟavu suṟṟam …* – emperumān who is matchless due to not having any (general) relatives or paternal relatives, who are usually present due to karma (bondage).

*ugandavar …* – Liking certain persons, he does not just remove their hurdles and give some results, but he eliminates their birth in this samsāra; thinking about him.

*ugandavar* – Also implies those who like him.

*en nenjam enbāy* – Shall I speak about him? ōr shall I speak about you? How can I praise you? āḻvār is greatly pleased with his heart and says “Oh my heart!”.

*kuṟavar …* – Along with the nomadic girls, beetles sing with music on the tune named kuṟinji.

*vēngadattu aṟava nāyagaṟku* – The most magnanimous lord who has placed a water-outlet to accept our service, where he is offering himself to us. For the most magnanimous lord who has arrived and is present on tirumalā to accept our service.

*adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē* – You have materialised the purpose of his arrival and stay on tirumalā, in a particular way \[by being favourable\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.3. Indaiyayina kondu

*iṇḍaiyāyina koṇḍu toṇḍargaḷ ēttuvār uṟavōdum vānidaik koṇḍu pōyidavum adu kaṇḍen nenjam enbāy! vaṇḍu vāḻ vada vēngada malai kōyil koṇḍu adanōdum mīmisai aṇḍam āṇḍiruppāṟku adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en nenjam enbāy – Oh favourable mind!; iṇḍaiyāyina – known as flower garlands; koṇḍu – carrying; ēttuvār – those who are praising; toṇḍargaḷ – servitors; uṟavōdum – along with their relatives; koṇḍu pōy – carrying from here; vānidai – in paramapadam; ida – placed; adu kaṇḍu – to see that simplicity; vaṇḍu – beetles; vāḻ – living gloriously; vada vēngada malai – tirumalā; kōyil koṇḍu – having it as his abode; adanōdum – with the leelā vibhūti (samsāram) which includes that tirumalā; mīmisai aṇḍam – and nitya vibhūti which is known as paramākāśam (supreme sky); āṇḍu iruppāṟku – to the one who rules over; adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē – you are engaged in serving him!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh favourable mind! As emperumān carried those servitors who were carrying flower garlands and praising him along with their relatives from here and placed in paramapadam, seeing that, the beetles are living gloriously on tirumalā; you are engaged in serving such sarvēśvaran who is having such tirumalā as his abode and is ruling over the leelā vibhūti which includes that tirumalā and nitya vibhūti which is known as paramākāśam.

*iṇḍai …* – iṇḍai is a name for flower garland. Thus, carrying those which are known as flower garlands, as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.7.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-7-8-kandu-kondu/) “*eṇḍisaiyum uḷḷa pūk koṇḍu*” (Bringing the flowers from eight directions).

*toṇḍargaḷ ēttuvār* – bhagavān’s servitors are carrying flower garlands in their hands and praising with their mouths; their,

*uṟavōdum vān idaik koṇḍu pōy idavum* – Along with their relatives and the relatives of those relatives. Thinking about his simplicity of carrying and placing everyone irrespective of those who are surrendered or not \[just by their connection with surrendered persons\] in nitya vibhūti, \[āḻvār says\] oh my mind! While we are fearing that we may lose even our existence in this world, you are having the desire to go and serve him in paramapadam! \[How great of you!\]

*vaṇḍu …* – Beetles are drinking the honey and living joyfully in tirumalā; having such tirumalā as his abode.

*adanōdum mīmisai aṇḍam āṇḍiruppārku* – sarvēśvaran who owns both nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti. aṇḍam is a name for sky. When asked “is it simply said as ‘aṇḍam’? “āḻvār is saying “mīmisai aṇḍam” indicating that it is paramapadam which is much higher than svargam etc. paramapadam is also known as mahākāśam, paramākāśam. Hence, for sarvēśvaran who owns ubhaya vibhūti (both nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti).

*adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē* – In a way, you have fulfilled the desire of avāpt samasta kāman (one who has no unfulfilled desires). He did not consider his wealth of ubhaya vibhūti as worthy before entering tirumalā and accepting āḻvār’s service. Though very wealthy, while losing a small portion of his wealth, such person will eagerly search the ground even resulting in his hand getting dirty, when it is just a coin falling down \[similarly, bhagavān having both vibhūtis before accepting āḻvār’s service, decided to enter tirumalā only in order to attain āḻvār\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.4. Paviyadu seyday

*pāviyādu seydāy en nenjamē! paṇḍu toṇḍu seydārai maṇmisai mēvi ātkoṇḍu pōy visumbēṟa vaikkum endai kōvi nāyagan koṇḍalunduyar vēngada malaiyāṇḍu vānavarkku āviyāy iruppāṟku adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en nenjamē – Oh my mind!; pāviyādu – without fumbling; seydāy – you did; paṇḍu – previously; toṇḍu seydārai – (to uplift) those who served; maṇmisai – on earth; mēvi – mercifully incarnated; āḷ koṇḍu – engaging (them) in service; pōy – carrying them (in arcirādi mārgam (the path leading to paramapadam) from here); visumbu ēṟa vaikkum – one who places in paramapadam; kōvi nāyagan – being dear to śrī gōpikās; endai – being my lord; koṇḍal – clouds; undu – pushing; uyar – tall; vēngada malaiyilē – on tirumalā; āṇḍu – ruling over both nitya and leelā vibhūtis; vānavarkku – for nityasūris; āviyāy iruppāṟku – for the one who is the life; adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē – you are engaged in serving him!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh my mind! emperumān mercifully incarnated on this earth to uplift those who previously served, by accepting their service, carrying them in arcirādi mārgam and placing them in paramapadam; being dear to śrī gōpikās, being my lord, he is the life of nityasūris; he is remaining on the tall tirumalā which is pushing clouds, and is ruling over both nitya and leelā vibhūtis. You are engaged in serving him! You have done this without fumbling.

*pāviyādu …* – Instead of wavering between “Should I do that? ōr Should I do this?”, you are firmly believing in this \[service to him\]! What a great fortune! Alternative explanation. \[bhāviyādadu seydāy\] It is natural to be engaged in samsāram! Instead of analysing “Should we engage in śabdam etc \[worldly pleasures\]? ōr should we do bhagavat kainkaryam?” you are firmly engaging in kainkaryam! I got all this favour due to you \[mind\] only.

*paṇḍu …* – The lord who would incarnate in this samsāram to uplift those who served him previously, to be called by them as “He is my friend”, “He is my cousin”, created kainkarya ruci (taste for kainkaryam) in them, accepted their service, and placed them in paramapadam to have such kainkaryam occur continuously without any break.

*kōvi nāyagan* – One who mingles with his devotees as he mingled with śrī gōpikās.

*koṇḍal undu uyar vēngadam* – Having tirumalā as his abode which has peaks which have grown tall enough to push the clouds over.

*vānavar …* – As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.18](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-18/) “*jñāni tvātmaiva mē matam*” (but the jñāni is the one who sustains (me) – this is my principle), have you also become the life of the one who has jñānis as his life?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.5. Pongu bodiyum

*pongu bōdiyum piṇḍiyummudaip puttar nōnbiyar paḷḷiyuḷḷuṟai tangaḷ dēvarum tāngaḷumēyāga en nenjam enbāy ! engum vānavar dānavar niṟaindēttum vēngadam mēvi ninṟaruḷ angaṇāyagaṟku inṟu adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en nenjam enbāy – You who can be desired as “my mind!”; pongu – grown well with stems and branches; bōdiyum – arasa (sacred fig) tree; piṇḍiyum – aśōka tree; udai – having as refuge; puttar – bauddas (followers of budda philosophy); nōnbiyar – amaṇas (jainas, followers of jaina philosophy); paḷḷi uḷ – inside their temples; uṟai – living; tangaḷ – their; dēvarum – vorśippable deity; tāngaḷumē āga – to have them only present; engum – in all four directions; vānavar – dēvatās; dānavar – asuras; niṟaindu – present densely; ēttum – praising; vēngadam – on tirumalā; mēvi ninṟu – present firmly; aruḷ – one who fulfils the desires of devotees; angaṇ – having beautiful eyes; nāyagaṟku – for the sarvasvāmy (lord of all); inṟu adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē – now, you are engaged in serving him!

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār’s mind asked “What is the reason for praising me saying ‘You are firmly believing without any doubt!’?” āḻvār says “Many philosophies exist outside our philosophy, to be analysed”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

You who can be desired as “my mind!” ! While bauddas and jainas who have as their refuge, the arasa and aśōka trees with well grown stems and branches, are only present along with their vorśippable deities in their temples, the dēvatās and asuras in all four directions are praising sarvasvāmy who is firmly present on tirumalā, fulfilling the desires of devotees and having beautiful eyes. Now, you are engaged in serving him!

*pongu bōdiyum* – Well grown arasa tree.

*piṇḍiyum* – aśōka tree. bauddas and ārhatas would consider these trees as important.

*puttar nōnbiyar* – bauddas and jainas are referred to, here.

*paḷḷi uḷ uṟai tangaḷ dēvarum tāngaḷumē āga* – Looks like they are only present \[everywhere\] along with their vorśippable deities in their temples. It appears that everyone else is considered as ignorant.

*en nenjam …* – As āḻvār’s divine heart disregarded those philosophies and became attached to bhagavān, others also followed it, giving up other philosophies and became attached to bhagavān.

*engum …* – dēvatās and asuras have gathered densely and are praising. Alternatively, tānavar means those who are in that stānam (abode).

*angaṇ nāyagaṟku* – You have become the target of the coolness of his eyes! You have fully offered yourself being defeated by those divine eyes saying as in jitantē stōtram 1 “*jitam*” (Victory)! Did you engage in the activity of those who have submitted themselves saying “*jitam*“?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.6. Tuvariyadaiyar

*tuvariyādaiyar mattaiyar samaṇ toṇḍargaḷ maṇḍiyuṇḍu pinnarum tamarum tāngaḷumē tadikka en nenjam enbāy! kavari mākkaṇam sērum vēngadam kōyil koṇḍa kaṇṇār visumbidai amara nāyagaṟku inṟu adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuvari – saffronised; ādaiyar – having cloth; mattaiyar – having tonsured head; samaṇ toṇḍargaḷ – those who follow kśapaṇa (jaina) matam; maṇḍi – remaining close to each other; uṇḍu – eat; pinnarum – subsequently; tamarum – their relatives; tāngaḷumē – them too; tadikka – becoming fat (due to eating as pleased); en nenjam enbāy – You, who are my mind; kavari mā – animals having fur; kaṇam – herds; sērum – gathering; vēngadam – tirumalā; kōyil koṇḍa – having as abode; kaṇ Ar – spacious; visumbu idai – residing in paramapadam; amarar – for nityasūris; nāyagaṟku – for the lord; inṟu adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē – now, you are engaged in serving him!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Those who follow kśapaṇa (jaina) matam, wearing saffronised cloth, having tonsured head, remaining close to each other, eat along with their relatives, and subsequently become fat due to eating as desired. While they remain in this world, you, who are my mind, are engaged in serving the lord of nityasūris residing in spacious paramapadam, who is having tirumalā where animals with fur are gathering, as his abode.

*tuvari …* – Having saffron cloth which was given that colour, there are those who pluck their hair from their heads and throw it down – they are followers of jaina philosophy; they eat a lot and further they and others who have interest in their philosophy, become fat.

*en nenjam enbāy* – While they do what they do, what can I call you, who are having a distinguished nature from them?

*kavari …* – One who is having tirumalā where herds of animals with fur gather, as his abode.

*kaṇ Ar …* – There is a spacious sky – tripād vibhūti (śrīvaikuṇṭam which is three times larger in size than the world we live in). The controller of ananta (ādiśēśa), vainatēya (garudāḻvār) et al who are present there.

*adimai …* – You have disregarded the acts of jainas and engaged in the routine of nityasūris! \[How great!\]

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.7. Tarukkinal

*tarukkināl samaṇ seydu sōṟu taṇ tayirināl tiraḷai midaṟṟidai nerukkuvār alakkaṇ adukaṇḍu en nenjam enbāy! marutkaḷ vaṇḍugaḷ pādum vēngadam kōyil koṇḍu adanōdum vānidai arukkan mēvi niṟpāṟku adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tarukkināl – By useless debate; samaṇ – their kśapaṇa (jaina) philosophy; seydu – established; taṇ – best; tayirināl – mixed with curd; sōṟṟut tiraḷai – handful of rice; midaṟṟidai – in their throat; nerukkuvār – will push and suffer (to have their eyes pop out); adu alakkaṇ – that sorrow; kaṇḍu – saw; en nenjam enbāy – Oh you who are known as “my heart”!; vaṇḍugaḷ – beetles; maruḷgaḷ – tunes such as maruḷ; pādum – singing; vēngadam – tirumalā; kōyil koṇḍu – having as abode; adanōdum – along with that; vānidai – roaming in the sky; arukkan – for sun; mēvi niṟpāṟku – sarvēśvaran who is the antarātmā; adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē – You are engaged in serving him!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are known as “my heart”! You saw the sorrow of those followers of kśapaṇa philosophy, who established their philosophy through useless debate, due to pushing handful of rice mixed with the best curd. After seeing that, you are engaged in serving sarvēśvaran who is having tirulamā where beetles sing tunes such as maruḷ, as his abode and along with residing there, he is the antarātmā for sun who is roaming in the sky!

*tarukkināl samaṇ seydu* – Establishing their philosophy by mere debates. As said in manu smriti 12.106 “*vēda śāstra virōdinā yastarkēṇānusandattē sadarmam vēdanētara:*” (One who is engaged in debates which are not contrary to what is seen by sages in vēdam and the smrutis which are based on that vēdam, is the one who knows darmam. Others don’t know darmam), instead of establishing the principles using debates which are aligned with pramāṇam (scriptures), establishing avaidika (contrary to vēdam) principles using useless debate which are hard.

*sōṟu …* – They survive with boiled (special type of) rice; they would make a paste of curd and rice, make a handful and push it inside the throat to pop out their eyes, as per their vrata (penance); they go through a particular sorrow at that time – seeing that.

*maruḷgaḷ …* – Having tirumalā as his abode where beetles sing the tunes of maruḷ, indaḷam and so on.

*arukkan mēvi niṟpāṟku* – Being the antaryāmi of sun who is approached by vaidikas.

*adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē* – You got to see him, serve him and enjoy him with your eyes instead of just needing to meditate upon him as the antaryāmi of sun.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.8. Seyan aniyan

*sēyan aṇiyan siṟiyan periyan enbadum silar pēsak kēttirundē en nenjam enbāy! enakku onṟu sollādē vēygaḷ ninṟu veṇmuttamē sori vēngada malai kōyil mēviya āyar nāyagaṟku inṟu adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sēyan enbadum – (when told “surrender unto paramapadanātan”) blaming him to be too far; aṇiyan enbadum – (when told “worship him in arcāvatāram”) disregarding him due to his close proximity; siṟiyan enbadum – (when told “approach kriṣṇa” and shown vibhavāvatāram) withdrawing from him highlighting his simplicity as the reason; periyan enbadum – (when told “surrender unto his vyūha state or antaryāmi state”) withdrawing from him highlighting his unreacability; silar – ignorant ones; pēsa – to speak; kēttirundē – though having heard; en nenjam enbāy – Oh you who are known as “my heart”!; enakku – for me who is having you as my internal sense; onṟu sollādē – without saying a word; vēygaḷ ninṟu – from bamboos; veḷ – whitish; muttam – pearls; sori – falling; vēngada malai – tirumalā; kōyil – as abode; mēviya – one who is firmly remaining; āyar – for covherds; nāyagaṟku – for the leader; inṟu adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē – You are engaged in serving him now!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are known as “my heart”! Though having heard ignorant ones speak about emperumān blaming him to be too far in paramapadam, disregarding him due to his close proximity in arcāvatāram, withdrawing from him highlighting his simplicity in vibhavāvatāram as the reason and withdrawing from him highlighting his unreacability in vyūha and antaryāmi states, for me who is having you as my internal sense, without saying a word, now, you are engaged in serving him who is firmly remaining on tirumalā where whitish pearls are falling from bamboos, having it as his abode and is the leader of the covherds.

*sēyan …* – Worldly people are doubting emperumān to be small or great, and become ruined. You, who are not joining such people and ignoring me who owns you, are engaged in serving his divine feet! \[How great!\]

*sēyan* – Some say emperumān is too far.

*aṇiyan* – Some say he is too close.

*siṟiyan* – Some cite his simplicity and withdraw from him.

*periyan* … – Some cite his greatness and unreacability and withdraw from him. Though you have heard others speak according to their limited understanding, you who are known as “my heart” are engaged in serving him!

*enakku onṟu sollādē* – Neither joining with them nor informing me who owns you, about this.

*vēy …* – As whitish pearls fall from the bamboo, the light from the pearls shows the path to reach there.

*āyar nāyagaṟku*– For the leader of covherds as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.1.1 “*tannēr āyiram piḷḷaigaḷ*” (thousand covherd boys who are at par with him). He is said as in tiruvāimoḻi 5.5.6 “*inavāyar talaivan*” (leader of the covherds).

*adimai …* – You engaged in service without any restriction to the one who protects all.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
