## 2.1.9. Kudiyadi

*kūdiyādi uraittadē uraittāy en nenjam enbāy! tuṇindu kēḷ pādiyādip palarum paṇindēttik kāṇgilār ādu tāmaraiyōnum īsanum amarar kōnum ninṟēttum vēngadattu ādu kūttanukku inṟu adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en nenjam enbāy! – Oh you who are known as “my heart”!; kūdi – gathered with worldly people; ādi – ate (what they ate); uraittadē – the words they spoke; uraittāy – you spoke; tuṇindu kēḷ – hear (my words) faithfully; palarum – many; pādi ādi – singing and dancing; paṇindu – vorśipping; ētti – praising; kāṇgilār – (even after these) cannot see (his real greatness); ādu – glorious; tāmaraiyōnum – brahmā who is born in the (blossomed) divine lotus in his divine navel; īsanum – rudran; amararkōnum – indran; ninṟu – remaining (as per their qualification); ēttu – to be praised; vēngadattu – one who is eternally residing on tirumalā; ādu kūttanukku – for sarvēśvaran who danced (with the gōpikās in kudakkūttu); inṟu adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē – now, you are engaged in his service!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are known as “my heart”! \[Previously\] You gathered with worldly people and ate along! Hear my words faithfully. Many persons, even after singing, dancing, vorśipping and praising, cannot see his real greatness; now, you are engaged in the service of sarvēśvaran who danced, and who is eternally residing on tirumalā to be praised by glorious brahmā who is born in the (blossomed) divine lotus in his divine navel, rudran and indran, remaining as per their qualification.

*kūdi ādi …* – \[Previously\] You gathered with people who are attached to śabda etc (sensual pleasures), enjoying what they enjoyed, and spoke the words which they spoke after enjoying those pleasures.

*tuṇindu kēḷ* – Now, I am telling you, who have given up such attachment and having attachment towards bhagavān, another good advice. Hear faithfully.

*pādi …* – Many would sing and dance and surrender unto him, but will still not see him. Further, even brahmā et al would surrender unto emperumān according to their qualification. \[Instead of kāṇgilār\] It is also said as kāṇgilā.  That is, dēvatās such as brahmā et al who are great due to being difficult to be seen by their devotees, would come and surrender to \[see\] bhagavān.

*ādu tāmaraiyōn …* – ādu implies greatness, saying “blossomed lotus”.  Alternatively – ādugai – being present, saying “present in the lotus”; another explanation – ādugai – appearing (being born), saying “one who is having the lotus as his birth place”; another explanation – ādugai – victory, saying “victorious lotus”.

*ādu kūttanukku* – In the divine form where it is visible that he danced previously. As said in tirunedundāṇḍagam 16 “*manṟamarak kūttādi magiḻndāy enṟum vada tiruvēngadam mēya maindā enṟum*” (As “Oh one who enjoyed the dance in the four-way junction! Oh youthful one who is permanently residing on tirumalā!”).

*adimait toḻil pūṇḍāyē* – Many surrendered to him but did not see him still; brahmā et al will come and surrender unto him according to their qualification; though you are not in either situation, you are engaged in serving him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.10. Minnu mamugil

*minnu māmugil mēvu taṇ tiruvēngada malai kōyil mēviyaannamāy nigaḻnda amarar perumānaikkanni māmadiḷ mangaiyar kali kanṟi intamiḻāl uraitta immannu pādal vallārkku idamāgum vānulagē*

**Пословный перевод:**

minnum – with lightning; māmugil – huge clouds; mēvu – arriving and gathering; taṇ – cool; tiruvēngada malai – tirumalā; kōyil – having as temple; mēviya – one who is eternally residing; annamāy – in the form of a swan; nigaḻnda – one who divinely incarnated; perumānai – on the controller; kanni – made of rock; mā – huge; madiḷ – having fort; mangaiyar – for the residents of tirumangai region; kali – sins; kanṟi – āḻvār who eliminated; in – sweet for the ear; tamiḻālē – in tamiḻ; uraitta – mercifully spoken; mannu – firmly remaining (in the divine heart of emperumān); ippādal – this decad; vallārkku – for those who practice; vān ulagu – paramapadam; idam āgum – will be the abode

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, the controller who divinely incarnated in the form of a swan, is having as his temple and is eternally residing on the cool tirumalā where huge clouds along with lightning have arrived and gathered; āḻvār who eliminated the sins of the residents of tirumangai region which is having a huge fort made of rock, mercifully spoke on such emperumān, this decad in tamiḻ which is sweet for the ear. For those who practice this decad, paramapadam will be the abode.

*minnu mā …* – The huge clouds which have fully absorbed water and are holding lamp in the form of lightning to suppress their darkness, have arrived on the invigorating tirumalā; emperumān is having such tirumalā as his eternal abode; sarvēśvaran who incarnated as a swan to rescue the vēdam for brahmā et al, rescued it for them and was easily approachable for them in that manner. He is praised here.

*kanni …* – āḻvār who is the leader for the residents of tirumangai which is having a huge fort which is being a protective layer, and is unable to be destroyed by anyone, mercifully spoke this decad in sweet tamiḻ; for those who can sing it; since this decad is having meanings which are recited towards bhagavān with deep attachment, just as vēdam, this will also remain forever. The greatness of this decad is similar to that of vēdam.

*idam āgum vān ulagē* – They will have as their abode the place where their servitude which was pursued by them will remain eternal.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2 Kasaiyadai

## 2.2.1. Kasaiyadai

*kāsaiyādai mūdiyōdik kādal seydān avanūr nāsamāga namba valla nambi namperumān vēyin anna tōḷ madavār veṇṇey uṇḍān ivan enṟu ēsa ninṟa emperumān evvuḷ kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kāsai ādai – with saffron cloth; mūdi – covering (the body); ōdi – rushed to (the hermitage); kādal seydān – one who had desire (towards pirātti); avan – that rāvaṇa’s; Ur – town; nāsamāga – vowing to destroy; namba valla – one who was able to complete the task; nambi – one who is complete with vīraśrī (the wealth of valour); nam perumān – being our lord; vēy anna – like bamboo; tōḷ – shoulders; madavār – gōpikās having humility, their; veṇṇey – butter; ivan uṇḍān enṟu – saying “he ate”; ēsa ninṟa – to be mercifully present to have the gōpikās make fun of him; emperumān – my lord; evvuḷ – in this divyadēśam \[divine abode\] named tiruvevvuḷ; kidandān – mercifully reclined

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being our lord, he is complete with vīraśrī due to vowing to destroy the town of rāvaṇa who had desire towards pirātti rushing to the hermitage (of pirātti) covering his body with saffron cloth, and was able to complete the task as well. He mercifully presented himself to have the gōpikās who are having bamboo like shoulders and humility, make fun of him saying “he ate our butter”. He is my lord who has mercifully reclined in this divyadēśam named tiruvevvuḷ.

*kāsai …* – Covering his whole body with saffron cloth, rushing towards the hermitage due to fear for śrī rāma, rāvaṇa who assumed the form of an ascetic who is free from desire and hatred, showed desire towards sītāp pirātti without considering that she is the mother \[of all\]; emperumān who is complete due to having vīraśrī to think in his divine heart to turn such evil rāvaṇa’s town to ashes, and complete the task.

*nam perumān* – In that manner, the one who showed the same partiality which was shown towards pirātti, towards us.

*vēy …* – sarvēśvaran being unable to sustain himself without the butter which was touched by gōpikās who have shoulders resembling bamboo and who have noble qualities, stole their butter and mercifully consumed the same, and stood to be scolded by them for that reason.

*evvuḷ kidandānē* – The wise people were saying as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 131.7 “*rāmōrāmōrāma iti prajānāmabhavankatā: \| rāma bhūtam jagatabhūt rāmē rājyam praśāsati \|\|*” (When cakravarti tirumagan ([śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), son of daśarata cakravarti) was ruling the kingdom, every one was constantly reciting “rāma rāma rāma”; everything in the world was seen as śrī rāma only). and those who have great love towards him were scolding in this manner, he is mercifully in tiruvevvuḷ hearing both of these.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2.2. Taiyalal mel

*taiyalāḷ mēl kādal seyda tānavan vāḷ arakkan poyyilāda pon mudigaḷ onbadōdu onṟum anṟu seyda vembōr tannil angōr senjarattāl uruḷa eyda endai emperumān evvuḷ kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

taiyalāḷ mēl – towards pirātti who has natural femininity; kādal seyda – one who showed desire; tānavan – demoniac person; vāḷ – one who had sword as his protection; arakkan – rāvaṇa’s; poy ilāda – true; pon mudigaḷ – heads with golden crowns; onbadōdu onṟum – ten; anṟu – the day when rāvaṇa imprisoned pirātti; seyda – performed; vem – cruel; pōr tannil – honest battle; ōr – matchless; sem – reddish (due to spitting flames); sarattāl – by killer arrow; uruḷa – to fall down as pieces; eyda – one who shot; endai – being my father; emperumān – my lord; evvuḷ – in tiruvevvuḷ; kidandān – mercifully reclined

**Перевод:**

**Again, āḻvār is reminiscing śrī rāmāvatāram. Just as parāśara bhattar, tirumangai āḻvār has favouritism towards śrī rāmāvatāram. siṟiyāttān (an ācārya in our guruparamparā) desirous of directly hearing bhattar’s favouritism towards śrī rāmāvatāram asked bhattar “Though perumāḷ (śrī rāma) has all glories, he does not have the glory of going as a messenger with a message tied his neck, for the sake of his devotees”. bhattar mercifully responded “It is not that he did not want to go; but because of his birth he could not go”. There is no one who would send a descendant of ikśvāku clan, as a messenger with the message on his neck. perumāḷ, on seeing tiruvadi (hanuman) going here and there as messenger and sharing the messages, observed the greatness in it and thought “We are unable to go as a messenger for our devotees” and longed for it; it is because of this reason that he incarnated as kriṣṇa subsequently and went as messenger. He grew hiding his kśatriya birth thinking that if that was known to others, they will not let him go as messenger. No one will send a crowned king as a messenger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

rāvaṇa, the demoniac person, showed desire towards pirātti who has natural femininity; he had sword as his protection; emperumān, as śrī rāma, performed honest and cruel battle, , shot with the matchless, reddish, killer arrow to make his real, golden crowned, ten heads fall down as pieces; he, who is my father and lord, mercifully reclined in tiruvevvuḷ.

*taiyal …* – rāvaṇa had inapt desire towards pirātti who has natural femininity, without realising that she is the mother. The reason for that is his demoniac nature.

*vāḷ arakkan* – Without knowing to weigh the strength of perumāḷ, he had faith on the sword which was given by a dēvatā (rudran).

*poy ilāda* – He is truly crowned matching his demoniac nature; alternative explanation – one \[an emperor\] would do victorious journeys, and earn crowns for valour, victory etc; having true greatness to acquire such crowns.

*seyda vem pōr tannil* – emperumān engaged in the honest, direct battle, unlike brahmā et al who vowed based on their strength of tapasya (penance) or rāvaṇa who engaged in mischievous battle.

*ōr sem sarattāl* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 16.22 “*dīpta pāvaka sankāśai:*” (resembling blazing fire), the arrow moving fiercely with blazing fire; alternatively, sem refers to the reddish colour due to blood oozing out  from the firm chest on being hit by the arrow. The arrows which were shot to knock down the heads which were pampered with the strength of the boons, like palm fruit falling off the tree.

*endai* … – My father; my lord.

*evvuḷ kidandānē* – He has arrived and reclined; now there is lack of those who will awaken him and get their tasks done.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2.3. Munnor tudu

*munnōr tūdu vānarattin vāyil moḻindu arakkan mannūr tannai vāḷiyināl māḷa munindu avanē pinnōr tūdu ādi mannarkkāgip peruṇilattār innār tūdan ena ninṟān evvuḷ kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mun – In śrīrāmāvatāram; ōr – matchless; tūdu – words to be conveyed; vānarattin – tiruvadi’s (hanuman’s); vāyil – through the mouth; moḻindu – informed and sent; arakkan – rāvaṇa, the demon; mannu – remaining firmly; Ur tannai – lankā; vāḷiyināl – with arrow; māḷa – to be destroyed; munindu – being the one who mercifully showed his anger; avanē – that cakravarti tiruamgan (divine son of emperor daśarati) himself; pin – in kriṣṇāvatāram; ādi mannarkku – pāṇḍavas who are the original kings; ōr tūdāgi – being the \[unique\] messenger; peru nilattār – the residents of this vast earth; innār tūdan ena – to say that he is the messenger of pāṇḍavas; ninṟān – stood (in front of arjuna’s chariot); evvuḷ kidandānē – reclined in tiruvevvuḷ

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In śrī rāmāvatāram, cakravarti tirumagan informed matchless words to be conveyed through hanuman’s mouth and sent him there; he mercifully showed his anger to have rāvaṇa, the demon who was remaining firmly in lankā, destroyed with arrow; the same emperumān, in kriṣṇāvatāram, remained as the messenger of pāṇḍavas who are the original kings, to have the residents of this vast earth say “he is the messenger of pāṇḍavas” and stood; he has now reclined in tiruvevvuḷ.

*mun …* – āḻvār is repeating what he said in the first pāsuram in “*ēsa ninṟa*“. This is similar to yajñas which are ordained in śāstram before and after sunrise \[udita, anudita hōmams\]. Though the yajña performed before sunrise is said to be lowly, mīmāmsakas will interpret such statement to be in glorification of such yajña as well. Here too, “*ēsa*” is not taken as insult, but as glorification only. That is because, āḻvār enjoys every aspect of emperumān.

*mun …* – Before dvāpara yugam, in trētā yugam, when he was unable to bear the separation from pirātti, he almost decided to kill himself by drowning in the ocean; at that time, he sent a message through a vānaram (hanuman).

*arakkan mannu Ur tannai* – The town of the demon, which was well built by boons.

*vāḷiyināl* – He used an arrow which is used by humans to torment the town which could not be threatened even by brahmāstram.

*avanē …* – Though he is having the arrow which can use the water of the ocean as ghee to light up and burn, he went as a messenger having a palm leaf around his neck as if he is helpless.

*ādi mannarkkāgi* – Though duryōdana et al were ruling the kingdom, āḻvār is saying pāṇḍavas to be the kings, since they are the rightful owners of the kingdom and duryōdana et al grabbed the kingdom as one would climb a reclining elephant without its permission. Just as a brāhmaṇa would show the proper documents to make a rightful king rule the kingdom when unqualified persons take over the kingdom, āḻvār, due to īśvara’s opinion, is saying pāṇḍavas to be “*ādi mannar*“.

*innār tūdan ena ninṟān* – He remained to be called by both great or insignificant people as “*innār tūdan ena ninṟān*“. He sustained himself by hearing that name of “*pāṇḍava tūdan*“. He sustained himself by the name “*pāṇḍava tūdan*” as someone who does not have a great family heritage or deeds will seek some greatness. This became the identity for him instead of identifying him with his family heritage, deeds etc. This is similar to saying “this person sustained himself with food”, “wall stands due to the soil”. If he gets anyone who will praise him based on his subservience towards devotees, he will be nourished without even eating.

*evvuḷ kidandānē* – There is good water source in this region. As we have devotees who will engage me for my tasks, he firmly reclined there thinking that he will not leave that abode.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2.4. Pandanainda

*pandaṇainda mel viralāḷ pāvai tan kāraṇattāl vendiṟal ēṟēḻum venṟa vēndan viripugaḻ sēr nandan maindanāga āgum nambi namperumān endai tandai tam perumān evvuḷ kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pandu – ball; aṇainda – having; mel – tender; viralāḷ – having fingers; pāvai than kāraṇattāl – to attain nappinnaip pirātti who has natural femininity; vem – cruel; tiṟal – strong; ēṟu ēḻum – seven bulls; venṟa – killed; vēndan – being the king; viri – well known; pugaḻ sēr – having fame; nandan maindanāga – being śrī nandagōpa’s divine son; āgum – placing himself; nambi – being full in all auspicious qualities; nam perumān – being our lord; endai tandai tam perumān – lord for our clan starting with me, my father and his father; evvuḷ kidandānē – reclined in tiruvevvuḷ

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Placing himself as śrī nandagōpa’s divine son with well known fame, being the king, \[emperumān\] killed seven cruel, strong bulls to attain nappinnaip pirātti who has natural femininity having tender fingers which are holding on to a ball; being full in all auspicious qualities, being our lord, the lord for our clan starting with me, my father and his father, reclined in tiruvevvuḷ.

*pandu …* – Again āḻvār reminisces kriṣṇāvatāram. Holding on to the ball to remain attractive for kriṣṇa, but she is having very tender fingers to even hold it. To attain nappinnaip pirātti who has natural femininity.

*vem tiṟal …* – As she is not born in kśatriya clan, he cannot use bow and arrow to kill. Hence he won over the bulls according to the rules of their clan \[by wresting with them\]. Killing the bulls, he became the king of that clan.

*viri pugaḻ sēr nandan* – When someone else (vasudēva and dēvaki) performed penance, he \[nandagōpan\] became famous to enjoy the result of being with kriṣṇa as said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.1.3 “*edutta pērāḷan*” (the great ruler who got kriṣṇa as his child).

*āgum* – He came to exist as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*santamēnam*” (to be existing) only after becoming the divine son of śrī nandagōpa, to eliminate the defect of being tāntōnṟi (unborn from anyone) without a father.

*maindanāga āgum* – \[periyavāccān piḷḷai explains the following pāsuram\] periya tirumoḻi 10.4.8 “*undam adigaḷ munivar*” yaśōdāp pirātti would say these words to threaten kriṣṇa; since she is his mother, she won’t scold him; hence, your father will scold you. “*unnai*” – You who are so mischievous and cannot be tolerated. “*nān …*” – Showing the stick in her hand, she would say “Look at this, it keeps saying ‘kriṣṇa’ repeatedly, looking for you”; I can use this to beat you to cause pain to you; but I am unable to do so.

*nambi* – Though he is present with all auspicious qualities in śrivaikuṇṭam, only after taking birth in this samsāra and standing in a humble manner, he became complete.

*nam perumān* – Our lord. The lord of our clan.

*evvuḷ kidandānē* – Instead of having to pack food for the journey to parampadam, to see emperumān who is all types of relatives to us, he has reclined in tiruvevvuḷ to fulfil the responsibilities as relatives to him.

## 2.2.5. Balanagi

*bālanāgi jñālam ēḻum uṇḍu paṇḍu ālilai mēl sāla nāḷum paḷḷi koḷḷum tāmaraik kaṇṇan eṇṇil neelamār vaṇḍuṇḍu vāḻum neydal andaṇ kaḻani ēla nāṟum paimbuṟavil evvuḷ kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

bālanāgi – as a small child; jñālam ēḻum – seven worlds; uṇḍu – consumed; paṇḍu – during the deluge; ālilai mēl – on a banyan leaf; sāla nāḷum – very long time; paḷḷi koḷḷum – mercifully rested; eṇ il – inconceivable; tāmaraik kaṇṇan – lotus-eyed sarvēśvaran; neelam – blue coloured; vaṇḍu – beetles; neydal – in water-lily; Ar – being seated; uṇḍu – drinking (the honey on it); vāḻum – living; am – beautiful; taṇ – cool; kaḻani – fertile fields; Elam – fragrance; nāṟum – blowing; pai – vast; puṟavil – having gardens outside; evvuḷ kidandān – reclined in tiruvevvuḷ

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Lotus-eyed sarvēśvaran, being inconceivable, being a small child, consumed seven worlds, and mercifully rested on a banyan leaf during the deluge; he has reclined in tiruvevvuḷ which is having fragrant, vast gardens outside, and beautiful, cool, fertile fields where blue coloured beetles, seated in water-lily and drinking the honey in it, are living.

*bālanāgi …* – Being a very young, nursing toddler \[who is so tender that even by slight touch, their skin will ooze blood\], in that young state, held all the worlds in his stomach.

*paṇḍu* – In that time of deluge when there is none to care for him, on a fresh banyan leaf.

*sāla* – Even yaśōdā et al were not there to care for him thinking “the child is sleeping at odd times, what is he doing?” and to wake him up.

*eṇṇil* – Joining the un-joinable aspects. If we start thinking about it, it will be impossible to do so.

*neelam …* – The coastal region where beetles are living, drinking the honey in water-lily flowers. Alternative explanation – neydal – water-lily.  The beetles which are living on the blue coloured flowers, are drinking honey from the water-lily flower. Another explanation – having beautiful, cool, fertile fields where blue coloured beetles are drinking honey from water-lily flower.

*Elam …* – In the abode which has very fragrant surroundings, the one who can do miracles, is mercifully resting; those who wake him up and get his help are only lacking.

## 2.2.6. Sotta nambi

*sōtta nambi enṟu toṇḍar miṇḍit todarndu aḻaikkum ātta nambi sengaṇambi āgilum dēvarkkellām mūtta nambi mukkaṇambi enṟu munivar toḻudu ēttum nambi emperumān evvuḷ kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

toṇḍar – śrīvaiṣṇavas who are ananyaprayōjanas (those who don’t expect any benefit other than kainkaryam\]; miṇḍi – densely gather; nambi – Oh one who is complete with all auspicious qualities!; sōttam enṟu – saying “we worship you”; todarndu – continuously; aḻaikkum – those who praise; āttan nambi – one who is complete in being most trustworthy; sengan nambi – is complete with the beauty of his reddish eyes; āgilum – though he is like this; dēvarkku ellām – for all the dēvatās; mūtta nambi – for brahmā who was born before; mukkaṇ nambi – saying “one who remains as antaryāmi of rudra who has three eyes”; munivar – sages such as sanaka et al; toḻudu – surrender; ēttum – to praise; nambi – one who is complete; emperumān – my lord; evvuḷ kidandānē – is reclining in tiruvevvuḷ

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

śrīvaiṣṇavas who are ananyaprayōjanas densely gather saying “Oh one who is complete with all auspicious qualities! We worship you” and continuously praise emperumān who is complete in being most trustworthy and is complete with the beauty of his reddish eyes; though he is like this, sages such as sanaka et al surrender and praise saying “one who remains as antaryāmi of brahmā who was born before all the dēvatās, and rudra who has three eyes”; my complete lord is reclining in tiruvevvuḷ.

*sōttam* – The words which are recited by humble persons, to surrender unto him and make him shower his mercy. The trustworthy lord who is called out by vaiṣṇavas who will jostle and say along the lines of “Oh one who is the abode of all auspicious qualities! We worship you”.

*nambi* – One who remains without any shortcoming due to being most trustworthy.

When asked “Who is that person who remains like this?” āḻvār says,

*sem kaṇ nambi* – He is well known through śāstram that he is puṇḍarīkākśa (lotus-eyed) as said in viṣṇu darmam 99.27 “*yajñēśa: yajña puruśa: puṇḍarīkākśa samjhita:*” (One who is vorśipped in yajñas; one who accepts the offerings of yajña; one who is known as lotus eyed).

*āgilum* – Though he is like this.

*dēvar …* – Being the antaryāmi for four-headed brahmā who is born before  all dēvatās and for rudra who has an extra eye on his forehead, the one who is praised by sanaka et al as the one who is performing sruśti etc. Thus, though he is having distinguished, divine form and is totally distinct from all other entities, he remains as antaryāmi for brahmā et al and performs creation etc and is praised by sanaka et al; such emperumān is reclining in tiruvevvuḷ.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2.7. Tingal appu

*tingaḷ appu vān eri kālāgi tisai muganār tangaḷ appan sāmiyappan pāgattirundu vaṇḍuṇ tongalappu neeṇmudiyān sūḻkaḻal sūdaṇinṟa engaḷ appan emperumān evvuḷ kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tingaḷ – moon; appu – water; vān – ether; eri – fire; kāl – air, these four elements; āgi – having as body (being the śarīri); tisai muganār tangaḷ – for four-headed brahmā; appan – being the father; sāmi – one who is revealed in sāma vēdam; appan – being the cause; vaṇḍu – beetles; uṇ – drinking honey; tongal – konṟai garland; appu – gangā water; nīḷ – lengthy; mudi – having in his matted hair; bāgattu – in one side of emperumān’s divine form; irundān – rudra who is present; sūḻ – spreading everywhere in earth; kaḻal – divine feet; sūda – to decorate (the head); ninṟa – one who stood; engaḷ appan – being our father; emperumān – one who is our lord; evvuḷ kidandānē – reclined in tiruvevvuḷ

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Having the moon and four elements water, ether, fire and air as body, being the father for the four-headed brahmā, being the one who is revealed in sāma vēdam, being the cause; being the one whose divine feet which were spread everywhere in earth, stood to decorate the head of rudra who is wearing konṟai garland where beetles are drinking honey from, and who is having lengthy matted hair where gangā water is present, and who is present in one side of emperumān’s divine form; being our father and our lord, he reclined in tiruvevvuḷ.

*tingaḷ …* – Identifying the moon as a sample for effectual entities and the four elements as samples for pancabhūtams (the five great elements) which are causal, saying that emperumān is standing as antaryāmi for all of these. And, he is the father for four-headed brahmā as well.

*sāmi appan* – The causal lord, who is revealed in sāma vēdam.

*bāgattu …* – bhagavān stood there to have rudra who is with the matted hair which is having both konṟai garland where beetles are drinking honey from and gangā water, and is present in a small portion of the divine form of bhagavān, to hold his expanded divine feet on the head.

*engaḷ …* – One who is our father and lord.

## 2.2.8. Munivan murtti

*munivan mūrtti mūvarāgi vēdam viritturaitta punidan pūvai vaṇṇan aṇṇal puṇṇiyan viṇṇavar kōn taniyan sēyan tān oruvan āgilum tan adiyārkku iniyan endai emperumān evvuḷ kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

munivan – one who vowed to create; mūrtti mūvar āgi – being brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra; vēdam – meanings of vēdam; virittu – to make everyone know; uraitta – one who mercifully explained in śrī gītā; punidan – having purity; pūvai – like kāyām pū (dark coloured flower); vaṇṇan – having divine complexion; aṇṇal – being lord; puṇṇiyan – being greatly magnanimous; viṇṇavar – for nityasūris; kōn – being the leader; taniyan – being matchless; sēyan – being difficult to be known even by yōgis; tān oruvan āgilum – though he remains distinguished (in this manner); than adiyārkku – for those who are surrendered unto him; iniyan – being good; endai – being my father; emperumān – being my lord; evvuḷ kidandānē – reclined in tiruvevvuḷ

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being the one who vowed to create, being brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra, one who mercifully explained in śrī gītā to make everyone know the meanings of vēdam, having purity, having kāyām pū like divine complexion, being the lord, being greatly magnanimous, being the leader for nityasūris, being matchless, though he remains distinguished, being difficult to be known even by yōgis, he remains good for those who are surrendered unto him; being my father and lord, he reclined in tiruvevvuḷ.

*munivan …* – When all the ātmās (sentient entities) in samsāra were devoid of body and senses, and were having no option for enjoyment or liberation, and had lost the effectual state, emperumān vowed in his divine heart as in cāndōjña upaniśat “*bahusyām*” (let me become many). Further, he remained as antarātmā (in-dwelling soul) as brahmā and rudra, and also remained in his own self as viṣṇu, and engaged in creation etc. One who revealed the meanings of vēdam explicitly. That is – he mercifully explained śrī gītā which is vēda upabruhmaṇam (explanation for vēdams).

*punidan* – As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 5.29](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/5-29/) “*suhrudam sarva bhūtānām*” (friend for all), the purity which is acquired by being unselfish and looking for the well-being of others only, is explained.

*pūvai vaṇṇan* – His divine, beautiful form is such that one cannot give him up even if he leaves aside the good advice and gives bad advice.

*aṇṇal* – Lord

*puṇṇiyan* – Greatly magnanimous.

*viṇṇavarkōn* – The lord of nityasūris who are free from ignorance.

*taniyan* – One who is distinguished from nityasūris too.

*sēyan* … – One who is much greater than them. Though he is matchless in this manner, he is good to those who surrender unto him. My father and lord.

## 2.2.9. Pandirukkum

*pandirukkum mel viralāḷ pāvai panimalarāḷ vandirukkum mārvan neela mēni maṇivaṇṇan andarattil vāḻum vānōr nāyaganāy amainda indiraṟkum tamperumān evvuḷ kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pandu – ball; irukkum – present; mel – tender; viralāḷ – having fingers; pani – cool; malarāḷ – having lotus flower as her birth place; pāvai – periya pirāttiyār who is having femininity with shyness, innocence, fear, humility; vandu – arriving from that flower; irukkum – eternally residing; mārvan – having the divine chest; neelam – like a dark kuvaḷai flower; mēni – having physical beauty; maṇi – like a gem; vaṇṇan – having the nature of simplicity; andarattil – in svargam (heaven); vāḻum – living; vānōr – for dēvatās; nāyaganāy – being the leader; amainda – who is present; indiraṟkum – for indra too; perumān – one who is the lord; evvuḷ kidandānē – is reclining in tiruvevvuḷ

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

periya pirāttiyār who is having femininity with shyness, innocence, fear, humility, who is holding a ball with her tender fingers, having lotus flower as her birth place, is arriving at the divine chest of emperumān from that flower, and is eternally residing there; such emperumān, having dark kuvaḷai flower like physical beauty, having the nature of simplicity like that of a gem, being the lord for indra who is present as the leader for the dēvatās living in heaven, is reclining in tiruvevvuḷ.

*pandu irukkum* … – Due to not having the sorrow of separation ever, having a ball in the hand, and being unable to tolerate even that, the tender fingers have become reddish; one who is having natural femininity; one who has the cool lotus flower as her birth place.

*vandu irukkum …* – Considering such flower to be a thorn, she was unable to stand the heat there and hence came and eternally resided in the divine heart of emperumān as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn*” (I will never leave). One who has a divine form which resembles a blue gem.

*andarattil …* – This can be an adjective for sarvēśvaran \[he is the lord of all the dēvatās and the lord of indra\]; alternative explanation – lord for indra who is the present as the leader of all dēvatās. Even indra depends on bhagavān for his wealth and control.

## 2.2.10. Indai kondu

*iṇḍai koṇḍu toṇḍar ētta evvuḷ kidandānai vaṇḍu pādum paimbuṟavil mangaiyar kōn kaliyan koṇḍa seerāl taṇ tamiḻ sey mālai īraindum vallār aṇḍam āḷvadu āṇai anṟēl āḷvar amarulagē*

**Пословный перевод:**

iṇḍai – flower garlands; koṇḍu – offering at the divine feet; toṇḍar – śrīvaiṣṇavas; ētta – to be praised by; evvuḷ – in tiruvevvuḷ; kidandānai – on the one who mercifully rested; vaṇḍu – beetles; pādum – humming; pai – vast; puṟavil – having surrounding areas; mangaiyar kōn – the king of the residents of tirumangai region; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; koṇḍa sīr – his auspicious qualities which are held in the heart; taṇ – wet (compassionate); tamiḻāl – in tamiḻ language; sey – mercifully spoke; mālai – in the form of a garland; īraindum – these ten pāsurams; vallār – those who can learn; aṇḍam – this oval shaped universe under the control of brahmā; āḷvadu – ruling over; āṇai – is certain; anṟēl – if that is not desired; amar ulagu – paramapadam; āḷvar – will get to rule

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār, the king of the tirumangai region which is having vast surrounding areas where beetles are humming, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams about the auspicious qualities of emperumān which are held in his heart. emperumān has mercifully rested in tiruvevvuḷ to be praised by śrīvaiṣṇavas by offering flower garlands at his divine feet; those who can learn this decad are certain to rule over this oval shaped universe under the control of brahmā; if that is not desired, they will get to rule paramapadam.

*iṇḍai* … – For the śrīvaiṣṇavas to offer flower garlands and live in tiruvevvuḷ serving the emperumān who has mercifully rested there. Such emperumān is being praised here. Just as muktātmās will sing sāmagānam, the beetles having drunk honey, will keep humming in the vast areas which surround tirumangai region – āḻvār who is the king of such tirumangai.

*koṇḍa seerāl …* – sīr – decoration for a poem; that is said here. Alternative explanation – as emperumān came and reclined here, his qualities remained firmly in āḻvār’s heart, and due to their impelling, the garland of words which could not be controlled in āḻvār’s heart was thus spoken. Those who learned this decad will certainly rule the aṇḍam.

*anṟēl* … – If one is detached thinking “Even after surrendering unto him, will we desire to rule this world?”, they will rule over parampadam.

## 2.3 Virperu vilavum

## 2.3.1. Virperu vilavum

*viṟperu viḻavum kanjanum mallum vēḻamum pāganum vīḻac ceṟṟavan tannai purameri seyda sivanuṟu tuyar kaḷai dēvai paṟṟalar vīyak kōl kaiyil koṇḍu pārttan tan tēr mun ninṟānaic ciṟṟavai paṇiyāl mudi tuṟandānait tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vil peru viḻavum – the great festival of danur yāgam (ritual with bow); kanjanum – kamsa; mallum – the wrestlers such as cāṇūra, muśtika et al; vēḻamum – the elephant named kuvalayāpeedam; pāganum – its mahout; vīḻa – to fall down; seṟṟavan tannai – being the one who destroyed; puram eri seyda – one who burnt tripuram (the three towns); sivan – rudran; uṟu – acquired; tuyar – the suffering due to harming his teacher (brahmā); kaḷai – eliminated; dēvai – being the lord; paṟṟalar – enemies; vīya – to be destroyed; kōl – thorny stick; kaiyil – in his hand; koṇḍu – holding; pārttan than – arjunan’s; tēr mun – in front of the chariot; ninṟānai – being the one who stood as the charioteer; siṟṟavai – step-mother kaikēyi’s; paṇiyāl – obeying the words; mudi – crown (which is to be given during coronation); tuṟandānai – śrī pārtasāraty who well abandoned; tiruvallikkēṇi – in tiruvallikkēṇi; kaṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān destroyed the great festival of danur yāgam, kamsa, the wrestlers such as cāṇūra, muśtika et al, the elephant named kuvalayāpeedam and its mahout to fall down; being the lord, he eliminated the suffering of rudran which he acquired due to harming his teacher; being the one who stood as the charioteer in front of arjunan’s chariot, holding the thorny stick in his hand, he got the enemies to be destroyed; obeying the words of his step-mother kaikēyi, he clearly abandoned the crown; I got to see such śrī pārtasāraty emperumān in tiruvallikkēṇi.

*vil peru viḻavum …* – Since kamsa was planning to kill his enemy, he planned it in a grand manner; kamsa who planned such event, the fierce wrestlers who are his strength and who resemble bouncing mountains, the intoxicated elephant which was placed on the way and which would continuously harm the enemy even if the wrestlers miss the opportunity, the mahout who can bring it back to life even if it was killed.

*vīḻac ceṟṟavan tannai* – The actions were so quick that all the tasks were done at once in a flash.

*puram …* – rudran who became prideful due to his act of burning down the three towns, became a sinner by severing the head his father and the teacher of the world (brahmā); emperumān eliminated that thinking “a respectable person cannot remain to be looked down upon”, and by that revealed to everyone that he is the saviour for all. mātsya purāṇam 182 “*tatra nārāyaṇa: śrīmān mayābhikśām prayācita: …* ” (That śrīman nārāyaṇa was asked for alms by me; by his mercy the skull which got stuck to my hand broke into many pieces). *viṣṇu prasādāt –* by the mercy of sarvēśvaran. *suśrōṇi* – rudran said “As I surrendered unto him, your beauty has become purposeful”.

*paṟṟalar …* – paṟṟalar – enemies; to have them destroyed; since he said “I won’t take up arms”, he used the thorny stick which is used to conduct the horses.

*pārttan than tēr mun ninṟānai* – When one shows anger on the rati (the owner of the chariot), one will try to kill the charioteer first. kriṣṇa placed arjuna behind self and made himself the target of the arrows and stood there.

*siṟṟavai paṇiyāl mudi tuṟandānai* – One who abandoned the crown which is apt for him, due to the word of his step-mother. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdya kāṇḍam 19.24 “*na nūnam mayi kaikēyi*” – kaikēyi revealed the heart of cakravarti “cakravarti is unable to speak now, he gave the kingdom to your brother and he is thinking to send you in exile to forest”; hearing that śrī rāma said “Oh middle mother! I thought I have served your divine feet well; since you are thinking that I don’t have noble qualities, you are saying it as father’s words instead of your own words”. He further said “I think of you on a par with father. I think about father as īśvara and you as some one on a par with īśvara”.

*vil peru viḻavum …* – In tiruvallikkēṇi, I got to see the one who completely eliminates the group of enemies, who will eliminate the struggles of those who consider themselves to be lords, who will transform himself for the sake of those who are dear to him, and who will obey the orders of even those who pretend to be loving towards him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.3.2. Vedattai

*vēdattai vēdattin suvaip payanai viḻumiya munivar viḻungum kōdil in kaniyai nandanār kaḷiṟṟaik kuvalayattōr toḻudēttum ādiyai amudai ennai āḷudai appanai oppavarillā mādargaḷ vāḻum mādamā mayilait tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēdattai – one who has vēdam as his wealth; suvai – matching the taste (of the devotees); vēdattin – for karmānuśtānams \[observance of deeds\] mentioned in vēdam; payanai – being the one who bestows the results; viḻumiya – great; munivar – sages such as sanaka et al; viḻungum – enjoying; kōdu il – faultless; in – sweet; kaniyai – very enjoyable like a fruit; nandanār – for śrī nandagōpa; kaḷiṟṟai – being the one who is enjoyable like an elephant calf; kuvalayattōr – residents of earth; toḻudu – surrendered; ēttum – praising; ādiyai – the cause of the universe; amudai – sweet like nectar; ennai āḷudai – who enslaved me; appanai – benefactor; oppavar – matching; illā – not having; mādargaḷ – women; vāḻum – living; mādam – having mansions; mā – rich; mayilai – having mylāpūr as capital; tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē – I got to see in tiruvallikkēṇi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān has vēdam as his wealth; he is the one who bestows the results for karmānuśtānams mentioned in vēdam matching the taste of the devotees; he is very enjoyable like a faultless, sweet fruit, who is enjoyed by great sages such as sanaka et al; he is enjoyable like an elephant calf for śrī nandagōpa; he is the cause of the universe; he is surrendered unto and praised by the residents of earth; he is sweet like nectar; he is the benefactor who enslaved me; I got see such emperumān in tiruvallikkēṇi, which is part of the region having rich mylāpūr as the capital city, having mansions where matchless women are living.

*vēdattai* – One who is having vēdam which gives good advice to everyone as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.45](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-45/) “*traiguṇya viśayā vēdā:*” (vēdams which are focussed on the well-being of the ones having the three qualities), as his wealth.

*vēdattin suvaip payanai* … – One who bestows results for those who perform the karmas (actions) mentioned in vēdam, with satva (goodness), rajō (passion) and tamō (ignorance) guṇam (qualities), according to their taste. One who is greatly enjoyable for sanaka et al who are focussed on brahmam only, unlike those who are in karma bhāvanā (focussed on karmam only) or ubhaya bhāvanā (focussed on both karmam and brahmam).

*nandanār kaḷiṟṟai* – One who is very enjoyable for śrī nandagōpa due to his super-human activities.

*kuvalayattōr …* – As said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*kāraṇam tu dyēya:*” (meditate upon the origin/cause), one who is the cause of the universe, to be vorśipped by the residents of the universe.

*amudai …* – The attainable goal for them. The benefactor who enslaved me who is lower than even such worldly people.

*oppavar illā …* – Since this divyadēśam has prime importance for pirātti as said in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 16](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/munram-thiruvandhadhi-16/) “*oruvallitt tāmaraiyāḷ onṟiya sīr mārvan*” (one who has beautiful divine heart in which pirātti who has the incomparable lotus flower which has beautiful petals as her dwelling place, fitted nicely), the women of this town are associates of such pirātti. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.8.35 “*nānayōr vidyatē param*” (There is nothing greater than the divine couple), her wealth and īśvara’s wealth remain as two parts. mylāpūr is the name of the city \[which has tiruvallikkēṇi inside it\]

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.3.3. Vanjanai seyya

*vanjanai seyyat tāyuruvāgi vanda pēy alaṟi maṇ sēra nanjamar mulaiyūdu uyir sega uṇḍa nādanait tānavar kūṟṟai vinjai vānavar sāraṇar sittar viyantudi seyyap peṇṇuruvāgi anjuvai amudam anṟaḷittānait tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vanjanai seyya – to cheat (kriṣṇa); tāy uruvāgi vanda – came disguising in the form of the mother; pēy – pūtanā; alaṟi – to cry out; maṇ – on earth; sēra – to fall; nanju amar – filled with poison; mulai ūdu – through the bosom; uyir – (her) vital air (life); sega – to leave; uṇḍa – mercifully consumed; nādanai – being sarvaśēśi (lord of all); dānavar – for demons; kūṟṟai – being death; vinjai vānavar – vidyādaras (celestial people); sāraṇar – cāraṇas (celestial people); sittar – siddas (celestial people) et al; viyandu – being amazed; tudi seyya – to praise; peṇ uruvu āgi – assuming a feminine form; anṟu – when indra had lost his wealth; am – beautiful; suvai – having taste; amudam – nectar; aḷittānai – one who gave to dēvatās; tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē – saw in tiruvallikkēṇi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

pūtanā came to cheat kriṣṇa, the sarvaśēśi, disguising in the form of \[kriṣṇa’s\] mother, cried out and fell on earth, after he made her life leave her by mercifully consuming it through her poison-filled bosom; he is death for demons; to be seen with amazement and be praised by vidyādaras, cāraṇās, siddas, emperumān assumed a feminine form, and gave beautiful, tasty nectar to dēvatās when indra had lost his wealth; I saw such emperumān in tiruvallikkēṇi.

*vanjanai …* – emperumān who consumed the life of pūtanā through her poison filled bosom, where the deceitful one assumed a feminine form to cheat him, and caused her to cry out and fall on earth.

*nādanai …* – One who saved and gave himself when he killed pūtanā who came in disguise of a contradictory form, to kill self  who is the life of the universe. harivamśam “*stanyam tat viśasammiśram rasyamāsīt jagatgurō:*” (her breast-milk which was poisoned, was very sweet for him).

*dānavar kūṟṟai* … – One who is death personified for demons. One who fed the dēvatās with a feminine form that does not match puruśōttama (best among men) and remained to be praised by vidyādaras, cāraṇas, siddas et al in amazement.

## 2.3.4. Indiranukku enru

*indiranukkenṟu āyargaḷ edutta eḻil viḻavil paḻa nadaisey mandira vidiyil pūsanai peṟādu maḻai poḻindidat taḷarndu āyar endammōdu ina ānirai taḷarāmal emperumān! aruḷ enna andamil varaiyāl maḻai taduttānait tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

indiranukku enṟu – to offer feast for indra; āyargaḷ – covherds; edutta – vowed; eḻil – beautiful; viḻavil – in the festival of sacrifice; paḻa nadai sey – as per previous practice; mandira vidiyil – as per mantrams; pūsanai peṟādu – due to not getting vorśipped; maḻai – hale; poḻindida – made it rain; āyar – covherds; taḷarndu – became sad; emperumān – Oh our lord!; endammōdu – with us; inam – herds of; ānirai – herds of cow; taḷarāmal – to not suffer; aruḷ – mercifully protect; enna – as they prayed; andam il – immeasurable; varaiyāl – by gōvardana mountain; maḻai – that rain; taduttānai – one who stopped; tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē – saw in tiruvallikkēṇi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

indra did not get vorśipped as per previous practice with mantrams in the beautiful festival of sacrifice which was vowed to be celebrated with offering of a feast; he became angry and sent a rain of hale to cause sadness to the covherds; as they prayed “Oh our lord! Mercifully protect us along with our herds and herds of cows, to not let us suffer”; I saw such emperumān who stopped that rain with the immeasurable gōvardana mountain, in tiruvallikkēṇi.

*indiran …* – Every year, the residents of tiruvāyppādi (gōkulam), would give a grand feast to indran, the lord of three worlds, for the sake of proper rain. kriṣṇa thought “In the town where I am born and living, just as a dog eats the offering placed for a sacrifice, how can a dēvatā come and consume food here?” and asked them “What are you doing?” They said “We are offering a feast to indra for the sake of rain”. He said “īsn’t it this gōvardana hill which gives shade to us and our cows, and also offers grass? When one entity helps should we show gratitude to someone else? Just offer to the hill”; can anyone refuse anything from kriṣṇa when he looks at the face and tells? Hence, they gathered all the food and mounted that in front of the hill.

*indiran …* – In the beautiful festival of sacrifice performed by covherds for indra, as he did not receive the worship as per previous practice with mantrams; he became angry due to hunger and caused hale; due to that, the covherds suffered and said “you mercifully protect us who are the protectors of cows and the herds of cows to not suffer”. With this, it is said that the protector – protected relationship in the world is of no use \[bhagavān is the protector and everyone else is protected\].

*andam il …* – Blocking that hale with the mountain which is bigger than the hale. Similarly, one who descended to eliminate the rain of samsāra for me as said in [stōtra ratnam 49](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/sthothra-rathnam-49/) “*santata du:kha varśiṇi*” (pouring down sorrows continuously).

## 2.3.5. Indunaip padumattu

*induṇaip padumattu alarmagaḷ tanakkum inban naṟpuvi tanakku iṟaivan tanduṇai āyar pāvai nappinnai tanakku iṟai maṟṟaiyōrkku ellām vanduṇai panja pāṇḍavarkkāgi vāyurai tūdu senṟu iyangum enduṇai endai tandai tammānait tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

in – sweet (for his heart); tuṇai – being a companion; padumam – one who has lotus flower as birth place; alar magaḷ tanakkum – for periya pirāttiyār; inban – being enjoyable; nal – one who forbears everything; puvi tanakku – for śrī bhūmip pirātti; iṟaivan – being dear; than tuṇai – having him as the only companion; āyar pāvai – covherd girl; nappinnai tanakku – for nappinnaip pirātti; iṟai – being the lord; maṟṟaiyōrkku ellām – for everyone else; val tuṇai – being a strong companion; panja pāṇḍavarkku – for panca pāṇḍavas; āgi – assuming all types of relationships; vāy urai – their words; senṟu – informed to duryōdana et al; en tuṇai – being a friend in need for people like me; endai tandai tammānai – the lord of my clan; tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē – I saw in tiruvallikkēṇi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is enjoyable for periya pirāttiyār who is his sweet companion and has lotus flower as birth place; is dear to śrī bhūmip pirātti who forbears everything; is dear to nappinnaip pirātti, the covherd girl who is having him as the only companion; is a strong companion for everyone else; assuming all types of relationships for panca pāṇḍavas, he informed their words to duryōdana et al by mercifully going as a divine messenger; he is a friend in need for people like me and is the lord of my clan; I saw such emperumān in tiruvallikkēṇi.

*in tuṇai …* – Being a sweet companion for the heart, there is a girl who is associated with lotus flower – that is periya pirāttiyār who is born in lotus flower; emperumān is enjoyable for her.

*tanakkum \[for her\]* – He is desirable for periya pirāttiyār who is desired by everyone, and who says as in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn*” (I will not leave) and will stay with him without leaving.

*nal puvi …* – He is dear to śrī bhūmip pirātti who is the teacher for patience to such sarvēśvaran himself.

*than tuṇai …* – Being the lord of the covherd girl who considers him as the only companion, that is, for nappinnaip pirātti.

*maṟṟaiyōrkku …* – Due to the aforementioned reasons, he is the strong companion for everyone else.

*panca …* – For pāṇḍavas who are his devotees, going to duryōdana et al and informing the message of pāṇḍavas, and returning with their message, and announced to me, his companionship by his humble disposition towards his devotees.

*endai* – Being my lord and the leader of my clan.

## 2.3.6. Andagan siruvan

*andagan siṟuvan arasar tam arasaṟkiḷaiyavan aṇiyiḻaiyaic cenṟu endamakku urimai sey enat tariyādu emperumān! aruḷ enna sandamal kuḻalāḷ alakkaṇ nūṟṟuvar tam peṇḍirum eydi nūl iḻappa indiran siṟuvan tēr mun ninṟānait tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

andagan – dritarāśtra, the blind man, his; siṟuvan – being the son; arasar tam arasaṟku – duryōdana, the king of kings; iḷaiyavan – brother duśśāsanan; aṇi – decorated; iḻaiyai – towards draupadi who is having ornaments; senṟu – went (since they lost you as well, to us in gambling); endamakku – for us; urimai sey – serve us; ena – as he told; dariyādu – being unable to bear (to have servitude towards others); emperumān! – “My lord!”; aruḷ – you should shower your mercy upon me and protect me; enna – as she prayed; al – dark; sandam – coloured; kuḻalāḷ – draupadi who has hair, her; alakkaṇ – sorrow; nūṟṟuvar tam – duryōdanan’s brothers, totally hundred in number, their; peṇḍirum – wives; eydi – attained; nūl – mangaḷasūtram; iḻappa – to lose; indiran siṟuvan – indra’s son arjuna, his; tēr mun – in front of the chariot; ninṟānai – stood and donned the role of charioteer; tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē – I saw in tiruvallikkēṇi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

duśśāsana, the brother of duryōdana, the king of kings who is the son of dritarāśtra, the blind man went to draupadi who is decorated with ornaments and told her “you serve us”; being unable to bear that, draupadi who has dark coloured hair, prayed to emperumān “My lord! You should shower your mercy upon me and protect me”. emperumān stood in front of the chariot of indra’s son arjuna and donned the role of charioteer, and made the wives of duryōdana and his brothers to go through the same sorrow as draupadi and lose their mangaḷasūtram. I saw such emperumān in tiruvallikkēṇi.

*andagan siṟuvan* – duryōdana was the son of the blind dritarāstra. With this, it is said that the ignorance is carried forward. One who was raised independently instead of being raised under the fear for a good father.

*arasar …* – One who is born after duryōdana, who is the kings of kings. That is duśśāsana. āḻvār is highlighting the wicked nature of duśśāsana who was pampered by duryōdana.

*aṇi iḻaiyai* – Since it is a great festive occasion, draupadi was well decorated with ornaments. duśśāsana approached her.

*endamakku urimai seyyena* – He said “pāṇḍavas lost you as well in the gambling game. You should come and serve us”.

*dariyādu …* – She cannot bear serving others. At that time, she prayed to emperumān “You who are my lord, should shower your mercy upon me”. When embār was asked “When the valorous husbands were present there, why is she calling upon the name of kriṣṇa, who is far away?” He replied “We know the answer! Looks like she was given instructions previously as said in mahābhāratam sabhā parvam 90.41 ‘*mahatyāpati samprāptē smartavyō bhagavān hari:’* (when you are in great danger, remember lord hari)” When the same questions was asked to bhattar, he mercifully replied “Though a woman walks along with her husband holding his hands, if she slips, she will naturally cry out ‘ammē’ (mother)”.

Though she prayed for her protection, he was so eager to punish duryōdana et al.

*sandamal kuḻalāḷ …* – sandam – colour. al – darkness. One who has dark coloured hair.

Alternatively,

*sandamak kuḻalāḷ* – One who has hair which always carries sandal flower. There is a sorrow which she endured. To make the wives of duryōdana et al go through the same suffering. As an ultimatum, they lost their mangaḷasūtram also. He ensured that they had permanent sorrow.

*indiran …* –  Implies that emperumān will reduce his stature and protect those who surrender unto him, though they may have strong support. draupadi was not helped by her husbands; arjuna was not helped by indra \[emperumān only helped both of them\].

## 2.3.7. Baradanum tambi

*baradanum tambi satturukkananum ilakkumanōdu maidiliyum iravum nanpagalum tudi seyya ninṟa irāvaṇāndaganai emmānai kuravamē kamaḻum kuḷir poḻilūdu kuyilodu mayilgaḷ ninṟāla iraviyin kadirgaḷ nuḻaidal seydaṟiyāt tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

baradanum – śrī bharatāḻvān; tambi – his younger brother; satturukkananum – śrī śatrugnāḻvān; ilakkumanōdu – with iḷaiyaperumāḷ (lakśmaṇa); maidiliyum – sītāp pirātti; iravum – in night; nal – distinguished (due to showing the entities); pagalum – in day; tudi seyya – to praise; ninṟa – one who is mercifully present; emmān – my lord; irāvaṇāndaganai – cakravartit tirumagan who killed rāvaṇan; kuravam – kurā flowers; kamaḻum – spreading fragrance; kuḷir – cool; poḻilūdu – in the garden; kuyilodu – with cuckoos (which are singing); mayilgaḷ – peacocks; ninṟu – standing along firmly; Ala – dancing; iraviyin kadirgaḷ – sun’s rays (due to the density of the garden); nuḻaidal seydaṟiyā – not knowing to enter; tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē – I saw in tiruvallikkēṇi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In tiruvallikkēṇi, in the cool garden where kurā flowers are spreading fragrance, cuckoos are singing and peacocks are dancing along, standing firm, where the sun’s rays are unable to penetrate inside due to the density of the garden, I saw my lord cakravartit tirumagan, who killed rāvaṇan, and is mercifully present, to be praised by śrī bharatāḻvān, younger brother śrī śatrugnāḻvān, iḷaiya perumāḷ and sītāp pirātti in the night and distinguished day.

*baradanum tambi satturukkananum* – śrī bharatāḻvān, and śrī śatrugnāḻvān who is totally surrendered to him.

*ilakkumanōdu maidiliyum* – This is a nice combination \[as both are totally surrendered to śrī rāma\].

*iravu nal pagalum* – Everyone will praise emperumān. That is – those who witnessed his valour during the war and those who heard about his valour from others. The leaders will gather in groups and praise him.

*iravu nal pagalum* … – We are used to praising him when we have free time. Unlike that, emperumān is of the nature that those who approach him will engage with him in day and night fully.

*irāvaṇāndaganai* … – They will praise the killing of rāvaṇa only; one who made me to praise him like them.

*kuravam …* – In the invigorating garden where kuravā flowers are spreading fragrance. Along with the cuckoos, the peacocks are also dancing joyfully.

*iraviyin …* – The abode where īśvara’s orders are not respected \[i.e. sun cannot enter\]. Where it is said in taittirīya upaniśat “*bhīśōdēti sūrya:*” (Sun fears bhagavān and does his work), this abode is excluded from that.

## 2.3.8. Palliyil odi

*paḷḷiyil ōdi vanda tan siṟuvan vāyil ōrāyira nāmam oḷḷiyavāgip pōda āngu adanukku onṟumōr poṟuppilanāgi piḷḷaiyaic cīṟi veguṇḍu tūṇ pudaippap piṟai eyiṟṟu anal viḻip pēḻvāy teḷḷiya singamāgiya dēvait tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paḷḷiyil – in school; ōdi – after studies; vanda – one who came to him; than siṟuvan – his son prahlādāḻvān, his; vāyil – divine lips; ōr āyira nāmam – (sarvēśvaran’s) one thousand divine names; oḷḷiyavāgi – beautifully; pōda – as it came towards him; āngu – there; adanukku – for reciting such emperumān’s divine names; onṟum ōr – even little bit; poṟuppu ilan āgi – not having tolerance; piḷḷaiyai – towards his son; sīṟi veguṇḍu – being very angry; tūṇ – the pillar (which was laid by himself); pudaippa – hit (in that); piṟai – like crescent; eyiṟu – teeth; anal – fire sparks emitting; viḻi – eyes; pēḻvāy – huge mouth; teḷḷiya – clear; singam āgiya – one who mercifully incarnated as narasimha; dēvai – lord; tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē – I saw in tiruvallikkēṇi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

prahlādāḻvān, the son of hiraṇyāsuran, returned after his studies in school and came to his father, with his divine lips reciting one thousand names of sarvēśvara; as those words beautifully came towards hiraṇya, unable to tolerate them, he became very angry and hit the pillar; I saw such emperumān who mercifully incarnated as clear narasimha with crescent like teeth and fire sparks emitting from his eyes and with huge mouth, in tiruvallikkēṇi.

*paḷḷiyil ōdi vanda than siṟuvan* – Whatever is recited by young students will be held on the head with respect. This is prahlādāḻvān’s age now. Further, whatever is spoken by one’s child should be tolerated.

*vāyil …* – Though he spoke a few names at that age, since his action was beyond his age, āḻvār lovingly says that he recited one thousand divine names.

*oḷḷiyavāgip pōda* – Since those are the words spoken by his own son, those words will be sweet.

*āngu* – There.

*adanukku onṟum ōr poṟuppilan āgi* – Whateve is spoken by a child in student stage will be dear; whatever is spoken by one’s own child will be sweet; prahlādāḻvān spoke those words which are to be held with reverence on one’s head, even if spoken by an enemy. Due to overwhelming asahyāpacāram (unbearable offence), he could not tolerate hearing the divine names and became very angry.

*piḷḷaiyai* – hiraṇya abandoned his own son just for reciting the divine name. āḻvār is \[lovingly\] saying piḷḷai (son) considering that recital of the divine name as the reason.

*veguṇḍu tūṇ pudaippa* – Knocking the pillar without knowing what to do, due to anger.

*piṟai …* – Having crescent like tooth, fire like eye and widely open mouth.

*teḷḷiya singam* – Being narasimha, without stepping back seeing the harsh form, through that revealed that he is the refuge.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.3.9. Minamar poygai

*mīnamar poygai nāḷmalar koyvān vētkaiyinōdu senṟiḻinda kānamar vēḻam kai eduttalaṟak karā adan kālinaik kaduva ānaiyin tuyaram tīrap puḷḷūrndu senṟu ninṟu āḻitottānait tēnamar sōlai mādamā mayilait tiruvallikkēṇik kandēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mīn amar poygai – in the pond filled with fish; nāḷ – freshly blossomed; malar – flowers; koyvān – to pluck; vētkaiynōdu – with desire; senṟu iḻinda – which came and entered; kān – in the forest; amar – which roams around freely; vēḻam – elephant; kai – its trunk; eduttu – lifted up; alaṟa – to cry out; karā – the crocodile; adan – its; kālinai – foot; kaduvu – as it caught (at that time); ānaiyin – śrī gajēndrāḻvān’s; tuyaram – sorrow; tīra – to go; puḷ ūrndu – riding on periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); senṟu – rushed; ninṟu – stood on the banks of the pond; āḻi tottānai – the lord who launched his tiruvāḻi (sudarśana cakram); tēn amar – always having beetles; sōlai – surrounded by gardens; māda mā mayilait tiruvallikkēṇik kaṇḍēnē – I saw in tiruvallikkēṇi which is in mylāpūr which has huge mansions

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

śrī gajēndrāḻvān, the elephant which roams around freely in the forest, desirously came and entered to pluck the freshly blossomed flowers in the pond filled with fish; as the crocodile caught the elephant’s foot, it lifted its trunk and cried out; I saw the lord who rushed riding on periya tiruvadi, stood on the banks of the pond and launched his tiruvāḻi to eliminate the sorrow of śrī gajēndrāḻvān, in tiruvallikkēṇi which is in mylāpūr which has huge mansions and is surrounded by gardens always having beetles.

*mīn amar …* – Searching for a flower for a long time and not getting it, it was anguished and roaming around searching for it, saw the pond with well-blossomed flowers; it desirously came and entered the pond without thinking about the evil crocodile more than the lowly fish, to pluck the fresh flower.

*kān amar vēḻam …* – The crocodile caught the foot of the elephant which was freely roaming around in the forest, only to end up crying out lifting up the trunk. The pond is natural habitat for the crocodile and foreign place for the elephant. emperumān rushed on periya tiruvadi and eliminated the sorrow endured by the elephant for a long time; he aimed at the crocodile and killed it without harming the elephant. I saw in tiruvallikkēṇi which is part of mylāpūr which is having huge mansions and is surrounded by gardens always having beetles.

## 2.3.10. Mannu tan

*mannu taṇ poḻilum vāviyum madiḷum māda māḷigaiyum maṇḍapamum tennan toṇḍaiyar kōn seyda nanmayilait tiruvallikkēṇi ninṟānaik kanni nanmāda mangaiyar talaivan kāmaru sīrk kali kanṟi sonna solmālai pattudan vallār sugam inidāḷvar vānulagē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mannu – eternally; taṇ – cool; poḻilum – gardens; vāviyum – water bodies; madiḷum – fortified streets; mādam – mansions; māḷigaiyum – multi-storeyed bungalows; maṇḍapamum – having halls; tennan – descendant of pāṇḍiya king; toṇḍaiyar – for the residents of toṇḍai nādu; kōn – the king, toṇḍaimān cakravarti; seyda – built; nal – beautiful; mayilait tiruvallikkēṇi – in tiruvallikkēṇi which is part of mylāppūr which is the capital city; ninṟānai – on the one who stood; kanni – as protection; nal – beautiful; mādam – having mansions; mangaiyar – for the residents of tirumangai region; talaivan – being the leader; kāmar – beautiful; sīr – having śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī (wealth of kainkaryam); kalikanṟi – āḻvār; sonna – mercifully sang; sol mālai – garland of words; pattudan – the ten pāsurams; vallār – those who can learn; inidu sugam – to have eternal experience; vānulagu – paramapadam; āḷvar – will reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is standing in beautiful tiruvallikkēṇi which is part of mylāppūr which is the capital city, which has eternally cool gardens, water bodies, fortified streets, mansions, multi-storeyed bungalows, halls, and is built by toṇḍaimān cakravarti, the descendant of pāṇḍiya king and is the king of the residents of toṇḍai nādu. tirumangai āḻvār, the leader of the residents of tirumangai region which is having beautiful mansions as protection, mercifully sang these ten pāsurams as a garland of words on such emperumān. Those who can learn these pāsurams will reach paramapadam to have eternal experience.

*mannu taṇ poḻilum …* – toṇḍaimān cakravarti built this divyadēśam with eternally cool gardens, water bodies, forts which give protection, mansions, multi-storeyed bungalows, halls, and other untold wonderful aspects.

*kanni …* – The leader of tirumangai which has mansions which give protection.

*kāmaru sīrk kalikanṟi* – Those who can learn and practice these ten pāsurams which are mercifully spoken by āḻvār who has beautiful śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī.

*sugam inidu āḷvar vānulagē* – Will reach nityavibhūti (paramapadam) where they can have eternal enjoyment.

## 2.4 Anrayar kulakkodi

## 2.4.1. Anrayar kulakkodi

*anṟāyar kulak kodiyōdu aṇimāmalar mangaiyodu anbaḷavi avuṇarkku endānum irakkam ilādavanukku uṟaiyum idamāvadu irumboḻil sūḻ nanṟāya punal naṟaiyūr tiruvāli kudandai tadam tigaḻ kōvalnagar ninṟān irundān kidandān nadandāṟku idam māmalaiyāvadu nīrmalaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – In kriṣṇāvatāram; āyar kulakkodiyōdu – with nappinnaip pirātti who is like a creeper for covherd clan; aṇi – beautiful; mā – best; malar mangaiyodu – with rukmiṇip pirātti who is an incarnation of periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi) who is having lotus flower as her birth place; anbu aḷavi – manifesting love; en tānum – at any time; avuṇarkku – towards asuras; irakkam ilādavanukku – one who is not having mercy; iru – vast; poḻil – gardens; sūḻ – being surrounded; nanṟāya punal – having abundance of water; naṟaiyūr – in tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟān – standing; tiruvāli – in tiruvāli; irundān – sitting; kudandai – in tirukkudandai; kidandān – reclined; tadam – by ponds; tigaḷ – shining; kōval nagar – in tirukkōvalūr; nadandāṟku – for sarvēśvaran who walked; uṟaiyum – eternally present; idam āvadu – abode; mā – best; malai – hill; nīr malai – tirunīrmalai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, manifesting love in kriṣṇāvatāram towards nappinnaip pirātti who is like a creeper for covherd clan and the best, beautiful rukmiṇip pirātti who is an incarnation of periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi) who is having lotus flower as her birth place, is not having mercy towards asuras at any time. The best hill tirunīrmalai is the abode where such emperumān who is standing in tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by vast gardens with abundance of water, who is sitting in tiruvāli, who has reclined in tirukkudandai and has walked in tirukkōvalūr which is shining due to ponds, is eternally present.

*anṟāyar …* – *munbu* – during ancient times; remaining lovingly together with nappinnaip pirātti and periya pirāttiyār who is having lotus flower as her abode.

*avuṇarkku …* – The abode of the eternal presence for the emperumān, who never shows mercy towards demoniac people, even while he is present with his divine consorts, is – tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by vast gardens which have abundance of water; tiruvāli which has similar greatness, tirukkudandai and tirukkōvalūr which is shining due to the ponds; in these abodes,

*ninṟān …* – He stood in tirunaṟaiyūr, seated in tiruvāli, reclined in tirukkudandai and walked in tirukkōvalūr.

*idam māmalaiyāvadu* – Though there are other hills, they are not abodes of emperumān. tirunīrmalai is the abode where he manifested himself with the love he has towards all the divyadēśams.

## 2.4.2. Kanda vanam

*kāṇḍā vanam enbadōr kādu amararkkaraiyan adu kaṇḍavan niṟka munē mūṇḍār aḻal uṇṇa munindaduvum aduvanṟiyum munnulagam poṟai tīrtu āṇḍān avuṇan avan mārbagalam ugirāl vagirāga munindu ariyāy nīṇḍān kuṟaḷāgi nimirndavanukku idam māmalaiyāvadu nīrmalaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

amararkku araiyan adu – the leader of dēvatās, indra, his; ōr – which cannot be destroyed by anyone; kāṇḍā vanam enbadu – which is known as kāṇḍava vanam; kādu – forest; avan – indra himself; kaṇḍu niṟka – while he was observing; munē – in front of him; Ar – complete; aḻal – fire; mūṇḍu – eagerly; uṇṇa – to consume; munindaduvum – mercifully showed his anger; adu anṟiyum – further; mun – during mahābhārata battle; ulagam – earth’s; poṟai – burden; tīrttu – eliminated; āṇḍān – one who protected the world; avuṇan avan – hiraṇya, the demon, his; agalam – broad; mārbu – chest; ugirāl – with nails; vagirāga – to split into two parts; munindu – mercifully showed anger; ariyāy – in the form of a lion; nīṇḍān – one who grew; kuṟaḷāgi – being in the form of vāmana (as a dwarf, after going to mahābāli and accepting water from him); nimirndavanukku – for sarvēśvaran who incarnated as trivikrama; idam āvadu – the abode; mā – best; malai – hill; nīr malai – tirunīrmalai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran mercifully showed his anger to have the complete fire eagerly consume the leader of dēvatās, indra’s forest which is known as kāṇḍava vanam which cannot be destroyed by anyone, in front of him while he was observing; further, during mahābhārata battle he eliminated earth’s burden and protected the earth; one who grew in the form of a lion and mercifully showed his anger to split the broad chest of hiraṇya, the demon, with his nails into two parts; the abode for sarvēśvaran who incarnated as trivikrama from being in the form of vāmana, is tirunīrmalai, the best hill.

*kāṇḍā vanam …* – kāṇḍava vanam – forest under indra’s protection, and cannot be destroyed by anyone. While arjuna and kriṣṇa were playing with a soft ball, agni bhagavān came and requested “Please give me a feast”; kriṣṇa told him “You consume the forest under the protection of indra” and let him consume it since demoniac entities had entered in that forest and kriṣṇa wanted them to be destroyed; that is being explained here. amararkku araiyan – leader of dēvatās, indra. While he was seeing, in his presence it was destroyed.

*mūṇḍār aḻal uṇṇa munindaduvum adu anṟiyum* – The fire which would at times become pale and withdraw, would show anger and consume eagerly, and further. Alternative explanation – mūṇḍār – those who opposed; i.e. to have the enemies burn.

*mun ulagam …* – One who previously eliminated the burden of earth and managed it. He mercifully showed anger and tore into the broad chest of the demoniac hiraṇya to split it into two parts.

*ariyāy nīṇḍān …* – Had he not incarnated at the same moment when prahlāda vowed, and helped prahlāda, it appears that his qualities would have had limits \[now by this incarnation, his qualities grew in a limitless manner\].

*kuṟaḷ …* – bhagavān who is greater than all, assumed the vāmana form and went to mahābali and begged for alms from him; on having the water touch his divine hand, he grew greatly to fill the space in the sky and measured the same. The abode of such emperumān is tirunīrmalai.

## 2.4.3. Alamannu madal

*alamannumadal surisangam eduttu adal āḻiyināl aṇiyār uruvin pulamannu vadam punai kongaiyināḷ poṟai tīra munāḷ aduvāḷamaril pala mannar padac cudar āḻiyinaip pagalōn maṟaiyap paṇi koṇḍu aṇisēr nila mannanumāy ulagāṇḍavanukku idam māmalaiyāvadu nīrmalaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

Ar aṇi – very beautiful; uruvil – in the divine form; adal – set to battle; āḻiyināl – with the tiruvāḻi (divine disc); alam – plough; mannum – being fixated; adal – set to battle; suri – having curved lines; sangam – śrī pāncajanyam (divine conch); eduttu – held; mun – when duryōdana et al remained unfavourable; pulam – (sarvēśvaran’s) senses such as eyes; mannu – to remain attached at all times; vadam – by ornaments such as necklace; punai – decorated; kongaiyināḷ – śrī bhūmip pirātti who is having \[such\] bosom, her; poṟai – burden; tīra – to eliminate; āḷ adu – which can destroy men; vāḷ – shining; amaril – in mahābhārata battle; pala mannar – many kings; pada – to be destroyed; sudar – very radiant; āḻiyinai – tiruvāḻi; pagalōn – sun; maṟaiya – to hide; paṇi koṇḍu – engaged in service; aṇi sēr – beautiful; nila mannanumāy – being the king of earth; ulagu āṇḍavanukku – one who ruled the world; idam āvadu – the abode; mā – best; malai – hill; nīr malai – tirunīrmalai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

When duryōdana et al remained unfavourable, in the mahābhārata battle which shines to destroy men, sarvēśvaran, in his very beautiful divine form, held the divine disc which is set to battle, plough and the divine conch which is fixated and is set to battle, to eliminate the burden of śrī bhūmip pirātti whose bosom is decorated with ornaments such as necklace etc to keep the senses of such sarvēśvaran attached to her, engaged his very radiant divine disc in service to hide the sun and destroy many kings; he then ruled the world, being the king of earth; the abode for such sarvēśvaran is tirunīrmalai, the best hill.

*alam* … – halam – plough; śrī pāncajanyam which has curved lines and is set to battle; holding them.

*adal āḻiyināl aṇi Ar uruvil …* – With tiruvāḻi which is set to battle, in the beautiful divine form; holding plough and śrī pāncajanyam in such divine form.

*aduttu* – \[Instead of *eduttu*, when read as *aduttu*\] With the beautiful divine form, the tiruvāḻi and the other weapons. That is – he concealed them as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.3.13 “*upasamhara*” (Conceal this divine form). Thus, he shows and hides them for the sake of his devotees.

*pula mannu …* – To eliminate the burden of śrī bhūmip pirātti who has beautifully decorated divine bosom to attract all senses of bhagavān towards her, previously, in the battle which has the radiance which kills men; or it is said as the great battle which kills valorous men.

*pala mannar pada* – To have ten thousand kings killed every day, emperumān engaged the ultimately radiant tiruvāḻi to hide the sun. *aṇi sēr* can be seen as an attribute for both the land and the king.

*nila mannanumāy ulagu āṇḍavanukku* – This could imply cakravartit tirumanga (śrīrāma); alternatively, this could imply kriṣṇa since removing the burden of earth through battle is highlighted here.

## 2.4.4. Tangadadu

*tāngādadōr āḷariyāy avuṇan tanai vīda munindu avanālamarum pūngōdaiyar pongeri mūḻgaviḷaittu aduvanṟiyum venṟikoḷ vāḷamaril pāngāga mun aivarodu anbaḷavip padiṟṟaindirattip padai vēndar pada nīngāc ceruvil niṟai kāttavanukku idam māmalaiyāvadu nīrmalaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāngādadu – being unstoppable (by enemies); ōr – matchless; āḷ ariyāy – being narasimha; avuṇan tanai – hiraṇya, the demon; vīda – to lose (his life); munindu – mercifully showing anger; avanāl – due to his acceptance; amarum – those who sustain; pū – decorated by flowers; kōdaiyar – women who adorn garlands; pongu eri – rising flame; mūḻga – to enter; viḷaittu – one who did; adu anṟiyum – not just that; mun – previously; venṟikoḷ – being victorious; vāḷ – respectable; amaril – in battle; aivarodu – with panca pāṇḍavas; pāngāga – aptly (for them); anbu aḷavi – mingled, showing friendship; padai – having weapons; padiṟṟaindu iratti vēndar – duryōdana et al who are one hundred in numbers; pada – to be destroyed; seruvil – in mahābhārata battle; niṟai – draupadi’s femininity; nīngā – to not lose; kāttavanukku – sarvēśvaran who protected; idam āvadu – the abode; mā – best; malai – hill; nīr malai – tirunīrmalai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being unstoppable, matchless narasimha, emperumān mercifully showed anger on hiraṇya to give up his life and made those women who sustained themselves by his acceptance and are wearing garlands decorated with flowers, to enter the rising flames; not just that, previously, in the victorious, respectable mahābhārata battle, he mingled with panca pāṇḍavas showing friendship, and destroyed duryōdana et al who are one hundred in numbers and were having weapons, and protected darupadi’s femininity; the abode of such emperumān is tirunīrmalai, the best hill.

*tāngādadu …* – Being narasimha who cannot be borne by enemies, showed his anger to have hiraṇya destroyed; there are women who are sustained by him – his wives; he made them give up their lives by jumping into rising fire. Not just that.

*venṟi …* – In the respectable battle where one cannot leave without being victorious.

*pāngāga …* – If he remains the lord, he cannot easily mingle even with pāṇḍavas. Hence, he reduced himself to be their friend and mingled with them. At that time, in the battle, where they cannot return without winning over the one hundred brothers, kriṣṇa eliminated draupadi’s fear which is natural for a woman. The abode of such emperumān is tirunīrmalai, the best hill.
