## 2.4.5. Malum kadal

*mālum kadalāra malaikkuvadittu aṇai katti varamburuva madi sēr kōla madiḷāya ilangai kedap padai tottu orukāl amaril adirak kālam iduvenṟu ayan vāḷiyināl kadir nīḷmudi pattum aṟuttu amarum neelamugil vaṇṇan emakku iṟaivaṟku idam māmalaiyāvadu nīrmalaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

orukāl – when rāvaṇa crossed his limits; mālum – having rising waves; kadal – ocean; Ara – to become filled; malaik kuvadu ittu – placing the peaks of mountain; varamburuva – to reach the other shore; aṇai katti – building the bridge; madi sēr – being tall to reach up to the moon; kōlam – beautiful; madiḷāya – having forts; ilangai – lankā; keda – to be destroyed; padai – weapons; tottu – holding on (launching); amaril – in the battle; adira – to cause tumult; idu kālam enṟu – determining that this is the right time to kill him; ayan vāḷiyināl – with brahmāstram; kadir – radiant; nīḷ mudi pattum – the ten heads which are decorated with large crowns; aṟuttu – severed; amarum – one who became mercifully seated in śrī ayōdyā; neela mugil – like a kāḷa mēgam (dark cloud); vaṇṇan – one who has divine complexion; emakku iṟaivaṟku – for our lord; idam āvadu – the abode; mā – best; malai – hill; nīr malai – tirunīrmalai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

empeurmān, as śrī rāma, when rāvaṇa crossed his limits, built the bridge on the ocean with rising waves to fill it, by placing the peaks of mountain to reach the other shore; holding on to the weapons, to destroy lankā which is having beautiful forts which are tall to reach up to the moon, caused tumult in the battle and severed rāvaṇa’s ten heads which are decorated with large, radiant crowns, with brahmāstram determining the right time to kill him and became mercifully seated in śrī ayōdyā; the abode for our lord who is having divine complexion like that of a dark cloud, is tirunīrmalai, the best hill.

*mālum kadal* – The ocean which is mad due to abundance of water; implying the ocean with rising waves.

*Ar* – Built the dam by breaking the peaks of mountains which will drown in the ocean, and placing them there.

*varamburuva* – To have them reach the other shore.

*madi …* – To have lankā which is surrounded by beautiful forts which reach up to the moon, destroyed, by holding on to the weapons and causing tumult in the battle. That is – building a bridge on the ocean, coming with the army, violating the forts, and after severely defeating rāvaṇa on the previous day and sending him home, śrī rāma thought “Let the evil rāvaṇa atone for his mistakes and come back”, and even after doing all of this, rāvaṇa came fighting again; at that time śrī rāma thought “if we continued this play any further, dēvatās will become very scared” and launched the brahmāstram and severed the ten radiant, great heads.

*amarum neela mugil vaṇṇan* – The completeness in his divine form after vanquishing rāvaṇa is explained here. One who has a rejuvenating form which resembles a cloud which is dark in colour.

*emakku iṟaiyavaṟku* – One who made me exclusively exist for him by showing the beauty of his divine form.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.4.6. Parar ulagum

*pārār ulagum panimāl varaiyum kadalum sudarum ivai uṇḍum enakku ārādena ninṟavan emperumān alai nīr ulagukku arasāgiya ap pērānai muninda munikkaraiyan piṟarillai nunakkenum ellaiyinān nīrār pērān nedumāl avanukku idam māmalaiyāvadu nīrmalaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

Ar – (during deluge) vast; pār ulagum – earth; pani – cool; māl – huge; varaiyum – mountains; kadalum – oceans; sudarum – moon and sun; ivai – all of these; uṇḍum – consumed; enakku – for me; ārādu ena – saying “not sufficient”; ninṟavan – one who is mercifully present; emperumān – being my lord; alai nīr – surrounded by ocean where the waves are striking; ulagukku – for the earth; arasu āgiya – those who are known as kings; appērānai – having that name of kśatriya clan; muninda – one who mercifully showed anger; munikku araiyan – being śrī paraśurāmāḻvān who is best among sages; nunakku – for you; piṟar illai – there is none beyond you; enum – to be said; ellaiyinān – one who remains in the boundary of being the prakāri (substratum); nīrār pērān – one who has the divine name, nīrvaṇṇan; nedumāl avanukku – for sarvēśvaran who has great love; idam āvadu – the abode; mā – best; malai – hill; nīr malai – tirunīrmalai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān who consumed all of the vast earth, cool huge mountains, oceans, moon and sun, during deluge, is mercifully present saying “these are not sufficient”; my lord, being śrī paraśurāmāḻvān who is best among sages, who mercifully showed anger on those who have that name of kśatriya clan, who are known as kings for the earth which is surrounded by ocean where the waves are striking; the abode for you, the sarvēśvaran who remains in the boundary of being the prakāri (substratum), to be said that there is none beyond you, who has the divine name, nīrvaṇṇan, who has great love, is tirunīrmalai, the best hill.

*pārār ulagum* – Earth which has abundance of land.

*pani māl varaiyum* – The kulaparvatams (anchoring mountains) which are supporting the earth as if being nailed, and have clouds resting on them; oceans, radiant objects – placing all of these in his stomach, he still said “these are not sufficient” and having abundance interest in protecting everyone where the protected entities are less and scope for protecting more entities is present. That is – doing everything for his children and feeling that he has not done anything for them. Further, instead of thinking about having rescued them all from the deluge and placed them in his stomach, he is feeling anguished for letting them suffer in the deluge until then.

*emperumān* – In this manner, showing how he protects everyone and enslaved me.

*alai …* – aḻagar perumāḷ araiyar enquired the meaning for this passage with many persons, and some śrīvaiṣṇavas told him “this is speaking about sarvēśvaran”. One who destroyed the kings of earth which is surrounded by ocean, to even erase their names.

*munikku araiyan* – śrī paraśurāmāḻvān, the best among sages, destroyed twenty one generations of kings to such an extent that their names are not even known.

*piṟar illai nunakku enum ellaiyinān* – To say that there is no lord beyond you, one who remains as prakāri (substratum) to have everything else as his prakāra (forms).

*nīrār pērān* – As said in manu smruti 1.10 “*āpōnārā itiprōktā:*” (Water is created by bhagavān who is known as nara; hence nāra indicates water. As he has such water as his abode, he is known as nārāyaṇa), since he is mercifully resting on water, he has the divine name nārāyaṇa; alternatively – nīr indicates nīrmai which implies a quality, that is śēśitvam (lordship), hence due to having all entities as his prakāra and being the prakāri, he is the one who has the divine name nārāyaṇa. Thus, sarvēśvaran, who is greater than all, has the divine name, nīr vaṇṇan.

## 2.4.7. Pugarar uruvagi

*pugarār uruvāgi munindavanaip pugaḻ vīda munindu uyir uṇḍu asuran nagarāyina pāḻ pada nāmam eṟindu aduvanṟiyum venṟikoḷ vāḷ avuṇan pagarādavan āyira nāmam adip paṇiyādavanaip paṇiyāl amaril nigarāyavan nenjidandān avanukku idam māmalaiyāvadu nīrmalaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

Ar – great; pugar – having radiance; uruvāgi – having such form; munindavanai – hiraṇyākśa who showed anger (saying “who is greater than I?”); pugaḻ vīda – to have (his) fame destroyed; munindu – mercifully showed anger; uyir – (his) prāṇa (vital air); uṇḍu – destroyed; asuran – the demon, his; nagarāyina – capital cities; pāḻ pada – to become ruins; nāmam eṟindu – (destroyed) to make even his name erased; adu anṟiyum – further; venṟi koḷ – being victorious; vāḷ – having the sword as his protective companion; āyiram nāmam pagarādavan – one who cannot recite even one among the thousand names (of emperumān); adi – at the divine feet; paṇiyādavan – being the one who did not bow down; amaril – in the battle; nigarāyavan – opposed; avuṇananai – hiraṇya, the demon’s; nenju – chest; paṇiyāl – as per the words of prahlādan (to do good for him); idandānavanukku – one who tore it down; idam āvadu – the abode; mā – best; malai – hill; nīr malai – tirunīrmalai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān mercifully showed his anger to have the fame of hiraṇyākśa, the demon who is having a greatly radiant form and who showed anger, destroyed, to turn his capital cities in to ruins and to even make his name erased; further, emperumān tore down the chest of hiraṇya, the demon, who is victorious, who cannot recite even one among the thousand names, who did not bow down at the divine feet, and who opposed in the battle, as per the words of prahlādan; the abode of such emperumān, is the best hill, tirunīrmalai.

*pugar …* – This incident could be related to pauṇḍrakan or hiraṇyākśan. It is said that pauṇḍrakan made his form look like kriṣṇa’s divine form which is in pure satva (goodness), infinitely radiant, and wandered around. When this is related to hiraṇyākśa, he is verily indicated in that manner. Showing his anger to eliminate the bewilderment about the identity of the self for the one who had a radiant form. He built many cities; to turn those cities into ruins and destroyed him so that even the trace of his name ceases to exist.

Further,

*venṟi …* – One who never retracts until he wins, and one who considers the boons of the dēvatās as his strength. pagarugai – reciting, he did not recite even one among the thousand divine names; that is – one who could not recite. Further, he also did not bow at the divine feet of emperumān and surrender unto him.

*paṇiyāl …* – On the words of śrī prahlādāḻvān. As śrī rāma obeyed the words of sugrīva as in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.70 “*sugrīva vacanāt*” (as per the words of sugrīva), here as per the humble words of śrī prahlādāḻvān. śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1.20.21 “*math pitu: tat krutam pāpam dēva tasya praṇaśyatu*” (Oh lord! Let the sins of my father which were acquired due to his disgust towards me since I vorśipped you, be destroyed) – previously, since śrī prahlādāḻvān prayed to emperumān to forgive his father, emperumān too forgave him. But now, emperumān thought “If hiraṇya continues to live, it will be bad for him” and hence killed him. amaril – in the battle, for emperumān who tore the chest of hiraṇya who opposed, into pieces \[the abode of such emperumān, is the best hill, tirunīrmalai\].

## 2.4.8. 2.4.8 -Piccac ciru peeli

*piccac ciṟu peeli pidittu ulagil piṇandin madavār avar pōl anganē accamilar nāṇilarādanmaiyāl avar seygai veṟuttu aṇimāmalar tūy nacci namanār adaiyāmai namakku aruḷ sey ena uḷ kuḻaindu ārvamodu niccam ninaivārkku aruḷ seyyumavaṟku idam māmalaiyāvadu nīrmalaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

piccam – having feathers; siṟu – small; peeli – peacock feather bunch; pidittu – holding in the hand; ulagil – in the world; piṇam – dead bodies; thin – eating; madavāravar pōl – like ghostly women; anganē – similarly; accam ilar – being fearless; nāṇ ilar – being shameless; ādanmaiyāl – due to this; avar seygai – seeing the acts of those worldly people; veṟuttu – having disgust; aṇi – being beautiful; mā – best; malar – flowers; tūy – submitting; nacci – desiring (for sarvēśvaran); namanār – yama et al; adaiyāmai – to be not reached; namakku aruḷ sey ena – saying “you should mercifully grant”; uḷ kuḻaindu – with a melted heart; ārvamodu – with love; niccam – daily; ninaivārkku – for those who meditate; aruḷ seyyumavarkku – one who showers his mercy; idam āvadu – the abode; mā – best; malai – hill; nīr malai – tirunīrmalai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

For those who are having disgust due to seeing the acts of those who are like ghostly women who are eating dead bodies in the world and are holding bunch of small peacock feathers and are fearless and shameless in this manner, and meditate daily with a melted heart and love, submitting beautiful, best flowers, saying “you should mercifully grant that we are not reached by yama et al”, desiring for sarvēśvaran, sarvēśvaran showers his mercy; the abode of such sarvēśvaran is the best hill, tirunīrmalai.

*piccac ciṟu peeli pidittu* … – Holding a bunch of small peacock feathers, they will roam like those who discard their clothes and eat dead bodies; similar to them, not having any fear to be standing in this manner, and not having any shame for being seen by others in this manner, they will roam around; due to being in this manner,

*avar seygai veṟuttu* … – having disgust meditating upon roaming around independently without respecting the boundaries of vēdam, vorśipping bhagavān and conduct as shown in vēdam; desiring for bhagavān, having items such as beautiful flowers for his worship, those who meditate upon bhagavān to be not reached by yama et al; alternative explanation – yama et al desirously reaching; that is, yama et al thinking – these persons are engaged in sinful deeds and let us go and do whatever we desire for them; to be not reached by such yama et al.

*namakku …* – Those who meditate daily with love and melted heart saying “You should shower your mercy”; alternative explanation – Those who meditate with love and melted heart saying “You should shower your mercy daily”.

## 2.4.9. Pesum alavanru

*pēsum aḷavanṟu idu vammin namar! piṟar kētpadan mun paṇivār vinaigaḷ nāsamadu seydidumādanmaiyāl aduvē namadu uyvidam nāḷmalar mēl vāsamaṇi vaṇḍaṟai paimbuṟavil manamaindodu nainduḻalvār madiyil nīsaravar senṟu adaiyādavanukku idam māmalaiyāvadu nīrmalaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

idu – the greatness of this bhagavat viśayam; pēsum aḷavu anṟu – cannot be fully spoken of by us; namar – Oh our people! (this best principle); piṟar – atheists; kētpadan mun – before hearing; vammin – come; adu – that bhagavat viśayam; paṇivār – those who worship, their; vinaigaḷ – sins; nāsam seydidum – will destroy; ādanmaiyāl – thus; aduvē – that bhagavat viśayam alone; namadu – our; uyvu idam – the abode of uplifting; manam – heart; aindodu – going towards śabda (sound), sparśa (touch), rūpa (form), rasa (taste) and ganda (smell); naindu – being weakened; uḻalvār – being those who suffer; madiyil – ignorant; nīsaravar – for lowly persons; senṟu adaiyādavanukku – one who is difficult to reach; idamāvadu – the abode; nāḷ – freshly blossomed; malarmēl – due to being spread on flower; vāsam – fragrant; aṇi – beautiful; vaṇḍu – beetles; aṟai – humming; pai – vast; puṟavil – having surroundings; mā malaiyāna nīr malai – the best hill, tirunīrmalai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh our people! The greatness of this bhagavat viśayam cannot be fully spoken of by us. Before the atheists hear this, you come to us. This will destroy the sins of those who worship it. Thus, this bhagavat viśayam alone is our abode of being uplifted. The abode of bhagavān who is difficult to be reached by those ignorant, lowly persons whose hearts are weakened by going towards śabda (sound), sparśa (touch), rūpa (form), rasa (taste) and ganda (smell) and are suffering, is the best hill, tirunīrmalai which has vast surroundings where beautiful beetles which are fragrant due to being spread on freshly blossomed flowers, are humming.

*pēsum aḷavu anṟu idu* – In matters other than bhagavat viśayam since there is nothing great to speak about, nothing can be said about them; in bhagavat viśayam, nothing can be said due to the indescribable nature of the same.

*vammin namar* – All those who are related to us! Please come.

*piṟar kētpadan mun* – Before those who are unrelated to this principle, hear the same. This cannot be said to those who are unqualified as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.68](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-68/) “*ya idam paramam guhyam*” (… this śāstram which is most confidential) and in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.67](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-67/) “*idam tē nātapaskāya*” (this śāstram should not be told to you, to one who has not performed penance); at the same time it should be instructed to those who are qualified – both aspects are present.

*paṇivār* – emperumān will eradicate the sins of those who fall at his divine feet and surrender unto him, along with the traces.

*adu …* – It will do the most difficult tasks as said in viṣṇu darmam 78 “*durvyādiriva naśyati*” (sins will leave just as bad diseases will leave when attended by a doctor). Due to being in this manner, such bhagavat viśayam is the abode of upliftment for us.

*nāḷ malar tūy* – If recited in this manner, those who offer fresh flowers and serve.

*nāḷ malar mēl* – If recited in this manner, fragrant beetles being spread on fresh flowers; the great hill which has surroundings where such beetles are humming.

*manam …* – *aindodu – manam – nainduḻalvār* – the one who cannot be reached by lowly persons who have their heart being desirous of śabda etc and being weakened due to that and are ignorant.

## 2.4.10. Nedumal avan

*nedumāl avan mēviya nīrmalai mēl nilavum pugaḻ mangaiyar kōn amaril kadamā kaḷiyānai vallān kaliyan oli sey tamiḻ mālai vallārkku udanē vidumāl vinai vēṇḍidil mēlulagum eḷidāyidum anṟi ilangoli sēr kodumā kadal vaiyagam āṇḍu madikkudai mannavarāy adi kūduvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīrmalai – in tirunīrmalai; mēviya – remaining firm; nedumālavan mēl – on sarvēśvaran; nilavum – eternal; pugaḻ – having fame; mangaiyar kōn – being the leader of tirumangai region; amaril – in battle; kadam – intoxication; mā – very; kaḷi – joyful; yānai – elephant; vallān – one who can conduct; kaliyan – āḻvār; oli sey – mercifully spoke with tune; tamiḻ mālai – this garland of tamiḻ pāsurams; vallārkku – for those who can practice; māl – great; vinai – karmas; udanē – immediately; vidum – will run away; vēṇḍidil – if desired; mēl ulagum – higher worlds such as heaven; eḷidāyidum – will be easily attainable; anṟi – otherwise; ilangu – shining; oli sēr – having sound; kodu – curved; mā – vast; kadal – surrounded by ocean; vaiyagam – earth; madikkudai – under the white umbrella matching the moon; mannavarāy – as kings; āṇḍu – ruling over (further); adi – his divine feet; kūduvar – will reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The eternally famous leader of tirumangai region, tirumangai āḻvār who can conduct very joyful, intoxicated elephant, mercifully spoke this garland of tamiḻ pāsurams with tune, on sarvēśvaran who is remaining firmly in tirunīrmalai. For those who can practice this decad, the great karmas will immediately run away; if desired by them, higher worlds such as heaven will be easily attainable; otherwise, they will rule over the earth surrounded by shining, resounding, curved and vast ocean, as kings, remaining under the white umbrella matching the moon and will reach sarvēśvaran’s divine feet.

*nedumāl …* – tirumangai āḻvār who is having eternal fame and is the leader of the residents of tirumangai and can conduct intoxicated elephant in the battle, composed this garland of tamiḻ pāsurams with tune, on tirunīrmalai where sarvēśvaran, who is greater than all, is eternally residing. For those who are able to practice this decad,

*udanē* – While surrendering, the sins will run away. Further if they desire for the attainment of the goal, that will be easy to attain. ōr, if they desire for worldly pleasures/wealth, they will become the singular rulers of the earth which is surrounded by shining, resounding, curved ocean, enjoying the wealth by remaining under a moon like whitish umbrella (which highlights supremacy in this world) and will eventually reach the divine feet of emperumān.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5 Parayadu

## 2.5.1. Parayadu

*pārāyadu uṇḍu umiḻnda pavaḷat tūṇaip padukadalil amudattaip parivāy kīṇḍa sīrānai emmānait toṇḍar tangaḷ sindai uḷḷē muḷaittu eḻunda tīngarumbinaip pōrānaik kombositta pōrēṟṟinaip puṇar marudamiṟa nadanda poṟkunṟinaik kārānai idar kadinda kaṟpagattaik kaṇḍadu nān kadal mallait talasayanattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pārāyadu – all of earth (during deluge); uṇḍu – consumed; umiḻnda – mercifully let it out; pavaḷam – being desirable for all similar to coral; tūṇai – being the sustainer; padu – where pearls etc originate; kadalil – in ocean; amudattai – being enjoyable similar to nectar, one who is mercifully resting; pari – of the horse, a form taken by the demon kēśi; vāy – mouth; kīṇḍa – tore; sīrān – one who has the wealth of valour (due to that act); emmānai – being my lord; toṇḍar tangaḷ – those who surrendered unto him, their; sindaiyuḷḷē – in the hearts; muḷaittu – having been born; eḻunda – which nurtured; tīm – enjoyable; karumbinai – one who is sweet like sugarcane; pōr – set to battle; ānai – the elephant named kuvalayāpīdam, its; kombu ositta – who broke the tusk; pōr ēṟṟinai – one who is like a lion in battle; puṇar – being united; marudam – the two maruda trees; iṟa – to snap and fall down; nadanda – one who entered in between those trees; pon kunṟinai – one who is beautiful like a golden mountain; kār – huge; ānai – śrī gajēndrāḻvān’s; idar – danger; kadinda – one who eliminated; kaṟpagattai – the most magnanimous emperumān who grants the desires similar to a kalpaka tree; talasayanam – stala sayanam (where he rests on the ground); kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; nān kaṇḍadu – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān consumed all of earth and mercifully let it out; he is being desirable for all, similar to coral, being the sustainer, being enjoyable similar to nectar and who is mercifully resting in the ocean where pearls etc originate; he is the one who tore the mouth of the horse, a form taken by the demon kēśi and thus having the wealth of valour; he is my lord; he is sweet like enjoyable sugarcane which is born and nurtured in the hearts of those who surrendered unto him; he is like a lion in battle who broke the tusk of the elephant, kuvalayāpīdam which was set to battle; he is beautiful like a golden mountain, who entered in between the two maruda trees which remain united to make them snap and fall down; he eliminated the danger of huge śrī gajēndrāḻvān; I got to see such most magnanimous emperumān who grants the desires similar to a kalpaka tree in stala sayanam, tirukkadalmallai.

*pārāyadu* – Whatever is known as “pār”. emperumān placed everything known as earth in his stomach during deluge and subsequently let them out to relieve them from suffocation and to let them see the outside.

When asked “Who protects in all these ways?” āḻvār says,

*pavaḷat tūṇai* – One who is desirable for all and who is the sustainer.

*padu kadalalil amudattai* – The ocean where precious gems are present; alternatively – the ocean which is deep; depth is said as in “*maduppattadu*” (that which is very deep). The purpose of this attribute/quality is – the enjoyable one who is present where good things are present; when spoken about depth, it implies that he is difficult to attain.

*pari vāy kīṇḍa* – One who is capable of eliminating powerful hurdles just as he tore the mouth of kēśi. pari – horse; one who has the wealth of valour to tear the mouth of horse.

*emmānai* … – He engaged in a very dangerous act \[while killing kēsi\]. One who enslaved me completely by being caught by it \[the demon in horse form\] and escaping from it.

*toṇḍar …* – emperumān cannot be said to be free from change etc; he cannot be said as eternally unchanging; happened as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*santamēnam*” (to be existing); while ātmā is said to be eternally unchanging, it is said in taittirīya upaniśat as “*asannēva*” (not to be existing) and “*santamēnam*” (to be existing) when the ātmā does not know about bhagavān and knows about bhagavān respectively. emperumān too exists when ātmā knows him and does not exist when ātmā does not know him. Had the ātmā not been very dear for bhagavān, ātmā being servitor and bhagavān being lord, ātmā bringing glories for bhagavān and bhagavān accepting them, this (bringing glories to bhagavān) being the goal for the ātmā etc will cease to exist. Such emperumān takes birth and grows, are in the heart of the ātmā.

When asked “What is the reason for that?” āḻvār says,

*karumbinai* – Since sugarcane is identified instead of sugar block, one may wonder if he is really sweet, but since “tīm” is present as an adjective, it indicates the great sweetness. Being very sweet.

*toṇḍar* … – There is greatness based on the land where things are born \[since the heart of servitors is a great abode, he is naturally sweet\].

*pōrānai …* – One who remains as a lion in a battle, having effortlessly broken the tusk of the elephant named kuvalayāpīdam which was ready to fight. ēṟu indicates both lion and ox. Since elephant was spoken about, it is matching to speak about bhagavān as a lion. This is his valour in the battle.

*puṇar …* – Should we speak only about his adulthood activities? He learnt to crawl by making the twin maruda trees which were united with each other, snap and fall down. He went in between them even while knowing that the demons who were present inside the trees were planning to kill him.

*pon kunṟinai* – Appearing to be the mēru mountain where lions reside. āḻvār is speaking about how he remained like a *pon kunṟu* (golden mountain) on hearing the noise of the twin trees falling down and seeing that purposefully. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.16 – 18 “*tata: katakatā sabda: samākārṇana tatpara:*” (the lotus-eyed lord went through the twin trees hearing the sound of their falling down).

*kār …* – One who eliminated the danger faced by śrī gajēndrāḻvān and stood there presenting himself fully to such gajēndrāḻvān. kār – greatness.

*kaṇḍadu …* – As emperumān arrived quickly at the banks of the pond when gajēndrāḻvān was suffering, emperumān arrived in this samsāram where I am suffering at the current times and I got to see him, says āḻvār.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.2. Pundavattam

*pūṇḍavattam piṟarkkadaindu toṇḍu pattup poynūlai meynūl enṟu enṟum ōdi māṇḍu avattam pōgādē vammin endai en vaṇangappaduvānai kaṇangaḷ ēttum nīṇḍavattaik karumugilai emmān tannai ninṟavūr nittilattait tottār sōlaik kāṇḍavattaik kanal eri vāyp peyvittānaik kaṇḍadu nān kadalmallait talasayanattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

avattam – some useless acts; pūṇḍu – taking up; piṟarkku – for lowly people; adaindu – holding on (to them); toṇḍupattu – serving; poy – false; nūlai – scriptures of those who reject vēdam; ōdi – learning (those); mey nūl enṟum – believing to be true meanings; māṇḍu – being finished; avattam – useless; pōgāmal – not becoming; vammin – come (to become liberated); endai – being my father; en – for those who are like me; vaṇangap paduvānai – one who is easily approachable and surrendered to; kaṇangaḷ – by the groups of wise people; ēttum – one who is praised; nīṇḍa attai – being that entity which is inconceivable; karumugilai – one who has dark cloud like complexion; ninṟavūr – in tiruninṟavūr; nittilattai – one who has a cool form like a collection of pearls; tottu – flower bunches; Ar – being abundant; sōlai – having garden; kāṇḍavattai – kāṇḍava forest; kanal – shining; eri – fire’s; vāy – in the mouth; peyvittānai – one who made to enter; emmān tannai – sarvēśvaran; talasayanam – stala sayanam (where he rests on the ground); kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; nān kaṇḍadu – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Come here giving up holding on to service to lowly people, taking up useless acts and learning the scriptures of those who reject vēdam, believing them to be true, instead of perishing and becoming useless. Being my father, and being easily approachable and surrendered to for those who are like me, and being praised by the groups of wise people, being the inconceivable entity, who is having dark cloud like complexion, having a cool form like a collection of pearls in tiruninṟavūr, sarvēśvaran made kāṇḍava forest which has gardens with abundant bunches of flowers, enter into the mouth of fire. I got to see such sarvēśvaran in tirukkadalmallai stala sayanam.

*pūṇḍavattam* – *avattam pūṇḍu* – Taking up useless acts. Ignoring the association with sātvika (noble) people and the desire to attain goals as outlined in vēdam, taking up useless acts.

*piṟarkku adaindu toṇḍu pattu* – Being humble towards inapt aspects as if remaining towards apt aspect (bhagavān). Worśipping those who are not to be vorśipped.

*poyn nūlai …* – Eagerly learning the scriptures created by those who cause confusion and those who are confused, with their intelligence, and subsequently perishing, being unable to retract analysing and knowing their true nature.

*avattam pōgādē* – Instead of becoming useless in both this world and the other (superior) world.

*vammin* – Oh losers! Quickly come and stand here.

*endai en vaṇangap paduvānai* – Being my father, being easily approachable by me.

*kaṇangaḷ …* –  The inconceivable entity who is praised by wise people. Alternatively,

*nīṇḍa vattak karumugilai* – One who has nīṇḍa hastam (one who has lengthy hand).

*emmān tannai* – He was captivated by the same aspect which won over tiruvadi (hanuman).  śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 3.14 “*kimartam na vibhūśitā:*” (Why are the shoulders not decorated?)

*ninṟa Ur …* – One who is standing in tiruninṟavūr like a rejuvenating bunch of pearls.

*tottār ..* – Making the kāṇḍava forest which is having garden with abundance of flower-bunches to enter into the shining mouth of fire. When arjuna and kriṣṇa were playing soft ball, agni bhagavān came there saying “I am hungry”, kriṣṇa let agni consume the forest under his watch. indra became angry and poured heavy rain and arjuna made a protective layer on top of the forest with his arrows and the water fell off.

*kaṇḍadu* – Just as it rained during the forest fire, I got to see emperumān in this samsāra where I am suffering.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.3. Udamburuvil munronray

*udamburuvil mūnṟonṟāy mūrtti vēṟāy ulaguyya ninṟānai anṟu pēycci vidam parugu vittaganaik kanṟu mēyttu viḷaiyāda vallānai varaimīkānil tadam parugu karumugilait tanjaikkōyil tava neṟikku ōr peru neṟiyai vaiyam kākkum kadum pari mēl kaṟkiyai nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn kadipoḻil sūḻ kadalmallait talasayanattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

udambu – body’s; uruvil – in the form; mūnṟu – three; ulagu uyya – for the protection of the world; onṟāy – in a singular form; mūrtti – true nature; vēṟāy – being different; ninṟānai – one who stands; anṟu – during kriṣṇāvatāram; pēycci – pūtanā’s; vidam – poisonous milk; parugu – one who drank; vittaganai – amazing; kanṟu – calves; mēyttu – tended; viḷaiyāda vallānai – one who incarnated to play; varaimī – atop the hill; kānil – in the forests; tadam – in the ponds, to train the calves to drink water, he would demonstrate that by folding his hands in the back; parugu – one who mercifully drinks water; karumugilai – one who resembles a dark cloud; tanjaik kōyil – one who is mercifully present in tanjaimāmaṇikkōyil; tava neṟikku – among the upāyams (means) (which are pursued to attain him); ōr peru neṟiyai – one who remains the greatest means; vaiyam – all the worlds; kākkum – to protect; kadu – having great speed; pari mēl – on the horse; kaṟkiyai – one who mercifully incarnated as kalki; kadi – guarded; poḻil – garden; sūḻ – surrounded; talasayanam – stala sayanam (where he rests on the ground); kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān stands in three forms of bodies, but having true nature which is different in a singular manner; during kriṣṇāvatāram, he is the amazing one who drank the poisonous milk of pūtanā; he incarnated to tend and play with the calves; in the forests atop the hill, he mercifully drinks water in the ponds, to train the calves to drink water, he would demonstrate that by folding his hands in the back; he resembles a dark cloud; he is mercifully present in tanjaimāmaṇikkōyil; he remains the greatest means among the means to attain him; he mercifully incarnated as kalki appearing on the horse which is having great speed, to protect the worlds; I got to see such emperumān in stala sayanam in tirukkadalmallai which is surrounded by guarded garden.

*udamburuvil mūnṟu onṟāy* – In view of body, in the form of body, having three forms which are the same. Being in his true form \[as viṣṇu\] and being antaryāmi (indvelling supersoul) for brahmā and rudra, in this manner, as all three are different forms of bhagavān, they are singular in this point of view.

*mūrtti vēṟāy* … – In this manner, all three forms are similar; emperumān too in śrī bhagavat gītā first spoke about aikyam (singularity) in 5.18 “*samadarśina:*” (see the same ātmā everywhere) and sāmyam (equality) in 5.19 “*yēśām sāmyē stitam mana:*” (one who firmly remains in equality of all ātmās). Why is he present in this manner? He is standing in this manner for protection during sruśti (creation), stiti (sustenance) and samhāram (annihilation).

*anṟu pēycci vidam parugu vittaganai* – In the created world, emperumān incarnated as the amazing kriṣṇa and drank the poisoned milk of pūtanā. What is amazing here? Drinking her life along with the poison from her bosom to kill her; alternative explanation – though she came in the disguise of his mother, by the taste of the milk from her bosom, he understood that she was not his mother and consumed her life.

*kanṟu …* – śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.35 “*sarvasya jagata: pālau vatsapālau babhūvatu:*” (kriṣṇa and balarāma, who protect the whole world, became the protectors of calves).

*varaimī …* – bhattar’s explanation for this section is very popular. When nanjīyar was explaining this section, piḷḷai aḻagiya maṇavāḷap perumāḷ araiyar mercifully reminded him about bhattar’s explanation. Being tired, when the calves reach the ponds on top of the hill, they will be scared to drink the water since they are young and do not know how to drink. To train them, kriṣṇa will fold his hands in the back side and mercifully drink water from the pond with his mouth. āḻvār is speaking about the acts of emperumān which match the covherd clan.

*tanjai …* – To protect all the worlds, he arrived and stood at the great tanjai mā maṇik kōyil.

*tava neṟikku ōr peru neṟiyai* – One who remains the greatest means among the means to attain him. One who helps even if a person goes through wrong ways, and brings him back. The means which will never fail.

*vaiyam …* – To protect the whole world, he climbs on very fast horse, and is having the form to crush the enemies under the horse’s feet. pari – motion; the great horse which has fast motion.

*kadi …* – āḻvār is saying “I have become the target of the protection of emperumān who protects the entire world”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.4. Peyt tayai

*pēyt tāyai mulai uṇḍa piḷḷai tannaip piṇai maruppiṟ karungaḷiṟṟaip piṇai mān nōkkilāyt tāyar tayir veṇṇey amarnda kōvai andaṇar tam amudattai kuravai munnēkōttānai kudamādu kūttan tannaik kōkulangaḷ taḷarāmal kunṟam ēndikkāttānai emmānaik kaṇḍu koṇḍēn kadipoḻil sūḻ kadalmallait talasayanattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāy – in the disguise of mother; pēyai – pūtanā’s; mulai – bosom; uṇḍa – mercifully consumed; piḷḷai tannai – being a child; piṇai – joined to each other; maruppil – tusk’s; karu – dark; kaḷiṟṟai – one who is similar to an elephant; mān piṇai – like a doe; nōkkil – having eyes; āyttāyar – yaśōda, the covherd mother, her; tayir – curd; veṇṇey – mercifully consuming the butter; amarnda – sustained himself; kōvai – being the controller; andaṇar tam – for brāhmaṇas; amudattai – one who is enjoyable like nectar; munnē – previously; kuravai kōttānai – one who held the hands of the girls and played with them (further); kudam ādu – one who danced with pots; kūttan tannai – having grand activities (when indra rained due to anger of hunger); kōkulangaḷ – herds of cows; taḷarāmal – to not suffer; kunṟam – gōvardana hill; ēndi – held; kāttānai – one who protected; emmānai – sarvēśvaran who enslaved us; kadi – fragrant; poḻil – by garden; sūḻ – surrounded; talasayanattu – in stala sayanam (where he rests on the ground); kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; nān kaṇḍadu – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being a child, emperumān mercifully consumed the bosom of pūtanā who came in the disguise of his mother; being the controller, kriṣṇa who looks like a dark elephant with joined tusks mercifully consumed the curd and butter of yaśōda, the covherd mother, who is having eyes similar to that of a doe, and sustained himself; he is enjoyable for brāhmaṇas, like nectar; previously he held the hands of the girls and played with them, danced with pots and had grant activities; he held the gōvardana hill and protected the cows to not let them suffer; I got to see such sarvēśvaran, who enslaved us, in stala sayanam in tirukkadalmallai, which is surrounded by fragrant garden.

*pēyt tāyai mulai uṇḍa piḷḷai tannai* – When the ghostly pūtanā assumed the form of his mother, he showed her the same affection he would show to his mother and consumed her bosom; one who is having such childish attitude.

*piṇai …* – One who is having sweet activities like that of a dark elephant which is having joined tusks. By saying “*piṇai maruppu*” – āḻvār indicates his prideful/strong roaming around.

*piṇai …* – There is the covherd mother who has doe like eyes – yaśōdā. Mercifully consuming the butter and curd which was prepared personally by her, he enslaved the entire world by sustaining himself with the materials that were touched by his devotees.

*andaṇar tam amudattai* – One who is the sustenance for brāhmaṇa clan by such deeds.

*kuravai …* – One who manifested this act of dancing with the girls, which are only to be revealed to a few, to everyone.

*kudamādi …* – Not just to be seen by a few in this manner, he manifested this dance with pots to everyone. One who protected the herds of cows from suffering in the rain, by plucking a hill which was present in front of him.

*emmānai* – One who exclusively enslaved me by showing his saviourśip.

*kaṇḍu …* – āḻvār is saying “I came to know that he is the protector; is there any grievance for me?”

## 2.5.5. Payndanait

*pāyndānait tiri sagadam pāṟi vīḻap pālaganāy ālilaiyil paḷḷi inbamēyndānai ilangoḷi sēr maṇik kunṟanna īriraṇḍu mālvarait tōḷ ammān tannaittōyndānai nilamagaḷ tōḷ tūdiṟ senṟu ap poyyaṟai vāyp pugappeyda mallar mangakkāyndānai emmānaik kaṇḍu koṇḍēn kadipoḻil sūḻ kadalmallait talasayanattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiri – rolling; sagadam – cakatāsuran; pāṟi – become pieces; vīḻa – to fall (by the divine feet); pāyndānai – one who kicked; bālaganāy – being a small child; ālilaiyil – in banyan leaf; paḷḷi inbam – bliss of sleeping; ēyndānai – one who enjoyed; ilangu oḷi – great shine; sēr – having; maṇikkunṟu anna – having beauty like that of a jewel hill; māl – huge; varai – strong like a mountain; īriraṇḍu tōḷ – having four divine shoulders; ammān tannai – being the lord of all; nila magaḷ tōḷ – with the divine shoulder of śrī bhūmip pirātti; tōyndānai – one who mingled; tūdil senṟu – going as the messenger of pāṇḍavas; poy – the mischievous throne placed by duryōdana in; avvaṟai vāy puga – to make kriṣṇa enter in that room beneath the ground and harm him; peyda – already discussed and arranged; malllar – group of wrestlers; manga – to finish; kāyndānai – one who mercifully showed anger; emmānai – one who is my lord; kadi – fragrant; poḻil – by garden; sūḻ – surrounded; talasayanattu – in stala sayanam (where he rests on the ground); kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; nān kaṇḍadu – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān kicked cakatāsuran who came rolling to become pieces and fell; being a small child, he enjoyed the bliss of sleeping on banyan leaf; he is the lord of all, having four divine shoulders which are strong like huge mountain which is having beauty like that of a very shining jewel hill; he mingled with the divine shoulder of śrī bhūmip pirātti; going as the messenger of pāṇḍavas, he mercifully showed anger to finish the group of wrestlers who were arranged to harm kriṣṇa by making him enter in that room beneath the ground under the mischievous throne placed by duryōdana; I got to see such emperumān who is my lord in stala sayanam in tirukkadalmallai which is surrounded by fragrant garden.

*pāyndānai …* – Mother yaśōdā placed the baby kriṣṇa in the cradle-swing under the wheeled-cart. Demons entered those wheels and tried to kill kriṣṇa. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.1 “*stanyārtī brarurōdaha*” (desiring for mother’s milk, he cried and lifted his feet), as his feeding was delayed by his mother, he became angry and kicked with his divine feet. The demons became a target of his kicking and died. One who kicked to destroy the rolling wheels into pieces.

*bālagan …* – Being a very small infant, he enjoyed the bliss of sleep on the freshly blossommed banyan leaf.

*ilangoḷi …* – One who has four divine shoulders which resemble very radiant blue mountain.

*ammān tannai –* That four-handed personality is sarvēśvaran.

*tōyndānai nila magaḷ tōḷ* – One who became immersed in the divine shoulders of śrībhūmip pirātti.

*tūdu …* – Going as the messenger of pāṇḍavas, one who showed anger on the wrestlers who were waiting with the army, thinking to make him enter the room under ground and destroy him.

*emmānai …* – One who escaped that mischievous attempt and enslaved me by that act.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.6. Kidandanait

*kidandānait tadangadaluḷ paṇangaḷ mēvik kiḷar poṟiya maṟitiriya adanin pinnē padarndānai padu madatta kaḷiṟṟin kombu paṟittānaip pāridattai eyiṟu kīṟa idandānai vaḷai maruppin ēnamāgi irunilanum peru visumbum eydā vaṇṇam kadandānai emmānaik kaṇḍu koṇḍēn kadipoḻil sūḻ kadalmallait talasayanattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tadam – vast; kadaluḷ – in tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean); paṇangaḷ – under the hoods of ādiśēśan; mēvi – remaining firm; kidandānai – one who mercifully rested; kiḷar – cheerfully; poṟiya – having dots in many colours; maṟi – fawn; tiriya – as it roams around here and there; adanin pinnē – behind it; padarndānai – one who went; padu – flowing; madatta – having water of exultation; kaḷiṟṟin – kuvalayāpīdam’s (elephant); kombu – tusk; paṟittānai – one who plucked and threw; vaḷai – curved; maruppin – having horn; ēnamāgi – being varāha; idam pārai – vast earth; eyiṟu – with his divine tooth; kīṟa – to tear; idandānai – one who released it; iru nilanum – the vast earth; peru visumbum – the vast sky; eydā vaṇṇam – grew to become insufficient; kadandānai – one who measured the worlds with his divine feet and accepted; emmānai – sarvēśvaran who enslaved me; kadi – fragrant; poḻil – by garden; sūḻ – surrounded; talasayanattu – in stala sayanam (where he rests on the ground); kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, remaining firm under the hoods of ādiśēśan, mercifully rested in tiruppāṟkadal; he went behind the fawn which was cheerfully having dots in many colours and was roaming around here and there; he plucked and threw the tusk of kuvalayāpīdam which is having flowing water of exultation; being varāha having curved horn, he released the vast earth with his divine tooth to tear it; he grew to make the vast earth and vast sky become insufficient and measured the worlds with his divine feet and accepted them; I got to see such sarvēśvaran, who enslaved me, in stala sayanam in tirukkadalmallai, which is surrounded by fragrant garden.

*kidandānai …* – One who mercifully rested in the vast ocean which is vast enough for his resting, on ādiśēśan to not rise even if woken up by his divine consorts.

*kiḷar …* – As sītāp pirātti requested śrī rāma to catch the fawn which was having multi-coloured dots and was roaming around cheerfully since it was evil, he chased it to lose his path. He went so far as to become separated from pirātti. One who plucked the tusk of the huge, exultant elephant, effortlessly like plucking green leaves.

*pār idattai …* – Being mahāvarāha (great wild-boar) with a curved horn, he lifted up the earth with his divine tooth to cause a tear in it.

*iru nilan …* – He grew and measured the worlds to make the earth and sky become insufficient for him.

*emmānai* – One who enslaved me by placing his divine feet on everyone’s head.

*kaṇḍu koṇḍēn* – āḻvār is saying “I who escaped his divine feet when he himself placed it on everyone’s head, got to see him here”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.7. Penada valiyarakkar

*pēṇāda valiyarakkar meliya anṟu peruvarait tōḷiṟa nerittu anṟu avuṇar kōnaipūṇāgam piḷavedutta pōr vallōnaip poru kadaluḷ tuyil amarnda puḷḷūrdiyaiūṇāgap pēymulai nanju uṇḍān tannai uḷḷuvār uḷḷattē uṟaiginṟānaikkāṇādu tiridaruvēn kaṇḍu koṇḍēn kadipoḻil sūḻ kadalmallait talasayanattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – when rāvaṇa crossed his limits; pēṇāda – those did not respect śrī rāma to be sarvēśvaran; vali – strong; arakkar – rākśasas; peru – huge; varai – mountain like; tōḷ – shoulders; iṟa – to break; nerittu – embraced; anṟu – when his devotee prahlāda was harmed; avuṇar kōnai – the leader of demons, hiraṇya, his; pūṇ – decorated with ornaments; āgam – chest; pōr – in the battle; piḷavedutta – one who split and threw; vallōnai – one who is capable; poru – having rising waves; kadaluḷ – in tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean); tuyil amarnda – being the one who mercifully rested; puḷ ūrdiyai – being the one who rides garuda; pēy mulai – present in pūtanā’s bosom; nanju – poison; ūṇāga – as food which sustains him; uṇḍān tannai – being the one who mercifully consumed; uḷḷuvār – those who become immersed in him by thinking about his killing of pūtanā; uḷḷattu – in the heart; uṟaiginṟānai – one who remains firmly; kāṇādu – without seeing; tiridaruvēn nān – I who searched; kadi – fragrant; poḻil – by garden; sūḻ – surrounded; talasayanattu – in stala sayanam (where he rests on the ground); kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

śrī rāma embraced the huge mountain like shoulders of the rākśasas who did not respect him to be sarvēśvaran when rāvaṇa crossed his limits; when his devotee prahlāda was harmed, the capable emperumān split and threw the chest decorated with ornaments of the leader of demons, hiraṇya, in the battle; he mercifully rested in tiruppāṟkadal which has rising waves; he rides garuda; he mercifully consumed the poison which was present in pūtanā’s bosom, as food which sustains him; he remains firmly in the hearts of those who become immersed in him by thinking about his killing of pūtanā; I got to see such sarvēśvaran, who was not seen and whom I searched, in stala sayanam in tirukkadalmallai, which is surrounded by fragrant garden.

*pēṇāda …* – Without respecting him knowing that he is sarvēśvaran, the demoniac clan considered their strength and fought him; to destroy such demons. As said in periya tirumoḻi 5.7.5 “*enganē uyvar dānavar ninaindāl*” (how will the demoniac people survive?), only those who remain free from anger like that child \[prahlādāḻvān\] will survive and how can demoniac persons survive? In this manner, he destroyed the whole demoniac clan; at that time, he embraced the huge mountain like shoulders to break them; one who is well capable in warfare who tore apart the body of hiraṇya, the leader of demons whose chest was decorated with ornaments, and threw it.

*poru …* – One who mercifully rested in tiruppāṟkadal to perform these tasks.

*puḷ ūrdiyai* – When brahmā et al cry out, emperumān will ride periya tiruvadi (garuda) and appear in front of them – āḻvār is talking about that.

*ūṇāga …* – When pūtanā came in the disguise of his mother and nursed him, just as she could not sustain herself without nursing him, he could not sustain himself without consuming from her bosom – āḻvār is talking about that.

*uḷḷuvār …* – āḻvār is talking about emperumān dealing honestly with those who deal with him honestly and being evil to those who try to harm him. The devotees are only thinking in their heart about how kriṣṇa being very young, was trapped by pūtanā and how he escaped that danger.

*kāṇāda …* – Just as in yātanā śarīram (body given while reaping the results of the sins in hell, where there is no scope for joy), I, who am roaming around seeking to see you, got to see you, just as a hungry person got fed.

*kadi …* – āḻvār is saying- instead of hearing about him in śāstram and seeing him only in paramapadam \[after shedding this body\], I got to see him in this same place where I was having the thirst to see him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.8. Pennagi innamudam

*peṇṇāgi innamudam vanjittānaip piṟai eyiṟṟu anṟu adalariyāyp peruginānait taṇṇārnda vārpunal sūḻ meyyam ennum tadavarai mēl kidandānai paṇangaḷ mēvi eṇṇānai eṇṇiṟanda pugaḻinānai ilangoḷi sēr aravindam pōnṟu nīṇḍa kaṇṇānaik kaṇṇārak kaṇḍu koṇḍēn kadipoḻil sūḻ kadalmallait talasayanattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

in – sweet; amudam – nectar (to be not consumed by demons); peṇ āgi – assuming a feminine form; vanjittānai – one who cheated them; anṟu – when prahlāda was tormented by hiraṇya; piṟai – resembling a crescent moon; eyiṟu – teeth; adal – strong; ariyāy – being narasimha; peruginānai – one who grew; taṇ ārnda – cool; vār – flowing; punal – by water; sūḻ – surrounded by; meyyam ennum – known as tirumeyyam; tada varai mēl – on the huge hill; paṇangaḷ – on tiruvanantāḻvān; mēvi – firmly; kidandānai – one who mercifully reclined; eṇṇānai – one who is thought about by everyone; eṇ iṟanda – unlimited; pugaḻinānai – one who is having divine, auspicious qualities; ilangu oḷi sēr – having great radiance; aravindam pōnṟu – vast like lotus petal; nīṇḍa – wide; kaṇṇānai – one who is having divine eyes; kaṇ Ara – to quench the thirst of the eyes; kadi – fragrant; poḻil – by garden; sūḻ – surrounded; talasayanattu – in stala sayanam (where he rests on the ground); kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**bhattar mercifully explained – sarvēśvaran is the one who grants same stature as him for those who surrender unto him; considering this point, to reveal his simplicity, pramāṇams (scriptures) will highlight greatness of others \[other dēvatās\]; they will also manifest some greatness just as a worm’s movement may end up making a proper letter accidentally; seeing that, the people of the world will become bewildered that these dēvatās have certain greatness; thus, as the scriptures are in this manner and the cētanas (sentient beings) are less intelligent, without realising the essence of these scriptures, people will become drowned in the ocean which is known as in jitantā stōtram “samsāra sāgaram” (the ocean of nescience) had it not been for the wet (compassionate) words \[of truth\] of these āḻvārs.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān assumed a feminine form and cheated the demons by stopping them from consuming the sweet nectar; when prahlāda was tormented by hiraṇya, being strong narasimha with crescent moon like teeth, emperumān grew; he mercifully reclined on tiruvanantāḻvān on the huge hill known as tirumeyyam which is surrounded by cool, flowing water; he is thought about by everyone; he is having unlimited, divine, auspicious qualities; he is having wide divine eyes which are vast like greatly radiant lotus petal; I got to see such sarvēśvaran to quench the thirst of my eyes, in stala sayanam in tirukkadalmallai, which is surrounded by fragrant garden.

*peṇ āgi …* – One who fulfils the tasks of his devotees even by performing actions which don’t match him. One who is known as puruśa and puruśōttama, assumed a feminine form which does not match him, and cheated saying “this sweet nectar should not be given to demoniac persons”.

*piṟai …* – When the young prahlāda was tormented by harsh hiraṇya, emperumān having crescent moon like teeth,

*adal ariyāy* – being narasimha who would expand for battle.

*peruginānai* – Had emperumān not appeared when prahlāda vowed, he would have considered to have shrunk and become incapable and would have lost his saviourśip.

*taṇ ārnda …* – When father et al ceased to be saviour and set to be tormentor, emperumān thought “we should not leave our devotees at the disposal of such enemies” and mercifully reclined. emperumān who is the real father mercifully reclined thinking “I sent some as protective fathers who will be caring and will do favours; but when such persons become tormentors, I cannot remain absent there”. One who mercifully reclined on tiruvanantāḻvān in tirumeyyam which is having rejuvenating, flowing water.

*eṇṇānai* – āḻvār is speaking about emperumān mercifully thinking about protecting the world, while reclining on that mattress; alternative explanation – one who is constantly thought as “emperumān who is constantly cared by nityasūris has come here and mercifully reclined! What a simplicity!”

*eṇ iṟanda pugaḻānai* – āḻvār is saying that there is no limit to his greatness due to constantly thinking about the protection of the world. Alternative explanation – for those who meditate upon his qualities, there are abundant qualities in him which cannot be fully thought about.

*ilangu …* – His physical beauty is such that, even without his qualities, he cannot be given up. Being very radiant, for blossomed nature etc, lotus can be cited as an example. But lotus will be round in shape. Unlike that, his eyes will be very wide. Alternative explanation – there is unlimited enjoyability in his eyes.

*kaṇ Ara* – Just as being filled with badabāmukhāgni (a type of fire), the eyes are withered and longing to see him; to quench the thirst of such eyes, I got to see him. Attaining a distinguished form and seeing him after reaching the special abode of paramapadam, is similar to one person having hunger and another person getting food; I got to see with the eyes that longed to see him. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 40.3 “*gātrai: śōkābhi karśitai:*” (to see śrī rāma with this same body which suffered in separation).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.9. Tondayar

*toṇḍāyār tām paravum adiyinānaip padi kadanda tāḷāḷaṟku āḷāy uydal viṇḍānai tennilangai arakkar vēndai vilanguṇṇa valangai vāyc carangaḷ āṇḍu paṇḍāya vēdangaḷ nāngum aindu vēḷvigaḷum kēḷviyōdu angam āṟum kaṇḍānai toṇḍanēn kaṇḍu koṇḍēn kadipoḻil sūḻ kadalmallait talasayanattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

toṇḍu āyār tām – servitors who have special knowledge; paravum – to praise; adiyinānai – one who is having divine feet; padi – earth; kadanda – measured; tāḷ āḷarkku – for the one who has divine feet; āḷāy – serving; uydal – remaining firm in that principle of uplifting; viṇḍānai – being different; then – remaining in southern direction; ilangai – in lankā; arakkar – of rākśasas; vēndai – rāvaṇa who is the king; vilangu – animals; uṇṇa – to feed on; valangaivāy – with the right hand; sarangaḷ – arrows; āṇḍu – one mercifully shot; paṇḍu āya – eternal; nāngu vēdangaḷum – four vēdams; aindu vēḷvigaḷum – five great sacrifices; kēḷviyōdu – along with the instruction from preceptor; āṟu angamum – six auxiliary subjects; kaṇḍānai – one who placed (as means to attain him with the help of knowledge from scriptures); toṇḍanēn – I who am a servitor; kadi – fragrant; poḻil – by garden; sūḻ – surrounded; talasayanattu – in stala sayanam (where he rests on the ground); kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is having divine feet to be praised by servitors who have special knowledge; rāvaṇa, the king of rākśasas in lankā which is in the southern direction, remained different from those who serve the one who has divine feet which measured the earth and remain firm in that principle of uplifting; as śrī rāma, with his right hand, he mercifully shot such rāvaṇa; he placed the eternal four vēdams, five great sacrifices, the instructions from preceptors and six auxiliary subjects; I who am a servitor, got to see such sarvēśvaran in stala sayanam in tirukkadalmallai, which is surrounded by fragrant garden.

*toṇḍāyār …* – āḻvār is speaking about those who are mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍum*” (We should perform all types of services without leaving anything). āyār indicates ānār (those who are). One who has divine feet which are praised incoherently as said in mahābhāratam mōkśa darmam 34 “*śrutōyamartō rāmasya jāmadagnyasya jalpata:*” (This principle is heard from the blabbering of paraśurāma who is the son of jamadagni).

*padi …* – The one who differs from the state of thinking “Let us serve him and preserve our existence” on being won over by the simplicity of emperumān who has the nature of himself placing his divine feet thinking “we cannot let even one of our belongings, escape” – that is the one who is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36.11 “*na namēyam*” (even if I am split into two, I will not bow to someone; my body will only fall backward). One who remains the leader of those who differ from the principle of serving him and uplifting oneself.

*vilangu uṇṇa* – To make him to be eaten by dogs, jackals, eagles, hawks etc.

*valangaivāyc carangaḷ āṇḍu* – His standing with the bow in his \[right\] hand is sufficient for the destruction of the enemies and to attract the devotees.

*paṇḍu …* – Due to being unautored, being eternal, being free from faults, the collection of letters of vēdam which is repeated based on the recital of the teacher, the five great sacrifices which are samples for the vaidika rituals which are a good form of worship of bhagavān. six auxiliary subjects which explain that these rituals are good form of his worship, and those which are learnt by listening to teachers.

*kaṇḍānai* – One who placed the means to reach him through knowledge from śāstram.

*toṇḍānēn …* – I got to see him with my \[materialistic\] eyes instead of knowledge through śāstram.

## 2.5.10. Pada nagattanai

*pada nāgattaṇaik kidandu anṟu avuṇar kōnaip pada veguṇḍu marudidai pōyp paḻanavēlit tadamārnda kadal mallait talasayanattut tāmaraik kaṇ tuyil amarnda talaivar tannaik kadamārum karungaḷiṟu vallān vel pōrk kalikanṟi oli seyda inbap pādal tidamāga ivai aindum aindum vallār tīvinaiyai mudalariya vallār tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

padam – hooded; nāgam – tiruvanantāḻvān; aṇai – having as mattress; kidandu – one who mercifully reclined; anṟu – when prahlāda vowed; avuṇar kōnai – hiraṇya, king of demons; pada – to be killed; veguṇḍu – one who mercifully showed his anger; marudu idai – in between two maruda trees; pōy – one who crawled; paḻanam – water bodies; vēli – having all around; tadam – by ponds; ārnda – filled; kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; tala sayanattu – having the ground as his mattress; tāmaraik kaṇ tuyil amarnda – one who mercifully rested revealing his lotus-eyed nature; talaivar tammai – on sarvēśvaran; kadam ārum – very mad; karum kaḷiṟu – huge elephant; vallān – one who can ride; pōr – in battle; vel – one who can win over the enemies; kali kanṟi – āḻvār who removed the defects of kali yugam; oli seyda – mercifully spoke to have garlands of words; inbam – that which causes joy; ivai aindum aindu pādalum – this decad; vallār – those who can learn with meanings; tī vinaiyai – sins; tāmē – on their own; tidamāga – certainly; mudal ariya – to remove with the traces; vallār – will become capable

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran mercifully reclined, having hooded tiruvanantāḻvān as mattress; when prahlāda vowed, he mercifully showed his anger to kill hiraṇya, the king of demons; he crawled between the two maruda trees; revealing his lotus-eyed nature, he mercifully rested on the ground in tirukkadalmallai, which is surrounded by water-bodies and is filled with ponds; āḻvār who can ride very mad, huge elephant, who can win over enemies in the battle, who removed the defects of kali yugam, mercifully spoke to have garlands of words in this decad which cause joy on such sarvēśvaran; those can learn this decad with meanings, will certainly become capable to remove their sins along with the traces, on their own.

*padam …* – Mercifully reclining on tiruvanantāḻvān who is having expanded hoods due to being in contact with him, and further, even after leaving that mattress, if enemies remain \[he will destroy them\].

*marudidai pōy* … – Learning to walk by going through the two maruda trees which remained together to be said as a single tree; āḻvār praised sarvēśvaran who reveals that he is greater than all, having lotus-eyes, by mercifully reclining in tirukkadalmallai stalasayanam which is surrounded by water bodies and having beautiful ponds.

*kadam …* – Those who can practice this decad mercifully spoken with tune by āḻvār who can control a mad elephant through his mind and who never loses any battle.

*tī vinaiyai mudal ariya vallār tāmē* – They will become capable to eliminate the accumulated wealth of sins, on their own, along with the traces. Can the very weak jīvātmā who can accumulate the sins heavily, become capable of eliminating those sins? Yes. This is certain.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6 Enattin uruvagi

## 2.6.3. Enattin uruvagi

*ēnattin uruvāgi nilamangai eḻil koṇḍān vānattil avar muṟaiyāl magiḻndu ētti valangoḷḷa kānattin kadalmallait talasayanattu uṟaiginṟa jñānattin oḷi uruvai ninaivār en nāyagarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēnattin uruvāgi – Being in the form of varāha; nilamangai – śrī bhūmippirātti’s; eḻil – (without disturbing the) beauty; koṇḍān – freed the connection (from the wall of the universe) and accepted; vānattil avar – dēvatās such as brahmā et al; muṟaiyāl – as per their respective position; magiḻndu – being joyful; ētti – praise; valam koḷḷa – to serve favourably; kānattin – forest (in the western side); kadal – having ocean (in the eastern side); mallai – in mallāpuri; tala sayanattu – in stalasayanam; uṟaiginṟa – mercifully reclining; jñānattin oḷi uruvai – one who has a luminous form revealing knowledge; ninaivār – those who meditate upon; en – for me; nāyagar – will be lords

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being in the form of varāha, emperumān freed the connection of śrī bhūmip pirātti with the wall of the universe and accepted her; to be joyfully praised and served favourably by dēvatās such as brahmā et al as per their respective position, such emperumān who has a luminous form revealing knowledge, is mercifully reclining in stalasayanam in mallāpuri having forest in the western side and ocean in the eastern side; those who meditate upon such emperumān will be my lords.

*ēnam …* – Just as those, who would like to engage with their dear ones, would dress up the way as their dear ones would like, emperumān accepted the form of varāha and hid his earlier form. Just as a king would decorate the bed room and get noticed by the main consorts, emperumān showed the beauty in the form of mahāvarāha and accepted śrī bhūmip pirātti’s beauty. Since earth, one of the forms of śrī bhūmip pirātti, was consumed by the ocean, to rescue such earth, he accepted the form of varāha which will not retract from water and mud, uplifted the earth and protected the same. śrī bhūmip pirātti was captivated by his great quality thinking “One who leads the assembly of nityasūris has taken this form for my sake!” and lost her beauty to him.

*vānattil avar* – nityasūris in paramapadam.

*muṟaiyāl magiḻndu ētti* – People here praise him thinking “this is good \[for us\]”, but those in parampadam praise him out of love.

*muṟaiyāl …* – Wherever they go, they will praise in the proper manner. To praise and serve favourably in the manner it is done in paramapadam.

*kānattu …* – While śrī bhūmip pirātti lost her beauty and the nityasūris were praising, he ignored them and desired for the forest, matching the animal species he is born in. Matching the form of varāha, he desired the forest.

*kadal mallait tala sayanattu* – Those who are meditating about how bhagavān is present here in advance to protect everyone thinking “We cannot wait until the deluge to protect them”.

*jñānattin oḷi uruvai* – One who is an embodiment of jñānam.

*ninaivār en nāyagarē* – Instead of being one-sided love, they too will think “he (āḻvār) has come here for us” as my lords. When we don’t become their servitors, we won’t serve anyone else too.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.4. Vindarai

*viṇḍārai venṟu āvi vilanguṇṇa melliyalār koṇḍādum mallagalam aḻalēṟa venjamattuk kaṇḍāraik kadalmallait talasayanattu uṟaivārai koṇḍādum nenjudaiyār avar engaḷ kula deyvamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇḍārai – enemies; venṟu – destroyed (their); āvi – body; vilangu – animals such as dogs, jackals etc; uṇṇa – to eat; mel iyalār – tender natured women; koṇḍu – desirously; ādum – to embrace; mal – strong; agalam – (rāvaṇa’s) chest; aḻal – fire; ēṟa – to catch (and consume); venjamattu – in the cruel battle; kaṇḍārai – one who saw (to eliminate that fatigue); kadal mallait tala sayanattu – one who is mercifully reclining in stalasayanam in tirukkadalmallai; koṇḍādum nejudaiyār – those who are having in their heart and cherish that; avar – them; engaḷ kula deyvam – are the lords for our clan

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār says “those who immerse in him meditating upon how emperumān,though having the ability to destroy the enemies, is still reclining here thinking to accept them by reforming them to be favourable, are not just lords for myself but for my whole clan”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān saw that the enemies are destroyed and their bodies are eaten by dogs, jackals etc and that the strong chest of rāvaṇa, which was desirously embraced by tender natured women, caught fire in the cruel battle; those who are having in their heart and cherish such emperumān who is mercifully reclining in stalasayanam in tirukkadalmallai, are the lords of our clan.

viṇḍārai venṟu – He will only defeat those who say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36.11 “*na namēyam*” (even if I am split into two, I will not bow to someone; my body will only fall backward) even when given good advice. After killing vāli, building a bridge over the ocean, surrounding the town of lankā, limiting lankā inside its fort, sending angadap perumāḷ thinking “will he become favourable?” and giving good advice through him, and after rāvaṇa did not heed to any of that, śrī rāma destroyed all his soldiers in his presence, and as he came fighting unable to bear that, when he remained unarmed being humiliated by śrī rāma, as he returned the next day and requested “you can even kill me”, only then śrī rāma killed rāvaṇa. He only kills the enemies. Where there is even a slight doubt of favourable attitude, he would surrender as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4.19 “*sugrīvam śaraṇamgata:*” (śrī rāma surrendered to sugrīva) and in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4.18 “*sugrīvam nātam iccati*” (śrī rāma is desiring to have sugrīva as his lord).

perumāḷ (śrī rāma) said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 “*na tyajēyam katancana*”  (I don’t abandon by any means, those who befriend me) and in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.34 “*ētat vratam mama*” (I won’t fail anyone who surrenders unto me. This is my vow). mahārājar said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.27 “*vadyatām*” (Let vibhīśaṇa be killed). bhattar explains here – both śrī rāma and sugrīva mahārāja are caring for those who are surrendered unto them.

*āvi vilanguṇṇa* – To have eagles and vultures feed on the life which they (demons) greatly cared for, he killed them. How was that done? As the birds and animals jumped on the bodies of the demons when they were almost dead, they took away the remaining life from the demons.

*mel iyalār* … – On the chest which was nurtured by the pampering of tender women, which was never approached by fire just as dogs will fear wild beasts, same fire entered.

*venjamattu mal agalam aḻal ēṟak kaṇḍavārai* – Unlike rāvaṇa who moved the princes \[śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa\] away from sītāp pirātti with the help of evil persons through mischief and who came with the disguise of a favourable person and took away sītāp pirātti, perumāḷ fought in an honest battle; pirātti said “rāvaṇa! Your action does not befit brave persons”.

*aḻal ēṟak kaṇḍārai* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 111.82 “*adyavai nirbhayā lankām praviśtā: sūryēraśmaya:*” (Today, sun along with his rays, entered lankā fearlessly) – as rāvaṇa was lying dead, maṇḍōdari, his wife said “Sun’s rays are entering inside your regime” thinking that such act will wake him up (since sun would never enter lankā without fear when rāvaṇa was alive). Making fire enter the chest of such respectable rāvaṇa.

*kadal mallait tala sayanattu uṟaivārai* – emperumān is reclining thinking “only when one does not obey soft advice, one needs to be shown the stick”. Such emperumān.

*koṇḍādum nenjudaiyār* – Those who become immersed in him thinking “With what expectation has he arrived here? īsn’t it for us?” as in tiruccanda viruttam 63 “*ninṟirundu vehkaṇaik kidandadenna nīrmaiyē*” (What a simplicity in standing, sitting and reclining in tiruvehkā!) \[those who are like tirumaḻisai āḻvār\].

*engaḷ kula deyvam* – Our view is not limited to saying as in stōtra ratnam 6 “*kula daivatam tat pādāravindam*” (the divine lotus feet of the lord for our clan) \[We extend it up to his devotees being our lords\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.5. Piccac ciru peeli

*piccac ciṟu peelic camaṇ kuṇḍar mudalāyōr viccaikkiṟai ennum avviṟaiyaip paṇiyādē kaccik kidandavanūr kadalmallait talasayanam naccit toḻuvārai naccu endan nannenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

piccam – bunch of peacock wings; siṟu – small; peeli – having peacock feather; samaṇ guṇḍar – the lowly amaṇas (jainas); mudalāyōr – et al; viccaikku – for all knowledge; iṟai ennum – will have someone as the controller; avviṟaiyai – such person who is established by them; paṇiyādu – without surrendering unto; kacci – in tiruvehkā; kidandavan – one who is mercifully reclining in; Ur – the abode (where emperumān arrived for the sake of his devotee, puṇḍarīka); kadal mallait tala sayanam – (mercifully reclining) in stalasayanam in tirukkadalmallai; nacci – desiring; toḻuvārai – those who worship; endan – my; nenjē – Oh mind!; naccu – (you too) desire and worship

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

People such as the lowly amaṇas having bunch of peacock wings and small peacock feather, have someone as the controller for acquiring knowledge. Oh my mind! You desire and worship those who desire and worship one who is mercifully reclining in tiruvehkā and is doing the same in stahalasayanam in tirukkadalmallai, without surrendering unto such controllers of other groups.

*piccac ciṟu peeli samaṇ kuṇḍar* – Assuming the form of favourable persons (devotees) such as holding a bunch of peacock wings and holding a peacock feather branch in another hand, they will make people think “How righteous are these people!”

*samaṇ kuṇḍar* – The lowly people who have taken up the amaṇa philosophy. kuṇḍu – deep. Indicates the depth of lowliness. The lowly persons who reject vēdam.

*mudalāyōr* – Others starting with them. Here āḻvār is referring to bauddas and lōkāyatas.

*viccaikku iṟai ennum* – While they reject bhagavān who is revealed exclusively and fully through vēdam, they will imagine a new lord who is omniscient; now, they will have to search for authentic scriptures to prove that lord is indeed omniscient; they will try to prove that with their own words; subsequently the unautentic nature of such works will be exposed; in this manner, they will have someone as the controller of knowledge.

*avviṟaiyaip paṇiyādē* – āḻvār is saying avviṟai (that god) keeping his face away from them \[showing dislike\].

*paṇiyādē* – Not surrendering unto him \[their lord\] and following him, considering them to be trustworthy.

*kacci …* – For the sake of his devotees, emperumān reclined in tiruvehkā in opposite direction and having the opposite hand as head rest. tirukkadalmallai is the abode where he is mercifully reclining on the ground for the sake of his devotee, puṇḍarīka. The abode which is considered by bhagavān as the ultimate destination.

*naccit toḻuvārai* – Instead of vorśipping as a duty while having the mind elsewhere, those who consider the result of their desire is to worship him. Show friendship towards those who worship tirukkadalmallai considering the greatness of such worship.

*endan nal nenjē* – \[Oh mind!\] I am telling this due to my desire. I need not tell this to you who have greater desire towards him irrespective of my instruction. Am I showing the path to you who shows me the path? śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 6.7.28 “*mana Eva manuśyāṇām kāraṇam banda mōkśayō:*” (mind is the main reason for a man’s bondage and liberation).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.6. Pulankol

*pulankoḷ nidikkuvaiyōdu puḻaik kaimmā kaḷiṟṟinamum nalangoḷ navamaṇikkuvaiyum sumandu engum nānṟosindu kalangaḷ iyangum mallaik kadalmallait talasayanam valamkoḷ manattāravarai valam koḷ en madanenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pulan – senses; koḷ – that which captivates; nidik kuvaiyōdu – along with heap of gold; puḻai – having hole; kai – having hand \[trunk\]; mā – huge; kaḷiṟṟinamum – herd of elephants; nalam koḷ – good; nava maṇik kuvaiyum – collection of nine types of gems; sumandu – carrying; engum – wherever seen (due to the weight of the loaded materials); nānṟu – lowered; osindu – swaying; kalangaḷ – boats; iyangum – moving around; mallai – greatness; kadal mallait tala sayanam – one who is mercifully reclining on the ground in tirukkadalmallai; valam koḷ manattār avarai – those who consider circum-ambulating him matches their true nature; en mada nenjē – Oh my obedient mind!; valam koḷ – You circumambulate them and be uplifted

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirukkadalmallai has the greatness of having boats which are swaying and moving around; these boats are lowered in level due to carrying heap of gold which captivates the senses, herd of huge elephants which are having trunks (hand with a hole at the end) and good collection of nine types of gems. Oh my obedient mind! You circum-ambulate those who consider circum-ambulating emperumān who is mercifully reclining on the ground in such tirukkadalmallai, matches their true nature, and be uplifted.

*pulan koḷ nidik kuvaiyōdu* – With heap of gold which makes those who see it to think “*mamētam*” (why should I not have it?).

*puḻaik kai mā kaḷiṟṟinam* – Herd of huge elephants which have trunks (hand with hole at the end).

*nalam …* – Nine types of gems.

*nalam koḷ* – They are such good that they need not be brought to the shore and tested by experts to prove their value. The value can be readily seen then and there.

*sumandu* – Since these are good materials, people will load them into the boat without considering whether the boat can handle them or not.

*sumandu engum nānṟu osindu* – talasayanam in tirukkadalmallaim which has the greatness of these boats are fearfully moving around making one think “it is going to break this side; it is going to break on the other side” due to the weight of the loaded materials. āḻvār is not speaking about these because he has some use for them. But he is considering them to be decorations for the divyadēśam just as the gardens are.

*valam koḷ manattār avarai* – Those who have their hearts immersed in tirukkadalmallai. nanjīyar would mercifully explain “I was once following piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar and \[parāśara\] bhattar while they were circum-ambulating the temple. Unlike us who do it as a duty in a hurried manner, they were glancing at the beauty of the divine residences, divine towers as if they were imbibing them with their eyes”.

*avarai valam koḷ* – We cannot remain in their mood. But we should engage in following their foot steps.

*en mada nenjē* – āḻvār is saying “You are like-minded with me and you are obedient towards me”.
