## 2.6.7. Panjic ciru kulai

*panjic ciṟu kūḻai uruvāgi maruvādavanjap peṇ nanjuṇḍa aṇṇal mun naṇṇādakanjaik kadandavanūr kadalmallait talasayanamnenjil toḻuvārait toḻuvāy en tūy nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

panji – soft like cotton; siṟu – small; kūḻai – having hair; uruvāgi – having a form; maruvāda – not aligning; vanjam – having mischief; peṇ – pūtanā’s; nanju – poison in her bosom; uṇḍa – mercifully consumed; aṇṇal – being the lord of all; mun – previously; naṇṇāda – one who did not approach and surrender; kanjai – kamsa’s thoughts; kadandavan – kriṣṇa who crossed, his; kadal mallait tala sayanam – merciful reclining in stalasayanam in tirukkadalmallai; nenjil – with their heart; toḻuvārai – those who worship; en – obedient towards me; tūy – very pure; nenjē – Oh heart!; toḻuvāy – try to worship

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Having a small form with soft hair which resembles cotton, being the lord of all, kriṣṇa mercifully consumed the poison in the bosom of pūtanā who was not aligning with him and was mischievous. Previously, he crossed the thoughts of kamsa who did not approach and surrender unto him. Oh very pure heart who is obedient towards me! Try to worship those who worship such kriṣṇa’s merciful reclining in stalasayanam in tirukkadalmallai, with their heart.

*panjic ciṟu kūḻai uruvāgi* – kriṣṇa is having a toddler’s form where he is having soft hair which is as soft as cotton and cannot be gathered and placed in a knot. Alternatively – since kūḻai is a term which indicates a woman’s hair, this could be explaining pūtanā’s hair which is small and cannot be gathered and placed in a knot. \[A question arises\] Since she is in the beautiful disguise of mother yaśōdā, would she not have dressed up like her? \[Why small hair?\] Though she can dress up as much as possible, the \[demoniac\] hair will naturally show up.

*maruvāda vanjap peṇ* – Having unfavourable attitude in her heart, but covering it with favourable mood, she will come carefully. pūtnā who came in a disguise.

*nanjuṇḍa aṇṇal* – The lord who consumed her poison. It is said in harivamśam “*stanyam tat viśasammiśram rasyamāsīt jagatgurō:*” (her breast-milk which was poisoned, was very sweet for kriṣṇa who is the lord of the universe). He protected himself who is the lord of the universe \[emphasis on aṇṇal\].

*mun naṇṇāda …* – Previously, āḻvār explained about the killing of the enemies sent by kamsa. Now he is talking about the killing of this evil kamsa who is the root of all the enemies. Killing kamsa who remained thinking “I will not let him live in any way”, emperumān arrived at tirukkadalmallai to help the favourable ones. Those who worship such tirukkadalmallai.

*nenjil toḻuvārai* – Those who are unable to even open their mouth due to overwhelming experience in their heart.

*toḻuvāy* – Instead of searching for tirukkadalmallai and the nāyanār (lord) who is present there, just consider these devotees as your goal and worship them.

*en tūy nenjē* – You are very pure to remain in tadīya śēśatvam (being subservient to bhāgavatas).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.8. Selunir

*seḻunīr malark kamalam tirai undu vanpagattāl uḻunīr vayal uḻavar uḻap pin mun piḻaittu eḻunda kaḻunīr kadi kamaḻum kadalmallait talasayanam toḻunīr manattavarait toḻuvāy en tūy nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

uḻunīr – those who are naturally engaged in ploughing; uḻavar – farmers; seḻu – beautiful; nīr tirai – waves of water; malar – blossomed; kamalam – lotus flowers; undu – pushing; van – strong; pagattāl – engaging the bulls; vayal uḻa – as they farm the land; pin mun – back and forth; piḻaittu eḻundu – which escaped and had risen; kaḻunīr – sengaḻunīr (water-lily) and lotus flowers; kadi kamaḻum – the fragrance blowing; kadal mallait tala sayanam – stalasayanam in tirukkadalmallai; toḻu – vorśipping; nīr – having the quality; manattavarai – those who are having the heart; en tūy nenjē – Oh my pure heart!; toḻuvāy – try to worship

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The farmers who are naturally engaged in ploughing, are engaging strong bulls in ploughing the land where beautiful waves of water and blossomed sengaḻunīr (water-lily) and lotus flowers are being pushed around; stalaysayanam in tirukkadalmallai is where the fragrance blowing from such flowers escaped when pushed by those bulls back and forth, and rose. Oh my pure heart! Try to worship those who are having the quality of vorśipping such stalasayanam.

*seḻu nīr …* – The farm lands are so fertile there that they have blossomed lotus flowers and abundance of water. The farmers will push the water and the flowers with their feet to see the ground and farm the same.

*van pagattāl* – The bulls are so strong that they can even farm the lands in \[total\] deluge.

*uḻu nīr uḻavar uḻa* – As the farmers who always have the habit of sowing the seeds and ploughing the land, engage in ploughing.

*pin mun piḻaittu eḻum kaḻunīr kadi kamaḻum* – As they farm the land, the sengaḻunīr flowers which escaped from the back and forth movement (of the plough), will blow their fragrance to reduce their strain. Alternative explanation – as they plough ahead, the sengaḻunīr flowers which were left behind, will start smelling nice. Another explanation – *vayal uḻavar uḻap pin mun piḻatitteḻunda* – Previously the farmers would have ploughed the land. It appears that the farmers roamed around to make the sengaḻunīr flowers which escaped then, blossom.

*kadalmallai …* – Those who have the heart of always vorśipping tirukkadalmallai instead of vorśipping rarely.

*toḻuvāy en tūy nenjē* – Just as their constant activity is in vorśipping the divyadēśam, you have to constantly engage in vorśipping them. Your purity is such that I can instruct you, without any hesitation, that bhāgavata śēśatvam (being a servitor of bhāgavatas) is good.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.9. Pinangalidu

*piṇangaḷidu kādu adanuḷ nadamādu pinjaganōdu iṇangu tiruccakkarattu emperumānārkku idam visumbil kaṇangaḷ iyangum mallaik kadalmallait talasayanam vaṇangum manattār avarai vaṇangu en tan mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

piṇangaḷ – burning the corpses; idu kādu adanuḷ – in the cremation ground; nadam ādu – one who dances; pinjaganōdu – with rudra who is the destroyer; iṇangu – fitting well; tiruccakkarattu – having tiruvāḻi āḻvān (sudarśana cakram); emperumānārkku – for my lord; idam – being the abode; visumbil – present in the abodes such as heaven; gaṇangaḷ – groups of dēvatās \[celestial entities\]; iyangum – coming and vorśipping; mallai – having greatness; kadal mallait tala sayanam – stalasayanam in tirukkadalmallai; vaṇangu manattāravarai – those who have the heart to worship; enṟan mada nenjē vaṇangu – Oh my humble mind! You worship

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh my humble mind! You worship those who have the heart to worship my lord who is having sudarśana cakram which is fitting well and who is present in the great abode stalasayanam in tirukkadalmallai where rudra, the destroyer who dances in the cremation ground where corpses are burnt and the groups of dēvatās who are present in the abodes such as heaven, are coming and vorśipping.

*piṇangaḷ …* – With rudra who is not humane in his heart \[due to residing in cremation ground where ghosts are only seen\]; with rudra who is dancing in the cremation ground. Here āḻvār is talking about emperumān’s simplicity of giving a place in his divine form for those who are prideful (like dēvatās) and nityasūris. sudarśana cakram is representative for nityasūris.

*visumbil gaṇangaḷ iyangum mallai …* – āḻvār is speaking about nityasūris roaming around on the sky looking at emperumān’s simplicity of mercifully reclining in tirukkadalmallai. Alternatively, he is speaking about tirukkadalmallai having the greatness of celestial beings, who enjoy pleasures, such as yakśas, gandarvas who are roaming around on the sky.

*vaṇangum manattāravarai* – Those who have the heart to worship such emperumān.

*vaṇangu – mada nenjē* – Those who are vorśipping such emperumān are the object of worship for you instead of having to search for the emperumān whom they are vorśipping.

## 2.6.10. Kadi kamalum

*kadi kamaḻum nedumaṟugil kadalmallait talasayanattu adigaḷ adiyē ninaiyum adiyavargaḷ tam adiyān vadikoḷ nedu vēl valavan kalikanṟi oli vallār mudikoḷ nedu mannavar tam mudalvar mudal āvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kadi – good fragrance; kamḻum – blowing; nedu – wide; maṟugil – having streets; kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; tala sayanattu – mercifully reclining in stalasayanam; adigaḷ – lord’s; adi – divine feet; ninaiyum adiyavargaḷ tam – the servitors who think about, their; adiyān – being a servitor; vadi koḷ – having sharpness; nedu – big; vēl valavan – one who can fight using the spear; kali kanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; oli – this decad which is mercifully spoken by; vallār – those who can learn; mudi koḷ – crowned; nedu mannavar tam mudalvar – for the emperors

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Those who can learn this decad which is mercifully spoken by tirumangai āḻvār who can fight using the sharp, big spear and who is servitor of the servitors who think about the divine feet of the lord who is mercifully reclining in stalasayanam in tirukkadalmallai which is having very fragrant, wide streets, will become the leader for the crowned emperors.

*kadi kamaḻum …* – āḻvār who remained a servitor of the servitors who always meditate upon the divine feet of the sarvasvāmi (lord of all) who is mercifully residing in tirukkadalmallai which has wide streets where fragrance is blowing. For āḻvār, the identity of self is not jñānam (knowledge) and ānandam (bliss), but is bhāgavata śēśatvam (servitude towards bhāgavatas).

*vadi koḷ nedu vēl valavan* … – Just as he is holding the spear for protection in his hand, he is having servitude also as his unique identity, by remaining in servitude towards bhāgavatas. Those who can learn and practice this decad which is composed by āḻvār who is having sharp and huge spear and is capable of eliminating the enemies.

*mudi koḷ …* – Will be at par with nityasūris who are the controllers of brahmā et al who control the crowned, independent emperors of this world.

## 2.7 Tivalum

## 2.7.1. Tivalum

*tivaḷum veṇmadi pōl tirumugattarivai      seḻungadal amudinil piṟandaavaḷum ninnāgattiruppadum aṟindum     āgilum āsai vidāḷālkuvaḷaiyam kaṇṇi kolliyam pāvai     sollu nin tāḷ nayandirundaivaḷai un manattāl en ninaindirundāy?     idavendai endai pirānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tivaḷum – shining; veḷ – whitish; madipōl – like moon; tiru – beautiful; mugattu – having divine face; arivai – one who is in her youth (age group of 19 to 24); seḻu – vast; kadal – born in the ocean; amudinil – in the nectar; piṟanda – one who is born in; avaḷum – that periya pirāttiyār; nin – your highness’; āgattu – in the divine chest; iruppadum – being mercifully present; aṟindum – even after knowing; āgilum – still; āsai – desire towards your highness (my daughter); vidāḷ – not giving up; am – beautiful; kuvaḷai – like kuvaḷai flower; kaṇṇi – having beautiful eyes; kolli – made in kolli mountain; am – beautiful; pāvai – having beauty like that of a doll; nin – your highness’; tāḷ – divine feet; nayandu irunda – one who is desiring for; ivaḷai – in her matter; un manattāl – in your divine heart; en ninaindirundāy – what are you thinking?; idavendai – having arrived in tiruvidavendai; endai pirānē – Oh lord of my clan!; sollu – You should mercifully speak a word

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Even after knowing that periya pirāttiyār, who is having shining, whitish moon like beautiful, divine face, who is in her youth, and is born from the nectar which was born from the vast ocean, is mercifully residing on your highness’ divine chest, still my daughter parakāla nāyaki, is not giving up the desire towards your highness; she is having beautiful eyes which resemble kuvaḷai flower and is having the beauty of a beautiful doll made in kolli mountain; what are you thinking in your divine heart in the matter of my daughter who is having desire towards your highness’ divine feet? Oh lord of my clan who has arrived in tiruvidavendai! You should mercifully speak a word.

*tivaḷum …* – The boundless desire of parakāla nāyaki is explained here. When someone who is more knowledgeable/capable becomes immersed in the experience, the one who is looking from the shore should naturally try to escape from drowning.

*tivaḷum veṇmadipōl –* Here periya pirāttiyār’s greatness of even being able to immerse in such great enjoyment of bhagavān is highlighted.

*tivaḷum* – Shining. Alternatively – the lustre due to shining is highlighted.

*veṇmadipōl* – Being whitish due to the youthfulness. Here, not being satisfied even after enjoying emperumān eternally is indicated.

*tirumugattu* – Since the moon will not be an exact match for the radiance in her face, the face is said to be tirumugam (divine face). It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 3.28 “*candra kāntānanam rāmam atīva priyadarśanam*” (śrī rāma who is having beautiful face like moon; he is more pleasing than moon). That is – being without dark spots and not waning. The face is like an unchanging moon which is wholly enjoyable.

*arivai –* Even without the facial lustre, her youth is such that it will make others become immersed in her. This is her youth.

Further, her birth is explained.

*seḻum kadal amudinil piṟanda* – First there is the milk ocean, which becomes extraneous pulp where the nectar is the essence; now the nectar too becomes extraneous pulp and she is born as the essence. It is said in periya tirumoḻi 6.1.2 “*viṇṇavar amuduṇa amudil varum peṇ amudu*” (As the dēvas consume the nectar, periya pirāttiyār is the real nectar who came out of that nectar which was consumed by dēvas). While he \[emperumān\] was praised for his magnanimity for churning the ocean to help the dēvas, in reality, he churned to fulfil his own desire.

*avaḷum* – Even such periya pirāttiyār who is great by her beauty and birth.

*nin āgattu* – The chest which is desirable even for such periya pirāttiyār. She resides there with constant fear thinking “Will I lose my residence in this chest?” as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum*” (I will not leave even for a moment).

*iruppadum* – Remaining implies being together with him; she cannot tolerate the separation.

*aṟindum* – We cannot say that parakāla nāyaki desired for emperumān without knowing that periya pirāttiyār is present on his divine chest. The one who pursued emperumān considering periya pirāttiyār’s presence as her main support.

*āgilum āsai vidāḷāl* – The reason for her desire is periya pirāttiyār’s presence there as she thinks “Why would I miss out when periya pirāttiyār is present there?” That is the main support for her desire.

*kuvaḷai am kaṇṇi* – Here, parakāla nāyaki’s greatness over periya pirāttiyār’s greatness is explained. For periya pirāttiyār, the collective beauty of the face was explained by saying “tirumugam”. Here parakāla nāyaki’s greatness is indicated by “*kuvaḷai am kaṇṇi*” where the beauty of each part is explained. Just as periya pirāttiyār’s eyes are more beautiful than emperumān’s eyes as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 16.21 “*asitēkśaṇā*” (one with dark eyes), parakāla nāyaki’s eyes are more beautiful than periya pirāttiyār’s eyes.

*kolli am pāvai* – There is a doll in kolli mountain. In tamiḻ literature, this doll is shown as the example for physical beauty. There can be no comparison for her birth; one has to draw a picture or sculpt a statue in a perfect manner to compare with her.

*sollu* – It is not that you would not have thought about a solution for this; but thinking for such solution is not sufficient; you have to mercifully speak a word to eliminate our fear as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mā śuca:*” (do not grieve).

*nin tāḷ nayandu irunda* – This is another greatness of parakāla nāyaki over periya pirāttiyār; periya pirāttiyār desired for his chest; parakāla nāyaki is desiring for his divine feet. Those who know emperumān’s greatness, will desire for his chest; those who know the greatness of emperumān who is with periya pirāttiyār, will desire for his divine feet only.

*ivaḷai* – Since the mother is not satisfied with praising her daughter enough, she is pointing to her and saying “ivaḷai” (her).

*un manattāl* – What are you thinking in your divine heart where you can give solution even for those who are totally away from you?

*un manattāl* – I have given up finding a solution with my heart. Now, what are you thinking in your heart?

*idavendai endai pirānē* – Oh lord of my clan, who has arrived and stood in tiruvidavendai to save those who have lost their way to the unshakable, great abode of paramparadam! As said in tirunedundāṇḍagam 10 “*pinnānār vaṇangum sōdi*” (The radiant one who is vorśipped by those who lost that opportunity previously).

*sollu* – This is the verb.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.2. Tulambadu muruval

*tuḷambadu muṟuval tōḻiyarkku aruḷāḷ tuṇai mulai sāndu koṇḍu aṇiyāḷ kuḷambadu kuvaḷaik kaṇṇiṇai eḻudāḷ kōla nanmalar kuḻaṟku aṇiyāḷ vaḷambadu munnīr vaiyam mun aḷanda mālennum, mālina moḻiyāḷ iḷambadi ivaḷukku en ninaindirundāy? idavendai endai pirānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuḷam padu – to defeat pomegranate seeds; muṟuval – with the teeth; tōḻiyarkku – in front of her friends; aruḷāḷ – not smiling; tuṇai – having beauty of togetherness; mulai – bosoms; sāndu koṇḍu – with sandalwood paste; aṇiyāḷ – not decorating; kuḷam – in pond; padu – present in; kuvaḷai – like kuvaḷai flower; kaṇ iṇai – in two eyes; eḻudāḷ – not applying black pigment; kōlam – beautiful; nal – distinguished; malar – flowers; kuḻaṟku – in the hair; aṇiyāḷ – not wearing; vaḷam – precious items (such as gems); padu – originating; munnīr – (surrounded) ocean; vaiyam – earth; mun – while going and accepting water from mahābali; aḷanda – measured and accepted; māl ennum – she says that he is the great one; māl – for her love; inam – being a match; moḻiyāḷ – having speech; iḷam padi – tender natured; ivaḷukku – on her matter; en ninaindirundāy – what are you thinking?; idavendai – having arrived in tiruvidavendai; endai pirānē – Oh lord of my clan!; sollu – You should mercifully speak a word

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

She is not smiling at her friends with her teeth which can defeat pomegranate seeds; she is not decorating her bosoms which are beautiful together, with sandalwood paste; she is not applying black pigment in her two eyes which resemble kuvaḷai flower in pond; she is not wearing beautiful, distinguished flowers in her hair; she says that emperumān is the great one who accepted and measured the earth which is surrounded by ocean where precious items originate from, while going and accepting water from mahābali; what are you thinking in the matter of parakāla nāyaki who is tender natured and whose speech matches her love? Oh lord of my clan who has arrived in tiruvidavendai! You should mercifully speak a word.

*tuḷam padu muṟuval* – tuḷam indicates māduḷam (pomegranate). That is usually compared to teeth. That is spoken about; \[alternative explanation\] nanjīyar would mercifully say “A tamiḻ scholar explains tuḷam to be stem of peacock feather”. That is compared in the context of the white colour. padugai – occurring; the smile which reveals the teeth; \[that is\] when we see the teeth, we are reminded of pomegranate seeds. Alternative explanation – being destroyed; speaking about being won over by the smile. Both these examples are spoken about.

*tōḻiyarkku aruḷāḷ* – Due to her distress, she will not smile in front of her mothers. Now, this is the main wealth of her lord. He will become engaged with that smile as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 63.12 “*kāntasmitā*” (one who has a gentle smile). That smile makes her friends sustain. Thus, she is making her friends who seek her smile, to starve. When she smiles to reveal her joy after uniting with the lord, they will live by having that as their sustenance.

*tuṇai mulai …* – She starved her lord also.

*tuṇai mulai* – Not having any other match, her bosoms can only be compared to each other.

*sāndu koṇḍu aṇiyāḷ* – If only she had set out to decorate her bosoms with sandalwood paste expecting his arrival, he would think “My arrival is desirable for her” and have scope to engage with her. Thus, she is not giving that opportunity to him.

*kuḷam …* – She is not decorating her eyes which resemble kuvaḷai flower blossomed from a perennial pond, for the sake of adding auspiciousness. Since these eyes are enjoying emperumān who is an ocean of qualities which is similar to an ocean of precious gems, they need not be decorated with anything else. Now, the black pigment decoration is to add auspiciousness. Only when she decorates her eyes with black pigment, will he have the opportunity to engage with her. She is not allowing that.

*kōlam …* – She is not decorating her hair, which is usually decorated with a mix of flowers instead of a single flower, with any flower. Since she is known as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-10-2-mayam-seyyel/) “*vāsanjey pūnguḻalāḷ*” (having distinguished, divine hair which brings great fragrance), she need not decorate it separately with flowers, but does so for auspiciousness. Even that is not done now. Her eliminating the decoration for the places which are desirable for the lord, is to eliminate the aspects which sustain him.

*vaḷam …* – emperumān who commonly protects everyone, is ignoring me.

*vaḷam padu munnīr* – Ocean.

*māl ennum* – One who is mad about protecting the entities which are protected by him. He is only ignoring parakāla nāyaki.

*māl ina moḻiyāḷ* – One who has speech which matches her love. It appears as if her love overflowed and became words.

*iḷam padi ivaḷukku* – For the one who is in a youthful state. For the one who is tender natured. parakāla nāyaki is more tender than sītāp pirātti who was separated from you and placed in aśōka vanam, who still said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 30.30 “… *tat tasya sadruśam bhavēt*” (it will be appropriate for śrī rāma, who is capable of annihilating enemies, to agitate lankā with his arrows and redeem me). It is well known that parāśara bhattar mercifully said – tirumangai āḻvār’s tenderness is such that he cannot tolerate too much union and too much separation similar to the tender persons who can neither eat more nor less.

*ivaḷukku …* – What are you, who have arrived and mercifully resided in tiruvidvendai knowing about her nature, to unite with her, thinking in your divine heart?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.3. Sandamum punum

*sāndamum pūṇum sandanak kuḻambum tadamulaikku aṇiyilum taḻalām pōnda veṇ tingaḷ kadir suda meliyum porukadal pulambilum pulambum māndaḷir mēni vaṇṇamum ponnām vaḷaigaḷum iṟaiṇillā endan ēndiḻai ivaḷuku en ninaindirundāy? idavendai endai pirānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

sāndamum – sandalwood paste mixed with other fragrant materials; pūṇum – pearl necklace; sandanak kuḻambum – sandalwood fluid; tadam mumlaikku – on the huge bosom; aṇiyilum – though applied; taḻalām – it burns like fire; pōnda – appeared; veḷ – white; tingaḷ – moon’s; kadir suda – as the rays burn; meliyum – she suffered (due to that); poru – rising waves; kadal – ocean; pulambil – when it makes noise; pulambum – she also calls out; māndaḷir – like mango spruce; mēni – divine form’s; vaṇṇamum – colour; ponnām – becoming pale; vaḷaigaḷum – bangles; iṟai – even little bit; nillā – not remaining; enṟan – my; ēndu – worn; iḻai – having ornament; ivaḷukku – for her; en ninaindirundāy – what are you thinking?; idavendai – having arrived in tiruvidavendai; endai pirānē – Oh lord of my clan!; sollu – You should mercifully speak a word

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Though she has decorated herself with sandalwood paste mixed with other fragrant materials, pearl necklace and sandalwood fluid on her huge bosom, it burns like fire; as the rays of the white moon which appeared, burn, she suffered; when the ocean with rising waves makes noise, she also calls out; her divine form’s colour which looks like mango spruce is becoming pale; her bangles are not even remaining a little bit on her; having arrived in tiruvidavendai, what are you thinking for my daughter who is wearing ornaments? Oh lord of my clan! You should mercifully speak a word.

*sāndamum …* – She has crossed the boundary of being protected by us. Sandalwood paste which was buried under the ground for a long time, pearl necklace and sandalwood fluid.

*tada mulaikku aṇiyilum* – Previously everyone would withdraw thinking “How can we remedy the situation when we don’t know the reason?”; still, since she is continuously suffering, they would think “let us try the methods which are used by everyone and see if there is any remedy” and will try to pamper her with these materials; but these materials will end up burning her more.

*pūṇ* – Will pūṇ refer to pearl necklace? Since the necklace is there to cool her down, it could be said as pearl necklace (which reduces heat). When asked “Is sandalwood paste not a heat producing material?” that is why it is explained to be sandalwood paste which was buried under the ground and cooled. When asked “Would sandalwood paste indicate mixed with fragrant materials?” since this is used to pamper her, it can be said in that manner. This is similar to pūṇ (ornament) indicating pearl necklace.

*sāndamum …* – When an old tree burns, it will burn along with the tree-barks; similarly, she is burning along with the decorations which are applied on her. Just as dry firewood is set on fire, as these materials are applied on her, they burn along with her.

*pōnda …* – As the rays of the moon appeared just then, she suffered. When the moon’s rays cause heat, nothing else can be done. Now, when she was together with her lord, as said in periya tirumadal “*munnam mugiḻtta mugil nilā*” (the moon with cool rays), the same moon was favourable.

*poru kadal* – When the waves clash with each other and the ocean makes noise, she will call out like an ocean being in the opposite side, competing with it.

*māndaḷir …* – Her complexion which resembled the colour of mango spruce, became pale.

*vaḷaigaḷum iṟai nillā* – It is not just one bangle which is hanging on the sky (instead of her shoulder). As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.29 “*śaitilyam upayāntyāśu karēśu valayānyapi*” (As kriṣṇa left us, our bangles are also leaving us immediately). In comparison with kriṣṇa, they are greatly distinguished. At least kriṣṇa would say “I won’t leave” giving a hint about the separation and leave; they left us immediately.

*enṟan ēndiḻai* – My daughter who is decorated with ornaments. The mother is thinking that seeing her daughter decorated with ornaments, will sustain her. \[Mother says\] It appears that my enjoyment in seeing her with the ornaments will end now.

*idavendai …* – Did you come here to make her relinquish her ornaments as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 26.5 “*naivārtai: na ca bhūśaṇai:*” (There is no use with wealth or ornaments)? Did you not come here to compensate the loss \[for sītāp pirātti\] which occurred in śrī rāmāvatāram?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.4. Uliyil peridal

*ūḻiyil peridāl nāḻigai ennum     oṇ sudar tuyinṟadāl ennum āḻiyum pulambum anṟilum uṟangā     tenṟalum tīyiniṟ kodidām tōḻiyō! ennum tuṇaimulai arakkum     sollumin en seygēn? ennum ēḻai en ponnukku en ninaindirundāy?     idavendai endai pirānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāḻigai – nāḻigai duration (24 minutes); ūḻiyil – more than a kalpa (one day of brahmā); peridu – stretching very much; ennum – she told that; oṇ – having great radiance; sudar – sun; tuyinṟadu ennum – she will tell that he has set; āḻiyum – ocean; pulambum – is making noise; anṟilum – anṟil bird; uṟangā – is not sleeping; tenṟalum – southerly breeze; tīyinil – more than fire; kodidām – is blowing in a cruel manner; tōḻī – Oh friend!; Oh! ennum – will call her saying “Oh”; tuṇai mulai – two nipples; arakkum – will control; en seygēn – what shall I do; sollumin ennum – she will tell “tell me”; ēḻai – very desirous; en – one who is born to me; ponnukku – in the matter of this best girl; en ninaindirundāy – what are you thinking?; idavendai – having arrived in tiruvidavendai; endai pirānē – Oh lord of my clan!; sollu – You should mercifully speak a word

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter told that one nāḻigai (24 minutes) stretches to be a kalpa (1 day of brahmā); she will tell that the greatly radiant sun has set; ocean is making noise; anṟil bird is not sleeping; southerly breeze is blowing in a cruel manner more than fire; she will call her friend saying “Oh!”; she will control her two nipples; she will tell me “What shall I do?” What are you thinking in the matter of this best girl who is born to me? Oh lord of my clan who has arrived in tiruvidavendai! You should mercifully speak a word.

*ūḻiyil peridāl nāḻigai ennum* – Even kalpa has an end, but these nāḻigais are going in an endless manner. This \[nāḻigai\] cannot be explained in comparison to anything else, and can only be said as in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*nēti nēti*” (bhagavān is not of this nature, not of this nature). The order of ūḻi being larger than nāḻigai is gone.

*oṇ sudar tuyinṟadāl ennum* – She told that sun who measures the nāḻigai (time) has disappeared. Sun becomes destroyed along with all other items which get destroyed towards the end of the kalpa; unlike then, now, though he is roaming around, his effect is not felt. Sun, who would fully eliminate the sorrows of night (due to separation from loved ones) by his appearance, has not come. It appears that bhagavān’s orders as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*bhīśōdēti sūrya:*” (Sun appears due to fear for bhagavān) have lapsed. Here “*tuyil*” indicates both sleep and death.

*āḻiyum pulambum* – As the ocean observed “Sun who is younger to me, is harming her. Why should I remain silent?” and set out to harm parakāla nāyaki. As the greatly powerful ocean loses its strength and makes noise out of fear/sorrow, it reminds her of how bhagavān in śrī rāmāvatāram, who is most powerful, became weak and spoke with fear/sorrow \[in separation from sītāp pirātti\].

*anṟilum uṟangā* – The sleepless state of the anṟil bird reminds her of her divine consort (emperumān) remaining sleepless while being together with her.

*tenṟalum tīyinil kodidām* – The coolness of the southerly breeze reminds her of her beloved lord’s touch and harms her. It appears that to reduce the heat of southerly breeze, one should dry it in the fire.

*tōḻiyō ennum* – \[Mother says\] I am not fortunate enough to be called out “ammē” (Oh mother!) when she is harmed by something \[she only calls her friend\]. \[parakāla nāyaki says\] “Oh evil friend! You told me that everything will become favourable and cool me down, as we unite with him. But you have caused the whole town to show enmity towards me”

But, her youth will not wait when she cries out saying “*tōḻiyō*“.

*tuṇai mulai arakkum* – As the bosoms start tormenting her saying “Show me what \[who\] is apt for me”, she will control her bosoms just as the children will cry out “Food! Food!” during famine and will be silenced by saying “Shut your mouth! Shut your mouth!”. periya tirumadal “*munnirundu mūkkinṟu*” (being present in front of my eyes and ageing more and more), as I witness, my youth is fading. If we are going to lose the youth anyway, why don’t I have my bosoms in my back \[at least I won’t see them age\]?.

*sollumin en seygēn ennum* – The torment by the bosoms is much greater than the torment given by southerly breeze etc. When all of those were tormenting, she cried out for her friend. Now, when these bosoms are tormenting her, she is asking everyone including friends, mothers to respond.

*ēḻai* – Even when told “You won’t get”, she would show desire as if she will get it.

*en ponnukku* – One who is so great that we cannot let her and her desire be tormented.

*idavendai* – What are you, who show your desire through your action \[by having bhūmip pirātti on your left\], unlike her who is showing her desire through speech, thinking about it?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.5. Odilum

*ōdilum un pēr anṟi maṟṟōdāḷ    urugum nin tiruvuru ninaindu kādanmai peridu kaiyaṟavu udaiyaḷ    kayal nedungaṇ tuyil maṟandāḷ pēdaiyēn pēdai piḷḷaimai peridu    teḷḷiyaḷ vaḷḷi nuṇmarungul ēdalar munnā en ninaindirundāy?    idavendai endai pirānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

idavendai endai pirānē! – Oh my lord in tiruvidavendai!; ōdilum – While speaking; un pēr anṟi – other than your name; maṟṟu – anyone else’s name; ōdāḷ – will not say; nin – your; tiruvuru – physical beauty; ninaindu – thinking about; urugum – she is melting; kādanmai – desire (in your matter); peridu – is growing more and more; (due to that); kaiyaṟavu udaiyaḷ – she is anguishing like the one who has lost her belonging; kayal – kayal (carp) fish like; nedu – very wide; kaṇ – in the eyes; tuyil – having sleep; maṟandāḷ – forgotten; pēdaiyēn pēdai – my very desirous daughter’s; piḷḷaimai – childishness; peridu – is big; (on your matter); teḷḷiyaḷ – she is having great clarity; vaḷḷi – like a creeper; nuṇ – slender; marungul – she who is having waist; ēdalar munnā – in front of those who don’t like; en ninanidirundāy – What are you thinking to do?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh my lord in tiruvidavendai! My daughter parakāla nāyaki, while speaking, will not say any other name than your name; she is melting thinking about your physical beauty; her desire is growing more and more in your matter; she is anguishing like the one who has lost her belonging; her kayal fish like very wide eyes have forgotten to sleep; my very desirous daughter’s childishness is big; she is having great clarity in your matter; in front of those who don’t like, what are you thinking to do for her who is having creeper like slender waist?

*ōdilum …* – To start with, she will not speak; but if she does,

*un pēr anṟi maṟṟu ōdāḷ* – She is not saying “aiyar, ācci” (Father, mother),

*urugum nin tiru uru ninaindu* – As she thinks about emperumān through his name, she will melt like ice.

*kādanmai peridu* – Her desire is greater than his physical beauty.

*kaiyaṟavu udaiyaḷ* – Her loss is greater than her desire.

When asked “What is the limit of her loss?”

*kayal …* – Eye which resembles a kayal (carp) fish, youthful and vast. Just as huge towns become empty, the sleep has exited fully from the vast eye.

*pēdaiyēn pēdai* – My foolish daughter. I who am having foolishness to pray to get a daughter like her. As said in tiruviruttam 37 “*nedungālamum kaṇṇan nīṇmalarp pādam*” (Praying for a long time to get kriṣṇa’s long flower like divine feet).

*piḷḷaimai peridu* – Her childishness is greater than her youthfulness. In worldly matters, she is not knowledgeable as those who are at her age.

*teḷḷiyaḷ* – But in your matters she is greater than those who have heard vēdāntam.

*vaḷḷi nuṇ marungul* – Her physical beauty is such that one cannot abandon her due to her childish nature. Her childishness and wisdom are of no use; her beauty is sufficient for you to not abandon her.

*ēdalar munnā* – In front of the enemies who scold her saying “You desired for him; now you have nicely attained him!”.

*en ninaindirundāy* – What are you, who thinks “I should not let her suffer in front of the enemies”, thinking in her matter? stōtra ratnam 25 “*natē’nurūpa:*” (It is not apt for you). It is alright for śrīvaikuṇṭanātan to abandon her. But you, who are in tiruvidavendai (who have arrived for this purpose), cannot do it.

## 2.7.6. Tan kudikkedum

*tan kudikku ēdum takkavā ninaiyāḷtadangadal nudangeyil ilangaivankudi madanga vāḷamar tolaittavārttai kēttu inbuṟum mayangumminkodi marungul surunga mēl nerungimenmulai ponpayandirundaenkodi ivaḷukku en ninaindirundāy?idavendai endai pirānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

than – her; kudikku – for the clan; takkavā – apt path; ēdum – any; ninaiyāḷ – does not analyse and know!; tadam – vast; kadal – ocean; nudangu – curved; eyil – having fort; ilangai – present in lankā; van – strong demons’; kudi – clan; vāḷ amar – in the cruel battle; tolaitta – destroyed; vārttai – news; kēttu – hear; inbuṟum – become joyful; (again); mayangum – will faint; min – lightning; kodi – like a slender creeper; marungul – waist; surunga – to bend; mēl – above; nerungi – close to each other; pon payandirunda – one who has golden coloured paleness; mel – soft; mulai – having bosoms; en kodi ivaḷukku – in my daughter’s matter; en ninaindirundāy – what are you thinking?; idavendai – having arrived in tiruvidavendai; endai pirānē – Oh lord of my clan!; sollu – You should mercifully speak a word

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter parakāla nāyaki does not analyse and know the apt path for her clan; she becomes joyful as she heard the news of lankā which is surrounded with vast ocean and curved fort where the clan of strong demons was destroyed in a cruel battle; then she will faint. What are you thinking in the matter of my daughter who is having soft bosoms which have golden coloured paleness, close to each other, above her waist, which resembles lightning and a slender creeper, and which makes her waist bend? Oh lord of my clan! Having arrived in tiruvidavendai, you should mercifully speak a word.

*than kudikkēdum* – Just as it is said in “*emperumānār darśanam*” (śrī rāmānuja darśanam), mother is saying “*than kudi*” (My daughter’s clan) instead of “*nam kudi*” (our clan). Instead of saying as per our understanding, perumāḷ himself would mercifully say “*irāmānusan udaiyār*” (servitors of śrī rāmānuja). piḷḷān would say “If a precious gem stone is placed in the middle and strung, the necklace will be fully valued as that gem \[similarly, emperumānār’s presence in the middle of the guruparamparā adds glory to it\]”.

*than kudikku ēdum takkavā ninaiyāḷ* – This is how parakāla nāyaki is now as she is saying “Are you going to protect your dignity or not?” We thought that we could increase the dignity of our clan starting with her. But while we were thinking like that, she is pushing it down into the ocean.

*than kudikku* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 67.22 “*janakānām kulē kīrtim āhariśyati mē sutā*” (king janaka tells of his daughter “My daughter sītā will bring celebrity to the clan of janakas”), it is after her birth in this clan that the clan attained new glories. One day, when embār heard how beautifully parāśara bhattar learnt/recited, he shed \[happy\] tears; with melted heart, he showed bhattar mercifully saying “*janakānām kulē kīrtim āhariśyati mē sutā*”. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 30.30 “… *tat tasya sadruśam bhavēt*” (it will be appropriate for śrī rāma, who is capable of annihilating enemies, to agitate lankā with his arrows and redeem me), we cannot worry for our result and should remain “It is achieved by his grace”. sītāp pirātti remained thinking “If we are reaching him, what is the purpose of these other means?” parakāla nāyaki remains thinking “Shall we not reach to be in front of him by any means, and then remain calm?”

*ēdum takkavā ninaiyāḷ* – She is thinking to perform madal, or to kill herself by hanging from a tree.

*ninaiyāḷ* – The divine mother is following her daughter’s thoughts, since she cannot lose her.

*tadam kadal …* – She will become pleased thinking about the helping nature of emperumān so that she need not try to hang herself etc. He helped sītāp pirātti after she tried to kill herself. Having the vast ocean as a moat, and the fort which will cause shivers in the enemies as they hear about it. Alternatively, having curved fort.

*ilangai van kudi madanga* – Not just the protection for the town, but the clan which is grown greatly due to the boons they (members of the clan) have received. To have such strong clan destroyed. Unlike rākśasas who fought deceitful battle, śrī rāma fought an honest battle to destroy such strong clan – that is the incident from śrī rāmāyaṇam. Hearing that,

*inbuṟum* – She becomes pleased thinking “When he helped another woman (sītāp pirātti) who was in the same situation (as I am), was it not similar to helping me!”

*mayangum* – She becomes bewildered thinking “Instead of an unhelpful person not helping, he is helpful in nature, yet not helping me!” and faints. First she becomes pleased thinking about his closeness and then faints thinking about him not helping even after being so close.

*min kodi …* – Could she be abandoned if she faints? \[No\] The bosoms at the upper portion of her body push to further shrink the lightning and creeper like waist, just as one would sit atop something and cut the base.

*men mulai* – Though the bosoms are hard in nature, they are said to be soft here to indicate that they cannot tolerate the separation.

*pon payandu irunda* – The paleness covered her body to make her beauty become dust.

*en kodi* – The mother is thinking “even if he is not helping seeing her beauty, he will at least help seeing her family heritage”.

*ivaḷukku en ninaindu irundāy* – Could you not help her even after she has paleness, firm belief, sorrow, beauty and family heritage?

*idavendai endai pirānē* – Your presence in tiruvidavendai reveals that you have got more paleness than she \[in separation from her\]. You would have remained in śrīvaikuṇṭam had your divine form not become pale. What are you, who have arrived and are mercifully residing in tiruvidavendai revealing your paleness, thinking in her matter?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.7. Ulam kanindu irukkum

*uḷanganindirukkum unnaiyē pidaṟṟum unakkanṟi enakku anbonṟu ilaḷāl vaḷangani poḻil sūḻ mālirunjōlai māyanē! enṟu vāy veruvum kaḷangani muṟuval kārigai peridu kavalaiyōdu avalam sērndirunda iḷangani ivaḷukku en ninaindirundāy? idavendai endai pirānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

uḷam kanindu irukkum – She has a contented heart; (while speaking); unnaiyē – You who are the object of her union; pidaṟṟum – incoherently speaking; unakkanṟi – other than in your matter; enakku – in my matter, where I have longed forever to give birth to her; onṟu – even a little; anbilaḷ – not having any love; vaḷam – very sweet; kani – having fruits; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; mālirunjōlai – one who is mercifully residing in tirumālirunjōlai; māyanē enṟu – saying “Oh one who is having amazing ability!”; vāy veruvum – she is blabbering; kaḷam kani – sweet like kaḷam fruit; muṟuval – smile; kārigai – having beauty; peridu kavalaiyōdu – with great sorrow in heart; avalam sērndirunda – being with paleness; iḷam kanni – young girl; ivaḷukku – in her matter; en ninaindirundāy – what are you thinking?; idavendai – having arrived in tiruvidavendai; endai pirānē – Oh lord of my clan!; sollu – You should mercifully speak a word

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter has a contented heart; she is incoherently speaking about you who are the object of her union; other than your matter, she is not even having a little bit of love for me who has longed forever to give birth to her; she is blabbering saying “Oh one who is having amazing ability and who is mercifully residing in tirumālirunjōlai surrounded by gardens having very sweet fruits!” Oh lord of my clan! What are you thinking in the matter of this young girl who is having sweet smile and beauty like the kaḷam fruit, and has great sorrow in heart and paleness? You should mercifully speak a word.

*uḷam kanindu irukkum* – Heart will be matured and will not reveal what is being thought in it. Heart being well matured is when emperumān who should enjoy does not do so, being helpless.

*unnaiyē pidaṟṟum* – Until she started speaking, the divine mother thought “This is based on mutual love”. As said in mahābhāratam śānti parvam 200 “*jāmadagnyasya jalpata:*” (I have heard paraśurāma, son of jamadagni, speaking incoherently), she is speaking incoherently while you don’t care for her. Had there been mutual love, then her speech would also be coherent.

*unakku …* – She cut off her desire “Will she not speak about me once?” She only has attachment towards her friends who made her become totally dependent on him, or towards him.

*vaḷam …* – She will relentlessly speak about his efforts which lead to such great love towards him. She thinks about emperumān’s amazing qualities and activities of presenting himself to mlēccas (those who are outside the varṇa system) in tirumālirunjōlai which is looked down upon by āryas (noble people), which is surrounded by garden having abundant fruits, and is speaking unconsciously by her impressions (on him) being her teacher inducing her to speak.

*vāy veruvum* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 32.11 “*vicintyā vācā bruvati tamēva*” (Since I am pondering with my mind about that śrī rāma only, and always saying “śrī rāma! śrī rāma!”) – first she was meditating, subsequently she could not even do it and was just repeating based on previous impressions.

*kaḷangani muṟuval* – Son! Who \[parakāla nāyaki\] is relentlessly speaking what should be spoken by whom \[bhagavān\]? śrī rāma would relentlessly speak about sītāp pirātti as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 64.78 “*sītēva cārudatīm*” (sītā who is having a smiling face). Just as the heart of sītāp pirātti, who desired to win over śrī rāma, was appearing in a well matured manner, parakāla nāyaki’s smile is very pleasing. śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 63.12 beautifully explains how śrī rāma was won over by sītāp pirātti’s smile. “*asmin mayā sārdam udāraśeelā śeelātalē pūrvam upōpaviśtā \| kāntasmitā lakśmaṇa jātahāsā tvāmāha sītā bahuvākya jātam \|\|*”

- *asmin* – Along with iḷāiya perumāḷ, perumāḷ was searching for pirātti while they were separated from her; at that time, as they came across a spot where perumāḷ would play water games with pirātti, perumāḷ saw that spot and mercifully spoke to iḷaiya perumāḷ.
- *asmin* – Previously I had great enjoyment where we are suffering in separation today,
- *mayā sārdam* – In loving affairs, perumāḷ has great regards on self. But even I had to remain like a spectator \[kāṇa vanda cōḻar – those kings who would come and witness events\], on seeing her expertise in romance and her loving interactions.
- *udāra śeelā* – While living in the capital city, due to being shy in front of mother-in-law and father-in-law, the enjoyment will be limited; but here being a secluded place, since there is no such restriction, she was offering herself fully to me.
- *śilātalē pūrvam* – There was a rock where they would play water games; while getting tired, perumāḷ was trying to climb there first, and as said in “*prēkśitajñāstu kōsalā:*” (Residents of kōsala town will understand the mind from one’s glance), since she also has that skill \[being related to kōsala clan\], she understood perumāḷ’s intent from his action and climbed that same rock ahead of him, and stayed there filling the place, to make him tired.
- *upōpaviśtā* – Similarly, whatever perumāḷ was trying to do, she would do before him and make him tired.
- *kāntasmitā* – Normally, she will attract anyone; the face looks great with the smile. Further, she was having a laughter to indicate her recent victory.
- *tvāmāha* – Previously, perumāḷ would never leave a job unfinished; this is the only place where he could not become victorious; due to that he hung his head in shame; she left perumāḷ and looked at the face of iḷaiya perumāḷ who greatly praises perumāḷ and mercifully spoke cheerfully in many ways “See brother! You have accomplished whatever you have thought about; you are very strong men; we are women; you go for hunting and war; we have never left our homes; you can do whatever you want; see your brother has won”.

*kārigai* – One who has natural femininity.

*peridu …* – kavalai – mental suffering; avalam – physical suffering; kavalai – instability in heart; avalam – not caring for physical appearance.

*iḷangani* – She is younger than the divine daughter of śrī janakarājan for whom you went and broke the above. She cannot sustain herself in separation from you as she did as said in śrīrāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 33.17 “*samā dvādaśa tatrāham*” (I enjoyed for twelve years). If she is very young, only if she had enjoyed the union previously, she could suffer in separation like this; did she have such union? Yes. She had natural union (through gāndarva vivāham – a type of marriage where man and woman would secretly marry on their own without any rituals) and her mother would not know about it.

*en …* – As you waited in the surrounding garden of śrī mitilā to marry the divine daughter of śrī janakarāja, you are waiting in tiruvidavendai; hence what are you thinking in her matter?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.8. Alangelu tadakkai

*alangeḻu tadakkai āyan vāy āmbaṟku aḻiyumāl en uḷḷam ennum pulangeḻu poru nīrp putkuḻi pādum pōdumō nīrmalaikkennum kulangeḻu kollik kōmaḷavalli kodiyidai nedu maḻaik kaṇṇi ilangeḻil tōḷikku en ninaindirundāy idavendai endai pirānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

alam – the weapon named halam (plough); keḻu – shining; tadam – huge; kai – having divine hands; āyan – kriṣṇa, the covherd boy, his; vāy – playing from his divine lips; āmbaṟku – for the sound of flute; en uḷḷam – my mind; aḻiyum – is getting destroyed; ennum – she is saying; pulam – all the senses; keḻu – to attract all senses towards it; poru – rising waves; nīr – having water; putkuḻi – incidents relating to vijayarāghavan emperumān of tirupputkuḻi; pādum – she is singing; nīr malaikku – for tirunīrmalai; pōdumō – let us go; ennum – she is saying; kolli – like the doll in kolli mountain; keḻu – best; kulam – born in the clan; kōmaḷam – beautiful; valli – one who is tender like a creeper; kodi idai – one who is having waist like a vanji creeper; nedu maḻai – continuously flowing tears, like a torrential rain; kaṇṇi – having eyes; ilangu – shining; eḻil – beautiful; tōḷikku – on the matter of this girl who is having shoulder; en ninaindirundāy – what are you thinking?; idavendai – having arrived in tiruvidavendai; endai pirānē – Oh lord of my clan!; sollu – You should mercifully speak a word

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter parakāla nāyaki is saying “My mind is getting destroyed for the sound of flute played from the divine lips of kriṣṇa, the covherd boy, who is having shining, huge, divine hands having the weapon, plough”; she is singing  incidents relating to vijayarāghavan emperumān of tirupputkuḻi which is having water with rising waves which attract all senses towards it; she is saying “let us go to tirunīrmalai”; she is born in the best clan like the doll in the kolli mountain, is tender like a beautiful creeper and is having waist like a vanji creeper. Oh lord of my clan! What are you thinking in the matter of this girl who is having eyes where tears are flowing continuously like a torrential rain and is having beautiful shoulder? You should mercifully speak a word.

*alam …* – While it is apt for her to hide her mind getting destroyed, she is speaking about the same in front of me who is her mother. alam indicates halam. She is saying “My innocent heart is getting destroyed for the flute sound of kriṣṇa’s divine lips, where he is having well-rounded shoulder which is holding the plough. His flute music will even melt diamond. *āmbal* is said to be “*ilaik kuḻal*” (flute made with leaf) also by some. What is the principle behind saying “one who is holding halam” – just as his weapon will destroy his enemies, she is getting destroyed by his flute music. He will play the music to indicate that he could not arrive on time since he was subservient to his parents. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.13-17 “*jagau kalapadam śauri: tāra mantra krutakramam \| ramyam gīta dvanim śrutvā santyajyāvasatāmstadā \|\|*” (kriṣṇa played beautiful music with high and low tones in his flute. The covherd girls left their homes and arrived at his place on hearing that music). Alternatively – this could be explaining nambi mūtta pirān’s (balarāma) flute music which precedes kriṣṇa’s arrival, just as the indication in a river bed before a flood.

It appears that emperumān’s presence in the divyadēśams will destroy with even greater force than that flute music. “pulam” could mean fertile land. Alternatively – as she meditated upon emperumān’s presence in tirupputkuḻi which has abundance of water where waves strike at each other, to attract the senses of those who see it, she is singing out without thinking that I am her mother.

*pōdumō nīr malaikku ennum* – She is telling her mother, as if telling her friends, who is trying to stop her thinking “Looking at her stage, she will quickly reach tirupputkuḻi”.

*kulam …* – There is a doll in kolli mountain; it is totally beautiful in each limb; her greatness, family heritage and tenderness where she cannot be stared at even by well-wishers, are similar to that doll. She is said, as in tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.7 “*ennudaik kōmaḷak koḻundu*” (my tender creeper).

*kodi …* – For the one who is having a creeper like waist and who is having the eye-glance which, when it hits anyone, will give him/her the experience of being drenched in a rain, and further having shining shoulders which are more beautiful than previously explained aspects.

*en …* – What are you thinking in the matter of parakāla nāyaki who is matching to you as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.5 “*raghavōrhati vaidēhim*” (śrī rāma suits sītā pirātti in all aspects)?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.9. Ponkulam payalai

*ponkulām payalai pūttana mentōḷ porukayal kaṇṭhuyil maṟandāḷ anbināl un mēl ādaram peridu ivvaṇanginukku uṟṟa nōy aṟiyēn minkulā marungul surunga mēl nerungi vīngiya vanamulaiyāḷukku en kolām? kuṟippil en ninaindirundāy? idavendai endai pirānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

mel – slim; tōḷ – shoulders; pon – golden complexion; kulāvum – having; payalai pūttana – became pale; poru – fighting with each other; kayal – like kayal fish; kaṇ – in the eyes; tuyil – having sleep; maṟandāḷ – forgotten; un mēl – in your matters; anbināl – love; ādaram – desire; peridu – is increasing further; ivvaṇanginukku – for this girl who is beautiful; uṟṟa – acquired; nōy – disease; aṟiyēn – I do not know; min – lightning; kulām – having (curved); marungul – waist; surunga – to shrink; mēl – on top; nerungi – fitting with each other; vīngiya – well grown; vanam – beautiful; mulaiyāḷukku – for the one who has bosoms; en Am kol – how will it end?; kuṟippil – in your divine heart; en ninaindirundāy – what are you thinking?; idavendai – having arrived in tiruvidavendai; endai pirānē – Oh lord of my clan!; sollu – You should mercifully speak a word

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

parakāla nāyaki’s slim shoulders having golden complexion became pale; her eyes which are like kayal fish fighting each other, have forgotten to have sleep; due to love in your matters, her desire is increasing further; I do not know what disease this beautiful girl has acquired. How will it end for the one who has beautiful, well grown bosoms which are fitting with each other, on top, to shrink the lightning like waist? What are you thinking in your divine heart? Oh lord of my clan who has arrived in tiruvidavendai! You should mercifully speak a word.

*pon kulām …* – Having golden complexion, the shoulders which became pale being unable to bear the separation.

*poru …* –  In her childish eyes which resemble fighting kayal fish, she has totally forgotten the concept of sleep, to be taught about it from the beginning.

*anbināl …* – Due to the attachment towards you, the love she has is very great.

*iv aṇanginukku* – For this distinguished girl who has such great beauty which will cause similar attachment towards her for others.

*uṟṟa nōy aṟiyēn* – I am not aware of the disease which she has occurred to cause such stiffness in her. While the disease and the reason for the disease are identified as in “She became pale, forgot sleep, she has great love towards you”, she is saying “she is not aware” since she is not aware of the specific details in the reason. That is – she is saying “I am not sure how she got caught by him. Is it in his smile? Glance? Form? Qualities? I don’t know the exact reason how she was caught by him”.

*min kulām …* – The bosoms which are grown on the top \[of her body\], which shrink the already curved, lightning-like waist. Already, the waist appears to be broken. On top of that, the bosoms grow together. For the one, who has such beautiful bosoms.

*en kolām* – Mother is speaking reflecting upon her abandonment of her daughter. What is going to happen to my daughter in the end?

*kuṟippu …* – When I, the mother abandon her and she gives up her self-effort, what are you who are in tiruvidavendai to protect her, having such helpless state of hers as the reason, thinking in your divine heart? We saw in the case of vāli, how brothers don’t help; we saw in the case of prahlādāḻvān, how father does not help; we saw how emperumān helped him saying as in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mām ēkam śaraṇam vraja*” (Surrender unto me only) for arjuna who thought about himself and became frightened.

## 2.7.10. Annamum minum

*annamum mīnum āmaiyum ariyum     āya em māyanē! aruḷāy ennum intoṇḍarkku innaruḷ puriyum     idavendai endai pirānai mannu māmāda mangaiyar talaivan     mānavēl kaliyan vāy oligaḷ panniya panuval pāduvār nāḷum     paḻavinai paṟṟaṟuppārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annamum – hamsāvatāram; mīnum – matsyāvatāram; āmaiyum – kūrmāvatāram; ariyumāya – one who mercifully performed narasimhāvatāram as well; em māyanē – Oh you who are my lord having amazing abilities!; aruḷāy – mercifully shower your mercy; ennum – one who prays; in – distinguished; toṇḍarkku – servitors; in aruḷ puriyum – one who gives his great mercy; idavendai endai pirānai – on nitya kalyāṇan who is eternally residing in tiruvidavendai; mannum – remaining eternally (surviving even the deluge); mā – huge; mādam – having mansions; mangaiyar – for the residents of tirumangai region; talaivan – being the leader; mānam – having broad leaf; vēl – holding the spear; kaliyan – āḻvār’s; vāy – in the divine lips; oli – to become famous; panniya – mercifully elaborated; panuval – songs; pāduvār – those who can recite, being stimulated by love; nāḷum – forever; paḻavinai – their past karmas’; paṟṟu – relationship; aṟuppār – will eliminate along with the traces

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

For those distinguished servitors who pray saying “Oh you who are my lord having amazing abilities who performed hamsāvatāram, matsyāvatāram, kūrmāvatāram and narasimhāvatāram! Mercifully shower your mercy”, nitya kalyāṇan emperumān who eternally resides in tiruvidavendai, gives his great mercy. On such emperumān, āḻvār who is the leader of the residents of tirumangai region which is having huge mansions which remain eternally, and who is holding the spear with a broad leaf, mercifully elaborated these songs in his divine lips, to have them become famous. Being stimulated by love, those who can recite these songs will forever eliminate the relationship with their past karmas, along with the traces.

*annamum …* – As he was suffering due to the bewilderment, he is thinking about the incarnations which gave him knowledge.

*in toṇḍarkku in aruḷ puriyum* – āḻvār sang about the benefactor who arrived and is standing in tiruvidavendai  for the sake of those who are subsequent to the incarnations and have the same taste as that of āḻvār. The poet is the one who is the leader of tirumangai which has eternal mansions; the leader of tirumangai where the mansions don’t get destroyed even in the deluge.

*māna vēl kaliyan* – The spear which would cause the same amount of śrīvaiṣṇavaśri (wealth of kainkaryam) as its own for those who hold it; the spear which has a broad leaf. The songs which were composed by āḻvār to have a beautiful tone.

*panniya panuval* – Those who can recite these ten pāsurams elaborately to have none of the qualities missing.

*nāḷum paḻa vinai paṟṟaṟuppārē* – They will have their karmas which were previously earned by them, eliminated along with the traces. They will enter the abode where bhagavān is fully enjoyed and enjoy that and will not have to become fainted as the daughter and calling out as the divine mother.

## 2.8 Tiripuram

## 2.8.1. Tiripuram

*tiripuram mūnṟu erittānum maṟṟai malarmisai mēl ayanum viyappa muri tirai mākadal pōl muḻangi mūvulagum muṟaiyāl vaṇanga eriyana kēsara vāḷ eyiṟṟōdu iraṇiyan āgam iraṇḍu kūṟā ari uruvām ivarār kol? enna attabuyakarattēn enṟārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiri – flying (in the sky); mūnṟu puram – three capital cities; erittānum – rudra who burnt down; maṟṟai – and; mēl – distinguished; malar misai ayanum – brahmā who is born from the lotus in the divine navel \[of bhagavān\]; viyappa – to become astonished; muri – moving; tirai – having waves; mā – vast; kadalpōl – like ocean; muḻangi – making tumultuous sound; mū ulagum – residents of the three worlds; muṟaiyāl – aptly; vaṇanga – bow down at the divine feet; iraṇiyan – hiraṇya’s; āgam – body; iraṇḍu kūṟā – to become two pieces; eri a(n)na – like fire; kēsari – mane; vāḷ – shining; eyiṟṟōdu – having canine teeth; ari uruvām – in the form of narasimha; ivar Ar kol? enna – when asked “Who is he?”; attabuyagarattēn – I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram; enṟār – mercifully said

**Перевод:**

**This is how it looked when emperumān appeared \[as narasimha\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān appeared in the form of narasimha having fire like mane and shining canine teeth, to split hiraṇya’s body to become two pieces; rudra who burnt down the three flying capital cities and the distinguished brahmā who is born from the lotus in the divine navel \[of bhagavān\] became astonished; residents of the three worlds made tumultuous sound like that of a vast ocean having moving waves and aptly bowed down at his divine feet; when asked “Who is he?” He mercifully said “I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram”.

*tiri puram* – ṭravelling city \[tiri indicates roaming\]; that is – the city would float in the sky and on reaching specific target, would land there to destroy everything beneath it; there were three such capital cities; they are explained here. Alternatively – tiri puram (tiri (tamiḻ) – tri (samskrutam)- three) could be the name for each of those cities as in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*panca pancajanā:*” (five jñānēndriyas – each sense is known as pancajana) and “*sapta saptarśaya:*” (seven saptariśis – each sage is known as saptariśi). rudra whose valour is shining due to the vanquishing of the three cities.

*maṟṟai ..* – When rudra is the controller for annihilation, brahmā is the controller for creation, and further he is the father of rudra and is known as ajan (unborn) due to being different from all other mortal beings, having directly been born from the lotus in the divine navel of bhagavān.

*viyappa* – They, who are causing astonishment by their amazing acts, are astonished as if a crane has seen an ocean.

*muri …* – Other than brahmā et al, others are making tumultuous sound like that of a vast ocean with moving waves.

*mū ulagum vaṇanga* – This is similar to “*mancā:krōśanti*” (Cot making noise) \[those who are in the cot are making noise; similarly, people in the three worlds worship him\].

*muṟaiyāl* – Due to unlawful deeds of hiraṇya, they were falling at his feet; now that he has died, vorśipping bhagavān due to his natural lordship; alternatively – aptly vorśipped.

*eri …* – Having fire like mane and shining canine teeth, emperumān assumed the form of narasimha to have hiraṇya’s body become split into two, just as certain entities \[elephants\] will be destroyed due to seeing their enemies \[lions\] who are their natural enemies.

*ivar Ar kol enna* – When a child’s \[prahlādāḻvān\] father became the child’s enemy, emperumān appeared to the child being closer than the child’s father; he stood in front of me similar to that. Still, she is asking “Who is this person?” emperumān’s nature is such that one can describe him, yet one cannot firmly say who he is.

*attabuyagarattēn enṟārē* – He is saying “Will I just help prahlāda? Have I not arrived here and stood here looking for an opportunity to help you?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.2. Vendiral viraril

*vendiṟal vīraril vīrar oppār vēdam uraittu imaiyōr vaṇangum sendamiḻ pāduvār tām vaṇangum dēvar ivar kol? terikkamāttēn vandu kuṟaḷ uruvāy nimirndu māvali vēḷviyil maṇ aḷanda andaṇar pōnṟu ivarār kol? enna attabuyakarattēn enṟārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

imaiyōr – brahmā et al; vēdam uraittu – reciting vēdam and arriving; vaṇangum – one who is surrendered upon; vem tiṟal – having great strength; vīraril – to have the brave men become impressed; vīrar oppār – having greatness that is similar to that of the masculine śrī rāma, the son of emperor daśarata; sem tamiḻ – beautiful tamiḻ; pāduvār tām – mudalāḻvārs who sing; vaṇangum – surrender; dēvar – having simplicity that is similar to that of tiruvēngadamudaiyān; ivar kol – his identity; terikka māttēn – I do not know; māvali – mahābali’s; vēḷviyil – in the sacrificial arena; kuṟaḷ uruvāy vandu – coming with the vāmana’s form (when the water hit his divine hand); nimirndu – grew; maṇ – earth; aḷanda – one who measured and accepted; andaṇar pōnṟa – one who resembles a brahmācāri (celibate); ivar Ar kol? enna – when asked “Who is he?”; attabuyagarattēn – I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram; enṟār – mercifully said

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

He is surrendered upon by brahmā et al who arrived reciting vēdam; he is having greatness that is similar to that of the masculine śrī rāma, the son of emperor daśarata, to have very strong brave men become impressed; he is having simplicity that is similar to that of tiruvēngadamudaiyān, to be surrendered to by mudalāḻvārs who sing in beautiful tamiḻ; I do not know his identity; he measured and accepted the earth, after coming with the vāmana’s form in the sacrificial arena of mahābali; when he, who resembles a brahmacāri, was asked “Who is he?” he mercifully said “I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram”.

*vendiṟal …* – Great strength – the ability to win over others; those who are having such valour will send madal to the masculine one – cakravarti tirumagan (the divine son of daśarata, the emperor). śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 104.6 is explained here.

- *śatrō:* – Fool! Who did you think my enemy is and retracted the chariot and left the battle?
- *prakyāta vīryasya* – His masculinity is famous even in the enemy’s (our) capital. Have you not heard about it? There is no place where it has not reached.
- *ranjanīyasya vikramai:* – When the enemy attacks him with invincible valour, he would have that as his standing ground and win over the enemy; such masculinity in him is even desirable for his enemies, just as a girl would desire her lover.

*vēdam …* – The one who is praised by brahmā et al using nārāyaṇa anuvākam (puruśa sūktam etc) after he vanquished rāvaṇa.

*vem tiṟal vīraril vīrar oppār* – This is his greatness.

*sem tamiḻ …* – If one looks at his śeelam (simplicity), he remains to be praised by all favourable persons. mudalāḻvārgaḷ (first three āḻvārs) are the ones who sing in pure tamiḻ as said in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 75](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-75/) “*perugu mada vēḻam*“. Here emperumān remains similar to tiruvēngadamudaiyān who is the refuge for such mudalāḻvārgaḷ.

*terikka māttēn* – Looking at his valour, enemies will praise him; looking at his greatness, brahmā et al will praise him; looking at his simplicity, all the favourable ones will praise him. One cannot determine his identity. Thus, the depth of his greatness and simplicity cannot be measured.

*vandu …* – Here, emperumān remains similar to śrī vāmana who arrived at the sacrificial arena of mahābali with a dwarf form and grew to measure the earth after water fell on his divine palms. When śukrācārya et al said “He is the lord and is coming to cheat you” mahābali responded “Looking at his humble posture, how can I refuse to give what he asks for?”

*ivar Ar kol enna attabuyagarattēn enṟārē* – emperumān is saying “I have not come here begging for some land; I have come begging for you”. He is saying “I am not begging for someone else; I am begging for myself”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.3. Sempon ilangu

*sempon ilangu valangai vāḷi tiṇ silai taṇḍodu sangamoḷ vāḷ umbar irusudar āḻiyōdu kēdagam oṇmalar paṟṟi eṟṟē! vembu sinattu adal vēḻam vīḻa veṇmarupponṟu paṟittu iruṇḍa ambudam pōnṟu ivarār kol? enna attabuyagarattēn enṟārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

valam kai – in his divine right hand; ilangu – shining; sem pon – made of fresh gold; vāḷi – arrows; tiṇ – strong; silai – bow; taṇḍodu – mace; sangam – śrī pāncajanyam, the conch; oḷ – shining; vāḷ – divine dagger; umbar – greater than (all other weapons); iru sudar – having great radiance; āḻiyodu – with the cakkarattāḻvār (the disc); kēdagam – shield; oḷ – beautiful; malar – flower; paṟṟi – holding; eṟṟē – wow!; vembu sinam – great anger; adal – strength; vēḻam – kuvalayāpīdam, the elephant; vīḻa – to be killed; veḷ maruppu onṟu – a white tusk; paṟittu – broke; iruṇḍa – being dark due to abundance of water; ambudam pōnṟa – like a cloud; ivar Ar kol? enna – when asked “Who is he?”; attabuyagarattēn – I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram; enṟār – mercifully said

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is holding shining arrows which are made of gold in his right hand, strong bow, mace, śrī pāncajanyam (the conch), shining dagger, the effulgent cakkarattāḻvār (the disc), shield and the beautiful flower; wow! He broke one of the whitish tusks to kill the very angry and strong elephant named kuvalayāpīdam ; when he, who resembles a cloud which is dark due to abundant presence of water, was asked “Who is he?” he mercifully said “I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram”.

*sem pon …* – His divine weapons are useful when he rises with great anger against the enemies and when he attracts helpless women.

*sem pon ilangu valangai vāḷi* – śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 16.22 “*dīpta pāvaka śankāśai:*” – the arrows don’t look the same when they are in his hands and when they are shot at someone; when they are shot at some one, they will come with blazing fire. *śitai:* – unlike other arrows, when these arrows come in contact with the target, the target cannot bear the heat and will get burnt. *kāncana bhūśaṇai:* – there is an area which will even win over me who is favourable. *natvām iccāmi aham draśtum* – I am telling you out of brotherly affection; *rāmēṇa nihatam śarai:* – A pond would allow someone to kill oneself there or to quench one’s thirst; similarly I don’t desire for you to die being a target of his arrow instead of enjoying his beauty.

*sem pon …* – His divine hand will look attractive even without any decoration; on top of that his hand has golden arrows. The arrows look attractive due to their natural beauty and due to the way they are held by him.

*tiṇ silai* – Even after launching the bow a few times on the enemies, it will not become tired.

*taṇḍu* – Similar mace.

*sangam oḷvāḷ* – The dagger which looks beautiful due to the way it is held.

*umbar …* – With the divine chakra which is having great radiance due to being the leader of the weapons.

*kēdagam* – Shield.

*oḷ malar* – The flower which is a tool to vanquish helpless girls, like kāma (manmada) will do.

*eṟṟē* – Wow!

*vembu …* – To kill kuvalayāpīdam which was very angry and was set out to fight, he broke the tusk which was whitish in colour, contrary to his own colour. When such emperumān was asked “Who is he?”

His subsequent words.

*attabuyagarattēn …* – He said “I have not just eliminated the fear of the ladies in the capital city of kamsa by killing the kuvalayāpīdam which was sent by kamsa; I have come here and am standing here to eliminate your fear”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.4. Manjuyar mamani

*manjuyar māmaṇik kunṟam ēndi māmaḻai kāttu oru māyavānai anja adan maruppu anṟu vāngum āyar kol? māyam aṟiya māttēn venjudar āḻiyum sangum ēndi vēdam mun ōduvar nīdi vānattu anjudar pōnṟu ivarār kol? enna attabuyakarattēn enṟārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

manju – up to cloud range; uyar – risen; māmaṇi – having best gems; kunṟam – gōvardana hill; ēndi – lifted; māmaḻai – huge rain; kāttu – stopped; oru – matchless; māyam – amazing; ānai – kuvalayāpīdam; anja – to fear; adan maruppu onṟu – one of its tusks; vāngum – broke; āyarkol – is it kriṣṇa!; māyam – amazing acts; aṟiya māttēn – I don’t know; vem sudar – having cruel radiance; āḻiyum – tiruvāḻi āḻvān (cakkarattāḻvār); sangum – śrī pāncajanyam; ēndi – holding; vēdam mun ōduvar – spoke words which are similar to vēdam; nīdi – orderly; vānattu – eternally residing in paramapadam; anjudar pōnṟa – like the greatly radiant bhagavān; ivar Ar kol? enna – when asked “Who is he?”; attabuyagarattēn – I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram; enṟār – mercifully said

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is reminded about kriṣṇāvatāram again.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Is it kriṣṇa who stopped the huge rain by lifting the gōvardana hill which is risen up to the cloud range and is having the best gems, and broke one of the tusks of the matchless, amazing kuvalayāpīdam to cause fear in it? I don’t know his amazing acts; he is holding tiruvāḻi āḻvān and śrī pāncajanyam and spoke words which are similar to vēdam; when he, who is like the greatly radiant bhagavān who is eternally residing in the orderly paramapadam, was asked “Who is he?” he mercifully said “I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram”.

*manjuyar …* – Holding gōvardana hill which is risen up to the cloud range and is having the best gems. As said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.5.4 “*kadu vāyc china vengaṇ kaḷiṟṟinukkuk kavaḷam eduttuk koduppānavan pōl*” (It appears that kriṣṇa is feeding the gōvardana hill to \[the clouds which resemble\] elephant which has wide mouth and angry eyes) the clouds resemble mad elephants;  the way he stood holding the hill, he appeared to be feeding the elephants with food balls.

*mā maḻai kāttu* – Stopping the huge rain which causes destruction and is unstoppable.

*oru māyavānai* – It is not an ordinary elephant which can catch or let one escape; it is intentionally made to stand there to kill.

*anja* – To cause fear in the elephant which has never feared before.

*adan maruppu onṟu vāngum* – Breaking one of its tusks effortlessly like pulling a plant.

*āyarkol* – Not knowing the distinguished strength of the elephant, kriṣṇa stood there showing his strength.

*māyam aṟiya māttēn* – I don’t know any of his amazing acts.

*vem sudar āḻiyum sangum ēndi* – Holding his divine weapons.

*vēdam mun ōduvar* – All his merciful utterings resemble vēdam.

*nīdi vānattu* – In paramapadam, where every interaction is in an orderly manner.

*am sudar pōnṟu* – As said in cāndōjña upaniśat 3.13.7 “*ata yadata: parōdivō jyōtir dīpyatē*” (emperumān who is the paranjyōti \[effulgence nonpareil\] resides in the paramapadam which is above these worlds).

*attabuyagarattēn* – He is saying “You need not withdraw, looking at such distance. See!  I have come closer for you”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.5. Kalaigalum vedamum

*kalaigaḷum vēdamum nīdi nūlum kaṟpamum soṟporuḷ tānum maṟṟai nilaigaḷum vānavarkkum piṟarkkum nīrmaiyināl aruḷ seydu nīṇḍa malaigaḷum māmaṇiyum malarmēl mangaiyum sangamum tanguginṟa alaikadal pōnṟu ivarār kol? enna attabuyakarattēn enṟārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kalaigaḷum – the second half of vēdam (i.e. vēdāntam) and brahma sūtram; vēdamum – the first half of vēdam; nīdi nūlum – itihāsam etc; kaṟpamum – kalpa sūtram; sollum – vyākaraṇam (grammar); poruḷum – mīmāsā; maṟṟai – further; nilaigaḷum – the abodes (which are attained by those who follow these śāstrams); nīrmaiyināl – by the quality of being a lord; vānavarkkum – for the dēvatās; piṟarkkum – for the humans; aruḷ seydu – bestowed; nīṇḍa malaigaḷum – divine shoulders which resemble huge mēru mountain; māmaṇiyum – śrī kaustuba jewel; malar mēl mangaiyum – periya pirāttiyār who has lotus flower as her birth place; sangamum – śrī pāncajanyam; tanguginṟa – eternally and firmly present; alai kadal pōnṟa – like an ocean with rising tides; ivar Ar kol? enna – when asked “Who is he?”; attabuyagarattēn – I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram; enṟār – mercifully said

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being the lord, emperumān mercifully bestowed vēdāntam, brahma sūtram, vēdam, itihāsam etc, kalpa sūtram, vyākaraṇam, mīmāmsā and further the abodes, for the dēvatās and humans; when such emperumān on whom the divine shoulders which resemble huge mēru mountain, śrī kaustuba jewel, periya pirāttiyār who has lotus flower as her birth place, śrī pāncajanyam are all eternally and firmly present and who is similar to an ocean with rising tides, was asked “Who is he?” he mercifully said “I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram”.

*kalaigaḷum* – The higher part of vēdam (vēdāntam) and vēdānta sūtrams.

*vēdamum* – The first part of vēdam (which talks about the worship).

*nīdi nūlum* – The itihāsas etc which elaborate upon the vēdam, vēdāntam and vēdānta sūtram.

*kaṟpamum* – kalpa sūtram.

*sol* – vyākaraṇam which can analyse and explain the words.

*poruḷum* – mīmāmsā which help in analysing the meanings.

*nilaigaḷum* – The target abodes which are explained as the goal for those who pursue the means explained in these śāstrams.

*vānavarkkum piṟarkkum* – For brahmā et al and humans.

*nīrmaiyināl aruḷ seydu* – Bestowing it due to his quality of lordship.

*nīṇḍa …* – Shoulders which are like mēru mountain; in place of priceless gems, śrī kaustuba is present; periya pirāttiyār and śrī pāncajanyam.

*tanguginṟa* – Unlike the ocean where these four are sometimes present and sometimes not present, emperumān is always being the abode for these. Who is he?

*attabuyagarattēn* – You need not remain thinking that I am inconceivable like ocean where one cannot enter; I am standing here for you to conceive me with your heart.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
