## 2.8.6. Enganum nam

*enganum nām ivar vaṇṇam eṇṇil ēdum aṟigilam ēndiḻaiyār sangum manamum niṟaivum ellām tam manavāgap pugundu tāmum pongu karungadal pūvai kāyā pōdaviḻ neelam punainda mēgam anganam pōnṟu ivarār kol? enna attabuyakarattēn enṟārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nām – we; ivar vaṇṇam – his qualities/aspects; engan – in any which way; eṇṇilum – try to find out; ēdum – even a little bit; aṟigilam – unable to know; ēndu – decorated; iḻaiyār – helpless girls who are with ornaments, their; sangum – bangle; manamum – mind; niṟaivum – humility; ellām – all of these; tam manavāga – considering to be his; pugundu – arrived and entered; pongu – very tumultuous; karum – dark; kadal – ocean; pūvai – leaved bilberry tree; kāyā – another tree named kāyā, its flower; pōdu aviḻ – blossoming at the right time; neelam – another dark coloured flower named karuneydal; punainda – spoken along with these; mēgam – cloud groups; anganam pōnṟa – one who resembles those; ivar Ar kol? enna – when asked “Who is he?”; attabuyagarattēn – I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram; enṟār – mercifully said

**Перевод:**

**Highlights from avatārikai (Introduction)**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

No specific introduction.

When we try to find out his qualities/aspects in any which way, we are unable to know even a little bit; he arrived and entered considering all of these aspects such as the bangle, mind, humility of helpless girls who are decorated with ornaments, as his own; he is spoken along very tumultuous dark ocean, pūvai (leaved bilberry) tree, kāyā flower and another dark coloured flower named karuneydal which blossoms at the right time; when such emperumān who resembles cloud groups along with previously told aspects, was asked “Who is he?” he mercifully said “I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram”.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*enganum …* – Not just trying superficially, but even if we try to know him truly, with all our strength, we are unable to know anything.

*ēndu iḻai …* – There are helpless girls who are wearing ornaments to claim the external and internal decorations of others; their bangle, mind, humility – all of these.

*tam manavāgap pugundu* – He arrived to claim everything we own to be his.

*tāmum …* – āḻvār is explaining the way he made everything his. Since one entity will not be sufficient to explain emperumān, āḻvār is gathering many examples. Ocean which is very tumultuous, pūvai, kāyā, freshly blossomed karuneydal. Cloud which is spoken on a par with these.

*anganam pōnṟu* – Since the highlighted examples don’t match bhagavān, āḻvār is saying “Who is the one who is similar to these?”

*attabuyagaram* – He said “You said that these cause ignorance about me; but am I not the one who has arrived and stood here for you to know about me?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.7. Mulusi vandadiya

*muḻusi vaṇḍādiya taṇ tuḻāyin moymmalark kaṇṇiyum mēni anjāndu iḻisiya kōlam irundavāṟu enganam sollugēn? ōvi nallār eḻudiya tāmarai anna kaṇṇum ēndeḻil āgamum tōḷum vāyum aḻagiyadām ivarār kol? enna attabuyakarattēn enṟārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu – beetles; muḻusi – being drowned (in honey); ādiya – dancing with great joy; taṇ – cool; tuḻāyin – tiruttuḻāy’s; moy – densely strung; malark kaṇṇiyum – the way in which the garland (was mercifully worn); mēni – on the divine form; am – beautiful; sāndu iḻusiya – decorated with sandalwood paste; kōlam irundavāṟum – the way in which such decoration was; enganam – how; sollugēn – am I going to completely speak about it?; ōvi – in drawing; nallār – experts; eḻudiya – drawn; tāmarai anna – like a lotus petal; kaṇṇum – divine eyes; ēndu eḻil – having great radiance; āgamum – divine chest; tōḷum – divine shoulders; vāyum – divine lips; aḻagiyadām – are beautiful!; ivar Ar kol? enna – when asked “Who is he?”; attabuyagarattēn – I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram; enṟār – mercifully said

**Перевод:**

**Highlights from avatārikai (Introduction)**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

No specific introduction.

How am I going to completely speak about the way in which the tiruttuḻāy garland was densely strung with cool tiruttuḻāy where beetles are drowned in the honey and are dancing joyfully? How am I going to completely speak about the way in which his divine form is decorated with sandalwood paste? His divine eyes which resemble lotus petal, greatly radiant divine chest, divine shoulders, divine lips are all looking as if they are drawn by experts in drawing. When such emperumān was asked “Who is he?” he mercifully said “I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram”.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*muḻusi …* – The garland which is densely strung with tiruttuḻāy where the beetles having heavily drunk the honey, similar to those who enter a flood, are dancing joyfully.

*mēni .*.. – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam kāṇḍam 5 “*āvayōrgātra sadruśam*” (matching the body), the divine form which is naturally beautiful is decorated fully with well matured sandalwood paste instead of just applying it here and there lightly. Such beautiful.

*enganam sollugēn* – How can I speak about those aspects which have no words to describe?

*ōvi …* – The eyes which look like they are drawn by those who are experts in drawing; that is – those eyes which will not let the ones who saw them to blink.

*ēndu eḻil …* – He was having very beautiful divine chest, shoulders and mouth/lips; when asked “Who is he?”

*attabuyagaram* – He said “Don’t shy away looking at this decoration thinking that I am in paramapadam; I have arrived here and am standing for you”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.8. Mevi eppalum

*mēvi eppālum viṇṇōr vaṇanga vēdam uraippar munnīr madandai dēvi appāl adir sangam ippāl sakkaram maṟṟivar vaṇṇam ennil kāvi oppār kadalēyum oppār kaṇṇum vadivum nediyarāy en āvi oppār ivarār kol? enna attabuyakarattēn enṟārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇṇōr – nityasūris; eppālum – in all directions; mēvi – remaining firmly; vaṇanga – vorśipped; vēdam – with vēdams; uraippar – will praise; munnīr – born in tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean); madandai – periya pirāttiyār; dēvi – remains his crowned consort; adir – tumultuous; sangam – śrī pāncajanyāḻvān; appāl – present in his left side; sakkaram – tiruvāḻiyāḻvān (chakra); ippāl – present in his right side; maṟṟu – further; ivar – his; vaṇṇam – complexion; eṇṇil – if we analysed and tried to speak about it; kāvi – the colour of karuneydal flower \[blue Indian water-lily\]; oppār – matching; kadal – the colour of ocean; oppār – matching; kaṇṇum – in the beauty of his divine eyes; vadivum – in the beauty of his divine form; nediyarāy – being immeasurable; en – for me; āvi oppār – is like my life; ivar Ar kol? enna – when asked “Who is he?”; attabuyagarattēn – I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram; enṟār – mercifully said

**Перевод:**

**Highlights from avatārikai (Introduction)**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

No specific introduction.

Remaining firmly in all directions, nityasūris worship him and will praise him with vēdams; periya pirāttiyār who is born in tiruppāṟkadal, remains his crowned consort; tumultuous śrī pāncajanyāḻvān is present in his left side; tiruvāḻiyāḻvān is present in his right side; further, if we analysed his complexion and tried to speak about it, his complexion matches the colour of karuneydal flower and ocean and the beauty of his divine eyes and divine form are immeasurable; when such emperumān who is like my life was asked “Who is he?” he mercifully said “I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram”.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*mēvi …* – brahmā et al will not have their feet planted on the ground \[since they detest the smell of earth\]. nityasūris who cannot tolerate the smell of such brahmā et al, remained in all directions and interact with him as in paramapadam.

*vēdam uraippar* – Whatever he says become vēdam.

*munnīr madandai dēvi* – munnīr madandai could mean either periya pirāttiyār \[born in milk ocean\] or śrī bhūmip pirāttiyār \[earth surrounded by ocean\].

*appāl adir sangam* – In the context of śrī bhūmip pirāttiyār, the conch is blowing in that earth; in context of periya pirāttiyār, the tumultuous conch is in the opposite side of where she is standing with emperumān \[periya pirāttiyār resides on the right side of his chest and conch is held on the left hand, by emperumān\].

*ippāl cakkaram* – When one stands in one side, the other side is said to be “ippāl”.

*maṟṟu …* – When we see his complexion, it resembles that of karuneydal flower and ocean.

*kaṇ …* – There is no match for his eyes and form; only when there is a boundary for the eyes, will there be such boundary for his form.

*en āvi …* – He remained in a manner that one cannot survive in his separation.

*attabuyagaram* – What you have said is not correct? emperumān said “Have you not heard in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.18](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-18/) ‘*jñāni tvātmaiva mē matam’* (but the jñāni is the one who sustains (me) – this is my principle)?” He is saying “I cannot sustain without you”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.9. Tanjam ivarkku

*tanjam ivarkku en vaḷaiyum nillā nenjamum tammadē sindittēṟku vanji marungul nerunga nōkki vāy tiṟandu onṟu paṇittadu uṇḍu nanjamudaittu ivar nōkkum nōkkam nān ivar tammai aṟiya māttēn anjuvan maṟṟu ivarār kol? enna attabuyakarattēn enṟārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – my; vaḷaiyum – bangles; tanjam – surely; ivarkku – for him; nillā – they are not staying (they are slipping); sindittēṟku – I have analysed this, my; nenjamum – heart; tammadē – is his; vanji – like a tender creeper named nīr vanji; marungul – waist; nerunga – to become weak; nōkki – saw; vāy tiṟandu – opening his divine mouth; paṇittadu – mercifully spoke; onṟu uṇḍu – there was a very secretive meaning; nōkkum nōkkam – his vision; nanjum udaittu – appears to be poisoned; nān – I; ivar tammai – him; aṟiya māttēn – unable to know; maṟṟu – further (as soon as I saw him); anjuvan – became fearful; ivar Ar kol? enna – when asked “Who is he?”; attabuyagarattēn – I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram; enṟār – mercifully said

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My bangles are surely not staying on my hands, for him; for me who has analysed this, my heart is his; he saw me to make my waist which is like a tender creeper named nīr vanji, become weak; when he opened his divine mouth and mercifully spoke, there was a very secretive meaning; his vision appears to be poisoned; I am unable to know him; further, I became fearful; when asked “Who is he?”, he mercifully said “I am the lord of tiruvattabuyagaram”.

*tanjam …* – Surely, my bangles will stay on my hand, for him; they are his, but were just having my hand as their residence. śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.29 “*śaitilyam upayāntyāśu karēśu valayānyapi*” (As kriṣṇa left, our bangles also left us). Just like him, the bangles also are not sticking to me. They are comparable to his previous actions.

*en vaḷaiyum* – It is only my bewilderment which made me think they are mine; as soon as he came near, they became his.

Even if the external items are like this, I thought “Will the internal aspects remain with me?”

*nenjamum tammadē sindittēṟku* – ([tiruvāimoḻi 7.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/thiruvaimozhi-7-9-10-udhavik-kaimmaru/) “*uṟṟeṇṇil aduvumaṟṟāngavan tannadu”* (if we aptly tried to determine \[offering\] my soul as the favour in return, in that state of favouring in return, since that soul is exclusively subservient to him)) While superficially it remained as mine, when I analysed, the ornament inside (mind) is also his.

*vanji …* – Already the waist remains very fragile that those who touch it will be blamed saying “cracked it; broke it”. Instead of showing mercy on it, stared at it to weaken it further.

*vāy …* – I cannot reveal to you what he said during uruvu veḷippādu (visualisation). While the words which were spoken remain, she is focussing on how he opened his mouth and spoke and hence saying “*vāy tiṟandu*“.

*onṟu* – Even now, if he says it, I can say the same. I cannot remember the same and repeat afterwards. It is implied that he said something along the lines of “looks like your waist is breaking, can I embrace you to stop your waist from breaking?”

*nanjam …* – His vision seems to finish us at the end. Looks like he was trying to execute what he was saying. It looks like he is thinking to materialise the words he spoke and make it happen.

*nān …* – I am unable to know whether he is trying to protect us or kill us.

*anjuvan* – His words are not bad; still when I looked at both him and me, I am becoming fearful.

When asked “Who is he?”

*attabuyagaram* – Don’t fear for me hearing my words; he said “to eliminate your fear, I am here as one amongst all of you”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.10. Mannavan tondaiyar kon

*mannavan toṇḍaiyar kōn vaṇangum nīḷmudi mālai vayiramēgan tan vali tan pugaḻ sūḻnda kacci attabuyakarattu ādi tannai kanni nan māmadiḷ mangai vēndan kāmaru sīrk kalikanṟi kunṟā innisaiyāl sonna senjol mālai ētta vallārkku idam vaigundamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vayiramēgan – Named vayiramēgan; mannavan – king; toṇḍaiyarkōn – by toṇḍaimān cakravarti; vaṇangum – vorśipped (due to that); nīḷ mudi – having tall crown; māl – being sarvēśvaran; than – that king’s; vali – by strength; than pugaḻ – by his fame; sūḻnda – being abundant; kacci – in kāncīpuram city; attabuyagarattu – mercifully present in tiruvattabuyagaram; ādi tannai – on the cause of all; kanni – indestructable by anyone; nal – good; mā – huge; madiḷ – surrounded by fort; mangai – for tirumangai region; vēndan – being the king; kāmaru – liked by all; sīr – having qualities; kali kanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; kunṟā – faultless; in – sweet; isaiyāl – with music; sonna – mercifully spoke; sem – beautiful; sol mālai – with this tirumoḻi (decad) which has garland of words; ētta vallārkku – for those who praise; idam – abode; vaigundam – paramapadam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār, who is the king of tirumangai region which is surrounded by indestructable, good, huge fort and whose qualities are liked by all, mercifully spoke this faultless decad with sweet music on sarvēśvaran who has tall crown; emperumān was vorśipped in tiruvattabuyagaram by toṇḍaimān cakravarti who is named as vayiramēgan and whose strength and fame are abundant in kāncīpuram city; those who praise emperumān with this beautiful decad which has a garland of words, will have paramapadam as their abode.

*mannavan …* – toṇḍaimān cakravarti, the king; after he vorśipped giving up his ego and pride, īśvaran acquired the crown nicely and his sarvēśvaratvam (being the lord of all) became firmly established. Previously, there were two lords (paramātmā and jīvātmā claiming lordship).

*vayiramēgan* – vaiyramēgan is his (family) name.

*than vali …* – His strength with which he can win over the enemies and his protection which acquired him fame, were in abundance. āḻvār praised in this decad, the lord of the universe who is mercifully standing in tiruvattabuyagaram.

*kanni …* – āḻvār is the leader of everyone in tirumangai which is surrounded by the fort which remains a protective layer and is also appearing ever-fresh; āḻvār has śrīvaiṣṇava lakshmi (the wealth of kainkaryam) which is desired by all.

*kunṟā … –* Not losing its significance, having music which will attract those who hear it, the pāsurams which are very helpful in vorśipping bhagavān.

*ētta vallārkku idam vaigundamē* – Instead of suffering like āḻvār in seeing emperumān through uruvu veḷippādu (visualisation) and informing to others, as said in yajur vēdam “*dēvai: saha mādam madēma*”  (We will enjoy with nityasūris in a group), they will enter paramapadam where there is eternal enjoyment.

## 2.9 Sollu

## 2.9.1. Sollu

*sollu van soṟporuḷ tānavaiyāyc cuvai ūṟu oli nāṟṟamum tōṟṟamumāy nallaran nānmugan nāraṇanukku idandān tadam sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci pallavan villavan enṟu ulagil palarāyp pala vēndar vaṇangu kaḻal pallavan mallaiyar kōn paṇinda paramēccura viṇṇagaram aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sollu – word; van sol – (more than that) the vēdam which is difficult to attain; poruḷ – meanings of vēdam; avai – for those; tān āy – being the controller; suvaiyum – taste; ūṟum – touch; oliyum – sound; nāṟṟamum – fragrance; tōṟṟamum – for form which is seen by eyes; āy – being the controller; nal – being the benefactor; aran – being the antaryāmi for rudra who destroys; nāraṇan – being nārāyaṇa (who protects in his original form); nānmuganukku – for sarvēśvaran who is the antaryāmi of brahmā who creates; idam tān – the abode; tadam – by ponds; sūḻndu – being surrounded; aḻagāya – being beautiful; kacci – in kānci town; pallavan enṟu – known as pallavan; villavan enṟu – and known as villavan; palarāy – countless; ulagil – who ruled in this world; pala vēndar – many kings; vaṇangu – worship; kaḻal – having brave feet; mallaiyar – for the residents of tirukkadalmallai which is known as mallāpuri; kōn – king; pallavan – one who is known as pallavan; paṇinda – surrendered; paramēccura viṇṇagaram – paramēśvara viṇṇagaram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is the controller of words, the vēdam which is difficult to attain and the meanings of vēdam; he is the controller of taste, touch, sound, fragrance and form which is seen by eyes; being the antaryāmi, he is the controller of rudra who destroys and who is a benefactor; he is the antaryāmi of brahmā who creates; the abode for such sarvēśvaran is paramēśvara viṇṇagaram which is in the beautiful town kāncī which is surrounded by ponds; this divyadēśam is surrendered by the king known as pallavan who is having brave feet and is the king for the residents of tirukkadalmallai which is known as mallāpuri, and who is vorśipped by countless kings who ruled in this world namely pallavan, villavan et al.

*sollu* – The words which can reveal the meaning of what is not seen through sense perception etc.

*van sol* – The vēdam which is eternal in comparison with the worldly words.

*poruḷ* – The meanings of vēdam which are difficult to grasp.

*tān avai āy* – being the controller for those.

*suvai …* – Being the controller for śabdam (sound) etc which are to be pursued by those who desire for aiśvaryam (worldly wealth) which is one of the goals revealed in vēdam.

*suvai …* – taste, touch, sound, fragrance, form which is target of eyes.

*nal aran …* – āḻvār is saying that emperumān is the cause for creation etc of universe which is to be pursued by those who seek liberation.

*nal aran* – Being the antaryāmi of rudra who destroys the world as a noble act for the ātmās who are suffering due to their karma, just as a father will keep a rogue child shackled in his hands and feet; protecting the ātmās, remaining in his original form; being the antaryāmi of brahmā, sarvēśvaran who creates; the abode of such sarvēśvaran is.

*tadam …* – In kāncī which is surrounded by good water bodies.

*pallavan …* – In those days, there were kings named pallavan, villavan et al. emperumān is having the divine feet to be vorśipped by those kings and their relatives.

*mallaiyar …* – tirukkadalmallai is his capital city; paramēśvara viṇṇagaram which is surrendered by such king, named pallavan.

## 2.9.2. Karmannu

*kārmannu nīḷ visumbum kadalum sudarum nilanum malaiyum tan undit tārmannu tāmaraik kaṇṇanidam tadam māmadiḷ sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci tērmannu tennavanai munaiyil seruvil tiṟal vāttiya tiṇsilaiyōn pārmannu pallavar kōn paṇinda paramēccura viṇṇagaram aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kār mannu – clouds remaining fixed; nīḷ visumbum – the great sky; kadalum – oceans; sudarum – candra (moon) and sūrya (sun); nilanum – earth; malaiyum – anchoring mountains; than undit tār – in the flower which is in his divine navel; mannu – remaining; tāmaraik kaṇṇan – for puṇḍarīkākśan (lotus-eyed lord); idam – residence; tadam – by ponds; mā – tall; madiḷ – forts; sūḻndu – surrounded by; aḻagāya – beautiful; kacci – in kāncīpuram town; tēr mannu – great charioteer; tennavanai – pāṇḍiyan; seruvil munaiyil – in the battle field; tiṟal – strength; vāttiya – destroyed; tiṇ – firm; silaiyōn – one who has the bow; pār – (his vīraśrī – the wealth of valour) on the earth; mannu – made it remain firmly; pallavarkōn – pallava king; paṇinda – surrendered; paramēccura viṇṇagaram – paramēśvara viṇṇagaram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In the flower in puṇḍarīkākśan emperumān’s divine navel, the great sky with clouds, oceans, moon and sun, earth, and anchoring mountains are present; the abode of such emperumān is paramēśvara viṇṇagaram which is in beautiful kāncīpuram town which is surrounded by ponds, tall forts, and where the pallava king who has the firm bow which destroyed the strength of pāṇḍiyan, the great charioteer and who made his wealth of valour remain firmly on the earth and where such king surrendered to such emperumān there.

*kār …* – āḻvār’s attachment is such that he did not see any difference between cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma) vanquishing rāvaṇa and pallava king vanquishing his enemies.

*kār …* – Sky which is roamed by the clouds, moon and sun who live in such sky, ocean surrounding the earth, the earth which is bound by the ocean, the mountains which seem to be anchoring such earth are all present in the divine navel flower. The abode of such puṇḍarīkākśan.

In the beautiful kāncīpuram, which is surrounded by ponds and forts.

*tēr …* – pāṇḍiyan who is a great charioteer who can travel/fight by remaining on a chariot.

*seruvil* – In the battle field.

*munaiyil* – In the forefront of the battle, the one who has the valour of the firm bow which destroyed the strength.

*pār …* – One whose wealth of valour remained even after his demise.

## 2.9.3. Urandaru mellanai

*urandaru mellaṇaip paḷḷi koṇḍān orukāl munnam māvuruvāyk kadaluḷ varandaru māmaṇi vaṇṇanidam maṇi mādangaḷ sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci nirandavar maṇṇaiyil puṇṇugar vēl neduvāyil ugac ceruvil muna nāḷ parandavan pallavar kōn paṇinda paramēccura viṇṇagaram aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

munnam oru kāl – Once, previously; mā uruvāy – having a distinguished form; kadaluḷ – in tiruppāṟkadal; uram tarum – strong; mel – tender; aṇai – on tiruvanantāḻvān; paḷḷi koṇḍān – being the one who mercifully rested; varam tarum – one who fulfils (everyone’s) desires; mā maṇi – like a cintāmaṇi (touchstone); vaṇṇan – for the one who is having the nature; idam – abode; maṇi – filled with gems; mādangaḷ sūḻndu – surrounded by mansions; aḻagāya kacci – in the beautiful kāncīpuram town; maṇṇaiyil – in the capital city named maṇṇai; nirandavar – enemies; puṇ – flesh; nugar – consuming; vēl – spear’s; neduvāyil – in the huge mouth; uga – to have (them) destroyed; muna nāḷ – previously; seruvil – in the battle; parandavan – one who engaged fully; pallavarkōn – pallava king; paṇinda – surrendered; paramēccura viṇṇagaram – paramēśvara viṇṇagaram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, once, previously having a distinguished form, mercifully rested on the strong and tender tiruvanantāḻvān in tiruppāṟkadal; he is having the nature of cintāmaṇi which fulfils desires; the abode of such emperumān is paramēśvara viṇṇagaram which is surrounded by mansions filled with precious gems and is in maṇṇai, the capital of the beautiful kāncīpuram town where the pallava king who previously fully engaged in the battle to have the enemies destroyed in the huge mouth of the spear which consumes the flesh of those enemies, surrendered to such emperumān there.

*uram* … – As said in stōtra ratnam 39 “*prakruśta vijñāna balaika dāmani*” (One who is the abode of great knowledge and strength), tiruvanantāḻvān is having the ability to bear even if bhagavān and his consorts jump on him and is having the tenderness to flexibly adapt himself  based on the divine heart of bhagavān; in tiruppāṟkadal, on such tiruvanantāḻvān, previously, emperumān mercifully rested with the best form.

*varam …* – The abode of emperumān who is granting all desires, being aruḷāḷap perumāḷ (one who mercifully bestows boons),

In the beautiful kāncīpuram which is surrounded by gem studded mansions.

*nirandavar …* – maṇṇai is the name of the river and the capital city; just as “tirucciṟṟāṟu” is the name of both the river and the divyadēśam. There are enemies in that capital city; their puṇ – flesh; the spear which will consume those enemies with its huge mouth; the enemies becoming prey to that spear and be killed. His valour/masculinity is respected by tirumangai āḻvār himself. The king is respected by tirumangai āḻvār who is greatly valourous in every field as said in periya tirumoḻi 2.4.10 “*kadamā kaḷi yānai vallān*” (one who can control very joyful, intoxicated elephant), periya tirumoḻi 5.8.10 “*ādalmā valavan*” (one who can ride the great horse named ādalmā) and in periya tirumoḻi 3.9.10 “*maruvalar tam udal tuṇiya vāḷ vīsum parakālan*” (parakālan who launches his sword to sever the bodies of enemies). This is similar to śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 104.6 “*ranjanīyasya*” (śrī rāma’s valour is liked even by his enemies).

*seruvil …* – He destroyed all the enemies in the battle and remained pervaded everywhere.

## 2.9.4. Andamum

*aṇḍamum eṇḍhisaiyum nilanum malai nīrodu vān erikāl mudalā uṇḍavan endai pirānadu idam oḷi mādangaḷ sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci viṇḍavar iṇḍaik kuḻāmudanē viraindār iriyac ceruvil munindu paṇḍu orukāl vaḷaittān paṇinda paramēccura viṇṇagaram aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇḍamum – oval shaped universes; eṇḍhisaiyum – eight directions; nilanum – earth; alai – rising waves; nīrodu – oceans; vān – sky; eri – fire; kāl – air; mudalā – etc; uṇḍavan – one who mercifully consumed; endai pirānadu – for one who is my clan’s lord; idam – abode; oḷi – shining; mādangaḷ – by mansions; sūḻndu – surrounded; aḻagāya – beautiful; kacci – in kāncīpuram town; seruvil – in battle; viraindārudanē – with those who rushed towards; viṇḍavar – of the enemies; iṇḍai – gathered; kuḻām – crowd; iriya – to break and disperse; munindu – showed anger; paṇḍu orukāl – previously; vaḷaittān – pallava king who launched his bow; paṇinda – surrendered; paramēccura viṇṇagaram – paramēśvara viṇṇagaram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abode of my clan’s lord who mercifully consumed oval shaped universes, eight directions, earth, oceans with rising waves, sky, fire, air etc is paramēśvara viṇṇagaram in the beautiful kāncīpuram town which is surrounded by shining mansions; pallava king who surrendered to such emperumān, previously showed his anger and launched his bow to break and disperse the gathered crowd of enemies and those who rushed towards him in the battle there.

*aṇḍamum …* – Oval shaped universe, eight directions, earth, those which are the cause and which are the effect were kept in his stomach and were protected by him.

*endai pirānadu idam* – He is the lord of my father. Implies, the lord of our clan.

*oḷi …* – In kāncīpuram which is surrounded by gem-studded, shining mansions.

*viṇḍavar …* – seruvil – in battle; viraindavar – those who approach with great force, raising the dust from the ground and approaching saying “Show us! Show us!”

With them,

*viṇḍavar iṇḍaik kuḻām iriya* – To make the dense crowd of enemies to break and run away.

*munindu* – Showing anger.

*paṇḍu …* – Surrendered by the one who previously, launched his bow.

## 2.9.5. Tumbudait

*tūmbudait tiṇkai vantāḷ kaḷiṟṟin tuyar tīrttu aravam veruva muna nāḷ pūmbunal poygai pukkān avanukku idandān tadam sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci tēmboḻil kunṟeyil tennavanait tisaippac ceru mēl viyandu anṟu senṟa pāmbudaip pallavar kōn paṇinda paramēccura viṇṇagaram aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tūmbudai – having hole; tiṇ – strong; kai – trunk; val – strong; tāḷ – leg; kaḷiṟṟin – śrī gajēndrāḻvān’s; tuyar – sorrow; tīrttu – eliminated; aravam – kāḷiya, the snake; veruva – to fear; muna nāḷ – previously; pūm punal poygai – into the pond which is filled with beautiful water; pukkānavanukku – for the one who jumped; idam – abode; tadam – by ponds; sūḻndu – surrounded by; aḻagāya kacci – in beautiful kāncīpuram; tēn – having honey; poḻil – garden; kunṟu – like a mountain; eyil – having fort; tennavan – pāṇḍiyan; tisaippa – to become bewildered; anṟu – previously; seru mēl – in battle; viyandu – with great desire; senṟa – who arrived; pāmbu udai – having snake as his flag; pallavarkōn – pallava king; paṇinda – surrendered; paramēccura viṇṇagaram – paramēśvara viṇṇagaram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān eliminated the sorrow of śrī gajēndrāḻvān who was having a strong trunk with hole and strong legs; previously emperumān had jumped into the pond which is filled with beautiful water to cause fear in kāḷiya, the snake; such emperumān’s abode is paramēśvara viṇṇagaram in beautiful kāncīpuram which is surrounded by ponds, where pallava king surrendered to the divyadēśam, and where he who is having snake flag came with great desire in the battle previously to cause bewilderment in pāṇḍiyan who is having garden filled with honey and mountain like fort \[in his town\].

*tūmbudai …* – For śrī gajēndrāḻvān who is having a strong trunk with hole, having strong leg, emperumān eliminated the sorrow inflicted by the crocodile.

*aravam …* – When kāḷiya poisoned a pond, emperumān jumped into the pond to frighten him and make him run away.

*tēn poḻil …* – pallava king reached with great desire to battle tennavan (pāṇḍiya king) who had the garden filled with honey in his surrounding, and mountain like fort, and caused bewilderment to him.

*pāmbudai …* – It is said that pallavan won over nāgalōkam and made snake his flag; the place where he surrendered.

## 2.9.6. Tin padai

*tiṇ padaik kōḷariyin uruvāyt tiṟalōn agalam seruvil muna nāḷ puṇ padap pōḻnda pirānadu idam poru mādangaḷ sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci veṇkudai nīḻal sengōl nadappa vidai velkodi vēṟpadai mun uyartta paṇbudaip pallavar kōn paṇinda paramēccura viṇṇagaram aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiṇ – strong (divine nail); padai – weapon; kōḷ – having strength; ariyin uruvāy – being in the form of narasimha; tiṟalōn – very strong hiraṇya’s; agalam – chest; muna nāḷ – previously; seruvil – in battle; puṇ pada – to become wounded; pōḻnda – split; pirānadu – for the benefactor; idam – abode; poru – joined with each other; mādangaḷ sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci – beautiful kāncīpuram surrounded by mansions; veṇ kudai nīḻal – under the white umbrella signifying being an emperor; sengōl nadappa – having his orders carried out; vel – showing victory; vidaik kodi – snake flag; vēl – spear; padai mun – in front of the army; uyartta – one who raised high; paṇbu udai – having beautiful nature; pallavarkōn – pallava king; paṇinda – surrendered; paramēccura viṇṇagaram – paramēśvara viṇṇagaram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being in the form of narasimha having strong weapon and strength, previously in the battle, split the chest of very strong hiraṇya to wound it; the abode of such benefactor is paramēśvara viṇṇagaram in beautiful kāncīpuram surrounded by mansions joined with each other, where pallava king who was having his orders carried out under the white umbrella signifying being an emperor, who is having beautiful nature and who raised high the snake flag and spear in front of the army, signifying victory.

*tiṇ padai …* – Being narasimha, having the divine nail as weapon which will not fear hiraṇya’s body, to cause wound in very strong hiraṇya’s chest in the battle.

*poru …* – poru – match; being joined with each other.

*veṇ kudai …* – Having the strength to conduct his orders in the country, with only his white victorious umbrella. vidai, vidam, viṟal. vidai – young snake; vidam – poison, implies snake; viṟal – having strength, one who previously raised the flag which implies victory and the spear.

*paṇbu udai …* – Having beautiful nature. Surrendered by such pallava king.

## 2.9.7. Ilagiya nilmudi

*ilagiya nīḷmudi māvali tan peru vēḷviyil māṇ uruvāy munanāḷ salamodu mānilam koṇḍavanukku idandān tadam sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci ulagudai mannavan tennavanaik kanni māmadiḷ sūḻ karuvūr veruva pala padai sāya venṟān paṇinda paramēccura viṇṇagaram aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ilagiya – shining; nīḷ – tall; mudi – having crown; māvali than – mahābali’s; peru vēḷviyil – in the great yāgam; māṇ uruvāy – being in the form of vāmana \[dwarf\]; muna nāḷ – previously; mā – vast; nilam – earth; salamodu – with water; koṇḍavanukku – for the one who accepted and measured; idam tān – abode; tadam sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci – beautiful kāncīpuram surrounded by ponds; kanni – eternal; mā madiḷ – with huge forts; sūḻ – surrounded by; karuvūr – karuvūr; veruva – to fear; pala padai – four types of armies; sāya – to be finished; ulagudai – for the whole world; mannavan – the king; tennavanai – pāṇḍiyan; venṟān – one who defeated; paṇinda – surrendered; paramēccura viṇṇagaram – paramēśvara viṇṇagaram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abode of emperumān who previously in the form of vāmana accepted the vast earth with water in the great yāgam of mahābali who was having tall crown, and measured the same, is paramēśvara viṇṇagaram in beautiful kāncīpuram surrounded by ponds, where pallava king who defeated pāṇḍiya king who was the ruler of the whole world in karuvūr which had eternal, huge forts, to fear and to finish the four types of armies, surrendered.

*ilagiya …* – In the sacrificial altar of mahābali who was wearing radiant crown which indicates that he is the king of all, assuming the form which is well-used to begging, previously, when water fell on his hand, emperumān accepted the vast earth and measured it.

*ulagudai* … – To frighten karuvūr which was surrounded by huge fort, pallava king defeated pāṇḍiyan who was the controller of the whole world, and destroyed his armies. Such pallava king surrendered to paramēśvara viṇṇagaram.

## 2.9.8. Kudaittiral

*kudait tiṟal mannavanāy orukāl kurangaip padaiyā malaiyāl kadalai adaittavan endai pirānadu idam aṇi mādangaḷ sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci vidaittiṟal villavan nenmeliyil veruvac ceruvēl valangaip piditta padaittiṟal pallavar kōn paṇinda paramēccura viṇṇagaram aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kudai – white victorious umbrella; tiṟal – having strength; mannavanāy – being cakravartit tirumagan (son of emperor daśarata); orukāl – when rāvaṇa separated pirātti; kurangai – monkeys; padaiyā – having as army; malaiyāl – with rocks; kadalai – ocean; adaittavan – one who stopped (built bridge); endai pirānadu – for my clan’s lord; idam – abode; aṇi – beautiful; mādangaḷ sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci – beautiful kāncīpuram surrounded by mansions; vidai – like a bull; tiṟal – having strength; nenmeliyil – and being the one who has capital city named nenmeli; villavan – king named villavan; veruva – to fear; seru – weapon for battle; vēl – spear; valangaip piditta – one who held in his right hand; padai – to handle weapons; tiṟal – one has the strength; pallavarkōn – pallava king; paṇinda – surrendered; paramēccura viṇṇagaram – paramēśvara viṇṇagaram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abode for my clan’s lord who is having white victorious umbrella and strength, being cakravartit tirumagan, when rāvaṇa separated pirātti, having monkeys as his army, stopped the ocean with rocks, is paramēśvara viṇṇagaram in beautiful kāncīpuram which is surrounded by beautiful mansions, where pallava king who had the strength to handle weapons and who held spear, which is a weapon for battle, in his right hand, to cause fear in the king named villavan who had bull-like strength and a capital city named nenmeli, surrendered.

*kudait tiṟal …* – Being cakravartit tirumagan who has white victorious umbrella and great strength.

*kurangaip padaiyā* – Having monkeys which fear battle, as the army and having rocks which will submerge in water, to build a bridge across the ocean.

*endai …* – the abode of my father and my benefactor.

*aṇi mādangaḷ sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci* – beautiful kāncīpuram surrounded by beautiful mansions

*vidai …* – villavan who had strength like that of a bull, feared in his capital city named nenmeli; pallava king held the spear in his right hand as a weapon in the battle.

*padait tiṟal …* – pallava king who has the skill to handle weapons.

## 2.9.9. Piraiyudai

*piṟaiyudai vāṇudal pinnai tiṟattu munnē orukāl seruvil urumin maṟaiyudai mālvidai ēḻ adarttāṟku idandān tadam sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci kaṟaiyudai vāḷ maṟa mannar kedak kadal pōl muḻangum kural kaduvāyp paṟaiyudaip pallavar kōn paṇinda paramēccura viṇṇagaram aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

piṟai – crescent like; vāḷ – lustre; udai – having; nudal – having forehead; pinnai tiṟattu – for nappinaip pirātti; munnē orukāl – once previously; seruvil – in battle; urumin – thunder like voice; maṟai – enmity; udai – having; māl – big; vidai ēḻu – seven bulls; adarttāṟku – for the one who killed; idam tān sūḻndu aḻagāya kacci – beautiful kāncīpuram surrounded by ponds, is the abode; kaṟai udai – having stains; vāḷ – sword; maṟam – having great anger; mannar – kings; keda – to be destroyed; kadalpōl – like ocean; muḻangum – making belligerent noise; kural – voice; kadu vāy – having hard mouth; paṟai – a percussion instrument; udai – having; pallavarkōn – pallava king; paṇinda – surrendered; paramēccura viṇṇagaram – paramēśvara viṇṇagaram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Once previously, emperumān killed seven huge bulls which were having thunder like voice and enmity, in battle for nappinnaip pirātti who is having lustrous crescent like forehead; the abode of such emperumān is paramēśvara viṇṇagaram in beautiful kāncīpuram surrounded by ponds, where pallava king, who is having a percussion instrument which has hard mouth and which has a voice like the belligerent noise of ocean to destroy the kings who were having stained swords and great anger, surrendered.

*piṟai …* – For nappinnaip pirātti who is having a crescent like forehead which is lustrous, once previously, in a battle, killed the huge bulls which appear like thunder and were mischievous. Also explained as the bulls which came with enmity.

*kaṟai …* – To kill kings who were holding swords which pierced through the bodies of enemies and did not have opportunity to clean those swords, and who have great anger; having a percussion instrument which makes a sound similar to the belligerent noise of an ocean and which has a hard mouth which will make those who heard the sound become destroyed and run away, tied to his waist – this appears similar to emperumān having the percussion instrument tied to his divine waist as said in periya tirumoḻi 11.5.6 “*kanṟap paṟai kaṟanga*” (sounding the percussion instrument to wither the hearts of enemies).

## 2.9.10. Parmannu

*pārmannu tol pugaḻp pallavar kōn paṇinda paramēccura viṇṇagar mēl kārmannu nīḷ vayal mangaiyar tam talaivan kali kanṟi kunṟādu uraitta sīrmannu sendamiḻ mālai vallār tirumāmagaḷ tan aruḷāl ulagil tēr mannarāy oli mākadal sūḻ seḻunīr ulagāṇḍu tigaḻvargaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pār – On earth; mannu – firmly remained; tol – ancient; pugaḻ – having fame; pallavarkōn – pallava king; paṇinda – surrendered; paramēccura viṇṇagara mēl – on paramēśvara viṇṇagaram; kār – dark; mannu – remaining firmly; niḷ – vast; vayal – having fertile field; mangaiyar tam – for tirumangai region; talaivan – king; kalikanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; kunṟādu – not minimising any of the qualities; uraitta – mercifully spoke; sīr – bhagavān’s qualities; mannu – remaining firm; sem – beautiful; tamiḻ mālai – tamiḻ garland; vallār – those who can learn with meanings; tirumāmagaḷ than – periya pirāttiyār’s; aruḷāl – by mercy; ualagil – in this world; tēr – mahārata (great charioteers); mannarāy – being kings; oli – resounding; mā kadal – by huge ocean; sūḻ – being surrounded; seḻu – beautiful; nīr – having water; ulagu – earth; āṇḍu – rule over; tigaḻvargaḷ – will shine

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār, the king of tirumangai region which is having huge fertile field which is remaining dark (well grown), mercifully spoke this beautiful garland of ten pāsurams without minimising any of the qualities of poetry, on paramēśvara viṇṇagaram which was attained by pallava king who had ancient, firm fame on earth. Those who can learn these pāsurams which are firmly filled with bhagavān’s qualities, with their meanings, will remain as kings who are great charioteers, and śiningly rule over earth which is surrounded by resounding ocean filled with beautiful water.

*pār …* – On paramēśvara viṇṇagara, where pallava king who had ancient, well established fame on earth, surrendered.

*kār …* – The town has pregnant fields \[dark – well grown\]. Just as muktātmās will always remain 25 years old. It is said in periya tirumoḻi 10.1.1 “*karunel sūḻ kaṇṇamangai*” (tirukkaṇṇamangai which is surrounded by dark paddy crops).

*kunṟādu …* – Whatever qualities mentioned for poetry, there is no shortcoming in any of that; those who are well versed in the tamiḻ garland which was mercifully composed in such manner; by the grace of periya pirāttiyār, they will be great charioteer kings in this world and rule over the earth which is surrounded by ocean.

*tigaḻvargaḷē* – Will become radiant. To not waste such wealth/control, they will get to use them for the sake of bhāgavatas just as āḻvār did.

Thus, with this decad, it is explained that since this divyadēśam is dear to sarvēśvaran, it is refuge and it is refuge for all. That is – only those who have noble qualities such as śamam, damam etc are qualified to surrender; this abode is such that even those who are without such qualities, will humbly surrender here.

## 2.10 Manjadu

## 2.10.1. Manjadu

*manjādu varai ēḻum kadalgaḷ ēḻum vānagamum maṇṇagamum maṟṟum ellām enjāmal vayiṟṟadakki ālin mēl ōr iḷandaḷiril kaṇ vaḷarnda īsan tannait tunjā nīr vaḷam surakkum peṇṇait tenpāl tūya nānmaṟaiyāḷar sōmuc ceyya senjāli viḷaivayaluḷ tigaḻndu tōnṟum tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ kaṇḍēn nānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

manju – clouds; ādu – roaming; varai ēḻum – seven anchoring mountains; kadalgaḷ ēḻum – seven oceans; vānagamum – higher worlds such as heaven etc; maṇṇagamum – earth; maṟṟum – other; ellām – all entities; enjāmal – not to be destroyed; vayiṟu – in divine stomach; adakki – placed; ōr – matchless; ālin – banyan leaf’s; iḷam taḷirin mēl – on the tender shoot; kaṇ vaḷarnda – one who mercifully had his yōga nidrā; īsan tannai – sarvēśvaran, who is friend in need; tunjā – without changing; vaḷam nīr – abundant water; surakkum – overflowing; peṇṇait then pāl – on the southern banks of peṇṇai river; tūya – being ananyaprayōjanar (those who don’t expect anything other than kainkaryam); nān maṟaiyāḷar – those who are experts in four vēdams; sōmu – sōma yāgams; seyya – as they perform (due to that); senjāli – red paddy; viḷai – growing; vayaluḷ – in the fertile field; tigaḻndu – beautiful; tōnṟum – appearing; tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ – in tirukkōvalūr; nān kaṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is said to be āpatsakan (one who is a friend in need).**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, who is a friend in need, mercifully had his yōga nidrā on the matchless banyan leaf’s tender shoot, having placed seven anchoring mountains where the clouds are roaming, seven oceans, higher worlds such as heaven etc, earth and all other entities in his divine stomach; I got to see such emperumān in the beautifully appearing tirukkōvalūr, where those who are experts in four vēdams and are ananyaprayōjanar, are performing sōma yāgams on the southern banks of peṇṇai river which is flowing, without changing, with abundant water and which is appearing amidst the fertile field where red paddy is growing.

*manjādu …* – The seven anchoring mountains of earth on top of which the clouds are roaming, the seven oceans which appear to be a moat surrounding all of these, ākāśam (ether) which provides space for all of these, the earth which is the base for all of these and all other untold entities.

*enjāmal …* – Placing all of these in his divine stomach so that they don’t shrink and get destroyed. emperumān assumed a toddler’s form where he does not even know that he should fear the deluge, and mercifully had his yōga nidrā (divine meditation) on a freshly grown tender shoot of a banyan tree; sarvēśvaran who his having the ādāra – ādēya bhāvam (relationship of being sustained and sustainer) under his disposal. As said in [mudal tiruvandādi 69](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-69/) “*ālanṟu vēlai nīr uḷḷadō*” (Is that banyan leaf inside the oceanic water?)

*tunjā nīr …* – On the southern banks of peṇṇai river where the water flow is never changing, and is throwing out gold, pearls and gems.

*tūya …* – ananyaprayōjanars perform sōma yāgams.

*senjāli …* – Though they perform the yāgams without any expectation of the result, just as someone walking in the eastern direction will reach a town there and another person walking towards western direction will reach another town there, by bhagavān’s will, whatever deeds done will lead to results; thus, the result of such performance of yāgams leading to abundance of wealth is seen here. senjāli – red paddy; āḻvār is saying “I got to see emperumān in tirukkōvalūr which is shining in the fertile field where red paddy is growing”.

## 2.10.2. Kondalarnda

*kondalarnda naṟunduḻāy sāndam dūbam dībam koṇḍu amarar toḻap paṇangoḷ pāmbil sandaṇi menmulai malarāḷ taraṇi mangai tām iruvar adi varudum tanmaiyānai vandanai seydu isaiyēḻ āṟangam aindu vaḷar vēḷvi nānmaṟaigaḷ mūnṟu tīyum sindanai seydu irupoḻudum onṟum selvat tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ kaṇḍēn nānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kondu alarnda – blossomed in bunches; naṟu – having fragrance; tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; sāndam – sandalwood paste; dūbam – incense; dībam – lamp; koṇḍu – carrying on hand; amarar – brahmā et al; toḻu – to surrender; paṇam koḷ – having vast hoods; pāmbil – on tiruvanantāḻvān; sandu – with sandalwood paste; aṇi – decorated; mel – soft; mulai – having bosoms; malarāḷ – periya pirāttiyār who is born in lotus flower; taraṇi mangai – śrī bhūmip pirātti; iruvar tām – both; adi – divine feet; varudum – massaging with their divine hands; tanmaiyānai – sarvēśvaran who has this nature; ēḻu isai – seven svarams (tones); āṟu angam – six limbs; aindu vaḷar vēḷvi – five great yajñas; mūnṟu tīyum – with three fires; vandanai seydu – surrendering unto him; nāl maṟaigaḷ – with four vēdams; iru poḻudum – night and day; sindanai seydu – meditate; onṟum – surrendering; selvam – having wealth; tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ – in tirukkōvalūr; nān kaṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is reclining on tiruvanantāḻvān to be surrendered to by brahmā et al who came carrying fragrant tiruttuḻāy garland blossomed in bunches, sandalwood paste, incense and lamp on their hands; sarvēśvaran has the nature of his divine feet being massaged both by periya pirāttiyār, who is born in lotus flower and is having soft bosom decorated with sandalwood paste, and śrī bhūmip pirātti, with their divine hands. I got to see such sarvēśvaran in tirukkōvalūr which is having the wealth of being surrendered with seven svarams, six limbs, five great yajñas, three fires, and meditate upon him night and day with four vēdams.

*kondalarnda* … – Carrying tiruttuḻāy garland which is blossomed in bunches, sandalwood paste, incense and lamp, brahmā et al will surrender unto emperumān from the shores of the milk ocean.

*paṇam …* – Reclining on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) who is having expanded hoods due to being in contact with emperumān, such sarvēśvaran is served by both periya pirāttiyār and śrī bhūmip pirātti who are decorated to be enjoyed by him. periya pirāttiyār who makes emperumān ignore the faults of brahmā et al, and śrī bhūmip pirātti who is the teacher to emperumān to not see their faults.

*adi varudum* – They will mesmerise him and make him sleep with the touch of their divine hands even though he is sarvajña (omniscient) and he knows that they are trying to make him sleep (and does not want to sleep).

*vandanai …* – Bowing to him, surrendering unto him with seven svarams, six limbs of vēdam, five great yajñams and three fires – that is, vorśipping him.

*sindanai seydu …* – With four vēdams, meditating night and day that he is the prakāri (substratum) and they are inseparable prakāram (attributes) as said in tanka bhāśyam “*ātmētyava tu gruhṇiyāt*” (parmātmā is to be meditated upon as one’s life) and brahma sūtram 4.1.3 “*ātmēti dūpagaccanti grāhayanti ca*” (brahmam should be vorśipped as ātmā. This is because those who worship him, know him in that manner; and śāstram too is explaining in that manner). In this manner, the wealth of such consideration of being prakāram of brahmam will go on forever.

## 2.10.3. Kolundalarum

*koḻundalarum malarc cōlaik kuḻāngoḷ poygaik kōḷ mudalai vāḷ eyiṟṟuk koṇḍaṟku eḷgi aḻundiya mākaḷiṟṟinukku anṟu āḻi ēndi andaram ēvarat tōnṟi aruḷ seydānai eḻunda malark karuneelam irundil kātta irumpunnai muttarumbic cempon kātta seḻundada nīrkkamalam tīvigai pōl kāttum tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ kandēn nānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

koḻundu – sprouts; alarum – blossoming; malar – having flowers; sōlaik kuḻām koḷ – being surrounded by garden; poygai – in pond; kōḷ mudalai – strong crocodile; vāḷ – sword like; eyiṟu – with teeth; koṇḍaṟku – having been grabbed; eḷgi – became weak; aḻundiya – drowned (into the pond); mā kaḷiṟṟinukku – for gajēndrāḻvān; anṟu – when he was invoked saying “ādimūlamē”; āḻi – divine chakra; ēndi – carrying; andaram – sky; ēvara – to be filled; tōnṟi – appeared; aruḷ seydānai – one who showed his mercy (to that elephant); eḻunda – born in water; karu neela malar – karuneydal flower; irundil – charcoal; kātta – as it showed; irum punnai – huge punnai trees (through the buds); muttuk kātta – as they showed pearls; arumbi – blossomed; sem pon kātta – as they showed fresh gold; seḻunīr – having abundance of water; tadam – in ponds; kamalam – lotus flowers; tīvigai pōl – like lamp; kāttum – appearing; tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ – in tirukkōvalūr; nān kaṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān appeared in the sky filling it, carrying the divine chakra, showed his mercy to gajēndrāḻvān who became weak and drowned having been grabbed by the sword like strong teeth of the crocodile in the pond surrounded by garden having sprouts blossoming into flowers, and who called out to him saying “ādimūlamē”; I got to see such emperumān in tirukkōvalūr where karuneydal flower born in water showed charcoal, huge punnai trees showed pearls through their buds \[before blossoming\] and they blossomed and showed fresh gold, and where lotus flowers appear like lamp in ponds having abundance of water.

*koḻundu …* – In the pond which is surrounded by garden which has sprouts and blossomed flowers.

*kōḷ mudalai* – Like the god of death, the crocodile which appeared to vanquish the elephant fully. It grabbed the elephant with its sword like teeth.

*eḷgi* – Being weakened by that.

*aḻundiya …* – For the intoxicated elephant whose mouth was filled with water thereby drowning it.

*anṟu* – When it lost all its strength.

*āḻi ēndi* – Appearing in the sky filling it, not \[immediately\] realising to launch the divine chakra in his hand.

*aruḷ seydānai* – ēvara – to fill the sky. Here by showing mercy, āḻvār is thinking about how emperumān touched the elephant with his divine hand to heal the wound by blowing hot air on his divine upper garment and fomenting it.

*eḻunda …* – The karuneydal plant which had risen with flower.

*irundil* … – Showed charcoal; the huge punnai trees showed gold and pearls through their buds \[unblossomed flowers\] and blossomed flowers, respectively. The lotus flowers in the ponds, which have abundant water, showed \[themselves as\] lamps; thus, with the charcoal, pearl, fire and gold, the fertile fields appeared like the workshop of a goldsmith.

## 2.10.4. Tangarum por

*tāngarum pōr māli padap paṟavai ūrndu tarādalattōr kuṟai muditta tanmaiyānai āngu arumbik kaṇṇīr sōrndu anbu kūrum adiyavargatku āramudam ānān tannai kōngarumbusura punnai kuravār sōlaik kuḻāvari vaṇḍu isai pādum pādal kēttu tīngarumbu kaṇvaḷarum kaḻani sūḻnda tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ kandēn nānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāngu arum – unable to bear for anyone; pōr – fighting the battle; māli – rākśasas starting with māli; pada – to die; paṟavai – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); ūrndu – ride; tarā talattōr – of those who are present on earth; kuṟai – complaints; muditta – one who eliminated; tanmaiyānai – having the nature; āngu – while eliminating the enemies; kaṇṇīr – tears; arumbi – appeared; sōrndu – overflowing; anbu kūrum – having great love; adiyavargatku – for servitors; Ar – complete; amudamānān tannai – one who is enjoyable like nectar; kōngu arumbu – kōngu flowers; surapunnai – surapunnai trees; kuravu – kuravu trees; Ar – present densely; sōlai – in gardens; vari – striped; vaṇḍu – beetles’; kuḻām – groups (having drunk honey); isai pādum – humming; pādal kēttu – hearing the songs; tīm karumbu – sweet sugarcanes; kaṇ vaḷarum – growing by one part; kaḻani – by fertile fields; sūḻnda – surrounded; tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ – in tirukkōvalūr; nān kaṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān rode garudāḻvār and fought the battle which was unable to bear for anyone, with rākśasas starting with māli to kill them and eliminated the complaints of those who were present on earth; he is having such nature that while eliminating the enemies, tears appeared and were overflowing for his servitors having great love and he is enjoyable as complete nectar for them; I got to see such emperumān in tirukkōvalūr which is surrounded by fertile fields where gardens which have kōngu flowers, surapunnai trees, kuravu trees are densely present and striped beetles are humming and sweet sugarcanes are growing by one part hearing those songs.

*tāngarum* … – Just as an old ant-hill will never become free from snakes, even before rāvaṇan, lankā was always filled with evil persons starting with māli et al; he killed them in this manner. In the battle which cannot be tolerated by anyone, māli who was engaged was killed by emperumān by riding his garudāḻvār.

*tarā talam* – Had māli lived even for a fraction of a moment further, the whole world would have been destroyed.

*āngu …* – emperumān being greatly enjoyable for those loving servitors who are getting tears due to love towards him, and have such tears overflow from their eyes.

*kōngu* … – In the gardens which have dense rows of kōngu flowers, surapunnai trees, kuravu trees, the beetles which gathered were humming songs having drunk honey; having heard such songs, the sugarcane grew one more part as if it was watered.

## 2.10.5. Karai valar

*kaṟai vaḷar vēl karan mudalāk kavandan vāli kaṇai onṟināl madiya ilangai tannuḷ piṟai eyiṟṟu vāḷ arakkar sēnai ellām perundagaiyōdu udan tuṇitta pemmān tannai maṟai vaḷarap pugaḻ vaḷara mādandōṟum maṇḍabam oṇṭhoḷi anaittum vāram ōda siṟai aṇainda poḻil aṇainda tenṟal vīsum tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ kaṇḍēn nānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṟai vaḷar – heavily stained; vēl – one who has spear; karan mudalā – karan et al; kavandan vāli – those who are known as kabandan, vāli et al; kaṇai onṟināl – with an arrow; madiya – to die; ilangai tannuḷ – in lankā; piṟai – bent like a crescent; eyiṟu – having teeth; vāḷ – having sword as weapon; arakkar sēnai ellām – all of the armies of rākśasas; perum tagaiyōdu udan – along with rāvaṇa who was their leader; tuṇitta – severed and pushed down; pemmān tannai – sarvēśvaran; mādam tōṟum – in all the houses; maṟai – vēda gōśam; vaḷara – rising greatly; pugaḻ – fame; vaḷara – to increase; maṇḍapam – in the halls; oṇḍu – close to the town; oḷi anaittum – in the coultries; vāram ōda – to repeat what was learnt previously; siṟai – water moat; aṇainda – in the gardens; poḻil – in garden; aṇainda – rested on; tenṟal – southerly breeze; vīsum – emitting fragrance; tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ – in tirukkōvalūr; nān kaṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran killed with one arrow karan et al who carry heavily stained spear and those who are known as kabandan, vāli et al; he severed and pushed down the heads of rākśasa army in lankā who were having crescent like bent teeth and sword as their weapon, along with their leader rāvaṇa who is the leader of all armies; I got to see such emperumān in tirukkōvalūr where every home chants vēda gōśam increasingly, the fame increases and repeatedly recite vēdam tumultuously; as the vēdam is repeatedly recited in halls and coultries, the southerly breeze which is rested on the garden along the water moat is emitting fragrance.

*kaṟai …* – Due to eagerness in harming others, always destroying enemies, there is no time to wash the blood stains, and because of that there is a lot of stains in the spear. These persons such as karan, kabandan, vāli et al who are having such spear. While karan, virādan et al appear, they will have lions, tigers etc hanging on the spears.

*kaṇai onṟināl madiya* – He finished them with an arrow which he could get hold of. This is how the leaders who were guarding, were killed.

*ilangai …* – All the rākśasas in lankā who were having crescent like teeth and weapons.

*perum tagai …* – perum tagai means periyōn (leader); controller – king. rāvaṇa being their king, their refuge and the one who is the shade to those evil persons who will take shelter of him, was eliminated along with them, by the lord; it is the owner who will take out the weeds.

Just as in śrī daṇḍakāraṇyam where recital of vēdam continued without a break after the killing of rāvaṇa, the same thing happened in tirukkōvalūr.

*mādam tōṟum* – As the sound of vēdam recital keeps increasing in houses, the fame increases. This is how the houses are.

*maṇḍabangaḷ* … – Halls; oṇṭhoḷi – beautiful tōḷi. tōḷi is shrunk as toḷi; implies pratōḷ (four way junctions). In halls, four way junctions, they will sit around and recite vēdams.

*siṟai …* – Well protected. Only air and emperumān who is quicker than air can enter. The southerly breeze which has entered and is resting on the garden which is along the moat for the town, picks up water drops and the fragrance from the garden, and gently serves those who are reciting vēdam to eliminate their fatigue. oḷi – oḻungai. Located close to the moat.

## 2.10.6. Uriyarnda

*uṟiyārnda naṟuveṇṇey oḷiyāl senṟu angu uṇḍānaik kaṇḍu āycci uralōdu ārkka taṟiyārnda karungaḷiṟē pōla ninṟu tadangaṇgaḷ pani malgum tanmaiyānai veṟiyārnda malarmagaḷ nāmangaiyōdu viyan kalai eṇṭhōḷināḷ viḷangu selvac ceṟiyārnda maṇimādam tigaḻndu tōnṟum tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ kaṇḍēn nānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṟi – pot in the ropes, hanging down from the ceiling; ārnda – safely placed; naṟu – fresh; veṇṇey – butter; oḷiyāl – by the light (emitting from his teeth when he smiles); angu senṟu – reaching there; uṇḍānai – one who mercifully ate; āycci – mother yaśōdā; kaṇḍu – seeing his theft; uralōdu – with the mortar; ārkka – as he was tied; taṟi ārnda – tied to a pole; karum kaḷiṟu pōla – like a black elephant; ninṟu – being bound; tadam kaṇgaḷ – vast divine eyes; pani malgum – to have tears; tanmaiyānai – one who has such nature; veṟi ārnda – fragrant; malar magaḷ – with periya pirāttiyār who is born in lotus flower; nāmangaiyōdu – with sarasvati; viyan – amazing; kalai – having deer as vehicle; eṇ tōḷināḷ – with durgā who has eight shoulders; viḷangu – shining; selvam – wealth; seṟi ārnda – very dense; maṇi mādam – mansions studded with gems; tigaḻndu – shine; tōnṟum – appearing to be having wealth; tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ – in tirukkōvalūr; nān kaṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

By the light from his teeth, reaching the place where fresh butter was safely placed in the pot in the ropes hanging down from the ceiling, emperumān mercifully ate it. Seeing his theft, mother yaśōdā tied him to a mortar, just like a black elephant was tied to a pole; I got to see the one who has such nature to be bound and thus have tears in his vast eyes in tirukkōvalūr where the wealth which is shining with periya pirāttiyār who is born in fragrant lotus flower, sarasvati and eight shouldered durgā who is having amazing deer as her vehicle, and radiantly appearing with great wealth of gem studded mansions.

*uṟi …* – Placed in a pot in the rope which will reveal the theft, hanging down from the ceiling, the butter was well secured and remained fresh as it was while being churned; kriṣṇa will trace the path of the butter from the churning spot up to where it was safely placed.

*oḷiyāl senṟu angu uṇḍānai* … – oḷi – theft, light. oḷiyāl – by theft; alternatively – as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-3-vasagame-eththa/) “*nāḷ iḷam tingaḷaik* …” (consuming the butter placed inside bamboo hut with the light generated by the pleasing radiance of the young rising moon which is fresh everyday \[here fresh young rising moon is an example for kriṣṇa’s shining teeth\]). He ate the butter to be said by others as “This could not have been stolen by humans; this must have been taken away by a celestial person”.

*kaṇḍu* – emperumān considers the items touched by the favourable ones to be those which sustain him and when he does not get those, he will perish; similarly these devotees (yaśōdāp pirātti, āḻvārs) will seek his acts since such acts sustain them; hence they follow him and catch him.

*āycci* – Since she has overwhelming love and care towards kriṣṇa, she tied him to the mortar without realising the outcome.

*uralōdu ārkka* – She tied him to a mortar which was found near by since had she gone in search of a good pole or mortar to bind him, he may escape in the meantime.

*taṟiyārnda …* – Just as when an intoxicated elephant which was roaming around freely in the town, gets caught accidentally and will stand being bound to a pole, kriṣṇa who roamed around freely got bound and stood without any other way to react, with tears in his vast eyes.

*tanmaiyānai* – Supremacy is artificial decoration for him; this simplicity is his inherent nature. yaśōdāp pirātti said as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.15 “*yadiśaknōśi*” (free yourself up, if you can).

*karum kaḷiṟē pōla* – The way he stood without realising about himself. Had he been bound by unfavourable persons like duryōdana et al, he would have easily escaped from it. But when he was bound by favourable persons, he cannot release that.

*veṟi ārnda malar magaḷ* … – āḻvār is speaking about the one who can control such elephant from independent roaming. By her presence, she will engage emperumān so that he does not see others’ mistakes. periya pirāttiyār who is the puruśakāra bhūtai (one who performs recommendation) for those who surrender to emperumān; sarasvati who lives in the tongue of brāhmaṇas and is subservient to periya pirāttiyār; she assists periya pirāttiyār and helps in praising emperumān.

*viyan kalai* … – durgā who has an amazing deer as her vehicle and who has eight shoulders; she is the guard for tirukkōvalūr. To compensate for her sadness of revealing kriṣṇa’s identity during his birth, she carefully guards the town.

*seṟi …* – I got to see in tirukkōvalūr where gem studded mansions are densely present in a radiant manner.

*nān* – I who had not realised the presence of such benefit, got to see him in this well protected divyadēśam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.10.7. Irungaimma

*irungai mā kari munindu pariyaik kīṟiina vidaigaḷ ēḻadarttu marudam sāyttuvarum sagadam iṟa udaittu mallai attuvanjam sey kanjanukku nanju ānānaikkarungamugu pasum pāḷai veṇmuttu īnṟukāy ellām maragadamāyp pavaḷam kāttaserundimiga mottu alarttum tēnkoḷ sōlaittirukkōvalūr adanuḷ kandēn nānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

iru – long; kai – having trunk; mā – huge; kari – kuvalayāpīdam \[regal elephant of king kamsan\]; munindu – mercifully showed anger; pariyai – the mouth of kēśi, the horse; kīṟi – tore; inam – matching with each other; ēḻu vidaigaḷ – seven bulls; adarttu – killed; marudam – maruda trees; sāyttu – broke; varum – moving towards him (due to being possessed by the demon); sagadam – wheel; iṟa – to break; udaittu – kicked with divine feet; mallai – the wrestlers; attu – killed; vanjam sey – thought to kill him by mischief; kanjanukku – for kamsa; nanjānānai – one who became the god of death; karu – having black complexion; kamugu – areca trees; pasum pāḷai – fresh spates; veḷ – whitish; muttu – pearls; īnṟu – yield; kāyēllām – its unripened fruits; maradagamāy – showed green gem (and the fruits); pavaḷam kātta – showed corals; serundi – surapunnai tree; mottu – buds; miga – specially; alarttum – blossoms; tēn koḷ – having honey; tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ – in tirukkōvalūr; nān kaṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān mercifully showed anger on kuvalayāpīdam which had long trunk; he tore the mouth of kēśi, the horse; he killed the seven bulls which were matching with each other; he broke the maruda trees; he kicked the wheel which was moving towards him with his divine feet, to break it; he killed the wrestlers; he became the god of death for kamsa who thought to kill him by mischief; I got to see such emperumān in tirukkōvalūr which has gardens where fresh spates of blackish areca trees yield whitish pears, its unripened fruits show green gems and its ripened fruits show corals and the surapunnai trees would specially blossom flowers and have honey.

*irum kai …* – kamsa placed the elephant on the way to narrate that an accident happened (which can be blamed for the killing of kriṣṇa); showing his anger on kuvalayāpīdam which is having a very long trunk which can reach as far as the target.

*pari …* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.16.14 “*vyāditāsya: mahāraudra:*” (having wide open eyes and causing great fear), the horse came with great anger and wide open mouth; he placed his hand in its mouth and tore it; it fell down as two parts. Tearing the mouth of kēśi which came with enmity.

*inam …* – Killing seven bulls, not just one or two; crawling and knocking down the marudu trees while passing by them; while the cart wheel which was placed as guard started rolling towards him, being possessed by a demon, he kicked with his divine feet to turn it into pieces. tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.4 “*piḷandu vīya*” (falling down in pieces).

*mallai attu* – Killing the group of wrestlers, who came jumping like mountains, after he killed the elephant.

*vanjam …* – One who became god of death for kamsa who arranged a bow festival just to invite kriṣṇa and kill him cunningly, by finishing kamsa’s thoughts within himself.

*karum kamugu …* – The fresh spates of areca tree which are blackish due to their youth, yielded white pearls; as the tree started yielding unripened fruits, they looked like maradagam \[emerald\]; as the fruits ripened, they looked like corals.

*serundi miga mottu alarttum* – It appeared that the surapunnai trees were smiling, thinking “What an amazing site! The areca trees are showing different entities simultaneously!”

*serundi miga mottu alarttum* – It appears like those who are smiling thinking “There is no similarity in identity between the cause and effect!”

*tēn koḷ sōlai* – Garden having beetles; alternatively – garden having honey.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.10.8. Pareru

*pārēṟu perum bāram tīrap paṇḍu bāradattut tūdu iyangi pārttan selvat tērēṟu sāradiyāy edirndār sēnai seruk kaḷattut tiṟal aḻiyac ceṟṟān tannai pōrēṟu onṟu udaiyānum aḷagaik kōnum purandaranum nānmuganum porundum ūr pōl sīrēṟu maṟaiyāḷar niṟainda selvat tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ kaṇḍēn nānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pār – On earth; ēṟu – loaded; perum bāram – huge burden; tīra – to be eliminated; paṇḍu – previously; bāradattu – in mahābhārata war; tūdu iyangi – went as messenger; pārttan – arjuna’s; selvam – beautiful; tēr – in the chariot; ēṟu – best; sāradiyāy – being the charioteer; edirndār sēnai – the army of the opposing enemies; seruk kaḷattu – in the battle field; tiṟal aḻiya – to destroy the strength; seṟṟān tannai – one who destroyed; pōr – (by its strength) pushing to fight; ēṟu onṟu – a bull; udaiyānum – rudra who has as vehicle; aḷagaik kōnum – vaiśravaṇa (kubēra); purandaranum – indra; nānmuganum – brahmā; porundum – remaining together; Ur pōl – like a town; ēṟu – lot of; sīr – having good qualities; maṟaiyāḷar – brāhmaṇas who are experts in vēdam; niṟainda – well gathered; selvam – having wealth; tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ – in tirukkōvalūr; nān kaṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, to eliminate the huge burden which got loaded on earth and to destroy the army of the opposing enemies, previously in the mahābhārata war, went as arjuna’s messenger and remained the best charioteer in arjuna’s beautiful chariot, destroyed them in the battle field; I got to see such emperumān in tirukkōvalūr which is similar to a town where rudra who has bull which is pushing to fight, kubēra, indra and brahmā can live together, and where brāhmaṇas who have lots of good qualities and are experts in vēdam, have well gathered wealth.

*pār ēṟu perum bāram tīra* – Earth has the names kśamai (forgiveness) and poṟai (tolerance). To eliminate the huge burden on earth which cannot tolerate it even though it is named “poṟai”. The earth which is named based on its tolerance could not bear it due to becoming heavy being possessed by demons.

*paṇḍu* – āḻvār is saying “What a day when he went as a messenger!”

*bāradattut tūdu iyangi* – pāṇḍavas said “Our relatives should also live happily”; duryōdana et al said “If our relatives (pāṇḍavas) lived, we cannot live”. kriṣṇa tried to create a truce between them by going as messenger; but as duryōdana et al said “We will not agree to your words” in any manner, kriṣṇa himself caused the war, and when they said to him “We will not let you pick up arms”, he killed them with chariot wheel (by riding it efficiently) itself.

*pārttan selvat tēr* – This is the chariot of arjuna who has kriṣṇa as his friend, brother-in-law, messenger and charioteer. It is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-14/) “*mahati syandanē stitau*” (seated in the huge chariot).

*sāradiyāy* – If he were the rati (one who is the owner of the chariot), victory will be his; hence he assumed the role of sārati (charioteer) and ensured that the victory was arjuna’s.

*edirndār …* – Though he reduced himself to be the charioteer and ensured the victory went for arjuna, those who know the root cause, will not leave it. āḻvār is saying “arjuna is just an instrument and it was kriṣṇa who won the war and brought fame to arjuna by doing so”. In the battle field, against the opposing army. duryōdana et al tried to cunningly defeat pāṇḍavas by trying to push them in a pond on the banks of river gangā, to push them into the lacquer palace and burn it down and defeat them in gambling; unlike that, kriṣṇa got them killed by eliminating their strength in direct battle in the battlefield.

*pōr …* – The presence of brāhmaṇas in that town appeared as if all the dēvatās migrated to a single place after the demoniac forces were eliminated. Resembling a town where rudra who has bull as his vehicle, vaiśravaṇa, indra and brahmā are present together. \[How can we compare brāhmaṇas who serve selflessly to these dēvatās?\] rudra who can burn down anyone, burnt down manmata (cupid) when manmata tried to induce lust in rudra towards his wife \[hence he has detachment\]. kubēra would donate generously and his wealth will double by giving \[generosity\]. indra will give joy to those who come to his abode.

*nānmuganum* – He has peace and he is the creator of all.

*sīr …* – The abode where brāhmaṇas with such qualities, are present with unlimited wealth.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.10.9. Tuvadivil

*tūvadivil pārmagaḷ pūmangaiyōdu sudar āḻi sangu irupāl polindu tōnṟak kāvadivil kaṟpagamē pōla ninṟu kalandavargatku aruḷ puriyum karuttinānai sēvadi kai tiruvāy kaṇ sivanda ādai sempon sey tiru uruvam ānān tannai tīvadivin sivan ayanē pōlvār mannu tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ kaṇḍēn nānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tū – beautiful; vadivil – having form; pār magaḷōdu – with śrī bhūmip pirātti; pū mangaiyōdu – with periya pirāttiyār; sudar – radiant; āḻi – tiruvāḻiyāḻvān (divine chakra); sangu – śrī pāncajanyāḻvān (divine conch); irupāl – on both sides; polindu tōnṟa – appearing effulgently; kā vadivil – grown as a garden; kaṟpagam pōla ninṟu – standing like a kalpaka tree; kalandavargatku – for those who hold emperumān as all types of relations; aruḷ puriyum – who eagerly gives; karuttinānai – one who has divine heart; sē – reddish; adi – divine feet; kai – divine hands; tiruvāy – divine lips; kaṇ – divine eyes; sivanda ādai – divine waist garment (having these); sembon sey – like beautiful gold; tiruvuruvam ānān tannai – one who has a beautiful form; tī vadivil – in the form of fire; sivan – rudran; ayan pōlvār – and like brahmā, who are experts in creation and annihilation; mannu – eternally residing; tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ – in tirukkōvalūr; nān kaṇḍēn – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is standing like a kalpaka tree which is grown into a garden, along with śrī bhūmip pirātti and śrī mahālakśmi who are having beautiful form, and the radiant tiruvāḻiyāḻvān and śrī pāncajanyāḻvān on his sides; for those who hold emperumān as all types of relations, he has the divine heart to eagerly give them; he has reddish divine feet, divine hands, divine lips, divine eyes and divine waist garment; he has beautiful gold like beautiful divine form; I got to see such emperumān in tirukkōvalūr where those who are similar to brahmā and rudran who has a fire like form and are experts in creation and annihilation, are eternally residing.

*tū vadivil …* – With śrī bhūmip pirātti who has a form which is opposite to all defects, who has the earth as her form and who is the controlling deity of earth, and periya pirāttiyār who has lotus flower as her abode; the divine weapons which protect this togetherness, appear radiantly as if the moon and sun rose together.

*sudar …* – When emperumān remains with his divine consorts and the divine weapons, he appears like a kalpaka tree branching out well.

*kā vadivil kaṟpagamē pōla ninṟu* – Not just a single kalpaka tree, but appearing like a garden of kalpaka trees, viz. emperumān being the benefactor of all desires.

*kalandavar …* – For those who look up to emperumān’s hands saying “We are not responsible for our protection; it is your responsibility”, he eagerly shows his great mercy.

*sēvadi …* – After seeing his divine form, can we even abandon him if he does not shower mercy?

*tī vadivil …* – The dēvatās appear as if the fire has taken into a shape. The residents of tirukkōvalūr can themselves perform creation and annihilation.

## 2.10.10. Varanam kol

*vāraṇam koḷ idar kadinda mālai neela maradagattai maḻai mugilē pōlvān tannai sīraṇangu maṟaiyāḷar niṟainda selvat tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ kandēn enṟu vāraṇangu mulai madavār mangai vēndan vāḷ kaliyan oli aindum aindum vallār kāraṇangaḷāl ulagam kalandu angu ēttak karandu engum parandānaik kāṇbar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāraṇam – śrī gajēndrāḻvān; koḷ – had; idar – sorrow; kadinda – one who eliminated; mālai – being affectionate towards devotees; neelam – karuneydal flower; maradagam – green gem; maḻai – cool; mugil – cloud; pōlvān tannai – sarvēśvaran who has physical beauty like these; aṇangu – desired by all; sīr – having noble qualities; maṟaiyāḷar – brāhmaṇas; niṟainda – abundant; selvam – having wealth; tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ – in tirukkōvalūr; kaṇḍēn enṟu – saying “I got to see”; vār – wearing knotted clothes; aṇangu – beautiful; mulai – having bosoms; madavār – filled with ladies; mangai – for tirumangai region; vēndan – being the king; vāḷ – having sword; kaliyan – mercifully spoken by āḻvār; oli – having garlands of words; aindum aindum – these ten pāsurams; vallār – those who can learn; ulagam – those who are in this world; kāraṇangaḷāl – to achieve goals starting with worldly wealth; kalandu – arrived together; ētta – surrendering with praises (though he is omnipresent); karandu – being invisible to all; engum parandānai – sarvēśvaran who is all pervading; kāṇbar – will get to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

āḻvār, the king of tirumangai region which is filled ladies with beautiful bosoms decorated with knotted cloth, where he has sword, said “I got to see sarvēśvaran who eliminated the sorrow of śrī gajēndrāḻvān, and who has beauty similar to that of karuneydal flower, green gem and cool cloud, in tirukkōvalūr where brāhmaṇas who are having noble qualities which are desired by all and abundant wealth, are present”; those who can learn such āḻvār’s ten pāsurams which are in the form of garland of words, will get to see sarvēśvaran who is praised and surrendered by everyone in the world seeking goals such as worldly wealth etc and who is all pervading and not seen by anyone.

*vāraṇam …* – One who became loving towards śrī gajēndrāḻvān who can cause harm to others, by eliminating its sorrow.

*neela maradagattai …* – He stood showering his cool mercy and eliminating its fatigue fully.

*sīr …* – Inhabited by brāhmaṇas who are desired for their noble qualities, having abundant wealth.

*tirukkōvalūr adanuḷ kaṇḍēn enṟu* – Unlike having to travel very far \[seen right here\].

*vāraṇangu …* – Those ladies having bosoms which are decorated by knotted clothes which shine due to those bosoms. aṇangu – desire and beauty. Not just the beauty of the clothes but also the beauty acquired by the bosoms which they decorate.

*vāḷ kaliyan …* – Those who can learn these ten pāsurams which were mercifully spoken by āḻvār who has the sword which will vanquish enemies.

*kāraṇangaḷāl …* – Surrendered by the people of world who have gathered seeking worldly wealth, self enjoyment and eternal service to bhagavān.

*karandu …* – As they surrendered, he entered everywhere and pervaded to fulfil the desires of those who surrendered and remained invisible for all others. They will see emperumān who waits for those who surrender unto him thinking “Who will come to us and surrender?”
