## Third Centum

## 3.1 Irundan

## 3.1.1. Irundan

*irundaṇ mānilam ēnamadāy vaḷai maruppinil agattu odukki karundaṇ mākadal kaṇ tuyinṟavanidam kamala nan malart tēṟal arundi innisai muranṟeḻum aḷikulam poduḷi am poḻil ūdē serundi nāṇmalar senṟu aṇaindu uḻitaru tiruvayindirapuramē*

**Пословный перевод:**

irum taṇ – very cool; mā nilam – vast earth (while deluge had consumed it); ēnam adāy – in the form of varāha \[wild boar\]; vaḷai maruppu agattinil – on the bent tusk; odukki – secured (then); karum taṇ mā kadal – in the great ocean which is black and cool; kaṇ tuyinṟavan – for the one who performed yōga nidrā; idam – the abode; kamalam – lotus’; nal – beautiful; malar – in the flower; tēṟal – honey; arundi – drank; in isai – beautiful tune; muranṟu – sang; eḻum – joyfully dance; aḷi kulam – swarms of beetles; poduḷi – gathered; am – beautiful; poḻil ūdē – in the middle of the garden; serundi – serundi tree’s; nāḷ malar – in the freshly blossomed flower; senṟu aṇaindu – went and reached; uḻi taru – roaming; tiruvayindirapuramē – is the divyadēśam known as tiruvahindrapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān in the form of varāha secured the very cool, vast earth, on his bent tusk; the abode for such emperumān who performed yōga nidrā in the great ocean which is black and cool, is the divyadēśam known as tiruvahindrapuram where swarms of beetles gathered and drank honey in the beautiful lotus flower, sang beautiful tunes and joyfully danced, went and reached the serundi tree’s freshly blossomed flower in the middle of the garden, and were roaming.

*irum taṇ mā nilam* – mā nilam indicates vast earth; hence taṇ indicates the earth being the place where enjoyment, the tools of enjoyment and the abode of enjoyment are shown well; irum – greatness. When such earth was consumed by deluge, in his divine heart, the form which will be useful for the ātmās, is only present.

*ēnam adāy* – As he understood the goal, he minimized his stature. He assumed the varāha form which will not hesitate to enter water and mud. He held the earth in a corner of his bent tusk. With this, emperumān the protector, being greater than what is to be protected, is explained.

As he realised in his divine heart that he has secured the earth,

*karum taṇ …* – It is well known that he is present in every ocean. Due to that, he is said here as in mūnṟām tiruvandādi 37 “*uvarkkum karu kadal nīruḷḷān*” (He is present in the salty ocean which is dark). Alternatively, it can be said that tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean) became a dust in the lotus feet of mahā varāha.

*kamalam …* – The beetles will enter the distinguished, blossomed lotus flowers and drink honey; having drunk honey till their necks, due to the overwhelming joy, they will hum sweet music. They will hum in a pleasant way for others to hear. Due to the honey which has gone in, it will not let one in a stable posture; as the beetles consumed the honey in the lotus flower, due to overwhelming desire, thinking that they can drink more honey from serundi tree, meditating upon its honey, just like those who would seek to enter a flooded river, will hold hands with others with similar intent, they also gather together.

*poduḷi* – The flowers will wait till all the beetles enter and will beautifully blossom. poḻil ūdē – in the garden, they will reach the fresh flower in the serundi tree.

*poduḷi* – They will gather together and roam around. The beetles which entered the lotus flower due to the desire towards it and drank the honey, think about the overflowing honey in serundi tree; thinking “it is not good to get caught, without analysing”, just as those who would fear to enter the flooded river, will roam around, reaching serundi flower, fearing to enter in there, would remain on the banks and roam around here and there.

poduḷi – Abundance. This can also be seen as an attribute of the garden.

## 3.1.2. Minnum ali

*minnum āḻi angai avan seyyavaḷ uṟai taru tirumārvan pannu nānmaṟaip palporuḷ āgiya paranidam varaic cāral pinnum mādavip pandalil pedai varap piṇi aviḻ kamalattu tenna enṟu vaṇḍu innisai mural taru tiruvayindirapuramē*

**Пословный перевод:**

minnum – shining; āḻi – divine chakra; am – beautiful; kaiyavan – having in divine hand; seyyavaḷ – periya pirāttiyār; uṟai taru – eternally residing; tirumārvan – one who has the divine chest; nānmaṟai – by vēdams which are of four categories; pannu – identified; pal poruḷ – many entities; āgiya – having as his prakāram (form); paran – for greater than all; idam – abode; varaic cāral – in mountain slope; pinnum – present densely; mādavip pandalil – in the mādavi creeper shed; vaṇḍu – beetles; pedai – with their female counter-parts; vara – to arrive; piṇi aviḻ – blossoming; kamalattu – (entering) in the lotus; tenna enṟu – saying “tennā! tenā!” (music); in isai mural taru – humming sweet songs; tiruvayindirapuramē – tiruvahindrapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is having the shining, divine chakra in his beautiful divine hand; he is having the divine chest where periya pirāttiyār is eternally residing; he is having all the entities identified by vēdams which are of four categories, as his forms; the abode of such emperumān who is greater than all is tiruvahindrapuram. The beetles which are in the densely present mādavi creeper sheds in the mountain slopes, are singing “tennā! tenā!” and humming sweet songs for their female counter-parts while entering blossoming lotus.

*minnum* … – sarvēśvara lakśaṇam (Identity of being supreme lord) is holding the divine chakra without shaking, being the husband of lakshmi, being known from vēdam only; all these three are present.

*minnum āḻi am kai avan* – One who is holding divine chakra in his hand, like a lightning occurs in a cloud.

*seyyavaḷ …* – Having periya pirāttiyār in his divine chest, just as a streak of lightning, embracing his divine chest.

*pannu …* – Being greater than all since he alone remains the prakāri (substratum) and has all other entities which are mentioned in four types of vast vēdams as his prakāram. He said in śrī bhagavat gītā 15.15 “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya:*” (I am only spoken about in all of vēdams). puruśa sūktam “*hrīścatē …*” (śrī bhūmip pirātti and śrī mahālakśmi are your divine consorts). yajur vēdam “*asyēśānā jagatō viṣṇu patnī*” (One who is leader of the world due to being the divine consort of viṣṇu).

*varai …* – The life of the animals there is similar to the constant romantic fights which occur between pirātti and bhagavān in their divine togetherness. The beetles which went to drink honey in the dense mādavi sheds in the mountain slope, showed their romantic anger blaming each other; at that time the female beetles vowed saying “Let me see how you live” towards their male counter-parts and entered the well blossomed lotus flowers; since the male beetles cannot live without their pairs even for a moment as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.42 “*naivadamśān*” (śrī rāma does not realise what crawls on him) and in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.10 “*na jīvēyam*” (I cannot live without sītā even for a moment); they suffered in this manner, tried in various ways and even tried to please the female beetles by trying to compromise; still the female beetles did not heed to the male beetles; they thought “What to do?” and “They will not abandon us; they are only hiding to see how we are suffering; let us sing and make them come out”

*pinnum mādavi pandalil pedai vara* – To make the female beetles which had entered the freshly blossomed lotus flowers, give up their romantic anger and show their face, they also entered those flowers and sang with tune. A person who accepted some service will not be able to blame. It is also said that enmity can be eliminated through songs; it is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-9-9-udhum-aththinguzharke/) “… *pēdai nenjaṟavaṟap pādum pāttai …*” (We are unable to comprehend in any manner the song which he sang to have the separation which happened due to the love-fight in the young girls’ hearts, eliminated fully).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.3. Vaiyam elum

*vaiyam ēḻum uṇḍu ālilai vaigiya māyavan adiyavarkku meyyan āgiya deyva nāyaganidam meytagu varaic cāral moykoḷ mādavi seṇbagam muyangiya mullaiyangodi āda seyya tāmaraic ceḻumpaṇai tigaḻtaru tiruvayindirapuramē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaiyam ēḻum – the seven lower level worlds; uṇḍu – consumed; Al ilai – on a banyan leaf; vaigiya – spent his time; māyavan – one who has amazing ability; adiyavarkku – for those who fully serve him; meyyan āgiya – one who reveals himself fully; deyvanāyagan – for deyvanāyagan (lord of lords); idam – abode is; mey tagu – matching emperumān’s tender, divine form; varaic cāral – in the mountain slope; moy koḷ – dense; mādavi – kurukkatti; seṇbagam – campaka flower; muyangiya – embraced; mullai – in forest land; am – beautiful; kodi – jasmine creeper; Ada – as it sways (by that wind); seḻu – rich; paṇai – in water bodies; seyya tāmarai – reddish lotus (blossom); tigaḻ taru – shining; tiruvayindrapuramē – tiruvahindrapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, who has amazing ability, consumed the seven lower worlds and spent time staying on a banyan leaf; the abode of such emperumān, who reveals himself fully to those who fully serve him, is tiruvahindrapuram where in the forest lands where the dense mādavi flower embraced the śenbaga flower in the mountain slope which matches his tender nature, the jasmine creeper sways, and the lotus flower in the rich water bodies is shining.

*vaiyam …* – emperumān who has amazing ability and who mercifully rested on the freshly grown banyan leaf. One who performs impossible acts and protects his devotees.

*adiyavarkku …* – nitya praḷayam (continuous deluge) is the separation for those devotees for a moment from bhagavān; this is not the same as the deluge which occurs once in a long while for the world where bhagavān protects the world. emperumān reveals all his qualities to those who are exclusively dependent on him, so that they can enjoy him by comprehending him saying “This is how he is”.

*deyva nāyaganidam* – Just as he allows nityasūris to enjoy all his qualities, this is the abode where he stands allowing the devotees of this world to enjoy all his qualities. He said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 11.54](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/11-54/) “*aham ēvam vid*a:” (This is my nature). As he mercifully said that he is to be attained through bhakti only, arjuna said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 10.12](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/10-12-part-1/) “*param brahma param dāma*” (Your highness is known as param brahma (the supreme brahman), param jyōti (the supreme light)); when arjuna asked “How are you easily approachable through bhakti?” he said “*aham ēvam vida:*” – “You cannot speak about me by interacting with me as people do in this world usually; you have to observe me as done by those nityasūris; this is my nature”.

*mey tagu* – Being tender. In the mountain slope which is distinguished from other places.

*moy koḷ …* – moy – strength, dense. Here it implies dense, the mādavi flowers, which are dense, went and embraced śeṇbaga flowers; as the jasmine creeper in the forest land swayed due to the wind, the lotus flowers which are ready to blossom in the fertile lands, being touched with that wind, blossomed. The fertile lands having reddish lotus flowers are causing the shine.

*tiruvayindrapuramē* – Just as he unites the aspects which are impossible to unite and protects his devotes, this is the place where the forest land and fertile land can be seen together and enjoyed.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.4. Maru kondu

*māṟu koṇḍu udanṟedirnda val avuṇan tan mārbagam irupiḷavā kūṟu koṇḍu avan kula magaṟku innaruḷ koduttavan idam midaindu sāṟu koṇḍa men karumbu iḷangaḻai tagai visumbuṟa maṇi nīḻal sēṟu koṇḍa taṇ paḻanamadu eḻil tigaḻ tiruvayindirapuramē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māṟu koṇḍu – Considering “I am an enemy”; udanṟu – being angry; edirnda – one who came opposing; val – very strong; avuṇan than – the rākśasa, hiraṇya’s; mārvagam – chest; iru piḷavā – to become two pieces; kūṟu koṇḍu – split him; avan kula magaṟku – for prahlādāḻvān who is his son; in aruḷ koduttavan – for the one who showered his good mercy; idam – abode; midaindu – being close to each other; sāṟu koṇḍa – as the juice is flowing; mel – tender; karumbu – sugarcane’s; iḷangaḻai – the edge of the sprout; visumbu – the sky; uṟa – as it reaches; tagai – stopped by (that sky) (that sugarcane’s); maṇi nīḻal – having beautiful shade; sēṟu koṇḍa – having mud (created by the sugarcane juice); taṇ – cool; paḻanamadu – fertile fields’; eḻil – beauty; tigaḻ – shining; tiruvayindrapuramē – tiruvahindrapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān split the chest of hiraṇya, the very strong rākśasa, who considered “I am an enemy” and angrily came opposing, to make it into two pieces and showered his good mercy on his son, prahlādāḻvān; tiruvahindrapuram is his abode where the closely packed sugarcane’s juice is flowing and such sugarcane’s sprout’s edge is reaching up to the sky and is being stopped by the sky; such abode is shining by the beauty of cool fertile fields with such sugarcane’s beautiful shade and mud.

*māṟu koṇḍu …* – He came saying “I am your enemy” to the one who remains as said in śrī bhagavat gītā “*suhrudam sarvabhūtānām*” (one who is kind-hearted towards all); saying “I am enemy”.

*udanṟu* – While one may be saying “I am enemy”, yet one may not have enmity in the heart; unlike that, he came forward with enmity in heart.

*val avuṇan* – hiṟanya’s. Saying “I am enemy” with his mouth, having hatred in the heart, and standing in front due to that – all three are explained. For the demoniac person who was fed with the boons of dēvas and who acquired great strength by that.

*mārvu …* – emperumān who split his vast chest to make it two pieces.  He became weak as he saw the angry form of narasimha; subsequently emperumān split him into two pieces. One who killed the hardcore enemy hiraṇya and showered his mercy on such hiraṇya’s son as if it is a benefit for him. sarvēśvaran is the one who makes a father protect his son realising his vātsalyam (motherly forbearance); when such vātsalyam is missing, and the father showed his true colours (of enmity) and stood, he undertook a closer relationship than being a father and helped prahlādāḻvān.

*midaindu …* – As the father himself became an enemy, and as emperumān helped him as a closer relative than the father, there is no one who is related closer than empeurmān; even the one who remains in this manner, as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 6.5](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/6-5/) “*ātmaiva ripurātmana:*” (mind alone is one’s enemy), when one showed enmity towards the self, and tried to commit suicide, emperumān arrived in this abode to care for ātmās saying “I will not allow you to control yourself”; being close to each other and pushing other trees causing the juice, honey is flowing from the tender; *iḷam kaḻai* – edge. As it reaches the sky, the sky will stop saying “We will not allow to grow further”. Such sugarcane which is grown, having good shade; having beautiful shade, and having mud which is caused by the juice flowing from the sugarcane; the fertile fields where such beauty and mud are present and is shining in tiruvahindrapuram. periya tiruvandādi 57 “*taḻīkkoṇḍu pōravuṇan tannai suḻittengum tāḻvidangaḷ paṟṟip pulāl veḷḷam tānugaḷa*” (in the battle, emperumān embraced him tightly, the flood of blood flowing with a swirl is pervading all the low lying places) – when he killed hiraṇyakaśipu, by hiraṇya’s flood of blood, there was mud everywhere just as closely packed sugarcanes cause the juice to flood the earth.

## 3.1.5. Angu mavali

*āngu māvali vēḷviyil irandu senṟu agalidam aḷandu āyar pūngodikku ina vidai porudavanidam ponmalar tigaḻ vēngai kōngu seṇbagak kombinil kudikodu kurakkinam iraittōdit tēn kalanda taṇ palangani nugartaru tiruvayindirapuramē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māvali – mahābali’s; vēḷviyil – in sacrificial arena; senṟu – reached; irandu – begged (for three feet of land); āngu – there itself; agal idam – vast earth; aḷandu – measured and accepted; āyar – covherds’; pūm kodikku – for nappinnaip pirātti who is like a blossomed creeper; ina vidai – collection of the seven bulls; porudavan – for the one who fought and destroyed; idam – abode is; kurakkinam – troop of monkeys; pon malar – like golden flower; tigaḻ – shining; vēngaik kōngu seṇbagam – trees such as vēngai, kōngu, śeṇbagam; kombinil – on the branches; kudikodu – jumping; iraittu – with great noise; ōdi – came running; tēn kalanda – with abundant honey; taṇ – beautiful; palam kani – jackfruit; nugartaru – eating; tiruvayindirapuramē – tiruvahindrapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān reached mahābali’s sacrificial arena, begged and measured and accepted the vast earth there itself; he fought and destroyed the collection of seven bulls for nappinnaip pirātti who is like a blossomed creeper of the covherds; tiruvahindrapuram is his abode where a troop of monkeys is jumping on the branches of trees such as vēngai, kōngu, śeṇbagam which are shining like golden flower, came running with great noise and eating beautiful jackfruit with abundant honey.

*āngu …* – As emperumān heard “mahābali is giving charity”, he made himself a beggar and went to mahābali’s sacrificial arena, and as the water from mahābali’s hand fell on emperumān’s hand, there itself he stood and measured the vast earth; for nappinnaip pirātti who is like a blossomed creeper for covherds. Her age makes her seek support. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 118.34 “*pati samyōga sulabham vaya:*” (Seeing my age which is apt to get married to a man), when united with a supporting pole she will survive and if not she will lose her existence. The abode of the one who fought with the collection of bulls.

*pon …* – The troop of monkeys, jumping on the branches of vēngai, kōngu and śeṇbaga trees which are having flowers which shine like gold – jumping on them and running at great speed; not going beyond,

*tēn kalanda* … – Will eat the jackfruit which is filled with honey.

## 3.1.6. Kunulaviya

*kūnulāviya madandai tan kodunjolin tiṟattu iḷangodiyōdum kānulāviya karumugil tiruniṟattavanidam kavinārum vānulāviya madi tavaḻ mālvarai māmadiḷ pudai sūḻat tēnulāviya seḻum poḻil taḻuviya tiruvayindirapuramē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kūn ulāviya madandai than – hump-backed woman’s; kodum solin tiṟattu – for the harsh words; iḷam kodiyōdum – pirātti and he; kān – in the forest; ulāviya – one who mercifully went; karu mugil – like a dark cloud; tiruniṟattavan – for the one who has beautiful form; idam – abode is; kavin – beauty; ārum – present abundantly; vān – in the sky; ulāviya – roaming; madi – candra (moon); tavaḻ – to float; māl varai – tall mountains; mā madiḷ – huge forts; pudai sūḻa – surrounding in the sides; tēn ulāviya – beetles roaming; seḻum poḻil – with beautiful fertile fields; taḻuviya – surrounded; tiruvayindirapuramē – tiruvahindrapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān who is having a beautiful form like that of a dark cloud, mercifully went to the forest along with pirātti due to the harsh words of the hump-backed woman; his abode is tiruvahindrapuram where the moon which is roaming in the abundantly beautiful sky, is floating atop the tall mountains and huge forts which are surrounding in the sides and is also surrounded by beautiful fertile fields where the beetles are roaming.

*kūn …* – As said in śrī gītā bhāśyam “*sarvātmanānda:*” (fully blind), just as dritarāśtra was not just blind in his eyes but in mind too, not just kūni’s back was hunched, but her mind was cruel too. kūni spoke harsh words. Those words made kaikēyi who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 7.35 “*rāmē vā bharatē vāham viśēśam nōpalakśayē*” (I don’t see any difference between rāma and bharata) to say “*ēśa mē jīvitasya anta: rāma: yadyabhiśicyatē*” (If rāma is crowned as the prince, that day will be my last day).

*iḷam kodiyōdum* – She needs support, but is not at an age where she can go and seek that support on her own.

*kān ulāviya* – perumāḷ mercifully explained the cruel nature of the forest in a whole sargam saying “You cannot tolerate the heat in the forest”.

*karu mugil* – Just as a cloud will be floating, being embraced by a streak of lightning, perumāḷ and pirātti roamed around.

*kavin …* – kavin – beauty; the moon which is floating in the abundantly beautiful sky, has to crawl and climb the tall mountains and forts just as a toddler will do, which are present in the surroundings of tiruvahindrapuram which is also surrounded by beautiful gardens where beetles are roaming. This is an abode where cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma) who dvelled in the forest can forget \[the most pleasing\] tiruccitrakūtam and daṇḍakāraṇyam.

## 3.1.7. Minnin nunnidai

*minnin nuṇṇidai madakkodi kāraṇam vilangalin misai ilangai mannan nīḷmudi podi seyda maindanadidam maṇi varai nīḻal anna māmalar aravindattu amaḷiyil pedaiyodum inidu amara sennelār kavarikkulai vīsu taṇ tiruvayindirapuramē*

**Пословный перевод:**

minnil – like lightning; nuṇ – slender; idai – waist; madam – and having humility; kodi kāraṇam – for the creeper like pirātti; vilangalin misai – built on the suvēlā mountain; ilangai – for lankā; mannan – the king, rāvaṇa’s; nīḷ mudi – ten tall crowns/heads; podi seyda – turned to dust; maindanadu – strong one’s; idam – abode is; maṇi varai – gem mountain’s; nīḻal – in the shade; annam – swans; mā – big; aravinda malar – lotus flower; amaḷiyil – on the bed; pedaiyodum – with their female counterparts; inidu – sweetly; amara – to resting; sennel Ar kulai – the crop filled with red paddy; kavari vīsu – like fanning with whisk; taṇ – cool; tiruvayindirapuramē – tiruvahindrapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, the strong one, turned the ten heads/crowns of rāvaṇa, the king of lankā, which was built on the suvēlā mountain for the creeper like pirātti who is having slender waist which was like lightning and who had humility, into dust; his abode is the cool tiruvahindrapuram where under the shade of the gem-like mountain, swans along with their female counterparts were sweetly resting on the bed of huge lotus flowers to be fanned by the whisk of crop filled with red paddy.

*minnil …* – For the divine daughter of king janaka who is having lightning like slender waist, being the abode of all noble qualities, and having the age to be united with an able support. Her beauty will make the rakśaka (emperumān, the saviour) to say these words. śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 64.78 is explained here. *purēva mē cārudatīm* – If I am not presented with sītāp pirātti as she was smiling, before I went chasing the mystic deer when she asked “Please get that deer for me”. *aninditām* – When told “He destroyed the whole world for her”, can anyone oppose that saying “He did a mistake in doing this for her”? One should say as in “*yuktam ityēva mē mati:*” (In my opinion even if śrī rāma destroys everything for her sake, it is apt). \[hanuman thought\] If I, who have not understood pirātti fully, can think in this manner, what will those who fully understood pirātti think? *sadēva …* – Should he go through the same amount of difficulty in destroying the world as he went through while creating it?

*vilangalin …* – There is the suvēlā mountain; there is trikūta peak atop the mountain; finally, there is the capital city atop the peak; the abode of the strong one who turned into dust, the ten heads of evil rāvaṇa which were enriched by the boons of dēvatās, and where he was prideful that he was the king of such lankā which cannot be destroyed by anyone.

*maṇi varai nīḻal* – Under the shade of the gem-like mountain.

*annam …* – The swan, resting on the huge lotus flower bed; that is the bed where they can bathe, eat, drink honey, and having vastness to sleep away from each other when there is romantic fight between each other; even if one tolerates caṇḍāḷa by birth, one cannot tolerate the person who has become caṇḍāḷa due to offending the spouse; \[Would animals/birds have romantic fight? Yes\] as said in periya tirumoḻi 6.7.6 “*paḷḷik kamalattidaippatta*” (being caught inside the lotus which is the bed).

*sennelār …* – To be seated sweetly along with the female counterpart on the bed, the red paddy being helpful for such presence instead of being a hurdle, would do fanning with the whisk; will serve with the fully filled paddy crop, so that one need not worry about the presence of another person during such intimate times.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.8. Virai kamalnda

*virai kamaḻnda men karunguḻal kāraṇam villiṟuttu adal maḻaikku nirai kalangida varai kudai eduttavan nilaviya idam tadamār varai vaḷam tigaḻ madakari maruppodu malai vaḷaragil undi tirai koṇarndu aṇai seḻunadi vayal pugu tiruvayindirapuramē*

**Пословный перевод:**

virai – nice fragrance; kamaḻnda – spreading; mel – tender; karum kuḻal kāraṇam – for pirātti who has dark hair; vil – bow; iṟuttu – broke; adal – battle ready; maḻaikku – for the rain; nirai – cattle; kalangida – as they suffer; varai – gōvardana mountain; kudai – as umbrella; eduttavan – one who lifted and protected; nilaviya – eternally residing; idam – abode is; tadam – ponds; Ar – filled; varai – for hills; vaḷam – being decoration; tigaḻ – shining; mada kari – intoxicated elephant’s; maruppodu – tusk; malai vaḷar – growing in mountain; agil – agil tree (a fragrant tree); undi – pushing; tirai – wave; koṇarndu – bringing; aṇai – reaching; seḻunadi – beautiful river; vayal – in fertile fields; pugu – flowing; tiruvayindirapuramē – tiruvahindrapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān broke the bow for pirātti who is having tender, dark hair which is spreading nice fragrance; he lifted the gōvardana mountain and protected the cattle as they suffered the battle-ready rain; the eternal abode of such emperumān is tiruvahindrapuram where the tusks of elephants which are shining as decorations for mountains which are filled with ponds, and the agil tree (a fragrant tree) are pushed by the waves of the beautiful river which flows into the fertile field.

*virai …* – Having king janaka’s divine daughter, sītāp pirātti who has tender, dark hair which spreads nice fragrance as the reason, emperumān broke the bow. Her hair’s fragrance is such that bhagavān who is known as in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sarva ganda:*” (the abode of all fragrances) eagerly broke the bow without thinking about whether it is possible or not to do so. That is, he thought “When the prize for breaking the bow is sītāp pirātti, what can the hurdles do?”

*adal maḻaikku …* – Not just the activity done, being engrossed in her beauty, he protected the cows and covherds who cannot protect themselves from the rain by lifting the mountain. When the clouds which were sent by indra started pouring down, and as the cows and covherds were suffering, he protected them by lifting the gōvardana mountain.

*adal maḻaikku* – As said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.5.8 “*pōrkkaḷattu*” (in the battle field), the rain which was set to fight the cows and covherds.

*nirai kalangida* – Suffering as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.11.18 “*atīvārtam*” (suffered greatly).

*nirai kalangida adal maḻaikku varai kudai eduttavan* – Had it been rāmāvatāram he could have consulted with viśvāmitra et al or janaka et al and acted; here he just lifted a mountain, which he could lay his hands on, and protected them.

*nilaviya idam* – This is the place where he is eternally residing, thinking “We cannot remedy the situation after the event, as in the case of gōkulam where he remedied the situation after indra poured down the rain and they \[herd and herds-folk\] suffered; we need to proactively go and remain there to protect before they suffer”.

*tadam …* – tadam – mountain slope; it can be explained as beautiful elephants which are intoxicated which look similar to a growing mountain; alternatively – tadam – pond; along with the tusk of intoxicated elephant, being a decoration for mountain which has many ponds. Elephants are highlighted as decoration for mountains.

*malai vaḷar agil undi* – Uprooting the agil trees which grow densely covering the whole sky, due to lack of human intervention in mountains, and pushing the same.

*tirai …* – As the rain pours down, the waterfalls in the mountain, with the waves which are its hands, will break and push the elephant tusks and agil trees, and enter the fertile fields. Water will either enter man-made canals or smaller channels which help farming or will enter the sea to become useless; unlike those situations, here river is entering the fields to facilitate farming.

## 3.1.9. Velkol

*vēlkoḷ kaittalattu arasar vempōrinil visayanukkāy maṇit tēr kōlkoḷ kaittalattu endai pemmānidam kulavu taṇ varaic cāral kālkoḷ kaṇkodik kai eḻak kamugu iḷampāḷaigaḷ kamaḻ sāral sēlgaḷ pāy taru seḻunadi vayal pugu tiruvayindirapuramē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaittalattu – in the hand; vēl koḷ – having spear; arasar – duryōdana et al, their; vem – fearsome; pōrinil – in mahābhārata battle; visayanukku āy – being exclusively favourable towards arjuna (his); maṇit tēr – in the front portion of the beautiful chariot; kōl – stick; kaittalattu – in the hand; koḷ – held and stood; endai – lord of my clan; pemmān – for sarvēśvaran; idam – abode is; kulavu – praised by everyone; taṇ – cool; varaic cāral – on the surroundings of the mountain; kāl – pole on which the creeper spreads; kaṇ koḷ – growing in every branch; kodi – creeper; kai eḻa – to nurture; kamugu – areca trees; iḷam pāḷaigaḷ – young swathes; kamaḻ – spreading fragrance; sāral – having surroundings; sēlgaḷ – sēl fish; pāy taru – jumping; seḻu nadi – beautiful river; vayal pugu – flowing into the fertile field; tiruvayindirapuramē – tiruvahindrapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In the fearsome mahābhārata battle involving duryōdana et al who were having spear in their hands, emperumān, the lord of my clan remained exclusively favourable towards arjuna, held a stick in his hand and stood in the front portion of arjuna’s beautiful chariot; his abode is tiruvahindrapuram where the cool surroundings of the mountain which is praised by everyone, which has the surroundings where young swathes of the areca trees spread the fragrance to nurture the betel leaves which are growing in every branch of the creeper supported by the poles and where the beautiful river having sēl fish jumping around, is flowing into the fertile field.

*vēl …* – There is none lesser than bagadatta \[in valour\] in that battle; it was as said in mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam 28.17 “*pārtam sancātya mādava*” (kriṣṇa accepted the arrow shot at arjuna on his chest which became a garland).

*arasar* – Unlike the kings who would put their army in the forefront, it was such a battle where these kings themselves were in the forefront.

*vem pōr* – It was such a fearsome battle that even those who heard about it became frightened and even those \[cōḷa kings\] who  came to witness the battle had to hold weapons and protect themselves.

*visayanukkāy* – For arjuna, he risked himself. When a person becomes angry at a fighter, first he will target the charioteer of the fighter. emperumān risked himself by not wearing any armour for his body. He placed himself in a submissive role to place his victory on arjuna. periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.1.2 “*malai purai tōl mannavarum …*” (As the great warriors, kings, the hundred brothers were killed by the arrows of arjuna, kriṣṇa stood in front of him and guided him to victory) should be remembered here.

*maṇit …* – On the best chariot, the lord of my clan stood, holding a stick. His abode.

*kulavu …* – In the surroundings/slope of the mountain which is very praiseworthy.

*kāl koḷ kaṇ kodi* – kāl – veṟṟilaik kāl – pole on which the creeper spreads; to hide those poles, the betel creepers spread on them just as lizards stick to the wall. These creepers are nurtured well by the fragrance of the young swathes of the areca tree. kai – betel leaf branches. Having such gardens. River flows next to these gardens. The sēl fish jump around as if they are drunk. Such beautiful river flows into the fertile field. That is – the river flows up to the fertile field and as it reaches here, it stops its flow. Thus, this is the abode where dārakam (that which supports) is hidden under the dāryam (that which is supported). While the water nurtures the crops, it appears that the fertile field itself nurtures it. This is similar to kriṣṇa crediting arjuna with the victory though it was he who got arjuna the victory.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.10. Muvaragiya

*mūvarāgiya oruvanai mūvulagu uṇḍu umiḻndu aḷandānai dēvar tānavar senṟu senṟiṟainjat taṇ tiruvayindirapurattu mēvu sōdiyai vēl valavan kalikanṟi virittu uraitta pāvu taṇ tamiḻ pattivai pādidap pāvangaḷ payilāvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mūvar āgiya – Having the forms of brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra; oruvanai – being matchless; mū ulagu – three worlds; uṇḍu – consumed; umiḻndu – letting them out; aḷandānai – (retrieving from mahābali) one who measured and accepted; dēvar – dēvatās; dānavar – asuras; senṟu senṟu – repeatedly go; iṟainju – to surrender; taṇ – invigorating; tiruvayindirapurattu – in tiruvahindrapuram; mēvu – eternally residing; sōdiyai – on the radiant one; vēl valavan – one who can defeat the enemies with his spear; kali kanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; virittu – elaborately; uraitta – mercifully explained; pāvu – vast; taṇ – beautiful; tamiḻ – tamiḻ language; ivai pattu – these ten pāsurams; pādida – as one sings; pāvangaḷ – sins; payilā – will not remain

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being matchless, having the forms of brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra, the radiant emperumān consumed the three worlds, let them out and measured and accepted the same; he is etenrally residing in the invigorating tiruvahindrapuram to be repeatedly approached and surrendered to by dēvatās and asuras; on such emperumān, tirumangai āḻvār who could defeat enemies with his spear, elaborately and mercifully explained these ten pāsurams in the vast, beautiful tamiḻ language; as one sings these pāsurams, one’s sins will not remain with the self.

*mūvar …* – Since emperumān is present as the antaryāmi for the souls and the bodies of brahmā and rudra and performs creation and annihilation, and protects in his natural form of viṣṇu.

*mūvarāgiya oruvanai* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.66 “*brahma viṣṇu śivātmikām*” (nārāyaṇa engages in creation, protection and annihilation in the forms of brahmā, viṣṇu and Siva), being the controller of all.

*mū ulagu …* – He is also the friend in need.

*dēvar …* – As said in jitantē stōtram “*dēvānām dānavānānca*” (For both dēvatās and asuras), since he remains common for both dēvas and asuras who are created by him, he eternally resides in tiruvahindrapuram to be approached by both of them to have their desires fulfilled, and hence he remains more radiant here than in paramapadam. The quality of helping the asuras is not seen in paramapadam \[since there are no asuras in paramapadam\]; since he helps them here, the greatness acquired by that act is present only here.

*vēl valavan* – Just as emperumān is said as “*āḻi valavan*” (one who can destroy enemies with chakra).

*viritturaitta* – Explained in the manner where all aspects are completely explained. There is *viritturaitta* and *togutturaitta;* viritturaitta means explaining elaborately; togutturaitta means explaining sharply; here we should consider both ways to be present in these ten pāsurams.

*pāvu* – Instead of being vast like mahābhāratam which has one lakh twenty five thousand ślōkams, this is just a decad.

*pāvangaḷ payilāvē* – Having to experience the result of sins, one is born in this samsāram; while learning and practicing this decad in such samsāram where we are present to experience the result of the sins, the sins will run away thinking “We don’t belong in this person”.

## 3.2 Un vada

## 3.2.1. Un vada

*ūn vāda uṇṇādu uyir kāvalittu udalil piriyāp pulan aindum nondu tām vāda vādat tavam seyya vēṇḍā tamadā imaiyōr ulagāḷakiṟpīr! kānāda manjnjaik kaṇamāda mādē kayalādu kānīrp paḻanam pudai pōy tēnāda mādak kodiyādu tillait tiruccitra kūdam senṟu sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

imaiyōr ulagu – paramapadam; tamadā – as yours; āḷgiṟpīr – Oh you who are desiring to rule!; Un – flesh; vāda – to wither; uṇṇādu – avoiding eating etc; uyir – prāṇa (vital air) (with the help of water, air etc, to not leave); kāval ittu – imprisoning it; udalil piriyā – not leaving the body; aindu pulanum – five senses; nondu – torture; tām – them; vāda vāda – to suffer further; tavam seyya vēṇḍā – no need to perform penance; kān – forest; Ada – to sway; manjaik kaṇam – pride of peacocks; Ada – dance; mādē – near by; kayal – kayal fish; ādu – roaming; nīr – water flowing; kāl – having canals; paḻanam pudai pōy – going near the water bodies; tēn – beetles; Ada – rise to fly (by that wind); mādam – on the mansions; kodi – flags; ādu – swaying; tillait tiruccittirakūdam – tillait tiruccittirakūdam; senṟu sērmingaḷ – go and reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are desiring to rule paramapadam as yours! You need not perform penance to suffer further, by avoiding eating etc to wither the flesh, imprisoning the vital air, torturing the senses which don’t leave the body;  you go and reach tillait tiruccittirakūdam where the prides of peacocks dance to make the forest sway, the beetles rise to fly near water bodies which have canals where the water is flowing and the kayal fish are roaming, and due to that wind (caused by beetles’ act), the flags on the mansions are swaying.

*Un vāda* – one need not perform penance to suffer further, by decreasing food intake, wearing of comfortable clothes etc to reduce the flesh, imprisoning the vital air inside the body by consuming water, air etc, torturing the senses which don’t leave the body due to not getting enough enjoyment on the matters which are desired by them.

*tamadā …* – Oh you who are desiring to rule over paramapadam as if it is yours!

*kān Ada* … – Prides of peacocks dance to cause the garden to sway; the beetles which left the garden due to that, went close to the water bodies which have canals where the water is flowing and kayal fish are joyfully jumping around. tēn – vaṇḍu – beetle; as they rise to fly, by that wind, the flags on the mansions start swaying.

## 3.2.2. Kayodu nidu

*kāyōdu nīdu kani uṇḍu vīsu kadungāl nugarndu nedungālam aindu tīyōdu ninṟu tavam seyya vēṇḍā tirumārbanaic cindaiyuḷ vaittumenbīr! vāyōdu vēdam malginṟa tol sīr maṟaiyāḷar nāḷum muṟaiyāl vaḷartta tīyōnga ōngap pugaḻōngu tillait tiruccitra kūdam senṟu sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tirumārvanai – one who is the lord of śrī mahālakśmi; sindaiyuḷ – in the heart; vaittum enbīr – you who reveal the desire to keep!; kāyōdu – with unripened fruits; nīdu kani – fruits which have dried for many days; uṇḍu – eat; vīsu – blowing; kadum kāl – harsh wind; nugarndu – consumed; nedum kālam – many days; aindu tīyōdu ninṟu – standing amidst five fires; tavam seyya vēṇḍā – no need to perform penance; vāy – with mouth; ōdu – recited; malginṟa – remaining fully; tol – natural; sīr – having wealth; maṟaiyāḷar – brāhmaṇas; nāḷum – everyday; muṟaiyāl – in the proper manner; vaḷartta – practiced; tī – fire; ōnga ōnga – as it rises (by that); ōngu – rising above; pugaḻ – having greatness; tillait tiruccittirakūdam – tillait tiruccittirakūdam; senṟu sērmingaḷ – go and reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who reveal the desire to keep the one who is the lord of śrī mahālakśmi in your heart! You need not perform penance eating unripened fruits and fruits which have dried for many days, consuming the blowing wind and standing amidst five fires for many days; you go and reach tillait tiruccittirakūdam where the brāhmaṇas who are having the natural wealth of vēdam which is recited by mouth, conduct the fire everyday in the proper manner, where the greatness of the town is rising as the fire rises.

*kāyōdu …* – Oh you who have the desire to keep śriya:pati in your heart without separating! Eating the unripened fruits which are yet to mature, the fruits which are dried in the heat and wind, drinking the harsh wind which is blowing, you need not perform penance for a long time, staying amidst five fires.

*vāyōdu …* – tillait tiruccittirakūdam where the fame is increasing by the continuous nurturing of the fire in the proper manner by the brāhmaṇas who are having abundant natural wealth due to the lack of shortcoming in the vēdam which is recited by mouth.

## 3.2.3. Vembum sinattu

*vembum sinattup punakkēḻal onṟāy virinīr mudu veḷḷam uḷpukku aḻunda vambuṇ poḻil sūḻ ulagu anṟeduttān adippōdu aṇaivān viruppōdu iruppīr! paimponnum muttum maṇiyum koṇarndu padai mannavan pallavar kōn paṇinda sempon maṇi mādangaḷ sūḻnda tillait tiruccittira kūdam senṟu sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vambu – fresh; uṇ – having food items; poḻil – garden; sūḻ – surrounded; ulagu – earth; viri – vast; mudu nīr veḷḷam uḷ pukku – entering the great ocean; aḻunda – as it drowned; anṟu – at that time; vembum sinam – having great anger; punam – living in the forest; onṟu – matchless; kēḻalāy – being mahāvarāham (great pig/wild-boar); eduttān – one who dug in and lifted it; adippōdu – divine lotus feet; aṇaivān – to reach; viruppōdu – with desire; iruppīr – Oh you who are living!; pai – beautiful; ponnum – golden flowers; muttam – pearls; maṇiyum – gems; koṇarndu – bringing; padai – along with the army; mannavan – king; pallavarkōn – pallava king; paṇinda – surrendered; sembon – with beautiful gold; maṇi – made with gems; mādangaḷ – by mansions; sūḻnda – surrendered; tillait tiruccittirakūdam – tillait tiruccittirakūdam; senṟu sērmingaḷ – go and reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being mahāvarāham, emperumān, with great anger, dug in to the ocean and lifted earth which is having food items in  garden and which is drowned in the ocean; oh you, who are living with the desire to reach his divine feet! Go and reach tillait tiruccittirakūdam where the pallava king, who came along with his army, bringing beautiful golden flowers, pearls and gems, and where the mansions are with beautiful gems, surrendered.

*vembum …* – Live with the desire of  uniting with the divine feet of emperumān, who dug out the earth which was surrounded by gardens, when it was immersed in huge ocean. He took the form of mahāvarāham, the wild boar, which was angry and which was dwelling in forest

*paim pon …* – pallava king brought gems etc along with his army and surrendered and further constructed mansions with pearls and gems – such tillait tiruccittirakūdam.

tillait tiruccittirakūdam

## 3.2.4. Aruma nilam

*arumā nilam anṟu aḷappān kuṟaḷāy avuṇan peru vēḷviyil senṟu iranda perumān tirunāmam pidaṟṟi nundam piṟavit tuyar nīngudum ennagiṟpīr! karumā kadaluḷ kidandān uvandu kavainā aravin aṇaip paḷḷiyin mēl tirumāl tirumangaiyōdādu tillait tiruccitra kūdam senṟu sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

When indra lost his kingdom, sarvēśvaran went and begged in the great yāgam of mahābali, the demon, in vāmana form, to measure the immeasurable, great earth; oh you who incoherently recite such sarvēśvaran’s divine name and say “let us eliminate our sorrow of birth” in this manner! Go and reach tillait tiruccittirakūdam where śriya:pati along with periya pirāttiyār has mercifully reclined joyfully, is eternally residing.

*arumā …* – To measure the immeasurable, great earth, emperumān being vāmana, went and begged in the demon’s great yāgam. Reciting such sarvēśvaran’s divine name incoherently, oh you who are saying “We will eliminate the sorrow of birth”!

*karumā …* – On the mattress of tiruvanantāḻvān who has two tongues, emperumān who mercifully reclined joyfully on the dark, vast ocean, along with periya pirāttiyār, is present in tillait tiruccittirakūdam.

## 3.2.5. Komanga vanga

*kōmanga vangak kadal vaiyam uyyak kulamannar angam maḻuvil tuṇiya tām angu amaruḷ padai totta venṟit tavamā muniyait tamakkākkagiṟpīr! pūmangai tangip pulamangai mannip pugaḻ mangai engum tigaḻap pugaḻ sēr sēmangoḷ paimpūmpoḻil sūḻnda tillait tiruccittirakūdam senṟu sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kō – kings; manga – to be destroyed; vangam – boats (filled); kadal – surrounded by ocean; vaiyam – those residents of earth; uyya – to be liberated; kula mannar – kings’; angam – body; maḻu – by the axe; tuṇiya – to sever; tām – himself; angu – occurred at that time; amaruḷ – entering the battle; padai totta – took up arms; venṟi – one who has victory; tavam – went to perform penance subsequently; māmuniyai – śrī paraśurāmāḻvān, the great sage; ākkagiṟpīr – you who desire to own him!; pū mangai – periya pirāttiyār; tangi – residing (on his divine chest); pula mangai – śrī bhūmip pirātti; manni – remaining firmly (on his left side) (due to that); pugaḻ – fame; mangai – woman; engum – everywhere; tigaḻa – shining radiantly; pugaḻ sēr – having fame; sēmam koḷ – having protection; paim pūm poḻil sūḻnda – surrounded by vast, blossomed garden; tillait tiruccittirakūdam – tillait tiruccittirakūdam; senṟu sērmingaḷ – go and reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are desirous to own śrī paraśurāmāḻvān, the great sage who wanted to destroy the kings and to liberate the residents of the earth which is surrounded by ocean filled with boats, who took up arms and entered the battle which was occurring at that time to sever the body of the kings with his axe, and became victorious and subsequently went to perform penance! Go and reach tillait tiruccittirakūdam where periya pirāttiyār is residing on his chest and śrī bhūmip pirātti is firmly remaining on his left side and the woman, who is an embodiment of his fame, is shining radiantly, and which is surrounded by famous, protected, vast, blossomed garden.

*kō manga …* – To have everyone claiming to be kings destroyed and to have the residents of the earth, which is surrounded by ocean, liberated, śrī paraśurāmāḻvān without minimising his anger, while severing the bodies of the kings with his axe, took up arms and was having great valour; oh you who are desiring to own him!

*pū mangai …* – periya pirāttiyār and śrī bhūmip pirāttiyār are eternally residing with him, and his fame which is visualised as a woman, is shining everywhere; tillait tiruccittirakūdam which has fame and protection.

*seruneela vēṟkaṇ madavār tiṟattuc cinattōdu ninṟu manattāl vaḷarkkum aruneela pāvam agalap pugaḻ sēr amararkkum eydāda aṇḍattu iruppīr! perunīr nivā undi muttam koṇarndu engum vittum vayaluḷ kayal pāyndu ugaḷa tiruneelam ninṟu tigaḻginṟa tillait tiruccitra kūdam senṟu sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

seru – tool for war; vēl – sharp like spear; neelam – cool like neydal flower; kaṇ – having beautiful eyes; madavār tiṟattu – towards women who have humility (towards those who stop the enjoyment of such women); sinattōdu – with anger; ninṟu – remained; manattāl – desire in heart; vaḷarkkum – increasing; aru – unable to eliminate; neelam – lowly; pāvam – sin; agala – to go; pugaḻ sēr – having fame; amararkkum – for brahmā et al; eydāda – difficult to reach; aṇḍattu – in paramapadam; iruppīr – oh you who desire to remain!; peru nīr – Having abundant water; nivā – river named veḷḷāṟu; muttam koṇarndu – bringing pearls; undi – pushed; vittum – planting; vayal uḷ engum – in every fertile field; kayal – kayal fish; pāyndu ugaḷa – as they jump; tiruneelam – beautiful neydal flower; ninṟu – spreading everywhere; tigaḻginṟa – shining; tillait tiruccittirakūdam – tillait tiruccittirakūdam; senṟu sērmingaḷ – go and reach

Remaining angry towards those who hinder the enjoyment of humble ladies who have beautiful eyes which are sharp like a spear which are a tool for war and are cool like neydal flower, due to the desire in heart towards such ladies which keeps increasing, the resulting lowly sin is difficult to eliminate; oh you who desire to eliminate such sin and reach paramapadam which is difficult to reach even for brahmā et al who have fame! Go and reach tillait tiruccittirakūdam which is having the river named veḷḷāṟu with abundant water, brings pearls, pushes them and plants them in every fertile field where the kayal fish jump around, and the beautiful neydal flower is spreading everywhere and has the town shining due to that.

*seru …* – Remaining angry towards those who hinder the enjoyment of humble ladies who have beautiful eyes which are sharp like a spear which are a tool for war and are cool like neydal flower, due to the desire in heart towards such ladies which keeps increasing, the resulting lowly sin is difficult to eliminate and is a hurdle to attain bhagavān; oh you who desire to eliminate such sin and reach paramapadam which is difficult to reach even for brahmā et al who have fame!

*peru nīr …* – The nivā river which has abundant water brings pearls and plants them in the fertile fields where the kayal fish jump and roam around and the beautiful neydal flower is present – such tillait tiruccittirakūdam which is shining.

## 3.3 Vada marudidai

## 3.3.1. Vada marudidai

*vāda marudidai pōgi mallaraik konṟu okkalittittu ādal nanmā udaittu āyar āniraikku anṟu idar tīrppān kūdiya māmaḻai kātta kūttan ena varuginṟān sēduyar pūmboḻil tillaic cittira kūdattu uḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

marudidai – in between two maruda trees; vāda – as they were in a withered state; pōgi – crawled and went; mallarai – the group of wrestlers such as cāṇūra, muśtika et al; konṟu – killed; okkalittittu – practising the art of walking; ādal – coming with a dance; nal – beautiful; mā – kēśi who assumed the form of a horse; udaittu – killed; anṟu – when indra caused rainfall; āyar – covherds’; āniraikku – occurred for the cattle; idar – sorrow; tīrppān – to eliminate; kūdiya – gathered; mā maḻai – great hailstorm (by lifting the mountain); kātta – protected; kūttan ena – to have everyone say “he has actions which steal the heart”; varuginṟān – one who is coming; sēdu – tender; uyar – tall; pūm poḻil – having beautiful gardens; tillaic cittirakūdattu – in tillait tiruccittirakūdam; uḷḷān – is eternally residing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa crawled and went through the two maruda trees, as they were in a withered state; he killed the group of wrestlers such as cāṇūra, muśtika et al; he killed kēśi, who assumed the form of a beautiful horse which came dancing, having practised the art of walking; when indra caused rainfall, kriṣṇa protected the herds of cattle of the covherds  to eliminate the sorrow occurred for them by lifting the mountain to stop the great hailstorm which gathered; one who is said to be having such activities which steal the heart of everyone, is eternally residing in tillait tirccittirakūdam which has beautiful gardens which are \[having trees which are\] tender and tall.

*vāda …* – Since these maruda trees were possessed by demons, as he approached them, they started withering. Going through such trees.

*mallaraik konṟu* – Killing cāṇūra, muśtika.

Practising walk,

*ādal …* – Killing Kēśi who was coming in a dancing manner to mesmerise kriṣṇa; to remedy the sorrow of the covherds, he protected them from the storms caused by indra namely puśkalā vartaka etc; he is coming to be praised by everyone saying “He who is having such amazing acts is coming”.

*sēdu* – Youthfulness, well-rounded.

## 3.3.2. Peymagal kongai

*pēymagaḷ kongai nanjuṇḍa piḷḷai parisu iduvenṟāl mānila māmagaḷ mādar kēḷvan ivan enṟum vaṇḍuṇ pūmagaḷ nāyagan enṟum pulangeḻu kōviyar pādi tēmalar tūva varuvān cittira kūdattu uḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pēy magaḷ – pūtanā, who is a demon; kongai – on bosom; nanju – poison; uṇḍa – mercifully consumed; idu – this amazing act; piḷḷai parisu enṟāl – hearing that it is the nature of this child; ivan – this kriṣṇa (is not a young child); mā – 50 crore yōjanā vast; nila mā magaḷ mādar – for śrī bhūmip pirātti who has earth as her body; kēḷvan enṟu – as dear husband; vaṇḍu – beetles; uṇ – entering to drink the honey; pū magaḷ – periya pirāttiyār who is having lotus flower as birth place; nāyagan enṟum – as the lord; pulan keḻu – having form which attracts the heart of those who saw; kōviyar – covherd girls; pādi – praising and singing; tēn malar – fresh flower; tūva – as they serve; varuvān – one who comes; cittirakūdattu – in tillait tiruccittirakūdam; uḷḷān – is eternally residing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The covherd girls who are having form which attracts the heart of those who saw, heard the amazing act of kriṣṇa mercifully consuming poison from the bosom of pūtanā, the demon, understood the nature of this child praised and sang saying “He is not a small child but he is the dear husband of śrī bhūmip pirātti who has earth, which is 50 crore yōjanā vast, as her body and is the lord of periya pirāttiyār who is having lotus flower where the beetles are entering to drink the honey, as birth place”, served him with fresh flowers; one who comes, being served in this manner, is eternally residing in tillait tiruccittirakūdam.

*pēy magaḷ …* – Same as in the simple translation.

pulan keḻu is also recited as,

*polan keḻu kōviyar* – gōpikās who are wearing golden ornaments.

*paṇḍu ivan veṇṇey uṇḍān enṟu āycciyar kūdi iḻippa eṇ tisaiyōrum vaṇanga iṇai marudūdu nadandittu aṇḍarum vānattavarum āyira nāmangaḷōdu tiṇ tiṟal pāda varuvān cittira kūdattu uḷḷānē*

ivan – This young child; veṇṇey uṇḍān enṟu – that he stole the butter and mercifully ate it; āycciyar – covherd girls; kūdi – gathered; iḻippa – blamed; eṇ tisaiyōṟum – those who are in eight directions; vaṇanga – to worship; iṇai marudūdu – in between two maruda trees which stood together; nadandittu – crawled; aṇḍarum – nityasūris; vānattavarum – brahmā et al; āyira nāmangaḷōdu – reciting the thousand names (his); tiṇ – strong; tiṟal – masculinity; paṇḍu – long ago; pāda – to sing; varuvān – one who came; cittirakūdattu – in tillait tiruccittirakūdam; uḷḷān – is eternally residing

**No specific introduction.**

The covherd girls gathered and blamed kriṣṇa saying “He stole the butter and mercifully ate it”; he crawled in between two maruda trees which stood together, to be vorśipped by nityasūris and brahmā et al by reciting the thousand names; such emperumān who came long ago with strong masculinity to be sung by them, is residing in tillait tiruccittirakūdam.

*āvar ivai seydaṟivār? anjana māmalai pōlē mēvu sinattu adal vēḻam vīḻa munindu aḻagāya kāvimalar nedungaṇṇār kai toḻa vīdi varuvān dēvar vaṇangu taṇ tillaic cittira kūdattu uḷḷānē*

ivai – these huge tasks; seydaṟivār Ar – Who did? None. **No specific introduction.**

## 3.4 Oru kuralay

## 3.4.1. Oru kuralay

*oru kuṟaḷāy irunilam mūvadi maṇ vēṇḍi ulaganaittum īradiyāl odukki onṟum tarugavenā māvaliyaic ciṟaiyil vaitta tādāḷan tāḷaṇaivīr! takka kīrtti arumaṟaiyin tiraḷ nāngum vēḷvi aindum angangaḷ avai āṟum isaigaḷ ēḻum teruvil mali viḻā vaḷamum siṟakkum kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagarē sērmin nīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oru – unique; kuṟaḷāy – assuming the form of dwarf, vāmana (went to mahābali); iru nilam – in the vast earth; mūvadi maṇ – three steps of land; vēṇḍi – begged; ulaganaittum – all the worlds; īradiyāl – with two steps; odukki – subdued; onṟum – with another step; taruga enā – asking to give; māvaliyai – mahābali; siṟaiyil vaitta – one who placed him in the prison of pātāḷam (nether world), his; tādāḷan – the supreme lord’s; tāḷ – divine feet; aṇaivīr – Oh you who desire to attain!; takka – matching his; kīrti – having greatness; aru – difficult to know the meanings; maṟaiyin – vēdams’; tiraḷ – collections; nāngum – four; aindu vēḷviyum – the five great yajñas (sacrifices); āṟu angangaḷum – ancillaries such as vyākaraṇam etc; ēḻu isaigaḷum – seven svarams (musical tunes); mali – having in abundance; viḻā – festivals’; vaḷamum – beauty; siṟakkum – to grow further; teruvin – streets’; kāḻi – in the town of kāḻi; sīrāma viṇṇagarē – śrīrāma viṇṇagaram; nīr – you; sērmin – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, assumed the form of a unique vāmana and begged three steps of land on the vast earth; subsequently, he subdued all the worlds with two steps and asked mahābali to give another step of land; oh you who desire to attain the divine feet of supreme lord who placed such mahābali in the prison of pātāḷam (nether world)! You surrender unto the śrīrāma viṇṇagaram in the town of kāḻi, where the collections of four vēdams which have as much greatness as himself and are difficult to attain, the five great sacrifices, six ancillaries such as vyākaraṇa etc, seven tunes, are all present abundantly and is having increasing beauty in the streets of śrī rāma viṇṇāgarm in kāḻi.

*oru kuṟaḷāy* … – Having a unique form, which will make anyone who has seen him to give whatever he asks for.

*iru nilam* – Vast earth.

*mū adi maṇ vēṇḍi* – As if he has no space to place his feet, emperumān, making mahābali to be the owner of this earth, begged for three steps of land from him, subdued everything with two steps and said “You promised to give three steps of land. Will you not give one more step of land?”

*māvaliyaic ciṟaiyil vaitta* – Subsequently, he made indra regain his position and placed mahābali in pātāḷam.

*tādāḷan tāḷ anaivīr* – Oh you who are desiring to attain the divine feet of emperumān who has the greatness of begging for the sake of his devotees!

*takka …* – Surrender unto śrīrāma viṇṇagaram in kāḻi where the collection of four vēdams which have great fame due to being apauruśēya (not authored by anyone), five great yajñas, six ancillaries of vēdams, seven svarams, the beauty due to abundance of festivals are all shining fully.

## 3.4.2. Nanmugan nal

*nānmugan nāḷ migat tarukkai irukku vāymai nalamigu sīr urōmasanāl naviṟṟi nakkanūn mugamār talaiyōttūṇ oḻitta endai oḷimalarc cēvadi aṇaivīr! uḻusē ōdaccūl mugamār vaḷaiyaḷaivāy ugutta muttait tol kurugu sinai ennac cūḻndu iyanga engumtēn mugamār kamala vayal sēl pāy kāḻiccīrāma viṇṇagarē sērmin nīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nānmugan – brahmā’s; nāḷ – life span; miga – as it is lengthy (caused by that); tarukkai – pride; irukku – vēdam; vāymai – one who is reciting; nalam migu sīr – having good conduct; urōmasanāl – by rōmasa bhagavān; naviṟṟu – eliminated; nakkan – the naked rudra’s (stuck on his hand); Un Ar – fleshy; mugan talaiyōttu – brahmā’s skull; ūṇ – (begged and eaten) food; oḻitta – eliminated; endai – lord of all, his; oḷi malar – like a fresh flower; sēvadi – reddish divine feet; aṇaivīr – Oh you who desire to attain!; uḻu – ploughing; sē – oxen; ōda – running (due to strength); sūl mugam Ar – pregnant; vaḷai – conces; aḷaivāy – in the holes; ugutta – gave birth; muttai – pearls; tol kurugu – huge kurugu (heron) birds; sinai enna – considering those to be their eggs; sūḻndu iyanga – flying around there (by that wind); engum – wherever seen; tēn – flood of honey; mugam Ar – flowing from face; kamalam – having lotus flowers; sēl – sēl fish; pāy – jumping; vayal – having fertile fields; kāḻi – in the town of kāḻi; sīrāma viṇṇagarē – śrīrāma viṇṇagaram; nīr – you; sērmin – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān eliminated brahmā’s pride which was caused by his lengthy life span, by rōmasa bhagavān who is reciting vēdams and having good conduct; he eliminated the suffering of the naked rudra where he had to beg and eat from brahmā’s fleshy skull; oh you who desire to attain the fresh flower like divine feet of such emperumān who is the lord of all! You surrender unto śrīrāma viṇṇagaram in the town of kāḻi where ploughing oxen are running to cause pregnant conces to give birth to pearls in the holes; in the fertile fields, the huge herons, considering those pearls to be their own eggs, flew around causing lotus flowers to spit flood of honey through their mouth and where sēl fish are jumping.

*nānmugan …* – rōmasa bhagavān said “How many persons who are known as brahmā appear like bubbles and disappear!” \[to subdue the pride of brahmā\]. Through rōmasa bhagavān who has the greatness acquired by reciting vēdams and having good conduct, the pride of brahmā caused due to having a lengthy life span, where brahmā thought “I am the lord of the fourteen layered worlds! Who has my life span!”, was eliminated.

*nakkan …* – Severing the head of rudra’s father and the teacher of the whole world, having become a sinner due to that, rudra was begging with that same fleshy skull and eating out of it. The lord who eliminated such humiliation for rudra. Both of these personalities are popularly known as lords for the world; emperumān eliminated their pride.

*oḷi malarc cēvadi aṇaivīr* – Oh you who desire to attain his divine feet which are shining due to his natural lordship!

*uḻu sē …* – Ploughing is done with very strong oxen which resemble elephants. As they run amok, the conces which fault those who touched them for delivering the pearls as said in “Its about to give birth now; its giving birth now”, gave birth to pearls in the holes they were residing; the elderly herons which are experienced, not knowing the difference between their eggs and the pearls, considering those pearls to be their own eggs, flew around those as they were unable to leave the place. By the wind caused by their flying, the lotus flowers which are well grown and are present everywhere, were blossoming and spitting well matured honey; the sēl fish which drank such honey are jumping around.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.4.3. Vaiyanainda

*vaiyaṇainda nudikkōttu varāgam onṟāy maṇṇellām idandu eduttu madangaḷ seydu neyyaṇainda tigiriyināl vāṇan tiṇ tōḷ nērndavan tāḷ aṇaigiṟpīr! neydalōdu maiyaṇainda kuvaḷaigaḷ tam kaṇgaḷ enṟum malark kumudam vāy enṟum kadaisimārgaḷ seyyaṇaindu kaḷai kaḷaiyādēṟum kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagarē sērmin nīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vai aṇainda – sharp; nudi – having edge; kōdu – having tusk; onṟu – unique; varāgamāy – assuming the form of a wild boar; maṇ ellām – the whole earth; idandu – gored it \[from the wall of the universe\]; eduttu – lifting it up; madangaḷ – mad acts; seydu – did; vāṇan – bāṇāsuran’s; tiṇ – strong; tōḷ – shoulders; ney aṇainda – sharp; tigiriyināl – by the tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); nērndavan – emperumān who severed, his; tāḷ – divine feet; aṇaigiṟpīr – Oh you who desire to attain!; kadaisi mārgaḷ – ladies of paḷḷar clan; neydalōdu – neydal flower; mai aṇainda – very dark; kuvaḷaigaḷ – kuvaḷai flower; tam kaṇgaḷenṟum – as their eyes; kumuda malar – reddish āmbal flower; tam vāyenṟum – considering to be their mouth; sey – in the fertile fields; aṇaindu – entered (to pick the weeds); kaḷai kaḷaiyādu – without picking the weeds; ēṟum – coming out to the shore; kāḻi – in the town of kāḻi; sīrāma viṇṇagarē – śrīrāma viṇṇagaram; nīr – you; sērmin – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān assumed the form of a unique wild boar, separated the whole earth with his tusk having sharp edge, lifted it up and engaged in mad acts; he severed the strong shoulders of bāṇāsuran with his sharp divine chakra; oh you who desire to attain such emperumān’s divine feet! You surrender unto śrīrāma viṇṇagaram in the town of kāḻi where the ladies of the paḷḷar clan who entered the fertile fields to pick the weeds, considered the neydal flower and kuvaḷai flower as their eyes, reddish āmbal flower as their mouth and came out without picking the weeds.

*vai …* – emperumān assumed the form of a unique wild boar, separated the whole earth with his tusk having sharp edge, lifted it up and came out; due to the pride of being the lord, he performed certain mad acts.

ney – sharpness. Sharp, divine chakra. With the sharp chakra, emperumān severed the strong shoulders of vāṇan who considered that he has acquired some strength by vorśipping other dēvatā (rudra). Oh you, who desire to attain the divine feet of such emperumān!

*neydalōdu …* – Considering the neydal flowers and dark kuvaḷai flowers as their eyes and considering the reddish āmbal flowers to be their mouth, the ladies of the last varṇa stepped into the fertile field to pick the weeds, but came out without doing so, seeing the similarity between those flowers and their eyes and limbs.

## 3.4.4. Panjiya melladi

*panjiya melladip pinnai tiṟattu munnāḷ pāyvidaigaḷ ēḻadarttup ponnan paimbūṇ nenjidandu kurudiyuga ugir vēlāṇḍa ninmalan tāḷ aṇaigiṟpīr! neela mālait tanjudaiya iruḷ taḻaippat taraḷam āngē taṇ madiyin nilāk kāttap pavaḷam tannāl senjudar veyil virikkum aḻagār kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagarē sērmin nīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

panjiya – like fresh cotton; mel adi – having tender, divine feet; pinnai tiṟattu – for nappinnaip pirātti; mun nāḷ – previously; pāy – jumping on whoever seen; ēḻ vidaigaḷ – seven bulls; adarttu – killed; ponnan – hiraṇyan’s; paimbūṇ – (filled with) well decorated ornaments; nenju – chest; idandu – tore; kurudi – blood; uga – to splash out; ugir vēl – the nails which are like spear; āṇḍa – used; ninmalan – the pure emperumān’s; tāḷ – divine feet; aṇaigiṟpīr – Oh you who desire to attain!; neelam – blue gems (placed on the mansions); mālai – the evening time; tanju udaiya – having as refuge; iruḷ – darkness; taḻaippa – to increase; āngu – placed in certain spots; taraḷam – pearls; taṇ – cool; madiyin – moon’s; nilā – rays; kātta – as they show; pavaḷam – corals; tannāl – since they are placed in certain spots; senjudar – sun; veyil – rays; virikkum – as it spreads; aḻagu Ar – having beauty (caused by these); kāḻi – in the town of kāḻi; sīrāma viṇṇagarē – śrīrāma viṇṇagaram; nīr – you; sērmin – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Previously, for the sake of nappinnaip pirātti who is having fresh cotton like tender, divine feet, emperumān killed the seven bulls which were jumping on whoever seen; he tore hiraṇyan’s chest which was well decorated with ornaments with his nails which are like spear, to splash out the blood; oh you who desire to attain such pure emperumān’s divine feet! You surrender unto śrīrāma viṇṇagaram in the town of kāḻi, where more beauty is acquired as the blue gems placed on the mansions would increase darkness which has the evening time as its refuge and as the pearls which are placed in certain spots on the mansions, show the rays of the cool moon and as the corals which are placed in certain spots on the mansions, spread the rays of the sun.

*panjiya …* – Previously, for nappinnaip pirātti who is having fresh cotton like tender, divine feet, emperumān killed the seven bulls which were jumping on whoever seen; he effortlessly tore hiraṇya’s chest which was decorated with ornaments and caused the blood to splash out; while doing so, instead of sending his representatives or his weapons, he killed the enemy of his devotee with the nails in his hands which are like spear and hence acquired purity \[by such act of directly helping his devotee\]; oh you who desire to attain such emperumān’s divine feet!

*neelam …* – The blue gems placed on the mansions would increase darkness which has the evening time as its refuge;  the pearls which are placed in certain spots on the mansions, show the rays of the cool moon; the corals which are placed in certain spots on the mansions will spread the rays of the sun. In this manner, the divine abode became enjoyable due to having darkness, moon-rise and sunshine at the same time.

## 3.4.5. Tevvaya

*tevvāya maṟa mannar kurudi koṇḍu tirukkulattil iṟandōrkkut tirutti seydu vevvāya mākīṇḍu vēḻam atta viṇṇavar kōn tāḷaṇaivīr! vigirda mādar avvāya vāḷ nedungaṇ kuvaḷai kātta aravindam mugam kātta arugē āmbal sevvāyin tiraḷ kāttum vayal sūḻ kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagarē sērmin nīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tevvāya – enemies; maṟam mannar – valorous kings; kurudi koṇḍu – by blood; tiruk kulattil – in his clan; iṟandōrkku – for those who died; tirutti seydu – satisfied (by performing rituals with water); vem – cruel; vāya – having mouth; mā – kēśi who came in the form of a horse; kīṇḍu – tore; vēḻam – elephant named kuvalayāpīdam; atta – killed; viṇṇavar kōn – leader of nityasūris, his; tāḷ – divine feet; aṇaivīr – Oh you who desire to reach!; vigirdam – distinguished; mādar – ladies’; avvāya – such; vāḷ – shining; nedu – wide (stretching up to ears); kaṇ – eyes; kuvaḷai – kuvaḷai flowers \[purple Indian water lily\]; kātta – show; aravindam – lotus flowers; mugam – radiance in face; kātta – show; arugē – near by; āmbal – red lily flowers; sevvāyin – reddish lips’; tiraḷ – collections; kāttum – showing; vayal sūḻ – surrounded by fertile fields; kāḻi – in the town of kāḻi; sīrāma viṇṇagarē – śrīrāma viṇṇagaram; nīr – you; sērmin – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān (as śrī paraśurāma) killed the valorous kings who were enemies and satisfied those who died in his clan by the blood of those enemies; as kriṣṇa, he tore the cruel mouth of kēśi who came in the form of a horse and killed the elephant named kuvalayāpīdam; oh you who desire to reach the divine feet of such emperumān who is the leader of nityasūris! You surrender unto the śrīrāma viṇṇagaram in the town of kāḻi, which is surrounded by fertile fields where the kuvaḷai flowers show the very shining and wide eyes of distinguished ladies, lotus flowers show the radiance in their face and the near by red lily flowers, collection of their reddish lips.

*tevvāya …* – emperumān killed the valorous kings who were enemies and satisfied those who died in his clan by performing water based rituals with the blood of those enemies; śrī paraśurāmāḻvān is implied up to here. He effortlessly tore the cruel mouth of kēśi who caused fear and who was an enemy for his devotees; he then killed kuvalayāpīdam; oh you who desire to reach the divine feet of such emperumān, who is the leader of nityasūris, yet who personally kills the enemies of his devotees!

*vigirda mādar …* – kuvaḷai flowers show the very shining and wide eyes of distinguished ladies, lotus flowers show the radiance in their face and the near by red lily flowers, the collection of their reddish lips.

## 3.4.6. Paingan viral

*paingaṇ viṟal semmugattu vāli māḷap padar vanattuk kavandanodum padaiyār tiṇ kai vengaṇ viṟal virādan uga viṟkunitta viṇṇavar kōn tāḷaṇaivīr! veṟpup pōlum tungamuga māḷigai mēl āyangūṟum tudi idaiyār mugak kamalac cōdi tannāl tingaḷ mugam pani padaikkum aḻagār kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagarē sērmin nīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paingaṇ – greenish eyes; viṟal – strength; semmugam – having reddish face (due to fear); vāli – the monkey named vāli; māḷa – to die; padar – vast; vanattu – present in the forest; kavandanodum – rākśasa named kabanda; tiṇ – firm; padai – weapons; Ar – filled; kai – hands; vem kaṇ – fierce eyes; viṟal – victorious; virādan – rākśasa named virādan; uga – to die; vil kunitta – one who bent his bow; viṇṇavar kōn – cakravartit tirumagan, who is the lord of lords, his; tāḷ – divine feet; aṇaivīr – oh you who desire to reach!; veṟpup pōlum – like mountains; tungam – tall; mugam – having front elevation; māḷigai – mansions’; mēl – standing atop; āyam kūṟum – calling out in a friendly manner; tudi – like udukkai (a percussion instrument which is slim in the middle); idaiyār – women who are having waist; mugak kamalam – lotus like faces’; sōdi tannāl – by the radiance; tingaḷ – (roaming in the sky) moon’s; mugam – face; pani – tears (caused by sorrow); padaikkum – having continuously; aḻagu Ar – filled with beauty; kāḻi – in the town of kāḻi; sīrāma viṇṇagarē – śrīrāma viṇṇagaram; nīr – you; sērmin – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who desire to reach the divine feet of cakravartit tirumagan, who is the lord of lords, who bent his bow to kill (a) the monkey named vāli who had greenish eyes, anger and reddish face, (b) the rākśasa named kabanda who was present in the vast forest and (c) victorious rākśasa named virādan who had fierce eyes and hands filled with weapons! You surrender unto the beautiful śrīrāma viṇṇagaram in the town of kāḻi, where the moon’s face is continuously having tears due to being subdued by the radiance of lotus like faces of the women who are having waist like udukkai (damuru, a percussion instrument) and are calling out in a friendly manner standing atop the mansions having tall front elevation, like mountains.

*paingaṇ …* – To have vāli who had greenish eyes matching his species, strength and reddish face due to the anger, killed; along with kabanda who would grab as many creatures in the vast forest and eat;

*padaiyār tiṇkai …* – emperumān who bent his bow, to have strong virādan with firm weapons filled hands and fierce eyes, killed.

*viṇṇavar kōn tāḷ aṇaivīr* – Oh you who desire to reach the divine feet of cakravartit tirumagan who eliminated the enemies and facilitated the residences for dēvatās.

*veṟpu …* – Standing atop the mansions which have front elevation which are tall like mountains, the women who call out showing friendliness and playing, and who have waist similar to tudi; by the radiance of the faces of such women, moon’s face which is like lotus will acquire sorrow, thinking “What life are we living! While we are compared to their faces, we are no match for those faces!” These women are like moon for the moon; it can also be said that they cause radiance to the moon.

## 3.4.7. Poruvil valamburi

*poruvil valamburi arakkan mudigaḷ pattum puṟṟu maṟindana pōlap puvi mēl sinda seruvil valamburi silaik kai malait tōḷ vēndan tiruvadi sērndu uygiṟpīr! tirai nīrtteḷgi maruvi valamburi kaidaik kaḻiyūdādi vayal naṇṇi maḻai taru nīr tavaḻ kāl manni teruvil valamburi taraḷam īnum kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagarē sērmin nīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

poru il – matchless; valam puri – having strength; arakkan – rāvaṇa’s; mudigaḷ pattum – ten heads; puṟṟu maṟindana pōla – just as a destroyed ant-hill will appear; puvi mēl – on earth; sinda – as they were scattered; seruvil – in battle; valam – victory; puri – having ability to grant; silai – holding śrī gōdaṇḍam (bow); kai – hand; malai – mountain like; tōḷ – having shoulders; vēndan – the prince, perumāḷ’s; tiruvadi – lotus feet; sērndu – reach; uygiṟpīr – oh you who desire to be liberated!; valam puri – conces; tirai – ocean which has tides; nīrttu – left; eḷgi – becoming weak; kaidaik kaḻi – salt-pan which is having tāḻai \[wild plant found on sea shores\]; maruvi – reached; ūdu – in the middle of the salt-pan; ādi – roaming here and there; vayal – (subsequently) in fertile fields; naṇṇi – entered; maḻai taru nīr – rain water; tavaḻ – falling; kāl – through canals; teruvil manni – entered the streets (once the water drained); valam puri – conces; taraḷam – pearls; īnum – giving birth; kāḻi – in the town of kāḻi; sīrāma viṇṇagarē – śrīrāma viṇṇagaram; nīr – you; sērmin – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

As rāvaṇa’s ten heads which don’t have any match for their strength are scattered like destroyed ant-hills on the battlefield, the prince, perumāḷ, is having hand which is holding śrī gōdaṇḍam which has the ability to grant victory and mountain like shoulders; oh you who desire to reach the lotus feet of such emperumān and be liberated! You surrender unto śrīrāma viṇṇagaram in the town of kāḻi where conces left the ocean and having become weak, reached the salt-pan which is having tāḻai \[wild plant found on sea shores\]; they were roaming here and there in the middle of the salt-pan and entered the fertile fields; from there, they entered the streets through the canal which is filled with rain water falling there; those conces then gave birth to conces and pearls.

*poru il* … – The ten heads which are having matchless strength, were scattered on the battlefield just as an ant-hill is destroyed; emperumān got his body which was nurtured by the boons of the dēvatās, break into pieces; unlike rāvaṇa who fought mischievously, emperumān is having the bow which has/gives strength; showing cakravartit tirumagan who has shoulders which are unshakable by enemies; as he removes the enemies, oh you who desire to reach his divine feet and be liberated.

*tirai nīr* … – The conces which were present in the ocean and reached the shores; alternatively – tirai – tides; nīttu – left the ocean, and the conces which are curved to the right, and reached the salt-pan which is having tāḻai; roaming here and there in the salt-pan, as the water in the salt-pan overflows and reaches fertile fields, the conces reach there; rain water also fell there and remained and through the canal, it reached the town and the street in the town; as the water drained, the conces remained there and gave birth to more conces and pearls. Nothing wrong in valamburi conch giving birth to the same.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
