## 3.4.8. Pattaraveragal algul

*pattaravēragal algul pavaḷac cevvāy paṇai nedundōḷ piṇai nedungaṇ pālām in sol mattaviḻum kuḻalikkā vānōr kāvil maram koṇarndān adiyaṇaivīr! aṇilgaḷ tāva nettilaiya karungamugin sengāy vīḻa neeḷ palavin tāḻ sinaiyil nerungu pīnat tetta paḻam sidaindu maduc coriyum kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagarē sērmin nīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pattu – wearing silk cloth; aravu – like a snake’s hood; ēr – beautiful; agal – wide; algul – thigh region; pavaḷam – like coral; sevvāy – reddish lips; paṇai – like bamboo; nedu – long; tōḷ – shoulders; piṇai – like a doe’s eye; nedum kaṇ – wide eyes; pāl Am – like nectar; in sol – having sweet words; mattu aviḻum – honey flowing; kuḻalikkā – for śrī satya bāmāp pirātti who has mass of hair; vānōr – dēvatās’; kāvin – from the garden; maram – pārijāta tree (which is always present in heaven); koṇarndān – kriṣṇa who uprooted and brought, his; adi – divine feet; aṇaivīr – oh ones who desire to reach!; aṇilgaḷ – squirrels; tāva – jumping from branch to branch; nedu – long; ilaiya – having leaves; karum kamugin – dark areca trees’; sengāy – reddish, unripened fruits; vīḻa – as they are falling; nīḷ – due to abundance of water, well grown; palavin – jack fruit trees’; tāḻ – lowered due to the weight of the unripened fruits; sinaiyil – on branches; serungu – dense; pīnam – bulgy; tetta paḻam – ripened fruits; sidaindu – being crushed; madu – honey; soriyum – raining; kāḻi – in the town of kāḻi; sīrāma viṇṇagarē – śrīrāma viṇṇagaram; nīr – you; sērmin – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

śrī satyabāmāp pirātti is wearing silk cloth and is having beautiful, wide thigh region like a snake’s hood, coral like reddish lips, bamboo like long shoulders, wide eyes like a doe’s eye, nectar like sweet words and mass of hair where honey is flowing; oh ones who desire to reach the divine feet of kriṣṇa who uprooted and brought the heavenly pārijāta tree from the garden of dēvatās! As the squirrels jump from branch to branch, the unripened, reddish fruits of the dark areca trees would fall; due to that the bulgy, ripened fruits which are dense on the branches which are lowered due to the weight of the unripened fruits, let the honey flow from them; you surrender unto śrīrāma viṇṇagaram in the town of kāḻ which has such environment.

*pattu …* – Same as simple explanation. With this, it is explained that emperumān will protect his devotees, even performing difficult tasks.

*aṇil …* – As the squirrels jump around independently, the reddish, unripened fruits of dark areca trees having long leaves, fall as if its a fault on those who touched them. On the tall jackfruit trees, fruits, which are densely present on the lowered branches, having ripened well, will fault those who touched them, let the honey flow from them as if they found a place to stagnate.

## 3.4.9. Pirai tangu

*piṟai tangu sadaiyānai valattē vaittup piramanait tan undiyilē tōṟṟuvittuk kaṟai tangu vēl tadangaṇ tiruvai mārbil kalandavan tāḷ aṇaigiṟpīr! kaḻunīr kūdit tuṟai tangu kamalattut tuyinṟu kaidait tōdārum podi sōṟṟuc cuṇṇam naṇṇic ciṟai vaṇḍu kaḷi pādum vayal sūḻ kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagarē sērmin nīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

piṟai tangu sadaiyānai – rudra who is donning moon on his matted hair; valattē vaittu – placed on right side; piramanai – brahmā; than undiyilē – in the lotus flower on his divine navel; tōṟṟuvittu – created; kaṟai tangu – with blood and flesh remains (of enemies); vēl – like a spear; tadam – wide; kaṇ – having divine eyes; tiruvai – periya pirāttiyār; mārbil – placed on his chest; kalandavan – one who eternally lives with her, his; tāḷ – divine feet; aṇaigiṟpīr – oh you who desire to reach!; siṟai vaṇḍu – beetles which have wings; kaḻunīr – in sengaḻunīr flowers (red lily flowers); kūdi – remaining together (to eliminate the fatigue from that); tuṟai tangu – present on the banks; kamalattu – in lotus flowers; tuyinṟu – rested (and further); kaidai ārum tōdu – in the tāḻam \[wild plant\] flower which has big petal; podi – filled in it; sōṟu – buds’; suṇṇam – in powder; naṇṇi – fell and rolled; kaḷi – (due to) the great joy; pādum – singing; vayal sūḻ – surrounded by fertile fields; kāḻi – in the town of kāḻi; sīrāma viṇṇagarē – śrīrāma viṇṇagaram; nīr – you; sērmin – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who desire to reach the divine feet of emperumān who has placed rudra, who is donning moon on his matted hair, on his right side, has created brahmā in the lotus flower on his divine navel, and has placed periya pirāttiyār, who is having wide divine eyes like spear with blood and flesh remains, on his chest and is eternally living with her! You surrender unto śrīrāma viṇṇagaram in the town of kāḻi which is surrounded by fertile fields where beetles having wings remained together in sengaḻunīr flowers and then rested in lotus flowers on the banks and subsequently fell and rolled in the tāḻam flower which has big petal which is filled with the powder of buds and are singing in great joy.

*piṟai …* – emperumān placed rudra who is a sādaka (one who pursues emperumān with his own effort, indicated by his matted hair) and who is enjoying (indicated by having moon on his hair), on the right side of his divine form; he created brahmā from the lotus on his divine navel; he is eternally living with periya pirāttiyār who is having divine eyes which look similar to a spear which was not washed off the stains, and is present on his divine chest; oh you who desire to reach such emperumān’s divine feet! Oh you who desire to reach the one who has the noble quality of giving space to the prideful brahmā, rudra et al and exclusively subservient pirātti without any difference!

*kaḻu nīr …* – Entered into sengaḻunīr flower and enjoyed together, and to eliminate the fatigue from such experience, the beetles entered the lotus flower on the banks, drank the honey and rested there; subsequently, entered the tāḻai flower which has huge petals, and rolled in there in such a manner to have the buds and fragrance become applied all over their bodies, sang in the joy of drinking honey and the fragrance.

## 3.4.10. Sengamalattu

*sengamalattu ayan anaiya maṟaiyōr kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagar en sengaṇ mālai angamalat tadavayal sūḻ āli nādan aruḷmāri arattamukki adaiyār sīyam kongu malark kuḻaliyar vēḷ mangai vēndan koṟṟavēl parakālan kaliyan sonna sanga mugat tamiḻ mālai pattum vallār tadangadal sūḻ ulagukkut talaivar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sengamalam – born from the beautiful lotus on the divine navel; ayan anaiya – matching brahmā; maṟaiyōr – where brāhmaṇas are living; kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagar – eternally residing in kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagar; en – my; sengaṇ mālai – on puṇḍarīkākśan (lotus eyed emperumān); am – beautiful; kamalam – filled with lotus flowers; tadam – ponds; vayal – fertile fields; sūḻ – surrounded by; Ali nādan – being the leader of tiruvāli region; aruḷ māri – being the one who rains mercy on the favourable ones, like a dark cloud; arattu amukki – being the one who suppresses the enemies (to not let them rise); adaiyār – for enemies; sīyam – being like a lion; kongu – filled with honey; malar – flowers; kuḻaliyar – for ladies who are having in their hair; vēḷ – being the one like cupid; mangai – for tirumangai region; vēndan – being the king; parakālan – being like yama for enemies; koṟṟam – able to grant victory; vēl – holding on to the spear; kaliyan – āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; sangam – poets; mugam – to meet and enjoy; tamiḻ mālai pattum – ten pāsurams which are like garlands; vallār – those who can learn with meanings; tadam – vast; kadal sūḻ – surrounded by ocean; ulagukku – in the world; talaivar – will remain the leader who is surrenderedto, by all

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

puṇḍarīkākśan emperumān is eternally residing in kāḻic cīrāma viṇṇagar where brāhmaṇas, who match brahmā who was born from the beautiful lotus on the divine navel, are living; tirumangai āḻvār who is (a) the leader of tiruvāli region which is surrounded by fertile fields and ponds which are filled with beautiful lotus flowers, (b) the one who rains mercy on the favourable ones, like a dark cloud, (c) the one who suppresses the enemies, (d) like a lion for enemies, (e) the one like cupid for ladies who are having flowers filled with honey in their hair, (f) the king of tirumangai region, (g) like yama for enemies and (h) holding on to the spear which is able to grant victory, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams which are like garlands for poets to meet and enjoy; those who can learn these with meanings will remain the leader who is surrendered to, by all in the world which is surrounded by vast ocean.

*sengamalam …* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇṭam 4.1 “*vālmīkir bhagavān ruśi:*” (the most knovledegable sage vālmīki). A beloved tiruviḷakkup piccan (servitor who holds the oil-lamp) of periya perumāḷ was constantly speaking ill of others in front of emperumān; at that time he assumed that periya perumāḷ had āḻvārs in heart and said “Identify some defects in my devotees (if you can)”; at that time, the servitor recited this pāsuram and said “nāyantē! āḻvār started singing the glories of your highness but ended up glorifying himself”; periya perumāḷ revealed his divine heart saying “That is also in praise of me”. The object of these pāsurams is puṇḍarīkākśan who is eternally residing in the abode where brāhmaṇas who are equivalent to caturmukha (four-headed brahmā) have gathered; āḻvār is the leader of tiruvāli region which is surrounded by fertile fields having ponds which are decorated by beautiful lotus flowers; one who grants everything to the favourable ones; one who suppresses the head of the enemies to not let them rise; he is like a lion which cannot be approached by enemies; he is desired by all; he is the leader of the tirumangai region; he is holding the spear for the protection of devotees just as sarvēśvaran, holding a weapon; he is death personified for enemies; those who are experts in these ten pāsurams which are praised by the gatherings of tamiḻ poets/experts.

*tadam kadal sūḻ ulagukkut talaivar tāmē* – Just as sarvēśvaran is surrendered to by all, these devotees will be the refuge for all.

## 3.5 Vandu

## 3.5.1. Vandu

*vandunadu adiyēn manam pugundāy pugundadaṟ pin vaṇangum en sindanaikku iniyāy! tiruvē! en āruyirē! andaḷir aṇiyār asōgin iḷandaḷirgaḷ kalandu avai engum sendaḻal puraiyum tiruvāli ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

am – beautiful; taḷir – acquired from sprouts; aṇi Ar – having abundant beauty; asōgin – aśōka tree’s; iḷam taḷirgaḷ avai – tender sprouts; engum kalandu – spreading everywhere; sem – reddish; taḻal puraiyum – like fire; tiruvāli ammānē – Oh you who are having tiruvāli as your abode!; tiruvē – Oh my wealth!; en Ar uyirē – Oh my sustainer!; vandu – coming to my place; unadu adiyēn – I, your servant’s; manam – in the heart; pugundāy – entered; pugundadaṟpin – after you entered; vaṇangum – surrender; en sindanaikku – for my mind; iniyāy – became sweet

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are having tiruvāli as your abode where the tender sprouts of aśōka trees which are having abundant beauty acquired from the beautiful sprouts, are spreading like reddish fire! Oh my wealth! Oh my sustainer! Coming to my place, you entered this servant’s heart; after you entered, you became sweet for my mind which is surrendering unto you.

*vandu* – Having tiruvāli, which is greatly enjoyable, as your abode, while I should have come and surrendered to you and while I did not show any interest towards you, you have come to my place on your own. When materials have to be exchanged between two islands, either they have to be transported to be exchanged mid-way or one party needs to bring all the materials to the other island; in this case, emperumān himself travelled all the way and came up to āḻvār’s place.

*unadu adiyēn* – This is the evidence he brought along with him, to claim entry into my heart; as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.10 “*adiyān ivan enṟu enakkāraruḷ seyyum*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is having in his tiruvuḷḷam (divine heart) “he ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) is my natural servitor”, while showering his complete mercy) – saying “Will you be responsible for your benefit? See, it is me!” and entered to assume all the burdens of āḻvār. He entered my mind, which is the entry into me and which is where I will say “I won’t accept you”, when he tries to enter there.

When asked “What did he do after emperumān entered?” āḻvār says,

*vaṇangum* – Even if it is enemies’ home, if one enters, they will be given a seat; similarly, āḻvār vorśipped emperumān as said in mahābhāratam sabhā parvam 75 “*yadārham kēśavē vruttimavaśā: pratibēdirē*” (with great enchantment towards kēśava, they performed obeisances etc).

*en sindanaikku iniyāy* – He is so sweet to my mind that he who entered my heart in this manner, will not be allowed to leave even if he says “I will leave”.

*tiruvē* – As said in periya tirumoḻi 7.7.1 “*tiruvukkum tiruvāgiya selvā*” (one who is the wealth for pirātti who is embodiment of wealth), he is āḻvār’s wealth.

*en Ar uyirē* – Instead of wealth being one thing and sustenance being another, you who are my sustainer! emperumān remains in such a manner that those who separate from him cannot sustain themselves!

*am taḷir …* – Being my sustainer and great enjoyment, you entered my heart as if you have no place, though having tiruvāli as your abode! The tender sprouts of the aśōka tree which is having abundant beauty due to the beautiful sprouts, spread everywhere and resembled fire. As the reddish, tender sprouts are grown well to be spread everywhere, they look attractive as if every place is set on fire. In this manner, you, who belonged to the abode which causes ignorance \[to make us think tender sprouts to be fire\] and remained the sarvēśvaran, have entered my heart!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.2. Neelat tada varai

*neelat tada varai māmaṇi nigaḻak kidandadu pōl aravaṇai vēlait talaik kidandāy! adiyēn manattu irundāy! sōlait talaik kaṇa māmayil nadamāda maḻai mugil pōnṟu eḻundu engum ālaip pugai kamaḻum aṇiyāli ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ālaip pugai – smoke from burning sugarcane juice; engum – everywhere; maḻai mugil – cloud in monsoon; pōnṟu – like; eḻundu – because of the rising; kamaḻum – fragrant; sōlait talai – in the garden; mā mayil gaṇam – huge prides of peacock; nadamāda – they dance; aṇi – beautiful; Ali ammānē – Oh lord of tiruvāli!; neelam – bluish; tada varai – huge mountain; mā maṇi – priceless gem; tigaḻa – to shine on it; kidandadu pōl – like reclining; vēlait talai – in tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi); aravaṇai – on tiruvanandāḻvān (with the kaustuba jewel shining); kidandāy – Oh one who is reclining!; adiyēn manattu – (now) in my heart, where I am your servitor; irundāy – entered and remained, without leaving!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli where the huge prides of peacocks dance in the fragrant garden because of the rising smoke from burning the sugarcane juice and appearing as clouds during monsoon! Oh one who is reclining on tiruvanandāḻvān in tiruppāṟkadal like a huge, bluish mountain with a priceless gem shining on it! You entered my heart and remained, without leaving!

*neelam …* – Just as a blue mountain reclined with a priceless gem on it, emperumān is reclining on tiruvandāḻvān in tiruppāṟkadal, with the śrī kaustuba jewel on his beautiful divine form.

*adiyēn manattirundāy* – He reclined on tiruppāṟkadal only to enter āḻvār’s heart as he was waiting for āḻvār to not reject him; as āḻvār stopped rejecting emperumān, he entered āḻvār’s heart and felt accomplished.

*sōlai …* – Huge prides of peacocks dance in the fragrant garden because of the rising smoke from burning the sugarcane juice which appears as clouds during monsoon. Seeing the cloud like smoke from the burning of sugarcane, the prides of peacocks in the garden would dance. Having such abode which caused bewilderment, you entered my heart and remained there!

## 3.5.3. Nennal poy

*nennal pōy varum enṟenṟu eṇṇi irāmai en manattē pugundadu immaikku enṟu irundēn eṟi nīr vaḷanjeṟuvil senneṟ kūḻai varamporeei arivār mugatteḻu vāḷai pōy karumbu annaṟkādu aṇaiyum aṇiyāli ammānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

eṟi – rising waves; nīr vaḷam – having abundance of water; seṟuvil – in fertile fields; sennel kūḻai – strong paddy crops; varambu oreei – placing the top portion of those crops on the boundaries of the fertile fields; arivār – those who harvest; mugattu – in the face; eḻu – jumping to reach; vāḷai – vāḷai fish \[scabbard fish\]; pōy – left those fields; annal – having dense bushes; karumbuk kādu – sugarcane forest; adaiyum – reaching; aṇiyāli ammānē – oh lord of the beautiful tiruvāli!; nennal pōy – went yesterday; varum – coming tomorrow; enṟu enṟu eṇṇi – thinking in this manner; irāmai – to not remain; en manattē – in adiyēn’s heart; pugundadu – your entry and presence; immaikku enṟu irundēn – I thought it is to cause joy for me in this world

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

vāḷai fish which were jumping to reach the faces of those who were  placing the top portion of the strong paddy crops on the boundaries of the fertile fields which are having abundance of water with rising waves, left those fields and are reaching the sugarcane forest having dense bushes; oh lord of such beautiful tiruvāli! Instead of having to remain thinking that you went yesterday and will be coming tomorrow, I thought that your entry and presence in adiyēn’s heart is to cause joy for me in this world.

*nennal …* – Having to constantly think “He went yesterday, will return today”; not having to spend the time thinking “yesterday was gone; today is here; tomorrow will also come” in the context of time.

*en …* – emperumān came and entered my heart so that I don’t have to spend my time thinking like this, and I thought this act was to add joy for me in this life. immai means “this world”; inmai means inimai, joy.

*eṟi nīr …* – seṟu – sey – fertile fields; there are those beautiful fields, where water is having rising waves; in those fields, there are sen nel kūḻai – sen nel talai – the top portion of reddish paddy; placing them on the boundaries of the field and cutting them; as said in paingūḻ, kūḻai implies kūḻ, which means reddish paddy crop; those who cut such a crop.

*varamboreei* – Being unable to cut them directly due to their strong nature like diamond, taking the top portion of the crop, placing them on the boundaries of the field and cutting the edge; when they gathered the crops and held, the vāḷai fish will try to jump on their face and move from the dangerous fields to the nearby sugarcane forest which is free of danger and has dense bushes; they will go and be safe in such a beautiful sugarcane forest.

## 3.5.4. Minnin mannu

*minnin mannu nudangidai madavār tam sindai maṟandu vandu nin mannu sēvadikkē maṟavāmai vaittāyāl punnai mannu serundi vaṇ poḻil vāy agan paṇaigaḷ kalandu engum annam mannum vayal aṇiyāli ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

punnai – punnai trees; serundi – surapunnai trees; mannu – filled with; vaṇ – beautiful; poḻil vāy agan – inside the garden; paṇaigaḷ – in the ponds; annam – swans; engum kalandu – remaining together with each other, everywhere; mannum – residing eternally; vayal – having fertile fields; aṇi Ali ammānē – Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli!; minnil mannu – matching lightning; nudangu – subtle; idai – having waist; madavār tam – towards women; sindai maṟandu – eliminating the attachment; vandu – coming towards you; mannu – always remaining in the same manner; nin – your; sēvadikkē – beautiful, divine feet only; maṟavāmai – to not let me forget; vaittāy – you have mercifully done; Al – How amazing is this!

**Перевод:**

**emperumān asks “Why are you suffering in your heart like this?” āḻvār says “After making me forget women and not forget your divine feet, what more do you have to do?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli which is having fertile fields where swans are remaining together with each other, everywhere and residing eternally in the ponds inside the beautiful garden which is filled with punnai and surapunnai trees! Eliminating my attachment towards women who have subtle waist matching lightning, you mercifully made me come towards you and not forget your beautiful, divine feet only, which are always remaining in the same manner. How amazing is this!

*min …* – Towards women who have subtle waist matching lightning.

*sindai maṟandu* – He can only think about them as enjoyable but to attain them is a huge task. To eliminate the attachment towards inapt aspects like these and develop attachment towards apt matter (bhagavān), in itself is emperumān’s favour. You mercifully made me give up my desire on such aspects and reach you to attain the goal of never forgetting your divine feet which remain the same always; you did this unconditionally, without my asking for it, just as someone will place water shelter \[in hot weather, without anyone asking for it\].

*punnai …* – Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli which is having fertile fields where swans are lovingly remaining together with each other, everywhere and residing eternally in the ponds inside the beautiful garden which is filled with punnai and surapunnai trees!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.5. Nidu palmalar

*nīdu palmalar mālai ittu nin iṇaiyadi toḻudu ēttum en manam vāda nī ninaiyēl maram eyda māmunivā! pādalin oli sangin ōsai parandu palpaṇaiyāl malindu engum ādal ōsai aṟā aṇiyāli ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pādal – singing bhagavān’s stories; in – sweet; oli – sound; sangin ōsai – sound of conch; parandu – pervading everywhere; pal paṇaiyāl – by the sounds of many different musical instruments; malindu – abundance; engum – wherever seen; ādal ōsai – sound of the dance; aṟā – continuously occurring; aṇi Ali ammānē – Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli!; maram – seven marāmaram (ebony trees); eyda – shot to fall at once; māmunivā – Oh one who meditates!; nin – your; iṇai adi – divine feet which match each other; pal – many different; malar – flowers; mālai – mixed flower garland; nīdu – long time; ittu – offered; toḻudu – vorśipped; ēttum – praising; en – my; manam – mind; vāda – to suffer (like a leaf in your separation); nī – you who have motherly forbearance towards your devotees; ninaiyēl – you should not think

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli where the sweet sound of singing bhagavān’s stories and sound of conch are pervading everywhere, the abundant sounds of many different musical instruments and the sound of the dance which is seen everywhere, are continuously occurring! Oh one who meditates, who shot seven ebony trees to fall at once! You who have motherly forbearance towards your devotees, should not think that my mind, which offered many different flowers and mixed flower garland at your divine feet which match each other, for a long time, vorśipped and praised, should suffer like a leaf.

*nīdu …* – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*oḻivil kālam ellām*” (At all times) and [tiruvāimoḻi 4.7.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-7-8-kandu-kondu/) “*eṇḍhisaiyum uḷḷa pūk koṇḍu*” (With flowers from eight directions), my mind offered garlands with many different types of flowers, at your divine feet which match each other, and praised; you should not think about such mind to suffer like a leaf.

*maram eyda māmunivā* – Is he not the one who instills faith in his devotees?

*māmunivā* – Your thought is unlike our thought which may fail or succeed.

*pādalin …* – Sound of the songs, the other sounds such as the sound of conch etc pervade everywhere, and further abundance of many different musical instruments, and the sound of the dancers who are seen everywhere are occurring continuously; paṇai – percussion instruments like murasu, palliyam.

## 3.5.6. Ganda mamalar

*ganda māmalar ettum ittu nin kāmar sēvadi kai toḻudu eḻum pundiyēn manattē pugundāyaip pōgal ottēn sandhi vēḷvi sadangu nānmaṟai ōdi ōduvittu ādiyāy varum andaṇāḷar aṟā aṇiyāli ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

sandhi – sandyāvandanam etc; vēḷvi – yāgam etc (which are naimittika karmas) \[periodic rituals\]; sadangu – other kāmya karmas (activities done with expectation of worldly benefits); nāl maṟai – four vēdams; ādiyāy – starting from creation; ōdi – learning from previous teachers; ōduvittu varum – those who are teaching; andaṇāḷar – brāhmaṇas; aṟā – continuously residing; aṇi Ali ammānē – Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli!; gandam – abundantly fragrant; mā – best; ettu malarum – eight types of flowers; nin – your; kāmar – beautiful; sēvadi – on reddish divine feet; ittu – offered; kai toḻudu – worship with hands; eḻum – to praise; pundiyēn manattu – with my heart which is having strong faith; pugundāyai – you who entered (coming as if it is for your benefit); pōgalottēn – I will not let you leave, now onvards

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli where brāhamaṇas, who perform sandyāvandanam etc, yāgam etc and kāmya karmas, who learnt four vēdams from previous teachers coming from the time of creation and teaching to others, are continuously residing! Now onvards, I, who have the strong faith in my heart where you have entered, will offer eight types of abundantly fragrant, best flowers at your reddish, beautiful divine feet, worship with my hands and praise you, and will not let you leave.

*gandam …* – Offering eight distinguished, abundantly fragrant flowers; they are – karumugai, kaṟpagam, nāḻal, mandāram, saugandi, sengaḻunīr, tāmarai and kaidai. Inner meaning – offering oneself towards emperumān who is revealed through the most enjoyable tirumantram; since he is known as “*sarvaganda:*” (the abode of all fragrance), \[āḻvār is saying\] vorśipping your desirable, reddish, divine feet with my hands, in my heart which is desiring to be liberated.

*pugndāyaip pōgalottēn* – You having entered my heart without my praying for it, will not let you leave. Will anyone abandon the relationship which occurred without any thought from self?

*sandhi …* – nitya karmam (daily rituals), naimittika karmam (periodic rituals), sadangu – kāmya karmam (rituals which are done for worldly benefits), four vēdams – which ordain the manner in which these karmams are to be performed; learning these from those who are already knowledgeable in these, such ancient brāhmaṇas are continuously residing in tiruvāli; in such tiruvāli, oh sarvēśvara who remains as their refuge! While they are present, you have entered my heart voluntarily; in such a case, I will never let you leave.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.7. Ulavu tirai

*ulavu tiraik kadal paḷḷi koṇḍu vandu un adiyēn manam pugunda ap pulava! puṇṇiyanē! pugundāyaip pōgal ottēn nilavu malarp punnai nāḻal nīḻal taṇ tāmarai malarin misai mali alavan kaṇ padukkum aṇiyāli ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nilavu – always blossoming; malar – having abundance of flowers; punnai – punnai tree; nāḻal – palini tree (their); nīḻal – in the shade; taṇ – cool; tāmarai malarin misai – on the lotus flower; mali alavan – huge male crabs; kaṇ padukkum – resting; aṇi Ali ammānē – Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli!; tirai ulavu – having rising waves; kadal – in tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi); paḷḷi koṇḍu – mercifully reclined; un adiyēn – (subsequently) I, your servitor, my; manam – in heart; vandu pugunda – you who entered as if it is your benefit; ap pulava – Oh that omniscient lord!; puṇṇiyanē – Oh my good deed!; pugundāyai – You who entered unconditionally; pōgalottēn – will not let go

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli where huge male crabs are resting on the cool lotus flower which are present under the shade of punnai tree and palini trees which are always having abundance of blossoming flowers! Mercifully reclined in tiruppāṟkadal which is having rising waves, you entered my heart, your servitor, as if it is your benefit. Oh such omniscient lord! Oh my good deed! I will not let you, who entered unconditionally, go.

*ulavu …* – Mercifully reclining in tiruppāṟkadal where the waves are moving around; you mercifully reclined there, to find an opportunity to enter my heart. Once you got such an opportunity when I didn’t reject you, and I became qualified to have you, you entered my heart.

*ap pulava* – Are you not specially knowledgeable! Won’t you know when to enter?

*puṇṇiyanē* – For me, who has no means to attain you, you remain the good deed!

*pugundāyaip pōgal ottēn* – After you arrived and entered voluntarily, I will not let you go any more.

*nilavu …* – On the lotus flower under the shade of punnai and nāḻal trees which are having ever-blossoming flowers.

*mali alavan kaṇ padukkum* – Huge male crab which can fill the whole area, without realising anything else (such as being together with its spouse), due to availability of the beautiful mattress, would sleep there. Due to being present in the divine abode, the activities of the animals are not different from those of vayalāli maṇavāḷan, for āḻvār.

## 3.5.8. Sangu tangu

*sangu tangu tadangadal kadal mallaiyuḷ kidandāy! aruḷ purindu ingu ennuḷ pugundāy! inip pōyināl aṟaiyō! kongu seṇbagam malligai malar pulgi inniḷa vaṇḍu pōy iḷam tengin tādaḷaiyum tiruvāli ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

in iḷa vaṇḍu – sweet, young beetles; kongu – very fragrant; seṇbaga malar – śeṇbaga flower; malligai malar – jasmine flower; pulgi – (entered to drink honey) embraced (as they were very hot); iḷam tengin – in tender coconut; pōy – went and entered; tādu aḷaiyum – stirring its buds; tiruvāli ammānē – Oh lord of tiruvāli!; sangu – conces; tangu – remaining forever; tadam – vast; kadaluḷ – in tiruppāṟkadal; kadal mallaiyuḷ – in divyadēśam named tirukkadalmallai; kidandāy – Oh you who are mercifully reclining!; ingu – here; ennuḷ – in the heart of me, the servitor; aruḷ purindu pugundāy – mercifully showered your grace and entered; inip pōyināl – now, if you left me and separated; aṟaiyō – victory

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh lord of tiruvāli where sweet, young beetles embrace very fragrant śeṇbaga flower and jasmine flower and then go and enter the tender coconut and stir the buds in it! Oh you who are mercifully reclining in the vast tiruppāṟkadal where conces remain forever and in divyadēśam named tirukkadalmallai! Here, you mercifully showered your grace and entered the heart of me, the servitor; now, if you left me and separated, that is victory \[implies impossible to leave āḻvār\].

*sangu …* – You are mercifully reclining in the vast tiruppāṟkadal where conces are remaining forever; from there, you came and mercifully reclined in tirukkadalmallai for the sake of your devotees; while such divine abodes are your residences, you have mercifully showed your grace upon me and entered my heart.

*inip pōyināl aṟaiyō* – Since your mercy does not change, if you left now, “*aṟaiyō aṟai*” (victory! victory!). Only if the cause \[bhagavān\] is changing, resulting aspect will change. Leaving me who cannot sustain without you, you cannot remain in those who are agreeable to your presence and absence.

*kongu …* – The beetles who entered fragrant śeṇbaga and jasmine flowers, embraced them and as they were very hot, to reduce such heat, just as those who were affected by the hot summer, will keep their hand in sandalwood paste, the beetles will enter the tender coconut and stir its buds. Oh lord of such tiruvāli!

## 3.5.9. Odi ayira namamum

*ōdi āyira nāmamum paṇindētti nin adaindēṟku oru poruḷ vēdiyā! araiyā! uraiyāy oru māṟṟam endāy! nīdi āgiya vēda māmuniyāḷar tōṟṟam uraittu maṟṟavarkku ādiyāy irundāy! aṇiyāli ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīdi āgiya – that which ordains the conduct of people; vēdam – vēdam; māmuniyāḷar – maharishis who can visualise the mantrams in such vēdam, their; tōṟṟam – birth etc; uraittu – spoke; maṟṟavarkku – for all others; ādiyāy irundāy – Oh you who remain the cause!; aṇi Ali ammānē – Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli!; vēdiyā – Oh you who are known through vēdam only!; araiyā – Oh you who eliminate the mischief and rule over me!; endāy – Oh my lord!; āyira nāmamum ōdi – reciting your thousand names; paṇindu ētti – falling at your divine feet and praise; nin adaindēṟku – for me who holds you as refuge; oru poruḷ – means for the distinguished goal; oru māṟṟam – a response; uraiyāy – please give

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who remain the cause for all others and who recite vēdam which ordains the conduct of people and the birth etc of maharishis who can visualise the mantrams in such vēdam! Oh lord of beautiful tiruvāli! Oh you who eliminate the mischief and rule over me! Oh my lord! For me who is reciting your thousand names, falling at your divine feet and praise and hold you as refuge, please give a response for my means for the distinguished goal.

*ōdi …* – For me who reached you reciting your divine names with my mouth, falling at your divine feet and praising you.

*oru poruḷ* – You should explain me the principle saying “This is the means through which you can attain me”.

*vēdiyā* – Oh you, who are known by vēdam only!

*araiyā* … – Oh you who eliminate my mischief and rule over me! Oh my lord! You should mercifully speak a word. You should mercifully say a word like in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mā śuca:*” (Don’t worry) to liberate me.

*nīdi …* – vēdam which ordains the conduct of people.

*māmuniyāḷar tōṟṟam* – The birth of the sages who can visualise the mantrams in such vēdam; reciting these, oh you who are the cause for all! This implies, emperumān creates the objects based on the words in vēdam, as existed previously. That is, as the word “*bhū:*” occurs, he creates earth. In this manner, creating each object, reciting the apt words.

## 3.5.10. Pulli vandaraiyum

*pulli vaṇḍaṟaiyum poḻil pudai sūḻ tennāli irunda māyanai kallin mannu tiṇ tōḷ kaliyan oli seyda nalla innisai mālai nālum ōr aindum onṟum navinṟu tām udan vallarāy uraippārkku idam āgum vānulagē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu – beetles; pulli – embracing each other; aṟaiyum – humming; poḻil – garden; pudai sūḻ – surrounding everywhere; then – beautiful; Ali – in divyadēśam named tiruvāli; irunda – mercifully residing; māyanai – on sarvēśvaran who is amazing; kallin – like a mountain; tiṇ – strong; mannu – eternally present; tōḷ – having shoulder; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; oli seyda – mercifully spoke; nalla – beautiful; in isai – having sweet tune; mālai nālum ōr aindum onṟum – ten pāsurams; navinṟu – recite; tām udan vallarāy uraippārkku – for those who constantly meditate their meanings; vān ulagē – paramapadam only; idam āgum – will become the abode

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār who is having shoulder, which is eternal and strong like a mountain,  mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams which are having sweet tune, on the amazing sarvēśvaran who is mercifully residing in the beautiful divyadēśam named tiruvāli which is surrounded everywhere by garden where beetles are embracing each other and humming; those who recite these pāsurams, constantly meditating on their meanings, will have paramapadam only as their abode.

*pulli …* – The amazing emperumān is mercifully residing in tiruvāli which is having garden where the beetles, embracing each other, having drunk honey, will be humming, in its surrounding; āḻvār who is having mountain like strong shoulder which is eternal, mercifully spoke this garland of pāsurams with tune on such emperumān; due to the great attachment in this decad, āḻvār is mercifully identifying individually as in four pāsurams plus five pāsurams plus one pāsuram.

## 3.6 Tuviriya

## 3.6.1. Tuviriya

*tūviriya malar uḻakkit tuṇaiyōdum piriyādē pūviriya madu nugarum poṟivariya siṟu vaṇḍē! tīviriya maṟai vaḷarkkum pugaḻāḷar tiruvāli ēvari venjlaiyānukku en nilaimai uraiyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tū – wings; viriya – to spread; malar – well blossomed flowers; uḻakki – stomped; tuṇaiyōdum – with your spouse; piriyādē – without separating; pū – flowers; viriya – as they blossom; madu – the honey in those flowers; nugarum – drinking; poṟi – dots; variya – having stripes; siṟu vaṇḍē – Oh little beetle!; tī viriya – to have the fire rise; maṟai – vaidika boundaries; vaḷarkkum pugaḻ āḷar – those who are having fame due to conducting without any shortcomings, their; tiruvāli – eternally residing in tiruvāli; ēvari venjilaiyānukku – for sarvēśvaran who is holding arrow and beautiful bow in his hands; en nilaimai – my situation; uraiyāy – you should inform

**Перевод:**

**Here, in this pāsuram, parakāla nāyaki is sending a beetle as messenger. She is saying “While your life is fulfilled, you have seen that my life is not so! Should you not inform emperumān, who has arrived to eliminate my shortcomings?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh little beetle who stomped on well blossomed flowers to have your wings spread, who without separating from your spouse, are drinking honey in the flowers as they blossom, are having dots and stripes! You should inform my situation to sarvēśvaran who is holding arrow and beautiful bow in his hands and is eternally residing in tiruvāli which is home to those who are having fame due to conducting \[rituals\], without any shortcomings for the vaidika boundaries, to have the (sacrificial) fire always rise.

*tūviriya malar uḻakki* – tū viriya – to have the wings spread, stomping the flower; alternatively – tū viriya – tūydāga virinda – that is stomping the well blossomed flower. Due to separation, she was avoiding to see the flower, and standing in a humble manner. The beetles, due to the joy of union, expanded their wings; śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.25 “*naiśā paśyati rākśasyō nēmān puśpa pala drumān \| ēkastahrudayā nūnam rāmamēvānupaśyati \|\|*” (sītā is not seeing the rākśasis; she is not seeing the trees filled with flowers and fruits; with single-focused mind, she is only seeing śrī rāma) – for sītāp pirātti, there is no difference between seeing rākśasis and seeing trees filled with flowers and fruits. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 28.17 “*nagōttamam puśpitam āsasāda*” (she approached the best trees) – just as someone approaches blazing fire, the well grown tree was filled with flowers. *āsasāda* – Her detachment towards life is visible.

*malar uḻakki* – The flower which seems to be fire for parakāla nāyaki, is being treated by the beetle as mud. The flower, honey, buds and the fragrance mixed and was stomped. They \[beetles\] need not be carefully stepping on flowers. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.1.6 “*punnai mēl uṟai pūnguyilgāḷ*” (Oh young cuckoos who are residing on punnai flower!), the flowers which are the abodes for birds, feel like fire-place for her.

She enquired “Why does it feel like stepping on fire?” \[She realised that\] They have the mantram which will let them remain on fire without getting burnt; the mantram is,

*tuṇaiyōdum* – When there is a couple, they can sustain on flower! Unlike me who is sending messenger, you are living along with your spouse!

*tuṇaiyōdum* – She is thinking about her own state \[where she is separated from emperumān\]. tuṇai (companion) means one person protects and other is protected. It is said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.3.4 “*tuṇai pirindār tuyaramum ninaigilai*” (You did not think about my suffering, where I have separated from my companion (you)). siṟiyāttān would say “tuṇai does not mean pair/couple; it only indicates a single person (who cares), i.e. the hero). Just as it was meant to say “*unnaip pirindār*“, here also tuṇai means the male beetle.

*piriyādē* – We are fortunate to have the messengers remaining a couple and not having to face the same suffering.

*tūviriya malar uḻakkit tuṇaiyōdum piriyādē* – What a strange desire to see the messengers also have same disease \[of suffering in separation\]! śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 1.40 “*mayūrasya vanē nūnam rakśasā na hrutā priyā*” (Certainly, no one has abducted the peacock’s spouse). perumāḷ is saying “Has that evil person not come to this place where these peacocks are present?” perumāḷ thinks that rāvaṇa will separate whoever is remaining as pairs.

*pū viriya madu nugarum* – Just as prideful princes will abandon used mattress and climb a new mattress, the beetle is moving away from well blossomed flower to a newly blossomed flower and drinking honey; their entry and the flower blossoming happen at the same time. Just as southerly breeze, sun rays and time, the arrival of these beetles will also cause the flower to blossom. Just as two persons who have already spoken and made arrangements such that when one touches the door, the other will open, by the wind blowing from their wings, the flower is blossoming.

*pū viriya* – Their arrival is becoming the reason for the flower’s blossoming instead of shrinking.

*madu nugarum* – śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.41 “*namāmsam rāghavō bhungtē nacāpi madu sēvatē*” (he is neither indulging in meat nor in alcohol) – your body is opposite to mine where I am weakened due to fasting! She is now blaming the beetle. They are drinking the honey, to have strength for their union with each other.

*nugarum* – They are not stopping the consumption of honey; they can stop drinking if it is for themselves; but here, they are drinking for each other; just as on particular occasions \[like the day of marriage\], the couple will eat from same plate \[they are drinking together\]; only when the honey goes below the throat will it satiate \[one sucks the honey and gives to the other\]; now, they are not drinking this honey to sustain themselves; are they not having it as a side-dish for their mutual enjoyment! Only when you make me also enjoy in this manner along with you, will your enjoyment be fulfilled. Is it not fair to feed those who have not eaten in the night? What kind of attitude is this to enjoy without sharing the joy with others!

*poṟi variya* – Oh beetle who is having dots and stripes! The shine acquired by the union is visible in your body. The bodily features of the gatakas (those who unite) are as much goal as the noble qualities of their selves. One should not see inferiority based on one’s birth, in the case of those who unite us with emperumān.

*siṟu vaṇḍē* – To help parakāla nāyaki, the beetle’s body is already small. One need not assume a very small form at the time of execution \[like hanumān who had to make himself small while going to lankā\]. hanuman reduced his body size as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 2.47 “*pruśadamśaka mātrassan*” (With the body size that is equal to that of a cat). These beetles need not be mentioned as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam1.207 “*cacāra nānāvida vēśadārī*” (He roamed around assuming different forms).

*poṟi variya …* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 27.47 “*prāśamsata mahākapim*” (She praised hanuman). hanuman’s greatness is similar to that of emperumān as said in tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.10 “*ētta ētta engeydum*” (As we continue to praise, we cannot see the end); riśi is saying that to speak about the greatness of hanuman is to try and take out water from ocean to make it dry. \[ślōkam 27.47 is explained here\] *tatassā* – After hearing the story of śrī rāma from tiruvadi (hanuman), she regained her existence. *hrīmati* – As said in “*sati darmiṇi darmāś cintyantē*” (Only after the entity is established, its qualities can be analysed), after regaining her existence, the natural qualties of women started showing in her. *bālā* – She was unable to bear overwhelming joy. *bhartus sandēśa harśitā* – She became joyful hearing the words of śrī rāma, her protector. *parituśtā* – the way the joy overflowed. *viśālākśī prācamsata* – She started praising. *mahākapim* – Like a person trying to dry out an ocean with his hand, she tried to praise him.

Assuming that – hearing these, the beetle became shy and said “Why are you praising us who are waiting to execute your orders? Will the one who united with you and left you and is not showing mercy even after seeing your state, listen to our words? This is why we are hesitating”, parakāla nāyaki is speaking further.

*tī viriya .*.. – Don’t you think like that. The residents of his town are very righteous. If you inform my situation, they will send him immediately; they will send him thinking “Are we vorśipping someone who is very cruel towards woman?” So, informing my situation is only required. This is the abode where those who would look at the sufferers and say “Alas!” and who are engaged in apt activities, are gathered; they will definitely send him; once they send him, he has no other refuge than me.

*tī viriya …* – In tiruvāli which belongs to the brāhmaṇas who are famous for conducting the fire without crossing the vaidika boundaries and where the fire expands like blossomed lotus.

She says “This is the abode where people of noble qualities are gathered; you blame him showing your body and saying ‘he is tormentor of woman’ “; the beetles responded “Even if we went and informed, and even if he starts his journey, what can he do if he has hurdles on his way to you?” She says “No need to fear as long as he has his bow in his hand”. If he starts towards us, he won’t have any hurdles.

*ēvari vem silaiyānukku* – Is he not holding the bow in his hand to ensure that no one cries out in sorrow? \[Message is\] For śrī rāma who is having the bow which will engage anyone who holds it in a battle, which is beautiful due to having stripes and strong, and which will torment the stomach of the enemies in the way it is held.

The beetles ask her “You have explained our nature, where we are the ones going as messengers; you have explained the nature of the one to whom we are carrying the message; but what is your message which needs to be given to him?”

*en nilaimai* – How can I explain what cannot be explained in words! You have seen my form; now you have to use the apt words to explain my situation. She believes that more than herself, those who have seen her can explain her situation with words. She is considering this beetle to be as good as hanuman, who is aindra vyākaraṇa paṇḍitan (very great scholar).

*uraiyāyē* – It is said that when a gandarva arrested duryōdana and was carrying him away, duryōdana called out for darmaputra and subsequently, darmaputra, out of compassion, rescued him; \[she is saying\] unlike that, is emperumān of such nature that he will not help the one who desired for him and is suffering in separation from him?

*uraiyāyē* – You need not bring him; you just need to inform him – that is all I need; coming here is his responsibility; if he does not come, it will be a shortcoming, being a protector. After you inform him, he will follow your words and come.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.2. Pini avilum

*piṇi aviḻum naṟu neela malar kiḻiyap pedaiyōdum aṇimalar mēl madu nugarum aṟu kāla siṟu vaṇḍē! maṇikaḻunīr marungalarum vayalāli maṇavāḷan paṇi aṟiyēn nī senṟu en payalai nōy uraiyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

piṇi aviḻum – blossoming; naṟu neela malar – fresh neela flowers \[blue Indian water-lily\]; kiḻiya – to tear; pedaiyōdum – with female counterpart; aṇi malar mēl – from dense flowers; madu nugarum – drinking honey; aṟu kāla – having six feet; siṟu vaṇḍē – little beetle!; maṇi – Beautiful; kaḻunīr – sengaḻunīr \[purple/red Indian water-lily\]; marungu – in all four sides; alarum – blossoming; vayal – surrounded by fertile fields; Ali – mercifully residing in tiruvāli; maṇavāḷan – lord’s; paṇi – acts; aṟiyēn – I don’t know; nī senṟu – you go; en payalai nōy – paleness spreading in my whole body; uraiyāy – You should inform, without ignoring

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh little beetle who is having six feet and is drinking honey along with your female counterpart, to tear the blossoming, fresh neela flowers! I don’t know the acts of the lord who is mercifully residing in tiruvāli which is surrounded by fertile fields having beautiful sengaḻunīr flowers on all four sides; without ignoring me, you go and inform him about paleness spreading in my whole body.

*piṇi aviḻum naṟu neela malar kiḻiya* – The flower blossoms partly due to the entry of the beetle and partly due to the change in time. The beetle knows the difference between well blossomed flowers and fresh flowers. With this – it is said that when he starts speaking, the beetle can understand his heart and solve the issue.

*piṇi aviḻum* … – The beetles are drinking the honey to tear the blossoming, fresh, neela flower; this implies – wherever they are sent, they will finish the task based on the situation.

*malar kiḻiya* – The beetle is not enjoying the togetherness carefully; due to its pride, without seeing that it is its own mattress, it is destroying it \[flower\]. They have not entered the flower to perform japa \[prayer\]! The beetles, which enjoy togetherness without any other duty, will not know anything else. Just as a person who has eaten unmattangāy (intoxicant material), will have his heart blinded and not know anything else.

When asked “What is the intoxicant here?” parakāla nāyaki says

*pedaiyōdum* – Don’t they need a separate mattress? They can unite on sky; each one’s body is the other’s mattress as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.14 “*tavāngē samupāviśam*” (then rest on your lap).

*aṇi malar mēl madu nugarum* – Will drink from dense flowers. When one is drinking from one flower, if it desires to drink from the next one, it need not fly. Since the whole pond is filled with flowers densely, when a beetle needs to go from one flower to another, it can just walk over. You like the dense nature of the flowers and are having this act of drinking honey as the only activity!

*aṟu kāla* – Unlike those with two feet, those with six feet can quickly go and accomplish the task.  They (āḻvārs) think that the feet of those who unite them with emperumān are their life as said in stōtra ratnam 2 “*atra paratra cāpi nityam yadīya caraṇau śaraṇam madīyam”* (in this world and in the other world as well, always the divine feet of that śrīman nātamunigaḷ are my refuge). She is saying “My livelihood is present in abundance”. One need not worry thinking about “*caraṇau*” (two feet).

*siṟu vaṇḍē* – While the skill is great, like embār’s divine form, the beetle is also little in size.

*maṇi kaḻu nīr marungu alarum* – In all of the surroundings, pearls and sengaḻunīr flowers only are to be seen. Alternatively, maṇi means beautiful. Beautiful sengaḻunīr flower blossoming.

*maṇi kaḻu nīr* … – Also explained as – one who has arrived and is residing in tiruvāli which is surrounded by fertile fields which have on their sides, beautiful sengaḻunīr flowers blossoming. Another explanation – the water which is throwing up pearls and sengaḻunīr flowers in the surroundings.

*vayalāli maṇavāḷan paṇi aṟiyēn* – \[paṇi – act\] Is he focussed on arriving here, to embrace me only? ōr is he engaged in plucking flowers and giving them to those who are like jāmbavati \[one of the wives of kriṣṇa, and the daughter of jāmbavān, the bear\]? I don’t know. Alternatively, is he being uncaring towards me like how duśyanta was towards śakuntalā? I don’t know that as well. \[paṇi – speak\] Without any wetness in his tongue and teeth, is he asking “What did she do?” “What happened to her?” paṇi can be considered as speech and action, in this manner.

Though we are unable to know his nature, we cannot live without him.

*nī senṟu* – To start with, we cannot be like him. He can live without us, but we cannot live without him.

*nī senṟu* – Even if it is wrong, you first go to him. It is proper for us to wait for him to come.

When asked “What should we say, when we go there?” parakāla nāyaki says,

*en payalai nōy uraiyāyē* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 35.35 “*tadāsīt niśprabha: atyartam rāhugrasta iva amśumān*” (sugrīva lost his shine, hearing the words of iḷaiya perumāḷ like the sun caught by rāhu), as iḷaiya perumāḷ informs the sorrow of perumāḷ to mahārājar, and as the words reached sugrīva mahārājar’s ears, the body started becoming pale), similarly you explain my situation to him in such a manner that his body acquires the same paleness as my body.

*payalai nōy urai* – Her paleness is beyond words. These beetles are so capable to speak about what is beyond words.

*en payalai nōy uraiyāyē* – Inform him about how my body is fully spread with paleness. She is saying that the beetle should inform in such a manner that wherever its word reaches, that place should become pale.

*en payalai nōy uraiyāyē* – What is the use of svatantrar’s \[bhagavān’s\] nature? You go and inform all this to him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.3. Nir vanam

*nīr vānam maṇ eri kālāy ninṟa nedumāl tan tārāya naṟunduḷavam perundagaiyēṟku aruḷānē! sīrārum vaḷar poḻil sūḻ tiruvāli vayal vāḻum kūrvāya siṟu kurugē! kuṟippaṟindu kūṟāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇ nīr eri kāl vānam āy – Being the five great elements – earth, water, fire, air and ether; ninṟa – remained as their antaryāmi (in-dwelling super-soul); nedu māl – sarvēśvaran; than – his; tārāya – garland; naṟum tuḷavam – fresh tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); peṟum tagaiyēṟku – for adiyēn (servitor) who has the nature of surviving if I get; aruḷānē – not giving; sīrārum – great; vaḷar poḻil – by growing gardens; sūḻ – surrounded everywhere; tiruvāli – in the town named tiruvāli; vayal – in fertile field; vāḻum – living; kūr vāya siṟu kurugē – Oh little bird with sharp beak \[typically crane or heron bird\]!; kuṟippu aṟindu – Coming back with knowledge about his thoughts; kūṟāy – you should tell that to make us sustain ourselves

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who remains as the antaryāmi of the five great elements – earth, water, fire, air and ether, is not giving his fresh tiruttuḻāy garland for adiyēn (servitor) who has the nature of surviving if I get; oh little bird with sharp beak living in the fertile field in the town named tiruvāli which is surrounded everywhere by great, growing gardens! Coming back with knowledge about his thoughts, you should tell that to make us sustain ourselves.

*nīr vānam maṇ eri kālāy ninṟa nedumāl* – emperumān who joined the five great elements starting with earth to yield the result, entered them to make them valid entities with names and stood in them; subsequently he remained in such a manner that when they are mentioned, that will lead up to him. Such greatly mad lord. One who remains well mixed with them, due to being unable to abandon his wealth.

*nīr vānam …* – He desires for the universe which does not desire him. Creating the five great elements starting with earth, to create the ability in them to transform into the result, just as a potter will mix water, dust and mud, beat them, heat them and create pot etc, joining the whole collection of cētanas, he created the effects such as dēva (celestial beings), manuśya (humans) et al; he remained as their antarātmā to help in the existence of the created entities, and remained in such a way that when someone talks about any of those entities, it will point to him – such state is mentioned. In this world, pot, cloth etc will not stop short of pointing up to paramātmā who is present inside them. taittirīya upaniśat ānanda valli “*tat sruśtvā tadēvānuprāviśat \| tadanupraviśya sacca tyaccā bhavat \|\|*” – After creating the world, paramātmā pervaded everywhere; subsequently cētanas and acētana were identified as that paramātmā – one who remains in this manner.

*nedu māl* – One who shows great attachment towards the universe which does not have any attachment towards him.

*than tārāya naṟunduḷavam perundagaiyēṟku aruḷānē* – Is it my fault to send a messenger to the one who cannot abandon even those who don’t desire him? For me who will exist if he accepts me and will cease to exist, if he rejects me. For me, who will sustain myself if I got the garland decorating his shoulder, and will die if I don’t get it.

*than tārāya naṟunduḷavam perundagaiyēṟku* – How beautifully she explains her true nature!

*aruḷānē* – Even if you don’t eliminate the suffering of your lady love (me), should you at least not show mercy like how it is shown towards commoners!

*than tārāya* – Will he not show his mercy towards me who will remain if I get fresh tuḷasi, which is distinguished and is in the form of garland, and will die if I did not get that? The nature of ātmā is to be attractive similar to tuḷasi and kaustuba jewel, when ātmā’s body is eliminated.

*aruḷānē* – Will one who does not abandon his general protection, abandon his special protection? Will one who protects the universe which has no desire towards him, abandon me who cannot sustain if I don’t get him? Even if we are not target of his love, are we not even a target of his mercy?

*sīr ārum …* – ṣouldn’t the comfortably living person uplift the suffering person?

*sīr ārum vaḷar poḻil sūḻ* – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.9.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-9-4-ur-valam/) “*Ur vaḷangiḷar sōlai*” (tall garden which reveals the wealth of the town), the garden itself will reveal the wealth of the town.

*vaḷar poḻil* – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.10.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-1-kilaroli-ilamai/) “*vaḷar iḷam poḻil*” (gardens which are growing yet youthful), as they grow, they remain young instead of being old. Oh little heron which is living in tiruvāli, surrounded by well grown gardens which reveal the abundance of wealth! Living there itself is great; just as living in kōyil (śrīrangam).

*kūr vāya siṟu kurugē* – Oh little heron with sharp beak! Alternatively – oh little heron which can speak firm words! \[Similar to hanuman\] who interacted between the princes \[śrī rāma and lakśamaṇa\] and sugrīva mahārājar in such a way that the same mahārājar who ran away four or five yōjanā \[1 yōjana – about eight miles\] after seeing them, came to them and told as in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 5-17 “*ēkam du:kham sukham ca nau*” (our mirth and misery are one).

*kuṟippaṟindu kūṟāyē* – You find out his thoughts and let me know; alternatively – instead of revealing what I spoke in suffering, to him, inform him the message which will make him sustain. If you inform too much, we will not get him. What is the intent in saying “Find out the reason for his detachment \[from us\]” ? When you inform our state, if he says “I need parakāla nāyaki”, we will survive, ignoring our suffering and if he says “I don’t need her”, we will die and survive.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.4. Tanaga ninaiyanel

*tānāga ninaiyānēl tan ninaindu naivēṟku ōr mīnāya kodi neduvēḷ vali seyya melivēnō? tēnvāya vari vaṇḍē! tiruvāli nagarāḷum ānāyaṟku ennuṟu nōy aṟiyac cenṟu uraiyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tān āga – on his own; ninaiyānēl – even if he does not think about me; than ninaindu – thinking about him; naivēṟku – I who am suffering; ōr mīnāya kodi nedu vēḷ – manmantan (cupid) who has a unique fish flag; vali seyya – to torment; melivēnō – will I become weak?; tēn vāya – having sweet speech; vari vaṇḍē – Oh beetle having stripes!; tiruvāli nagar āḷum – residing in the divyadēśam named tiruvāli; An āyaṟku – for sarvēśvaran who incarnated as kriṣṇa; en uṟu nōy – the disease which is present in my body; senṟu – you go; aṟiya uraiyāy – you should tell him to be known by him

**Перевод:**

**Highlights from avatārikai (Introduction)**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

No specific introduction.

Even if he does not think about me, will I, who am suffering thinking about him, become weak to be tormented by manmantan (cupid) who has a unique fish flag? Oh beetle having sweet speech and stripes! sarvēśvaran who incarnated as kriṣṇa is residing in the divyadēśam named tiruvāli. You should go and tell him the disease which is present in my body, to be known by him.

**Highlights from vyākhyānam (Commentary)**

*tānāga ninaiyānēl* – Like the one saying in periya tirumoḻi 11.8.7 “*vēmbu …*” (Like a worm in neem tree). If emperumān does not think about his own possession. If he is not acting properly. If not thinking about devotees is his sustenance (sarcasm); if he is not thinking about me to sustain himself (sarcasm).

*than ninaindu naivēnō* – Can we also not be like him? We did not have a heart to not think about him. One can sustain only if the target entity is such that it can be acquired or not; since emperumān is distinguished from all of the entities, immediately after meditated upon, one will start suffering.

*ōr mīnāya kodi neduvēḷ vali seyya melivēnō? –* Will I, who desire for emperumān and suffer in not attaining him, be tormented by manmatan who has fish flag? \[Will it match emperumān’s stature to let this happen?\] If he cannot avoid our suffering, as said in periya tirumoḻi 10.8.3 “*karuḷak kodi onṟudaiyīr*” (Oh one who has garuda flag!), if he himself torments us, what should he do? Think about nanjīyar’s words \[shown in pravēśam/Introduction of this decad\], that even if emperumān did not help in advance, at least he should help after the fact.

*tēn vāya vari vaṇḍē* – Oh beetle with sweet speech! hanuman helped sītāp pirātti when she was trying to tie her divine hair to kill herself and helped perumāḷ (śrī rāma) when he was saying as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.9 “*avagāhyārṇavam svapsyē*” (I am going to sleep under the sea); in this manner hanuman, was a messenger who helped both pirātti and perumāḷ with his speech. You can speak sweetly to make him come here even if he is not willing to come.

*tiruvāli nagar āḷum An āyaṟku* – If he gets to rule the wealth of tiruvāyppādi along with the wealth of tiruvāli, then will he have the time to feel sorry for those who are suffering?

*en uṟu nōy aṟiyac cenṟu uraiyāyē* – He has not come since he does not know about my situation; you go and inform him.

Alternatively,

*aṟiyac cenṟu urai* – By your weakened walk, he should realise my situation and he should lose wetness in his tongue and teeth and his body should become pale. You should go and tell him in such a manner.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.5. Valaya kan

*vāḷāya kaṇ panippa menmulaigaḷ pon arumba nāḷ nāḷum nin ninaindu naivēṟku ō! maṇ aḷanda tāḷāḷā! taṇ kudandai nagarāḷā! varai edutta tōḷāḷā! en tanakku ōr tuṇaiyāḷan āgāyē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇ aḷanda – measured the world; O tāḷāḷā – Oh one who has divine feet!; O! taṇ kudandai nagar āḷā – Oh one who is mercifully reclining in invigorating tirukkudandai!; varai edutta – lifted up gōvardana mountain as umbrella; O! tōḷāḷā – Oh one who has divine shoulders!; vāḷ āya kaṇ panippa – to have overflowing tears in sword like eyes; mel mulaigaḷ – on tender bosoms; pon arumba – as paleness shows; nāḷ nāḷum – everyday; nin ninaindu – thinking about you, the protector; naivēṟku en tanakku – for me, this servitor, who is in sorrow; ōr tuṇaiyāḷan āgāy – you should be distinguished helper

**Перевод:**

**The roles have reversed. parakāla nāyaki said to the messengers that while he should have suffered in separation from her, here she is suffering due to the unfulfilled desire of attaining him. Now, she is thinking that the messengers have gone and informed him the matter, he has arrived in front of her; she is visualising his presence and is speaking to him – this is the subject of subsequent pāsurams. This is similar to what happened in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.37 “kśamasē tam mahīpatē” (Oh lord of the universe! You are being patient towards rāvaṇa). sītāp pirātti was speaking to the messenger hanuman, and suddenly she visualised śrī rāma’s presence there and hence spoke to her as if he is present in person.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who has divine feet which measured the world! Oh one who is mercifully reclining in invigorating tirukkudandai! Oh one who has divine shoulders which lifted up gōvardana mountain as umbrella! For me, this servitor, who is in sorrow, to have overflowing tears in sword like eyes and to have the paleness showing on my tender bosoms, and who is thinking about you, the protector, everyday, you should be the distinguished helper.

*vāḷāya kaṇpanippa* – The roles have reversed. The tears which are to be seen in his eyes are now seen in her eyes. While I have the weapon \[my eyes\] which can defeat others, I am suffering like this. Just as a person who has weapon, still gets killed. She is saying “While he was set to leave, I should have said “Don’t go” and imprisoned him with my eyes and enjoyed him; instead I hung my head in shyness and lost him due to that”. Had I glanced at him then, now he will be sending messenger to me.

*vāḷāya kaṇ panippa* – What a suffering for these eyes which can easily attack and capture a person with a glance! She is saying “Being a tiger, I have lost my nail”. She is speaking about self similar to how her divine mother will praise her; everyone can speak about the truth \[nothing wrong in praising self in this case\]. She would have heard from him saying “What a beautiful pair of eyes!” The nature of self which exists for his sake is also part of the goal.

*men mulaigaḷ pon arumba* – Though firmness is the nature of her bosom, here it is said to be soft, since it cannot tolerate separation from him. Acquiring paleness on the bosoms which cannot tolerate his separation.

*vāḷāya kaṇ panippa* – For her, it is sufficient to keep seeing herself. It is applicable for both her and him since it is said as in “*sarvadēhibhi:*” (Whoever has a body should keep looking at devotees). The ślōkam from viṣṇu tatvam is explained in detail:

- *āhlāda śīta nētrāmbu:* – Having cool tears in the eyes due to the joy acquired by enjoying bhagavān’s qualities.
- *puḷakīkruta gātravān* – The tears are flowing like three layered necklace and five layered necklace.
- *paraguṇāviśta:* – Inside too is decorated with bhagavān’s qualities.
- *draśtavya: sarvadēhibhi:* – If such a person is present, whoever is having a body, the purpose of such body is to keep looking at such a person who is very devoted towards bhagvān.
- *sadā draśtavya:* – One need not pack food for the lengthy travel to paramapadam and travel all that distance to do *sadā darśanam* (constantly seeing).

A man with such a woman, need not leave her in search of wealth \[to please her\]. Her tears and paleness appear to be telling him, “You just keep these pearls and gold”. nammāḻvār too said in tiruviruttam 11 “*oṇmuttum paimbonnum ēndi*” (Having the shining pearls and fresh gold), along the same lines.

*nāḷ nāḷum …* – For your delay in arrival, am I thinking about you one day and thinking about something else on the next day?

*nāḷ nāḷum* – Am I joyful one day and sorrowful the next day?

*nin ninaindu naivēṟku* – You don’t know about me. But don’t you know about yourself? Should you not think “If a person separates from me, she cannot sustain”. Have you not seen yourself in a mirror?

*nin ninaindu naivēṟku* – I am asking this to you as said in yajur vēdam kātakam 1.8.8 “*dēhi mē*” (Give me this) out of sorrow in separation.

*maṇ aḷanda tāḷāḷā* – The divine feet which were placed on those who had no desire, are not difficult to attain for these bosoms which are pale!

*O! maṇ aḷanda tāḷāḷā* – Who requested you long ago to have your divine feet placed on everyone? On whose eyes did you see the tears and on whose body did you see the paleness to bring your divine feet and place on their head? Can you not place your divine feet on these bosoms which are pale due to separation from you?

*taṇ kudandai nagarāḷā* – Can I not reap the benefit of your presence in tirukkudandai which is for the sake of those who are subsequent to your trivikrama avatāram?

*taṇ kudandai nagarāḷā* – You mercifully reclined in the invigorating tirukkudandai thinking “Is there anyone who would need me to measure the worlds?”

*varai edutta tōḷāḷā* – Unlike in the previous cases, instead of considering commonly as “subsequent to incarnation”, did you not specifically protect the young covherd girls and boys?

*varai edutta tōḷāḷā* – When the cows and covherd boys were to be destroyed, he lifted up the mountain and protected them. His divine body is scarred with the service he rendered to his devotees. [mudal tiruvantādi 23](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/07/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-23/) “*taḻumbirunda sārnga nāṇ tōyndavām am kai taḻumbirunda tāḷ sagadam sādi taḻumbirunda*  
*pūngōdaiyāḷ veruvap pon peyarōn mārvidanda* *vīngōda vaṇṇar viral*” (The beautiful arms which have the rough marks due to rubbing with the string of the bow, śārnga; in the divine feet, scar due to kicking the demon who had entered the wheel, was present; piratti with beautifully platted divine hair, was fearful as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who has the complexion of ocean with agitating waves, is having scars on his fingers due to tearing hiraṇya kaśipus’s chest). emperumān attempted to hide his scar thinking “Who are those who can bind me? How can I be bound by some? How can these be known to the world?”. parakāla nāyaki says “If it is just one scar, you can hide; in your whole body, you have scars from helping devotees”.

- *taḻumbirunda sārnga nāṇ tōyndavām am kai* – His beautiful, divine hands will have the scar from the cord of the bow; his divine hands are having the scar from holding śrī śārngam.
- *taḻumbirunda tāḷ sagadam sādi –* His divine foot is having the scar from killing cakatāsura.

Now, what did the finger of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has the complexion of ocean with agitating waves do?

- *pūngōdaiyāḷ veruvap pon peyarōn mārvidanda* – The divine finger of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has the complexion of ocean with agitating waves, is having scar due to tearing hiraṇya’s chest for the sake of pirātti; even she feared “How is this going to end?” – in such a manner he split and acquired scar from that. You who protected devotees by minimising yourself.

*enṟanakku ōr tuṇaiyāḷan āgāyē* – Leaving aside the gōvardana mountain, can you not carry half of my burden?

*tuṇaiyāḷan āgāyē* – Implies, you should become my companion.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.6. Taraya

*tārāya taṇ tuḷava vaṇḍuḻuda varai mārban pōrānaik kombositta putpāgan en ammān tērārum nedu vīdit tiruvāli nagarāḷum kārāyan ennudaiya kanavaḷaiyum kavarvānō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu – beetles; tārāya – garland; taṇ tuḷavam – in tiruttuḻāy (with the honey, buds and fragrance); uḻuda – to become slushy; varai mārban – having a vast, divine chest; pōr ānai – kuvalayāpidam which was set to fight; kombu ositta – being the one who broke the tusk; puḷ pāgan – having periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) as his vehicle; en ammān – being my lord; tēr ārum – having shelter for chariot; nedu – huge; vīdi – having divine street; tiruvāli nagar āḷum – eternally residing in tiruvāli town; kār āyan – sarvēśvaran who is having an invigorating, divine form; ennudaiya – me who is thinking about him only, my; kana vaḷaiyum – golden bangles on my hand; kavarvānō – will he steal?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is having a vast, divine chest where the beetles cause slush in tiruttuḻāy garland; he broke the tusk of kuvalayāpidam which was set to fight; he is having periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) as his vehicle; he is my lord; he is eternally residing in tiruvāli town which is having huge, divine street which is having shelter for chariot; I am thinking about him only; will he steal the golden bangles on my hand?

*tārāya taṇ tuḷava vaṇḍuḻuda varai mārban* – His divine chest will be slushy due to the overflowing honey in his distinguished tuḷasi garland. In the tuḷasi garland which is decorating his divine chest, honey, buds and fragrance overflow and the divine chest becomes fully slushy being stomped by the beetles. Now, the divine chest is well prepared to bring her bosoms which have acquired golden complexion to plant there; now, she just needs to plant her bosoms there \[embrace him\]. Looks like the divine chest only accepts those \[beetles\] who have no desire towards him; the divine chest remains embraceable all the time.

*pōr ānaik kombu ositta* – One who effortlessly broke the tusk of the battle-ready kuvalayyāpīdam.

Are there any hurdles on his way?

*puḷ pāgan* – He has periya tiruvadi as his vehicle. Having the nature of eliminating the enemies, the \[garuda\] flag can be seen from afar while he comes, which will make those who see, become free from their sorrows.

*en ammān* – He made her exist exclusively for him, by showing his presence on cōḷēndra simhan (the name of namperumāḷ’s elephant).

*tēr ārum nedu vīdi* – The divine street is very vast to have himself and his companions/vehicles to move along simultaneously. He will come along with his thousand friends as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.1.1 “*tannērāyiram piḷḷaigaḷōdu taḷar nadai ittu varuvān*” (He will arrive walking beautifully, along with his thousand matching friends).

*kār āyan* – emperumān who showed his invigorating form and stole the bangles of the girls of five lakh families \[in gōkulam\], remained dissatisfied due to not taking my bangles. Should he steal the bangles of those who are born after his times as well? For him, even after stealing all the bangles of the girls of the whole town, his body is not showing the satisfaction if parakāla nāyaki’s bangles remains with her.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.7. Kondaravat tirai

*koṇḍaravat tirai ulavu kurai kadal mēl kulavarai pōl paṇḍaravin aṇaik kidandu pār aḷanda paṇbāḷā! vaṇḍamarum vaḷar poḻil sūḻ vayalāli maindā! en kaṇ tuyil nī koṇḍāykku en kanavaḷaiyum kadavēnō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇḍu – Before danger was inflicted by mahābali et al on earth; aravam tirai ulavu – having tumultuous noise and tides; kurai kadal mēl – on the vast tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi); aravin aṇai – on tiruvandāḻvān (ādiśēśan); kula varai pōl – reclining like a huge anchoring mountain reclining; koṇḍu – having that abode nicely in his divine heart (and subsequently when there was danger inflicted by mahābali); pār aḷanda – measured the world; paṇbāḷā – Oh one who has simplicity!; vaṇḍu amarum vaḷar poḻil – surrounded by garden with tall trees where beetles are present; vayal – having fertile fields; Ali – in tiruvāli; maindā – oh youthful one!; en kaṇ tuyil – my sleep; nī koṇḍāykku – for you who fully stole; en kana vaḷaiyum – golden bangles on my hand; kadavēnō – will I lose?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Before danger was inflicted by mahābali et al on earth, emperumān reclined on ādiśēśan like a huge anchoring mountain reclining on the vast tiruppāṟkadal having tumultuous noise and tides; oh one who has simplicity in having that abode nicely in his divine heart and measured the world! Oh youthful one in tiruvāli which is having fertile fields surrounded by garden with tall trees where beetles are present! Will I lose the golden bangles on my hand for you who fully stole my sleep?

koṇḍu – Considering in his divine heart that this is the abode from where he can hear the sorrowful cry of his devotees. Having tumultuous noise, making loud sound, the tides are moving around in tiruppāṟkadal where he is mercifully resting like an anchoring mountain reclining there, on ādiśēśan. kurai – vastness. Like an anchoring mountain reclining on the ocean to fill the vast space there.

*paṇḍu* – He rested on that mattress before the earth was tormented by mahābali et al.

*pār aḷanda paṇbāḷā* – Leaving his mattress, he measured the whole world. Thus, oh one who has the simplicity to rescue the earth which was stolen by mahābali and gave it to indra!

*vaṇḍu amarum …* – He is standing in tiruvāli for those who are \[born\] subsequent to his such simplicity. Oh one who is standing in tiruvāli which is having fertile fields surrounded by garden with tall trees where beetles are present like buds and are drinking the honey! Just as he incarnated as śrī vāmana from tiruppāṟkadal and secured the earth, he captured āḻvār by showing his youthfulness having arrived and standing in tiruvāli.

*en kaṇ tuyil nī koṇḍāykku* – As āḻvār came to know that the target entity (bhagavān) is present in an easily approachable manner, āḻvār’s sleep left his eyes.

*en kana vaḷaiyum kadavēnō* – You can take away what is present on my body \[i.e. sleep\]. But what right do you have on my golden bangles? He also gave gold \[golden complexion – paleness\] and took away my golden bangles. For him too, while accepting what is present on his body, she need not consent for the same. Will you take everything that I claim as mine, whether it is natural or incidental for me? As he started liking her belongings, she is also claiming ownership of those.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
