## 3.6.8. Kuyilalum

*kuyilālum vaḷar poḻil sūḻ taṇ kudandaik kudamādee! tuyilāda kaṇ iṇaiyēn nin ninaindu tuyarvēnō! muyalālum iḷa madikkē vaḷai iḻandēṟku idu naduvē vayalāli maṇavāḷā! koḷvāyō maṇiniṟamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuyil Alum – cuckoos singing; vaḷar poḻil sūḻ – surrounded by tall gardens; taṇ kudandai – residing in cool tirukkudandai; kudamādi – oh one who performed kudak kūttu (dance with pots)!; tuyilāda – sleepless; kaṇ iṇaiyē – I who am having eyes; nin ninaindu – thinking only about you; tuyarvēnō – will I feel sorrow?; muyalālum – having jumping rabbit on his body; iḷa madikkē – for youthful moon; vaḷai iḻandēṟku – for me who has lost the bangles; vayalāli maṇavāḷā – oh lord who is residing in tiruvāli which is surrounded by fertile fields!; idu naduvē – amidst these harming entities (your arrival); maṇi niṟamō koḷvāyō – will you hurt by stealing my beautiful complexion?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who performed kudak kūttu and is residing in cool tirukkudandai which is surrounded by tall gardens where cuckoos are singing! Will I who am having sleepless eyes and thinking only about you, feel sorrow? I have lost already the bangles for the youthful moon having jumping rabbit on his body. Oh lord who is residing in tiruvāli which is surrounded by fertile fields! āmidst these harming entities, will you hurt me, by stealing my beautiful complexion?

*kuyil Alum …* – In this town, cuckoos will dance upside down. In this town, the cuckoos will drink honey and joyfully sing. In this town, only cuckoos are helpless. She lost her sleep as she heard that the one, who danced with pots on the four-way junction to be seen by all covherd girls and gave his beauty fully to them, has now become easily approachable in tirukkudandai so that those who are subsequent to kriṣṇāvatāram do not lose out. As she heard that he has come close to tirukkudandai, she lost her sleep. She now has two lakhsmaṇas to not have sleep \[lakśmaṇa did not sleep while staying in the forest to serve śrī rāma and sītāp pirātti\]. Her eyes were born in the same muhūrtam (time) as that of iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa). Here, it is unlike in the case of lakśmaṇa where he had to give up sleep on a particular day as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 56.3 “*jahau*” (relinquished). Should he make her inner eyes also not to sleep? Even if he is not seen by the external eyes, should he be seen by the inner eyes? It is said in periya tiruvandādi 28 “*nenjennum utkaṇ*” (The heart which is known as inner eye). Though he does not allow her to embrace him, should there be a periya tirunāḷ (grand festival) inside the heart?

*tuyarvēnō* – Should we not survive by forgetting him?

*muyal Alum …* – \[This question is to the moon\] Is my state such that you have to hurt me with your rays? I have already lost my bangles for the moon who cannot eliminate his own scars and defects. For me who lost my bangles to the moon who cannot rid of the rabbit which is jumping in his body, and is youthful.

*idu naduvē …* – On top of hurting me with your paraphernalia, are you also going to enter the battle? Just as those who come and harm others in the middle while a wrestling battle is going on between two people. While one is being attacked with sling and hammer, the person who attacks also harms directly. Are you aiming to hurt me directly, on top of hurting me through your wealth (moon)?

*koḷvāyō maṇi niṟamē* – She has heard him repeatedly say “What a complexion you have!” while being together with her \[she is repeating that\]; otherwise, she will not glorify her own form.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.9. Nilaiyala

*nilaiyāḷā! nin vaṇanga vēṇḍāyē āgilum en mulaiyāḷa oru nāḷ un agalattāl āḷāyē? silaiyāḷā! maram eyda tiṟalāḷā! tirumeyya malaiyāḷā! nīyāḷa vaḷaiyāḷa māttōmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

silai āḷā – Oh you who have śrī kōdaṇḍam in your hand!; maram eydda tiṟal āḷā – Oh you who can shoot arrow to uproot the marāmaram!; tirumeyya malai āḷā – Oh you who are mercifully reclining in tirumeyyam!; nilai āḷā nin vaṇanga – As I surrender unto you without any other expectation; vēṇḍāyē āgilum – even if you don’t desire for it; en mulai āḷa – to have my bosoms serve; oru nāḷ – at least one day; un agalattāl āḷa – you should rule me by embracing with your vast chest; nī āḷa – after you accepted; vaḷai āḷa māttōmē – we will not seek out the ability to rule over our bangles

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who have śrī kōdaṇḍam in your hand! Oh you who can shoot arrow to uproot the marāmaram! Oh you who are mercifully reclining in tirumeyyam! Even if you don’t desire for my surrender unto you without any other expectation, you should rule me by embracing me with your vast chest, at least one day, to have my bosoms serve you; after you accepted, we will not seek out the ability to rule over our bangles.

*nilai āḷā …* – The activity which matches the true nature of the self is to worship his divine feet and live  as long as one has existence.

*nin …* – Though this is the truth, it will materialise only when he thinks “let this ātmā attain this goal”.

*nilai āḷā! nin vaṇanga vēṇḍāyē āgilum –* If something is to be attained, it is this – āḻvār is desiring to perform eternal kainkaryam at emperumān’s divine feet being close to him, instead of getting other benefits and leaving him. Though āḻvār is in the mood of emperumān’s divine consort, she is only desiring for servitude towards him just as brāhmaṇas will constantly recite vēda mantrams even when they become mad.

*nilai āḷā nin vaṇanga* – With this, the goal is established \[to serve emperumān is the goal\].

*vēṇḍāyē āgilum* – With this, the means is established \[emperumān’s mercy is the means\]. If he does not desire, this goal will not be attained. This is what we desire – even if you remain like neem \[which is bitter\].

*en mulai āḷa* – To let me manage my existence;  to have me retain my femininity and manage myself instead of suffering by the urge of my bosoms which are like children crying out saying “Food! Food!” as in nācciyār tirumoḻi 5.7 “*kongai kiḷarndu kumaittu*” (my stout bosoms are melting my life joyously).

*en mulai āḷa* – To control and rule over my bosoms like those who control and rule over an intoxicated elephant.

emperumān says “When we don’t have the desire, if you ask me to do this for your purpose, should I do it?” parakāla nāyaki responds,

*oru nāḷ* – You can avoid coming everyday; but should you not come one day, for the sake of others?

*oru nāḷ* – Don’t think that I need you to come many days; even if you come one day, it is sufficient.

emperumān says “If I don’t have the interest in my heart to do that even one day, should I do it?” parakāla nāyaki responds,

*un agalattāl āḷāyē* – You keep your heart in those who are desirable for you and you can just embrace me with your body.

emperumān says “Why should I be having my heart with others and embracing you? Why should I engage with you even for one day, when I don’t desire for it?” parakāla nāyaki says,

*silai āḷā* – To avoid my sorrowful cry \[you have to come\]. śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 10.3 “*kśatriyair dāryatē*” (the kings are holding \[the bow to eliminate the cry of the suffering ones\]), aren’t you holding the bow to not hear the sorrowful cry.

emperumān says “Where did you see us using our bow to eliminate the sorrow, and forcing me to do the same now?” parakāla nāyaki says,

*maram eyda tiṟal āḷā* – Are you not the one who will take up arms and help even those who don’t believe in your ability? Did you not shoot the seven marāmaram with your arrow to eliminate the sorrow of sugrīva mahārājar?

emperumān says “In that case, you should have come during rāmāvatāram and got my help” parakāla nāyaki says,

*tirumeyya malaiyāḷā* – Have you not mercifully arrived in tirumeyyam to eliminate such loss \[in not getting your help in avatārams\]? In such case, will being accepted by you and having bangles in hand occur together? Now, due to her sorrow, she is saying like that. Bangles will never stay in her hands; if he is with her, her body will swell in happiness and the bangles will break and fall down; if he leaves her, she will become lean, and they will fall down. Being accepted by you, how can I protect myself with my femininity? \[An incident is explained here\] During the final moments of ammangi ammāḷ, nanjīyar heard about the situation and went to see him. At that time, nanjīyar told him “While you should be joyful in this world with service to ācārya and enjoying bhagavān’s qualities, it is unfortunate that you have to suffer like this like common people”. ammangi ammāḷ responded quoting the words “*nī āḷa vaḷai āḷa māttōmē*” from this pāsuram and said “If we are accepted by bhagavān, we must suffer \[in separation\] and finally give up the body”. As nanjīyar left from there, he mercifully told nampiḷḷai “If he can say such words even in his final moments, it is due to the firm placement of his strong relationship due to the strong faith in bhagavān”.

Thus, in this pāsuram, the following aspects are explained:

- Establishing the goal
- the state of those who have taste
- the nature of emperumān who is the refuge
- ātmā having lot of desire to reach him

*nilai āḷā* – It is explained that the goal is to be engaged in eternal kainkaryam.

*vēṇḍāyē āgilum* – It is explained that bhagavān is the upāyam as well.

*en mulai āḷa oru nāḷ* – The nature of those who have taste is explained.

*silai āḷā* – bhagavān being refuge is explained.

*maram eyda* – It is explained that there is no shortcoming in his protection and ātmā should seek his protection.

All of these principles are explained in this pāsuram.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.10. Maiyilangu

*maiyilangu karunguvaḷai marungalarum vayalāli neyyilangu sudarāḻip padaiyānai nedumālaik kaiyilangu vēl kaliyan kaṇḍuraitta tamiḻ mālai aiyiraṇḍum ivai vallārkku aruvinaigaḷ adaiyāvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kai ilangu vēl kaliyan – āḻvār who has shining spear in his hand; mai ilangu karum kuvaḷai – black kuvaḷai flowers which shine like black pigment; marungu – in the surrounding; alarum – blossoming; vayal – surrounded by fertile fields; Ali – present in tiruvāli; ney – sharp; ilangu – shining; sudar – having radiance; āḻip padaiyānai – having tiruvāḻi (sudarśana chakra) in his hand; nedumālai – sarvēśvaran; kaṇḍu – seeing in front; uraitta – mercifully spoke; tamiḻ mālai aiyiraṇḍum ivai vallār – those who are able to clearly know this garland of ten pāsurams; aru vinaigaḷ – evil deeds; adaiyāvē – will not reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Seeing in front of him, āḻvār who has shining spear in his hand, mercifully spoke about sarvēśvaran who is having śiningly radiant sudarśana chakra in his hand and is present in tiruvāli which is surrounded by fertile fields where black kuvaḷai flowers which shine like black pigment are blossoming in the surrounding; evil deeds will not reach those who are able to clearly know this garland of ten pāsurams.

*mai ilangu …* – This is how barren lands, which have no crops, look like in tiruvāli.  The barren lands of the town look like this. In the surroundings, the kuvaḷai flowers which have black colour shining, are present all around. tiruvāli which has fertile fields which has surroundings where kuvaḷai flowers shine increasingly day by day.

*ney ilangu …* – If the divine chakra is not present in hands, one cannot see anything due to the darkness outside \[the town\] by the kuvaḷai flowers and darkness inside \[the town\] by his complexion.

*ney ilangu* – For the dark complexion from his divine form and the darkness caused by the kuvaḷai flowers, if the light from the divine chakra is not there, one cannot place the next step.

*nedu mālai* – \[Due to his overwhelming love\] It appears that he is neither sending a messenger nor speaking a word. He is so flattened \[by love\] that he cannot send a messenger. If pirātti says as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.25 “*ūrdvam māsānam najīviśyē*” (I will not live for more than one month), he will say as in sundara kāṇḍam 66.10 “*na jīvēyam kśaṇamapi*” (I cannot live for a moment more).

*kai ilangu* – bhattar would mercifully say – sarvēśvaran will go along with tirumangai āḻvār, while āḻvār is going on his horse \[ādal mā\]! He will have his divine chakra as a decoration for his divine form. āḻvār’s spear will be stained with blood since he has no time to wash them after destroying the enemies”. Just as emperumān holds his divine chakra revealing his lordship, āḻvār is holding the spear revealing his servitude.

*kaṇḍuraitta* – As he arrived hearing the words of the messengers \[as trained by āḻvār\] in front of āḻvār, āḻvār spoke to him.

*aru vinaigaḷ adaiyāvē* – One will not be impacted by the sins which will make one separate from emperumān and send messenger to him. One need not go through the suffering of trying to send a messenger while being separated from sarvēśvaran and being unable to do so. sarvēśvaran will send messenger to those who practice and recite these ten pāsurams.

## 3.7 Kalvankol

## 3.7.1. Kalvankol

*kaḷvankol? yān aṟiyēn kariyān oru kāḷai vandu vaḷḷi marungul endan madamāninaip pōda enṟu veḷḷi vaḷaik kaip paṟṟap peṟṟa tāyarai vittaganṟu aḷḷalam pūngaḻani aṇiyāli puguvar kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaḷvankol – Is he a thief (or the owner)?; yān aṟiyēn – I don’t know; kariyān oru kāḷai vandu – a dark, young person came; vaḷḷi marungul – having slender waist; endan mada māninai – my daughter, who is very young; pōda enṟu – urged her saying “Come! Come!”; veḷḷi vaḷaik kai paṟṟa – holding her hand which has silver bangles; peṟṟa tāyarai – me who is her mother; ittu aganṟu – leaving alone; aḷḷal – in mud; am pūngaḻani – having fertile fields which are filled with beautiful flowers; aṇi Ali – in tiruvāli which is an ornament for the earth; puguvarkolō – will they enter?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Is he a thief (or the owner)? I don’t know. A dark, young person came and urged my daughter, who is very young and having slender waist, holding her hand which has silver bangles, saying “Come! Come!”. Leaving me, who is her mother, alone, will they enter tiruvāli which is an ornament for the earth and is having fertile fields which are filled with beautiful flowers in mud?

*kaḷvankol* – As said in mahābhāratam udyāna parvam 42.35 “*yō(a)nyatā santamātmānam anyatā pratipadyatē, kim tēna na krutam pāpam cōrēṇa ātmāpahāriṇā*” (what sin has not been committed by one who thinks that ātmā (soul), which is the property of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), is his own and steals such ātmā?), emperumān taking her, who is his wealth, away appears similar to ātmā’s theft of self (claiming ātmā to be independent), due to ātmā’s impressions of claiming independence.

*kol* – Though the owner carried his own possession and since he carried under our watch, it is not apt to say “kaḷvan” (Thief); still she says “kaḷvan” due to her deep involvement in mamakāram (ownership).

*yān aṟiyēn* – If she, who is guarding there, does not know, one should ask the one who carried.

When told “Though you don’t know, can you not tell the features you know?” parakāla nāyaki’s mother says,

*kariyān …* – piḷḷai amudanār explained this as “Just as a person would carry away the sword while the holder remains in tact, while the mother was embracing and resting along with parakāla nāyaki, he carried her away”; bhattar mercifully heard that and said “One need not try so hard; some thieves would have lights on and will carry the children even as the parents start screaming ‘Son! ḍaugter!’; this is done similar to that”.

*oru* – Just as one will be stunned if water enters the mouth, while speaking about his complexion, without being able to determine his identity, she can only say “someone”.

*kāḷai* – She is saying “Leaving like this is not his mistake; it is the fault of his age”; his youthful state impressed her so much that she starts speaking about its greatness though she has nothing do with it, while trying to blame him for carrying her daughter away. Even my daughter who went with him is thinking “This will cause accusation”, but is saying that it is the fault of his youthful state which makes us not withdraw seeing the disaster. sūrpaṇakā, who went to complain about her disfigured face, was the one who said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 19.14 “*taruṇau*” (They are youthful). Subsequently she accused them due to her \[natural\] previous impressions. Otherwise, what use is it for her to speak about their youth while complaining about her suffering? She thinks of whatever happened in between as the bodily impacts during union.

*vandu* – If this is his complexion and youthful state, just as all the snakes came and fell in the sarpa yāgam (the fire sacrifice performed by janamē jayan), all the women should go and fall for him, if he has arrived; would she not go? Whoever it may be, if one attains bhagavān, it is not without his arrival.

*vaḷḷi …* – This is the viśvāmitran which brought him. It is her beauty which brought him. While he has to be narrated with many aspects, it is sufficient for her to be attributed with one feature. In [tiruvāimoḻi 6.6.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-6-1-malukku/) “*mālukku …*“, emperumān was narrated with many attributes and finally parānguśa nāyaki was identified as “*kongalarēlak kuḻali*” (one with honey filled, fragrant hair). Here also it is similarly explained.

*enṟan mada māninai* – my daughter; young one; she is so young that she does not think about her tenderness, femininity and the difficult path.

*enṟan* – As she he came and tried to carry her, she \[the mother\] is claiming ownership on her saying “my daughter”.

*pōda enṟu* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.15 “*uktam artam imam cara*” (You do as I say), he is telling her. The dark youthful person came and said “Come! Come!” Just as an ātmā uses karma yōgam, jñāna yōgam etc to reach sarvēśvaran, this is the sādanam (means) he performed to attain the ātmā.

*veḷḷi vaḷaikkai paṟṟa* – She remained stunned being impressed by his speech; at that time, he held her hand; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116.16 “*na pramāṇīkruta: pāṇi: bālyē bālēna pīdita:*” (When you were a boy, you held my hand; you did not think about that), you held my hand in such a way that I became as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/08/thiruvaimozhi-9-6-6-engannan-kalvam/) “*angaṇṇan uṇḍa en Ar uyirk kōdu idu*” (my faulty soul considering his being lovingly desirous and consuming of it). The way he held her hand, she gave up her attachment towards her mother with whom she has a lengthy relationship. Covherd girls would wear silver bangles by purchasing them in place of gold and other precious gems.

When asked “How deep will his holding of her hand impact?”, mother says

*peṟṟa tāyarai* – Am I her step-mother for her to abandon me instantaneously?

*ittu* – Even when one abandon others, one will atone for doing so; but here she abandoned as if abandoning insentient entities.

*aganṟu* – Even if she leaves us, we can follow her and catch her; she is not even allowing me as she has gone too far.

*aḷḷalam …* – The divyadēśam tiruvāli is such that, once they cross the border of this town and enter tiruvāli, they will have to place every step on flower only. As said in śrīguṇa ratna kōśam 42 “*pādāruntudamēvā pankaja raja:*” (the buds of the lotus flower are bothering your highness’ divine feet), the flowers are harmful for her \[She is so tender\].

*aṇi Ali* – tiruvāli which is an ornament for samsāram (material world).

*puguvarkolō* – Both are young \[and hence ignorant\] – one who prays to capture the mystic deer and the other who chases to catch it. Without realising, will they reach the gates of lankā or will they reach their destination in the day time? Both are deeply indulging in each other.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.2. Pandivan

*paṇḍu ivan āyan nangāy! padiṟan pugundu en magaḷ tan toṇḍaiyanjenganivāy nugarndānai ugandu avan pin keṇḍai oṇ kaṇ miḷirak kiḷi pōl miḻaṟṟi nadandu vaṇḍamar kānal malgum vayalāli puguvar kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

nangāy – Oh neighbourhood girls!; ivan – this youthful person; paṇḍu – previously; āyan padiṟan – was a thief in the covherd clan (who would steal the covherd girls); pugundu – entered (into my home physically); en magaḷ than – my youthful daughter, her; toṇḍai sengani am vāy nugarndān – drank the nectar from her beautiful lips which are like reddish kōvai fruit; ugandu – (my daughter) desiring him; keṇḍai – like keṇḍai fish; oṇ kaṇ – beautiful eyes; miḷira – becoming expanded and shining (due to seeing something unseen); kiḷi pōl – like a parrot; miḻaṟṟi – speaking some words; avan pin nadandu – walking behind him (both of them, who became united); vaṇḍu amar – filled with beetles; kānal malgum – surrounded by seaside gardens; vayal – having fertile fields; Ali – in tiruvāli; puguvar kolō – they may reach or not!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh neighbourhood girls! Previously, this youthful person was a thief in the covherd clan; he entered my home and drank the nectar from her beautiful lips which are like reddish kōvai fruit; desiring him, her keṇḍai fish like beautiful eyes became expanded and shining; speaking some words like a parrot, she started walking behind him; they may or may not reach tiruvāli which is having fertile fields surrounded by seaside gardens filled with beetles.

*paṇḍu ivan āyan nangāy* – \[Previously he was a covherd\] His current state makes his previous state to be considered as cakravartit tirumagan (son of emperor daśarati). The lowly one who tried to steal butter but could not do it well, is now doing this to my daughter.

**Alternative explanation**

*paṇḍu ivan …* – Previously he was as said in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 12.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/05/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-12-simple/) “*kādu vāḻ sādi*” (belonging to forest tribe), has now become civilised.

*padiṟan pugundu* – Previously he would steal without the knowledge of others; now he has become paśyatōharn (one who steals while others are watching).

*en magaḷ …* – Beyond defeating her with his beauty etc, he mesmerised her with his ability in romantic acts!

*avan pin* – As said in periya tirumoḻi 9.3.3 “*pēdai ninnaip piriyēn ini*” (Oh innocent girl! I will never leave you), he made her lose by certain romantic acts; he did not even call her saying “Come!” He is using his nectarean saliva which is like the magic powder, to make her follow him.

*keṇḍai oṇ kaṇ miḷir* – Seeing some new/unseen things, she keeps asking her hero “What are these?” with her eyes.

*kiḷi pōl miḻaṟṟi* – Speaking sweet words with her mouth, after asking certain questions with her eyes.

*nadandu* – She followed him since if she goes in front of him, he will not be able to focus on the destination.

*vaṇḍu …* – Will they enter the town where even the animals which enter will not leave as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.15 “*na ca punar āvartatē*” (there is no return). She is saying that she cannot desire for her daughter anymore.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.3. Anjuvan venjol

*anjuvan venjol nangāy! arakkar kulap pāvai tannai venjina mūkkarinda viṟalōn tiṟam kētkil meyyē panjiya melladi em paṇait tōḷi parakkaḻindu vanjiyandaṇpaṇai sūḻ vayalāli puguvarkolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

nangāy – Oh neighbourhood girl!; vem sol – This is a very cruel word; arakkar kulap pāvai tannai – sūrpaṇakā who was celebrated as the only daughter of the whole rākśasa clan, her; vem sinam – by the cruel anger; mūkku – her nose; arinda – severed; viṟalōn – the youthful person who is strong, his; tiṟam – way; kētkil – if heard now; meyyē anjuvan – will fear thinking that it is happening now; (while this is the case); panju mel adi – very tender feet, similar to cotton; em paṇait tōḷi – my daughter who has bamboo like shoulder; parakku aḻindu – without humility (being together with him, both of them); vanji – by collection of creepers; am – beautiful; taṇ paṇai – by cool bamboo bushes; sūḻ – surrounded; vayal – having fertile fields; Ali – in tiruvāli; puguvarkolō – will they reach?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh neighbourhood girl! This is a very cruel word. By her cruel anger, sūrpaṇakā who was celebrated as the only daughter of the whole rākśasa clan, got her nose severed by the youthful one. If I heard about his such ways, I will fear thinking that it is happening now \[to my daughter\]. Will my daughter who is having very tender feet similar to cotton, bamboo like shoulder and is without humility, along with him, reach tiruvāli which is surrounded by fertile fields which has collections of creepers, cold bamboo bushes?

*anjuvan …* \[should be recited as “arakkar kulap pāvai … meyyē anjuvan”\] – bhattar mercifully recited this pāsuram and asked \[kidāmbi\] āccān “Since it is said that I fear hearing the ways of the one who disfigured a woman, as it appears to affect the good qualities of bhagavān, this should not be mercifully said by āḻvār. How can this be reconciled?” āccān said “Should one stir the pot with one’s hand painfully while there is a lengthy ladle? emperumānār himself mercifully explained this” bhattar asked “How is this mercifully explained?” āccān mercifully replied “parakāla nāyaki’s mother is fearing thinking about the danger which occurred when sītāp pirātti was going along with śrī rāma”.

*meyyē anjuvan* – \[This is in present tense\] She does not realise that such incident happened in the past and now we are in the present; she is fearing as if it is happening now.

*panjiya mel adi* – She is having foot which is so tender that even while resting on a mattress, one should fear about it.

*em paṇait tōḷi* – Having shoulder which is having circumference, freshness and length which are similar to that of a bamboo.

*parakku aḻindu* – Not fearing for accusations. Also explained as para kaḻivu – very much lost.

*vanji …* – Is she going to a destination which has matching entities for her?

## 3.7.4. Edu avan

*ēdu avan tol piṟappu? iḷaiyavan vaḷaiyūdi mannar tūduvanāy avanūr solluvīrgaḷ! solleer aṟiyēn mādavan tan tuṇaiyā nadandāḷ tadam sūḻ puṟavil pōdu vaṇḍādu semmal punalāli puguvarkolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

avan – That youthful person’s; tol piṟappu – previous birth; ēdu aṟiyēn – I don’t know whether it is kśatriya birth or covherd birth; iḷaiyavan – young person; vaḷai ūdi – (to cause fear in enemies) one who blew the conch; mannar – for kings; tūduvanāyavan – one who went as a messenger, his; Ur – birth; solluvīrgaḷ īdenṟu – Oh you who are able to know and tell!; solleer – You tell me truthfully and decisively; mādavan – śriya:pati (the lord of śrī mahālakśmi); than tuṇaiyāga nadandāḷ – she walked, having him as her companion; vaṇḍu – beetles; tadam sūḻ – surrounded by ponds; puṟavil – blossomed in the surroundings; semmal pōdu – big flowers; ādu – indulging (having entered to drink honey); punal Ali – in tiruvāli which has abundance of water; puguvarkolō – will they enter?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I don’t know that youthful person’s previous birth, whether it was kśatriya birth or covherd birth. Oh you who are able to know and tell about the birth of the young person who blew the conch and who went as the messenger for the kings! You tell me truthfully and decisively. My daughter walked with śriya:pati having him as her companion; will they enter tiruvāli where beetles are indulging in the big flowers blossomed in the surroundings, in the ponds that surround the town which has abundance of water?

*ēdu avan tol piṟappu* – Was he born in kśatriya clan or covherd clan? I don’t know.

*iḷaiyavan* – Adolescent one (who acts without realising the effect).

*vaḷai ūdi* – One who reveals the place where he is \[by blowing the conch\].

*mannar tūduvanāy avan Ur* – The abode of the one who goes to his enemies’ place without carrying any weapons.

*avan Ur solluveergaḷ solleer aṟiyēn* – Oh you desire him seeing his birth in kśatriya clan or covherd clan! I cannot see his birth being either one.

*mādavan …* – She thought the deep ocean to be a boat; she followed him without realising that even the greatly knowledgeable persons were caught in his matters and he is unreachable for her.

*tadam sūḻ …* – When the flowers blossom in that town, flood of honey will start flowing and the beetles will immerse in it and drink it. Only after the flowers blossom fully and the honey flow reduces, could the beetles drink it. Will they enter tiruvāli where the beetles will search for fully blossomed flowers and drink honey? pōdu – Fresh flower. Newly blossomed flower. semmal – greatness, being ancient and flower.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.5. Tay enai

*tāy enai enṟu irangāḷ tadandōḷi tanakku amainda māyanai mādavanai madittu ennai aganṟa ivaḷ vēyana tōḷ visiṟip pedai annamena nadandu pōyina pūngodiyāḷ punalāli puguvarkolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

tadam tōḷi ivaḷ – She who is having huge shoulders; enai – me who is having mental suffering; tāy enṟu irangāḷ – not showing her mercy considering that I am her mother; tanakku amainda – one who is having physical beauty etc matching her qualities such as beauty etc; māyanai mādavanai – the amazing śriya:pati; madittu – considering to be the refuge; ennai aganṟu – leaving me alone; vēyana tōḷ visiṟi – swaying her bamboo like shoulders; pedai annam ena – like a female swan; nadandu pōyina – walking behind him; pūm kodiyāḷ – my daughter who is having beautiful creeper like waist (and him); punal Ali – in tiruvāli which has abundant water; puguvarkolō – will they enter?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter who is having huge shoulders is not showing her mercy to me who is having mental suffering, considering that I am her mother. Considering the amazing śriya:pati who is having physical beauty etc matching her qualities such as beauty etc, to be her refuge, leaving me alone, swaying her bamboo like shoulders like a female swan, she, who is having beautiful creeper like waist, is walking behind him; will they enter tiruvāli which has abundant water?

*tāy enai enṟu irangāḷ* – She is not showing her mercy, considering that I, her mother, will have my stomach burn.

*tadam tōḷi tanakku amainda māyanai* – Her shoulder’s beauty will in itself match his overall beauty.

*mādavanai madittu ennai aganṟa ivaḷ* – She abandoned me considering that he is very knowledgeable in romantic acts.

*vēyana tōḷ visiṟi* – Swaying her bamboo like shoulders.

*pedai annam ena nadandu* – If she said just “*annam*“, it may imply masculinity and hence says “*pedai annam*” (female swan.

*pōyina …* – Will they enter the town where both of them can play water sports together?

## 3.7.6. En tunai

*en tuṇai enṟu eduttēṟku iṟaiyēnum irangiṟṟilaḷ tan tuṇaiyāya endan tanimaikkum irangiṟṟilaḷ van tuṇai vānavarkkāy varam seṟṟu arangattu uṟaiyum in tuṇaivanodum pōy eḻilāli puguvarkolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

en tuṇai enṟu – considering as “my companion”; eduttēṟku – for me who gave birth; iṟaiyēnum – even a little bit; irangiṟṟilaḷ – she did not have mercy; than tuṇai āya – her companion; endan tanimaikkum – for me being alone; irangiṟṟilaḷ – she did not have mercy; vānavargaḷ – for dēvatās; van tuṇaiyāy – going as strong companion; varam seṟṟu – subduing the strength received by the demons of lankā; arangattu uṟaiyum – residing eternally in kōyil (śrīrangam); in tuṇaivanodum pōy – went with her favourite companion; eḻil Ali – in beautiful tiruvāli; puguvarkolō – will they enter?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter did not have even a little bit of mercy for me who gave birth to her, considering her as my companion; she did not have mercy for me who was her companion, to be left alone; she went along with her favourite companion who is eternally residing in kōyil, who went as the strong companion for dēvatās and subdued the strength received by the demons of lankā; will they enter the beautiful tiruvāli?

*en tuṇai …* – She did not have even a little bit of mercy considering that I gave birth to her and raised her as my companion, who will be my refuge.

*than tuṇai …* – Though one does not have love, one will show mercy when one sees a suffering person; she did not even do it.

*van tuṇai vānavarkkāy* – Being a strong companion means placing him in front of the arrows without caring for self, for dēvatās.

*varam seṟṟu* – Destroying the boons which were granted by dēvatās. He will become a companion only when all that were earned by self are destroyed.

*arangattu uṟaiyum …* – Just as śrī ayōdyā was decorated when emperumān, who is very enjoyable, easily accessible and the protector, entered śrī ayōdyā after destroying rāvaṇa, they \[my daughter and her dear companion\] had tiruvāli decorated nicely and entered.

## 3.7.7. Annaiyum attanum

*annaiyum attanum enṟu adiyōmukku irangiṟṟilaḷ pinnai tan kādalan tan perundōḷ nalam pēṇinaḷāl minnaiyum vanjiyaiyum venṟu ilangum idaiyāḷ nadandu punnaiyum annamum sūḻ punalāli puguvarkolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaiyum – Mother; attanum – and father; enṟu – considering that; adiyōmukku – in our matters; irangiṟṟilaḷ – she is not showing mercy; pinnai than – for nappinnaip pirātti; kādalan than – beloved’s; perum tōḷ nalam – the joy of embracing his great shoulders; pēṇinaḷ – desiring; minnaiyum vanjiyaiyum – lightning and vanji creeper; venṟu – defeat; ilangum – shining; idaiyāḷ – my daughter who is having waist region; nadandu – walked and went; punnaiyum – punnai gardens; annamum – groups of swans; sūḻ – surrounded; punal Ali – in tiruvāli which has abundant water; puguvarkolō – Will they enter?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter is not showing mercy in our matters considering us to be her mother and father; desiring for the joy of embracing the great shoulders of emperumān who is the beloved of nappinnaip pirātti, my daughter, who is having waist region which will defeat lightning and vanji creeper, walked and went with him; will they enter tiruvāli which has abundant water and is surrounded by punnai gardens and groups of swans.

*annaiyum …* – Even if she desired to go, should she leave blaming us? She did not show mercy towards us, the servitors, considering us to be mother and father. Should she leave us who are the servitors, blaming us to be the controllers?

*pinnai …* – If she leaves two persons here, she should hold on to two persons there \[nappinnaip pirātti and emperumān\]. The reason for abandoning us is the greatness of emperumān to be enjoyed there.

*minnai …* – The one who would defeat lightning and vanji creeper with her thin waist, walked.

*punnai …* – Would they enter the abode which has enjoyable places \[gardens\] and their species \[swans\]?

## 3.7.8. Murrilum

*muṟṟilum paingiḷiyum pandum ūsalum pēsuginṟa siṟṟilmen pūvaiyum vittaganṟa seḻungōdai tannaip peṟṟilēn muṟṟiḻaiyai piṟappili pinnē nadandu maṟṟellām kai toḻap pōy vayalāli puguvarkolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

muṟṟilum – winnow; paingiḷiyum – green parrot; pandum – ball; ūsalum – swing; siṟṟil – from a small nest; pēsuginṟa – speaking; men pūvaiyum – tender natured myna bird; vittu aganṟa – left these and went away; seḻum kōdai tannai – one who is like a beautiful garland; muṟṟiḻaiyai – my daughter who is fully decorated with ornaments; peṟṟilēn – I did not get to see her; maṟṟellām kai toḻa – to be vorśipped by everyone other than her; piṟappili pinnē – behind the one who is opposite to all defects; nadandu pōy – walked; vayal Ali – in tiruvāli which has abundance of crops; puguvarkolō – will they enter?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter who is fully decorated with ornaments and is like a beautiful garland left her winnow, green parrot, ball, swing, tender natured myna bird which is speaking from its small nest; I did not get to see her; she walked behind the one who is opposite to all defects, to be vorśipped by everyone other than her; will they enter tiruvāli which has abundance of crops?

*muṟṟil* … – Went away leaving even the tender natured myna bird which is speaking from its small nest.

*seḻum kōdai tannai* – The completeness which she acquired in her body after leaving her play-toys and going behind him.

*peṟṟilēn muṟṟiḻaiyai* – I did not get to follow her seeing her from behind, where her ornaments are fastened.

*piṟappili pinnē nadandu* – Walking behind emperumān who has no births, where one can be redeemed saying “This is damaging to your qualities”.

*maṟṟellām kai toḻap pōy* – Due to having the fault of being her mother, I am unable to worship her; all others could worship her and follow her.

*vayal Ali puguvarkolō* – Will they enter the abode which has beautiful sceneries to be seen by those who see it? Alternatively, it can be said as the abode which has all enjoyments.

## 3.7.9. Kaviyanganni

*kāviyangaṇṇi eṇṇil kadimāmalarp pāvai oppāḷ pāviyēn peṟṟamaiyāl paṇait tōḷi parakkaḻindu tūvisēr annam anna nadaiyāḷ nedumālodum pōy vāviyandaṇ paṇai sūḻ vayalāli puguvarkolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

kāvi am kaṇṇi – having beautiful eyes resembling kāvi flower; eṇṇil – if we analyse; kadi mā malar – living in very fragrant lotus flower; pāvai oppāḷ – one who is matching periya pirāttiyār; tūvi sēr – having wings; annam anna – matching a swan’s; nadaiyāḷ – having the gait; paṇait tōḷi – my daughter who is having bamboo like shoulder; pāviyēn – me, the sinner; peṟṟamaiyāl – due to the defect of giving birth to her; parakku aḻindu – without even a little bit of shame; nedumālodum – with the one who has great love; pōy – going alone; vāvi – ponds; taṇ ambaṇai – cool water bodies; sūḻ – surrounded fully; vayal – having abundant crops; Ali – in tiruvāli; puguvarkolō – will they enter?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

If we analyse my daughter, who is having bamboo like shoulder, winged swan like gait and beautiful eyes resembling kāvi flower, she matches periya pirāttiyār who is living in very fragrant lotus flower; due to the defect of me, who is a sinner, giving birth to her, she is going alone, without even a little bit of shame, with the one who has great love; will they enter tiruvāli which is having abundant crops surrounded by ponds and cool water bodies?

*kāvi …* – Just as pirātti is having greatness of being more “*asitēkśaṇā*” (black eyed) than īśvaran, parakāla nāyaki is greater than pirātti.

*kāvi am kaṇṇi* – Her eyes are fortunate to enjoy the togetherness of pirātti and emperumān.

*pāviyēn …* – It is because of being born as my daughter that she had to go alone.

*tūvi sēr …* – One who can make others go crazy with her gait.

*nedumālodum pōy* – One who becomes madly in love by going crazy with her gait.

*vāvi …* – Will they enter the town where they can play water sports, throwing flowers at each other?

## 3.7.10. Tay manam

*tāy manam ninṟirangat taniyē nedumāl tuṇaiyā pōyina pūngodiyāḷ punalāli puguvar enṟu kāysina vēl kaliyan oli sey tamiḻ mālai pattum mēviya nenjudaiyār tanjamāvadu viṇṇulagē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāy – mother; ninṟu manam iranga – while suffering and having her stomach burn; nedumāl – one who is bewildered due to more love than she; tuṇaiyā – as company; taniyē pōyina – one who went without the company of anyone like her; pūm kodiyāḷ – my daughter who is like a beautiful creeper (and he, both of them); punal Ali – in tiruvāli which has abundance of water; puguvar enṟu – “will they enter or not?”; kāy sinam – great anger towards enemies; vēl – and having the spear to destroy such enemies; kaliyan – āḻvār; oli sey – mercifully spoke; tamiḻ mālai pattum – the ten pāsurams, each of which is a garland; mēviya nenju udaiyār – for those who can recite with heart’s involvement; viṇ ulagu – the leader of the residents of paramapadam; tanjamāvadu – is the protector (he will grant them paramapadam)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār who is having great anger towards enemies and the spear to destroy such enemies, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams each of which is a garland, saying “My daughter is like a beautiful creeper; while I, her mother, am suffering and having my stomach burn, went without the company of anyone like her, she, has the one who is bewildered due to more love than she, as her company; will they or will they not  enter tiruvāli which has abundance of water?” For those who can recite this decad with heart’s involvement, the leader of the residents of paramapadam, is the protector.

*tāy manam …* – tirumangai āḻvār who is having attachment towards bhagavat viśayam, great anger towards enemies and the spear to destroy such enemies, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams where he speaks as the divine mother of parakāla nāyaki instead of parakāla nāyaki herself saying “While I, the mother, am suffering with my stomach burning, will my distinguished daughter, who went along with the one who is more bewildered than she due to his great love,  enter tiruvāli?”

*pattum mēviya nenjudaiyār tanjamāvadu viṇṇulagē –* For those who can learn this decad with heart’s involvement, reaching paramapadam is certain. One need not go as in the case of parakāla nāyaki where her mother was fearing for her lone travel, but can go where one is led by bhagavān himself along with group of ātivāhikas (Those who can travel between different planets).

## 3.8 Nanda vilakke

## 3.8.1. Nanda vilakke

*nandā viḷakkē! aḷattaṟku ariyāy! nara nāraṇanē! karumāmugil pōl endāy! emakkē aruḷāy ena ninṟu imaiyōr paravum idam ettisaiyum kandāram am tēn isai pāda mādē kaḷivaṇḍu miḻaṟṟa niḻal tudaindu mandāram ninṟu maṇamalgu nāngūr maṇimādak kōyil vaṇangu en mananē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nandā viḷakkē – Oh you who are having the true nature of being eternal and self-illuminating knowledge!; aḷattaṟku ariyāy – Oh you who are incomprehensible!; nara nāraṇanē – Oh you who incarnated as nara and nārāyaṇa!; karu mā mugil pōl endāy – Oh you, my lord, who are having divine form which matches a dark, great cloud!; emakkē – For us who are favourable and have no other refuge than you; aruḷay ena – saying “you should mercifully give your grace”; imaiyōr – dēvatās; ninṟu – coming and standing on earth; paravum idam – being the abode where they will sing stōtrams (hymns in praīse)etc and surrender; am tēn – beautiful beetles; ettisaiyum – in all directions; kandāram isai pāda – to sing rāgas like dēva gāndāri etc; kaḷi vaṇḍu – beetles who have drunk honey; mādē – in the surroundings; miḻaṟṟa – to hum; niḻal tudaindu – giving shade to those beetles; mandāram ninṟu maṇam malgum – mandāra trees blossoming in all seasons and spreading abundant fragrance; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; maṇi mādak kōyil – tirumaṇimādak kōyil; en mananē – Oh my heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are having the true nature of being eternal and having self-illuminating knowledge! Oh you who are incomprehensible! Oh you who incarnated as nara and nārāyaṇa! Oh you, my lord, who are having divine form which matches a dark, great cloud! The dēvatās come and stand on earth, saying “For us ,who are favourable and have no other refuge than you, you should mercifully give your grace”, in the abode tirumaṇimādak kōyil in tirunāngūr,  where they will sing stōtrams etc and surrender; in this abode, mandāra trees blossom in all seasons and spread abundant fragrance, give shade to beetles for them to sing rāgas such as dēva gāndāri etc in all directions and to hum in the surroundings after drinking honey. Oh my heart! Surrender unto that abode.

*nandā viḷakkē* – Oh heart! You go and enjoy tirumaṇimādak kōyil where brahmā et al pray,saying “You should fulfil our desires” – says āḻvār.

*nandā viḷakkē* – Perennial lamp. Lamp implies both light and the one (lamp) who emits the light. Implies – emperumān is having svarūpam (true nature) which is eternal and self-illuminating.

*aḷattaṟku ariyāy* – Oh you who are incomprehensible due to your vibhutvam (omnipresence) and auspicious qualities, wealth etc! kūrattāḻvān would say that āḻvār is saying the equivalent of taittirīya upaniśat “*satyam jñānam anantam brahma*” (brahmam which is eternal, knowledgeable and endless). Such emperumān revealed himself through the incarnations of nara and nārāyaṇa.

*karu mā mugil pōl endāy* – The enjoyable form in those incarnations. Alternatively – oh you who showed your rejuvenating form which is more attractive than the previously said qualities, and made us exclusively exist for you!

*emakkē aruḷāy …* – The abode where dēvatās would come and sing praises and surrender unto you saying “Instead of seeing your common relationship with us and asuras as said in jitantē stōtram 2 ‘dēvānām dānavānām sāmānyam atidaivatam’ (emperumān is equal towards celestial people and demoniac people), you should help us who are without refuge and shower your mercy instead of helping asuras”.

*ettisaiyum …* – andēn – beautiful beetles which are known as tēn.  They drink the honey and hum the tune named kandāram everywhere.

*mādē …* – In that surrounding, the beetles which are enjoying joyfully due to the togetherness.

*miḻaṟṟa* – singing with sweet, childish words.

*niḻal tudaindu* – making shade for those beetles to let them enjoy; like those who would make shelters for singers. mandāra – a type of kalpaka vrukśa (tree). Remaining in all seasons and spreading fragrance. *maṇam malgum* is also recited as *maṇam nalgum* . Implies, it is giving fragrant materials, just as those who give gifts to singers. āḻvār is telling his heart “Go and surrender unto such tirumaṇimādak kōyil in tirunāngūr”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.2. Mudalait tanima

*mudalait tanimā muraṇ tīra anṟu mudunīr tadattuc cengaṇ vēḻam uyya vidalait talaic cenṟadaṟkē udavi vinai tīrtta ammānidam viṇṇaṇavum padalaik kabōdattoḷi māda neṟṟip pavaḷak koḻungāla paingāl puravam madalait talai men pedai kūdu nāngūr maṇi mādak kōyil vaṇangen mananē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – At that time; mudu nīr – having ancient water; tadattu – in the pond (grabbing the elephant’s foot); tani mā mudalai – the matchless big crocodile’s; muraṇ tīra – to eliminate the endless strength; sem kaṇ vēḻam – the elephant which has reddish eyes due to anger; uyya – to be freed; vidalait talaic cenṟu – arriving during the sorrowful times; adaṟkē udavi – helping that elephant; vinai tīrtta – one who eliminated its sorrow; ammān – sarvēśvaran’s; idam – being the abode; viṇ aṇavum – touching the heaven; padalai – kalaśas (pot like structures); kabōdam – pigeon holes; oḷi – having the shine of gems which were embossed; māda neṟṟi – on the balconies; pavaḷak koḻum kāla – like the well-grown feet of corals; paingāl puṟavam – pigeon which is having greenish feet; madalait talai – atop the short pillars; men pedai – with the female pigeon which is tender by nature; kūdum – residing together; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; maṇi mādak kōyil – tirumaṇimādak kōyil; en mananē – Oh my heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār says “Oh heart! The one who eliminated the danger for śrī gajēndrāḻvān is mercifully standing in tirumaṇimādak kōyil. You go and worship him there to eliminate all of your sorrows”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

During the sorrowful times for the elephant which had reddish eyes due to its anger and which was caught by the matchless, big crocodile, sarvēśvaran arrived at the ancient pond to eliminate the endless strength of the crocodile and free the elephant; being the abode of such sarvēśvaran, tiru maṇi mādak kōyil in tirunāngūr which has mansions where the kalaśa (pot like structures) and pigeon holes are planted in the balconies and where the pigeon which is having greenish feet, which are like the well-grown feet of corals, is standing atop the short pillars, residing along with the the female pigeon which is tender by nature; oh my heart! surrender unto such divyadēśam.

*mudalai …* – To eliminate the matchless and endless strength of the crocodile.

*mudu nīrt tadattu* – It is well known that ocean has ancient water.

*sem kaṇ vēḻam uyya* – Though elephant is strong, since the pond is not the natural habitat for it, it could not act with its strength; hence it became angry and its eyes turned reddish. To free such elephant. *sem kaṇ* – also implies the elephant which has reddish eyes being unable to protect itself.

*senṟu* – Instead of abandoning thinking it’s gone, going and helping during dangerous times.

*vidalait talai* – While suffering.

*vinai tīrtta ammān idam* – The abode of the one who eliminated its sorrow. Eliminating the sorrow implies presenting himself to it to let it serve the flower at his lotus feet as it desired.

*viṇ aṇavum …* – Being tall to reach heaven, having rows of kalaśas and pigeonholes, the mansions are shining due to being built using gold and gems; they have forehead – in the structures which have the face of tiger; padalai – row of kalaśas.

*pavaḷak koḻum kāla paim kāl puṟavam* – Having well grown feet which are reddish like coral, the pigeons which are greenish.

*madalait talai* – Atop the short pillars (which are on top of the tall pillars).

*men padai kūdum* – In tirunāngūr where the male pigeon is residing with the female pigeon which is too tender to even bear the union with it.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.3. Kolaippun

*kolaippuṇ talaik kunṟam onṟu uyya anṟu kodumā mudalaikku idar seydu kongār ilaip puṇḍarīgattavaḷ inbam anbōdu aṇainditta ammānidam āḷariyāl alaippuṇḍa yānai maruppum agilum aṇimuttum veṇsāmaraiyōdu ponni malaippaṇḍam aṇḍat tiraiyundu nāngūr maṇimādak kōyil vaṇangu en mananē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – At the time; kolai – the act of killng; puṇ talai – having a wounded head due to being poked by the mahout; kunṟam onṟu – gajēndrāḻvān who is like a huge mountain; uyya – to be freed; kodu mā mudalaikku – for the crocodile (which grabbed its foot) which is cruel and very strong; idar seydu – caused sorrow; kongu ilai Ar – having a lot of honey and leaves; puṇḍarīgattavaḷ – periya pirāttiyār who is residing in lotus flower, her; inbam – the joy of union; anbōdu aṇainditta – enjoying with great affection; ammān – lord of all, his; idam – being the abode; ponni – kāvēri; āḷ ariyāl – by lions which are manly; alaippuṇḍa – destroyed; yānai – elephants’; maruppum – tusks; agilum – agaru (kind of fragrant) trees; aṇimuttum – beautiful pearls; veṇ sāmaraiyōdu – with whitish cāmara (covry; fly-whisk); malaip paṇḍam aṇḍa – all other materials from the mountain; tirai undu – pushing with the tides and giving; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; maṇi mādak kōyil – tirumaṇimādak kōyil; en mananē – Oh my heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**As emperumān eliminates the crocodile, the enemy of śrī gajēndrāḻvān, pirātti embraces him as she did during karavada (the vanquishing of kara); such emperumān mercifully stood in tirumaṇimādak kōyil; oh heart! You go and enjoy him there,**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

At the time when gajēndrāḻvān who was like a huge mountain, engaged in the act of killing and having a wounded head due to being poked by the mahout, was suffering, to have him freed, emperumān caused sorrow to the crocodile (which grabbed its foot) which is cruel and very strong; tirumaṇimādak kōyil in tirunāngūr is the abode of such lord of all, who enjoys with great affection, the joy of union with periya pirāttiyār who is residing in lotus flower which is having a lot of honey and leaves; oh my heart! Surrender unto this divyadēśam where kāvēri river is pushing with the tides and yielding the tusks of elephants destroyed by the manly lions, agaru trees, beautiful pearls with fly-whisk and all other materials from the mountain.

*kolaip puṇ talaik kunṟam onṟu* – being engaged in the act of killing and having a raw wounded head, there is an elephant which is like mountain – śrī gajēndrāḻvān. Wounded because of the poking by the mahout using the hook; or wounded by the fight with other elephants since it is a wild elephant; or it is said by āḻvār since this is a natural quality of elephants (to have wounded head).

*uyya* – To be freed from its sorrows when it was inflicted with pain.

*kodu mā mudalaikku idar seydu* – Causing sorrow for the crocodile which is cruel and very strong.

*kongār …* – Just as a father who would eliminate the sorrow of the children and seek solace from the mother.

*kongu Ar …* – kongu – honey or fragrance. Being filled with honey.

*ilaip puṇḍarīgattu* – Having the lotus flower which has rejuvenating leaf, as abode.

*avaḷ inbam …* – The abode of sarvēśvara who enjoyed the joy of periya pirāttiyār’s embrace, with his love.

*āḷari …* – The manly lions will catch the elephants and kill them; alaikkai – killing. At that time, the flooded river will arrive and pluck the tusks of the elephants and carry them.

*agilum aṇi muttum* – Carrying the pearls which fell from the heads of the elephants and the whitish fly-whisks.

*ponni …* – kāvēri will bring the enlisted and non-enlisted items from the mountain and will hand them over with its tides, just as those who generate wealth; such tirunāngūr.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.4. Siraiyar

*siṟaiyār uvaṇappuḷ onṟu ēṟi anṟu tisai nāngum nāngum iriyac ceruvil kaṟaiyār neduvēl arakkar madiyak kadal sūḻ ilangai kadandān idandān muṟaiyāl vaḷarkkinṟa muttīyar nālvēdar aivēḷvi āṟangar ēḻin isaiyōr maṟaiyōr vaṇangap pugaḻ eydu nāngūr maṇimādak kōyil vaṇangu en mananē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – At the time when cruelty was abundant; siṟai – wings which help to fly; Ar – present without any shortcoming; onṟu – matchless; uvaṇap puḷ – on garudāḻvār who is known as periya tiruvadi; ēṟi – climbed and mercifully arrived; seruvil – opposed in the battle; kaṟaiyār – complete with stains; nedu vēl – having long spear; arakkar – rākśasas; tisai nāngum nāngum – in eight directions; iriya – to make (some) run; madiya – to kill (some); kadal sūḻ – fortified by ocean; ilangai – the town, lankā; kadandān – emperumān who won over, his; idam – being the abode; muṟaiyāl – by the methods explained in vēdam; vaḷarkkinṟa – performing hōmam (fire sacrifice; oblation); muttīyar – those who have three fires; nāl vēdar – those who are well versed in four vēdams; aivēḷvi āṟu angar – those who are endowed with five great oblations and six ancillary subjects of vēdam; ēḻin isaiyōr – those who truly know the seven svaras (tunes); maṟaiyōr – distinguished brāhmaṇas; vaṇanga – due to surrendering with offering obeisances; pugaḻ eydum – acquiring great fame; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; maṇi mādak kōyil – tirumaṇimādak kōyil; en mananē – Oh my heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār says “sarvēśvaran who defeated rākśasas like māli, sumāli et al is mercifully standing in tirumaṇimādak kōyil; oh heart! You go there and enjoy him”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

At the time when cruelty was abundant, emperumān climbed on the matchless garudāḻvār who is known as periya tiruvadi, and has wings which help him fly and are present without any shortcoming, and mercifully arrived to make the rākśasas who have long spears which are completely stained with the blood of those who opposed them, run in eight directions and to kill some of them, and won over lankā, the town fortified by ocean. Oh my heart! Surrender unto such emperumān’s abode tirumaṇimādak kōyil in tirunāngūr which has acquired great fame due to the surrender preceded by offering of obeisances by distinguished brāhmaṇas who perform fire oblations by the methods explained in vēdam, with the three types of fire (gārhapatya, āhavanīya, dakśiṇāgni), who are well versed in four vēdams, who are endowed with five great sacrifices and six ancillary subjects of vēdam and who truly know the seven svaras.

*siṟai Ar uvaṇappuḷ* – siṟai – wing. Having wings which help in movement, without any shortcoming.

*uvaṇappuḷ* – The bird named uvaṇam. uvaṇam is a name for periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār).

*onṟu ēṟi* – Climbing on that distinguished bird.

*tisai nāngum nāngum iriya* – To have them run away in eight directions.

*seruvil* – In the battle.

*kaṟai Ar …* – To destroy the clan of rākśasas who carry long spears which cannot be washed of their stains. Some run away and some die.

*kadal sūḻ …* – He defeated lankā which is surrounded by ocean and is always filled with evil entities just as anthill will never cease to host snakes. It is said that emperumān climbed on garudāḻvār and defeated māli, sumāli, mālyavān et al.

*kadandān idam tān* – The abode of the one who won over lankā.

*muṟaiyāl …* – Aptly; or as said in vēdam, those who have three types of agni (fire) and raise them.

*nāl vēdar* – Those brāhmaṇas who sustain the four vēdams in the same manner; those who properly perform panca mahā yajñams (five great oblations) etc and are experts in six ancillary subjects of vēdam, and sapta svarams.

*vaṇanga …* – tirunāngūr which has the fame of being surrendered by such distinguished personalities.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.5. Ilaiyadu

*iḻaiyādu kongait talai nanjam uṇḍittu iḷanganṟu koṇḍu viḷangāy eṟindu taḻai vāda vantāḷ kurundam osittut tadandāmaraip poygai pukkān idandān kuḻaiyāda vallik kulamāda mādē kuyil kūva nīdu kodi mādam malgu maḻaiyādu sōlai mayilālu nāngūr maṇimādak kōyil vaṇangu en mananē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

iḻai – ornaments; ādu – swaying; kongait talai – in the pūtanā’s bosom tips; nanjam – poison; uṇḍittu – consumed; viḷangāy – on the demon who stood as the wood apple; iḷam kanṟu koṇḍu – lifted up the demon who came as the young calf; eṟindu – threw to kill both of them; van tāḷ – having strong roots; kurundam – kurunda tree; taḻai vāda – to make its branches wither; osittu – broke; tadam – vast; tāmaraip poygai – in lotus pond; pukkān – kriṣṇa who went and stole the clothes of the gōpikā girls, his; idam – being the abode; kuḻai – sprouts of trees; Ada – as they sway (due to the soft breeze); vallik kulam – the collection of creepers (which spread on those branches); Ada – to sway; mādu – in the surroundings; kuyil – cuckoos; kūva – to sing; maḻai ādu – where the clouds are roaming; sōlai – in the garden; mayil Alum – peacocks dance; nīdu – tall; kodi – flags planted; mādam – mansions; malgum – are present closely to each other; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; maṇi mādak kōyil – tirumaṇimādak kōyil; en mananē – Oh my heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār says “Oh heart! The one who eliminated the enemies and enjoyed together with covherd girls is mercifully standing in tirumaṇimādak kōyil. You surrender unto that abode”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa consumed the poison in the pūtanā’s bosom tips where ornaments are swaying; he lifted up the demon who came as a young calf and threw it on the demon who stood as wood apple to kill both of them; he broke kurunda tree having strong roots, to make its branches wither; he went to the vast lotus pond and stole the clothes of the gōpikā girls. Oh my heart! Surrender unto such tirumaṇimādak kōyil in tirunāngūr which is his abode where sprouts of trees sway to cause the collection of creepers to sway, the cuckoos in the surroundings sing, the peacocks dance in the garden where clouds are roaming and where mansions which have tall flags planted on them, are present closely to each other.

*iḻai ādu …* – iḻai – ornaments. Consumed the poison on the tip of the bosoms which are decorated with ornaments. As pūtanā changes her demoniac appearance to resemble yaśōdāp pirātti, her bosoms were decorated with ornaments. He consumed the milk from those bosoms.

*iḷam kanṟu …* – He used the demon who stood as a calf and threw him on the demon who stood as wood apple and made them kill each other.

*taḻai …* – The tree was lively due to being possessed by a demon; as he went close to it, its branches withered; he broke the kurunda tree which had strong roots.

*tadam tāmarai …* – As kāḷiya, the snake entered the pond which was fit for water-sports for him and the gōpikās and poisoned it, he went and entered it; alternative explanation – in the pond which has sufficient space to let the girls play and was having lotus flowers, he stole their clothes. The abode of such emperumān.

*kuḻai …* – As the branches and flower creepers sway,

*mādē kuyil kūva* – The cuckoos sucked the fragrance in the flowers which are present in the garden in the surroundings.

*nīdu kodi māda malgu* – Being densely populated with mansions which have tall flags.

*maḻai ādu sōlai mayil ālu nāngūr* – As the clouds travel just above the tall garden, the peacocks start dancing on seeing them. In such tirunāngūr.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.6. Pan ner

*paṇ nēr moḻi āycciyar anja vanjap paguvāyk kaḻudukku irangādu avaḷ tan uṇṇā mulai maṟṟavaḷ āviyōdum udanē suvaittānidam ōngu paindāḷ kaṇṇār karumbin kaḻai tinṟu vaigik kaḻunīril mūḻgic ceḻunīrt tadattu maṇṇēndu iḷamēdigaḷ vaigu nāngūr maṇimādak kōyil vaṇangu en mananē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇ nēr – matching a song; moḻi – having speech; āycciyar – covherd girls; anja – to fear; vanjam – deceit of coming in mother’s form; pagu vāy – having huge mouth; kaḻudukku – in pūtanā (the demon); irangādu – without him suffering; avaḷ than – her; uṇṇā – due to being poisoned, none other could consume; mulai – breast milk; maṟṟu – further; avaḷ āviyōdum – with her life; udanē suvaittān – kriṣṇa who mercifully consumed simultaneously, his; idam – being the abode; iḷa mēdigaḷ – buffalo calves; ōngu – tallness; paim tāḷ – greenish bottoms; kaṇ Ar – having narrow joints; karumbin – sugarcanes’; kaḻai tinṟu – eating the shoots; vaigi – stayed in the same place for some time; kaḻu nīril – in the water-body with sengaḻunīr (purple Indian water lily) flowers; mūḻgi – entered and immersed; seḻu nīrt tadattu – immersed in the pond having beautiful water; maṇ ēndu – holding mud on horns; vaigum – remaining there without climbing on the shore; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; maṇi mādak kōyil – tirumaṇimādak kōyil; en mananē – Oh my heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**Oh heart! Go and enjoy sarvēśvaran who consumed from the bosom of pūtanā to kill at once, and who is mercifully standing in tirumaṇimādak kōyil.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

To create fear among the covherd girls, whose speech resembles song, pūtanā came in a huge form, with the deceit of coming in kriṣṇa’s mother’s form; without any suffering, he mercifully consumed her breast milk, which could not be consumed by anyone due to their being poisoned, along with her life. Oh my heart! Surrender unto tirumaṇimādak kōyil in tirunāngūr which is the abode of such kriṣṇa, where buffalo calves ate the shoots of tall sugarcanes which have greenish bottoms and narrow joints, stayed there for some time, entered and remained immersed in the water-body for sometime, and then immersed in the pond with beautiful water, held the mud and remained there without climbing on the shore

*paṇ nēr moḻi āycciyar anja* – To create fear in the covherd girls whose speech resembles song.

*vanjam …* – Having deceitful nature, fearsome huge mouth as per her demoniac birth, kaḻudu – ghost/demon. Not fearing it. Not fearing implies not suffering. That is, not suffering in its hands.

*avaḷ than uṇṇā mulai* – Since it has poison, there is none who can consume; such bosom.

*maṟṟu avaḷ āviyōdum udanē suvaittān* – The abode where emperumān who not just mercifully sucked the poison but also the life which sustains it, simultaneously.

*ōngu paim tāḷ …* – śugarcanes which are tall, greenish, have strong feet \[roots\] with narrow joints. Remaining there \[young buffaloes\], consuming those; and due to consuming more than its capacity, being unable to roam around, rested there in that same place and subsequently went and immersed in the pond which has sengaḻunīr flowers to eliminate their heat.

*seḻu nīr …* – Entered a pond with beautiful water and immersed in it, carrying the mud on their horns and playing with it; just as mahā varāham (the great varāhap perumāḷ) rose.

*vaigu nāngūr …* – Subsequently, being unable to push themselves \[out of the pond\], they remained there itself. In such tirunāngūr.

piḷḷai viḻupparaiyar and āppān recited this portion of the pāsuram, and asked bhattar “There is vaigi (remained) in both places. Why do they do like that?” bhattar mercifully explained “Due to their tender nature, they rested in both places”.

## 3.8.7. Talaik kattavil

*taḷaik kattaviḻ tāmarai vaigu poygait tadam pukku adangā vidangāl aravam iḷaikkat tiḷaittittu adan ucci tan mēl adi vaitta ammānidam māmadiyam tiḷaikkum kodi māḷigai sūḻ teruvil seḻumuttu veṇṇeṟkenac cenṟu munṟil vaḷaikkai nuḷaip pāvaiyar māṟu nāngūr maṇimādak kōyil vaṇangu en mananē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

taḷait tāmarai – unblossomed lotus flower; kattu aviḻ tāmarai – blossomed lotus flower; vaigu – present; poygait tadam – in the pond; pukku – entered; adangā – (inside that) without remaining submissive, rising; vidam kāl – ejecting poison; aravam – kāḷiyan (the snake); iḷaikka – to become weak; tiḷaittittu – played (with it); adan ucci than mēl – on its head; adi vaitta – placed the divine feet and eliminated its pride; ammān – sarvēśvaran’s; idam – being the abode; vaḷaikkai – having hands which are decorated with bangles; nuḷaip pāvaiyar – tribal girls \[fisher folk\]; mā madiyam – the moon; tiḷaikkum – (being unable to cross) to play there; kodi – having flags; māḷigai sūḻ – surrounded by mansions; teruvil – in the streets; seḻu muttu – huge pearls; veṇ neṟku – for white paddy; ena – saying that they are bartering and going; munṟil – in front of everyone’s house; senṟu māṟum – voluntarily going and exchanging; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; maṇi mādak kōyil – tirumaṇimādak kōyil; en mananē – Oh my heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār says “emperumān who eliminated the danger caused by kāḷiyan is mercifully standing in tirumaṇimādak kōyil. Oh heart! You go and enjoy him there”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In the pond where unblossomed and blossomed lotus flowers are present, sarvēśvaran entered and played with kāḷiyan who rose, without remaining submissive and ejected poison; to make kāḷiyan weak, he played with it to weaken it and placed his divine feet on its head and eliminated its pride. Oh my heart! Surrender unto tirumaṇimādak kōyil in tirunāngūr which is the abode of such sarvēśvaran where fisher girls, whose hands are decorated with bangles, are going on the streets which are surrounded by mansions having flags and where the moon is playing, saying that they are bartering white paddy for huge pearls and eventually voluntarily going in front of everyone’s house and exchanging the materials.

*taḷaik kattaviḻ tāmarai vaigu poygai* – unblossomed lotus flower and blossomed lotus flower; entering the banks of the pond where unblossomed lotus flower and blossomed lotus flower are present; or entering the pond.

*adangā vidam kāl aravam* – not being submissive and rising, spittinging poison, a snake was there – kāḷiyan; acted to weaken it by playing with it; he placed his divine feet, which were prayed for by āḻvārs to be placed on their heads as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.3.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/11/thiruvaimozhi-10-3-6-adichchiyom/) “*adicciyōm talai misai nī aṇiyāy*” (Place your divine feet on our heads), on such snake’s head.

*ammān idam* – The abode of such sarvēśvaran who protects in all ways.

*mā madiyam …* – The moon who is roaming around to protect the world, being caught in flags, remained there and would play with those flags; in the streets which are surrounded by mansions which have such flags

*seḻu muttu veṇ neṟkena* – They \[the pearl maercants\] said “Whatever paddy you give is acceptable; these are beautiful pearls”.

*veṇ neṟkena* – They said “Red paddy is not required; white paddy is sufficient”.

*senṟu* – Due to the abundance of pearls remaining, they will go door to door and sell those. munṟil – Entrance.

*vaḷaik kai nuḷaip pāvaiyar māṟum* – Just as the covherd girls will decorate themselves and churn curd, the fisher girls too would decorate themselves and go to sell the pearls; in tirunāngūr, where the decorated, tribal girls are roaming around to sell pearls.

## 3.8.8. Tulaiyar

*tuḷaiyār karumen kuḻal āycciyar tam tugil vāriyum siṟṟil sidaittum muṟṟā iḷaiyār viḷaiyāttodu kādal veḷḷam viḷaivitta ammānidam vēl nedungaṇ muḷaivāḷ eyiṟṟu madavār payiṟṟu moḻi kēttu irundu mudirāda insol vaḷaivāya kiḷḷai maṟai pādu nāngūr maṇimādak kōyil vaṇangu en mananē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuḷai Ar – Having big hole (due to the curls); karu men kuḻal – having black, soft hair; āycciyar tam – the covherd girls’; tugil vāriyum – stealing their clothes; siṟṟil sidaittum – destroying their small (play) houses; muṟṟā iḷaiyār – not attained youth; viḷaiyāttodu – the childish sports with such girls who are in their childhood; kādal veḷḷam – ocean of love (for them); viḷaivitta – caused; ammān idam – being the abode of sarvēśvaran; mudirāda in sol – sweet words which are not hard; vaḷai vāya – having curved mouth; kiḷḷai – parrots; vēl – sharp like spear; nedum kaṇ – wide eyes; muḷai – in budding stage; vāḷ – having radiance; eyiṟu – having teeth; madavār – vaidika girls; payiṟṟu – words from vēdam; kēttu irundu – hearing those (subsequently as they chanted); maṟai pādum – chanting vēdam; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; maṇi mādak kōyil – tirumaṇimādak kōyil; en mananē – Oh my heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār says “Oh heart! kriṣṇa, who enjoyed endless union with the girls from tiruvāyppādi, is mercifully standing in tirumaṇimādak kōyil. You go and enjoy him there”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran played childish sports with covherd girls who are having black, soft hair with big holes (due to the curls), who are in their childhood and not attained youth yet, caused ocean of love for them towards him. Oh my heart! Surrender unto such emperumn in the abode tirumaṇimādak kōyil in tirunāngūr where the parrots, having sweet words which are not hard and curved mouth, chant words from vēdam after hearing them from the vaidika girls who are having wide eyes which are sharp like spear and radiant teeth which are in budding stage.

*tuḷaiyār karu men kuḻal āycciyar tam* – tuḷaiyār – having lot of holes. That is, having curly, black, soft hair, the covherd girls, who are at the \[very young\] age, will bathe in the river, placing their clothes on the banks. It can also be said as “*tuḷaiyā niṟkiṟa*” (those who are playing).

*tugil vāriyum siṟṟil sidaittum* – Gathering all their clothes which were placed on the banks and climbing on the kurunda tree to be requested by them as in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 3.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/05/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-3-simple/) “*masimaiyilee! kūṟai tārāy*” (Oh shameless one! Give our clothes” and destroying their play houses as said in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 2.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/05/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-2-simple/) “*tīmai seyyum sirīdarā! engaḷ siṟṟil vandu sidaiyēlē”* (Oh who indulges in mischievous acts and who is the consort of śrī mahālakśmi! Do not come to our place to destroy our little sand houses).

*muṟṟā iḷaiyār viḷaiyāttodu* – Those who are at an age where they cannot be engaged in anything but playing. The age where youth is not yet manifested; the playing which occurred with them.

*kādal …* – The abode of sarvēśvaran who caused an ocean of love in them towards him.

*vēl nedum kaṇ …* – The women who have spear like sharp, wide eyes, and budding, radiant teeth.

*payiṟṟum moḻi kēttu irundum* – They would teach words like “Kiss me”, though the parrots have heard those words.

*mudirāda …* – The parrot has soft, sweet words since their tone has not matured, and curved mouth .

*maṟai pādum* – It will chant the vēdams which it is used to; since the residents of the town keep reciting vēdams these parrots are also used to them; hence it is said that as they are chanting, these parrots are also chanting. Alternatively – since these girls are daughters of teachers who teach vēdam, these girls chant the words from vēdam and the parrots repeat the same.

*mudirāda in sol* – The speech of the parrots are \[youthful and hence\] unlike that of those who teach vēdam; such tirunāngūr.

## 3.8.9. Vidaiyoda

*vidaiyōda venṟu āycci men tōḷ nayanda vigirdā! viḷangu sudar āḻi ennum padaiyōdu sangonṟu udaiyāy! ena ninṟu imaiyōr paravum idam paindadattup pedaiyōdu sengāla annam tugaippat togaip puṇḍarīgattidaic cengaḻunīr madaiyōda ninṟu madu vimmu nāngūr maṇimādak kōyil vaṇangu en mananē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vidai – seven bulls; ōda – to run away and die; venṟu – winning (those); āycci – nappinnaip pirātti’s; men tōḷ – embracing of tender shoulders; nayanda – desired; vigirdā – Oh one who has distinguished acts!; viḷangu – shining; sudar – having radiance; āḻi ennum padaiyōdu – with the weapon tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); onṟu sangu udaiyāy – Oh one who has the distinguished śrī pāncajanyam!; ena ninṟu – saying this; imaiyōr – dēvatās such as brahmā et al; paravum – continuously praising; idam – being the abode; pedaiyōdu – with female swan; sem kāla – having reddish feet; annam – swan (due to drinking honey, being unable to see next steps); paim tadattu – in the beautiful pond; togaip puṇḍarīkam – gathered lotus flowers; tugaippa – as they stomp (due to that); idai – present in between those lotus flowers; sengaḻunīr – sengaḻunīr flowers \[purple Indian water lily\]; madai ōda – though the canals are filled and flowing; ninṟu madu vimmum – the flood of honey from inside is flowing; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; maṇi mādak kōyil – tirumaṇimādak kōyil; en mananē – Oh my heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār says “emperumān is mercifully standing in tirumaṇimādak kōyil to be praised by dēvatās highlighting his acts of killing the seven bulls for nappinnaip pirātti and his beautiful holding of the divine weapons. Oh heart! You go and enjoy him there”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh my heart! Surrender unto tirumaṇimādak kōyil in tirnāngūr which is the abode where dēvatās such as brahmā et al are constantly praising saying “Oh one who has distinguished acts who desired to embrace the tender shoulders of nappinnaip pirātti by winning the seven bulls by making them run away and die! Oh one who has the radiantly shining tiruvāḻi  as the weapon and the distinguished śrī pāncajanyam!”; there, as the male swan having reddish feet along with its female swan stomps on the gathered lotus flowers, the sengaḻunīr flowers which are present in between those lotus flowers, start flooding the honey from inside into the canals though the canals are filled and flowing.

*vidai ōda* – Winning the bulls, which were hurdles for his union with nappinnaip pirātti, to make them run away

*āycci men tōḷ nayanda vigirdā* – Oh who has the distinguished act of desiring her tender shoulders!

*viḷangu …* – Oh one who is having the distinguished śrī pāncajanyam along with the weapon tiruvāḻi which is having radiance and which is contrasting your divine complexion!

*ena ninṟu* – Saying in this manner.

*imaiyōr paravum idam* – The abode where dēvatās such as brahmā et al are continuously praising.

*paim tadam …* – The male swan entered the beautiful ponds to drink the honey; as it entered along with its spouse, due to drinking the honey, being unable to see the next steps, it is unable to preserve the lotus flowers which is its abode; the  flowers get stomped due to that.

*togai …* – In between the gathered lotus flowers, the honey flooding from the sengaḻunīr flower is flowing out and reaching the canals which are already filled, due to having too much of it. As the swans stomp in between the dense lotus flowers, the sengaḻunīr flower will create  a flood of honey. In such tirnāngūr.
