## 3.8.10. Vandar polil

*vaṇḍār poḻil sūḻndu aḻagāya nāngūr maṇimādak kōyil nedumālukku enṟum toṇḍāya tol sīr vayal mangaiyar kōn kaliyan olisey tamiḻ mālai vallār kaṇḍār vaṇangak kaḷiyānai mīdē kadal sūḻ ulagukku oru kāvalarāy viṇ tōy nedu veṇkudai nīḻalin kīḻ viri nīr ulagāṇḍu virumbuvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu Ar – Having abundance of beetles; poḻil sūḻndu – surrounded by gardens; aḻagāya – beautiful; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; maṇi mādak kōyil – eternally residing in tirumaṇimādak kōyil; nedu mālukku – for sarvēśvaran; enṟum toṇḍāya – acquired due to engaging in eternal kainkaryam; tol sīr – having endless wealth; vayal mangaiyar kōn – the king of tirumangai region which is surrounded by fertile fields; kaliyan – āḻvār; oli sey – mercifully spoke; tamiḻ mālai vallār – those who can willingly learn these ten pāsurams which are like garlands; kaṇḍār vaṇanga – to be bowed down at their divine feet by those who saw them; kaḷi yānai mīdē – being seated on intoxicated elephant and coming on a procession; kadal sūḻ ulagaukku – the earth which is surrounded by four oceans; oru kāvalarāy – being the independent controller; viṇ tōy – going up to sky; nedu veṇ kudai nīḻalin kīḻ – remaining under the shade of pearl umbrella; viri nīr ulagāṇḍu – ruling over the brahmāṇḍam (universe of brahmā) which is surrounded by āvaraṇa jalam (layer of water); viirumbuvar – will remain endlessly joyful

**Перевод:**

**This pāsuram identifies the benefit for those who learn this decad.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār who is the king of tirumangai region, which is surrounded by fertile fields, and is having endless wealth which was acquired due to engaging in eternal kainkaryam for sarvēśvaran who is eternally residing in tirumaṇimādak kōyil in beautiful tirunāngūr which is surrounded by gardens with abundance of beetles, mercifully spoke these pāsurams. Those who can willingly learn these ten pāsurams which are like garlands, will be the independent controller of the earth which is surrounded by four oceans, will be seated on intoxicated elephant and go on a procession, to be bowed down at their divine feet by those who saw them; remaining under the shade of pearl umbrella which is going up to the sky, ruling over the brahmāṇḍam (universe of brahmā) which is surrounded by āvaraṇa jalam (layer of water), they will remain endlessly joyful.

*vaṇḍār poḻil sūḻndu* – It is a garden for name sake only and will be filled with beetles which enter to drink the honey.

*aḻagāya …* –  For sarvēśvaran who is eternally residing in tirumaṇimādak kōyil in the beautiful tirunāngūr.

*enṟum toṇḍāya tol sīr* – Having endless wealth due to being engaged in eternal kainkarayam.

*vayal mangaiyar kōn* – tirumangai āḻvār who is the king of tirumangai region which has good fertile fields.

*oli sey tamiḻ mālai vallār* – Those who have learnt this decad which is a garland of tamiḻ words, which was mercifully spoken with tune.

*kaṇḍār vaṇanga* – Without any distinction among favourable, unfavourable and neutral persons, climbing on an elephant in exult, to have the whole world coming and falling down at their feet.

*kadal sūḻ ulagukkuk kāvalarāy* – Being born in kśatriya birth, being the independent controller of the earth which is surrounded by four oceans.

*viṇ tōy …* – Remaining under a pearl umbrella which can reach up to the sky, ruling over the earth which is surrounded by ocean, will be desired by all; will have endless joy.

nanjīyar asked bhattar “Why is āḻvār highlighting worldly wealth as the benefit?” bhattar mercifully said “tirumangai āḻvār thinks ‘Even if it is īśvaran, he can be born and be crowned once, if the kingdom can be made to be subservient to bhāgavatas’ ”

## 3.9 Salam konda

## 3.9.1. Salam konda

*salangoṇḍa iraṇiyanadu agal mārvam kīṇḍu tadangadalaik kadaindu amudam koṇḍu uganda kāḷai nalangoṇḍa karumugil pōl tirumēni ammān nāḷdōṟum magiḻndu inidu maruvi uṟai kōyil salangoṇḍu malar soriyum malligai oṇ serundi saṇbagangaḷ maṇa nāṟum vaṇpoḻilin ūdē valangoṇḍu kayalōdi viḷaiyādu nāngūr vaigunda viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

salam koṇḍa – having anger (towards prahlādan); iraṇiyan – hiraṇyan’s; adu – built by the strength of the boons; agal mārvam – wide chest; kīṇḍu – effortlessly tore; tadam kadalai – the huge tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean); kadaindu – churned; amudam – the nectar which came out of it; koṇḍu – distributed it to dēvatās; uganda – one who became happy; kāḷai – being youthful; nalam koṇḍa – beautiful; karu mugil pōl – like a dark cloud; tirumēni ammān – sarvēśvaran who has a divine form; nādōṟum – everyday; magiḻndu – with joy; inidu – to be sweet for the devotees; maruvi uṟai kōyil – eternally residing without any other expectation; kayal – the kayal fish (which cannot survive outside water); ōdi – running away from the water which is its habitat; salam koṇḍu malar soṟiyum – competing with each other and showering flowers; oṇ malligai serundi senbagangaḷ – beautiful jasmine, serundi and campak flowers; maṇam nāṟum – spreading fragrance; vaṇ – rich; poḻilinūdē – in the garden; vaḷam koṇḍu viḷaiyādum – playing joyfully (due to breathing in that fragrance); nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; vaigunda viṇṇagaram – vaigunda viṇṇagaram; vaṇangu – worship; mada nenjē – Oh humble heart!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who has a divine form which resembles beautiful dark cloud, effortlessly tore the angry hiraṇyan’s wide chest which was built by the strength of boons and is the youthful one who became happy  after churning the huge tiruppāṟkadal and distributing the nectar which came out of it to dēvatās; everyday he is joyfully and eternally residing without any other expectation, to be sweet for his devotees, in vaigunda viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr. Oh humble heart! Worship such abode where kayal fish is running away from the water which is its habitat and playing joyfully in the rich garden where beautiful jasmine, serundi and campaka flowers are competing with each other and spreading fragrance.

*salam koṇḍa* … – hiraṇya was made of anger. emperumān showed his anger and softened the angry hiraṇya’s strong, wide chest which was strengthened by the boons, and then tore it effortlessly. He comprehended and churned the ocean which cannot be comprehended by anyone as if it is a small lowly object, extracting the nectar which is the good life in that ocean \[distributed it to dēvatās\] and thought “We got to fulfil the task for the dēvatās who surrendered unto us” and acquired the joy which would be acquired by those who received that nectar, and is not having the old-age etc which will be eliminated for those dēvatās.

*nalam koṇḍa …* – He is having such a beautiful form to make us say “throw that nectar to the dogs”. As said in mēghasandēśam 1-5 “*dūmajyōti*:” (mixture of smoke and fire), since the cloud which is a mixture of multiple entities is not a match for his divine form, he can be said to be having divine form which is similar to a cloud which has distinguished beauty and is rejuvenating, and due to that he appears to be praised as “He is the sarvēśvaran”. Since emperumān is eternally residing here with great joy due to being present in advance since it will not possible to destroy hiraṇya when danger occurs and then churn the ocean.

*salam koṇḍu …* – The reason for this joy \[is explained here\]. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 1.9 “*sangarśādiva puśpitā:*” (the flowers are competing with each other and blossoming), jasmine which is flowering competing with each other, beautiful serundi, and similar campaka. They let out their fragrance.

*vaṇ poḻil …* – The kayal fish which will be strong in water and weak on land, considering the water to be hard and the garden to be soft, breathing in the fragrance from the garden and becoming strong, jump around and play in tirunāngūr, like muktātmās (liberated souls) enjoy bhagavān as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*aham annam aham annam*” (I am food, I am food).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.9.2. Tinniyador

*tiṇṇiyadōr ari uruvāyt tisai anaittum nadungat tēvarodu tānavargaḷ tisaippa iraṇiyanai naṇṇi avan mārvagalattu ugir madutta nādan nāḷ dōṟum magiḻndu inidu maruvi uṟai kōyil eṇṇil migu perunjelvattu eḻil viḷangu maṟaiyum ēḻisaiyum kēḷvigaḷum iyanṟa perunguṇattōr maṇṇil migu maṟaiyavargaḷ maliveydu nāngūr vaigunda viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tisai anaittum – those who are in all directions; nadunga – to fear; dēvarodu dānavargaḷ – dēvatās (noble celestials) and dānavas (demons); tisaippa – to be bewildered; tiṇṇiyadu ōr – strong and distinguished; ari uruvāy – in the form of narasimha; iraṇiyanai – hiraṇyāsuran; naṇṇi – approached; avan – his; mārvu agalattu – wide chest; ugir madutta – placed the nail and tore; nādan – lord; nādōṟum – everyday; magiḻndu – with joy; inidu – to be sweet for the devotees; maruvi uṟai kōyil – eternally residing without any other expectation; eṇṇil migu – countless; perum selvattu – having great wealth; eḻil viḷangu – radiantly beautiful; maṟaiyum – vēdams; ēḻu isaiyum – seven rāgas; kēḷvigaḷum – hearing the meanings (of such vēdams etc); iyanṟa – complete (filled with); perum guṇattōr – those who are with noble qualities; maṇṇil migu – best among the bhūsuras (noble personalities on the earth); maṟaiyavargaḷ – brāhmaṇas; malivu eydum – residing densely; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; vaigunda viṇṇagaram – vaigunda viṇṇagaram; vaṇangu – worship; mada nenjē – Oh humble heart!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The lord appeared in the form of strong and distinguished narasimha to make those who are living in all directions to fear and to bewilder the celestial beings and demons; he approached hiraṇya, the demon, and placed the nail on his chest and tore it; everyday he is joyfully and eternally residing without any other expectation, to be sweet for his devotees, in vaigunda viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr. Oh humble heart! Worship such abode where brāhmaṇas, who are best among the bhūsuras and are with noble qualities, are residing densely, are complete with radiantly beautiful vēdams which have countless great wealth, seven rāgas and hearing the meanings (of such vēdams etc).

*tiṇṇiyadu ōr ari uruvāy* – Being narasimha who will not step back hearing about hiraṇyan’s anger, to make those who are in all directions to fear and to bewilder everyone irrespective of the favourable or unfavourable ones.

*iraṇiyanai naṇṇi* – Approached the cruel, evil hiraṇyan like those who would approach burning fire.

*avan mārvu agalattu ugir madutta* – The eternal abode of emperumān who established his lordship by placing his divine nail on hiraṇyan’s wide chest as if making way for the blood which is seeking an exit point while circulating \[in his body\] and destroying him.

*eṇṇil migu …* – vēdam which is having countless wealth, which is endless due to qualities such as nirdōśatva (being faultless) and hence radiantly shining, sapta svarams (seven rāgas), and the hearing of angams (ancillary aspects) and other topics; those who are filled with noble qualities by being engaged in these.

*eṇṇil …* – The abode where brāhmaṇas who are well learned as said in “He is the only deserving person!” are densely residing.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.9.3. Andamum

*aṇḍamum ivvalaikadalum avanigaḷum ellām amudu seyda tiruvayiṟṟan aran koṇḍu tiriyum muṇḍamadu niṟaittu avankaṇ sābam adu nīkkum mudalvan avan magiḻndu inidu maruvi uṟai kōyil eṇḍhisaiyum perunjennel iḷandengu kadali ilaikkodi oṇkulaik kamugodu isali vaḷam soriya vaṇḍu pala isai pāda mayilālu nāngūr vaigunda viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇḍamum – oval shaped universes; ivvalai kadalum – these oceans which throw up waves; avanigaḷum ellām – all worlds (of the sapta dvīpas); amudu seyda – swallowed; tiruvayiṟṟan – one who has the divine stomach; aran – rudra (being affected by the curse); koṇḍu – carrying; tiriyum – roaming; muṇḍamadu – skull; niṟaittu – filled; avan kaṇ sābamadu nīkkum – mercifully eliminated the curse which will always remain with him; mudalvan avan – lord, who is the controller of all; magiḻndu – with joy; inidu – to be sweet for the devotees; maruvi uṟai kōyil – eternally residing without any other expectation; eṇḍisaiyum – everywhere; perum sennel – tall, red paddy crops; iḷam tengu – young coconuts; kadali – plantain; ilaik kodi – betel creepers; oṇ kulaik kamugōdu – areca trees which are beautifully grown; isali – competing with each other; vaḷam soriya – generating richness; vaṇḍu – beetles; pala isai pāda – as they hum many tunes; mayil Alum – peacocks dancing; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; vaigunda viṇṇagaram – vaigunda viṇṇagaram; vaṇangu – worship; mada nenjē – Oh humble heart!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The lord, who is the controller of all, has the divine stomach which swallowed oval shaped universes, the oceans which throw up waves and all the worlds; he mercifully eliminated the curse of rudra when he was cursed to carry the skull in his hand which will always remain with him and roam around; he is joyfully and eternally residing without any other expectation, to be sweet for his devotees, in vaigunda viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr. Oh humble heart! Worship such abode where tall, red paddy crops, young coconuts, plantain, betel creepers and areca trees which are beautifully grown are competing with each other, everywhere, and are generating richness, beetles hum many tunes and peacocks are dancing.

*aṇḍam …* – emperumān is having the divine stomach which mercifully consumed the oval shaped universe, the oceans which surround this world, with waves being thrown up and all the islands.

*aran …* – emperumān filled the skull which was carried by rudran, who was affected by the curse and was roaming, and relieved him from the curse which would always remain with him. The abode where such controller of all, resides.

*eṇḍisai …* – Everywhere, tall paddy crops, young coconuts which remain youthful similar to muktātmās (liberated souls) who always appear to be twenty five years old, plantain, betel creepers, beautifully grown areca, are remaining together and competing with each other and enrich the place; the beetles enter in these, drink the honey and start humming many tunes due to the honey not letting them remain quiet, and the peacocks start dancing hearing those tunes.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.9.4. Kalai ilangum

*kalai ilangum agalalgul arakkar kulak kodiyaik kādodu mūkkudan ariyak kadaṟi avaḷ ōdi talaiyil angai vaittu malai ilangai pugac ceyda tadandōḷan magiḻndu inidu maruvi uṟai kōyil silai ilangu maṇimādattu ucci misaic cūlam seḻungoṇḍal agadiriyac corinda seḻumuttam malai ilangu māḷigai mēl maliveydu nāngūr vaigunda viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ilangum kalai – having shining clothes; agal algul – having wide thighs; arakkar kulam – born in demoniac clan; kodiyai – sūrpaṇakā who is having creeper like waist, her; kādodu mūkku – ear and nose; udan ariya – severing at once; avaḷ – she; kadaṟi – crying out loudly; talaiyil – on her head; am kai vaittu – placing her beautiful hand; ōdi – ran; malai – present atop the mountain; ilangai pugac ceyda – made her to enter lankā; tadam tōḷan – cakravartit tirumagan who has mighty shoulders; magiḻndu – with joy; inidu – to be sweet for the devotees; maruvi uṟai kōyil – eternally residing without any other expectation; silai ilangu – shining; maṇi mādattu – homes studded with gems; ucci misai – atop the tall roofs; sūlam – tridents; seḻum koṇḍal – rich clouds’; agadu iriya – tearing the bottom portion of their stomach; sorinda – delivered; seḻu muttam – beautiful pearls; malai ilangu – shining like a mountain; māḷigai mēl – atop the mansions; malivu eydu – present as heaps; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; vaigunda viṇṇagaram – vaigunda viṇṇagaram; vaṇangu – worship; mada nenjē – Oh humble heart!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

cakravartit tirumagan, who has mighty shoulders, at once severed the ears and nose of sūrpaṇakā who is born in demoniac clan, having wide thighs, creeper-like waist, and made her cry out loudly, place her hands on her head and run towards lankā which is present atop the mountain and enter there; he is joyfully and eternally residing without any other expectation, to be sweet for his devotees, in vaigunda viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr. Oh humble heart! Worship such abode where the tridents placed atop the tall roofs of the homes, which are studded with shining gems, are tearing the bottom portion of the rich clouds’ stomach which made them deliver beautiful pearls which are present as heaps atop the mansions which are shining like a mountain.

*kalai …* – sūrpaṇakā who appeared with shining clothes on her wide thigh region and is celebrated by the whole demoniac clan. She appeared presenting her clothes and femininity.

*kādu …* – He eliminated her assumed form and made her regain her real form.

*kadaṟi …* – Subsequently, emperumān who has mighty shoulders made her cry out, place her hand on her head and run towards lankā which is atop the mountain and enter there. His eternal abode.

*silai …* – “*silai”* is a synonym for “*vil*“. vil (bow) indicates light; the trident which is seen atop the gem studded mansions  which are studded with shining gems. This is how the homes are in this town. The clouds will gather pearls from the ocean and move slowly without being able to move swiftly; the tridents atop the palaces will tear the bottom of the stomach of the clouds; the clouds which are ready to shower, will pour the pearls.

*malai ilangu māḷigai mēl malivu eydum* – At that time, the pearls are heaped to make it appear as if one mountain is standing on another.

## 3.9.5. Minnanaiya

*minnanaiya nuṇmarungul melliyaṟkā ilangai vēndan mudi orupadum tōḷ irubadum pōy udira tannigaril silai vaḷaittu anṟu ilangai podi seyda tadandōḷan magiḻndu inidu maruvi uṟai kōyil sennelodu sengamalam sēl kayalgaḷ vāḷai sengaḻunīrodu midaindu kaḻani tigaḻndu engum mannu pugaḻ vēdiyargaḷ maliveydu nāngūr vaigunda viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – At that time; min anaiya – matching a lightning; nuṇ marungul – slender waist; melliyaṟkā – for pirātti who is tender-natured; ilangai vēndan – rāvaṇa, who is the leader of lankā, his; mudi oru padum – ten heads which have shining crowns; tōḷ irupadum – twenty arms; pōy udira – to have them break into hundreds of pieces; nigar il – matchless; than silai vaḷaittu – launching his tall bow, kōdaṇḍam; ilangai – lankā; podi seyda – one who turned \[it\] to dust; tadam tōḷan – mighty shouldered cakravartit tirumagan; magiḻndu – with joy; inidu – to be sweet for the devotees; maruvi uṟai kōyil – eternally residing without any other expectation; sen nelodu – red paddy crops; sem kamalam – reddish lotus flowers; sēl vayalgaḷ vāḷai – sēl fish, kayal fish and vāḷai fish; sengaḻunīrodu – with sengaḻunīr flowers; midaindu – together; kaḻani engum – in all the fertile fields; tigaḻndu – shining; mannu pugaḻ – having eternal fame; vēdiyargaḷ – brāhmaṇas; malivu eydum – having \[them\] densely residing in all the streets; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; vaigunda viṇṇagaram – vaigunda viṇṇagaram; vaṇangu – worship; mada nenjē – Oh humble heart!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

At that time, mighty shouldered cakravartit tirumagan made the ten heads which have shining crowns and twenty arms of rāvaṇa, who is the leader of lankā, to break into hundreds of pieces and turned lankā into dust by launching his matchless, tall bow, kōdaṇḍam for the tender-natured pirātti who is having a slender waist; he is joyfully and eternally residing without any other expectation, to be sweet for his devotees, in vaigunda viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr. Oh humble heart! Worship such abode where red paddy crops, reddish lotus flowers and sēl fish, kayal fish and vāḷai fish, along with sengaḻunīr flowers are shining together in all the fertile fields and eternally famous brāhmaṇas are densely residing in all the streets.

*min anaiya …* – For the sake of pirātti who is of tender nature and who is having slender waist like a lightning, the one who has mighty shoulders launched his matchless bow (even if he has a match, his bow has no match) to sever the ten heads and twenty arms of rāvaṇa, the king of lanka, and turn them into dust. The abode which is pleasing due to his loving presence there, as if the task which was done for pirātti was for everyone.

*sem nel …* – This is how all the fertile fields look like, in there. With red paddy crops, lotus, sēl fish, kayal fish, vāḷai fish and sengaḻunīr, all of these remain together in a shining manner, in all the fields.

*mannu pugaḻ …* – This is how the land regions look like in there. The abode where eternally famous brāhmaṇas are residing. This is how the town and the fields are in there.

## 3.9.6. Penmai migu

*peṇmai migu vadivu kodu vandavaḷaip periya pēyinadu uruvu kodu māḷa uyir uṇḍu tiṇmai migu marudodu naṟcagadam iṟuttu aruḷum dēvan avan magiḻndu inidu maruvi uṟai kōyil uṇmai migu maṟaiyodu naṟkalaigaḷ niṟai poṟaigaḷ udavu kodai enṟu ivaṟṟin oḻivillāp periya vaṇmai migu maṟaiyavargaḷ maliveydu nāngūr vaigunda viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

peṇmai migu vadivu kodu – assuming the form of the best woman; vandavaḷai – pūtanā, who came to deceive; periya pēyinadu uruvu kodu – to have her original huge demoniac form; māḷa – to die; uyir uṇḍu – took her life; tiṇmai migu – having great strength; marudodu – maruda tree; naṟcagadam – the wheel which has the ability to finish the task which was started; iṟuttu aruḷum – one who broke; dēvanavan – kriṣṇa; magiḻndu – with joy; inidu – to be sweet for the devotees; maruvi uṟai kōyil – eternally residing without any other expectation; uṇmai migu maṟaiyodu – vēdams which speak the truth as it is; naṟ kalaigaḷ – (their) good ancillary subjects; niṟai – complete qualities (acquired by their familiarity); poṟaigaḷ – tolerance etc; udavu kodai enṟu ivaṟṟin – the generosity of helping, once asked – all such aspects; oḻivillā – those who are not leaving (having them at all times); periya vaṇmai – magnanimity (i.e. ātma samarpaṇam – submitting oneself); migu – filled; maṟaiyavargaḷ – brāhmaṇas; malivu eydum – residing densely; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; vaigunda viṇṇagaram – vaigunda viṇṇagaram; vaṇangu – worship; mada nenjē – Oh humble heart!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa made pūtanā who came to deceive, assuming the form of the best woman, to have her original huge demoniac form and took her life by killing her; he broke the very strong maruda tree and the wheel which has the ability to finish the task which was started; he is joyfully and eternally residing without any other expectation, to be sweet for his devotees, in vaigunda viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr. Oh humble heart! Worship such abode where brāhmaṇas who are filled with vēdams which speak the truth as it is, ancillary subjects of such vēdams, complete qualities, tolerance, the generosity of helping, once asked and magnanimity, are residing densely.

*peṇmai …* – pūtanā who came in the guise of yaśōdāp pirātti who is best among women, regained her huge demoniac form and got killed; kriṣṇa turned her into a dead body. The maruda which became very strong due to being possessed by demon; the wheel which had the ability to complete the undertaken task. The abode where sarvēśvaran, who mercifully vanquished all of them and became radiant thinking “Got the enemies eliminated”, eagerly resides.

*uṇmai …* – Having abundance of brāhmaṇas who have noble qualities due to being familiar with vēdams which speak the truth as it is and their ancillary subjects which are good, and who have humility, tolerance, generosity to give whatever is requested by suffering persons. vaṇmai – ātma samarpaṇam.

## 3.9.7. Vilanganiyai

*viḷanganiyai iḷanganṟu koṇḍu udira eṟindu vēl nedungaṇ āycciyargaḷ vaitta tayir veṇṇey uḷam kuḷira amudu seydu ivvulaguṇḍa kāḷai ugandu inidu nāḷ dōṟum maruvi uṟai kōyil iḷambadi naṟkamugu kulaittengu kodic cennel īnkarumbu kaṇvaḷarak kāl tadavum punalāl vaḷangoṇḍa perunjelvam vaḷarumaṇi nāngūr vaigunda viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

iḷam kanṟu koṇḍu – lifted up the youthful vatsāsuran (demon in the form of a calf); viḷanganiyai udira eṟindu – threw on the demon who was in the form of a wood apple to kill him; vēl – like a spear; nedum kaṇ – having wide eyes; āycciyargaḷ vaitta – covherd girls securely placed; tayir veṇṇey – curd and butter; uḷam kuḷira – to his divine heart’s content; amudu seydu – ate (further); ivvulaguṇḍa – mercifully ate this world too; kāḷai – ever youthful emperumān; ugandu – with joy; inidu – to be sweet for the devotees; nādōṟum – everyday; maruvi uṟai kōyil – eternally residing without any other expectation; iḷam padi nal kamugu – beautiful areca trees which are naturally youthful; kulait tengu – coconut trees with clusters \[of coconuts\]; kodi – beetle creepers; sem nel – red paddy crops; In karumbu – sweet sugarcane – all of these; kaṇ vaḷara – to grow everyday; kāl tadavum – flowing into their roots; punalāl vaḷam koṇḍa perum selvam – the noble, great wealth which is acquired by the abundance of water; vaḷarum – grown; aṇi nāngūr – in beautiful tirunāngūr; vaigunda viṇṇagaram – vaigunda viṇṇagaram; vaṇangu – worship; mada nenjē – Oh humble heart!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The ever youthful emperumān lifted up the youthful vatsāsuran (demon in the form of a calf) and threw on the demon who was in the form of a wood apple to kill him; he ate the curd and butter which were securely placed by the wide-eyed covherd girls to his divine heart’s content and further mercifully ate this world too; he is joyfully and eternally residing without any other expectation, everyday, to be sweet for his devotees, in vaigunda viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr. Oh humble heart! Worship such abode where noble, great wealth which is acquired by the abundance of water flowing into the roots of beautiful areca trees which are naturally youthful, coconut trees which have clusters, beetle creepers, red paddy crops and sweet sugarcane crops, to grow everyday.

*viḷangani …* – kriṣṇa lifted up vatsāsuran and threw him on the demon who stood as wood apple; he mercifully consumed the curd and butter which were securely placed by the covherd girls who have spear like wide eyes; subsequently since he placed the whole world in his divine stomach and protected everything which are to be protected, he remains soft.

*iḷam padi …* – Water will touch the roots of the areca trees which are naturally young, coconut trees which have clusters of coconuts, beetle creepers, red paddy crops, sweet sugarcane, to make them grow; the water would touch the root of the sugarcane crops to make them grow one layer each day. The abode where eternal wealth goes on.

## 3.9.8. Arada sinattin

*āṟāda sinattin migu naragan uram aḻitta adal āḻit tadakkaiyan alarmagatkum amaraṟkum kūṟāgak koduttu aruḷum tiruvudamban imaiyōr kula mudalvan magiḻndu inidu maruvi uṟai kōyil māṟāda malark kamalam sengaḻunīr tadumbi madu veḷḷam oḻuga vayal uḻavar madai adaippa māṟāda perunjelvam vaḷaru maṇi nāngūr vaigunda viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

āṟāda – That which cannot be subdued; sinattin – anger; migu – charging; naragan – narakāsuran’s; uram – strength; aḻitta – eliminated; adal āḻi – battle-ready tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); tadakkaiyan – being the one who is having in his huge hand; alar magatkum – for periya pirāttiyār; ararkkum – for rudran; kūṟu āga – to be enjoyed as their share; koduttu aruḷum tiru udamban – one who is having the śeelam (simplicity) to give the limbs of his divine form; imaiyōr kula mudalvan – sarvēśvaran, who is the controller of nityasūris; magiḻndu – with joy; inidu – to be sweet for the devotees; maruvi uṟai kōyil – eternally residing without any other expectation; māṟāda malark kamalam – the lotus which is continuously blossoming; sengaḻunīr – sengaḻunīr (flowers such as this, from them); tadumbi – densely flowing; madu veḷḷam oḻuga – since the flood of honey is flowing everywhere; uḻavar – farmers; vayal madai adaippa – as they close the canals in their fields; māṟāda – continuously growing; perum selvam vaḷarum – filled with abundant wealth of water; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; vaigunda viṇṇagaram – vaigunda viṇṇagaram; vaṇangu – worship; mada nenjē – Oh humble heart!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, who is the controller of nityasūris, is having battle-ready tiruvāḻi (divine chakra) which eliminated the strength of narakāsuran, who was charging at \[emperumān\] and who had anger which cannot be subdued; he is having the śeelam (simplicity) to give the limbs of his divine form to be enjoyed as their share for periya pirāttiyār and rudran; he is joyfully and eternally residing without any other expectation, to be sweet for his devotees, in vaigunda viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr. Oh humble heart! Worship such abode where the flood of densely flowing honey is flowing everywhere from the lotus which is continuously blossoming and sengaḻunīr flower; the farmers are closing the canals in their fields; and the abode is filled with abundant wealth of water which is continuously growing.

*āṟāda …* – narakāsuran was having anger which cannot be subdued anytime and was charging at sarvēśvaran; sarvēśvaran is having battle-ready divine chakra which eliminated the strength of such narakāsuran; he is having the śeelam to give his divine form where periya pirāttiyār and rudran are claiming different limbs as their share; he is the lord of the group of nityasūris.

*māṟāda …* – As the honey overflows from lotus which always blossoming, sengaḻunīr etc, farmers will close the inlet of the canals when such flood will lead to destruction of the crops.

*māṟāda perum selvam vaḷarum* – The noise of the farmers saying “The flood is breaching the shore there”, “The flood is breaching the shore here” and saying “The river source is flooding”.

## 3.9.9. Vangamali

*vangamali tadangadaluḷ vānavargaḷōdu māmunivar palar kūdi māmalargaḷ tūvi engaḷ tani nāyaganē! emakku aruḷāy ennum īsan avan magiḻndu inidu maruvi uṟai kōyil sengayalum vāḷaigaḷum sennelidaik kudippac cēlugaḷum seḻumpaṇai sūḻ vīdi toṟum midaindu mangul madi agadurinju maṇimāda nāngūr vaigunda viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vanga mali – Filled with ships; tadam kadaluḷ – in the vast tiruppāṟkadal; vānavargaḷōdu māmunivar palar kūdi – dēvatās along with sages such as sanaka et al gathered together and arrived; mā malargaḷ tūvi – offering the best flowers and other things for worship; engaḷ tani nāyaganē – Oh you, sarvēśvaran, who are our lord!; emakku aruḷāy – You should show your mercy towards us; ennum – to be prayed in this manner; īsanavan – the lord; magiḻndu – with joy; inidu – to be sweet for the devotees; maruvi uṟai kōyil – eternally residing without any other expectation; sem kayalum – reddish kayal fish; vāḷaigaḷum – vāḷai fish; sem nel idai – in between the red paddy crops; gudippa – as they jump around; sēlugaḷum – sēl fish which were joyfully present in between those crops; seḻum paṇai suḻ – surrounded by vast fertile fields; vīdi toṟum – in every street; midaindu – being dense; mangul madi – moon which is roaming in the sky; agadu urinjum – to rub the bottom portion of the stomach; maṇi mādam – having gem studded mansions; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; vaigunda viṇṇagaram – vaigunda viṇṇagaram; vaṇangu – worship; mada nenjē – Oh humble heart!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān who is present in the vast tiruppāṟkadal to be praised by the dēvatās along with sages such as sanaka et al gathered together, offered the best flowers and other things for worship and arrived saying “Oh you, sarvēśvaran, who are our lord! You should show your mercy towards **us”;** he is joyfully and eternally residing without any other expectation, to be sweet for his devotees, in vaigunda viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr. Oh humble heart! Worship such abode where reddish kayal fish and vāḷai fish are jumping in between the red paddy crops and is surrounded by such vast fertile fields where sēl fish are joyfully present in between those crops and gem studded mansions which are present densely in every street, rubbing the bottom portion of the stomach of moon which is roaming in the sky.

*vanga …* –  In the vast tiruppāṟkadal which has no shortage of ships/boats. Just as a mountain is glorified based on the elephants in there, an ocean is glorified by the ships in it. Along with dēvatās, sages such as sanaka et al, would submit things for worship such as flowers etc, and praise sarvēśvaran saying “Oh you, sarvēśvaran, who are our lord! You should mercifully shower your grace to us”; the abode where such sarvēśvaran is lovingly residing.

*sem kayal …* – Beautiful kayal fish, vāḷai fish would jump in between the red paddy crops seeing the coolness there; sēl fish would joyfully reside in the fertile fields which surround the abode. There, in every street, gem studded mansions which rub the bottom portion of the stomach of moon which roams in the sky, are present.

## 3.9.10. Sangu mali

*sangu mali taṇḍu mudal cakkaram mun ēndum tāmaraikkaṇ nediya pirān tān amarum kōyil vangamali kadal ulagil maliveydu nāngūr vaigunda viṇṇagar mēl vaṇḍaṟaiyum poḻil sūḻ mangaiyar tam talaivan maruvalar tam udal tuṇiya vāḷ vīsum parakālan kalikanṟi sonna sangamali tamiḻ mālai pattivai vallārgaḷ taraṇiyodu visumbāḷum tanmai peṟuvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sangu – śankha (conch); mali – firm; taṇḍu – mace; cakkaram – chakra (disc); mudal – and khadga (sword), śārnga (bow) – all of these; mun – in front of our eyes; ēndum – holding; nediya – wide; tāmaraik kaṇ – having lotus like divine eyes; pirān – sarvēśvaran, the great benefactor; amarum kōyil – the abode where he is eternally residing; vangam – ships; mali – filled; kadal – surrounded by ocean; ulagil – in earth; malivu eydu – abundantly rich; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; vaigunda viṇṇagar mēl – on vaigunda viṇṇagaram; vaṇḍu – beetles; aṟaiyum – humming; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; mangaiyari tam – for those who are in tirumangai region; talaivan – being the leader; maruvalar tam udal – enemies’ bodies; tuṇiya – to become pieces; vāḷ vīsum – one who uses his sword; parakālan – being death for enemies; kali kanṟi – āḻvār who is kalivairi (enemy of kali); sonna – mercifully spoken; sangam mali – worthy to be praised by the assembly of poets; tamiḻ mālai – garland of drāvida (tamiḻ) words; ivai pattu – these ten pāsurams; vallārgaḷ – those who can recite; taraṇiyodu – earth; visumbu – and paramākāśam (paramapadam); āḷum – to rule; tanmai – greatness; peṟuvār – will have

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

vaigunda viṇṇagaram, in abundantly rich tirunāngūr on the earth which is surrounded by ocean which is filled with ships, is the eternal abode of the great benefactor who is holding śankha, firm mace, chakra, sword and the bow in front of our eyes; tirumangai āḻvār, who is the leader of those who are in tirumangai region which is surrounded by gardens where beetles are humming, uses his sword to cut the enemies’ bodies to pieces, is death for enemies and is kalivairi, mercifully spoke this decad which is worthy to be praised by the assembly of poets and is a garland of tamiḻ words on such divyadēśam; those who can recite these ten pāsurams, will have the greatness to rule over earth and paramapadam.

*sangu …* – This is the abode where sarvēśvaran who is puṇḍarīkākśan (lotus-eyed) and is holding the five weapons for the sake of his devotees, is eternally residing. āḻvār sang vaigunda viṇṇagaram in abundantly rich tirunāngūr on the earth which is surrounded by ocean which is having ships. The one who sang is āḻvār who is the leader of the residents of tirumangai which is surrounded by gardens which are filled with beetles which have drunk honey. parakālan who uses his sword to sever the enemies, mercifully spoke this decad. If the sangam (the ancient, tamiḻ, literary assembly) poets gather and decide to praise tamiḻ, they will praise this decad only; those who are well versed in this decad, will have the nature to have nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti at their disposal.

## 3.10 Tirumadandai

## 3.10.1. Tirumadandai

*tirumadandai maṇmadandai irupālum tigaḻat tīvinaigaḷ pōy agala adiyavargatku enṟum aruḷ nadandu ivvēḻulagattavar paṇiya vānōr amarndu ētta irunda idam perum pugaḻ vēdiyar vāḻ tarum idangaḷ malargaḷ migu kaidaigaḷ sengaḻunīr tāmaraigaḷ tadangaḷ toṟum idangaḷ toṟum tigaḻa aruvidangaḷ poḻil taḻuvi eḻil tigaḻum nāngūr arimēya viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tirumadandai – periya pirāttiyār; maṇ madandai – and śrī bhūmip pirātti; iru pālum – on either side; tigaḻa – shine; adiyavargatku – towards devotees; enṟum – always; aruḷ nadandu – granting mercy; tī vinaigaḷ – cruel sins; pōy agala – to run away; ivvēḻ ulagattavar – the residents of these seven worlds; paṇiya – to surrender; vānōr – nityasūris; amarndu – remaining rooted, in this abode of samsāram; ētta – to praise; irunda – eternally residing; idam – being the divyadēśam; perum pugaḻ – very famous; vēdiyar – brāhmaṇas; vāḻ tarum – residing; idangaḷ – having places; malargaḷ migu – having abundance of flowers; kaidaigaḷ – tāḻai plants (which are found on seashore); sengaḻunīr – sengaḻunīr flowers; tāmaraigaḷ – lotus flowers; idangaḷ toṟum – everywhere; tigaḻa – as they shine; poḻil – garden; aruvidangaḷ – the whole sky; taḻuvi – growing tall to fill; eḻil tigaḻum – beauty is shining; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; arimēya viṇṇagaram – emperumān in arimēya viṇṇagaram; mada nenjē – Oh obedient heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh obedient heart! Surrender unto emperumān in arimēya viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr, the divyadēśam where beauty is shining, and where he is eternally residing, along with periya pirāttiyār and śrībhūmip pirātti on his either side, always granting his mercy to his devotees, to let the residents of the seven worlds to be rid of their cruel sins and to let the nityasūris remain rooted in this samsāram and praise him; it is having places where very famous brāhmaṇas are residing; everywhere there is abundance of tāḻai, sengaḻunīr and lotus flowers and they are shining; the garden there has grown tall to fill the whole sky.

*tirumadandai maṇmadandai irupālum tigaḻa* – pirātti \[śrī mahālakśmi\] who makes emperumān forgive our mistakes as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed) and śrībhūmip pirātti who considers that seeing the mistake and then forgiving it is too much and would say “Why first see the mistake, then forgive? \[Just don’t see the mistakes\]”, are shining on either side of emperumān. To forgive the faults after seeing them, there is pirātti, and there is śrībhūmip pirātti who remains thinking “What is the point in seeing the mistake?” for those who cannot be abandoned for their mistakes.

*tī vinaigaḷ pōy agala* – Due to the eternal presence of these pirāttis, for sarvēśvaran, there is no scope to say to his devotees as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 16-19](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-19/) *“samsāreśu narādamān* – *kśipāmi*” (I push those who hate me, who are cruel, who are the worst among people  and sinners, into the demonic species repeatedly). Due to the eternal presence of the one who makes him forgive and the one who is his teacher for tolerance, he will always grant his mercy to his devotees and due to that, the cruel mistakes will run away thinking “These \[devotees\] are not our abodes”; seeing that, all the people in these seven worlds will surrender unto him thinking “There is no other protector in this world like him” and is surrendered to by nityasūris who are untouched by samsāram, rooted in this samsāra where even dēvatās will not place their feet; such emperumān’s abode.

*perum pugaḻ …* – tirunāngūr which is having the places where brāhamaṇas who are very famous due to being always engaged in emperumān only; also having kaidai (tāḻai) etc which have abundance of flowers; alternatively – kaidai etc flowers are present in the places where the brāhmaṇas are present, for their purpose; in each pond abundant flowers of tāḻai, sengaḻunīr and lotus are fully spread; as there is no space left here, the garden grows upwards and fills the whole sky and remains shining with beauty; **aru**midam (place without form) indicates ākāśam due to its subtle nature.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.2. Venri migu

*venṟi migu naragan uram adu aḻiya visiṟum viṟal āḻit tadakkaiyan viṇṇavargatku anṟu kunṟu kodu kuraikadalaik kadaindu amudam aḷikkum kurumaṇi en āramudam kulavi uṟai kōyil enṟum migu perunjelvattu eḻil viḷangu maṟaiyōr ēḻisaiyum kēḷvigaḷum iyanṟa perunguṇattōr anṟu ulagam padaittavanē anaiyavargaḷ nāngūr arimēya viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

venṟi migu – very victorious; naragan – narakāsura’s; adu uram – such strength; aḻiya – to be destroyed; visiṟum – flowing; viṟal – having strength; āḻi – tiruvāḻi (chakra); tadam – big; kaiyan – having in his divine hand; anṟu – when the clan of dēvatās prayed; viṇṇavargatku – for dēvatās such as indra et al; kunṟu kodu – mantara mountain; kurai kadalai – tumultuous ocean; kadaindu – churned; amudam – nectar; aḷikkum – mercifully gave (them); kuru maṇi – like the best gem; en Ar amudam – my nectar which will never satiate; kulavi uṟai – residing desirously; kōyil – being divine abode; enṟum – everyday; migu – over flowing; perum selvattu – having unlimited wealth; eḻil viḷangum – with shining beauty; maṟaiyōr – those who have mastered vēdam; ēḻ isaiyum – sapta svaras (seven tunes); kēḷvigaḷum – other ancillary subjects; iyanṟa – learnt; perum guṇattōr – those who have abundance of great qualities; anṟu – at that time; ulagam padaittavanē anaiyavargaḷ – where brāhmaṇas who are capable of performing creation just as brahmā is capable of doing, are residing; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; arimēya viṇṇagaram – emperumān in arimēya viṇṇagaram; mada nenjē – Oh obedient heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, who is like the best gem and my nectar which will never satiate, was having tiruvāḻi with flowing strength, in his big, divine hand to have the great strength of victorious narakāsura destroyed. When the clan of dēvatās prayed, he churned the tumultuous ocean with mantara mountain and gave nectar to dēvatās such as indra et al. He is residing desirously in arimēya viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr. Oh obedient heart! Surrender unto emperumān there, where brāhmaṇas who have unlimited wealth \[of knowledge\] which is overflowing everyday, who have mastered vēdam which has shining beauty,  have learnt sapta svaras and other ancillary subjects, are with abundance of great qualities and are capable of performing creation just as brahmā is capable of doing, are residing.

*venṟi …* – emperumān has divine hand which has divine chakra having flowing strength, which destroyed the strength of narakāsura who roamed around, destroying the abode of indra et al and who remained victorious wherever he went. Not only he got back the abodes of the clan of dēvatās by destroying narakāsura, when they asked “Please churn the ocean and get us the nectar” he churned the tumultuous ocean by placing the mantara mountain for them and gave that to them.

*kuru maṇi* … – When those dēvatās say “We don’t want you; we only need the salt water”, without caring for his invaluable divine form, causing pain to his shoulders, he churned the ocean, he bestowed the nectar to them.

*en Ar amudam* – Unlike their nectar, this (emperumān) is āḻvār’s nectar. He lives in that \[nectar\] in celebration.

*enṟum …* – Having unlimited wealth \[of knowledge\] which grows everyday, and shining due to that, those who have mastered vēdam, and having learnt sapta svaras and other ancillary subjects as said in “There is no one who has learnt more than them”, and having abundance of noble qualities due to their familiarity in these subjects, they are capable of performing creation. tirunāngūr where such brāhmaṇas are residing.

## 3.10.3. Umbarum

*umbarum ivvēḻulagum ēḻkadalum ellām uṇḍa pirān aṇḍargaḷ mun kaṇḍu magiḻveyda kumba migu mada yānai marupposittuk kanjan kunji pidittu aditta pirān kōyil marungengum paimbonodu veṇmuttam pala punnai kāttap palanganigaḷ tēn kātta padavaravēr algul ambanaiya kaṇ madavār magiḻveydu nāngūr arimēya viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

umbarum – dēvatās; ivvēḻulagum – these seven worlds; ēḻ kadalum – seven oceans; ellām – all of these; uṇḍa – mercifully consumed during praḷayam; pirān – being the benefactor (incarnated as kriṣṇa); aṇḍargaḷ – covherd people; kaṇḍu magiḻvu eyda – to enjoy on seeing; mun – in front of them; kumbam migu – having huge head which resembles a pot; mada yānai – intoxicated kuvalayāpīdam’s; maruppu – tusk; osittu – broke; kanjan – kamsan’s; kunji pidittu – dragging by hair; aditta – destroyed; pirān – benefactor’s; kōyil – being the abode; marungu engum – all the surroundings; pala punnai – many punnai trees (blossoming as buds and flowers); paim ponōdu – and beautiful gold; veḷ muttam – having gathered white pearls; kātta – as they show; palam kanigaḷ – jackfruits; tēn kātta – as they show the flowing honey; padam – hooded; aravu – like snake; ēr – beautiful; algul – thigh; ambu anaiya – like arrows; kaṇ madavār – women who have eyes; magiḻvu eydum – rejoicing; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; arimēya viṇṇagaram – emperumān in arimēya viṇṇagaram; mada nenjē – Oh obedient heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is the benefactor who mercifully consumed dēvatās, these seven worlds and seven oceans during praḷayam; to be seen and rejoiced by the covherd people, in front of them, he broke the tusk of intoxicated elephant which had pot like head and killed kamsa, dragging him by his hair; being the abode of such emperumān, arimēya viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr is having in its surroundings, many punnai trees showing beautiful gold and whitish pearls, and the jackfruits showing the overflowing honey; the women who have hooded snake like thighs and arrow like eyes are rejoicing. Oh obedient heart! Surrender unto the emperumān there.

*umbarum …* – As all of the clan of dēvatās, these seven types of worlds, the seven oceans which surround them, were going to suffer in praḷayam (deluge), being the benefactor, he mercifully placed them in his stomach and protected them; such benefactor incarnated as kriṣṇa; to make the covherd people see and rejoice, he broke the tusk of the elephant kuvalayāpīdam which has pot like head; subsequently, he dragged kamsa by his hair, pushed him upside down, slapped him on his back and killed him. The abode of such benefactor.

In the surroundings,

*paim ponodu veṇ muttam pala punnai kātta …* – As the punnai trees have blossomed buds and flowers, they appear like pearls embossed in gold; jackfruits showed honey in them; the women who have hooded snake like thighs and arrow like eyes will feel satisfied thinking “There is no order of what exists at a particular time”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.4. Odada

*ōdāda vāḷ ariyin uruvamadu koṇḍu anṟu ulappil migu peruvaratta iraṇiyanaip paṟṟi vādāda vaḷḷugirāl piḷandu avan tan maganukku aruḷ seydān vāḻum idam malligai sengaḻunīr sēdēṟu malar serundi seḻungamugam pāḷai seṇbagangaḷ maṇam nāṟum vaṇpoḻilin ūdē ādēṟu vayalālaip pugai kamaḻum nāngūr arimēya viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – When prahlādan was compelled; ōdāda – not stepping back; adu – such strong; āḷariyin uruvam koṇḍu – assuming the form of narasimha; ulappu il – countless; migu peru varatta – having very great boons; iraṇiyanai – hiraṇyan; paṟṟi – grabbed; vādāda – unbending; vaḷ – sharp; ugirāl – with nails; piḷandu – to make his chest split into two; avan than maganukku – for śrī prahlādāḻvān, who is his son; aruḷ seydān – lord who showed his mercy; vāḻum idam – the abode where he is residing; malligai – jasmine; sengaḻunīr – water-lily; sēdu ēṟu malar – having well blossomed flowers; serundi – sura punnai; seḻu – beautiful; kamugam pāḷai – areca spates; senbagangaḷ – śeṇbaga flowers; maṇam nāṟum – fragrance is smelling; vaṇ poḻilin ūdē – amidst the beautiful garden; ādu ēṟu vayal – in the fields, where sugarcane are to be processed; ālaip pugai kamaḻum – the smoke from the factory is smelling; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; arimēya viṇṇagaram – emperumān in arimēya viṇṇagaram; mada nenjē – Oh obedient heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

When prahlādan was compelled, emperumān assumed the form of very strong naraiśma, who will not step back, and grabbed hiraṇyan who is having countless, very great boons. emperumān showed his mercy to śrī prahlādāḻvān, who is hiraṇyan’s son, by making hiraṇyan’s chest split into two, with his sharp, unbending nails; being the abode of such emperumān, arimēya viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr, is having beautiful garden where the fragrance of jasmine, water-lily, sura punnai which is having well blossomed flowers, beautiful areca spates and śeṇbaga flowers, are smelling; amidst such garden, in the fields, the smoke from the factory where sugarcane are to be processed is smelling nicely. Oh obedient heart! Surrender unto the emperumān there.

*ōdāda …* – narasimha who does not step back seeing hiraṇyan’s rough body; alternatively – narasimha who is not usually seen in this world.

*ulappu il …* – Countless; while each of the boons is having endless greatness, he had great boons which caused those dēvatās who gave the boons to lose their residences; grabbing such hiraṇyan.

*vādāda …* –  Splitting hiraṇyan’s chest with the divine nails which did not bend even after piercing through the rough body of hiraṇyan, To compensate the loss of not having hiraṇyan as his devotee, he showed his mercy to śrī prahlādāḻvān considering him to be “hiraṇyan’s son”. The abode of such emperumān.

*malligai …* – In the beautiful garden where jasmine, water-lily, sēdu – collection, that is, serundi which has bunches of blossomed flowers, dense and beautiful areca spates, śeṇbagam flowers are spreading their fragrance, the sugarcane which are brought in to the fields for processing are smelling with fragrance, through the factory smoke.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.5. Kandavar tam

*kaṇḍavar tam manam magiḻa māvali tana vēḷvik kaḷavin migu siṟu kuṟaḷāy mūvadi enṟu irandittu aṇḍamum ivvalai kadalum avanigaḷum ellām aḷanda pirān amarum idam vaḷangoḷ poḻil ayalē aṇḍamuṟu muḻavoliyum vaṇḍinangaḷ oliyum arumaṟaiyin oliyum madavār silambin oliyum aṇḍamuṟum alaikadalin oli tigaḻum nāngūr arimēya viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇḍavar tam manam – The hearts of everyone who has seen; maghiḻa – to rejoice; māvali than vēḷvi – in the sacrificial arena of mahābali; kaḷavu il – appearing to be non-deceitful; migu siṟu kuṟaḷāy – being very short vāmana; mūvadi enṟu – saying “need three steps of land”; irandittu – begged; aṇḍamum – sky; i – here; alai kadalum – oceans which are throwing up waves; avanigaḷum – the worlds which are in the form of seven islands; ellām – all of these; aḷanda – effortlessly scaled and accepted; pirān – benefactor; amarum – eternally residing; idam – being the abode; vaḷam koḷ – rich; poḻil ayalē – near the garden; aṇḍam uṟum – reaching the sky; muḻavu oliyum – sound of the musical instruments; vandu inangaḷ oliyum – humming of the beetles which are joyful due to drinking honey; aru maṟaiyin oliyum – chants of vēdam which is difficult to grasp; madavār – (dancing) women’s; silambin oliyum – sound of the anklets; aṇḍam uṟum – reaching up to the wall of the oval shaped universe; alai – throwing up the waves; kadalin oli – like the sound of the ocean of deluge; tigaḻum – heard; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; arimēya viṇṇagaram – emperumān in arimēya viṇṇagaram; mada nenjē – Oh obedient heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

To be rejoiced by the hearts of everyone who has seen him, emperumān the benefactor, being very short vāmana, entered the sacrificial arena, appearing to be non-deceitful, begged saying “need three steps of land” and effortlessly scaled the sky, oceans which are here throwing up waves, and the worlds which are in the form of seven islands, and accepted all of these; he is eternally residing in the abode arimēya viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr, which has rich garden near which the sound of musical instruments which reaches up to the sky, the humming of beetles which are joyful due to drinking honey, the chants of vēdam which is difficult to grasp, the sound of dancing women’s anklets which is similar to the sound of the ocean of deluge throwing up the waves which are reaching up to the wall of the oval shaped universe. Oh obedient heart! Surrender unto the emperumān there.

*kaṇḍavar tam manam magiḻa* – Without any difference between favourable and unfavourable persons, to be rejoiced by the hearts of those who have seen him, in the sacrificial arena of mahābali, without appearing that he has come to fulfil the task of dēvatās, he assumed the form of a very short vāmana where dwarfs in this world will appear like trivikrama in front of him; he begged saying “I need three steps of land”, he scaled the sky, ocean which throws up waves and the islands; the abode where such benefactor is eternally residing.

*vaḷam …* – Near the rich garden, the sound of the musical instruments which reaches up to the sky, the humming of the beetles which are joyful due to drinking the honey, the chants of vēdam which is difficult to grasp, the sound of the dancing women’s anklets are heard similar to the sound of the ocean of deluge throwing up the waves which are reaching up to the wall of the oval shaped universe.

## 3.10.6. Val nedungan

*vāḷ nedungaṇ malark kūndal maidilikkā ilangai mannan mudi orubadum tōḷ irubadum pōy udira tāḷ neduntiṇ silai vaḷaitta tayaradan sēy enṟan taniccaraṇ vānavarkku arasu karudum idam tadamār sēṇidangoḷ malark kamalam sēlkayalgaḷ vāḷai sennelodu maduttariya udirnda seḻumuttam vāḷ nedungaṇ kadaisiyargaḷ vārumaṇi nāngūr arimēya viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāḷ – sharp like sword; nedu – wide; kaṇ – divine eyes; malar – decorated with flower; kūndal – having hair; maidilikkā – for pirātti; ilangai mannan – rāvaṇa, who is the king of lankā, his; oru padu mudiyum – ten heads; irubadu tōḷum – twenty shoulders; pōy udira – to fall down; tāḷ – having string which is tied; nedu – long; tiṇ – firm; silai – bow; vaḷaitta – bent; dayaradan sēy – son of daśarata; enṟan – for me; taniccaraṇ – being matchless protector; vānavarkku arasu – being the lord of nityasūris; karudum idam – the abode where he resides desirously; tadam Ar – filled with ponds; sēṇ idam koḷ – tall to reach up to the sky; malar – having flowers; kamalam – lotus; sēl kayalgaḷ vāḷai – sēl, kayal and vāḷai fish; sem nelodum – with red paddy; aduttu ariya – as they are gathered and harvested; udirnda – fell from them; seḻu – beautiful; muttam – pearls; vāḷ – sharp like sword; nedu – wide; kaṇ – having eyes; kadaisiyargaḷ – farming women; vārum – collect; aṇi – beautiful; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; arimēya viṇṇagaram – emperumān in arimēya viṇṇagaram; mada nenjē – Oh obedient heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

For pirātti who has wide, divine eyes which are sharp like sword and hair decorated with flower, emperumān, the son of daśarata, bent his long, firm bow, which is having tied string, to make the ten heads and twenty shoulders of rāvaṇa, the king of lankā, fall down; he is my matchless protector and the lord of nityasūris; being the desirable abode of such emperumān, arimēya viṇṇagaram in beautiful tirunāngūr is filled with ponds; the farming women who have sword like sharp eyes, gather and collect the beautiful pearls which fall from the red paddy crops which are harvested along with the lotus which have flowers which reach up to the sky and with sēl, kayal and vāḷai fish. Oh obedient heart! Surrender unto the emperumān there.

*vāḷ …* – vāḷ could mean radiance or sword; for the divine daughter of śrī janakarājan, who is having such wide eyes and hair which is decorated with flower, daśarata’s son bent his long, firm bow which is strung, to knock down the ten heads and twenty shoulders of rāvaṇa, the controller of lankā. sēy – son.

*enṟan tanic caraṇ* – āḻvār thinks similar to [tiruvāimoḻi 3.6.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-6-8-thuyarame-tharu/) “*tayaradaṟku magan tannai anṟi maṟṟilēn tanjam āgavē*” (other than such śrī rāma, who appeared as the son of daśarati cakravarti, I will not have any one, even another form of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), as my refuge). The abode of emperumān who is known as in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (lord of nityasūris).

*tadamār …* – The abode is filled with ponds; the farming women who have sword like sharp eyes, gather and collect the beautiful pearls which fall from the red paddy crops which are harvested along with the lotus which have flowers which reach up to the sky, sēl, kayal and vāḷai fish.

## 3.10.7. Timanattan

*tīmanattān kanjanadu vanjanaiyil tiriyum tēnuganum pūdanai tan āruyirum seguttān kāmanait tān payanda karumēniyudai ammān karudum idam porudu punal tuṟai tuṟai muttu undi nāmanattāl mandirangaḷ nālvēdam aindu vēḷviyōdu āṟangam navinṟu kalai payinṟu angu āmanattu maṟaiyavargaḷ payilu maṇi nāngūr arimēya viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tī manattān – having cruel heart; kanjanadu – by kamsan’s instigation; vanjanaiyil – having a deceitful form; tiriyum – roaming; tēnuganum – dēnukāsaran’s; pūdanai than – pūtanā’s; Ar uyir – good life; seguttān – one who finished; kāmanai – manmanta (cupid), the most handsome one in the world; payanda – gave birth; karu mēni udai ammān – the lord who is having divine form with dark complexion; karudum idam – being the desirously residing abode; porudu punal – water where waves are hitting each other; tuṟai tuṟai – in every ghat; muttu undi – pushing pearls; nā – with tongue; manattāl – and with mind; mandirangaḷ – bhagavān’s mantrams; nāl vēdam – four vēdams; aindu vēḷviyodu – five great yajñas (fire sacrifices); āṟu angam – six ancillary subjects; navinṟu – learnt; kalai payinṟu – learnt the other śāstrams; angu Am manattu – having pure heart which is apt for bhagavat viśayam; maṟaiyavargaḷ – vaidikas; payilum – due to living densely; aṇi – having beauty; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; arimēya viṇṇagaram – emperumān in arimēya viṇṇagaram; mada nenjē – Oh obedient heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān finished the good life of dēnukāsuran and pūtanā who were roaming with deceitful forms by the instigation of the cruel-hearted kamsan; he is the lord who is having divine form with dark complexion, who gave birth to manmanta (cupid), the most handsome one in the world; being the desirable abode of such emperumān, the arimēya viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr is having water where waves are hitting each other, which pushes pearls in every ghat and is beautiful due to the vaidikas who are having their tongue and mind engaged in bhagavān’s mantrams, who have learnt four vēdams, five great yajñas  and six ancillary subjects and all other śāstrams, and have pure heart which is apt for bhagavat viśayam, and are living densely. Oh obedient heart! Surrender unto the emperumān there.

*tī manattān …* – Cruel-hearted kamsan – one who cannot tolerate the presence of bhagavān in a place (āyarpādi/gōkulam); his servants such as dēnukāsuran and pūtanā, who are roaming in disguise – one who killed them. In beauty, he is the father of manmata, and has even greater divine form which is rejuvenating. The desirable abode of such sarvēśvaran.

*karudum idam* … – Water which is having waves which are hitting against each other, are pushing pearls in every ghat. The abode which has the beauty due to having vaidikas who have pure heart since they are engaging their tongue and mind in bhagavān’s mantrams, four types of vēdams, five great yajñams, six ancillary subjects etc, and are living densely.

## 3.10.8. Kanradanal

*kanṟadanāl viḷaveṟindu kani udirtta kāḷai kāmaru sīr mugil vaṇṇan kāligaḷ mun kāppān kunṟadanāl maḻai taduttuk kudamādu kūttan kulavum idam kodi madiḷgaḷ māḷigai gōburangaḷ tunṟu maṇi maṇḍabangaḷ sālaigaḷ tūmaṟaiyōr tokku īṇḍit toḻudiyodu migap payilum sōlai anṟu alarvāy madu uṇḍu angu aḷimuralum nāngūr arimēya viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kanṟu adanāl – With vatsāsuran (demon in the form of a calf); viḷavu eṟindu – knocking down the demon who stood as the wood apple; kani – its fruit; udirtta – made it fall; kāḷai – being ever youthful; kāmaru – being desired by all; sīr – beautiful; mugil vaṇṇan – having beautiful form like that of a dark cloud; mun – previously; kāligaḷ – cows; kāppān – to protect; kunṟu adanāl – with mountain; maḻai – rain; taduttu – stopped; kudam ādu kūttan – one who danced with pots; kulavum idam – abode where he is joyfully residing; kodi – having flags; madiḷgaḷ – compound walls(around forts); māḷigai – mansions; gōburangaḷ – towers; tunṟu – dense; maṇi – filled with gems; maṇḍabangaḷ – halls; sālaigaḷ – having sacrificial arenas too; tū – very pure; maṟaiyōr – brāhmaṇas; tokku īṇḍi – due to gathering in groups; toḻudiyōdu – being abundant with tumultuous noise; migap payilum – very dense; sōlai – present in the gardens; madu uṇḍu – drinking the honey; angu – in that place; aḷi – beetles; muralum – humming; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; arimēya viṇṇagaram – emperumān in arimēya viṇṇagaram; mada nenjē – Oh obedient heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān who is ever youthful, desired by all, having beautiful form like that of a beautiful, dark cloud, made the fruit from wood apple tree, which was a demon, to fall down using vatsāsuran; previously, he stopped the rain with a mountain to protect the cows; he then danced with pots; being the joyful abode of such emperumān, arimēya viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr is having compound walls with flags, mansions, towers, halls which are filled densely with gems, sacrificial arenas, having abundance of the tumultuous noise of very pure brāhmaṇas who have gathered in groups; the beetles have drunk honey and are humming in the freshly blossomed flowers in the dense garden. Oh obedient heart! Surrender unto the emperumān there.

*kanṟu adanāl …* – The pet child who used the demon, who stood as a calf, to kill the demon, who stood as wood apple, and enjoyed leelārasam (joy); kāmaru – desirable; sīr – qualities; one who has such qualities and rejuvenating form; to protect the cows, he lifted the gōvardana mountain and stopped the rain; this is the abode of the one who danced with pots in the four-way junction, joyfully residing.

*kodi madiḷgaḷ …* – Having compound walls which have flags, mansions, towers, halls which have densely packed gems, sacrificial arenas; the abode where brāhmaṇas are making tumultuous noise by gathering together in groups, the beetles which drank honey from the fresh flowers, are humming beautifully.

## 3.10.9. Vanjanaiyal

*vanjanaiyāl vandavaḷ tan uyir uṇḍu vāytta tayir uṇḍu veṇṇey amudu uṇḍu vali mikka kanjan uyiradu uṇḍu ivvulaguṇḍa kāḷai karudum idam kāviri sandu agil kanagam undi manjulavu poḻilūdum vayalūdum vandu vaḷam koduppa māmaṟaiyōr māmalargaḷ tūvi anjalittu angu ari saraṇ enṟu iṟainju maṇi nāngūr arimēya viṇṇagaram vaṇangu mada nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vanjanaiyāl – assuming a deceitful form; vanadavaḷ than – pūtanā who came; uyir – life; uṇḍu – ate; vāytta – present near by; tayir uṇḍu – drank the curd; veṇṇey amudu uṇḍu – mercifully ate the butter; vali mikka – very strong; kanjan uyiradu – kamsan’s life; uṇḍu – ate; ivvulagu – this world; uṇḍa – mercifully placed in his stomach; kāḷai – the youthful one; karudum idam – abode where he desirously resides; kāviri – river kāvēri; sandu – sandalwood trees; agil – agaru (fragrant) trees; kanagam – gold; undi – pushed and came; manju ulavu poḻilūdum – in the garden which has grown tall up to clouds; vayalūdum – in fertile field; vandu – entered; vaḷam koduppa – creating wealth; mā maṟaiyōr – brāhmaṇas who are great vaidikas; mā malargaḷ tūvi – submitting the best flowers; angu anjalittu – standing there performing anjali (joining the palms); ari saraṇ enṟu – saying “Oh hari! Your divine feet are our refuge”; iṟainjum – surrendering with praises; aṇi – having beauty; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; arimēya viṇṇagaram – emperumān in arimēya viṇṇagaram; mada nenjē – Oh obedient heart!; vaṇangu – surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, the youthful one, ate the life of pūtanā who came assuming a deceitful form, ate the curd which was present near by, mercifully ate the butter, ate the life of the very strong kamsan, and mercifully placed this world in his divine stomach; being the desirable abode of such emperumān, arimēya viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr is having beauty of kāvēri river flowing and pushing along sandalwood trees, agaru trees and gold, enters the garden which has grown tall up to clouds and the fertile field and creates wealth; the brāhmaṇas who are great vaidikas, submitting the best flowers, standing there performing anjali, saying “Oh hari! Your divine feet are our refuge”, are surrendering with praises.

*vanjanai …* – Consuming the life of pūtanā who came with a deceitful form; mercifully ate the curd which was present near by; mercifully ate the butter; consumed kamsan’s life. For him, there is no difference between the objects which are touched by favourable persons and the life of the unfavourable persons.

*ivvulagu uṇḍa* – Just as he mercifully ate butter, he has taken the earth and placed in his stomach.

*kāviri …* – kāviri brings sandalwood. agil, gold and pushes into the garden which has grown tall to reach the clouds, and in the fertile field and creates unlimited wealth; as the brāhmaṇas see the arrival of the river, they offer flowers and perform anjali saying “sarvēśvaran has sent this for our livelihood” and reside there surrendering unto him.

## 3.10.10. Senru sinavidai

*senṟu sinavidai ēḻum pada adarttup pinnai sevvit tōḷ puṇarndu uganda tirumāl tan kōyil anṟu ayanum aran sēyum anaiyavargaḷ nāngūr arimēya viṇṇagaram amarnda seḻungunṟai kanṟi neduvēl valavan mangaiyar tam kōmān kalikanṟi olimālai aindinodu mūnṟum onṟinodum onṟum ivai kaṟṟu vallār ulagattu uttamargatku uttamarāy umbarum āvargaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

senṟu – himself went; sinam – angry; eḻu vidaiyum – seven bulls; pada adarttu – fought with them to have them killed; pinnai – nappinnaip pirātti’s; sevvit tōḷ – with her beautiful shoulder; puṇarndu – embraced; uganda – rejoiced; tirumāl than – where śriya:pati is residing; kōyil – being the abode; ayanum – brahmā; aran sēyum – subrahmaṇyan who is son of rudran; anaiyavargaḷ – having similar tranquility and beauty,who are residing; nāngūr – in tiunāngūr; arimēya viṇṇagaram – in arimēya viṇṇagaram; amarnda – eternally residing; seḻum kunṟai – the lord who is similar to a beautiful mountain; kanṟi nedu vēl valavan – having stained, long spear in his hand; mangaiyar tam kōmān – being the leader of the residents of tirumangai; kali kanṟi – composed by āḻvār who is kalivairi (enemy of kali); oli mālai – garland which has music; aindinodu – five pāsurams (which speak about kriṣṇa leelā); mūnṟum – three pāsurams which speak about narasimha and vāmana leelās; onṟinodum – first pāsuram which is about arcāvatāram; onṟum – this pāsuram which is palastuti (explains the fruit of reciting this decad); ivai – these ten pāsurams; kaṟṟu – learnt; vallār – those who can see the meanings; ulagattu – in this world; uttmargatku uttamarāy – being the leader of vaiṣṇavas (and further); umbarum āvargaḷ – will join the group of nityasūris

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

śriya:pati himself went and fought with the seven, angry bulls to have them killed and embraced nappinaip pirātti’s beautiful shoulder and rejoiced; being the abode of such emperumān, where those who, having similar tranquility and beauty of brahmā and subrahmaṇyan who is son of rudran, are residing, lord who is similar to a beautiful mountain is eternally residing in arimēya viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr; having stained, long spear in his hand, being the leader of the residents of tirumangai, āḻvār who is kalivairi, composed these ten pāsurams as garland with music, where five pāsurams speak about kriṣṇa leelā, three pāsurams speak about narasimha and vāmana leelās, first pāsuram which is about arcāvatāram and this pāsuram which is palastuti; those who learnt these pāsurams and see the meanings, will be the leader of vaiṣṇavas in this world and will eventually join the group of nityasūris.

*senṟu …* – The abode of śriya:pati who went to the place where the seven bulls where present and killed those seven bulls which were angry, embraced nappinnaip pirātti’s beautiful shoulder and rejoiced.

*anṟu …* – The lord who is similar to a beautiful mountain, who is residing in arimēya viṇṇagaram in tirunāngūr where those who reside are similar to brahmā in tranquility and subrahmaṇya in beauty, is being praised in these poems.

*kanṟi nedu vēl …* – āḻvār who is having the spear which has stains from piercing the bodies of enemies, due to not having time to cleanse them, and who is the leader of the residents of tirumangai, mercifully composed these garlands of words with music. Those who are able to learn these ten pāsurams (eight + two), will remain leaders of vaiṣṇavas as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-1-payilum-sudaroli/) “*payilum tiru udaiyār evarēlum – emmai āḷum paramarē*” (those who have the wealth of being together with him to be eternally engaged in him, even if they lack (high birth, knowledge, actions), even in that same state, they are the supreme masters having us as servitors in many births) and subsequently will become the residents of paramapadam. They will get to be in the group of tiruvadi (garudāḻvār), tiruvanandāḻvān (ādi śēśan),

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## Fourth Centum

## 4.1 Podalarnda

## 4.1.1. Podalarnda

*pōdalarnda poḻiṟcōlaip puṟam engum poru tiraigaḷ tādudira vandalaikkum tadamaṇṇit ten karai mēl mādavan tān uṟaiyum idam vayal nāngai varivaṇḍu tēdena enṟu isai pādum tiruttēvanār togaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pōdu – flowers; alarnda – blossomed; poḻil sōlai – filled with dense gardens; puṟam engum – in all of the surroundings; tādu – pollen; udira – to fall down; poru – hitting each other; tiraigaḷ vandu – waves come; alaikkum – throwing up; tadam – vast; maṇṇi – the river named maṇṇi, its; then karai mēl – on the southern banks; mādavan tān – sarvēśvaran who is the divine lord of śrī mahālakśmi; uṟaiyum – eternally residing; idam – being the abode; vayal – surrounded by fertile fields; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; vari – striped; vaṇḍu – beetles; tēdena – as in “tenna tenna” (head-swaying tune); in isai – beautiful song; pādum – singing; tiruttēvanār togai – the divine abode named tiruttēvanār togai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who is the divine lord of śrī mahālakśmi, is eternally residing in the divine abode named tiruttēvanār togai where striped beetles are singing beautiful songs as in “tenna tenna” (head-swaying tune), in tirunāngūr which is surrounded by fertile fields, which is located on the southern banks of the vast river named maṇṇi, which is throwing up its waves which come hitting each other, to make the pollen of the flowers in the dense gardens in all the surroundings, which have blossomed flowers, fall down.

*pōdalarnda* – Blossomed at the apt time; alternative explanation – blossomed flowers.

*poḻil sōlaip puṟam engum* – In the surroundings which are filled with dense gardens, the waves in the vast river named maṇṇi, which hit each other, throw up to make the pollen fall down in those gardens. On the southern banks of such river.

*mādavan tān uṟaiyum idam* – The abode where the tasteful person (who enjoys śrī mahālakśmi) is residing; just as sītāp pirātti and he resided in tiruccitrakūtam. tiruttēvanār togai is in tirunāngūr which has fertile fields, the striped beetles consume the honey and are singing songs with tune, as muktātmās would sing sāma vēdam.

*tēdena* – Humming of beetles is said as “*tenna tenna*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.1.2. Yavarumay

*yāvarumāy yāvaiyumāy eḻil vēdap poruḷgaḷumāy mūvarumāy mudalāya mūrtti amarndu uṟaiyum idam māvarum tiṇpadai mannai venṟi koḷvār mannu nāngai dēvarum senṟu iṟainju poḻil tiruttēvanār togaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yāvarumāy – having all cētanas (sentient beings) as his prakāram (form); yāvaiyumāy – having all acētanas (insentient objects) as his prakāram; eḻil – beautiful; vēdam – shown in vēdams; poruḷgaḷumāy – having entities as his prakāram; mūvarumāy – being the antaryāmi of brahmā and rudra who perform creation and annihilation, and incarnating as viṣṇu who sustains; mudalāya – being the cause for such brahmā and rudra; mūrtti – sarvēśvaran who is supreme; amarndu – firmly placed; uṟaiyum – eternally residing; idam – being the abode; mā – riding the horse; varum – arriving; tiṇ – firm; padai – having weapons; mannai – royal kings; venṟi koḷvār – brāhmaṇas who can defeat; mannu – residing firmly; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; dēvarum – dēvatās such as indran et al; senṟu – approach; iṟainjum – remaining to be prayed to; poḻil – having gardens; tiruttēvanār togai – divyadēśam named tiruttēvanār togai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who is supreme, who is having all cētanas, acētanas and entities shown, in beautiful vēdam, as his prakāram, being the antaryāmi of brahmā and rudra who perform creation and annihilation, and incarnating as viṣṇu who sustains, being the cause for such brahmā and rudra, is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruttēvanār togai; this divyadēsam which has gardens and is the abode where sarvēśvaran remains to be approached and prayed to by dēvatās such as indran et al, is in tirunāngūr where brāhmaṇas who can defeat the royal kings who arrive riding the horse, wielding firm weapons, are residing firmly.

*yāvarumāy yāvaiyumāy* – emperumān who remains prakāri and has all cētanas and acētanas who are qualified to be seen, as his prakāram, to be identified by the word “Him”.

*eḻil vēdap poruḷgaḷumāy* – the meanings which are only revealed in vēdam such as ātmā is beyond body, cit and acit are in causal state, auspicious qualities \[of bhagavān\], bhagavān’s true nature.

*mūvarum …* – Entering into brahmā and rudran who are capable of performing creation and annihilation, as antaryāmi and facilitating such actions for them, and remaining as self and managing the task of protecting others; due to this he can be said to be remaining as all three entities. Being the cause for such brahmā and rudran, the eternal abode of such supreme lord.

*mā …* – In tirunāngūr which is the abode of brāhmaṇas who oppose and defeat kings who arrive on mā – horse, and wield firm weapons. The residents of this divyadēśam are said as in periya tirumoḻi 4.5.6 “*ondiṟal tennan ōda vadavarasōttam kaṇḍa, tiṇḍiṟalāḷar*” (The very strong brāhmaṇas who defeated the very strong pāṇḍiya king and the cōḷa king who were staying north of pāṇḍiyas). A person named udaiya piḷḷai came saying “I am going to sing about the temple \[of other dēvatā\]” , they went opposing him and drove him away and he ran away without singing about that temple – this is well known.

*dēvarum …* – tiruttēvanār togai where the dēvatās would come and surrender unto him to attain their positions.
