## 4.1.3. Van nadum

*vānādum maṇṇādum maṟṟuḷḷa palluyirum tānāya emperumān talaivan amarndu uṟaiyum idam ānāda perunjelvattu arumaṟaiyōr nāngai tannuḷ tēnārum malarp poḻil sūḻ tiruttēvanār togaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vān nādum – paramapadam which is located in the supreme sky; maṇ nādum – leelā vibhūti (samsāram) which has the earth; maṟṟu uḷḷa – further, present in those worlds; pal uyirum – different types of ātmās; tān āya – having these as his prakāram, and being antarātmā for all of these; talaivan – the lord; emperumān – sarvēśvaran; amarndu uṟaiyumidam – firmly residing abode; ānāda – imperishable; perum – endless; selvattu – having wealth; aru – difficult to learn; maṟaiyōr – where brāhmaṇas, who have completely learnt vēdam, are residing; nāngai tannuḷ – in tirunāngūr; tēn ārum – filled with honey; malar – having flowers; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruttēvanār togai – divyadēśam named tiruttēvanār togai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, the lord is having paramapadam which is located in the supreme sky, leelā vibhūti (samsāram) which has the earth, and further, different types of ātmās present in those worlds as his prakāram; he is the antarātmā for all of these, firmly residing in the divyadēśam named tiruttēvanār togai which is surrounded by gardens which are having flowers filled with honey; this is in tirunāngūr where brāhmaṇas, who are having imperishable, endless wealth and who have completely learnt vēdam which are difficult to learn, are residing.

*vān nādum maṇ nādum …* – paramapadam, samsāram, and not just the places but the different ātmās who are present in such abodes, are all present as his prakāram (form) to be identified by the word “him” – such sarvēśvaran. sarvēśvaran who is the abhimāni (controller) of everything as in when a person who lives with his family is asked “What do you need for your livelihood?” he would say “I will need a pot of paddy” considering his family is implied by the word “I”.

*talaivan amarndu uṟaiyum idam …* – The abode where the lord is eternally residing; he is the lord because he is having every entity other than him to be his prakāram (form) and there is none other than him and he is having all other entities to be taking shelter in his shade; hence he is the lord.

*ānāda …* – In tirnāngūr where brāhmaṇas who have imperishable and boundless wealth.

*tēn …* – Having abundance of honey; alternative explanation – densely filled with beetles.

## 4.1.4. Indiranum

*indiranum imaiyavarum munivargaḷum eḻil amainda sanda malarc cadumuganum kadiravanum candiranum endai emakku aruḷ ena ninṟu aruḷum idam eḻil nāngai sundara naṟpoḻil pudai sūḻ tiruttēvanār togaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

indiranum – dēvēndra; imaiyavarum – (other) dēvatās; munivargaḷum – great sages (such as sanaka et al); eḻil amainda – having beauty which fits in him (due to always reciting vēdam); sandam – having learnt vēdam (fully); malar – having lotus flower as birth place; sadumuganum – four-headed brahmā; kadiravanum – sun; candiranum – moon; endai – “Oh my lord!; emakku – In our matter; aruḷ ena – You should shower your mercy” – as they pray this way; ninṟu aruḷum idam – (to fulfil their desires) the abode where he is mercifully present; eḻil – beautiful; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; sundaram – beautiful; nal – distinguished; poḻil – by gardens; pudai – all the surroundings; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruttēvanār togai – divyadēśam named tiruttēvanār togai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

dēvēndra, (other) dēvatās, great sages, four-headed brahmā who is having beauty which fits in him, who learnt vēdam and has lotus flower as birth place, sun and moon pray saying “Oh my lord! You should shower your mercy in our matter” to emperumān in divyadēśam named tiruttēvanār togai, where he is mercifully present and which is surrounded by beautiful, distinguished gardens in the surroundings, in beautiful tirnāngūr.

*indiran …* – indran, dēvatās, sages such as sanaka et al, four-headed brahmā who is beautiful, having vēdam and is having lotus flower as his birth place; he always recites vēdam and teaches vēdam. Sun, moon and those who have strong heads in samsāram, which is his wealth would say “You, who are our lord, should mercifully give your grace to us”; he arrived here and mercifully stood in this divyadēśam to conduct their positions.

*eḻil …* – Instead of having to deal with such tasks (of dēvatās et al), this abode is where he remains continuously seeing the beautiful gardens.

## 4.1.5. Andamum

*aṇḍamum ivvalai kadalum avanigaḷum kulavaraiyum uṇḍa pirān uṟaiyum idam oḷimaṇi sandu agil kanagam teṇ tiraigaḷ varat tirattum tigaḻ maṇṇit tenkarai mēl tiṇ tiṟalār payil nāngait tiruttēvanār togaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇḍamum – sky; alai – waves agitating; ikkadalum – these oceans; avanigaḷum – the islands (such as jambūdvīpam); kula varaiyum – anchoring mountains (such as himavān); uṇḍa – mercifully consumed (these during praḷayam); pirān – benefactor; uṟaiyum idam – the abode where he resides; oḷi – having radiance; maṇi – precious gems; sandu – sandalwood trees; agil – dēvadāru (eagle wood) logs; kanagam – gold; teḷ – pure, flawless; tiraigaḷ – waves’; vara – in the arrival; tirattum – bringing and making a heap of collections; tigaḻ – shining; maṇṇi – river maṇṇi’s; then karai mēl – on the southern banks; tiṇ – firm; tiṟalār – those who are strong; payil – densely living; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; tiruttēvanār togai – tiruttēvanār togai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abode where the benefactor who mercifully consumed the sky, these oceans where waves are agitating, and the anchoring mountains, is residing, is tiruttēvanār togai in tirunāngūr which is on the southern banks of the river maṇṇi; the  river is bringing radiant precious gems, sandalwood trees, dēvadāru (eagle wood) logs and gold in the arrival of its pure, flawless waves and making heaps of those materials which make the river shine and where those who are with firm strength are living densely.

*aṇḍam …* – When there was the danger of deluge, emperumān, the benefactor placed all of the sky, oceans and anchoring mountains, and protected them; the abode where such benefactor resides; the pure, flawless waves bring radiant precious gems, sandalwood, agil (eagle wood) and gold, and make them as heaps and cause radiance to the river; on the southern banks of such river.

*tiṇ tiṟalār* – Just as it is said in the “den where lion lives”, the abode where those who are very strong and cannot be defeated by anyone, are densely living.

## 4.1.6. Jnalam ellam

*jñālam ellām amudu seydu nānmaṟaiyum todarāda pālaganāy ālilaiyil paḷḷi koḷḷum paraman idam sāli vaḷam perugi varum tadamaṇṇit tenkarai mēl sēl ugaḷum vayal nāngait tiruttēvanār togaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāl maṟaiyum – vēdams which are best among the pramāṇams \[authentic texts\] and are of four types; todarāda – having greatness of not being able to be aptly spoken by; pālaganāy – being a young child; jñālam ellām – the whole world; amudu seydu – swallowed; Al ilaiyil – in a tender banyan leaf; paḷḷi koḷḷum – mercifully resting; paraman – supreme lord; idam – the abode where he eternally resides; tadam – vast; maṇṇit then karai mēl – on the southern banks of maṇṇi river; sāli – of the reddish paddy crops; vaḷam – richness; perugi varum – growing; sēl – sēl (carp) fish; ugaḷum – jumping; vayal – having fertile fields; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; tiruttēvanār togai – divyadēśam named tiruttēvanār togai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Having greatness of not being able to be aptly spoken of by vēdams which are best among the pramāṇams and are of four types, the supreme lord, being a young child, swallowed the whole world, mercifully rested on a tender banyan leaf; the abode where he eternally resides is the divyadēśam named tiruttēvanār togai in tirunāngūr which is on the southern banks of the vast maṇṇi river, which is having fertile fields with richness of the reddish paddy crops growing and where carp fish are jumping around.

*jñālam ellām amudu seydu* – Swallowed the whole world.

*nān maṟai …* – He is having super-human activities which cannot be understood even by vēdam, which understands that sarvēśvaran is incomprehensible; he is mercifully resting on a fresh banyan leaf; the abode of such emperumān.

*sāli …* – On the southern banks of the vast maṇṇi river; in tirunāngūr which has fertile fields where paddy crops have grown very well and carp fish are jumping around.

## 4.1.7. Odada

*ōdāda vāḷariyin uruvāgi iraṇiyanai vādāda vaḷḷugirāl piḷandu aḷainda māladidam ēdēṟu perunjelvattu eḻil maṟaiyōr nāngai tannuḷ sēdēṟu poḻil taḻuvu tiruttēvanār togaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōdāda – (new) not usually seen (in this world); āḷ ariyin – narasimha’s; uruvāgi – assuming the form; vādāda – not bending (remaining firm); vaḷ – sharp; ugirāl – with the nails; iraṇiyanai – hiraṇyāsuran; piḷandu – tore; aḷainda – stirring (the limbs); māladu – sarvēśvaran who has great love towards his devotees, his; idam – abode; ēdu – in the book; ēṟu – to be seen after writing; perum – being incomprehensible; selvattu – having wealth; eḻil – having beauty of revealing bhagavān’s svarūpam etc; maṟaiyōr – the eternal residence of śrīvaiṣṇavas who are experts in vēdams; nāngai than uḷ – in tirunāngūr; sēdu – youthfulness; ēṟu – growing; malar – of the flowers; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruttēvanār togai – tiruttēvanār togai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who has great love towards his devotees, assumed the narasimha form which is not usually seen, tore hiraṇyāsuran with his sharp nails which don’t bend, and stirred the limbs in his body; his abode is tiruttēvanār togai which is surrounded by flower gardens which have growing youthfulness in tirunāngūr; this is the eternal residence of śrīvaiṣṇavas who are experts in vēdams which are having beauty of revealing bhagavān’s svarūpam etc and are having incomprehensible wealth which is to be seen after writing about them in books.

*ōdāda …* – Assumed the narasimha form which is not usually seen in this world, with the firm, divine nails which will not bend even while operating on the hard body of hiraṇyan.

*piḷandu aḷainda māladu idam* – Not just satisfied after killing him, as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.1.1 “*udiram aḷainda kaiyōdirundānai*” (one who remained with the blood-soaked hand), due to the anger on the one \[hiraṇyan\] who showed anger on the child \[prahlādāḻvān\], he stirred the body of hiraṇyan. The abode of emperumān with such love towards prahlādāḻvān.

*ēdēṟu …* – The wealth of the brāhmaṇas in this divyadēśam cannot just be seen and left, but should be written on a book and seen as in śrīrāmāyaṇam. \[2nd meaning\] ēṟugai – going. ēdu – defect. Great wealth which has no defect. \[3rd meaning\] Alternatively – the wealth which will go over the book – i.e., the book will get destroyed \[being unable to hold the greatness\].

*sēdēṟu poḻil taḻuvu* – Being surrounded by youthful garden.

*sēdēṟu malarp poḻil sūḻ* – Being surrounded by garden which has flowers; similar to what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.10.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-1-kilaroli-ilamai/) “*vaḷariḷam poḻil sūḻ*” (surrounded by gardens which are growing yet youthful).

## 4.1.8. Vararum

*vārārum iḷangongai maidiliyai maṇam puṇarvān kārār tiṇ silai iṟutta tanik kāḷai karudumidam ērārum perunjelvattu eḻil maṟaiyōr nāngai tannuḷ sīrārum malarp poḻil sūḻ tiruttēvanār togaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

var – by cloth; ārum – held; iḷam kongai – having youthful bosoms; maidiliyai – pirātti, the daughter of the ruler of mitilā; maṇam puṇarvān – to marry; kār Ar – very black; tiṇ – strong; silai – bow; iṟutta – being the one who broke; tani – distinguished; kāḷai – youthful cakravartit tirumagan; karudum idam – the abode where he is desirously residing; ēr ārum – very beautiful; perum – unbounded; selvattu – wealthy; eḻil maṟaiyōr – filled with śrīvaiṣṇavas who analyse the beautiful vēdams; nāngai tannuḷ – in tirunāngūr; sīr ārum – very beautiful; malar – having flowers; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruttēvanār togai – tiruttēvanār togai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The distinguished, youthful cakravartit tirumagan broke the very black, strong bow to marry pirātti, the daughter of the ruler of mitilā, who is having youthful bosoms, held by cloth. He resides desirously in tiruttēvanār togai which is surrounded by gardens having very beautiful flowers, in tirunāngūr, which is filled with śrīvaiṣṇavas who analyse the beautiful vēdams and who have very beautiful, unbounded wealth.

*vār Ar …* – To marry the divine daughter of śrī janakarāja, who is having bosoms which need to be held by cloth, cakravartit tirumagan who broke the bow which is so strong that it cannot be moved by anyone and who is having matchless age; the desirous abode of such emperumān.

*ērārum* … – In tirunāngūr where brāhmaṇas who have very beautiful, unbounded wealth.

*sīr ārum …* – Being surrounded by garden which have very beautiful flowers. The garden will reveal the wealth in the town.

## 4.1.9. Kumbamigu

*kumbamigu mada yānai pāganodum kulaindu vīḻa kombu adanaip paṟitteṟinda kūttan amarnduṟaiyum idam vambaviḻum seṇbagattin maṇangamaḻum nāngai tannuḷ sembon madiḷ poḻil pudai sūḻ tiruttēvanār togaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

migu – huge; kumbam – having head; madam – fleshy \[being fat\]; yānai – kuvalayāpīdam, the elephant; pāganodum – with its mahout; kulaindu – shivered; vīḻa – to fall; adan kombai – its tusk; paṟittu – plucked; eṟinda – threw down; kūttan – kriṣṇan who has beautiful leelās; amarndu – firmly; uṟaiyumidam – abode where he is eternally residing; seṇbagattin – śeṇbaga flower’s; vambu – freshness; aviḻum – spreading; maṇam – fragrance; kamaḻum – smelling nicely; nāngai tannuḷ – in tirunāngūr; sem pon – made with reddish gold; madiḷ – fortified streets; poḻil – gardens; pudai – to have them within it; sūḻ – being vast; tiruttēvanār togai – tiruttēvanār togai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇan who has beautiful leelās caused shivering for kuvalayāpīdam, the elephant with huge head and fleshy body, plucked its tusk and made it to fall down along with its mahout. His firm abode is tiruttēvanār togai which is vast enough to have fortified streets which are made with reddish gold and gardens, in tirunāngūr where śeṇbaga flowers’ freshness is spreading and its fragrance is smelling nicely.

*kumba* … – kriṣṇan effortlessly plucked the tusk of the elephant which has a huge head, just as one will pluck green leaves; he made the elephant to shiver and fall down along with its mahout. This was similar to wild grass falling down in a flood; the abode where such emperumān is residing with heart-stealing leelās.

*vambaviḻum …* – Freshly blossoming śeṇbaga flower is smelling fragrantly in tirunāngūr; tiruttēvanār togai has fortified streets, and gardens which surround those streets.

## 4.1.10. Kararnda

*kārārnda tirumēnik kaṇṇan amarndu uṟaiyum idam sīrārnda poḻil nāngait tiruttēvanār togai mēl kūrārnda vēṟkaliyan kūṟu tamiḻ pattum vallār ērārnda vaigundattu imaiyavarōdu iruppārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kār – with cloud; Ar – matching; tirumēni – having divine form; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇan; amarndu – firmly; uṟaiyum – residing; idam – being the abode; sīr ārnda – beautiful; poḻil – having gardens; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; tiruttēvanār togai – on the divyadēśam named tiruttēvanār togai; kūr ārnda – very sharp; vēl – having the weapon, spear; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; kūṟu – mercifully spoke; tamiḻ – in the divya prabandam in drāvida (tamiḻ) language; pattum – these ten pāsurams; vallār – those who have learnt; ēr ārnda – very noble; vaigundattu – in śrīvaikuṇṭam; imaiyavarōdu – being united with nityasūris; iruppār – will eternally reside there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇan, who is having divine form which matches a cloud, is firmly residing in the abode tiruttēvanār togai in tirunāngūr which is having beautiful gardens; on such divyadēśam, tirumangai āḻvār who is having sharp spear, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams in this divyaprabandam which is in tamiḻ language; those who have learnt these pāsurams, will eternally reside in the very noble śrīvaikuṇṭam, along with nityasūris.

*kār ārnda …* – kriṣṇan who is having cloud like rejuvenating form, is desirously residing in tiruttēvanār togai in tirunāngūr which has very beautiful gardens. On such divyadēśam.

*kūr ārnda …* – Just as he is a leader in using the spear on the opponents, he is a leader in singing poems too. Those who can recite these ten pāsurams, will unite with tiruvadi (garudāḻvār), tiruvanandāḻvān (ādiśēśan) et al in śrīvaikuṇṭam which has no end to goodness and will remain there eternally without separation as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*na ca punar āvartatē*” (There is no return).

## 4.2 Kamba ma kadal

## 4.2.1. Kamba ma kadal

*kamba mākadal adaittu ilangaikku man kadir mudi avai pattum ambināl aṟuttu arasu avan tambikku aḷittavan uṟai kōyil sembalānirai seṇbagam mādavi sūdagam vāḻaigaḷ sūḻ vambulām kamugōngiya nāngūr vaṇpurudōttamamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kambam – swaying (having waves); mā – vast; kadal – ocean; adaittu – building a bridge; ilangaikku – for the lankā city; man – rāvaṇa who is the lord, his; kadir – radiant; avai – such; mudi pattum – ten heads; ambināl – with arrows; aṟuttu – severed; avan tambikku – for vibhīśaṇāḻvān who was rāvaṇa’s brother; arasu aḷittavan – cakravartit tirumagan who mercifully gave the kingdom; uṟai – firmly residing; dēsam – abode; palā – jackfruit trees’; sem – best; nirai – rows; seṇbagam – śeṇbaga trees; mādavi – kurukkatti; sūdagam – mango trees; vāḻaigaḷ – plantain trees (by these); sūḻ – being surrounded; vambu – fragrance; ulā – spreading; kamugu – areca trees; ōngiya – being tall; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; vaṇ purudōttamam – divyadēśam named vaṇ purudōttamam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Building a bridge on the vast ocean which was swaying, cakravartit tirumagan severed the ten radiant heads of rāvaṇan who was the lord of lankā city, with arrows and mercifully gave the kingdom to vibhīśaṇāḻvān who was rāvaṇa’s brother; divyadēśam named vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr is the firm abode of such emperumān, which is surrounded by the best rows of jackfruit trees, śeṇbaga flowers, kurukkatti, mango trees, plantain trees and where fragrance is spreading and where areca trees are very tall.

*kamba mā …* – Built a bridge on the vast ocean which will dissolve everything with its waves; rāvaṇa who was prideful thinking “I am the controller of this well fortified lankā”; his.

*kadir mudi avai pattum* – The ten heads which were crowned during his victorious travels.

*ambināl aṟuttu* – Severing the heads which were strengthened by the boons such that they cannot be attacked even by brahmāstram, with bows which are natural for kings.

*arasu …* – emperumān mercifully gave rāvaṇa’s wealth/kingdom to vibhīśaṇāḻvān, rāvaṇa’s brother, thinking “Glad that one of our kinsmen is getting to rule the wealth/kingdom of rākśasas!”; the abode where such emperumān is eternally residing.

*sem palā …* – The gardens in the outskirts are surrounded by proper row of jackfruit trees, śeṇbagam, kurukkatti, mango trees, plantain trees.

The inner gardens are as in,

*vambu ulām kamugu ōngiya …* – In tirunāngūr where the fragrance of areca is always present.

## 4.2.2. Pallavam tigal

*pallavam tigaḻ pūngadambu ēṟi akkāḷiyan paṇavarangil ollai vanduṟap pāyndu arunadanjeyda umbar kōn uṟai kōyil nalla vendaḻal mūnṟu nālvēdam aivēḷviyōdu āṟangam valla andaṇar malgiya nāngūr vaṇpurudōttamamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pallavam – shoots; tigaḻ – shining; pū – blossomed; kadambu – on the kadamba tree; ēṟi – climbed; a kāḷiyan – such \[cruel\] kāḷiya’s; paṇam – hoods; arangil – on the \[dance\] stage; uṟa – to make him tired (and not escape); vandu – approached; ollai – quickly; pāyndu – jumped; aru – rare; nadam – dances; seyda – one who did; umbar kōn – the lord of dēvas; uṟai kōyil – abode where he resides; nalla – having the goodness to perform karmānuśtānams (carrying out deeds prescribed in vēdas); vem – hot; taḻal mūnṟu – three types of fire; nāl vēdam – four vēdams; ai vēḷvi – five great yajñas; āṟu angam – six ancillary subjects \[of vēdam\]; valla – those who can teach to others; andaṇar – brāhmaṇas; malgiya – is abundantly filled; nāngūr vaṇpurudōttamamē – vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa, the lord of dēvas, climbed on the kadamba tree which has blossomed and has shining shoots, approached and quickly jumped on the hoods of such cruel kāḷiya, which are the dancing stage, to make him tired and performed rare dances; vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr is the abode where he resides, which is abundantly filled with brāhmaṇas who can teach three types of hot fire which are having the goodness to perform karmānuśtānams, four vēdams, five great yajñas and six ancillary subjects \[of vēdam\], to others.

*pallavam …* – The kadamba tree was withered due to being burnt by kāḷiyan’s poison; having been touched by the divine feet of kriṣṇa, it blossomed nicely with flowers and leaves. Climbing on the blossomed kadamba tree with shining leaves, kriṣṇa quickly jumped on kāḷiyan’s hoods which were like dance stage, when kāḷiyan was not expecting it, so that he cannot escape.

*aru nadam seyda* – There are hard and soft forms of dance – he performed all of them. The abode where such leader of nityasūris, has arrived and is residing.

*nalla …* – The abode of brāhmaṇas who not only work hard and practice the three types of fire, four types of vēdam,  five great yajñams and six ancillary subjects of vēdam, but will also make others follow the same.

## 4.2.3. Andaranavar

*aṇḍarānavar vānavar kōnukku enṟu amaitta sōṟadu ellām uṇḍu kōnirai mēyttu avai kāttavan ugandu inidu uṟai kōyil koṇḍalār muḻavil kuḷirvār poḻil kula mayil nadamāda vaṇḍu tān isai pādidu nāngūr vaṇpurudōttamamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇḍar ānavar – covherds; vānavar kōnukku enṟu – considering to offer to dēvēndran \[the head of celestial entities\]; amaitta – prepared; adu sōṟu – that food; ellām – fully; uṇḍu – mercifully consumed; kō nirai – herds of cow; mēyttu – tended; avai – those cows; kāttavan – kriṣṇan who protected; ugandu – joyfully; inidu – being pleased; uṟai kōyil – abode where he is residing; koṇḍal – clouds; Ar – complete; muḻavu – having the roar; kuḷir – rejuvenating; vār – well grown; poḻil – in gardens; mayil kulam – pride of peacocks; nadam Ada – as they dance; vaṇḍu tān – beetles; isai – songs; pādidum – singing; nāngūr vaṇ purudōttamamē – vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇan mercifully consumed all of that food which was prepared by covherds to be offered to dēvēndran, tended those herds of cows and protected them; vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr is the joyful abode of such emperumān where he is residing, being pleased and where the clouds are roaring unitedly, and where the pride of peacocks is dancing and beetles are singing songs in the rejuvenating, well grown gardens.

*aṇḍar …* – The honest, simple covherds who do not know anything beyond what is seen in front as in “there is no other dēvatā greater than kriṣṇa who is standing in front of us and protecting us and our cattle”, prepared food for indran who is the leader of all the dēvatās; emperumān mercifully consumed all of that food.

*kō nirai mēyttu* – Subsequently since their protection is his responsibility, he tended them and eliminated their danger and protected them.

*ugandu inidu uṟai kōyil* – The abode where he is eternally residing with joy, considering “This is the abode which is apt for me to continue such protection”.

*koṇḍal …* – As the great roar of the clouds remains as the musical instrument, the pride of peacocks in the middle of the rejuvenating, vast garden dances, and the beetles which drink the honey in that garden sing songs matching their dance steps.

## 4.2.4. Parungai yanaiyin

*parungai yānaiyin kombinaippaṟittu adan pāganaic cādip pukku orunga mallaraik konṟu pin kanjanai udaittavan uṟai kōyil karumbinūdu uyar sāligaḷ viḷai taru kaḻaniyil mali vāvi marungelām poḻilōngiya nāngūr vaṇpurudōttamamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

parum – huge; kai – having trunk; yānaiyin – kuvalayāpīdam’s; kombinai – tusks; paṟittu – plucked; adan pāganai – the mahout who can conduct that elephant; sādi – killed; pukku – entered inside; orunga – who came together; mallarai – cāṇūra and muśtika; konṟu – destroyed; pin – subsequently; kanjanai – kamsan; udaittavan – kriṣṇa who kicked; uṟai kōyil – the abode where he is residing; karumbin – sugarcane garden’s; ūdu – in the middle; uyar – grown tall; sāligaḷ – red paddy crops; viḷai taru – growing; kaḻaniyil – in fertile fields; mali – present abundantly; vāvi – wells’; marungu elām – in the surroundings; ōngiya – grown tall; poḻil – having gardens; nāngūr vaṇ purudōttamē – vaṇ purudōttam in tirunāngūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa plucked the tusks of kuvalayāpīdam which is having huge trunk and killed the mahout who can conduct that elephant, entered inside and destroyed cāṇūra and muśtika who came together, and subsequently kicked kamsan; vaṇ purudōttam in tirunāngūr is the abode where he is residing, where reddish paddy crops are growing tall in fertile fields which are present in the middle of the sugarcane fields and which is having well grown gardens in the surroundings of abundantly present wells.

*parum kai …* – kriṣṇa broke the tusk of kuvalayāpīdam which is having long trunk; he then killed the mahout who can bring that elephant back to life even if it dies; subsequently he killed the wrestlers cāṇūra, muśtika et al; he then entered inside and killed kamsan by dragging him by his hair and pushed him to have his face hit the ground, by kicking him with divine feet. The abode where he is residing to eliminate similar hurdles.

*karumbu …* – In the middle of the sugarcane field, in the fertile field which has reddish paddy crops which compete with those sugarcane, in the surroundings of many ponds, the gardens have grown to fill the space in the sky.

## 4.2.5. Sadu poy

*sādu pōy viḻat tāḷ nimirttu īsan tan padaiyōdum kiḷaiyōdum  ōda vāṇanai āyiram tōḷgaḷum tuṇittavan uṟai kōyil āduvān kodi agal visumbu aṇavip pōyp pagalavan oḷi maṟaikkum māda māḷigai sūḻ taru nāngūr vaṇpurudōttamamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sādu – the wheel which was possessed by the demon; pōy – went far away; viḻa – to fall down and be destroyed; tāḷ – divine feet; nimirttu – stretched; īsan – rudran; than padaiyōdum – with his armies; kiḷaiyōdum – with his close aides such as śaṇmukha, gaṇapati et al; ōda – made to be defeated and run away; vāṇanai – bāṇāsura’s; āyiram tōḷgaḷum – thousand shoulders; tuṇittavan – kriṣṇa who destroyed; uṟai kōyil – the temple where he is residing; ādu – swaying; vān – big; kodi – flags; agal – vast; visumbu – sky; aṇavi – embracing; pōy – flying high; pagalavan – sun’s; oḷi – rays; maṟaikkum – blocking, to be not seen; mādam – by halls; māḷigai – by homes; sūḻ taru – being surrounded; nāngūr vaṇ purudōttamē – vaṇ purudōttam in tirunāngūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa stretched his divine feet to make the wheel which was possessed by the demon, to go far away, and to fall down and be destroyed; to have rudran, along with his armies and his family members, be defeated and run away, he severed the thousand shoulders of bāṇāsuran; the temple where he is residing is vaṇ purudōttam in tirunāngūr which is surrounded by halls and homes which have swaying. big flags which are embracing the vast sky and flying high to block the sun’s rays from those halls and homes.

*sādu …* – As śakatāsura approached when kriṣṇa did not get mother’s milk on time, he lifted his divine feet to kill that demon; rudran who considers himself to be the lord, came with his aides such as muṇḍan, nīṟan et al and fought, and subsequently ran away along with all of them and kriṣṇa severed the thousand shoulders of bāṇāsura who surrendered to other dēvatā; the abode where he has come and is residing to eliminate the enemies of his devotees.

*ādu …* – vaṇ purudōttam in tirunāngūr which is surrounded by halls and homes which have swaying. big flags which are embracing the vast sky and flying high to block the sun’s rays from those halls and homes.

## 4.2.6. Angaiyal

*angaiyāl adi mūnṟu nīr ēṟṟu ayan alar kodu toḻudu ētta gangai pōdarak kāl nimirttu aruḷiya kaṇṇan vanduṟai kōyil kongai kōngavai kātta vāy kumudangaḷ kātta māpadumangaḷ mangaimār mugam kāttidu nāngūr vaṇpurudōttamamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mūnṟu adi – for three steps of land; am – beautiful; kaiyāl – with his divine hand; nīr ēṟṟu – accepting the water which was given in charity; ayan – brahmā; alar kodu – gathering flowers; toḻudu – vorśipped; ētta – to praise; gangai – river gangā; pōdara – to start the flow of; kāl – divine feet; nimirttu aruḷiya – one who stretched; kaṇṇan – sarvēśvaran; vandu – (further) came for the protection of devotees; uṟai kōyil – the temple where he is residing; kōngu avai – the buds of the kōngu tree; mangaimār – the women (of that town); kongai – bosoms; kātta – show; kumudangaḷ – reddish āmbal flowers; vāy kātta – show their lips; mā – beautiful; padumangaḷ – lotus flowers; mugam – face; kāttidum – showing (things which resemble various limbs of the women); nāngūr vaṇ purudōttamamē – vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran accepted the water which was given in charity with his beautiful, divine hand for the three steps of land and stretched his divine feet to brahmā who gathered flowers, worshiped, and praised sarvēśvaran, and started the flow of river gangā; such emperumān came for the protection of devotees to the temple where he is residing which is in vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr where the buds of the kōngu tree show the bosoms of the women in that town, reddish āmbal flowers show their lips and the lotus flowers show their face.

*angai …* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21-7 “*gōsahasrapradātāram*” (one who gives away a thousand cows), with his beautiful hand which had stretched by giving charity, accepted the three steps of land and as he grew immediately after the water touched his hand, his divine foot reached up to brahmā’s abode and stayed close to brahmā’s han; brahmā gathered flowers etc and vorśipped him; gangā started flowing from there; the eternal abode of such sarvēśvaran who mercifully lifted his divine foot in this manner.

*kongai …* – The buds of the kōngu trees show the bosoms of the women of that town, the reddish āmbal flowers which have blossomed there show their lips and freshly blossomed reddish lotus flowers show their faces. With this, it is explained that, it is difficult to distinguish between the fertile fields there and the town itself.

## 4.2.7. Ulaiya on tiral

*uḷaiya oṇ tiṟal ponpeyarōn tanadu uram piḷandu udirattai aḷaiyum venjinattu ari pari kīṟiya appan vanduṟai kōyil iḷaiya mangaiyar iṇaiyadic cilambinōdu eḻilkoḷ pandadippōr kai vaḷaiyil ninṟoli malgiya nāngūr vaṇpurudōttamamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oḷ – very; tiṟal – strong; pon peyarōn – hiraṇyan; uḷaiya – to feel sorrowful; (avan) tanadu – his; uram – chest; piḷandu – tore; udirattai – blood; aḷaiyum – stirred with hand; vem – cruel; sinattu – angry; ari – being narasimha; pari – kēśi who came in the form of a horse; kīṟiya – one who tore down; appan – benefactor; vandu uṟai kōyil – the temple where he came and resided; iḷaiya mangaiyar – young girls (while dancing); iṇai adi – worn in their both feet; silambinōdu – with the sound from the anklets; eḻil koḷ – beautiful; pandu adippōr – those who play ball; kai vaḷaiyil ninṟu – originating from the bangles worn in the hands; oli – sound; malgiya – is abundant; nāngūr vaṇ purudōttamamē – vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, being cruel and angry narasimha, caused sorrow in the heart of very strong hiraṇyan, tore his chest and stirred the blood with his hand; he tore down kēśi who came in the form of a horse; the temple where such benefactor came and resided is vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr where the sound from anklets worn in both feet of the young girls and the sound originating from the bangles worn in the hands of those who play ball, are abundant.

*uḷaiya …* – To have the heart of hiraṇyan who has never feared, never had to eat/experience the unexpected and who is very strong, feel sorrow, emperumān tore his chest in to two parts.

*udirattai aḷaiyum vem sinattu ari* – Even after hiraṇyan became dead, narasimham stirred the flood of blood like stirring butter, due to the anger in him not being reduced, out of motherly forbearance towards prahlādāḻvān.

*pari kīṟiya* – The abode where the great benefactor who saved himself by tearing down kēśi who appeared causing fear to all.

*iḷaiya mangaiyar …* – The sound of the anklets of the little girls in that town who dance and the sound of the bangles in the hands of those who play ball, will suppress all other sounds of the town.

## 4.2.8. Valaiyar

*vāḷaiyār tadangaṇ umai pangan van sābam maṟṟadu nīnga mūḷaiyār sirattu aiyam mun aḷitta em mugil vaṇṇan uṟai kōyil pāḷai vān kamugūdu uyar tengin vanpaḻam viḻa veruvip pōy vāḷai pāy tadam sūḻ taru nāngūr vaṇpurudōttamamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāḷ – radiance; Ar – filled; tadam – vast; kaṇ – having eyes; umai – pārvati; pangan – rudra who is having in one part (of his body), his; van – cruel; sābam – curse; nīnga – to rid; adu – the sin which caused such curse; aṟṟu – to be exhausted; mūḷai – bone; Ar – complete; sirattu – brahmā’s skull (which got stuck to his hand); aiyam – alms; mun – previously; aḷitta – who gave; em – being my benefactor; mugil vaṇṇan – sarvēśvaran who has cloud like nature; uṟai kōyil – the temple where he resides; pāḷai – having swathes; vān – grown tall reaching up to the sky; kamugu – areca trees’; ūdu – in the middle; uyar – tall; tengin – coconut trees’; van – big; paḻam – fruit; viḻa – fall (into the tank); vāḷai – fish which are present there; veruvi – got afraid; pōy – leaving that place; pāy – jumping into another place; tadam – by ponds; sūḻ – surrounded by; nāngūr vaṇ purudōttamamē – vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, being our benefactor, previously gave alms to rudran who has given one part of his body to pārvati who has vast, very radiant eyes and who is having brahmā’s skull, to rid the cruel curse and to eliminate the sin which is the cause of such curse; such sarvēśvaran is having cloud like nature, is residing in the temple in vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr where areca trees which have grown tall reaching up to the sky and have swathes, are having in their middle, tall coconut trees, from where the coconut falls into the pond; seeing that, the fish got fearful and leaving that place, are jumping into another place.

*vāḷai …* – For dēvi, pārvati, who has very radiant and vast eyes, rudra is giving a part of his body; to have him freed from the strong curse, and to make the great sin which cannot be easily eliminated and which was caused by his act of  severing the head of brahmā who is the master of the universe and his father, without any reason, be eliminated, the greatly generous emperumān mercifully gave alms into the skull which has no blood and which only has bones; the abode of such emperumān \[who eliminated rudran’s suffering\].

*pāḷai …* – The big fruit from the coconut trees in the middle of tall areca trees which have swathes and which have filled the space in the sky, falls in to the pond, due to the close proximity between the coconut trees and the pond; the vāḷai fish think that the coconuts fall in there, aiming at them and leave the place seeking a place which is safer for them.

## 4.2.9. Induvar sadai

*induvār sadai īsanaip payanda nānmuganait tan eḻilārum undi māmalar mīmisaip padaittavan ugandu iniduṟai kōyil kundi vāḻaiyin koḻungani nugarndu tan kuruḷaiyait taḻuvippōy mandi māmbaṇai mēl vaigu nāngūr vaṇ purudōttamamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

indu – having moon; vār – lengthy; sadai – having matted hair; īsanai – rudran; payanda – created; nānmuganai – brahmā; than – his; eḻil – beauty; ārum – filled; undi – in divine navel; mā – huge; malar – lotus flower’s; mīmisai – on; padaittavan – sarvēśvaran who created; ugandu – being joyful; inidu – with pleasure; uṟai kōyil – the temple where he is residing; mandi – female monkey; vāḻaiyin – in plantain tree; koḻu – rich; kani – fruits; kundi – being in a crouching posture; nugarndu – ate; than – its; kuruḷaiyai – younger one; taḻuvi – embraced; pōy – left from there; mām paṇai mēl – on the branches of the mango tree; vaigu – sleeping; nāngūr vaṇ purudōttamamē – vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran created brahmā on the huge lotus flower in his divine navel which is filled with beauty; brahmā in turn created rudran who is having lengthy matted hair which has the moon in it. vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr is the temple where such emperumān is joyfully residing with pleasure, where the female monkey remained in crouching posture near the plantain tree which have rich fruits; the monkey ate those fruits and left from there embracing its younger one and slept on the branches of the mango tree.

*indu …* – sarvēśvaran created brahmā on the huge lotus flower in his divine navel which is filled with beauty; brahmā in turn created rudran who is having lengthy matted hair which has the moon in it. Such sarvēśvaran joyfully resides with pleasure in vaṇ purudōttamam in tirunāngūr, considering that this universe is created by brahmā who was created by him, for its protection.

*kundi …* – As the plantain trees are well ripened to touch the ground; the female monkey thinking “these are easily reachable for us” will come close; still the fruits will be unreachable for it; hence, the monkey would stretch itself in a crouching position and pluck the beautiful fruits and eat it. Further, it would embrace its younger one, set out to eat the mangoes, will sleep on the mango tree branches due to the contact of its younger one and for digesting the food which was eaten.

## 4.2.10. Mannular pugal

*maṇṇuḷār pugaḻ vēdiyar nāngūr vaṇ purudōttamattuḷ aṇṇal sēvadik kīḻ adaindu uyndavan āliman aruḷmāri paṇṇuḷār tarap pādiya pādal ippattum vallār ulagil eṇṇilāda pērinbam uṟṟu imaiyavarōdum kūduvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇṇuḷ – In earth; Ar – abundant; pugaḻ – having fame; vēdiyar – where śrīvaiṣṇavas, who are naturally engaged in vēda adyayanam, are residing; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; vaṇ purudōttamattuḷ – mercifully present in divyadēśam named vaṇ purudōttamam; aṇṇal – sarvēśvaran, who is lord; sē – beautiful; adik kīḻ – under the divine feet; adaindu – reached; uyndavan – who became redeemed; Ali – for the residents of tiurvāli; man – being the king; aruḷ māri – tirumangai āḻvār who is a cloud, raining mercy; paṇṇuḷ – in tune; Ar tara – being complete; pādiya – sang; pādal – being pāsurams; ip pattum – these ten pāsurams; vallār – those who have learnt; ulagil – in this world; eṇ ilāda – countless; pēr inbam – great joy; uṟṟu – attain (and subsequently); imaiyavarōdum – with nityasūris; kūduvar – will unite

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is the lord who is mercifully present in the divyadēśam named vaṇ purudōttamam where śrīvaiṣṇavas who are naturally engaged in vēda adyayanam, and are having abundant fame on the earth, are residing; tirumangai āḻvār who is a cloud raining mercy, reached under the divine feet of such emperumān and became redeemed;  he is the king for the residents of tiurvāli and sang these ten pāsurams which are complete in tune; those who have learnt these pāsurams will attain countless, great joy and will unite with nityasūris.

*maṇṇuḷ …* – *maṇṇuḷ Ar pugaḻ vēdiyar* – brāhmaṇas who have great fame on the earth; *maṇṇuḷār pugaḻ* – those who are praised by the residents of earth. Attained sarvēśvaran’s divine feet, and attained self realisation from being in the state as mentioned in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva sabhavati*” (considered as insentient).

*Ali man* – āḻvār who is the chief of the residents of tiruvāli.

*aruḷ māri* – Very magnanimous āḻvār who is like a cloud while giving mercy to his devotees, sang these ten pāsurams which are complete with tune. Those who are experts in these pāsurams, will have unlimited joy in this world, and subsequently, will become part of the group of nityasūris who are joyful.

## 4.3 Peranindu

## 4.3.1. Peranindu

*pēraṇindu ulagattavar toḻudēttum pēraruḷāḷan empirānai vāraṇi mulaiyāḷ malarmagaḷōdu maṇmagaḷum udan niṟpa sīraṇi māda nāngai nannaduvuḷ sembonsey kōyilin uḷḷē kāraṇi mēgam ninṟadoppānaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu uyndoḻindēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ulagattavar – all the residents of the world; pēr aṇindu – gather as a huge crowd; toḻudu – surrender; ēttum – one who remains to be praised; pēr aruḷāḷan – (on them) one who gives boundless mercy; kār – seen in rainy season; aṇi ninṟadu – beautiful; mēgam oppānai – one who is similar to a cloud; em pirānai – being our benefactor; vār aṇi – tied up by a corset; mulaiyāḷ – having bosoms; malar magaḷōdu – with periya pirāttiyār who was born in flower and is eternally youthful; maṇ magaḷum – and śrī bhūmip pirātti; udan niṟpa – while they stand together; sīr – having wealth; aṇi – beautiful; mādam – having mansions; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; nal naduvuḷ – present in the good central location; sem pon sey kōyilin uḷḷē – in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – enjoyed with my eyes; uyndu – enlivened; oḻindēn – became satisfied

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān remains to be surrendered and praised by all the residents of the world who have gathered as a huge crowd; he gives boundless mercy to them; he is similar to a beautiful cloud seen in the rainy season; he is our benefactor; as he stands together with periya pirāttiyār who has bosoms tied up by a corset,  who was born in flower and is eternally youthful, and śrī bhūmip pirātti, in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil which is present in the good central location of tirunāngūr which is having beautiful mansions, I enjoyed him with my eyes, enlivened and became satisfied.

*pēr aṇindu …* – As all the residents of the world gather and constantly fall at his divine feet, praise him by reciting his divine names and surrender unto him, he gives them his mercy to such an extent that it is beyond their surrender; in this manner he became my benefactor. Both periya pirāttiyār who has eternal youth, using which she involves the divine heart of sarvēśvaran towards her and makes him ignore the defects of the devotees as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed) and śrībhūmip pirātti who  would say “Why first see the mistake, then forgive? \[Just don’t see the mistakes\]” are the teachers for him in the matter of patience.

*sīr …* – To start with, tirunāngūr is more wealthy in comparison to the wealth in the world; in the divyadēśam sembonsey kōyil, which is in the perfect centre of such city where such wealth is revealed through the beautiful mansions.

*kār aṇi …* – I got to enjoy with my eyes, the emperumān who is having a beautiful form which is similar to a cloud in the rainy season, which is about to pour down, and got relieved from the state as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (as good as acit) and became enlivened as said in the same upaniśat “*santamēnam*” (to be considered as cit) and became satisfied – says āḻvār.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.3.2. Pirappodu muppu

*piṟappodu mūppu onṟillavan tannaip pēdiyā inba veḷḷattai iṟappedir kālak kaḻivum ānānai ēḻisaiyin suvai tannai siṟappudai maṟaiyōr nāngai nannaduvuḷ sembonsey kōyilin uḷḷē maṟaip perum poruḷai vānavar kōnaik kaṇḍu nān vāḻndoḻindēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

piṟappodu – Birth; mūppu – old-age (and other changes); onṟu – even a little bit; illavan tannai – being the one who is not having; bēdiyā – not having differences such as inequality etc (and being the same at all times); inba veḷḷattai – being the firm abode of bliss like an ocean; iṟappu – in past; edir kālam – in future; kaḻivum – and in present (in all three times); ānānai – one being present; ēḻ isaiyin – sapta svara’s (seven tunes’); suvai tannai – being enjoyable like the taste; maṟai – revealed by vēdam; perum poruḷai – important principle; vānavar kōnai – sarvēśvaran who is the leader of nityasūris; siṟappu udai maṟaiyōr – eternally inhabited by best among the brāhmaṇas who have greatness; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; nal naduvuḷ – present in the good central location; sem pon sey kōyilin uḷḷē – in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – enjoyed with my eyes; vāḻndu – enlivened; oḻindēn – became satisfied

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is not having even a little bit of change such as birth, old-age; he is the firm abode of bliss like an ocean which is not having differences such as inequality etc; he is present in past, future and present; he is enjoyable like the taste of sapta svaras; he is the important principle revealed by vēdam; he is the leader of nityasūris; in the good central location of tirunāngūr which is eternally inhabited by best among the brāhmaṇas who have greatness, I enjoyed him with my eyes, enlivened and became satisfied.

*piṟappu …* – Since there is no specific reason \[karma\] for taking birth or becoming old, sarvēśvaran is not having the scope for janma (birth) jarā (old-age) etc. While brahmā et al are born and grow old, just because they live long enough, survive brahma kalpa (brahmā’s reign) and still die in the end, they were said to be not having birth and old-age \[using the terms aja, amara etc\]; but such aspect cannot be attributed to emperumān, to start with \[since he always remains the same\].

*bēdiyā inba veḷḷattai* – Unchanging ocean of bliss. He is said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ānandamaya:*” (filled with bliss). Abundance of bliss in indicated here. Though the true nature of jīvātmā and his darmabhūta jñānam (knowledge) are eternal, as per the expansion and contraction of mind which is the entrance for knowledge, dawn and dusk of knowledge is spoken about. Similarly, though the jīvātmā is eternal, due to acquiring and discarding of body based on one’s karma, he is spoken of as to be “born” and to “die”; since such karma does not exist for bhagavān, he is always having a singular nature which never changes.

Due to this reason, he is present at all three times.

*iṟappedir …* – iṟappu – past; edir – future; kaḻivu – present; one who is present at all times. Not having birth and old age, having a singular form and being present at all times.

*ēḻu isaiyin suvai tannai* – One who is greatly enjoyable as the embodiment of the taste in the sapta svaras.

*bēdiyā inba veḷḷam* – spoken about the sweetness of his true nature; here the sweetness acquired due to being present with auspicious qualities is spoken about.

*siṟappu …* – siṟappu – abundance. Thus, in the centre of tirunāngūr which has brāhmaṇas who have greatness due to their brāhmaṇyam (being pure in their qualities).

*sem pon sey kōyilin uḷḷē* – Not having to go to paramapadam \[right here in sembonsey kōyil\].

*maṟaip perum poruḷai* – jīvātmās and brahmā et al are explained in vēdams; unlike them, since bhagavān is distinguished and has everyone other than him as his prakāram (form) and remains the prakāri (substratum), he is the primary object of vēdam. [śrī bhagavat gītā 15.15](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/15-15/) “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya:*” (I am only spoken about in all of vēdams). katōpaniśat “*sarvē vēda yat padamāmananti*” (the one whose nature is spoken about in all of vēdam).

*vānavar kōnai* – Such person is as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (Lord of the faultless nityasūris); now, vēdam too proclaims in viṣṇu sūktam “*tadviprāsō vipanyavō jāgruvāgumsa: samindatē*” (The best, vast abode of viṣṇu, paramapadam, which is reached by nityasūris who are filled with wisdom, is always engaged in devotion and is careful). I got to see such emperumān instead of just hearing about him as the one who is known only from vēdam.

*vāḻndu oḻindēn* – āḻvār is saying “I am satisfied here itself since I don’t need to seek a special place (paramapadam) for a great life, pack food for the travel and travel for a long distance”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.3.3. Tidavisumbu

*tidavisumbu eri nīr tingaḷum sudarum seḻunilattu uyirgaḷum maṟṟum padar poruḷgaḷumāy ninṟavan tannai pangayattu ayanavan anaiya tidamoḻi maṟaiyōr nāngai nannaduvuḷ sembonsey kōyilin uḷḷē kadal niṟa vaṇṇan tannai nān adiyēn kaṇḍu koṇḍu uyndoḻindēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tidam – firm; visumbu – sky; eri – fire; nīr – water; tingaḷ – moon; sudarum – sun; seḻu – rich; nilattu – on earth; uyirgaḷum – creatures; maṟṟum – further; padar – vast; poruḷgaḷum – objects (for these); āy – being antarātmā (in-dwelling super-soul); ninṟavan tannai – one who is present; kadal – ocean’s; niṟam – matching the colour; vaṇṇan tannai – one who has the divine form; pangayattu – born in the lotus flower in the divine navel; avan – being famous in this manner; tidam – unśakeable; moḻi – having speech; ayan anaiya – matching brahmā; maṟaiyōr – best among brāhmaṇas are residing; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; nal naduvuḷ – present in the good central location; sem pon sey kōyilin uḷḷē – in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – enjoyed with my eyes; uyndu – enlivened; oḻindēn – became satisfied

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, the antarātmā for the firm sky, fire, water, moon, sun, creatures on the rich earth and other vast objects, has divine form with the complexion of ocean; I enjoyed such emperumān with my eyes in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil which is present in the good central location in tirunāngūr where the best among brāhmaṇas who are matching brahmā who is famous for being born in the lotus flower in the divine navel of emperumān, and who is having unśakeable speech, enlivened and became satisfied.

*tida visumbu* – lōkāyadika (cāruvāka – materialistic philosophy), said “There is no entity named ākāśa” to start with; to reject his philosophy āḻvār is saying “*tida visumbu*” as per vaidika method as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ākāśādvāyu:*” (From sky comes air), being created before all other entities, and remaining even after all other entities are destroyed. Alternatively, \[since rejecting other philosophy is not the objective\] āḻvār is speaking about panca bhūtam (five great elements) where each element has a particular firm quality \[here tida is common for all elements mentioned here\]; the three elements mentioned here are representatives for the five great elements, and the nature mentioned for one element is applicable for all elements.

*tingaḷum sudarum* – representastive for all of the effectual (fully created) objects. Among those, being moon and sun, humans on earth, and the unspoken dēva (celestial beings), triyak (animals, birds) stāvara (plants etc), emperumān remains in a vast manner. He created all of them as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*tat sruśtvā*” (He created it) etc, entering in all of them and due to that he remains to be known as those. As said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*tatvamasi*” (You are that), bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*ayam ātmā brahma*” (This ātmā is brahmam) and atarvaṇa brahma sūktam “*brahma dāśā:*” (even the \[inferior\] dāśas are brahmam only since brahmam pervades everywhere).

*pangayam* … They would have the speech which will never go in vain, just as that of brahmā who was born in the lotus flower in the divine navel. If they give their words, those cannot be broken even by them – some other alternative to rectify the situation. dēvatās told brahmā “Due to your unfailing words, we are now suffering” \[in the context of brahmā giving boons to demons\].

*kadal …* – āḻvār says that he became enlivened by seeing and enjoying the one who is having rejuvenating form which is similar to the ocean which eliminates the tāpatrayam (three types of sufferings) of those who saw it.

## 4.3.4. Vasaiyaru kuralay

*vasaiyaṟu kuṟaḷāy māvali vēḷvi maṇ aḷavittavan tannai asaivaṟum amarar adiyiṇai vaṇanga alaikadal tuyinṟa ammānai tisaimugan anaiyōr nāngai nannaduvuḷ sembonsey kōyilin uḷḷē uyarmaṇi magudam sūdi ninṟānaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu uyndoḻindēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vasai – defect; aṟu – not having; kuṟaḷāy – being vāmana; māvali – mahābali’s; vēḷviyil – sacrifice; maṇ – earth; aḷavittavan tannai – one who measured; asaivu – shaking; aṟum – not having; amarar – nityasūris; adi iṇai – at the two divine feet; vaṇanga – to surrender and serve; alai – waves are agitating; kadal – in tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi – milk ocean); tuyinṟa – mercifully rested; ammānai – being the benefactor; uyar – best; maṇi – embossed with precious gems; magudam – divine crown; sūdi – wearing; ninṟānai – one who mercifully remains; tisaimugan – with four-headed brahmā; anaiyōr – brāhmaṇas who are having fame which is comparable, their; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; nal naduvuḷ – present in the good central location; sem pon sey kōyilin uḷḷē – in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – enjoyed with my eyes; uyndu – enlivened; oḻindēn – became satisfied

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, being vāmana who is free from all defects, measured the earth during mahābali’s sacrifice; he is the benefactor who mercifully rested in tiruppāṟkadal where waves are agitating, to have the nityasūris surrender and serve at his divine feet; he is wearing divine crown embossed with the best precious gems; I enjoyed such emperumān with my eyes in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil which is present in the good central location in tirunāngūr which belongs to brāhmaṇas who are having fame which is comparable with the four-headed brahmā.

*vasai aṟu kuṟaḷāy* – While accepting the vāmana form, he is having the dwarf form which cannot be attributed with any defects, and grew filling the whole earth in mahābali’s sacrificial arena.

*asaivu …* – One who is mercifully resting in tiruppāṟkadal where the waves are agitating, being served by nityasūris who are untouched by the smell of samsāram; this is because brahmā et al can only call out from the shores of the ocean while going there to pray to him and cannot enter. asaivu aṟu – not being great one day and not being lowly the other day.

*tisai mugan …* – Where brāhmaṇas who are individually capable of creation, are residing.

*uyar …* – Just as he remained crowned as gōvinda to protect the cows and covherd people, here he has crowned and is standing to protect the worldly people.

## 4.3.5. Timanattu

*tīmanattu arakkar tiṟal aḻittavanē! enṟu senṟu adaindavar tamakkut tāy manattirangi aruḷinaik kodukkum tayaradan madalaiyaic cayamē tēmalarp poḻil sūḻ nāngai nannaduvuḷ sembonsey kōyilin uḷḷē kāmanaip payandān tannai nān adiyēn kaṇḍu koṇḍu uyndoḻindēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tī – evil; manattu – having mind; arakkar – demons’; tiṟal – strength; aḻittavanē – oh one who destroyed!; enṟu – saying this; senṟu – reached; adaindavar tamakku – for those who surrendered, being refugeless; tāy manattu – like mother’s heart; irangi – melted; aruḷinai – mercy; kodukkum – showering; dayaradan – daśarata’s; madalaiyai – being the one who became the son; kāmanai – manmata (cupid); payandān tannai – sarvēśvaran who gave birth to; sayam – being surrounded as a bunch; tē – filled with honey; malar – having flowers; poḻil – gardens; sūḻ – surrounded by; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; nal naduvuḷ – present in the good central location; sem pon sey kōyilin uḷḷē – in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil; adiyēn – your servitor; nān – I; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – enjoyed with my eyes; uyndu – enlivened; oḻindēn – became satisfied

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

As the son of daśarata, for those who reached you saying “Oh one who destroyed the strength of the demons having evil mind!” and surrendered to you, being refugeless, you are having a melted heart like that of a mother and shower your mercy; you are the sarvēśvaran who gave birth to manmata; I, your servitor, enjoyed you, with my eyes in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil which is present in the good central location in tirunāngūr which is surrounded by gardens having bunch of flowers filled with honey.

*tī manattu …* – The evil hearted demons’; saying “Oh one who destroyed the strength of the demons who had the evil heart to not realise that sītāp pirātti is the mother!”

*senṟu adaindavar tamakku* – For those who approached saying “Similarly, you should eliminate our hurdles and protect us”, showering mercy with a melted heart of a mother, divine son of daśarata cakravarti who mercifully gives his mercy saying “Without any refuge, they have come to us”.

*sayamē* – svayam (himself) – emperumān himself coming and residing; alternatively – sayam – jayam (victory) tirunāngūr which is fit to be glorified with all victories.

*sayamē tē malarp poḻil* – caya (bunch) Having gardens which are having bunch of flowers with honey.

*kāmanaip payandān tannai* – kāma (manmata) walks around being respected by all beautiful persons in the world; I got to see the lord who is the creator of such manmata.

## 4.3.6. Mallaima munnir

*mallaimā munnīr adarpada malaiyāl aṇai seydu magiḻndavan tannai kallin mīdu iyanṟa kadimadiḷ ilangai kalanga ōr vāḷi tottānai selva nānmaṟaiyōr nāngai nannaduvuḷ sembonsey kōyilin uḷḷē allimā malarāḷ tannodum adiyēn kaṇḍu koṇḍu allal tīrndēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mallai – abundant; mā – having wealth; munnīr – ocean; adarpada – to worship; malaiyāl – by rocks; aṇai seydu – building a bridge; magiḻndavan tannai – being the one who became joyful; kallin mīdu – on the mountain named trikūtam; iyanṟa – built; kadi – protection; madiḷ – having fort; ilangai – lankā; kalanga – to become agitated; ōr – distinguished; vāḷi – arrow; tottānai – one who touched and shot; selvam – having wealth; nālmaṟaiyōr – brāhmaṇas who are learned in four vēdams, their; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; nal naduvuḷ – present in the good central location; sem pon sey kōyilin uḷḷē – in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil; alli – having petals; mā – best; malarāḷ tannodum – along with periya pirāttiyār who is residing on the lotus flower; adiyēn – I, the servitor; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – enjoyed with my eyes; allal – sorrow; tīrndēn – got to eliminate

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān became joyful on building a bridge with rocks on the ocean which is abundantly wealthy, to be vorśipped by that ocean; he touched and shot the distinguished arrow to have lankā which is built on the mountain named trikūtam and is fortified, become agitated; I, the servitor, enjoyed such emperumān along with periya pirāttiyār who is residing on the best lotus flower having petals, with my eyes in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil which is present in the good central location in tirunāngūr which belongs to brāhmaṇas who are learned in four vēdams which are wealthy, and got to eliminate my sorrow.

*mallai …* – The ocean which is abundantly wealthy and vast – to have it worship (emperumān). There will be abundance of precious gems etc in ocean. Building a bridge with rocks which will drown, on the ocean to have it worship him, and became joyful in enjoying such sport. lankā was on top of the trikūta peak; further, it was fortified; emperumān who shot an arrow which he could place his hands on, to have many residents of lankā scrambling for a single piece of cloth in such lankā.

The divyadēśam which belongs to the brāhmaṇas who were abundantly wealth.

*alli …* – I got to see emperumān along with periya pirāttiyār who is the cause for their wealth, and got to eliminate all my worldly sorrows.

## 4.3.7. Venjinak kalirum

*venjinak kaḷiṟum villodu mallum veguṇḍu iṟuttu adarttavan tannai kanjanaik kāynda kāḷai ammānaik karumugil tiruniṟattavanai senjol nānmaṟaiyōr nāngai nannaduvuḷ sembonsey kōyilin uḷḷē anjanak kunṟam ninṟadoppānaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu allal tīrndēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vem – cruel; sinam – having anger; kaḷiṟu – kuvalayāpeedam; veguṇḍum – showing anger; vil – bow; iṟuttum – broke; mallum – wrestlers; adarttavan tannai – one who tormented; kanjanai – kamsan; kāynda – showing anger and killed; kāḷai – young; ammānai – being the lord; karu – blackish; mugil – like a cloud; tiru niṟattavanai – one who has the best divine form; anjanak kunṟam – a mountain of black pigment; ninṟadu oppānai – one who is shining as if it is standing; sem sol – having beautiful (true) words; nāl maṟaiyōr – experts in four vēdams; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; nal naduvuḷ – present in the good central location; sem pon sey kōyilin uḷḷē – in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – enjoyed with my eyes; allal – sorrow; tīrndēn – eliminated

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, being young and the lord, showed anger towards kuvalayāpeedam which was having cruel anger, broke the bow, tormented the wrestlers, showed his anger on kamsan and killed him; he has the best divine form which is similar to a blackish cloud; he is shining as if a mountain of black pigment is standing; I enjoyed such emperumān with my eyes in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil which is present in the good central location in tirunāngūr which belongs to brāhmaṇas who are experts in four vēdams having truthful words, and eliminated my sorrow.

*vem sinam …* – kuvalayāpeedam, the elephant which was having cruel anger, the bow which was placed beyond it, the wrestlers who were placed inside \[the arena\]; one who showed anger on kuvalayāpeedam, broke the bow and tormented the wrestlers; the youthful kriṣṇa who killed kamsan who was standing inside all of these protections. īśvaran did all of these before attaining adult stage; emperumān stood there feeling happy thinking “got to eliminate the enemies of my devotees” with a rejuvenating form, after killing kamsan.

*sem sol …* – The brāhmaṇas of the town are having truthful speech; brāhmaṇas who always speak words which are good for all creatures, in truthful words.

*anjanam* – emperumān who is standing like a mountain made of black pigment, to cool down those who see him.

## 4.3.8. Anriya vanan

*anṟiya vāṇan āyiram tōḷum tuṇiya anṟu āḻi tottānai mintigaḻ kudumi vēngada malai mēl mēviya vēda nalviḷakkai tendisait tiladam anaiyavar nāngaic cembonsey kōyilin uḷḷē manṟadu poliya magiḻndu ninṟānai vaṇangi nān vāḻndoḻindēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟiya – one who became angry (and fought); vāṇan – bāṇāsuran’s; āyiram tōḷum – thousand shoulders; tuṇiya – to be severed and to fall on the ground; anṟu – at that time; āḻi – sudarśana chakra; tottānai – being the one who touched and launched; min – radiance; tigaḻ – shining; kudumi – having peaks; vēngada malai mēl – on tirumalā which is known as tiruvēngadam; mēviya – one who eternally resides; vēdam – being the one who is revealed in vēdam; nal – distinguished; viḷakkai – one who is self-illuminous like a lamp; manṟu – in the assembly (of bhāgavatas); adu – that assembly; poliya – to become abundant; magiḻndu – became joyful; ninṟānai – one who is mercifully present; then tisai – for the southern direction; tiladam anaiyavar – the best among the brāhmaṇas who are shining like the tilak (vertical symbol) on the forehead; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; sem pon sey kōyilin uḷḷē – in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil; vaṇangi – surrendered; nān vāḻndu oḻindēn – I became enlivened

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is the one who touched and launched sudarśana chakra at that time when bāṇāsuran was angry and set out to fight, to have the thousand shoulders of such bāṇāsuran severed and fall down; he is eternally residing on tirumalā tiruppati which is having peaks which are shining with radiance; he is revealed in vēdam and is self-illuminous like a distinguished lamp; he remains joyful and is mercifully present to have such assembly of bhāgavatas become enriched; I surrendered to such emperumān in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil which is present in the good central location in tirunāngūr which belongs to the best among the brāhmaṇas who are shining like the tilak (symbol on forehead) and became enlivened.

*anṟiya …* – The one who touched his divine chakra to have the thousand shoulders of bāṇan who developed enmity with his grandson, to be severed. He is eternally residing on tirumalā which is having peaks which are shining with radiance, thinking “What if new enemies like bāṇa come up?” He is fully known by vēdam and is having self-illuminated svarūpam (true nature). The best among the brāhamaṇas who are like the tilak for the southern direction, their

*manṟadu poliya magiḻndu ninṟānai* – In the place where everyone gathers, emperumān is residing with boundless joy just as in paramapadam, to have such a place become enriched.

## 4.3.9. Kalangani vanna

*kaḷangani vaṇṇā kaṇṇaṇē endan kārmugilē ena ninaindittu uḷam kanindirukkum adiyavar tangaḷ uḷḷattuḷ ūṟiya tēnai teḷinda nānmaṟaiyōr nāngai nannaduvuḷ sembonsey kōyilin uḷḷē vaḷangoḷ pērinbam manni ninṟānai vaṇangi nān vāḻndoḻindēnē*

kaḷangani – like kaḷāppaḻam (a berry fruit); vaṇṇā – Oh one who has the complexion!; kaṇṇanē – Oh kriṣṇa!; enṟan – shining to me; kārmugilē – Oh one who is having rejuvenating form similar to monsoon cloud!; ena – in this manner; ninaindittu – meditated; uḷam – heart; kanindu irukkum – well matured; adiyavar tangaḷ – servitors’; uḷḷattuḷ – in the heart; ūṟiya – remaining permanently; tēnai – being sweet like honey; vaḷam koḷ – beautiful; pēr inbam – immeasurable bliss; manni – acquired; ninṟānai – one who is mercifully present; teḷinda – those who are certain about the truth; nānmaṟaiyōr – experts of four vēdams; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; nal naduvuḷ – present in the good central location; sem pon sey kōyilin uḷḷē – in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil; nān – I; vaṇangi – vorśipped; vāḻndoḻindēn – became enlivened

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is mercifully present as honey which is sweet, with immeasurable bliss which is beautiful in the well matured hearts of servitors due to meditating upon him thinking “Oh one who has the complexion of kaḷāppaḻam! Oh kriṣṇa! Oh one who is having rejuvenating form similar to monsoon cloud, which is shining to me!”; I enjoyed such emperumān with my eyes in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil which is present in the good central location in tirunāngūr which belongs to brāhmaṇas who are experts in four vēdams and are certain about the truth of such emperumān, and became enlivened.

*kaḷangani …* – emperumān who is like well aged honey in the heart of servitors who are having their heart matured thinking “Oh one who is having complexion of kaḷāppaḻam which is cool to the eyes unlike being reddish or whitish! Oh kriṣṇa! Oh one who let me fully enjoy your rejuvenating form!”.

*teḷinda* … – Unlike being in a confused state of thinking once “sarvēśvaran is the protector” and thinking at other times “another dēvatā is protector”, brāhmaṇas who are always remaining certain that sarvēśvaran is our protector. emperumān who is remaining beautiful, boundless bliss.

## 4.3.10. Tenamar solai

*tēnamar sōlai nāngai nannaduvuḷ sembonsey kōyilin uḷḷē vānavar kōnaik kaṇḍamai sollum mangaiyār vātkalikanṟi  ūnamil pādal onbadōdu onṟum oḻivinṟik kaṟṟu vallārgaḷ māna veṇkudaik kīḻ vaiyagam āṇḍu vānavar āguvar magiḻndē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēn – beetles; amar – filled; sōlai – having gardens; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; nal – beautiful; naduvuḷ – in the central location; sem pon sey kōyilin uḷḷē – in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil; vānavar – for nityasūris; kōnai – sarvēśvaran who is the lord; kaṇḍamai – the way he saw; sollum – one who reveals; mangaiyār – protection for the residents of tirumangai region; vāḷ – having strong sword; kalikanṟi – āḻvār’s; ūnam il – not having any shortcoming in the qualities; pādal – song; onbadōdu onṟum – these ten pāsurams; oḻivu inṟi – without missing any word or sentence; kaṟṟu vallārgaḷ – those who can recite; mānam – being vast; veṇ – whitish; kudaik kīḻ – remaining under the umbrella; vaiyagam – earth; āṇḍu – rule over (and then); magiḻndu – being joyful; vānavar āguvar – will blend into the group of nityasūris

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In these ten pāsurams which are not having any shortcoming in their qualities, āḻvār, who is having a strong sword which is the protection for the residents of tirumangai region, reveals the way he saw sarvēśvaran who is the lord of nityasūris in the divyadēśam named sembonsey kōyil which is located in the beautiful central location of tirunāngūr, which is having gardens filled with beetles; those who can recite these without missing any word or sentence, will remain under the vast, whitish umbrella and rule over the earth, and then being joyful, will blend into the group of nityasūris.

*tēn …* – In sembonsey kōyil which is located in tirunāngūr which is having gardens filled with beetles, seeing the “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (lord of nityasūris who are free from confusion) was sung. āḻvār, who is having a sword which gives pride/strength to the residents of tirumangai, spoke ten pāsurams which are not having any shortcoming in their qualities; those who can recite without missing out on any of them, remaining under vast, whitish umbrella, will rule over the earth to have them used for bhāgavatas and subsequently with endless joy, become part of the group of nityasūris.

## 4.4 Marrarasar

## 4.4.1. Marrarasar

*māṟṟarasar maṇimudiyum tiṟalum tēsum maṟṟavar tam kādalimār kuḻaiyum tandai kāl taḷaiyum udan kaḻala vandu tōnṟik kadanāgam kāttaḷitta kaṇṇar kaṇḍīr nūṟṟidaḻ koḷ aravindam nuḻainda paḷḷattu iḷangamugin mudupāḷai paguvāy naṇḍin sēṟṟaḷaiyil veṇmuttam sindu nāngūrt tirutteṟṟiyambalattu en sengaṇmālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paḷḷattu – sprouted from a pit; nūṟu idaḻgaḷ – having many petals; aravindam – lotus flowers; nuḻainda – entered; paguvāy – having huge mouth; naṇḍin – crab’s; sēṟu aḷaiyil – mud filled hole; iḷam kamugin – young areca trees’; mudu pāḷai – ripened swathes; veṇ muttam – white pearls; sindu – dispersing; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tirutteṟṟi ambalattu – mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam; en – being my lord; sem kaṇ māl – sarvēśvaran who is having reddish eyes; māṟṟu arasar – duryōdana et al, who are enemies, their; maṇi – embossed with precious gems; mudiyum – crowns; tiṟalum – strength; tēsum – fame; maṟṟu – further; avar tam – their; kādalimār – wives’; kuḻaiyum – earrings, mangaḷasūtram etc; tandai – his father vasudēva’s; kāl – tied on his feet; taḷaiyum – shackles; udan – at once; kaḻala – to slip and fall down; vandu – descended from paramapadam; tōnṟi – being the one who incarnated; kadam – angry; nāgam – gajēndrāḻvān; kāttu – protected; aḷitta – showed his mercy; kaṇṇar kaṇḍīr – merciful kriṣṇa

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Reddish-eyed sarvēśvaran, my lord, is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam in tirunāngūr. It is the place where the matured swathes of the youthful areca trees will disperse white pearls into the huge-mouthed crab’s muddy hole where lotus flowers which have many petals and are sprouted from a pit have entered; such sarvēśvaran is kriṣṇa who descended from paramapadam and incarnated to make the precious gem-studded crowns, strength and fame of duryōdana et al, who were enemies, their wives’ earrings, mangaḷasūtram etc and the shackles on the feet of his father vasudēva to get removed at once and showered his mercy on gajēndrāḻvān and protected him.

*māṟṟu arasar …* – duryōdana et al who are enemies of pāṇḍavas as said in mahābhāratam “*dviśadannam na bhōktavyam dviśantam naiva bhōjayēt*” (kriṣṇa said – Neither should one accept food from enemies nor should one serve them food. Oh duryōdana! Since you considered pāṇḍavas as your enemies and as pāṇḍavas are my life \[you are my enemy\]); as he mercifully said “You are all my enemies; your food cannot be consumed by me; you cannot feed me”, duryōdana et al who are his enemies; their crowns which are made of precious-gems, strength and the fame acquired by winning over many territories.

*maṟṟavar …* – As said in [periya tirumoḻi 2.3.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-3-6/) “*sandamar kuḻalāḷ*” (draupadi who has coloured hair), the mangaḷasūtram of the wives of duryōdana et al.

*tandai kāl taḷaiyum udan kaḻala vandu tōnṟi* – The shackles on śrī vasudēva’s feet. He descended and incarnated to eliminate all of these.

*kada nāgam* – It is kriṣṇa who protected the angry elephant. sīṟṟam – anger – when he was grabbed by the crocodile with the mouth, gajēndrāḻvān thought “Should I feel sorrow having to take care of myself as if I have no refuge? Why should I worry like this?” since emperumān did not come immediately to protect him.

*nūṟṟu idaḻ koḷ …* – To get the meaning clearly, the pāsuram should start with these words. In the pit, there is a lotus flower which has many petals; the huge-mouthed crab entered that flower; the matured swathes of the youthful areca trees will disperse whitish pearls into the holes of the crab. Alternatively, “*paguvāy iḷam kamugin mudu pāḷai*” – all of these such as having a matured mouth, the youthful areca trees’ matured swathe, are attributes of the areca tree, and then the crab’s muddy hole is spoken about; in tirunāngūr where the lotus flower enters the crab’s muddy hole and gives its fragrance and the youthful areca tree’s matured swathe disperses the white pearls.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.4.2. Porrodit tol

*poṟṟodit tōḷ madamagaḷ tan vadivu koṇḍa pollāda vanpēycci kongai vāngi peṟṟedutta tāy pōla maduppa ārum pēṇā nanjuṇḍu uganda piḷḷai kaṇḍīr nel todutta malar neelam niṟainda sūḻal irunjiṟaiya vaṇḍoliyum nedungaṇār tam siṟṟadi mēl silamboliyum miḻaṟṟum nāngūrt tiruttetṟiyambalattu en sengaṇmālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nel – on paddy grains; todutta – tied in rows; neelam malar – by karuneydal flowers; niṟainda – complete; sūḻal – in the surroundings; irum – beautiful; siṟaiya – having wings; vaṇḍu – beetles’; oliyum – sound; nedum – wide; kaṇār tam – ladies who are having eyes; siṟu – small; adi mēl – worn on the feet; silambu – anklets’; oliyum – sound; miḻaṟṟu – sounding in an incoherent manner; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tirutteṟṟi ambalattu – mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam; en – being my lord; sem kaṇ māl – sarvēśvaran who is having reddish eyes; pon – golden; todi – having bangles on the forearm; tōḷ – having shoulders; madam – filled with noble qualities; magaḷ than – yaśōdāp pirātti’s; vadivu – form; koṇḍa – one who came accepting; pollāda – evil; van – cruel-hearted; pēycci – pūtanā; kongai – (her) bosom; vāngi – pulled out from the cloth which was covering it; peṟṟu edutta – one who gave birth; tāypōla – like the mother; maduppa – placed (in his mouth) (at that time); ārum – anyone; pēṇā – not desired; nanju – poison (in that bosom); uṇḍu – mercifully consumed; uganda – became joyful; piḷḷai kaṇḍīr – this is the child

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Reddish-eyed sarvēśvaran, my lord, is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam in tirunāngūr. This abode is having surroundings which are filled with karuneydal flowers tied in rows on top of paddy grains, where the sound of beautifully winged beetles and the sound of the anklets which decorate the small feet of the wide-eyed ladies are heard incoherently; such sarvēśvaran is the child who became joyful on consuming the poison which was given by evil, cruel-hearted pūtanā who assumed the form of yaśōdāp pirātti, who was having shoulders with her forearm decorated with golden bangles, by pulling out her bosom from the cloth which was covering it and gave it like the mother who gave birth to him, and which was not desired by anyone.

*poṟṟodi …* – pūtanā disguised herself as yaśōdāp pirātti who is having shoulder which has forearm decorated with golden bangles and is having noble qualities, who decorates herself thinking “If we don’t decorate nicely, kriṣṇa will feel bad”.

*vadivu koṇḍa pollāda van pēycci* – Who is imitating whose form! pūtanā is a cruel demoness; yaśōdāp pirātti is having beautiful shoulders with decorated forearms.

*kongai vāngip peṟṟedutta tāy pōl maduppa* – Taking her bosom and feeding him as if she were his mother.

*ārum pēṇā nanjuṇḍu uganda piḷḷai kaṇḍīr* – Consuming the poison which is not desired by anyone and remained childish and hence became joyful. If one had knowledge one would not consume poison.

*nel todutta …* – In the surroundings which are filled with kuvaḷai flowers tied in rows on top of paddy grains, there was the sound of the beautifully winged beetles and the sound of the anklets from the small feet of the ladies who have distinguished eyes.

*miḻaṟṟu nāngūr* – Since both sounds are of incoherent words which cannot distinguish the letters, words and meanings, it is not possble to differentiate between the sound of the anklets and the sound of the beetles.
