## 4.4.3. Padal adaitta

*padal adaitta siṟukurambai nuḻaindu pukkup  pasu veṇṇey padamārap paṇṇai muṟṟum adal adartta vēṟkaṇār tōkkai paṟṟi alandalaimai seyduḻalum aiyan kaṇḍīr madal edutta nedundengin paḻangaḷ vīḻa mānganigaḷ tiratturuttā varunīrp ponni tidal eduttu malar sumandangu iḻiyu nāngūrt tirutteṟṟiyambalattu en sengaṇmālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

madal edutta – with abundant branches; nedu – tall; tengin – from coconut trees; paḻangaḷ – fruits; vīḻa – as they fall (on the mangoes, dropping off due to that); mānganigaḷ – mangoes; tirattu – as a bunch; uruttā – pushing along; varu – coming; nīr – having water; ponni – river kāviri; tidal – dunes; eduttu – eliminated; angu – in those places where there were dunes; malar – flowers; sumandu – carrying and arriving; iḻiyum – flowing; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tirutteṟṟi ambalattu – mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam; en – being my lord; sem kaṇ māl – sarvēśvaran who is having reddish eyes; pasu veṇṇey – freshly churned butter; padam – in the well formed state (before it loses its freshness); Ara – to mercifully consume; padal adaitta – closed with the door; siṟu – small; kurambai – in the huts; pukku – carefully analysed and entered inside; adal adartta – set out to fight; vēl – sharp like spear; kaṇār – the covherd girls who are having eyes, their; tōkkai – top end of sari (near border); paṟṟi – held (and pulled); alandalamai – torment; seydu – caused; paṇṇai muṟṟum – everywhere in the town of the covherds; uḻalum – roaming around; aiyan kaṇḍīr – is the lord

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

As the fruits from the tall coconut trees, which are having abundant branches, fall on the mango tree and gather the mangoes which fall on the river kāviri which is having water which is pushing along those fruits, the kāviri would flush out the sand dunes and fill them with flowers in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam in tirunāngūr, where reddish-eyed sarvēśvaran, my lord, is mercifully residing. He is the lord who carefully analysed and entered the small huts which are secured with doors, to mercifully consume the well prepared freshly churned butter in that fresh state, pulled the top end of sari of the covherd girls who are having battle-ready spear like eyes and roamed around the town of the covherds, causing torment.

*padal …* – If the covherd girls secured the lock on the door at the entrance of their small huts, he would unlock it and enter. The hut becomes great when he opens and enters it \[until then it remains small\].

*pasu veṇṇey padamāra* – To mercifully consume the freshly churned butter before it loses its freshness.

*paṇṇai – idaiccēri* (neighbourhood)

*adal adartta* – Those who have eyes which appear like battle-ready spear.

*paṇṇai muṟṟum* – In all the groups \[of residences\].

*tōkkai paṟṟi* – They will stop him with their eyes. He will pull them their top end of the sari.

*alandalaimai* – He made the whole town become tormented that one sari needs to be worn by seven persons \[its a passage which indicates huge torment\].

*madal edutta* – As the coconut fruits, from the trees which are having tall branches, fall on the mango trees, the mangoes fall down; ponni (kāviri) river is having water which gathers all of those fruits and flushes out the sand dunes to fill them with flowers; in such tirunāngūr.

## 4.4.4. Vararum mulai madaval

*vārārum mulai madavāḷ pinnaikkāgi vaḷai maruppil kadunjnattu vandāḷārnda kārār tiṇ vidai adarttu vaduvai āṇḍa karumugil pōl tiruniṟattu en kaṇṇar kaṇḍīr ērārum malarp poḻilgaḷ taḻuvi engum eḻil madiyaik kāl todara viḷangu sōdi sīrārum maṇimādam tigaḻum nāngūrt tiruttetṟiyambalattu en sengaṇmālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēr ārum – Having complete beauty; malar – having flowers; poḻilgaḷ – in the gardens; engum – at all places; taḻuvi – embraced and came; eḻil – having beauty (fragrance); kāl – wind; madiyai – moon; todar – stopped from moving; viḷangu – shining due to that; sōdi – having radiance; sīr ārum – complete in wealth; maṇi mādam – on the mansions which are studded with precious gems; tigaḻum – shining; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tirutteṟṟi ambalattu – mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam; en – being my lord; sem kaṇ māl – sarvēśvaran who is having reddish eyes; vār ārum – held by the corset; mulai – having bosoms; madavāḷ – having humility; pinnaikkāgi – for nappinnaip pirātti; vaḷai – curved; maruppil – having horns; kadum – cruel; sinattu – having anger; van – strong; tāḷ ārnda – having feet; kār Ar – being black (due to their youth); tiṇ – firm; vidai – bulls; adarttu – crushed together; vaduvai āṇḍa – one who directed the auspicious marriage ceremony; karu mugil pōl – like a black cloud; tiru niṟattu – having nice beauty; en – one who enslaved me showing that beauty; kaṇṇar kaṇḍīr – is kriṣṇa

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Reddish-eyed sarvēśvaran, my lord, is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam in tirunāngūr. This abode is having mansions which are studded with precious gems and are complete in wealth and are shining due to the moon being stopped by the beautifully fragrant wind which came after embracing all the places in the gardens which are having completely beautiful flowers; such sarvēśvaran is kriṣṇa who crushed together the firm, black bulls which were having curved horns, cruel anger and strong feet, for the sake of nappinnaip pirātti who is having bosoms  held by the corset and who is humble, and who directed the auspicious marriage ceremony; he is having nice beauty like that of a black cloud and enslaved me showing that beauty.

*vār ārum …* – Since she is in the apt stage of youth, nappinnaip pirātti is having bosoms which are held by corset; for her sake, my kriṣṇa, who is like a black cloud, killed the seven bulls which were having curved horns, cruel anger, strong feet and were black in complexion, and conducted the auspicious marriage.

*ēr Ar …* – As the wind picks up the fragrance in the beautiful flower gardens and stops the moon, tirunāngūr is shining with the gem-studded mansions which are having shining radiance and are filled with wealth.

## 4.4.5. Kalai ilangum

*kalai ilangum agalalgul kamalap pāvai kadir muttaveṇṇagaiyāḷ karungaṇ āycci mulai ilangum oḷi maṇippūṇ vadamum tēyppa mūvāda varai nedundōḷ mūrtti kaṇḍīr malai ilangu niraic candi māda vīdi ādavarai madamoḻiyār mugattu iraṇḍu silai vilangi mananjiṟai koṇḍirukkum nāngūrt tiruttetṟiyambalattu en sengaṇmālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

malai ilangu – shining like mountains; nirai – in rows; sandhi – connected with each other; mādam – having mansions; vīdi – on the streets; madam – incoherently sweet; moḻiyār – ladies who have the speech; mugattu – shining in the face; iraṇḍu silai – eye-brows which resemble two bows; vilangi – curved; ādavarai – heroes’; manam siṟai koṇḍu irukkum – capturing the heart; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tirutteṟṟi ambalattu – mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam; en – being my lord; sem kaṇ māl – sarvēśvaran who is having reddish eyes; kalai – by the garment; ilangum – shining; agal – wide; algul – having waist region; kadir – having rays; mutta – like pearl; veṇ – whitish; nagaiyāḷ – having rows of teeth; kamalap pāvai – periya pirāttiyār’s; karum kaṇ – having black eyes; āycci – napinnaip pirātti’s; mulai – bosoms; ilangum – shining; oḷi maṇi – made of radiant gems; pūṇ – necklace; vadamum – pearl necklace; tēyppa – as they rub (his divine chest) (due to that); mūvāda – not ageing (i.e. not losing freshness); varai – mountain like; nedum – lengthy; tōḷ – having shoulders; mūrtti kaṇḍīr – is the lord

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Reddish-eyed sarvēśvaran, my lord, is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam in tirunāngūr. This abode is having mansions which are connected with each other, in rows, and are shining like mountains, on the streets where ladies, with incoherently sweet speech, with pair of eye-brows in their shining face, which resemble two curved bows, capture the heart of the heroes; such sarvēśvaran is the lord who is having lengthy shoulders which resemble a mountain and who is not ageing due to having his divine chest rubbed with the necklace which is made of shining, precious gems and pearl necklace which are shining on the bosoms of periya pirāttiyār whose wide waist region is shining due to the garment and is having whitish teeth rows which resemble pearls with rays, and nappinnaip pirātti who is having black eyes.

*kalai ilangum* … – periya pirāttiyār who is having wide waist region which is having shining garments and is having whitish pearl like teeth rows.

*karum kaṇ āycci* – nappinnaip pirātti whose eyes are having black complexion due to constantly staring at his divine form.

*mulai ilangum* – As the necklace which is made of shining, precious gems which are shining on both their bosoms, and pearl necklaces which are three-layered, five-layered etc, rub on the divine chest of emperumān, due to that he remains with vast shoulders which are similar to a mountain which is not ageing. Just see that.

*malai …* – tirunāngūr where on the streets, where mansions, which are connected and densely seen in rows, are shining like a mountain, the bows (eye-brows) which are present in the sweetly speaking ladies, become curved and capture the heart of the heroes. sandhi indicates the name of dusk, it is also explained as tirunāngūr where the ladies capture the heart of their dear ones, and imprison them. silai ilangi – bending the eye-brows.

## 4.4.6. Tan polum enrelundan

*tān pōlum enṟeḻundān taraṇiyāḷan adu kaṇḍu tarittiruppān arakkar tangaḷ kōn pōlum ēnṟeḻundān kunṟam anna irubadu tōḷudan tuṇitta oruvan kaṇḍīr mān pōlum mennōkkin seyya vāyār maragadam pōl madakkiḷiyaik kai mēl koṇḍu tēn pōlum menmaḻalai payiṟṟum nāngūrt tiruttetṟiyambalattu en sengaṇmālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mān pōlum – like a deer; mel – tender; nōkkil – vision; seyya – reddish; vāyār – ladies who are having lips; maradagam pōl – having greenish complexion similar to that of emerald; madam – having childishness; kiḷiyai – parrot; kai mēl koṇḍu – having on their hands; tēn pōlum – like honey; mel – sweet; maḻalai – tender speech; payiṟṟum – teaching; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tirutteṟṟi ambalattu – mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam; en – being my lord; sem kaṇ māl – sarvēśvaran who is having reddish eyes; daraṇiyāḷan – cakravartit tirumagan who is the emperor of earth; tān pōlum – like a king; ēnṟu – arose; eḻundān – came opposing; enṟu – simply considering this; adu kaṇḍu – seeing such simplicity; darittu iruppān – being fearless; arakkar tangaḷ – demons’; kōn pōlum – like the king (considering himself to be great); ēnṟu – arose; eḻundān – rāvaṇa who came fighting, his; kunṟam anna – like a mountain; irubadu tōḷ – twenty shoulders; udan – at once; tuṇitta – severed; oruvan kaṇḍīr – is the unique one

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Reddish-eyed sarvēśvaran, my lord, is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam in tirunāngūr. This is the abode where the ladies who are having tender vision like that of a deer and reddish lips, keep a parrot which is green like emerald and childishness, and teach honey like sweet speech to such parrot; such sarvēśvaran is the unique one who at once severed the mountain like twenty shoulders of rāvaṇan who remained fearless looking at the simplicity of śrī rāma thinking “Here is cakravartit tirumagan who has risen as a king and has come fighting” and who considered himself to be the king of the demons.

*tān pōlum …* – āppān tiruvaḻundūr araiyar and other elders went and requested clarification for this pāsuram asking “What is the mood of this pāsuram?” \[Since there is the word “*tān pōlum*” (as himself), it appears demeaning to śrī rāma’s stature, where he is already the emperor and rāvaṇan is said as “*kōn pōlum*” (as the king). The śrīvaiṣṇavas’ question relates to how āḻvār would form such a sentence\] bhattar heard the pāsuram once and mercifully said “These are rāvaṇan’s words” \[That is – āḻvār quoting rāvaṇan where rāvaṇan is thinking cheaply about śrī rāma and considering himself to be great\].

*tān pōlum …* – The enemy (śrī rāma) came to fight as a king would do.

*adu kaṇḍu …* – The unique, valorous śrī rāma, who severed the mountain-like twenty shoulders of rāvaṇan who considered himself to be the king of demons, arose and came fighting.

*mān pōlum …* – It appears that one parrot \[the lady\] is teaching another parrot. It is to be understood that the speech of the parrot \[lady\] who is teaching is sweeter than the parrot which is learning. Ladies who are having deer like tender vision and reddish lips, having the obedient parrot which is resembling emerald, are teaching honey like sweet and tender speech. Such tirunāngūr.

## 4.4.7. Pongilangu

*pongilangu purinūlum tōlum tāḻap pollāda kuṟaḷuruvāyp porundā vāṇan mangalam sēr maṟai vēḷvi adanuḷ pukku maṇṇagalam kuṟai iranda maindan kaṇḍīr kongalarnda malark kuḻalār kongai tōynda kungumattin kuḻambaḷainda kōlam tannāl sengalangal veṇmaṇal mēl tavaḻum nāngūrt tiruttetṟiyambalattu en sengaṇmālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kongu – fragrance; alarnda – spreading; malar – decorated with flowers; kuḻalār – ladies who are having hair; kongai – on the bosoms; tōynda – spread; kungumattin – kumkum (vermillion), its; kuḻambu – slush; alainda – mixed; kōlam tannāl – by the beauty; sem – reddish; kalangal – the flood which is muddy; veṇ – whitish; maṇal mēl – on the sand dunes; tavaḻum – slowly spreading; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tirutteṟṟi ambalattu – mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam; en – being my lord; sem kaṇ māl – sarvēśvaran who is having reddish eyes; pongu – having well-grown radiance; ilangu – shining; puri – having strings; nūlum – yajñōpavītam (sacred thread); tōlum – kriṣṇājinam (deer skin); tāḻa – hanging; pollāda – beautiful; kuṟaḷ uruvāy – being in the vāmana \[dwarf\] form; porundā – having a birth which does not align with him; vāṇan – mahābali’s; mangalam – auspicious; sēr – apt; maṟai – having chants of vēdam; vēḷvi adanuḷ – in the fire sacrifice; pukku – entered; kuṟai – which he was not owning; maṇ agalam – the earth; iranda – begged; maindan kaṇḍīr – is the young boy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Reddish-eyed sarvēśvaran, my lord, is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam in tirunāngūr. This abode is where the muddy flood which is reddish from the beautiful, slushy vermillion which is spread on the bosoms of the ladies whose hair is decorated with flowers which spread the fragrance, is slowly spreading over the whitish sand dunes; such sarvēśvaran is the young boy in the beautiful vāmana form, who is having the yajñōpavītam which is having shining, well-grown radiance and multiple strings, and kriṣṇājinam, hanging on him, entered the fire sacrifice which is conducted by mahābali who is having a birth which does not align with emperumān, and which is having apt chants of vēdam, and begged for the earth which he was not owning.

*pongu ilangu …* – Having very shining yajñōpavītam and kriṣṇājinam hanging.

*pollāda kuṟaḷ uruvāy* – āḻvār is using the method of viparīta lakśaṇā (saying the opposite way) since if he said “*aḻagidu*” (beautiful), it will cause evil eyes of the worldly people; alternatively – he is indicating that due to his strange (dwarf) form, one cannot take their eyes off him.

*porundā vāṇan* – Not just having lowly heart as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.15](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-15/) “*āsuram bhāvam āśritā:*” (those with demoniacal nature), but having a lowly demoniac birth.

*mangalm sēr* – The yāgam to sarvēśvaran himself went – such auspiciousness.

*maṇ agalam* – mahābali being the owner, and emperumān, lacking it, begged for it.

*maindan kaṇḍīr* – What childishness!

*kongu alarnda …* – tirunāngūr where the muddy flood which is reddish from the beautiful, slushy vermillion which is spread on the bosoms of the ladies whose hair is decorated with flowers which spread the fragrance, is slowly spreading over the whitish sand dunes \[in kāviri\]; just as tārā was walking in a staggered way as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 33.37 “*sā praskalantī*…” (the famous tārā arrived with a staggered walk).

## 4.4.8. Silambinidaic

*silambinidaic ciṟu paral pōl periya mēru tirukkuḷambil kaṇagaṇappat tiruvākāram kulunga nila madandai tanai idandu pulgik kōttidai vaittu aruḷiya engōmān kaṇḍīr ilangiya nānmaṟai anaittum angam āṟum ēḻisaiyum kēḷvigaḷum eṇḍhikku engum silambiya naṟperunjelvam tigaḻum nāngūrt tiruttetṟiyambalattu en sengaṇmālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ilangiya – shining; nāl maṟai anaittum – all vēdams which are of four classifications; angam āṟum – the six ancillary subjects \[of vēdams\] viz vyākaraṇam, śīkśā, niruktam, kalpam, candas, jyōtiśam; ēḻu isaiyum – sapta svaras (seven notes); kēḷvigaḷum – itihāsas (epics) etc; eṇ dikku – in all eight directions; engum – in all areas; silambiya – roaring; nal – distinguished; perum – immeasurable; selvam – wealth; tigaḻum – shining; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tirutteṟṟi ambalattu – mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam; en – being my lord; sem kaṇ māl – sarvēśvaran who is having reddish eyes; silambin idai – placed inside the anklets; siṟu paralpōl – like the small stones; periya mēru – the huge, stout mēru mountain; tirukkuḷambil – on the beautiful hoof; kaṇagaṇappa – to sound; tiru – (present in his divine chest) periya pirātti’s; ākāram – presence; kulunga – to sway; idandu – dug out and picked up (the earth); nila madandai tanai – śrī bhūmip pirātti; pulgi – embraced; kōttidai – on the tusk; vaittu aruḷiya – one who mercifully placed; en kōmān kaṇḍīr – is my lord

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Reddish eyed sarvēśvaran, my lord, is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam in tirunāngūr. This abode is where distinguished, immeasurable wealth is shining in the form of roaring sounds of all shining vēdams which are of four classifications, the six ancillary subjects viz vyākaraṇam, śīkśā, niruktam, kalpam, candas, jyōtiśam, sapta svaras, itihāsas etc in all eight directions; such sarvēśvaran is my lord on whose beautiful hoof, anklets inside which the huge, stout mēru mountain is placed as small stones, are sounding. He dug out and picked up the earth, embraced śrī bhūmip pirātti and mercifully placed her on his tusk, to have the presence of periya pirātti on his chest sway.

*silambin idai …* – As the huge, great mēru mountain make sounds in the anklets as the small stones inside it, on his divine hoof as said in the taniyan of kaiśika māhātmyam “*mēru:kaṇakaṇāyatē*” (mēru mountain is making sounds).

*tiruvākāram kulunga* – To make the presence of pirātti who says as in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum*” (I will not leave even for a moment from his chest), sway.

*nila madandai* – Lifted up earth and embraced its abhimānini (controller), śrī bhūmip pirātti, and placed her on his tusk, like embossing it with a blue-gem, and enslaved me, by that act.

*ilangiya …* – Four vēdams which are shining due to the strength of being authentic, the six ancillary subjects, seven notes, itihāsas, purāṇas are resounding in all eight directions – tirunāngūr which has such beautiful, great wealth.

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Reddish-eyed sarvēśvaran, my lord, is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam in tirunāngūr. This abode is having brāhmaṇas who are having the tongue sustaining all vēdams which are in four categories which are rising in tumult and having wealth which is grown through ages, and is shining by the very tall gem-studded mansions; such sarvēśvaran is our lord who secured the overflowing flood during the deluge from the ocean, which climbed and flew over the seven islands and mountains which have nearby hills and all other areas and at all other places in the eight directions of brahmā’s universe, with overflowing bubbles, in his divine stomach, in the previous times.

*ēḻ ulagum* – Climbing everywhere over the seven islands and the mountains which have surrounding hills, flowing over the eight directions at all places in brahmā’s universe with greatly appearing bubbles, sarvēśvaran who secured the greatly flooded ocean in a small portion of his divine form.

*ūḻidoṟum …* – tirunāngūr which is having brāhmaṇas who are having rising great wealth, instead of reducing over time, as said in śrī bhāgavatam 11.5.38 “*kalau krutayugam tasya*” (kruta yugam appearing in kali yugam), and having gem-studded mansions which touch the sky.

## 4.4.10. Siraninda manimadam

*sīraṇinda maṇimādam tigaḻum nāngūrt tiruttetṟiyambalattu en sengaṇmālai kūraṇinda vēlvalavan āli nādan kodimāda mangaiyar kōn kuṟaiyalāḷi pāraṇinda tol pugaḻān kaliyan sonna pāmālai ivai aindum aindum vallār sīraṇinda ulagattu mannarāgic cēṇ visumbil vānavarāyt tigaḻvar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sīr – wealth; aṇinda – having; maṇi – filled with gems; mādam – mansions; tigaḻum – shining; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tirutteṟṟi ambalattu – mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam; en – being my lord; sem kaṇ mālai – on sarvēśvaran who is having reddish eyes; kūr aṇinda – sharp; vēl – spear; valavan – one who handles; Ali nādan – being the ruler of tiruvāli region; kodi – having flags; mādam – filled with mansions; mangaiyar – for the residents of tirumangai region; kōn – being the king; kuṟaiyal āḷi – being the protector of tirukkuṟaiyalūr; pār aṇinda – spread all over the earth; tol – natural; pugaḻān – having fame; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; pāmālai – in the form of a garland of songs; ivai aindum aindum – these ten pāsurams; vallār – those who can recite; sīr aṇinda – having wealth; ulagattu – in this world; mannar āgi – being kings (subsequently); sēṇ visumbil – in paramapadam; vānavarāy – being present along with nityasūris; tigaḻvar – will shine

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār who is having natural fame which is spread all over the earth, who handles sharp spear, being the ruler of tiruvāli region, the king for the residents of tirumangai region which is filled with mansions with flags, the protector of tirukkuṟaiyalūr, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams in the form of a garland of songs on my lord, sarvēśvaran who is having reddish eyes and who is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirutteṟṟi ambalam in tirunāngūr where wealthy mansions which are filled with gems, are shining. Those who can recite these pāsurams will be kings in this wealthy world and will shine, being present along with nityasūris in paramapadam.

*sīr aṇinda …* – sarvēśvaran who is puṇḍarīkākśan (lotus-eyed lord) who is present in tirutteṟṟiyambalam in tirunāngūr which has wealthy mansions which are filled with gems.

*kūr aṇinda …* – Just as his spear is sharp, his poems are also sharp. The ruler of tiruvāli, the king of tirumangai which has mansions with flags, and the leader of tirukkuṟaiyalūr.

*pār aṇinda …* – Just like flood in a small place, āḻvār, who has great fame all over the earth, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams. Those who are well versed in these pāsurams.

*sīr aṇinda …* – Will enjoy wealth in this life without any shortcoming, and will remain together with nityasūris in paramapadam and shine.

## 4.5 Tumbudai

## 4.5.1. Tumbudai

*tūmbudaip panaikkai vēḻam tuyar keduttaruḷi mannu kāmbudaik kunṟam ēndik kadumaḻai kātta endai pūmbunal ponni muṟṟum pugundu pon varaṇḍa engum tēmboḻil kamaḻum nāngūrt tirumaṇikkūdattānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tūmbu udai – having holes; panai – stout like a palm tree; kai – having trunk; vēḻam – gajēndrāḻvān’s; tuyar – sorrow; keduttu aruḷi – mercifully eliminated; mannu – fitting well (on earth) and remaining (well rooted); kāmbu udai – having bamboos; kunṟam – gōvardana mountain; ēndi – held as umbrella; kadu – cruel; maḻai – hailstorm; kātta – stopped and protected gōkulam; endai – my lord; pū – beautiful; punal – having water; ponni – the divine kāvēri river; muṟṟum – at all places; pugundu – entered; pon – gold (which were present there); varaṇḍa – as brought along; engum – at all places; tēm poḻil – water filled gardens; kamaḻum – spreading fragrance; nāngūr – present in tirunāngūr; tirumaṇik kūdattān – is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My lord mercifully eliminated the sorrow of gajēndrāḻvān who is having trunk with holes, which is stout like a palm tree; he held gōvardana mountain which is having bamboos which are fitting well and remaining on earth, as umbrella and stopped the cruel hailstorm and protected gōkulam; such emperumān is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam which is present in tirunāngūr where the divine kāvēri river, which is having beautiful water, entered all places, brought along gold and is having gardens, which are filled with water everywhere and are spreading fragrance.

*tūmbudai …* – Mercifully eliminating the sorrow of the elephant which is having trunk which is having holes, remaining like palm tree as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.1.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thiruvaimozhi-4-1-4-ninaippan-pugin/) “*panait tāḷ mada kaḷiṟu*” (mad elephant \[kuvalayāpīdam\] which had well rounded palm tree like feet). If it is recited as “*paṇaikkai*“, it means the elephant which throws those who are caught by it, to break their waist. With this, it is always respected; the elephant which had never been insulted.

*mannu …* – Holding the mountain which has bamboo which is well rooted in the earth, my lord who protected from the unstoppable rain.

*pūm punal …* – River ponni which has water with blossomed flowers; “*pū*” also implies beautiful.

*muṟṟum pugundu* – Spreading everywhere and filling fully instead of just entering through a single canal. If recited as “*muṟṟam*“, spreading everywhere outside.

*pon varaṇḍa engum* – Bringing along all the available gold.

*tēm poḻil …* – Since there is continuous flow of water, tirunāngūr which is having gardens with continuous fragrance.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.5.2. Kavvai valeyirru

*kavvai vāḷeyiṟṟu vanpēyk kadir mulai suvaittu ilangai manniya idumbai tīrak kadungaṇai turanda endaikovvai vāy magaḷir kongaik kungumam kaḻuvip pōnda deyva nīr kamaḻum nāngūrt tirumaṇikkūdattānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kavvai – having loud roar; vāḷ – sword like; eyiṟu – having teeth; van – cruel minded; pēy – pūtanā’s; kadir – shining (due to abundance of poison); mulai – bosom; suvaittu – mercifully consumed; ilangai – lankā’s; manniya – eternal; idumbai – poverty of being connected to evil people; tīra – to eliminate; kadum – cruel; kaṇai – (killer) arrows; turanda – who shot; endai – my lord; kovvai – like kōvai fruit; vāy – having lips; magaḷir – ladies’; kongai – applied on bosoms; kungumam – vermillion mix; kaḻuvi – wash; pōnda – and flowing; deyvam – distinguished; nīr – water; kamaḻum – spreading fragrance; nāngūr – present in tirunāngūr; tirumaṇik kūdattān – is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My lord mercifully consumed from the shining bosom of cruel minded pūtanā, who was having loud roar and sword like teeth; he shot cruel arrows to eliminate lankā’s eternal poverty of being connected to evil people; such emperumān is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam which is present in tirunāngūr where the distinguished water, which is washing the vermillion mix applied on the bosoms of the ladies, who are having kōvai fruit like lips, is flowing, spreading fragrance,

*kavvai …* – Considering that yaśōdāp pirātti will lovingly speak to kriṣṇa with emotions, pūtanā, the strong demon,  was trying to imitate her making huge sounds, and was having sword like teeth; she was having bosom which was shining due to the poison in it. He tasted such bosom.

*ilangai manniya idumbai tīra* – lankā has an eternal poverty – just as an anthill will be constantly inhabited by snakes, lankā is inhabited by evil demon clan; to eliminate such poverty. Greatness for a town – being inhabited by noble people; lowliness for a town – being inhabited by evil people. If recited as “*kūra*” instead of “*tīra*“, it should be understood as “as the suffering increased, emperumān, my lord, eliminated it with his arrow”.

*kadum kaṇai turanda endai* –  My lord who mercilessly shot arrows on the enemies. If recited as “*vavviya idumbai tīra”* it is to be understood as “to eliminate the poverty which fell upon lankā”; to eliminate the sorrow which occurred due to the connection with rāvaṇa.

*kovvai …* – Washing away the vermillion mix on the bosoms of ladies who have kōvai fruit like reddish mouth, the divine water is spreading fragrance; such tirunāngūr.

## 4.5.3. Mattolil madanga

*māttoḻil madangac ceṟṟu maṟudiṟa nadandu vantāḷ sēttoḻil sidaittup pinnai sevvit tōḷ puṇarnda endai nāttoḻil maṟai vallārgaḷ nayandu aṟam payanda vaṇkait tīttoḻil payilum nāngūrt tirumaṇikkūdattānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā – kēśi, the demon’s; toḻil – act; madanga – to be controlled; seṟṟu – killed; marudu – maruda trees; iṟa – to break; nadandu – crawled in between those; van – strong; tāḷ – having feet; sē – bulls; toḻil – act; sidaittu – destroyed; pinnai – nappinnaip pirātti’s; sevvi – beautiful; tōḷ – with shoulders; puṇarnda – one who embraced; endai – my lord; nā toḻil – the act of the tongue, adyayanam (learning/reciting) which was done; maṟai – vēdams; vallārgaḷ – brāhmaṇas who can handle; nayandu – eagerly; darmattai – conducted; vaṇ – generous; kai – with the hands; tī toḻil – fire rituals; payilum – conducting; nāngūr – present in tirunāngūr; tirumaṇik kūdattān – is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My lord killed kēśi, the demon, to have his acts controlled, crawled in between the two maruda trees to break those, and embraced the beautiful shoulders of nappinnaip pirātti by destroying the acts of the bulls which had strong feet; such emperumān is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam where brāhmaṇas who are experts in vēdams,which are recited by the tongue, eagerly conduct darmam and who conduct fire rituals with their generous hands, are residing.

*māttoḻil …* – my lord who killed kēśi to control his acts, broke the maruda trees by crawling through those trees while learning to walk, destroyed the acts of the bulls which were having strong feet as if he were knocking down sand-castles and embraced nappinnaip pirātti’s beautiful/fresh shoulders.

*nāttoḻil …* – Experts of vēdams, with the ability of the tongue, would conduct fire rituals with their generous hands which eagerly conducted darmam. If we read “*tīttoḻil*” to be “bad acts”, it will be contrary as saying “One who is good in conduct became devoid of good conduct”. Hence it should be taken as acts involving fire. After performing adyayanam (learning of vēdam), they will engage in karma (actions) which are ordained in such vēdam. Having learnt vēdam, since they are merciful towards others, they will remain compassionate towards the suffering persons; with their hands, which conduct darmam, they will engage in three types of fire viz dakśiṇāgni, āhavanīyam and trētāgni. Just as learning of vēdams and conducting themselves as per vēdam are the routine for the residents of tirumaṇikkūdam, emperumān has destruction of enemies as his routine.

## 4.5.4. Tangarum sinattu

*tāngarum sinattu van tāḷ tadakkaimā maruppu vāngki pūngurundu osittup puḷvāy piḷandu erudadartta endai māngani nugarnda mandi vandu vaṇḍiriya vāḻait tīngani nugarum nāngūrt tirumaṇikkūdattānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāngu arum – unable to bear (for anyone); sinattu – having anger; van tāḷ – having strong feet; tadam kai – kuvalayāpeedam, which is having huge trunk, its; mā – large; maruppu – tusk; vāngi – plucked; pūm – blossomed; kurundu – kurunda tree; osittu – broke; puḷ – bakāsura’s; vāy – mouth; piḷandu – tore; erudu – bulls; adartta – one who crushed and killed; endai – my lord; māngani – mangoes; nugarnda – ate; mandi – female monkey; vandu – left there; vaṇḍu – (came to drink honey) beetles; iriya – to disperse and run away; vāḻai – plantain tree’s; tī – sweet; kani – fruits; nugarum – ate; nāngūr – present in tirunāngūr; tirumaṇik kūdattān – is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My lord plucked the large tusk of kuvalayāpeedam, which is having anger, which is unbearable, strong feet and huge trunk; he broke the blossomed kurunda tree; he tore bakāsura’s mouth; he crushed and killed the bulls; such emperumān is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam where the female monkey ate mangoes, left there and came to eat the sweet banana fruits in the plantain trees to have the beetles disperse and run away.

*tāngu arum …* – Just as plucking green leaves, my lord effortlessly plucked the large tusk of kuvalayāpeedam, which is having anger, which is unbearable, strong feet and huge trunk; he broke the beautiful kurunda trees which was fully blossomed; he tore bakāsura’s mouth; and killed the seven bulls.

*māngani …* – Female monkey which ate the mango, thought “we should spend our time enjoying a different taste”, went and ate the banana fruits, to disperse the beetles which had gathered there to consume honey. Just as emperumān would not spend his time, without eliminating the enemies, these monkeys too would not spend their time, without enjoying different tastes.

## 4.5.5. Karumagal

*karumagaḷ ilangaiyātti pilangoḷ vāy tiṟandu tan mēl varumavaḷ seviyum mūkkum vāḷināl tadinda endai perumagaḷ pēdai mangai tannodum pirivilāda tirumagaḷ maruvum nāngūrt tirumaṇikkūdattānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karumagaḷ – very lowly like a caṇḍāḷa woman; ilangai ātti – being the controller of lankā; pilam koḷ – cave like; vāy tiṟandu – opening her mouth; than mēl – on self; varum avaḷ – sūrpaṇakā, who came; seviyum – ear; mūkkum – nose; vāḷināl – with the sword; tadinda – severed; endai – my lord; peru magaḷ – having natural femininity; pēdai – one who is ignorant on the defects of devotees; mangai – bhūmip pirātti; tannodum – with her; pirivu ilāda – one who never separates (being together always); tirumagaḷ – śrīdēvi; maruvum – eternally residing; nāngūr – present in tirunāngūr; tirumaṇik kūdattān – is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sūrpaṇakā who is very lowly like a caṇḍāḷa woman, being the controller of lankā, opened her cave like mouth and came towards my lord who severed her ear and nose with the sword; such emperumān is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam where he is eternally residing with śrī bhūmip pirātti who is having natural femininity and who is ignorant of the defects of devotees and with śrīdēvi who never separates from him.

*karu magaḷ …* – Lowly woman; being born with rāvaṇa, she was glorified by all the residents of lankā, opened her cave like mouth.

*than mēl varum avaḷ* – As sūrpaṇakā marched towards the inseparable sītāp pirātti, śrī rāma felt that she marched towards him.

*sevi …* – He ensured that she regained her natural (ugly) form after eliminating her assumed pride. She opened her mouth fully and went towards pirātti thinking that she was the hurdle for her to enjoy him; my lord who severed her ear and nose.

*perumagaḷ* – Having natural femininity.

*pēdai mangai* – One who is ignorant about others’ defects. Here śrī bhūmip pirātti is indicated.

*tannodu pirivilāda tirumagaḷ* – periya pirāttiyār who never separates from him as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum*” (I cannot separate even for a moment). The abode where śrī bhūmip pirātti and periya pirāttiyār are eternally residing.

## 4.5.6. Kendaiyum kuralum

*keṇḍaiyum kuṟaḷum puḷḷum kēḻalum ariyum māvum aṇḍamum sudarum allā āṟṟalum āya endai oṇḍiṟal tennanōda vadavarasōttam kaṇḍa tiṇḍiṟalāḷar nāngūrt tirumaṇikkūdattānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

keṇḍaiyum – matsya (fish); kuṟaḷum – vāmana; puḷḷum – hamsa (swan), the bird; kēḻalum – varāha (pig); ariyum – narasimha; mavum – hayagrīva (having such incarnations); aṇḍamum – brahmā’s oval shaped universe; sudarum – sun and moon; allā – other; āṟṟalum – best entities; āya – one who is mercifully present to have as his prakāram (forms); endai – my lord; oṇ tiṟal – very strong; tennan – pāṇḍiya, who was the ruler of southern region; ōda – to flee; vadavarasu – cōḻa who was the king of the region north of pāṇḍiya’s kingdom; ōttam kaṇḍa – made to flee after losing; tiṇ tiṟalāḷar – very strong brāhmaṇas’; nāngūr – present in tirunāngūr; tirumaṇik kūdattān – is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My lord who incarnated as matsya, vāmana, hamsa, varāha, narasimha is mercifully present to have brahmā’s oval shaped universe, sun and moon, and all other best entities as his prakāram ; such emperumān is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam in tirunāngūr which belongs to very strong brāhmaṇas who made the very strong pāṇḍiya who was the ruler of southern region to flee and cōḻa, who was the king of the region which is to the north of pāṇḍiya’s kingdom, to flee after losing.

*keṇḍaiyum …* – He remained having matsya, śrī vāmana, hamsa, śrī varāham, narasimha and hayagrīva, his wealth \[universe\], moon and sun who light up the universe, and further the best entities in the universe as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 10.41](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/10-41/) “*yad yad vibhūtimat satvam śrīmad ūrjitam Eva vā \| …*” (Whichever creature is having glories which are controlled by it, having radiance and is fixed on starting auspicious activities, you know that those creatures acquired that from a fraction of my controlling ability), to be said as himself.

*āṟṟalumāy* – My lord who remained as the strong and eternal entities.

*oṇ tiṟal …* – Where the very strong brāhmaṇaas, who made pāṇḍiya, who has shining strength, to flee and the king of northern region too flee, are residing. The residents of the town are able to do whatever he does incarnating.

## 4.5.7. Kunramum vanum

*kunṟamum vānum maṇṇum kuḷir punal tingaḷōdu ninṟa venjudarum allā nilaigaḷum āya endai manṟavum vayalum kāvum mādamum maṇam koṇḍu engum tenṟal vandu ulavum nāngūrt tirumaṇikkūdattānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kunṟamum – mountains; vānum – ether; maṇṇum – earth; kuḷir – cool; punal – water; tingaḷōdu – moon; ninṟa – firmly stood; vem sudarum – sun which has hot rays; allā nilaigaḷum – all other stars (all of these); āya – having as his prakāram; endai – my lord; manṟamum – wide streets; vayalum – fertile fields; kāvum – gardens; mādamum – mansions (caused from these); maṇam – fragrance; koṇḍu vandu – extracting it; engum – in all places; tenṟal – southerly breeze from the mountain; ulavum – roaming; nāngūr – present in tirunāngūr; tirumaṇik kūdattān – is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My lord is having mountains, ether, earth, cool water, moon, sun which has hot rays and all other stars as his prakāram; such emperumān is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam in tirunāngūr where the southerly breeze from the mountain is extracting the fragrance from the wide streets, fertile fields, gardens, mansions, and is roaming in all places.

*kunṟam …* – emperumān remains as the mountains which arrange enjoyments, tools for enjoyments and abode for enjoyments for sentient beings, ether which provides space for those mountains, earth which provides enjoyments, water which cools down, moon, sun which eliminates the coolness caused by moon and stars which indicate the good and bad which conduct the life of sentient beings.

*manṟamum …* – Gardens will be present in large streets; ponds will be present in fertile fields; women will be present in gardens and mansions; the southerly breeze which is roaming, brings along the fragrance from those places and spreads everywhere; alternatively – bringing fragrance from everywhere and roaming.

## 4.5.8. Sangaiyum tunivum

*sangaiyum tuṇivum poyyum meyyum ittaraṇi ōmbum pongiya mugilum allāp poruḷgaḷum āya endai pangayam ugutta tēṟal parugiya vāḷai pāya sengayal ugaḷum nāngūrt tirumaṇikkūdattānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sangaiyum – doubt; tuṇivum – clarity; poyyum – untruth; meyyum – truth; ittaraṇi – this earth; ōmbum – one which protects; pongiya – growing; mugilum – cloud; allā – other; poruḷgaḷum – entities (all of these); āya – one who can control; endai – my lord; pangayam – from lotus flower; ugutta – flowing; tēṟal – honey; parugiya – drank; vāḷai – huge fish; pāya – as it jumps; sem – reddish; kayal – small fish; ugaḷum – jump away (due to fear); nāngūr – present in tirunāngūr; tirumaṇik kūdattān – is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is saying “emperumān who is the controller of the entities which are to be abandoned, pursued and are made of panca bhūtams has arrived here and residing”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My lord, who can control doubt, clarity, untruth, truth, growing cloud which protects this earth and all other entities, is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam in tirunāngūr where as the huge fish jumps after drinking the honey flowing from lotus flower, the reddish, small fish jump away.

*sangaiyum …* – Doubt which would lead to destruction as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.40](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-40/) “*samśayātmā vinaśyati*” (one who is doubtful will be finished), clarity as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.41](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-41/) “*vyavasāyātmikā buddir ēkā*” (For those who have firm faith in the true nature of self, their intelligence is single minded), poyyum – harmful lies which are told without any purpose, truth which is good.

*ittaraṇi …* – sarvēśvaran who is the controller of the vast clouds which protect the earth without any expectation, and thunder, lightning etc.

*pangayam …* – The lotus flowers which are filled with honey, let it out; the huge fish drank that honey and jumped, out of ecstasy and the reddish small fish feared and left its abode. Such tirumaṇikkūdam.

## 4.5.9. Pavamum aramum

*pāvamum aṟamum vīdum inbamum tunbam tānum kōvamum aruḷum allāk kuṇangaḷum āya endai mūvaril engaḷ mūrtti ivan ena munivarōdu dēvar vandu iṟainjum nāngūrt tirumaṇikkūdattānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pāvamum – pāpam (sin); aṟamum – puṇṇiyam (puṇyam/virtue); vīdum – mōkśam; inbamum – joy; tunbam tānum – sorrow; kōvamum – anger; aruḷum – mercy; allā – other; guṇangaḷum – qualities such as satva (goodness) etc (all of these); āya – one who controls; endai – my lord; mūvaril – among brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra; engaḷ – one who is our refuge; mūrtti – lord; ivan ena – being clear that it is only this viṣṇu; munivarōdu – along with sages such as sanaka et al; dēvar – dēvatās such as indra et al; vandu – approach; iṟainjum – remaining to be surrendered to; nāngūr – present in tirunāngūr; tirumaṇik kūdattān – is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My lord who controls pāpam, puṇṇiyam, mōkśam, joy, sorrow, anger, mercy and all other qualities such as satva, is the one who is mercifully present in tirumaṇik kūdam in tirunāngūr where he is remaining to be approached and surrendered to by dēvatās such as indra et al along with sages such as sanaka et al, who are clear that it is this viṣṇu who is the lord and refuge among brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra.

*pāvamum …* – Forbidden deeds, ordained deeds, liberation, joy, sorrow which occurs since that joy is temporary, anger which is to be abandoned by wise people, mercy, and other qualities such as satva etc are all remaining as his prakāram (attribute), to be said as himself.

*mūvaril …* – Being antaryāmi of brahmā et al, and being himself and protecting, he remains the refuge for us who have abundance of satva guṇam, being one among the three primary dēvatās of the world, he is mercifully standing to be surrendered to by dēvatās such as indra et al along with sages such as sanaka et al.

## 4.5.10. Tingal toy

*tingaḷ tōy māda nāngūrt tirumaṇikkūdattānai mangaiyar talaivan vaṇ tār kaliyan vāyoligaḷ vallār pongu nīrulagam āṇḍu ponnulagāṇḍu pinnum vengadirp paridi vattattūdu pōy viḷanguvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tingaḷ – (reaching) in the orbit of moon; tōy – touching; mādam – having mansions; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tirumaṇikkūdattānai – on emperumān who is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirumaṇikkūdam; mangaiyar – for the residents of tirumangai region; talaivan – being the king; vaṇ – beautiful; tār – having garland; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; vāy – mercifully spoke; oligaḷ – these ten pāsurams which are a garland of words; vallār – those who can recite; pongu – rising; nīr – being surrounded by water-filled ocean; ulagam – earth; āṇḍu – rule over; pon ulagu – heaven; āṇḍu – enjoy; pinnum – further; vem kadir – sun’s; parudi vattattu – orbit’s; ūdu pōy – going through the middle (i.e. going through the arcirādi mārgam); viḷanguvār – will shine (in paramapadam)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

On emperumān who is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirumaṇikkūdam in tirunāngūr where the mansions are reaching up to the moon and touching it, tirumangai āḻvār who is the king of tirumangai region and who is wearing a beautiful garland, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams which are a garland of words; those who can recite this decad, will rule over the earth which is surrounded by ocean with rising water, enjoy heaven and further will shine in paramapadam going through the middle of sun’s orbit.

*tingaḷ …* – One who is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirumaṇikkūdam in tirunāngūr where the mansions are reaching up to the moon and touching it.

*mangaiyar …* – Chief of the residents of tirumangai region, āḻvār who is having beautiful garland, mercifully spoke this decad; those who are experts in this, will rule over the earth which is surrounded by ocean, rule over the heaven and further go through the middle of sun in the arcirādi mārgam, reach paramapadam and realise the true self and shine.

## 4.6 Tavalandu ulagam

## 4.6.1. Tavalandu ulagam

*tāvaḷandu ulaga muṟṟum tadamalarp poygai pukku nāvaḷam navinṟangu ētta nāgattin nadukkam tīrttāy!māvaḷam perugi mannu maṟaiyavar vāḻum nāngaik kāvaḷambādi mēya kaṇṇanē! kaḷaigaṇ nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ualgam muṟṟum – (śrī gajēndrāḻvān) all worlds; tāvaḷandu – hopped around (seen at that time); tadam – huge; malar – having flower; poygai – in the pond; pukku – entered; angu – in that pond; nā – for the tongue; vaḷam – divine name which is decoration; navinṟu – recited; ētta – as it praised; nāgattin – (that) elephant’s; nadukkam – fear; tīrttāy – oh one who eliminated!; mā vaḷam – great wealth; perugi – grew; mannu – remaining fixed; maṟaiyavar – brāhmaṇas; vāḻum – living joyfully; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; kāvaḷambādi – in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi; mēya – one who is residing firmly; kaṇṇanē – Oh kriṣṇa!; nīyē – you who are partial towards devotees; kaḷaigaṇ – should be the protector

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

śrī gajēndrāḻvān, the elephant, hopped around all the worlds and entered the pond which was having huge flower; it recited the divine name (of emperumān) as decoration for tongue and praised; oh one who eliminated such elephant’s fear! Oh kriṣṇa who is residing firmly in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr where brāhmaṇas are having well grown great wealth and remaining fixed, living joyfully! You who are partial towards devotees should be the protector \[for me\].

*tāvaḷandu …* – When the elephant was attacked by the crocodile, did the elephant rescue itself or did the crocodile rescue it? That which harms will not be protection. I am like that elephant; others are like crocodile.

*tāvaḷanadu ulagam muṟṟum* –  This is fully seen in the context of the elephant \[without any mention of crocodile\] – since the elephant did not see any flower anywhere, it hopped around the whole earth; alternatively – this is explained in the context of trivikrama avatāram where emperumān mercifully scaled the world – emperumān effortlessly scaled and accepted the world. Did the residents of the earth do anything for you to scale the world?

*tāvaḷandu …* – With the desire of “Can I find a blossomed flower?”, the elephant roamed around the entire earth; subsequently it saw a pond with a huge flower and entered the pond without knowing about the presence of the crocodile in it and got caught, trapped in its mouth; without knowing any escape route, just as one would cry out “*ammē*” (mother) while stepping on a thorn and being pierced by it, due to impressions from previous birth, recited the divine name of emperumān which is a decoration for the tongue. It is said in [mudal tiruvandādi 95](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-95/) “*nā vāyil uṇḍē namō nāraṇā enṟu ovādu uraikkum urai uṇḍē*” (tongue is inside the mouth; tirumantram which is apt to be recited continuously, is available). It called out as said in siṟiya tirumadal “*nārāyaṇāvō!*”  (Oh nārāyaṇa!)

*angu* – Oh you who eliminated the fear of the elephant which recited the divine name, standing in the pond where it was caught! Did the elephant help itself or did the crocodile help? Wasn’t it you who came to the banks of the pond, without having your hair properly decorated and your clothes well adorned, and helped him?

*māvaḷam …* – The boundless wealth of the brāhmaṇas are growing just as flood will rise in the river entrance, and that too without any break. Oh kriṣṇa who is known only through vēdas and who is being seen by such brāhmaṇas, sinces you are eternally residing in tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr!

*mēya* – Difference from avatārams, where he leaves within a specific period of time; remaining eternally here.

*kaṇṇanē kaḷaigaṇ nīyē* – You who are residing without being able to live in separation from those who are dear to you, should be the protector. āḻvār is mercifully stating the words of kriṣṇa who said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*māmēkam*” (Only me).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.2. Mannidandu

*maṇṇidandu ēnamāgi māvali vali tolaippān viṇṇavar vēṇḍac cenṟu vēḷviyil kuṟai irandāy tuṇṇena māṟṟār tammait tolaittavar nāngkai mēya kaṇṇanē! kāvaḷandaṇpādiyāy! kaḷaigaṇ nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēnamāgi – Being ādivarāha; maṇ – earth which was stuck in the wall of the aṇḍam (oval shaped universe); idandu – dug out; māvali – mahābali’s; vali – strength; tolaippān – to eliminate; viṇṇavar – dēvatās; vēṇḍa – as they prayed; senṟu – went; vēḷviyil – (in his) fire sacrifice; kuṟai – earth which was missing from his possession; irandāy – Oh one who begged!; tuṇṇena – quickly; māṟṟār tammai – enemies; tulaittavar – where the brave men who won over, are residing; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; kāvaḷam taṇ pādiyāi – Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi!; mēya – One who is eternally residing (in that divyadēśam); kaṇṇanē – Oh kriṣṇa!; nīyē kaḷaigaṇ – You should be the protector; kāvaḷandaṇpādi – Note that the meaning for this word is as in, kā – gardens’, vaḷam – due to abundance, taṇ – cool, pādi – divyadēśam. divyadēśam which is cool due to abundance of gardens

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being ādivarāha you dug out the earth which was stuck in the wall of the aṇḍam; oh one who begged for the earth which was missing from your possession, after going to mahābali’s fire sacrifice as the dēvatās prayed to eliminate mahābali’s strength! Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr where the brave men, who quickly won over the enemies, are residing! Oh kriṣṇa who is eternally residing in there! You should be the protector.

*maṇ idandu …* – As the ocean which was arranged as the protective layer became harmful \[in consuming the earth\], he assumed a form which does not back out from water and mud, and dug out the earth.

*māvali vali tolaippān* – Since mahābali had a good quality named generosity, emperumān need not sever his head as he did for rāvaṇa et al; still, since maHabali troubled dēvatās, he had the deeds of rāvaṇa; though mahābali had to be killed, he would not do it; instead of destroying him, he destroyed himself \[his own stature\]. To eliminate mahābali’s strength, since dēvatās who were troubled by him, prayed,

*senṟu* – emperumān went to mahābali’s sacrificial arena.

*vēḷviyil* – Not in seclusion \[but in a huge gathering\].

*kuṟai irandāy* – emperumān who is avāpta samasta kāman (one who has no unfulfilled desires) had a shortcoming; as he saw the suffering of dēvatās, he also assumed that suffering.

*tuṇ ena …* – The residents of this divyadēśam don’t have the nature of indra et al; they will not make emperumān beg, and nurture themselves. Instead, similar to \[sugrīva\] mahārājar, they would protect others, at the cost of themselves. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 40.29 “*ata harivara nāta:* *prāpya sangrāma kīrttim* *niśicara patim* *ājau*  *yōjayitvā śramēṇa”* (sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, acquiring the fame as a warrior, reduced rāvaṇa to exhaustion) \[Note: This ślōkam is explained in detail in [https://divyaprabandam.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/tiruvaimoḻi-7-4-1-aḻi-eḻa/](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-4-1-azhi-ezha/)\] He caused fear which was unknown to rāvaṇa previously.

*kāvalam taṇ pādiyāy kaḷaigaṇ nīyē* – You, who are entered as one among the residents of the town, should be my protector.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.3. Uruttelu

*urutteḻu vāli mārvil ōru kaṇai uruva ōtti karuttudait tambikku inbak kadir mudi arasu aḷittāy parutteḻu palavum māvum paḻam viḻundu oḻugum nāngaik karuttanē! kāvaḷantaṇpādiyāy! kaḷaigaṇ nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

eḻu – rising; uruttu – having anger; vāli – vāli’s; mārvil – on the chest; oru kaṇai – an arrow; uruva – to pierce well; ōtti – shot; karuttudai – being the target of your divine heart; tambikku – sugrīva mahārajar who is the brother (of such vāli); inbam – to cause joy; kadir – radiant; mudi – crown; arasu – and the kingdom; aḷittāy – oh you who mercifully granted!; paruttu – being stout; eḻu – sprouting; palavum – jack fruit tree’s; māvum – mango trees’; paḻam – fruits; viḻundu – fell down; oḻugum – honey is flooding; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; kāvaḷam taṇ pādiyāi – Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi!; karuttanē – Oh you who are skillful!; nīyē kaḷaigaṇ – You should be the protector

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who shot an arrow on the chest of vāli who is having rising anger\`, to pierce it well, and who mercifully granted the radiant crown and the kingdom to sugrīva mahārajar who was vāli’s brother, who was the target of your divine heart, to cause joy for him! Oh you who are present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr where the fruits falling down from the stout, sprouting jack fruit trees and mango trees are causing a flood of honey! Oh you who are skillful! You should be the protector.

*uruttu …* – uru – anger. It is said in tiruccanda viruttam 43 “*venjinatta vēḻa veṇmarupposittu urutta mā kanjanaik kadandu*” (Broke the very angry elephant’s tusk and killing the very angry kamsa). One who came with rising anger asking “Who is giving the war cry in wrong time?)

*vāli mārvil oru kaṇai uruva ōtti* – On vāli’s firm chest, where any arrows shot at would go in vain and who is indestructible. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.66 “*ēkēna mahēśuṇā*” (With a single arrow, śrī rāma pierced the seven ebony trees and the lower worlds) – he shot an arrow which he could lay his hands on and shot at him to make the arrow to pierce though his chest and come out, on the other side. Even the arrow which was shot at in a careless manner could pierce him through.

*karuttu …* – sugrīva who has the talent to rule the kingdom as done by vāli; alternative explanation – sugrīva who stayed in exile in the forest on hearing the name of vāli; he made pāṇḍavas though they did not want victory as they said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.32](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-32/) “*na kānkśē vijayam kriṣṇa*” (Oh kriṣṇa! I don’t desire for victory). making sugrīva mahārājar who is dear to your divine heart victorious. śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.76 is explained here. *tat rājyē* – sugrīva ruling the regime is similar to a doe present in a lion’s den. *rāghava:* – śrī rāma, who is born in the raghu clan, where the kings can appoint anyone to rule any kingdom. śuka and sāraṇa who are rāvaṇa’s spies themselves told in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 28.27 “*śrīmatā rājarājēna lankāyām abhiśēcita:*” (vibhīśaṇa was crowned by śrī rāma who is the king of kings and owns all wealth). *śrīmatā* – Unlike the wealth of brahmā et al who crowned you, vibhīśaṇa was crowned by śrī rāma who has perennial wealth. *rāja rājēna* – śrī rāma who incarnated to help brahmā et al, who crowned you, retain their crown. *lankāyām abhiśēcita:* – Now, you go and search a place to stay. śuka and sāraṇa, though being rāvaṇa’s servants who know about his wealth and control, speak in praise of śrī rāma like this due to having seen śrī rāma standing with his bow in his hands; they are speaking like this since rāvaṇa was disrespectfully thinking “What are these mosquito like people going to do for us?”

*inbak kadir mudi arasu aḷittāy* – You mercifully gave the crown which brings joy and respect, and the kingdom which is ruled under such crown.

*paruttu …* – The trees are similar to śrī vāmanan, where they were well-grown even while sprouting. They are fruit-bearing even while sprouting.

*paḻam* – There is endless enjoyment while there is scarcity for enjoyers.

*karuttanē* – It is apt for an incapable person ( like me) to hold on to a capable person (like you).

*kāvaḷam taṇ …* – After you, who are capable are present here, you should be the protector.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.4. Munai mugattu

*munai mugattu arakkan māḷa mudigaḷ pattu aṟuttu vīḻttu āngu anaiyavaṟku iḷaiyavaṟkē arasaḷittu aruḷinānē! sunaigaḷil kayalgaḷ pāyac curumbu tēn nugarum nāngaik kanai kaḻal kāvaḷandaṇpādiyāy! kaḷaigaṇ nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

munai mugattu – in the battlefield; arakkan – rāvaṇan; māḷa – to be killed; pattu mudigaḷ – (his) ten heads; aṟuttu – severed; vīḻttu – to make them fall down; āngu – there; anaiyavaṟku – for such rāvaṇan; iḷaiyavaṟkē – for vibhīśaṇan who is his younger brother; arasu – kingdom; aḷittaruḷinānē – Oh one who mercifully granted!; sunaigaḷil – in water-bodies; kayalgaḷ – fish; pāya – (feared) to run away; surumbu – beetles; tēn – honey; nugarum – drank (with a roar); nāngai – in tirunāngūr; kāvaḷam taṇ pādiyāi – Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi!; kanai – resounding; kaḻal – oh one who is having an anklet of valour!; nīyē kaḷaigaṇ – You should be the protector

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who severed rāvaṇan’s ten heads to make them fall down and have him killed and mercifully granted the kingdom to vibhīśaṇan, his younger brother, there! Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr where beetles drank honey to make the fish in water-bodies to run away! Oh one who is having a resounding anklet of valour! You should be the protector.

*munai mugattu …* – In the battle front.

*arakkan māḷa* – Unlike the rākśasas who would fight deceitful battles to kill the enemies, śrī rāma stood in the battlefront to kill rāvaṇa.

*mudigaḷ pattu aṟuttu vīḻttu* – Severing the heads which were strengthened by rāvaṇan by his acts of severing them and offering them in sacrifice. Making them fall down.

*āngu* – In that battle field itself, for vibhīśaṇa who was the younger brother of such rāvaṇa who was deeply unfavourable by separating perumāḷ and pirātti like separating body and life.

*arasu aḷittu aruḷinānē* – Looking at the great betrayal \[act of disrespecting bhagavān/pirātti\] of rāvaṇan, śrī rāma should have destroyed the entire lankā, but he granted the kingdom to vibhīśaṇa, his brother. For his defects, he himself said in śrī rāmāyaṇa yudda kāṇḍam 17.12 “*tasyāham anuja: brātā*” (I am such evil rāvāṇan’s younger brother). When sugrīva mahārājar lovingly invited vibhīśaṇāḻvān, he controlled his great joy and became flattened by such love and said “I , who am the brother of lowly rāvaṇan, am being invited lovingly by you!”

*sunai …* – In tirunāngūr where the kayal fish which are living in the ponds think about the roar of the beetles drinking honey and fear that they are falling on them, and jump away.

*kanai …* – āḻvār is speaking about the sound of the ornament (anklet); or he is saying about the dense feet which are brave. Is there any one else who is our protector other than you who are having anklet showing your valour as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.34 “*ētat vratam mama*” (I won’t fail anyone who surrenders unto me. This is my vow) and are present here for that.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.5. Padavara ucci

*padavara ucci tan mēl pāyndu pal nadangaḷ seydu madavaral mangai tannai mārvagattu iruttinānē!  tadavarai tangu mādat tagu pugaḻ nāngai mēya kadavuḷē! kāvaḷandaṇpādiyāy! kaḷaigaṇ nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

padam – having (expanded) hoods; aravu – kāḷiyan’s; ucci than mēl – on the head; pāyndu – jumped; pal nadangaḷ – many different types of dances; seydu – performed; madavaral – having humility; mangai tannai – eternally youthful periya pirātti; mārvagattu – on his divine chest; iruttinānē – oh you who have eternally placed!; tadam – vast; varai – like mountains; mādam – mansions; tangu – present; tagu – apt; pugaḻ – glory; mēya – is present; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; kāvaḷam taṇ pādiyāi – Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi!; kadavuḷē – Oh lord of all!; nīyē kaḷaigaṇ – You should be the protector

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you jumped on the head of kāḷiyan who had expanded hoods and performed many different types of dances! Oh you who have eternally placed the eternally youthful periya pirātti on your divine chest! Oh you who are present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr where mansions which resemble vast mountains are present, having apt glory! Oh lord of all! You should be the protector.

*padavarasu …* – When kriṣṇa reached the banks of the pond where kāḷiyan lived and joyfully roared, kāḷiyan angrily hissed thinking “Who is disturbing my enjoyment here?” and came out showing his expanded hoods, kriṣṇa skillfully jumped on the head and danced in many ways such that new definitions had to be written in bharata (dance) śāstram.

*madavaral mangai tannai …* – emperumān would be eternally together with pirātti for the complete protection of devotees and the complete destruction of enemies; alternatively – one who is very tender to unite with pirātti, jumped on the head of kāḷiyan, the enemy. Oh you who are eternally having periya pirāttiyār, who has noble qualities and eternal youth, on your divine chest!

*tada varai …* – When the mansions in that town are seen, they will remind us about the huge anchoring mountains. Alternatively – tirunāngūr where mountain like mansions are present, and which will be worthy of all glories attributed to them.

*kadavuḷē* – kadavuḷ – paradeyvam (supreme lord). Oh sarvēśvaran who is greater than all! When you are present here, should I go and search for someone else!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.6. Mallarai attu

*mallarai attu māḷak kanjanai malaindu konṟu pallarasu avindu vīḻap pāradap pōr mudittāy! nallaraṇ kāvin nīḻal naṟai kamaḻ nāngai mēya kallaraṇ kāvaḷandaṇpādiyāy! kaḷaigaṇ nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mallarai – wrestlers such as cāṇūra et al; attu – fought; māḷa – killed; kanjanai – kamsan; malaindu – fought; konṟu – killed; pal arasu – many kings; avindu vīḻa – to be destroyed; bāradap pōr – mahābhārata war; mudittāy – Oh one who completed!; nal – distinguished (dense); araṇ – having beauty (shade); kāvin – gardens’; nīḻal – in the shade; naṟai – fragrance; kamaḻ – smelling; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; mēya – firmly residing; kal – strong; araṇ – being the one who is having protection; kāvaḷam taṇ pādiyāi – Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi!; nīyē kaḷaigaṇ – You should be the protector

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who fought with wrestlers such as cāṇūra et al and killed them! Oh one who fought with kamsa and killed him! Oh one who completed mahābhārata war to have many kings destroyed! Oh you who are firmly residing in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr where the fragrance is smelling in the distinguished, beautiful gardens and having strong protection! You should be the protector.

*mallarai attu māḷa* – Fought with the wrestlers cāṇūra, muśtika et al who came with a lot of anger, and killed them instead of making them tired and letting them go; as kamsan angrily came, hearing the death of the wrestlers, emperumān killed and destroyed him. These were done when he was a child.

Now, āḻvār is talking about his acts which were done after he became old.

*pal arasu …* – All the evil people gathered in a single location; oh you who eliminated the burden of the earth by killing all those who came as kings supporting duryōdana et al!

*nal araṇ …* – In the shade of the garden which has abundance of shade, in tirunāngūr which is very fragrant showing that this is the place where bhagavān who is known as in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sarvaganda:*” (root of all fragrance) is eternally residing.

*kal araṇ …* – āḻvār’s upāyam (means) is well protected here. Should I go searching for another protection giving up the well protected upāyam?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.7. Muttavarku

*mūttavaṟku arasu vēṇḍi munbu tūdu eḻundaruḷi māttamar pāgan vīḻa madagari maruppu osittāy! pūttamar sōlai ōngip punal parandu oḻugum nāngaik kāttanē kāvaḷandaṇpādiyāy! kaḷaigaṇ nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mūttavaṟku – for dharma putra, who is the eldest; arasu vēṇḍi – desired for (to give) kingdom; munbu – previously; tūdu eḻundaruḷi – went as messenger; māttu – on elephant; amar – sitting firm; pāgan – mahout; vīḻa – to fall down and die; madam – fleshy; kari – kuvalayāpīdam’s; maruppu – tusk; osittāy – oh one who broke!; pū amar – filled with flowers; sōlai – gardens; ōngi – being tall; punal – water; parandu – spread (all over the garden); oḻugum – flowing; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; kāvaḷam taṇ pādiyāi – Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi!; kāttanē – Oh protector!; nīyē kaḷaigaṇ – You should be the protector

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who went as a messenger previously, desiring to give the kingdom for dharma putra, the eldest! Oh you who  made the mahout who was sitting firmly on the fleshy kuvalayāpīdam to fall down and die and broke its tusk! Oh you who are firmly residing in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr where the tall gardens are filled with flowers and water is spreading and flowing in those gardens! Oh protector! You should be the protector.

*mūttavaṟku …* – Previously emperumān went as a messenger thinking “While the apt one is present, the inapt one cannot have the crown; the eldest one should have the kingdom”. Though dritarāśtra was the eldest, since he had disability in his body, he did not have the qualification to rule the kingdom and hence pāṇḍu ruled the kingdom. After pāṇḍu’s time, duryōdana et al started ruling the kingdom saying “The kingdom is ours”. emperumān said “One cannot change the tradition; son should get to rule the kingdom of the father” and went as messenger for that.

*māttamar …* – Oh you who made the mahout who remained so firmly on the elephant that he would not lose his grip even if he died, to fall down and die, and effortlessly broke the tusk of the intoxicated kuvalayāpīdam!

*pūttamar …* – In tirunāngūr which is having tall gardens which had abundance of flowers and water which is spreading out and flowing, to grow such gardens.

*kāttanē* – Oh you who have vowed to protect all of these worlds as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.34 “*ētat vratam mama*” (I won’t fail anyone who surrenders unto me. This is my vow)!

*kāvaḷam …* – Instead of remaining away after vowing to protect, you are present in tirukkāvaḷambādi. \[Hence\] Only you should be my protector.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.8. Evilam kannikkagi

*ēviḷam kannikkāgi imaiyavar kōnaic ceṟṟu kāvaḷam kaditiṟuttuk kaṟpagam koṇḍu pōndāy! pūvaḷam poḻilgaḷ sūḻnda purandaran seyda nāngaik kāvaḷambādi mēya kaṇṇanē! kaḷaigaṇ nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēvu – in battle; iḷam kannikkāgi – for the young satyabhāmā; imaiyavar kōnai – dēvēndran; seṟṟu – defeated; kā – garden’s; vaḷam – beauty; kadidu – quickly; iṟuttu – destroyed; kaṟpagam – kalpaka tree \[a type of tree which grants all the wishes prayed to it, for\]; koṇḍu pōndāy – oh you who brought!; vaḷam – beautiful; pū – having flowers; poḻilgaḷ – gardens; sūḻnda – surrounded; purandaran – by indran; seyda – made; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; kāvaḷam pādi mēya – firmly present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi; kaṇṇanē – Oh kriṣṇa!; nīyē kaḷaigaṇ – You should be the protector

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who defeated dēvēndran in battle, quickly destroyed the garden’s beauty and brought the kalpaka tree, for the sake of the young satyabhāmā! Oh you who are firmly present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr, which is made by indran to be surrounded with gardens having beautiful flowers! You should be the protector.

*ēvu iḷam kannikkāgi …*

*ēvu* – battle.

*iḷam kannikku āgi* – For satyabhāmāp pirātti \[who is so youthful\], one can take up any suffering to fulfil her desire.

Alternative explanation. *Eva* – As she ordered.

While śaśi (indran’s wife) and satyabhāmāp pirātti were together, a flower from the kalpaka tree was brought there. śaśi accepted it and being prideful due to being a celestial woman, said a few insulting words to satyabhāmāp pirātti as in “You are humans; this cannot be donned by you; your head will ache”; satyabhāmāp pirātti then came to kriṣṇa and told about it and ordered kriṣṇa saying “You should immediately bring that kalpaka tree and plant it in my garden”.

*imaiyavar kōnaic ceṟṟu* – Defeating the leader of the celestial clan, indran, quickly destroyed the beauty of the garden and brought the kalpaka tree.

*pū vaḷam …* – In tirunāngūr which is surrounded by gardens which are having beautiful flowers and which was made/praised by indran. indran prepared this town to bring the glories of heaven to earth. You who are present now in tirukkāvaḷambādi to help everyone just as you helped satyabhāmā back then, should be my protector.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.9. Sandamay

*sandamāy samayamāgic camaya aimbūdamāgi andamāy ādiyāgi arumaṟai avaiyum ānāy! mandamār poḻilgaḷ tōṟum madamayil ālum nāngai kandamār kāvaḷandaṇpādiyāy! kaḷaigaṇ nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sandamāy – being the controller of candas (meter in poems); samayamāgi – being the controller of the order (that is, count of letters) matching that candas; samayam – the orderly nature; aimbūdamāgi – being the controller of the five elements; andamāy – being the cause of deluge; ādiyāgi – being the cause of creation; avai – revealing those principles; aru – difficult to know the meanings; maṟaiyum ānāy – Oh you who are the controller of vēdams!; mandam – mandāra trees; Ar – filled; poḻilgaḷ tōṟum – in all the gardens; madam mayil – humble peahens; Alum – dancing; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; gandam Ar – very fragrant; kāvaḷam taṇ pādiyāi – Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi!; nīyē kaḷaigaṇ – You should be the protector

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are the controller of candas, order matching that candas, the five elements which are in an orderly manner! Oh you who are the cause of deluge and creation! Oh you who are the controller vēdams in which the meanings are difficult to be known and which reveal these principles! Oh you who are present in the very fragrant divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr where the humble peahens are dancing in all the gardens which are filled with mandāra trees.

*sandamāy* – Being the controller of candas.

*samayamāgi* – Being the controller of the rules which say that there are these many akśarams (letters) in anuśtupu, druśtupu, jagati etc.

*samaya aim būdamāgi* – Being the controller of panca bhūtams (five elements) which are present in an orderly manner and which remain as the cause of everything else.

*andamāy …* – When everything effectual in this samsāram becomes destroyed, everything rests in him and he alone remains as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sadēva*” (only sat existed); being the cause of everything when he desired to split them \[from the subtle/collapsed state\] into individual cit and acit; being the controller of beginning and end.

*aru maṟai avaiyum ānāy* – Being the one who is revealed in vēdams as “brahmam is the one which is present in causal and effectual states”.

*mandam Ar …* – In tirunāngūr where in all the gardens which are filled with mandāra trees, the peahens are dancing.

*gandam Ar …* – It appears that this is the abode where the entity who is said as in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sarvaganda:*” (root of all fragrance) is eternally present.

*kaḷaigaṇ nīyē* – You who are greatly enjoyable should be my protector.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.10. Mavalam perugi

*māvaḷam perugi mannu maṟaiyavar vāḻum nāngaik kāvaḷambādi mēya kaṇṇaṇaik kaliyan sonna pāvaḷam pattum vallār pār misai arasarāgi kōviḷa mannar tāḻak kudai niḻal polivar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā vaḷam – great wealth; perugi – grew; mannum – remaining firm; maṟaiyavar – best among brāhmaṇas; vāḻum – living happily; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; kāvaḷam pādi – in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi; mēya – remaining firmly; kaṇṇanai – on kriṣṇa; kaliyan – āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; vaḷam – beautiful; pā pattum – ten pāsurams; vallār – those who can recite; pār misai – on earth; arasarāgi – being kings; kō (gō) – on earth; iḷa mannar – all the princes; tāḻa – to be subservient; kudai niḻal – in the shade of the umbrella; polivar – will remain wealthy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa is remaining firmly in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr where the best of brāhmaṇas who are with well grown, great wealth, are living happily; āḻvār mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams on such emperumān; those who can recite these pāsurams will remain as kings on earth and be wealthy under the shade of the umbrella to be served by all the princes on the earth.

*mā vaḷam …* – kriṣṇa is eternally living in the divyadēśam named tirukkāvaḷambādi in tirunāngūr where the brāhmaṇas who are having boundless wealth which keeps growing and does not stop growing on a particular day, and where such sarvēśvaran who is the essence of vēdam, can be seen through our eyes; while looking at the saulabhyam (easy approacability) here in this divyadēśam, kriṣṇāvatāram appears as paratvam (his presence in śrīvaikuṇṭam). Those who are experts in this decad which is having a beautiful meter as said in “Just reciting these pāsurams with our mouth, which were mercifully spoken by āḻvār, in itself is the goal”. pāvaḷam – type of poem.

Those who are well versed in this decad will become kings on this earth and

*kō iḷa mannar tāḻa …* – āḻvār is showing them worldly pleasure thinking “If we say that mōkśam is attained as a result of this decad, there will be no one interested. Hence, if we identify this as the means for their worldly desires, they will learn and then we will lead them to mōkśam”.

## 4.7 Kannar kadal

## 4.7.1. Kannar kadal

*kaṇṇār kadal pōl tirumēni kariyāy! naṇṇār munai venṟi koḷvār mannu nāngūr tiṇṇār madiḷ sūḻ  tiruveḷḷakkuḷattuḷ aṇṇā! adiyēn idaraik kaḷaiyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇ Ar – vast; kadal pōl – like ocean (having beauty and depth); tirumēni – having divine form; kariyāy – Oh kriṣṇa!; naṇṇār – enemies’; munai – in the battle; venṟi koḷvār – best among brāhmaṇas who can defeat (the enemies); mannu – eternally residing; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tiṇ Ar – strong; madiḷ – by forts; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruveḷḷak kuḷattuḷ – mercifully living in the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷakkuḷam; aṇṇā – Oh you who are naturally related!; adiyēn – I, who have no refuge, my; idarai – sorrows (viz. connection with prakruti (this body)); kaḷaiyāy – you should mercifully sever

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh kriṣṇa who is having divine form like a vast ocean! Oh you who are naturally related to all and are living in the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷakkuḷam surrounded by strong forts in tirunāngūr where the best among brāhmaṇas who can defeat the enemies in their battle, reside eternally! You should mercifully sever my sorrows, and I have no other refuge.

*kaṇṇār …* – Can anyone lose the enjoyment of such divine form? Oh you who are having ocean like divine form, from which one cannot take the eyes off! Alternatively – oh you who are having divine form which is like a vast ocean! Sometimes one engages in the beautiful form, other times one engages in his depth.

*naṇṇār munai venṟi koḷvār mannu nāngūr* – In tirunāngūr which is inhabited by those who don’t turn away without victory in the battles started by the enemies.

*tiṇṇār madiḷ …* – Oh you who are naturally related and are present in the abode where there is no scope for fear!

*adiyēn …* – I can remain relaxed only if I have refuge outside; you should sever the sorrows for me who has no other refuge.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
