## 4.7.2. Kondar tulava

*kondār tuḷava malar koṇḍu aṇivānē! nandāda perum pugaḻ vēdiyar nāngūr sendāmarai nīrt tiruveḷḷakkuḷattuḷ endāy! adiyēn idaraik kaḷaiyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kondu Ar – filled with flower bunches; tuḷavam – tuḷasi’s; malar koṇḍu – stringing flowers as garland; aṇivānē – you who are mercifully adorning (on the divine crown)!; nandāda – imperishable; perum – inconceivable; pugaḻ – having glories; vēdiyar – best of brāhmaṇas, their; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; sendāmarai – having reddish lotus flowers; nīr – surrounded by ponds; tiruveḷḷak kuḷattuḷ – mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam; endāy – Oh my lord!; adiyēn – I, who have no refuge, my; idarai – sorrows (viz. connection with prakruti (this body)); kaḷaiyāy – you should mercifully sever

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are mercifully adorning garland strung with bunches of tuḷasi flowers! Oh my lord who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam which is surrounded by ponds having reddish lotus flowers and which belongs to the best of brāhmaṇas who are having imperishable and inconceivable glories! You should mercifully sever my sorrows, and I have no other refuge.

*kondu Ar …* – You are having a garland on your divine crown, to show that you are the protector. Oh you who are adorning tuḷasi flowers which are growing in bunches due to coming in contact with your divine hair!

*nandāda perum pugaḻ …* – tirunāngūr which belongs to brāhmaṇas who are having glories which don’t have any break or boundary. āḻvār is asking emperumān “Don’t you want to be like the brāhmaṇas who are in that town?”

*sem tāmarai nīr ….* – The water in pond and the lotus flower of the town match the decoration on his divine form and beautiful limbs respectively.

## 4.7.3. Kunral kulir mari

*kunṟāl kuḷir māri taduttu ugandānē! nanṟāya perum pugaḻ vēdiyar nāngūr senṟār vaṇangum tiruveḷḷakkuḷattuḷ ninṟāy! nediyāy! adiyēn idar nīkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kunṟāl – lifting up gōvardana mountain; kuḷir māri – rain which made everyone freeze; taduttu – stopped; ugandānē – oh you who became joyful!; nanṟāya – distinguished; perum pugaḻ – great glories; vēdiyar nāngūr – of brāhmaṇas in tirunāngūr; senṟār – those who go; vaṇangum – vorśipping; tiruveḷḷak kuḷattuḷ – in tiruveḷḷakkuḷam; ninṟāy – oh you who are mercifully residing!; nediyāy – Oh you who are having inconceivable svarūpam, guṇam etc!; adiyēn idar nīkku – you should mercifully eliminate my sorrows

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who became joyful lifting up the gōvardana mountain and stopped the rain which made everyone freeze! Oh you who are mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷakkuḷam where those who go, will worship, in tirunāngūr belonging to brāhmaṇas who have distinguished, great glories! Oh you who are having inconceivable svarūpam, guṇam etc! You should mercifully eliminate my sorrows.

*kunṟāl …* – There is no restriction \[or rule\] in protecting a particular person (or group) with a specific instrument. He held the mountain as the umbrella and saved people from the rain and became joyful thinking “We got to help them!” Please observe the difference between sorrow of the covherds who were caught in that rain and me \[refers to āḻvār who is caught in samsāram. Implies that his sorrow is greater\].

*nanṟāya …* – sarvēśvaran’s greatness is that he is the opposite to all defects and the abode of all auspicious qualities only. The glories of the brāhmaṇas in that town, are similar to that.

*senṟār vaṇangum …* – mahābhāratam sabhā parvam 42.4 “*yatārham kēśavē vruttim avaśā: pratipēdirē*” (Seeing kriṣṇa’s entrance to the assembly, without realising, they got up and offered their respects) \[The essence of this ślōkam is explained here\] duryōdanan, thinking that kriṣṇa has arrived to broke peace, due to his partiality towards pāṇḍavas, decorated himself along with associates and discussed with everyone that no one should get up or offer respects towards kriṣṇa. But in the end, everyone including duryōdanan, got up and offered respects to kriṣṇa without realising it. This \[act of servitors of duryōdanan etc\] is similar to dry leaves gathering and declaring that “We won’t fly” when the wind blows; similarly servitors vowing that they wont be favourable towards the lord; in this manner, you remained in tiruveḷḷakkuḷam.

*nediyāy* – Oh you for whom the boundary of svarūpam and guṇams cannot be seen!

*adiyēn idar nīkkē* – Only when there is sorrow on both sides, could one remain relaxed. (Here) Only, I am suffering.

## 4.7.4. Kanar kari

*kānār kari kombadu ositta kaḷiṟē! nānā vagai nallavar manniya nāngūr  tēnār poḻil sūḻ tiruveḷḷakkuḷattuḷ ānāy! adiyēnukku aruḷ puriyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kān – in the forest; Ar – youthful (and roaming around in the forest); kari – kuvalayāpīdam’s; adu kombu – great, matching tusk; ositta – broke; kaḷiṟē – Oh wild elephant!; nānā vagai – complete in all manner; nallavar – distinguished, noble persons; manniya – residing firmly; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tēn Ar – filled with beetles; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruveḷḷak kuḷattuḷ – mercifully present in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam; ānāy – Oh you who are like a wild elephant!; adiyēnukku – towards me, the servitor; aruḷ puriyāy – kindly shower your mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh wild elephant who broke the great, matching tusk of youthful kuvalayāpīdam which was roaming in the forest! Oh you are like a wild elephant, being mercifully present in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam which is surrounded by gardens filled with beetles in tirunāngūr where distinguished, noble persons who are complete in all manner, are residing firmly! Kindly shower your mercy towards me, the servitor.

*kān Ar kari …* – As said in tiruccanda viruttam 52 “*poṟṟai uṟṟa muṟṟal yānai*” (Elephant which reached the forest and grew there) – the elephant grew without being familiar with humans; oh wild elephant who broke the tusk of such elephant! A wild elephant broke another elephant’s tusk.

*nānā vagai …* – tirunāngūr which is firmly inhabited by those who are having distinguished goodness in birth, conduct, knowledge and valour.

*tēn Ar …* – Oh elephant of tiruveḷḷak kuḷam which is surrounded by gardens which are filled with beetles! āḻvār is calling emperumān as elephant, since he attracts everyone who goes and comes, and since he does not see the faults of those who approach him. Kindly shower your mercy towards me, the servitor.

## 4.7.5. Vedar tiruvengadam

*vēdār tiruvēngadam mēya viḷakkē! nādār pugaḻ vēdiyar manniya nāngūr sēdār poḻil sūḻ tiruveḷḷakkuḷattāy! pādā varuvēn vinai āyina pāṟṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēdu Ar – filled with hunters; tiruvēngadam – on tiruvēngadam mountain; mēya – eternally residing; viḷakkē – you who are self-illuminous!; nādu Ar – spread all over the nation; pugaḻ – having glories; vēdiyar manniya nāngūr – in tirunāngūr which is firmly inhabited by brāhmaṇas; sēdu Ar – filled with sprouts; poḻil sūḻ – surrounded by gardens; tiruveḷḷakkuḷattāy – Oh you who are mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷakkuḷam!; pādā – Singing (about you); varuvēn – I, who am coming; vinai āyina – all the sins; pāṟṟu – you should mercifully drive away (destroy)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are self-illuminous and who are eternally residing on tiruvēngadam mountain which is filled with hunters! Oh you who are mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷakkuḷam which is surrounded by gardens filled with sprouts, in tirunāngūr which is firmly inhabited by brāhmaṇas who are having glories which are spread all over the nation! You should mercifully drive away all the sins of mine; I am coming, singing about you.

*vēdu Ar …* – Oh you who are self-illuminous and who are eternally residing on tiruvēngadam mountain which is filled with divine hunters who have no shortcoming in being caring towards you and valorous, and who consider stepping down from tirumalā will cause shame to their clan! Oh you who are revealing your svarūpam (nature), rūpam (forms) and guṇam (qualities) yourself!

*nādu Ar …* – Just as an ocean cannot be filled into a hoof, there is not enough space to hold the glories of the brāhmaṇas of that town.

*sēdu Ar …* – sēdu – abundance; sprouts.

*pādā varuvēn* – Sins of mine, I who am coming, singing your qualities.

*pāṟṟē* – Make them become pieces so that they cannot be seen as a full entity.

Alternative explanation.

*pādā varuvēn* – I will eagerly come towards you, as you try to catch me by all means.

## 4.7.6. Kallal kadalai

*kallāl kadalai aṇai katti ugandāy! nallār palar vēdiyar manniya nāngūrc celvā! tiruveḷḷakkuḷattu uṟaivānē! ellā idarum kedumāṟu aruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kallāl – with rocks; kadalai – ocean; aṇai katti – built a bridge; ugandāy – oh you who became joyful!; nallār – having the goodness named compassion; palar – many; vēdiyar – brāhmaṇas; manniya nāngūr – tirunāngūr where they remain firmly; tiruveḷḷak kuḷattu – in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam; uṟaivānē – oh you who are eternally residing!; selvā – Oh śrīmān! \[one who has all the wealth\]; ellā idarum – all sins; kedumāṟu – to be destroyed; aruḷāy – you should kindly shower your mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who became joyful building a bridge with rocks on the ocean! Oh you who are eternally residing in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam in tirunāngūr where many brāhmaṇas who are having the goodness named compassion are remaining firmly! Oh śrīmān! You should kindly shower your mercy to have all my sins destroyed.

*kallāl kadalai aṇai katti ugandāy* – Building a bridge on the ocean with rocks which would usually drown in water, you became joyful thinking “We got to help samsāris (materialistic people)”.

*nallār palar vēdiyar manniya nāngūr* – tirunāngūr which is firmly inhabited by brāhmaṇas who are focussed on helping others exclusively and are having compassion.

*selvā …* – You should shower your mercy to have all of avidyā (ignorance), karma (virtues/vices), vāsanā (impressions), ruci (taste), bhagavat apacāram (offenses towards bhagavān) etc, prārābada karma (karma which has started yielding results), destroyed.

## 4.7.7. Kolal nirai

*kōlāl nirai mēytta engōvalar kōvē! nālāgiya vēdiyar manniya nāngūr sēlār vayal sūḻ tiruveḷḷakkuḷattuḷ mālē! ena valvinai tīrttu aruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōlāl – Having a stick as the instrument; nirai mēytta – tended the cows; em – one who made me exist for you; kōvalar kōvē – Oh best among the covherd people!; nāl āgiya – in four categories; vēdiyar – best among brāhmaṇas who have learnt vēdams; manniya nāngūr – firmly inhabited tirunāngūr; sēl Ar – filled with sēl fish; vayal sūḻ – surrounded by fertile fields; tiruveḷḷak kuḷattuḷ – mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam; mālē – Oh great one!; ena valvinai – my cruel sins; tīrttu aruḷāy – you should mercifully eliminate

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh best among the covherd people who tended the cows with a stick as the instrument and made me exist for you \[by that act\]! Oh great one who are mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam which is surrounded by fertile fields which are filled with sēl fish, in tirunāngūr which is firmly inhabited by the best among brāhmaṇas who have learnt vēdams which are in four categories! You should mercifully eliminate my cruel sins.

*kōlāl …* –  You who do creation and annihilation with your sankalpam (divine will), instead of such pride of lordship, took up a stick and engaged in acts which match your clan in which you took birth and have the whole covherd clan give in themselves for you by that act and made me exist for you!

*nālāgiya …* – tirunāngūr which is firmly inhabited by brāhmaṇas who are experts in four vēdams.

*sēl Ar …* – Due to having perennial water flow, sēl fish is filled in the fertile fields. Oh great one who is standing in such tiruveḷḷak kuḷam!

*ena valvinai tīrttu aruḷāyē* – Kindly eliminate my unbearable sins.

## 4.7.8. Varagam adagi

*vārāgam adāgi immaṇṇai idandāy!  nārāyaṇaṇē! nalla vēdiyar nāngūr sīrār poḻil sūḻ tiruveḷḷakkuḷattuḷ ārāvamudē! adiyēṟku aruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

adu – such distinguished; vārāgam āgi – being the one who incarnated as varāha \[wild boar\]; immaṇṇai – this earth; idandāy – (from the wall of the oval shaped universe) oh you, who dug out!; nārāyaṇanē – Oh you who have vātsalyam (motherly love towards all creatures)!; nalla – having good conduct; vēdiyar – brāhmaṇas’; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; sīr Ar – filled with wealth; poḻil sūḻ – surrounded by gardens; tiruveḷḷak kuḷattuḷ – in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam; ārāvamudē – Oh you who are very sweet who never satiates!; adiyēṟku – for me who is a servitor; aruḷāy – kindly shower your mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who incarnated as distinguished varāha and dug out this earth! Oh you who have vātsalyam (motherly love towards all creatures)! Oh you who are very sweet who never satiates and are residing in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam which is surrounded by rich gardens in tirunāngūr which belongs to brāhmaṇas who are having good conduct!  Kindly shower your mercy on me who is your servitor.

*vārāgam …* – As the earth was swallowed by deluge, you dug out the earth as varāha which can dig out even the earth!

*nārāyaṇanē* – Just as a mother would embrace the child while the child does not realise that, oh you who are having motherly love which is not understood by the samsāris (materialistic people)!

*nalla vēdiyar* – tirunāngūr which is inhabited by brāhamaṇas who have good conduct.

*sīr Ar …* – Oh you who are every sweet/enjoyable in tiruveḷḷakkuḷam which is surrounded by gardens which reveal the wealth of the town!

*adiyēṟku aruḷāyē* – Whose possession is suffering in this manner! \[Yours\]

## 4.7.9. Puvar tirumamagal

*pūvār tirumāmagaḷ pulgiya mārbā! nāvār pugaḻ vēdiyar manniya nāngūrt tēvā! tiruveḷḷakkuḷattu uṟaivānē! āvā! adiyān ivan enṟu aruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pū Ar – firmly residing on the lotus flower; tirumāmagaḷ – periya pirāttiyār; pulgiya – embraced; mārbā – oh you who are having divine chest!; nā Ar – filled in the tongue (of the people of the world); pugaḻ – having glory; vēdiyar – brāhmaṇas; manniya – residing firmly; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tiruveḷḷak kuḷattu uṟaivānē – Oh you who are residing in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam!; dēvā – Oh you who are shining due to your simplicity!; ivan – this; adiyān – servitor; A A – Alas! Alas! (He is suffering in this samsāram); enṟu aruḷāy – you should kindly shower your mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are having divine chest which is embraced by periya pirāttiyār who is firmly residing on the lotus flower! Oh you who are residing in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam in tirunāngūr where brāhmaṇas who are glorified fully by the tongues of the people of the world, are residing firmly! Oh you who are shining due to your simplicity! You should kindly shower your mercy saying “Alas! Alas!” on this servitor.

*pūvār …* – Oh you who are having divine chest which is desired and embraced by periya pirāttiyār who was born in the flower but could not handle the heat of the flower \[i.e. emperumān’s divine chest is more tender than flower\]!

*nāvār …* – tirunāngūr which is inhabited by brāhmaṇas who would be glorified all the time thinking “We got the purpose of our tongue fulfilled by glorifying their qualities” unlike in other cases where one glorifies others while in their presence and say “What did we have to do!” in their absence.

*dēvā …* – Oh you who are shining due to descending from paramapadam into this world amidst the samsāris (materialistic people)!

*āvā …* – You should shower your mercy saying “He is living in this samsāram! Alas! Alas!”.

## 4.7.10. Nallanbudai

*nal anbudai vēdiyar manniya nāngūrc celvan tiruveḷḷakkuḷattu uṟaivānai kallin mali tōḷ kaliyan sonna mālai vallar ena vallavar vānavar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nal anbudai – having paramabhakti (supreme state of devotion); vēdiyar – best among brāhmaṇas; manniya – firmly residing; nāngūr – in tirunāngūr; tiruveḷḷak kuḷattu – in the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷak kuḷam; uṟaivān – one who eternally resides; selvanai – towards śrīmān; kallil – more than mountain; mali – great (having strength); tōḷ – having shoulders; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; mālai – these ten pāsurams which are in form of a garland of words; vallar ena – that they can recite; vallavar – those who could be classified (by others); vānavar tāmē – will become part of the assembly of nityasūris

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār who is having shoulders which are greatly stronger than mountain, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams which are in the form of a garland of words, on śrīmān who eternally resides in the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷak kuḷam in tirunāngūr where best among brāhmaṇas who are having paramabhakti are firmly residing. Those who are able to be classified \[by others\] that “they can recite these pāsurams well”, will become part of the assembly of nityasūris.

*nal anbudai …* – The śrīmān of tirunāngūr which is inhabited by brāhmaṇas who are having paramabhakti. The one who is present in tiruveḷḷak kuḷam.

*kallin mali …* – His strength to sing pāsurams is similar to his shoulder strength.

*vallar ena …* – Though they are not experts in these pāsurams, at least if others say that they are experts, they will become part of the assembly of nityasūris.

## 4.8 Kavala yanai

## 4.8.1. Kavala yanai

*kavaḷa yānaik kombositta kaṇṇan enṟum kāmaru sīrk kuvaḷai mēgam anna mēni koṇḍa kōn ennānai enṟum  tavaḷa māda nīdu nāngkait tāmaraiyāḷ kēḷvan enṟum pavaḷa vāyāḷ en madandai pārttanpaḷḷi pāduvāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pavaḷam – beautiful like coral; vāyāḷ – having lips; en madandai – my daughter; kavaḷam – which can eat a lot; yānai – kuvalayāpīdam’s; kombu – tusks; ositta – who broke; kaṇṇan enṟum – saying “kriṣṇa”; kāmaru – desirable; sīr – having beauty; kuvaḷai anna – matching karuneydal \[blue Indian water-lily\] flower; mēgam anna – matching cloud; mēni – form; koṇḍa – accepted; kōn – being the lord; en ānai enṟum – saying “my strong elephant” (one who is having such activities); tavaḷam – whitish; mādam – houses’; nīdu – being tall; nāngai – eternally residing in tirunāngūr; tāmaraiyāḷ kēḷvan – beloved the consort of periya pirāttiyār; enṟum – blabbering in this manner; pārttan paḷḷi – divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi; pāduvāḷ – she sings

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter who is having coral like beautiful lips is blabbering “kriṣṇa broke the tusks of the kuvalayāpīdam which can eat a lot”, “My lord is a strong elephant, who accepted the form matching karuneydal which is having desirable beauty and cloud” and “Beloved consort of periya pirāttiyār, who is eternally residing in tirunāngūr which is having tall, whitish houses” and sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi.

*kavaḷa yānai …* – parakāla nāyaki’s mother is saying “My daughter who is having beautiful limbs which will make bhagavān blabber, has her joy matured; thus, she is blabbering about the town which is dear to him”. Saying “kriṣṇa effortlessly broke the tusk of kuvalayāpīdam which was fully fed, intoxicated and would jump on anyone it sees”.

*kāmaru sīr …* – His beauty is such that he is desirable even if it does not eliminate the hurdles and nurtures them; we cannot leave him. His beauty is desirable for those who have seen him; the lord has accepted such beautiful form which is comparable to karuneydal flower, cloud and so on; he is having activities which are to be seen by me always – my daughter blabbers like this. Since there is no single comparable entity for his beauty, āḻvār is picking several entities to compare with his beauty.

*davaḷa māda …* – The houses in that town are always painted with white colour; śrīman nārāyaṇa who is eternally residing in tirunāngūr which has the whitish, tall mansions.

*pavaḷa vāyāḷ …* – Whatever he blabbers when he sees her coral like lips, she is now blabbering the same saying about his town.

## 4.8.2. Kanjan vitta

*kanjan vitta venjinatta kaḷiṟadartta kāḷai enṟum vanjamēvi vanda pēyin uyirai uṇḍa māyan enṟum senjolāḷar nīdu nāngait tēvadēvan enṟenṟu ōdi panji anna melladiyāḷ pārttanpaḷḷi pāduvāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

panji anna – like cotton; mel – soft; adiyāḷ – this girl, parakāla nāyaki who is having divine feet; kanjan – by kamsa; vitta – sent by; vem – cruel; sinatta – having anger; kaḷiṟu – kuvalayāpīdam; adartta – killed; kāḷai enṟum – as youth; vanjam – with mischief; mēvi – fixed (having such mind); vanda – approached; pēyin – pūtanā’s; uyirai – life; uṇḍa – consumed (finished); māyan enṟum – as the amazing person; sem – beautiful; sol āḷar – brāhmaṇas who have the truthful words; nīdu – eternally inhabited; nāngai – mercifully residing in tirunāngūr; dēva dēvan enṟu – as dēvādi dēvan; enṟu ōdi – repeatedly saying in this manner; pārttan paḷḷi pāduvāḷē – sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

This girl, parakāla nāyaki who is having cotton like divine feet repeatedly says as in “Youth who killed cruelly angry kuvalayāpīdam which was sent by kamsa”, “The amazing person who consumed the life of pūtanā who was sent by pūtanā whose mind is fixed with mischief”, “dēvādi dēvan who is mercifully residing in tirunāngūr where brāhmaṇas who have truthful, beautiful words are eternally residing” and sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi.

kanjan … – The gratitude for his favour of killing kuvalayāpīdam, again engages āḻvār in kriṣṇāvatāram.

*kanjan vitta* – Evil kamsan is the one who sent. kuvalayāpīdam is the which is having such cruel anger which does not need anyone’s instigation, came charging. One cannot escape either way – looking at the nature of the one who sent or looking at the nature of the elephant which does not need any instigation. kriṣṇa was still a child when he killed the very angry kuvalayāpīdam which was instigated by kamsan.

*vanjam …* – Even without the mischief, she is naturally a ghost; on top of that, she came with mischief; my daughter says “the amazing person who killed such pūtanā”. Alternative explanation – one who has amazing qualities and acts to inflict her the fate which she desired to inflict on him.

*sem sol āḷar …* – Everyone in the town would have truthful words. He should also have the same nature as the residents of the town; after vowing “I won’t leave you”, he cannot leave her in their watch; this is the hold for her. Saying “The lord of nityasūris who is in tirunāngūr where the brāhmaṇas with truthful words are residing”.

*panji anna …* – While he should speak incoherently looking at the tender nature of her feet, she is repeatedly reciting the name of the town where he is residing.

## 4.8.3. Andar kon

*aṇḍar kōn ennānai enṟum āyar mādar kongai pulgu seṇḍan enṟum nānmaṟaigaḷ tēdi ōdum selvan enṟum vaṇḍulavu poḻil koḷ nāngai mannum āyan enṟenṟu ōdi paṇḍu pōlanṟu en madandai pārttanpaḷḷi pāduvāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en madandai – my daughter; aṇḍar kōn – being the controller of the residents of the universe; en ānai enṟum – as one who is having acts of an enjoyable elephant for me; āyar mādar – covherd girls’; kongai – with bosoms; pulgum – embracing; seṇḍan enṟum – as one who is having flower bouquet; nān maṟaigaḷ – four vēdams; tēdi – analysed; ōdum – and chasing; selvan enṟum – as one who is having wealth; vaṇḍu ulavu – beetles are roaming; poḻil koḷ – having gardens; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; mannu – eternally residing; māyan enṟu – as amazing person; enṟu ōdi – saying repeatedly; paṇḍu pōl anṟu – unlike previously; pārttan paḷḷi pāduvāḷē – sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi

**Перевод:**

**parakāla nāyaki’s mother is saying “parakāla nāyaki is not speaking about his form/nature for time pass; she is appearing to go towards him if he does not come to her”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter is saying repeatedly as in ” the controller of the residents of the universe who is having acts of an enjoyable elephant for me”, “one who is having flower bouquet who is embracing the bosoms of the covherd girls”, “wealthy one whom the four vēdams analysed and are chasing” and “the amazing person who is eternally residing in tirunāngūr which is having gardens where the beetles are roaming”. Unlike previously, she sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi.

*aṇḍar kōn en ānai enṟum* – Saying “Being the controller of all the residents of the universe, one who has acts which are always enjoyable to me”.

*āyar …* – Saying “Manifesting his toy (flower bouquet), he attracted the covherd girls who are of his age and having the nature of being together with them always”.

*nānmaṟai …* – One, who is subservient to the covherd girls in this manner, is having control/wealth which is beyond the reach of vēdams.

*vaṇḍu ulavu …* – Saying “In tirunāngūr which is having gardens where beetles are roaming, unlike avatārams (vibhava avatārams) where he leaves after the purpose is fulfilled, the amazing one is eternally residing here”.

*paṇḍu pōl anṟu en madandai* – Won’t everyone sing about different towns, when one is young? What is special in her? Unlike them, she is singing due to a particular connection with that town (which is the abode of her lord).

## 4.8.4. Kollai anal

*kollai ānāḷ parisaḻindāḷ kōl vaḷaiyār tam mugappē mallai munnīr tattilangai kattaḻitta māyan enṟum selvam malgu maṟaiyōr nāngai dēvadēvan enṟenṟu ōdi palvaḷaiyāḷ en madandai pārttanpaḷḷi pāduvāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pal vaḷaiyāḷ – having many bangles; en madandai – my daughter; kōl – beautiful; vaḷaiyār tam – girls who are wearing bangles; mugappē – in front of; kollai ānāḷ – crossed the limit (she went out alone); parisu aḻindāḷ – she became devoid of shyness etc, which are important identities of a woman; mallai – abundant; mun – ancient; nīr – ocean having water; tattu – built a bridge; ilangai – lankā; kattu aḻitta – made it lose its structure; māyan enṟum – as the amazing person; selvam – wealth; malgum – present in abundance; maṟaiyōr – best of the brāhmaṇas’; nāngai – mercifully residing in tirunāngūr; dēva dēvan enṟu – as dēvādi dēvan; enṟu ōdi – repeatedly saying in this manner; pārttan paḷḷi pāduvāḷē – sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter, having many bangles, went out alone in front of the girls who are wearing beautiful bangles, crossed the limit and became devoid of shyness etc which are important identities of a woman; she is repeatedly saying “the amazing person who built a bridge on the ocean which is having abundant, ancient water, made lankā lose its structure”, “dēvādi dēvan who is mercifully residing in tirunāngūr which belongs to the best of brāhmaṇas who are having abundant wealth” and sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi.

*kollai ānāḷ* – She acted in a way which crosses the limits.

*parisu aḻindāḷ* – She has natural femininity; she destroyed her limits of femininity in front of other young girls who are of her age.

*mallai mun nīr tattu* – Saying “Blocked the ocean which is having abundant, ancient water, and made many persons share one person’s clothes in lankā \[this implies that emperumān destroyed the richness of lankā\]; such greatly loving emperumān”.

*selvam malgu …* – Saying “In tirunāngūr which belongs to brāhmaṇas who are having overflowing wealth”.

*pal vaḷaiyāḷ* … He will go through lot of torment on seeing a single bangle in her hand \[desiring it\]; but she is wearing many such bangles and incoherently speaking about his divyadēśam.

## 4.8.5. Arakkar avi

*arakkar āvi māḷa anṟu āḻkadal sūḻ ilangai seṟṟa kurakkarasan enṟum kōlavilli enṟum māmadiyainerukku māda nīdu nāngai ninmalan enṟenṟu ōdi parakkaḻindāḷ en madandai pārttanpaḷḷi pāduvāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en madandai – my daughter; anṟu – when rāvaṇa came to fight; arakkar – demons’; āvi – lives; māḷa – to be destroyed; āḻ – deep; kadal – by ocean; sūḻ – surrounded; ilangai – lankā; seṟṟa – destroyed; kurakku – for monkeys; arasan enṟum – as the lord; kōlam – beautiful; villi enṟum – as the one who holds the bow; māmadiyai – beautiful moon; nerukkum – blocking the movement; mādam – by the mansions; nīdu – being tall; nāngai – mercifully present in tirunāngūr; ninmalan enṟu – very pure natured one, as he does not have any expectation; enṟu ōdi – repeatedly saying in this manner; parakku aḻindāḷ – having lost her femininity; pārttan paḷḷi pāduvāḷē – sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter is repeatedly saying “Lord of monkeys who destroyed the lives of the demons when rāvaṇa came to fight and destroyed lankā which is surrounded by the deep ocean”, “the one who holds the beautiful bow”, “very pure natured one as he does not have any expectation, who is mercifully present in tirunāngūr which is tall due to the mansions which are blocking the movement of the beautiful moon”; having lost her femininity, she sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi.

*arakkar …* – Instead of destroying the evil one who separated pirātti from him, he destroyed the whole clan.

*anṟu* – When he came fighting, he, the one who is the lord of the monkey clan, destroyed lankā which is surrounded by the ocean which has depth. He destroyed the abode of rāvaṇa who destroyed the abodes of brahmā et al, with the help of monkeys which don’t know the difference between left and right hands.

*kōla villi enṟum* – Having the beautiful bow in his hand such that those who are prideful about their valour become defeated and respect him.

*māmadiyai …* – emperumān who is eternally residing in tirunāngūr where the mansions are having height to stop the roaming moon. Saying that he is of the nature to help without any expectation. Instead of presenting himself being pleased with their upāsanam, he is appearing without any prayer from their side.

*parakku aḻindāḷ* – My bad!  She has become fearless about losing her shame.

When asked “How did we know about that?”

*pārttan paḷḷi pāduvāḷē* – She is singing the name of the town where he resides, to make me hear it. If she can do that, what else she will do? As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 58.35 “*adruśta pūrva vyasanā mruduśeelā manasvinī \| tēna du:khēna rudatī naivamākincit abhravīt \|\|*” (sītāp pirātti who is tender, grave and in great sorrow which was never seen by her previously, was crying due to that sorrow and could not speak to me) – she is of the nature to absorb his beautiful form with her eyes, will hang her head down and shed tears.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.8.6. Jnalamurrum

*jñālamuṟṟum uṇḍumiḻnda nādan enṟum nānilam sūḻ vēlai anna kōla mēni vaṇṇan enṟum mēl eḻundu sēl ugaḷum vayal koḷ nāngait tēvadēvan enṟenṟu ōdi pālin nalla menmoḻiyāḷ pārttanpaḷḷi pāduvāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pālil – more than milk; nalla – being sweet; mel – soft; moḻiyāḷ – this girl, who is having speech; jñālam muṟṟum – whole earth; uṇḍu – mercifully consumed (during deluge); umiḻnda – let out (during creation); nādan enṟum – saying one who is the lord; nāl nilam – earth which is made of four types of lands; sūḻ – surrounding; vēlai anna – matching the ocean; kōlam – beautiful; mēni – having complexion; vaṇṇan enṟum – saying one who is having form; sēl – sēl fish; mēl eḻundu – rising up; ugaḷum – jumping; vayal koḷ – having fertile fields; nāngai – mercifully residing in tirunāngūr; dēva dēvan enṟu – as dēvādi dēvan; enṟu ōdi – repeatedly saying in this manner; pārttan paḷḷi pāduvāḷē – sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

This girl who is having soft speech which is sweeter than milk is repeatedly saying “the lord who mercifully consumed the whole earth during deluge and who let it out during creation”, “the lord who is having form which is having beautiful complexion matching that of the ocean which is surrounding the earth which is made of four types of lands”, “dēvādi dēvan who is mercifully residing in tirunāngūr which is having fertile fields where sēl fish are rising up and jumping” and sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi.

*jñālam …* – To be protected by emperumān, one has to be in danger only, one need not perform any sādanānuśtānam (pursuit of means); he is the lord who gives all kinds of protection – she says. When one is not having anything other than danger, the reason for his protection is the fact that he is the natural lord; the owner will naturally seek and protect his possession.

*nāl nilam …* – The ocean which is surrounding the earth which is having four types of lands as in neydal (ocean and areas on the shore), marudam (fertile lands and areas around that), mullai (forest and areas around that), kuṟinji (mountain and areas around that); having its form, one who is having beautiful complexion.

*mēl eḻundu …* – The sēl fish which are present there would remain without touching the water and will be jumping around. This is the abode where even the aquatic creatures would live joyfully.

*pāl …* – Sweeter than milk; as sweet as milk. She, who should have him blabber about her being won over by her sweet speech, is incoherently reciting the name of his abode. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.15 “*madurā madurālāpā*” (sītāp pirātti who is sweet and has sweet speech), he would listen to her speech and incoherently speak about it.

## 4.8.7. Nadi endan

*nādi endan uḷḷam koṇḍa nādan enṟum nānmaṟaigaḷ tēdi enṟum kāṇa māttāc celvan enṟum siṟai koḷ vaṇḍu sēdulavu poḻil koḷ nāngait tēvadēvan enṟenṟu ōdi pādagam sēr melladiyāḷ pārttanpaḷḷi pāduvāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pādagam – the ornament decorating the foot; sēr – fitting well; mel – tender; adiyāḷ – my daughter having divine feet; nādi – seeking; enṟan uḷḷam – my mind; koṇḍa – mesmerised; nādan enṟum – as “the lord”; nānmaṟaigaḷ – vēdams which are categorized into four; enṟum – always; tēdi – analysed; kāṇa māttā – to be unable to see; selvan enṟum – as “śrīmān”; siṟai koḷ – having nice wings; vaṇḍu – beetles; sēdu – swarm; ulavu – roaming; poḻil koḷ – having gardens; nāngai – mercifully residing in tirunāngūr; dēva dēvan enṟu – as dēvādi dēvan; enṟu ōdi – repeatedly saying in this manner; pārttan paḷḷi pāduvāḷē – sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter who is having divine, tender feet which are having well fitting ornament decorating the feet, repeatedly says as in “the lord who came seeking me and mesmerised my mind”, “śrīmān who is unable to be seen always by vēdams which are categorized into four, even after being analysed by the vēdams”, “dēvādi dēvan who is mercifully residing in tirunāngūr which is having gardens where swarms of beetles with nice wings are roaming” and sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi.

*nādi …* – My lord who captivated my heart and made it his, after seeking me in various ways.

*nānmaṟai …* – One who seeks me with great effort and made me his, is having the wealth of being unable to be seen by vēdams even after they seek him.

*siṟai koḷ …* – Saying “dēvādi dēvan who is residing in tirunāngūr where the winged beetles are roaming around in the garden”.

*pādagam …* – She who should be glorified for her fitting feet and pādagam (the ornament), is now singing about his town.

## 4.8.8. Ulagam ettum

*ulagam ēttum oruvan enṟum oṇsudarōdu umbar eydā nilavum āḻip padaiyan enṟum nēsan enṟum tendisaikkut tiladam anna maṟaiyōr nāngait tēvadēvan enṟenṟu ōdip palarum ēsa en madandai pārttanpaḷḷi pāduvāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en madandai – my daughter; ulagam – the whole world; ēttum – qualified to be praised; oruvan enṟum – as “the distinguished one”; oḷ – beautiful; sudarōdu – with moon and sun; umbar – by dēvatās; eydā – unable to be approached; nilavum – shining; āḻi – tiruvāḻi (sudarśana chakra); padaiyan enṟum – as “the one who has divine weapon”; nēsan enṟum – as “the one who has love towards his devotees”; then tisaikku – for southern direction; tiladam anna maṟaiyōr – brāhmaṇas who are like tilakam (chief, like the symbol on the forehead), their; nāngai – mercifully residing in tirunāngūr; dēva dēvan enṟu – as dēvādi dēvan; enṟu ōdi – repeatedly saying in this manner; palarum – everyone; ēsa – to accuse her; pārttan paḷḷi pāduvāḷē – sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter is repeatedly saying “the distinguished one who is qualified to be praised by the whole world”, “the one who has divine weapon, tiruvāḻi, which cannot be approached by dēvatās including the beautiful moon and sun”, “the one who has love towards his devotees”, “dēvādi dēvan who is mercifully residing in tirunāngūr which belongs to brāhmaṇas who are like tilakam (chief, like the symbol on the forehead) for the southern direction” and sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi, to be accused by everyone.

*ulagam …* – He is the refuge for all and is distinguished to be surrendered to by the whole world.

*oṇ sudar …* – tiruvāḻi which cannot be approached by dēvatās including moon and sun, is held by him all the time as said in [periya tiruvandādi 87](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/periya-thiruvandhadhi-87/) “*eppōdum kai kaḻalā nēmiyān*” (one who always has the chakra in his hand).

*nēsan enṟum …* – One who is fully loving towards his devotees.

*then tisai …* – dēvādi dēvan who is mercifully standing in tirunāngūr where brāhamaṇas who are the chief of south direction are residing.

*palarum ēsa …* – While many are accusing her, she considers them as her companions and sings about his town.

## 4.8.9. Kannan enrum

*kaṇṇan enṟum vānavargaḷ kādalittu malargaḷ tūvum eṇṇan enṟum inban enṟum ēḻulagukku ādi enṟum tiṇṇa māda nīdu nāngait tēvadēvan enṟenṟu ōdi paṇṇin anna menmoḻiyāḷ pārttanpaḷḷi pāduvāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇ anna – like a song; mel – soft; moḻiyāḷ – this girl who is having speech; kaṇṇan enṟum – as “kriṣṇa”; vānavargaḷ – dēvatās; kādalittu – having love; malargaḷ – flowers; tūvum – to sprinkle; eṇṇan enṟum – as “the one who resides in their thoughts”; inban enṟum – one who gives joy; ēḻ ulagukku – for all the seven worlds; ādi enṟum – as “the cause”; tiṇṇam – firm; mādam – having mansions; nīdu nāngai – mercifully residing in tirunāngūr; dēva dēvan enṟu – as dēvādi dēvan; enṟu ōdi – repeatedly saying in this manner; pārttan paḷḷi pāduvāḷē – sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

This girl who is having soft song like speech is repeatedly saying “kriṣṇa”, “the one who resides in the thoughts of dēvatās to be loved by them and to be sprinkled upon with flowers by them”, “one who gives joy”, “the cause for all the seven worlds” and “dēvādi dēvan who is mercifully residing in tirunāngūr which is having firm mansions” and sings about the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi.

*kaṇṇan …* – She is saying “kriṣṇa”, “One who is remaining in the thoughts of brahmā et al to have them show love towards him and surrender unto him offering flowers etc”.

*inban enṟum* – One who gives joy.

*ēḻ ulagukku ādi enṟum* – One who is the cause of the universe.

*tiṇṇam …* – Repeatedly saying – dēvādi dēvan who is residing in tirunāngūr where firm mansions are present.

## 4.8.10. Parul nalla

*pāruḷ nalla maṟaiyōr nāngaip pārttanpaḷḷic cengaṇ mālai vārkoḷ nalla mulai madavāḷ pādalai tāy moḻinda māṟṟam  kūrkoḷ nalla vēl kaliyan kūṟu tamiḻ pattum vallār ērkoḷ nalla vaigundattuḷ inbam nāḷum eyduvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pāruḷ – on earth; nalla – distinguished; maṟaiyōr – best among brāhmaṇas are residing; nāngai – in tirunāngūr; pārttan paḷḷi – one who is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi; sem kaṇ – having reddish eyes (due to motherly love); mālai – on sarvēśvaran who is having great love towards his devotees; vār koḷ – being covered by a cloth; nalla – distinguished; mulai – having bosoms; madavāḷ – the girl (sang); pādalai – divine words; tāy – her mother; moḻinda – spoke; māṟṟam – the way; kūr koḷ – sharp; nalla – best; vēl – having spear as the weapon; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; kūṟum – mercifully explained; tamiḻ – in tamiḻ; pattum – these ten pāsurams; vallār – those who can recite; ēr koḷ – beautiful; vaigundattu – in śrīvaikuṇṭam; nāḷum – everyday; inbam eyduvār – will be joyful

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, who is having having reddish eyes and great love towards his devotees, is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named pārttan paḷḷi in tirunāngūr where the best among the distinguished brāhmaṇas of the earth are residing; tirumangai āḻvār who is having the best, sharp spear as the weapon, mercifully explained the way the mother of parakāla nāyaki, who is wearing a cloth on her distinguished bosoms, spoke her divine words, in these ten pāsurams in tamiḻ; those who can recite these pāsurams will get to be joyful everyday in beautiful śrīvaikuṇṭam.

*pāruḷ nalla …* – On emperumān who is having vātsalyam (motherly affection) and vyāmōham (love) and is residing in pārttan paḷḷi in tirunāngūr where the noble, distinguished brāhmaṇas of earth are gathered.

*vār koḷ nalla …* – The way the mother spoke the words of the aptly youthful daughter.

*kūr koḷ …* – Those who are experts in these ten pāsurams of āḻvār spoken in the mood of that pirātti.

*ēr koḷ …* – To eliminate the lowliness of the sorrowful words of one girl to be spoken by her mother, they will get to remain in the abode where there is no separation.

## 4.9 Nummait toludom

## 4.9.1. Nummait toludom

*nummait toḻudōm nundam paṇi seydirukkum nummadiyōm immaikku inbam peṟṟōm endāy! indaḷūrīrē! emmaik kadidāk karumam aruḷi āvā! enṟirangi nammai orugāl kātti nadandāl nāngaḷ uyyōmē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

nummai – Your highness; toḻudōm – surrendered, considering to be the means; nundam – your highness’; paṇi – kainkaryam (service); seydu – performed; irukkum – to sustain; num adiyōm – became servitors; immaikku – now; inbam peṟṟōm – got the joy of acquiring knowledge; indaḷūṟīr – one who is mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr; en tāy – you who are like my mother!; emmai – for me; kadidā – quickly; karumam – kainkaryam which is the ultimate goal; aruḷi – mercifully grant; A A enṟu – saying “Alas! Alas!”; irangi – being merciful; nammai – for us; oru kāl – some time; kātti – showing your divine form; nadandāl – if you mercifully come; nāngaḷ – we who are ananya prayōjanar (who don’t seek anything other than kainkaryam); uyyōmō – will we not live well?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

We surrendered to your highness considering you to be our means; we became your servitors and performed kainkaryam to sustain ourselves; now, we got the joy of acquiring knowledge; oh you who are like my mother who is mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr! Mercifully grant me kainkaryam which is the ultimate goal, quickly; will we who are ananya prayōjanar not live well if you mercifully come and show your divine form some time, being merciful to us and saying “Alas! Alas!”

*nummait toḻudōm* – Should we remain patient due to vorśipping you through other dēvatās where you remain their antaryāmi? [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.21](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-21/) “*yō yō yām yām tanum bhakta: śraddayārcitum iccati \| tasya tasyācalām śraddām tām Eva vidadāmyaham \|\|”* (Whichever devotee of the dēvatāntarams (other dēvatās) who desires to worship faithfully whichever dēvatā who is \[my\] śarīra (body), I bestow unśakeable faith to such devotee towards that dēvatā only). When one surrenders to dēvatās thinking “dēvatās such as indra et al, are bhagavān’s body. He is their antaryāmi”, since the result will be appropriate to their abilities, there will be delay in the attainment of the goal.

Alternatively,

*nummait toḻudōm* – We have been destroyed. That is – we did not get to surrender unto someone where if we separate from that person, we can survive playing chess or gambling.

*toḻudōm* – Previously we thought that there were two kings (self and bhagavān). Only for those who accept that performing kainkaryam is the goal, it will be possible to be subservient.

*nundam paṇi seydu irukkum num adiyōm* – We can sustain ourselves if we can manage without performing kainkaryam or if we don’t have the scope to perform kainkaryam. We are exclusively surrendered unto your highness where we will live if we get to perform kainkaryam at your highness’ divine feet, else we will die. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 53.31 “*na ca sītā tvayā hīnā na cāham api rāghava \| muhūrtam api jīvāva: jalān matsyā vivōdrutau \|\|”*  is elaborated here.

- *na ca sītā …* – When separated from your highness, sītāp pirātti will not exist; I will also not exist. When separated from your highness, there is no question of survival.
- *api jīvāva:* – yati jīvāva: (If we survive)
- *muhūrtam* – A moment.
- *jalān matsyāviva* – When a fish separates from water, it will survive only as long as it has some water left on it; similarly, we will survive only until we find out that your word “Don’t come with me” is coming from your divine heart. His (lakśmaṇa’s) sattā – truth, is similar to moon, southerly breeze, sandalwood and water which exist for others; one’s true nature is attained by bringing greatness to śēśi (lord).

*adiyōm* – One’s scope is to have the true nature of the self bringing greatness to bhagavān.

*immaikku inbam peṟṟōm* – For us who consider servitude is the true benefit matching our true nature, your highness nicely gave us water when we were thirsty \[i.e you gave us something to survive here\]. Alternatively – āḻvār is speaking about the sustenance by acquiring knowledge. While āḻvār is speaking about not attaining bhagavān, is this satisfaction apt? It is this knowledge which makes him feel anguished. If it was not there, one can live joyfully in this world like others.

*en tāy …* – Oh you who descended from śrīvaikuṇṭam and are mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr to grant such knowledge! Oh you who announced this principle of “This ātmā is your servitor”!  Why did you who are staying relaxed today previously did mischief and grant the knowledge about our mutual relationship!

emperumān asks “You said we granted you this knowledge about our mutual relationship; if this is what you got, what have you not received?” āḻvār responds,

*emmaik kadidāk karumam aruḷi* – You mercifully granted knowledge about servitude;  you should also mercifully accept service matching my servitude.

*emmai* – Is my state such that “We will take you to paramapadam in time and engage you in kainkaryam there”? My state is similar to that of śri vibhīśaṇāḻvān who could not remain comfortably in rāvaṇa’s abode and could not enter śrī rāma’s assembly as well, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.17 “*kśipram nivēdayata mām*” (Inform about my arrival quickly to śrī rāma); I too am suffering being unable to remain comfortably in this samsāra due to acquiring knowledge and unable to engage in kainkaryam which is the result of reaching paramapadam.

*kadidāk karumam aruḷi* – āḻvār’s saukumāryam (tenderness) is such that his inability to remain patient to get the result in time has to be announced to emperumān who is omniscient.

While mercifully granting such kainkaryam …

*A A enṟu irangi* – Thinking about my pitiable state as in “One who is not having anything in his side and who has no other refuge and is withered due to not getting to do kainkaryam”, he should give his mercy thinking “Alas! Alas!” We cannot force him saying “We surrendered”; while getting our desired result, it should occur only by his mercy.

*nammai* – It is not that you have not seen you in a mirror and known about you; should you not remain thinking “Those who have separated from us, will not survive”?

*orugāl kātti nadandāl* – Don’t think that if I show myself, he is forcing me to do so; this is like one who is affected by fever saying “I just need to sip water once”.

*kātti* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 1.13 “*ēśa sarvasva bhūtastu*” (This embrace of mine is equivalent to everything else), showing your form saying “See how I look”.

*nadandāl* – It is not merely coming. But if you place a few steps in front of me. He should give the feast that was given to pirātti as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 11.1 “*agrata: prayayau rāma:*” (śrī rāma walks first), to āḻvār.

When asked “What do you get if I walk like that?” āḻvār says,

*nāngaḷ uyyōmē* – We will get back our lost lives. Does it need to be said that when a big rain falls on withered crop, the crop will come back to life?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.2. Sindai tannul

*sindai tannuḷ nīngādirunda tiruvē! maruviniya maindā! andaṇāli mālē! sōlai maḻakaḷiṟē! nandā viḷakkin sudarē! naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambī! en endāy! indaḷūrāy! adiyēṟku iṟaiyum irangāyē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

sindai tannuḷ – in the heart; nīngādu – without separating; irunda – residing; tiruvē – Oh wealth!; maruva iniya – one who is enjoyable as we experience him repeatedly; maindā – Oh youthful one!; am – beautiful; taṇ – cool; Ali – mercifully present in tiruvāli; mālē – Oh you who are very loving towards your devotees!; sōlai – roaming in the garden; maḻa kaḷiṟē – Oh you who are like an elephant calf!; nandā – always burning; viḷakkin – lamp’s; sudarē – Oh you who are radiant like the light!; naṟaiyūr – in tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – mercifully residing; nambī – Oh you who are complete!; indaḷūrāy – being mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr; en endāy – Oh my lord!; adiyēṟku – for me, the servitor; iṟaiyum – this small favour (kainkaryam); irangāy – you are not granting

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are the wealth residing in my heart without separating! Oh youthful one who are enjoyable as we experience you repeatedly! Oh you who are very loving towards your devotees mercifully present in beautiful, cool tiruvāli! Oh you who are like an elephant calf roaming in the garden! Oh you who are radiant like the light of a lamp which is always burning! Oh my lord who are complete and are mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr! You are not granting this small favour for me, the servitor.

*sindai tannuḷ nīngādu irunda tiruvē* – Only if I have put in any effort for your continuous, shining presence in my heart, could I put in efforts for carrying out kainkaryam to you. He is always shining in my heart continuously.

*tiruvē* – āḻvār’s wealth is emperumān only. He is known as in periya tirumoḻi 7.7.1 “tiruvukkum tiru”.

*maruviniya* – His presence is very sweet for āḻvār. As one engages in him, instead of having to take breaks, he is greatly enjoyable.

*maindā* … – Oh you who are having eternal youthfulness! Oh you who revealed your love by eternally residing in the beautiful, cool tiruvāli.

*sōlai …* – All his acts are enjoyable like those of a young elephant calf which grew in a garden.

*nandā viḷākku …* – While continuously burning in a lamp, there is no smoke and dirt, you who are having true nature which is in the form of radiance!

*naṟaiyūr …* – Oh you who came and resided in tirunaṟaiyūr and are complete to not have to think “There is something missing in the one who is our refuge”!

*en endāy indaḷūrāy* – Oh you who arrived in tiruvindaḷūr and created the knowledge about our relationship in me!

*adiyēṟku …* – Is it too difficult for you, who gave knowledge about our relationship, to also accept kainkaryam which matches my true nature?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.3. Pesuginradu

*pēsuginṟadu iduvē vaiyam īradiyāl aḷanda mūsi vaṇḍu muralum kaṇṇi mudiyīr! ummaik kāṇum āsai ennum kadalil vīḻndu ingu ayarttōm ayalārum ēsuginṟadu iduvē kāṇum indaḷūrīrē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

indaḷūrīrē – Oh you who are mercifully residing in tiruvindaḷūr!; vaiyam – earth; īradiyāl – with two steps; aḷanda – one who scaled; vaṇḍu – beetles; mūsi – swarmed; muralum – humming; kaṇṇi – garland; mudiyīr – Oh you who are wearing on your divine crown!; ingu – in this world; kāṇum – to see; āsai ennum – that which is known as desire; kadalil – in the ocean; vīḻndu – fell; ayarttōm – became bewildered; ayalārum – neighbours; iduvē – on this matter; ēsuginṟadu – blaming; nān – I am too; iduvē – this matter only; pēsuginṟadu – speaking

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh you who are mercifully residing in tiruvindaḷūr! Oh you who scaled the earth with two steps and are wearing garland on your divine crown which is swarmed by humming beetles! In this world, we became bewildered due to falling in the ocean of desire to see you. ṇeighbours are blaming on this matter and I am speaking as well about this matter only.

*pēsuginṟadu iduvē* – We are talking only about eliminating the blame which will occur to you.

*vaiyam* – You know the difficulty you faced in acquiring good qualities; by delaying slightly in the case of an individual (that is me), you are going to lose all those great qualities. Will it not cause a bad name for you who protected everyone without any restriction previously, if you don’t protect a person (that is me)? Measured the entire earth with two steps. mūsugai – swarming. Oh you who are wearing garland on your divine crown which is swarmed by beetles which are humming after drinking honey! It is popularly known that your form is for the sake of others; did you not crown yourself, having protected all!

emperumān asks “All of those are facts; what is happening to those aspects?” āḻvār says “Of course! It is causing damage to such reputation only”

*ummai* – If some people, who desired to see you, died since they were unable to see you, is there any more blame for you than that? We became bewildered due to falling in the ocean of desire to see you.

emperumān asks “Does that cause any blame for me?” āḻvār says

*ayalār …* – Those neighbours blame you saying “She desired nicely; he nicely showed himself to those who desired for him; this is what happens when someone desires for him”. This is what the neighbours are saying and I am also speaking about this only.

*indaḷūrīrē* – Did you not come and eternally stay in tiruvindaḷūr to eliminate the accusations of those who don’t desire for you and to let those who desire for you, enjoy as per their desire?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.4. Asai valuvadu

*āsai vaḻuvādēttum emakkingu iḻukkāyttu adiyōrkkut tēsamaṟiya umakkē āḷāyt tiriginṟōmukku kāsinoḷiyil tigaḻum vaṇṇam kāttīr emperumān! vāsi valleer! indaḷūrīr! vāḻndē pōm nīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ingu – in this, your matter; āsai – desire to worship you; vaḻuvādu – without a break; ēttum – having the nature to praise you; adiyōrkku – your servitors; emakku – for us; iḻukkāyttu – (praising) ended up causing blame; tēsam – all over the place; aṟiya – to be known; umakkē – for you, the lord; āḷāy – as servitors; tiriginṟōmukku – for us, who are roaming around; kāsin – (molten) golden coins’; oḷiyil – more than the shine; tigaḻum – shining; vaṇṇam – beauty; kāttīr – not showing; emperumān – being our lord; indaḷūrīr – oh you who are mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr!; vāsi valleerē – you who understand the difference of various aspects; nīrē – you; vāḻndu pōm – remain joyful

**Перевод:**

**emperumān says “You are worrying thinking this \[not showing myself to you\] will cause blame to me; But I will tolerate that”. āḻvār says “There is something which cannot be tolerated by you and is also a blame for us”. It is said in jitantē stōtram “na tē rūpa:” (Your form is not for yourself but your devotees).**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

We, your servitors who are having the desire to worship you without a break and having the nature to praise you, ended up causing blame; for us who are roaming around as servitors for you, the lord, to be known all over the world, you are not showing your beauty which is having more shine than the shining molten golden coins; oh you who are mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr as our lord! You who can understand the difference of various aspects, remain joyful.

*āsai …* – As said in “*ahanyahani vardatē*” (Everyday hari’s names are growing) as time goes by, my desire overflows and became a blame for us who are having the great sin of having the nature to praise you always.

*adiyōrkku* – Instead of having to think “īsn’t it apt for the servitor to eagerly praise his lord?” it ended up being a blame.

*emakku* – You can remain relaxed for the blame you may acquire, but how can you remain like that in our case?

*tēsam …* – We, the unfortunate ones do not realise what is coming. Had we known about this, we could have kept our affection private. For us, who are roaming around as your servitor, to be known all over the world. Are you remaining relaxed thinking “There is another protector who can be visited and who will fulfil the shortcomings caused by me”.

*kāsin …* – For us who exclusively exist for you, you are not showing your divine form which is more shining than the molten gold’s lustre as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-2-katturaikkil/) “*sutturaitta nan pon un tirumēni oḷi ovvādu*” (the best molten gold that is prepared does not compare to the collective radiance of your divine (spiritual) body/form).

*emperumān vāsi valleer* – You are able to directly see the greatness of your divine form and inferiority of us who desired for it.

*indaḷūrīr* – You have descended to and are standing in tiruvindaḷūr to manifest the same divine form which is shown to nityasūris, to samsāris here. You are distinguishing between different people where you have come to not see such differences.

*vāḻndē pōm nīrē* – We thought your divine form is for those who desire for you. If that is not the case, you enjoy it alone and live happily.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.5. Ti emperuman

*tī emperumān nīr emperumān tisaiyum iru nilanum āy emperumānāgi ninṟāl adiyōm kāṇōmāl tāy emperumān tandai tandai āvīr adiyōmuk kē emperumān allīrō? nīr indaḷūrīrē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tī – being antaryāmi of agni (fire); emperumān – being its controller; nīr – being antaryāmi of jalam (water); emperumān – being its controller; tisaiyum – directions; iru – vast; nilanum – for earth; āy – being antaryāmi; emperumān āgi – being their controller; ninṟāl – though you mercifully remain; adiyōm – we, the servitors; kāṇōmāl – (what is the use) if (we are) unable to see you and worship you; tāy – being mother; emperumān – being the lord; tandai tandai āvīr – being father of father (as the lord of our clan); indaḷūrīr – mercifully residing in tiruvindaḷūr; nīr – your highness; adiyōmukku – engaging us who are without refuge in kainkaryam; emperumān alleerō – are you not the lord?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Though you mercifully remain the antaryāmi (in-dwelling soul) and controller of fire, water, directions and vast earth, what is the use if we, your servitors, are unable to see you and worship you? Are your highness not the lord, who are engaging us, who are without refuge in kainkaryam, by being the mother, lord and father of father for us, mercifully residing in tiruvindaḷūr?

*tī emperumān nīr emperumān* – These two (fire and water) are sample for panca bhūtams (five great elements); with this, all the causal entities are thought of and his being the cause is explained.

*tisaiyum iru nilanumāy* – With this, effectual entities are thought of.

In this manner, if you try to manifest your lordship by being the cause and effect,

*adiyōm kāṇōmāl* – What will we, who are your servitors who desire to interact with you, will do?

*tāy emperumān* – \[As you are the mother\] If your highness abandon us, do we have any other refuge?

*tandai tandai āvīr* – Is this limited to me? \[No, you are the lord for our clan\]

*adiyōm …* – Have your highness not arrived in tiruvindaḷūr for the sake us, who are without refuge, so that whenever we get the taste, we can enjoy as we desire? Are your highness not standing here seeing the apt time to engage us in kainkaryam, as someone would wait for the exact time when the flower blossoms and pluck it? Your paratvam (supreme state) is enjoyable for nityasūris; vyūham is to hear the sorrowful cries of brahmā et al; avatārams such as śrī rāma, kriṣṇa et al are based on the fortune of daśarata, vasudēva et al; divyadēśams are exclusively for samsāris (materialistic people) who don’t know what is good for them and that samsāram should be abandoned. For a charity home meant for blind people, can someone with good vision enter? It is said in tirunedundāṇḍagam 10 “*pinnānār vaṇangum sōdi*” (The radiant form which is to be vorśipped by those who are of later times).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.6. Solladu oliyagillen

*sollādu oḻiyagillēn aṟinda sollil num adiyār ellārōdum okka eṇṇi irundīr adiyēnai nallār aṟivīr tīyār aṟivīr namakku ivvulagattu ellām aṟivīr īdē aṟiyīr indaḷūrīrē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

indaḷūrīrē – Oh lord who are mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr!; sollādu – not telling (forcefully to your highness); oḻiyagillēn – unable to remain; aṟinda – known (to me); sollil – if I try to tell; adiyēnai – I who cannot bear the separation; num adiyār – servitors of your highness; ellārōdum okka – equal to others; eṇṇiyirundīr – you are thinking; nalllār – the nature of those who have the goodness of being unable to bear the separation of your highness; aṟivīr – you know; tīyār – the nature of those who have the bad quality of being able to bear the separation of your highness; aṟivīr – you know; ivvulagattu – in this world; ellām – everything else; aṟivīr – you know; namakku – for us who are unable to bear the separation of your highness; īdē aṟiyīr – you do not know about our tender nature only

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh lord who are mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr! I am unable to remain without forcefully telling you; if I, who cannot bear the separation, try to tell what is known, you are thinking about me to be equal to other servitors of your highness; you know the nature of those who have the goodness of being unable to bear the separation of your highness; you know the nature of those who have the bad quality of being able to bear the separation of your highness; you know everything else in this world; for us who are unable to bear the separation of your highness, you do not know about our tender nature only.

*sollādu oḻiyagillēn* – I am unable to interact with you in the proper manner, as a servitor would do in the presence of the lord. The servitor should accept whatever is done by the lord and cannot force the lord; I am unable to do that.

*aṟinda sollil* – While telling what is known. While being unable to speak properly, speaking what is known. While doing so,

*um adiyār …* – Even after separating from you, with the desire “I will somehow see him”, sītāp pirātti sustained herself for ten months; you are considering me to be similar to such pirātti who has strong bones, while I am unable to survive even a fraction of a moment without seeing you. It appears that those who surrender to bhagavān through pirātti, have such greatness. nammāḻvār’s nature is such that, while surviving, he will enjoy bhagavān continuously for several days, and in separation, he will remain fasting \[from enjoying bhagavān\] for some time; unlike him, tirumangai āḻvār is so tender that he can neither enjoy bhagavān continuously nor sustain in separation. In periya tirumoḻi 3.6 “*tūviriya malar uḻakki*” padigam, āḻvār sent a messenger but started crying out even before the messenger returned from bhagavān.

nallār aṟivīr … – Your highness know about the nature of those who cannot survive without your highness; your highness know about the nature of those who can survive without your highness.

Why should I explain individually in this manner?

*ivvulagattu ellām aṟivīr* – In this world, there is nothing beyond your knowledge as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.33 “*ajñātam nāsti tē kincit triśu lōkēśu rāghava*” (śrī rāma! There is nothing beyond your knowledge on the three types of persons (favourable, unfavourable and neutral)).

*īdē aṟiyīr* – āḻvār’s tender nature is such that it will turn the omniscient bhagavān to be ignorant \[on āḻvār’s matters\].

*indaḷūrīrē* – Have you not arrived and stood in tiruvindaḷūr to eliminate the blame of “He is not showing his face knowing the nature of those who desired him”? Why are you forgetting the purpose of your presence here?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.7. Mattiranir

*māttīrānīr paṇi nīr koḷḷa emmaip paṇi aṟiyā vīttīr idanai vēṟē sonnōm indaḷūrīrē! kāttīrānīr nundam adikkaḷ kāttil umakku inda nāttē vandu toṇḍarāna nāngaḷ uyyōmē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

indaḷūrīrē – Oh lord who are mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr!; nīr – your highness; paṇi koḷḷa – to accept (our) kainkaryam; māttīr ānīr – not having the desire; emmai – us; paṇi – taste for kainkaryam; aṟiyā – made to know; vīttīr – have abandoned; idanai – this; vēṟē – separately (in a distinguished manner); sonnōm – informed to you; nundam – your highness’; adikkaḷ – divine feet; kāttīr ānīr – did not show; kāttil – if you showed; inda nāttē – in this world which does not accept servitude; vandu – came agreeably; umakku – for your highness; toṇḍarāna – being engaged in servitude; nāngaḷ – us; uyyōmē – will we not survive?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān asks āḻvār – pramāṇams (scriptural evidences) such as muṇḍaka upaniśat “yassarvajñas sarvavit” (He who is omniscient and fully knowledgeable) highlight that we (emperumān) have no defects; while such pramāṇams identify me as “sarvajña”, “sarvaśakti” (omnipotent), how are you identifying shortcomings in my knowledge and ability? āḻvār says – I observed it manifested in an entity. āḻvār is highlighting emperumān who is omniscient to be ignorant since he did not present himself knowing the nature of āḻvār; since emperumān did not help matching āḻvār’s situation, āḻvār is highlighting emperumān who is omnipotent to be incapable.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh lord who are mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr! Your highness are not having the desire to accept our kainkaryam; you have abandoned us after giving us the taste for kainkaryam; we have informed this to your highness separately; your highness did not show your divine feet; if you showed, will we, who have come agreeably and are engaged in servitude for your highness, in this world which does not accept servitude, not survive?

*māttīr ānīr paṇi nīr koḷḷa* – You can neither create nor destroy servitude \[in us\]! But you are not accepting our service which matches such servitude in us.

*emmaip paṇi aṟiyā vīttīr* – For us who are of the nature of not surviving without you, you introduced the servitude towards your divine feet and then abandoned us.

*idanai vēṟē sonnōm* – Unlike other aspects, we explained this to you in a distinguished manner.

*sonnōm* – Not just speaking about it matching our sorrow in separation, we informed in such a manner that no one will believe bhagavān.

*indaḷūrīrē* – I am speaking to you, who have arrived in tiruvindaḷūr while your original abode is paramapadam, to accept our kainkaryam.

emperumān asks “If you have gratitude for my act, why would you speak like this?” āḻvār says “There is a reason for that”

*kāttīr ānīr nundam adikkaḷ* – You are keeping your divine feet which exist for others, for yourself. Not showing your divine feet has become your nature. If you eliminate that thought and show your divine feet,

*inda nāttē vandu toṇḍarāna nāngaḷ uyyōmē* – Are we nityasūris in your paramapadam with whom you can think “If we abandon them, is there any other refuge for them? Hence, I will fulfil their desire, when I like to do so”? Just like water in a desert, in this samsāram everyone is eating, wearing clothes and roaming around, not thinking about you; will we, who are present in such samsāram, not be uplifted, if you show your divine feet?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.8. Munnai vannam

*munnai vaṇṇam pālin vaṇṇam muḻudum nilai ninṟa pinnai vaṇṇam koṇḍal vaṇṇam vaṇṇam eṇṇungāl ponnin vaṇṇam maṇiyin vaṇṇam puraiyum tirumēni inna vaṇṇam enṟu kāttīr indaḷūrīrē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

indaḷūrīrē – Oh one who is mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr divyadēśam!; vaṇṇam – (your highness’) physical beauty; eṇṇungāl – if we start thinking about it; munnai vaṇṇam – the physical beauty in kruta yugam, first; pālin vaṇṇam – will be milk’s complexion, that is white; pinnai vaṇṇam – physical beauty in the subsequent trētā yugam; ponnin vaṇṇam – will have the reddish complexion of gold; maṇiyin vaṇṇam – (subsequently the physical beauty in dvāpara yugam) will have the complexion of a dark-blue gem; muḻudum – at all times; nilai ninṟa – remaining firm; vaṇṇam – physical beauty; koṇḍal vaṇṇan – cloud’s complexion; puraiyum – remaining together (with the four complexions); tirumēni – divine form; inna vaṇṇam enṟu – having such complexion; kāttīr – mercifully show

**Перевод:**

**emperumān asks “Is there any shortcoming in getting your desires fulfilled by me who assumes the form with the complexion desired by cētanas (ātmās)? Why don’t you identify your desire?” āḻvār says “Though you assumed the forms desired by different people and manifested those forms to them, you should bring your distinguished form which is accepted by your desire and show me saying ‘See this’ “.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr divyadēśam! If we start thinking about your highness’ physical beauty, first, the physical beauty in kruta yugam, will be milk’s complexion, that is white; physical beauty in the subsequent trētā yugam will have the reddish complexion of gold; subsequently the physical beauty in dvāpara yugam), will have the complexion of a dark-blue gem; at all times, the physical beauty which is remaining firm will be cloud’s complexion. You mercifully show the divine form which is remaining together with the four complexions, to make me understand which complexion the body has.

*munnai vaṇṇam …* – Since, the people in kruta yugam have more satva guṇam, considering that they will enjoy white colour, he assumed a divine body with white complexion, thinking that as we do what pleases them, they will remain thinking “He did what is desirable for us; let us also show love towards him”.

Similarly, in the next \[trētā\] yugam, since the people were having more rajō guṇam, subsequently, he assumed reddish complexion for them; subsequently, he assumed the form of a dark blue gem stone;

*vaṇṇam enṇṇungāl* – If we start analysing his divine form, his eternal, distinguished form, appeared like a fully loaded dark cloud. Instead of just hearing about this in śāstram saying “In every yugam, he would assume the form which is desirable for cētanas of that time, his distinguished form will be like a dark cloud”; you should show your form mercifully saying “This is how the form which you heard in śāstram is”.

*indaḷūrīrē* – When I ask “Are there no śāstram for the forms which you accept?” \[Yes there are\] Are you not standing in tiruvindaḷūr to prove “These cannot just be heard in śāstram for my devotees; I should show them saying ‘See, this is my form'”?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.9. Endai tandai

*endai tandai tammān enṟenṟu emar ēḻ aḷavum vandu ninṟa toṇḍarōrkkē vāsi valleerāl sindai tannuḷ mundi niṟṟīr siṟidum tirumēni inda vaṇṇam enṟu kāttīr indaḷūrīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

indaḷūrīrē – Oh one who is mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr divyadēśam!; endai – for me and my father; tandai – for his father (in this manner, for our whole clan); tammān – being the lord; enṟu – saying in this manner; emar – our ancestors; ēḻ aḷavum – for seven generations; vandu – accepting and arriving to do kainkaryam (to your highness); ninṟa – stood firmly; toṇḍarōrkkē – in our matters only; vāsi valleer – you are analysing (that I cannot show myself); sindai tannuḷ – in (my) heart; mundi – for a very long time; niṟṟīr – are present; tirumēni – divine form; inda vaṇṇam enṟu – as having such nature; siṟidum – even a little bit; kāttīr – you are not showing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr divyadēśam! Our ancestors, for seven generations, stood firmly saying “being the lord of mine, my father, his father”, accepting and arriving to do kainkaryam; on our matters, you are analysing (to not show yourself) in our matters only. You are present in my heart for a very long time. Still, you are not showing your divine form, even a little bit, as having such nature.

*endai …* – For us, who identify you to be the lord of our clan, for seven generations living without being able to sustain ourselves without kainkaryam at your divine feet, you are hesitating in this manner.

*sindai tannuḷ mundi niṟṟīr* – piḷḷān would say “Why are you, who are remaining far to be embraced by me, are increasing my love towards you?” emperumān asks “Why are you speaking like this? What partiality did I show towards others?” āḻvār says “Instead of remaining satisfied thinking that shining in āḻvār’s heart is sufficient, you should be reachable by my hand to embrace you just as you are shining in my heart. ōr, you should not shine in my heart just as you are not reachable for an embrace. Both are not happening”.

*siṟidum* – Just as he is showing inside the heart without any shortcoming, he is not showing anything to the eyes. Previously, a king was too involved with his queen and did not present himself to the kingdom, many citizens were doubting his existence; the ministers went to the king’s private quarters and called out and the king showed his feet through the windows. \[At least you can do like that\].

*indaḷūrīrē* – You have come and are standing in tiruvindaḷūr to fully show your divine form which is shown to nityasūris, apart from shining in the heart.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.10. 4.9.10 -Er ar polil

*ērār poḻil sūḻ indaḷūril endai perumānaik kārār puṟavin mangai vēndan kaliyanoli seyda sīrār in sol mālai kaṟṟut tirivār ulagattu ārār avarē amararkku enṟum amarar āvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēr Ar – very beautiful; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; indaḷūril – mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr; endai – my lord; perumānai – on sarvēśvaran; kār Ar – filled with clouds; puṟavil – having surroundings; mangai – for tirumangai region; vēndan – king; kaliyan – āḻvār; oli seyda – mercifully spoke; sīr Ar – filled with bhagavān’s qualities; in sol – having sweet words; mālai – these ten pāsurams which are a garland of words; kaṟṟu – learnt; tirivār – those who fearlessly roam around; ulagattu – in this world; Ar Ar – those people (irrespective of their birth, conduct etc); avarē – they; amararkku – for nityasūris; enṟum – at all times; amarar āvār – will remain praiseworthy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār, the king of tirumangai region which is having surroundings filled with clouds, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams which are a garland of words, having sweet words filled with bhagavān’s qualities, on my lord, sarvēśvaran who is mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr which is surrounded by very beautiful gardens; irrespective of who they are, those who learn these pāsurams and roam around this world fearlessly, will remain praiseworthy for nityasūris, at all times.

*ēr Ar …* – Sang poems on my lord, sarvēśvaran who is mercifully present in tiruvindaḷūr which is surrounded by very beautiful gardens.

*kār Ar …* – āḻvār who is the leader of tirumangai region which is having surroundings which have eternal presence of clouds, mercifully spoke these pāsurams.

The poems are,

*sīr Ar …* – The garland which is strung with bhagavān’s qualities. viṣṇu darmam 8.3.7 “*aham vaktā bhavān śrōtā vācyō yōgō vimuktida:*” (I am the speaker; you are the listener; spoken subject is that which bestows liberation); śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 2.43 “*raghuvara caritam muni praṇītam daśaśiraśca vadam niśāmayadvam*”  is explained here. *raghuvara caritam* – Speaks about the protector in raghu kulam, perumāḷ (śrī rāma); *muni praṇītam* – Spoken by the most trustworthy person; *daśaśiraśca vadam* – Spoken about how śrī rāma removed the weeds from the country.

*kaṟṟut tirivār* – Learning these pāsurams, due to that pride, placing their feet on yama et al and roaming around.

*Ar Ar* – The only qualification is to recite these pāsurams; they may be in any birth, have any conduct etc.

*avarē amararkku enṟum amarar āvārē* – With this current birth, conduct and knowledge, they will be praised by nityasūris who do not need any greatness by such aspects.
