## 4.10 Aycciyar alaippa

## 4.10.1. Aycciyar alaippa

*āycciyar aḻaippa veṇṇey uṇḍu oru kāl ālilai vaḷarnda emperumān pēycciyai mulai uṇḍu iṇaimarudu iṟuttup perunilam aḷandavan kōyil kāytta nīḷ kamugum kadaliyum tengum engum mām poḻilgaḷin naduvē vāytta nīr pāyum maṇṇiyin tenpāl tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āycciyar – covherd women; aḻaippa – to complain; veṇṇey – butter; uṇḍu – mercifully ate; oru kāl – once (during deluge); ālilai – on a banyan leaf; vaḷarnda – mercifully resting there; emperumān – my lord; pēycciyai – pūtanā’s; mulai – bosom; uṇḍu – mercifully sucked (and finished her); iṇai – joined; marudu – maruda trees; iṟuttu – broke; peru nilam – vast earth; aḷandavan – the eternal abode of sarvēśvaran who accepted (from mahābali) and measured; kōyil – divyadēśam is; kāytta – having unripe fruits; nīḷ – tall; kamugum – areca trees; kadaliyum – plantain trees; tengum – coconut trees; engumām – present everywhere; poḻilgaḷin – gardens’; naduvē – in the middle; vāynda – abundant; nīr – water; pāyum – flowing; maṇṇiyil – maṇṇi river’s; tenpāl – present on the southern bank; tiruveḷḷiyangudi – known as tiruveḷḷiyangudi; aduvē – is that divyadēśam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran mercifully ate butter to be complained by the covherd women; once, her mercifully rested on a banyan leaf and remained my lord; he mercifully sucked pūtanā’s bosom; he broke the maruda trees which were joined; he accepted the vast earth (from mahābali) and measured it; the divyadēśam where he is eternally residing is tiruveḷḷiyangudi  which is on the southern bank of maṇṇi river where abundant water is flowing in the middle of the gardens which are filled with tall areca trees with unripe fruits, plantain trees and coconut trees.

*āycciyar aḻaippa* – emperumān mercifully ate the butter to have the five lakh covherd women who don’t know the difference between left and right hand, to complain, raising their hands.

*oru kāl ālilai vaḷarnda* – At a very young age, he kept the whole universe in his stomach, where there is none to call out, he mercifully rested on a banyan leaf which had just sprouted.

*emperumān* – One who made me exist exclusively for him by showing how he cannot sustain without the butter which was touched by his devotees and making the impossible, possible \[by consuming the whole universe and resting on a small banyan leaf\].

*pēycciyai* – Finishing pūtanā who came with an evil intent, by sucking on her bosom, and broke the two maruda trees which joined together having evil intent.

*peru nilam …* – The abode where emperumān who effortlessly measured and accepted the earth which was stolen by mahābali.

*kāytta …* – The enjoyability of the abode is such that it will show “emperumān who is our refuge, is nearby”. Everything is well-ripened in the abode.

*vāytta nīr pāyum* – Like those prideful ones who would unite and just drink cool water.

*tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē* – Since it is said that it is his temple, it implies that this is the target abode for us.

## 4.10.2. Anirai meyttu

*ānirai mēyttu anṟu alai kadal adaittittu arakkar tam sirangaḷai uruttik kār niṟai mēgam kalandadōr uruvak kaṇṇanār karudiya kōyil pūniraic cerundi punnai muttarumbip podumbidai varivaṇḍu miṇḍit tēn iraittuṇḍu angu innisai muralum tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ānirai – herds of cows; mēyttu – being the one who protected; anṟu – during śrī rāmāvatāram; alai – tides striking; kadal – ocean; adaittittu – building bridge; arakkar tam – strong rākśasas’; sirangaḷai – heads; urutti – one who severed; kār – in rainy season; nirai – dense; mēgam kalandu – matching a cloud; ōr – unique; uruvam – who is having a form; kaṇṇanār – kriṣṇa; karudiya – desirously living; kōyil – divyadēśam is; nirai – in bunches; pū – flowering; serundi – serundi trees’ (a type of sedge); arumbi – sprouting (and growing further); muttu – having pearls; punnai – punnai trees’ (mast-wood); podumbu – holes; idai – in the middle; vari – having stripes (beautiful); vaṇḍu – beetles; miṇḍi – being closely together; tēn – honey; iraittu – making noise; uṇḍu – consumed; angu – there itself; in – sweetly; isai – song; muralum – humming; tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē – it is tiruveḷḷiyangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa protected the herds of cows; during śrī rāmāvatāram, he severed the heads of the strong rākśasas after building a bridge on the ocean with tides striking; he is having a unique form which is matching a dense cloud in the rainy season; the divyadēśam where he desirously lives is tiruveḷḷiyangudi which has striped beetles remaining closely together, consuming the honey and humming the sweet songs there in the middle of the holes of serundi trees which are blossoming and punnai trees which are sprouting pearls.

*ānirai …* – Protecting the cows, building bridge across the bewildered ocean, severing the heads of rākśasas who have become strong by the boons.

*kār nirai …* – kriṣṇa who is having the form which resembles a fllled cloud in the rainy season. The divine abode where he is considering in his divine heart “This is the apt place to protect all”.

*pū nirai …* – serundi trees which are blossoming bunches of flowers and punnai trees which are sprouting pearls. In the holes in these trees, beautiful beetles are present closely with each other, drinking honey with great noise just as the venerable monkeys which entered the maduvanam, and are humming due to the drink which does not let them remain calm – they are singing out of their will.

## 4.10.3. Kadu vidam

*kadu vidam udaiya kāḷiyan tadattaik kalakki mun alakkaḻittu avan tan padamiṟap pāyndu pal maṇi sindap pal nadam payinṟavan kōyil padavaravalgul pāvai nallārgaḷ payiṟṟiya nādagattu oli pōy adai pudai taḻuvi aṇḍam ninṟu adirum tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mun – In the past; kadu – cruel; vidam udaiya – having poison; kāḷiyan – kāḷiyan’s; tadattai – pond; kalakki – agitated it to become slushy; alakkaḻittu – tormented him; avan than – his; padam – hood; iṟa – to break; pāyndu – jumped; palmaṇi – many gems (which were on his head); sinda – to scatter; pal nadam – many types of dances; payinṟavan – kriṣṇa who danced, where he is residing; kōyil – divyadēśam is; padam – having vast hood; aravu – like a snake; algul – thigh region; nallār – distinguished; pāvaigaḷ – ladies; payiṟṟiya – practicing; nādagattu oli – the sound of the drama; pōy – rising high; adai pudai – day and night; taḻuvi – being together; aṇḍam – on the sky; ninṟu – remaining firm; adirum – sounding tumultuously; tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē – the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷiyangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In the past, kriṣṇa agitated the pond of kāḷiyan who was having cruel poison to make it become slushy, tormented him and jumped on his hood to break it and cause the many gems on his head to scatter by performing many dances; the abode of such kriṣṇa is the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷiyangudi where the ladies who are having thigh region similar to that of a snake with vast hood, are practicing drama the sound of which is rising high, day and night, being together and remaining on the sky with tumultuous sound.

*kadu vidam udaiya …* – kāḷiyan is having such cruel poison which will make even birds which are flying forty to fifty miles above the pond will have their wings break and fall down; kriṣṇa jumped into such kāḷiyan’s pond, made it become slushy and caused torment to him.

*avan than padam iṟap pāyndu* – Climbing atop the kadamba tree on the shore, he jumped to crash kāḷiyan’s hoods and to make the gems which were present on the hoods to scatter.

*pal nadam payinṟavan kōyil* – He danced in many ways to write down many aspects of bharata (dance) śāstram. The abode where he is residing.

*pada aravu …* – Ladies, who are having thigh region looking similar to snake with vast hood, are practicing drama. That sound goes and reaches,

*adai pudai taḻuvi* – Being together in day and night, goes to the sky and makes tumultuous sound.

## 4.10.4. Karavai mun kattu

*kaṟavai mun kāttuk kanjanaik kāynda kāḷamēgat tiru uruvanpaṟavai munnuyarttup pāṟkadal tuyinṟa paramanār paḷḷikoḷ kōyil tuṟai tuṟai tōṟum ponmaṇi sidaṟum togudirai maṇṇiyin tenpāl seṟimaṇi mādak kodi kadir aṇavum tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṟavai – cows; mun – during kriṣṇāvatāram; kāttu – protected; kanjanai – on kamsan; kāynda – mercifully showed his anger; kāḷamēgam – dark cloud like; tiru – beautiful; uruvan – having complexion; mun – in the past; paṟavai – garudāḻvār; uyarttu – hoisting as flag; pāṟkadal – in tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean); tuyinṟa – mercifully rested; paramanār – sarvēśvaran who is greater than all; kōyil – divyadēśam is; tuṟai tuṟai tōṟum – on all ghats; pon – gold; maṇi – precious gems; sidaṟum – abundantly scattering; togu – coming together; tirai – having tides; maṇṇiyin tenpāl – on the southern bank of maṇṇi river; seṟi – densely embossed; maṇi – having precious gems; mādam – hoisted on the houses; kodi – flags; kadir – orbit of sun; aṇavum – touching; tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē – is the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷiyangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who is having beautiful complexion which resembles that of a dark cloud, protected the cows and mercifully showed his anger on kamsan during kriṣṇāvatāram, in the past; the divyadēśam where such sarvēśvaran, who is greater than all, who mercifully rested in tiruppāṟkadal hoisting garudāḻvār as his flag, is the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷiyangudi which is on the southern bank of maṇṇi river which is abundantly scattering gold and precious gems in all ghats, coming together through the tides and where flags hoisted on the houses which are having densely embossed precious gems, are touching the orbit of sun.

*kaṟavai …* – One who protected the cows and killed kamsan who could not tolerate such protection for cows.

*kāḷamēgat tiru uruvan* – This is how his beautiful form is, which was meant to destroy others. Matching his ability to protect, he hoisted periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) as flag and mercifully rested close-by in tiruppāṟkadal, to hear the cries of brahmā et al; the abode of such emperumān who is greater than all.

*tuṟai tuṟai …* – In each ghat, gold and precious gems are abundantly being pushed by the gathered tides of maṇṇi river; on the southern bank of such river, the flags hoisted on the mansions which are having densely embossed precious gems, went up to the abode of sun and stopped his movement.

## 4.10.5. Parinai undu

*pārinai uṇḍu pārinai umiḻndu bāradam kai eṟindu oru kāl tērinai ūrndu tērinait turanda sengaṇmāl senṟu uṟai kōyil ērnirai vayaluḷ vāḷaigaḷ maṟugi emakkidam anṟu idenṟu eṇṇi sīrmali poygai senṟu aṇaiginṟa tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pārinai – earth; uṇḍu – (during deluge) mercifully consumed; pārinai – earth; umiḻndu – (during creation) spat out; oru kāl – during kriṣṇāvatāram; bāradam – in mahābhārata war; kai eṟindu – organised the army in various groups; tērinai – arjuna’s chariot; ūrndu – conducted; tērinai – chariots of bhīśma et al; turanda – chased to drive them away; sem kaṇ – having reddish eyes (due to motherly forbearance); māl – sarvēśvaran who is mad about his devotees; senṟu – came; uṟai – and eternally residing; kōyil – divyadēśam is; ēr – ploughs which are used for farming; nirai – having rows; vayal uḷ – present in the fertile fields; vāḷaigaḷ – vāḷai fish; maṟugi – fears; idu – this fertile field; emakku – for us to reside; idam anṟu – not the apt place; enṟu eṇṇi – thinking this way; sīr – by beauty; mali – abundant; poygai – ponds; senṟu – went; aṇaiginṟa – and reached; tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē – it is tiruveḷḷiyangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, who is mad about his devotees and who is having reddish eyes, mercifully consumed the earth and spat it out; during kriṣṇāvatāram, in mahābhārata war, he organised the army in various groups, conducted arjuna’s chariot and chased and drove away the chariots of brahmā et al; the divyadēśam where he arrived and is eternally residing is tiruveḷḷiyangudi where vāḷai fish which are present in the fertile fields, which are having rows of ploughs  are used for farming, fear that the fields are not apt for them to reside, and thinking in this manner, went to ponds which are having abundance of beauty, and reached there.

*pārinai uṇḍu …* – Securing the vast earth in his divine stomach, letting it out to let it see the outside so that it does not weaken remaining inside, setting up the army during mahābhārata war, due to vātsalyam (motherly forbearance) towards his devotee, he remained the charioteer and chased the great charioteers such as bhīśma et al to drive them away.

*sem kaṇ senṟu uṟai kōyil* – Remaining in the manner of showing his vātsalyam fully in his eye, the one who is madly in love towards his devotees, has come and is residing.

*ēr nirai …* – As the farmers started ploughing continuously, vāḷai fish in the fertile fields, which are having rows of ploughs, feared thinking “This dangerous place is not apt for us to reside; let us go to a safe place and reside there” and reached the beautiful pond; no one will go and use the plough in the ponds. This is similar to those who think “samsāram is impermanent and sorrowful”, abandon samsāram and reach virajā river.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.6. Karridaip pulai

*kāṟṟidaip pūḷai karandana arandai uṟak kadal arakkar tam sēnaik kūṟṟidaic cellak kodungaṇai turanda kōlavilli irāman tan kōyil ūṟṟidai ninṟa vāḻaiyin kanigaḷ ūḻttu vīḻndana uṇḍu maṇḍic cēṟṟidaik kayalgaḷ ugaḷ tigaḻ vayal sūḻ tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kāṟṟidai – in great wind; pūḷai – a tender flower; karandana – just as it will be destroyed; kadal – like ocean; arakkar tam – rākśasas’; sēnai – army; arandai uṟa – to suffer; kūṟṟidai – yama’s place; sella – to reach; kodu – cruel; kaṇai – arrows; turanda – shot; kōla – beautiful; villi – having bow; rāman than – cakravartit tirumagan’s; kōyil – divyadēśam is; ūṟṟidai – in the land where there are water-springs; ninṟa – sprouted; vāḻaiyin – plantain trees’; ūḻttu – (well ripened and) separated; vīḻndana – and fell down; kanigaḷ – fruits; maṇḍi – eagerly; uṇḍu – ate; kayalgaḷ – kayal fish; sēṟṟidai – in the muddy areas; ugaḷ – jumping; tigaḻ – shining; vayal – by fertile fields; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē – it is tiruveḷḷiyangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruveḷḷīyangudi is the divyadēśam of cakravartit tirumagan who is having a beautiful bow with which he shot cruel arrows on the ocean-like army of rākśasas to make them suffer and reach yama’s abode, just as tender pūḷai flower will be destroyed in a great wind. It is surrounded by shining fertile fields where kayal fish, which eagerly eat fruits which got separated and fell down from the sprouted plantain trees which are in the land where there are water-springs, are jumping in the muddy areas.

*kāṟṟidai …* – Just as pūḷai flower will be blown away and be destroyed, in a great wind.

*arandai uṟa* – To suffer. The whole army of rākśasas who came like an agitated ocean with waves.

*kūṟṟidaic cella* – These rākśasas who previously subdued yama and collected taxes from him, have now become his citizens. When the rākśasas went on a victorious journey, they first defeated yama.

*kodungaṇai turanda* – He shot the arrows which will not show mercy even if he shows mercy.

*kōla villi rāman kōyil* – All of those rākśasas who will be destroyed just by the way he holds his bow, were thinking “Would we not be killed by him?” – the abode where such cakravartit tirumagan who is having such beautiful bow is residing. It was told in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 104.6 “*ranjanīyasya*” (śrī rāma’s valour is liked even by his enemies). As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 59.130 “*cacāla cāpanca mumōca vīra:*” (rāvaṇa walked unsteadily; he let go of his bow), one would drop one’s bow being disheartened. It has to be like that when it is said “*vīra:*” (the valorous one).

*ūṟṟidai …* -Bananas will ripe well, separate from the trees which were in the water bodies and fall on vāḷai fish in the muddy area; as their food appears close to them, they will eagerly consume the same and will  jump around showing their strength; being surrounded by such shining fertile fields. The vāḷai fish are moving around in the muddy area just as in water. Even if they are placed in deluge, they will make that muddy with their strength.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.7. Olliya karumam

*oḷḷiya karumam seyvan enṟu uṇarnda māvali vēḷviyil pukkut  teḷḷiya kuṟaḷāy mūvadi koṇḍu tikkuṟa vaḷarndavan kōyil aḷḷiyam poḻilvāy irundu vāḻ kuyilgaḷ ari ari enṟavai aḻaippa veḷḷiyār vaṇanga viraindu aruḷ seyvān tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oḷḷiya – beautiful; karumam – the deed of offering oneself fully; seyvan – let me do; enṟu uṇarnda – thought as; māvali – mahābali’s; vēḷviyil – in the yāgam; teḷḷiya – having clarity (firm belief); kuṟaḷāy – being vāmanan; pukku – entered; mūvadi – three steps of land (from that mahābali); koṇḍu – accepted as charity; tikku uṟa – to reach in all directions; vaḷarndavan – one who grew in his divine form; kōyil – divyadēśam is; aḷḷi – having buds; am – beautiful; poḻilvāy – in the gardens; irundu – residing; vāḻ – remaining joyful; avai kuyilgaḷ – those cuckoos; ari ari enṟu – as “hari: hari:”; aḻaippa – to remain calling out; veḷḷiyār – those who have satva nature; vaṇanga – as they worship; viraindu – very quickly; aruḷ seyvān – sarvēśvaran who is showing his mercy to them, his; tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē – it is tiruveḷḷiyangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān being vāmanan who is having clarity, entered the yāgam of mahābali who was thinking “let me do the beautiful deed of offering self”, accepted three steps of land as charity and grew in his divine form to reach all directions; the divyadēśam of such sarvēśvaran is tiruveḷḷiyangudi where the cuckoos are joyfully residing in beautiful gardens which are having buds, and are calling out “hari: hari:”, as those with satva nature worship him.

*oḷḷiya karumam …* – Having the yāgam as a reason, mahābali thought “Let me give all my wealth to others”. If we consider “*uṇarndu*” instead of “*uṇarnda*“, alternative explanation – emperumān entering mahābali’s sacrificial arena thinking “I will make myself a mendicant for the sake of indra who came begging to me”.

*teḷḷiya kuṟaḷāy* – vāmanan who is having firm clarity of “I will not leave without getting \[what I want\]; will I return without completing my task?” even if śukran et al where advising mahābali saying “He has come to fulfil the desires of dēvas; don’t be cheated”. Even if śukra stopped and even if mahābali says “I won’t give”, he entered thinking “I will not go without accepting”. He was seeking, saying “You should give three steps” and subsequently placed all the directions under his divine form.

*aḷḷi …* – aḷḷi – alli – buds; beautiful garden with buds; alternative explanation – aḷi is transformed as aḷḷi; aḷi means coolness; cool, beautiful garden; cuckoos consumed the fruits etc in such garden, are doing tirunāma sankīrtanam (singing bhagavān’s divine names) just as those who are in satva niśtai (goodness) will wake up in brahma muhūrtam and chant “hari: hari:”. Even the birds of that town have the lifestyle of brāhmaṇas.

*veḷḷiyār …* – Surrendered by pure natured persons; alternatively, it is popularly known that śukran vorśipped in this divyadēśam – that is being mentioned here. veḷḷiyār indicates respect towards śukran.

*veḷḷiyār vaṇanga …* – \[Here veḷḷiyār indicates rudra who is residing in veḷḷi malai – kailāśa hill\] As rudran came and surrendered, as said in śrīmatsya purāṇam “*svapnalabdam danam yatā”* (disappeared like wealth acquired in dream), emperumān eliminated his sin/suffering quickly.

*viraindu aruḷ* – Even before rising, after offering obeisance, they will have their desires fulfilled.

## 4.10.8. Mudiyudai

*mudi udai amararkku idar seyum asurar tam perumānai anṟu ariyāy madi idai vaittu mārvai mun kīṇḍa māyanār manniya kōyil padi idai mādattu adiyidait tūṇil paditta pan maṇigaḷin oḷiyāl vidi pagal iravenṟu aṟivaridāya tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mudiyudai – being crowned (and thus prideful); amararkku – for dēvatās; idar – sorrow; seyyum – causing; asurar tam – for asuras; perumānai – hiraṇya, who is the king; anṟu – when prahlādan was tortured; ariyāy – being narasimha; mun – previously; madiyidai – on the lap; vaittu – kept; mārvai – his chest; kīṇḍa – tore apart; māyanār – amazing sarvēśvaran; manniya – remaining fixed; kōyil – divyadēśam is; padiyidai – on earth; mādattu – in mansions; adiyidai – placed; tūṇil – pillars; paditta – embossed; pal – many types of; maṇigaḷin – gems’; oḷiyāl – lustre; vidi – as early morning; pagal – as day; iravu enṟu – as night; aṟivu aridāya – being difficult to know; tiruveḷḷiyangudi aduvē – it is tiruveḷḷiyangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, being narasimha, previously kept hiraṇya who was the king of asuras who would cause sorrow for the crowned dēvatās, and tore apart his chest; the divyadēśam where such amazing sarvēśvaran is remaining fixed is tiruveḷḷiyangudi, where it is difficult to know whether it is early morning, day or night due to the lustre from the many types of gems embossed on the pillars placed in the mansions on the earth.

*mudi …* – There is the lord of asuras who cause sorrow for dēvatās who considered themselves to be lords as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 16.4](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-14/) “*īśvarōham*” (I am the controller of everything) – he is hiraṇya.

*anṟu* – When he tortured his son prahlādan. Being narasimha.

*madiyidai vaittu* – On his lap, where he keeps śrī mahālakśmi et al, he kept the evil hiraṇyan. nampiḷḷai would mercifully say that he heard from parāśara bhattar for periya tirumadal phrase “*tannudaiya tāḷ mēl kidātti*” – It is apt to keep me who is desirous towards him instead of the unfavourable hiraṇyan. nampiḷḷai says that bhattar would directly look at him and explained this. This is the abode where emperumān who has unbounded love towards his devotees, and who tore apart the wide chest of hiraṇyan, resides permanently.

*padi …* – From the lustre of the gems embossed on the pillars which are planted in the mansions on the earth, it is difficult to differentiate between day and night there. āḻvār could be narrating this since such eminence occurred on some special occasions. Alternatively, he could be saying this since there is no end to his joy. In the objects which we like, all eminence will be felt \[even if not present\].

## 4.10.9. Kudi kudiyagak

*kudi kudiyāgak kūdi ninṟu amarar guṇangaḷē pidaṟṟi ninṟētta adiyavarkku aruḷi aravaṇait tuyinṟa āḻiyān amarndu uṟai kōyil kadi udaik kamalam adi idai malarak karumbodu perunjennel asaiya vadivudai annam pedaiyodum sērum vayal veḷḷiyangudi aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

amarar – dēvatās such as brahmā et al; kudi kudiyāga – along with wife, children; kūdi ninṟu – remaining together; guṇangaḷē – (his) auspicious qualities only; pidaṟṟi ninṟu – reciting; ētta – as they praise; adiyavarkku – for those servitors; aruḷi – showering his grace; aravaṇai – on anantaśayanam (ādiśēśa); tuyinṟa – mercifully resting; āḻiyān – sarvēśvaran who is holding the divine chakra; amarndu – remaining fixed; uṟai – eternally residing; kōyil – divyadēśam is; kadiyudai – having fragrance; kamalam – lotus flower; adiyidai – at the bottom of the sugarcane and paddy crops; malara – as they blossom (due to that); karumbodu – along with sugarcane; perum – huge; sennel – reddish paddy crops; asaiya – as they sway; vadivudai – having beautiful form; annam – swan; pedaiyodum – along with its female spouse; sērum – living in that lotus flower; vayal – having fertile fields; veḷḷiyangudi aduvē – is tiruveḷḷiyangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, who is holding the divine chakra, is mercifully resting on anantaśayanam (ādiśēśa), showering his grace to those servitors such as dēvatās starting with brahmā et al who are remaining along with their wives and children, reciting the auspicious qualities of emperumān and praising him only; the divyadēśam of such sarvēśvaran is tiruveḷḷiyangudi which is having fertile fields where a beautiful swan is living with its female spouse in a fragrant, blossomed lotus flower at the bottom of the sugarcane and paddy crops, which makes those sugarcane and huge reddish paddy crops, sway.

*kudi kudi …* – brahmā et al, as said in “*umayāsārdam īśāna:*” (Siva along with pārvati), along with their wives and children, gathered and praised his qualities saying “When we are in danger, is there any refuge other than your highness?”; emperumān showering his mercy upon those (dēvatās) who are totally surrendered at his divine feet,  he is mercifully resting in the milk ocean, having it as his divine abode, which is nearby to hear their cries.

*āḻiyān* – Alternatively, the divine abode where the one who is having divine chakra which is the tool for protection, is remaining fixed.

*kadi …* – As the very fragrant lotus flower blossoms under the sugarcane and paddy crops, those crops sway due to that; the swan which lives on that flower along with its spouse, appears like a prince along with his consort being seated on a tall throne, being fanned from the sides.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.10. Pandu mun

*paṇḍu mun ēnamāgi anṟorugāl pār idandu eyiṟṟinil koṇḍu teṇḍirai varudap pāṟkadal tuyinṟa tiruveḷḷiyangudiyānai vaṇḍaṟai sōlai mangaiyar talaivan mānavēl kaliyan vāy oligaḷ koṇḍivai pādum tavam udaiyārgaḷ āḷvar ikkurai kadal ulagē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇḍu – In the beginning of varāha kalpam; mun – before the earth got destroyed; ēnam āgi – being mahāvarāham (great wild-boar); anṟu orugāl – when the ocean of deluge formed (with the divine heart of “I could not help before”); pār – earth; idandu – dug out; eyiṟṟinil – on the tusk; koṇḍu – held; teḷ – pure; tirai – waves; varuda – to caress (his divine feet); pāṟkadal – in tiruppāṟkadal; tuyinṟa – mercifully rested; tiruveḷḷiyangudiyānai – on sarvēśvaran who is mercifully present in the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷiyangudi; vaṇḍu – beetles; aṟai – humming; sōlai – having gardens; mangaiyar – for the residents of tirumangai region; talaivan – being the controller; mānam – which can cause attachment towards vaiṣṇavas; vēl – having the weapon, spear; kaliyan – āḻvār’s; vāy oligaḷ – divine words; ivai – these ten pāsurams; koṇḍu – with loving care; pādum – learning/practicing; tavamudaiyār – fortunate ones; kurai – resounding; kadal – surrounded by ocean; ivvulagu – this world; āḷvar – will get to rule over

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In the beginning of varāha kalpam, before the earth got destroyed, sarvēśvaran, being mahāvārāham, when the ocean of deluge formed, dug out the earth and held it on his tusk; he then mercifully rested on tiruppāṟkadal to have the pure waves caress his divine feet; the fortunate ones who are learning/practicing these ten pāsurams on such sarvēśvaran who is mercifully present in the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷiyangudi, with divine words of tirumangai āḻvār who is the controller of the residents of the tirumangai region which is having gardens with humming beetles, who is having the weapon, spear which can cause attachment towards vaiṣṇavas, will get to rule over this world which is surrounded by resounding ocean.

*paṇḍu* – In the beginning of varāha kalpam.

*mun* – Being mahāvārāham, before the earth gets stuck into the wall of the oval shaped universe and gets destroyed

*anṟu* … – Thinking “I did not get to help you \[before you drowned\]”, he dug out the earth, held it on his divine tusk; to eliminate the fatigue, he mercifully rested on tiruppāṟkadal to be caressed by the waves; such sarvēśvaran is present in tiruveḷḷiyangudi.

*vaṇḍu …* – Being the controller of the residents of tirumangai region having gardens where beetles who have drunk honey, are humming.

*māna vēl* – Huge spear; (alternative explanation) the spear which will cause attachment towards vaiṣṇavas.

*koṇḍu …* – The greatly fortunate persons who would lovingly learn/recite these pāsurams, will have the world surrounded by ocean, to be under their control. Since he \[tirumangai āḻvār\] was able to caringly engage his wealth for the service of bhāgavatās, he considered wealth to be his goal; due to that, since he thinks that even those who learn these pāsurams deserve the same spirit, he is saying that they will get the wealth of kingdom. Alternatively, it could be said that he is identifying these worldly benefits to make this prabandam pursuable by everyone. If those who desire wealth do not see worldly benefits being highlighted, they will not pursue this. Since he lovingly thinks that they too should not miss out on these deep philosophical aspects, he is highlighting the worldly benefits, to attract them.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## Fifth Centum

## 5.1 Arivadariyan

## 5.1.1. Arivadariyan

*aṟivadariyān anaittulagum udaiyān ennai āḷudaiyān kuṟiya māṇi uruvāya kūttan manni amarumidam naṟiya malar mēl surumbārkka eḻilār manjñai nadamāda poṟi koḷ siṟai vaṇḍu isai pādum puḷḷam būdangudi tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṟivadu – To know, by self effort; ariyān – being difficult; anaittulagum – all the worlds; udaiyān – having as his possession; ennai – me; āḷudaiyān – having me as his servitor; kuṟiya – dwarf; māṇ uruvāgiya – in the form of a brahmacāri; kūttan – sarvēśvaran who is having heart-captivating actions; manni – remaining fixed; uṟaiyum – living; idam – divyadēśam is; naṟiya – fragrant; malar mēl – on the flowers; surumbu – beetles known as surumbu; ārkka – as they are humming; eḻil Ar – beautiful; manjñai – peacocks; nadamāda – as they dance; poṟikoḷ – having stripes; siṟai – having wings; vaṇḍu – beetles; isai pādum – humming songs; puḷḷambūdangudi (tānē) – divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divyadēśam where sarvēśvaran, who is having heart-captivating actions in the form of a dwarf brahmacāri, who is difficult to be known by self effort, having all the worlds as his possession and is having me as his servitor, is remaining fixed and residing, is the divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi where beetles known as surumbu which are present on fragrant flowers, are humming, beautiful peacocks are dancing and beetles with stripes and wings are humming songs.

*aṟivadariyān* – One who is having the nature of being not known by those who try to know him through self efforts.

*anaittulagum udaiyān* – While the possibilities to know him and not know him are there, he is the lord of all worlds and can be well known by all.

*ennai āḷ udaiyān* – Specifically one who enslaved me. śaraṇāgati gadyam “*asmat svāmin* !” (Oh, one who is my lord!).

*kuṟiya …* – Such lord who is greater than all, accepted the form of vāmana, with the form that is very much used to seeking alms, entered mahābali’s sacrificial arena; the divine abode where such emperumān who has heart-captivating actions, is eternally residing saying “I will not leave”. When he walked into the sacrificial arena, it appeared as if an expert dancer danced.

*naṟiya …* – On the fragrant flowers, a specific species in beetles named surumbu, are making humming noise; peacocks with beautiful form are dancing.

*poṟi …* – Beetles which are having stripes and wings, are humming songs, matching the dance.

## 5.1.2. Kallak kuralay

*kaḷḷak kuṟaḷāy māvaliyai vanjittu ulagam kaippaduttu poḷḷaik karatta pōdagattin tunbam tavirta punidanidam paḷḷac ceṟuvil kayal ugaḷap paḻanak kaḻani adanuḷ pōy puḷḷup piḷḷaikku irai tēdum puḷḷam būdangudi tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaḷḷam – mischievous; kuṟaḷāy – being a dwarf; māvaliyai – mahābali; vanjittu – cheated; ulagam – (his) world; kai paduttu – got full control of it; poḷḷai – having hole; karatta – having trunk; pōdagattin – gajēndrāḻvān’s; tunbam – sorrow; tavirtta – one who eliminated; punidan – the purest sarvēśvaran’s eternal abode; idam – the divyadēśam is; paḷḷam – low-lying; seṟuvil – in fertile fields; kayal – fish; ugaḷa – as they jump; puḷḷu – birds; paḻanam – having water-bodies; kaḻani adanuḷ – in the fertile fields; pōy – entered; piḷḷaikku – for their little ones; irai – food; tēdum – searching; puḷḷambūdangudi tānē – it is divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān as a mischievous dwarf cheated mahābali and got full control of the world; he eliminated the sorrow of gajēndrāḻvān who was having a trunk with a hole; the divyadēśam where the purest sarvēśvaran is eternally residing is puḷḷambūdangudi where the fish in the low-lying fertile fields jump, the birds enter the fertile fields which are having water-bodies and are searching food for their little ones.

*kaḷḷam …* – Accepting the form of vāmana (dwarf) which will not let mahābali accept the words of śukra et al who were saying “He is sarvēśvaran; he has come to do good for dēvas; don’t become captivated by him” and accepted the world from mahābali who was thinking the world, which does not belong to him, as his property.

*poḷḷai …* – The abode where emperumān eliminated the sorrow of gajēndrāḻvān who is having a trunk with a hole, and considered his own sorrow to have been eliminated.

*paḷḷam …* – In the low-lying fertile fields, fish would jump around due to their pride, the birds will enter those fertile fields which are having water-bodies.

*puḷḷup piḷḷaikku irai tēdum* – It is usually explained by me \[vyākyātā, periyavāccān piḷḷai\] that when ālavāyudaiyān asked, bhattar mercifully explained this. ālavāyudaiyān asked “When the fish are jumping around, why should the birds go searching for food?” bhattar mercifully replied “Son! Don’t you understand the situation; birds are searching food for their little ones; due to the nature of the soil, the fish would be well-grown like pillar and heavy (weighing) stone; hence they will look for smaller fish which can be consumed by the little ones”.

## 5.1.3. Meva arakkar

*mēvā arakkar tennilangai vēndan vīyac caram turandu  māvāy piḷandu malladarttu marudam sāytta māladidam kāvār tengin paḻam vīḻak kayalgaḷ pāyak kurugiriyumpūvār kaḻani eḻilārum puḷḷambūdangudi tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mēvā – those who don’t fit (with him); arakkar – rākśasas’; then – present in the south direction; ilangai – for lankā; vēndan – rāvaṇa, who was the king; vīya – to be killed; saram – arrows; turandu – shot; mā – kēśi who came as a horse, his; vāy – mouth; piḷandu – tore; mal – wrestlers; adarttu – tormented and turned to dust; marudam – maruda trees; sāytta – one who made them fall; māladu – sarvēśvaran who is infatuated towards his devotees, his; idam – divyadēśam is; Ar – densely present; kā – in the groves; tengin – from coconut trees; paḻangaḷ – fruits; vīḻa – as they fall (seeing that); kayalgaḷ – fish (became frightened); pāya – jumped out to another place (seeing that); kurugu – cranes; iriyum – scattered and ran; pū Ar – filled with flowers such as lotus etc; kaḻani – fertile fields’; eḻil – by the beauty; ārum – being complete; puḷḷambūdangudi tānē – it is divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, who is infatuated towards his devotees, shot arrows to kill rāvaṇa the king of lankā which was in the southern direction where rākśasas who were not fitting with him were present; he tore the mouth of kēśi who came as a horse; he tormented the wrestlers and turned them into dust; he made the maruda trees fall down. The divyadēśam of such sarvēśvaran is puḷḷambūdangudi which has densely present groves where the fruits from coconut tree fall, seeing which the fish jumped out to another place; seeing which the cranes scattered and ran; it is complete due to the beauty of the fertile fields which are filled with flowers such as lotus etc.

*mēvā …* – emperumān shot arrows to kill rāvaṇa who was the king of lankā where rākśasas who were naturally hateful instead of being hateful due to a particular reason; tore the mouth of kēśi; killed the group of wrestlers; broke the maruda trees which were standing together.

*māladu idam* – The abode of emperumān who shows equal love towards pirātti and his devotees.

*kā Ar …* – As the fruits from coconut trees in the dense groves fall, fish jumped thinking that they are falling on them.

*kurugu iriyum* … – The cranes think that the fish are jumping aiming at them and scattered and ran away. The bewilderment is matching for both the fish and the cranes. Fish became frightened while the fruits were not aimed at them; cranes, while are harmful to the fish which are their food, were running away fearing the fish.

## 5.1.4. Verpal mari

*veṟpāl māri paḻudākki viṟal vāḷarakkar talaivan tan  vaṟpār tiraḷ tōḷ ainnāngum tuṇitta valvil irāmanidam kaṟpār purisai seykunṟam kavinār kūdam māḷigaigaḷ poṟpār mādam eḻilārum puḷḷambūtangudi tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

veṟpāl – with gōvardana mountain; māri – rain; paḻudākki – becoming wasted (by not harming cows and covherds); viṟal – strong; vāḷ – having sword; arakkar – rākśasas; talaivan than – rāvaṇa, who is the controller, his; vaṟpu – strength; Ar – having more; tiraḷ – well rounded (being fleshy); ai nāngu tōḷgaḷaiyum – twenty shoulders; tuṇitta – severed; val – strong; vil – having bow; irāman – cakravartit tirumagan’s (divine son of daśarata, his); idam – divyadēśam is; kaṟpu Ar – having renowned workmanship; purisai sey – being made as forts; kunṟam – rocks; kavin Ar – having a lot of beauty; kūdam – houses; māḷigaigaḷ – palaces; poṟpu Ar – desirable; mādam – halls (their); eḻil – by the beauty; ārum – being rich; puḷḷambūdangudi tānē – it is divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān made the rain become wasted with gōvardana mountain; as cakravartit tirumagan, with his strong bow, he severed the very strong, well rounded twenty shoulders of rāvaṇa who is the controller of rākśasas having sword; the divyadēśam of such emperumān is puḷḷambūdangudi which is very rich by the beauty of the very beautiful houses, palaces and desirable halls and which is surrounded by forts made of rocks with renowned workmanship.

*veṟpāl māri paḻudākki* – With the gōvardana mountain, emperumān wasted the rain which was intentionally sent by indran; as cakravartit tirumagan, he had a very strong bow which severed the well-rounded, strong shoulders of rāvaṇa, who was the refuge for the very strong rākśasas who were armed. The abode of such emperumān.

*kaṟpār …* – Mountains which are turned into skillful workmanship from rocks; very beautiful halls, palaces, very beautiful mansions – being beautiful due to the presence of these.

## 5.1.5. Maiyar tadangan

*maiyār tadangaṇ karungūndal āycci maṟaiya vaitta tayir neyyār pālōdu amudu seyda nēmi angai māyanidam seyyār āral irai karudic cengāl nārai senṟaṇaiyum poyyā nāvin maṟaiyāḷar puḷḷambūdangudi tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mai Ar – fully decorated with black pigment; tadam – wide; kaṇ – having eyes; karu – having black colour; kūndal – having hair; āycci – yaśōdā; maṟaiyā – to be not seen by kriṣṇa; vaitta – securely placed; tayir – curd; Ar – abundant; ney – ghee; pālōdu – with milk; amudu seyda – one who mercifully consumed; nēmi – with divine chakra; am – beautiful; kai – having hand; māyan – amazing sarvēśvaran’s; idam – divyadēśam is; sey – in fertile fields; Ar – abundant; Aral – fish named Aral; irai – as (its) food; karudi – considering; sengāl – having reddish feet; nārai – crane; senṟu – went; aṇaiyum – reaching; poyyā – having no lies; nāvil – in tongues; maṟai – vēdas; āḷar – where brāhmaṇas who rule over, are residing; puḷḷambūdangudi tānē – it is divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

yaśōdā, who is having her wide eyes fully decorated with black pigment and black colour hair, securely placed curd, abundant ghee and milk, to be not seen by kriṣṇa; such kriṣṇa who is having a divine hand which is beautiful due to the presence of divine chakra, mercifully consumed all of those. The divyadēśam of such amazing sarvēśvaran is puḷḷambūdangudi where brāhmaṇas, who rule over vēdas and are having no lies in their tongues, are residing and where the crane with reddish feet, went and reached considering the abundant Aral fish in the fertile fields as its food.

*maiyār …* – Due to vātsalyam (motherly forbearance) towards kriṣṇa, to not have him become distressed \[fearful of seeing a stranger\], she will always decorate her eyes with black pigment and have her hair well-combed.

*āycci maṟaiya vaitta tayir* – She will secure everything in a place which is not known to him. She will place the curd in a sandalwood paste container.

*neyyār …* – He mercifully consumed ghee and milk too.

*nēmi angai māyan idam* – Though he is sarvēśvaran, he will also behave as if he does not know where those are hidden and play along with the efforts of yaśōdā in hiding those.

*seyyār …* – Aral fish are filled in the fertile fields; just as hungry people would say “I will eat a whole container of rice”, considering those fish as their food, cranes with reddish feet will reach there.

poyyā – Where the brāhmaṇas, who only speak the truth, are residing.

## 5.1.6. Minnin anna

*minnin anna nuṇmarungul vēyēy tadandōḷ melliyaṟkāy mannu sinatta maḻa vidaigaḷ ēḻ anṟadartta māladidam mannu mudunīr aravinda malar mēl varivaṇḍu isai pāda punnai ponnēy tādudirkkum puḷḷambūdangudi tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

minnin anna – matching a lightning; nuṇ – slim; marungul – waist; vēy ēy – matching a bamboo; tadam – vast; tōḷ – having shoulders; melliyaṟkāy – for nappinnaip pirātti who is an elegant lady; mannu – remaining fixed (without changing); sinatta – angry; maḻam – youthful; ēḻ vidaigaḷ – seven bulls; adartta – one who killed; māl adu – sarvēśvaran who has love, his; idam – divyadēśam is; mannu – remaining fixed (without drying up); mudu – ancient; nīr – born in water; aravinda malar mēl – on the lotus flowers; vari – having stripes; vaṇḍu – beetles; isai pāda – humming songs; punnai – punnai trees; ponnēy – having the colour of gold; tādu – pollen; udirkkum – shredding; puḷḷambūdangudi tānē – it is the divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who has love, killed the seven youthful bulls which have fixed anger, for the sake of nappinnaip pirātti who is an elegant lady and who is having a slim waist matching a lightning and vast shoulders matching a bamboo; the divyadēśam of such sarvēśvaran is puḷḷambūdangudi where striped beetles on the lotus flowers which are born in perennial water, are humming songs and punnai trees are shredding golden colour pollen.

*minnin anna …* – For nappinnaip pirātti who is having slim waist matching a lightning and vast shoulders which are matching a bamboo. Her beauty is such that one would even jump into a tank where spears are planted, to prove one’s love for such person.

*mannu …* – The abode of the most romantic emperumān who crushed the seven bulls which were having unchanging anger and youthful nature which make them have the urge to fight.

*mannu …* – As the striped beetles which are on the lotus flowers born in perennial water, and are drunk with honey, are humming songs, punnai trees are shedding pollen which appear like gold; it appears like scattering golden powder on those who sing songs.

## 5.1.7. Kudaiya vilangal

*kudaiyā vilangal koṇḍu ēndi māri paḻudu ānirai kāttu sadaiyān ōda adal vāṇan tadandōḷ tuṇitta talaivanidam kudiyā vaṇḍugaḷ uṇṇak kōla neelam mattugukkum pudaiyār kaḻani eḻilārum puḷḷambūdangudi tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vilangal – gōvardana mountain; kudaiyā koṇḍu – accepting it as umbrella; ēndi – effortlessly held; māri – rain; paḻudā – making it go waste; nirai – herds of cows; kāttu – protected; sadaiyān – rudran; ōda – as he ran (away from the battlefield); adal – battle-ready; vāṇan – bāṇāsuran’s; tadam – vast; tōḷ – shoulders; tuṇitta – one who severed; talaivan – kriṣṇa who is controller of all, his; idam – divyadēśam is; kudiyā – remaining with the clan; vaṇḍugaḷ – beetles; uṇṇa – to drink honey; kōlam – beautiful; neelam – karuneydal flower; mattu – honey; ugukkum – let out in abundance; pudai Ar – being vast; kaḻani – fertile fields’; eḻil – by beauty; ārum – complete; puḷḷambūdangudi tānē – it is the divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa who is controller of all, accepting gōvardan mountain as an umbrella, effortlessly held it, making the rain go waste, and protected the herds of cows; during the battle with bāṇāsuran, as rudran ran away, he severed the battle-ready bāṇāsuran’s vast shoulders; his divyadēśam is puḷḷambūdangudi where the vast, fertile fields are complete with beauty, are having beautiful karuneydal flowers which let out honey in abundance, to make the beetles remain with their clan and drink honey.

*kudaiyā …* – As a remedy for the hailstorm, he held a mountain as protection.

*ēndi* – Since it was done for the sake of others, it did not cause any pain for him.

*māri …* – To make the effort of indra, the leader, be wasted, he protected the cows which cannot even understand his favour.

*adal vāṇam …* – As rudra who considers himself to be īśvara (controller), ran away from the battle-field, emperumān severed the shoulders of bāṇāsura who had the urge to fight. kriṣṇa did not sever the head and only severed the shoulders thinking “His protector has run away; we should not sever his head”. kriṣṇa’s mercy is due to rudran abandoning his follower. tiruccanda viruttam 71 “*muṇḍan nīṟan makkaḷ veppumōdi angi ōdida*” (mundan nīṟan – Siva; veppu – fever; mōdi – kāḷi; angi – agni (deity for fire); all these deities ran away from the battlefield) – Seeing rudran who has anointed his body with ash, his children, deity of fever, kāḷi and agni ran away. “*nāṇi*” – He became embarrassed thinking “Did we come to kill the one who surrendered to those who ran away seeing the enemies?”, showed his mercy to bāṇan; just as one would show mercy towards a woman who has lost her husband.

*talaivan idam* – The abode of the one who continuously has such dominance.

*kudiyā …* – Beetles along with their children, grandchildren, wives et al, drank the honey. If a mosquito enters into an ocean, the ocean will not lose any of its water. It is only puḷḷambūdangudi which is beautiful due to having vast fertile fields where beautiful neelam flower is letting out a flood of honey.

## 5.1.8. Karaiyar neduvel

*kaṟaiyār neduvēl maṟamannar vīya visayan tēr kadavi iṟaiyān kaiyil niṟaiyāda muṇḍam niṟaitta endaiyidam maṟaiyāl muttī avai vaḷarkkum mannu pugaḻāl vaṇmaiyāl poṟaiyāl mikka andaṇar vāḻ puḷḷambūdangudi tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṟai Ar – with blood stains not disappeared; nedu – long; vēl – those who have the weapon, spear; maṟam – angry; mannar – kings; vīya – to be killed; visayan – arjunan’s; tēr – chariot; kadavi – conducted; iṟaiyān – rudran who considers himself to be lord, his; kai – attached to the hand; niṟaiyāda – cannot be filled by anyone; muṇḍam – brahmā’s skull; niṟaitta – one who filled; endai – my lord’s; idam – divyadēśam is; maṟaiyāl – by vēdams; muttī avai – three fires; vaḷarkkum – those who nurture; mannu – (due to that) firm; pugaḻāl – by fame; vaṇmaiyāl – by magnanimity; poṟaiyāl – by patience; mikka – very; andaṇar – best among brāhmaṇas; vāḻ – eternally residing; puḷḷambūdangudi tānē – it is divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My lord conducted arjunan’s chariot to have those angry kings who have the weapon, long spear with blood stains not having disappeared, killed; he filled brahmā’s skull which was attached to the hand of rudran who considers himself to be lord, could not be filled by anyone; his divyadēśam is puḷḷambūdangudi where the very best among brāhmaṇas who are like that due to their firm fame by nurturing three fires with vēdam, magnanimity and patience, are eternally residing.

*kaṟai Ar …* – To have the angry kings who have spear which have blood stains due to their not having time to wash the stains, killed, emperumān conducted the chariot for arjunan; rudran who considers himself to be the lord, due to brahmā’s curse, was having brahmā’s skull attached to his hand, which was never getting filled; the divyadēśam of my lord who filled that skull with his sweat.

*maṟaiyāl …* – The abode where best brāhmaṇas who have in abundance, firm fame of nurturing three fires with vēdam, magnanimity and patience, are residing.

## 5.1.9. Tunni mannum

*tunni maṇṇum viṇṇādum tōnṟādu iruḷāy mūdiya nāḷ annamāgi arumaṟaigaḷ aruḷic ceyda amalanidam minnu sōdi navamaṇiyum vēyin muttum sāmaraiyum ponnum ponni koṇarndu alaikkum puḷḷambūdangudi tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇṇum – bhūlōkam (Earth); viṇṇādum – svargam (heaven) etc on the sky; tōnṟādu – to be not seen; iruḷāy – being fully dark; tunni – densely; mūdiya – covered; nāḷ – on that day; annamāgi – accepting the form of a swan; aru – difficult to attain; maṟaigaḷai – vēdams; aruḷicceyda – one who mercifully taught; amalan – pure sarvēśvaran’s; idam – divyadēśam is; minnu – shining; sōdi – radiant; navamaṇiyum – navaratnams (nine types of gems); vēyil – scattered from the bamboo sticks; muttum – pearls; sāmaraiyum – cāmarams (hand fans); ponnum – gold; koṇarndu – brought; ponni – river tirukkāvēri; alaikkum – pushing; puḷḷambūdangudi tānē – it is divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

On that day when bhūlōkam and svargam etc on the sky were fully covered with darkness, accepting the form of a swan, the pure sarvēśvaran mercifully taught the difficult to attain vēdams; his divyadēśam is puḷḷambūdangudi where the river tirukkāvēri brought śiningly radiant nine types of gems, pearls which scattered from the bamboo sticks, cāmarams and gold, and pushed them.

*tunni …* – Darkness covered earth and sky; the day when darkness fully covered.

*annamāgi …* – Considering “These people are not qualified to serve and learn under an ācārya”, he assumed the form of a bird; just as he stood as the charioteer and instructed \[arjuna\]. To separate the entities who had mixed with asuras and became destroyed, he assumed the form of a swan which will separate milk and water \[from a mixture of both\].

*amalan idam* – What a purity where he helps without any expectation! Instead of helping, based on someone requesting, he helped as if it is for his own benefit!

*minnu …* – kāvēri is also having the same nature of emperumān who helps without any expectation. navaratnams which are shining and have no dirt on them. Unlike some gems which will shine outside but will be dirty inside, these are fully shining. The inside and outside are shining just as jñātā (knover) and jñānam (knowledge) are both shining on their own. ponni (kāvēri) will bring and push pearls shed by the bamboo sticks, cāmaram and gold saying “Accept them! Accept them!”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.1.10. Karra marittu

*kaṟṟā maṟittuk kāḷiyan tan senni nadunga nadam payinṟa poṟṟāmaraiyāḷ tan kēḷvan puḷḷambūdangudi tan mēl kaṟṟār paravum mangaiyar kōn kārār puyaṟkaik kalikanṟi sol tān īraindu ivai pādac cōra nillā tuyar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

A – grown up like a cow; kanṟu (kaṟṟu) – calves; maṟittu – one who blocked (and tended); kāḷiyan than – kāḷiyan’s; senni – head; nadunga – to shake; nadam – dance; payinṟa – one who did; pon – desirable; tāmaraiyāḷ than – for periya pirāttiyār who has lotus flower as her abode; kēḷvan – where sarvēśvaran, who is dear to her, is eternally residing; puḷḷambūdangudi than mēl – on the divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi; kaṟṟār – those who understand the greatness of bhāgavatas, and can learn that; paravum – praised by; mangaiyar – for those who are in tirumangai region; kōn – being the controller; kār Ar – completely black; puyal – like a cloud; kai – having magnanimity; kalikanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār’s; ivai – this; īraindu – ten; sol tān – pāsurams; pāda – as one learns; sōra – that which makes ātmā fall into narakam (hell) etc; tuyar – sins which give sorrow; nillā – will not remain

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, who is dear to periya pirāttiyār who has the desirable lotus flower as her abode, blocked and tended the calves which are grown up like cows; he danced on kāḷiyan’s head to shake it; on the divyadēśam named puḷḷambūdangudi where he is eternally residing, tirumangai āḻvār, who is praised by those who understand the greatness of bhāgavatas, and can learn that, and is the controller of those who are in tirumangai region and is having magnanimity like that of a completely black cloud, composed these ten pāsurams; for the one who learns these pāsurams, the sins which give sorrow to ātmā which makes the ātmā fall into narakam (hell) etc, will not remain.

*kaṟṟā maṟittu …* – For him tending the cows is like giving his presence to the assembly of nityasūris; while tending the cows, as the beautiful pond there was poisoned by kāḷiyan, kriṣṇa thought “We should drive him out of there” and danced on him to make him tremble.

*poṟṟāmariyāḷ kēḷvan* – He placed himself in danger without seeing his nature. This brave act will not match his tenderness for being śriya:pati (consort of śrī mahālakśmi).

*kaṟṟār …* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 128.103 “*rāmō rāmō rāma:*” (while śrī rāma ruled the kingdom, the people kept reciting rāma, rāma, rāma), there are many who can join two syllables and praise bhagavān. But āḻvār is praised by those who understand the greatness of bhāgavatas.

*kār Ar …* – Your magnanimity resembles a full loaded, black cloud which has risen.

*sol tān īraindu ivai pāda* – There is nothing sweeter than this padigam (decad).

sōra nillā tuyar tānē – The sins which will make the ātmā go down, will not remain.

## 5.2 Tam tam

## 5.2.1. Tam tam

*tām tam perumai aṟiyār tūdu vēndarkkāya vēndar ūr pōl kāndaḷ viral menkalai nanmadavār kūndal kamaḻum kūdalūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tām – He who is sarvajña (omniscient); tam perumai – his own greatness; aṟiyār – one who does not know; vēndarkku – for the pāṇḍavas; tūdu āy – being the messenger; vēndar – kriṣṇa, who is the king of kings, his; Ur – divyadēśam; kāndaḷ – like kāndaḷ flower \[flame lily\]; viral – having fingers; mel – soft; kalai – wearing vastrams (clothes); nal – distinguished; madavār – ladies’; kūndal – hair; kamaḻum – spreading fragrance; kūdalūr – divyadēśam named kūdalūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divine abode of kriṣṇa who is the king of kings, who is sarvajña yet does not know his own greatness, and who went as the messenger for pāṇḍavas, is the divyadēśam named kūdalūr where distinguished ladies have kāndaḷ flower like fingers, wear soft clothes and whose hair is spreading fragrance.

*tām* – Though he is omniscient on his own. Though śruti and smriti declare as in muṇḍaka upaniśat “*yassarvajña: sarvavit*” (one who knows the basic nature and basic qualities of all entities) and in śvētāśvatara upaniśat “… *parāsya śaktir vividaiva śrūyatē śvābhāvikī jñāna bala kriyāca”* (that supreme bhagavān who has full ability and natural knowledge, strength etc).

*tam perumai aṟiyār* – His devotees would enjoy him and will become immersed in him saying “What a simplicity of his, presenting himself in a humble way for his devotees!” But he cannot understand his greatness.

*tūdu …* – As said in [periya tirumoḻi 2.2.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/08/periya-thirumozhi-2-2-3/) “*innār tūdan ena ninṟān*” (to have the residents of this vast earth say “he is the messenger of pāṇḍavas”) and [tiruvāimoḻi 6.6.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-6-4-pidudai-nanmuganai/) “*nādudai mannarkkut tūdu sel nambikku*” (he went as the messenger on behalf of pāṇḍavas, the kings who are the leaders of the kingdom and hence became fully complete) – for the sake of others, he minimized his own stature and went as a messenger. Even those who are very lowly, will not agree to go as a messenger for others; unlike that he went as a messenger for those pāṇḍavas who were declared by him as the kings.

*vēndar Ur pōlum* – Though he minimized his own stature, there is none who would think of him in a lowly manner; his greatness is additionally appearing to be great due to his being king of kings.

*kāndaḷ …* – The ladies who are distinguished in all manner, due to having reddish kāndaḷ flower like fingers and wearing soft clothes.

*kūndal kamaḻum kūdalūrē* – Though this abode is the residence of the one who is praised in cāndōjña upaniśat as “*sarvaganda:*” (the origin of all fragrances), the fragrance from the hair of the ladies will suppress his fragrance and spread everywhere.

## 5.2.2. Serundin

*seṟundiṇ timil ēṟudaiya pinnai peṟundaṇ kōlam  peṟṟār ūr pōl naṟundaṇ tīndēn uṇḍa vaṇḍu kuṟinji pādum kūdalūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

seṟum – Charging at; tiṇ – strong; timil – humps; ēṟu – bulls; udaiya – having as challenge; pinnai – nappinnaip pirātti’s; peṟum – only deserving for her; taṇ – to cool down those who see her; kōlam – beauty; peṟṟār – kriṣṇa who acquired; Ur – divyadēśam is; naṟu – fragrant; taṇ – cool; tīn – sweet; tēn – honey; uṇḍa – drinking; vaṇḍu – beetles; kuṟinji – song named kuṟinji; pādum – singing; kūdalūr – divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa acquired the beauty of nappinnaip pirātti, which will cool down those who see her and is deserved only by her, by beating the challenge of the bulls with strong humps which came charging; his divine abode is the divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr where beetles are drinking fragrant, cool, sweet honey and singing the song named kuṟinji.

*seṟum …* – The bulls which are charging at the opponents and are having strong humps.

*pinnai peṟum taṇ kōlam peṟṟār Ur pōl* – The beauty which is present only on nappinnaip pirātti and will not stay on anyone else was acquired by kriṣṇa and he thought that he got unattainable benefit;  his abode is

*naṟum …* – Beetles which drank fragrant, cool, sweet honey, and being unable to stay still, due to the fluid which entered into them, will sing the tune named kuṟinji at all times, without any time restrictions.

## 5.2.3. Pillai uruvay

*piḷḷai uruvāyt tayir uṇḍu adiyēn uḷḷam pugunda oruvar ūr pōl kaḷḷa nārai vayaluḷ kayal mīn koḷḷai koḷḷum kūdalūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

piḷḷai uruvāy – Having the form of a child; tayir – curd; uṇḍu – mercifully consumed; adiyēn – I, the servitor, my; uḷḷam – in the heart; pugunda – entered; oruvar – where the distinguished kriṣṇa is residing; Ur – abode is; kaḷḷam – mischievous; nārai – bird named crane; vayaluḷ – in fertile fields; kayal mīn – fish named kayal \[carp\]; koḷḷai koḷḷum – stealing; kūdalūrē – divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Distinguished kriṣṇa who is having the form of a child, mercifully consumed curd and entered the heart of mine, the servitor; the abode where he is residing is the divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr where the mischievous bird crane is stealing kayal fish in fertile fields.

*piḷḷai uruvāyt tayir uṇḍu* … – Being sarvēśvaran, if he wanted to mercifully eat butter, people would not accept that; hence he took the form of child kriṣṇa and mercifully ate curd. In this manner he manifested his simplicity of not sustaining without the food item which is touched by his devotees, he made me exist fully for him, and when he got an opportunity where I cannot push him out, he entered my heart. Such emperumān’s abode.

*kaḷḷam …* – The cranes in that divydēśam will remain indifferent even when the fish keep banging at their feet and when the right prey is seen, they will charge at the prey and grab it. Their nature is similar to that of kriṣṇa who would pretend to be sleeping as said in siṟiya tirumadal “*ōrādavan pōl uṟangi*” (Sleeping as if he does not know what is happening around) when yaśōdāp pirātti is securing curd and butter, and as she steps away, he will steal them. Just as he caused agitation in the town, these would too.

## 5.2.4. Kurrer uruvin

*kūṟṟēr uruvin kuṟaḷāy nilam nīr ēṟṟān endai perumān ūr pōl sēṟṟēr uḻavar kōdaip pōdūṇ kōl tēn muralum kūdalūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kūṟu – to tell (to praise); ēr – being apt; uruvil – having form; kuṟaḷāy – being vāmanan \[dwarf\]; nilam – earth; nīr ēṟṟān – one who accepted as charity; endai – being my lord; perumān – kriṣṇa, who is the leader of my clan; Ur – abode is; sēṟu – in mud; ēr – who can plough with the plough; uḻavar – farmers; kōdai – placed on the hair; pōdu – honey in the flowers; ūṇ – drinking; kōl – living in the gardens; tēn – beetles; muralum – singing; kūdalūrē – divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being vāmanan, who is having aptly praiseworthy form, accepted the earth as charity; the abode of my lord, kriṣṇa, who is the leader of my clan, is the divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr where the beetles, living in the gardens, drinking honey from the flowers placed on the hair of the farmers who can plough in the mud with the plough, are singing.

*kūṟṟēr …* – Accepting the form of vāmanan who is having the desire as said in “*mamētam*” (why should I not have it?); alternative explanation – one who is having the form of vāmanan, where whoever saw that proclaimed “What an amazing dwarf form!” This is the abode where emperumān, who is the lord of my clan and who remained as if he accepted something which did not originally belong to him, by measuring the whole earth after accepting water, made me exist fully for him by that act.

*sēṟṟēr …* – The farmers who can run through their plough even in very muddy fields, were donning flowers on their hair. The beetles which drank from those flowers will sing more beautifully, even better than after drinking from fresh flowers on trees.

kōl tēn – Beetles from the gardens.

## 5.2.5. Tondar parava

*toṇḍar paravac cudar senṟu aṇava aṇḍattu amarum adigaḷ ūr pōl  vaṇḍal alaiyuḷ keṇḍai miḷirak koṇḍal adirum kūdalūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

toṇḍar – devotees; parava – as they praise; sudar – sun; senṟu – (his divine form) reached; aṇava – to touch; aṇḍattu – whole sky; amarum – omnipresent; adigaḷ – kriṣṇa, the lord, his; vaṇḍal – having sediment; alaiyuḷ – in water bodies having waves; keṇḍai – keṇḍai fish \[carp\]; miḷira – as they shine (due to their own lustre) (seeing that); koṇḍal – clouds; adirum – roaring; kūdalūrē – divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

As the devotees praise, kriṣṇa, the lord, \[as trivikrama\] had his divine form touch the sun, and remained omnipresent in the whole sky; the abode of such lord is the divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr where the keṇḍai fish shine in the water-bodies with sediment and having waves; seeing that, the clouds are roaring.

*toṇḍar …* – As said in viṣṇu darmam “*sangaissurāṇām …*” (groups of dēvas from the heavenly planets, groups of humans from earth, dwellers from celestial vehicles in the sky, glorified trivikrama. Let such trivikrama who measured the world be there for my auspiciousness), as the devotees gathered and praised, a part of his divine form \[i.e. divine foot\] reached up to the sun and the whole sky was pervaded by him, the lord. The divine abode of such lord.

*aṇḍattu amarum* – As the keṇḍai fish are shining due to their strength in water-bodies with sediment and having waves.

*koṇḍal adirum kūdalūrē* – Seeing the lustre on the fish, the cloud considers it to be lightning and roars with the noise of thunder which follows lightning usually. Their act is similar to vāmana being seen here while accepting the water and immediately seen as trivikrama up in the sky.

## 5.2.6. Takkan velvi

*takkan vēḷvi tagartta talaivan dukkam tudaitta tuṇaivar ūr pōl ekkalidu nuṇmaṇal mēl engum kokkin paḻam vīḻ kūdalūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

takkan – dakśa prajāpati’s; vēḷvi – yāgam (fire sacrifice); tagartta – one who destroyed; talaivan – rudran who is considering himself to be the chief; dukkam – sorrow; tudaitta – one who eliminated; tuṇaivar – the abode of kriṣṇa, the āpatsaka (companion during dangerous times); Ur – abode is; ekkal idu – formed as sediments; nuṇ maṇal mēl – on tiny sand particles; engum – everywhere; kokkin paḻam – mango fruits; vīḻ – falling; kūdalūrē – divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abode of kriṣṇa, the āpatsaka (companion during dangerous times) who eliminated the sorrow of rudran who is considering himself to be the chief and who destroyed dakśa prajāpati’s yāgam, is the divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr where mango fruits are falling everywhere on tiny sand particles which are formed as sediments.

*takkan …* – rudran is said to be “*dakśādvara dvamsan*” (one who destroyed dakśa’s fire sacrifice); this is the abode of emperumān who is the āpatsaka who eliminated the sorrow of rudran who is considering pridefully “I should be higher than everyone”.

*ekkal …* – When the mangoes have fallen in the sediments of tiny sand particles and are present, it appears that they have been buried there to ripen them.

## 5.2.7. Karundan kadalum

*karundaṇ kadalum malaiyum ulagum arundum adigaḷ amarum ūr pōl perundaṇ mullaip piḷḷai ōdi kurundam taḻuvum kūdalūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karu – blackish; taṇ – cool; kadalum – oceans; malaiyum – mountains; ulagum – (other) worlds; arundum – mercifully consuming; adigaḷ – sarvēśvaran who is the lord; amarum – eternally residing; Ur – abode is; peru – big; taṇ – cool; mullaip piḷḷai – creeper of mullai (jasmine); ōdi – spreading everywhere; kurundam – kurunda tree; taḻuvum – embracing to cover it; kūdalūrē – divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abode of sarvēśvaran who is the lord and who mercifully consumes blackish, cool oceans, mountains and the worlds, where he eternally resides is the divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr where big, cool creeper of mullai (jasmine) is spreading everywhere and embracing the kurunda tree to cover it.

*karum taṇ …* – The lord who consumed blackish, cool ocean, mountains which are like anchors for earth and other worlds, without them losing their shape, is firmly residing in this divyadēśam to protect everyone if such dangers occur again.

*perum taṇ …* – where big, cool jasmine creeper is covering the whole kurunda tree.

*kalaivāḻ piṇaiyōdu aṇaiyum tirunīr malai vāḻ endai maruvum ūr pōl ilai tāḻ tengin mēl ninṟu iḷanīr kulai tāḻ kidangin kūdalūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kalai – buck (male deer); piṇaiyōdu – with doe (female deer); aṇai – together; vāḻum – living; tirunīrmalai – in the divyadēśam named tirunīrmalai; vāḻ – mercifully residing with joy; endai – my lord; maruvum – firmly residing; Ur – abode is; tāḻ – well grown; ilai – having leaves; tengin mēl – on the coconut trees; ninṟu – present; iḷanīr kulai – bunches of tender coconuts; tāḻ – lowering on; kidangin – having betel leaf gardens; kūdalūrē – divaydēśam named tirukkūdalūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

The abode where my lord, who is mercifully residing with joy in the divyadēśam named tirunīrmalai, where buck is living together with its doe, is firmly residing is the divaydēśam named tirukkūdalūr which is having betel leaf gardens where the bunches of tender coconuts which are present on the coconut trees having well grown leaves, are lowering on those gardens.

*kalai vāḻ …* – Bucks are living together with the doe, embracing them in tirunīrmalai which is the residence of my lord; while he has that divyadēśam as well, this is the abode where he is firmly residing.

*ilai tāḻ …* – The coconut trees with well grown leaves, are present at the edge of the betel leaf gardens; when the tender coconuts lower on the gardens, it appears as if those gardens are filled with the tender coconut water and are covered with the betel leaves.

## 5.2.9. Perugu kadal

*perugu kādal adiyēn uḷḷam urugap pugunda oruvar ūr pōl arugu kaidai malarak keṇḍai kurugenṟu anjum kūdalūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

perugu – increasing; kādal – having desire; adiyēn – this servitor’s; uḷḷam – mind; uruga – to melt; pugundu – entered; oruvar – where the distinguished sarvēśvaran is residing; Ur – abode is; arugu – in close proximity; kaidai – tāḻai (wild plants found on sea shores); malara – as they blossom (seeing that); keṇḍai – keṇḍai fish; kurugu enṟu – considering them to be stork; anjum – fearing; kūdalūrē – divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

The abode where the distinguished sarvēśvaran, who entered in my mind, which is having increasing desire, to melt it, is residing, is the divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr where as the tāḻai plants blossom in close proximity, the keṇḍai fish, seeing that, are fearing, considering them to be stork.

*perugu kādal …* – To melt my heart, which is having increasing love similar to a flood which increases day by day, the distinguished sarvēśvaran entered in there. The abode where he resides.

*arugu kaidai …* – As the tāḻai plant blossoms, the keṇḍai fish considered that to be stork and feared. Though both are present eternally, the fear will also remain forever.

## 5.2.10. Kavip perunir

*kāvip perunīr vaṇṇan kaṇṇan mēvit tigaḻum kūdalūr mēl kōvait tamiḻāl kaliyan sonna pāvaip pādap pāvam pōmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kāvi – like karuneydal (black coloured flower); peru – abundant; nīr – ocean having water; vaṇṇan – having complexion; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇan; mēvi – remaining fixed; tigaḻum – eternally residing in a shining manner; kūdalūr mēl – on the divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr; kōvai – having proper qualities; tamiḻāl – with tamiḻ language; kaliyan – āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; pāvai – pāsurams; pāda – as one sings; pāvam – sins; pōm – will be eliminated

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams in tamiḻ language, having proper qualities on kriṣṇan who is having the complexion of karu neydal flower and ocean with abundant water, and is remaining fixed and eternally residing in a shining manner, in the divyadēśam named tirukkūdalūr; the sins of those who sing these pāsurams, will be eliminated.

*kāvi …* – On tirukkūdalūr where kriṣṇan who is having form with complexion like that of karu neydal flower and huge ocean, is eternally residing in a shining manner, with full agreement of his heart.

## 5.3 Venri mamalu

## 5.3.1. Venri mamalu

*venṟi māmaḻu ēndi mun maṇ misai mannarai mūveḻu kāl konṟa dēva! nin kurai kaḻal toḻuvadōr vagai enakku aruḷ puriyē manṟil māmboḻil nuḻai tandu malligai mauvalin pōdalartti tenṟal māmaṇam kamaḻ tara varu tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tenṟal – southerly breeze; manṟil – present in the gaps; mām poḻil – in the mango gardens; nuḻai tandu – entered; malligai – jasmine’s; mauvalin – mullai (another variety of jasmine); pōdu – flowers; alartti – made them blossom; mā – great; maṇam – fragrance; kamaḻ tara – to spread in the world; varu – coming and roaming; tiruveḷḷaṟai – in the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷaṟai; ninṟānē – oh lord who is mercifully present!; mun – previously; venṟi – giving victory; mā – big; maḻu – the weapon named paraśu (axe); ēndi – carried; maṇ misai – on the earth; mannarai – kings; mū eḻu kāl – twenty one generations; konṟa – killed; dēva – Oh lord!; nin – your; kurai – resounding; kaḻal – divine feet; toḻuvadu – to surrender; ōr vagai – one way; enakku – for me; aruḷ puri – should mercifully show

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh lord who is mercifully present in the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷaṟai where southerly breeze entered the mango gardens which are present in the gaps/spaces , made the jasmine flowers blossom and is coming and roaming to spread the great fragrance in the world! Oh lord, who previously carried the big weapon named paraśu which gives victory and killed twenty one generations of kings! You should mercifully show a way for me to surrender unto your resounding divine feet.

*venṟi …* – āḻvār is saying “Is it as difficult to protect me as protecting the world by eliminating the kings who tormented it?”

*mun* – Are you just starting to eliminate the enemies today? (Haven’t you been doing this for long?)

*venṟi …* – Wielding the axe which can bring victory to anyone who is wielding it and is having greatness above and beyond that of the enemies, as if it is for decoration, previously, you gathered kings of twenty one generations and destroyed them; oh one who is considering this act of eliminating the hurdles as your own benefit rather than helping others, and showing it in the lustre of your divine form! As said in śrī rāmāyaṇa yudda kāṇḍam “*abhiśicya ca lankāyām rākśasēndram vibhīśaṇam* I *krutakrutyas tadā rāmō* ***vijvara: pramōda ha*** īī” (śrī rāma, on completing the coronation of vibhīśaṇa as the king of demons in lankā, felt relieved of his fever, and was joyous that his task has been completed).

emperumān asks “Yes. We did it back then. What shall I do for you now?” āḻvār says

*nin …* – You should grant your mercy so that I could do kainkaryam (service) matching my true nature, at your divine feet which are decorated by resounding anklets.

*manṟil …* – All the objects in that town exist for the sake of others. The goal is to remain for others rather than remaining for self. Entering the mango gardens which have dense growth and are present in the open spaces, the southerly breeze makes the different types of jasmine flowers blossom, accepting their fragrance on its body, and is roaming here. Oh one who is present in such tiruveḷḷaṟai! For the desires of the residents of the town to be fulfilled, they need not go anywhere else. The breeze is having cillness, fragrance, pleasantry and tenderness. śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 1.72 “*padma kēsara samsruśta:*” (fragrance carrying lotus pollens) – eliminating the extraneous aspects, just touching the flower instead of going deep into it; *vrukśāntara vinisruta:* –  Since there is no scope for sun’s rays entering in, the breeze would travel only in the gaps between the trees. periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.8.9 “*kunṟūdu poḻil nuḻaindu”* (The southerly breeze entered the gardens on the mountains) – entering candanagiri (sandalwood mountain – mountain like bosoms which are anointed with sandalwood paste); *kodiyidaiyār mulai aṇavi* (touching the bosom of the ladies who have slender waist) – touching/caressing the bosoms which are upset; *manṟudu tenṟaluga* – Having got control of those bosoms also, the breeze was roaming outside with pride. Here, āḻvār is explaining the breeze as a cētana (sentient person).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.3.2. Vasaiyil nanmarai

*vasaiyil nānmaṟai kedutta ammalar ayaṟku aruḷi mun parimugamāy isaikoḷ vēda nūl enṟivai payandavanē! enakku aruḷ puriyē uyarkoḷ mādavip pōdodu ulāviya mārudam vīdiyin vāy tisai ellām kamaḻum poḻil sūḻ tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uyar koḷ – growing tall in the sky; mādavi – on kurukkatti trees; pōdōdu – while they blossom (embraced); vīdiyin vāy – in every street; ulāviya – blowing; mārudam – wind; tisai ellām – in all directions; kamaḻum – spreading the fragrance; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē – Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai!; vasai il – faultless; nāl maṟai – four vēdams; kedutta – one who lost; ammalar – present in the lotus flower in the divine navel; ayaṟku – for brahmā; aruḷi – showing mercy; mun – in the past; pari mugamāy – being hayagrīva; isai koḷ – having nice tone; vēdam – vēdams; nūl – śāstrams; enṟu – these; payandavanē – oh one who brought them in to existence!; enakku – for me; aruḷ puri – kindly grant your mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai where the wind is blowing in every street and in all directions, embracing the mādavi trees which grow tall in the sky while they blossom and spreading the fragrance, and is surrounded by gardens! Oh you who incarnated as hayagrīva and brought vēdams and śāstrams into existence, by showing mercy to brahmā who is present on the lotus flower in your divine navel and who lost the faultless, four vēdams! Kindly grant your mercy for me.

*vasai …* – Granting four vēdams which don’t have four faults such as vipralamba (deceit) etc. As said in taittirīya upaniśat “*dātā yatā pūrvam akalpayat*” (The lord created everything as existed previously), emperumān said “You create them as they existed” and he lost the vēdams in the hands of asuras. He then stood with tears in his eyes as said in “*vēdā mē paramam cakśur vēda mē paramam danam*” (vēdams are my best eyes and best wealth) and cried out. emperumān granted his mercy upon such brahmā.

*ammalar ayaṟku aruḷi* – He prayed to emperumān standing in his stature.

*mun pari mugamāy* – emperumān considered “brahmā will withdraw from learning if he had to serve an ācārya and learn from him” and hence he remained as hayagrīva and instructed him. This is similar to how he instructed arjuna being his charioteer.

*isai koḷ …* – Oh one who created vēdam which has nice music, itihāsams etc! You should kindly grant your mercy upon me. nūl indicates śāstram. Alternatively – when nūl indicates the other itihāsams, purāṇams etc, as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.22.38 “*tat sarvam vaiharēstanu:*” (Everything is hari’s body) – since he is authoring these through riśis et al, who are his body, it can still mean bhagavān only.

*uyar koḷ mādavi …* – At the apt times in mādavi trees which have grown to cover the whole sky.

*vīdiyin vāy* – On the streets.

*ulāviya mārudam* – The wandering breeze is spreading the fragrance in all directions and is surrounded by gardens.
