*veyyanāy ulagēḻudan nalindavan udalagam iru piḷavāk kaiyil nīḷ ugirp padaiyadu vāyttavanē! enakku aruḷ puriyē maiyinār taruvarālinam pāya vaṇ tadattidaik kamalangaḷ deyva nāṟum oṇ poygaigaḷ sūḻ tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mai Ar taru – being very black; varāl – fish; inam – school of; vaṇ – beautiful; tadattu ida – in the ponds; pāya – as they jump into; kamalangaḷ – lotus flowers (there, blossomed); deyvam – in the best way; nāṟum – spreading fragrance; oṇ – beautiful; poygaigaḷ – by ponds; sūḻ tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē – oh one who is mercifully present in tiruveḷḷaṟai which is surrounded!; veyyanāy – being very cruel; ulagu ēḻ – seven worlds; udan – together; nalindavan – hiraṇya who tormented, his; udal – in the body; agam – inner parts; iru piḷavā – to become two parts; kaiyil – in his divine hands; nīḷ – long; ugir – nails; adu – such; padai – as weapon; vāyttavanē – oh one who has!; enakku – for me; aruḷ puri – kindly grant your mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is mercifully present in tiruveḷḷaṟai which is surrounded by beautiful ponds where schools of very black fish jump into those ponds and where the lotus flowers are spreading fragrance in the best way! Oh one who has long nails in your divine hands as the weapon to make the inner part of the body of the very cruel hiraṇya who tormented the seven worlds together, split into two parts! Kindly grant your mercy for me.

*veyyanāy …* – hiraṇya was very cruel to torment the seven worlds together; to have such hiraṇya’s body become two parts, emperumān worked with his divine nails as the weapon, since hiraṇya had a boon that will not let emperumān use the divine chakra against him. Oh such emperumān!

*enakku aruḷ puriyē* – You should eliminate my hurdles and kindly grant your mercy to me.

*mai …* – There is a species of fish which is very black, named varāl. Schools of such fish tear into the flowers and jump into the beautiful ponds; oh one who is standing in tiruveḷḷaṟai where such lotus flowers are spreading their fragrance,

## 5.3.4. Vambariyuga

*vāmbariyuga mannar tam uyir sega aivargatku arasaḷitta kāmbinār tiruvēngadap poruppa! nin kādalai aruḷ enakku māmboḻil taḷir kōdiya madakkuyil vāyadu tuvarppeyda tīmbalanganit tēnadu nugar tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mām poḻil – in mango groves; taḷir – their sprouts; kōdiya – pecking; madam – humble; kuyil – cuckoos; vāyadu – in their mouth; tuvarppu – astringent taste; eyda – as they attained (to change that); tī – sweet; palam kani – in jack fruit; tēnadu – honey; nugar – drinking; tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē – Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai!; vām – charging at; pari – horses; uga – to be destroyed; mannar tam – kings’; uyir – lives; sega – to be destroyed; aivargatku – for panca pāṇḍavas; arasu – kingdom; aḷitta – one who granted; kāmbu Ar – filled with bamboo; tiruvēngadap poruppa – Oh one who is residing in the divine hill named tiruvēngadam!; nin kādalai – parama bhakti towards you; enakku – for me; aruḷ – you should kindly grant

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai where humble cuckoos are pecking the sprouts in the mango groves and having attained the astringent taste in their mouths, they are going and drinking the honey in the sweet jack fruit! Oh one who is residing in the divine hill named tiruvēngadam which is filled with bamboo and who granted the kingdom for panca pāṇḍavas to have the horses which came charging, destroyed and to have the lives of the kings destroyed! You should kindly grant parama bhakti towards you.

*vām pari …* – To have the horses which are hopping and charging, destroyed and to have the kings who ride those horses, killed, kriṣṇa gave the throne to the pāṇḍavas. He showed his partiality towards pāṇḍavas, by destroying those with the (horse) army.

*kāmbinār …* – Oh one who has the mountain named tiruvēngadam which has abundance of bamboo.

*nin kādalai aruḷ enakku* – Your highness should kindly grant me parama bhakti which is the stage before kainkaryam at your highness’ divine feet.

*mām poḻil …* – After entering the mango grove, the female cuckoo pecked the sprouts in there.

*vāyadu tuvarppeyda …* – Considering “I should change the taste in my mouth to some other taste”, it consumed the honey in the sweet jack fruit.

## 5.3.5. Manavel onkan

*mānavēl oṇkaṇ madavaral maṇmagaḷ aḻunga munnīrp parappil ēnamāgi anṟu iru nilam idandavanē! enakku aruḷ puriyē kāna māmullai kaḻaik karumbu ēṟi veṇmuṟuval seydu alarginṟa tēnin vāy malar murugu ugukkum tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kānam – present in the forest; mā – big; mullai – jasmine creeper; karumbu – sugarcane’s; kaḻai – up to the top; ēṟi – stretched and spread; veṇ – whitish; muṟuval – gentle smile; seydu – like doing; alarginṟa – blossoming; malar – (jasmine) flower; tēnin – beetles’; vāy – in the mouth; murugu – honey; ugukkum – flowing into; tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē – Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai!; mānam – huge; vēl – like the weapon, spear; oḷ – beautiful; kaṇ – having eyes; madavaral – having noble qualities such as patience; maṇ magaḷ – śrī bhūmip pirātti; aḻunga – as she was submerged in the ocean of deluge; anṟu – at that time; munnīr – that ocean’s; parappil – in the great water; ēnamāgi – being mahāvarāham; iru nilam – the vast earth; idandavanē – Oh one who dug out from the wall of the universe!; enakku – for me who is a seeker; aruḷ puri – kindly grant your mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai where the honey is flowing into the mouth of the beetles from the jasmine flower which is blossoming as if gently smiling in a whitish manner, on the big jasmine creeper which is stretching and spreading on to the top of the sugar canes which are present in the forest! Oh one who dug out the vast earth from the wall of the universe, being mahāvarāham, at the time when śrī bhūmip pirātti, who is having huge spear like beautiful eyes and noble qualities such as patience, was submerged in the great water of the ocean of deluge! Kindly grant your mercy to me who is a seeker.

*māna vēl …* – Having beautiful eyes which resemble a spear which has a huge leaf, having noble qualities such as kśamā (patience) etc, śrī bhūmip pirātti, became submerged through her possession (earth).

*mun nīrp parappil …* – Accepting a varāha form, which does not hesitate stepping into the mud and vast waters in the deluge, oh one who dug out the earth from the wall of the universe and arose!

*enakku aruḷ puriyē* – For you who protected the earth which had not even prayed to do so, is it difficult to protect me who is praying to do so?

*kāna mā mullai …* – The abode is having the qualities of the five different lands named neydal (ocean side), marudam (fertile field side), kuṟinji (mountain side), pālai (desert side) and mullai (forest side). The jasmine in the forest which is located near the fertile fields which is adjacent to the town, stretching and spreading on up to the top of the sugar cane, is blossoming as if gently smiling due to the joy of climbing onto a tall place. They shed honey into the mouth of the beetles which came seeking the honey.

## 5.3.6. Pongu nilmudi

*pongu nīḷmudi amarargaḷ toḻudu eḻa amudinaik koduttaḷippān angu ōr āmai adāgiya ādi! nin adimaiyai aruḷ enakku tangu pēdaiyōdu ūdiya madugaram taiyalār kuḻal aṇaivān tingaḷ tōy senni mādam senṟaṇai tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tangu – residing on the flower; pēdaiyōdu – with the female beetle; ūdiya – had romantic-quarrel; madugaram – beetle; taiyalār – ladies’; kuḻal – hair; aṇaivān – reached (to remain in hiding there); tingaḷ – on the moon; tōy – reaching up to; senni – having peaks; mādam – mansions; senṟu – reached; aṇai – remained together; tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē – Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai!; pongu – well grown; nīḷ – remaining for a long time; mudi – having crowns; amarargaḷ – dēvatās such as indra et al; toḻudu – to surrender unto (him); eḻa – as they tried; angu – at that time (for them); amudinai – nectar; koduttu – gave; aḷippān – to protect; ōr – unique; adu – such strong; āmaiyāgiya – one who accepted kūrmāvatāram; ādi – Oh cause!; nin – towards you; adimaiyai – kainkaryam; enakku – for me; aruḷ – should kindly grant

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai where the beetle which was residing on the flower along with the female beetle, reached up to the mansions which have tall peaks which reach up to the moon, to hide in the hair of the ladies, and remained together! Oh the cause of all, who, at that time accepted a unique, very strong kūrmāvatāram to give nectar to dēvatās such as indra et al who are having well grown crowns which remain for a long time! You should kindly grant me kainkaryam towards you.

*pongu nīḷ mudi …* – Well expanded dēvatās having eternal crowns, desired to worship the lotus feet of emperumān; to eliminate the danger caused by asuras and protect them; he accepted a tortoise form which can sustain the mandara mountain, protected them and became the reason for their existence!

*nin adimaiyai aruḷ enakku* – For me, your highness should grant service unto your divine feet and mercifully grant my existence.

*tangu …* – With the female beetle which resided with it in the flower. The male beetle cited some reason or the other and had a romantic-quarrel, and thought “I should hide in a place which is not known to my lady beetle” and went to the mansion which has tall peaks which reach up to the moon, with the intent to hide inside the hair of the ladies.

*āṟinōdu oru nāngudai nedu mudi arakkan tan siram ellām vēṟu vēṟuga villadu vaḷaittavanē! enakku aruḷ puriyē māṟil sōdiya maradagap pāsadait tāmarai malar vārnda tēṟal māndi vaṇḍu innisai mural tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māṟu il – matchless; sōdiya – having radiance; maradagam – like maradaga gem \[emerald\]; pāsu – having greenish colour; adai – having leaves; tāmarai – lotus’; malar – from the flowers; vārnda – flowing; tēṟal – honey; māndi – drank; vaṇḍu – beetles; in – sweet; isai – songs; mural – singing; tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē – Oh who one is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai!; āṟinōdu – with six heads; oru nāngu udai – having another four heads; nedu – tall; mudi – having crowns; arakkan than – rāvaṇāsuran’s; siram ellām – all the heads; vēṟu vēṟuga – to be separated and knocked down; adu – such; vil – bow; vaḷaittavanē – Oh cakravartit tirumagan who drew and launched!; enakku – for me; aruḷ puri – kindly grant your mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh who one is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai where beetles which drank the honey which was flowing from the lotus flowers which are having green colour leaves like maradaga gem with matchless radiance, are singing sweet songs! Oh cakravartit tirumagan who drew and launched your great bow to have all the heads of rāvaṇāsuran who had ten heads with crowns, to have them separated and fall down! Kindly grant your mercy for me.

*āṟinōdu …* – Oh one who drew your bow to break the ten heads of the ten headed rāvaṇan, into pieces! You should kindly grant your mercy on me.

*māṟil …* – Having drunk the honey flowing from the lotus flowers which are having greenish leaves which have the radiance of maradaga gem, the beetles are singing sweet songs.

## 5.3.8. Mun ivvelulagu

*mun ivvēḻulagu uṇarvinṟi iruḷ miga umbargaḷ toḻudētta annamāgi anṟu arumaṟai payandavanē! enakku aruḷ puriyē  mannu kēdagai sūdagam enṟivai vanattidaic curumbu inangaḷ tennavenṟu vaṇḍu innisai mural tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mannu – blossoming eternally; kēdagai – tāḻai (wild plants found on sea shores); sūdagam – mango trees; enṟu ivai – having these; vanattu idai – in the middle of the gardens; surumbu – beetles of the type “surumbu”; inangaḷ – swarms; tenna enṟu – singing “tenna tenna” (hearing that); vaṇḍu – beetles; in isai – (being well matured) enjoyable song; mural – singing; tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē – Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai!; mun – previously; ivvēḻulagu – these seven worlds; uṇarvu inṟi – as they remained without any knowledge; iruḷ miga – remaining covered by darkness; umbargaḷ – dēvatās starting with brahmā; toḻudu – as they vorśipped (you); ētta – praised; anṟu – at that time; annamāgi – assuming the form of a hamsa \[swan\]; aru maṟai – vēdas which are difficult to attain; payandavanē – Oh one who brought to existence!; enakku – for me; aruḷ puri – kindly grant mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟa which has gardens of mango trees having tāḻai which are blossoming eternally where swarms of beetles of the type “surumbu” are singing “tenna tenna” and hearing that, the beetles are singing enjoyable song! Oh one who brought vēdas which are difficult to attain, to existence, assuming the form of a hamsa at the time when dēvatās starting with brahmā vorśipped and praised you, previously, when these seven worlds remained without any knowledge being covered with darkness! Kindly grant your mercy for me.

*mun ivvēḻulagu …* – Previously, when this world became covered with darkness having lost the knowledge, brahmā et al surrendered at the divine feet of emperumān and praised him; to separate the vēdam which became mixed with asuras (demons) and lost its form, he assumed the form of hamsa which can separate water and milk; oh one who brought vēdam which is more difficult than emperumān to attain, and which can fully speak about emperumān’s nature, into existence! You should kindly grant your mercy towards me.

*mannu …* – In the garden which has dense tāḻai with flowers always and mango trees, surumbu beetles drank the honey, and due to the substance which went in, not allowing them to remain calm, they started singing “tenna, tenna” and the beetles will sing songs which are well matured.

## 5.3.9. Angu mavali

*āngu māvali vēḷviyil irandu senṟu agalidam muḻudinaiyum pāngināl koṇḍa parama! niṟpaṇindu eḻuvēn enakku aruḷ puriyē ōngu piṇḍiyin semmalar ēṟi vaṇḍu uḻidara māvēṟit tīnguyil miḻaṟṟum padappai tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōngu – well grown, tall; piṇḍiyin – aśōka tree’s; semmalar – on the reddish flowers; vaṇḍu – beetles; ēṟi – climbed; uḻi tara – as they roam around; tīn – having sweet voice; kuyil – cuckoos; mā ēṟi – climbing the mango trees and standing there; miḻaṟṟum – making sweet, incoherent sounds; padappai – having creeper gardens; tiruveḷḷaṟai ninṟānē – Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai!; māvali – mahābali’s; vēḷviyil – in the sacrifice; āngu – in that great assembly; senṟu – went; irandu – begged; agal – vast; idam muḻudinaiyum – all of the earth; pāngināl – due to honesty (considering that to be mahābali’s place); koṇḍa – accepted and brought under his control; parama – Oh one who is greater than all!; nin – you; paṇindu – to surrender; eḻuvēn – for me who is set out to; enakku – for me; aruḷ puri – kindly grant your mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is mercifully residing in tiruveḷḷaṟai which is having creeper gardens where atop the well grown tall aśōka tree, as the beetles climb on the reddish flowers and roam around there, the cuckoos with sweet voice are climbing the  mango trees, standing there, making sweet, incoherent sounds! Oh one who is greater than all, who went to the great assembly of mahābali’s fire sacrifice, begged for all of the vast earth and due to his honesty, accepted and brought the earth under his control! Kindly grant your mercy for me who is set out to surrender unto you.

*āngu māvali …* – Oh one who is greater than all, who went in that place of mahābali’s fire sacrifice, assumed the form of an alms-seeker and measured the entire earth! Though emperumān could have severed his head just as he did for rāvaṇa et al, he did not do that and retained the worlds, since mahābali had magnanimity, and hence he made himself an alms-seeker and accepted the earth as if it is his \[mahābali’s\] possession.

*nin paṇindu eḻuvēn enakku aruḷ puriyē* – Is my surrender not as good as indra’s surrender?

*ōngu …* – As the aśōka tree which has grown tall to fill the entire sky has reddish flowers blossomed, the beetles roam around thinking “let us drink honey from these flowers”, the cuckoos thought of them to be fire, became frightened and climbed on the mango trees which were there, started crying out thinking that the beetles were caught in the fire, as if saying incoherently “they are getting killed”. Though their stay is permanent there, they will also have fear perpetually.

## 5.3.10. Majula mani

*manjulā maṇi mādangaḷ sūḻ tiruveḷḷaṟai adan mēya anjanam puraiyum tiru uruvanai ādiyai amudattai nanju ulāviya vēl valavan kalikanṟi sol aiyiraṇḍum enjal inṟi ninṟu ēṟṟa vallār imaiyōrkku arasu āvargaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

manju – up to the region of clouds; ulā – reaching up to; maṇi – embossed with precious gems; mādangaḷ – by mansions; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruveḷḷaṟai adan – in the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷaṟai; mēya – one who is residing eternally; anjanam puraiyum – like black pigment; tiru – beautiful; uruvanai – having form; ādiyai – being the cause of the world; amudattai – on sarvēśvaran who is enjoyable; nanju ulāviya – moving around like poison; vēl valavan – one who rules over the spear; kali kanṟi – āḻvār; sol – mercifully spoke; ai iraṇḍum – these ten pāsurams; enjal inṟi – without any shortcoming; ninṟu – remaining firm; ētta vallār – those who can praise; imaiyōrkku – for nityasūris; arasāvargaḷ – will be desirable like kings

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār who rules over the spear which is moving around like poison, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams on sarvēśvaran who is having black pigment like beautiful form, the cause of the world, is enjoyable and is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruveḷḷaṟai which is surrounded by mansions which are embossed with precious gems and which are reaching up to the region of clouds. Those who can firmly praise these ten pāsurams, without any shortcoming, will be desirable like kings for the nityasūris.

*manju …* – tiruveḷḷaṟai which is surrounded by mansions which are embossed with precious gems, are reaching up to the region of clouds. mēya – eternally residing.

*anjanam …* – He is having such physical beauty that he cannot be abandoned even if he is not present in front of us; his aptness will not let us abandon him even if he is not beautiful; his enjoyability will not let us abandon him even if he is not apt for us.

*nanju …* – nityasūris will abandon śrīvaikuṇṭanātan and desire those who can praise/recite these ten pāsurams without missing out any of the pāsurams, which were mercifully spoken by āḻvār who has the spear which is like poison and will kill when seen.

## 5.4 Undi mel

## 5.4.1. Undi mel

*undi mēl nānmuganaip padaittān ulagu uṇḍavan endai pemmān imaiyōrgaḷ tādaikku idam enbarāl sandinōdu maṇiyum koḻikkum punal kāviri andi pōlum niṟattār vayal sūḻ tennarangamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sandinōdu – With sandalwood logs; maṇiyum – precious gems; koḻikkum – bringing along, while coming; punal – having water; kāviri – by the sacred kāviri river; andipōlum – like evening time; niṟam – by the colour; Ar – complete; vayal – by fertile fields; sūḻ – surrounded; then – beautiful; arangam – divyadēśam named tiruvarangam; undi mēl – (on his) divine navel; nānmuganai – Four-headed brahmā; padaittān – one who created; ulagu – worlds (during deluge); uṇḍavan – one who mercifully consumed and placed in his divine stomach; endai – for the elders starting with my father; pemmān – one who is the lord; imaiyōrkku – for nityasūris; tādaikku – for sarvēśvaran, who is the lord; idam enbar – is explained as the abode

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The beautiful divaydēśam named śrīrangam is surrounded by the kāviri river which is having sacred water which brings in sandalwood logs and precious gems, and fertile fields which are complete due to having the colour of the evening time. It is said to be the abode of sarvēśvaran who created four-headed brahmā in his divine navel, mercifully consumed the worlds and placed them in his stomach, is the lord of my elders starting with my father and is the lord of nityasūris.

*undi mēl nānmuganaip padaittān* – He himself created everything up to brahmā’s creation, with his own hands, and then thinking “We should create the effectual entities here through brahmā”, created four-headed brahmā in the lotus flower in his divine navel.

*ulagu uṇḍavan* – As the praḷayam (deluge) was about to consume everyone here, he placed the earth in his stomach and protected.

*endai pemmān* – One who became the lord of my clan by manifesting his being the creator of all and the friend in need.

*imaiyōr …* – \[Wise people\] will say “this is the abode of the lord of nityasūris who are never touched by the samsāram \[materialistic realm\]. Even nityasūris who are spoken about in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷai – udan kūduvadu enṟukolō*” (when will I enter the groups of nityasūris), will desire this abode and remain flattened here.

*sandu …* – kāviri which brings along sandalwood and precious gems and pushes them out; andi – sandyā; the fertile fields which are having dark colour like that of the evening time; the beautiful śrīrangam which is surrounded by these. As said in periya tirumoḻi 10.1.1 “*karu nel sūḻ kaṇṇamangai*” (tirukkaṇṇamangai surrounded by dark paddy crops), since the crops are ready for harvest, they appear dark everywhere. If it is insisted that sandyā time will be reddish, it can be said that “surrounded by paddy crops which are ripened at the top \[hence appearing reddish\]”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.4.2. Vaiyam undu

*vaiyam uṇḍu ālilai mēvum māyan maṇi nīḷ mudip paigoḷ nāgattaṇaiyān payilum idam enbarāl taiyal nallār kuḻal mālaiyum maṟṟavar tadamulaic ceyya sāndum kalandiḻi punal sūḻ tennarangamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nal – having noble conduct; taiyalār – ladies’; kuḻal – decorating the hair; mālaiyum – flower garland; maṟṟu – further; avar – such ladies’; tadam – vast; mulai – anointed on the bosoms; seyya – reddish; sāndum – sandalwood paste (with these); kalandu – mixed (and become slushy); iḻi – flowing; punal – by (kāviri) water; sūḻ – surrounded; tennarangam – beautiful divyadēśam named śrīrangam; vaiyam – earth; uṇḍu – mercifully consumed (during deluge); ālilai – on a banyan leaf; mēvum – fitting well and mercifully resting; māyan – being the one with amazing ability; maṇi – embossed with precious gems; nīḷ – tall; mudi – having crown; pai koḷ – vast; nāgam – tiruvanatāḻvān (ādiśēśan); aṇaiyān – sarvēśvaran who is having as mattress; payilum – eternally residing; idam enbar – said to be his abode

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The beautiful divaydēśam named śrīrangam, surrounded by the kāviri river which is flowing with water mixed with the flower garland decorating the hair of the ladies and the reddish sandalwood paste anointed on the vast bosoms of those ladies, is said to be the abode of sarvēśvaran, who mercifully consumed the earth and is fitting well and mercifully resting on a banyan leaf, who is with amazing ability, who is having tall crown embossed with precious gems, and who is having tiruvanantāḻvān as vast mattress.

*vaiyam uṇḍu …* – emperumān is having amazing ability to mercifully rest on a just-sprouted banyan leaf during deluge after placing the vast earth in his stomach.

*maṇi …* – Having tall, divine crown which signifies his reign over everyone and is mercifully resting on tiruvanantāḻvān who has the vastness to let emperumān rest on him. They say that this is the abode of such emperumān.

*taiyal nallār …* – Ladies who are wearing flowers on their hair and have applied kumkum (vermillon) on their bosoms. They will wake up and go for bath during brahma muhūrtam (time before sunrise); the kāviri river is flowing with water which has the garlands from their hair and the kumkum.

## 5.4.3. Pandu ivvaiyam

*paṇḍu ivvaiyam aḷappān senṟu māvali kaiyil nīr koṇḍa āḻit tadakkaik kuṟaḷan idam enbarāl vaṇḍu pādum maduvār punal vandiḻi kāviri aṇḍa nāṟum poḻil sūḻndu aḻagār tennarangamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu – beetles; pādum – to sing; madu – honey; vār – flowing; punal – water; vandu – came; iḻi – flowing; kāviri – by the sacred kāviri; aṇḍam – all over the sky; nāṟum – spreading fragrance; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻndu – surrounded; aḻagu Ar – very beautiful; tennarangam – divyadēśam named śrirangam; paṇḍu – in the past; iv vaiyam – this earth; aḷappān – to measure and capture; senṟu – went; māvali – mahābali’s; kaiyil – from the hand; nīr – water given for charity; āḻi – which holds tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); tadam – big; kai – on the divine hand; koṇḍa – accepted; kuṟaḷan – vāmanan’s; idam enbar – said as abode

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The very beautiful divyadēśam named śrīrangam which is surrounded by the sacred kāviri in which water came flowing with honey to make the beetles sing and with gardens which are spreading fragrance all over the sky, is said as the abode of vāmanan, who in the past, went to mahābali to measure and capture the earth, and accepted on his divine hand which can hold the divine chakra, the water which was given as \[an affirmation for\] charity from mahābali’s hand.

*paṇḍu …* – To retrieve the earth which was captured by mahābali, śrī vāmanan went to his sacrificial arena and accepted water on his divine hands which can hold the divine chakra; they say that the abode where such emperumān resides.

*vaṇḍu …* – Due to the sweetness of the water, beetles swarm the river. Very beautiful śrīrangam which is surrounded by the kāviri where water is flowing with honey which will make the beetles become drunk with such honey and sing, and by the gardens which are spreading fragrance all of the sky. aṇḍa nāṟum – this can also indicate many fragrant objects such as nāvi, kastūri etc.

## 5.4.4. Vilaitta vembor

*viḷaitta vembōr viṟal vāḷarakkan nagar pāḻpada vaḷaitta valvil tadakkai avanukku idam enbarāl  tuḷaikkai yānai maruppum agilum koṇarndu undi mun tiḷaikkum selvap punal kāviri sūḻ tennarangamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuḷai – having hole; kai – having trunk; yānai – elephant’s; maruppum – tusks; agil – fragrant wooden logs; koṇarndu – bringing along; mun – in front; undi – pushed; selvam – wealth (of sportive enjoyment); tiḷaikkum – enjoying; punal – having water; kāviri sūḻ tennarangam – beautiful śrīrangam surrounded by kāviri; vem pōr – cruel war; viḷaitta – one who does; viṟal – strong; vāḷ – having sword, the weapon; arakkan – rāvaṇan’s; nagar – lankā, the town; pāḻ pada – to be destroyed; vaḷaitta – drawn; val – strong; vil – bow; tadam – huge; kai – having in his hand; avanukku – for that cakravartit tirumagan; idam enbar – is said to be the abode

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The beautiful divaydēśam named śrīrangam, surrounded by the kāviri river which is enjoying the wealth of bringing along tusks of the elephants which have trunk with hole and fragrant wooden logs and pushing them, is said to be the abode of cakravartit tirumangan who is holding the drawn, strong bow in his huge hand to destroy the town, lankā which belonged to rāvaṇan who fought a cruel war and who was strong and having sword, the weapon.

*viḷaitta …* – To have lankā which was the town of rāvaṇan who fought cruel battle, was very strong and was going in the wrong path due to these reasons and who was armed, became barren land as said in “Should become similar to a cremation ground”, śrī rāma had drawn, very strong bow and divine hand which is the abode of such bow; they say that this is the abode of such emperumān. āḻvārs such as toṇḍaradipppodi said in tirumālai 11 “*seruvilē arakkar kōnaic ceṟṟa nam sēvaganār maruviya periya kōyil*” (periya kōyil, śrīrangam, where brave emperumān who killed the king of demons, rāvaṇan, is eternally residing).

*tuḷaikkai …* – The water which is bringing along the tusk of elephant which has hole in its trunk, agil (fragrant wooden log) and pushed it as if saying “Are there any takers?” and enjoying due to its pride. River kāviri also has the same nature as that of śrī rāma.

## 5.4.5. Vambulam kundal

*vambulām kūndal maṇḍōdari kādalan vān puga ambu tannāl muninda aḻagan idam enbarāl umbar kōnum ulagēḻum vandīṇḍi vaṇangum nal sembonārum madiḷ sūḻndu aḻagār tennarangamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

umbar – for dēvatās; kōnum – brahmā who is the lord; ulagu ēḻum – all worlds; vandu – approached; īṇḍi – gathered together; vaṇangum – surrendering; nal – desirable; sem pon – with pure gold; ārum – having radiance matching; madiḷ – by layers; sūḻndu – surrounded; aḻagu Ar – abundantly beautiful; tennarangam – śrīrangam; vambu – fragrance; ulām – spreading; kūndal – having hair; maṇḍōdari – for maṇḍōdari; kādalan – rāvaṇan, who is the dear consort; vān – vīra svargam (heaven which is a prize for bravery); puga – to enter; ambu tannāl – by arrow; muninda – showed anger (and killed him); aḻagan – cakravartit tirumagan who is having vīraśrī (wealth of bravery); idam enbar – said to be his abode

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abundantly beautiful divyadēśam named śrīrangam which is surrounded by layers matching the radiance of desirable, pure gold where brahmā who is the lord for dēvatās and \[people of\] all worlds have approached and gathered together, and surrender, is said to be the abode of cakravartit tirumagan who is having vīraśrī (wealth of bravery). He showed his anger using his arrow on rāvaṇan, who is the dear consort of maṇḍōdari who is having hair where fragrance is spreading, to enter vīra svargam.

*vambulām kūndal* … – Just as cakravartit tirumangan enjoys with pirātti, rāvaṇan should have enjoyed with maṇḍōdari; instead he tried to enjoy in illegitimate manner; śrī rāma tormented him and made him reach heaven (for his bravery); unlike those demons who practised deceitful warfare, cakravartit tirumagan hit them directly with arrows and hence is not having any shortcoming in the wealth of bravery; abode of such emperumān. Even his enemies praise him as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 104.6 “*ranjanīyasya vikramai:*” (bringing joy by his valour and bravery).

*umbar …* – To have brahmā who is the leader of dēvatās, and the people of this world who are created by him gather together and surrender, beautiful śrīrangam is desirable, having fortified walls which are protective layers for the emperumān who is resting inside.

## 5.4.6. Kalai udutta

*kalai udutta agalalgul vanpēy magaḷ tāyena mulai koduttāḷ uyir uṇḍavan vāḻumidam enbarāl kulai edutta kadalip poḻilūdum vandu undi mun alai edukkum punal kāviri sūḻ tennarangamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

edutta – risen tall; kulai – having bunches; kadali – banana’s; poḻil ūdum – in the plantation; vandu – entered (uprooting those trees); mun – in front; undi – pushed; alai edukkum – tides being thrown; punal – having water; kāviri sūḻ tennarangam – divyadēśam named śrī rangam which is surrounded by kāviri; kalai – silk garment; udutta – worn; agal – wide; algul – having waist portion; tāy ena – like mother yaśōdā; mulai koduttāḷ – one who gave her bosom; van – cruel natured; pēy magaḷ – pūtanā, the demon, her; uyir – life; uṇḍavan – kriṣṇa who consumed; vāḻum – eternally residing; idam enbar – said to be his abode

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divyadēśam named śrī rangam which is surrounded by kāviri, having water with tides being thrown and which entered into the banana plantation having tall bunches of banana and pushed them in front, is said to be the abode of kriṣṇa, where he is eternally residing, and who consumed the life of cruel natured pūtanā who was wearing silk garment on her wide waist portion like mother yaśōdā and gave her bosom.

*kalai udutta agal algul* – Having wide waist portion which is decorated with garment, similar to that of mother yaśōdā.

*van pēy magaḷ* – The greatness of pūtanā over yaśōdāp pirātti is in her cruelty \[in a sarcastic way\].

*tāy …* – Just as yaśōdāp pirātti, she lifted up kriṣṇa gently, showing her care for him.

*mulai koduttāḷ uyir uṇḍavan* – Just as she came, being unable to sustain herself without giving her bosom to kriṣṇa, he too appeared to be unable to sustain himself without consuming her milk, killing her. They say “He is residing in the nearby divyadēśam to eliminate similar enemies now as well”.

*kulai …* – The water having entered the banana plantation where the trees are having tall bunches, uprooting them, pushed them here just as those who carry heavy baggage will push them down; beautiful śrīrangam which is surrounded by such kāviri. Just as kriṣṇa will eliminate his enemies, the water is uprooting tall trees and pushing them here.

## 5.4.7. Kanjan nenjum

*kanjan nenjum kadu mallarum sagadamum kālināl tunja venṟa sudar āḻiyān vāḻumidam enbarāl manju sēr māḷigai nīdu agil pugaiyum maṟaiyōr senjol vēḷvip pugaiyum kamaḻum tennarangamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

manju – cloud region; sēr – (risen and) touching; māḷigai – present in the homes; nīdu – moving high; agil pugaiyum – smoke of agil (a fragrant wood); maṟaiyōr – conducted by brāhmaṇas; sem sol – revealed in the vēdam which is a collection of beautiful words; vēḷvi – in the yāgam (fire sacrifice); pugaiyum – smoke; kamaḻum – spreading fragrance; tennarangam – beautiful divyadēśam named śrīrangam; kanjan – kamsan’s; nenjum – mind; kadu – cruel; mallarum – cāṇūra et al; sagadamum – śakatāsuran; tunja – to be destroyed; kālināl – by divine feet; venṟa – (kicked and) became victorious; sudar – radiant; āḻiyān – sarvēśvaran who is having tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); vāḻum – eternally residing; idam enbar – said to be his abode

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divyadēśam named śrī rangam which is having homes which are touching the cloud region, which are having smoke of agil (fragrant wood) and the smoke from the yāgam which is revealed in the vēdam which is a collection of beautiful words, and which is conducted by brāhmaṇas, are present, is said to be the abode of sarvēśvaran who used his divine feet to destroy and become victorious over kamsan’s mind, cruel cāṇūra et al, śakatāsuran and who is having radiant divine chakra.

*kanjan …* – kamsan’s strong mind, wrestlers who are cruel due to engaging in kamsan’s goal more fiercely than kamsan himself, the wheel which appeared without revealing its cruel nature and hid itself.

*kālināl* – Though he had divine chakra in his hand, since he did not want to use that to kill, he killed with his divine feet as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-9-4-thalarndhum-murindhum/) “*tirukkāl āṇḍa perumānē!*” (Oh one who used your divine feet!). The abode of such emperumān. He dragged kamsan by his hair, pushed him down and kicked kamsan’s back with his divine feet; he pressed the wrestlers with his divine feet; he kicked the śakatāsura, having stretched his divine feet due to the delay in getting mother’s milk.

*manju …* – In the homes which are touching the cloud region, which are having smoke of agil (fragrant wood) and the smoke from the yāgam which is ordained in the vēdam conducted by brāhmaṇas of that abode; the beautiful śrīrangam, which is filled with such smoke.

## 5.4.8. Enam min

*ēnam mīn āmaiyōdu ariyum siṟu kuṟaḷumāyt tānumāya taraṇit talaivan idam enbarāl vānum maṇṇum niṟaiyap pugundu īṇḍi vaṇangum nal tēnum pālum kalandu annavar sēr tennarangamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānum – nityasūris (ever liberated) who are in paramapadam; maṇṇum – samsāris (materialistic people) who are on earth; niṟaiya – to fill; pugundu – came and entered; īṇḍi – gathered together; vaṇangum – as they surrender (at that time); nal – sweet; tēnum – honey; pālum – milk; kalandannavar – the devotees who remain as a single entity with same taste; sēr – reached; then arangam – beautiful divyadēśam named śrīrangam; ēnam – as mahā varāha \[huge, wild boar\]; mīn – in the form of fish; āmaiyōdu – as tortoise; ariyum – as narasimha; siṟu – very short; kuṟaḷum – as vāmana \[dwarf\]; āy – one who incarnated; tānum āya – having incarnated in a complete manner; taraṇi – for earth; talaivan – for sarvēśvaran who incarnated as cakravartit tirumagan, the controller; idam enbar – said to be the abode

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is saying that the abode where emperumān who came as the protector by incarnating in many forms and is present for the sake of those who are subsequent to those incarnations, to not lose out, is śrīrangam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divyadēśam named śrīrangam where the nityasūris who are in paramapadam and the samsāris who are on earth have reached and gathered together, came and entered, to fill the abode, where the devotees remain as a single entity with same taste as sweet honey and milk, is said to be the abode of sarvēśvaran who incarnated as cakravartit tirumagan, the controller for earth, and who \[had earlier\] incarnated as mahāvarāha, a form of fish, narasihma, very short vāmana and himself in a complete manner.

*ēnam …* – He assumed the form of varāha to lift up the world which was drowned in the deluge, the form of fish which can subside such deluge in its scales, as tortoise which will hold the mantara mountain from falling, instead of taking just a singular form to help, he came as narasimha who joined two unrelated forms and accepted the form of vāmana, where the dwarfs in the world will appear like tall giants in front of him.

*tānumāya* – It is said in periya tirumoḻi 8.8.10 “*munnum irāmanāyt tānāyp pinnum irāmanāy*” (First rāma (paraśurāma), himself and subsequent rāma (balarāma). śrī rāmāvatāram is said to be himself, while others are his partial incarnations. They say that this is the abode where cakravartit tirumagan who rules over the vast earth is residing.

*vānum …* – As the nityasūris from paramapadam and samsāris from this world entered to fill the place and gathered together, it appears that everyone here is having like-mindedness to be like honey and milk mixed together. It appears like material of same type mixed together instead of different types. Without showing the difference of nityasūris and samsāris, they will mix freely. When strangers who don’t know each other unite and then leave, they will remain with teary eyes thinking “We are going to separate from each other”.

## 5.4.9. Seyan enrum

*sēyan enṟum migap periyan nuṇ nērmaiyināya im māyai yārum aṟiyā vagaiyān idam enbarāl vēyin muttum maṇiyum koṇarndu ārpunal kāviri āya pon māmadiḷ sūḻndu aḻagār tennarangamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēyil – scattering from the bamboo; muttum – pearls; maṇiyum – precious gems; koṇarndu – bringing and pushing; Ar – abundant; punal – having water; kāviri – from tirukkāviri; āya – apt; pon – desirable like gold; mā – big; madihḷ – by forts; sūḻndu – surrounded; aḻagu Ar tennarangam – beautiful divyadēśam named śrīrangam; sēyam – being far away; migap periyan – being greater than all; nuṇ – in subtle objects; nērmaiyināya – entered and remaining very subtle; immāyaiyai – this amazing ability; yārum – by anyone; enṟum – at all times; aṟiyā – unable to know; vagaiyān – sarvēśvaran who is having such nature; idam enbar – said to be the abode

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divyadēśam named śrī rangam which is surrounded by big forts which are desirable like apt gold, and where tirukkāviri which is having abundant water, is bringing pearls and precious gems scattered from the bamboo and pushing them, is said to be the abode of sarvēśvaran who is far away from us, greater than all yet has entered and remained in very subtle objects; this amazing ability of sarvēśvaran is unable to be known by anyone at all times.

*sēyan …* – sarvēśvaran’s amazing ability of being far away and being greater than all, yet being very subtle and entering into all subtle objects and supporting them, is unable to be known by even the most intelligent persons, ever. śrīrangam is said to be the abode of such emperumān.

*vēy …* – kāviri river with abundant water, which is bringing the pearls and precious gems which were scattered from the bamboo on the sahya mountain, and pushing them out. The beautiful kōyil (śrīrangam) which is surrounded by desirable forts which are matching protection for the bhagavān who is resting inside.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.4.10. Alli madar

*alli mādar amarum tirumārvan arangattai kallin mannu madiḷ mangaiyar kōn kalikanṟi sol nallisai mālaigaḷ nāliraṇḍum iraṇḍum udan vallavar tām ulagāṇḍu pin vānulagu āḷvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

alli – having lotus flower as her abode; mādar – periya pirāttiyār, the lady; amarum – firmly residing eternally; tiru – beautiful; mārvan – the abode where sarvēśvaran who is having divine chest, is eternally residing; arangattai – on divyadēśam named śrīrangam; kallil – built with stone; mannu – firm; madiḷ – having forts; mangaiyar – residents of tirumangai; kōn – one who is the lord; kali kanṟi – āḻvār; sol – mercifully spoke; nal – beautiful; isai – having tune; mālaigaḷ – in the form of a garland of words; nāl iraṇḍum iraṇḍum – ten pāsurams; udan – with meditation on the meanings; vallavar tām – those are reciting; ulagu – remaining in śrīrangam, in this world; āṇḍu – enjoying bhagavān’s qualities; pin – after shedding this body; vān ulagu – paramapadam; āḷvar – will rule over

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

āḻvār who is the lord of the residents of tirumangai, which is having firm forts built with stone, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams in the form of a garland of words, with beautiful tune, on the abode where sarvēśvaran, who is having the lady, periya pirāttiyār having lotus flower as her abode, is firmly residing on the beautiful, divine chest, is eternally residing; those who are reciting these pāsurams meditating upon the meanings, will enjoy bhagavān’s qualities remaining in śrīrangam in this world and will rule over paramapadam, after shedding this body.

*alli …* – āḻvār sang the glories of śrīrangam which is the abode of sarvēśvaran who is having beautiful, divine chest which is the abode of śrī mahālakśmi who resides on the lotus flower. He is having a chest which  makes her fear “What will I do if I have to leave this chest and go back to the flower?” She is said to have told in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn*” (I will never leave).

*kallil …* – The garland of words which are mercifully spoken by tirumangai āḻvār who is the chief of the residents of tirumangai which is surrounded by forts which are protective, and having ten pāsurams (in 5 pairs). Due to his attachment in the pāsurams, he is pairing them and enjoying them. Those who can recite these pāsurams with their meanings, will remain in kōyil (śrīrangam) enjoying and after shedding the body, will get to rule over paramapadam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5 Veruvadal

## 5.5.1. Veruvadal

*veruvādāḷ vāy veruvi vēngadamē! vēngadamē! enginṟāḷāl maruvāḷāl en kudangāl vāḷ nedungaṇ tuyil maṟandāḷ vaṇḍār koṇḍal uruvāḷan vānavar tam uyirāḷan oli tirai nīrp pauvam koṇḍa tiruvāḷan en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ enganam nān sindikkēnē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

veruvādāḷ – (My daughter) being fearless; vāy veruvi – blabbering; vēngadamē vēngadamē enginṟāḷ – she is repeatedly saying “Oh tiruvēngdam!”; Al – alas!; en kudangāl – on my lap; maruvāḷ – she is not resting; Al – alas!; vāḷ – sharp like a sword; nedu – wide; kaṇ – in her eyes; tuyil – sleep; maṟandāḷ – she has forgotten (she is not sleeping); vaṇḍu – by beetles; Ar – filled; koṇḍal – like cloud; uru āḷan – having divine form; vānavar tam – for nityasūris; uyirāḷan – being life; oli – resounding; tirai – tides’; nīr – having water; pauvam – in the ocean; koṇḍa – having born; tiru – for periya pirāttiyār; āḷan – sarvēśvaran who is the dear consort of; en magaḷai – my daughter; seydanagaḷ – what he did; nān – I; enganam – how; sindikkēn – can think about?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being fearless, my daughter is repeatedly blabbering “Oh tiruvēngdam!”. Alas! She is not resting on my lap! She has forgotten about sleep in her wide eyes which are sharp like a sword. sarvēśvaran is having a divine form which resembles a cloud filled with beetles, he is the life of nityasūris and is the dear consort of periya pirāttiyār who was born from the ocean which is having water in the resounding tides. How can I think about what he did to my daughter?

*veruvādāḷ …* – parakāla nāyaki’s great desire makes her remain unbearable starting from the place (tiruvēngadam) from where (periya) perumāḷ came here (to śrīrangam). tiruppāṇāḻvār followed perumāḷ from rāvaṇa vadam (Killing of rāvaṇa) as said in amalanādipirān second pāsuram “*anṟu nērnda nisāsararai*” (When he killed the rākśasas then) – he entered through the south gate. In the third pāsuram “*mandi pāy*“, āḻvār followed periya perumāḷ from paramapadam; emperumān arrived at tirumalai; he observed emperumān standing there; he observed that emperumān is appearing to be going somewhere; he followed emperumān who entered śrīrangam through north gate and rested there. nampiḷḷai mercifully says that bhattar mercifully gave this explanation while explaining amalanādipirān.

*veruvādāḷ* – Being fearless, since there is no mischief in her heart. She is so young that she cannot hide her feelings to some and reveal the same to some others. Another explanation – one who does not know fear. Apart from childishness, due to her state, she concealed what she could, but could not do fully \[her emotions\]. That is not all. Giving up paratvam (his presence in paramapadam), vyūham (kśīrābdi / milk ocean) and vibhavam (incarnations) and is constantly speaking about divyadēśams which are dear to him. After saying “tirumalai” once, she does not even know to enter it. She is unable to do as done by nammāḻvār in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/08/thiruvaimozhi-9-6-7-katkarai-eththum/) “*kātkarai ēttum adanuḷ kaṇṇā! ennum*” (my ātmā which appears to have some enjoyment remaining in it, will praise tirukkātkarai).

*enginṟāḷāl* – Daughter’s speech is attractive for the mother. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.44 “*anidras satatam rāma: suptōpica narōttama: \| sītēti madurām vāṇīm vyāharan pratibudyatē \|\|*” (śrī rāma never sleeps, and even if he sleeps he blabbers the sweet word “sītā” and wakes up), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) should be the one blabbering your name, but the roles are reversed here. Since śrī rāma who says these words “*sītēti madurām*” is one who is intelligent and is speaking about sītāp pirātti, and due to the throat being weak because of separation from her, that speech will be very sweet. This is similar to bhattar saying “aḻagiya maṇavāḷap perumāḷ” and anantāḻvān saying “tiruvēngadamudaiyān”, the speech reflects their love – says nanjīyar.

She will not speak anything else; When asked “previously, whatever may be the situation, if you keep her on your lap, she will become pacified; why don’t you try to pacify her?”, the mother says “the one who previously was comfortably seated on my lap, is no longer doing it”. She says “I still tried to do that. She also agreed to rest on my lap. But still, she could not do. One cannot consider it to be a comfortable place since it is mother’s lap, and remains on fire. I don’t know whose lap has reformed her to not fit on mother’s lap. She cannot fit on any other lap than mine, is not fitting on my lap now”.

When asked “So what if she is not resting on your lap? Why don’t you make her rest on a mattress?”

*vāḷ nedum kaṇ …* – We have to start training her in that, from the beginning.

*vāḷ* – It is so sharp to knock off a man.

*nedum kaṇ* – The eye which cannot be fully enjoyed by the enjoyer. Just as a huge city became fully empty, the wide eye has lost sleep. Hence the vastness of the eye is just a burden now.

Subsequently, there is talk about the one who made her as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smarannidam śarīram*” (the muktātmā \[who has been liberated from samsāram\] does not even think of his \[just left behind\] physical form which is lying near his dear ones)

*vaṇḍār …* – He made her change like this, with his physical beauty and pastimes. Another explanation – since his heart is sweet like water, it is said that beetles have filled the cloud.

*vaṇḍu* – As said in nācciyār tirumoḻi “*sengatkarumugilin tiruvuruppōl malarmēl tongiya vaṇḍinangāḷ*“, beetles were shown as example for his form.

*vānavar …* – One who makes the whole (spiritual) world cease to exist, if he makes his divine form invisible for them even for half a moment.

*oli …* – One who churned the ocean and acquired śrī mahālakśmi.

*en …* – Whatever he did to acquire śrī mahālakśmi, he has done the same to torment parakāla nāyaki, my daughter.

*enganam …* – Can I think about her acts which were done after submitting her everything \[to him\]? He can capture her and she can be drowned in him; but how can I, standing on the shore, think about this as “This is how, he is”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.2. Kalaiyala

*kalaiyāḷā agalalgul kanavaḷaiyum kaiyāḷā en seygēn nān? vilaiyāḷā adiyēnai vēṇḍudiyō? vēṇḍāyō? ennum meyya malaiyāḷan vānavar tam talaiyāḷan marāmaram ēḻ eyda venṟic cilaiyāḷan en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ enganam nān sindikkēnē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

agal – vast; algul – waist region; kalai – garment; āḷā – not holding; kanam – golden; vaḷaiyum – bangles; kai – (her) hands; āḷā – not remaining; nān – I; en seygēn – what will do?; adiyēnai – I who am fixed in servitude; vilaiyāḷā – to have me as a product which can be transferred at will; vēṇḍudiyō – will you desire?; vēṇḍāyō – will you not desire?; ennum – she is saying in this manner; meyyam – known as tirumeyyam; malai āḷan – having tirumalai as his abode; vānavar tam – for nityasūris; talai āḷan – being the lord; ēḻ – seven; marāmaram – sāla vrukśas (ebony trees); eyda – pierced; venṟi – victorious; silai āḷan – cakravartit tirumagan, who has the \[bow and\] arrow; en magaḷai – my daughter; seydanagaḷ – what he did; nān – I; enganam – how; sindikkēn – can think about?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter’s vast waist region is not holding the garment; her golden bangles on her hand are not remaining; what will I do? She is saying “Will you or will you not desire to have me who is fixed in servitude, as an entity which can be bought/sold at will?” cakravartit tirumagan who has the victorious \[bow and\] arrow which pierced the seven sāla vrukśas (ebony trees), is the lord of nityasūris and is having tirumalai (divine hill) known as tirumeyyam as his abode. How can I think about what he did to my daughter?

*kalai āḷā agal algul* – The waist region which was vast previously, has now become thin due to suffering in separation. Hence the garment is not held properly.

*kana vaḷaiyum kaiyāḷā* – The best bangle is not remaining on the hand.

*en seygēn yān* – What can I who live by seeing her beautiful garment and combination of hand and bangles, do now? Can I make the garment and bangles remain? Can I make her not indulge in him in this manner? Can I make him accept her as a servitor? What can I do?

*vilai āḷā …* – This is explained in two ways. 1) I who exist only for you such that even you cannot make me a servitor of someone else. 2) To have me at your total disposal to buy/sell me as you please. Will you do this or not? She says “Do this to have me alive”. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.30 “*tāvat hi aham*” (sītāp pirātti says “I wish to be alive only as long as I hear about my husband’s activities”.

*meyyam …* – He came to and remained in tirumeyyam to make her say “*vilaiyāḷā adiyēnai vēṇḍudiyō?*“, after manifesting his saulabhyam (easy approacability) even after being as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (lord of nityasūris who have no bewilderment). As said in tirunedundaṇḍagam 10 “*pinnānār vaṇangum sōdi*” (the radiant lord who is vorśipped in arcā form, by those who missed his incarnations). bhagavān who is even beyond nityasūris who are described as in puruśa sūktam “*tēha nākam mahimānas sacantē yatra pūrvē sādyās santi dēvā*:” (in which paramapadam the sādyās, who have been present since time immemorial, are residing, make that paramapadam great) to be front runners \[in bhagavat viśayam\], has arrived here to help those who are falling behind, here.

*marāmaram …* – īsn’t he the one who helps by taking up arms for even those who don’t trust his abilities and take his help?

*en magaḷai …* – Whatever he has done to bring confidence in sugrīva mahārajar, has been done to make her lose confidence in him. He made her, who completely believes him to be the protector, to call out explicitly \[which shows lack of faith. If one is confident, one will remain quiet, patiently\]. The mother who sees the one \[bhagavān\] who is the means, remains thinking “Do we have to do anything?” Daughter remains thinking “If we are to attain him, can we remain quiet where we are?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.3. Manaya mennokki

*mānāya mennōkki vāḷ nedungaṇ nīr malgum vaḷaiyum sōrum tēnāya naṟunduḻāy alangalin tiṟam pēsi uṟangāḷ kāṇmin kānāyan kadi manaiyil tayir uṇḍu ney paruga nandan peṟṟa ānāyan en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ ammanaimīr! aṟigilēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mānāya – matching a deer’s; mel – tender; nōkki – my daughter who is having eyes; vāḷ – radiant; nedu – wide; kaṇ – in the eyes; nīr – tears; malgum – shedding; vaḷaiyum – bangles; sōrum – slipping (from the hands); tēnāya – fully having honey; naṟu – very fragrant; tuḻāy – made with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); alangalin – garland’s; tiṟam – aspects; pēsi – speaking; uṟangāḷ kāṇmin – is not sleeping; kān āyan – one who resides in forest; kadi – well protected; manaiyil – present in the homes of the covherd men; tayir – curd; uṇḍu – ate; ney – ghee; paruga – to drink; nandan – nadagōpa; peṟṟa – begot; An āyan – kriṣṇa who is a covherd boy; en magaḷai – to attract my daughter; seydanagaḷ – what he did; ammanaimīr – Oh mothers!; aṟigilēn – I am unable to know

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter who is having tender eyes which match those of a deer’s, is shedding tears from those radiant, wide eyes; her bangles are slipping from her hands; she is speaking about the aspects of emperumān’s garland which is made of the fragrant tuḷasi which is filled with honey, and is not sleeping; kriṣṇa who is a covherd boy and stays in the forest, was begotten by nadagōpa, to eat the curd and drink the ghee which are present in the well protected homes of the covherd men; oh mothers! I am unable to know what such emperumān did to attract my daughter!

*mān āya* – Having a sight which is childish and tender.

*vāḷ …* – The eye which can bring tears to the eyes of the opponent. vāḷ – radiance; or sharp to knock out a person on one sight.

*nedum* – The eye which has more enjoyment than those who enjoy it. She is neither able to hold the tears nor the bangles.

When asked “Why can’t she spend the time sleeping?”, the mother says

*tēn āya …* – My daughter is simply saying “Oh flood of honey! How fresh the garland is! How nicely the garland is strung! How cool the garland is! What a fragrance it has!”.

*kān āyan …* – I don’t understand the purpose of his arrival and what he is doing now.

*kān āyan* – As said in tiruppāvai 28 “*kānam sērndu*” (reaching the forest) – one who resides in the forest, is now doing what is done by elite persons! One who knows the differences among the various types of trees in the forest, is now knowing about women! kadi – protection. As said in periya tirumadal “*tunnu padal*” – they would protect the place with densely packed palm leaves.

*tayir …* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam ślōkam 66-3 “*mahatā tapasā rāma mahatā cāpi karmaṇā* l *rājyā daśaratēnāsi labhdō’mrutam ivāmarai* ll” (Oh Rama! You were attained by king daśarata due to great penance and great acts, just as celestial entities attained ambrosia), as daśarata cakravarti begot a son through great penance thinking “I need someone to rule over the kingdom after me”, nandagōpa begot kriṣṇa to consume the curd and ghee thinking “We cannot waste the cow products. We need a son to enjoy these”.

*An āyan* – īsn’t he the one who tends the cows?

*en magaḷai …* – As said in taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli 9-1 “*yatō vācō nivartantē aprāpya manasā saha* l” (Word and mind which set out to estimate brahmam, returned without success), we can know the greatness of bhagavān a little bit, but we cannot understand even a little bit about his actions done out of love.

*aṟigilēn* – Whatever I said is just a little bit. I cannot understand \[anything more in it\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.4. Tay vayil

*tāy vāyil sol kēḷāḷ tan āyattōdu aṇaiyāḷ tadamen kongai yē ārac cāndu aṇiyāḷ emperumān tiruvarangam engē? ennum pēy māya mulai uṇḍu ivvulagu uṇḍa peru vayiṟṟan pēsil nangāy māmāyan en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ mangaimīr! madikkilēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāy – I, who am the mother, my; vāyil – spoken through mouth; sol – word; kēḷāḷ – she is not listening to; than – her; āyattōdu – her friends; aṇaiyāḷ – she is not joining; tadam – vast; mel – tender natured; kongaiyē – bosoms; Ar – completely; sāndu – with sandalwood paste; aṇiyāḷ – not decorating (as done previously); emperumān – where my lord is present; tiruvarangam – divyadēśam named śrīrangam; engē ennum – she is asking “where is it?”; mangaimīr – youthful; nangāy – oh girls!; pēy – pūtanā; māya – to be finished; mulai – her bosom; uṇḍu – consumed; ivvulagu – this earth; uṇḍa – one who consumed (during deluge); peru vayiṟṟan – one who has huge, divine stomach; mā – inconceivable; māyan – one who has amazing power; en magaḷai – on the matter of my daughter; seydanagaḷ – what he did; pēsil – if I try to speak; madikkilēn – unable to conceive it and speak about it

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter is not listening to the word spoken through my mouth though I am her mother; she is not joining with her friends; she is not decorating her vast, tender-natured bosoms with sandalwood paste completely; she is asking “where is the divyadēśam named śrīrangam where my lord is present?”. Oh youthful girls! He consumed pūtanā’s bosom to have her finished; he is the one with huge, divine stomach, who consumed this earth; he has inconceivable, amazing power; if I try to speak about what he did on the matter of my daughter, I am unable to conceive it and speak about it.

*tāy vāyil …* – In all situations, one should obey mother’s words. “*jīvatōr vākyakaraṇāt*” (While alive, one should do as per \[mother’s\] instructions). Even if I speak matching her state of love, she disregards, considering those to be my words.

*kēḷāḷ* – Is it not enough if she just doesn’t follow it? \[She is not even listening\]

*than āyatttōdu aṇaiyāḷ* – It is alright if she abandons the mother who gives advice and has to be abandoned; but should she be indifferent towards those friends who are to be accepted? Even the friends have become like mother. In vihagēśvara samhitā “pitaram mātaram .. sakeen”, just as it is said that the mother should be abandoned, it is also said that friends should be abandoned. Here, she remains with mother, but does not listen to her. But she does not even remain with the friends. The opportunity of approaching her through them is also lost.

*tadam …* – After abandoning mother and friends, should she abandon him also? He will come. She is avoiding the acts which are done for his arrival. At other times, she would care for her bosoms which are huge and enjoyable, and are tender to bear the separation, \[Now she is not doing so\]

*kongaiyē Ara* – \[Previously\] even when he came, she would ignore him and care for those bosoms.

*emperumān …* – She is asking “Where is the divyadēśam where the one who is eternally related and who developed love towards him, to disregard the mother and others equally?”. His svāmitvam (lordship) is not based on karma.

*emperumān* – She knows him as the one who won over her. This is the meaning of the term “*nama:*“.

*pēy …* – The demon’s bosom which was deceptive to appear as mother’s bosom; or, to destroy the demon.

*ivvulagu …* – When it comes to being his food, protecting his followers and destroying his enemies are not different.

*nangāy* – As \[affectionately\] said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*maitrēya*” (Oh maitrēya).

*māmāyan* – One who has amazing aspects which will not let one be finished in separation. \[Like\] drinking a demon’s milk, while being a toddler. He did to my daughter without thinking whether it should be done or not.

*mangaimīr* – You are retaining your youth and femininity.

*madikkilēnē* – I am unable to conceive that to be “this much”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.5. Pun mulai

*pūṇ mulai mēl sāndaṇiyāḷ poru kayal kaṇ mai eḻudāḷ pūvai pēṇāḷ ēṇaṟiyāḷ ettanaiyum emperumān tiruvarangam engē ? ennum nāṇmalarāḷ nāyaganāy nāmaṟiya āyppādi vaḷarnda nambi āṇmaganāy en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ ammanaimīr! aṟigilēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pūṇ – decorated; mulai mēl – on the bosoms; sāndu – sandalwood paste; aṇiyāḷ – she is not applying; poru – matching with each other; kayal – like fish; kaṇ – on her eyes; mai – black pigment; eḻudāḷ – she is not applying; pūvai – pet parrot; pēṇāḷ – she is not liking; ettanaiyum – any thing; ēṇ aṟiyāḷ – she is not thinking; emperumān – sarvēśvaran who is the benefactor, his; tiruvarangam – divyadēśam named tiruvarangam; engē ennum – she is asking “where is it?”; nāḷ – fresh; malarāḷ – for periya pirāttiyār who is residing in lotus flower; nāyaganāy – being the beloved; nām aṟiya – to be known to all of us; āyppādi – in śrī gōkulam; vaḷarnda – one who mercifully grew up; nambi – the complete one; āṇ maganāy – being the best among men; en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ – what he did to my daughter; ammanaimīr – oh mothers!; aṟigilēn – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter is not applying sandalwood paste on her decorated bosoms; she is not applying black pigment on her eyes which are like fish matching with each other; she is not liking her pet parrot; she is not thinking about any thing else; she is asking “where is the divyadēśam named śrīrangam where my lord is present?” emperumān, the complete one, who is the beloved one for periya pirāttiyār who is residing in fresh lotus flower, mercifully grew up in śrī gōkulam to be known to all of us. Oh mothers! I don’t know what he, being the best among men, did to my daughter.

pūṇ mulai – The bosoms which are decorated with pearl necklaces; or it can be said as “bosoms which are decoration for themselves”.

*poru* – On the eyes which cannot be glorified further, by anything else, she is not applying black pigment, even for auspiciousness.

*pūvai …* – Even before claiming ownership on her items such as pet parrot, she would care for them. Now she is not caring for them.

*ēṇ aṟiyāḷ* – She is not thinking about anything in worldly aspects.

*emperumān …* – While asking about bhagavān’s divyadēśam, she does not even need the help of mind.

*nāḷ malarāḷ …* – \[Mother is saying angrily\] He identifies himself as śriya:pati (divine consort of periya pirāttiyār).

*nām aṟiya* – Should we drill an old well \[it is well known from ancient scriptures that he is the husband of śrī mahālakśmi\]? īsn’t it well known that these divine consorts favourably engage with him?

*nambi* – Being subservient to the women, isn’t he thinking that he is complete due to that?

*āṇ maganāy* – When it comes to my daughter, he is manifesting his masculinity as said in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*patim viśvasya*” (He is the lord of the universe). How can one who is subservient, claim to be supreme!

*en magaḷ …* – Will his supremacy become dented if he shows subservience towards her?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.6. Tadadu vana malai

*tādādu vana mālai tārānō? enṟenṟē taḷarndāḷ kāṇmin yādānum onṟu uraikkil emperumān tiruvarangam ennum pūmēl mādāḷan kudamādi madusūdan mannarkkāy munnam senṟa tūdāḷan en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ enganam nān sollugēnē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

tādu ādu – filled with pollen; vanam – in forest; mālai – flower garland; tārān – he is not giving; O – alas!; enṟu enṟē – saying repeatedly; taḷarndāḷ kāṇmin – see, she is breaking down; yādānum – any; onṟu – a statement; uraikkil – if I try to make; emperumān tiruvarangam – tiruvarangam where sarvēśvaran is mercifully residing; ennum – will respond saying; pū mēl – eternally residing on lotus flower; mādu – the woman, periya pirāttiyār; āḷan – being the beloved; kudam ādi – being the one who danced with pots; maduhsūdan – being the one who killed the demon, madu; mannarkkāy – for panca pāṇḍavas; tūdu senṟa – one who went as messenger; āḷan – the lord; en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ – what he did to my daughter; enganam nān sollugēnē – how will I speak?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter is breaking down, repeatedly saying “Alas! He is not giving forest flower garland filled with pollen”. If I try to make any statement, she will respond saying “tiruvarangam is where sarvēśvaran is mercifully residing”. The lord is the beloved consort of periya pirāttiyār, who is eternally residing on lotus flower; he danced with pots; he killed the demon, madu; he went as messenger for the panca pāṇḍavas. How will I speak about what such lord did to my daughter?

*tādu ādu …* – Pollen remaining constantly. ādugai – being present. In the forest, as said in “*tannērāyiram piḷḷaigaḷ*” (His thousand friends who are like him), he and his friends would pluck flowers and prepare garlands – those would remain fresh. We thought that he had those garlands for others \[to give to me\]; my daughter is repeatedly saying “Alas! Will he not give that to me!”, like the repeated sound of bell-metal.

Now, will I even stop hearing these words?

*yādānum …* – If I tried to advise her saying “You cannot have so much love; this does not match the stature of our clan; this suffering will lead to your destruction; he is involved with other women \[periya pirāttiyār\]”, she would respond saying “śrīrangam is the abode of the one who made me to exist for him”.

*pū mēl …* – Is he not the one who makes a woman (periya pirāttiyār) remain inseparable from him? Is he not the one who makes one, not even to know about separation?

*kudam ādi* – Is he not the one who fully gives himself on a four-way junction for the women? periya tirumadal “*mannu paṟai kaṟanga mangaiyar tam kaṇ kaḷippa* *konnavilum kūttanāyp pērttum kudamādi*” (To have the eyes of the (herd) ladies rejoice, he played the drum tied to his waist, carrying out the dance which kills and further danced with pots). It is better to be tormented by his hands than watching his dance.

*madusūdan* – One who has destruction of his enemies as the main task for him.

*mannarkku …* – For those who are favourable towards him, he will lower himself.

*en magaḷai* – How can I speak about his act of destroying her and him living happily?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.7. Varalum ilangongai

*vārāḷum iḷangongai vaṇṇam vēṟāyinavāṟu eṇṇāḷ eṇṇil pērāḷan pērallāl pēsāḷ ippeṇ peṟṟēn en seygēn nān? tārāḷan taṇ kudandai nagarāḷan aivarkkāy amaril uytta tērāḷan en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ enganam nān seppugēnē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

vār – by a corset; āḷum – apt to be tied; iḷam – youthful; kongai – bosom’s; vaṇṇam – complexion; vēṟāyina āṟu – the way it changed; eṇṇāḷ – she is not thinking; eṇṇil – if she tries to think; pēr – great; āḷan – lord’s; pēr allāl – other than the divine name; pēsāḷ – she cannot say; ippeṇ peṟṟēn – gave birth to such girl; nān – I; en seygēn – what will I do?; tār āḷan – wearing a divine garland; taṇ – cool; kudandai nagar āḷan – one who has reached tirukkudandai; aivarkkāy – for panca pāṇḍavas; amaril – in the war; tēr – chariot; uytta – one who rode; āḷan – lord; en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ – what he did to my daughter; enganam – how; nān seppugēnē – will I speak about

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

She is not thinking about the way the complexion of her youthful bosom which is apt to be tied by a corset, has changed. If she tries to think about it, she cannot say anything but the divine name of the great lord. What will I, who gave birth to such girl, do? emperumān is wearing a divine garland; he has reached the cool tirukkudandai; he rode the chariot for panca pāṇḍavas in the war. How will I speak about what he did to my daughter?

*vār āḷum* – The bosom which will not obey orders due to its youthfulness, which is apt to be enjoyed and eagerly looking out asking “show me the target \[bhagavān’s divine chest\]”. To be held by a corset, the bosom which is growing with the intent “Show me, show me”, due to not having its desire fulfilled, is losing its usual complexion and attaining paleness. She is not realising any of these. She is not having any knowledge about herself. “*visasmāra tadātmānam*” \[pramāṇam source not known\]. One who cannot think about her own state, cannot think about anything else.

*eṇṇil …* – More time is spent on not thinking about anything; if she thinks, she does not say anything but the divine name of sarvēśvaran. “*avāpa paramām kāśtām manasaścāpi samyamē*” \[pramāṇam source not known\]. Hence, she does not think about her situation; and she speaks without thinking in her mind.

*ippeṇ …* – Thinking about her daughter “not thinking about anything and having her mind and speech focussed on bhagavān”, she pretends to be upset for the sake of others, but speaking, revealing her joy. She is \[joyfully\] saying “Is there anyone who has given birth to such a girl who is detached from matters related to self and others and has love towards matters related to bhagavān?”.

*tār āḷan* – The one who is wearing a distinguished garland to show that his protection is hurting a woman here.

*taṇ kudandai …* – He is the one who is having tirukkudandai as his capital city for the protection of those who have shortcomings \[in this samsāram\] instead of nityasūris who have no shortcomings.

*aivarkku …* – Practically implementing it, he accepted the arrows shot at his devotees, on his divine chest, for their sake! As said in **tiruvāimoḻi 7.5.9** “*tēsam aṟiya ōr sāradiyāy*” (to be popularly known everywhere as the unique charioteer for the five pāṇḍavas), he made himself as the charioteer to be seen by everyone, and hence lowered himself, by transforming, for the sake of his devotees.

*en magaḷai …* – Just as he placed himself as the target for the arrows of bhīśma et al, now he is placing her as the target of the love arrows, for his sake; the mother is saying “How can I speak about his act of destroying her?”.

## 5.5.8. Uravadum ilal

*uṟavādum ilaḷ enṟu oḻiyādu palar ēsum alar āyiṟṟāl maṟavādē eppoḻudum māyavanē! mādavanē! enginṟaḷāl piṟavāda pērāḷan peṇṇāḷan maṇṇāḷan viṇṇōr tangaḷ aṟavāḷan en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ ammanaimīr! aṟigilēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ādum – any type of; uṟavu ilaḷ – not having relatives; enṟenṟu – in this much only; oḻiyādu – continuously; palar – many; ēsum – to blame; alar – accusations (everywhere in the world); āyiṟṟu – has occurred; Al – alas!; maṟavādē – without forgetting; eppoḻudum – at all times; māyavanē – Oh amazing person!; mādavanē – Oh lord of śrī mahālakśmi!; enginṟāḷ – she is saying; piṟavāda – that which gets rid of birth; pēr āḷan – having divine name; peṇ āḷan – being the controller of women; maṇ āḷan – being the protector of earth; viṇṇōr tangaḷ – on the matter of nityasūris; aṟavāḷan – one who has mercy, he; en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ – what he did to my daughter; ammanaimīr! – oh mothers!; aṟigilēnē – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Accusations occurred for many to blame continuously as “she is not having any relatives”;  alas! Without forgetting, she is saying “Oh amazing person! Oh lord of śrī mahālakśmi!”. emperumān is having the divine name which gets rid of birth; he is the controller of women; he is the protector of earth; he has mercy on the matter of nityasūris. Oh mothers! I don’t know what he did to my daughter.

*uṟavādum ilaḷ enṟu* – People will say “She is not interacting with her parents and friends, without any difference”. She is not seeing her past and maintaining her relationship with them. She is thinking as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*pitānām mūrda śirōrōga:*” (Father is the foremost of diseases) and as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*druśtvā stitvā bahirgurum*” (Seeing the elders outside, she stopped from going to kriṣṇa). bhattar mercifully explained saying “She is new to love towards kriṣṇa”; since she saw these others \[than seeing kriṣṇa only\]. *kācit* – A covherd girl going towards kriṣṇa’s place. When asked who showed her the route; it is said that “due to her love, everything became dark; that darkness was leading her towards kriṣṇa”.

*enṟu …* – Not just saying that, but many ended up accusing her.

*maṟavādē* – When those who remind about him are present, she cannot forget him. They will first say his name, then her name and then the accusations. When they were accusing them, what did she do?

*māyavanē* – One who has amazing guṇas and leelās.

*mādavanē* – She is saying – One who is a great rasika (enjoyer) due to his leading her in loving interactions just as an elephant is made to run by chasing a horse. That is – while uniting, he lowered himself in stature and interacted. śeela guṇam (simplicity) which is the reason for that, the different experiences during the union and the source of his expertise.

*piṟavāda* – Even after taking birth hundreds of thousands of ways for the sake of his devotees,, he thinks he has not done anything for them as said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*ruṇam pravruttam iva*” (I feel like someone in debt, for draupadi), having great love towards devotees. The great personality. Alternatively – he is carrying the divine name which will eliminate our bondage. His names which eliminate our sorrows are causing sorrows for her now!

peṇṇāḷan – One who does this to all the women. As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.2.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/thiruvaimozhi-4-2-9-nangaimir-nirum/) “*nangaimīr nīrum ōr peṇ peṟṟu nalginīr enganē sollugēn yān peṟṟa ēḻaiyaic cangennum cakkaram ennum tuḻāy ennum* *inganē sollum irāp pagal en seygēn?*” (Oh girls who are complete in all aspects! All of you have given birth to a daughter and raised them too. How can I speak about my daughter who is desirous \[of attaining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]? She is individually saying Sanka, chakra (which are his unique symbols) and tuḷasi (from his divine feet) day and night, without any difference. What shall I do for this!).

*maṇṇāḷan* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam “*rakśitā jīva lōkasya*” (You are the protector of all living beings).

*viṇṇōr …* – One who grants his presence to nityasūris as they praise his mercy.

*en magaḷ …* – I cannot speak about his acts of mercy \[sarcasm\], now.
