## 5.5.9. Pandodu kalal

*pandōdu kaḻal maruvāḷ paingiḷiyum pālūttāḷ pāvai pēṇāḷ vandānō! tiruvarangan vārānō! enṟenṟē vaḷaiyum sōrum sandōgan pauḻiyan aintaḻal ōmbu taittiriyan sāma vēdi andō! vandu en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ ammanaimīr! aṟigilēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pandōdu – With ball; kaḻal – the unripe fruits which are known as kaḻal (and used by girls for playing); maruvāḷ – not desiring; pai – green; kiḷiyum – for the parrot; pāl ūttāḷ – not feeding milk; pāvai – doll; pēṇāḷ – not liking; tiruvarangan – aḻagiya maṇavāḷan; vandān – has mercifully arrived; O – amazing; enṟu – saying this; vārān – he is not coming; O – alas!; enṟē – saying this; vaḷaiyum – (on her hands) bangles; sōrum – losing; candōgan – one who knows the meaning of the special portion of sāma vēdam; pavuḻiyan – one who knows the meaning of kauśīdakī brāhmaṇam; aindu aḻal – one who remains amidst five fires; ōmbu – one who performs fire sacrifice; taittiriyan – one who knows the meaning of taittirīya upaniśat; sāma vēdi – one who knows the meaning of sāma vēdam, he; vandu – arrived where she remains; en magaḷaic ceydanagaḷ – what he did to my daughter; ammanaimīr – Oh mothers!; aṟigilēnē – I don’t know; andō – alas!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter is not desirously playing with ball and unripe fruits which are known as kaḻal; she is not feeding milk to her green parrot; she is not liking her doll; she is saying “aḻagiya maṇavāḷan has mercifully arrived! Amazing!” and “Alas! He is not coming”; she is losing her bangles; emperumān knows the meaning of the special portion of sāma vēdam; he knows the meaning of kauśīdakī brāhmaṇam; he remains amidst five fires; he performs fire sacrifice; he knows the meaning of taittirīya upaniśat; he knows the meaning of sāma vēdam. He arrived where she remains. Oh mothers! I don’t know what he did to my daughter. Alas!

*pandu* – She would not leave these even while sleeping; but now she has abandoned them.

*paingiḷiyum* – Not only she remains indifferent towards her parents but also her children \[pets\].

*pāvai pēṇāḷ* – Previously, if someone did not care for her doll, that will not be liked by her. Now, she is herself not caring for it. As said in *“tasmāt bālyē vivēkātmā yatēta śrēyasē nara:”* (Wise person seeks goodness while being young), she has become wise. Thus, it is said that she has given up her past acts. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.5 “*parityaktā mayā lankā*” (I have abandoned lankā). Just as in the case of prāpaka (means), when bhagavān is considered as the means, one would abandon all other means, in the case of prāpya (goal) too, other goals will be considered as false goals and be abandoned.

She abandoned everything else; she thought that his arrival is confirmed; considering her state as the reason,

*vandānō tiruvarangam enṟu* – She will say “Will one who would come and remain \[in/with us\] to eliminate the external attachment, not come even if we eliminated our attachment to everything else?”

*vārānō* – She will say “Should I die, remaining in this state itself?”. She will say “For us, it so happened that we will get the same result in being attached to those who don’t have noble qualities, even after being attached to bhagavān \[who has noble qualities\]”.

*vaḷaiyum …* – Even bangles faced the same fate as the ball, kaḻal and doll, and slipped from her hands. śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.29 “*śaitilyam upayāntyāśu karēśu valayānyapi*” (As kriṣṇa left, our bangles also left us).

*candōgan …* – We can tolerate this if an ignorant person did this to us; one who is said to be, as in śrī bhagavat gītā 15.15 “*vēdavidēva cāham*” (Only I am the knover of vēdam) is doing this.

*candōgan* … – This could imply cāndōjña upaniśat in sāma vēdam; alternatively – this implies that he is known only through vēdam and subsequent portion indicates that he is an expert in vēdāntam.

*andō …* – If the omniscient one does what an ignorant person would do, can I seek any other refuge?

*vandu* – When she was not interested in him, he came voluntarily and made her like this and then ignores her! He is the one who troubled her first and then ignores her.

When recited as “*en pon magaḷ*“, it means “my best daughter”.

## 5.5.10. Selugalum

*sēlugaḷum vayal pudai sūḻ tiruvarangattu ammānaic cindai seyda neela malarkkaṇ madavāḷ niṟaivu aḻivait tāy moḻinda adanai nērār kāla vēl parakālan kalikanṟi oli mālai kaṟṟu vallār mālai sēr veṇ kudaik kīḻ mannavarāyp ponnulagil vāḻvar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sēl – fish; ugaḷum – jumping; vayal – by fertile fields; pudai – in the regions surrounding; sūḻ – spread out; tiruvarangattu – mercifully reclining in the divyadēśam named tiruvarangam; ammānai – on namperumāḷ, the lord; sindai seyda – thought; neela malar – like karuneydal (a dark-purple flower); kaṇ – having eyes; madavāḷ – (parakāla nāyaki) woman’s; niṟaivu – complete femininity; aḻivai – destroyed; tāy – mother; moḻinda – spoke; adanai – on that special state; nērār – enemies who came opposing; kālan – like yama (deity of death); vēl – having spear, the weapon (due to that); parakālan – like death for enemies; kalikanṟi – āḻvār; oli – mercifully composed; mālai – these ten pāsurams which are in the form of a garland of words; kaṟṟu – learning through ācārya; vallār – those who remain well-versed; mālai sēr – strung with layers of pearl necklaces; veḷ – whitish; kudaikkīḻ – remaining under the umbrella; mannavarāy – being kings ruling over (and then); pon ulagil – in paramapadam; vāḻvar – will enjoy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

namperumāḷ, the lord, is mercifully reclining in the divyadēśam named tiruvarangam which is surrounded by fertile fields which are spread out and where fish are jumping. parakāla nāyaki, the woman, who thought about such lord and who is having karuneydal flower like eyes, lost the completeness in her femininity. tirumangai āḻvār who is like yama for his enemies and is having spear, a weapon which is like yama for the enemies who come opposing, spoke about that special state in the mood of parakāla nāyaki’s mother and mercifully composed these ten pāsurams which are in the form of a garland of words. Those who learn these pāsurams through an ācārya and remain well-versed, will remain as kings ruling over, being seated under whitish regal umbrella which is strung with layers of pearl necklaces and (will subsequently) enjoy in paramapadam.

*sēl ugaḷum …* – Thinking about sarvēśvaran who is residing in kōyil (śrīrangam) which is surrounded by fertile fields which is joyfully inhabited by animals (fish) too.

*neela malar …* – One who is having beauty which is meditated upon by the opponent.

*niṟaivu aḻivai* – Destroyed her femininity.

*tāy …* – When she has lost her knowledge and femininity, her divine mother explained her state.

*nērār …* – For anyone who comes opposing saying “I am your enemy”, beating their chest, āḻvār is having the name “parakālan” (death personified for enemies), and is having a spear which is like death. Those who learnt these garlands of pāsurams by āḻvārs. Instead of grabbing on their own, those who learn from ācāryas.

*mālai …* – If one is interested to rule the wealth, one will remain under the pearl umbrella and enjoy it. And then will eternally enjoy in paramapadam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.6 Kaimmana

## 5.6.1. Kaimmana

*kaimmāna maḻakaḷiṟṟaik kadal kidanda karumaṇiyaimaimmāna maradagattai maṟai uraitta tirumālai emmānai enakku enṟum iniyānaip panikātta ammānai yān kaṇḍadu aṇinīrt tennarangattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mānam – lengthy; kai – having trunk; maḻam – young; kaḷiṟṟai – like an elephant; kadal – on the ocean; kidanda – one who is mercifully resting; karu maṇiyai – like a bluish gem; mai – black colour; mānam – abundantly having; maradagattai – one who is like an emerald; maṟai – by vēdas; uraitta – revealed; tirumālai – one who is the divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi; emmānai – being my lord; enakku – for me (who is meditating upon him); enṟum – at all times; iniyānai – being enjoyable; pani – hail; kātta – stopped (by lifting the gōvardana hill) and protected; ammānai – one who is my lord; yān – I; aṇi – beautiful; nīr – surrounded by water; then – beautiful; arangattu – in the divyadēśam named tiruvarangam; kaṇḍadu – am seeing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I am seeing the one who is like a young elephant which is having a lengthy trunk, one who is like a bluish gem mercifully resting on the ocean, one who is like emerald stone which is having abundance of black colour, one who is revealed in the vēdas as the divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi, one who is my lord, one who is always enjoyable for me, one who is my lord who protected by stopping the hail by lifting the gōvardana hill, in the beautiful divyadēśam named tiruvarangam which is surrounded by beautiful water.

**kaimmāna mada kaḷiṟṟai** – As said in “*ānaiyil kidanda kidakkai*” (resting like an elephant), emperumān is reclining just as an elephant resting with its limbs stretched out, and like a youthful elephant having large trunk, reclining.

**kadal kidanda karu maṇiyai** – One who is reclining on tiruppāṟkadal like a bluish gem reclining on an ocean to fill the void there.

**maimmāna maradagattai** – One who is like an emerald gem which has abundant blackish complexion.

**maṟai uraitta tirumālai** – emperumān who is śriya:pati and is spoken of, loudly, in vēdams. puruśa sūktam “*hrīścatē lakśmīśca patnyau*” (one who is having śrī bhūmip pirātti and śrī mahālakśmi as his consorts), śrī sūktam “*asyēśānā jagatō viṣṇupatni*” (one who is the lord of the worlds and the divine consort of viṣṇu).

**emmānai** – One who manifested his togetherness with her and made me totally exist for him.

**enakku** – Even in the most sorrowful situations, one who is enjoyable for me, if I think about him.

**pani kātta ammānai** – In this manner, for those who are not having any refuge other than him, he who protects by performing most difficult tasks.

**yān kaṇḍadu aṇinīrt tennarangattē** – Instead of just hearing from others who heard “Once he lifted the hill and protected the cows and the herds-people, he reclined on tiruppāṟkadal”, I got to see him in kōyil (śrīrangam).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.6.2. Peranai

*pērānaik kuṟungudi emperumānai tiruttaṇkālūrānaik karambanūr uttamanai muttilangukārār tiṇ kadal ēḻum malai ēḻu ivvulagēḻu uṇḍumārādenṟu irundānaik kaṇḍadu tennarangattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pērānai – one who is present in the divyadēśam named tiruppēr; kuṟungudi – mercifully present in tirukkuṟungudi; emperumānai – being the lord; tiruttaṇkāl ūrānai – one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruttaṇkāl; karambanūr – mercifully present in tirukkarambanūr; uttamanai – being the supreme lord; muttu – pearls; ilangum – shining; kār Ar – abundantly black; tiṇ – firm (being unable to suppress); ēḻ kadalum – seven oceans; ēḻ malai – seven anchoring mountains; ēḻ ivvulagum – this world which is having seven islands; uṇḍu – consumed; ārādu enṟu – saying that he is not satisfied; irundānai – sarvēśvaran who remains unsatisfied in protecting others; kaṇḍadu then arangattē – seeing him in this beautiful śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I am seeing the sarvēśvaran who is present in the divyadēśam named tiruppēr, who is mercifully present as the lord in tirukkuṟungudi, who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruttaṇkāl, who is mercifully present as the supreme lord in tirukkarambanūr and who consumed the firm, seven oceans which are abundantly black and having shining pearls, seven anchoring mountains and this world which is having seven islands, and still said that he was not satisfied and remained unsatisfied in protecting others, in this beautiful śrīrangam.

**pērānai** – On the banks of the river \[kāvēri\], present in tiruppēr, to be enjoyed by all.

**kuṟungudi emperumānai** – tirumangai āḻvār has a special privilege in tirukkuṟungudi; it is only āḻvār’s will which prevails there \[Since āḻvār got mōkśam in this divyadēśam, as granted by bhagavān as per his desire\].

**tiruttaṇkāl ūrānai** – One who remains as a resident of this divyadēśam, without distinguishing himself from others.

**karambanūr uttamanai** – One who is reclining where the temple door cannot be closed due to constant visitors, as it is on the way to many important divyadēśams.

**muttu ilangaum …** – With shining pearls, abundantly dark, the seven oceans which are firm in not breaching the shore, the seven mountains which seem to be nails anchoring the earth – while keeping these seven worlds which have such features, in his stomach and protecting them, he thinks he did not do enough, for those who were helped by him, need not worry thinking how they can repay for his help.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.6.3. Enagi

*ēnāgi ulagidandu anṟu irunilanum peru visumbumtānāya perumānait tannadiyār manattu enṟumtēnāgi amudāgit tigaḻndānai magiḻndu orugālānāyan ānānaik kaṇḍadu tennarangattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – in the beginning of varāha kalpa; ēnāgi – being mahā varāha; ulagu – earth; idandu – (from the wall of the oval shaped universe) one who lifted by digging out; iru – vast; nilanum – earth; peru – vast; visumbum – sky; tānāya – one who is having as his prakāram (form); perumānai – being the lord; than adiyār – his servitors; manattu – in the heart; enṟum – at all times; tēnāgi – like honey; amudāgi – being enjoyable like nectar; tigaḻndānai – being the one who is shining; magiḻndu – with love; oru kāl – at the end of dvāpara yuga; An – one who can tend cows; āyan ānānai – one who became kriṣṇa; kaṇḍadu then arangattē – seeing in the beautiful śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I am seeing bhagavān who as mahā varāha, lifted the earth by digging it out from the wall of the oval shaped universe, in the beginning of varāha kalpa, who is having the vast earth and vast sky as his prakāram, who is enjoyable like honey and nectar in the hearts of his servitors at all times, who is shining and who can lovingly tend cows by becoming kriṣṇa at the end of dvāpara yuga, in the beautiful śrīrangam.

**ēnāgi mun idanda** – When the earth was consumed by deluge, as a vaāha, he lifted it up.

**iru nilanum** – All of earth and sky are prakārams for sarvēśvaran, to have all entities to be subdued in the word “*tān*” (mine).

**than adiyār …** – When a person steps on a thorn to have his feet affected, the śarīrī (ātmā) will suffer. Similarly, āḻvār is thinking about bhagavān being the abhimāni (one who cares) for the universe to feel the danger experienced by the universe. For those who purely exist for him, he will remain as all types of relatives and is shining because of that.

**magiḻndu …** – Having incarnated as kriṣṇa, instead of thinking along the lines of “We happily enjoyed in paramapadam, but now we have to stand here in this samsāra in an inferior way”, with overwhelming love “At least in this manner, we could help them”. In dvāpara yugam, he mercifully tended cows and calves, and remained faultless in that.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.6.4. Valarndavanai

*vaḷarndavanait tadangadaluḷ valiyuruvil tirisagadamtaḷarndu adira udaittavanait tariyādu anṟu iraṇiyanaippiḷandavanai perunilam īradi nīttip paṇḍu oru nāḷaḷandavanai yān kaṇḍadu aṇinīrt tennarangattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tadam – vast; kadal uḷ – in the ocean; vaḷarndavanai – one who is mercifully resting; vali – strong; uru – having body; tiri – strolling; sagadam – śakatāsura; taḷarndu – to become weak; udira – and fall down; udaittavanai – one who kicked; tariyādu – being unable to bear the suffering of prahlāda; anṟu – at that time; iraṇiyanai – hiraṇyāsura; piḷandavanai – one who tore and knocked; paṇḍu oru kāl – once, in the past; peru – vast; nilam – earth; īradi – to be subdued in two steps; nītti – stretched the divine feet; aḷandavanai – trivikrama, who measured; yān – I; aṇi – beautiful; nīr – surrounded by water; then – beautiful; arangattu – in the divyadēśam named tiruvarangam; kaṇḍadu – am seeing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I am seeing bhagavān who is mercifully resting in the vast ocean, who kicked śakatāsura who was having a strong body and was strolling towards him, who tore and knocked down hiraṇyāsura back then, being unable to bear the suffering of prahlāda, and who as trivikrama, measured the vast earth by stretching his divine feet and subduing it, once in the past, in the beautiful divyadēśam named tiruvarangam which is surrounded by beautiful water.

**vaḷarndavanai …** – One who is mercifully resting in the vast ocean, being the root for the incarnations.

**vali …** – Subsequently, when he heard “Demoniac persons have increased”, he incarnated; one who kicked with his divine feet, the strong cart-wheel which was possessed by a demon, to have it broken down completely into pieces.

**tariyādu …** – As hiraṇya went on to torment his child, prahlāda, by pushing him into the ocean, placing a stone on him to crush him, emperumān, being unable to bear it, incarnated as narasimha and tore hiraṇya and knocked him down.

**peru nilam …** – One who stretched his divine feet to contain the vast earth in two steps, and measured and accepted it.

## 5.6.5. Nir alalay

*nīr aḻalāy nedu nilanāy ninṟānai anṟu arakkanūr aḻalāl uṇḍānaik kaṇḍār pin kāṇāmē pēraḻalāyp peruvisumbāyp pin maṟaiyōr mandirattin āraḻalāl uṇḍānaik kaṇḍadu tennarangattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīrāy – being in the form of water; aḻalāy – being in the form of fire too; nedu – vast; nilanāy – being the earth; ninṟānai – being the antaryāmi for panca bhūtams; anṟu – during the time of śrī rāmāvatāram; arakkan – rāvaṇāsura’s; Ur – town of lankā; kaṇḍār – those who had seen (previously); kāṇāmē – be unable to see (with the same beauty); aḻalāl – through fire; uṇḍānai – one who destroyed; pēr – huge; aḻalāy – being in the form of badabāgni (batabā indicates female horse. It is said that a female horse resides in the middle of the ocean which controls the agitation of the ocean, with fire in its mouth); peru – immeasurable; visumbāy – being the controller of paramapadam; pin – further; maṟaiyōr – brāhmaṇas’; mandirattu – havis (offering) in the form of mantra; Ar aḻalāl – (by that offering) through fire which became satisfied; uṇḍānai – one who mercifully consumed; kaṇḍadu then arangattē – seeing in the beautiful śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I am seeing in the beautiful śrīrangam, bhagavān who is in the form of water, fire, vast earth and thus being the antaryāmi of panca bhūtams, who during the time of śrī rāmāvatāram, destroyed through fire, rāvaṇāsura’s town of lankā such that those who had previously seen it could not see it subsequently; he is in the form of batabāgni (a type of fire) and is the controller of the immeasurable paramapadam; further, he mercifully consumed brāhmaṇas’ havis in the form of mantra through fire which became satisfied in accepting it.

**nīr …** – Through trivrut karaṇam (creation through 3 elements), pancī karaṇam (creation through 5 elements) is explained.

**anṟu …** – When rāvaṇa was tormenting others; those who saw his town with fort, kitchens, streets, could subsequently not see the same, by destroying it with fire as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 26.22 “*smaśāna sadruśī bhavēt*” (This lankā will become like graveyard),

**pēr aḻalāy** – Being batabā mukāgni here and being the apt destination of paramapadam for those who escaped the boundaries of this material world and reached there.

**maṟaiyōr …** – To help them attain paramapadam, one who consumes the havis in the form of mantram, in the yajñas (fire sacrifice), through trētāgni (a type of fire in the yajña). [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.24](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-24/) “*aham hi sarvayajñānām bhoktā ca prabhur Eva ca \|* *na tu mām abhijānanti tatvēnātaś cyavanti tē \|\|*” (I am only the enjoyer and the benefactor of all yajñas. Those who are only engaged in pūrva bhāgam (ritualistic aspects), do not know me truly (as the antaryāmi (indvelling super soul)) and hence they miss out on the main benefits).

## 5.6.6. Tan sinattait

*tan sinattait tavirttu adaindār tava neṟiyait tariyādukanjanaik konṟu anṟu ulagam uṇḍu umiḻnda kaṟpagattaivenjinatta kodum toḻilōn visai uruvai asaivittaanjiṟaip puḷ pāganai yān kaṇḍadu tennarangattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tam – their; sinattai – anger; tavirttu – giving up; adaindār – those who reached him; tavam – in the form of firm belief; neṟiyai – being the one who conducts their means; tariyādu – being unable to tolerate the sufferings (underwent by his mother and father); kanjanai – kamsan; konṟu – being the one who killed; anṟu – during the time of deluge; ulagam – world; uṇḍu – swallowed; umiḻnda – one who let it out during creation; kaṟpagattai – being most magnanimous; vem – very fierce; sinatta – being angry; kodum – cruel; toḻilōn – rudra who is having activities, his; visai – having fast movement; uruvai – body; asaivitta – (in the bāṇāsura battle) one who made to tremble; am – beautiful; siṟai – having wings; puḷ – garudāḻvār; pāganai – sarvēśvaran, who rides; yān kaṇḍadu then arangattē – I am seeing in the beautiful śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I am seeing in the beautiful śrīrangam, sarvēśvaran who is the one who conducts the means of those who give up their anger and reach him; being unable to tolerate the sufferings (underwent by his mother and father), he killed kamsan; during the time of deluge he, being most magnanimous, swallowed the world and let it out during creation; rudra, being fiercely angry, is having cruel activities; in the bāṇāsura battle, bhagavān made such rudra’s body tremble; he rides garudāḻvār who is having beautiful wings.

**tam sinattai** – Saying as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.1](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-1/) “*anasūyavē*” (those who are not jealous of me), kriṣṇa told \[arjuna\] “There is none as qualified as yourself; when I spoke about my greatness, you did not get angry; I am going to tell you more, carefully listen to me”. One should only avoid hatred; for those who eliminated hatred and approached him, he himself conducts the means to attain him.

**tariyādu** – Explains how he remains with those who have hatred. As kamsan was trying to torment śrī vasudēvar and dēvaki, being unable to tolerate it, he thought “we cannot leave him here even for one more moment” and killed him.

**anṟu …** – This is how he remains towards those who neither hate him nor approach him. Hear he protects those who are in danger. He protects seeing the presence of danger. He only sees the relationship \[between jīvātmā and paramātmā\].

**kaṟapagattai** – One who does not even think that “I have helped so much”.

**vem sinatta …** – Having cruel anger, rudran is having the cruel activity of upasamhāram (annihilation) which is in the form of hurting creatures; kriṣṇa made such rudra’s form shake. As the bull ran with its tail lifted, rudran spread out his matted hair and was running away saying as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*kriṣṇa kriṣṇa mahābhāhō*” (Oh kriṣṇa! Oh kriṣṇa! Oh one who has mighty shoulders!). One who has garuda as vehicle and made rudra run away like this. This section could be explaining bāṇāsura vadam and narakāsura vadam as well.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.6.7. Sindanaiyait

*sindanaiyait tava neṟiyait tirumālai piriyāduvandu enadu manattu irunda vadamalaiyai varivaṇḍārkondaṇainda poḻil kōval ulagaḷappān adi nimirttaandaṇanai yān kaṇḍadu aṇinīrt tennarangattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sindanaiyai – one who is the target of my desire; tavam – in the form of firm belief; neṟiyai – one who conducts the means; tirumālai – one who is śriya:pati (divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi); vada malaiyai – tiruvēngadam (tirumalā); piriyādu – without separating (and remaining there); vandu – arriving from there; enadu – my; manattu – in the mind; irunda – one who is eternally present; vari – having stripes; vaṇḍu – by the beetles; Ar – filled; kondu – flower bunches; aṇainda – present densely; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; kōval – in tirukkōvalūr; ulagu – worlds; aḷappān – to measure; adi – divine feet; nimirtta – one who stretched; andaṇanai – my lord; yān – I; aṇi – beautiful; nīr – surrounded by water; then – beautiful; arangattu – in the divyadēśam named tiruvarangam; kaṇḍadu – am seeing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is the target of my desire; he conducts the means (to attain him) in the form of firm belief; he, who is śriya:pati, is eternally present in my mind having arrived from tiruvēngadam where he remains, without separating from there; my lord stretched his divine feet to measure the worlds, in tirukkōvalūr, which is surrounded by orchards which have dense presence of flower bunches which are filled with beetles having stripes. I am seeing such bhagavān in the beautiful divyadēśam named tiruvarangam which is surrounded by beautiful water.

**sindanaiyai** – One who is the goal which is the target of my desire as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍum nām*” (we should perform continuous kainkaryam).

**tava neṟiyai** – he himself is the means to get that eternal kainkaryam.

When asked “Who is that entity who remains the one as goal and means?” āḻvār says

**tirumālai** – She remains puruśakāram (one who recommends) while bhagavān is prāpakam (means) and remains as part of the goal just like him, while bhagavān is prāpyam.

**piriyādu …** – Being the one who has tirumalā as his eternal abode, he entered my heart to make these features blossom in my heart, and is aptly residing there.

**vari …** – In trirukkōvalūr which has dense orchards, which have dense flower bunches, where beetles with beautiful complexion are present. bhagavān is present having his divine feet stretched out, in a humble manner and accepted everything as his own.

**yān kaṇḍadu** – While he remains as the mendicant seeking alms, I saw him in śrīrangam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.6.8. Tuvaritta

*tuvaritta udaiyavarkkum tūymai illāc camaṇarkkumavargatku angu aruḷillā aruḷānai tannadaindaemargatkum adiyēṟkum emmāṟkum emmanaikkumamararkkum pirānāraik kaṇḍadu tennarangattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuvaritta – reddish; udaiyavarkkum – bauddas who wear saffron clothes; tūymai illā – impure; samaṇarkkum – jainas; avargatku angu – in this manner, on matters relating to these people who are vēda bāhyas (those who reject vēdam); aruḷ illā – one who does not show mercy; aruḷānai – one who is merciful; than adainda emargatkum – for my people who surrendered unto him; adiyēṟkum – for me too; emmāṟkum – for my father; emmanaikkum – for my mother; amararkkum – for nityasūris; pirānārai – one who is the benefactor; kaṇḍadu then arangattē – I am seeing in beautiful śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Merciful bhagavān does not show mercy on matters relating to vēda bāhyas such as bauddas who wear reddish saffron clothes and impure jainas; \[But\] he is the benefactor for my people who surrendered unto him, me, my father, my mother and nityasūris. I am seeing such bhagavān in beautiful śrīrangam.

**tuvaritta …** – For bauddas who wear reddish clothes and for jainas who are not to be touched due to not being vaidikas; merciful bhagavān who does not show his mercy ever to those who approach him without actions which are prescribed in vēdam. Just as even a milk bearing tree, if it is poked during inapt times, will not provide milk. bhagavān is similar to that.

**tannadainda …** – For those who are connected to me and are surrendered to him only – that is, for vaiṣṇavas; for me, my mother and father, and for nityasūris, he is the lord, without any favouritism towards any one of these persons.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.6.9. Poy vannam

*poy vaṇṇam manattu agaṟṟip pulan aindum sela vaittumey vaṇṇam ninaindavarkku mey ninṟa vittaganaimaivaṇṇam karumugil pōl tigaḻ vaṇṇam maradagattinavvaṇṇa vaṇṇanai yān kaṇḍadu tennarangattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

poy – objects which are temporary, based on worldly-matter; vaṇṇam – holding on to their nature; manam – mind; agaṟṟi – freed; aindu pulan – five senses; sela vaittu – withdrawing from the worldly matters; mey vaṇṇam – truly; ninaindavarkku – for those who meditated upon him; mey ninṟa – one who remained truly; vittganai – being amazing; mai vaṇṇam – like black-pigment’s complexion; karu mugil pōl – like a dark cloud; tigaḻ – shining; vaṇṇam – having complexion; maradagattin – the jewel named emerald, its; avvaṇṇam – such complexion; vaṇṇanai – having complexion; yān kaṇḍadu then arangattē – I am seeing in the beautiful śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

For those who truly meditated upon him after freeing the mind which was holding on to the nature of worldly-matter based objects which are temporary and withdrawing the five senses from the worldly matters, bhagavān is true and amazing; he is having the complexion of black pigment, dark cloud and the shining complexion of the jewel named emerald; I am seeing such bhagavān in the beautiful śrīrangam, having such complexion.

**poy vaṇṇam** – poy indicates prakruti (primordial matter) and prākrutam (matter based objects); taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli 6 says “*satyancā nrutanca satyamabhavat*” (the *paravastu* \[greatest entity\] was *satyam* (without any change) even though it exists as *satyam* (cētana tatvam or sentient entity) and *asatyam* (acētana tatvam or insentient entity). Mind which is attached to the nature of such worldly objects.

**agaṟṟi** – Giving up the thought of considering prakruti and prākrutam as good and permanent.

**pulan …** – Even if we take the mind away, the external sense will again engage the mind with the same matter; ensuring that they don’t run behind worldly pleasures.

**mey vaṇṇam …** – One who performs bhakti (devotion) towards him with true knowledge about self.

**mey ninṟa vittaganai** – The amazing bhagavān who truly reveals his svarūpam (true nature) etc.

When asked “What does he reveal them?” āḻvār responds

**mai vaṇṇam …** – As said in kata upaniśat 1-2-23 “*nāyamātmā pravacanē na labhyō na mēdayā na bahūnā śrutēna* l *yamēvaiśa vruṇutē tēna labhyas tasyaiśa ātmā* ***vivruṇutē tanūm svām*** ll” (This supreme entity cannot be attained by hearing, by thinking or by meditation (devoid of devotion). To that person, who the supreme entity draws towards him, he manifests his auspicious divine form), one who has complexion of an emerald which is having complexion of black pigment and dark cloud .

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.6.10. Amaruvi

*āmaruvi nirai mēytta aṇi arangattu ammānaikkāmaru sīrk kalikanṟi oli seyda malipugaḻ sērnāmaruvu tamiḻ mālai nāliraṇḍōdu iraṇḍinaiyumtāmaruvi vallār mēl sārā tīvinai tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ānirai – cow herd; maruvi – remaining fixed; mēytta – one who protected; aṇi – decoration for bhūlōkam; arangattu – one who is mercifully resting in śrīrangam; ammānai – on the lord’s matter; kāmaru – desirable; sīr – having śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī (wealth of kainkaryam); kali kanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; oli seyda – mercifully composed; mali – abundant; pugaḻ sēr – having fame; nā maruvu – fixed on the tongue; tamiḻ mālai – in the form of tamiḻ songs; nāl iraṇḍōdu iraṇḍinaiyum – ten pāsurams; tām – those; maruvi – remaining fixed; vallār mēl – who learnt; tānē – on their own; tīvinai – sins; sārā – will not come close

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

On the matters relating to the lord who remained fixed with the cow herd and protected them and who is mercifully resting in śrīrangam which is a decoration for bhūlōkam, tirumangai āḻvār, who is having desirable śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī, mercifully composed these ten pāsurams in the form of tamiḻ songs which are abundantly famous and are well fixed on the tongue; sins on their own, will not come close to those who learnt these pāsurams, remaining fixed on them.

**āmaruvi …** – Remaining fixed with the cows which don’t have any thing in them for their protection and protected them; such simplicity is considered to be supremacy when we see his total simplicity in śrīrangam. āḻvār who is having vaiṣṇavalakśmi (wealth of vaiṣṇavam) which is desirable for all, composed these pāsurams with music.

**nā maruvu …** – Even without the help of mind, if we place these pāsurams on tongue once, they will remain fixed on the tongue.

**maruvi vallār** – On those who have learnt this decad with their heart, while they are not thinking “we should get rid of these sins”, the sins, on their own, will run away thinking “this person is not our abode”.

## 5.7 Pandai nanmaraiyum

## 5.7.1. Pandai nanmaraiyum

*paṇḍai nānmaṟaiyum vēḷviyum kēḷvip padangaḷum padangaḷin poruḷumpiṇḍamāy virinda piṟangoḷi analum perugiya punalodu nilanumkoṇḍal mārudamum kurai kadal ēḻum ēḻumā malaigaḷum visumbumaṇḍamum tānāy ninṟa emperumān arangamā nagar amarndānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇḍai – time immemorial; nāl maṟaiyum – four vēdams; vēḷviyum – yāgams (sacrifices); kēḷvi – to be heard and learnt; padangaḷum – vyākaraṇa śāstram (grammar); padangaḷin – words’; poruḷum – meanings, viz. the group of ātmās (which are revealed through śāstram); piṇḍamāy – being in the causal state; virinda – (subsequently) expanded; piṟangu – shining; oḷi – having radiance; analum – fire; perugiya – overflowing; punalodu – with water; nilanum – earth; koṇḍal – cloud; mārudamum – wind; kurai – boisterous; ēḻ kadalum – seven oceans; mā – vast; ēḻ malaigaḷum – seven anchoring mountains; visumbum – sky; aṇḍamum – brahmāṇḍam (oval shaped universe); tānāy – having as his prakāram (form); ninṟa – mercifully present; emperumān – sarvēśvaran; aranga mā nagar – in this divyadēśam named śrīrangam; amarndān – mercifully resting

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran who is mercifully present having the four vēdams which are time immemorial, yāgams, vyākaraṇa śāstram which is to be heard and learnt, meanings of the words, viz. the group of ātmās, the prakruti which was in causal state first and then expanded as shining fire which is having radiance, earth with overflowing water, cloud, wind, boisterous seven oceans, vast seven anchoring mountains, sky and brahmāṇḍam, as his prakāram (form), is mercifully resting in this divyadēśam named śrīrangam.

**paṇḍai nānmaṟai …** – As said in kātakam 3-9-50 “*pūrvē pūrvēbhyō vaca ētadūcu:*” (the forefathers repeated the words of their forefathers), since vēdams are learnt based on the repetition of previously spoken words, vēdams which are free from all faults which occur from being created by an individual; the rituals such as yāgams which are ordained in those vēdams; vyākaraṇa śāstram (grammar) which should be learnt as words and letters, by hearing; the group of all ātmās which are known by those words; panca bhūtams (five elements) starting with fire, water, earth etc which are expanded from acit samaśti (group of insentient entities which are together) which is the cause for the multitude of effects; clouds which show up and help the cētanas when they need; wind which also helps similarly; the seven oceans which are boisterous and are like a fence for the earth; the huge mountains which are like anchors for the earth; the ether/space which accommodates all of these in it; pervading the oval shaped universe which is made of all of these, and performing anupravēśam (manifesting his presence to guide all the entities), as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.22.86 “*tāni sarvāṇi tatvapu:*” (everything is a śarīram (body) for that paramātmā), since he remains to be indicated by any word which indicates these entities, sarvēśvaran, who is being the lord by being the ātmā of all these entities which are his bodies, is mercifully resting in śrīrangam. āḻvār says that he got to enjoy that emperumān.

## 5.7.2. Indiran piraman

*indiran piraman īsan enṟu ivargaḷ eṇṇil pal guṇangaḷē iyaṟṟatandaiyum tāyum makkaḷum mikka suṟṟamum suṟṟi ninṟu agalāppandamum pandam aṟuppadōr marundum pānmaiyum palluyirkku ellāmandamum vāḻvum āya emperumān arangamā nagar amarndānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

indiran – indra; piraman – brahmā; īsan – rudra; enṟu – known as; ivargaḷ – these persons; eṇ il – countless; pal guṇangaḷ – reciting the qualities; iyaṟṟa – as they praise; pal uyirkkellām – for the countless jīvātmās; tandaiyum – the father; tāyum – the mother; makkaḷum – children; mikka – abundant; suṟṟamum – paternal relatives; suṟṟi ninṟu – surrounding; agalā – inseparable; bandamum – other relatives; bandam – connection with samsāram; aṟuppadu – eliminating; ōr – unique; marundum – medicine; pānmaiyum – attainable nature; andamum – final resting place; vāḻvum – joy; āya – one who is in the form of these; emperumān – sarvēśvaran; aranga mā nagar – in this divyadēśam named śrīrangam; amarndān – mercifully resting

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

As the persons known as indra, brahmā, rudra et al praise sarvēśvaran reciting his countless auspicious qualities, for countless jīvātmās, he, who is in the form of the father, mother, children, abundant paternal relatives, other relatives who surround and remain inseparable, unique medicine which eliminates the connection with samsāram, attainable nature, final resting place and joy, is mercifully resting in this divyadēśam named śrīrangam.

**indiran …** – Primary dēvatās such as indra, brahmā, rudra who are all created by bhagavān. Since indra is spoken in the beginning, even before brahmā and rudra, it is to be understood that, overall there is not much difference between them; when some say caturmukha (four headed brahmā) as īśvara (supreme lord), rudra will also have such īśvaratvam (lordship); in this manner these persons who are primary for the world, being freed from pride, surrender to sarvēśvaran, reciting his countless auspicious qualities and praising him.

**pal uyirkkellām …** – Being the father who looks after the well-being for all creatures, mother who fulfils the desires, sons who relieve their parents from hell, countless paternal relatives, other relatives who approach and never leave, the medicine which eliminates such connection with samsāram, state of absolute peace after being relieved from the connection with samsāram, the resting abode during deluge for all ātmās, the joy attained through protection, and the creation too which is indicated by these two (deluge and protection). In this manner, sarvēśvaran who is the controller of creation, sustenance and annihilation for all creatures.

## 5.7.3. Mannumanilanum

*mannumānilanum malaigaḷum kadalum vānamum tānavar ulagumtunnu māyiruḷāyt tulangoḷi surungit tollai nānmaṟaigaḷum maṟaiyapinnum vānavarkkum munivarkkum nalgip piṟangiruḷ niṟam keda oru nāḷannamāy anṟangu arumaṟai payandān arangamā nagar amarndānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mannu – firm (hard); mā – vast; nilanum – earth; malaigaḷum – anchoring mountains; kadalum – ocean; vānamum – sky; tānavar – demoniac persons’; ulagum – world (abodes) (all of these); tunnu – dense; mā – huge; iruḷāy – being (covered by) darkness; tulangu – shining; oḷi – radiance; surungi – become shrunk; tollai – anādi (from time immemorial); nāl maṟaigaḷum – four vēdams; maṟaiya – as they disappear; pinnum – again; vānavarkkum – for dēvatās \[celestial entities\]; munivarkkum – for riśis \[sages\]; nalgi – with friendship; piṟangu – abundant; iruḷ – darkness; niṟam keda – to eliminate; anṟu oru nāḷ – at that time; annamāy – being in the form of a swan; angu – for them; aru – difficult to attain; maṟai – vēdams; payandān – one who gave; aranga mā nagar amarndānē – is mercifully resting in this town of śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

When the firm, vast earth, anchoring mountains, ocean, sky and the abodes of demoniac persons became covered by darkness and the shining radiance had shrunk, and as the ancient, four vēdams disappeared, at that time, bhagavān, in the form of a swan. with friendship towards dēvatās and riśis, gave four vēdams which are difficult to attain, to eliminate the abundant darkness; such bhagavān is mercifully resting in this town of śrīrangam.

**mannu mā nilanum …** – All of the hard earth, anchoring mountains, ocean, sky and the abodes of demoniac persons came under the influence of abundant darkness, lost their radiance and at that time the vēdams, which can give light, also disappeared

**pinnum …** – As said in śvētāsvatara upanishad 6-18 “*yō brahmāṇam vidadāti pūrvam* ***yō vai vēdāmśca prahiṇōti tasmai*** l *tam ha dēvam ātmabuddi prasādam mumukśurvai śaraṇam aham prapadyē* ll” (I, desiring to attain mōkśam (śrī vaikuṇṭam), surrender to that supreme entity, who initially created brahmā and who instructed him all the vēdams), instead of backing out thinking “What can I do if they lost the vēdams which I taught them once?”, showing his friendship towards dēvatās and brāhmaṇas, to eliminate the darkness (ignorance), bhagavān performed upadēśam (instructions). That too, he performed upadēśam in the form of a swan which would not seek any service before instructing others \[since one has to serve first, before getting good instructions\]. He revealed the vēdams which are more difficult to attain than attaining bhagavān himself.

**aranga mā nagar amarndānē** – bhagavān who revealed pramāṇam (scriptures) back then, is now mercifully resting in this divyadēśam, śrīrangam, revealing the pramēyam (bhagavān, himself).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.7.4. Mayirum kunram

*māyirum kunṟam onṟu mattāga māsuṇam adanodum aḷavipāyirum pauvam pagadu viṇḍalaṟap padu tirai visumbidaip padarasēyiru visumbum tingaḷum sudarum dēvarum tāmudan tisaippaāyiram tōḷāl alai kadal kadaindān arangamā nagar amarndānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā – vast; irum – being tall; onṟu – unique; kunṟam – mantara mountain; mattāga – placing as churning staff; adanodum – with that (in that mountain); māsuṇam – snake named vāsuki; aḷavi – coiled around; pā – vast; irum – lengthy; pauvam – ocean; pagaduviṇḍu – opening its mouth; alaṟa – to cry out; padu – formed (in it); tirai – waves; visumbidai – in the middle of the sky; padara – to pervade; sē – being distant; iru – vast; visumbu – worlds such as heaven; tingaḷum – moon; sudarum – other radiant objects; dēvarum – dēvatās; udan – simultaneously; tisaippa – to become amazed; alai – agitated with waves; kadal – ocean; āyiram tōḷāl – with thousand shoulders; kadaindān – one who churned; aranga mā nagar amarndānē – is mercifully resting in this town of śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Placing the vast and tall mantara mountain as the churning staff, coiling the snake vāsuki around it, to have the vast and lengthy ocean cry out, to have the waves which are formed in it reach the middle of the sky and pervade, and to have the worlds such as heaven which are at a far distance, moon, other radiant objects and dēvatās become amazed simultaneously, bhagavān churned the ocean which is agitated with waves, with his thousand shoulders. Such bhagavān is mercifully resting in this town of śrīrangam.

**māyirum …** – Having mantara mountain which is not short of vastness and height, coiling vāsuki’s body around it, to have the vast and lengthy ocean cry out like an elephant’s roar, and due to the agitation at that time, the waves which were formed reached up to the sky, filling it; to have worlds such as vast heaven etc which are far away from here, moon, other radiant objects, other dēvatās, to be amazed amazed, bhagavān churned the ocean.

**āyiram tōḷāl …** – Though he churned with four shoulders, \[due to the pace at which he was churning\] it appeared like he churned with thousand shoulders.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.7.5. Engane uyvar

*enganē uyvar? tānavar ninaindāl iraṇiyan ilangu pūṇ agalampongu vengurudi pon malai piḷandu poḻi tarum aruvi ottiḻiyavengaṇ vāḷeyiṟṟōr veḷḷimā vilangal viṇṇuṟak kanal viḻittu eḻundaduanganē okka ari uruvānān arangamā nagar amarndānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tānavar – demoniac persons; ninaindāl – if they thought about (killing of hiraṇya); enganē uyvar – how will they sustain their lives?; iraṇiyan – hiraṇya; pūṇ – with ornaments; ilangu – shining; agalam – from the chest; pongu – overflowing; vem – warm; kurudi – blood; ponmalai – mēru mountain which is made of gold; piḷandu – piercing; poḻi tarum – flowing; aruvi ottu – like a river from the mountain; iḻiya – to run; vem – reddish; kaṇ – eyes; vāḷ – sword-like; eyiṟu – having teeth; mā – huge; ōr – unique; veḷḷi vilangal – silver mountain; viṇ uṟa – reaching the sky; kanal viḻittu – staring cruelly; eḻundadu okka – appearing to be like; angan – such; ari uru ānān – one who incarnated as narasimha; aranga mā nagar amarndānē – is mercifully resting in the divyadēśam, śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān incarnated as narasimha with reddish eyes and sword-like teeth, appearing to be like a huge, unique, silver mountain reaching up to the sky, which is staring cruelly, to make the warm blood from hiraṇya’s chest which is shining with ornaments, overflow to reach the mēru mountain which is made of gold, and to pierce and flow from there. How will the demoniac persons sustain their lives if they thought about hiraṇya’s killing? Such bhagavān is mercifully resting in the divyadēśam, śrīrangam.

**enganē …** – Only those who are favourble towards bhagavān like us and who think like prahlāda “He did this for us” will be uplifted. Other than that how will those demoniac persons who belong to the enemy clan, sustain themselves if they think about this incident? On the chest which is decorated with ornaments.

**pongu vem kurudi …** – The blood which was tumultuously gushing out, not having any other outlet, piercing the mēru mountain and flooding it and falling as a waterfalls. īsn’t he also hiraṇya (golden)? Blood flowing out of hiraṇya’s body due to tearing hiraṇya’s body looks similar to the flow of fluid mixed with many minerals, piercing the mēru and falling down. bhagavān assumed the narasimha form where he was having reddish eyes and shining teeth, and looking similar to a huge, silver mountain piercing through the sky and having reddish eyes. Such bhagavān is mercifully present in śrīrangam to eliminate similar enemies if they are present.

## 5.7.6. Ayiram kunram

*āyiram kunṟam senṟu tokkanaiya adal purai eḻil tigaḻ tiraḷ tōḷāyiram tuṇiya adal maḻup paṟṟi maṟṟavan agal visumbu aṇaiyaāyiram peyarāl amarar senṟu iṟainja aṟi tuyil alai kadal naduvēāyiram sudar vāy aravaṇait tuyinṟān arangamā nagar amarndānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āyiram kunṟam – thousand mountains; tokku – together; senṟadu anaiya – like going; adal purai – fit for a battle; eḻil – radiance; tigaḻ – shining; tiraḷ – gathered; tōḷ āyiram – (kārtavīryan’s) thousand shoulders; tuṇiya – to be severed; adal – in the battle; maḻu – the weapon named maḻu (axe); paṟṟi – holding in his hand; maṟṟu – further; avan – that kārtavīryan; agal – vast; visumbu – heaven (for bravery); aṇaiya – to reach (subsequently); amarar – dēvatās; senṟu – reached; āyiram peyarāl – with sahasranāmam \[thousand names\]; iṟainja – as they praise; alai – as the waves pound; kadal naduvē – in the middle of the ocean; sudar – radiant; āyiram vāy – having thousand mouths; aravu aṇai – on the mattress of tiruvanantāḻvān \[ādiśēśan\]; aṟi tuyil – yōga nidrā (meditation); tuyinṟān – one who did; aranga mā nagar amarndānē – is mercifully resting in the divyadēśam, śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kārtavīryan’s radiant, shining, thousand shoulders looked like thousand mountains gathered together and fit for battle. bhagavān as paraśurāma, holding the weapon named maḻu (axe) severed those shoulders of kārtavīryan and made him reach heaven. Subsequently, dēvatās reached there and praised, reciting sahasranāmam. That bhagavān is resting in the middle of the ocean as the waves are pounding, on the mattress of tiruvanantāḻvān and is in yōga nidrā. Such bhagavān is mercifully resting in the divyadēśam, śrīrangam.

**āyiram kunṟam …** – Just as thousand mountains gathered together, fit for battle, with shining radiance, well-rounded, thousand shoulders were severed by paraśurāma holding an axe in his hand. maṟṟavan – the other person is sahasra bāhu arjunan (kārtavīryārjunan who had thousand shoulders); by such bhagavān’s vanquishing by hand, kārtavīryārjunan attained vīra svargam (heaven of bravery). All the dēvatās who were tormented by him, subsequently recited the thousand divine names of bhagavān and took shelter of him. In the middle of the ocean where waves are pounding within, due to the joy of the presence of bhagvān, bhagavān was having yōga nidrā on tiruvanantāḻvān who is having many radiant mouths as an outlet for the continuous enjoyment of bhagavān. Such bhagavān has mercifully arrived and is present here in the same manner, in śrīrangam.

## 5.7.7. Suri kulal

*suri kuḻal kanivāyt tiruvinaip piritta kodumaiyil kaduvisai arakkaneri viḻittu ilangu maṇi mudi podi seydu ilangai pāḻ paduppadaṟku eṇṇivari silai vaḷaiya adusaram turandu maṟi kadal neṟi pada malaiyālarikulam paṇi koṇḍu alai kadal adaittān arangamā nagar amarndānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

suri – beautiful; kuḻal – hair; kani – like kōvai fruit (a reddish fruit); vāy – having mouth; tiruvinai – sītāp pirātti; eri viḻittu – with cruel sight; piritta – one who separated; kodumai – cruelty; kadu visai – having great speed; arakkan – rāvaṇāsuran’s; ilangu – shining; maṇi – made of precious gems; mudi – crowns; podi seydu – turning to dust; ilangai – lankā; pāḻ paduppadaṟku – to destroy; eṇṇi – vowed; vari – beautiful; silai – bow; vaḷaiya – bent; adu – to be able to kill; saram – arrows (on it); turandu – (joined and) launched; maṟi – waves overlapping; kadal – ocean; neṟi pada – to give way; ari kulam – vānaras (monkeys); paṇi koṇḍu – engaged in service; alai – waves pounding; kadal – ocean; malaiyāl – by hills; adaittān – built a dam; aranga mā nagar amarndānē – is now mercifully resting in the divyadēśam, śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

rāvaṇa, with a cruel sight, separated sītāp pirātti who is having beautiful hair and mouth which is like reddish fruit, from śrī rāma; bhagavān; śrī rāma vowed to turn such rāvaṇāsuran’s shining crowns made of precious gems to dust and destroy lankā. He bent his beautiful bow and launched arrows which can kill, to make the ocean with waves which are overlapping, give way . He engaged the vānaras in service and built a dam on the ocean which has poundinging waves. Such bhagavān is now mercifully resting in the divyadēśam, śrīrangam.

**suri kuḻal …** – As said in “*sukēśyā*” (one who has beautiful hair) and in “*cārukēśīm*” (having beautiful hair), having beautiful divine hair, and well matured mouth – such pirātti. rāvaṇa had the cruelty to separate sītāp pirātti and śrī rāma who said as seen in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.6 “*ananyā rāghavēṇāham*” (I always remain united with śrī rāma) and śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 122.19 “*ananyāhi mayā sītā*” (Does sītā not remain united with me always?) and placed them in separate places. He was having cruelty and great speed; turning his crowns which are made with precious gems which are shining like fire, into dust; alternatively, it can be said that rāvaṇa had a fire like sight with which he stared at pirātti and separated her. śrī rāma vowed to throw lankā into ruin and to be roamed around by dogs and foxes; for that, he used his beautiful bow and killer arrows, and the ocean \[king\] with great agitation came up and said “I will place myself in a favourable way; you can build a dam” and facilitated. The ocean which will swallow whatever is placed in it, let rocks and hills which will drown in the water usually, to stay afloat; bhagavān engaged vānaras who are incapable of doing anything in an organised manner, in service and built the dam on the ocean with rising waves.

## 5.7.8. Uliyay omattu

*ūḻiyāy ōmattu ucciyāy oru kāludaiya tēr oruvanāy ulagilsūḻimāl yānait tuyar keduttu ilangaimalanga anṟu adusaram turandupāḻiyāl mikka pārttanukku aruḷippagalavan oḷi kedap pagalēāḻiyāl anṟangu āḻiyai maṟaittānarangamā nagar amarndānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ūḻiyāy – being the controller of all entities starting with time; ōmattu – in the fire sacrifice; ucciyāy – being the best (due to being vorśipped); oru kāl udaiya – having one wheel; tēr – being the antaryāmi of sūrya who has a chariot; oruvanāy – being unique; ulagil – in the world; sūḻi – having caparison; māl – exulted; yānai – gajēndrāḻvān’s; tuyar – sorrow; keduttu – eliminated; ilangai – lankā; malanga – to become sorrowful; anṟu – during rāmāvatāram; adu – able to kill; saram – arrows; turandu – shot; pāḻiyāl – by strength; mikka – having more; pārtanukku – on arjuna; aruḷi – showing mercy; pagalavan – sun’s; oḷi – radiance; keda – to diminish; pagalē – during the daytime; angu anṟu – during the mahābhārata war; āḻiyāl – by his divine chakra; āziyai – sun; maṟaittān – one who covered; aranga mā nagar amarndānē – is mercifully resting in the divyadēśam, śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being the controller of all entities starting with time, being the best in the fire sacrifice, being the antaryāmi of sūrya who has a chariot which is having one wheel and being unique, bhagavān eliminated the sorrow of gajēndrāḻvān who was caparisoned and who was in exultation, in this world; during rāmāvatāram, he shot arrows which are able to kill, to make lankā become sorrowful; showing mercy on very strong arjuna, he covered the sun to diminish its radiance during the daytime, with his divine chakra; such emperumān is mercifully resting in the divyadēśam, śrīrangam.

**ūḻiyāy …** – Being the controller of all the entities which are indicated by time, being the vorśippable entity of all rituals as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.24](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-24/) “*aham hi sarvayajñānām bhoktā ca prabhur Eva ca*” (I am only the enjoyer and the benefactor of all yajñas) and [śrī bhagavat gītā 5.29](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/5-29/) “*bhōktāram yajñatapasām*” (one who accepts yajña (sacrifices) and tapas (penances)); being the antaryāmi of sun who is having one wheel and thus being the focus of upāsana (worship); he eliminated the sorrow of śrī gajēndrāḻvān who was in exultation and roaming around with caparison; he shot his killer arrows to have the residents of lankā suffer by having to share one garment among seven persons; showing mercy towards very strong arjuna, to have sun’s radiance diminish, in the \[day\] time which is apt for his radiance, he covered the sun with his divine chakra which has the radiance of thousand suns. Since the radiance of the worldly sun is limited, it will eliminate darkness; unlike that, the radiance of tiruvāḻi āḻvān (sudarśana chakra) cannot be seen directly and hence it blinded everyone’s eyes.

## 5.7.9. Peyinar

*pēyinār mulaiyūṇ piḷḷaiyāy orugālperu nilam viḻungi adu umiḻndavāyanāy mālāy ālilai vaḷarndumaṇi mudi vānavar tamakkuccēyanāy adiyēṟku aṇiyanāy vanduen sindaiyuḷ venduyar aṟukkumāyanāy anṟu kunṟam onṟu eduttānarangamā nagar amarndānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pēyin – pūtanā’s; Ar – filled with poison; mulai – bosom; ūṇ – one who consumed; piḷḷaiyāy – being a child; oru kāl – once (during deluge); peru – vast; nilam – earth; viḻungi – consumed; adu – that earth (during the time of creation); umiḻnda – one who let it out; vāyanāy – having mouth; mālāy – being greater than all; ālilai – on a tender banyan leaf; vaḷarndu – one who mercifully rested; maṇi – filled with precious gems; mudi – having crowns; vānavar tamakku – for the dēvatās; sēyanāy – being one who is far away; adiyēṟku – for me, the servitor; aṇiyanāy – being one who is in close proximity; vandu – he himself arrives; en sindaiyuḷ – in my mind; vem – cruel; tuyar – sorrows; aṟukkum – one who destroys; anṟu – during that kriṣṇāvatāram; āyanāy – being kriṣṇa, a covherd boy; onṟu kunṟam – gōvardana hill; eduttān – one who lifted up and protected the cows; aranga mā nagar amarndānē – is mercifully resting in the divyadēśam, śrīrangam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being a child, he consumed the milk from pūtanā’s bosom which was filled with poison; having the mouth which once consumed the vast earth and let it out; being greater than all, he mercifully rested on a tender banyan leaf; being the one who is far away for the dēvatās who are having crowns filled with precious gems, and is in close proximity for me, the servitor; he is the one who himself arrives in my mind and destroys the cruel sorrows in my mind; he lifted up the gōvardana hill and protected the cows as kriṣṇa, a covherd boy, during kriṣṇāvatāram; such emperumān is mercifully resting in the divyadēśam, śrīrangam.

**pēyinār …** – One who suckled on pūtanā’s bosom filled with poison, being an ignorant child, without knowing the difference between mother’s bosom and other person’s bosom.

**oru kāl** – Being ignorant about the result, is common at all times for bhagavān. He is having such mouth with which, once, he placed the vast earth in his stomach, and since he could not digest it, he spat it out; he is greater than all and the controller of all; he assumed a small form and placed the great worlds in his stomach and mercifully rested on a fresh banyan leaf; he is far away from brahmā et al and is a servitor for persons like me; even as I did not even have the desire for him, he himself came to me and destroyed my sorrows in the mind, as kriṣṇa.

**anṟu kunṟam onṟu eduttān** – Held the gōvardana hill, and protected the cows and covherd people, who cannot even realise the favours done by him.

## 5.7.10. Ponnum

*ponnum māmaṇiyum muttamum sumanduporudirai mānadi pudai sūḻnduannamādu ulavum alai punal sūḻndaarangamā nagar amarndānaimannu māmāda mangaiyar talaivanmānavēl kaliyan vāy oligaḷpanniya panuval pāduvār nāḷumpaḻavinai paṟṟu aṟuppārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ponnum – gold; mā – great; maṇiyum – precious gems; muttamum – pearl; sumandu – collecting; porudu – banging against one another; tirai – having waves; mā – great; nadi – by tirukkāvēri (river kāvēri); pudai – in the surroundings; sūḻndu – surrounded; mādu – on the sides; annam – swans; ulavum – roaming around; alai – having waves; punal – by ponds such as candra puśakariṇi; sūḻnda – surrounded; aranga mā nagar – in the great town of śrīrangam; amarndānai – on periya perumāḷ who is mercifully reclining; mannu – eternal; mā – great; mādam – having mansions; mangaiyar – for the residents of the town tirumangai; talaivan – one who is the lord; mānam – expansive; vēl – having the weapon spear; kaliyan – āḻvār; vāy oligaḷ – mercifully spoken; panniya – one which is having no shortcomings in the qualities; panuval – pāsurams; pāduvār – those who sing; nāḷum – daily; paḻa vinai – the ancient karma; paṟṟu aṟuppār – will rid of completely, without the scent

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The great town of śrīrangam is surrounded by tirukkāvēri which is having great waves which are banging against one another and whose water is collecting gold, great precious gems and pearl; it is also surrounded by ponds such as candra puśakariṇi which are having swans roaming around, in the surroundings. periya perumāḷ is mercifully reclining in such śrīrangam. tirumangai āḻvār, who is having the expansive spear and is the lord of the residents of the town tirumangai which is having eternal, great mansions, has mercifully spoken these ten pāsurams which are having no shortcomings in the qualities; those who sing these pāsurams daily, will rid the ancient karma completely, without the scent.

**ponnum …** – There is a great river which is carrying gold, precious gems which are priceless, pearl and is having waves which are banging against one another – that is kāvēri. In those surroundings, the sides in śrīrangam are surrounded with ponds such as candra puśkariṇi which have swans roaming around; sarvēśvaran has descended on such śrīrangam and is mercifully resting here. tirumangai āḻvār who is the leader of the residents of tirumangai which is having mansions which are not desytroyed even in praḷayam (deluge) and is having expansive spear, mercifully spoke ten pāsurams on such emperumān. Those who can recite these ten pāsurams which are faultless in all qualities, will get to eliminate their karma which has been accumulated since time immemorial, along with their vāsanā (scent).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8 Elai edalan

## 5.8.1. Elai edalan

*ēḻai ēdalan kīḻ magan ennāduirangi maṟṟavaṟku innaruḷ surandu māḻai mān mada nōkki un tōḻi umbi embi enṟoḻindilai ugandutōḻan nī enakku ingoḻi enṟasoṟkaḷ vandu adiyēn manattu irundida āḻi vaṇṇa! nin adiyiṇai adaindēn aṇipoḻil tiruvarangattammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēḻai – desirous for worldly pleasures (ignorant); ēdalan – enemy; kīḻ magan – lowly; ennādu – not considering; irangi – showing his mercy; maṟṟu – further; avaṟku – for such guhapperumāḷ; in – sweet (without any expectation); aruḷ – mercy; surandu – showed; māḻai – young; mān – deer’s; madam – tender; nōkki – this sītāp pirātti who is having eyes like; un tōḻi – your friend; umbi – lakśmaṇa, who is your brother; embi – is my brother; enṟu – just on saying this; oḻindilai – not stopping; ugandu – affectionately; nī – you; enakku – for me; tōḻan – a friend; ingu oḻi – remain here; enṟa soṟkaḷ – the words which were spoken; vandu – arriving through narrations repeated for generations, into my ears; adiyēn manattu – me, the servitor, in my heart; irundida – remaining firm (becoming involved in that); āḻi vaṇṇa – having nature of the ocean; aṇi – decorative; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; tiruvarangattu – mercifully reclining in śrīrangam; ammānē – Oh lord!; nin adiyiṇai – your pair of divine feet; adaindēn – I surrender unto

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

śrī rāma, not considering that guhapperumāḷ was desirous for worldly pleasures (ignorant), an enemy and lowly, showed mercy to him and further showed sweet mercy to him in saying “This sītāp pirātti, who is having tender eyes which are like those of a young deer, is your friend, and your brother lakśmaṇa is my brother, you are my friend and you remain here”. Such words spoken by you, arriving through narrations repeated for generations, into my ears, are remaining in this servitor’s (my) heart firmly. Oh one who is having the nature of the ocean! Oh lord who is mercifully reclining in śrīrangam which is surrounded by decorative orchards! I surrender unto your pair of divine feet.

**ēḻai** – ajñan (ignorant. When asked “Would ēḻai mean ignorant?” it actually means desirous. Since desiring for worldly pleasures is resulting from ignorance, ēḻai could mean ignorant. ajñānam is in three forms – jñāna anudayam (not acquired knowledge), anyatā jñānam (understanding an object to be something else) and viparīta jñānam (misunderstanding the quality of an object). When knowledge occurs, jñāna anudayam will be eliminated; by true knowledge, anyatā jñānam will be eliminated; but viparīta jñānam in the form of worldly enjoyment is difficult to eliminate. He \[guhap perumāḷ\] is opposite to your highness, who is said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.12 “*jñāna sampanna:*” (endowed with knowledge). With this, his shortcoming in knowledge is identified.

**ēdalan** – Inimical. His inimical nature of flashing his sword while asking his mother to feed him, is explained. He is opposite to what is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 50.56 “*ripūṇām api vatsala:*” (Oh, one who has motherly forbearance even towards enemies!). He is opposite to one who who is mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 35.11 “*maryādānām ca lōkasya kartā kārayitā ca sa:*” (That śrī rāma is the epitome of maintaining honour/dignity and one who engages others to be honourable/dignified), by always disregarding the rules. With this, his shortcoming in conduct is identified.

**kīḻmagan** – He is having a birth where all of the aforementioned qualities are ornaments. The previously mentioned two aspects can be remedied through knowledge and atonement respectively. But this cannot be remedied. He is opposite to one who is mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.8 “… *ikśvāku vamśa prabhava:*” (the descendant of ikśvāku dynasty). With this, his shortcoming in birth is identified. With these three, greatness of perumāḷ’s (śrī rāma’s) simplicity is explained.

**ennādu irangi** – śrī rāma showed his mercy without seeing any of these; śrī rāma showered his mercy towards guhap perumāḷ, the same mercy which was shown to sages who are said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.44 “*riśīṇām agnikalpānām*” (sages who are like fire) who are upāsakas (those who practice bhakti yōgam) having high birth, knowledge and conduct, to help in their sādanā (bhakti yōgam) and to iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31-25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (I would carry out all tasks of servitude). Alternative explanation. **ennādu irangi** – While guhap perumāḷ did not utter these words, śrī rāma himself showered his mercy towards him. It is said that those who surrender are supposed to inform their lowliness as in [stōtra ratam 22](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-22/) “*na darmaniśtō’smi*” (I am not firm on karma yōgam), [stōtra ratnam 62](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/sthothra-rathnam-62/) “*amaryāda:*” (one who crossed the boundaries of vēdam) andśrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17-12 “*rāvaṇō nāma durvruttō rākśasō rākśasēśvara*: l *tasyāhamanujō bhrātā vibhīśaṇa iti śruta*: ll” (There is a person, rāvaṇa, who is a demon, having bad conduct and who is the leader of demons. I, who am his brother, am known by the name vibhīśaṇa).

When asked “Why is āḻvār uttering words which are to be uttered by śrī guhap perumāḷ?” It is by bhagavān’s thoughts.

**maṟṟu avaṟku** – Further, for him.

**in aruḷ surandu** – Further to accepting him, śrī rāma showered mercy to him.

**in aruḷ** – Mercy for śrī rāma’s sake.

**surandu** – Just like a cow will secrete milk on seeing the calf nearby, śrī rāma showered his qualities.

Subsequent portion of the pāsuram, explains this aspect of showering mercy.

**māḻai mān mada nōkki** – Now, āḻvār is highlighting who is to be approached first, after identifying the defects of self. sītāp pirātti who is having the eyes which are similar to the tender of eyes of a young deer. With this – though the relationship is common for the ātmā towards pirātti and bhagavān, the importance of pirātti’s merciful glance is identified. As she glances the ātmā, she will then glance at bhagavān. It is said “*prēkśitajñāstu kōsalā:*” (Residents of kōsala town will understand the mind from one’s glance). For a loving couple, there is no need to exchange words. Her glance seems to be saying “Why are you not accepting such a defective person?” He is of the nature who will follow her if he observes her youthfulness and glance.

**un tōḻi** – Due to his simplicity, he is saying \[about pirātti to guhap perumāḷ\] “your friend” instead of saying “your lord”. Noble ones will even call their servitors \[respectfully\] as “*aṇṇā*” (brother), “*āccī*” (mother). They \[sītāp pirātti and śrī rāma\] will also speak in this manner only. śrī rāma tells the assembly of his advisors in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 “*mithra bhāvēna*” \[Even if they pretend to be friends). sītāp pirātti tells rāvaṇa in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.19 “*mitramaupayikam*” (befriend śri rāma) and in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.20 “*tēna maitrī bhavatu tē*” (let friendship develop for you, with him). These words are not mere lip-service, but even during the attainment of goal, bhagavān grants equality \[for the ātmā\] in guṇa (qualities) as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.1.3 “*niranjana: paramam sāmyam upaiti*” (muktātmā (the liberated soul) attains distinguished equality with emperumān), bhōgam (enjoyment), dēham (body) and bhōjñam (matter of enjoyment).

**umbi embi** – Your brother \[lakśmaṇa\] is my brother. Why is śrī rāma saying like this? It is by the will of iḷaiyaperumāḷ who considers those who are dearly accepted by śrī rāma, on a par with himself. garuda purāṇam 219.6 to 219.9 “*bhaktiraśtavidā hyēśā yasmin mlēccē’pi vartatē \| sa viprēndrō muni: śrīmān  sa yatis sa ca paṇḍita: \|\| mayā pūjyas sadā cālau madbhakta: śvapcō’pi ya: \| tasmai dēyam tatō grāhyam sa ca pūjyō yatā hyaham \|\|*” (The mlēcca \[one who is outside the varṇāśrama system\], who has these eight types of bhakti, is the top-most of brāhmaṇa who meditates upon (bhagavān); he is the one who has the wealth of kainkaryam; he is a renunciate; he is a scholar; though he is a caṇḍāḷa, my devotee is always to be vorśipped along with me. One can give (knowledge to) him; and can accept (knowledge) from him; he is always venerable on a par with me); [tirumālai 42](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/thirumalai-42/) “*toḻuminīr kodumin koḷmin enṟu ninnōdum okka* *vaḻipada aruḷināy pōl*” (saying “worship (them), teach them (the special knowledge that you have), learn from them (if they have special knowledge)” you mercifully ordered to worship them as your equal). When one goes from samsāram to paramapadam as a liberated person, the residents of paramapadam will wash such liberated person’s divine feet and accept that person as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-9-10-vidhi-vagai/) “*padiyinil pānginil pādangaḷ kaḻuvinar*” (being pleased, the nityasūris who are well versed in vēdam and having distinguished nature, cleansed the divine feet of such śrīvaiṣṇavas, in an honourable manner, in their respective abode). iḷaiyaperumāḷ is one who has separated from such nityasūris and descended here. With this, śrī rāma, brought acceptance of a vaiṣṇava for guhap perumāḷ. It is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.5.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/09/thiruvaimozhi-7-5-10-varththai-aribavar/) “*avan seyyum sēmam*” (the protection given by the one who eliminated the sorrow) and amalanādipirān 1 “*adiyārkkennai ātpadutta vimalan*” (The pure lord who will make me become a servitor of his devotees).

**enṟu oḻindilai** – You did not stop there. His friendship with guhap perumāḷ is impicitly understood when pirātti was said to be a friend and lakśmaṇa was said to be a brother.

**ugandu** – Due to joy, śrī rāma is saying “*tōḻan nī*” (you are a friend). Joy does not have a limit.

**tōḻan nī enakku** – When one announces self’s defects, pursues puruśakāram (recommendation) and acquires acceptance of vaiṣṇavas (devotees), subsequently the true nature of upāyam \[bhagavān\] will be thought about. āḻvār is highlighting that \[i.e., by “enakku”\].

**ingu oḻi** – ītnappears that even guhap perumāḷ set out to follow śrī rāma. \[śrī rāma is thinking\] We placed one person \[bharatāḻvān\] to preserve the capital city. You remain here to preserve the route. Unlike these two personalities, iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) acted against the will of perumāḷ to serve perumāḷ as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.7 “*kriyatām iti mām vada*” (Your should order me to make me serve you).

**enṟa soṟkaḷ** – Not the meanings, even the words \[*māḻai mān mada nōkki un tōḻi umbi embi*\] are bringing sorrow to āḻvār \[i.e. such quality of śrī rāma is melting āḻvār\].

**vandu** – Though this happened long ago, the message came through continuous transmission; the matter is now well settled in āḻvār’s divine heart. These words were documented by śrī vālmeeki bhagavān as in śrī rāmāyaṇam bālakāṇḍam 1.28 “*guhēna sahitō rāma: lakśmanēna ca sītayā*” (only after uniting with guhan, śrī rāma felt that he had united with lakśmaṇa and sītā)!

**adiyēn manattu irundida** – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 16.39 “*samsmarāmyasya vākyāni …*” (I am reminded with those pleasing, sweet, heart-felt, nectar-like words of bharata), these become rooted in āḻvār’s heart. Just as a servitor’s pitiful words will be rooted in the master’s heart for the servitor’s protection, the master’s words will remain rooted in the servitor’s heart to serve him.

**āḻi vaṇṇa** – Just as an ocean is filled with precious gems, bhagvān is an ocean which is filled with qualities which facilitate surrender. śaraṇāgati gadyam “*apāra kāruṇya sauśeelya vātsalya audārya aiśvarya saundarya mahōdadē*” (Oh one who is like an ocean of auspicious qualities such as mercy, approacability, forbearance, magnanimity, opulence, beauty etc), As said in matsya purāṇam 20 “*yatā ratnāni jaladē: asankyēyāni putraka! tatā guṇāhyanantasya asankyēyā mahātmana:*” (Oh child! Just like the ocean contains countless gems and precious stones, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has countless auspicious qualities), just as the precious stones are born in the ocean, remain there and not present everywhere and desired by everyone, bhagavān’s qualities are similar. Alternative explanation: One who has a rejuvenating form similar to that of an ocean! As soon as one sees his form, one’s sufferings will get eliminated.

**nin adiyiṇai** – The “*caraṇau*” (divine feet) in dvaya mahā mantram is thought about.

**adaindēn** – It is explained that in the verb \[i.e. prapadyē in dvaya mahā mantram\], the present tense is guaṇam (of secondary importance) \[i.e. surrendering once is sufficient. Continuously repeating is just to remind ourselves of our first surrender\].

**aṇi poḻil …** – Since āḻvār first speaks about śrī rāmāvatāram and then concludes that here in śrīrangam, as said in [tirumālai 11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thirumalai-11/) “*nam sēvaganār* *maruviya periya kōyil*” (the famous śrīrangam where the valorous śrī rāma is reclining), it is to be understood that the same śrī rāma is reclining here. aṇi (decoration) is an adjective for both orchard and the temple. That is, being an ornament for samsāra (material world). Though it appears that he reclined here seeing the natural beauty, the real reason for his merciful reclining here is to seek devotees.

**ammānē** – Since he is the owner, he is seeking his possessions and mercifully reclined here.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan
