## 5.8.2. Vada ma magan

*vāda mā magan maṟkadam vilangumaṟṟōr sādi enṟoḻindilai ugandukādal ādaram kadalinum perugac ceytagavinukku illai kaimmāṟu enṟukōdil vāymaiyināyodum udanēuṇban nān enṟa ōṇporuḷ enakkumādal vēndum enṟu adiyiṇai adaindēnaṇipoḻil tiruvarangattammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṟṟu ōr sādi – Born in a different species (other than human); vilangu – (that is) animal species which lacks knowledge; maṟkadam – (that too) monkey; vādam – (further, reason for pride) vāyu’s \[deity for wind\]; mā – best; magan – son; enṟu – seeing these inferior aspects; oḻindilai – not abandoning (further); ugandu – showing affection (towards him); kādal – friendship; ādaram – (ultimate stage of such friendship being) love; kadalilum – becoming greater than ocean; peruga – as it grows; sey – (you) did; tagavinukku – (matching) for the favour; kaimmāṟu – return favour; illai – not there; enṟu – saying that; kōdu il – faultless; vāymaiyināyodum – with you who have (sweet) speech; udanē – remaining together (embracing you); nān – I; uṇban – (ultimately pleasant divine form) will enjoy; enṟa – mercifully said in this manner; oḷ – beautiful; poruḷ – principle; enakkum – in my case also; ādal vēṇḍum enṟu – considering that it should happen; aṇi – decorative; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; tiruvarangattu – mercifully reclining in śrīrangam; ammānē – Oh lord!; nin adiyiṇai – your pair of divine feet; adaindēn – I surrender unto

**Перевод:**

**In the previous pāsuram, āḻvār surrendered unto periya perumāḷ highlighting that bhagavān should show the acceptance which was shown towards śrī guhap perumāḷ who was inferior in birth, conduct etc, towards āḻvār too. In the previous pāsuram, the inferiority highlighted is in human species. Here, āḻvār is highlighting that just as bhagavān not only accepted an animal which is in a different species without seeing the defects but also engaged that hanuman in his intimate service \[of going and meeting sītāp pirātti\], he should accept service from āḻvār also. For such adikāri \[who is a prapanna, a surrendered person\], after bhagavān’s acceptance, it appears that he need not pursue any means and only engage in service. In the previous pāsuram, this was explained in “ingoḻi” (remain here).**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Not abandoning hanuman, seeing inferior aspects such as being born in animal species which lacks knowledge and is different from humans, that too monkey and that too being the best son of vāyu, which can be a reason for pride, śrī rāma showed affection, friendship and love which grows bigger than ocean, towards hanuman. He said “There is no matching return favour for the favour you have done; I will embrace you, who have sweet and faultless speech and remain together with you and enjoy you”. Oh lord who is mercifully reclining in śrīrangam which is surrounded by decorative orchards! I surrender unto your pair of divine feet, considering that, this same principle should also happen to me.

**vāda mā magan …** – Just as we need to highlight our inferior nature for his acceptance, we need to do the same for kainkaryam (to serve him); even while highlighting the inferior nature of an entity from a different species, it is enough to say “*maṟṟōr sādi*” (a different species); to highlight the lowliness in that, āḻvār is saying “*vilangu*” (animal). tiryak – vilangu – animal; due to shortcoming in knowledge, they are known as vilangu. It is said “*yastu tiryak pravruttissyāt tiryak yōnissa ucyatē”* (Due to their ignorant acts they are known as tiryak). Shortcoming in knowledge – not having regulated food, not respecting parent-child relationship while mating etc.

**maṟkadam** – Further lowliness is highlighted. Monkey is of the nature to forcefully grab even what is offered to it out of kindness as said in “*vānarēṇa mayāsaha*” (with me, who is a monkey).

**vāda mā magan** – vāyu’s best son. While explaining the inferior nature of his birth, why is superior birth (dēvatās), highlighted? Here, it is not to speak about the birth, but the nature. The lowliness mentioned previously is nothing compared to the ahankāram (ego) which is derived from being vāyu’s son. ahankāram is the reason for arta and kāma \[wealth and lust/desire\]. This will lead to destruction of one’s svarūpam (true nature). This superior birth is the reason for such ahankāram. Even this has to be abandoned first among the aspects which are to be abandoned as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat “*puṇya pāpē vidūya*” (Abandoning puṇyam and pāpam, one attains liberation); that is why it is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*sarvadarmān parityajya*” (Abandoning all means).

**enṟu oḻindilai** – To abandon, any one of these inferior aspects is sufficient; you did not abandon seeing these aspects. For a merciful person, these will not be the reason to abandon someone.

Not only did he not abandon, but

**ugandu** – That is- creating kainkaryams for the servitor, and instead of thinking that it is apt for the servitor, thinking that it is a benefit for bhagavān himself, and not making the servitor worry about how to do return favour. Subsequently in the pāsuram, this ugappu (joy) is further elaborated.

**kādal ādaram** – īsn’t this repetition \[of the earlier mentioned quality\]? Only in statements which are meant to identify a particular entity, bound by the rules of avyāpti (absence of a trait) and ativyāpti (trait which is present elsewhere also), this defect of repetition is seen; since āḻvār is saying out of sorrow and affection, such defects are not seen. Further, by the intent also, these words are different. As in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.5.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-1-andhamaththu-anbu/) “*sendāmarait tadangaṇ*” (reddish lotus like eyes which are expansive), same words are repetitively used due to this reason \[of overwhelming affection\]. The result of kādal (love) is ādaram (great affection) as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.62](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-62/) “*sangāt sanjāyatē kāma:*” (due to that attachment, lust (that, without engaging in which, one finds it unbearable) occurs abundantly). Whatever is said in the interaction of the worldly people, the same thing is explained in śrī rāma and sītāp pirātti. As soon as pirātti saw śrī rāma, she first developed attachment thinking “Hopefully he will break the bow and marry me”; subsequently she remained unsustainable without enjoying him; for śrī rāma, he acquired attachment towards sītāp pirātti thinking “She is handed over by elders”. As said in [stōtra ratnam 38](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-38/) “*guṇēna rūpēṇa vilāsacēśtitai*:” ([pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) amazes you with her qualities, beautiful form and nice activities), he acquired great desire towards her.

**kadalinum peruga** – At the time when it increases, even ocean becomes small like a hoof-step. It appears that both the entities \[śrī rāma and hanuman\] are like ocean. Increasing means – \[For sītāp pirātti\] violating the boundaries. That is, instead of remaining in the state as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 39-30 “*śaraistu sankulām krutvā lankām parabalārdana*: l *mām nayēd yadi kākutstas tat tasya sadruśam bhavēt* ll” (If śrī rāmapirān, who annihilates the strength of his enemies, bewilders lankā with his arrows and takes me with him, it will be apt for him), trying to kill oneself by hanging from the tree using the hairlock. \[For śrī rāma\] instead of remaining in the state as said in “*avākyanādara:*” (Will not speak anything and not support anyone), becoming as in “*avagāhyārṇavam svapsyē*” (in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.9 “*avagāhyārṇavam svapsyē*” (I am going to sleep under the sea).

**sey tagavinukku** – tagavu – darmam. That is, an act which is done without any intent for return favour. As said in  \[śrī rāmāyaṇam – yudda Kāṇḍam – 1-11 “*darmata: parirakśitā:*” (we got protected by your grace), isn’t he the one who protected us without any expectation.

**illai kaimmāṟu enṟu** – The words which are to be spoken by śēśabhūtan (servitor) towards jīvātmā, are spoken by śrī rāma, the lord himself, out of his simiplicity. āḻvār’s opinion is “hanuman is thinking – He handed over his divine ring to me, and while everyone was roaming and searching for sītāp pirātti, he made me get this great benefit as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 30.3 says ‘*yām kapīnām sahasrāṇi subhahūnyayutāni ca* l *dikśu sarvāsu mārgantē sēyamāsāditā mayā* ll’ (She, who was searched in all directions by thousands of monkeys in many groups, was found out by me) . I should be saying these words, but he is saying such words filled with gratitude towards me”.

**kōdil vāymaiyināyodum** – vāymai – act of speech. That is – speaking. Speech not having fault means – as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 31.1 “*samśravē maduram vākhyam*” (words which are sweet to hear), making pirātti accept in her divine heart that these words are truthful, making her sustain herself and making śrī rāma sustain himself by saying as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 65.10 “*druśtā sītā*” (I have seen sītā).

**udanē uṇban nān enṟa** – Let us live together from now onvards. This principle is explained based on what is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 1.13 “*ēśa sarvasva bhūtastu*” (This embrace of mine is equivalent to everything else) – bhagavān’s tirumēni (divine form) is very dear to both bhagavān and his servitors, just as eating from the same plate. *sarvasva bhūta:* – bhagavān’s divine form is dearer than true nature, \[ordinary\] forms, qualities and even his divine consorts. This is because – the divine form instills taste \[in the mind of the ātmā\], it is the means \[i.e., divine feet are the means\]. For the rakśakan (protector), his divine form is the main tool for protection \[of his devotees\]; hanuman also did not want to give up his body \[and ascend to paramapadam\], because his body was embraced by bhagavān’s divine form.

**oṇ poruḷ** – This ultimate principle.

**enakkum ādal vēṇḍum enṟu** – Those who are desirous will not give up thinking “How can we desire for such great benefit?”.

**adiyiṇai adaindēn** – āḻvār is thinking that nothing will go unaccompliśed through surrender. When it comes from bhagavān, everything will be successful.

**adiyiṇai adaindēn** – Difference from hanuman who came announcing that “I found your wealth”.

**aṇi poḻil tiruvarangattammānē** – Did you not come and mercifully recline here to engage those who become favourable towards you, in your kainkaryam?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.3. Kadigol pumbolil

*kadigoḷ pūmboḻil kāmaru poygaivaigu tāmarai vāngiya vēḻammudiyum vaṇṇam ōr muḻuvali mudalaipaṟṟa maṟṟadu nin caraṇ ninaippakkodiya vāy vilanginnuyir malangakkoṇḍa sīṟṟam onṟuṇḍuḷadu aṟindu unadiyanēnum vandu adiyiṇai adaindēnaṇipoḻil tiruvarangattammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kadi koḷ – having fragrance; pū – filled with flowers; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; kāmaru – desirable; poygai – in the pond; vaigu – present; tāmarai – lotus flower; vāngiya – plucked; vēḻam – śrī gajēndran \[elephant\]; mudiyum vaṇṇam – to terminate (its curse); ōr – contemplating; muḻuvali – having complete strength; mudalai – crocodile; paṟṟa – as it tightly clutched; maṟṟu – further; adu – that elephant; nin saraṇ – your divine feet; ninaippa – as it meditated upon (at that time); kodiya – cruel; vāy – having mouth; vilangin – crocodile’s; uyir – life; malanga – to suffer; koṇḍa – assumed; onṟu – unique (for the sake of his devotee); sīṟṟam – anger; uṇḍu – occurred; uḷadu – the anger which was present (to destroy the enemy of the devotee); aṟindu – knowing; un – for you; adiyanēn – I, who am your servitor; vandu – came helplessly; aṇi – decorative; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; tiruvarangattu – mercifully reclining in śrīrangam; ammānē – Oh lord!; nin adiyiṇai – your pair of divine feet; adaindēn – I surrender unto

**Перевод:**

**In the previous pāsurams, bhagavān’s acceptance and kainkaryam, which is the result of such acceptance, were spoken about; here, āḻvar is saying “Just like you eliminated the hurdles for kainkaryam for śrī gajēndrāḻvān and engaged him in kainkaryam, you should eliminate my hurdles and engage me in kainkaryam”. Since lowliness should be announced for acceptance and kainkaryam, he did that before; to eliminate the hurdles, one’s lowliness need not be announced; acceptance will occur if one reaches out to the upāyam (means, that is bhagavān); as bhagavān becomes the upāyam, he will engage the servitor in his kainkaryam; now, the only thing which remains is the elimination of hurdles; the hurdles are in two forms – indriya vaśyatā (bound by senses) and yama vaśyatā (bound by yama, the deity for death); in the subsequent pāsurams, yama vaśyatā is explained; here indriya vaśyatā is explained. How is this done? āḻvār is saying “Just as you eliminated the crocodile which was the hurdle for śrī gajēndrāḻvān, you should mercifully eliminate the senses which are my hurdles”. For a prapanna (surrendered person), indriya vaśyatā starts from attachment towards worldly pleasures and goes up to having pride and possessiveness in kainkaryam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

śrī gajēndran (the elephant) plucked the lotus flower which was present in the desirable pond which was surrounded by orchards which are filled with fragrant flowers; the completely strong crocodile which was contemplating the means to terminate its curse, tightly clutched the elephant; as the elephant meditated on your divine feet, you assumed a unique anger to make the crocodile with cruel mouth, suffer. Oh lord who is mercifully reclining in śrīrangam which is surrounded by decorative orchards! I, who am your servitor and have come helplessly, surrender unto your pair of divine feet, considering the anger you had (towards the enemy of your devotee).

**kadi koḷ …** – It would have been enough to say “*poygai vaigu tāmarai*” (lotus in a pond) for the task taken up by śrī gajēndrāḻvān, i.e., to find a flower to offer to bhagavān. Why is the pond described in this manner? Due to lack of rain, the whole world was tormented and there were no flowers anywhere; at that time, he observes this orchard in front of him; as he observes that the orchard is well grown, he assumed that he will find a pond inside.

**kadi koḷ pūm poḻil** – The orchard which has lots of fragrance and flowers. As he went towards the orchard, he was hit by the fragrance and understood that there is flower inside.

**kāmaru poygai** – Attractive pond. Being attractive means being very deep and making one jump into it without thinking “Would there be any dangerous entities inside?”

**vaigu tāmarai** – Due to lack of rain, the lotus flowers will leave everywhere else and will be present in the pond on the mountain top.

**vāngiya vēḻam** – By its strength and eagerness, the elephant plucked it as if plucking something which was placed by self.

**mudiyum vaṇṇam …** – As it entered eagerly in this manner and plucked the flower, the crocodile which was contemplating “Will I see an elephant’s foot?” caught the elephant’s foot.

**vēḻam mudiyum vaṇṇam –** The crocodile did not got hold of the elephant’s foot to kill it; but to be free from the curse, it had. āḻvār is using these words out of his sorrow on thinking about the elephant’s situation.

**ōr mudalai** – Unique crocodile. This is not a crocodile which got hold of a favourable person’s (devotee’s) foot, for getting uplifted.

**muḻu vali** – Since the pond is not the natural habitat of the elephant, it lost its strength; but the crocodile became stronger since it was its natural habitat.

**paṟṟa** – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.2 “*sa bhrātuścaraṇau gādam nipīdya*” (lakśmaṇa, who brings joy to the clan of raghu and who is highly renowned, getting hold of his elder brother’s divine feet firmly), to have its desire fulfilled, it held the elephant’s foot tightly. Since the crocodile does not have any other faculty, it can only hold on with its mind.

**maṟṟadu** – The elephant, subsequently. As said in viṣṇu darmam 69-46 says “*gaja ākarśatē dīrē grāham ākarśatē jalē* l *tayōr dvandvasamam yuddam divyam varśasahasrakam* ll” (gajēndran was pulling the crocodile towards land; crocodile was pulling the elephant towards water. This equal fight between them went on for thousand years by dēvamānam (one dēvamānam is equivalent to 360 earth years), for a long time, the crocodile pulled the elephant inside the pond and the elephant pulled the crocodile outside the pond, and the elephant finally lost its strength. ahankāram (pride) is the cause for non-attainment of the goal; if one drops that and surrenders to bhagavān, he will accomplish his goal.

**nin saraṇ ninaippa** – While śrī gajēndrāḻvān was suffering in this manner, he did not call out for bhagavān \[initially\]; the reason for that – he thought “Why should I disturb sarvēśvaran for this small worm in water? let me defeat it”. bhagavān is not unaware of his suffering; he thought “let me help him when he gives up his pride”.

**saraṇ ninaippa** – \[viṣṇu darmam “*paramāpadam āpanna:*” ślōkam is explained\] As śrī gajēndrāḻvān became weak and started meditating upon bhagavān’s divine feet as said in viṣṇu darmam “*manasā cintayan harīm*” (thought about hari in his mind), he could have thought “I have been suffering for long, but he has not come to my rescue”, but did not think like that; “*paramāpadam āpanna:*” The greatness of the danger is – it made sarvēśvaran to come and help; the danger has become valuable. “*nārāyaṇa parāyaṇa:*” – Unlike brahmā et al who surrender unto bhagavān for worldly benefits, śrī gajēndrāḻvān is surrendering to attain bhagavān only. The body which tried for a long time, had become weak. Even the act of speech as said in siṟiya tirumadal “nārāyaṇā! Oh maṇivaṇṇā!” (Oh nārāyaṇa! Oh maṇivaṇṇa!) became subdued and got to a state where he could only meditate in his mind as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*vāng manasi sampadyatē*” (speech dissolved into mind).

**kodiya vāy vilangu** – Crocodile clutched the elephant’s foot only; but āḻvār’s divine heart is paining. One should think that – when a vaiṣṇava is in danger, if one does not consider it to be danger for self, one is not having vaiṣṇava quality. Just like when one’s son has enmity with someone, one should consider that to be one’s own; otherwise there will be shortcoming in the bodily affection. \[Similarly, when a śrīvaiṣṇava suffers, we should feel the pain.\]

**uyir malanga** – Not just the body and senses, but the life which is the abode of prāṇa (vital air), to be tormented.

**koṇḍa sīṟṟam** – Since it is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 1.10 “*sa ca nityam prāśāntātmā mrudupūrvam ca bhāśatē ucyamānōpi paruśam nōttaram pratipadyatē* ” (always having a soft heart, he talks softly. Even if others use harsh words, he does not respond to that), not having anger in him, assuming the anger on himself as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 24.34 “*krōdamāhārayat tīvram*” (śrī rāma made himself very angry). śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 59.136 “*kōpasya vaśamēyivān”* (he comes under the influence of anger). If the body gets hurt, the ātmā in the body will not remain quiet, just as the ātmā will go behind the body which is incidentally acquired for him. Just as the ātmā is bound by karma, bhagavān is bound by his anugraham (mercy).

**onṟuṇḍu** – Just as an impoverished person will hold on to a generous and rich person, āḻvār is holding on to bhagavān considering that bhagavān has anger. sauśeelyam etc are qualities which facilitate surrender. But for eliminating the hurdles, anger is required.

**un adiyanēnum vandu adiyiṇai adaindēn** – As one acquires svarūpa jñānam (knowledge about true nature of the self), one should pursue the means which is appropriate for that true nature \[i.e. surrender\].

**aṇi poḻil …** – As said in śrī rangarāja stavam 2.57 “*atantrita camūpati prahitahastam asvīkruta-praṇīta maṇi pādukam kimiti cākulānta*:*puram* l *avāhana pariśkriyam patagarājamārōhata*: *karipravarabrumhitē bhavatas tvarāyai nama*: ll” (I offer my salutations to the speed of emperumān, who, upon hearing the cry of gajēndān, disregarded the helping hand offered by sēnai mudaliyār \[viśvaksēnar\], did not accept the divine gemstone-studded sandals, with the divine consorts getting startled, wondering “What is this? What happened?”, without any decoration for the vehicle \[garuda\], mounted the divine garuda), you need not travel all the way up to the pond, since you are already reclining in the same water-body (samsāra) where I am caught. There was one crocodile; here we have five crocodiles (five senses). There the duration was limited as said in viṣṇu darmam 69.46 “*divyam varśa sahasrakam*” (For thousand celestial years); here, duration is anādi (without a beginning). There the pond is limited in size; here it is samsārārṇavam (the ocean of nescience) \[without any limit\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.4. Nanju sorvador

*nanju sōrvadōr venjina aravamveruvi vandu nin saraṇ enac caraṇāynenjil koṇḍu nin anjiṟaip paṟavaikkuadaikkalam koduttu aruḷ seydadu aṟinduvenjolāḷargaḷ naman tamarkkadiyarkodiya seyvanavuḷa adaṟku adiyēnanji vandu nin adiyiṇai adaindēnaṇipoḻil tiruvarangattammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vem – harsh; solāḷargaḷ – those who have speech; naman tamar – yama’s messengers; kadiyar – having fearsome forms; kodiya – being very cruel (during the time of death); seyvana – the acts which are done; uḷa – there are many; adiyēn – I, the servitor; adaṟku – for those acts; anji – became scared; nanju – poison; sōrvadu – spitting; ōr – unique; vem – cruel; sinam – angry; aravam – sumukhan, the serpent; veruvi – becoming scared (for periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) who came to kill it); vandu – came to you; nin saraṇan ena – as it told “You should be my protector”; saraṇāy – being the protector (for it); nenjil koṇḍu – considering (its request) in his divine heart; nin – being your servitor; am siṟai – having beautiful wings; paṟavaikku – on periya tiruvadi; adaikkalam – as (serpent) to be protected; koduttu – gave; aruḷ seyda – the way you mercifully protected; aṟindu – realised; vandu – came to you, highlighting my offenses; aṇi – decorative; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; tiruvarangattu – mercifully reclining in śrīrangam; ammānē – Oh lord!; nin adiyiṇai – your pair of divine feet; adaindēn – I surrender unto

**Перевод:**

**Explaining the acceptance, the kainkaryam which is the result of acceptance, and praying for the elimination of the connection with the body, which is the hurdle for kainkaryam – these were explained in two pāsurams; in the previous pāsuram, āḻvār requested to eliminate indriya vaśyatā (being bound by senses) which is the result of a part of one’s sins, while the body is still present and which is a hurdle for our experience; in this pāsuram, āḻvār is praying to eliminate yama vaśyatā (being bound by yama for our sins) which is a result of all our sins, after leaving this body and is a hurdle.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

There are many cruel acts which are done by yama’s messengers who have very harsh speech and fearsome forms; I, the servitor became scared of such acts; sumukhan, the unique, angry, cruel serpent which is spitting poison, became scared of garudāḻvār who came to kill it, came to you and told “you should be my protector”; being its protector, considering its request in your divine heart, you gave that serpent to periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) who is your servtior having beautiful wings, as that which is to be protected by him. I realised the ways you mercifully protected sumukhan, have come to you highlighting my offenses. Oh lord, who is mercifully reclining in śrīrangam which is surrounded by decorative orchards! I, who am your servitor and have come helplessly, surrender unto your pair of divine feet.

**nanju …** – Just as emperumān eliminated the danger faced by sumukhan from garudāḻvār, āḻvār is asking bhagavān to eliminate the fear acquired by thinking about the subservience to yama, by making yama himself do it as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 3.7.4 “*parihara madusūdana prapannān prabhuraham anya nruṇam na vaiṣṇavānām*” (yama says to his servitors – do not approach those who have surrendered to madusūdana (emperumān)). One who is surrendering, will usually highlight one’s lowliness and surrender. That lowliness is in the form of ākincanyam (not having any means) and aparādam (having done mistakes). That is – saying that there is no goodness and there is badness. āḷavandār observed those sequentially in [stōtra ratnam 22](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-22/) “*na darmaniśtōsmi na cātmavēdī na bhaktimāmstvaccaraṇāravindē* l *akincanō’nanya gati*: *śaraṇya*! *tvat pādamūlam śaraṇamprapadyē*” (Oh emperumān who is appropriate for surrendering to! I am not rooted in *karmayōgam* (path of deeds); I do not have *ātmajñānam* (knowledge about the supreme entity, the path of knowledge); I do not have *bhakti yōgam* (the path of devotion) at your divine feet. I, who do not have any means and who am without any other refuge, affirm with certainty that your divine lotus-like feet are the means) and in [stōtra ratnam 23](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-23/) “*na ninditam karma tadasti lōkē sahasraśō yanna mayā vyadāyi \| sō’ham vipākāvasarē mukunda! krandāmi sampratyagatis tavāgrē \|\|*” (Oh lord who bestows liberation! Those prohibited actions which were performed by me thousands of times, are not present even in śāstram \[world indicates śāstram which conducts the world\]; right now, when \[such actions\] culminate into results, I am crying in front of your highness, due to having no other refuge). Also, explained in “*jñāna kriyāca bhajana:*” \[Not sure of the source\]. In the previous pāsurams – āḻvār highlighted his ākincanyam; here, he is highlighting his aparādam.

While it is sufficient to say “*nanju, aravam*” (poisonous snake/serpent), why has āḻvār said “*nanju sōrvadōr venjina aravam*“? As said in [mudal tiruvandādi 11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-11/) “*vāy avanai alladu vāḻttādu*” (my mouth will not praise anyone other than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) and viṣṇu darmam 1.13 says “*sā jihvā yā harim stauti*” (whatever praises hari, that is tongue), with the mouth which is to be used to uplift oneself by praising him, this serpent is spitting poison which will destroy others, and is coming; with the same mouth, now it is saying “śaraṇam” (I surrender). The principle understood from this is to say that there is no one unqualified to perform śaraṇāgati.

**venjinam** – Unique anger. When the poison is in the heart, it will not harm others. But when anger manifests, it is spat out and will be harmful. It is opposite to what was said previously in [periya tirumoḻi 5.8.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/02/periya-thirumozhi-5-8-3/) “*sīṟṟam uṇḍu*” \[emperumān had to assume anger, here the serpent is naturally angry\].

**aravam** – The species where the aforementioned aspects are decorations for it. It is said as “*sarpa jātiriyam krūrā:*” (The serpent species is very cruel).

**veruvi vandu** – It came with fear of its enemy.

**ni saraṇ ena** – It said “You should be my refuge”. It was just said by him \[his heart was not fully surrendered\].

**saraṇāy** – While the serpent should have become the food for periya tiruvadi, bhagavān eliminated that. He is being the protector, not thinking “What kind of śaraṇāgati it has done?” but thinking “īsn’t it sufficient if he has the friendly disposition!”.

**nenjil koṇḍu** – Considering in his divine heart “For such lowly serpent, there is no refuge other than me”. The completeness in the qualification of the person who surrenders and the completeness of the surrender which was performed, are not the aspects which will give the benefit; it is only the thought of the one who accepts such surrender. If this is not the case, śrī bharatāḻvān’s surrender should have succeeded \[Though bharatāḻvān was complete in all aspects and his śaraṇāgati was perfect, because śrī rāma’s desire was different, śrī bharatāḻvān’s surrender did not succeed\].

**nin anjiṟaip paṟavai …** – You showed the serpent to periya tiruvadi and made him protect it. This is very dear to īśvara’s divine heart. Both verses from varāha purāṇam “*na kśamāmi*” (I will not forgive) and śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 “ *na tyajēyam*” (I will not let down), should be reconcilled by bhagavān. He cannot abandon the one who surrendered; he cannot tolerate offenses committed towards his devotees; now, when periya tiruvadi came to eat sumukhan, the serpent, it neither fought him nor sought refuge from someone else, but surrendered to bhagavān; is there any offense in it? If we analyse īśvara’s divine heart, he has made the whole world exist for the purpose of his devotees; because of that, as the serpent is the apt food for periya tiruvadi (the garuda bird), bhagavān has anger in his divine heart that sumukhan is not letting periya tiruvadi eat him. When vāli asked śrī rāma “Why did you kill me?” śrī rāma replied “You captured your brother’s wife” and faulted him. But the same fault is in sugrīva mahārāja too. But he said “If anyone spoke about this I will hang them wherever I see them”.

How did he reconcile “*na kśamāmi*” and “*na tyajēyam*“? Instead of keeping sumukhan who surrendered unto him under his refuge, he showed him to periya tiruvadi and made him protect it. If he had protected it, periya tiruvadi will be upset \[that bhagavān took away his food\]; but when periya tiruvadi accepted sumukhan as his dependent, his hunger will be eliminated thinking “When bhagavān himself can protect sumukhan he made me protect it”. Now, between them there is rakśya (protected) and rakśaka (protector) mood only. bhādya (affected) and bhādaka (one who hurts) mood is eliminated. Though there is natural enmity between two entities, when both of those entities surrender unto bhagavān, they will become very friendly towards each other.

**nin am siṟaip paṟavai** – Since when bhagavān showed sumukhan to periya tiruvadi, periya tiruvadi needs to protect sumukhan as per the lord’s thoughts, if both periya tiruvadi and sumukhan are inimical towards each other, that will cause sorrow to bhagavān. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 128.101 “*rāmamēva anupaśyantō nābhyahimsan parasparam*” (Seeing śrī rāma alone, entities did not kill one another)

**adaikkalam koduttu aruḷ seydadu aṟindu** – He made periya tiruvadi to protect sumukhan with full intent.

**aruḷ** – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.5.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/09/thiruvaimozhi-7-5-10-varththai-aribavar/) “*avan seyyum sēmam*” (the protection given by the one who eliminated the sorrow), he made it in such a way that sumukhan remains inseparable from periya tiruvadi.

When emperumān asked “He came fearing his enemy and surrendered unto me; hence I protected; who are you fearing and surrendering unto me?” āḻvār responds

**vem solāḷargaḷ** – Their acts can be tolerated; but their words cannot be tolerated.

**naman tamar** – They are such close servitors of yama that they can even refuse his orders a few times.

**kadiyar** – Their forms cannot be seen.

**kodiya seyvanavuḷa** – They will torment according to the sins of the individual instead of the individual himself.

**uḷa** – Only if there is a limit to the individual sins, their acts have a limit.

**adaṟku** – For the torments of the servitors of yama.

**adiyēn anji vandu** – What is the connection between a servitor of bhagavān and being fearful of yama et al? śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*bhayam bhayānām*” (He is fear for fear).

**nin adiyiṇai adaindēn** – yama himself became scared and told as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 3.7.4 “*parihara*” (Leave them).

**aṇi poḻil …** – Did you not come and mercifully recline here to eliminate the hurdles of devotees and let them enjoy you?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 5.8.5. Maga manilam

*māga mānilam muḻudum vandu iṟainjum malaradik kaṇḍa māmaṟaiyāḷan tōgai māmayil annavar inbam tuṟṟilāmaiyil atta! ingu oḻindu bōgam nī eydip pinnum nammidaikkē pōduvāy enṟa ponnaruḷ enakkumāga vēṇḍum enṟu adiyiṇai adaindēn aṇipoḻil tiruvarangattammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā – vast; kam – nityasūris who are in paramākāśam (supreme sky); mā – vast; nilam – the residents of the aṇḍam (oval shaped universe) which includes earth; muḻudum – everyone; vandu – came together; iṟainjum – vorśipping; malar – like a flower; adi – (your) divine feet; kaṇḍa – saw; mā – having greatness; maṟaiyāḷan – towards the brāhmaṇa named gōvindasvāmi; atta – appā! (Son!) (while doing penance); nī – you; tōgai – having plumage; mā – best; mayil annavar – by the union with women who are having hair which is similar to peacock; inbam – joy; tuṟṟu ilāmaiyil – due to not experiencing; ingu oḻindu – remaining here (for some time); bōgam – the enjoyment of union with a woman; eydi – experience; pinnum – subsequently; nammidaikkē – close to me; pōduvāy – you can come; enṟa – said mercifully in this manner; pon – best (matching the devotee’s heart); aruḷ – mercy; enakkum – in my case also; āga vēṇḍum enṟu – expecting to happen; aṇi – decorative; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; tiruvarangattu – mercifully reclining in śrīrangam; ammānē – Oh lord!; nin adiyiṇai – your pair of divine feet; adaindēn – I surrender unto

**Перевод:**

**In the previous pāsurams, āḻvār explained bhagavān’s acceptance \[of āḻvār\], kainkaryam, and requested for removal of two forms of hurdles to kainkaryam; here – āḻvār is saying “Just as you acted knowing the thoughts of gōvindasvāmi, you have to act knowing my thoughts”. His thoughts for his past state – you should eliminate the connection with this body which is the cause for being bound by senses and yama. When the ātmā will leave the body one day naturally as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.10.5 “maraṇām ānāl” (When death occurs), why is āḻvār beseeching emperumān? This is because he has great urge and cannot wait for the natural process.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Your flower like divine feet are vorśipped by everyone including nityasūris who are in the vast paramākāśam and the residents of the vast aṇḍam (oval shaped universe) which includes earth; when gōvindasvāmi, who is having greatness of having darśan of such divine feet approached you, you mercifully said “appā (Son)! Due to not experiencing joy from the union with women who are having hair which is similar to the best peacock with plumage, you remain here and experience the enjoyment of union with a woman, and subsequently come close to me”. Oh lord who is mercifully reclining in śrīrangam which is surrounded by decorative orchards! I, who am your servitor and have come helplessly, surrender unto your pair of divine feet, expecting such mercy to happen in my case also.

**māga …** – A brāhmaṇa named gōvindasvāmi, having heard itihāsas and purāṇas, became desirous to visualise kriṣṇa’s childhood pastimes and rāsa krīdā etc; he thought – isn’t emperumān such that for those who previously thought as in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/03/thiruvaimozhi-8-5-2-kana-varay/) “*kāṇa vārāy*” (Please come to be seen by me), he will present himself as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.8](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-8/) “*paritrāṇāya sādūnām*” (To protect the noble people)? Even if we get such desire, it will occur; let us pray for that. In this manner he tormented his body and engaged in penance; bhagavān, as per his desire, enacted the aspects of kriṣṇāvatāram and made him enjoy that. And then he mercifully asked “What do you need?” He responded “I should accompany your highness and enjoy you?” bhagavān told “when you were performing penance, you were free from material desires, eliminated food and water etc and changed the body to become very lean; you should remain here, enjoy the missed experiences and then come to me; in this manner, just as he did as per gōvindasvām’s help; āḻvār is saying “you should help me according to my thoughts”.

While this meaning is not explicitly seen, how is it said to be his thoughts? It is said by context and how the meaning is explained. This should be the thoughts for āḻvār who said in [periya tirumoḻi 1.3.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/02/periya-thirumozhi-1-3-8/) “*nāsamāna pāsam*” (attachment which will lead to destruction) and periya tirumoḻi 6.3.4 “*pōndēn*” (reached your divine feet).

**māga …** – Seen the divine feet which are taken shelter of, by the residents of both nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti. This surrender is not based on bhagavān being paramapadanātan, but is based on his presence as kriṣṇa. How is it that nityasūris, who are residents of paramapadam, approach kriṣṇa? That is explained in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*āccādyānuyayēva śēśa; paṇairānaga dundupim*” (ādiśēśa covered and protected kriṣṇa and went with him when vasudēva was carrying kriṣṇa) and in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 14.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/11/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-14-3/) “*vinadai siṟuvan siṟagu ennum* *mēlāppin kīḻ varuvānai*” (kriṣṇa was coming mercifully under the canopy of garudan’s wings). Even the divine weapons of bhagavān stayed in the womb along with kriṣṇa and took birth \[Alternatively, we can say that even divine weapons like śankha and chakra stayed in the womb and were born as bharata and śatrugna\].

**mā nilam** – Herdsmen, cows who make herdsmen look like vasiśta, calves and bhīśma et al came and surrendered to kriṣṇa.

**muḻudum** – Even from higher worlds. In the middle of the night, after kriṣṇa mercifully drank milk and was mercifully going to rest, indran came to the divine gates and told kriṣṇa’s servant maids “Kindly inform kriṣṇa that I have come” and subsequently entered and told kriṣṇa “narakan (narakāsuran) is forcing me to give my four-tusked airāvatam to him”. Hearing that kriṣṇa requested him to give a hand to get up, and immediately climbed on the shoulders of periya tiruvadi, along with satyabāmāp pirātti and killed narakāsuran. In “*pādēna kamalābhēna brahma rudrārārcitēna*” (his divine feet vorśipped with lotus flowers by brahmā, rudra), brahmā and rudra vorśipping kriṣṇa is shown. He also showed them in his divine form as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 11.15](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/11-15/) “*brahmāṇam īśam kamalāsanastam*” (I am seeing brahmā, Siva (rudra) who is obedient towards brahmā, who is seated in a lotus flower).

**malaradi** – The divine feet which are incomparably enjoyable. He became approachable by all as in following the cows, being the charioteer in going as messenger.

**kaṇḍa** – He (gōvindasvāmy) saw the divine feet which are to be attained at their place by everyone and surrendered to, coming to him.

**māmaṟaiyāḷan** – He is the best among vaidikas who got to see bhagavān directly instead of seeing him through śāstram or upadēśams (instructions).

**tōgai …** – As soon as gōvindasvāmy saw kriṣṇa, he said “I should go along with you”; kriṣṇa said “that can be done later”; gōvindasvāmy said “What is the reason for that?”; kriṣṇa said “You should experience the lost enjoyment”; gōvindasvāmy said “Why is that required?”; kriṣṇa said “When you were performing penance, though you had attachment for worldly enjoyment, you controlled that urge and did not enjoy them”. bhagavān, who grants mōkśam, would say “Alright! Come along!” and is not the one who would abandon a person who cannot survive without him and is willing to go along with him. And the one who is very attached towards such bhagavān and who will not agree to remain in this samsāram which will make one more attached to it, will not agree to remain in samsāram. In such a case, bhagavān asking gōvindasvāmy to remain here and he agreeing to remain here, must have a reason. That is – to reveal that īśvaran is capable of liberating a person who is very attached to worldly pleasures and is capable of continuing bodily connection for a very great devotee and making such devotee perish. śrī prahlādāḻvān who is considered as the best among his noble devotees, opposed him. A direct example for this – his acts towards śrī mālākārar (the garland maker at maturā). As kriṣṇa along with balarāma entered mālākārar’s residence, he saw him stringing the garlands and told him “Can you give us garlands?”; as soon as he saw kriṣṇa’s beautiful form, he thought “Let kamsa kill me if he desires so; let us offer these garlands to them” and offered the garlands to them; kriṣṇa, became pleased and analysed “Should we carry him to the special abode of paramapadam and accept garlands from him there as said in [tiruviruttam 21](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/01/thiruviruththam-21/) “*sūttu nanmālaigaḷ*” (the best garlands to be offered) or should we place him here?” and decided to place him in this world itself thinking “Since he disregarded kamsa and honoured us, let us make him enjoy worldly pleasures here and then carry him to paramapadam”.

śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.19.26 “*bhuktvāca vipulān bhōgān*” (I am granting great enjoyment for you to enjoy) – I am not giving the enjoyment which is similar to the food given by kamsan \[these are far superior\]. “*tvamantē*” (no end) – since the enjoyment given by bhagavān has no limit and the enjoyer (ātmā) will not be satisfied with some enjoyment, there is no end to enjoyment in this world. mahābhāratam ādi parvam 79.12 “*najātukāma: kāmānām upabhōgēna cāmyati \| haviśā kriṣṇavartmēva bhūya ēvābhivardatē \|\|*” (Just as when we pour oil on fire, that will increase the intensity of fire, if we feed our desires, it will only increase the desires) and mahābhāratam ādi parvam 79.13 “*yat pritivyām vrīhi yavam hiraṇyam paśavasstriya: \| ēkasyāpi naparyāptam iti matvā śamam vrajēt* \|\|” (Though this earth has paddy, gold, domesticated animals, the desirous person will not get satisfaction) – if we think about these materialistic enjoyments, we cannot separate from those. Still, for those who are deeply attached to bhagavān, they can withdraw from these, when they choose to do so. The sage, saubhari assumed 50 forms and married 50 girls on seeing the family of fish; after a while, he became disgusted about them and returned to his spiritual path. Both karmam (actions) and jñānam (intelligence) are going hand-in-hand. The past impressions of karmam will lead one to worldly enjoyment; jñānam will make oneself feel disgusted about those acts and retract one. The karmam which is incidental will naturally be overpowered by the jñānam which is natural. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.1 “*math prasādada: mamānusmaraṇam prāpya:*” (By my grace one attains constant remembrance of me) just as upāsaka will get antima smruti (remembrance of me during his last moments), you will also get antima smruti; alternative explanation – not having to worry about the shortcoming of your not thinking about me and instead we will think about you. jīvātmā needs firm faith in accepting bhagavān as his means.

**tōgai mā mayil annavar inbam** – Women who are as beautiful as a beautiful peacock with plumage. With this, the beauty and the gait which can attract even those who are far away, are spoken of. If one enjoys in this manner, being unable to see anything, one should return with the tools for taking bath (to purify oneself).

**annavar inbam** – If we analysed, there is nothing to enjoy really. He is just sarcastically saying “*tōgai mā mayil annavar inbam*“. These are the words of āḻvār who said in [periya tirumoḻi 1.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/06/periya-thirumozhi-1-9-1/) “*tāyē tandai enṟum tāramē kiḷai makkaḷ enṟum* *nōyē pattoḻindēn*” (I considered unreal ones as mother, father, wife, relatives and children and experienced disaster); alternative explanation – The strength of āḻvār’s tongue is such that whatever he says will be elegant and beautiful.

**tuṟṟilāmaiyāl** – Due to not having enjoyed union (with a woman).

**atta** – To make him follow his orders, he is saying lovingly, calling him “Son!”

**ingoḻindu** – Remaining here in this world for some time.

**bōgam nī eydi** – Experiencing all the lost enjoyment.

**nī eydi** – āren’t you, who can withdraw whenever you want, engaging in this? Will these aspects which you abandoned during your penance, become hurdles for you?

**pinnum nammidaikkē pōduvāy** – āḻvār is explaining in a way which emphasises bhagavān’s greatness which will make anyone withdraw from worldly aspects and enjoy him. You can directly come to me who is apt for you.

**enṟa ponnaruḷ** – That desirable mercy.

**enakkum āga vēṇḍum enṟu adiyiṇai adaindēn** – Just as you acted according to his desire, you should act according to my desire.

**aṇi poḻil …** – Haven’t you mercifully arrived and reclined here to analyse and fulfil the desires of your devotees? Haven’t you mercifully reclined here to grant a) worldly wealth for those who desire that, b) pamper the body for those who desire that and c) eliminate the connection with this body for those who desire that?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.6. Mannu nanmarai

*mannu nānmaṟai māmuni peṟṟamaindanai madiyāda vengūṟṟamtannai anji nin saraṇ enac caraṇāyttagavil kālanai uga munindoḻiyāppinnai enṟum nin tiruvadi piriyā vaṇṇameṇṇiya pēraruḷ enakkumannadu āgum enṟu adiyiṇai adaindēnaṇipoḻil tiruvarangattammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

mannu – being eternal; nāl – four types of; maṟai – one who recites vēdam; mā – best (without any other expectation); muni – the sage who has dhyāna yōgam (meditation); peṟṟa – begot; maindanai – son named mārkaṇḍēyan; madiyāda – not considering (him to be son of a bhāgavata and approached); vem – very cruel; kūṟṟan tannai – (seeing) yama; anji – became fearful; nin saraṇ ena – as he told that (for me) you are the only refuge; saraṇāy – (for him) being the protector; tagavu il – merciless; kālanai – yama; uga – to destroy (him); munindu – became angry; oḻiyā – not stopping with that; pinnai – further; enṟum – forever; nin tiruvadi – your divine feet; piriyā vaṇṇam – to remain inseparable from; eṇṇiya – one who vowed; pēr aruḷ – (your) great mercy; enakkum – in my case also; annadāgum – should happen the same way; enṟu – thinking this; aṇi – decorative; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; tiruvarangattu – mercifully reclining in śrīrangam; ammānē – Oh lord!; nin adiyiṇai – your pair of divine feet; adaindēn – I surrender unto

**Перевод:**

**In the previous pāsuram, āḻvār said emperumān should fulfil his desire just as he fulfilled gōvindasvāmy’s desire; in this pāsuram āḻvār says – when mārkaṇḍēyan surrendered unto you fearing for death, you eliminated his death and his fear; not only that, you blessed him to remain inseparable from your divine feet; similarly you should eliminate my fear for samsāram (material world), bestow me the benefit of being inseparable from you; that too you should not do it because I prayed to you which is similar to getting a ring made by yama; the result matching my svarūpam is – I have to accept as given by you; that is what is needed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The best sage who recites the eternal four vēdams and has dhyāna yōgam begot a son named mārkaṇḍēyan; seeing the very cruel yama approaching such mārkaṇḍēyan without considering him to be a son of a bhāgavata, mārkaṇḍēyan became fearful and prayed to bhagavān “You are my only refuge”. Being the protector, bhagavān became angry to destroy yama and not stopping with that, bhagavān vowed to make him remain inseparable from his divine feet and showed his great mercy. Oh lord, who is mercifully reclining in śrīrangam which is surrounded by decorative orchards! I, who am your servitor and have come helplessly, surrender unto your pair of divine feet, thinking that it should happen the same way for me.

**mannu …** – It is sufficient to say “*muni peṟṟa*“; why is he saying “*mannu nānmaṟai māmuni*“? It is to say that even after having such high heritage, yama went to him. mārkaṇḍēya, having studied the four vēdams which are eternal, remains in vorśipping bhagavān as explained in those vēdams. There are those who worship bhagavān through avaidika (non-vēdam based) means such as reasoning and logic. Unlike that, realising that bhagavān who is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 15.15](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/15-15/) “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya:*” (I am only known from all vēdams) is to be vorśipped, one who engaged in such worship. mahattai (mā) is to worship bhagavān, being free from pursuing other goals, and considering “everything is bhagavān” as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.19](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-19/) “*vāsudēva: sarvam*” (vāsudēvan is both upāyam (means) and upēyam (goal)).

**mannu –** One who is fully engaged in four vēdas. For, an upāsaka (bhakti yōga follower) should continue till the end as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.28](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-28/) “*svādyāyajñānayajñāś ca*” (Some others engage in the sacrifice of studying vēdam and few others in the sacrifice of studying the meanings of vēdam); one who is progressing in yōgam as ordained in vēdams and subsequently again engaging in adyayanam (learning/recital) to check whether whatever he has seen during yōgam is appearing truly or otherwise due to karma, as said in “*svādyāyāt yōgamāsīta yōgāt svādyāyamāmanēt \| svādyāya yōga sampatyā paramātmā prakāśatē \|\|*” (From svādyāyam (learning/recital), one progresses to yōgam (meditation) and to check the nature of what is visualised in yōgam, one returns to svādyāyam; with the help of svādyāyam and yōgam, one sees paramāmātmā).

ācārya instructed śiśya as said in taittirīya upaniśat bruguvalli “*yatō vā imāni bhūtāni jāyantē … tadvijijñāsasva tadbrahma*” (From which, the universe is created, on which, the universe is sustained, in which the universe dissolves, that is to be known and that is brahma) and told him “You do penance until the object of meditation is seen as explained here”. The śiśya did that and said that food is brahmam as in taittirīya upaniśat “*annam brahmēti vyajanāt*” (Food is understood as brahmam). The ācārya said “That is not enough; do some more penance”; in this manner, the śiśya meditated up to ānandamaya (bhagavān who is filled with bliss); the ācārya finally said “That is brahmam”.

**muni peṟṟa** – mārkaṇḍēya was born when mrukaṇḍu was in a matured state of knowledge \[it could also be said as mārkaṇḍēya was born with a matured state of knowledge\].

**madiyāda** – When those who are related to bhagavān themselves are to given up by yama as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 3.7.4 “*parihara*” (yama says to his servitors – do not approach). it is obvious that one cannot approach those who are related to vaiṣṇavas (bhagavān’s devotees); still, yama approached mārkaṇḍēya \[though he is the son of mrukaṇḍu maharishi\]. cāndōjña upaniśat “*nāsyā’vara puruśā: kśīyantē*” (The descendants will not perish) – for a bhāgavata, two types of descendants occur – one by knowledge and another by progeny; it is said that both types of descendants do not perish. kśayam (perishing) for ātmā, who is atomic \[minute\] and eternal, is contraction of knowledge. That will not happen. The explanation for this is “*kulam dārayatē*” (Will sustain the clan) and those who follow this \[vēdam, śāstram\], i.e., āḻvārs also said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-1-kesavan-thamar/) “*emar ēḻ eḻu piṟappum*” (Many generations of my descendants).

**vem kūṟṟam** – Instead of seeing his greatness, they \[messengers of yama\] only saw themselves and came with cruelty.

**vem kūṟṟam tannai anji nin saraṇena** – Being scared of death, he said “You only should be my refuge”.

**nin saraṇ ena** – śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 3.7.4 “*mamāsti chakra pratihata vīrya balasya*” – you who are having the weapon which is feared by yama et al, should be my refuge. *vasati manasiyasya sōvyayātmā* – even when the ātmā is facing away from bhagavān, bhagavān remains the eternal antaryāmi (in-dwelling super-soul). puruśa varasya – considering him to be the upāyam. *na tasya druśtipātē tava gati:* – You don’t even roam around in his vicinity. \[Yama tells his servitor not to be even present nearby those who consider bhagavān to be his upāyam, since that bhagavān remains as the eternally in-dwelling soul even in those who are facing away from him. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 3.7.18 “*vraja parihrutya yatāgnim ājya siddam*” – just as how one moves away from the fire when ghee is poured in it, being present with such intent near devotees, will be unbearably hot.

Alternatively – śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 3.7.4 “*mamāsti chakra pratihata vīrya balasya*” – looking at bhagavān’s greatness, even I cannot go close to him. The reason for that is as explained in viṣṇu darmam 78th adyāyam, “*avyāhatāni kriṣṇasya cakrādīnyāyudāni tam \| rakśanti sakalāpadbhyō yēna viṣṇurupāsita: \|\|*” (That prapanna who worships kriṣṇa is protected from all dangers by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s weapons such as tiruvāḻi (cakram)” etc) – even if emperumān becomes their enemy, the weapons will try to protect such devotees) – yama et al were scared of the divine weapons of bhagavān. periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.4 ‘*kodumai seyyum kūṟṟamum en kōlādi kuṟugap peṟā tadavaraittōḷ cakrapāṇī sārngaviṟcēvaganē”* (Even yama, who cruelly punishes everyone, will not come close to the places which are ruled under my sceptre. Oh one who has mountain like shoulders and divine chakra in your divine hand! Oh the valourous one who has the śārnga bow!) – if yama comes nearby, bhagavān will severe his head with the divine chakra, and if yama stays at a distance, he will torment yama with his lengthy arrow. But is bhagavān not the ātmā for yama also? Yes – but yama is not supposed to roam around in this place (where devotees live). It is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.2.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/05/thiruvaimozhi-5-2-6-konruyir-unnum/) “*nēmip pirān tamar pōndār*” (they are devotees of one who is having divine chakra in his hand).

**saraṇāy** – Did he consider someone who is not the real refuge, as his refuge?

**mannu …** – Here, āḻvār is highlighting mārkaṇḍēya’s greatness due to being born in a superior clan, and explaining that such person surrendered to bhagavān; previously, the inferior nature of the persons taking refuge was shown as in “*ēḻai ēdalan*“, “*vātamā magan*” and “*nanju sōrvadōr*“; the connection between these is: one’s superior nature or inferior nature is irrelevant for śaraṇāgati. Remember the instruction mercifully given by nampiḷḷai to vēlvetti nambiyār \[nampiḷḷai says “śrī rāma performing ritualistic bath and then śaraṇāgati to samudra rāja and vibhīśaṇāḻvān not taking bath before performing śaraṇāgati show that one’s adherence to rituals is irrelevant for śaraṇāgati\].

**tagavil kālanai** – Being merciless even at a stage when one has to show mercy upon suffering persons. He will only see the person’s sins and his control.

**uga munindu** – Whatever yama thought to do to mārkaṇḍēya was done by bhagavān to yama. He destroyed yama thinking “Even in future, he should not torment those who are connected to vaiṣṇavas”.

**oḻiyā** – Not stopping with that, thinking “īsn’t it sufficient to destroy yama who tormented mārkaṇḍēya and protect him?”

**pinnai …** – You gave the ultimate benefit \[to mārkaṇḍēya\] of being together with your divine feet without separating ever, after eliminating the connection with samsāra.

**nin tiruvadip piriyā** – Becoming free from samsāra is there for kēvala (those who seek kaivalya mōkśam) too. Unlike that, emperumān gave him the benefit of reaching his divine feet.

**eṇṇiya …** – Instead of speaking about the mercy, here āḻvār is speaking about his magnanimity. Since bhagavān is “*sakala pala pradan*” (one who grants everything), even if a person surrenders unto him for worldly benefits, when the person does not push away bhagavān, bhagavān will not leave that opportunity \[and bless him the highest benefit\]. Even for the one who surrenders, it is important to meditate upon bhagavān’s magnanimity as done in [śaraṇāgati gadyam cūrṇikai 5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/12/saranagathi-gadhyam-5-part-4/) “apāra kāruṇya …”.

**enakkum** – For me also, who is not having any greatness based on my birth. That is, āḻvār is the one who says as in [periya tirumoḻi 1.9.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/06/periya-thirumozhi-1-9-9/) “*pāvamē seydu pāviyānēn*” (being a sinner who is performing sins only) and [periya tirumoḻi 1.9.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/06/periya-thirumozhi-1-9-5/) “*eppāvam palavum ivaiyē seydu*” (Having performed these many types of sins).

**annadāgum enṟu adiyiṇai adaindēn** – I have surrendered unto you expecting the same benefit by your desire just as you bestowed such benefit to him even when he was not aiming for it, having the only reason which is “If I grant him this, he will not reject it” and gave him the benefit of remaining inseparable from you.

**aṇi poḻil …** – Have you not arrived here and mercifully reclined to give the benefit which matches their true nature, even if they approached you for other benefits, as long as they don’t reject such benefit when granted?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 5.8.7. Odu vaymaiyum

*ōdu vāymaiyum uvaniyap piṟappumunakku mun tanda andaṇan oruvankādal en magan pugalidam kāṇēnkaṇḍu nī taruvāy enakku enṟukōdil vāymaiyinān unai vēṇḍiyakuṟai mudittu avan siṟuvanaik koduttāyādalāl vandu un adiyiṇai adaindēnaṇipoḻil tiruvarangattammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōdu – being learned/recited; vāymaiyum – vēdam in the form of sentences; uvaniyam – acquired through upanayanam; piṟappum – birth (of being a dvija (twice-born)); unakku – for you; mun – first; tanda – gave; oruvan – unique (scholar); kōdu il – not going useless; vāymaiyinān – having words; andaṇan – brāhmaṇa known as sāndīpini; kādal – target of my love; en magan – my son; pugal idam – the place he went; kāṇēn – I don’t know; nī – you, who are sarvajña (omniscient) and sarvaśakta (omnipotent); kaṇḍu – finding out (where he is); enakku – to me (bringing him); taruvāy – should give; enṟu – saying this; unai – towards you; vēṇḍiya – requested; kuṟai – (his) sorrow (the contraction of his mind); mudittu – eliminated (completed); avan siṟuvanai – his son; koduttāy – brought him back from yama lōkam and gave; ādalāl – since you are omnipotent; vandu – I come; aṇi – decorative; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; tiruvarangattu – mercifully reclining in śrīrangam; ammānē – Oh lord!; nin adiyiṇai – your pair of divine feet; adaindēn – I surrender unto

**Перевод:**

**Previously – first highlighting bhagavān’s acceptance, then highlighting kainkaryam (service), then requesting him to eliminate the hurdles for such kainkaryam, that is being bound by senses, first and then requesting him to eliminate the subservience towards yama which is due to the sins caused by being bound by senses, then requesting him to eliminate the connection with prakruti (matter, i.e., this body) which is the cause for that, and finally requesting that not only bhagavān should do it knowing āḻvār’s will, but that he also should do it out of compassion. Since there is nothing more to ask beyond this, there is no reason for the subsequent pāsurams. In such a case, what is āḻvār doing further? As emperumān said “āḻvīr! If I am the lord and you are the servitor, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 39-30 ‘śaraistu sankulām krutvā lankām parabalārdana: l mām nayēd yadi kākutstas tat tasya sadruśam bhavēt ll’ (If śrī rāmapirān, who annihilates the strength of his enemies, bewilders lankā with his arrows and takes me with him, it will be apt for him), servitor should remain patiently and observe my acts and cannot push me like this”; āḻvār says “If I see me, is there opportunity for eternal kainkaryam, even at the end of this body? I am urging you due to your omnipotence”. Just like his enjoyability, his omnipotence also will make others show their urge to reach him; āḻvār is saying “Rescuing me who is caught in this ocean of samsāra and is suffering, and granting me your divine feet is even more difficult than the agadita gatanā sāmartyam (ability to accomplish impossible tasks) of rescuing the son of sāndīpini (sāndīpani) who drowned in the ocean. You should mercifully do it with your omnipotence”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The unique brāhmaṇa named sāndīpini whose words will not become useless, gave you vēdam which is learned/recited and is in the form of sentences, and the dvija status \[being twice-born as kśatriya\] which is acquired through upanayanam. He requested you saying “I don’t know where my son who is the target of my love, went ; as you are sarvajña (omniscient) and sarvaśakta (omnipotent), you should find out his whereabouts and bring him to me”; you eliminated his sorrow by bringing his son back from yama lōkam and gave him. Oh lord, who is mercifully reclining in śrīrangam which is surrounded by decorative orchards! I, who am your servitor, have come and surrendered unto your pair of divine feet.

**ōdu vāymaiyum** – vāymai – action of speech. That is sentences \[from vēdam\]. To avoid violating the rules, āḻvār is using words which represent the meaning of vēda vākyams. \[nammāḻvār too\] While antaryāmi brāhmaṇam \[portion of vēdam which speaks about bhagavān’s omnipresence\] is present in the divine heart, he said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/04/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-7-thidavisumbu-erivali/) “*udanmisai uyir enak karandengum paranduḷan* *sudarmigu surudiyuḷ*” (He is pervading in everything similar to [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is pervading in the body. Not only that, he is present inside and outside of everything. He is the main object of the most radiant vēdam). They \[those āḻvārs who are not twice-born\] don’t recite the words of the vēdam. But they don’t miss out any of the meanings.

**ōdu vāymai** – vēdam, which is said in kātakam 3-9-50 “*pūrvē pūrvēbhyō vaca ētadūcu:*” (the forefathers repeated the words of their forefathers), cannot be learnt just by reading from books, by casual listening, and should be learnt only by hearing from an ācārya first and repeating the same. Why is this hearing and repeating emphasised to grasp the words? If it is not learnt that way, the meanings will not be known. As said in “*artam tam tamanarta rūpam apitassandarśya muktairhrudā nityam tairap durgraha svahrudyaā vēśyā sadēśyā trayī: yasminnavyabhicāriṇi svahrudayam sandarśya pātivratam dattē lakśmaṇa lakśmaṇāya munayē tasmai namaskrumahē*” – just as a woman who married a man, having fire as the witness, will show herself fully to her husband, only for a person who holds on to vidyā (knowledge from vēdam) through the instructions and knowledge of a true ācārya, such vidyā will reveal itself.

**uvaniyap piṟappum** – For a brāhmaṇa \[and kśatriya, vaiśya\], there are two births. Birds also have dvijatvam \[two births – first in the shell and then outside\]. Just as the first birth inside the shell, the brāhmaṇa’s first birth is inside the womb\[he is not qualified for any vaidika rituals\]; only after the second birth, the bird can stretch and act \[only after the second birth through upanayanam, the brāhmaṇa becomes qualified for any vaidika ritual\]. For kriṣṇa, he became twice-born only after killing kamsa; he did that only to establish that he is of the same clan as yādavas \[the descendants of king yadu\]. After crowning ugrasēna, and establishing him in his dharma \[natural duty\], and stabilising the kingdom, he went to sāndipini thinking “Let us go to sāndīpini in avantīpuram and go through samskārams such as upanayanam etc” and told him “Previously garga performed samskārams such as jāta karma (birth ritual), nāma karaṇa (naming) etc; you should give me subsequent samskārams” and sāndīpini obliged.

**unakku** – He has given to you who created brahmā and gave him vēdam as said in śvētāśvatara upaniśat “*yōvai vēdāmśca prahiṇōti tasmai*” (One who taught vēdam to brahmā). As said in cāndōjña upaniśat 6.3 “*anēna jīvēna ātmanānupraviśya nāma rūpē vyākaravāṇi*” (all names and forms are created by my entry into acit through ātmās) – bhagavān is the one who entered into acit through jīvātmās and made the division of everything by name and form; also said in manu smruti “*nāma rūpanca bhūtānām*” (paramātmā gave name and form to all entities). kriṣṇa going through this was in the end of dvāpara yuga; now āḻvār is saying this to periya perumāḷ; from this we can understand that both kriṣṇa and periya perumāḷ are the same.

**andaṇan** – One who is qualified to teach.

**oruvan** – advitīyan (unique). One who is capable of all vidyāstānams (knowledge bases). Even those knowledge bases which are not part of standard \[vēda\] adyayanam (vēdam learning). As said in śrī rangarāja stavam 2.18 “*śīkśāyām varṇa śikśā padasamadikamō vyākriyā nirvacōbhyām canda: canda: citausyāt gamayati samayam jyōtiśam ranganāta \| kalpēnuśtānamuktam hyucita gamitayōr nyāya mīmāmsayōssyāt arta vyakti: purāṇa smrutiśu tadanukās tvām vicinvanti vēdā: \|\|*” (Oh śriranganāta! In the angam for vēdam śīkśā, how to pronounce the syllables is explained; in vyākaraṇam and niruktam, knowledge about words is present; in candas, grammar relating to gāyatri candas etc is present; in jyōtiśam, the time to perform the rituals is present; in kalpa sūtram, what is to be performed is present; in tarka (nyāya) śāstram and mīmāmsā, clear meanings are present; in purāṇams and smrutis, explanations with examples are given; vēdam which has such angas is searching for you). He learnt danurvēdam (the branch of weaponry), āyurvēdam (the branch of medicine) also from sāndīpini only. ***muṟpada dvayattaik kēttu, itihāsa purāṇangaḷaiyum adikarittu, parapakśapratikśēpattukudalāga nyāya mīmāmsaigaḷum adikarittu, pōdupōkkum aruḷicceyalilēyāmpadi piḷḷaiyaip pōlē adikarippikka vallavanaiyiṟē “oruttan” enbadu*** **(First hearing \[and understanding\] dvayam, then learning itihāsas and purāṇas, subsequently learning nyāya, mīmāmsā etc to condemn opposing philosophy, spending one’s time in divyaprabandam – someone like nampiḷḷai who can teach students to become like this can only be said as “a unique teacher”)**.

After teaching in this manner, seeing kriṣṇa’s knowledge and ability to learn while studying, sāndīpini thought “What should we accept as dakśiṇā?” and asked “My son drowned in the ocean; I don’t know where he went; you should search for him and bring him back the same way he was before”. As he reached the seashore with a bow in his hand, varuṇa (the king of ocean) became scared and came out; kriṣṇa asked “My ācārya’s son entered the ocean; show him to me”; when varuṇa had no other choice, he said “pancajana ate him”; it is not possible to retrieve the food which was eaten the day before; varuṇa drained the water and showed the ocean-bed to kriṣṇa; kriṣṇa eliminated pancajana; śrī pāncajanyāḻvān came and presented himself at that time; kriṣṇa placed him on his divine lips and kept blowing it while going towards yamapuram (the abode of yama) and mercifuly reached there; yama, offered arghyam (water to wash hands) etc and asked “Why have mercifully come here?”; kriṣṇa responded “My ācārya’s son came here; you should show him to me”; yama, brought him from one of the narakas (hells) and showed him; kriṣṇa then brought him to sāndīpini and showed him to make sāndīpini exclaim “This is my son indeed” and vouch for his son’s identity.

**kādal en magan** – The son who is an embodiment of my love.

**pugalidam kāṇēn** – I don’t know where he has gone. Is he in hell? ōr in some womb?

**kaṇḍu nī taruvāy** – You, who are omnipotent, should find him and give him to me. He saw kriṣṇa’s ability while he was grasping and sustaining the knowledge.

**kōdil vāymaiyinān** – Here āḻvār is praising sāndīpini who said “*kādalen magan*” (My son who is an embodiment of love) \[still being in a materialistic platform\], as “*kōdil vāymaiyinān*” (Not speaking useless words); why is that? That is based on kriṣṇa’s opinion as said in “*guruvacanam alanganīyam*” (guru’s words should not be diśonoured) \[i.e., kriṣṇa’s has great respect for his guru\]. āḻvār is saying the words which are used to praise tiruvadi (hanuman) who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 65.10 “*druśtā sītā*” (I have seen sītā), when both śrī rāma and sītāp pirātti were separated!

**unai vēṇḍiya** – He is considering kriṣṇa only to be a śiśya; not as one who is able to grant mōkśam (liberation). The taste towards mōkśam is not acquired based on superior birth, knowledge and conduct; it is acquired by individuals through bhagavān’s mercy based on their faultless nature. Only when such mercy is there, would one pray for liberation.

**kuṟai mudittu** – He said “You should bring my son and show him to me”; when kriṣṇa said “We will do it”, the sorrows got elmiinated at once.

**avan siṟuvanaik koduttāy** – If he smelled his son, he would feel his blood relationship – that is how truly he was brought back. periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.8.1 “*mādavattōn puttiran pōy maṟi kadal vāy māṇḍānai ōduvitta takkaṇaiyā uruvuruvē koduttān*” (As the son of sāndīpini who has great penance, drowned and died in the ocean, he was brought back as guru dakśiṇā (an offering to the teacher) in the same way he was when he died). He gave in such a way that sāndīpini will confirm that this is the same form which was there back then.

**takkaṇaiyā** – He gave it to establish his nature as śiśya \[not as a benefit to the guru, that is, the śiśya must serve the guru by offering whatever is asked by the guru\].

**uru uruvē** – \[This is similar to\] granting śēśatva jñānam (knowledge of servitude) to ātmā which remains in the state of acit as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (As good as asat/acit only) and granting a form and granting kainkaryam (service) which matches that śēśatvam.

**ādalāl vandu un adiyiṇai adaindēn** – I surrendered unto you due to the urge thinking “Anyway, the liberation will be granted at the end of this body; but since you are omnipotent, why should I remain patient till then?”

**aṇi poḻil …** – Haven’t your highness arrived here to rescue me who has been swallowed by the ocean of samsāra and lead me up to kainkaryam, just as you brought back the ātmā with his body as it is, which was swallowed by the ocean?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
