## 5.8.8. Veda vaymoli

*vēda vāymoḻi andaṇan oruvanendai! nin saraṇ ennudai manaivikādal makkaḷaip payattalum kāṇāḷkadiyadōr deyvam koṇḍoḷikkum enṟaḻaippaēdalār munnē innaruḷ avarkkucceydu un makkaḷ maṟṟivar enṟu koduttāyādalāl vandu un adiyiṇai adaindēnaṇipoḻil tiruvarangattammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēdam – vēdas; vāy – with the mouth; moḻi – (always) reciting; oruvan – unique; andaṇan – a vaidika who has purity in knowledge; endai – my father; nin – you only; saraṇ – be (my) upāyam (means) (that is); ennudai – my; manaivi – wife; kādal – dear (to me); makkaḷai – children; payattalum – even at the time of giving birth; kāṇāḷ – she is not seeing; kadiyadu – cruel; ōr deyvam – a dēvatā; koṇḍu – taking away; oḷikkum – hid; enṟu aḻaippa – requested in this manner; avarkku – for that vaidika; ēdalār munnē – in front of the enemies; in – (you) sweetly (considering that as your benefit); aruḷ seydu – showed your mercy; maṟṟu – further; un makkaḷ – your children; ivar enṟu – saying that they are the ones who were brought by me; koduttāy – you mercifully gave; ādalāl – in this manner, since you are omnipotent; vandu – came to you, highlighting my offenses; aṇi – decorative; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; tiruvarangattu – mercifully reclining in śrīrangam; ammānē – Oh lord!; nin adiyiṇai – your pair of divine feet; adaindēn – I surrender unto

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is surrendering unto bhagavān highlighting the story of the children of a vaidika. In this pāsuram also, āḻvār is highlighting the previously explained omnipotence – but the difference is: the ability of executing the task in spite of the distance in time and place.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

A unique vaidika who had purity in knowledge and was always reciting vēdas with his mouth came to kriṣṇa and requested “Oh my father! You have to be my means; even at the time of giving birth to children who are dear to me, my wife is not seeing them since a cruel dēvatā took away and hid them”; in front of the enemies, you sweetly showed your mercy for that vaidika and further said “here are your children who were brought by me” and mercifully gave them to him. In this manner I have to come to you since your are omnipotent, highlighting my offenses. Oh lord, who is mercifully reclining in śrīrangam which is surrounded by decorative orchards! I, who am your servitor and have come helplessly, surrender unto your pair of divine feet.

**vēda vāymoḻi andaṇan oruvan** – Why is āḻvār adding the adjective “*vēda vāy moḻi*” instead of just saying “*andaṇan oruvan*“? āḻvār is talking about a jīvātmā’s utmost duty to fulfil īśvaran’s desire, due to his greatness. One who is having the speech which has learnt vēdam. One who is engaged in vēda pārāyaṇam (recital). With this – it is explained that he has svarūpa jñānam (that is, being a servitor). One who has determined the essence of vēdam and is engaged in pārāyaṇam of the same.

**andaṇan oruvan** – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-1-piravith-thuyar/) “*aṟavanai āḻippadai andaṇanai*” (who is most benevolent, who carries the sudarsana cakram and who is the purest supreme lord) – here his purity is spoken about. Purity for ātmā is the purity of \[śēśatva\] jñānam which is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.38](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-38/) “*na hi jñānēna sadruśam*” (There is nothing as purifying as knowledge about self); it is not acquired from penance and going on holy yātrās \[undertaking pilgrimage\]. Previously sāndīpini was said as andaṇan, due to his being “*cāndasan*“; here it is said andaṇan, due to this brāhmaṇa being vaidika. cāndasa means one who learns and recites vēdam for specific result; vaidika means one who knows the essence of vēdam as said in [stōtra ratnam 11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/sthothra-rathnam-11/) “*vaidika: ka:*” (which vaidika (one who practices vēdam) cannot tolerate your aiśvarya (ability to control) which is natural and having boundless greatness?). One who is unique due to his purity. These two words explain svarūpa jñānam elaborately.

**endai** – My father. Unlike mother and father who take birth and die eventually, he is imperishable father as said in sahasranāmam “*avyaya:pitā*“. ātmā would think that bhagavān is the benefactor, who gave existence to this ātmā and who gave svarūpa jñānam to him.

**nin saraṇ** – You should be my upāyam (means); that brāhmaṇa was not having any other means and any other goal.

When asked “If you consider me as the goal and means, what is your worry now?” He said “I have no worries, but”

**ennudai manaivi** – My wife; my sahadarmacāriṇi (one who conducts dharma along with me). She is not the one who is to be abandoned as said in  vihagēndra samhitā 22 (and quoted in śaraṇāgati gadyam) “*pitaram mātaram dārān putrān bandūn sakīn gurūn* l *ratnāni danadānyāni kśētrāṇi ca gruhāṇi ca* ll *sarvadarmāmśca santyajya sarvakāmāmśca sākśarān* ll *lōkavikrānta caraṇau śaraṇam tē’vrajam vibhō* ll” (Oh bhagavān! Leaving aside father, mother, wife, children, relatives, friends, teachers, gems, wealth and food grains, fields, houses, all the means \[to attain you\] and all the benefits including *kaivalyam* \[where the ātmā enjoys itself\], along with any impression in these, I take refuge under your divine feet which had mercifully measured the worlds). When tears are seen in her eyes, she deserves to be helped out of compassion. Such is her nature.

**kādal makkaḷai** – She has great love towards her children.

**payattalum kāṇāḷ** – After doing everything it takes to carry the children in her womb, when it is time to see them after delivery, they are not to be seen.

What is the reason for that?

**kadiyadu ōr deyvam koṇḍu oḷikkum** – I have not seen such dēvatā which steals children, previously. Even yama would leave the body and will only take the ātmā; even before being seen by the mother, like those who steal while being watched, this dēvatā would take away the children with their bodies. This was done by nācciyārs (divine consorts of bhagavān) to see kriṣṇa’s bodily beauty.

**aḻaippa** – Informing kriṣṇa in this manner.

That is – kriṣṇa had taken dīkśā (vow) in a particular yāgam and was present, having all his divine limbs covered. At that time, the brāhmaṇa went and said “My wife gave birth to three children; but before even she could see them, a dēvatā took them away. Now, she is pregnant again and is due for delivery soon and you should protect this child”. When kriṣṇa said “Alright! We shall do as you requested” and started rising, at that time arjuna told “Do your highness, who have taken a vow in this yāgam, have to go and take care of this? I will go and give the remedy to him”. kriṣṇa gently smiled at him and said “Why don’t you do it?” arjuna reached the pregnancy \[delivery\] house and made a protective layer with his arrows; subsequently, as the crying sound of the child was heard, the child disappeared. The brāhmaṇa caught hold of the frontal hair of arjuna saying “When kriṣṇa came to help, why did you, who are an inferior kśatriya, cause further, huge problems?” and dragged arjuna by his hair, to kriṣṇa. Then kriṣṇa, understanding the situation, took the vaidika and arjuna in his chariot, stopped at the end of mūla prakruti, entered paramapadam, and brought back the four children and showed them with their earrings, sandalwood paste and turmeric which were applied on their bodies. Since paramapadam is not transformed by time, he brought them back with the same forms, without any change.

**ēdalār munnē** – He brought them back in front of those who made fun of the vaidika saying “The children were gone long ago; no one knows where they went; while this is the case, the vaidika is going to bring them back with the help of kriṣṇa!”.

**ēdalār** – These are the words of āḻvār \[on observing the vicinity\]. They are enemies who are in our proximity \[i.e., they follow vēdam like us, but don’t understand bhagavān’s greatness\]. That is, those upāsakas (who believe in self-effort) will say – isn’t it said in pūrvamīmāmsā 3-7-19 ‘*śāstrapalam prayōktari*‘ (One who carries out activities will reap the benefits mentioned in śāstram)? He (vaidika) does not have anything in his hand, but he is going to get something through someone else (bhagavān).

**in aruḷ …** – He helped the vaidika as if it is a help for self. Showing his mercy.

**un makkaḷ maṟṟu ivar enṟu koduttāy** – You brought them back and gave them with the same limbs to make him accept “these are my children”.

**ādalāl vandu un adiyiṇai adaindēn** – I surrendered unto you thinking about your great ability. He \[bhagavān\] asked “I brought those children from paramapadam back to this earth;; do you have such need?” āḻvār responded “īsn’t it more difficult to take someone (me) from here to paramapadam?” It is easy to bring people from paramapadam to samsāram, since it happens purely based on bhagavān’s desire; but when he has to take people from samsāram to paramapadam, he has to convince the individuals to go there. That is more difficult to do.

**aṇi poḻil …** – Haven’t you come and reclined here to take the people from here to there? I am drowned in samsāra, being dēhātmābhimāni (one who considers body to be self) and viśaya pravaṇa (one who is desirous of worldly enjoyments). Haven’t your highness mercifully come here and reclined here, only to give svarūpa jñānam (knowledge about the self) to me who is in such state and to create desire towards you in me, and to make me stay in the assembly of devotees where there is endless joy?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 5.8.9. Tulangu ninmudi

*tuḷangu nīṇmudi arasar tam kurisiltoṇḍai mannavan tiṇ tiṟal oruvaṟkuuḷangoḷ anbinōdu innaruḷ suranduangodu nāḻigai ēḻudan iruppavaḷangoḷ mandiram maṟṟavaṟku aruḷicceydavāṟu adiyēn aṟindu ulagamaḷanda ponnadiyē adaindu uyndēnaṇipoḻil tiruvarangattammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuḷangu – shining; nīḷ – showing his supremacy over everyone; mudi – having crown; arasar tam – for the kings; kurisil – being the king; tiṇ – firm; tiṟal – having strength; oruvan – (due to that, being) unique; toṇḍai mannavaṟku – in the matter of toṇḍaimān cakravarti; uḷam koḷ – in (his) divine heart; anbinōdu – with love; in aruḷ – mercy without any other expectation; surandu – showed; maṟṟu – further; avaṟku – for that king; angu – in protecting his kingdom; odu – being wasted; nāḻigai – during the times; ēḻu nāḻigaiyōdu – a time period of 24 minutes focussed on 7 principles; iruppa – to remain (to have those 7 principles remain in my heart); vaḷam koḷ – having magnanimity of being pursuable by all; mandiram – tirumantram (aśtākśaram); aruḷicceyda āṟu – the way he instructed; adiyēn – I, who am a servitor; aṟindu – analysed; ulagam – worlds; aḷanda – measured and held in his control; pon – desirable; adiyē – (your) divine feet only; adaindu – considering to be the means; uyndēn – got uplifted; aṇi – decorative; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; tiruvarangattu – mercifully reclining in śrīrangam; ammānē – Oh lord!

**Перевод:**

**In the previous two pāsurams, bhagavān having śakti (ability) and being the complete upāyam (means) were explained. What is the reason for this pāsuram’s arrival? bhagavān says to āḻvār “You are considering the lowliness of the samsāram and my great ability and urging to reach me; this is not natural; it is natural for you to remain patient and observe how I grant you mōkśam”. āḻvār responds “Just as you gave svarūpa jñānam (true knowledge) to toṇḍaimān cakravarti who remained fully subervient to you without thinking about anything else, you have to grant svarūpa jñānam to me as well” and surrenders to bhagavān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In the beginning, as said in [periya tirumoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/11/periya-thirumozhi-1-1-1/) “*nān kaṇḍu koṇḍēn nārāyaṇā ennum nāmam*” (I, who am unqualified to recite the divine name, got to see the divine name, nārāyaṇa), āḻvār first got tirumantram with meanings and then realised the same up to tadīya śēśatvam (servitude towards bhāgavatas) as said in periya tirumoḻi 8.10.3 “*nin tiruvetteḻuttum kaṟṟu nān uṟṟadum un adiyārkku adimai*” (I learnt aśtākśaram and understood that I am the servant of your servitors). Did he not acquire svarūpa jñānam before itself \[i.e. in the beginning itself\]? It is apt to consider that the knowledge we have is not fully trustworthy \[and practice humility\]. bhagavān made śrī nārada bhagavān instruct tirumantram with its meanings to śrī puṇḍarīka as said in itihāsa samuccayam “*kim tatra bahubhirmantrai: kim tatra bahubhirvratai: namō nārāyānēti mantra: sarvārta sādaka:* ” (what is the purpose of other mantrams and other vratams (vows)? The incantation namō nārayaṇāya will give all benefits) and mahābhāratam “*narājjātāni*” (Everything came from nara (that is, nārāyaṇa)). But when it was time to bestow the benefit, īśvaran asked śrī puṇḍarīka “What do you need?” He responded as in jitantā stōtram “*kvāham atyanta durbuddi:*” (I am having very inferior mind. What do I know?”. śaraṇāgati is sarvābhimata sādanam (the means to get all benefits).

toṇḍaimān cakravarti was the king of kings who were having shining crowns which show their supremacy over everyone; he is having firm strength and is unique due to that; having love in his divine heart with love towards such king, you showed mercy without any other expectation; further during the times the king wasted in protecting the kingdom, you instructed in one nāḻigai (24 minutes) the tirumantram having magnanimity of being pursuable by all, focussed on 7 principles and made those 7 principles remain in him. Oh lord who is mercifully reclining in śrīrangam which is surrounded by decorative orchards! I who am a servitor, analysed your words towards such king, got uplifted by considering your desirable divine feet only which measured the worlds and held the worlds in your control.

**tuḷangu** – Shining instead of being dull. With this – it is not speaking just about radiance, but it is speaking about the radiance of ruling the kingdom without having mutual conflicts.

**nīḷ mudi** – Not just the length of the crown, but the vastness of the kingdom, is spoken about here.

**arasar tam kurisil** – Emperor. Just like there is king for men and women, he is emperor for kings. mahābhāratam āśva parvam 43-13 “*rājādi rājas sarvēśām viṣṇur brahmamayō mahān* l *īśvaram tam vijānīma*: *sa pitā sa prajāpati* ll” (viṣṇu alone is the radiant entity who is the emperor of all the kings, who is eminent as *brahmasvarūpi* (with the nature of the supreme entity). Due to the vastness of the kingdom, it will be difficult to assert “He is the crowned king of this kingdom”, hence it is emphasised that he is the emperor of kings.

**toṇḍai mannavan** – While he was crowned in toṇḍai maṇḍalam (present day’s chennai, kāncīpuram region), he extended his kingdom all over.

The reason for that is explained.

**tiṇ tiṟal oruvaṟku** – As said in viṣṇu darmam “*vīra bhōjñā vasundarā*” (Earth is fit to be ruled and enjoyed by the brave persons), he was fighting everywhere by his valour, remained unique for his valour. His valour is so great that it was honoured by tirumangai āḻvār who is known for valour as in [periya tirumoḻi 3.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/10/periya-thirumozhi-3-9-10/) “*maruvalar tam udal tuṇiya* *vāḷ vīsum parakālan*” (uses his sword to cut the enemies’ bodies to pieces). If āḻvār is explaining this as an example for surrendering unto bhagavān to get svarūpa jñānam, why did he choose to explain this which will lead to pride? āḻvār is speaking about this valour, thinking “This valour will be useful for protecting the devotees and destroying the enemies, after acquiring svarūpa jñānam”.

**uḷam koḷ anbinōdu** – Since this affection which bhagavān showed towards toṇḍaimān was to instruct for his well-being, it will be matching bhagavān’s divine heart.

**in aruḷ** – The mercy which is considered to be for bhagavān’s benefit. While he considers all types of devotees who approach him, including those who seek worldly benefits, to be generous as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.18](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-18/) “*udārā:*” (generous), those who are very dear to him are addressed in the same ślōkam as “*jñāni tvātmaiva*” (but the jñāni is the one who sustains (me)).

**surandu** – Just as those who would let out milk from the bosom, due to unbearable pain (of not feeding their child), bhagavān let the mercy flow.

**angodu nāḻigai** – While his days are being wasted in the burden of administering the kingdom.

**ēḻudan iruppa** – Seven times indicate seven principles (six hurdles which are shown in [8th ślōkam of aśta ślōki](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/01/ashta-sloki-slokams-1-4/) that is, considering body to be the self, considering the self to be independent, having servitude towards others, considering self/others to be the refuge, considering bodily relatives as relatives, considering sense enjoyment as the goal, and are eliminated by the different parts of tirumantram, and the seventh principle of servitude towards bhāgavatas).

**vaḷam koḷ mandiram** – Beauty. Wandering. vaḷam means the ability to wander to everyone just as īśvara who can grant all wishes does. It will assist karma yōga etc for a prapanna, will lead to svarūpa jñānam and deliver him to paramapadam.

**maṟṟavaṟku aruḷicceyda āṟu** – Instructed tirumantram and created tadīya śēśatvam (being devoted to devotees) in him. Here it is speaking about toṇḍaimān cakravarti becoming devoted to kuṟumbaṟutta nambi (a potter who was greatly devoted to śrīnivāsa bhagavān). \[kuṟumbaṟutta nambi would offer a clay flower to tiruvēngadamudaiyān (śrīnivāsa bhagavān) at the end of his day, with the left-over clay. śrinivasa bhagavān would keep that on his head and discard the golden flowers submitted by toṇḍaimān cakravarti. When the king asked bhagavān about it, bhagavān explained about nambi’s devotion\] kuṟumbaṟutta nambi said “Just as a husband will share his private/intimate interactions with his chaste wife in public, tiruvēngadamudaiyān is revealing my devotion to others! Why is he being loud-mouthed like this”.

**adiyēn aṟindu** – This is āḻvār’s “nān” (I) \[i.e., he always says adiyēn to indicate his total servitude\].

**ulagam aḷanda** – The divine feet which were placed even on those who turn away from bhagavān.

**ponnadi** – Desired by all. That is, as with water placed in a golden pot which can be touched by vasiśta or caṇḍāḷa, without any difference, his divine feet are approachable by all.

**adaindu uyndēn** – I surrendered unto him praying “You should grant me svarūpa jñānam” and got uplifted.

**aṇi poḻil …** – āḻvār is identifying the principle which was demonstrated by tiruvēngadamudaiyān and surrendering unto the divine feet of periya perumāḷ. When bhagavān was standing on tirumalā, a purpose is revealed; subsequently the same bhagavān reclined in śrīrangam.

Since āḻvār started with “*māḻai mān mada nōkki*” and concluded with “*ulagam aḷanda ponnadiyē adaindu uyndēn*“, in all these 9 pāsurams, the theme is based on the single principle (revealed in dvaya mahā mantram) which is surrender at the divine feet of bhagavān with the help of śrī mahālakśmi.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.10. Mada maligai

*mādamāḷigai sūḻ tirumangaimannan onnalar tangaḷai vellumādalmā valavan kali kanṟiaṇipoḻil tiruvarangattammānainīdu tol pugaḻāḻi vallānaiendaiyai nedumālai ninaindapādal pattivai pādumin tondīr!pāda nummidaip pāvam nillāvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mādam – by maṇḍapams (festive halls); māḷigai – by homes; sūḻ – surrounded; tirumangai – for tirumangai region; mannan – being the king; onnalar tangaḷai – enemies; vellum – one who defeats; ādal mā – a prancing horse which is named ādal mā; valavan – one who rides; kali kanṟi – āḻvār who eradicates sins; aṇi – decorative; poḻil – having orchards; tiruvarangattu – for the divyadēśam named tiruvarangam; ammānai – being the lord; nīdu – being immeasurable; tol – eternal; pugaḻ – having fame; āḻi – tiruvāḻi (sudarśana chakra); vallānai – one who controls; endaiyai – being my lord; nedu – endless; mālai – aḻagiya maṇavāḷan who is having love towards his devotees; ninainda – enjoyed and sung due to that experience; ivai pattu pādal – these ten pāsurams; toṇḍīr – Oh bhāgavatas!; pādumin – sing; pāda – as you sing (these pāsurams); nummidai – with you; pāvam – sins which are hurdles for the goal; nillā – will be eradicated

**Перевод:**

**It is said that though those who sing these pāsurams may not have the same emotions/purity of āḻvār, just by doing so, their hurdles for the ultimate goal will leave them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār, who is the king of tirumangai region which is surrounded by maṇḍapams and homes, who defeats the enemies, who rides a prancing horse which is named ādal mā and who eradicates sins, sang these ten pāsurams, after enjoying aḻagiya maṇavāḷan who is having endless love towards his devotees, who is the lord of the divyadēśam named tiruvarangam which is having decorative orchards, who controls tiruvāḻi which is having immeasurable, eternal fame, due to that experience. Oh bhāgavatas! Sing these pāsurams. As you do that, the sins which are with you and are hurdles for the goal, will be eradicated.

**mādam …** – āḻvār is saying that it is because of the birth in this town, he got all the goodness. With this, the greatness of his birth place is identified. For the world to accept something, it should be said “This is spoken by a trustworthy person” as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 4.1 “*vālmīkir bhagavān ruśi:*” (the most knovledegable sage vālmīki), “*sa hōvāca vyāsa: pārāśarya:*” (thus spoke vyāsa, the famous son of parāśara), “*kurugūrc cadagōpan*” (nammāḻvār from tirukkurugūr).

**onnalar …** – As tirumangai āḻvār started his procession with decorations, enemies will be destroyed like a full vegetable boiling and breaking down. Enemies of āḻvār are – bāhyas who insult pramāṇams (vēdams etc) and kudruśtis who insult pramēyam (bhagavān). \[bāhyas reject vēdas; kudruśtis reject bhagavān’s true nature, forms, qualities etc\]. Winning them means – as said in śrīrangarāja stavam pūrva śatakam 36 “*jita bāhya jinādi maṇipratimā api vaidikayan iva rangapurē \| maṇimaṇḍapa vapragaṇān vitanē parakāla kavi: praṇamēmahi tān \|\|*” (tirumangai āḻvār who was like yama for jainas et al who were speaking against vēdams, defeated them with his debates. He converted their idols which are made of gold and gems, to vaidika purpose. With this wealth, he built beautiful maṇḍapams and forts in śrīrangam), he built forts with the outsiders’ idols; he eliminated the supremacy of rudra which is held by the followers of śaiva āgama.

**kalikanṟi** – Destroyer of enemies. These words are said, respecting bhagavān’s greatness.

Further, he is explaining the nature of the entity who is sung about.

**aṇi poḻil tiruvarangattammānai** – parāśara bhattar would say “As soon as he saw the tirumangai region, where did the beautiful orchards of śrīrangam disappear?” .

**nīdu tol pugaḻ āḻi vallānai** – In the protection of devotees, sudarśana chakra will be ahead of bhagavān’s divine heart. It is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.10.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-5-thiramudai-valaththal/) “*aṟamuyal āḻi*” (divine chakra engaged in righteous acts).

**tol pugaḻ** – It is not incidental. \[But it is natural.\]

**āḻi vallānai** – His greatness is such that he can keep the sudarśana chakra at his disposal and get anything accomplished.

**endaiyai** – If there is no relationship, even if he had the tools, he need not engage in others’ tasks; here, the relationship which makes him act for us, is highlighted.

Even if he has the relationship, if he lacks love towards us, there is no use.

**nedu mālai** – One who is greatly affectionate. With these, the qualities which are required in him for others to surrender unto him are explained.

**ninainda pādal** – The words of those who follow these principles clearly. The words which are an outcome of the overflowing experience.

**pattivai** – Collected in ten pāsurams, just as one who knows the nature of pearls, makes a necklace and checks them by wearing in their hands.

**pādumin toṇḍīr** – Oh you who are all desirous towards bhagavat viśayam (matters relating to bhagavān)! Speak out due to overflowing joy.

**pāda nummidaip pāvam nillāvē** – Just as a disease gets eradicated by drinking milk, as we recite āḻvār’s pāsurams, the hurdles for the goal will be eradicated automatically, as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*sarvapāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi*” (I will ensure that all sins are eradicated for you). In saying “*nīdu tol pugaḻ āḻi vallānai*“, āḻvār is focussing on bhagavān’s ability indicated in “*aham*” in the same ślōkam from śrī bhagavat gītā.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9 Kai ilangu

## 5.9.1. Kai ilangu

*kaiyilangu āḻi sangan karumugil tiruniṟattanpoyyilan meyyan tan tāḷ adaivarēl adimai ākkumseyyalar kamalam ōngu seṟi poḻil ten tiruppērpaiyaravaṇaiyān nāmam paravi nān uyndavāṟē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kai – in his divine hand; ilangu – shining; āḻi – tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); sangan – and having śrī pāncajanyam; karu – dark; mugil – like a cloud; tiru – beautiful; niṟattan – having complexion; poy ilan – (in the greatness revealed in śāstram about him) not having any falsity (having such greatness); meyyan – (for the devotees) one who reveals them; than tāḷ – his divine feet; adaivarēl – if they surrender; adimai ākkum – one who makes them servitors (for him); sey – farmland; alar – blossoming; kamalam – lotus flowers’; ōngu – height; seṟi – being dense; poḻil – having orchards; then – beautiful; tiruppēr – in the divyadēśam named tiruppēr; pai – having expansive hoods; aravu – tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan); aṇaiyān – sarvēśvaran who is having as mattress, his; nāmam – divine names; paravi – recited; nān – I; uynda āṟu – the way I got uplifted; E – How amazing!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is having shining divine chakra and śrī pāncajanyam in his divine hands; he is having beautiful complexion like that of a dark cloud; he is not having any falsity; he reveals these aspects to his devotees; he makes those who surrender unto his divine feet to be his servitors; in the beautiful divyadēśam named tiruppēr, which is having orchards with tall and dense lotus flowers which blossom in farmland, such sarvēśvaran is having tiruvanantāḻvān with expansive hoods, as his mattress. How amazing is it that I recited his divine names and the way I got uplifted!

It is said both as “*kai ilangu āḻi sanga****n*** *karumugil tiruniṟattan*” and as “*kai ilangu āḻi sanga****m*** *karumugil tiruniṟattan*“.

**kai ilangu āḻi sangan karumugil tiruniṟattan** – In the divine hands which are so beautiful on their own and should be rid of druśti (evil eyes), he is having the shining tiruvāḻi and śrī pāncajanyam.

**karumugil tiruniṟattan** – As said in [tiruppāvai 4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2014/12/thiruppavai-04-azhi-mazhai/) “*āḻi pōl minni*” (Shining like the chakra), the combination of the divine weapons with bhagavān’s divine form appears like lightning with a cloud.

**poy ilan** – In the greatness of being different from all other entities, there is no doubt of exaggeration.

**meyyan** – All of these are held by bhagavān for the sake of his devotees as said in jitantā stōtram “*bhaktānām*” – this remains the truth.

**than tāḷ …** – As said in yajur vēdam “*dēhi mē dadāmi tē*” (you grant me something and I will do something for you), instead of getting some benefits and leaving, towards those who surrender exclusively unto his divine feet, he will engage them in eternal servitude instead of giving some benefits and sending them off.

**sey alar** – As they plant paddy seeds in the farmlands, they yield lotus flowers. In tentiruppēr which is having the blossomed lotus flowers which are tall and dense orchards, bhagavān is having tiruvanantāḻvān who is having expanded hoods due to the joy from the eternal enjoyment of sarvēśvaran, as his mattress. His divine name.

**paravi nān uynda āṟē** – If we go to paramapadam, the words which are spoken out of joy as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*aham annam aham annam*” (I am enjoyed by him, I am enjoyed by him) and taittirīya upaniśat “*saha brahmaṇā*” (Enjoy bhagavān’s qualities, being together with him), are said here in this divyadēśam after arriving here. What a life I have attained!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.2. Vangamar

*vangamār kadalgaḷ ēḻum malaiyum vānagamum maṟṟumangaṇmā jñālam ellām amudu seydu umiḻnda endaitingaḷ māmugil aṇavu seṟi poḻil ten tiruppērengaḷ māl iṟaivan nāmam ētti nān uyndavāṟē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vangam – boats; Ar – filled; ēḻ kadalgaḷum – seven oceans; malaiyum – seven anchoring mountains; vānagamum – sky; maṟṟum – further; am kaṇ – beautifully spacious; mā jñālam – vast earth; ellām – all of these; amudu seydu – consuming (during deluge); umiḻnda – spitting out (during creation); endai – being my lord; tingaḷ – moon’s orbit; mā mugil – huge cloud region; aṇavu – reaching up to; seṟi – being dense; poḻil – having orchards; then – beautiful; tiruppēr – in the divyadēśam named tiruppēr; engaḷ – towards us, devotees; māl – having love; iṟaivan – sarvēśvaran’s; nāmam – divine names; ētti – praised; nān – I; uynda āṟu – the way I got uplifted; E – How amazing!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran consumed seven oceans filled with boats, seven anchoring mountains, sky and beautifully spacious, vast earth during deluge and spat them out during creation; being my lord, he is in the divyadēśam named tiruppēr which is having dense orchards which are reaching up to the cloud region and moon’s orbit; he is having love towards us, devotees. How amazing is it that I recited his divine names and the way I got uplifted!

**vangam …** – Boats are said as decorations for ocean. \[emperumān\] Consumed the seven oceans which are filled with boats, the mountains which are like anchors for earth, the sky which gives space to all of these, and further, the vast earth which is like a fence for these, during the danger of deluge and placing them in his stomach, and subsequently spat them to see the outside world thinking “They cannot remain inside for too long and become weak”. This is similar to those who swallow their wealth (precious gems) and subsequently spit it out to see them, and enjoy them.

**tingaḷ …** – In tentiruppēr which is having dense orchards which are tall to reach the abode of moon and clouds.

**engaḷ māl iṟaivan nāmam ētti nān uynda āṟē** – One who is having great love towards devotees like us, and one who cannot be abandoned due to his relationship with us, even if he does not love us. Praising such sarvēśvaran’s divine name.

**nān uynda āṟē** – As said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (As good as asat/acit only), I, who was like acit, became uplifted! How amazing!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.3. Oruvanai undippu mel

*oruvanai undippū mēl ōnguvittu āgam tannāloruvanaic cābam nīkki umbar āḷ enṟu vittānperuvarai madiḷgaḷ sūḻnda perunagar aravaṇai mēlkaruvarai vaṇṇan tenpēr karudi nān uyndavāṟē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

oruvanai – the unique brahmā; undi pū mēl – on his divine lotus navel; ōnguvittu – created; oruvanai – another one, rudra; āgam tannāl – with the drop of a sweat from his divine chest (by sprinkling it on the skull that rudra had); sābam – (his) curse; nīkki – eliminated; umbar āḷ – “(You, like previously) can rule the higher worlds”; enṟu vittān – being the one who sent him off; peru varai – like huge mountains; madiḷgaḷ – by forts; sūḻnda – surrounded; peru nagar – in the vast tirurppēr nagar; aravu aṇai mēl – on anantaśayanam (ādiśēśan); karu varai – black coloured mountain’s; vaṇṇan – sarvēśvaran who is having complexion; tenpēr – in tentiruppēr where he is mercifully residing; karudi – desired (to enjoy him); nān – I; uynda āṟu – the way I got uplifted; E – How amazing!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran created the unique brahmā on his divine, lotus navel; he eliminated the curse of another one, rudra, with the drop of a sweat from his divine chest and told him “You can rule the higher worlds” and sent him off; I desired to enjoy him who is mercifully residing in the vast tentiruppēr which is surrounded by forts which are like huge mountains, on anantaśayanam and is having the complexion of black coloured mountains.  How amazing is the way I got uplifted!

**oruvanai …** – brahmā who remains so unique that after counting him, there is none to count subsequently, and is the controller of 14 layered universe; creating such brahmā in his divine lotus navel, and with the sweat from his divine chest, eliminating the curse acquired by rudra.

**umbar āḷ enṟu vittān** – He sent off rudra telling him to conduct the world without losing any of the greatness of being the leader of celestial entities. He sent him off saying “Rule over the higher worlds”.

**peru varai …** – Being surrounded by the forts which are said to be like huge mountains. One who is mercifully reclining like a black mountain on tiruvanantāḻvān in the great town which can be said as in [mudal tiruvandādi 51](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/munram-thiruvandhadhi-51/) “*kalangāp perunagaram*” (paramapadam, the great town, which has no bewilderment).

**tenpēr karudi** – I who desired “Let me go there and be uplifted” and became uplifted! How amazing!

\[Alternative recital\]

**than pēr karudi** – How amazing is it that I recited the divine name matching his beautiful form and became uplifted!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.4. Unamar talai

*ūnamar talai onṟu ēndi ulagelām tiriyum īsanīnamar sābam nīkkāy enna oṇ punalai īndāntēnamar poḻilgaḷ sūḻnda seṟivayal ten tiruppērvānavar talaivan nāmam vāḻtti nān uyndavāṟē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

Un amar – filled with flesh; onṟu talai – the skull of brahmā; ēndi – holding in hand; ulagu ellām – in all worlds; tiriyum – roaming around (to get alms); īsan – rudran; In amar – “lowly; sābam – (my) curse; nīkkāy – (you) should remove”; enna – as he requested; oṇ punalai – (from your divine chest) beautiful sweat (which can eliminate the curse); īndāy – one who gave (one who sprinkled on that skull); tēn amar – filled with beetles; poḻilgaḷ – by orchards; sūḻnda – surrounded; seṟi – dense; vayal – having fertile fields; tentiruppēr – in the divyadēśam named tentiruppēr; vānavar – for nityasūris; talaivan – lord, his; nāmam – (reciting) divine names; vāḻtti – praised; nān – I; uynda āṟu – the way I got uplifted; E – How amazing!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

rudran who was holding brahmā’s skull filled with flesh, in his hand, and was roaming around all the worlds; \[he went to śrīman nārāyaṇa in kśīrābdi or badarīkāśramam\] and requested “you should remove this lowly curse from me”; the one who gave the beautiful sweat \[to eliminate the curse\] is present in the divyadēśam named tentiruppēr which is having orchards filled with beetles, surrounded by dense fertile fields.  How amazing is it that I praised the divine names of the lord of nityasūīris and the way I got uplifted!

**ūnamar …** – Holding the flesh filled skull, just as the one who ruled over a town ended up roaming around with shackles, rudra roamed around the world where he was well respected, seeking remedy; he went to bhagavān and surrendered unto his divine feet saying “You should eliminate this lowly curse which is causing me disaster”; bhagavān gave the sweat from his divine chest \[and eliminated his curse\].

**tēn …** – In tentiruppēr which is having dense fertile lands which are surrounded by orchards filled with beetles.

**vānavar …** – Just as a person will drink milk \[a desirable material, unlike a bitter medicine\] and get rid of his disease, how amazing is it to recite the divine name of the leader of nityasūris and be uplifted! Even if this divine name causes destruction, we cannot abandon it.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.5. Vakkaran vay

*vakkaran vāy mun kīṇḍa māyanē! enṟu vānōrpukku araṇ tandu aruḷāy ennap pon āgattānainakkari uruvamāgi nagam kiḷarndu idandu ugandasakkarac celvan tenpērt talaivan tāḷ adaindu uyndēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vakkaran – “danta vakra’s; vāy – mouth; mun – in the past; kīṇḍa – one who tore; māyavanē – Oh amazing person!”; enṟu – saying this; vānōr – dēvatās; pukku – gathered and came; araṇ tandaruḷāy – (for us) mercifully give protection; enna – as they prayed; ponnāgattānai – hiraṇya (who is their enemy); ari uruvamāgi – being in the form of narasimha; nakku – laughed; kiḷarndu – grew; nagam – with nails; idandu – tore; uganda – one who felt joyful; sakkaram – with sudarśana cakram; selvan – being śrīmān (the consort of śrī mahālakśmi); tenpēr – for tentiruppēr; talaivan – one who is the lord; tāḷ – divine feet; adaindu – reached; uyndēnē – I got uplifted

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

dēvatās gathered and came saying “Oh amazing person who tore the mouth of danta vakran, in the past!” and prayed “Mercifully give your protection for us”; as they did that, bhagavān in the form of narasimha, laughed, grew big and tore hiraṇya with his nails and felt joyful. I reached the divine feet of the lord of tiruppēr who is the śrīmān (the consort of śrī mahālakśmi) and got uplifted.

**vakkaran …** – An asura named danta vakran tormented all the dēvatās and was roaming around in that manner. Saying “Oh one who is having amazing ability to tear his mouth effortlessly!”

**vānōr** – All the dēvatās gathered together and came and requested “You should mercifully give us a refuge”.

**pon āgattānai** – hiraṇya. Assuming the form of a narasimha (human-lion form), laughed, growing big, he tore with his divine nails, and became joyful thinking “prahlādan’s hurdle is gone now”.

**sakkarac celvan** – hiraṇya’s body was not sufficient enough for bhagavān’s divine nails. Further the divine chakra is just present for decoraton.

**tenpēr …** – How amazing is it that I have become uplifted after surrendering unto sarvēśvaran who is greater than all and is eternally residing in tentiruppēr!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.6. Vilangalal

*vilangalāl kadal adaittu viḷangiḻai poruttu villālilangai mānagarkku iṟaivan irubadu puyam tuṇittānnalangoḷ nānmaṟai vallārgaḷ ōttoli ēttak kēttumalangu pāy vayal tiruppēr maruvi nān vāḻndavāṟē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vilangu – shining; iḻai poruttu – for pirātti who is having ornaments; vilangalāl – with rocks; kadal – ocean; adaittu – built a bridge; mā ilangai nagarkku – for the huge city of lankā; iṟaivan – rāvaṇa, who is the lord, his; irubadu puyam – twenty shoulders; villāl – by bending (his) bow; tuṇittān – one who severed; nalam koḷ – having good conduct; nāl maṟai – four vēdams; vallārgaḷ – brāhmaṇas who can recite; ētta – loudly recited; ōttu oli – sound of vēdam; kēttu – listened; malangu – fish; pāy – jump and move away; vayal – having fertile fields; tiruppēr – divyadēśam named tentiruppēr; maruvi – desiring to worship; nān – I; vāḻnda āṟē – How amazing is it that I got uplifted!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

For pirātti who is having shining ornaments, bhagavān built a bridge with rocks on the ocean and severed the twenty shoulders of rāvaṇa who is the lord of the huge city of lankā, by bending his bow. Such emperumān is present in the divyadēśam named tentiruppēr which is having fertile fields where the fish listen to the loudly recited sound of the vēdam which is recited by by brāhmaṇas who are having good conduct and who can recite all four vēdams, jump and move away. How amazing is it that I desired to worship such emperumān and got uplifted!

**vilangal** – Having built a bridge on the ocean with rocks which will submerge in the water, being defeated by the beauty of pirātti who is decorated with shining ornaments, with the bow which is distinct for being a warrior, he severed rāvaṇa’s shoulders which were like a protective layer of lankā, where rāvaṇa was thinking “lankā is the capital of my country, which cannot by destroyed even by brahmāstram; am I not the controller here?”.

**nalam koḷ** … – brāhmaṇas who mastered vēdams which are free from defects and are four in categories; alternative explanation – brāhmaṇas who have good conduct and have mastered all four vēdams.

**ōttoli ēttak kēttu** – Hearing their loud chanting, the fish in the fertile fields think that these are sounds made towards them and jump away; how amazing is it that I have desired to worship such divyadēśam and got uplifted!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.7. Venney tan

*veṇṇey tān amudu seyya veguṇḍu mattāycci ōccikkaṇṇiyār kuṟungayiṟṟāl katta vettenṟu irundāntiṇṇamā madiḷgaḷ sūḻnda ten tiruppēruḷ vēlaivaṇṇanār nāmam nāḷum vāy moḻindu uyndavāṟē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tān – he who was begotten by yaśōdā after performing penance; veṇṇey – butter; amudu seyya – as he mercifully consumed; āycci – mother yaśōdā; veguṇḍu – became angry; mattu – the pestle which helps in churning the curd; ōcci – threw; kaṇṇi – with knots; Ar – filled; kuṟu – small; kayiṟṟāl – with rope; katta – bound; vettenṟu – accepting (that); irundān – one who remained; tiṇṇam – being firm; mā – huge; madiḷgaḷ – by forts; sūḻnda – surrounded; then tiruppēruḷ – in the divyadēśam named tentiruppēr; vēlai – like ocean; vaṇṇanār – for the one who is having complexion; nāmam – divine names; nāḷum – every day; vāymoḻindu – recited; uynda āṟē! – How amazing is it that I got uplifted!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

As kriṣṇa, who was begotten by yaśōdā after performing penance, mercifully consumed the butter, mother yaśōdā became angry, threw the pestle which helps in churning the curd and bound him with small rope filled with knots; he remained there accepting that. Such sarvēśvaran is present in the divyadēśam named tentiruppēr which is surrounded by huge, firm forts. How amazing is it that I got uplifted by reciting the divine names of such bhagavān who is having complexion like that of an ocean!

**veṇṇey …** – She performed penance thinking “The cow’s products should not go waste. We should have a child to enjoy these” and begot kriṣṇa. Still, if kriṣṇa ate too much which will lead to indigestion, it will not be accepted by them; as they continue to hide them from him, he develops more interest in them. He would not miss out on that which sustains him. As they churn the curd with so much difficulty and preserve the butter, he would take it and eat it.

**veguṇḍu** … – Became angry. Mother yaśōdā desiring to hit him with the pestle, bound him with the rope which had many knots; the rope cannot be extended and hence his body needed to be shrunk to bind him down. She bound him in that manner.

**vettu enṟu irundān** – Just as those who accept beatings saying “If you beat us considering us to be ordinary persons, we will accept all of those”, instead of beating and binding for any other reason, if they do it for stealing butter, he will accept it happily.

**tiṇṇam …** – In tentiruppēr which is surrounded by forts which give protection.

**vēlai …** – How amazing is it that I got uplifted by reciting the divine names which narrate the divine form of the one who has the form which is similar to ocean which eliminates ennui.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.8. Ambonar

am – beautiful; ponār – like gold (best); ulagam ēḻum – seven worlds; aṟiya – to know; āyppādi tannuḷ – in tiruvāyppādi; kombu – having body like a stick \[she was that slender\]; pinnai – nappinnaip pirātti’s; kōlam – with beauty; kūdudaṟku – to unite; ēṟu – bulls; konṟān – one who killed; sem – reddish; ponār – like gold; madiḷgaḷ sūḻnda tentiruppēruḷ – inside the divyadēśam named tentiruppēr which is surrounded by forts; mēvum – one who is remaining fixed; em pirān – our svamy’s; nāmam nāḷum ētti nān uynda āṟē! – How amazing is it that I recited his divine names and became uplifted!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

To let know the seven worlds, which are beautiful like gold, bhagavān killed the seven bulls to unite with the beauty of nappinnaip pirātti who is having body which is like a stick, in tiruvāppādi. He is remaining fixed inside the divyadēśam named tentiruppēr which is surrounded by forts which are reddish like gold. How amazing is it that I recited our svamy’s divine names and became uplifted!

**ambon …** – Not just the town of the covherd, but to let the best, seven worlds know, to unite with nappinnaip pirātti who is having a form which resembles a stick, in tiruvāyppādu, he killed the seven bulls. How amazing is it that I praised the divine names of my benefactor who is eternally residing in tirurppēr which is surrounded by beautiful forts, and got uplifted!

**nāl vagai …** – brāhmaṇas who are having more expertise than brahmā in four vēdams, five types of great yajñams, six ancillary subjects such as vyākaraṇam, have been residing in tiruppēr since the time of creation, just as sarvēśvaran himself has been residing here. sarvēśvaran who has owned the hearts of brāhmaṇas who are very simple and having great penance, is present in my heart.

*vaṇḍaṟai poḻil tiruppēr vari aravaṇaiyil paḷḷikoṇḍu uṟaiginṟa mālaik kodi madiḷ māda mangaitiṇ tiṟal tōḷ kaliyan senjolāl moḻinda mālaikoṇḍivai pādi ādak kūduvar nīḷ visumbē*

vaṇḍu – beetles; aṟai – humming; poḻil – having orchards; tiruppēr – in the divyadēśam named tiruppēr; vari – having moles; aravu – ādiśēśan; aṇaiyil – on the mattress; paḷḷi koṇḍu – reclining; uṟaiginṟa – eternally residing; mālai – on sarvēśvaran; kodi – with hoisted flags; madiḷ – forts; mādam – having mansions; mangai – being the leader of tirumangai region; tiṇ – firm; tiṟal – having strength; tōḷ – having shoulders; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; sem – beautiful (pursuable by all); sollāl – in tamiḻ; moḻinda – mercifully spoke; ivai mālai – these ten pāsurams; koṇḍu – recite; pādi – sing; Ada – as \[they\] dance; nīḷ – expansive; visumbu – paramapadam; kūduvar – will reach

**vaṇḍu aṟai …** – In tiruppēr where the beetles, having drunk honey, are humming in the orchards, sarvēśvaran who is mercifully reclining on the mattress, tiruvanantāḻvān who is having stripes, is the object of the praises here. ## 5.10 Tidaru

## 5.10.1. Tidaru

*tīdaṟu nilattodu eri kālinodu nīr keḻu visumbum avaiyāymāsaṟu manattinodu uṟakkamodu iṟakkai avaiyāya perumāntāy seṟa uḷaindu tayir uṇḍu kudamādu tadamārvar tagai sērnādan uṟaiginṟa nagar nandipura viṇṇagaram naṇṇu manamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tīdu aṟu – faultless; nilattodu – with earth; eri – fire; kālinodu – with air; nīr – water; keḻu – abundant (being the one which gives for all of these); viśumbum – ether; avaiyāy – being the antarātmā (in-dwelling super-soul) of panca bhūtams; māsu aṟu – faultless; manattinodu – with mind; uṟakkamodu – with the stages of susupti (deep sleep), svapnam (dream); iṟakkai – death; avaiyāga – being the controller of all of these; perumān – being sarvēśvaran; tāy – mother yaśōdā; seṟa – to become angry; uḷaindu – becoming fearful and having a softened heart; tayir – (before that) curd; uṇḍu – mercifully consumed; kudam ādu – one who danced with pots; tadam – expansive; mārvar – one who is having divine chest; tagai sēr – one who is complete with natural, auspicious qualities; nādan – the lord; uṟaiginṟa – eternally residing; nandipura viṇṇagaram – having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram; nagar – the divyadēśam; manamē – oh heart!; naṇṇu – try to reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being the antarātmā of panca bhūtams, viz. faultless earth, fire, air, water and abundant ether, being the controller of the four states of mind/body such as jāgrata (awake and faultless), suśupti (deep sleep), svapna (dream) and maraṇa (death), being sarvēśvaran, the lord became fearful with a softened heart as mother yaśōdā became angry, (and previously) mercifully consumed curd and danced with pots and who is having expansive divine chest and is complete with natural, auspicious qualities; he is eternally residing in the divyadēśam with the divine name nandipura viṇṇagaram. Oh heart! Try to reach there.

**tīdaṟu …** – Being the antarātmā of panca bhūtams starting with earth which is faultless due to being the place from where cētanas (souls) can attain enjoyment or liberation, sarvēśvaran who is being the controller of faultless mind, svapna (dream), suśupti (deep sleep) and maraṇam (death).

Previously (in the first portion of the pāsuram), bhagavān being antarātmā and protecting others is explained; subsequently, bhagavān incarnating to be seen by our eyes and protecting others is explained.

**tāy …** – As yaśōdā, the mother, became angry and lifted a stick, here kriṣṇa’s torment in front of that is explained. Whatever may be the result, he would not give up curd, which sustains him.

**tayir uṇḍu** – bhagavān who is self-satisfied, consumed butter which has the touch of favourable persons (devotees) and became joyful; to let out that joy, he danced with pots; he remains in a form which reveals such complete enjoyment.

**tagai sēr nādan** – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.13 “*trailōkyamapi nātēna yēna syānnātavattaram*” (If śrī rāma becomes the lord, the three worlds also will have the best master), those who are protected will be less and the shadow under sarvēśvaran’s shoulder will be more; such sarvēśvaran is eternally residing in this divyadēśam, unlike avatārams where he left after a stipulated period of time.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.2. Uyyum vagai

*uyyum vagaiyuṇḍu sona seyyil ulagēḻum oḻiyāmai muna nāḷmeyyin aḷavē amudu seyya vala aiyan avan mēvu nagar tānmaiya varivaṇḍu madu uṇḍu kiḷaiyōdu malar kiṇḍi adan mēlnaivaḷam naviṟṟu poḻil nandipura viṇṇagaram naṇṇu manamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

sona seyyil – if we are to do what was told; uyyum vagai – way for uplifting; uṇḍu – is there; ulagu ēḻum – the seven worlds; oḻiyāmai – without missing anything; muna nāḷ – in the past (during deluge); meyyin aḷavē – within the divine form (without showing any increase in size); amudu seyyavala – one who is able to mercifully consume; aiyan – natural relative; avan – that sarvēśvaran; mēvum – eternally residing; nagar tān – the divyadēśam; maiya – in dark complexion; vari – stripes; vaṇḍu – beetles; madu – honey; kiḷaiyōdu – with relatives such as sons, grandsons et al; uṇḍu – drank; malar – flowers; kiṇḍi – sucked; adan mēl – further; naivaḷam – kurinji tune; naviṟṟu – humming; poḻil – having orchards; nandipura viṇṇagaram – having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram; nagar – the divyadēśam; manamē – oh heart!; naṇṇu – try to reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

If we are to do as told, the way for uplifting is there. sarvēśvaran, who is the natural relative for all, was able to mercifully consume the seven worlds without missing anything, in the past (during deluge) and keep them within his divine form, without showing any increase to his form; such sarvēśvaran is eternally residing in the divyadēśam having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram, which is having orchards where beetles with dark complexion and stripes on their body, drank honey from flowers and sucked them along with their relatives such as sons, grandsons et al and further, are humming kurinji tune. Oh heart! Try to reach there.

**uyyum …** – If we try to do as I say, there is hope for uplifting ourselves. There is no need to think “We have no other choice than being finished”. This nandipura viṇṇagaram is the eternal abode of eternal relative, sarvēśvaran, who would consume everything in all the worlds without missing anything during deluge and if the deluge asks “Where is everything?”, he consumes them to keep them in his same divine form where he can say “I don’t know”.

**maiya …** – Having dark complexion and stripes, the beetles, along with their relatives, consumed the honey, and due to over-drinking the honey, being unable to move, remained there and sucked the flowers, and are humming the tune “*naivaḷam*“, in the orchards.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.3. Umbar ulagelu

*umbar ulagēḻu kadal ēḻu malai ēḻum oḻiyāmai muna nāḷ tambon vayiṟāraḷavum uṇḍu avai umiḻnda tadamārvar tagai sēr vambu malarginṟa poḻil paimbon varu tumbi maṇi kangul vayal sūḻ namban uṟaiginṟa nagar nandipura viṇṇagaram naṇṇu manamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

umbar ulagu ēḻum – the seven upper worlds; kadal ēḻum – the seven oceans; malai ēḻum – the seven anchoring mountains; oḻiyāmai – not missing (anyone of these); muna nāḷ – in the past (during deluge); tam – his; pon – best; vayiṟu – divine stomach; āraḷavum – to the brim; uṇḍu – mercifully consumed; avai – those; umiḻnda – let out (during creation); tadam – vast; mārvar – being the one who has divine chest; tagai sēr – having greatness; namban – he, who is trustworthy; uṟaiginṟa nagar – the residence; vambu – flowers; malarginṟa – blossoming; poḻil – in the orchards; pai pon – like beautiful gold; varu – coming; maṇi tumbi – having best dragon flies; kangul – dark; vayal sūḻ – surrounded by farm fields; nandipura viṇṇagaram – having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram; nagar – the divyadēśam; manamē – oh heart!; naṇṇu – try to reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran mercifully consumed the seven upper worlds, seven oceans, seven anchoring mountains in the past (during deluge) to the full extent of his best, divine stomach without missing anyone of those and let them out (during creation); he is having the greatness of being the one with the divine chest and is trustworthy; he is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam which is having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram, which is having orchards where the flowers are blossoming and the beautiful gold like, best dragon flies are coming and is surrounded by dark, farm fields. Oh heart! Try to reach there.

**umbar …** – The seven upper worlds, seven oceans and seven mountains were mercifully consumed to his stomach’s content without missing anyone of those; he then spat those out thinking “They cannot struggle, remaining inside”. He has a divine form manifesting that these acts are done for his own sake. tagai – greatness.

**vambu …** – Orchard having blossoming flowers; dragon-flies are roaming around like a golden cover for the orchard. maṇi – beauty. Since the crops are always dark (being ready for harvest), the farm-field is dark; being surrounded by such field.

**namban uṟaiginṟa nagar** – The eternal abode of sarvēśvaran who is trustworthy in any situation.

## 5.10.4. Piraiyin oli

*piṟaiyin oḷi eyiṟilaga muṟugi edir porudumena vanda asurariṟaigaḷ avai neṟuneṟu ena eṟiya avar vayiṟaḻala ninṟa perumānsiṟai koḷ mayil kuyil payila malargaḷ uga aḷi murala adikoḷ nedumā naṟai sey poḻil maḻai tavaḻum nandipura viṇṇagaram naṇṇu manamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

piṟaiyin – young moon’s; oḷi – having radiance; eyiṟu – teeth; ilaga – as they shine; muṟugi – coming forth; edir – stood in front; porudum – we will fight; ena vanda – came, saying this; asurar – demons’; avai – such; iṟaigaḷ – bodies; neṟu neṟu ena – to crack and fall down; eṟiya – as he collected his fist and punched; avar – those demons; vayiṟu aḻala – (to be frightened) and have their stomach burn; ninṟa – one who stood (in the war); perumān – sarvēśvaran’s; siṟaikoḷ – having best wings; mayil – peacocks; kuyil – cuckoos; payila – living densely; malargaḷ – flowers; uga – as they fall down; aḷi – beetles; murala – as they hum; adi koḷ – having vast roots; nedu – tall; mā – sourced from the mango trees; naṟai sey – having honey; poḻil – in the orchards; maḻai – clouds; tavaḻum – roaming around; nandipura viṇṇagaram – having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram; nagar – the divyadēśam; manamē – oh heart!; naṇṇu – try to reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

As their teeth, having radiance as that of a young moon, shine, the demons came forth and stood in front of sarvēśvaran saying “We will fight”; he gathered his fist and punched them to make their bodies crack and fall down. Such sarvēśvaran is residing in the divyadēśam having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram, which has orchards where peacocks having the best wings and cuckoos are living densely and due to that the flowers fall down and where the beetles are humming after consuming honey sourced from the tall mango trees which are having vast roots and the clouds roam around. Oh heart! Try to reach there.

**piṟai …** – To break the joints of the bodies of the demons who came forth with their teeth shining like a crescent moon saying “We will fight”;

**veṟiya avar** – sarvēśvaran stood there to cause the fire of fear in the hearts of those angry demons to make them drop their weapons as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 59.139 “*yō vajrapātāśani sannipātāt na sukśubhē nāpi cacāla rājā* l *sa rāma bāṇābhihatō bhruśārta*: ***cacāla cāpanca mumōca vīra*****:** ll” (That rāvaṇa, who did not move even when hit by vajram \[indra’s weapon\] or when hit by thunder, without any bewilderment, after being hit by the arrows of that warrior śrī rāma, felt very hurt, staggered and let go of his bow). Alternatively – ***neṟuneṟena vida*** – launching his fist on them to break them down.

**siṟai …** – As the winged peacocks and cuckoos came close, the flowers fell down, as the beetles hum in the orchards, which have mango trees with expansive roots, where the clouds are roaming.

mūḷa – to be covered by smoke; eri – fire; sindhi – let it spread; munivu eydu – became angry; amar seydum – we will fight; ena vanda – thought this way and came; asurar – monsters’; tōḷum – shoulders; avar tāḷum – and their feet; mudiyōdu – with their heads; podiyāga – to become dust; nodiyām aḷavu – in a second; eydān – one who hit; vāḷum – nandaka, the sword; vari – beautiful; villum – śārngam, the bow; vaḷai – having curved mouths; āḻi – sudarśana, the disc; gadai – kaumōdaki, the mace; sangam – pāncajanyam, the conch; ivai – these five weapons; am kai – in his beautiful hands; udaiyān – one who holds; nāḷum – eternally; uṟaiginṟa – residing; nagar – town; nandipura viṇṇagaram – having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram; nagar – the divyadēśam; manamē – oh heart!; naṇṇu – try to reach

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran holds the five weapons viz. 1) nandaka, the sword 2) śārngam, the beautiful bow 3) sudarśana, the disc with curved mouths, 4) kaumōdaki, the mace and 5) pāncajanyam, the conch, in his beautiful hands; he hit the monsters, who let the fire spread and cause the place to be covered with smoke, who were angry and thought “we will fight” and came, to make their shoulders, feet and heads to become dust, in a second; such sarvēśvaran is eternally residing in the town which is a divyadēśam having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram. Oh heart! Try to reach there.

**mūḷa …** – The asuras (monsters) spread the fire to make the place be covered with smoke and came thinking “We will fight”; bhagavān severed their shoulders, feet and heads within a moment by launching his weapons. In this manner, if there are further battles, he is having the five weapons 1) sword which helps in the battle 2) beautiful bow 3) divine chakra which is having curved mouths 4) mace and 5) the divine conch, in his divine hands. Unlike incarnations, where it is said “He is no more present here” (after ascending to paramapadam), he is eternally present in nandipura viṇṇagaram.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.6. Tambiyodu

*tambiyodu tām oruvar tan tuṇaivi kādal tuṇaiyāga muna nāḷvembi eri kānagam ulāvum avar tām inidu mēvu nagar tānkombu kudi koṇḍu kuyil kūva mayil ālum eḻilār puṟavu sērnambi uṟaiginṟa nagar nandipura viṇṇagaram naṇṇu manamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

oruvar – distinguished (very tender) one; tām – him; tambiyodu – with his brother, iḷaiya perumāḷ; kādal – dear to him; than tuṇaivi – sītāp pirātti who will help him; tuṇaiyā – accompanying him; muna nāḷ – in the past (during śrī rāmāvatāram); vembi – being very hot; eri – blowing fire; kānagam – in the forest; ulāvumavar – cakravartit tirumagan who roamed around; inidu – being joyful (with pirātti); mēvu – eternally residing; nagar tān – divyadēśam is; kuyil – cuckoos; kombu – from branches; kudi koṇḍu – jumped; kūva – as they make noise; mayil – peacocks; Alum – as they dance; eḻil sēr – having beauty; puṟavu sēr – having surroundings; nambi – sarvēśvaran who is complete in all auspicious qualities; uṟaiginṟa – eternally residing abode; nandipura viṇṇagaram – having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram; nagar – the divyadēśam; manamē – oh heart!; naṇṇu – try to reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, in the past, during śrī rāmāvatāram, as distinguished cakravartit tirumagan (divine son of cakravati, daśarata), accompanied by his brother iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) and his beloved sītāp pirātti who would help him, roamed around in the forest which was very hot and was blowing fire. Such joyful emperumān who is complete in all auspicious qualities, is eternally residing in the diyadēśam having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram where the cuckoos jumped from the branches making noise to make the peacocks dance in the beautiful surroundings. Oh heart! Try to reach there.

**tambi …** – He who is distinguished for tender nature roamed around in the hot forest where fire was blowing, along with his younger brother.

What is his hold there?

**than tuṇaivi …** – Since he went with sītāp pirātti, he did not feel the heat of the forest. As said in periya tirumadal “*tunnu veyil veṟutta vembaralmēl panjadiyāl*” (With the tender feet on the rocks/stones which were roasted by sun), this is how it felt for her. The rocks will in turn roast the sun (after having been roasted by the sun first); on them, *panjadiyāl* – With the lotus feet which will get burnt even if they stepped on a flower. *mannan irāman pin* – śrīrāma is her water and shade for such hot earth.

**vembi eri kānagam ulāvumavar** – The one who roamed in the forest where the ground keeps itself as firewood and is burning.

The abode where he is residing along with pirātti is,

**kombu …** – The cuckoos jumped from the branches and made noise just like muktātmās will sing sāma gānam, the peacocks danced and in this manner, there are beautiful surroundings in the divyadēśam, nandipura viṇṇagaram.

**nambi uṟaiginṟa nagar** – The abode where bhagavān, who is complete in all auspicious qualities, is residing.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.7. Tandai manamundu

*tandai manamundu tuyar nanda iruḷ vanda viṟal nandan madalaiendai ivan enṟu amarar kanda malar koṇḍu toḻa ninṟa nagar tānmanda muḻavōsai maḻaiyāga eḻu kār mayilgaḷ ādu poḻil sūḻ nandi paṇi seyda nagar nandipura viṇṇagaram naṇṇu manamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tandai – nandagōpa, the father, his; manam – heart; undu – pushing (causing grief); tuyar – sorrow (due to not having children); nanda – to destroy; iruḷ – in the dark (without anyone knowing); vanda – came from (maturā); viṟal – strong; nandan – nandagōpa’s; madalai ivan – kriṣṇa, who is the son; endai – my lord; enṟu – saying this; amarar – dēvatās; kandam – filled with fragrance; malar – flowers (from kalpaka tree); koṇḍu – gathering them and bringing them; toḻa – to approach; ninṟa – mercifully present in the town; muḻavu – musical instruments; mandam – mild; ōsai – sound; maḻaiyāga – considering it to be the sound of a cloud; kār – in the rainy season; eḻu – rising; mayilgaḷ – peacocks; ādu – dancing; poḻil sūḻ – being surrounded by gardens; nandi – a king named nandi; paṇi seyda – served; nagar – will be the town; nandipura viṇṇagaram – having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram; nagar – the divyadēśam; manamē – oh heart!; naṇṇu – try to reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

To have the dēvatās who came saying “To destroy the sorrow which was pushing his father nandagōpa’s heart, this strong kriṣṇa came in the dark from maturā as nandagōpa’s son; such kriṣṇa is our lord” and with flowers which were gathered and brought, approach him, he is mercifully present in the divyadēśam which is having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram; this abode is where the peacocks heard the mild sound of the musical instruments and considering them to the sound a cloud, will rise in the raining season, and dance in the orchards which have surrounded the town; it was served by the king named nandi. Oh heart! Try to reach this abode.

**tandai …** – To destroy the sorrow which was pushing śrī nandagōpa’s heart, kriṣṇa, the very strong son of śrī nandagōpa, came in the dark to conceal himself from the eyes of evil entities. nanjīyar asked bhattar “kriṣṇa was born in maturā; again returned to maturā and grew up there \[after 10 years in gōkulam\]; due to fear for kamsa, kriṣṇa stayed there for a short period; in such case, unlike ignorant people, we who have knowledge also speak in this manner \[that, kriṣṇa was in covherd clan, yaśōdā is his mother, nandagōpa is his father, etc\]. How does it make sense?” For that bhattar replied “Not just us, even great jñānis (most knowledgeable ones), have spoken about this even before his birth in covherd clan, as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.20.41 ‘*ayam sa katyatē prājñai:*‘ (Spoken by great elders); why should you analyse this if mother yaśōdā’s bosoms give milk and kriṣṇa accepts the same?” The abode where dēvatās stood saying “He is our lord” and approached and surrendered to him.

**manda …** – Considering the mild music of instruments to be the cloud’s noise, peacocks are dancing in the orchards which surround the divyadēśam.

**nandi paṇi seyda nagar** – The abode where anya paran (one who has many engagements) served bhagavān after becoming ananyapara (exclusively devoted to bhagavān). That is, there was a king named nandi, who became favourable towards bhagavān.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.8. Ennil ninaiveydi

*eṇṇil ninaiveydi ini illai iṟai enṟu muniyāḷar tiruvārpaṇṇil mali gīdamodu pādi avar ādalodu kūda eḻilārmaṇṇil idu pōla nagar illai ena vānavargaḷ tām malargaḷ tūynaṇṇi uṟaiginṟa nagar nandipura viṇṇagaram naṇṇu manamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

eṇṇil – If analysed; ninaivu eydu – target of dyānam; iṟai – lord; ini – other than him; ilai – none is present; enṟu – confirmed in this manner; muniyāḷar – sanaka et al who have ultimate penance; tiru Ar – abundantly beautiful; paṇṇil – in music; mali – great; gīdamodu – with song; pādi – reciting words of praise (and danced); avar – their; ādalodu kūda – along with the dance; vānavargaḷ – dēvatās; tām – them; eḻil Ar – best; maṇṇil – in the bhūlōkam; idu pōla – matching this; nagar – divyadēśam; illai ena – saying that it is not there (praising in this manner); malargaḷ tūy – proffering flowers; naṇṇi – approached; uṟaiginṟa nagar – the town where they are residing; nandipura viṇṇagaram – having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram; nagar – the divyadēśam; manamē – oh heart!; naṇṇu – try to reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sanaka et al who have ultimate penance, confirmed that there is none other than bhagavān who can be the target of dyānam, if analysed; they sang great songs with abundantly beautiful music, reciting words of praise (and danced); dēvatās danced along with them and said “There is no abode which is present, matching this divyadēśam, in the best bhulōkam”; they approached bhagavān in the town where they are residing which is having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram and proffered flowers. Oh heart! Try to reach there.

**eṇṇil …** – Unlike being covered with rajō guṇam (passion) and tamō guṇam (ignorance), falling at the feet of some entities without analysing, if we analysed – there is none other than śrīman nārāyaṇa who is our target of worship – saying this, sanaka et al, sang great songs with abundantly beautiful music.

Along with their dance,

**eḻilār …** – In general it is said that “On the earth, bhārata varśam is the ideal place to remain; since svargam is a place where one will be pushed down once their puṇyam (virtues) are exhausted like water fetched from a pot; is svargam a place to live? There is no other place than bhārata varśam where one can perform sādanānuśtānam (different processes) to attain any benefit”; similarly, there is no abode which matches this nandipura viṇṇagaram which is the best abode on the earth. Saying this dēvatās approached bhagavān proffering flowers etc and reside here eternally.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.9. Vangamali

*vangamali pauvam adu māmugadin ucci puga mikka perunīrangam aḻiyār avanadu āṇai talai sūdum adiyār aṟidiyēl pongu punal undu maṇi kangul iruḷ sīṟum oḷi engum uḷadāl nangaḷ perumān uṟaiyum nandipura viṇṇagaram naṇṇu manamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vangam – with boats; mali – filled; adu – that (which is protection for the earth); pauvam – the ocean; mā – tall; mugadin – the oval shaped universe’s wall’s; ucci – up to the top; puga – to reach; mikka – rising; peru nīr – in the great waters (during deluge); avanadu – that sarvēśvaran’s; āṇai – order; talai sūdum – those who hold on their heads; adiyār – servitors; angam aḻiyār – will not get their bodies destroyed; manamē – oh heart!; aṟidiyēl – if you know (this); pongu – rising; punal – water; undu – pushing; maṇi – from the precious gems; kangul – occurs in the night; iruḷ – darkness; sīṟum – being angry (eliminating); oḷi – radiance; engum – everywhere; uḷadu – spread out; nangaḷ – our; perumān – lord; uṟaiyum – eternally residing; nandipura viṇṇagaram – having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram; nagar – the divyadēśam; manamē – oh heart!; naṇṇu – try to reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The causal ocean which is filled with boats rose to reach the top of the wall of the oval shaped universe; even in that great water, those servitors who hold the orders of sarvēśvaran on their heads, will not have their bodies destroyed. Oh heart! Our lord is eternally residing in the divyadēśam having the divine name, nandipura viṇṇagaram, where the rising water is pushing the precious gems which eliminate the darkness which occurs in the night and radiance is spread out everywhere. Oh heart! If you know this, try to reach there.

**vangam …** – The ocean which is filled with boats, just as those who are \[appointed as\] the protectors of the town will engage in stealing \[from the residents of the town\], though placed as the protective layer around the earth, when it became filled with abundant water, would reach the top of the wall of the oval shaped universe as if pushing it. In that deluge, those servitors \[of emperumān\] who hold his orders on their heads will not experience the results of the karma which lead to suffering due to the dangers of deluge. This is as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 14.2](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/14-2/) “… *sargē’pi nōpajāyantē praḷayē na vyatanti ca*” (Those who attain this knowledge (which is to be explained), will have attained equality with me, and are neither created here nor destroyed).

**aṟidiyēl** – If it is understood in the mind.

**pongu …** – The precious gems pushed out by the overflowing water will drive out the darkness which is created in the night and that radiance is spread out everywhere.

**nangaḷ perumān uṟaiyum** – His para state (in paramapadam) is for nityasūris; his vyūha state (in kśīrābdi) is to eliminate the insults experienced by brahmā, rudra et al; vibhava avatārams are for the very fortunate ones like śrī vasudēvar, \[daśarata\] cakravarti et al; ugandaruḷina nilangaḷ (divyadēśams which are mercifully occupied by bhagavān with eagerness) is for those who are like us, who are in later times. Even nityasūris, when they come here, should come with some shortcomings. To the coultry, which is kept for blind people, people with proper vision should come there covering their eyes.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.10. Narai sey

*naṟai sey poḻil maḻai tavaḻum nandipura viṇṇagaram naṇṇi uṟaiyumuṟai koḷ pugar āḻi suri sangam avai angai udaiyānai oḷi sērkaṟai vaḷarum vēl valla kaliyan oli mālai ivai aindum aindummuṟaiyil ivai payila vala adiyavargaḷ koduvinaigaḷ muḻudagalumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

naṟai sey – having honey; poḻil – in the orchards; maḻai – clouds; tavaḻum – roaming around; nandipura viṇṇagaram – the divyadēśam named nandipura viṇṇagaram; naṇṇi – approached; uṟaiyum – one who is eternally residing; uṟaikoḷ – placed in the pouch; pugar – having radiance; āḻi – divine chakra; suri – curved; sangam – divine conch; avai – those divine weapons; am kai – in the beautiful divine hands; udaiyānai – on sarvēśvaran who is having; oḷi sēr – radiant; kaṟai vaḷarum – having abundance of blood stains; vēl – spear; valla – one who can rule over; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; oli – mercifully spoke; ivai – these distinguished; mālai – collection of words in the form of a garland; aindum aindum – ten pāsurams; muṟaiyil – in the proper manner (considering them to be the goal); payilavala – those who can learn/recite; adiyavargaḷ – servitors’; kodu – cruel; vinaigaḷ – sins; muḻudu – completely; agalum – will go away

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is having the divine weapons such as the radiantly divine chakra in its pouch and the curved divine conch, in his beautiful divine hands and has approached and is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named nandipura viṇṇagaram which is having honey in the orchards where clouds are roaming around; tirumangai āḻvār who can rule over the radiant spear which is having abundance of blood stains, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams which are a distinguished collection of words in the form of a garland; the cruel sins of those servitors who can learn/recite these pāsurams in the proper manner, will go away completely.

**naṟai sey …** – Reaching śrī nandipura viṇṇagaram, where the orchards are filled with honey and clouds are roaming around, sarvēśvaran is eternally residing there too. After tirumangai āḻvār took the spear to vanquish enemies, bhagavān placed his divine chakra in a pouch (since he need not do anything now). āḻvār praised the one who is having in his beautiful divine hands, the divine weapons starting with the divine chakra which is pouched and which is radiant.

**oḷi sēr kaṟai vaḷarum …** – There is no scope for tirumangai āḻvār’s spear to remain in the pouch; there would be no time to remove the blood stain after killing the enemies; these ten pāsurams.

**muṟaiyil ivai payila vala** – Since āḻvār said “*naṇṇu manamē*” (Oh heart! Try to reach) this divyadēśam to be the goal, one should learn/recite these pāsurams with the consideration that this abode is our objective. For those servitors who do that, the cruel sins which cannot be exhausted by any other means than experiencing the results, will be eliminated along with the traces.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## Sixth Centum

## 6.1 Annal seydu

## 6.1.2. Annal seydu

*aṇṇal seydu alai kadal kadaindu adanuḷkaṇṇudal nanjuṇṇak kaṇḍavanē!viṇṇavar amuduṇa amudil varumpeṇṇamudu uṇḍa emperumānē!āṇḍāy! unaik kāṇbadōr aruḷ enakku aruḷudiyēlvēṇḍēn manai vāḻkkaiyai viṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇṇal seydu – showing magnanimity (towards dēvatās); alai kadal – ocean where waves were agitating; kadaindu – churned; adanuḷ – came out of that (at that time); nanju – poison; nudal kaṇ – rudra who has an eye on the forehead; uṇṇa – to swallow; kaṇḍavanē – one who saw (vowed); viṇṇavar – dēvatās; amudu uṇa – as they drink the nectar; amudil – from that nectar; varum – coming out (as the essence); amudu – very enjoyable; peṇ – periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi); uṇḍa – (got and) enjoyed; emperumānē – Oh our benefactor!; āṇḍāy – Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)!; viṇṇagar – in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar; mēyavanē – Oh one who is residing permanently!; unnai – you; kānbadu – to have me worship you; ōr aruḷ – unconditional grace; enakku – on me; aruḷudiyēl – if you can give (you should do); manai vāḻkkaiyai – presence in this samsāram; vēṇḍēn – (I) don’t desire

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is repeating the last 2 lines of the first pāsuram, in every pāsuram of this padigam, to ensure that bhagavān’s divine heart understands that āḻvār’s taste is very fixated.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh our benefactor who showed magnanimity towards dēvatās, churned the ocean where the waves were agitating, saw rudra swallow the poison which came out of the ocean, and as the dēvatās were drinking the nectar, you enjoyed periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi) who came out of that nectar! Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)! Oh one who is residing permanently in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! If you can bestow the unconditional grace to have me worship you, please do so. I don’t desire to be present in this samsāram.

**aṇṇal …** – Showing magnanimity; showing ownership; churned the greatly agitated ocean.

**adanuḷ – nanjai – kaṇṇudal – uṇṇak kaṇḍavanē** – Oh one who ensured that the dēvatās did not consume the poison which came out of that ocean and got killed by that!

**viṇṇavar …** – As the dēvatās consumed the nectar and got uplifted, you attained periya pirāttiyār who made that nectar to be like pulp, and in that manner you helped your devotees! īsn’t whatever favour is done towards the mother (śrī mahālakśmi), a favour for the children \[devotees\] too?

**āṇḍāy …** – If you are going to bless me by granting me the sight of your togetherness with her, I will not desire for this life in samsāra which was nurtured by the dēvatās through you.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
