## 6.1.3. Kulal nira

*kuḻal niṟa vaṇṇa! nin kūṟu koṇḍataḻal niṟa vaṇṇan naṇṇār nagaramviḻa nani malai silai vaḷaivu seyduangu aḻal niṟa ambaduvānavanē!āṇḍāy! unaik kāṇbadōr aruḷ enakku aruḷudiyēlvēṇḍēn manai vāḻkkaiyai viṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuḻal niṟa – like the (dark) complexion of his divine hair; vaṇṇa – oh one who is having bodily complexion!; nin – on your divine form; kūṟu koṇḍa – took a portion and kept as his residence; taḻal niṟam – by rudra whose complexion is like the complexion of the fire; naṇṇār – asuras who are enemies, their; nagaram – tripura (three towns); viḻa – to be destroyed; nani – big; malai – like a mountain; silai – bow; vaḷaivu seydu – launched; angu – (being launched) in that bow; aḻal niṟam – in the form of fire; adu – very cruel in that manner; ambu ānavanē – one who entered in the arrow and stood there!; āṇḍāy – Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)!; viṇṇagar – in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar; mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing!; unnai – you; kānbadu – to have me worship you; ōr aruḷ – unconditional grace; enakku – on me; aruḷudiyēl – if you can give (you should do); manai vāḻkkaiyai – presence in this samsāram; vēṇḍēn – (I) don’t desire

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is having bodily complexion like the (dark) complexion of his divine hair! Oh you from whom rudra took a portion of your divine form and kept as his residence, and who \[referring to emperumān\] entered in the very cruel arrow which is in the form of fire and was launched by rudra whose complexion is like the complexion of the fire, to destroy the tripura (three towns), launched the big mountain like bow. Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)! Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! If you can bestow the unconditional grace to have me worship you, please do so. I don’t desire to be present in this samsāram.

**kuḻal niṟa vaṇṇa …** – Oh one who is having the divine complexion of your divine hair on your divine body! As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.8.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-8-1-eralum-iraiyonum/) “*kūṟāḷum*” (individually, enjoy and consider to be their own abodes) – \[rudra who is\] having a portion in your divine form, having fire’s complexion. sarvēśvaran’s divine form will be cool for our eyes; rudra’s form will be like blazing fire making it invisible to our eyes. To have the three towns which are the capital of asuras destroyed, rudra launched the mēru mountain like big bow, as said in mahābhāratam karṇa parvam “*viṣṇurātmā bhagavatō bhavasya amitatējasa:* ***tasmāt*** *danurjyā samsparśam saviśēhē mahēśvara:*” (The omnipresent viṣṇu is the antaryāmi for Siva who is infinitely valorous and vorśippable; due to this fact, Siva was able to launch the arrow on the bow during the destruction of the three towns), bhagavān entered the arrow and remained there as the power. What is the reason for this leelā? It is said in that ślōkam “*viṣṇurātmā*” – because bhagavān is the antaryāmi, he helps all, including dēvatās.

**angu aḻal niṟa ambadu** – Oh one who entered as the sharpness of the arrow, destroyed the enemy and made sure that rudra got the honours as in “rudra performed this victorious act”!

**āṇḍāy …** – In my case, you don’t need to make me announce my greatness saying “I have performed this act”.

**vēṇḍēn …** – You just need to eliminate the hurdles for my true nature and bestow the result matching my true nature.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.4. Nilavodu veyil

*nilavodu veyil nilaviru sudarumulagamum uyirgaḷum uṇḍu oru kālkalai taru kuḻaviyin uru vinaiyāyalaikadal ālilai vaḷarndavanē!āṇḍāy! unaik kāṇbadōr aruḷ enakku aruḷudiyēlvēṇḍēn manai vāḻkkaiyai viṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nilavodu – with coolness; veyilodu – with heat; nilavu – roaming; iru sudarum – moon and sun which are two radiant entities; ulagamum – worlds; uyirgaḷum – the creatures (which are living there); oru kāl – at one time (during deluge); uṇḍu – swallowed (and kept in his stomach); kalai taru – very small; kuḻaviyin – child’s; uruvinaiyāy – having the form; alai – agitated waves; kadal – in the ocean; Al ilai – in a banyan leaf; vaḷarndavanē – Oh one who is reclining!; āṇḍāy – Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)!; viṇṇagar – in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar; mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing!; unnai – you; kānbadu – to have me worship you; ōr aruḷ – unconditional grace; enakku – on me; aruḷudiyēl – if you can give (you should do); manai vāḻkkaiyai – presence in this samsāram; vēṇḍēn – (I) don’t desire

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who swallowed the moon and sun which are two radiant entities which are roaming with coolness and heat, the worlds and the residents of those worlds during deluge and assumed a very small child’s form and reclined on a banyan leaf in the ocean which is having agitated waves! Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)! Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! If you can bestow the unconditional grace to have me worship you, please do so. I don’t desire to be present in this samsāram.

**nilavodu …** – Along with coolness and heat. Roaming. Being the controller of moon and sun. Alternative explanation – moon and sun which are having coolness and heat respectively. Worlds and the creatures living in them. Keeping all of them in his stomach once during deluge, assuming a child with a very small form, Oh one who is having *agatita gatanā sāmartyam* (ablitiy to unite contradictory objects) and mercifully reclining on a newly sprouted banyan leaf on the agitated ocean!

**āṇḍāy …** – You need not unite contradictory aspects in me. You just need to shower your mercy to make me see you.

**vēṇḍēn …** – There is no shortcoming in what I have to do.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.5. Parelu

*pāreḻu kadaleḻu malaiyeḻumāysīrkeḻum ivvulagēḻum ellāmārkeḻu vayiṟṟinil adakki ninṟu anguōreḻuttu ōruruvānavanē!āṇḍāy! unaik kāṇbadōr aruḷ enakku aruḷudiyēlvēṇḍēn manai vāḻkkaiyai viṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pār eḻum – the earth which is made of seven islands; kadal eḻum – the seven oceans; malai eḻum – the seven anchoring mountains; āy – being the controller of; sīr keḻum – very beautiful; ivvulagu ēḻum – these seven worlds; ellām – (and) all others; Ar keḻu – very beautiful; vaiyṟṟinil – in his divine stomach; adakki – (placed) and subdued; angu ninṟu – remaining on the banyan leaf; ōr – distinguished among the words; eḻuttu – for akāra (the letter/syllable “a”); ōr uru ānavanē – Oh one who remains the prime meaning!; āṇḍāy – Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)!; viṇṇagar – in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar; mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing!; unnai – you; kānbadu – to have me worship you; ōr aruḷ – unconditional grace; enakku – on me; aruḷudiyēl – if you can give (you should do); manai vāḻkkaiyai – presence in this samsāram; vēṇḍēn – (I) don’t desire

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being the controller of the earth which is made of seven islands, the seven oceans, the seven anchoring mountains, oh one who remains the prime meaning for the akāra which is distinguished among the words, who subdued the very beautiful seven worlds and everything else in your very beautiful stomach and remained on the banyan leaf! Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)! Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! If you can bestow the unconditional grace to have me worship you, please do so. I don’t desire to be present in this samsāram.

**pāreḻu …** – Being the controller of seven \[layered\] earth, seven oceans and seven mountains; you subdued these beautiful seven worlds and everything else in your beautiful stomach. With this – bhagavān being the ādāram (substratum) of everything which is indicated by words, is shown.

**ōr eḻuttu ōr uru ānavanē** – Oh one who is indicated by the akāra which is the foremost of the collection of words!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.6. Karkelu

*kārkeḻu kadalgaḷum malaigaḷumāyērkeḻum ulagamumāgi mudalārgaḷum aṟivaru nilaiyinaiyāyccīrkeḻu nānmaṟai ānavanē!āṇḍāy! unaik kāṇbadōr aruḷ enakku aruḷudiyēlvēṇḍēn manai vāḻkkaiyai viṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kār keḻu – filled with clouds; kadalgaḷum – for oceans; malaigaḷum – for mountains; āy – being the ādāram (abode); ēr keḻum – organised; ulagamum – for the worlds; āgi – being the controller; mudalārgaḷum – brahmā et al who are primary; aṟivarum – unable to be known; nilaiyinaiyāy – having qualities; sīr keḻu – having the beauty of authenticity; nāl maṟai – for four vēdams; ānavanē – Oh one who is the object!; āṇḍāy – Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)!; viṇṇagar – in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar; mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing!; unnai – you; kāṇbadu – to have me worship you; ōr aruḷ – unconditional grace; enakku – on me; aruḷudiyēl – if you can give (you should do); manai vāḻkkaiyai – presence in this samsāram; vēṇḍēn – (I) don’t desire

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is the abode for cloud-filled oceans and mountains and is the controller of organised worlds and who is having the qualities to be unable to be known by the primary personalities like brahmā et al and who is the object of four vēdams which are having the beauty of authenticity! Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)! Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! If you can bestow the unconditional grace to have me worship you, please do so. I don’t desire to be present in this samsāram.

**kār …** – Oceans which are having clouds atop, the anchoring mountains. Why should these be identified individually? Being the worlds which are organised. With this, āḻvār is indicating bhagavān’s position as the abode of the world and the antaryāmi of the world \[world as his body\].

**mudalārgaḷum aṟivaru nilaiyinaiyāy** – Even by those primary personalities such as the four-headed brahmā who is the lord of the fourteen layered universe, bhagavān is having qualities which are unpredictable to say “this much”. Oh one who is revealed in the four vēdams which speak the truth as it is, to be trustworthy.

**āṇḍāy …** – To not spoil your reputation of being the abode of the world and greater than all, if you show your mercy upon me to visualise your special form, I also truly hate this samsāram.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.7. Urukkuru

*urukkuṟu naṟuney koṇḍu āraḻalilirukkuṟum andaṇar sandiyin vāyperukkamodu amarargaḷ amara nalgumirukkinil innisai ānavanē!āṇḍāy! unaik kāṇbadōr aruḷ enakku aruḷudiyēlvēṇḍēn manai vāḻkkaiyai viṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

amarargaḷ – dēvatās; perukkamodu – with wealth; amara – to have the materials for the yāgam (sacrifice) remain well (for them); urukku uṟu – melted; naṟu ney koṇḍu – with new ghee; Ar aḻalil – in the beautiful fire; sandiyin vāy – in the sandyā (dawn / dusk) times; nalgum – offering (the havis); irukku uṟum – engaged in vēda adyayanam; andaṇar – brāhmaṇas’ (wealth); irukkinil – in the vēdam; in – sweet; isai – praṇavam in the form of svaram (meter); ānavanē – Oh one who is the meaning!; āṇḍāy – Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)!; viṇṇagar – in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar; mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing!; unnai – you; kānbadu – to have me worship you; ōr aruḷ – unconditional grace; enakku – on me; aruḷudiyēl – if you can give (you should do); manai vāḻkkaiyai – presence in this samsāram; vēṇḍēn – (I) don’t desire

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

To have the materials for the yāgam remain well with the wealth of dēvatās, the brāhmaṇas, who are practitioners of vēdam during the sandyā times, offered freshly melted ghee in the beautiful fire; oh one, who is the meaning of praṇavam which is in the form of sweet svaram in the vēdam of such brāhmaṇas! Oh one, who ruled me (even in the past)! Oh one, who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! If you can bestow the unconditional grace to have me worship you, please do so. I don’t desire to be present in this samsāram.

**urukkuṟu …** – Using melted, fresh ghee, in the fire, brāhmaṇas who are engaged in vēda adyayanam, during every sandyā time.

**perukkam …** – As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 3.11](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/3-11/) “*parasparam bhāvayanta: śrēya: param avāpsyata \|\|*” (By being helpful in this manner to each other, \[you\] will attain the great benefit of liberation), to make the dēvatās provide abundance of tools for the yāgam along with wealth, brāhmaṇas are offering the havis (offering); the vēdams of such brāhmaṇas have sweet meter, that is praṇavam in the form of svaram. Oh one who is revealed by such praṇavam!

As said in “*sāhiśrīramrutāsadām*” – brāhmaṇas are said to be those who have the wealth of vēdam. praṇavam is said as svaram. As said in taittirīya upaniśat nārāyaṇavalli 10 “***yat vēdādau svara*****:** ***prōkta*****:** *vēdāntē ca pratiśtita*: l *tasya prakruti leenasya ya*: *para*: *sa mahēsvara*: ll” (sarvēśvaran (lord of all) is the meaning of akāram (the syllable *‘a’* which is the causative factor for *ōnkāram*, which is recited at the beginning and end of vēdam). Is praṇavam speaking about parasvarūpam (bhagavān’s true nature)? ōr is it also speaking about ātma svarūpam (jīvātmā’s true nature)? It is speaking about both as said in taittirīya upaniśat nārāyaṇavalli 5-1 “*ōmityātmānam yunjīta*” (one should meditate on ātmā, by reciting the praṇava mantram, *Om*) as well as in the vēdic saying “*ōnkārō bhagavān viṣṇu*” (viṣṇu is identified by the mantram *Om*).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.8. Kadal seydu

*kādal seydu iḷaiyavar kalavi tarumvēdanai vinaiyadu veruvudalāmādalin unadadi aṇuguvan nānpōdalar nedu mudip puṇṇiyanē!āṇḍāy! unaik kāṇbadōr aruḷ enakku aruḷudiyēlvēṇḍēn manai vāḻkkaiyai viṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pōdu alar – decorated with fresh flower garlands; nedu mudi – one who is having tall divine crown; puṇṇiyanē – Oh one who is pure!; iḷaiyavar – young girls; kādal seydu – showing love; tarum – giving; vēdanai – in the form of sorrow; kalavi – for the union; adu – such; vinai – karma (if we start thinking); veruvudal Am – causing fear (in me); ādalil – Hence (to have it eliminated); unadu adi – your divine feet; nān – I; aṇuguvan – approach and surrender unto; āṇḍāy – Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)!; viṇṇagar – in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar; mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing!; unnai – you; kāṇbadu – to have me worship you; ōr aruḷ – unconditional grace; enakku – on me; aruḷudiyēl – if you can give (you should do); manai vāḻkkaiyai – presence in this samsāram; vēṇḍēn – (I) don’t desire

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is having tall divine crown which is decorated with fresh flower garlands and who is pure! The karma which leads to young girls showing love and giving union which is in the form of sorrow is causing fear in me. Hence I approach and surrender unto your divine feet. Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)! Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! If you can bestow the unconditional grace to have me worship you, please do so. I don’t desire to be present in this samsāram.

**kādal …** – Young girls engage in love – the women having attachment, give union which is filled with sorrow. As I meditate upon the karma which leads to that, I become fearful; hence, I surrender unto your divine feet which lets us escape such dangers. īsn’t that union filled with sorrow? If one sets out to enjoy such love, a) it does not let him become satisfied one day, b) it makes one lose one’s masculinity, c) it makes one hang his head in shame in front of others, d) eventually it will lead to narakam (hell). When I think about the karma which is the cause for such union which causes svarūpa hāni (damage to true nature), it makes me fearful; hence, I will approach and surrennder unto the divine feet which will let me step on the heads of yama et al, even after roaming around anywhere.

**pōdalar nedumudip puṇṇiyanē** – Oh one who is having the purity of eliminating my desire towards other matters by showing your presence with the garland, decorated around your divine crown! This does not occur to people of this world \[generally\]; only āḻvār has had this occur to him.

**āṇḍāy …** – If you, who eliminated my taste towards matters other than you, can shower your mercy upon me to see you with my eyes, I will have distaste towards these.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.9. Sadalum

*sādalum piṟattalum enṟu ivaṟṟaikādal seyyādu una kaḻal adaindēnōdal sey nānmaṟaiyāgi umbarādal sey mūvuruvānavanē!āṇḍāy! unaik kāṇbadōr aruḷ enakku aruḷudiyēlvēṇḍēn manai vāḻkkaiyai viṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōdal sey – learnt/practised; nāl maṟaiyāgi – being the controller of four vēdams; umbarādal – primary among the dēvatās; sey – created; mūvuru ānavanē – Oh one who is having brahmā, rudra and indra as śarīram!; sādalum – death; piṟattalum – birth; enṟu – analysing these sorrowful sequences; ivaṟṟai – these birth etc; kādal seyyādu – having no taste; una kaḻal – your highness’ divine feet; adaindēn – surrendered; āṇḍāy – Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)!; viṇṇagar – in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar; mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing!; unnai – you; kāṇbadu – to have me worship you; ōr aruḷ – unconditional grace; enakku – on me; aruḷudiyēl – if you can give (you should do); manai vāḻkkaiyai – presence in this samsāram; vēṇḍēn – (I) don’t desire

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is the controller of four vēdams which are learnt/recited and who has created brahmā, rudra and indra who are primary amongst dēvatās as your śarīram! Having analysed the sorrowful sequences of death, birth etc and having no taste in them, I have surrendered unto your highness’ divine feet. Oh one who ruled me (even in the past)! Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! If you can bestow the unconditional grace to have me worship you, please do so. I don’t desire to be present in this samsāram.

**sādal …** – Sufferings during death, sufferings acquired while experiencing punishments in hell, the sufferings acquired while being in the womb as explained in pancāgni vidyā – thinking about these, instead of desiring for birth etc, I have surrendered unto your highness’ divine feet which will eliminate these. When asked “Are there takers for these sufferings?”, yes. While śāstrams declare “One should eliminate the undesirable birth etc by surrendering unto bhagavān”, since many are not following that, those are considered to be supporting such sufferings in the worldly life.

**ōdal …** – Since vēdam is always learnt and recited, you are having faultless vēdams as your wealth and oh one who is having brahmā, rudra and indra who are primary among dēvatās and are well qualified, as your servitors through śarīra-ātma bhāvam \[bhagavān is ātmā and the dēvatās are his śarīram\].

**āṇḍāy …** – You don’t need to give me such qualification and tie my feet.

**vēṇḍēn …** – I have no taste in their powers.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.10. Pumaru

*pūmaru poḻil aṇi viṇṇagar mēlkāmaru sīrk kali kanṟi sonnapāmaru tamiḻ ivai pāda vallārvāmanan adi iṇai maruvuvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pū maru – Filled with flowers (always blossoming); poḻil – orchards; aṇi – having as decoration; viṇṇagar mēl – on the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar; kāmaru – desirable; sīr – having śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī (wealth of kainkaryam); kalikanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoken; pā maru – filled with beautiful pāsurams; tamiḻ ivai – these ten pāsurams in the drāvida (tamiḻ) form; pāda vallār – those who can learn/recite; vāmanan – sarvēśvaran who incarnated as vāmana, his; iṇai adi – divine feet which match each other; maruvuvar – will reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār who is having desirable śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams in the drāvida form (tamiḻ language) on the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar which is having orchards which are filled with blossomed flowers, as decoration; those who can learn/recite these pāsurams will reach the divine feet of sarvēśvaran, who incarnated as vāmana, which match each other.

**pū maru …** – Spoken on tiruviṇṇagar which has orchards where flowers continuously blossom, as decoration. On tiruviṇṇagar which has eternal spring season.

**kāmaru** … – Desirable – āḻvār who is having vaiṣṇavaśrī (divine wealth of kainkaryam) which is desirable by all, composed. Those who can learn and recite these pāsurams which have good meter.

**vāmanan adi …** – They will become free from what is declared by āḻvār as “*vēṇḍēn*” (I don’t want) and will get what is declared by āḻvār as “*aruḷudiyēl*” (If you mercifully grant).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2 Porutten

## 6.2.1. Porutten

*poṟuttēn punsol nenjil poruḷ inbam ena iraṇḍumiṟuttēn aim pulangatkadanāyina vāyilottiaṟuttēn ārvac ceṟṟam avai tammai manattagaṟṟiveṟuttēn ninnadaindēn tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pun sol – harsh words (spoken by others); nenjil – in my heart; poṟuttēn – I tolerated!; aim pulangaḷ – for the five sense organs; kadan āyina – apt and ordained like debt; poruḷ – wealth; inbam – lust; ena iraṇḍum – these two; iṟuttēn – gave; ārvam – love (towards favourable persons); seṟṟam – hate (towards unfavourable persons); avai tannai – these; vāyil otti – vowed; aṟuttēn – showed; manattu – in the heart (such love and hate); agaṟṟi – made to go away (expanded); veṟuttēn – (subsequently) despised; tiruviṇṇagar – in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar; mēyavanē – Oh sarvēśvara who is eternally residing!; nin adaindēn – I attained you as my refuge

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I tolerated in my heart, the harsh words spoken by others. I gave wealth and lust to five sense organs, as if it is apt and I am in debt towards them; I showed love and hate; I despised them to go away from my heart. Oh sarvēśvara who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! I attained you as my refuge.

**poṟuttēn …** – If one considers samsāris (worldly people) as relatives, even if they are enemies, they remain like close friends, accept one’s favours, and speak as if one did not serve them; I tolerated their harsh words thinking “Did they speak to anyone else like this? āren’t they saying these words to us because of our very close friendship?”; alternative explanation – with the words which are meant to glorify sarvēśvaran who is the abode of all auspicious qualities and having lotus-eyes, I held lowly words in my heart to glorify a lowly person who is as good as a straw as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.9.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-9-7-serum-kodai/) “*pāril ōr paṟṟaiyai*” (an entity which is as useless as a blade of grass, on earth), as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-9-3-iniyirundhu-ennuyir/) “*pani irum kuḻalgaḷ*” (Cool, expansive hair) and [nācciyār tirumoḻi 9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/09/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-9-1/) “*sundarat tōḷ*” (Beautiful shoulders). Lowly nature of the word will be based on the matter which is being spoken about.

**poruḷ …** – If we consider some people as relatives, we need wealth to help them; praising some one is to earn wealth; thus, I gave the wealth and lust which are the expected result of praising others etc, to the sense organs, being conquered by them, as if I have to fulfil my debt to them. As I tried to earn wealth, I vowed that I will be friendly towards those who help in that and nurture them and fight and finish those who hinder that, and executed that vow. I gave both wealth and joy.

**avai tannai manattagaṟṟi** – Trying to eliminate these aspects which I was used to for a long time, since that cannot be done by me, I became upset and surrendered unto your divine feet; alternative explanation – while one can vow to do this, but cannot implement these; but due to taste, the craving will be in the heart; expanding them in the heart and accumulating such desires. Here avaitannai – indicates *rāga* (love) and *dvēśa* (hate).

**veṟuttēn** … – Those love and hate will eventually lead to sorrow and bewilderment; hence, I surrendered unto your highness’ divine feet.

**tiruviṇṇagar …** – The actions which are performed by him now will lead to disaster eventually. At that time as if those who are saying “*sukkidat tittuṇḍō*” \[This is explained in arumpadam. A vaiśya \[a miser, probably\] was crossing a river by feet. A boatman came by and asked for money to help him cross the river. The vaiśya told “I am crossing the river with my feet. Why should I give you money?” After some time, while returning, suddenly he got caught in neck-deep water, and called out for the boatman saying “I will give you money. Are there any shallow rocks?” This indicates the approach of addressing dangers when they come our way, instead of pre-planning\], he will \[ātmā\] analyse “Who will protect us?”. At that time, bhagavān thinks that he should not remain far away, and came to tiruviṇṇagar and remained there; when I started engaging in contrary activities, he remained in tiruviṇṇagar. In this manner, to be said by āḻvār as in “I am surrendering unto you”, bhagavān came and stood here.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.2. Maranden

*maṟandēn unnai munnam maṟanda madiyil manattāliṟandēn ettanaiyum adanāl idumbaik kuḻiyilpiṟandē eyttu oḻindēn perumān! tirumārbā!siṟandēn ninnadikkē tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

unnai – you who have to be remembered at all times; munnam – since time immemorial; maṟandēn – did not think (further); maṟanda – that I did not think about you; madi il – not having knowledge (atonement); manattāl – being with the mind; ettanaiyum – very much (even more than acit); iṟandēn – went away (became very lowly); adanāl – hence; idumbai – in the form of sorrow; kuḻiyil – in the womb; piṟandē – continuously having birth (and death); eyttu – becoming weak (lacking strength); oḻindēn – I withdrew from engaging in self-effort; perumānē – Oh lord!; tirumārbā – Oh one who is having pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi) who is the puruśakāra bhūtā, on your divine chest!; nin adikkē – for your divine feet; siṟandēn – I became qualified; tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I did not think about you, who have to be remembered at all times, since time immemorial and further I am with the mind which did not even have the knowledge that I did not think about you, and because of this I went away very much; hence, having continuous birth in the womb which is in the form of sorrow, becoming weak, I withdrew from engaging in self-effort. Oh lord! Oh one who is having pirātti who is the puruśakāra bhūtā, on your divine chest! I became qualified to exist for your divine feet. Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!

Did you only perform so many faulty activities as mentioned in previous pāsuram?

**maṟandēn unnai munnam** … – I did not support you somewhere in the corner of my mind, even as much as I supported such wealth and lust.

When asked “If he did like that then, has he atoned for that now?” āḻvār says

**maṟandēn** **unnai munnam** – The matter which is to be meditated upon at all times, I forgot that alone. While explaining this in madurai, oppilāda perumāḷ (a śrīvaiṣṇava) said “I forgot the aspect which is said as ‘*dyēyō nārāyaṇas sadā’* (Meditate upon nārāyaṇa always)”. While I am engaged in other aspects, I forgot you in the beginning; alternative explanation – I have forgotten you since time immemorial. If this forgetfulness about bhagavān has been there for a long time, should āḻvār not say “Originally I did not forget you \[but long ago I have forgotten\]” Not necessary. Since when āḻvār said “*unnai*” he remembered his eternal relationship with bhagavān, and since that relationship is natural, though he had forgotten bhagavān forever, it appeared to āḻvār that he first remembered bhagavān and then forgot about him.

When asked “āḻvār did not forget about him in paramapadam which is known, as in [mudal tiruvandādi 51](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/munram-thiruvandhadhi-51/) ‘*kalangāp perunagaram*‘ (paramapadam, the great town, which has no bewilderment), but forgot him while being in samsāram. That is nothing wrong \[since it’s natural for us to forget bhagavān here\]”, āḻvār is saying I did not even remain as a cētana (sentient). If one is cētana (conscious), one should feel atonement for having forgotten bhagavān; acit is not qualified to say “*maṟandōm*” (We have forgotten). jñātrutvam for cit (for an ātmā, being knowledgeable) is to be the abode of jñāna and other qualities. Since those qualities are not seen in self, the abode (ātmā himself) is not present. Since āḻvār is saying “I have the heart which doesn’t even know it has forgotten” – the gate for feeling atonement is the heart, since that is not there,

**iṟandēn ettanaiyum** – I have become lower than acit (insentient). To start with, acit has no ability to think; but since chit has the ability and since I still did not meditate upon bhagavān, I have become lower than acit. I came to be known, as said in pramāṇams (authentic texts) such as taittirīya upaniśat, “*asannēva*” (non-existing). I reached a state where I can be declared as non-existing while I am existing.

**adanāl …** – śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.7.11 “*anātmani ātma buddiryā asvē svamiti yā mati: \|*  
***avidyā taru sambhūti bījamētat dvividā stittam*** *\|\|” (*Considering that which is not [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (i.e., body) as [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and considering that which is not one’s property (i.e., [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and that which is owned by the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which are fully owned by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) as one’s own are the two seeds for this tree of samsāram (which is the cycle of birth and death based on one’s actions) – considering body etc to be ātmā and considering self to be owner, are considered to be the seeds for samsāram, in general; āḻvār is considering that the lack of atonement is the seed for samsāram.

**idumbai … –** idumbai – sorrow. Entering the womb which will cause sorrow, I suffered repeatedly through death and birth.

**piṟandē …** – In this manner, while repeatedly going through death and birth, in between if one occasionally surrenders to bhagavān, that will become an obstacle (block) for \[more such\] births; I did not see/show any such puruśakāram and escape \[from the suffering\].

**eyttu oḻindēn** – Though there are impressions of karma to take more births, I became so weak that there is no substance to take birth; though I have the impression of karma which forces me to take birth, I cannot do it anymore. Hence the time is ripe for the owners (bhagavān) to take possession of me.

When asked “What are your reasons in you saying that the owners can take possession?” āḻvār says

**perumān …** – bhagavān asks “If you think about your own abilities and are leaving, what can I do?”.

**perumān** – āḻvār says “Am I only there for me? Are you not there?” bhagavān says “If you are talking about my śēśitva prāpti (the natural relationship due to being the lord), lords will have freewill to do, why are you expecting me who is completely independent?” āḻvār says,

**tirumārvā** – pirātti who will subdue your freewill and make you accept me, is present in close proximity to you. The one who says, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed), is right next to you.

**siṟandēn …** – I have become qualified for your divine feet since both you who will not abandon me even if she finds fault in me, and she who will subdue your freewill and make you accept me, are present here.

**tiruviṇṇagar ….** – While your abode is paramapadam as said in [mudal tiruvandādi 51](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/munram-thiruvandhadhi-51/) ‘*kalangāp perunagaram*‘ (paramapadam, the great town, which has no bewilderment), you left that abode and came to tiruviṇṇagar along with pirātti, to uplift those who are suffering. I am suffering; isn’t there an apt connection between those who are suffering and those who have arrived to uplift the suffering ones?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.3. Maney

*mānēy nōkkiyar tam vayiṟṟuk kuḻiyil uḻaikkumūnēr ākkai tannai udavāmai uṇarndu uṇarnduvānē! mānilamē! vandu vandu en manattu irundatēnē! ninnadaindēn tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānē – Oh one who is the controller of nitya vibhūti!; mā – vast; nilamē – Oh one who is the controller of leelā vibhūti which has earth in it!; vandu – coming from paramapadam; uvandu – joyfully; en manattu – in my heart; irunda – one who is eternally residing; tēnē – Oh very enjoyable lord!; mān ēy – matching a deer’s; nōkkiyar tam – women who are having beautiful eyes, their; vayiṟṟuk kuḻiyil – in the womb; uḻaikkum – suffering; Un – filled with flesh; ēr – Having the beauty of being the means for the goal; ākkai tannai – the body; udavāmai – (for my goal) not being means; uṇarndu uṇarndu – knowing well; nin adaindēn – I held you as my means; tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē! – Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! Oh one who is the controller of nitya vibhūti! Oh one who is the controller of leelā vibhūti which has the vast earth in it! Oh very enjoyable lord who came from paramapadam and is eternally and joyfully residing in my heart! Suffering in the womb of women who are having beautiful eyes matching those of a deer, my body, which is filled with flesh and is having the beauty of being the means for the goal, is not being the means for me; knowing this well, I held you as my means.

**mān ēy** – Women who are having eyes which are similar to those of deer; their.

**vayiṟṟuk kuḻiyil uḻaikkum** – While there is the suffering in hell, being punished by yama, there is no end to the suffering in the womb. While they \[women\] are young and ignorant, they will try hard thinking “We should have a child”; they are putting efforts for ātmā’s \[the child’s\] suffering.

**ūnēr ākkai** – It is recited as both “*ūnēy ākkai*” and “*ūnēr ākkai*“. Body which is filled with flesh; the body has to be given up both inside and outside equally. The body has two states – 1) it will desire the one who desires it and 2) it will abandon those who hate it; hence, while it has the state of being the means for the real goal, it ends up being in the state of causing bondage.

**udavāmai aṟindu aṟindu \[uṇarndu uṇarndu\]** – Having affiliation with the body which is visible and thinking it to be ātmā; if one abandons ātmā and īśvaran who is the lord of the ātmā, it only ends up in bondage. Knowing well that while there is scope for pursuing a good path, the body is leading to disaster and hence to be given up.

**vānē mānilamē** – While he \[emperumān\] is having the greatness of being together with ubhaya vibhūti (nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti), he stood there as if attaining me is a great benefit which is difficult to attain. **vānē** – nitya vibhūti – paramapadam; **mā nilamē** – leelā vibhūti – samsāram. Thus it is saying that he is the one who has both spiritual and material realms. Having both vibhūtis as his prakāra (body), he came here thinking “attaining āḻvār is desirable for me”.

**vandu vandu** – Here it is revealing how bhagavān kept coming to attain āḻvār since time immemorial and did not get him and went back, only to come back and try to get him again. It is said that he roamed around trying to get ātmās as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-6-madhusudhanai-anri/) “*edir sūḻal pukku*” (comes across from the opposite side and catches).

Alternative explanation,

**vandu uvandu** – That is – one who is having paramapadam which is said as in [mudal tiruvandādi 51](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/munram-thiruvandhadhi-51/) ‘*kalangāp perunagaram*‘ (paramapadam, the great town, which has no bewilderment), as his abode, came here as if he has no place to live and became satisfied. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 5.34 “*āvāsam tvahamiccāmi pratiśtam iha kānanē*” (As I am looking for a place to say, I will live in this forest as you desire). śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4-18 says “*ēśa datvā ca vittāni prāpya ca anuttamam yaśa*: l ***lōkanāta*****:** ***purā bhūtvā sugrīvam nātam iccati*** ll” (This rāmapirān, who has given all the materials to all the people, who has attained eminent fame, who was the lord of the entire word earlier, desires sugrīva (today) as the lord). \[This ślōkam is explained a little bit here\] bhagavān becoming the lord of the universe is to qualify himself to become the lord of sugrīva mahārāja. *nātam iccati* – There is no constraint that whatever is desired should be attained. Whether śrī rāma gets what he desires or not, he desired. śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4.21 “*yasya prasādē satatam prasīdēyu*: *imā: prajā*: l ***sa rāma*****:** ***vānarēndrasya prasādam abhikānkśatē*** \|\|” (That rāmapirān, who is such that when he is happy, the people of the entire world are always happy, seeks benefaction from sugrīva, who is the leader of monkeys).

**en manattirunda** – He remained firmly in my heart as an immovable entity to show that there is no going and coming anymore.

**tēnē** – When āḻvār thought about how bhagavān comes and goes to attain him, he became very sweet \[like honey\] for him. stōtra ratnam 27 “*tavāmrutasyandini pādapankajē*  
***nivēśidātmā*** *gatamanyadiccati? \|* *stit’ravindē makarandanirbharē* *maduvratō nēkśurakam hi vīkśatē \|\|*” (How will **my mind which is placed (by your grace)** at your divine lotus foot generating abundance of nectar, desire for anything else? When reddish lotus flower filled with honey is present, will a bee even see a grass flower?). yajur vēdam 2.4.6 \[and viṣṇu sūktam\] “*viṣṇō: padē paramē madva utsa:*” (from the supreme feet of viṣṇu, nectar originates and flows).

**nin …** – The lord to reach whom we have to carry food for the lengthy journey, is present in front of us here.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.4. Pirinden

*piṟindēn peṟṟa makkaḷ peṇḍir enṟivar pin udavāduaṟindēn nī paṇitta aruḷ ennum oḷ vāḷ uruvieṟindēn aimpulangaḷ idar tīra eṟindu vanduseṟindēn ninnadikkē tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

peṟṟa – own; makkaḷ – children; peṇḍir – wives; enṟu – said in this manner; ivar – these relatives; pin – for the end times; udavādu – not being helpful; aṟindēn – I knew (then); piṟindēn – I abandoned (them); nī – you are a friend in need; paṇitta – mercifully spoke (to arjuna); aruḷ ennum – carama ślōkam which shows bhagavān’s mercy as the only means; oḷ – beautiful; vāḷ – sword; uruvi – bringing out from the pouch; aim pulangaḷ – caused by matters such as śabda etc and their means; idar tīra – to eliminate the sorrow; eṟindēn – I launched; eṟindu – destroying (them in this manner); vandu – I came to you; nin adikkē – at your divine feet; seṟindēn – remained in a fixed manner; tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing in the divydēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

As I knew that these relatives such as children, wives are not helpful for the end times, I abandoned them. You are a friend in need and mercifully spoke carama ślōkam which shows your mercy as the only means; I launched the beautiful sword of such mercy, after bringing it out from the pouch, to eliminate the sorrow caused by matters such as śabda etc and their means and destroyed them. Oh one who is eternally residing in the divydēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! I came to you and remained at your divine feet in a fixed manner.

**piṟindēn** – A person helps others in this samsāra considering them as relatives, with the expectation that they will tell bhagavān’s divine name in his ear during the last moments when he is helpless and to seek good path for him subsequently; but, they \[those who got help from him\] would usually do as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.5.3 “*sōrvināl poruḷ vaittadu uṇḍāgil sollu sollu*” (Have you forgetfully placed some wealth somewhere? Tell us! Tell us!); when he regains consciousness, he will make all his wealth to be at their disposal. They will insist on him to reveal anything which is hidden forgetfully; he is as inferior as they are. Even after his placing all his wealth at their disposal, they think that he is still having something more and stay put with him. *suṟṟum irundu* – On one side yama’s servants are waiting and on the other side these relatives are present. When asked “How does he react when they do like this?” *Ar vinavilum …* – He is in his death bed such that he cannot respond to anyone – even if they bring his young (subsequent) wife to whom he gave all his wealth to marry her.

**peṟṟa …** – One’s own son and wife will remain the closest relative; even they will accept his help when it is necessary, and when they are expected to help him, they will leave. The relationship with them is similar to how an entity seen in the dream will disappear after waking up.

**aṟindēn – piṟindēn** – There is no need for separate timelines to acquire knowledge and abandoning such people \[it should happen as soon as the knowledge is acquired\].

Relatives here are not benefactors for us. Now, once we realise who will really help us for the ultimate aspects, there was a statement mercifully spoken by bhagavān as in “Consider me as the only refuge”; now, that is coming to me and helping me.

**nī paṇitta** – His word as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*māmēkam*” (Only me).

**aruḷ** – Why is āḻvār saying “*aruḷ*” (Mercy)? Because, bhagavān said “Be faithful that my mercy will be the means for your being uplifted”.

**oḷ vāḷ** – It is capable of eliminating all our doubts and making us say as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.73](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-73/) “*stitō’smi gatasandēha:*” (being freed from doubts, I am standing firm, with realisation of truth). What was said in [periya tirumoḻi 3.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/10/periya-thirumozhi-3-9-10/) “*maruvalar tam udal tuṇiya* *vāḷ vīsum parakālan*” (uses his sword to cut the enemies’ bodies to pieces) is seen in the context of upāyam (means).

**aim pulan …** – āḻvār is thinking about all the superficial goals and superficial means. Alternative explanation – to be not touched by the activities which are built in with ahankāra (ego, misunderstanding body to be self) and mamakāra (possessiveness, misunderstanding self to be independent). Another explanation – to be not touched by the worldly pleasures which will make one think those to be the goal.

**seṟindēn** – I united with him so closely that even if he said “Not me”, it will be impossible to separate me from him even by a swan which can use its beak to separate milk and water, which are mixed together.

**nin …** – bhagavān gave this special intelligence to āḻvār by coming and being present in tiruviṇṇagar. tiruviṇṇagar has become like arjuna’s chariot \[where kriṣṇa instructed arjuna about important principles\]. Whatever was mercifully said to arjuna, will be applicable for anyone who is having the same connection with bhagavān like arjuna.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.5. Pan ten

*pāṇ tēn vaṇḍaṟaiyum kuḻalārgaḷ pallāṇḍu isaippaāṇḍār vaiyam ellām arasāgi mun āṇḍavarēmāṇḍār enṟu vandār andō! manai vāḻkkai tannaivēṇḍēn ninnadaindēn tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pāṇ – singing; tēn – drinking honey; vaṇḍu – beetles; aṟaiyum – humming; kuḻalārgaḷ – women who are having hair; pallāṇḍu isaippa – as they pray for auspiciousness, more and more; arasāgi – being kings; vaiyam ellām – all the worlds; āṇḍār – those who ruled; mun āṇḍavarē – those who ruled in this manner; māṇḍār enṟu – being known as “they have died”; vandār – (since time immemorial) they are coming (no one is permanent); andō – alas! This wealth is temporary; manai vāḻkkai tannai – enjoyment in samsāra; vēṇḍēn – not liking it; nin adaindēn – I surrendered unto you; tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing in tiruviṇṇagar!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is eternally residing in tiruviṇṇagar! As the women, who are having hair where beetles which have drunk honey are hummimg through singing, pray for more and more auspiciousness, those kings who ruled all the worlds came to be known as “Those who ruled in this manner have died”. Since time immemorial, such kings are coming. Alas! This wealth is temporary. Not liking the enjoyment in samsāra, I have surrendered unto you.

**pāṇ tēn** … – For those kings who are having great wealth and kingdom already instead of having to gather elephants, horses, chariots and ground soldiers, destroying the enemies with the help of those, and through that the wealth of others have to be taken over, there is great desire to be praised by others in the form of mangaḷāśāsanam. The king, who doesn not need to gather any new wealth, is the one who is desiring to be praised by others. And, they desire to be praised by beautiful women who are having hair which has beetles which are singing and drunk fully with honey and are humming being in that drunk state.

**āṇḍār** – Instead of being the king for a small region, as said in tiruvāimoḻi 4.1.1 “*oru nāyagamāy*” (Being the distinguished ruler), being under the pearl umbrella, they ruled the whole world.

Those who ruled over previously like this, now

**māṇḍār enṟu vandār** – When his coronation was announced through a message, there will be not much time before the next message which says “he died” will be announced. Since this is the case, in the back side of the palm leaf having the message “He is coronated”, it will be already written “He has died”. We can’t say that those who ruled, ruled forever.

**enṟu vandār** – This is how it is said all over the world. Even “*āṇḍār*” and “*māṇḍār*” sound very similar. As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.13](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-13/) “*tatā dēhāntara prāptir*” (In the same manner, begetting another body will also occur), these are all different states of body for the ātmā only.

**āṇḍavarē māṇḍār** – While the king would think “All of these expansive world will remain permanently with me”, his life will end.

As āḻvār is looking at such person’s desire and the temporary nature of such person’s kingdom, wealth etc, showing mercy and being unable to tolerate his suffering, āḻvār is saying “***andō***” (alas!). śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 105-24 “*nandanti udita ādityē nandanti astamitē ravau*” (people are delighted when the sun rises and are happy when the sun sets) – as the sun sets, people will become happy that it is time to gather enjoyable materials and enjoy with lovers/spouses in seclusion; as the sun rises, people will become happy that it is time to gather wealth for such enjoyment later. Like water getting depleted by continuously being fetched from a pot, their life span is continuously getting depleted. Instead of knowing this and in the meantime trying to ensure that one does not get punished after the end of their lives, everyone is doing contrary to it. No one is trying to do what is ideal.

**manai vāḻkkai** – Only if one tries to rule like this, one will die; bhagavān is coming to tiruviṇṇagar and standing there to negate that aiśvaryam (wealth) is perceivable by your senses and what you desire \[that is, bhagavān\] is beyond your senses; this presence in tiruviṇṇagar is to grant kainkaryam sāmrājyam (the kingdom of servitude). When you have come here and stood as my refuge, what I am going to do with them (those who praise)?

**āṇḍār māṇḍār** – These two words do not occur in two different persons – the same person who rules everything, dies soon after. āḻvār is seeing the damage to dharma and saying “Alas!” just like a flood will be hot for the feet to bear \[rare occurrence\].

**manai vāḻkkai tannai vēṇḍēn** – Only if one desires to rule, one will pray for continuous life; even if such enjoyment is permanent, I don’t need it \[I only need to serve you\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.6. Kalla

*kallā aimbulangaḷ avai kaṇḍavāṟu seyyagillēnmallā! mallamaruḷ mallar māḷa malladarttamallā! mallal am sīr madiḷ nīr ilangai aḻittavillā! ninnadaindēn tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kallā – illiterate (not following the principles of śāstram); avai – very cruel; aim pulangaḷ – five senses; kaṇḍa – tried to enjoy śabda (sound) etc; āṟu – the way; seyya killēn – unqualified to do; mallā – Oh strong one!; mal amaruḷ – in the wrestling fight; mallar – cāṇūra et al; māḷa – to be killed; mal – (their) strength; adartta – destroyed; mallā – Oh one who is having very simple act!; mallal – abundant; am – beautiful; sīr – wealth; madiḷ – forts; nīr – ocean (standing as a protective layer); ilangai – lankā; aḻitta – one who destroyed; villā – Oh one who is having the bow!; nin adaindēn – I surrendered unto you; tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing in tiruviṇṇagar!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I am unqualified to do the way my illiterate, very cruel, five senses tried to enjoy śabda (Sound) etc. Oh strong one! Oh one who is having very simple act which destroyed the strength of cāṇūra et al to have them killed in the wrestling fight! Oh one who is having the bow and who destroyed lankā which is abundant with wealth, forts and the ocean! Oh one who is eternally residing in tiruviṇṇagar! I surrendered unto you

When \[emperumān\] asked “Would you not follow the sense organs which are meant for gārhastya (gruhastāśrama – married life), desire the aspects which are desired by those senses? In this case why should you worry?” āḻvār responds,

**kallā …** – Only when those senses desire to see you \[referring to emperumān\] and hear you, they are bound by me. Instead, they are all illiterate \[in not desiring for you\]. They are like rāvaṇa. Those senses will try to rule over us and kill us, and will let not let us take the path of goodness. I am unable to take the path shown by them. That is – enjoying worldly pleasures based on sound, etc; as I think about the disaster which is to be faced in future, I cannot engage in such activities.

When asked “If the sense organs control us without being able to be freed by anyone, is there anything I can do?” āḻvār says

**mallā …** – Don’t you have the ability to eliminate by submission towards my senses? Did you not say “If you cannot control your senses, place your heart on me?”

When asked “Where did you see me use my ability?” āḻvār says

**mal amar …** – Oh one who is expert in wrestling to destroy the strength of the wrestlers to have them killed in the wrestling fight!

**mallal …** – He is capable of killing the enemies in wresting fight as well as in direct war. Is it as difficult as killing rāvaṇa who did not understand that sītā is the mother for all, to eliminate my submission towards my senses? Seeing the protection of the town which has unlimited wealth and control, tiruvadi (hanuman) said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 49.17 “*ahō vīryam ahō dairyam ahō satvam ahō dyuti*: *\| ahō rākśasa rājasya sarvalakśaṇa yuktatā \|\|*” (How valiant! How brave! How strong! How radiant! How superior this rākśasa king’s marks are!). Seeing the presence of rāvaṇa along with his wives, hanuman thought “*yadīdruśī rāgava darmapatnī”* (if sītā were like this), if only rāvaṇa agreed for such presence of perumāḷ (śrī rāma) and sītāp pirātti in this manner, this wealth and control will remain in tact for him. Oh one who is having the bow which destroyed lankā which has the fort and the ocean as another protective layer!

**nin …** – When bhagavān says “To use my bow, you did not come to lankā and show your presence there” āḻvār says “Did you destroy that enemy and left for elsewhere? Have you not entered here in tiruviṇṇagar by deceiving others?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.7. Vera yan iranden

*vēṟā yān irandēn veguḷādu manakkoḷ endāy!āṟā vennaragattu adiyēnai idak karudikūṟā aivar vandu kumaikkak kudi vittavaraitēṟādu unnadaindēn tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

yān – I, who have been facing away from you, till date; vēṟā – being different from drupta prapanna (one who remains satisfied with mōkśam at the end of the life); irandēn – I begged you; endāy – Oh my lord!; veguḷādu – without being angry; manakkoḷ – you should mercifully accept in your divine mind; aivar – (that is) the five senses; āṟā – continuously; vem – very cruel; naragattu – in this hell known as samsāra; adiyēnai – me; ida – to keep here; karudi – thinking; kūṟā – dividing me (among those senses); vandu – reaching me; kumaikka – as they hurt; kudi vittavarai – (to reform me, towards me) the senses which stay in me; tēṟādu – without depending; un – you; adaindēn – I surrendered; tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē – Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I, who have been facing away from you, till date, being different from drupta prapanna (one who remains satisfied with mōkśam at the end of the life), begged you (for mōkśam). Oh my lord! Without being angry, you should mercifully accept me in your divine mind. That is, my five senses which stay in me, thinking continuously to keep me here in this very cruel hell known as samsāra, are dividing me among them, reaching me and hurting me. Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! Without depending on them, I surrendered unto you.

**vēṟā yān irandēn** – There are some begging where one can fulfil the request over time; there are some begging where one has to immediately fulfil the request; when it appears that the one who prays can remain patient if the result is given over time, that process will be tolerated (accepted); but when it appears that the one who prays cannot survive if the result were not bestowed immediately, that result needs to be bestowed immediately; in this, āḻvār is saying “*vēṟā yān irandēn*” indicating that he is begging in a manner that his goal should be fulfilled immediately.

**yān irandēn** – You should mercifully see how the tables have turned \[i.e., you should be craving to get me, but now I am doing so\]. While you were trying to get me, as said in  [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-6-madhusudhanai-anri/) “*edir sūḻal pukku*” (comes across from the opposite side and catches), I was rejecting that and roaming around. You should mercifully consider that lengthy period. I, who rejected you when you were begging me, am now begging you.

**veguḷādu** – When your highness listens to my words, it will cause anger in your highness’ heart; it will make you angry at me when you look at my past acts, thinking “the one who is remaining without a refuge today, was evading me since I tried to catch him since time immemorial”. I am filled with all defects and you are omniscient; hence you may become angry thinking “He is neither seeing my qualities nor his faults, and is surrendering unto me as if he has no defects”. Don’t become angry like that.

**manakkoḷ** – At the time of delivering the results, one should not remain indifferent as if playing chess; please keep my prayer in your divine heart. It is not only that you should not be angry, you should also mercifully consider my prayer in your heart.

When asked “While you admit that you have defects, why are you asking me who is svatantra (fully independent) ‘Mercifully accept my prayer instead of showing anger’?”

**endāy** – With the relationship we have, which cannot be destroyed by me, you should tolerate my defects; do we have such a relationship that will make you abandon me counting my mistakes? It is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 11.44](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/11-44/) “*pitēva putrasya*” (as a father dealing with his son’s mistakes).

When asked “When tolerating your mistakes, instead of becoming angry seeing your mistakes, to accept you seeing our relationship, what is happening to you now?” āḻvār responds

**āṟā vennaragam** … – The senses have a very evil plan. When the sins are reduced, yama’s punishment will stop and resume after some time. But this hell named samsāra is continuously tormenting me.

**adiyēnai** – Just as leaders \[for example – maṇiyakārar, who keeps time of all activities in a temple\] will try to torment in close quarters \[the senses are remaining with me and tormenting with me from inside\]. While I am having relationship with bhagavān to attain the reason after performing all the services to him as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31-25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (I would carry out all tasks of servitude), the senses are planning to push me into samsāra where we will be bound by ahankāra and mamakāra.

**kūṟā aivar vandu kumaikka** – The senses are not thinking that I am common for all of them; rather they individually try to torment me.

**aivar** – āḻvār is not just thinking that these senses are just gateway for knowledge, but he is thinking about them to be individual cētanas, who are having knowledge, due to the severe nature of the torment.

**aivar kumaikka** – Just as a weak person will be surrounded from 5 sides and will be attacked by 5 strong persons.

**kudivittavarai** – Those who you made enter inside me. You gave these senses to me thinking “He will surrender unto me with the help of these senses and attain me”; but that is in your thought only; they are taking me away from you and engaging me with worldly pleasures and are finishing me.

**tēṟādu** – Since those senses are not acting according to your thought, I am not going to believe them.

**un …** – While you, who are trustworthy, are present here, should I serve these senses which cause fear in me and roam around?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.8. Tivay valvinaiyar

*tīvāy valvinaiyār udan ninṟu siṟandavar pōlmēvā vennaragattu idaruṟṟu viraindu vandārmūvā vānavar tam mudalvā! madi kōḷ viduttadēvā! ninnadaindēn tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tī vāy – spitting fire from the mouth (granting very cruel results); val – very cruel (difficult to eliminate by any means); vinaiyār – the sins; siṟandavarpōl – like very close relatives; udan ninṟu – minging (with me) and remaining without separating; mēvā – not matching (for the true nature of the self); vem – very cruel; naragattu – in the hell; idar uṟṟu – trying to place me; viraindu – very quickly; vandār – came (to grant the results); mūvā – not having changes like old-age etc; vānavar tam – for nityasūris; mudalvā – oh controller!; madi – moon’s; kōḷ – disease of waning; vidutta – eliminated; dēvā – Oh lord!; nin adaindēn – I surrendered unto you; tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē – oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The very cruel sins which are spitting fire from the mouth, minging with me and remaining without separating, like very close relatives, came very quickly and are trying to place me in the very cruel hell which is not matching the true nature of the self. Oh controller of nityasūris who are not having changes like old-age etc! Oh lord who eliminated the moon’s disease of waning! Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! I surrendered unto you.

**tī vāy** – Energetic. Having mouth which is spitting fire.

**val** – They cannot be exhausted through atonement. As said in brahma vaivartam-prakruti kaṇḍam 26-90 “*avaśyam anubhōktavyam krutam karma śubhāśubham l* *nābhuktam kśīyatē karma kalpakōti śatairapi* ll´ (The effects of deeds of vice and virtue, carried out by a person, have to be necessarily experienced. The effects cannot be wished away, even after passage of hundreds of crores of *kalpam*) – they cannot be exhausted by any other way than experiencing the results.

**udan ninṟu** – Minging as if they are natural relatives and remaining together, as said in [periya tiruvandādi 65](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/01/periya-thiruvandhadhi-65/) “*kalandu  naliyum kadum tuyar*” (Cruel sin which is being together with us and troubling us).

**siṟandavar pōl** – They are like brothers and others who never leave us even for a moment.

**mēvā vennaragattu** – They came to push this ātmā, who is qualified to enjoy bhagavān who is said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ānanda maya:*” (one who is filled with bliss), into the hell which is not matching for the true nature of the self. Usually, hell is the place where we will reach after completing the experience of sufferings here; here āḻvār is saying this place (samsāra) to be “*naragam*” (hell).

**viraindu vandār** – With this, āḻvār is indicating that there is no scope for a good deed entering in now into the self. For karma too, there is anāditvam (being beginningless) through continuous flow since time immemorial.

bhagavān asked “āren’t these, results of karma performed by you? ṣouldn’t one experience the result of the karma performed by oneself? What can we do now?” āḻvār responds

**mūvā vānavar** … – You have made nityasūris to be free from karma and constantly enjoy you. In the whole paramapadam, everyone will remain twenty five years old. There, when one enjoys something, one need not worry “Is it reducing for us?”

**mudalvā** – Making them free from karma, presenting yourself for their enjoyment, in this manner, you are managing their existence. It is as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.1.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-1-5-thir-marundhu/) “*viṇṇuḷār perumānēyō!*” (Oh leader who is infinitely enjoyable for the residents of paramapadam!) – among brothers, while one person is crowned and leading a joyful life, other person is suffering in the prison. \[āḻvār is suffering while nityasūris are enjoying\]. \[Another explanation\] śrī rāmāyaṇām sundara kāṇḍam 28.8 “*hā rāma hā lakṣmaṇa hā sumitrē hā rāmamāta: saha mē jananya: \| ēśā vipadyāmyaham alpabhājñā mahārṇavē nauriva mūdavātā \|\|*” (Oh rāma! lakṣmaṇa! śumitrā! Mother of rāma! My mothers! I who do not have good deeds in me, have been affected by sorrows, like a boat caught in the sea storm). “*hā rāma! hā lakśmaṇa!*” – Oh lakśmaṇa who makes śrī rāma understand that it is a mystic deer and protect bhagavān! “*hā sumitrē!*” Talking about sumitrā who said in  śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 40-5 “*sruśtatvam vanavāsāya* – *pramādam mākārśī:*” (you were sired by me only to follow śrī rāma to the forest – don’t look at his beauty and miss out on serving him).

āḻvār tells him so that he cannot say “Such interactions are only present in paramapadam and not here”

**madi kōḷ vidutta dēvā** – You grant their \[nityasūris\] wish for those who desire to act according to their svarūpam and serve you; you also grant the wish of those \[candra et al\] who desire to eliminate the defects in their body.

**dēvā** – Whose bodily defects do you think you have eliminated? \[candra is also your body only\]

**nin …** – When you have arrived here and are present here to eliminate my defects, should I serve others \[my senses\] and roam around here?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.9. Podar

*pōdār tāmaraiyāḷ pulavik kulavānavar tamkōdā! kōdil sengōl kudai mannar idai nadandatūdā! tūmoḻiyāy! sudar pōl en manattirundavēdā! ninnadaindēn tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pōdu Ar – blossomed at the right time (fresh); tāmaraiyāḷ – periya pirāttiyār who is having lotus flower as her abode, her; pulavi – bhūmip pirāttiyār’s; kulam – being part of the servant clan; vānavar tam – nityasūris’; kōdā – Oh one who is the matter of joy!; kōdu il – being free from defect of obstacles; sengōl – having their sceptre; kudai – having pearl umbrella; mannar – for kings such as duryōdana et al; idai – in their royal assembly; nadanda tūdā – Oh one who went as a messenger!; tū moḻiyāy – Oh one who is having pure words which are having partiality towards pāṇḍavas!; sudarpōl – being radiant like a lamp; en manattu – in my heart; irunda – Oh one who is residing!; vēdā – Oh one who is revealed in vēdam!; nin adaindēn – I surrendered unto you; tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanē – oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is the matter of joy for periya pirāttiyār who is having lotus flower which is blossomed at the right time, as her abode, bhūmip pirāttiyār and nityasūris who are part of the servant clan! Oh one who went as a messenger to kings such as duryōdana et al who are having the sceptre which is free from defect of obstacles and having pearl umbrella, in their royal assembly! Oh one who is having pure words which are having partiality towards pāṇḍavas! Oh one who is residing in my heart being radiant like a lamp! Oh one who is revealed in vēdam! Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! I have surrendered unto you.

**pōdār tāmaraiyāḷ** – One who is having lotus flower which blossomed at the right time, as her abode. ōr, one who is having lotus which is freshly blossomed flower, as her abode. pōdu means time as well as flower.

**pulavi** – pulavi indicates śrī bhūmip pirāttiyār. Alternative explanation – pulavi means separation \[for subsequent union\]. In the separation for pirātti from bhagavān, the nityasūris enthusiastically pacify her/him. In such a case, if pirātti and bhagavān are having separation for subsequent union, at that time, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 1-127 “*rarakśa darmēṇa balēna ca*” ((lakśmaṇa vigilantly) protected (śrī rāma) (with an undespaired mind and) even by his virtue and strength), the nityasūris will remove the romantic fight and pacify. Oh one who is the matter of enthusiasm for such nityasūris!

**kula vānavar** – Those who don’t move away from experiencing bhagavān. As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-2-10-mudivu-ival/) “*vadivudai vānōr*” (for nityasūris who are having matching form). When romantic fight happens with periya pirāttiyār, nityasūris eliminate that and pacify you. One who is object of that! kōdā is used in place of kōtukulam (kutūhalam). Alternative explanation – as in “*pulavik kula vānavar*“, it is an adjective for nityasūris. With this, it is explained that – though they are eternally residing with bhagavān, they are unsatisfied with the experience as if they have not enjoyed him previously. In this manner, āḻvār is talking about bhagavān who is greater than all and controller of all, yet he went as a messenger minimising his own greatness, for the sake of his devotees.

**kōdil sengōl kudai mannar** – Our pūrvācāryas have mercifully explained this phrase as talking about duryōdana et al or pāṇḍavas. Oh one who went as a messenger having a palm-leaf tied to your neck amidst the kings duryōdana et al, who usurped pāṇadavas’ umbrella, covrie etc, and having orders (sceptre) which cannot be stopped by anyone, remaining under the pearl umbrella and ruling over the vast earth as the kings! Alternative explanation – by kriṣṇa’s opinion, pāṇḍavas are the real kings who have the sceptre.

**tūmoḻiyāy** – kriṣṇa asked duryōdana et al “What are pāṇḍavas and you planning to do?” They said “They have dharma (righteousness) and the result of that, which is heaven; they are five, and we are hundred of us; hence we need the whole earth for ourselves; hence we cannot even give them the piece of land measuring the tip of a needle”. kriṣṇa said “If this is your opinion. the king (yudiśtira) who is eating whatever he gets, wearing whatever garments he gets, applying whatever sandal paste he gets, and remaining peaceful in all manners, is eager to become victorious in the battle”, showing his partiality towards his devotees. Because of speaking such words, oh one who is unstoppably shining radiantly in my heart!

**vēdā** – Who is shining like this? One who is fully known from vēdam.

**nin …** – Instead of having to just hear from śāstram, you are present in tiruviṇṇagar to be seen by our eyes. I surrender unto you – says āḻvār.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.10. Tenar

*tēnār pūm puṟavil tiruviṇṇagar mēyavanaivānārum madiḷ sūḻ vayal mangaiyar kōn maruvār ūnār vēl kaliyan oli sey tamiḻ mālai vallārkōnāy vānavar tam kodi mānagar kūduvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēn Ar – filled with honey; pū – having flowers; puṟavil – having surroundings; tiruviṇṇagar – in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar; mēyavanai – on sarvēśvaran who remains eternally; vān ārum – touching the sky; madiḷ – by forts; vayal – by fertile fields; sūḻ – surrounded; mangaiyar – for the residents of tirumangai region; kōn – being the leader; maruvār – enemies’; Un Ar – which can pierce through the bodies; vēl – having the weapon spear; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; oli sey – mercifully spoke; tamiḻ mālai – these ten pāsurams in tamiḻ; vallār – those who can recite; kōnāy – being the (independent) lord; vānavar tam – the abode of nityasūris; kodi – decorated by flags; mā – best; nagar – śrīvaikuṇṭam; kūduvar – will reach

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran resides eternally in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar which is having surroundings having flowers filled with honey; tirumangai āḻvār, who is the leader for the residents of tirumangai region which is surrounded by forts touching the sky and fertile fields and who is having the weapon, spear which can pierce through the bodies of the enemies, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams in tamiḻ; those who can recite these pāsurams, will reach the best abode, śrīvaikuṇṭam which is decorated by flags, being the lord of the abode of nityasūris.

**tēn Ar …** – One who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar which is having surroundings having flowers filled with honey. tēn can also mean beetles.

**vānārum madiḷ sūḻ vayal mangaiyar kōn** – tirumangai āḻvār, who is the leader of tirumangai region which is surrounded by tall forts which pervade the whole sky and which has fertile fields.

**maruvār …** – Bodies of the enemies are the prey for tirumangai āḻvār’s spear. Those who are well versed in these ten pāsurams mercifully sung by tirumangai āḻvār whose spear has bathed in the bodies of the enemies.

**kōnāy …** – Instead of being subservient to someone in paramapadam, these persons who are well versed in these pāsurams, will reach śrīvaikuṇṭam and remain the controller there as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-9-6-velviyul-maduththalum/) “*āṇmingaḷ vānagam*” (rule over these abodes such as svarga (heaven) etc).

## 6.3 Turappen

## 6.3.1. Turappen

*tuṟappēn allēn inbam tuṟavādu nin uruvammaṟappēn allēn enṟum maṟavādu yān ulagilpiṟappēnāga eṇṇēn piṟavāmai peṟṟadu nintiṟattēn ādanmaiyāl tiruviṇṇagarānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruviṇṇagarānē – Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!; inbam – the bliss caused by experiencing you; tuṟappēn allēn – I will not abandon; tuṟavādu – not abandoning (that bliss) means; nin uruvam – your physical beauty; enṟum – at all times; maṟappēn allēn – I will not forget; maṟavādu – due to not forgetting; yān – I; ulagil – in this samsāra; piṟappēn āga eṇṇēn – will not think that I will take birth; piṟavāmai – (that) elimination of birth; nin – your; tiṟattēn ādanmaiyāl – since I am on your side (being your servitor); peṟṟadu – got it

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! I will not abandon the bliss caused by experiencing you. Not abandoning (that bliss) means I will not forget your physical beauty, at all times. Due to not forgetting you, I will not think about taking birth in samsāra. Elimination of such birth is acquired since I am on your side always.

**tuṟappēn allēn inbam** – While I will abandon worldly pleasures, I won’t abandon the primary bliss of being your servitor.

When bhagavān asked “If you can abandon pleasures acquired from śabdam etc what is the reason for not abandoning the pleasure in my matters?” āḻvār responds

**tuṟavādu …** – Not abandoning the pleasure means not forgetting your divine form. Though I forgot you in the past as said in [periya tirumoḻi 6.2.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/05/periya-thirumozhi-6-2-2/) “*maṟandēn unnai munnam*” (I did not think about you), in the future, I will ensure that I won’t forget you.

What is derived from this? I did not think about you in the past; because of that I took births and suffered; now, if I constantly think about you without forgetting, will it not lead to stopping the birth for me?

**enṟum …** – By not forgetting, I got to eliminate the thought of taking birth in samsāram.

When bhagavān asked “Good! Are you thinking that you won’t be born again since you have continuous remembrance about me?” āḻvār responds

**piṟavāmai …** – I got to the point of not having to take birth again only by being subservient to your mercy and accepting “You are the controller” and not because of my efforts.

**tiruviṇṇagarānē** – It is because of your divine presence here that I became the target of your mercy.

\[Simple explanation in sequence of the words in the pāsuram\]

**tuṟappēn allēn inbam** – I won’t abandon the joy.

**tuṟavādu nin uruvam maṟappēn allēn** – Not abandoning the joy – not forgetting your divine form.

**enṟum maṟavādu yānulagil piṟappēnāga eṇṇēn** – Not taking birth is acquired by not forgetting you.

**nin tiṟattēn ādanmaiyāl – piṟavāmaip peṟṟadu – tiruviṇṇagarānē** – I became yours due to your divine presence in tiruviṇṇagar.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
