## 6.3.2. Turanden

*tuṟandēn ārvac ceṟṟac cuṟṟam tuṟandamaiyālsiṟandēn ninnadikkē adimai tirumālē!aṟandānāyt tirivāy! unnai en manattagattētiṟambāmal koṇḍēn tiruviṇṇagarānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruviṇṇagarānē – Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!; tirumālē – Oh śrīman nārāyaṇa!; aṟam tānāy – being the real darmam; tirivāy – Oh one who is roaming around! (to see the best time to bestow the results); suṟṟam – relationship (with materialistic people); ārvam – affection; seṟṟam – hatred; tuṟandēn – I abandoned; tuṟandamaiyāl – due to abandoning that; nin adikkē – at your divine feet; adimai – to perform kainkaryam; siṟandēn – I became qualified; unnai – Such you; en manattagattē – in my heart; tiṟambāmal – without any break; koṇḍēn – I have placed

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is present in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! Oh śrīman nārāyaṇa! Oh one who is roaming around being the real darmam! I have abandoned relationship, affection and hatred towards materialistic people. Due to that, I became qualified to perform kainkaryam at your divine feet. I have placed such you in my heart, without any break.

**tuṟandēn …** – I have become such that your highness cannot blame me saying “You have some desires other than me”; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.5 “*parityaktā mayā lankā*” (I have abandoned lankā). Due to impressions from time immemorial, acquiring remembrance on worldly pleasures, due to that acquiring attachment, and then reaching the stage of surviving if we attain such pleasure and dying if we could not attain such pleasure, when such pleasure is not attained, becoming angry on everyone thinking “He is the one who stopped me from attaining it”, without being able to analyse what is apt and what is inapt, roaming around as desired; the cause for all these is the consideration of worldly people as relatives; I abandoned that thought. As I eliminated the attachment, the hatred which comes due that attachment will go. If those other than bhagavān are eliminated, these two aspects (desire and attachment), will also be eliminated.

**tuṟandamaiyāl …** – The reason for our loss (in spiritual matters) is due to considering worldly people as relatives; once that is abandoned, we need not earn the relationship (with bhagavān). Relationship with bhagavān is natural. Once worldly relationships are given up, divine experience will commence. As soon as śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān rose to the sky abandoning rāvaṇa’s palace, he became śrīmān. After abandoning inapt matters, I have become settled in the ultimate state of apt matters; I have become qualified for kainkaryam which is the outcome of attaining bhagavān.

bhagavān asked “I am omniscient; all along, you have considered worldly persons as your relatives; how did you become qualified now?” āḻvār responds

**tirumālē** – Because you are the divine lord of śrī mahālakśmi. Since the one (śrī mahālakśmi) who would pacify him saying “Would you abandon him for the mistakes he did being away from you? Should you not see your natural relationship with him and accept him?”, is in his very close proximity, for this ātmā, being subservient to karma is incidental and being subservient to īśvara is natural. Is there any shortcoming for me to attain you when the one, who says as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed), is present with you? Also, here āḻvār is speaking about bhagavān’s nature towards his children (ātmās), having pirātti’s relationship as just a nod of her head in acceptance \[he himself is waiting to help the ātmās\]. He has the greatness of arguing with her as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4-9-2 “*tannadiyār tiṟattagattut tāmariyāḷāgilum sidaguraikkumēl,* ***ennadiyār adu seyyār*** *seydārēl nanṟu seydār enbar pōlum*” (emperumān tells pirāttiyār when she complains to him about the bad deed of vibhīśaṇāḻvān “My follower will not carry out any harmful action towards you; even if he carries out, it will be only for your good”). bhagavān remains as an embodiment of mercy, instead of being just a person who shows mercy while someone \[pirātti\] makes him to shower such mercy. With this, his greatness over other upāyams, is explained. Other upāyams (like karma yōgam etc) will be acētana (insentient) and will perish when performed; hence without knowing what was done by an ātmā, it has to get the help of another person \[bhagavān\] to get the result. When we try to attain him by holding on to him, we need to give up engagement in other upāyams; that is why sādana nairapēkśyam (not expecting ātmā to engage in other means), is told. When a local administrator grants something, he will need the written order from the king. But when the king grants something, there is no need for the local administrator’s consent.

**aṟam tānāy** –  mahābhāratam vana parvam 71-123 says “*yē ca vēda vidō viprā yē cādyātma vidō janā*: l *tē vidanti mahātmānam* ***kriṣṇam darmam sanātanam***  ll” (brāhmaṇas who know vēdams and the elders who know the nature of ātmā know that kriṣṇa symbolises the ancient righteousness), śrī rāmāyaṇam “*lōkānām tvam parō dharma:*” (you are the superior darmam for all the people in the world), śri rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam “*rāmo vigrahavān dharma:*” (rāma is darmam personified), śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.29 “*sākśāt rāmāt vinirvruttō darmaścāpi śriyāsaha:*” (Only śrī rāma can make both righteousness and wealth combine truly).

**tirumālē aṟandānāyt tirivāy** – As said in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 52](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-52/) “*niṟam kariyan seyya nedumalarāḷ mārvan* *aṟam periyan*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has periya pirātti, who is reddish in complexion and who resides in an expansive lotus, on his chest, who is dark-coloured, is very generous in his mercy); “*āradaṟivār*” – While his nature is like this, some people torment their bodies and try using different means.

**tirivāy** – The darmam (that is, bhagavān) which is roaming around seeking opportunities to bestow the results.

**unnai en manattagattē tiṟambāmal koṇḍēn** – I eliminated your perplexity. I firmly placed you, who are the divine lord of śrī mahālakśmi, with the help of pirātti, manifesting my refuge-less state, in my heart, so that if you try to leave from there, you will be considered as an evil person. It implies that when you enter my heart yourself, I did not stop you. If bhagavān abandoned such a refuge-less person, he will be considered as cruel; if he does what is not pleasing to pirātti, he will not be considered as a beloved. Thus, both your true nature and love, will be lost.

bhagavān asked “How are you able to hold me in your heart?” āḻvār responds,

**tiruviṇṇagarānē** – It is because you are sulabha (easily attainable) and you are present in tiruviṇṇagar in an easily reachable manner.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.3. Maney nokku

*mānēy nōkku nallār madi pōl mugattu ulavumūnēy kaṇ vāḷikku udaindōttattu unnadaindēnkōnē! kuṟungudiyuḷ kuḻagā! tirunaṟaiyūrttēnē! varupunal sūḻ tiruviṇṇagarānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōnē – Oh lord!; kuṟungudiyuḷ – in tirukkuṟngudi; kuḻagā – Oh one who is present!; tirunaṟaiyūr – one who is mercifully present in tirunaṟaiyūr; tēnē – Oh enjoyable one!; varu – overflowing; punal – by water; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruviṇṇagarānē – Oh one who is residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!; mān ēy – like a deer; nōkku – having vision; nallār – distinguished (beautiful) women’s; madipōl – moon like; mugattu – on the face; ulavum – present; Un ēy – having abundant flesh; kaṇ – the eyes; vāḷikku – for the arrow; udaindu – became weak; ōttandu – came running; un adaindēn – I surrendered unto you

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh lord! Oh one who is present in tirukkuṟungudi! Oh enjoyable one who is mercifully present in tirunaṟaiyūr! Oh one who is residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar which is surrounded by overflowing water! I became weak being hit with the arrow of the abundantly fleshy eyes on the moon like face of the distinguished (beautiful) women who are having eyes like those of a deer. Due to this, I came running and surrendered unto you.

**mān ..** – I escaped from that which is very difficult to escape from, and surrendered unto your divine feet. Hence you should mercifully shower your grace upon me.

**mānēy nōkku nallār** – The beautiful, abundantly fleshy eyes, which are seen in the face of women, who are having eyes which are like those of deer, having goodness for other aspects of beauty, and which are attractive and inviting, are like arrows. Being tormented by those eyes, I came running and surrendered unto your divine feet. These women will firmly captivate the men with their eyes, by glancing at them as if they expect nothing, and once the men get caught, the women will take themselves away and torment the men; I escaped that and surrendered unto your divine feet.

**kōnē** – When I escaped such torment and took refuge at your divine feet, they look like apt matrer just like resting on a mother’s lap.

**kuṟungudiyuḷ kuḻagā** – While emperumān was in the divine assembly in paramapadam, he descended and became present in tirukkuṟungudi to unite with āḻvār and accept him.

**tirunaṟaiyūrt tēnē** – It became pleasant to āḻvār when he thought about emperumān being present in tirunaṟaiyūr just as mother and father will remain together to eliminate the sorrow of a child. bhattar would mercifully say “For the tirunaṟaiyūr flood (of 100 pāsurams), this is an indication”.

**varu punal …** – As you have arrived and are present in tiruviṇṇagar which is having abundance of water which will eliminate all the ennui on just seeing it, I have escaped the eyes of such women and surrendered unto your divine feet.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.4. Sandendu

*sāndēndu men mulaiyār tadandōḷ puṇar inba veḷḷattuāḻndēn arunaragattu aḻundum payan padaittēnpōndēn puṇṇiyanē! unnai eydi en tīvinaigaḷtīrndēn ninnadaindēn tiruviṇṇagarānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruviṇṇagarānē – Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!; puṇṇiyanē – Oh my sukrutam (good deed)!; sāndu – vermilion; ēndum – wearing; men – tender; mulaiyār – women having bosoms; tadam – vast; tōḷ – with shoulders; puṇar – acquired by the embrace; inbam – bliss; veḷḷattu – in the ocean of; āḻndēn – (until now) I was immersed; aru – cruel; naragattu – in the hell of samsāram; aḻundum – being immersed eternally; payan – result; padaittēn – acquired; pōndēn – (without any reason) I got your divine feet as the means; unnai eydu – reaching you; en – my; tīvinaigaḷ – cruel sins; tīrndēn – got them to be eliminated; nin adaindēn – I attained you

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! Oh my sukrutam (good deed)! I was immersed in the ocean of bliss which is acquired by embracing the vast shoulders of the women having tender bosoms which are applied with vermilion; due to that I got the result of being eternally immersed in the hell of samsāram. While it is like this, I got your divine feet as the means. After attaining you, I got my cruel sins to be eliminated. After that, I attained you.

**sāndēndum …** – It is said as in “*tadamulaic ceyya sāndu*” (reddish paste on the vast bosoms), here vermilion is spoken about. When bhattar was asked “Why is āḻvār, who has abandoned worldly pleasures and engaged in bhagavat viśayam, speaking in a manner which will create desire even in those who are detached from worldly pleasures?” bhattar mercifully responded “tirumangai āḻvār is so eloquent that even if he has to waste water of a dam, he will explain it beautifully”. \[bhattar’s eloquence is glorified\] kidāmbi ammāḷ would many times quote siṟiyāṇḍān perumāḷ “One should not think that bhattar is also speaking the same words and meanings as I would do, there is special greatness for him; if I say “tūṇ” about a pillar which is in front of me, it will appear like a dead-wood; if he says the same think it will appear as a well grown tree”

**men mulaiyār** – Women whose bosoms cannot tolerate separation from the beloved. Their,

**tadam tōḷ …** – As one would be bound by the ropes (shoulders) with the mountains (bosoms) and pushed into the ocean (samsāra), I drowned into the blissful ocean of embracing their shoulders, like drowning into a bottomless pit; hence, I became unqualified for your grace. āḻvār, who truly realised bhagavān who is said in taittirīya upaniśat as “*ānandamaya*:” (embodiment of bliss), is now narrating this worldly enjoyment as “*inba veḷḷam*” (ocean of bliss); this is due to the thought that they blocked āḻvār from surrendering unto bhagavān, thus far. āḻvār is saying about this samsāra which is said as in jitantā stōtram “*ananta klēśa bhājanam*” (abode of unlimited sorrow), to be “*inba veḷḷam*“, seeing how this samsāra tormented him for a long time.

There is a purpose for this as well.

**aru naragattu …** – I who am born to enjoy his auspicious qualities forever, got the result of being a nitya samsāri, forever (until now). āḻvār is thinking “Attachment towards worldly pleasures is the seed for samsāra”.

**pōndēn** – Unlike those who perform karma yōga, reduce their sins by that, and then acquire jñānam and engage in jñāna yōga, and with the understanding of “This is good; this is bad” and reach bhagavān through bhakti, I reached bhagavān’s divine feet suddenly just as those residents of śrī maturā who went to sleep in the night and who woke up in śrī dvārakā by bhagavān’s grace.

When asked “All along, if you have not done any good deeds, how did you attain me?” āḻvār responds

**puṇṇiyanē** – You are my principal, good deed to attain you.

**unnai eydi** – Reaching you, who are superior to all, I eliminated all the sins which are hurdles for the attainment of the goal.

When asked “How did you attain me?” āḻvār responds

**tiruviṇṇagarānē** – Just as you presented yourself on the seashore as the refuge for śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān who was tormented and made refugeless by rāvaṇa, as you have arrived in tiruviṇṇagar, which is refuge for me who was tormented by the worldly pleasures in this samsāra, I escaped that samsāra and reached your divine feet.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.5. Marror deyvam

*maṟṟōr deyvam eṇṇēn unnai en manattu vaittuppeṟṟēn peṟṟaduvum piṟavāmai emperumān! vaṟṟā nīḷ kadal sūḻ ilangai irāvaṇanaicceṟṟāy! koṟṟavanē! tiruviṇṇagarānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṟṟā – perennial; nīr – having water; kadal – by the ocean; sūḻ – surrounded; ilangai – king of lankā; irāvaṇanai – rāvaṇa, the asura (monster); seṟṟāy – Oh one who killed!; koṟṟavanē – Oh king!; tiruviṇṇagarānē – Oh one who is residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!; maṟṟu ōr deyvam – any other dēvatā; eṇṇēn – I won’t consider as refuge; emperumān – Oh lord!; unnai – you, who are superior to all; en manattu – in my heart; vaittu – placed; peṟṟēn – attained (an impossible benefit); peṟṟaduvum – What did I get?; piṟavāmai – no more birth in this samsāram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who killed rāvaṇa, the asura who was the king of lankā which is surrounded by the ocean which is having perennial water! Oh king! Oh one who is residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! I won’t consider any other dēvatā as my refuge. Oh lord! I placed you, who are superior to all, in my heart and I attained the state of no more birth in this samsāram.

**maṟṟōr …** – Even while desiring, I will not consider the presence of another dēvatā as refuge.

**unnai en manattu vaittu …** – I, who am having non-rejection as the only reason, placed you who are superior to all, in my heart, attained an impossible feat.

When asked “What was that benefit you attained?” āḻvār responds

**peṟṟaduvum piṟavāmai emperumān** – I got rid of births which will qualify me to take refuge of other dēvatās. Now, I no longer have the qualification to even approach other dēvatās.

**vaṟṟā …** – Breaking the barriers which are unbreakable by anyone, oh one who uprooted rāvaṇa who pridefully thought “Am I not the controller of this town?”! āren’t you the one who effortlessly completes impossible tasks!

**koṟṟavanē** – Is uniting me with you, after eliminating my hurdles, as difficult as killing the very powerful rāvaṇa?

When asked “I destroyed lankā by first staying on the seashore. Where did I stay to eliminate your hurdles?” āḻvār responds

**tiruviṇṇagarānē** – The place where you have arrived and are standing for me is tiruviṇṇagar.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.6. Maiyon karum

*maiyoṇ karungadalum nilanum aṇivaraiyumseyya sudar iraṇḍum ivaiyāya ninnai nenjiluyyum vagai uṇarndēn uṇmaiyāl ini yādum maṟṟōrdeyvam piṟidaṟiyēn tiruviṇṇagarānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruviṇṇagarānē – Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!; mai – like black pigment; oḷ – beautiful; karu – having dark complexion; kadalum – ocean; nilanum – earth; aṇi – great; varaiyum – mountains; seyya – having the beauty of radiance; iraṇḍu sudarum – moon and sun, the two luminous entities; ivai – these; āya – one who is having them as subordinates; ninnai – you; uṇmaiyāl – truly; uyyum vagai – to become uplifted; nenjil – with the heart; uṇarndēn – I realised; ini – now; maṟṟu – further; piṟidu ōr – other than you; yādum – any entity; deyvam – as dēvatā who can be a refuge; aṟiyēn – I will not consider

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! You are the one who is having ocean which is having dark complexion like that of black pigment, earth, great mountains, the two luminous entities named moon and sun which are having the beauty of radiance, as your subordinates. I realised you truly with my heart to become uplifted. Now, I will not consider any entity other than you as dēvatā who can be a refuge.

**mai …** – The ocean which looks like an imitation of sarvēśvaran’s divine form, which appears beautiful like black pigment, the earth which is having such ocean as the fence, the anchoring mountains which appear to be nailing down the earth, the moon and sun which appear to be a pair of lamps which are lighting up these entities.

**ivaiyāya** – You, who are having the universe as your body, in this manner

**nenju …** – With my heart, I, who was as good as non-existing as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (as good as asat), started following you to become uplifted in the manner as said in “For this ātmā, you are the lord; this ātmā is completely subservient towards you”.

**ini yādum maṟṟōr …** – As one should think about an aspect in truth only and not in any other manner, I did not consider anyone else as refuge.

**tiruviṇṇagarānē** – In this manner, other than you, who are present in tiruviṇṇagar, I don’t even know the supreme lord (in any other state as in śrīvaikuṇṭam etc).

## 6.3.7. Vere kuruvadundu

*vēṟē kūṟuvaduṇḍu adiyēn viritturaikkumāṟē nī paṇiyādu adai nin tirumanattukūṟēn nenju tannāl guṇam koṇḍu maṟṟōr deyvamtēṟēn unnai allāl tiruviṇṇagarānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruviṇṇagarānē – Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!; adiyēn – I, who am a servitor; vēṟē – in a distinguished manner; kūṟuvadu uṇḍu – will give a message; virittu – elaborately; uraikkumāṟu – (for me) to explain; nī – you; paṇiyādu – not mercifully saying; nin tirumanattu – in your divine heart; adai – you should mercifully accept (whatever I requested); unnai allāl – other than you; maṟṟu ōr deyvam – any dēvatā; kūṟēn – I will not say with my mouth; guṇam koṇḍu – (in them) seeing a special quality; nenju tannāl – with my heart (them); tēṟēn – I will not believe (them to be refuge)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! I, who am a servitor, will give a message in a distinguished manner. Instead of letting me explain that elaborately, you should mercifully accept my brief message in your divine heart. I will not say with my mouth about any other dēvatā than you. I will not believe them to be my refuge with my heart, seeing any special quality in them.

**vēṟē …** – I am requesting to you in a manner that it is well taken by your divine heart and I get the result, instead of just being a message given in the assembly. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśikintā kāṇḍam 44.1 “*viśēśēṇa tu sugrīvō hanūmatyartam utavān*” (sugrīva māhārājar broached this topic specifically with hanūman). Though all the monkey leaders were sent to all directions, sugrīva mahārājar specifically looked at tiruvadi (hanūman) and gave the identity details and perumāḷ’s divine ring. Similar to that.

**viritturaikkum …** – My message cannot become like arjuna’s question; it should \[quickly\] conclude with “*bhagavān uvāca*” (bhagavān said). It cannot go on elaborately talking about various things as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.47](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-47/) “*karmaṇi ēvādikāras tē*” (Being a mumukśu, you can desire only for the true nitya (daily) naimittika (perioidic) karmas); you should speak \[quickly\] for me to say as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.73](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-73/) “*stitō’smi*” (standing firm, with realisation of truth). You should mercifully consider in your divine heart that you don’t mercifully speak to make me elaborately convey my message.

**kūṟēn …** – āḻvār is saying “I am an ananyagati” (one who has no other refuge) – I will not speak about other dēvatās through my mouth; not just that, I won’t consider with my heart that they have some speciality; even if superficially some greatness seems to be present in them, I will not consider that.

**unnai allāl tiruviṇṇagarānē** – You, who are superior to all, have arrived and are present in tiruviṇṇagar, and announced that you are the refuge. After this, I will not consider those who are your property as supreme.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.8. Mulindinda

*muḷindīynda vengadattu mūrip perungaḷiṟṟālviḷindīynda māmaram pōl vīḻndārai ninaiyādēaḷindōrnda sindai nin pāl adiyēṟkku vānulagamteḷindē enṟu eyduvadu? tiruviṇṇagarānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

muḷindu tīynda – (having trees which are) withered naturally and burnt \[and fallen down\]; vem – very cruel; kadattu – being present in forest; mūri – strong; peru – big; kaḷiṟṟāl – by the elephant; viḷindīynda – pushed down; mā – huge; marampōl – like a tree; vīḻndārai – those who got killed; ninaiyādē – instead of thinking; nin pāl – on your matters; teḷindu – having firm faith; aḷindu – having affection; ōrnda – having constant remembrance; sindai – having mind; adiyēṟku – for this servitor; vān ulagam – paramapadam; enṟu – when; eyduvadu – planning to give?; tiruviṇṇagarānē – Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! I, the servitor, am having firm faith on your matters and am affectionately having a mind with constant remembrance instead of thinking about those who got killed, like a huge tree being pushed down by strong, big elephant which is present in the cruel forest which is having trees which have withered naturally. When are you planning to give paramapadam for me?

**muḷindīynda …** – In the desert land (forest) which is having short trees like vāgai, veṇḍu which wither due to the heat of the earth and get burnt.

**mūrip perum kaḷiṟṟāl** – Some entities will be born and die immediately; other entities remain for a long time and will die due to exhaustion of their karma. Lowly entities like small insects etc will die soon after their birth; but indra et al (brahmā et al) will live for a long time and then will die; this is the nature of samsāram. Hence, instead of remaining here and thinking “some entities lived for long and then died, some died as soon as they were born”.

**aḷindu ōrnda …** – Having clarity towards you, having affection and having desire which is alert at all times towards you, for me who is not having any other refuge, when are you planning to grant mōkśam where there is no return to samsāram?

**tiruviṇṇagarānē** – For you, who have arrived here to transport me to there, it will be known when you are planning to do so.

Instead of a mango tree in a barren land, which gets pushed and knocked down by a heavier entity, instead of thinking about those who live in samsāram and die, having affection towards your highness and be alert and being clear to always desire you. For such me, when are you planning to grant liberation where there is no return? You have arrived to grant me that.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.9. Sollay tirumarva

*sollāy tirumārvā! unakkāgit toṇḍu pattanallēnai vinaigaḷ naliyāmai nambu nambīmallā! kudamādī! madusūdanē! ulagilsellā nallisaiyāy! tiruviṇṇagarānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

mal Ar – being very strong; kudam ādi – one who danced with pots; madusūdanē – oh one who killed the demon named madu!; ulagil – in this world; sellā – unseen (rare); nal isaiyāy – oh one who is having distinguished fame!; nambī – Oh one who is complete!; tiruviṇṇagarānē – Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar!; tirumārbā – Oh one who is having periya pirāttiyār on your divine chest!; sollāy – you should answer me; unakkāgi – being for you; toṇḍu pattu – one who is engaged in your service; nallēnai – me, who is distinguished; naliyāmai – to not torment; nambu – you should trust me and bless me

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh one who danced with pots, being strong and killed the demon named madu! Oh one who is having distinguished fame which is unseen in this world! Oh one who is complete! Oh one who is eternally residing in the divyadēśam named tiruviṇṇagar! Oh one who is having periya pirāttiyār on your divine chest! You should answer me. You should trust me who is distinguished due to being for you and engaged in your service and bless me to be not tormented.

**sollāy …** – Your highness should give an answer for that. You are the lakśmīpati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi) and hence you cannot escape from answering. Did I surrender to a brahmacāri emperumān, for you to remain undisturbed thinking “He is reaping the results of his sins”?

**unakkāgi …** – I, who am having distinguished nature to eternally serve the divine feet of your highness, who is śriya:pati. You should acknowledge me so that the sins which are staying far away from me do not torment me.

**nambī** – Your highness’ completeness makes lakshmi sambandam (relationship with śrī mahālakśmi) superfluous. You are so complete with auspicious qualities that you will argue with her as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.2 “*tannadiyār tiṟattagattut tāmaraiyāḷ āgilum sidakuraikku mēl ennadiyār adu seyyār*” (Even if śrī mahālakśmi complains about his devotees, he will argue with her saying ‘my devotees will not do anything wrong’ “).

**mal Ar kudam ādi** – With great strength, dancing with the pots in the four-way junction, oh one who freely gave your beauty to everyone! If he \[emperumān\] independently roams around, it is difficult to control him.

Alternative explanation,

If recited as **mallā kudamādi** – Oh strong one! Oh one who danced with pots to show your strength!

**madusūdanē** – Oh one who eliminated the demoniac clan along with their roots!

**ulagil sellā nallisaiyāy** – Oh one who is having fame which is not seen in this world!

**tiruviṇṇagarānē** – It appears that in his supreme state (in paramapadam), his qualities are conceivable. Since he leaves the materialistic people and is manifesting himself to nityasūris, his qualities will be conceivable there; only after arriving in tiruviṇṇagar to manifest himself to materialistic people that his qualities became inconceivable.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.10. Tarar malar

*tārār malark kamalat tadam sūḻnda taṇ puṟavilsīrār nedumaṟugil tiruviṇṇagarānaikārār puyal tadakkaik kaliyan oli mālaiārār ivai vallār avarkku allal nillāvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tār Ar – having petals; malar – having flowers; kamalam – having lotus; tadam – by the ponds; sūḻnda – surrounded; taṇ – cool; puṟavil – having places in the proximity; sīr Ar – having abundant wealth; nedu – long; maṟugil – having streets; tiruviṇṇagrānai – on appan who is mercifully present in tiruviṇṇagar; kār – in rainy season; Ar – filled with water; puyal – having magnanimity of a cloud; tadam – huge; kai – having hands; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; oli – mercifully spoke; mālai – in the form of pāsurams; ivai – these; ārār – anyone; vallār – if practiced; avarkku – for them; allal – sins; nillā – will not remain (will be destroyed)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

appan (bhagavān) is mercifully present in tiruviṇṇagar which is having long streets with abundant wealth, having places in the cool proximity, surrounded by ponds which are having lotus flowers with petals; tirumangai āḻvār who is having huge hands which are having the magnanimity of a cloud filled with water in the rainy season, mercifully spoke these pāsurams on such appan; for those who practiced these pāsurams, sins will not remain.

**tār Ar …** – tār – petal; being surrounded by ponds which are having lotus with flowers having petals. Alternative explanation; tār – radiance; that is, flower with radiance. All the places in the town are decorated with ponds with lotus flowers.

**sīr Ar …** – One who has arrived and residing in tiruviṇṇagar which is having long streets which are manifesting wealth, is glorified here.

**kār Ar …** – āḻvār whose hands grew big by giving to others like a cloud in the rainy season, which has absorbed water fully upto its neck, mercifully spoke this garland of tamiḻ pāsurams, to have beautiful tune. Those who are experts in these pāsurams. As said in viṣṇu darmam 8.3.7 “*aham vaktā bhavān śrōtā vācyō yōgō vimuktida:*” (I am the speaker; you are the listener; spoken subject is that which bestows liberation), when asked “Do those who learn these pāsurams have such great qualities \[like āḻvār to benefit like him\]?”

**Ar Ar …** – Their birth, knowledge can be in any manner. They only need to be free from the shortcoming in the taste to learn these pāsurams. They need not even pray “Whatever is obstructing the attainment of bhagavān, let that be removed”. Those sins will leave them on their own thinking “This is not the place for us”.

## 6.4 Kannum sulanru

## 6.4.1. Kannum sulanru

*kaṇṇum suḻanṟu pīḷaiyōdu īḷai vandu ēnginālpaṇṇin moḻiyār paiya nadamin ennāda munviṇṇum malaiyum vēdamum vēḷviyum āyinān naṇṇu naṟaiyūr nām toḻudum eḻu nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pīḷaiyōdu – with dirt in the eyes; kaṇṇum – eyes; suḻanṟu – becoming dizzy (and further); īḷai vandu – mucus overflowing; ēngināl – if one becomes weak (at that time); paṇ in – sweeter than beautiful tune; moḻiyār – women, who have speech; paiya – “slowly; nadamin – you walk away”; ennāda mun – before they say; viṇṇum – sky; malaiyum – mountains; āyinān – one who is having as prakāram (form); vēdamum āyinān – being the one who is revealed in vēdam; vēḷviyum āyinān – sarvēśvaran who is vorśipped through various rituals; naṇṇum – eternally residing with desire; naṟaiyūr – tirunaṟaiyūr; nenjamē – Oh heart!; nām – us; toḻudum – we will reach; eḻu – let us go

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

If one becomes weak with the eyes having dirt and become dizzy, and mucus is overflowing, women who have speech which is sweeter than beautiful tune will say “You walk away from here slowly”. Oh heart! Before that happens, we will reach tirunaṟaiyūr which is eternal, beloved abode of sarvēśvaran who is having sky and mountains as his prakāram (form), who is revealed in vēdam and vorśipped through various rituals. Let us go.

**kaṇṇum suḻanṟu …** – After losing the principal which is youth, which made a person roam around freely and enjoying, the fleshy eyes will become incapable to clearly see any object and be dizzy. Just as dust/dirt will gather when there is a flood, the dirt in the eyes gather together. Further, mucus forms and will make the person weak to even complete the sentence which was begun. At that time, the girls who can speak sweeter than a tune, will tell “Why don’t you walk away slowly (as you have aged)?”. Before they disregard the person in this manner.

**viṇṇum …** – ākāśam (sky/ether) which came first among the panca bhūtams which are causes for subsequent creation, mountain which is a transformation of earth which came subsequently. āḻvār includes ākāśa as a sample for causal elements and mountain for effectual elements. With these two, bhagavān being present with the entire creation as his form is explained.

**vēdamum** – In this manner, bhagavān who is having the entire creation as his form, is the one who is revealed in vēdam. cāndōjña upaniśat says “*sarvam kalvidam brahma*” (Whatever we see here is brahmam, i.e., brahmam’s body).

**vēḷviyum … –** bhagavān who is the goal of all ritualistic worship which are spoken in such vēdam, has arrived and is residing in tirunaṟaiyūr for the protection of samsāris (materialistic people). Let us reach that tirunaṟaiyūr. Please agree and cooperate with me. Thus says āḻvār to his own divine heart.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.4.2. Kongun kulalar

*konguṇ kuḻalār kūdi irundu sirittu nīringen? irumi embāl vandadenṟu igaḻāda muntingaḷ eri kāl senjudarāyavan tēsudainangaḷ naṟaiyūr nām toḻudum eḻu nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

konguṇ – very fragrant; kuḻalār – women who have hair; kūdi irundu – gather as a crowd; sirittu – laugh and ridicule; nīr – “You; irumi – coughing; ingu – here; em pāl vandu – coming close to us; en – why?”; enṟu – saying; igaḻāda mun – before they disregard you; tingaḷ – moon; eri – fire; kāl – wind; sem – reddish; sudar – sun; āyavan – the abode of one who is having as prakāram (body); tēsu udai – radiant; nangaḷ – our goal; naṟaiyūr – tirunaṟaiyūr; nenjamē – Oh heart!; nām – us; toḻudum – we will reach; eḻu – let us go

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Women, who have very fragrant hair, would gather as a crowd, would laugh and ridicule you saying “Why are you coughing here and coming close to us?” Oh heart! Before they disregard you in this manner, we will reach our radiant goal, tirunaṟaiyūr, which is the eternal, beloved abode of sarvēśvaran who is having moon, fire, wind and reddish sun as his prakāram (form). Let us go.

**konguṇ kuḻalār …** – kongu – honey; or kongu – fragrance. Women with very fragrant hair. When the man had wealth and youth, they will not unite together due to fights \[competing for him\], but once he lost them, they gather together to insult him and laugh at him.

**nīr ingu en** … – Before you listen to their insulting words such as “Don’t you know about yourself? Don’t you know about us? Why did you come here? Is this place an apt one for you to come?”

**tingaḷ …** – The abode is radiant due to being pursued by sarvēśvaran who is the protector and who created entities which help the universe.

**nangaḷ naṟaiyūr nām toḻudum eḻu nenjamē** – Let us go and approach his abode where he is present for us.

## 6.4.3. Kongar kulalar

*kongār kuḻalār kūdi irundu sirittu emmaiengōlam aiyā! en? inik kāṇbadu ennāda munsengōl valavan tān paṇindu ēttit tigaḻumūrnangōn naṟaiyūr nām toḻudum eḻu nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kongu Ar – very fragrant; kuḻalār – women who are having hair; kūdi irundu – having gathered together; sirittu – ridicule and laugh at him; aiyā – “Oh old man!; ini – After becoming old; emmai – us; em kōlam – our decorations (beauty); en kāṇbadu – Why are you seeing?”; ennāda mun – before they say in this manner; sengōl – reign; valavan tān – one (cōḻa king) who was prideful and could conduct (after having eliminated his pride); paṇindu – surrendered to emperumān; ētti – praised (and got his desire fulfilled); tigaḻum – one who is shining; Ur – being the divyadēśam; nam kōn – the abode where our lord is mercifully present; naṟaiyūr – tirunaṟaiyūr; nenjamē – Oh heart!; nām – us; toḻudum – we will reach; eḻu – let us go

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

āḻvār says to his heart – one (cōḻa king) who was prideful and could conduct his reign, became pure and surrendered to emperumān in this divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr, praised him and became shining due to that. Women who are having very fragrant hair, having gathered together, will ridicule and laugh at him saying “Oh old man! After becoming old, why are seeing us and our decorations?” Oh heart! Before the women say in this manner, let us reach the abode, tirunaṟaiyūr where our lord is mercifully present. Let us go.

**kongār …** – The women, who are having very fragrant hair, gathered together and laughed.

**em kōlam …** – You are not thinking about your state any more. Why should you see our decorations any more? Before you hear such insulting words,

**sem kōl …** – The egoistic king gave up his pride and fell at your divine feet, praised you, got what he wanted for his livelihood and subsequently became uplifted too – such abode.

**nam kōn naṟaiyūr …** – It is the abode which is the shade for those who have become weak. Let us go and surrender in his abode where he is mercifully standing to fulfil everyone’s desires.

## 6.4.4. Kombum aravamum

*kombum aravamum valliyum venṟa nuṇṇēridaivambuṇ kuḻalār vāsal adaittu igaḻāda munsembon kamuginam tān kaniyum seḻum sōlai sūḻnamban naṟaiyūr nām toḻudum eḻu nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kombum – vanjik kombu (a thin pole); aravum – snake; valliyum – creeper; venṟu – being victorious (having more weakness than they); nuṇ – being slender; ēr – beautiful; idai – having waist; vambu uṇ – very fragrant; kuḻalār – women who have hair; vāsal adaittu – (pushing him out) shutting the main door; igaḻāda mun – before they insult him; kamugu inam tān – areca trees which are in groves; sem pon – like reddish gold; kaniyum – giving fruits; seḻum – being rich; sōlai sūḻ – surrounded by orchards; namban – the eternal abode of sarvēśvaran, the trustworthy person; naṟaiyūr – tirunaṟaiyūr; nenjamē – Oh heart!; nām – us; toḻudum – we will reach; eḻu – let us go

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Women whose slender, beautiful waists are victorious over pole, snakes and creepers and are having very fragrant hair will insult the man by pushing him out and shutting the main door on him. āḻvār says – Oh heart! Before that happens, we will reach the eternal abode of sarvēśvaran, the trustworthy one, that is tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by rich orchards which are having areca trees which are in groves and are giving reddish gold like fruits. Let us go.

**kombum …** – Women who are having waists which will defeat a thin pole, snake, creeper etc, and are having very fragrant hair.

**vāsal …** – Previously they loved him, but as he has become worthless now, they will push him out and shut the door on him. But due to desire, he will remain there without leaving; to make him feel ashamed and leave, they will inform that he does not have any qualification to enjoy and ridicule him. Before hearing such insulting words.

**sem pon …** – It seems that everything in that abode is well ripened. The town is surrounded by orchards filled with areca trees which yield reddish fruits which resemble reddish gold. It will resemble paramapadam which is abode reached by muktātmās.

**namban …** – Let us approach tirunaṟaiyūr where one, who is trustworthy to be approached at all situations, is residing.

## 6.4.5. Vilangum kayalum

*vilangum kayalum vēlum oṇ kāviyum venṟa kaṇsalam koṇḍa sollār tāngaḷ sirittu igaḻāda munmalangum varālum vāḷaiyum pāy vayal sūḻ tarunalangoḷ naṟaiyūr nām toḻudum eḻu nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vilangum – young deer; kayalum – (jumping) fish; vēlum – (sharp) spear; oḷ – beautiful (reddish); kāviyum – sengaḻunīr (a kind of lotus) flower; venṟa – defeated; kaṇ – having eyes; salam koṇḍa sollār tāngaḷ – women who (previously pursued) are having mischievous words, now; siritttu – ridicule; igaḻāda mun – before they disregard; malangum – fish named malangu; varālum – fish named varāl; vāḷai – fish named vāḷai; pāy – (joyfully) jumping; vayal – by fertile fields; sūḻ taru – surrounded; nalam koḷ – having the goodness of fulfilling desires; naṟaiyūr – tirunaṟaiyūr; nenjamē – Oh heart!; nām – us; toḻudum – we will reach; eḻu – let us go

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Women whose eyes defeated those of young deer, fish, spear and beautiful sengaḻunīr flowers will now have mischievous words for him. āḻvār says – Oh heart! Before such women ridicule and disregard us, we will surrender unto sarvēśvaran’s beloved abode tirunaṟaiyūr which is our radiant goal and which is surrounded by fish named malangu, varāl and vāḷai, and is having the goodness of fulfilling the desires. Let us go.

**vilangum …** – For the eyes’ youthfulness deer, cheerfulness kayal fish, sharpness spear and reddiśness lotus flower are compared. Further, having the eyes which defeated all of those compared items. Women who won’t ever speak favourably and instead will always speak in a mischievous way. Before such women ridicule and disregard.

**malangum …** – Even the animals which are present there will not have sorrow of “we have not attained this” and are happily living due to attaining what is desired by them. Thus, we will reach tirunaṟaiyūr, the divine abode, which is having the goodness of the residents living joyfully with the attainment of their goal instead of not attaining what they need.

## 6.4.6. Minner idaiyar

*minnēr idaiyār vētkaiyai māṟṟi irundu en nīr irumi embāl vandadu? enṟu igaḻāda mun tonnīr ilangai malanga vilangeri ūttinān nannīr naṟaiyūr nām toḻudum eḻu nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

min ēr – matching lightning (very subtle); idaiyār – women having waist; vētkaiyai – love (which was there before); māṟṟiyirundu – being changed now; nīr – “You, who are old; irumi – coughing; en pāl vandadu – coming to my place; en – for what purpose?”; enṟu – saying this way; igaḻāda mun – before insulting; tol nīr – surrounded by ancient ocean; ilangai – lankā; malanga – to suffer; vilangu – with hanūman; eriyūttinān – one who burnt, his; nal nīr – having abundance of good water (which eliminates the heat); naṟaiyūr – tirunaṟaiyūr; nenjamē – Oh heart!; nām – us; toḻudum – we will reach; eḻu – let us go

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Women having waist matching lightning and having now changed from the loving state, would say “For what purpose did you, who are old and coughing, come to my place?”. āḻvār says – Oh heart! Before such women insult in this way, let us reach tiruaṟaiyūr which is having abundance of good water and which is the abode of sarvēśvaran who made lankā, which is surrounded by ancient ocean, suffer in the hands of hanūman and burnt it through him. Let us go.

**minnēr …** – Women who are having waist which is matching lightning, giving up their loving attitude towards him, will ask “Is this cough the gift you brought us? Why did you come here?” Before they speak in this indifferent manner.

**tonnīr …** – One who set fire to lankā which is having ocean as the moat, to make seven people wear one garment. Alternative explanation – set fire in a shining manner. When it is recited as vilangu – he set fire through hanūman; when it is recited as ilangu – fire was pale since it was allowed to burn only as much as it is required to boil rice and now having taken shelter of śrī rāma, it burnt to its best ability and became shining because of that.

**nal nīr …** – Let us reach tirunaṟaiyūr which is having abundance of water to eliminate the heat of everyone. Let us reach tirunaṟaiyūr where the most powerful sarvēśvaran has arrived and is residing to eliminate our hurdles with their traces, just as cakravartit tirumagan, who killed rāvaṇa and remained as the refuge for vibhīśaṇāḻvān.

*villēr nudalār vētkaiyai māṟṟic cirittu ivanpollān tiraindān ennum puṟanuṟai kētpadan munsollār maṟai nāngu ōdi ulagil nilāyavarnallār naṟaiyūr nām toḻudum eḻu nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vil ēr – matching a bow (having the shape of a bow); nudalār – women, having forehead; vētkaiyai – love (which was there previously); māṟṟi – abandoned; sirittu – ridiculed; ivan – “This old man; pollān – bad (vomaniser); tiraindān – having broken body”; ennum – saying; puṟan urai – indifferent words; kētpadan mun – before they are heard; sol Ar – having fresh words; nāngu maṟai ōdi – learning four vēdams; ulagil – in the world; nilāyavar – those who can spread (establish); nallār – inhabited by brāhmaṇas who are having distinguished forms; naṟaiyūr – tirunaṟaiyūr; nenjamē – Oh heart!; nām – us; toḻudum – we will reach; eḻu – let us go

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Women, having forehead which is matching a bow, having now changed from the loving state, would say “This old man is bad and having broken/weakened body” and ridicule him and would say words which show their indifference towards him. āḻvār says – Oh heart! Before such words are heard, let us reach tirunaṟaiyūr which is inhabited by brāhmaṇas who are having distinguished forms and have learnt four vēdams which are having fresh words and spread them in the world. Let us go.

**vil ēr …** – Women who have foreheads which match a bow. Previously they would remain as if non-existing when a person \[who they desired\] was not attained; abandoning such situation, not hiding that they have abandoned their love for him and still laughing at him.

**pollān …** – Those who previously praised his physical beauty and its consistent nature, are now referring to him as “He is pollān (one never keeps his word), tiraindān (having broken body)”. Before such lowly words are heard.

**sollār …** – Just as there are rules for letters in words, there are rules for words in sentences as well. Such vēdams.

**ōdi …** – Learning in the proper/traditional way of the teacher reciting first and the student repeating it subsequently. Instead of this happening occasionally,

**ulagil nilāyavar** – Being the propagator/establiśer of vēdam, as their main quality. Instead of forgetting the familiarity in vēdam and having shortcomings in their good conduct, it is the abode of those who give great importance to good conduct. Let us go and reach there – says āḻvār to his heart.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.4.8. Valon kan

*vāḷoṇ kaṇ nallār tāngaḷ madanan enṟār tammaikēṇmingaḷ eeḷaiyōdu ēngu kiḻavan ennāda munvēḷvum viḻavum veediyil enṟum aṟāda ūrnāḷum naṟaiyūr nām toḻudum eḻu nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāḷ – sharp like the weapon, sword; oḷ – beautiful; kaṇ – having eyes; nallār – beautiful women; tāngaḷ – them (who are ridiculing now); madanan – “He is cupid”; enṟār tammai – (seeing) those men who were said to be (previously); eeḷaiyōdu – “(Coughing) With mucus; ēngu – becoming weak; kiḻavan – (this) old man; kēṇmingaḷ – ask him (where did he come?)”; ennāda mun – before saying (to the girls who are in their proximity); vēḷvum – worship in the form of yajña etc; viḻavum – festivals; veediyil – on the streets; enṟum – at all times; aṟāda Ur – tirunaṟaiyūr, the abode where it never stops; nāḷum – every day; nenjamē – Oh heart!; nām – us; toḻudum – we will reach; eḻu – let us go

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Beautiful women who are having beautiful eyes which are sharp like the weapon, sword, who were speaking about the men previously as “He is cupid” will speak about those same men “Ask that old man who is coughing with mucus and becoming weak, as to where did he come?” āḻvār says to his heart – oh heart! Everyday, we will reach tirunaṟaiyūr, the abode where the worship of bhagavān in the form of yajña etc and the festivals on the streets do not stop ever. Let us go.

**vāḷoṇ kaṇ …** – Women who have eyes which will knock out men just in one glance and whose eyes have all the necessary goodness. Such women, who were praising a person as “He is cupid” when he had youth and wealth, now look at the others in proximity and say “Ask that old man, what is he doing with the cough and mucus?” Before that happens.

**eeḷaiyōdu ēngu kiḻavan – ungaḷ – kēḷ** – Previously the women were desiring for him saying “He is mine”, but now they see each other and say “He is yours, He is yours”.

**vēḷvum viḻavum …** – nityōtsavam (daily festivals) and vaidika samārādanam (vēdam based rituals) are eternally continuing, on a daily basis.

**nāḷum …** – Until we reach paramapadam and enjoy eternally there, with this body, let us reach tirunaṟaiyūr which is similar to paramapahdam, and enjoy there.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.4.9. Kani serndu

*kani sērndu ilangu nal vāyavar kādanmai vittida kuni sērndudalam kōlil taḷarndu iḷaiyāda mun pani sēr visumbil pāl madi kōḷ viduttān idam nani sēr naṟaiyūr nām toḻudum eḻu nenjamē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kani sērndu – matching kōvai fruit (a reddish fruit); ilangu – shining; nal – beautiful; vāyavar – women having lips; kādanmai – desire (towards him); vittida – as they abandon (further); kuni sērndu – having hunch back; udalam – the body; taḷarndu – being broken; kōlil – the stick (which is held as a support) (being weak to even hold it); iḷaiyāda mun – before becoming weak; visumbil – roaming in the sky; pani sēr – having cool rays; pāl madi – moon which is shining like milk; kōḷ – waning; viduttān – sarvēśvaran who eliminated; idam – being the abode; naṟaiyūr – tirunaṟaiyūr; nenjamē – Oh heart!; nām – us; toḻudum – we will reach; eḻu – let us go

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Women having shining, beautiful lips which are like kōvai fruit (a reddish fruit) will abandon their desire for him who is having a hunch-back in his body which is broken and becoming weak to even hold the stick which is for his support. āḻvār says to his heart – oh heart! Before this happens, we will reach tirunaṟaiyūr which is the abode of sarvēśvaran who eliminated the waning of moon which is shining like milk and is having cool rays and is roaming in the sky. Let us go.

**kani …** – Women who are having lips which are shining like kōvai fruit, will abandon their love towards him.

**kuni sēr …** – Previously he would have stood straight brimming with pride; now, hunch-back has become natural for him and will be unable to stand straight and perform any tasks. Subsequently, he will get a stick for support; but since he would be unable to hold it tight, neither it would support him nor he would be its support. Before becoming weakened, in this manner.

**pani sēr …** – The abode where sarvēśvaran who eliminated the waning disease of the moon which illuminated the whole sky, has arrived and is residing.

**nani …** – Let us, who are his servitors, go and reach tirunaṟaiyūr which is famous for being accepted for the sake of pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi). nani – fame.

## 6.4.10. Piraiser nudalar

*piṟai sēr nudalār pēṇudal nammai ilāda munnaṟai sēr poḻil sūḻ naṟaiyūr toḻu nenjamē! enṟakaṟaiyār nedu vēl mangaiyar kōn kalikanṟi solmaṟavādu uraippavar vānavarkku innarasu āvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

piṟai sēr – matching the crescent (of moon); nudalār – women who have forehead; nammai – on us; pēṇudal ilāda mun – before they abandon their love and ridicule us; naṟai sēr – honey flooding; poḻil sūḻ – surrounded by orchards; naṟaiyūr – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; nenjamē – Oh heart!; toḻu – try to reach; enṟa – one who mercifully said; kaṟai Ar – very stained; nedu vēl – having long spear; mangaiyar – for those who are in tirumangai region; kōn – one who is the lord; kali kanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār’s; sol – these ten pāsurams which are divine words; maṟavādu – without being distracted; uraippavar – those who can recite; vānavarkku – the abode of nityasūris; in arasu – beautiful (invincible) king; āvar – will become

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh heart! Before the women, who have foreheads matching the crescent, abandon their love towards us and ridicule us, try to reach the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by orchards where honey is flooding. In these ten pāsurams, tirumangai āḻvār who is the lord of tirumangai region, who is having long, very stained spear, mercifully said in this manner, which are his divine words. Those can recite these pāsurams without being distracted, will become beautiful king of the abode of nityasūris.

**piṟai sēr** … – Women who have forehead matching the crescent – before they discard love towards us.

**naṟai sēr …** – Uniting with his divine heart saying “Let us reach tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by orchards filled with honey.

**kaṟai Ar …** – tirumangai āḻvār is having in his hand, a long spear which is stained due to not having time to wipe off the blood stains after eliminating the enemies. One who is the leader of the tirumangai region. Mercifully spoken by him.

**maṟavādu …** – Those who can recite learn/recite these pāsurams without forgetting, even while women, who are having such beautiful youth are present, as target for the eyes. They will become the controller of the abode of nityasūris who always remain at twenty five years of age. They remain with the same form as his, at all times. due to his granting of sāmyāpatti mōkśam \[equivalence in 8 divine qualities\].

## 6.5 Kalanga munnir

## 6.5.1. Kalanga munnir

*kalanga munnīr kadaindu amudam koṇḍu imaiyōrtuḷangal tīra nalgu sōdic cudarāyavalangai āḻi idangaic cangam udaiyānūrnalangoḷ vāymai andaṇar vāḻum naṟaiyūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

munnīr – ocean; kalanga – to agitate; kadaindu – churned; amudam koṇḍu – fetch amrutam (from it); imaiyōr – dēvatās’; tuḷangam – worry; tīra – to eliminate; nalgu – giving it (to them); sōdi sudar āya – being radiant (due to that); valam kai – in his right hand; āḻi – sudarśana cakram; idam kai – in his left hand; sangam – śrī pāncajanyam; udaiyān – sarvēśvaran who is having; Ur – divyadēśam; nalam koḷ – having goodness of truth; vāymai – those who are having acts of speech; andaṇar – brāhmaṇas; vāḻum – eternally residing; naṟaiyūr – divyadēśam known as tirunaṟaiyūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divyadēśam (divine abode) of sarvēśvaran who is having sudarśana cakram in his right hand and śrī pāncajanyam in his left hand, and who churned the kśīrābdi (milk ocean) to agitate it, fetch amrutam from it and give it to dēvatās to eliminate their worry and hence became radiant, is the divyadēśam known as tirunaṟaiyūr, where brāhmaṇas, who have the acts of speech which is having goodness of truth, are eternally residing.

**kalanga …** – Churned the ocean to bring out the aquatic beings to the top along with the sand from the ocean bed, fetch the amrutam and give it to dēvatās who were tormented by asuras. He did not do this for the sake of his divine consorts or his dear devotees, but for dēvatās who say as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 16.14](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-14/) “*īśvarō’ham*” (I control everyone with my ability) after receiving the nectar. While he did all the efforts, he granted the enjoyment of drinking the nectar to them and once they consumed it, he considered it to be his own benefit and became radiant,

**valam kai …** – The abode where sarvēśvaran who is having the divine weapons to eliminate the enemies of those who are enjoying the nectar.

**nalam koḷ …** Those who are experts in vēdam which shows the truth as it is; alternative explanation – the abode which is inhabited by brāhamaṇas who are truthful.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.5.2. Munaiyar siyamagi

*munaiyār sīyamāgi avuṇan muraṇ mārvampunai vāḷ ugirāl pōḻpada īrnda punidanūrsinaiyār tēmām sendaḷir kōdik kuyil kūvumnanaiyār sōlai sūḻndu aḻagāya naṟaiyūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

munai – in battle; Ar – matching; sīyamāgi – being narasimha; avuṇan – hiraṇyāsura’s; muraṇ – strong; mārvam – chest; punai – having; vāḷ – radiant; ugirāl – with the nails; pōḻ pada – to be split into two; īrnda – tore; punidan – the pure one’s; Ur – abode; kuyil – cuckoos; sinai Ar – pregnant (i.e. well grown); tēmām – sweet mango trees’; sem taḷir – reddish sprouts; kōdi – pecked; kūvum – making noise; nanai Ar – filled with freshly blossomed flowers; sōlai – by orchards; sūḻndu – surrounded; aḻagāya – being beautiful; naṟaiyūr – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divine abode of the pure sarvēśvaran who incarnated as narasimha matching the battle skills of hiraṇyāsura who is a match in battle skills for bhagavān and who tore his strong chest with the radiant nails to have his body split into two, is the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr which is beautiful due to being surrounded by orchards which are filled with freshly blossomed flowers and where cuckoos are pecking the reddish sprouts of the well grown sweet mango trees and are making noise after pecking those trees.

**munai Ar …** – narasimha will grow if he hears about battle; hiraṇya who cannot be vanquished in the battle and is having chest which is enriched with boons; narasimha with his beautiful, radiant nails which look like decoration for him, tore hiraṇya’s chest; the abode of such bhagavān who is having the purity of helping his devotee at the time of the request from the devotee. Having the purity of doing it himself instead of sending his servitors to do it.

**sinai Ar …** – Cuckoos which drank the honey from the sweet mango tree which are well grown, would peck on the sprouts to change the taste in their mouth; they would make sound just as muktātmās are singing sāma gānam.

**nanai Ar …** – The beautiful tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by orchards which are always in the spring-mode having fresh flowers. nanai – flower bud.

## 6.5.3. Anaip puravi

*ānaip puravit tērodu kālāḷ aṇi koṇḍasēnait togaiyaic cādi ilangai seṟṟānūrmīnait taḻuvi vīḻndu eḻum maḷḷarkku alamandunānap pudalil āmai oḷikkum naṟaiyūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ānai – elephants; puravi – horses; tērodu – with chariots; kālāḷ – foot soldiers; aṇi koṇḍa – having a special arrangement; sēnait togaiyai – the army; sādi – destroyed; ilangai – lankā; seṟṟān Ur – the abode of the one who destroyed; mīnai – fish; taḻuvi – embraced (with two hands, to catch); vīḻndu – falling down (being pushed); eḻum – getting up (with the desire to catch again); maḷḷarkku – for the farmers; alamarndu – frightened; nānam – turmeric’s; pudalil – in the bushes; āmai – tortoise; oḷikkum – hiding; naṟaiyūr – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abode of the one, who destroyed lankā by destroying the special arrangement of the army with elephants, horses, chariots and foot soldiers, is the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the tortoise become frightened and is hiding in the turmeric bushes, seeing the farmers who embraced the fish to catch them and end up falling down to get up again to catch the same.

**ānai …** – rāvaṇa’s rising army is spoken out in proper sequence. Sending elephants which look like walking mountains, and then sending horses, and then decorating the army with chariots and finally sending the foot soldiers for their protection. The abode where the one who tormented and destroyed such group of army and destroyed lankā.

**mīnai …** – The fish there are grown like mountains due to the nature of the land; the farmers who catch them will embrace them with both hands; still, they will slip out of such farmers to push them down; one, who fell like that, will eagerly try to catch the fish again; the tortoise which sees that becomes frightened and hides in the turmeric bush, in the boundary \[of the water body\]. nānam – turmeric. āltenatively nānam indicates certain plants which carry flowers such as karumugai, picci etc. maḷḷar – farmer.

## 6.5.4. Uriyar venney

*uṟiyār veṇṇey uṇḍu uralōdum kattuṇḍuveṟiyār kūndal pinnai poruttu ān venṟānūrpoṟiyār manjjñai pūmboḻil tōṟum nadamādanaṟu nāṇ malar mēl vaṇḍu isai pādum naṟaiyūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṟi – in ropes suspended from the ceiling; Ar – preserved in large quantity; veṇṇey – butter; uṇḍu – mercifully consumed; uralōdu – with the mortar; kattuṇḍum – bound (by mother yaśōdā); veṟi Ar – abundantly fragrant; kūndal – having hair; pinnai poruttu – for the sake of nappinnaip pirātti; An – (seven) bulls; venṟān Ur – the abode of the one who defeated and killed; poṟi Ar – having dots (multi-coloured); manjñai – peacocks; pū poḻil tōṟum – in all the orchards which are having flowers; nadamāda – as they are dancing; vaṇḍu – beetles; naṟu – abundantly fragrant; nāḷ – freshly blossomed; malar mēl – on the lotus flowers; isai pādum – will sing (matching their dance); naṟaiyūr – the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abode of the one who mercifully consumed the butter which was preserved in large quantity in the ropes suspended from the ceiling and because of that bound to the mortar and who defeated and killed the seven bulls for the sake of nappinnaip pirātti who is having abundantly fragrant hair, is the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where peacocks, having dots, are dancing in all the orchards which are having flowers and where beetles on the abundantly fragrant, freshly blossomed lotus flowers will sing according to their dance.

**uṟiyār …** – Butter which was preserved in the ropes which are suspended on the ceiling in a secretive manner, was mercifully consumed by kriṣṇa to make everyone wonder “Did some dēvatā come and consume the butter?” But then they will determine that none other than kriṣṇa would have stolen it and will bind him to the mortar; since he cannot sustain without the butter which has the physical contact of his devotees, he would remain bound; when he remains bound there, it will be difficult to differentiate between the mortar and kriṣṇa – he will remain in such manner.

**veṟiyār …** – For the sake of nappinnaip pirātti who is having abundantly fragrant hair, he killed the seven bulls; the abode of such kriṣṇa.

**poṟiyār …** – In the gardens which are fully with blossomed flowers, the multi-coloured peacocks will dance.

**naṟu nāṇ …** – The beetles which entered into the freshly blossomed lotus flowers, will sing matching the steps placed by the peacocks.

## 6.5.5. Vidaiyel venru

*vidai ēḻ venṟu men tōḷ āyccikku anbanāynadaiyāl ninṟa marudam sāytta nādanūrpedaiyōdu annam peyvaḷaiyār tam pin senṟunadaiyōdiyali nāṇi oḷikkum naṟaiyūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēḻ vidai – seven bulls; venṟu – killed; men tōḷ – having tender shoulders; āyccikku – towards nappinnaip pirātti; anbanāy – having love; ninṟa – standing on the way; marudam – the maruda tree; nadaiyāl – with his crawling; sāytta – pushed to fell; nādan Ur – the abode of the protector; annam – swans; pediayōdu – being together with their female spouse; pey – dense; vaḷaiyār tam – women who are wearing bangles, their; pin senṟu – following them; nadaiyōdu – matching their walk; iyali – roamed around (and being unable to walk like them); nāṇi – becoming shy; oḷikkum – hiding; naṟaiyūr – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abode of the protector who killed seven bulls due to his love towards nappinnaip pirātti who is having tender shoulders, and who pushed the maruda tree which was standing on the way to fell it, with his crawling, is the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the swans which are together with their female spouse are following the women who are wearing bangles in a dense manner, trying to match their walk and being unable to walk like them, are becoming shy and hiding.

**vidai ēḻ …** – For the sake of nappinnaip pirātti who is having beautiful shoulders which are tender, kriṣṇa killed the seven bulls, due to his love towards her.

**nadai …** – The abode of the protector felled the maruda trees which were possessed by demons, along with their roots, with his walk which is in the form of crawling.

**pedai …** – The swan along with its female spouse, observing the beautiful walk of the women there, will follow such women to walk in the same manner; since it could not walk the same way, it will become shy and will hide there.

## 6.5.6. Paguvay vanpey

*paguvāy vanpēy kongai suvaittu āruyir uṇḍupuguvāy ninṟa pōdagam vīḻap porudānūrneguvāy neydal pūmadu māndik kamalattinnaguvāy malar mēl annam uṟangum naṟaiyūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pagu vāy – having huge mouth; van – having cruel heart; pēy – pūtanā who was a monster; kongai – bosom; suvaittu – suckled; Ar uyir – (her) precious vital air; uṇḍu – consumed; puguvāy – in the entrance; ninṟa – present; pōdagam – kuvalayāpeedam, the elephant; vīḻa – to kill; porudān Ur – one who fought the battle, his abode; negu vāy – having blossomed mouth; neydal pū – in the karu neydal flowers \[blue-coloured water lily\]; madu – honey; māndi – drank; nagu vāy – having blossomed mouth; kamalattin – lotus’; malar mēl – in the flowers; annam – swans; uṟangum – sleeping; naṟaiyūr – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa consumed the vital air by suckling the bosom of pūtanā, the monster who was having huge mouth and cruel heart; he fought the battle to kill kuvalayāpeedam, the elephant which was present in the entrance; the abode of such kriṣṇa is the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the swans drank the honey from the karu neydal flowers which are having blossomed mouth and are sleeping in the flowers of the lotus plant having blossomed mouth.

**pagu vāy …** – Having a huge mouth matching her huge form, having cruel heart to not have compassion even after nearing him, pūtanā’s bosom was suckled by kriṣṇa and through that he destroyed her vital air.

**puguvāy …** – kamsa made kuvalayāpeedam to stand at the entrance with the plan of getting kriṣṇa killed through that and subsequently pretending that it happened by mistake and crying for that; but kriṣṇa, the brave one, fought it to make it fall down as a mountain breaks down. The abode of such kriṣṇa.

**negu vāy …** – After drinking the honey from the neydal flower, the swan will treat the well-blossomed lotus flower as its bed, go there and sleep in it.

## 6.5.7. Mundu nulum

*mundu nūlum muppuri nūlum munnīnda andaṇāḷan piḷḷaiyai annānṟu aḷittānūr pondil vāḻum piḷḷaikkāgip puḷḷōdinanduvārum paimbunal vāvi naṟaiyūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mundu – ancient (apauruśēya – unautored); nūlum – vēda śāstram; muppuri nūlum – yajñōpavītam \[sacred thread\]; mun īnda – previously gave; andaṇāḷan – sāndīpani’s; piḷḷaiyai – son; annānṟu – when he was swallowed by the ocean; aḷittān Ur – the abode of the one who brought back and gave; puḷ – birds; bondil – in the tree holes; vāḻum – living; piḷḷaikkāgi – to feed the little ones; ōdi – run to distant places; nandu – snails; vārum – gathering; pai punal – having pure water; vāvi – having ponds; naṟaiyūr – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abode of the one who brought back and gave the son of sāndīpani, who gave yajñōpavītam and the ancient vēda śāstram to him, when the boy was swallowed by the ocean, is the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the birds which run to distant places to fetch food for their little ones living in the tree holes, gather the snails which are gathered in the ponds having pure water.

**mundu nūl …** – To make kriṣṇa familiar with the subject, first sāndīpani gave the alphabets of vēdam, which is apauruśēyam and then gave upanayana samskāram etc which give qualification to learn vēdam. andaṇāḷan – sāndīpani. As his son was swallowed by the ocean, kriṣṇa retrieved him. The abode of such kriṣṇa. The abode of the one who would fix the losses of those who lost anything.

**pondil vāḻum …** – For their little ones which are living in the tree holes, the birds will go to distant places and gather the shells thinking that they will feed the apt ones for their little ones. nandu – nattai – snail.

## 6.5.8. Vellaip puravi

*veḷḷaip puravit tēr visayaṟkāy viṟal viyūgamviḷḷac cinduk kōn viḻa ūrnda vimalanūrkoḷḷaik koḻu mīn uṇ kurugu ōdip pedaiyōdumnaḷḷak kamalat tēṟal ugukkum naṟaiyūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

veḷḷaip puravi – having white horses; tēr – having chariot; visayaṟkāy – for arjunan; viṟal – strong; viyūgam – sea of army; viḷḷa – to be broken into pieces; sinduk kōn – jayadrata, the king of sindu dēśam; viḻa – to be killed; ūrnda – one who rode; vimalan Ur – the abode of pure kriṣṇa; koḷḷai – abundant; koḻu – well-grown; mīn – fish; uṇ – consuming; kurugu – crane; ōdi – went; pedaiyōdum – with its female spouse; naḷḷam – dense (having petals); kamalam – in the lotus flower; tēṟal – honey; ugukkum – drinking; naṟaiyūr – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abode of pure kriṣṇa,who rode the chariot, having white horses for arjunan, to have the opponent’s strong army broken into pieces and to have jayadrata, the king of sindu dēśam killed, is the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the crane along with its female spouse would go and drink the honey in the lotus flower having dense petals, after consuming the abundantly well-grown fish.

**veḷḷaip puravi …** – For vijayan, i.e., arjunan who is having a chariot which is drawn by white horses. kriṣṇa had partiality towards such arjunan to get the very strong army which was well arranged, and marched towards jayadrata, and to have the head of jayadrata severed. He is so pure to have such partiality towards his devotees to come and help them when they vow for it. The abode of such lord.

**koḷḷaik koḻu mīn …** – In tirunaṟaiyūr, the crane would consume the abundantly well-grown fish, along with its female spouse, would go, revealing its pride, and drink the honey which is abundantly present in the lotus which is having dense petals. Such tirunaṟaiyūr is the abode of kriṣṇa.

## 6.5.9. Parai urum

*pārai ūrum pāram tīrap pārttan tantērai ūrum dēva dēvan sērumūrtārai ūrum taṇ taḷir vēli pudai sūḻanārai ūrum nal vayal sūḻnda naṟaiyūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pārai – in earth; ūrum – existing; pāram – burden; tīra – to be eliminated; pārttan than – arjunan’s; tērai ūrum – riding the chariot; dēva dēvan – lord of lords; sērum Ur – the abode where he reached and is eternally residing; tārai ūrum – (honey is) flowing; taṇ taḷir – having cool spruces; vēli – by the fence (which is kept as a fort); pudai sūḻa – fully surrounded; nārai ūrum – the cranes are roaming; nal vayal – by beautiful fields; sūḻnda – surrounded; naṟaiyūr – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa, the lord of lords, rode arjunan’s chariot to eliminate the burden which existed on earth. The abode where such kriṣṇa has reached and is eternally residing is the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by beautiful fields where cranes are roaming, which are fully surrounded and protected by the fence having cool spruces and where honey is flowing.

**pārai ūrum …** – To eliminate the unbearable burden on earth, he conducted arjunan’s chariot. While he has the supremacy as said in śvētāśvatara upaniśat “*tamīśvaraṇām paramam mahēśvaram*” (That lord who is the lord of all lords), he became the charioteer for the sake of his devotee. The abode of such bhagavān.

**tārai ūrum …** – Having fence which has spruces which are better than flowers; tārai indicates dārā – flowing honey, implying fence which is having honey which is flowing.

**nārai ūrum …** – tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by beautiful fields where cranes are roaming around.

## 6.5.10. Tamat tulaba

*tāmat tuḷaba nīḷ mudi māyan tān ninṟanāmat tiraḷ māmāḷigai sūḻnda naṟaiyūr mēlkāmak kadir vēl vallān kaliyan oli mālaisēmat tuṇaiyām seppum avarkkut tirumālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuḷabam – strung with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); tāmam – decorated with garland; nīḷ – tall; mudi – having crown; māyan – amazing sarvēśvaran; ninṟa – eternally residing; nāmam – famous; tiraḷ – dense; mā māḷigai – by huge homes; sūḻnda – pervaded; naṟaiyūr mēl – on tirunaṟaiyūr; kāmam kadir – very radiant; vēl – the weapon, spear; vallān – one who can hold; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; oli – mercifully composed; mālai – these ten pāsurams which are a garland of words; seppumavarkku – for those who recite; tirumāl – śrīman nārāyaṇan; sēmam – always being the protector; tuṇai Am – will become the supporter

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirunaṟaiyūr is pervaded by huge homes which are famous and densely located and is where the amazing sarvēśvaran, who is having tall crown decorated with tuḷasi garland, is eternally residing. tirumangai āḻvār, who can hold the very radiant weapon, spear, mercifully composed these ten pāsurams which are a garland of words. For those who recite these pāsurams, śrīman nārāyaṇan will always be the protector and supporter.

**tāmat tuḷaba …** – sarvēśvaran is having divine crown which is decorated with tiruttuḻāy garland and indicates his reign over everything, and is having amazing qualities. The eternal abode of such sarvēśvaran.

**nāmat tiraḷ …** – Mercifully spoken about tirunaṟaiyūr which is pervaded by tall mansions which are densely present and are famous to be known as “This mansion”, “This mansion”.

**kāmak kadir …** – Having beautiful radiance. kāmam – prakāma which means abundance, indicating great radiance. tirumangai āḻvār, having the very radiant spear on his hands, mercifully spoke this garland of pāsurams. For those who can recite these pāsurams,

**tirumāl sēmat tuṇaiyām** – Accepting his refuge will not go waste. Rather it will fully take care of his \[one who recites these pāsurams\] protection – such a companion.

## 6.6 Ambaramum

## 6.6.1. Ambaramum

*ambaramum perunilanum tisaigaḷ ettumalaikadalum kulavaraiyum uṇḍa kaṇḍankombamarum vada marattin ilai mēl paḷḷikūdinān tiruvadiyē kūdagiṟpīr!vambaviḻum seṇbagattin vāsam uṇḍumaṇivaṇḍu vaguḷattin malar mēl vaigusembiyan kōc cengaṇān sērnda kōyiltirunaṟaiyūr maṇimādam sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ambaramum – sky; peru – vast; nilanum – earth; ettut tisaigaḷum – eight directions; alai – banging waves; kadalum – ocean; kulavaraiyum – anchoring mountains; uṇḍa – one who mercifully consumed; kaṇḍan – one who has the neck; amarum – abundant; kombu – having branches; vadamarattin – banyan tree’s; ilai mēl – on the fresh leaf (during deluge); paḷḷi kūdinān – sarvēśvaran, who is mercifully resting, his; tiruvadi – divine feet; kūdagiṟpīr – those who desire to attain!; maṇi – beautiful; vaṇḍu – beetles; vambu – fragrance; aviḻum – emitting; senbagattin – present in campak flowers; vāsam – fragrance; uṇḍu – enjoying that (and further); vaguḷattin malar mēl – on vakuḷa flower; vaigu – present; sem kaṇān – having reddish eyes; sembiyan – named sembiyan; kōn – (cōḻa) king; sērnda – residing; maṇi – embossed with gems; mādam – having mansions; tirunaṟaiyūr kōyil – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; sērmingaḷ – reach and eternally live there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, those who desire to attain the divine feet of sarvēśvaran, who is mercifully resting on the fresh leaf of the banyan tree having abundant branches, after having mercifully consumed sky, vast earth, eight directions, ocean with banging waves and anchoring mountains! Reach the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the cōḻa king, named sembiyan, who is having reddish eyes, is residing and where beautiful beetles are enjoying the fragrance present and emitted from campak flowers and further enjoying the fragrance present on vakuḷa flowers and which is having mansions embossed with gems, and eternally live there.

**ambaramum …** – One who is having the neck which mercifully consumed the sky, vast earth, eight directions, agitated ocean, mountains which anchor the earth.

**kombu amarum** … – Oh, those who desire to attain the divine feet of sarvēśvaran who is having agatita gatanā sāmārtyam (reconciling contradictory aspects) and is mercifully resting on the leaf of banyan tree which is having well-grown branches!

**vambaviḻum …** – The beetles, on enjoying the fragrance from the campak flower which is emitting fragrance, and in the process acquire heat from there, subsequently will enjoy the fragrance of vakuḷa flower and try to eliminate that heat.

**sembiyan …** – The king’s name is sembiyan kōccengaṇān. With this, it is explained that bhagavān’s agatita gatanā sāmartyam and the beetles remaining on the vakuḷa flower, are equally desirable, due to the connection with that divyadēśam.
