## 6.6.2. Kolungayalay

*koḻungayalāy nedu veḷḷam koṇḍa kālamkulavaraiyin mīdōdi aṇḍattappāleḻundu inidu viḷaiyādum īsan endaiiṇaiyadik kīḻ inidu iruppīr! inavaṇḍālumuḻum seṟuvil maṇi koṇarndu karai mēl sindiulagellām sandanamum agilum koḷḷaseḻum ponni vaḷangodukkum sōḻan sērndatirunaṟaiyūr maṇimādam sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nedu – overflowing; veḷḷam – the ocean of deluge; koṇḍa – consumed (earth); kālam – at that time; koḻu – well-grown (strong); kayalāy – assuming the form of a fish; kula varaiyin – on the anchoring mountains; mīdu ōdi – roaming atop; appāl – further; aṇḍattu – up to the wall of the oval shaped universe; eḻundu – rose (jumped); inidu – joyfully; viḷaiyādum – independently moving around; īsan – being uncontrollable; endai – my lord’s; iṇai – matching; adikkīḻ – under the divine feet; inidu – joyfully; iruppīr – oh those who desire to remain!; inam – gathered in a swarm; vaṇḍu – beetles; Alum – dancing; seḻu – beautiful; ponni – the divine kāvēri river; uḻum – ploughing; seṟuvil – fields’; karai mēl – on the borders; maṇi – precious gemstones; koṇarndu – gathered and brought; sindhi – scattered; ulagellām – all the people; sandanamum – sandalwood trees; agilum – eaglevood tree logs; koḷḷa – to take; vaḷam – prosperity; kodukkum – granting; sōḻan – cōḻa king; sērnda – residing; maṇi – embossed with gems; mādam – having mansions; tirunaṟaiyūr kōyil – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; sērmingaḷ – reach and eternally live there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran assumed the form of a well-grown fish at the time when the ocean of deluge consumed the earth. He roamed atop the anchoring mountains and further rose up to the wall of the oval shaped universe, and independently roamed around there. Oh those who desire to remain joyfully under the divine feet of my lord who is uncontrollable! Reach the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the cōḻa king, named sembiyan, who is having reddish eyes, is residing and where the beetles are gathered in a swarm and are dancing, and where the divine kāvēri river is gathering and bringing the precious gemstones and scattering them on the borders of the fertile fields which are being ploughed, and which is having the prosperity to let all the people take sandalwood trees and eaglevood tree logs.

**koḻum kayal …** – The time when the ocean of deluge consumed the whole earth; being a strong fish, climbing atop the anchoring mountains, jumping up to the roof of the oval shaped universe, bhagavān who is freely enjoying leelā.

**endai …** – Oh those who desire to surrender unto the divine feet of the apt lord!

**ina vaṇḍu …** – Swarms of beetles are dancing joyfully. kāvēri river is bringing the precious gemstones and scattering them along the borders of the fertile fields which are being ploughed. Also letting the people of the world take the sandalwood and eaglevood tree blocks, the river ponni (kāvēri) is bringing and giving prosperity to tirunaṟaiyūr. ōr, it could be an adjective to the cōḻa king – the king who brings prosperity. Since these are present in that divyadēśam, both the king’s leelā and the free-flowing movement of kāvēri are desirable for āḻvār.

## 6.6.3. Pavva nirudai

*pavva nīrudai ādaiyāgac cuṟṟippāragalam tiruvadiyāp pavanam meyyāsevvi mādiram ettum tōḷā aṇḍamtirumudiyā ninṟān pāl sellagiṟpīrkavvai mākaḷiṟu undi veṇṇiyēṟṟakaḻal mannar maṇi mudi mēl kāgam ēṟadeyva vāḷ valam koṇḍa sōḻan sērndatirunaṟaiyūr maṇimādam sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

suṟṟi – surrounded (the earth); pavvam – ocean’s; nīr – water; udai – apt to be worn; ādaiyāga – being the tiruppītāmbaram (divine yellow garment); pār agalam – the expansive earth; tiruvadiyā – being the divine feet; pavanam – the air; meyyā – being his divine form; sevvi – beautiful; ettu mādiramum – eight directions; tōḷā – being the shoulders; aṇḍam – the roof of the oval shaped universe; tirumudiyā – being the divine crown (having the universe as his form in this manner); ninṟān pāl – sarvēśvaran who is like this; sellagiṟpīr – oh those who are desiring to reach!; kavvai – noisy; mā – huge; kaḷiṟu – elephants; undi – pushed (and killed); viṇṇi – in the battle; ēṟṟa – those who came opposing; kaḻal – having valourous anklets; mannar – kings’; maṇi – having crowns which are embossed with precious gemstones; mudi mēl – on the heads; kāgam – crows; ēṟa – to climb (and consume the flesh); deyvam – best; vāḷ – the weapon sword; valam – on his right hand; koṇḍa – one who is holding; sōḻan – cōḻa king; sērnda – residing; maṇi – embossed with gems; mādam – having mansions; tirunaṟaiyūr kōyil – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; sērmingaḷ – reach and eternally live there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh those who are desiring to reach sarvēśvaran who is having water of the ocean which surrounds the earth, as the divine garment to be worn, and the expansive earth as his divine feet, the air as his divine form, the beautiful eight directions as his divine shoulders and the roof of the oval shaped universe as his divine crown! Reach the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the cōḻa king, named sembiyan, who is having reddish eyes, is residing and who is holding the best weapon, sword, on his right hand, which will push the noisy, huge elephants down and kill them, and will make crows climb on the heads of the kings who came opposing in the battle and are having valourous anklets, and are decorated with crowns which are embossed with precious gemstones.

**pavva nīr …** – Oh, those who are desiring to reach sarvēśvaran who is having the whole universe as his form as in having water of the ocean which surrounds the earth, as the divine garment to be worn, and the expansive earth as his divine feet, the air as his divine form, the beautiful eight directions as his divine shoulders and the roof of the oval shaped universe as his divine crown!

**kavvai …** – Pushing the elephant which is having great strength and rushing with huge noise.

**viṇṇi …** – viṇṇi – battle, capital city. Those kings who come opposing in the battle, and are having valourous anklets, to be killed and to make the crows climb their heads, the cōḻa king fought. Due to the fame attained by the connection with tirunaṟaiyūr, bhagavān remaining with the universal form and the cōḻa king remaining victorious in the battle are both equally enjoyable.

## 6.6.4. Painganal ari

*paingaṇāḷ ari uruvāy veruva nōkkipparuvarat tōḷ iraṇiyanaip paṟṟi vāngiangai vāḷ ugir nudiyāl avanadu āgamangurudi ponguvittān adik kīḻ niṟpīr!vengaṇ mā kaḷiṟu undi viṇṇiyēṟṟaviṟal mannar tiṟal aḻiya vemmā uyttasengaṇān kōccōḻan sērnda kōyiltirunaṟaiyūr maṇimādam sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pai – greenish; kaṇ – having divine eyes; āḷari uruvāy – being in the narasimha form; veruva – (to have the enemies) be afraid; nōkki – seen; vara – with the strength of the boons; paru – became huge; tōḷ – having shoulders; iraṇiyanai – hiraṇyāsura; paṟṟi – grabbed; vāngi – pulled; am kai – in the beautiful divine hand; vāḷ – shining; ugir nudiyāl – by the edges of the nails; avanadu – such hiraṇya’s; āgam – from the body; am kurudi – beautiful blood; ponguvittān – one who caused flood, his; adikkīḻ – under the divine feet; niṟpīr – Oh those who are desiring to be!; vem kaṇ – having reddish eyes; mā kaḷiṟu – huge elephants; undi – pushed (and killed); viṇṇi – in the battle; ēṟṟa – came opposing; viṟal – strong; mannar – kings’; tiṟal – strength; aḻiya – to be destroyed; vem – having a cruel walk; mā – horse; uytta – conducted; sengaṇān – one who is having reddish eyes; kō – the king; sōḻan – cōḻa king; sērnda – residing; maṇi – embossed with gems; mādam – having mansions; tirunaṟaiyūr kōyil – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; sērmingaḷ – reach and eternally live there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh those who are desiring to be under the divine feet of narasimha bhagavān with his greenish eyes, who looked at hiraṇyāsura to cause fear in him and who grabbed and pulled hiraṇya whose shoulders had become huge by the strength of the boons, and made beautiful blood from hiraṇya’s body flow out like a flood, using his radiant nails in his beautiful hands! Reach the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the cōḻa king, named sembiyan, who is having reddish eyes, is residing and who conducts the horses with cruel walk to destroy the strength of the strong kings, who pushed the elephants which are having reddish eyes, and came fighting.

**paingaṇ …** – Being narasimha and having greenish eyes matching the nature of the lion species, bhagavān stared at hiraṇya to cause fear for him; without hesitating, he went close to hiraṇya who was having strong shoulders due to the strength of his boons, and pulled him, grabbing his body.

**am kai …** – With a minute portion of the naturally beautiful, radiant divine nails, he caused a flood of blood in hiraṇya’s body. Oh those who desire to attain the divine feet of such lord!

**vem kaṇ …** – Pushing the elephant having cruel eyes, sembiyan, the cōḻa king, conducted the horses to destroy the strength of the kings who came and opposed in the battle. For āḻvār, bhagavān eliminating the enemies of the devotees and the cōḻa king fighting the battles, are both enjoyable \[due to the connection with tirunaṟaiyūr\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.6.5. Anru ulagam

*anṟu ulaga mūnṟinaiyum aḷandu vēṟōrari uruvāy iraṇiyanadu āgam kīṇḍuvenṟu avanai viṇṇulagil sela uyttāṟkuvirundāvīr! mēleḻundu vilangal pāyndupon sidaṟi maṇi koṇarndu karai mēl sindippulam parandu nilam parakkum ponni nādanten tamiḻan vadapulak kōn sōḻan sērndatirunaṟaiyūr maṇimādam sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – During the time of vāmanāvatāram; ulaga mūnṟinaiyum – three worlds (as trivikrama); aḷandu – measured; vēṟu – distinguished; ōr – unique (in valour); ari uruvāy – being narasimha; iraṇiyanadu – hiraṇya’s; āgam – body; kīṇḍu – tearing it apart into two pieces; veṇṟu – becoming victorious; avanai – that hiraṇya; viṇṇulagil – vīra svargam (the heaven for valourous persons); sela uyttāṟku – for sarvēśvara who did this; virundāvīr – oh those who desire to be his guests!; mēl eḻundu – rising in tumult; vilangal – mountains; pāyndu – breaking the barriers and flowing; pon – gold; sidaṟi – scattering (all over); maṇi koṇarndu – gathering and bringing precious gemstones; karai mēl – on the banks; sindhi – scattering; pulam – in the outside lands; parandu – spreading (in this manner); nilam – all over the earth; parakkum – spreading; ponni – the divine kāvēri river which is flowing; nādan – one who is having the country; then tamiḻan – being the king of the tamiḻ region which is in the southern direction; vada pulam – for the northern region; kōn – being the king; sōḻan – being the king of cōḻa region also (which is in the middle part); sērnda – residing; maṇi – embossed with gems; mādam – having mansions; tirunaṟaiyūr kōyil – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; sērmingaḷ – reach and eternally live there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh those who desire to be the guests of sarvēśvaran who measured the three words during vāmanāvatāram and being distinguished, unique narasimha, tore apart hiraṇya’s body into two pieces, becoming victorious and granting vīra svargam for him! Reach the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the mansions are embossed with precious gemstones and where the cōḻa king, named sembiyan, who is having reddish eyes, is residing and who is the tamiḻ king of the southern, middle and northern regions, who is having the kingdom where the divine kāvēri river is rising with tumult, breaking the mountains and flowing, scattering gold and gathering and bringing the precious gemstones and scattering them on the banks and is spreading to the outside lands and all over the earth.

**anṟulagam …** – Placing all the three worlds under his divine feet and assumed an unseen form of narasimha in this world, and became victorious against hiraṇya by tearing his body.

**viṇṇulagu …** – It is said that “hiraṇya got vīra svargam having been killed by bhagavān himself”.

**virundāvīr** – Oh those who desire to become guests of bhagavān!

**mēl eḻundu …** – Rising with a tumult, breaking the mountains which are barriers, gathering the gold and the precious gemstones on those mountains and sahyam (the origin of the river), scattered them on the banks.

**pulam …** – By spreading in the outside lands, it consumes all the earth. ponni nādan – One who has the kingdom around ponni (kāvēri).

**then tamiḻan …** – Thus, he ruled all the 3 kingdoms. Since this king’s wealth was acquired by the mercy of bhagavān, āḻvār considers his rule to be as desirable as bhagavān measuring the three worlds.

## 6.6.6. Tannale tannuruvam

*tannālē tannuruvam payanda tānāyttayangu oḷi sēr mūvulagum tānāy vānāytannālē tan uruvin mūrtti mūnṟāyttānāyan āyinān saraṇ enṟu uyvīr!minnādu vēlēndu viḷainda vēḷaiviṇṇēṟat tani vēl uyttu ulagam āṇḍatennādan kuda kongan sōḻan sērndatirunaṟaiyūr maṇimādam sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tannālē – by his own desire; than uruvam – his divine form; payanda – one who created; tānāy – having divine svarūpam (true nature); tayangu oḷi sēr – having great radiance; mūvulagum – three worlds; tānāy – having under his control; vānāy – being the controller of paramapadam; tannālē – with his vow; than uruvil – from his svarūpam; mūnṟu mūrttiyāy – one who created the trimūrti – brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra; tān – himself; āyan āyinān – (being free from karma) became kriṣṇa; saraṇ enṟu – considering him to be the upāyam (means); uyvīr – Oh, those who seek to be uplifted!; min ādu – radiant; vēl ēndu – holding the spear; viḷainda vēḷai – one who is named viḷainda vēḷ; viṇ ēṟa – to attain vīra svargam (reach the heaven of valour, by getting killed in a battle); tani – once; vēl – the weapon, spear; uyttu – launched; ulagam āṇḍa – one who protected the worlds; then nādan – one who is the king of southern regions; kuda kongan – king of the kongu region which is in the western side; sōḻan – cōḻa king; sērnda – residing; maṇi – embossed with gems; mādam – having mansions; tirunaṟaiyūr kōyil – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; sērmingaḷ – reach and eternally live there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān created his divine form by his own desire, and is having a divine svarūpam and is having the three worlds with great radiance, under his control; he is the controller of paramapadam; with his vow, he created the trimūrti – brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra, from his svarūpam. Oh those who seek to be uplifted, considering such bhagavān who became kriṣṇa, to be the upāyam (means)! Reach the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the cōḻa king, named sembiyan, who is having reddish eyes, is residing and who once launched the weapon, spear, to facilitate vīra svargam for the one named viḷainda vēḷ who was holding the radiant spear, thus protecting the worlds and who is the king of southern regions as well as the king of the kongu region which is in the western side.

**tannālē tannuruvam …** – As said in “*ananyādipati*” (not having any other controller), since bhagavān has his svarūpam etc under his control, he is different from everyone else. One is said to be īśvaran only when one’s svarūpam etc are under his disposal.

**tayangu oḷi …** – Having the leelā vibhūti at his disposal; the worlds are classified into three categories – krutaka, akrutaka and krutakākrutaka, Here the radiance is an adjective for the worlds which are moving with splendour, since they are owned by bhagavān. Alternatively, radiance can be seen as an adjective for bhagavān’s divine form, as in *tayangoḷi sēr mūrtti*.

Note: krutaka \[The bottom seven layers of the universe – atala to pātāla and the three middle layers – bhūr lōka, bhuva lōka and svarga lōka; these are completely destroyed as part of avāntara praḷayam (intermediary deluge at the end of brahmā’s day) and subsequently recreated\], akrutaka \[The top three layers of the universe – satya lōka, tapa lōka and jana lōka; these remain in tact during avāntara praḷayam with their residents\] and krutakākrutaka \[mahar lōka; this remains intact during avāntara praḷayam, but the residents shift to higher layers at that time\].

**tannālē …** – Having three forms matching the creation etc of the leelā vibhūti (material realm). Being himself as viṣṇu, he protects and being the antaryāmi of brahmā and rudra, he conducts creation and annihilation. In this manner, he is having three forms for three purposes.

**tānāya …** – Such bhagavān, in this leelā vibhūti, incarnated as kriṣṇa, to be proudly claimed by a few from among those who exist in his world, saying “He is my son”. Oh those who have such kriṣṇa as our refuge! Oh those who try to hold on to the divine feet of the one who said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66) “*māmēkam*” (Only me)!

**min ādu …** – To send the evil person named viḷainda vēḷ, who is holding a shining spear in his hand, to vīra svargam, sembiyan, the cōḻa king, launched his spear, just once. In this manner, he conducted the whole world under his control. Such king went and attained tirunaṟaiyūr.

**tennādan …** – The cōḻa who is the ruler of pāṇḍiya kingdom in the south and kongu kingdom in the west, is residing here. Since the king acquired these greatness by taking refuge of this town, āḻvār feels the reign of this king over three different kingdoms is as enjoyable as sarvēśvaran having the whole universe as his form.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.6.7. Mulait tadatta

*mulait tadatta nanjuṇḍu tunjap pēyccimudu tuvaraik kulapadiyāk kālip pinnēilait tadatta kuḻalūdi āyar mādarinavaḷai koṇḍān adik kīḻ eydagiṟpīr!malait tadatta maṇi koṇarndu vaiyam uyyavaḷam kodukkum varu punalam ponni nādansilait tadakkaik kulaccōḻan sērnda kōyiltirunaṟaiyūr maṇimādam sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pēycci – pūtanā; tunja – to die; tadam – huge; mulai – in (her) bosom; nanju – poison; uṇḍu – mercifully consumed; mudu – ancient; tuvarai – for dvārakā; kulapadiyāy – being the controller; kālip pinnē – behind the cows; tadam – big; ilaik kuḻal – flute made using leaf; ūdi – one who went, playing it; āyar mādar – covherd girls’; vaḷai inam – ornaments such as bangles etc; koṇḍān – one who took away (playfully); adik kīḻ – under the divine feet; eydagiṟpīr – oh those who are desiring to reach!; malait tadatta – present in the slopes of the mountains; maṇi koṇarndu – gathering and bringing the precious gemstones; vaiyam uyya – for the prosperity of the whole world; vaḷam kodukkum – giving abundance of wealth; varu – overflowing; punal – having water; am – beautiful; ponni – having divine kāvēri; nādan – being the king of the region; silai – bow; tadam kai – holding on his vast hand; kulam – born in kśatriya clan; sōḻan – cōḻa king; sērnda – residing; maṇi – embossed with gems; mādam – having mansions; tirunaṟaiyūr kōyil – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; sērmingaḷ – reach and eternally live there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh those who are desiring to reach the divine feet of kriṣṇa who mercifully consumed the poison in pūtanā’s bosom to kill her, who is the controller of the ancient dvārakā, who went behind the cows, playing the flute made of big leaf and who took away the ornaments such as bangles etc of the covherd girls! Reach the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the cōḻa king, named sembiyan, who is having reddish eyes, is residing, who is the king of the region, which is having beautiful, divine kāvēri which is overflowing with water which is gathering and bringing the precious gemstones from the mountain slopes and giving for the prosperity of the whole world, and is holding the bow in his vast hand and who is born in kśatriya clan.

**mulait tadatta …** – To have pūtanā killed, kriṣṇa consumed the huge bosom of pūtanā which matched her form.

**mudu tuvarai …** – Being the controller of śrīmad dvārakā, he went behind the cows tending them by playing the flute made with huge leaf. Again, he returned to tiruvāyppādi and took away the covherd girls’ ornaments such as bangles etc. Oh those who are desiring to reach his divine feet and become uplifted!

**malait tadatta maṇi …** – River kāvēri brings prosperity to whole earth by bringing the precious gemstones from the mountain slopes and pushing them here. The king who has such a region having kāvēri with abundance of water.

**silait tadakkai …** – The divyadēśam which is reached by a very valourous person to manage his valour.

## 6.6.8. Murukkilangu

*murukkilangu kanittuvarvāyp pinnai kēḷvanmannellām mun aviyac cenṟu venṟiccerukkaḷattut tiṟal aḻiyac ceṟṟa vēndansiram tuṇittān tiruvadi num senni vaippīr!irukkilangu tirumoḻi vāy eṇṭhōḷ īsaṟkueḻil mādam eḻubadu seydu ulagamāṇḍatirukkulattu vaḷaccōḻan sērnda kōyiltirunaṟaiyūr maṇimādam sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

murukku – like murukkam flower (flower from a type of teak wood tree); ilangu – shining; kani – like kōvai fruit (reddish fruit); tuvar – reddish; vāy – having lips; pinnai – for nappinnaip pirātti; kēḷvan – being beloved; mun – in the past (during paraśurāma avatāram); man ellām – all the (evil) kings; aviya – to be destroyed; venṟi – yielding victory; seruk kaḷattu – in the battle field; senṟu – went; teṟṟa – enemy; vēndan – kārtavīryārjunan’s; tiṟal – strength; aḻiya – destroyed; siram – (his) head; tuṇittān – severed, his; tiruvadi – divine feet; num senni – on your head; vaippīr – oh those who are desiring!; irukku – by rig (mantras); ilangu – shining; tirumoḻi – puruśa sūktam, which is the best word; vāy – having in his mouth (that is, reciting); eṇ tōḷ – having eight shoulders; īsaṟku – beautiful; eḻubadu mādam – seventy temples; seydu – consecrated; ulagam āṇḍa – one who protected the world; tirukkulattu – one who is born in the best clan; vaḷam – having abundant wealth; sōḻan – cōḻa king; sērnda – residing; maṇi – embossed with gems; mādam – having mansions; tirunaṟaiyūr kōyil – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; sērmingaḷ – reach and eternally live there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is the beloved lord of nappinnaip pirātti who is having lips which are shining like murukkam flower and reddish like kōvai fruit. In the past, during paraśruāma avatāram, he went to the battlefield, which yields victory, to have all the evil kings destroyed. He destroyed the strength of kārtavīryārjunan and severed his head. Oh, those who are desiring to keep the divine feet of such bhagavān on your heads! Reach the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where the cōḻa king, named sembiyan, who is having reddish eyes, is residing and who consecrated seventy beautiful temples for rudra who is having eight shoulders and is constantly reciting puruśa sūktam, and who is born in the best clan and is having abundant wealth.

**murukku ilangu …** – He is the beloved lord of nappinnaip pirātti who is having lips which are shining like murukkam flower and reddish like kōvai fruit

**man ellām …** – Went to the battlefield, vanquishing all the evil kings, on the way.

**seṟṟa vēndan siram tuṇittān …** – Oh those who are desiring to keep the divine feet of the one who incarnated as paraśurāma and killed sahasra bāhu arjunan, who is the reason for all the enemies, by destroying his strength, making him tired and severing his head!

**irukku ilangu …** – For rudra who is having in his mouth śrī puruśa sūkta etc from vēdam, and who is having eight shoulders. tirunaṟaiyūr is the abode, which was approached by the cōḻa king, sembiyan, to fulfil his desires, after consecrating seventy beautiful temples for rudra and still being unable to fulfil his desires. In the previous pāsuram, sembiyan’s actions are praised at par with the kāvēri’s flow of water which brings precious gemstones etc, and kriṣṇa’s act of grabbing the clothes and bangles of the gōpikās. In this pāsuram, his actions are praised at par with kriṣṇa being the beloved lord of nappinnaip pirātti and paraśurāma destroying the enemies of the devotees.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.6.9. Taralan

*tārāḷan taṇṇaranga vāḷan pūmēltaniyāḷan muniyāḷar ētta ninṟapērāḷan āyiram pērudaiya vāḷanpinnaikku maṇavāḷan perumai kētpīr!pārāḷar avarivar enṟu aḻundai ēṟṟappadai mannar udal tuṇiyap parimā uyttatērāḷan kōccōḻan sērnda kōyiltirunaṟaiyūr maṇimādam sērmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tār āḷan – being decorated with divine garlands; taṇ – rejuvenating; arangavāḷan – eternally residing in śrīrangam; pū mēl – residing on the lotus flower; taniyāḷan – being beloved lord of the distinguished pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi); muniyāḷar – the sages such as sanaka et al; ētta ninṟa – mercifully present to be praised by; pērāḷan – having greatness; āyiram pēr udaiyavāḷan – having thousand divine names; pinnaikku – for nappinnaip pirātti; maṇavāḷan – being the lord, his; perumai – glories; kētpīr – oh those who desire to hear!; avar ivar enṟu – being famous as “such and such person”; pār āḷar – kings who control earth; aḻundai – in tiruvaḻundūr; ēṟṟa – as they opposed; padai – (in that) battle; mannar – (those) kings; udal – body; tuṇiya – to be severed into pieces; parimā – horses; uytta – drawn by; tērāḷan – one who conducted the chariot; sōḻan – cōḻa king; sērnda – residing; maṇi – embossed with precious gemstones; mādam – having mansions; tirunaṟaiyūr kōyil – divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; sērmingaḷ – reach and eternally live there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh those who desire to hear the glories of sarvēśvaran who is decorated with divine garlands, who is eternally residing in rejuvenating śrīrangam, who is the beloved lord of the distinguished pirātti who is residing on the lotus flower, who is mercifully present to be praised by the sages such as sanaka et al, who is having the greatness of having thousand divine names and who is the lord for nappinnaip pirātti! Reach the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr which is having mansions embossed with precious gemstones and where the cōḻa king, named sembiyan, who is having reddish eyes, is residing and who conducted the chariot drawn by horses to sever the bodies of the kings who control the earth and are famous as said in “such and such person” as they came opposing him in the battle in tiruvaḻundūr, into pieces.

**tārāḷan** – One who is decorated with a special garland to identify that he is the protector of ubhaya vibhūti.

**taṇ arangavāḷan** – For the protection of the universe, he is residing in śrīrangam.

**pū mēl …** – Beloved consort of periya pirāttiyār who is having the lotus as her abode and having distinguished femininity.

**muniyāḷar …** – One who has the greatness of being praised by sages such as sanaka et al who are fully focussed on bhagavān.

**āyiram …** – One who is having thousand divine names which facilitate variety of enjoyment for those who set out to enjoy him.

**pinnaikku …** – Oh those who desire to hear the glories of the beloved lord of nappinnaip pirātti!

**pārāḷar …** – As the great rulers of the whole earth, those kings who are famous individually, came along with their armies and fought in tiruvaḻundūr, the cōḻa king fought them to sever their bodies.

**parimā uytta tērāḷan …** – One who is having chariot drawn by horses.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.6.10. Semmoli vay

*semmoḻi vāy nāl vēda vāṇar vāḻumtirunaṟaiyūr maṇimādac cengaṇmālaipoymmoḻi onṟillāda meymmaiyāḷanpulamangaik kulavēndan pulamai ārndaammoḻi vāyk kalikanṟi inbap pādalpāduvār viyan ulagil namanār pādivemmoḻi kēttu anjādē meymmai sollilviṇṇavarkku virundāgum perundakkōrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

semmoḻi – having honesty to reveal the meaning truthfully; vāy – having speech; nāl vēda vāṇar – brāhmaṇas who are experts in four vēdams; vāḻum – eternally residing; maṇi mādam – having mansions which are fitted with abundance of precious gemstones; tirunaṟaiyūr – in the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; sem kaṇ mālai – on sarvēśvaran who is having reddish eyes; poymmoḻi – untruthful words; onṟu illāda – not having even a little bit; meymmaiyāḷan – having truthful speech; pulam – beautiful; mangaik kulam – for the residents of tirumangai region; vēndan – being the king; pulamai ārnda – having completeness in knowledge; ammoḻi – having such words; vāy – having the divine mouth; kali kanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār’s; inbam – came out due to the joy caused by the experience; pādal – (these) pāsurams; viyan – famous; ulagil – in the world; pāduvār – those who can recite; namanār – yama’s; pādi – spoken by the messengers; vemmoḻi – cruel words; kēttu – hearing; anjādē – becoming scared; meymmai – truth (of the upcoming benefit); sollil – if told; viṇṇavarkku – for the nityasūris; virundu āgum – desirable; perum takkōr – will be most knowledgeable

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran, who is having reddish eyes, is present in the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr where brāhmaṇas, who are experts in four vēdams and having speech which is honest to reveal the meaning truthfully, are eternally residing. tirumangai āḻvār, who is not having even a little bit of untruthful words, is having truthful speech, is the king for the residents of beautiful tirumangai region and is having the divine mouth having such words of complete knowledge, composed these pāsurams which came out due to the joy caused by the experience, on such sarvēśvaran. Those who can recite these pāsurams in this famous world, will not be scared on hearing the cruel words of yama’s messengers and if truth is told, they will become most knowledgeable and be desirable for the nityasūris.

**semmoḻi …** – The beautiful abode of tirunaṟaiyūr, where brāhmaṇas, who speak the truth and who can conduct vēdam, being on vyāsapadam (the position of a great teacher) are dwelling, where the mansions are embellished with gemstones and where sarvēśvaran, who is puṇḍarīkākśa (lotus-eyed), is praised here.

**poymmoḻi …** – āḻvār who has the words which are as truthful as present in that vēdam.

**pula mangai …** – tirumangai āḻvār, is the king of the beautiful tirumangai; his wisdom is revealed in his speech; such āḻvār’s inbap pādal – the outlet for āḻvār;s experience, that is, the pāsurams spoken by him. That,

**viyan ulagil pāduvār …** – Those who are in this samsāra, who are different from others who are just eating and roaming around, and are singing these pāsurams, will not be scared to listen to the cruel words of the messengers of yama.

**meymmai sollil …** – If we are to explain the benefit that they will attain eventually, they will reach paramapadam (śrīvaikuṇṭam), and as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-9-10-vidhi-vagai/) “*padiyinil pānginil*” (in an honourable manner, in their respective abode), nityasūris will come out and invite such persons who sing these pāsurams into their residence, give them a high seat, remain subservient and wash their divine feet. They will attain such benefit.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7 Alum paniyum

## 6.7.1. Alum paniyum

*āḷum paṇiyum adiyēnaik koṇḍān viṇḍa nisāsararaittōḷum talaiyum tuṇiveydac cudu venjilai vāyc caram turandānvēḷum sēyum anaiyārum vēṟkaṇārum payil vīdināḷum viḻavin oli ōvā naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇḍa – inimical; nisāsararai – rākśasas; tōḷum – shoulders; talaiyum – heads; tuṇivu eyda – to turn into pieces (further); sudu – burning; vem – very cruel; silaivāy – from the bow; saram – arrows; turandān – one who shot; vēḷum – cupid; sēyum – skanda; anaiyārum – those beautiful men like; vēl – spear like; kaṇārum – women having eyes; payil – residing; vīdi – on the streets; nāḷum – nityōtsavam (daily festivals); viḻavil – naimittika utsavams’ (occasional festivals); oli – sound; ōvā – happening continuously without a break; naṟaiyūr – in tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – one who is mercifully present; nambi – sarvēśvaran who is complete; adiyēnai – I, the natural servitor; āḷum – to make me knowledgeable about being a servitor; paṇiyum – kainkaryam (service); koṇḍān – accepted

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The complete sarvēśvaran who shot arrows from the burning, very cruel bow to turn the heads and shoulders of the inimical rākśasas into pieces and who is mercifully present in tirunaṟaiyūr where men who are like cupid and skanda and women with spear-like eyes are residing and in the streets of the town where the sounds of nityōtsavams and naimittikōtsavams are occurring without a break, accepted me, the natural servitor, to make me knowledgeable about being a servitor and my kainkaryam. Hence, he is our refuge.

**āḷum …** – bhagavān accepted the ātmā which is qualified to remain for his divine feet, not to remain for the ātmā, and accepted kainkaryam which is the benefit for being bhagavān’s possession.

**adiyēnai āḷum paṇiyum koṇḍān** – Though I am qualified (to be his servitor), instead of making me think that I am independent and thus making me unqualified, he created the thought in me that I am subservient to him. He created the taste towards the result of such subservience – that is, being a servitor.

**viṇḍa …** – Here, āḻvār is explaining how bhagavān is destroying those who have the birth which will protest such servitude towards him. He would wait as much as possible for them to acquire some taste in the servitude and if they continue to remain as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36-11 “*dvidā bhajyēyam apyēvam na namēyam* . .” (Even if I am broken into two pieces, I will not bend before anyone), without showing any mercy, he will kill them. Severing the shoulders, breaking their legs, severing the head – in this manner, he spends the time and subsequently to kill them using his arrows, he will launch them from his bow which causes fear in the enemies’ stomach just on seeing it, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam ślōkam 46-22 “*dīpta pāvaka sangkāśai*: *śitai: kāncanabhūśaṇai*: l *na tvāmiccāmyaham draśtum rāmēṇa nihatam śarai*: ll” (I do not wish to see you killed by śrī rāma whose arrows are like burning fire, sharp and decorated with gold), he conducted the arrows, which appear like arrows while launching, but while entering the bodies of the enemies, they will appear like fire.

**vēḷum sēyum …** – Those who live in tirunaṟaiyūr are women who are enjoyers and enjoyable. Men who are comparable to cupid and subrahmaṇya in beauty, and the women who can make such men to exist exclusively for them, with their single glance, are residing there.

**nāḷum viḻavin oli ōvā …** – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.3.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/thiruvaimozhi-7-3-3-sengani-vayin/) “*tingaḷum nāḷum viḻā aṟāda*” (tentiruppēreyil where festivals are happening continuously without a break, every day and month), nambi who is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr where daily utsavams and monthly utsavams are continuously happening – he accepted my servitude and kainkaryam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.2. Muniyay vandu

*muniyāy vandu mūveḻugāl mudisēr mannar udal tuṇiyattanivāy maḻuvin padai āṇḍa tārār tōḷān vārpuṟavilpani sēr mullai pallarumbap pānal orupāl kaṇ kāttananisēr kamalam mugam kāttum naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

muniyāy – being paraśurāmāḻvān; vandu – came and incarnated; mūveḻugāl – 21 times; mudi sēr – crowned; mannar – kings’; udal – bodies; tuṇiya – to be severed; tani – matchless; vāy – having edge; maḻu – axe; padai – weapon; āṇḍa – one who controlled; tār Ar – decorated with garland; tōḷān – having shoulders; vār – lengthy (vast); puṟavil – in the surroundings; pani sēr – cool and beautiful; mullai – jasmine flower; pal – like the teeth (of the women of that town); arumba – as they blossom; pānal – pānal flower; oru pāl – in one way; kaṇ kātta – showing their eyes (appear like their eyes); nani sēr – having glory; kamalam – lotus flower; mugam kāttum – showing their face; naṟaiyūr ninṟa – one who is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; nambi – nambi is the refuge

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān came and incarnated as paraśurāmāḻvān, controlled the axe with matchless edge, to sever the bodies of the crowned kings for 21 generations; his shoulders are decorated with garlands; he is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr which has vast surroundings where the cool and beautiful jasmine flowers look like the teeth of the women of that town, are blossoming, the pānal flowers look like their eyes and the glorious lotus flowers look like their faces. Such emperumān is our refuge. This implies that the women’s teeth etc shine like the different flowers.

**muniyāy …** – Incarnating as a riśi who vowed to be compassionate. Even for such compassionate persons, the violence \[killing the evil persons\] which is ordained, cannot be abandoned.

**mū eḻu kāl …** – Conducted the axe, which has distinguished edge, to kill 21 generations of \[evil\] kings.

**tārār tōḷān …** – One who is decorated with a distinguished garland for the protection of the world.

**vār puṟavil …** – In the vast surroundings. Beautiful jasmine matches the teeth of the women there, pānal which is a kind of karuneydal flower, matches the eyes of the women there.

**nani sēr vayaluḷ muttalaikkum** … – \[Different recital\] In the vast field which resembles ocean, the pearls are moving here and there. Alternatively, if it is recited as **kamalam mugam kāttum**, the lotus flower matches the faces of the women there, where the face is the abode for the teeth and eyes.

## 6.7.3. Tellar kadalvay

*teḷḷār kadalvāy vidavāya sinavāḷ aravil tuyil amarndutuḷḷā varu mān vīḻa vāḷi turandān irandān māvali maṇpuḷḷār puṟavil pūngāvi pulan koḷ mādar kaṇ kāttanaḷḷār kamalam mugam kāttum naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

teḷ Ar – having clarity (pure); kadal vāy – in tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi – milk ocean); vidavāya – having mouths which spit poison; sinam – angry (on enemies); vāḷ – shining; aravil – on tiruvanantāḻvān; tuyil amarndu – mercifully resting (subsequently); tuḷḷāvaru – jumping while coming; mān vīḻa – to kill the mystic deer; vāḷi – arrow; tuṟandān – one who shot; māvali – from mahābali; maṇ – earth; irandān – begged; puḷ Ar – filled with birds; puṟavil – in the surroundings; pū kāvi – beautiful sengaḻunīr flower; pulan koḷ – wearing beautiful ornaments; mādar – women’s; kaṇ – eyes; kātta – as they show; naḷ Ar – dense (petals); kamalam – lotus; mugam kāttum – showing their face; naṟaiyūr ninṟa – one who is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; nambi – nambi is the refuge

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is mercifully resting on the shining tiruvanantāḻvān who is having mouths which spit poison and is angry, in clear tiruppāṟkadal. \[Subsequently\] He shot an arrow to kill the mystic dear which came jumping; he begged the earth from mahābali. Such bhagavān is the nambi in tirunaṟaiyūr where, in the surroundings which are filled with birds, the beautiful sengaḻunīr flower is showing the eyes of the women who are decorated with beautiful ornaments and the lotus flower with dense petals is showing their face. Such nambi is our refuge.

**teḷḷār …** – In the ocean which is having clear waters and were the tides are rising; just like coconut is tied with thorn, matching the simplicity of bhagavān, tiruvanantāḻvān is having mouths which are spitting poison on enemies and is angry on them; he is having radiance due to constant enjoyment of bhagavān; having such tiruvanantāḻvān as his mattress, resting on him, when evil persons like rāvaṇa appear, he gets up from that mattress and incarnates, and launches his arrow to shoot the mystic deer which is coming close, jumping here and there, and kills it.

**irandān …** – While he had the arrow in his hand, he went to mahābali and begged for earth, as if he has no strength/abiility. Only where sāma (discussions) does not work out, bēda (tricks) should be used.

**puḷḷār …** – In the surroundings which are filled with birds such as swan etc, the beautiful sengaḻunīr shows the eyes of the women decorated with ornaments, the lotus flower, which has dense petals, shows the face which is the abode of those eyes. Such tirunaṟaiyūr.

## 6.7.4. Oliya venney

*oḷiyā veṇṇey uṇḍān enṟu uralōdu āycci oṇkayiṟṟālviḷiyā ārkka āppuṇḍu vimmi aḻudān menmalar mēlkaḷiyā vaṇḍu kaḷḷuṇṇak kāmar tenṟal alar tūṟṟanaḷir vāy mullai muṟuvalikkum naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oḷiyā – Hiding; veṇṇey – butter; uṇḍān enṟu – saying that he swallowed; āycci – yaśōdāp pirātti; viḷiyā – being angry; oḷ – beautiful; kayiṟṟāl – with a rope; uralōdu – with the mortar; ārkka – as she bound; āppuṇḍu – being bound; vimmi – sobbed; aḻudān – cried; mel – tender; malar mēl – on the flowers; vaṇḍu – beetles; kaḷiyā – joyfully; kaḷ – honey (which is forbidden); uṇṇa – as they drink; kāmar – beautiful; tenṟal – southerly breeze; alar tūṟṟa – throwing the flowers (blaming the beetles); naḷir – glorious; vāy – having mouth; mullai – jasmine flower; muṟuvalikkum – blossoming (smiling); naṟaiyūr ninṟa – one who is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; nambi – nambi is the refuge

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

yaśōdāp pirātti became angry on kriṣṇa saying that he was hiding and swallowing butter, she bound him with a beautiful rope to the mortar. Being bound, he sobbed and cried. Such kriṣṇa is eternally residing tirunaṟiyūr where the beetles joyfully drink the honey on the tender flowers and the beautiful southerly breeze throws the flowers on those beetles and jasmine flower having glorious mouth is blossoming. Such nambi is our refuge.

**oḷiyā veṇṇey …** – Hiding from others, kriṣṇa would mercifully consume the butter which was saved by yaśōdā/gōpikās. Alternative explanation. He mercifully consumed the butter which is difficult to hide from him. Saying this, yaśōdā would become angry and bind him with the mortar, where the rope presses on his divine form. Alternative explanation, as the rope came in contact with his divine form, it became shining.

**āppuṇḍu …** – As he cannot sustain without butter, which has been touched by his dear devotees, he remained bound in that manner. He is capable of breaking free from nāgāstram (a weapon which ties down people); alternative explanation – if duryōdana et al bind him – he will free himself; but if his devotees bind him, he will not free himself. She said, as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.15 “*yadiśaknōśi*” (free yourself up, if you can). vangipurattu nambi prayed to emperumānār for a long time saying “Please teach how to do tiruvārādanam”; due to some hurdles emperumānār could not teach him that; but when he was mercifully present in tirumalā, he mercifully taught the same to kūrattāḻvān and śrī hanumat dāsar; towards the end, vangipurattu nambi arrived there and emperumānār became scared and mercifully spoke these words “I had a doubt for a long time; now it is cleared – when the controller became scared by those who are controlled by him, being bound, got beaten and stood sobbing, we thought ‘if this is possible/truth?’ – but now for the two mistakes (not teaching when vangipurattu nambi who had asked at first, not inviting him while teaching to kūrattāḻvān and śrī hanumat dāsar now), I have become scared seeing you. Now I understand that the controllers will fear for the controlled ones”. Here also emperumānār is the controller and all others are controlled by him.

**vimmi aḻudān** – There is no limit to what is going on in his mind; he let all of those thoughts out in the form of sobbing; she will say “Don’t cry; don’t cry” – so he will control his emotions and sob.

**men malar …** – Everywhere flowers are blossomed; beetles which reached there to drink the honey, becoming joyful having attained that, would drink the honey as if drinking intoxicant. The beautiful southerly breeze which saw that, threw accusations (in the form of flowers). The jasmine flower, seeing these, gently smiled, controlling the laughter, thinking about the events which happened there as in “Beetles are drinking honey; the breeze is throwing flowers”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.5. Villar vilavil

*villār viḻavil vadamadurai virumbi virumbā malladarttukallār tiraḷ tōḷ kanjanaik kāyndān pāyndān kāḷiyan mēlsollār surudi muṟaiyōdic cōmuc ceyyum toḻilinōrnallār maṟaiyōr palar vāḻum naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vada madurai – in śrī maturā which is in northern direction; vil Ar – having bow; viḻavil – in danur yāgam (in the bow festival); virumbi – desiring to go (there); virumbā – those who did not like him; mal – wrestlers such as cāṇūra et al; adarttu – turned them to dust; kal Ar – (strong) like a rock; tiraḷ – rounded; tōḷ – having shoulders; kanjanai – kamsan; kāyndān – one who angrily killed; kāḷiyan mēl – on kāḷiyan’s hoods; pāyndān – jumped; sol Ar – having (faultless) words; surudi – vēdams; muṟai – in proper manner; ōdi – learnt; sōmu – sōma yāgam etc; seyyum – those who perform; toḻilinōr – karmatar (those who eagerly engage in religious rites); nallār – distinguished (those who don’t expect anything); palar maṟaiyōr – countless brāhmaṇas; vāḻum – eternally residing; naṟaiyūr ninṟa – one who is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; nambi – nambi is the refuge

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Desiring to go to the danuryāgam which consists of bows, in śrī maturā which is in the northern direction, kriṣṇa went there, turned the wrestlers such as cāṇūra et al, who did not like him, into dust, and then angrily killed kamsan who has rounded, rock like shoulders; he then jumped on the hoods of kāḷiya; he is the nambi who is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr  
where countless, distinguished brāhmaṇas who have properly learnt vēdam which is having faultless words and are performing sōma yāgam etc and are eagerly engaged in fire rituals, are eternally residing. Such nambi is our refuge.

**villār …** – kamsa being the maternal uncle, brought kriṣṇa to śrī maturā through the guise of “vil viḻavu” (bow festival), made an elephant stand at the entrance, and thought of pretending to cry and be sorrowful (on getting kriṣṇa killed); kriṣṇa, instead of being ignorant about it, knowing every one of kamsa’s evil plans from the beginning, disregarding that, entered joyfully, considering the “vil viḻavu” occurrence.

**virumbā mal adarttu** – Killing the group of wrestlers who had no affection/devotion towards kriṣṇa.

**kal Ar …** – kriṣṇa gave the result, which was desired by kamsan who had strong shoulders, to kamsan and killed him.

**kāḷiyan mēl pāyndān** – Just as kriṣṇa jumped on kamsan’s back, he jumped on kāḷiyan’s hoods as well.

**sol Ar …** – Learning the vēdams which are faultless due to not being composed by any person, in the proper manner. These brāhmaṇas are not mere learners of vēdam but also follow the principles shown in such vēdam. And, not every now and then, but continuously, having that learning and practicing as the routine. And finally, they are distinguished due to the fact that they don’t learn and practice for any benefit other than giving joy for bhagavān.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.6. Valli kolunan

*vaḷḷi koḻunan mudalāya makkaḷōdu mukkaṇānveḷgi ōda viṟal vāṇan viyantōḷ vanattait tuṇittu ugandānpaḷḷi kamalattu idaippatta paguvāy alavan mugam nōkkinaḷḷiyūdum vayal sūḻnda naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaḷḷi – For a woman named vaḷḷi; koḻunan – subrahmaṇya who is the beloved; mudalāya – having him as the chief; makkaḷōdu – with sons; mukkaṇān – rudran who is three-eyed (got defeated); veḷgi – being ashamed; ōda – as he ran; viṟal – strong; vāṇan – bāṇāsuran’s; viyan – huge; tōḷ vanam – the forest of shoulders; tuṇittu – severed; ugandān – became joyful; kamalattu idai – in the middle of a lotus flower; paḷḷi patta – went to sleep and got caught; paguvāy – having huge mouth; alavan – male crab’s; mugam – face (which is smeared with flower buds); nōkki – seeing; naḷḷi – female crab; ūdum – showing romantic anger; vayal – by the fertile fields; sūḻnda – surrounded; naṟaiyūr ninṟa – one who is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; nambi – nambi is the refuge

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Having subrahmaṇya, who is the beloved husband of vaḷḷi, as the chief, the three-eyed rudra along with his sons, ran away in shame; kriṣṇa then severed the forest of the strong bāṇāsuran’s huge shoulders and became joyful. Such bhagavān is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by fertile fields where the male crab, which is having huge mouth, went to sleep in the middle of a lotus flower and got caught there and its face became smeared with the buds, on seeing which, the female crab showed romantic anger. Such nambi is our refuge.

**vaḷḷi …** – vaḷḷi is the name of a caṇḍāḷa (forest dweller) girl; subrahmaṇyan – her husband; starting with him, rudra along with all his sons; here it is as said in “*avinīta brutya varga:*” (disobedient followers). [tiruccanda viruttam 71](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/01/thiruchchandha-viruththam-71/) “… *muṇḍanīṟan makkaḷ veppu mōdiyangi ōdidak* *kaṇḍu nāṇi vāṇanukku iranginān em māyanē*” (For the sake of his daughter, uśai, around whose garland, beetles were roaming continuously, bāṇāsuran, with anger, waged a battle with kriṣṇa. When that bāṇāsuran neared kriṣṇan in the battlefield, kriṣṇan severed the thousand shoulders of bāṇāsuran. rudran \[who had come to help and protect his devotee bāṇāsuran\], with a tonsured head and ash smeared over his body, along with his sons skanda et al, kāḷi the deity of diseases such as fever, and agni, the deity of fire, ran away from the battlefield, leaving bāṇāsuran at the mercy of kriṣṇa. Looking at this, kriṣṇa, taking pity on bāṇāsuran since he felt ashamed at the action of rudran, let go of bāṇāsuran with his life) – the one who has his head shaven and has applied ashes all over, his sons, jvaras (fire dēvatās), pidāri (durgā), agni – as all these personalities ran away showing their back; seeing that, kriṣṇa thought “Oh we started fighting those who are as good as women (in the aspect of fighting)!” and became embarrassed.

**vāṇanukku iranginān** – kriṣṇa thought about bāṇāsura’s helpless state as in “One who has no refuge, has come to us surrendering” and showered his mercy upon him.

**mukkaṇān veḷgiyōda …** – rudra came there saying “I will protect you” but made bāṇa face the heat, and ran away along with his army; kriṣṇa became joyful after eliminating the thousand shoulders of the very strong bāṇa. He severed the shoulders which helped bāṇa worship other dēvatās. \[When asked if the hands which vorśipped the other dēvatās should be severed\] Since it is said that saluting with one hand should warrant the punishment of having that hand removed, those who worship other dēvatās should also face the same punishment.

**paḷḷi kamalam …** – It is mercifully said that “parāśara bhattar would eagerly like this pāsuram”. The big-mouthed male crab got stuck in the middle of the flower. The female crab was pregnant. The male crab wanted to give something sweet to the female crab, It went into the lotus flower; as the sun had set and the flower became closed, it spent the night there; the buds and fragrance from the flower got smeared on its body, As the sun rose, the flower opened. Right from the time the male crab left, the female crab was waiting for the male crab, keeping the doors open. As it saw the male crab, due to staying out for the whole night and the bodily marks, it turned its face away, went in and shut the door. After parāśara bhattar explained this, piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar said “Should the female crab not analyse the situation and then if the mistake is proven, shut the door?” bhattar responded “What can we do! Here it is ruling of the woman i.e., tāyār, where she is beyond questioning”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.7. Midaiya vanda

*midaiyā vanda vēl mannar vīya visayan tēr kadavikkudaiyā varai onṟu eduttu āyar kōvāy ninṟān kūrāḻippadaiyān vēdam nāngu aindu vēḷvi angam āṟu isai ēḻnadaiyā valla andaṇar vāḻ naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

midaiyā – gathering as a crowd; vanda – came (for battle); vēl – having the weapon, spear; mannar – kings; vīya – to be killed; visayan – arjunan’s; tēr – chariot; kadavi – one who conducted; onṟu varai – a mountain which was within his reach; kudaiyā eduttu – lifted it as an umbrella (and protected the covherd); āyar kōvāy – (due to that) being the lord for covherds; ninṟān – one who remained; kūr āḻi padaiyān – having sharp tiruvāḻi (chakra) as the weapon; nāngu vēdam – four vēdams; aindu vēḷvi – panca mahā yajñams (five great sacrifices); āṟu angam – six ancillary subjects of vēdam such as śīkśā etc; ēḻ isai – sapta svarams (seven tunes); nadaiyā valla – those who are always capable of conducting; andaṇar – brāhmaṇas; vāḻ – eternally residing; naṟaiyūr ninṟa – one who is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; nambi – nambi is the refuge

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa conducted arjunan’s chariot to have the kings who came for battle in a crowd, with the weapon, spear, killed. He remained as the lord of the covherds, due to lifting of gōvardan mountain which was within his reach, as an umbrella. He is having sharp tiruvāḻi (chakra) as the weapon. Such bhagavān is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr where brāhmaṇas, who are always capable of conducting four vēdams, panca mahā yajñams, six ancillary subjects of vēdam such as śīkśā and sapta svarams, are eternally residing. Such nambi is our refuge.

**midaiyā vanda …** – All the evil kings/persons gathered in duryōdana’s side. To make the earth tremble, the kings came in a huge crowd with weapons. To have them killed, kriṣṇa conducted the chariot to accomplish the task instead of taking up arms. To stop the hail sent by indra, kriṣṇa lifted up the gōvardan mountain which was within his reach, and kept it as an umbrella to stop the rain. While lifting the mountain, he did it effortlessly.

**āyar kō …** – He remained as the lord of the covherds and cows, to be crowned by indra in gōvinda pattābhiśēkam.

**kūr āḻip padaiyān** – Even while having the sharp chakra in his hand, he lifted the mountain. kriṣṇa thought “\[Instead of killing him\] if we keep him hungry and torment him, he will realise his mistake and stop the hail. Until then, let me take care of my people/cows”.

**vēda nāngu …** – The abode where brāhmaṇas who can conduct all of these, are residing. To protect themselves, they are capable of protecting him with their knowledge and conduct.

## 6.7.8. Pandar viralal

*pandār viralāḷ pānjāli kūndal mudikkap pāradattukandār kaḷiṟṟuk kaḻal mannar kalangac cangam vāy vaittānsendāmarai mēl ayanōdu sivanum anaiya perumaiyōrnandā vaṇkai maṟaiyōr vāḻ naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pandu Ar – Having a ball (for sport); viralāḷ – having fingers; pānjāli – draupadi; kūndal – (her) hair; mudikka – to tie; bāradattu – in mahābhārata war; kandu Ar – filled with the fragrance of mada jalam (fluid which flows out of elephant); kaḷiṟu – coming atop elephants; kaḻal – having valorous anklet; mannar – kings (such as duryōdana et al); kalanga – to become bewildered; sangam – śrī pāncajanyam (the divine conch); vāy vaittān – one who blew it, placing on his divine mouth; sendāmarai mēl – one who was born from the reddish flower (on the divine navel); ayanōdu – along with brahmā; sivamum anaiya – along with rudra, completely; perumaiyōr – having the talent; nandā – imperishable; vaṇ – magnanimous; kai – having hands; maṟaiyōr – brāhmaṇas; vāḻ – eternally residing; naṟaiyūr ninṟa – one who is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; nambi – nambi is the refuge

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

To make draupadi who is holding a ball in her fingers, tie her hair, kriṣṇa blew śrī pāncajanyam (the divine conch) in mahābhāratam war which caused bewilderment to the kings such as duryōdan et al who were wearing valorous anklets and were coming atop elephants which are filled with the fragrance of mada jalam. Such bhagavān is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr where brāhmaṇas, who are having talent as brahmā who was born from the reddish lotus flower and rudra, and having imperishable, magnanimous hands, are eternally residing. Such nambi is our refuge.

**pandār …** – draupadi who is apt to play with the ball and enjoy and is not deserving to be insulted. Such draupadi, being insulted, spread out her hair and vowed saying “I will not tie my hair until my enemies are killed and I stomp on their heads”.

**bāradattu …** – kriṣṇa blew his śrī pāncajanyam to burn down the kings who had come to fight and who had valorous anklets indicating that they can control and ride elephants, which roam around breaking pillars.

**sendāmarai …** – The eternal abode of the brāhmaṇas who are individually capable to do creation and annihilation and having more magnanimity than brahmā and rudra.

## 6.7.9. Arum piraiyum

*āṟum piṟaiyum aravamum adambum sadai mēl aṇindu udalamnīṟum pūsi ēṟūrum iṟaiyōn senṟu kuṟai irappamāṟu onṟillā vāsa nīr varai mārbagalattu aḷittu ugandānnāṟum poḻil sūḻndu aḻagāya naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āṟum – gangā river; piṟaiyum – crescent moon; aravamum – snake; adambum – adamba flower; sadaimēl – on his matted hair; aṇindu – wearing; udalam – on the body; nīṟu – ashes; pūsiyum – smearing; ēṟu ūrum – riding the bull; iṟaiyōn – rudra, who considers himself to be īśvaran; senṟu – reached; kuṟai – shortcoming (of brahmahatti dōśam – defect caused by plucking brahmā’s head); irappa – as he prayed (to eliminate it) (at that time); varai – mountain like; agalam – vast; mārvattu – present on his divine chest; onṟu māṟu illā – not having a match; vāsa nīr – fragrant sweat; aḷittu – gave; ugandān – one who became joyful; nāṟum – abundantly fragrant; poḻil – by the gardens; sūḻndu – surrounded; aḻagāya – beautiful; naṟaiyūr ninṟa – one who is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; nambi – nambi is the refuge

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

rudra who considers himself to be īśvaran and who is wearing gangā river, crescent moon, snake and adamba flower on his matted hair and is having ashes smeared on his body, reached bhagavān and prayed to him to eliminate his shortcoming; bhagavān gave the matchless, fragrant sweat from his vast mountain like divine chest and became joyful. Such bhagavān is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by abundantly fragrant gardens. Such nambi is our refuge.

**āṟum piṟaiyum …** – rudra was prideful thinking “I can protect myself” and was having such qualities like having gangā river in a small portion of his matted hair, to show that he was an enjoyer, he was having the crescent moon, having snake, having adamba flower, also having ashes smeared on his body and was riding a bull. Such rudra considers himself to be īśvara. He plucked the head of brahmā who is the guru for the whole world (including rudra) and his father, and became pātaki (great sinner) and went to sarvēśvaran and informed his trouble.

**māṟu …** – bhagavān gave the sweat from his divine form which is known in cāndōjña upaniśat as “*sarva ganda:*” (the abode of all fragrances) and became joyful thinking “We got to remove the suffering of rudra who was roaming around respectfully”.

**nāṟum poḻil …** – Beautiful tirunaṟaiyūr is surrounded by fragrant garden which will mesmerise bhagavān who is said to be “*sarva ganda:”*.

## 6.7.10. Nanmaiyudaiya

*nanmai udaiya maṟaiyōr vāḻ naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyaikanni madiḷ sūḻ vayal mangaik kaliyan oli sey tamiḻ mālaipanni ulagil pāduvār pādu sārā paḻa vinaigaḷmanni ulagam āṇḍu pōy vānōr vaṇanga vāḻvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nanmai udaiya – having goodness of ananyaprayōjatai (not expecting any other benefits); maṟaiyōr – brāhmaṇas; vāḻ – residing; naṟaiyūr ninṟa – mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; nambiyai – on nambi; kanni – imperishable; madiḷ – by forts; vayal – by fertile fields; sūḻ – surrounded; mangai – leader of tirumangai region; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; oli sey – mercifully composed; tamiḻ mālai – these ten pāsurams which are garland of tamiḻ words; panni – analysed; ulagil – in this world; pāduvār pādu – near those who sing; paḻa vinaigaḷ – ancient karmas; sārā – will not come; (further); manni – being here for a long time; ulagam – this world; āṇḍu – rule over; pōy – going (subsequently to paramapadam); vānōr – nityasūris; vaṇanga – to be honoured; vāḻvār – will get to enjoy bhagavān

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār, the leader of the tirumangai region, which is surrounded by forts and fertile fields, mercifully composed these ten pāsurams which are garland of tamiḻ words on nambi who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr where brāhmaṇas, who are having goodness of ananyaprayōjatai are residing. Ancient karmas will not come near those who analyse and sing these pāsurams, in this world. Being here for a long time, they will rule over this world, and subsequently going to paramapadam, will get to enjoy bhagavān, being honoured by nityasūris.

**nanmai udaiya …** – One who is complete in all auspicious qualities and is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr where brāhmaṇas who are ananyaprayōjanas are residing.

**kanni …** – āḻvār who is the king of tirumangai region which is surrounded by fort which acts as a protective layer, mercifully composed with tune these ten pāsurams which are like garland of tamiḻ words. Sins will not come close to those who analyse and sing these pāsurams, in this world. Instead of having to pray for the elimination of the sins as they come, the previously accumulated wealth of sins will themselves leave thinking “This is not our abode”.

**manni ulagam āṇḍu …** – Remaining in this samsāra, they will enjoy worldly pleasures and then will reach paramapadam and will eternally enjoy bhagavān, to be honoured by nityasūris.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8 Man konda

## 6.8.1. Man konda

*mān koṇḍa tōl mārvil māṇiyāy māvali maṇṭhān koṇḍu tāḷāl aḷanda perumānaittēn koṇḍa sāral tiruvēngadattānainān senṟu nādi naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mān koṇḍa – deer’s; tōl – skin (kriṣṇājinam); mārvil – wearing on his chest; māṇiyāy – being a brahmacāri \[bachelor\]; māvali – from mahābali; maṇ – earth; tān – He who is the owner; koṇḍu – accepted as dānam (charity) and making it his own; tāḷāl – (subsequently) with his divine feet; aḷanda – occupied; perumānai – being the lord of all; tēn koṇḍa – having honey; sāral – having slopes; tiruvēngadattānai – one who is mercifully present in tiruvēngadam; nān – I, who was facing away from him until now; nādic cenṟu – went searching; naṟaiyūril – in tirunaṟaiyūr; kaṇḍēn – got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

vāmana bhagavān, the owner of the earth, being a brahmacāri wearing deer’s skin on his chest, accepted that earth from mahābali as dānam and made it his own. Subsequently, with his divine feet he occupied it fully. Such bhagavān is mercifully present in tiruvēngadam which is having mountain-slopes having honey. I, who was facing away from him all along, went searching for him and got to see him in tirunaṟaiyūr.

**mān koṇḍa …** – Being a brahmacāri who is having deer’s skin on his chest, he showed his humble form to mahābali and melted mahābali’s heart, and then only accepted the earth.

**māṇiyāy …** – Appearing so apt in his role as to make people think “He must have been seeking alms even in his previous birth”. Well focussed on the begging as said in “I won’t leave without getting earth”.

**māvali maṇ …** – mahābali’s earth which was forcefully taken as in the case of climbing an elephant which was resting, was accepted by bhagavān through alms – that is how it appears to be. bhagavān made earth as mahābali’s possession while it was not so, and then accepted it from him, as if accepting something which does not belong to him already. He remains “We just need to get it from mahābali through any means”.

**tāḷāl …** – As soon as the water (which was poured by mahābali to initiate the dānam) touched bhagavān’s hand, before mahābali’s mind changed, he sent his divine feet up to the boundary and accepted it. He measured the earth, which is a tough terrain, with his tender, divine feet which are carefully held on her bosoms and eyes by pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi).

**perumānai** … – He, who is the lord of all and greater than all, placed himself in a lowly form, still it does not appear lowly – that is how he can do it.

**tēn koṇḍa …** – One who has arrived and is standing in tiruvēnagadam which has slopes with lots of honey. He stood in tirumalā to help those who missed out on his grace while measuring the world with his divine feet.

**nān senṟu nādi …** – When he came searching for me, I looked away and remained separated from him; but now I am going in search of him.

**naṟaiyūril …** – Instead of travelling a long distance and seeing him in paramapadam, I got to see him in tirunaṟaiyūr, just as one would get water where he was thirsty.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.2. Munnirai munnal

*munnīrai munnāḷ kadaindānai mūḻtta nāḷannīrai mīnāy amaitta perumānaittennāli mēya tirumālai emmānainannīr vayal sūḻ naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

munnīrai – ocean which is having three types of water viz river water, ground water, rain water; munnāḷ – in the past; kadaindānai – being the one who churned; mūḻtta nāḷ – during the deluge (when that ocean consumed the higher worlds too); mīnāy – being with the form of fish; annīrai – that ocean; amaitta – one who placed in his stomach; perumānai – being the lord; then Ali – in the beautiful tiruvāli; mēya – eternally residing; tirumālai – being the supreme lord who is with śrī mahālakśmi; emmānai – being my lord; nal nīr – having water which is having the goodness of being abundant; vayal sūḻ – surrounded by fertile fields; naṟaiyūril – in tirunaṟaiyūr; kaṇḍēn – got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In the past, bhagavān churned the ocean which is having three types of water viz river water, ground water and rain water. During the deluge, he assumed the form of a fish and placed that ocean in his stomach. He is eternally residing in the beautiful tiruvāli as the supreme lord who is with śrī mahālakśmi and is also my lord. I got to see him in tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by fertile fields which are having water which is having the goodness of being abundant

**munnīr …** – One who churned the ocean which has three types of water, in kruta yugam. When the dēvatās were tormented by asuras, to help the dēvatās, he churned the ocean.

**mūḻtta nāḷ …** – When the world was consumed by deluge.

**annīrai …** – That same water (which was kept as protection for the world) spread everywhere, just like the guards of a town themselves stealing; at that time, bhagavān appeared as a fish and held the world in a small portion of his fin. To churn the ocean, he had to gather the dēvatās and asuras and still stood there showing his supremacy; but while saving the world from the deluge, he had no such support and had to do it on his own. While accomplishing a task, he is capable of both working with many others and doing it on his own. Such lord. These acts are those of the supreme lord.

**tiruvāli …** – One who is mercifully present in tiruvāli along with śrī mahālakśmi, to eliminate my deluge of this samsāram, just as he churned the ocean to help dēvatās and protected the world from deluge. Alternative explanation – sarvēśvaran who fulfils the desire of everyone such as dēvatās, worldly people and myself, without any difference. One who has the prāpti (relationship) with everyone.

**nal nīr …** – tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by fertile fields having not bad water, but good water which is in abundance.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.3. Tuvaya pul

*tūvāya puḷ ūrndu vandu tuṟai vēḻammūvāmai nalgi mudalai tuṇittānaidēvādi dēvanaic cengamalak kaṇṇānaināvāyuḷānai naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tū āya – faultless; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); ūrndu – rode; tuṟai – on the banks (of the pond); vandu – went; vēḻam – śrī gajēndrāḻvān; mūvāmai – to not suffer; nalgi – mercifully showing his grace; mudalai – the crocodile (which was his enemy); tuṇittānai – one who broke it into two pieces; dēvādi dēvanai – being the lord of nityasūris; sem kamalam – like reddish lotus flower; kaṇṇānai – having divine eyes; nāvāy – in the divyadēśam named tirunāvāy; uḷānai – one who is mercifully residing in; naṟaiyūril – in tirunaṟaiyūr; kaṇḍēnē – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The lord of the nityasūris rode on the faultless periya tiruvadi and went to the banks of the pond. He mercifully showered his grace on śrī gajendrāḻvān to stop his suffering and broke the crocodile into two pieces. He is having reddish lotus flower like divine eyes. He is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirunāvāy. I got to see such bhagavān in tirunaṟaiyūr.

**tūvāya …** – When sarvēśvaran climbs on garudāḻvār, nudges-kicks his back with the divine feet, he will become rejuvenated due to the joy of being touched by bhagavān and will start praising “How joyful my dear lord’s touch is!” garudāḻvār is having such pure mouth. Alternative explanation – having faultless śabdam (vēdam) as his form. It is said in catu:ślōki “*vēdātmā*” (garudāḻvār is the soul of vēdam). Not being satisfied with gaurdāḻvār’s natural speed, bhagavān pulled him along in a super fast manner and reached the banks of the pond where śrī gajēndrāḻvān was suffering.

**vēḻam mūvāmai nalgi …** – He showed his favouritism towards the elephant, so that it is not killed. That is, before the freshness of the flower changed, he accepted it at his divine feet.

**mudalai …** – He averted his own suffering as well. When his devotee was in trouble, even if \[the devotee\] waited for a fraction of a second, his good qualities will be lost. He reached the banks of the pond where śrī gajēndrāḻvān was suffering, carefully pulled both of them out and placed them on the banks, and caused torment for the crocodile exclusively without harming the elephant. bhattar mercifully explained “Just as a prisoner who was hand-cuffed along with the prince, he will get milk and food which the prince gets. Here the crocodile also got liberated from its suffering (in this birth as a crocodile)”.

**tuṇittānai –** Just as he would be angry at bhīśma et al, just as he would be angry at his enemies, though the crocodile is like a small insect, he angrily charged at it, due to its being inimical towards his devotee, considering it to a big enemy.

When asked “Who is the one who came with great anger to the banks of the pond where the elephant was suffering, without caring for him?” āḻvār says

**dēvādi dēvanai** – The lord of nityasūris who have no confusions.

**sem kamalak kaṇṇānai** – sarvēśvaran who is puṇḍarīkākśa (lotus-eyed).

**nāvāy uḷānai** – While he was having paramapadam as his divine assembly, he has come to tirunāvāy and is eternally residing here for my protection.

**naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēnē** – He is residing very near in tirunaṟaiyūr to make tirunāvāy look similar to paramapadam (in distance).

## 6.8.4. Oda ariyay

*ōdā ariyāy iraṇiyanai ūn idandasēdār poḻil sūḻ tiruneermalaiyānaivādā malart tuḻāy mālai mudiyānaināḷ tōṟum nādi naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōdā – not stepping back (in front of enemies); ariyāy – being narasimha; iraṇiyan – hiraṇyan’s; ūnai – body; idanda – one, who tore down; sēdu Ar – very youthful; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruneermalaiyānai – being the one who is mercifully present on tiruneermalai; vādā – fresh; malar – having flower; tuḻāy – strung with tiruttuḻāy; mālai – garland; mudiyānai – one, who is wearing on the divine crown; nāḷdōṟum – every day; nādi – searching; naṟaiyūril – in tirunaṟaiyūr; kaṇḍēn – got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being narasimha who does not step back, bhagavān tore down hiraṇyan’s body; he is mercifully present in tiruneermalai which is surrounded by very youthful gardens; searching every day for that bhagavān who is wearing garland which is strung with fresh tiruttuḻāy flower, I got to see him in tirunaṟaiyūr.

**ōdā …** – narasimha who did not step back seeing the tough body of hiraṇyan. Alternative explanation – narasimha who is not seen in this world, in general. Tearing hiraṇyan’s body which was made strong through the boons, thinking “What if our devotees have to face such enemies!”, to eliminate such enemies, he remained in tiruneermalai which is surrounded by very youthful gardens. He is wearing a garland to protect the world. I got to see him here in tirunaṟaiyūr, by desiring everyday for the love nityasūris have to towards him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.5. Kallar madil

*kallār madiḷ sūḻ kadi ilangaik kār arakkanvallāgam kīḷa vari venjaram turandavillānai selva vibīdaṇaṟku vēṟāganallānai nādi naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kal Ar – built with rocks; madiḷ – by forts; sūḻ – surrounded; kadi – well-formed (due to having moat etc); ilangai – being the king of lankā; kār – lowly; arakkan – rāvaṇāsuran’s; val āgam – strong body; kīḷa – to be split; vari – beautiful; vem – fire-like; saram – arrow; turanda – one who launched; villānai – having bow; selvam – śrīmān (one who has the wealth of kainkaryam); vibīdaṇaṟku – towards śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān; vēṟāga – in a distinguished manner; nallānai – one who has affection; nādi – searching; naṟaiyūril – in tirunaṟaiyūr; kaṇḍēnē – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān having bow, launched beautiful, fire-like arrow to split the strong body of lowly rāvaṇāsuran who is the king of lankā which is surrounded by forts built with rocks and is well-formed. I searched and got to see such śrī rāma in tirunaṟaiyūr, who has affection towards śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān who is a śrīmān, in a distinguished manner.

**kal Ar …** – rāvaṇan who is dark in complexion, in lankā which is well protected by forts built with rocks. Alternatively – lowly rāvaṇan. (kār) kaṟuppu indicates both black colour and lowly nature.

**val āgam** – To split the strong body which does not get affected even by brahmāstram etc, one who is having the strong bow which can launch arrows which appear like arrows when they are launched and appear like fire when they hit the enemy target, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam ślōkam 46-22 “*dīpta pāvaka sangkāśai*: *śitai: kāncanabhūśaṇai*: l *na tvāmiccāmyaham draśtum rāmēṇa nihatam śarai*: ll” (I do not wish to see you killed by śrī rāma whose arrows are like burning fire, sharp and decorated with gold), he conducted the arrows, which appear like arrows while launching, but while entering the bodies of the enemies, they will appear like fire).

**selva vibīdaṇaṟku** … – He acquired the wealth due to the connection with śrī rāma as soon as he rose to the sky and remained there as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 16.17 “*antarikśagata: śrīmān*” (vibhīśaṇa, who went through the path of sky and who is wealthy).

**vēṟāga nallānai** – As sugrīva mahārājar et al stop śrī rāma from accepting vibhīśaṇāḻvān saying “We should not accept vibhīśaṇan who is coming”, perumāḷ insisted “I will not avoid accepting him”, sugrīva mahārājar said “In such case, the army of kiśkindā will retract” and perumāḷ said “You can do whatever you want; I will not abandon him in any manner”. In this manner, śrī rāma showed special affection towards śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān.

**nādi naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēn** – I searched for him and got to see him in tirunaṟaiyūr.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.6. Umbar ulagodu

*umbar ulagōdu uyir ellām undiyilvambu malar mēl padaittānai māyōnaiambanna kaṇṇāḷ asōdai tan singattainambanai nādi naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

umbar ulagōdu – Along with dēva lōkam; uyir ellām – all creatures; undiyil – in (his) tirunābi (divine navel); vambu – very fragrant; malar mēl – on the lotus flower; padaittānai – created; māyōnai – one who is having amazing ability; ambanna – matching arrow; kaṇṇāḷ – one who is having eyes; asōdai than – yaśōdā’s; singattai – son who is like a lion; nambanai – one who is trustworthy; nādi – searching; naṟaiyūril – in tirunaṟaiyūr; kaṇḍēnē – I got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān created all creatures along with dēva lōkam on the very fragrant lotus flower in his divine navel. He is having amazing ability. I searched and got to see the trustworthy one, who is like a lion and the son of yaśōdā, whose eyes are like arrows.

**umbar ulagu …** – sarvēśvaran who is an amazing entity and who, through his sankalpam (vow), created the abode of brahmā et al and all of humans et al, on the fresh flower in his divine navel.

The one who creates everything through his vow, truly incarnated.

**ambanna kaṇṇāḷ …** – piḷḷai uṟangāvilli dāsar would mercifully say “kriṣṇa got his attractive eyes from his mother”.

**nambanai** – One who is so trustworthy that those who approach him can submit themselves to him completely.

**nādi naṟaiyūril …** – Even while being in samsāram, we could trust him and surrender unto him.
