## 6.8.7. Katteru

*kattēṟu nīḷ sōlaik kāṇḍavattait tīmūttivittānai meyyam amarnda perumānaimattēṟu kaṟpagattai mādarkkāy vaṇ tuvarainattānai nādi naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kattu ēṟu – well guarded; nīḷ sōlai – having vast garden; kāṇḍavattai – kāṇḍava forest; tī – for agni (fire); mūtti vittānai – gave permission and sent; meyyam – in tirumeyyam; amarnda – eternally residing; perumānai – being supreme lord; mattu ēṟu – having abundance of honey; kaṟpagattai – kalpaka tree; mādarkkāy – for satyabhāmā; vaṇ tuvarai – in beautiful śrī dvārakā (at satyabhāmā’s residence); nattānai – one who planted; nādi – searched; naṟaiyūril – in tirunaṟaiyūr; kaṇḍēn – got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa gave permission and sent agni to consume the kāṇḍava forest which is having well guarded, vast garden. He is eternally residing in tirumeyyam as the supreme lord. He brought the kalpaka tree which is having abundance of honey and planted at the residence of satyabhāmā, in beautiful śrī dvārakā. I searched and got to see him in tirunaṟaiyūr.

**kattēṟu nīḷ sōlai** – Due to being indra’s well-guarded forest, it was well protected.

**kāṇḍavattai tī mūtti vittānai** – When arjuna and kriṣṇa were playing with a ball on the banks of river yamunā, agni (dēvatā) came there in the guise of a brāhmaṇa. kriṣṇa ordered him saying “You consume indra’s forest”.

**mūtti vittānai** – Set him on the evil beasts. Since agni would fear to enter, here āḻvār is saying how difficult it is for kriṣṇa to convince him to go in.

**meyyam amarnda perumānai** – One who is mercifully residing in tirumeyyam thinking “What if more people come and request like that?”

**mattēṟu …** – kalpaka tree which has abundance of fragrance.

**mādarkkāy** – He completely manifested tādartyam (existing for someone) towards śrī satyabhāmāp pirātti.

**vaṇ tuvarai nattānai** … – As enmity grows between indra and narakāsura, kriṣṇa went to fight for the sake of indra against narakāsura, killed narakāsura and returned to svargam and helped indra et al settle down there. At that time, kalpaka flowers arrived for indrāṇi and as śrī satyabhāmāp pirātti asked some flower for her, indrāṇi said “This is not applicable for you (humans); you sweat \[celestials don’t sweat\]; need the support of the earth to stand \[celestials don’t need the earth to stand\]” and wore it highlighting her celestial nature and śrī satyabhāmāp pirātti’s human nature. śrī satyabhāmāp pirātti, held on to kriṣṇa’s shoulder and told “This kalpaka tree is to be planted in my backyard”. He then uprooted one such tree and planted it in śrī dvārakā and then only he took bath (i.e., he looked into his next task). piḷḷai amudanār would say “indra was comfortably settled in his abode by kriṣṇa even before \[kriṣṇa\] returned to śrī dvārak; when kriṣṇa plucked a waste tree – seeing that indra went after kriṣṇa with his vajrāyudam – what a shame!”. I got to see the lord who has arrived in tirunaṟaiyūr to fulfil my desire.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.8. Mannin mi bharam

*maṇṇin mī bhāram keduppān maṟa mannarpaṇṇin mēl vanda padai ellām bhāradattuviṇṇin mīdēṟa visayan tēr ūrndānainaṇṇi nān nādi naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇṇin mī – caused (by demoniac clan) on the earth; bhāram – burden; keduppān – to destroy; maṟam – angry; mannar – kings; paṇṇin mēl – with the army groups; vanda – came opposing; padai ellām – all of the army; viṇṇin mīdu – vīra svargam (to attain heaven for valorous fight and death); ēṟa – to reach; bhāradattu – in mahābhārata war; visayan – arjunan’s; tēr ūrndānai – one who conducted the chariot; naṇṇi – desired; nān nādi – I searched; naṟaiyūril – in tirunaṟaiyūr; kaṇḍēnē – got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa conducted arjunan’s chariot in mahābhārata war to destroy the burden caused by demons on the earth, by making all the angry kings who came with their armies reach vīra svargam. I desired and searched for him and got to see him in tirunaṟaiyū.

**maṇṇin mī bhāram …** – The earth, which can tolerate everything, cried out saying “I cannot tolerate anymore”. kriṣṇa conducted arjunan’s chariot in such a way that those karṇa, duryōdana et al along with their armies could not return to their homes and instead they attain vīra svargam.

**naṇṇi nān nādi …** – Approaching him with desire; I got to see in tirunaṟaiyūr matching my desire.

## 6.8.9. Pongeru

*pongēṟu nīḷ sōdip ponnāḻi tannōdumsangēṟu kōlat tadakkaip perumānaikkongēṟu sōlaik kudandaik kidandānainangōnai nādi naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pongu ēṟu – increasing more and more and being in abundance; nīḷ sōdi – having incomprehensible radiance; pon – beautiful; āḻi tannōdum – along with sudarśana āḻvān (cakkarattāḻvār); sangu – śrī pāncajanyāḻvān; ēṟu – being present; kōlam – beautiful; tadam kai – having vast divine hands; perumānai – being sarvēśvaran; kongu ēṟu – having abundance of honey; sōlai – surrounded by garden; kudandai – in tirukkudandai; kidandānai – one who is mercifully resting; nam kōnai – our lord; nādi – searched; naṟaiyūril – in tirunaṟaiyūr; kaṇḍēnē – got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is being with beautiful sudarśana āḻvān who is having incomprehensible radiance which is increasing more and more and being in abundance, and śrī pāncajanyāḻvān, on his beautiful, vast, divine hands. He is mercifully resting in tirukkudandai which is surrounded by garden, having abundance of honey. I searched for such lord and got to see him in tirunaṟaiyūr.

**pongēṟu nīḷ sōdi …** – sarvēśvaran who is having beautiful divine shoulders which are with beautiful tiruvāḻi which is having unlimited radiance, which is rising like flood water and śrī pāncajanyām. The beauty of his divine shoulders is such that even without the āḻvārs (śankam and cakram), they need to be rid of evil eyes through hāratti. They are like ornaments for ornaments (i.e. bhagavān’s shoulder itself is an ornament for him – on top it there is śankam and cakram).

**kongēṟu sōlai …** – kongu – fragrance, honey. Just as his presence in paramapadam is for nityasūris, one who became our lord. I got to see him in tirunaṟaiyūr where he has descended for us.

## 6.8.10. Mannu madurai

*mannu madurai vasudēvar vāḻ mudalainannaṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyai vambaviḻtārkkannavilum tōḷān kaliyan oli vallārponnulagil vānavarkkup puttēḷir āguvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mannu – having connection with bhagavān always; madurai – in śrī maturā; vāḻ – for his sustenance and greatness; mudalai – one who is the reason; nal naṟaiyūr – in the distinguished tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – mercifully present; nambiyai – on the one who is complete with auspicious qualities; vambu aviḻ tār – wearing fragrant garland; kal navilum – said to be rock (strong); tōḷān – having shoulders; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; oli – these ten pāsurams, which have been mercifully spoken; vallār – those who are able to learn and recite; pon ulagil – in the beautiful paramapadam; vānavarkku – for nityasūris (who are there); puttēḷir – as (vorśippable) dēvatās; āguvar – will become

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa who is the reason for vasudēva’s sustenance and greatness, in śrī maturā which is always connected to bhagavān, is mercifully present in the distinguished tirunaṟaiyūr as the one who is complete with auspicious qualities. tirumangai āḻvār who is wearing fragrant garland and is having shoulders which are said to be rock, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams. Those who are able to learn and recite these pāsurams will become vorśippable dēvatās for the nityasūris in the beautiful paramapadam.

**mannu madurai …** – Just as a forest where elephants will be born again and again, śrī maturā is having eternal connection with bhagavān as in śrī vāmanāvatāram, it was known as siddāśramam where he performed tapasya, in śrī rāmāvatāram, śatrughnāḻvān eliminated the evil enemies from there and ruled over and in kriṣṇāvatāram, kriṣṇa himself joyfully appeared.

**vasudēvar …** – kriṣṇa is the cause for śrī vasudēvar’s existence. He constantly sees kriṣṇa and holds onto his existence.

**nal naṟaiyūr …** – The one who is complete in auspicious qualities and who is present in tirunaṟaiyūr which is having more goodness than śrī maturā \[due to divine, eternal presence in arcā form\].

**vambaviḻ tār …** – tirumangai āḻvār who is wearing fresh garland which is supported by the shoulders which are said to be rock, mercifully composed this garland in the form of ten tamiḻ pāsurams, with tune. Those who are able to master it, will become vorśippable deyvam for nityasūris who are present in paramapadam. They are also said to be, as in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-9-9-vaigundham-pugudhalum/) “*vaigundan tamar emar*” (these śrīvaiṣṇavas, who have attained śrīvaikuṇṭanāta); they will become refuge for the nityasūris.

## 6.9 Pedai adartta

## 6.9.1. Pedai adartta

*pedai adartta madavannam piriyādu malark kamalammadal eduttu madu nugarum vayal udutta tirunaṟaiyūrmudai adartta siram ēndi mūvulagum bali tirivōnidar kedutta tiruvāḷan iṇaiyadiyē adai nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pedai – by the feminine spouse; adartta – tormented due to romantic fight (due to that); madam – became submissive; annam – the bird, swan; piriyādu – without separating from its spouse (always remaining together); kamala malar – in the lotus flower; madal eduttu – removing the petals; madu – honey; nugarum – drinking; vayal – by fertile fields; udutta – surrounded; tirunaṟaiyūr – one who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; mudai adartta – very stinking; siram – brahma kapālam (brahmā’s skull); ēndi – holding in his hand; mū ulagum – in the three worlds; bali – for bhikśā (alms); tirivōn – one who roamed around, his; idar – sorrow; kedutta – eliminated; tiruvāḷan – śrīya:pati’s; iṇai – matching with each other; adi – divine feet; nenjē – Oh heart!; adai – try to surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The male swan became submissive towards the female swan due to being tormented by the female swan due to romantic fight that they had. Hence, the male swan remained without separating from its spouse and both are drinking honey in the fertile fields which surround tirunaṟaiyūr. bhagavān is mercifully residing in such tirunaṟaiyūr. Such śriya:pati eliminated the sorrow of rudra who is holding the very stinking brahma kapālam in his hand and roamed around the three worlds for bhikśā. Oh heart! Try to surrender unto the divine feet of such lord, which match each other.

**pedai adartta mada annam** – Since the male swan is roaming around the flower, the female swan is always suspecting the male swan \[that it may be seeking other female swans\]. The submissive male swan, which was tormented by the female swan, went to the female swan and the tables turned around. It started showing its teeth (seeking enjoyment), held the female swan’s feet and prayed.

**piriyādu** – Not even separating for a moment. Not even going in search of honey thinking “We need to give something sweet to the female swan”.

**malark kamalam madal eduttu** – Instead of going to another flower, remaining in the same flower, eliminating the petals in that same flower, it will taste the honey a bit and then feed that to the female swan also.

This is how the fertile fields are seen in this town. The one who is present inside the town is such that, anyone who has any amount of pride can enter.

**mudai …** – rudra, plucked the head of brahmā who is the guru (elder, teacher) of the world and also his own father, and due to that became pātaki (big sinner); mudai – durgandam – stench. Holding such brahma śiras (brahmā’s head), just as a person who ruled a town became roaming in the town with the skull in his hand, and roamed around seeking alms in the same place where he had ruled previously, as the īśvara.

**idar kedutta tiruvāḷan** – bhagavān’s divine heart became wounded thinking “Why such a honourable person has become insulted!”, and he eliminated the curse for Siva.

When asked “What is the reason for his help?” āḻvār says

**tiruvāḷan** – Since he is said to be śriya:pati, as said in mātsya purāṇam 182 “*tatra nārāyaṇa: śrīmān mayābhikśām prayācita: …* ” (That śrīman nārāyaṇa was asked for alms by me; by his mercy, the skull which got stuck to my hand broke into many pieces).

His,

**iṇai adiyē adai nenjē** – Oh heart! You seek the divine feet which are held even by prideful/powerful persons during dangerous times.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.9.2. Kaliyarum

*kaḻiyārum kanasangam kalandu engum niṟaindēṟivaḻiyāra muttīnṟu vaḷangodukkum tirunaṟaiyūrpaḻiyārum viṟal arakkan parumudigaḷ avai sidaṟaaḻalāṟum saram turandān adiyiṇaiyē adai nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaḻi – saltpans; ārum – to fill; kanam – great; sangam – conces; engum – everywhere; kalandu – arrived; niṟaindu – remaining in rows; ēṟi – (subsequently, from those saltpans) climbing out; vaḻi Ara – to fill the streets; muttu – pearls; īnṟu – yielded; vaḷam kodukkum – giving prosperity; tirunaṟaiyūr – tirunaṟaiyūr; paḻi ārum – having very bad reputation; viṟal – strong; paru – huge; avai mudigaḷ – those (ten) heads; sidaṟa – to be severed and to fall down; aḻal ārum – fire like; saram – arrows; turandān – launched, his; iṇai – matching with each other; adi – divine feet; nenjē – Oh heart!; adai – try to surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The great conces arrived everywhere to fill the saltpans, remained in rows and subsequently climbed up and filled the streets and yielded pearls, giving propserity to tirunaṟaiyūr. śrī rāma launched his fire like arrows to sever and fell the huge heads of the strong rāvaṇāsura who was having a very bad reputation. Oh heart! Try to surrender unto his divine feet which match each other.

**kaḻi ārum …** – The conces from the ocean will enter the saltpans to fill them, seeking pure water from the salt water of the ocean.

**kana sangam kalandengum niṟaindēṟi** – Just as everyone will gather here in aippasi utsavam \[In śrīrangam, in aippasi (tulā) māsam, an annual brahmōtsavam was celebrated. That was discontinued subsequently\], the conces due to being in pain from pregnancy, will arrive in a gathering and remain in rows.

**vaḻiyāra muttīnṟu** – The righteous people who envisioned and built the town, created small lanes and big streets; these conces will yield mountain of pearls enroute to limit movement of others.

**paḻiyārum …** – To scatter the heads of rāvaṇa, who has acquired a bad reputation due to not observing that sītāp pirātti is mother, roamed around independently due to his muscle strength. tirunaṟaiyūr is the abode of śrī rāma, who, instead of tormenting the enemies with arrows, would torment them with arrows which are like fire.

suḷai koṇḍa – having pieces; palanganigaḷ – from jackfruits; tēn pāya – as the honey floods; kadaligaḷin – from the plantain tree; tiḷai koṇḍa – huge; paḻam – fruits; keḻumi – in a dense manner; tigaḻ – shining; sōlai – having orchard; tirunaṟaiyūr – tirunaṟaiyūr; vaḷai koṇḍa – like the complexion of a conch; vaṇṇattan – for balarāma who is having a complexion; pin tōnṟal – one, who was born after (as brother); mū ulagōdu – with three worlds; aḷai – churned curd; veṇṇey – butter; uṇḍān than – one, who mercifully consumed, his; iṇai – matching with each other; adi – divine feet; nenjē – Oh heart!; adai – try to surrender

This is the abode of kriṣṇa who is born after balarāma, who is having the complexion of a conch and who mercifully consumed the three worlds, churned curd and butter. Oh heart! Try to surrender unto his divine feet which match each other.

**suḷai koṇḍa …** – As the jackfruits which are having lots of pieces ooze out the honey, the huge fruits in the plantain tree are present in a dense manner in orchards which surround tirunaṟaiyūr.

**vaḷai koṇḍa vaṇṇattan …**– One who is born after nambi mūtta pirān (balarāma).

**mū ulagu …** – Surrender unto the divine feet of the one, who mercifully consumed the vast earth, along with curd and butter.

*tunṟōḷit tukiṟpadalam tunni engum māḷigai mēlninṟāra vān mūdum nīḷ selvat tirunaṟaiyūrmanṟārak kudamādi varai eduttu maḻai taduttakunṟārum tiraḷ tōḷan kurai kaḻalē adai nenjē!*

tunṟu – dense; oḷi – placed in a row; tugil padalam – the group of flags made with clothes; māḷigai mēl – atop the homes; engum – everywhere; tunni – squeezed; Ara ninṟu – spread out; vān – the sky; mūdum – covering; nīḷ – incomprehensible; selvam – having wealth; manṟu Ara – all the open spaces; udam ādi – dancing with pot; varai eduttu – lifting the gōvardana mountain; maḻai tadutta – one who stopped the rain; kunṟu ārum – like a mountain; tiraḷ – rounded; tōḷan – one who is having shoulders, his; kurai – having resounding anklets; kaḻal – having divine feet; nenjē – Oh heart!; adai – try to surrender

In tirunaṟaiyūr, the group of flags made with clothes which are placed in a dense row, atop the homes, squeezed and spread everywhere and covered the sky. **tunṟōḷi …** – Flags which are made with cloth and placed in a dense and orderly manner, are spread everywhere and, being dense, cover the whole sky. tirunaṟaiyūr which is having such unlimited wealth.

**manṟāṟa …** – He performed kudakkūttu to eliminate the void nature of the places.

**varai eduttu …** – As indra sent the hailstorm, kriṣṇa lifted the gōvardana mountain and saved everyone.

**kunṟārum tiraḷ tōḷan …** – He is having rounded shoulders which make one think that he lifted the (gōvardana) mountain with his (shoulder) mountain.

## 6.9.5. Agir kuradum

*agiṟ kuṟadum sandanamum ambonnum aṇimuttummigak koṇarndu tirai undum viyan ponnit tirunaṟaiyūrpagal karanda sudarāḻip padaiyān ivvulagēḻumpugak karanda tiruvayiṟṟan ponnadiyē adai nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

agil kuṟadum – dēvadāru logs; sandanamum – sandalwood logs; ambonnum – beautiful gold; aṇi muttum – beautiful pearls; miga koṇarndu – gathering and bringing in abundance; tirai – waves; undum – pushing; viyan – amazing; ponni – having divine kāvēri; tirunaṟaiyūr – tirunaṟaiyūr; pagal – (in mahābhārata war) sun; karanda – covered; sudar – radiant; āḻi – sudarśana chakra; padaiyān – having as weapon; ivvulagu ēḻum – these seven worlds; puga – to make them enter; karanda – hid (to be not seen by anyone); tiruvayiṟṟan – having divine stomach, his; pon – beautiful; adiyē – divine feet; nenjē – Oh heart!; adai – Try to surrender

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirunaṟaiyūr is having amazing kāvēri which is gathering and bringing in abundance, dēvadāru logs, sandalwood logs, beautiful gold, beautiful pearls and pushing them there. sarvēśvaran covered the sun with his radiant weapon, sudarśana chakra and \[during deluge\] made the seven worlds enter his divine stomach and hide there. Oh heart! Try to surrender unto the beautiful, divine feet of such sarvēśvaran.

**agil …** – tirunaṟaiyūr is having amazing kāvēri which is gathering and bringing in abundance, dēvadāru logs, sandalwood logs, beautiful gold, beautiful pearls and pushing them there, beyond the capacity of the enjoyers.

**pagal kaṟanda sudar āḻip padaiyān** – With matchless radiance (sudarśana chakra), he hid the radiant object (sun). Sun’s radiance can be seen by eyes; but since sudarśana chakra’s radiance cannot be held in these eyes, the eyes became blinded for everyone.

**ivvulagum …** – One who is having divine stomach where he keeps all the worlds and when deluge comes and enquires as to where the worlds are, he will shrink his stomach and say that he does not know.

**pon adiyē adai** – Try to surrender unto the divine feet of one who places those who take refuge under him, within him, and makes himself as the target for deluge.

## 6.9.6. Pon muttum

*ponmuttum ariyugirum puḻaik kaimmā karikkōdumminnat taṇ tirai undum viyan ponnit tirunaṟaiyūrminnotta nuṇmarungul melliyalai tirumārbilmannat tān vaittugandān malaradiyē adai nenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirunaṟaiyūr is having the amazing kāvēri gathering gold, pearls, lion’s nails, tusks of elephants having trunk with hole, and pushing them with the help of its cool water’s waves. bhagavān has himself arranged to have periya pirātti, who is naturally tender and is having very slim waist that is matching lightning, on his beautiful chest and being joyful due to that. Oh heart! Try to surrender unto his divine feet which are tender like flower.

**pon muttum …** – As the lions fight with the elephants, the lions will break the elephants’ heads with a huge blow and pearls will come out of those heads. Those pearls, the gold which is present on the mountains, lions’ nails, elephants’ tusks, will be brought by the cool waves of kāvēri as lighning lights up the western direction, and pushed over.

**min otta …** – periya pirātti, who is having lightning like waist and who is more tender than bhagavān himself, is held on his divine chest.

**manna …** – Surrender unto the tender, divine feet of bhagavān who is always joyfully keeping periya pirātti on his divine chest. When we go and surrender unto him, if he starts counting our defects \[to punish us\], she will pacify him saying as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed).

Oh heart! Try to surrender unto the tender divine feet of such kriṣṇa.

**sīr taḻaitta kadir …** – Reddish paddy crops which have beautiful ears, from which eyes cannot be taken away by those who see them. Similar to that crop is lotus flower too.

**tār taḻaitta tuḻāy mudiyan …** – One who is having the garland around the divine crown which shows that he is the lord of nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti.

Will we not lose this beautiful sight of his standing posture?” He remained firm in tirunaṟaiyūr which has beautiful mansions which are as tall as mountain and are embedded with precious gemstones.

Oh heart! Try to surrender unto his divine feet which are matching each other.

**maṟai ārum …** – The abundant smoke from the great yajñas which are ordained in vēdam and performed by those brāhmaṇas who don’t expect any results, spread everywhere and covering the sky. Such unlimitedly wealthy abode where even the sky is not seen due to the smoke.

**piṟai ārum …** – rudran, who is having matted hair which shows that he is a sādaka (one who perceives penance to attain a goal) and having moon in his matted hair, which shows that he is an enjoyer; his father brahmā; both of them praise emperumān and surrender unto him.

**iṟaiyāgi ninṟān …** – He is greater than all since he is the refuge for those who are refuge for the people of this world; try to surrender unto his divine feet.

*tiṇkaḷaga madiḷ pudai sūḻ tirunaṟaiyūr ninṟānaivaṇkaḷaga nilaveṟikkum vayal mangai nagarāḷanpaṇkaḷagam payinṟa sīrp pādal ivai pattum vallārviṇkaḷagattu imaiyavarāy vīṟṟirundu vāḻvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

Those who recite these ten pāsurams, will reach paramapdam which is better than svargam etc and enjoy bhagavān mingling with nityasūis, revealing their greatness.

**tiṇ kaḷaga madiḷ pudai …** – sarvēśvaran is standing in tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by firm forts which were anointed with lime mortar. The moon appears like swans. The fertile fields which have such moon. tirumangai āḻvār who is the leader of tirumangai which is surrounded by such fertile fields.

**paṇ kaḷagam …** – Those who are experts in these ten pāsurams, which are composed with the best among the tunes.

**viṇ kaḷagattu imaiyavarāy …** – The most important among the enjoyable abodes, that is, paramapadam. Going there, being a part of the group of nityasūris, they will eternally enjoy bhagavān.

## 6.10 Kidanda nambi

## 6.10.1. Kidanda nambi

*kidanda nambi kudandai mēvik kēḻalāy ulagaiidanda nambi engaḷ nambi eṟijñar araṇ aḻiyakadanda nambi kadiyār ilangai ulagai īradiyālnadanda nambi nāmam sollil namō nārāyaṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kudandai – in tirukkudandai; mēvi – remaining firm; kidanda – reclining; nambi – complete (in beauty); kēḻalāy – as varāha; ulagai – worlds; idanda – digging out (from the wall of the oval shaped universe); nambi – complete (in skill); engaḷ – for us who are samsāris (materialistic); nambi – complete (in eliminating our defects); eṟijñar – enemies’; araṇ – fort; aḻiya – to be destroyed; ilangai – lankā; kadanda – occupied (and destroyed); nambi – complete (in valour); ulagai – worlds; īradiyāl – with two steps; nadanda – measured; nambi – complete (in amazing activities), his; nāmam – divine name; sollil – if we were to utter; namō nārāyaṇamē – it is in the form of “namō nārāyaṇa“

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

If we were to utter the divine name of sarvēśvaran who is complete in beauty in reclining posture, remaining firm in tirukkudandai, who is complete in skill in digging out the worlds as varāha, who is complete in eliminating the defects of ours who are samsāris, who is complete in valour to destroy the enemies’ fort and occupy/destroy lankā, who is complete in amazing activities to measure the worlds with two steps, it is in the form of “*namō nārāyaṇa*“.

**kidanda nambi …** – The beauty of bhagavān is more in tirukkudandai’s reclining posture than his presence in paramapadam and tiruppāṟkadal. He is mercifully reclining there with complete beauty without us having to worry, saying “What if we lose this sight if bhagavān changes his posture to standing and sitting?” He has no shortcoming in the skill to dig out the earth which got stuck to the wall of the oval shaped universe.

**engaḷ nambi** – One who is having the completeness to eliminate the shortcomings of ours, who are identified by shortcomings only, due to being samsāris.

**eṟijñar …** – Having completeness in valour due to destroying lankā where cruel demons have gathered, by destroying the forts of the enemies. Being complete in endless, amazing activities in measuring the vast earth by two steps. If we were to utter the divine name of such sarvēśvaran, it is in the form of “*namō nārāyaṇa*“.

## 6.10.2. Vidam tan udaiya

*vidam tān udaiya aravam veruvac ceruvil muna nāḷ muntadam tāmarai nīrp poygai pukku mikka tādāḷanidandān vaiyam kēḻalāgi ulagai īradiyālnadandān udaiya nāmam sollil namō nārāyaṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vidam udaiya – poisonous; aravam – snake named kāḷiyan; veruva – to fear; muna nāḷ – in the past (during kriṣṇāvatāram); seruvil – in war; mun – in front of the covherd boys; tadam – vast; tāmarai – lotus flowers; nīr – having water; poygai – in the pond; pukku – entered (and drove him out); mikka – great; tāḷāḷan – having divine feet; kēḻalāgi – being mahāvarāham (great boar); vaiyam – world; idandān – being the one who dug out (from the lower regions of the universe); ulagai – worlds (during vāmanāvatāram); īradiyāl – with two steps; nadandānudaiya – one who measured, his; nāmam – divine name; sollil – if we were to utter; namō nārāyaṇamē – it is in the form of “namō nārāyaṇa“

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In the past, during kriṣṇāvatāram, to cause fear for the poisonous snake named kāḷiyan, bhagavān who is having great divine feet, entered into the pond having vast lotus flowers and water, in a war, in front of the covherd boys; being mahāvarāham, he dug out the world; in vāmānavātāram, he measured the worlds with two steps; If we were to utter the divine name of sarvēśvaran, it is in the form of “*namō nārāyaṇa*“.

**vidam tān udaiya …** – What was spoken by āḻvār in the previous pāsuram, is being repeated by him again here (because he remembered that again). One day in a war, in front of the covherd boys, who are said as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.1.1 “*tannērāyiram piḷḷaigaḷ*” (thousand boys matching kriṣṇa), kriṣṇa entered the pond which had well-blossomed lotus flowers and abundant water which can be used in many ways. He drove out kāḷiyan from that pond – having such greatness.

**tāḷāḷan …** – one who has the divine feet.

He assumed the form which will not hesitate to enter water and mud, and rose after rescuing earth which was consumed by deluge. The name of the one who measured the worlds with his two steps.

## 6.10.3. Punadu analum

*pūṇādu analum taṟu kaṇ vēḻam maṟuga vaḷai maruppaippēṇān vāngi amudam koṇḍa perumān tirumārvanpāṇā vaṇḍu muralum kūndal āycci tayir veṇṇeynāṇādu uṇḍān nāmam sollil namō nārāyaṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pūṇādu – (even when bound to a pole) not being bound; analum – breathing fire; taṟu – rounded; kaṇ – having eyes; vēḻam – elephant named kuvalayāpeedam; maṟuga – to suffer; pēṇān – disregarding it; vaḷai – (its) curved; maruppai – tusk; vāngi – pulled; amudam – nectar; koṇḍa – (from kśīrābdi) one who churned and brought out; perumān – being sarvēśvaran; tirumārvan – being the one who is having pirātti in his divine chest; pāṇā – having songs; vaṇḍu – beetles; muralum – humming; kūndal – having hair; āycci – mother yaśōdā (preserved); tayir – curd; veṇṇey – butter; nāṇādu – disregarding (her); uṇḍān – one who mercifully consumed, his; nāmam – divine name; sollil – if we were to utter; namō nārāyaṇamē – it is in the form of “namō nārāyaṇa“

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

To make kuvalayāpeedam, not being bound, breathing fire and having rounded eyes, suffer, disregarding it \[it’s power\], sarvēśvaran pulled its curved tusk; being sarvēśvaran who is having pirātti in his divine chest, he churned and brought out nectar; disregarding mother yaśōdā who is having hair with singing beetles humming tunes, he mercifully consumed the curd and butter \[which were preserved by her\]; if we were to utter his divine name, it is in the form of “*namō nārāyaṇa*“.

**pūṇādu analaum taṟu kaṇ …** – To make kuvalayāpeedam which is not being bound by the pole, breathing fire on those who try to bind it, having rounded eyes as per the species, suffer, kriṣṇa effortlessly pulled its tusks, disregarding the fact that it is a very powerful elephant; further, he churned the ocean and retrieved the nectar from it and remained joyful from the joy of those who consumed it. The reason for that is because he is sarvēśvaran.

**tirumārvan …** – As said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1-9-105 “*paśyatām sarvadēvānām yayau vakśastalam harē:* ” (even as the celestial entities were watching, śrī mahālakśmi attained the divine chest of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)), he remains as the one with pirātti in his divine chest.

**pāṇā vaṇḍu …** – Having learnt \[to hum\], being drunk with honey, while singing, they are humming with tunes. Having such beetles in her hair.

**āycci tayir …** – If kriṣṇa steals the curd and butter which were preserved by mother yaśōdā and mercifully tries to consume it, she will bind him and beat him; at that time, he will think “Is there any shame in stealing the butter \[and getting caught\]? \[No\]”.

## 6.10.4. Kallar madil

*kallār madiḷ sūḻ kacci nagaruḷ naccip pādagattuḷellā ulagum vaṇanga irunda ammān ilangaik kōnvallāḷ āgam villāl muninda endai vibīdaṇaṟkunallān udaiya nāmam sollil namō nārāyaṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kal Ar – built with rocks; madiḷ – forts; sūḻ – surrounded; kacci nagaruḷ – in the city of kāncīpuram; nacci – with desire; ellā ulagum – all creatures; vaṇanga – to surrender; pādagattuḷ – in the divyadēśam named tiruppādagam, there; irunda – one who is mercifully residing; ammān – being sarvēśvaran; ilangai kōn – rāvaṇa, who is the king of lankā, his; val āḷ – very strong; āgam – body; villāl – with his bow; muninda – angrily destroyed; endai – being my lord; vibīdaṇaṟku – for vibhīśaṇāḻvān; nallānudaiya – one who is having affection, his; nāmam – divine name; sollil – if we were to utter; namō nārāyaṇamē – it is in the form of “namō nārāyaṇa“

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Desiring the town of kāncīpuram which is surrounded by forts built with rocks, sarvēśvaran is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tiruppādagam, to let all creatures surrender unto him. Being my lord, he angrily destroyed the very strong body of rāvaṇa, who was the king of lankā. He is having affection towards vibhīśaṇāḻvān. If we were to utter the divine name of such sarvēśvaran, it is in the form of “*namō nārāyaṇa*“.

**kallār madiḷ …** – Desiring kāncīpuram which is having forts which are a protective layer, sarvēśvaran is mercifully residing in tiruppādagam, to be surrendered to, by everyone.

**ilangai …** – My lord who eliminated the very strong body of rāvaṇa who was prideful thinking “Am I not the leader of this place?”, with his bow.

**vībīdaṇaṟku nallān …** – Just as śrī rāma had abundance hatred towards rāvaṇa, the elder brother, he had the same amount of affection towards vibhīśaṇa; the affection, which he collectively showed towards all the vānaras, he showed just towards śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān.

If we were to utter such bhagavān’s divine name,

**namō nārāyaṇamē** – nārāyaṇa indicates one who has vātsalyam (motherly forbearance).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.10.5. Kudaiya varaiyal

*kudaiyā varaiyāl nirai mun kātta perumān maruvādavidai tān ēḻum venṟān kōval ninṟān tennilangaiadaiyā arakkar vīyap porudu mēvi vengūṟṟamnadaiyā uṇṇak kaṇḍān nāmam namō nārāyaṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mun – in the past; kudaiyā – held as umbrella; varaiyāl – by the gōvardana mountain; nirai – herds of cattle; kātta – one who protected; perumān – being the lord; maruvāda – not joining (with each other); ēḻ vidaiyum – the seven bulls; venṟān – being the one who (killed and) won over; kōval – (now) in tirukkōvalūr; ninṟān – mercifully residing; then ilangai – residing in lankā which is in southern direction; adaiyā – those who did not surrender unto him; arakkar – rākśasas; vīya – to be killed; porudu – fought (with them); vem kūṟṟam – yama who is having a cruel nature; mēvi – (without fear) remaining firm; nadaiyā – having this as the yātrā (life); uṇṇak kaṇḍān – one who vowed to consume them, his; nāmam – divine name; sollil – if we were to utter; namō nārāyaṇamē – it is in the form of “namō nārāyaṇa“

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

In the past, by lifting the gōvardana mountains and holding it as an umbrella. kriṣṇa protected the herds of cattle using that mountain. Being the lord, he killed and won over the seven bulls which were not joining with each other. He is now mercifully residing in tirukkōvalūr. He fought with those rākśasas who were not surrendering unto him and were residing in lankā which is in southern direction, to get them killed. He vowed to get yama, who is having a cruel nature to consume them who are remaining firm. If we were to utter such divine name, it is in the form of “*namō nārāyaṇa*“

**kudaiyā varaiyāl …** – With the varai (montain), he protected nirai (cattle). When he lifted the mountain, he did not consider it as a burden, but held it as effortlessly as holding an umbrella for rain.

**perumān …** – Protecting the cows and the covherd boys, kriṣṇa remained as their lord,

**maruvāda …** – One who killed the seven bulls which were not aligning with each other due to being possessed by demons, and are equivalent to mrutyu (yama, death).

**kōval …** – He is mercifully present in tirukkōvalūr for those who are saying “that was in different times, we have lost”.

**then ilangai …** – The demons of lankā told śrī rāma “We will not align with you in any manner”; subsequently, he fought them, to have them killed.

**mēvi vengūṟṟam …** – In the past, when yama sees the rākśasas, he will fear; subsequently, he fought with them to finish them due to taking shelter of śrī rāma’s shoulders.

**nadaiyā …** – If we were to utter the divine name of the one who is having this as his yātrā (life), it is in the form of “*namō nārāyaṇa*“

## 6.10.6. Kana engum

*kāna eṇgum kurangum musuvum padaiyā adal arakkarmānam aḻittu ninṟa venṟi ammān enakku enṟumtēnum pālum amudumāya tirumāl tirunāmamnānum sonnēn namarum uraimin namō nārāyaṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kānam – in the forest; eṇgum – bears; kurangum – monkeys; musuvum – monkeys which are known as gōlāngūla \[also known as langur\]; padaiyā – having as army; adal – strong; arakkkar – rākśasas’; mānam – pride; aḻittu ninṟa – one who destroyed; venṟi – victorious; ammān – being the lord; enakku – for me; enṟum – always; tēnum – like honey; pālum – like milk; amudum – like nectar; āya – one who is enjoyable; tirumāl – śriya:pati’s; tirunāmam – divine name; namō nārāyaṇam – that which is said as “namō nārāyaṇa”; nānum – I, who am attached to worldly pleasures; sonnēn – uttered; namarum – our followers too; uraimin – utter

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The victorious lord destroyed the pride of the strong rākśasas using an army of bears, monkeys and gōlāngūla monkeys; I, who am attached to worldly pleasures, uttered that divine name which is said as “namō nārāyaṇa” of śriya:pati who is enjoyable like honey, milk and nectar for me; our followers should also utter that name.

**kāna eṇgum …** – While eliminating the pride of the strong rāvaṇa on seeing whom dēvatās such as indra et al run away, being unable to oppose him, the supreme lord, having bears and monkeys which are residing in the forest but not familiar with wars and which do not know the difference between left and right hand, as army, eliminated the pride of the strong rāvaṇa who destroyed dik pālakas (the protectors of the different directions).

**enakku enṟum …** – The divine name of śriya:pati which is enjoyable in all manner for me. He only enjoys bhagavān along with śrī mahālakśmi, as a couple. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bālakāṇḍam 1-31 “*ramyamāvasatam krutvā ramamāṇā vanē traya*: l *dēva gandarva sankāśās tatra tē nyavasan sukham*” (Those three (śrī rāma, sītāp pirātti and lakśmaṇa) who were like dēvas and gandarvas \[celestial entities\] and who were happily roaming in the forest, were living comfortably in a hermitage).

**nānum sonnēn …** – Have I, who have always uttered the names of worldly entities, not uttered this divine name? Now seeing this, anyone can utter this name. Oh those who are related to me! You also utter this name only.

**namō nārāyaṇamē** – Recite the name which is apt for us. In the āḻvārs’ gōśti, there is no one who thinks about any other name than this one. If they are there, they will only say “*āyiram*” (thousand), together \[instead of separately identifying those other divine names of bhagavān\]. [tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/06/thiruvaimozhi-9-3-1-orayiramay/) “*pēr āyiram koṇḍadōr pīdudaiyan*” (One who has the greatness of having thousand names), mahābhāratam “*dēvō nāma sahasravān*” (The shining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has thousand names) just as saying “he has many cows”. Only when śruti (vēdam) identifies bhagavān with other divine names, will they also identify like that. antaryāmi brāhmaṇam (the section which explains bhagavān being the in-dwelling supersoul) and kāraṇa vākyam (phrases which speak about bhagavān being the cause) explain this divine name only. Just as satyam (eternal), jñānam (sentient) and anantam (endless) are the qualities which identify his intrinsic nature, and jñānam (knowledge), śakti (ability) etc show his additional aspects, nārāyaṇa is the primary divine name which identifies bhagavān and other divine names reveal other aspects of his.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.10.7. Ninra varaiyum

*ninṟa varaiyum kidanda kadalum tisaiyum irunilanumonṟum oḻiyā vaṇṇam eṇṇi ninṟa ammānārkunṟu kudaiyā edutta adigaḷudaiya tirunāmamnanṟu kāṇmin toṇḍīr! sonnēn namō nārāyaṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ninṟa – firmly standing; varaiyum – mountains; kidanda – remaining stationary; kadalum – ocean; tisaiyum – directions; iru nilanum – vast earth (all of these); onṟum – even a little bit; oḻiyā vaṇṇam – to be not ruined; eṇṇi – vowed (more and more); ninṟa – continuously engaged in creation; ammānār – being the supreme lord; kunṟu – mountain; kudaiyā – as umbrella; eduttu – one who lifted; adigaḷudaiya – lord’s; tirunāmam – divine name; toṇḍīr – oh devotees!; nanṟu – sweetly (for you); sonnēn kāṇmin – I have explained

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran vowed and continuously engaged in creation to ensure that firmly standing mountains, ocean which is remaining stationary, directions and the vast earth, are not ruined even a little bit. He lifted the gōvardan mountain as an umbrella. Oh devotees! I have sweetly explained such lord’s divine name to you.

**ninṟa varai …** – Anchoring mountains which remain firm as anchors for the earth, the ocean which remains within its boundary without crossing the shore until īśvaran’s vow remains, the directions which help in identifying the position of individuals, earth which is qualified to be roamed around by creatures – thinking that none of these aspects should diminish, sarvēśvaran creates these from his vow.

**kunṟu kudaiyā …** – The divine name of the lord, who held the mountain as umbrella to not cause any harm to covherd people and the cattle.

**nanṟu kāṇmin** – It is good for oneself to recite the divine name of such person. Even if you don’t want to engage in apt actions, still you will desire for something sweet \[which is bhagavān himself\].

**toṇḍīr sonnēn** – I have explained this to everyone who has interest in serving bhagavān. Those who don’t have interest in serving him, will not listen to this, in any case.

**namō nārāyaṇamē** – It is not having thousand syllables like sahasrākśarī mālā – but it is having only eight syllables.

## 6.10.8. Kadungal mari

*kadungāl māri kallē poḻiya allē emakkenṟupadungāl nīyē saraṇ enṟu āyar anja anjā munnedungāl kunṟam kudai onṟēndi niraiyaic ciramattālnadungā vaṇṇam kāttān nāmam namō nārāyaṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kadu – cruel; kāl – with wind; māri – the cloud; kal – hail; poḻiya – as it rained; emakku – “for us (this); allē – is like very dark night”; enṟu – as; padungāl – thought in the heart; āyar – covherd people (at that time); nīyē – “You who are the protector of all; saraṇ – (our) protector”; enṟu – saying this; anja – as they feared (for that rain); anjāmun – before that fear materialised; nedungāl – huge, with surrounding mountains; kunṟam – gōvardana mountain; onṟu kudai – as an (unseen) umbrella; ēndi – held; niraiyai – herds of cows; siramattāl – with fatigue; nadungā vaṇṇam – to not suffer; kāttān – the protector’s; nāmam – divine name; namō nārāyaṇamē – is in the form of “namō nārāyaṇa”

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

As the cloud with cruel wind rained hail, covherd people thought in their heart “for us, this is like very dark night” and said “You, who are the protector of all, are our protector”. Saying this, as they feared, before that fear materialised, kriṣṇa lifted the huge gōvardana mountain with the surrounding mountains, and held, to not let the herds of cows suffer with fatigue. Such protector’s divine name is in the form of “namō nārāyaṇa”.

**kadungāl māri …** – Cloud with harsh wind poured down hail.

**allē emakku …** – As the covherd people thought “This is like a night during deluge”, the covherd people became frightened and said “We are not qualified to take care of our acts; you should be our protector”. Before the outcome of their fear materialised, kriṣṇa held the gōvardana mountain with broad bottom portion; also said as held the gōvardana mountain along with the surrounding mountains. He protected the cows, which cannot understand the favour done by him, from suffering. For his protection, danger,which is known to an individual and his non-rejection are only required; there is no shortcoming in the natural relationship.

## 6.10.9. Pongu punari

*pongu puṇarik kadal sūḻ ādai nilamāmagaḷ malarmāmangai piraman sivan indiran vānavar nāyagarāyaengaḷ adigaḷ imaiyōr talaivar udaiya tirunāmamnangaḷ vinaigaḷ tavira uraimin namō nārāyaṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pongu – agitated; puṇari – having waves; kadal sūḻ – being surrounded by ocean; ādai – having that itself as waist string; nila mā magaḷ – for bhūmip pirātti; malar – residing on lotus flower; māmangai – for periya pirātti; piraman – for brahmā; sivan – for rudran; indiran – for indran; vānavar – for (the other) dēvatās; nāyagarāy – being the lord; engaḷ – for us; adigaḷ – being the lord; imaiyōr – for nityasūris; talaivarudaiya – one who is the leader, his; tirunāmam – divine name; namō nārāyaṇam – that which is said as “namō nārāyaṇa”; nangaḷ – our; vinaigaḷ – sins; tavira – to be destroyed; uraimin – utter

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is the lord for bhūmippirātti, who is surrounded by ocean with agitating waves and having that itself as waist string, for periya pirātti, who is residing on lotus flower, for brahmā, rudran, indran and other dēvatās, and is the lord for us and is the leader for the nityasūris. His divine name is said as “namō nārāyaṇa”. Utter this name to have our sins destroyed.

**pongu puṇari …** – When āḻvār was asked “You have been supporting this divine name for a long time. What is the meaning for it?” āḻvār explains it here. śrī bhūmip pirātti who is surrounded by ocean with agitating waves and having that itself as the waist string.

**malar mā mangai** – periya pirāttiyār who is having lotus flower as her residence.

**piraman …** – He is the controller of brahmā, rudran and all other dēvatās starting with indran.

**engaḷudaiya adigaḷ** – As said in śaraṇāgati gadyam “*asmat svāmin*” (Our lord).

**imaiyōr …** – Since brahmā et al were explained in the previous lines, imaiyōr indicates nityasūris. The divine name of the leader of nityasūris as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*“. Thus, it is implied that he is ubhaya vibhūti yuktan (one who is with both nitya and leelā vibhūtis). With these, the intent is to say that bhagavān is ubhaya vibhūti yuktan. Thus, he is the lord of those who have no shortcomings, those who think themselves to be free from shortcomings and those who have shortcomings.

**nangaḷ vinaigaḷ …** – You utter this divine name to eliminate the sins which all of you have knowingly committed since time immemorial. \[A disciple by he name\] eṇṇāyirattut tirukkulattāḻvān asked nanjīyar \[one of our preceptors\] “Will prapatti \[surrender\] be a remedy for sins accumulated by mistakes committed knowingly too or only for mistakes committed unknowingly?” nanjīyar mercifully responds “If we look at its greatness, it can be a remedy for mistakes committed knowingly too. But when one, who has surrendered, has jñānam (knowledge), he will not be lacking in atonement. Hence, he will only have mistakes which are done unknowingly. When it eliminates the mistakes which were committed before the surrender, that cannot be said as eliminating mistakes which were committed knowingly, since everything was done knowingly back then”.

**namō nārāyaṇamē** – This divine name is to be uttered even if it causes sins, since the name is so desirable.

## 6.10.10. Vavit tadam

*vāvit tadam sūḻ maṇi muttāṟṟu naṟaiyūr nedumālaināvil paravi nenjil koṇḍu nambi nāmattaikkāvit tadangaṇ madavār kēḷvan kaliyan oli mālaimēvic colla vallār pāvam nillā vīyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāvi – by tanks; tadam – by ponds; sūḻ – surrounded; maṇi – gemstones; muttu – having pearls; āṟṟu – having divine kāvēri; naṟaiyūr – mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; nedumālai – on the supreme lord; kāvi – like a karuneydal (blue lily) flower; tadam – vast; kaṇ – having eyes; madavār – for women; kēḷvan – one was the hero (previously); kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; nambi – tirunaṟaiyūr nambi’s; nāmattai – divine name; nāvil – with tongue; paravi – praised; nenjil – with heart; koṇḍu – remembered; oli – mercifully spoke; mālai – these ten pāsurams which are in the form of a tamiḻ garland; mēvi – remaining focussed on this, with desire; solla vallār – those who recite, their; pāvam – sin; nillā – will not remain permanently; vīyum – will be destroyed

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār who was previously the hero of women who are having eyes which are like vast blue lilies, praising the divine name of tirunaṟaiyūr nambi and remembering it in his heart, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams which are in the form of a tamiḻ garland on the supreme lord who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by tanks and ponds, and is having divine kāvēri river which is having gemstones and pearls. For those who recite these pāsurams, remaining focussed on this and with desire, sins will not remain permanently for them, and they will be destroyed.

**vāvit tadam sūḻ …** – sarvēśvaran, who is the supreme lord who has arrived and is standing in tirunaṟaiyūr which is having ponds and tanks (which are bounded in size). Praising nambi’s divine name with the tongue and thinking about it in the heart.

**kāvi …** – Previously I thought this (being the hero of beautiful women) as my greatness; now you can see the greatness I have acquired (being true servitor of lord). Now, you can see that bhagavān is the target of my mind, speech and body.

**mēvic colla vallār …** – The sin of those who can remain focussed on this decad and recite it, will not remain with them. The sin will leave them and become destroyed as well. There will be nothing remaining to distribute to others at the end of the life which is mentioned in śātyāyana śākhai “*tasya putrā: dāyamupayanti: dviśanta: pāpakrutyām suhrudas sādukrutyām* īī” ((when the mumukśu (one interested in mōkśam) goes to paramapadam, his sons will inherit his wealth; his enemies will inherit his sins and his friends, his virtues).

## Seventh Centum

## 7.1 Karava mada nagu

## 7.1.1. Karava mada nagu

*kaṟavā madanāgu tan kanṟu uḷḷināṟ pōlmaṟavādu adiyēn unnaiyē aḻaikkinṟēnnaṟavār poḻil sūḻ naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambi!piṟavāmai enaip paṇi endai pirānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṟavā – not milked; madam – humble; nāgu – cow; than kanṟu – its calf; uḷḷināp pōl – just as it would think about; adiyēn – I, who am your servitor; maṟavādu – without forgetting; unnaiyē – (telling) you who are the lord; aḻaikkinṟēn – I am calling; naṟavu Ar – having abundant honey; poḻil sūḻ – surrounded by orchards; naṟaiyūr – in tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – mercifully residing; nambi – Oh, one who is complete in auspicious qualities!; endai – being my father; pirānē – Oh, benefactor!; enai – me; piṟavāmai – to be not born (in this samsāra, from now onvards); paṇi – you should mercifully do

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is praying to bhagavān that he should mercifully eliminate the connection with this samsāra, which is the hurdle to experience bhagavān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Just as a calf would think about its humble, mother cow which was not milked, I, who am your servitor, without forgetting, keep calling you who are the lord, telling your name. Oh, one who is complete in auspicious qualities, who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by orchards having abundant honey! Oh, benefactor who is my father! You should mercifully ensure that I am not born any more in this samsāra.

**kaṟavā …** – Just as a calf would think about its humble, mother cow which was not milked. piḷḷai amudanār wanted to explain it as “Just as a humble, mother cow which was not milked, will think about its calf”, but since it did not match with the intent of āḻvār, became upset. That is apakśa darmam – it will not be apt to refer to āḻvār as mother cow and bhagavān as calf. Hence, bhattar mercifully explained – kaṟavā mada nāgai (the humble, mother cow), than kanṟu uḷḷināp pōlē (the calf called out for its mother), Because of not having been milked, it will have the pain from the stiffness in the udder; with that, bhagavān’s pain (in not helping his devotees) is revealed. Because of not being milked, the calf’s tongue becoming dry due to not suckling its mother, is revealed; with that, ātmā’s pain (in not being helped by bhagavān) is revealed. Just as the calf of a cow which was not milked, will think about its mother.

**maṟavādu …** – Though being in this samsāra where there is scope to forget you, I am not forgetting you. I, who am ananyārha (not existing for anyone else), am telling you, who are the lord, and calling out.

**naṟavār …** – Oh one who is complete in auspicious qualities, who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by orchards having abundant honey!

**piṟavāmai …** – Taking birth will lead to forgetting you. You should mercifully bless me to avoid such birth for me, which will lead to forgetfulness.

**endai pirānē** – If you, who can eliminate my hurdles (birth), don’t do it, is there anyone else who can do it? If you think about me and help me, I will exist; otherwise, I will cease to exist. I, who am ananya gati (refuge-less) in this manner, thinking about you who are my lord, am calling you. If you don’t eliminate my hurdle, is there anyone else who can do it?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.2. Varra mudunirodu

*vaṟṟā mudunīrodu māl varai ēḻumtuṟṟāga mun tuṟṟiya tol pugaḻōnē!aṟṟēn adiyēn unnaiyē aḻaikkinṟēnpeṟṟēn aruḷ tandidum endai pirānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṟṟā – perennial; mudu nīrodu – with the ocean; māl – huge; varai ēḻum – seven mountains; mun – previously; tuṟṟāga – as a handful; tuṟṟiya – (gathered and) swallowed; tol – ancient; pugaḻōnē – one who is having fame; endai pirānē – Oh benefactor, being my father!; aṟṟēn – existing completely for you; adiyēn – I, the servitor; unnaiyē – (telling) you who are the lord; aḻaikkinṟēn – I am calling; peṟṟēn – I acquired this great benefit; aruḷ – (your highness’) mercy; tandidum – (towards me) you should mercifully do

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, one who is having the ancient fame of gathering and swallowing the perennial ocean and the huge, seven mountains as a handful! Oh benefactor, being my father! I, the servitor, am existing completely for you and keep calling you who are the lord, telling your name. I acquired this great benefit. You should mercifully shower your mercy towards me.

**vaṟṟā mudu nīr …** – īsn’t my calling out even too much? One, who consumed the world which was taken in by the deluge. For you to protect someone, all you need is for you to know the danger and for the others to not reject you. The earth which was consumed by the deluge drowned and did not call out saying “Please lift me up and protect me”.

**vaṟṟā mudu nīr** … – With the perennial ocean, the seven anchoring mountains, the earth which is the support for those, were casually consumed by you. In this manner, you are going to lose these qualities which you have acquired since long time, by delaying to help me when I cried out.

The differences between the earth which was caught in the deluge and āḻvār are – being fully determined on bhagavān, having self-realisation and calling out for him as a refuge-less person.

**peṟṟēn …** – In my dangerous situation, instead of having to try on my own, I got the great benefit of calling out for you only.

**aruḷ tandidum …** – Now, there is no block for your mercy to flow towards me. You cannot say “While I am ready to do everything for you, you did not cooperate with me”. I have withdrawn from my efforts. Show your mercy. Oh, the lord of my clan!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.3. Taren pirarkku

*tārēn piṟarkku un aruḷ ennidai vaittāyārēn aduvē parugik kaḷikkinṟēnkārēy kadalē malaiyē tirukkōttiyūrē ugandāyai ugandēn adiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

un aruḷ – your mercy; ennidai – towards me; vaittāy – showed; piṟarkku – for others; tārēn – I will not give (that mercy); adiyēn – in me; ugandu – showing love (due to that); kār ēy – with clouds floating; kadalē – tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean); malaiyē – tirumalā (tiruppati); tirukkōttiyūrē – tirukkōśtiyūr; ugandāy – you desired (as your abode); adaiyē – that same mercy; parugi – enjoyed; ārēn – being unsatisfied; kaḷikkinṟēn – (enjoying that mercy) I am rejoicing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I will not give the mercy you showed towards me, for others. Showing love for me, you desired for tiruppāṟkadal, tirumalā and tirukkōśtiyūr as your abode. Being unsatisfied even after enjoying that mercy, I am rejoicing.

**tārēn piṟarkku …** – I will not give to anyone else. I will not share your mercy with anyone else. What does it mean when he says like this? It implies that āḻvār is the recipient of bhagavān’s mercy fully. No one else. You have placed your mercy which has no shortcoming, on me.

**ārēn aduvē parugi …** – After enjoying your mercy, instead of being satisfied, I desired for your mercy more and more and due to the joy acquired from such enjoyment, I became prideful and started roaming around, stepping on the heads of yama et al.

**kārēy …** – I desired for you, who came to me with desire. Having clouds looking over.

**kadalē malaiyē tirukkōttiyūrē …** – Just as saubhari (the sage) assumed many (50) forms \[to marry 50 girls\], he is residing in every one of those abodes, as if he is not present anywhere else.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.4. Pul vay pilanda

*puḷ vāy piḷanda punidā! enṟu aḻaikkauḷḷē ninṟu en uḷḷam kuḷirum oruvā!kaḷvā! kadal mallaik kidanda karumbē!vaḷḷāl! unnai enganam nān maṟakkēnē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

puḷ vāy – bakāsura, who is in the form of a bird, his mouth; piḷanda – one who tore; punidā – Oh, pure one!; enṟu aḻaikka – as I call in this way; uḷḷē ninṟu – remaining in my heart; en uḷḷam – my heart; kuḷirum – one who is cooling me; oruvā – Oh, unique one!; kaḷvā – Oh, one who is having the nature of being impossible to be known!; kadal mallai – in tirukkadalmallai; kidanda – reclining; karumbē – Oh, enjoyable one!; vaḷḷāl – generous; unnai – you; nān – I; enganam – through which means; maṟakkēn – capable of forgetting? (I won’t forget)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I called him “Oh, pure one who tore the mouth of bakāsura who is in the form of a bird!” As I did that, he remained in my heart to cool me down! Oh, unique one who did that! Oh, one who is having the nature of being impossible to be known! Oh, enjoyable one who is reclining in tirukkadalmallai! Through which means am I capable of forgetting you, who are generous?

**puḷ vāy piḷanda …** – Tearing bakāsura’s mouth. Instead of sending someone to eliminate the enemy of his devotees, he is having the purity of himself coming and doing it with his own hand.

āḻvār called out saying “**puḷ vāy piḷanda punidā**“, What did bhagavān do?

**uḷḷē ninṟu …** – He thought it would not be sufficient to just come to him, he remained in āḻvār’s heart and made him so cool as if a very dry place became shivering in cold.

**kaḷvā** – It is impossible to estimate what he does for his devotees.

**kadal mallaik kidanda karumbē** – Oh, most tasteful one who has come and mercifully reclined in tirukkadalmallai! Here āḻvār is saying “karumbē” (Oh, sugarcane!) to differentiate from milk which becomes curd when touched with bare hands.

**vaḷḷāl …** – As said in kata upaniśat 1-2-23 “*nāyamātmā pravacanē na labhyō na mēdayā na bahūnā śrutēna* l *yamēvaiśa vruṇutē tēna labhyas* ***tasyaiśa ātmā*** ***vivruṇutē tanūm svām*** ll” (This supreme entity cannot be attained by hearing, by thinking or by meditation (devoid of devotion), he fully manifested his beauty to be enjoyed by āḻvār.

**unnai enganam nān maṟakkēnē** – What can I, who have accepted your favour, say and forget you, who are my benefactor?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.5. Viller nudal

*villēr nudal vēl nedungaṇṇiyum nīyumkallār kadungānam tirinda kaḷiṟē!nallāy! naranāraṇanē! engaḷ nambi!sollāy unnai yān vaṇangit toḻumāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kal Ar – filled with stones; kadum – very cruel (due to the beasts); kānam – in the forest; vil ēr – like a bow; nudal – forehead; vēl – like a spear; nedu – lengthy; kaṇṇiyum – pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi) who is having eyes; nīyum – you who are beloved for her; tirinda – roamed around; kaḷiṟē – Oh intoxicated elephant!; nallāy – Oh one who is having the goodness of āśrita vātsalyam (forbearance towards devotees)!; nara nāraṇānē – Oh one who incarnated as nara and nārāyaṇa riśis (for the people here)!; engaḷ – our (to eliminate the shortcomings); nambi – Oh complete one!; unnai – you, who are the lord of all; yān – I, who am a servitor; vaṇangi – falling at your divine feet; toḻum āṟu – surrendering way; sollāy – you should mercifully tell

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh intoxicated elephant who roamed around along with your beloved pirātti who is having forehead like a bow and lengthy eyes like a spear, in the very cruel forest which is filled with stones! Oh one who is having the goodness of āśrita vātsalyam (forbearance towards devotees)! Oh one who incarnated as nara and nārāyaṇa riśis (for the people here)! Oh our complete one! You, who are the lord of all, should mercifully tell me, who is your servitor, the way to surrender unto you by falling at your divine feet.

**vil ēr nudal …** – Having a forehead which is like a bow, having eyes which are like spear, periya pirāttiyār who has tenderness which attracts even you and you who are having tenderness which even makes her worry about you, roamed around in the very cruel forest which is filled with beasts and is not fit for roaming around, like an intoxicated elephant which will roam around freely along with its female spouse. [nānmugan tiruvandādi 60](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-60/) “*āḷpārttuḻi taruvāy kaṇḍu*” (Oh! Lord you are in search of a person who has surrendered unto your divine feet).

**nallāy** – Oh one who is having motherly forbearance towards your children (ātmās) even more than they are towards you!

**nara nāraṇanē** – Just as a nursing mother will drink medicated water for the sake of her child, oh one who performed penance for them!

**engaḷ nambi** – Oh one who is complete to fill in for our shortcomings!

**sollāy …** – You should mercifully tell a word like in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mā śuca:*” (don’t grieve) saying “I will eliminate the hurdles for your kainkaryam, don’t fear”. You should tell something like in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.33, “*sakrudēva prapannāya tavāsmīti ca yācatē* l *abhayam sarvabhūtēbhyō dadami ētat vratam mama* ll” (To the person who surrenders to me once and to the person who tells me ‘I am your servitor’ I offer protection from all entities alive. This is my solemn vow).

## 7.1.6. Paniyey

*paṇiyēy parangunṟin pavaḷat tiraḷē!muniyē! tirumūḻikkaḷattu viḷakkē!iniyāya toṇḍarōm parugu innamudāyakaniyē! unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu uyndoḻindēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pani ēy – covered with snow; param – being the best; kunṟin – mercifully residing in tiruppiridi which is in himavat mountain; pavaḷam tiraḷē – Oh one who is beautiful like a bunch of corals!; muniyē – Oh one who meditates (upon the well-being of the devotees)!; tirumūḻikkaḷattu – one who is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirumūḻikkaḷam; viḷakkē – Oh self-illuminous one!; iniyāya – Oh sweet one!; toṇḍarōm – we, who are your servitors; parugu – to be drunk; in amudāya – Oh one who is like sweet nectar!; kaniyē – Oh one who is like a ripened fruit!; unnai – you, who are like this; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – having seen; uyndu oḻindēn – got to be uplifted

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, one who is beautiful like a bunch of corals and who is mercifully residing in tiruppiridi which is in the best himavat mountain which is covered with snow! Oh, one who meditates (upon the well-being of the devotees)! Oh, self-illuminous one who is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirumūḻikkaḷam! ōhmsveet one! Oh, one who is like sweet nectar who is to be drunk by us, who are your servitors! Oh,one who is like a ripened fruit! Having seen you, who are like this, I got to be uplifted.

**pani ēy param kunṟin …** – Oh one who is present as the most likable person in tiruppiridi which is present on himavān which has abundance of snow!

**muniyē** – Oh one who is constantly contemplating about the well-being of these cētanas (sentient beings) while they don’t know about it.

**tirumūḻikkaḷattu viḷakkē** – Oh one who has arrived in tirumūḻikkaḷam and is revealing your svarūpam, rūpam and guṇam yourself!

**iniyāy** – Instead of revealing sweetness, you are being sweet.

**toṇḍarōm parugu …** – Unlike the nectar consumed by dēvatās, you are being the nectar drunk by śrīvaiṣṇavas who have the taste for servitude and being the one who is consumable immediately like a ripened fruit!

**unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu …** – I, who was as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (to be like acit) due to not seeing him, became uplifted.

## 7.1.7. Gadiyel illai

*gadiyēl illai nin aruḷ alladu enakkunidiyē! tiruneermalai nittilattottē!padiyē! paravit toḻum toṇḍar tamakkukkadiyē! unaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu uyndoḻindēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nin aruḷ alladu – Other than your mercy; enakku – for me; gadiyēl – (other) means; illai – not there; nidiyē – Oh, one who is enjoyable like a treasure!; tiruneermalai – in tiruneermalai; nittilam – pearl’s; tottē – Oh, one who is like a garland!; padiyē – Oh, one who is the abode (for your devotees)!; paravi – praise; toḻum – surrendering; toṇḍar tamakku – for the servitors; gadiyē – Oh, one who is the goal!; unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu uyndoḻindēn – Having seen you, I got to be uplifted

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I have no other means than your mercy; oh, one who is enjoyable like a treasure! Oh, one who is like a garland of pearls in tiruneermalai! Oh, one who is the abode (for your devotees)! Oh, one who is the goal for the servitors who praise and surrender unto you! Having seen you, I got to be uplifted,

**gadiyēl illai …** – When it comes to the means, I have nothing other than your mercy. gati – refuge. When it comes to the goal, I have nothing other than your divine feet. I am refugeless.

**nidiyē** – Oh, one who is a treasure!

**tiruneermalai …** – Oh, one who has arrived in tiruneermalai and is remaining there to be embraced just as one will wear a pearl garland, to cool down the body!

**padiyē** – Oh, one who is the abode of the devotees!

**paravit toḻum …** – Oh, one who is the goal of śrīvaiṣṇavas who praise you incoherently and surrender unto you!

Alternatively,

**padiyē paravit toḻum toṇḍar …** – Oh one who is the goal for those who are sagōtri (having same gōtram) with me \[i.e. āḻvārs\] and go around divyadēśams enjoying you as said in [tiruneduntāṇḍakam 6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thirunedunthandakam-6-part-1/) “*tānuganda Ur ellām than tāḷ pādi*” (Glorifying bhagavān’s divine mercy at all the divyadēśams which are dear to him)!

**unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu …** – Since you have arrived and are present in ugandaruḷina nilam (the divine abodes), I got to see you and became uplifted.

## 7.1.8. Atta ariye

*attā! ariyē! enṟu unnai aḻaikkappittā enṟu pēsuginṟār piṟar ennaimuttē! maṇimāṇikkamē! muḷaikkinṟavittē! unnai enganam nān vidugēnē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

attā – Oh lord!; ariyē – Oh eliminator of hurdles!; enṟu – saying these; unnai – you; aḻaikka – as I call; piṟar – others; ennai – me who is calling in this manner; pittā enṟu – saying “Oh mad person!”; pēsuginṟār – are saying; muttē – Oh one who is cool like pearl!; maṇi – best; māṇikkamē – Oh one who is easily approachable like a carbuncle!; muḷaikkinṟa – sprouting (to become a fruit); vittē – Oh one who is like a seed!; unnai – you who are like this; nān – I who know your nature; enganam – in which way; vidugēn – will be able to leave?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

As I call you saying “Oh lord! Oh, eliminator of hurdles!”, others call me “Oh, mad person!”. Oh, one who is cool like pearl! Oh one who is easily approachable like a carbuncle, which is the best! Oh, one who is like a sprouting seed! In which way will I, who know your nature, be able to leave you who are like this?

**attā ariyē …** – As I call out for you saying “Oh my lord! Oh one who eliminated my hurdles!”

**pittā enṟu …** – Others are saying “He is calling incoherently saying ‘attā’; he is mad”. I think about them as in “These people are speaking incoherently; they are mad” – they are calling me like this.

But you cannot be abandoned just because others are speaking about me in this manner.

**muttē …** – Oh one who is rejuvenating like a pearl! Oh one who is like an expensive carbuncle Oh one who never fails to give the result! What can I tell about you and abandon you! \[I can’t abandon you\]

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.9. Tuyay sudar

*tūyāy! sudar māmadi pōl uyirkkellāmtāyāy aḷikkinṟa taṇ tāmaraik kaṇṇā!āyā! alainīr ulagēḻum mun uṇḍavāyā! unnai enganam nān maṟakkēnē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

tūyāy – Oh, pure one!; sudar – having (cool) rays; mā madi pōl – like full moon; uyirkku ellām – for all creatures; tāyāy – being mother; aḷikkinṟa – showering mercy; taṇ – cool; tāmaraik kaṇṇā – Oh, one who is having eyes which are like reddish lotus!; āyā – Oh, one who incarnated as kriṣṇa!; alai – having rising waves; nīr – surrounded by the ocean; ulagu ēḻum – seven worlds; mun – during deluge; uṇḍa vāyā – Oh, one who is having the mouth which consumed!; unnai – you, who are a friend-in-need; nān – I, who understand your favours; enganam – in which way; maṟakkēn – will be able to forget?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, pure one! Oh, one who is being our mother, having cool eyes which are like reddish lotus and showering your mercy for all creatures like a full moon having cool rays! Oh, one who incarnated as kriṣṇa! Oh, one who is having the mouth which consumed the seven worlds surrounded by the ocean, which is having rising waves, during deluge! In which way will I, who understand your favours be able to forget you, who are a friend-in-need?

**tūyāy …** – As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 5.29](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/5-29/) “*suhrudam sarvabhūtānām*” (being the friend of all creatures), being friendly towards all creatures, he helps both who are favourable and unfavourable, without any difference. Oh, one who is having such purity! Oh, one who is having cool, divine eyes which shower mercy upon all creatures, in a motherly mood, just as a full moon would eliminate all the heat with cool rays! Here *taṇ* is an adjective for the eyes. Alternative explanation – like a cool, full moon, one who showers your mercy on all creatures, and having divine eyes which manifest such vātsalyam fully. Here *taṇ* is an adjective for the moon.

**āyā …** – Oh, one who incarnated as kriṣṇa to be claimed by one of your servitors \[dēvaki, vasudēva, yaśōdā, nandagōpa\] saying “He is my son”, even after being the mother of all!

**alai nīr ulagēḻum** – Oh, one who is having the nature of protecting everyone without any discrimination, when danger rises! Oh, one who is having the divine lips which consumed the earth which is surrounded by the ocean which is having rising waves! How can I forget you, who are a friend-in-need like this.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.10. Vandar polil

*vaṇḍār poḻil sūḻ naṟaiyūr nambikku enṟumtoṇḍāyk kaliyan oli sey tamiḻ mālaitoṇḍīr! ivai pādumin pādi ninṟādauṇḍē visumbu undamakku illai tuyarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

toṇḍīr – Oh devotees!; vaṇḍu Ar – filled with beetles; poḻil sūḻ – surrounded by orchards; naṟaiyūr nambikku – for tirunaṟaiyūr nambi; enṟum – always; toṇḍāy – having servitude; kaliyan – āḻvār; oli sey – mercifully spoke; tamiḻ mālai – garland of tamiḻ pāsurams; ivai – these ten pāsurams; pādumin – sing; pādi ninṟu – singing (in this manner); Ada – as you dance; undamakku – for you; tuyar – sorrow; illai – will be destroyed; visumbu – paramapadam; uṇḍu – will get

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh devotees! Sing these ten pāsurams, which are in the form of a garland of tamiḻ pāsurams, mercifully spoken by tirumangai āḻvār, who is always having servitude for nambi of tirunaṟaiyūr, which is surrounded by orchards, filled with beetles. As you sing and dance, your sorrow will be destroyed; you will get paramapadam.

**vaṇḍār …** – Due to the flood of honey, beetles are spreading on the orchards like buds on flower. āḻvār sang the lord who is complete with all auspicious qualities, in tirunaṟaiyūr, which is having such orchards.

**toṇḍāy …** – tirumangai āḻvār, who engaged in eternal kainkaryam at such nambi’s divine feet, mercifully spoke these ten tamiḻ pāsurams with music, which are like a garland. As all of you sing and dance just like I do with taste in them, paramapadam will be automatically attained by you and the sins which are the hurdles for such attainment will be automatically gone too.

## 7.2 Pullay

## 7.2.1. Pullay

*puḷḷāy ēnamumāyp pugundu ennai uḷḷam koṇḍakaḷvā! enṟalum en kaṇgaḷ nīrgaḷ sōrtarumāluḷḷē ninṟu urugi nenjam unnai uḷḷiyakkālnaḷḷēn unnai allāl naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambīyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

naṟaiyūr – in the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – one who is mercifully residing; nambi – Oh complete one!; pugundu – (inside me, as antaryāmi) entered; puḷḷāy – as (hamsa/swan) bird; ēnamumāy – as varāha (manifesting the leelās from these incarnations); en – me who is engaged in worldly pleasures, my; uḷḷattai – heart; koṇḍa – made it as his; kaḷvā – oh mischievous one!; enṟalum – even while saying so; en kaṇgaḷ – my eyes; nīrgaḷ – happy tears; sōr tarum – flooded; Al – Alas!; nenjam – (my) heart; unnai – you, who worked for my liberation; uḷḷiyakkāl – when meditated; uḷḷē ninṟu – being in (my) heart; urugi – melted; unnai allāl – (now) other than you, any matter; naḷḷēn – I won’t desire

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, complete one who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr! Entering me in my heart and manifesting the leelās of hamsāvatāram and varāhāvatāram, oh mischievous one who made my heart as yours! Even while saying these, my eyes are flooeded with happy tears. Alas! When I meditated in my heart on you who worked for my liberation, I melted. Other than you, I won’t desire for any matter. “O” indicates great joy.

**puḷḷāy …** – \[For you\] To eliminate my sorrow, is the sorrow I endured, not enough? Have you not taken birth in the species in which even I have not been born? He manifested his forms such as hamsa (swan), varāha (wild boar) etc and captivated my heart. He made the heart which is the cause for bondage to become the cause for my liberation as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*mana Eva manuśyāṇām kāraṇam banda mōkśayō:*” (mind is the only cause for a person’s bondage and liberation).

**kaḷvā …** – bhagavān entered āḻvār’s heart without āḻvār’s knowledge since āḻvār will not accept his entry, if known about his arrival. As āḻvār meditated upon this favour of bhagavān, his eyes became wet.

**en kaṇgaḷ …** – My eyes which were previously crying for women.

As I started meditating upon you, my heart became melted and broken.

**naḷḷēn …** – Now, I will not engage with any other matter, even if one hundred thousand things come in front of me.

**naṟaiyūr …** – Will I fit with these worldly matters when you have arrived ahead of me in this samsāram where I am suffering, and are standing there? Due to his overwhelming joy, he is saying “O” \[in *nambiyō*\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.2. Oda alariyin

*ōdā āḷariyin uruvāy maruvi endanmādē vandu adiyēn manam koḷḷa valla maindā!pādēn toṇḍar tammaik kavidaip panuval koṇḍunādēn unnai allāl naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambīyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

naṟaiyūr nambi! – Oh, the complete one who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr!; ōdā – not seen (in this world); āḷ ariyin – narasimha’s; uruvāy – having the form; enṟan mādē – for me; vandu – being present; maruvi – mingling (with me); adiyēn – I, who am a servitor, my; manam – heart; koḷḷa valla – able to make it to be at your disposal; maindā – Oh, the youthful one!; panuval – as per śāstram (having the proper symptoms); kavidai koṇḍu – with poems; toṇḍar tammai – people who are attached to worldly pleasures; pādēn – (from now onvards) I will not praise; unnai allāl – other than you (to praise anyone); nādēn – will not even analyse in my heart

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, the complete one who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr! Oh, the youthful one who is having the narasimha form which is not seen in this world and is present for me mingling with me, and who is able to make my heart to be at your disposal! I will not praise people who are attached to worldly pleasures, with poems as per śāstram. I will not even analyse anyone other than you in my heart.

**ōdā āḷ ariyāy** – In the previous pāsuram, āḻvār said “*puḷḷāy ēnamumāyp pugundu*“. He says “You can choose to take birth in inferior species. But can’t you at least take birth in the species which are seen in this world?” Oh one who is having the narasimha form which is not seen in this world.

**maruvi** – Right from the day of assuming the narasimha form, bhagavān is present only in āḻvār’s heart.

**enṟan mādē vandu** – If you are in the supreme abode, can you come to me? \[How amazing!\]

**adiyēn manam koḷḷa valla maindā** – For you who made my heart to be at your disposal, is it your strength to have made prahlādāḻvān’s heart to be at your disposal? \[i.e. It is more difficult to change my heart than to change prahlādāḻvān’s heart\]

bhagavān says “I have done that. Further, what are you going to do?”

**pādēn …** – I avoided praising lowly people with poems which have the proper qualities mentioned in śāstram. “*kavidaip panuval*” should be seen as “*panuval kavidai*“, where panuval is nūl (śāstram), that is poems which have no shortcomings as per the qualities mentioned in śāstram.

**nādēn unnai allāl** – I even eliminated the analysis (whether to praise bhagavān) \[and straightaway praised\].

**naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyō** – While you have presented yourself to be enjoyed by my senses, is there any scope for me to enjoy something else, abandoning you?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
