## 7.2.3. Emmanum emmanaiyum

*emmānum emmanaiyum enaip peṟṟu oḻindadaṟ pinammānum ammanaiyum adiyēnukkāgi ninṟananmāna oṇsudarē! naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambī! unmaimmāna vaṇṇam allāl magiḻndu ētta māttēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

emmānum – my father; emmanaiyum – my mother; ennai peṟṟu – begetting me (and subsequently); oḻindadaṟpin – after abandoning me (considering me to be an obstacle for their enjoyment); adiyēnukku – for me who has natural servitude; ammānum – father; ammaniyumāgi – being mother too; ninṟa – oh, one who remained in close proximity!; nal – distinguished; mānam – having greatness; oḷ – beautiful; sudarē – oh, one who is having radiance!; un – your; mai mānam – like black pigment; vaṇṇam allāl – other than your divine form (any other divyadēśams); magiḻndu – joyfully; ētta māttēn – I won’t praise

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

After my father and mother begot me and abandoned me, oh, one who remained in close proximity being father and mother for me who has natural servitude! Oh, one who is having beautiful radiance which is having distinguished greatness! Other than your divine form which resembles black pigment, I won’t joyfully praise any divyadēśams.

**emmānum …** – I can forget you only if you had helped to the extent done by worldly people. You cannot be said to have helped just at the level of mother and father; even when they abandoned me, you showed up and helped me.

Mother and father, being blinded by desires, will give birth to a child and then abandon the child considering the child to be “*yauvana virōdi*” (obstacle for their youthful enjoyment). Since the ātmā has become used to the parents in countless births, he will only say “ammē” (mother!) and “appā” (father!) \[when in distress\]; in that, when he calls out saying “ammē”, bhagavān will respond to him in a feminine voice saying “What?”; and when he calls out saying “appā”, bhagavān will respond to him in a masculine voice saying “What?” In this manner, bhagavān will respond to me the way he expects response.

**adiyēnukku …** – Unlike the level of such parents, for me who is having natural relationship towards you, you remained such mother and father.

**nal māna oḷ sudarē …** – Oh, one who is having distinguished, unlimitedly radiant light! When asked “īsn’t that seen only in paramapadam?” āḻvār says “Oh, one who has arrived in tirunaṟaiyūr and remained in close proximity and is complete in auspicious qualities!”

**un maimmāna vaṇṇam …** – Other than you, who have the complexion of black pigment, which is rejuvenating, I will not joyfully praise, even if they tried to indulge me in them. Here, “others” imply other divydēśams.

**maimmāna vaṇṇam** – As dark as black pigment; like black pigment.

## 7.2.4. Siriyay

*siṟiyāy ōr piḷḷaiyumāy ulaguṇḍu ōr ālilai mēluṟaivāy! en nenjin uḷḷē uṟaivāy uṟaindadu tānaṟiyādirundu aṟiyēn adiyēn aṇivaṇḍu kiṇḍumnaṟaivārum poḻil sūḻ naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambīyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇi – beautiful; vaṇḍu – beetles; kiṇḍu – to remain; naṟai – honey; vārum – overflowing; poḻil – by orchards; sūḻ – surrounded by; naṟaiyūr – in the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – one who is mercifully residing; nambi – Oh complete one!; siṟiyāy – having young age; ōr – being distinguished; piḷḷaiyumāy – being a child; ulagu uṇḍu – swallowing the worlds; ōr – a youthful; ālilai mēl – on a banyan leaf; uṟaivāy – oh, one who remains in a fitting manner!; uṟaindadu – (in this manner, your) presence; aṟiyādu – being ignorant; adiyēn – I; irundu aṟiyēn – never remained

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, complete one who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by orchards where honey is overflowing to make the beautiful beetles remain there! Oh, one who remains on a banyan leaf in a fitting manner, being a distinguished and young child, having swallowed the worlds! I never remained ignorant of your such presence.

**siṟiyāy ōr piḷḷai …** – Though you had been nursed by yaśōdāp pirātti, even that age appeared to be a matured age for you, swallowing all the worlds and lying down on a tender banyan leaf, just as it has been mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.2.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thiruvaimozhi-4-2-1-balanay-ezhulagundu/) “*bālanāy ēḻulaguṇḍu*” (being a child who has swallowed all the worlds). Oh, one who has the *agatitagatanā sāmartyam* (the ability to unite contradictory entities)! In a similar vein, you had entered my heart, residing as if you were residing in paramapdam, unlike lying on that tender banyan leaf, making me as your servitor. I am not a thankless person, not knowing this great favour. I knew all about that matter.

Did you do this because you don’t have any other place to reside? Oh one who is having tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded by orchards which have abundance of honey which makes sure that beautiful beetles can simply remain here and enjoy that honey, as your abode! For you, who have this abode, is there no other space (other than my heart) to remain in an expansive manner?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.5. Nindayai vanavargal

*nīṇḍāyai vānavargaḷ ninaindu ēttik kāṇbaridālāṇḍāy enṟu ādarikkappaduvāykku nān adimaipūṇḍēn en nenjin uḷḷē pugundāyaip pōgalottēnnāṇ tān unakku oḻindēn naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambīyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

naṟaiyūr – in the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – one who is mercifully residing; nambi – Oh complete one!; nīṇḍāyai – you are inconceivable; vānavargaḷ – dēvatās such as brahmā et al; ninaindu – meditated; ētti – praised; kāṇbadu – to see you; aridu – very difficult; Al – How amazing!; āṇḍāy enṟu – saying “Oh (our) lord!”; ādarikkap paduvāykku – (by the dēvatās) being loved, on such you; nān – I; adimai pūṇḍēn – I held the activities of a servitor; en nenjinuḷḷē – in my heart; pugundāyai – you who entered; pōgal ottēn – I will not allow to go somewhere else; nāṇ tān – shame; unakku – for your sake; oḻindēn – have abandoned

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, complete one who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr! How amazing that even for the dēvatās such as brahmā et al, it is very difficult to meditate upon you and praise you! I held the activities of a servitor towards you, who are loved by dēvatās saying “Oh, lord!” I will not allow you, who have entered in my heart, to go somewhere else. I have abandoned my shame for your sake.

**nīṇḍāyai …** – If someone tries to speak about your svarūpa (true nature), rūpa (forms), guṇa (qualities), vibhūti (wealth), you are inconceivable to be completely spoken about. If such you are desired to be seen by brahmā et al by meditating in the heart and praising, oh, one who is difficult to be seen!

**āṇḍāy …** – brahmā et al say “My lord!” towards you who are liked by all. For such you, I got to do all types of kainkaryams (service) as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31-25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (I would carry out all tasks of servitude), Will I allow you, who entered my heart to engage me in your service, to leave me? He thought “Our task is now accomplished \[we have made āḻvār our servitor\]. Now we shall go somewhere else”. āḻvār said “Will I allow him to go?”

bhagavān says “You are saying ‘adiyēn’, ‘adiyēn’ (I am your servitor). śervitors should observe and accept what the master does. Will it suit your true nature to say ‘I will not allow’?”

**nāṇ tān adu oḻindēn** – Will those who set out to perform madal think about what is right and what is wrong!

**naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambīyō** – Are you having any shame? Did you not perform madal \[tried to get me\] before making me perform madal towards you? bhagavān performing madal means his arrival in tirunaṟaiyūr before āḻvār’s arrival.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.6. En tadai

*en tādai tādai appāl eḻuvar paḻavadimaivandār en nenjin uḷḷē vandāyaip pōgalottēnandō! en āruyirē! arasē! aruḷ enakkunandāmait tanda endāy! naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambīyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

en Ar uyirē – Oh, one who is my vital air which sustains me!; arasē – Oh, one who rules me!; enakku – in my matters; aruḷ – mercy; nandāmai – without a break; tanda – one who showed; en tāy – oh, my lord!; naṟaiyūr – in the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – one who is mercifully residing; nambi – Oh, complete one!; en tādai – my father and I; tādai – his father; appāl – born before him; eḻuvar – persons from seven generations (thus, totally ten generations); paḻa adimai – natural servitude; vandār – performing; en nenjin uḷḷē – in my heart; vandāyai – you have come and entered; pōgal ottēn – will not allow you to leave; andō – alas!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, complete one who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr! Oh, one who is my vital air which sustains me! Oh, one who rules me! Oh, my lord who showed mercy in my matters, without a break! I, My father, his father who was born before him and persons from his past seven generations have been performing natural servitude towards you. Alas! I will not allow you, who have come and entered in my heart, to leave.

**en tādai …** – I, my father, his father, seven generations from him (i.e. my grandfather). It is said in mahābhāratam – bhīśma saying to darmaputra (yudiśtra) – “*ēkāhamapi kauntēya bhūmistam udagam kuru \| kulam tārayatē tāta! sapta saptaca sapta ca*” (Oh yudiśtira, my dear child! At least one day offer water to earth; that will help uplift your 21 generations of family members). Whatever benefit a person acquires, while it spreads to the near/dear ones, it will go for seven generations as said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruppallandu-6-enthai-thanthai/) “*ēḻpadikāl*” (seven generations). This implies that the whole clan exists for bhagavān only. While I did not beseech you, you have come and entered my heart. Will I allow such you to leave? Is there anyone who would throw away the treasure he/she got?

**andō …** – Even after āḻvār saying “*ottēn*” (will not allow), bhagavān thought of leaving; āḻvār is saying “You are losing this entity (me)”. Oh, one who conducts my sustenance where I cannot sustain myself without you!

**arasē** – Oh, one who eliminated my enemies and ruled over!

**aruḷ enakku nandamait tanda endāy** – Oh, my lord who showered so much mercy that I can hold your divine feet and stop you saying “Don’t leave”! He came and stood in tirunaṟaiyūr and blessed āḻvār in this manner.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.7. Mannanja ayiram

*mannanja āyiram tōḷ maḻuvil tuṇitta maindā!en nenjattu uḷḷirundu ingu inip pōy piṟar oruvarvannenjam pukkirukka ottēn vaḷaittu vaittēnnannenjam annam mannum naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambīyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nal – filled with mercy; nenjam – having heart; annam – periya pirāttiyār who is having the gait of a swan; mannum – eternally residing; naṟaiyūr – in the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – one who is mercifully residing; nambi – Oh complete one!; man – kings; anja – to frighten; āyiram tōḷ – kārtavīryārjuna’s thousand shoulders; maḻuvil – with axe; tuṇitta – one who severed and knocked down; maindā – oh, strong one!; en nejattuḷ – (until now) in my heart; irundu – continuously residing; ini – further; ingu pōy – leaving from here; piṟar oruvar – an outsider’s; val – being hard (not melting in your separation); nenjam – heart; pukku irukka – for you to enter there and remain there; ottēn – will not agree; vaḷaittu vaittēn – I stopped you (from going)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, complete one who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr which is eternally inhabited by periya pirāttiyār who is having the gait of a swan and is having a heart filled with mercy! Oh, strong one who severed and knocked down the thousand shoulders of kārtavīryārjuna to frighten the kings! I will not agree for you to enter the heart of an outsider and remain there after leaving my heart where you have been continuously residing. I stopped you (from going).

**man anja …** – īśvaran who entered and remained in āḻvār’s heart, thought about leaving. āḻvār is not allowing that. emperumān asks “How can you not allow me? Can you argue with me and win over for you? I have the great strength of destroying twenty one generations of kśatriyas (kings)” āḻvār says “That is fine. Would you not react and interact based on each one’s nature?” Oh one who severed the thousand shoulders of sahasra bāhu arjuna who was the leader of all the kings to frighten them! I am neither the one who would say that there will be obstacles for the actions you set out to do nor I would reject your strength. Still would you not interact with each person according to their nature?

**en nenjattu uḷ irundu …** – Entering my heart where I don’t know anything other than you. I will not let you go to someone’s heart where that person allows you to leave his/her heart.

If bhagavān says “Even if you don’t allow, I cannot avoid (leaving)” āḻvār says

**vaḷaittu vaittēn** – āḻvār is saying “I will die if you leave”. If he would lose āḻvār, he will not take another step.

bhagavān asks “With which strength are you stopping me?” āḻvār says

**nal nenja annam mannum naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambīyō** – When you try to find fault in me and abandon me, isn’t the one who would say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed) residing in proximity?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.8. Eppodum ponmalar

*eppōdum ponmalar ittu imaiyōr toḻudu tangaḷkaippōdu koṇḍu iṟainjik kaḻal mēl vaṇanga ninṟāyippōdu en nenjin uḷḷē pugundāyaip pōgalottēnnaṟpōdu vaṇḍu kiṇḍum naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambīyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nal – beautiful; pōdu – in the flowers; vaṇḍu – beetles; kiṇḍum – spread over (sweet); naṟaiyūr – in the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – one who is mercifully residing; nambi – Oh complete one!; eppōdum – at all times; pon – beautiful; malar – flowers; ittu – to proffer; imaiyōr – nityasūris; toḻudu – to surrender; tangaḷ – their; kai pōdu koṇḍu – with their flower-like hands; irainji – performing anjali (joined palms); kaḻal mēl – (falling) at the divine feet; vaṇanga – for them to surrender; ninṟāy – Oh, one who is mercifully present!; ippōdu – Now, after knowing your sweetness; en nenjinuḷḷē – in my heart; pugundāyai – you, who entered; pōgal ottēn – I will not allow to go somewhere else

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, the complete one who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr where beetles are spread over the beautiful flowers! Oh, one who is mercifully present for the nityasūris to proffer beautiful flowers and surrender unto you by performing anjali (joined palms) with their flower-like hands! Now, after knowing your sweetness, I will not allow you, who entered in my heart, to go somewhere else.

**eppōdum …** – \[bhagavān says\] Did we come and enter your heart due to some shortcoming in my side? Will I leave you now \[due to becoming fulfilled\]? \[āḻvār says\] You remained to be vorśippable as said in viṣṇu sūktam “*sadā paśyanti*” (nityasūris are always seeing); with the ever-attractive flowers, nityasūris vorśipped and performed anjali with their hands which are like flowers and falling at your divine feet.

**ippōdu en nenjin uḷḷē …**– I had no idea even a moment before your arrival \[that you will arrive in my heart\]

**pugundāyai …** – While I did not even beseech you, you came voluntarily and announced your sweetness. Now, will I allow you to leave me?

**nal pōdu vaṇḍu kiṇḍum …** – On the distinguished flowers, the beetles as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-11-kudainthu-vandunnum/) “*kudaindu vaṇḍu uṇṇum*” (beetles are submerged into the flowers while drinking their honey), oh, one who is having as your residence, tirunaṟaiyūr which is an enjoyable place where the beetles can only go deep into the flowers and enjoy the honey and not go elsewhere! Is the town’s enjoyability such that those who were immersed in the sweetness of the town can seek other places?

## 7.2.9. Uner akkai

*ūnēr ākkai tannai uḻandōmbi vaittamaiyālyānāy enṟanakkāy adiyēn manam pugundatēnē! tīn karumbin teḷivē! en sindai tannālnānē eydap peṟṟēn naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambīyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

yānāy – being my antaryāmi; enṟanakkāy – being obedient towards me; adiyēn – this servitor’s (my); manam – in the heart; pugunda – one who entered; tēnē – oh, one who is sweet like honey!; tīn – sweet; karumbin – sugarcane juice’s; teḷivē – oh, one who is sweet like the essence!; naṟaiyūr – in the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – one who is mercifully residing; nambi – Oh, the complete one!; Un ēr – filled with flesh; ākkai tannai – body; uḻandu – with much strain; ōmbi vaittamaiyāl – having nurtured; en – my; sindai tannāl – with my heart; nānē – I (who nurtured); eydap peṟṟēn – attained (you)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, the complete one who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr! Oh one who is sweet like honey and entered my heart being this servitor’s obedient antaryāmi! Oh, one who is sweet like the sweet sugarcane’s essence! Having nurtured my body which is filled with flesh, with much strain, I attained you with my heart.

**ūnēr ākkai …** – āḻvār is saying that he attained the benefit of bhagavān’s efforts where bhagavān incarnated in many forms and pursued āḻvār. The body which is filled with flesh. Through wrong means, I gathered wealth, nurtured this body and got the result for that.

**yānāy …** – bhagavān thought “If I remain as I am and he remains as he is, if we try to unite with him, he will stop me and avoid me. Hence, let me become part of the word ‘him’ and will unite with him” and being counted in the word “I”, he came and united with me \[as antaryāmi, the in-dwelling super-soul\].

**enṟanakkāy** – The one who is greater than all, has made himself available for me.

**adiyēn …** – bhagavān presented himself to āḻvār and entered āḻvār’s heart. As āḻvār thought about this, he felt joyful.

**tēnē** – Oh, one who is enjoyable in all ways!

**en sindai …** – Instead of accepting another body and attaining bhagavān in that new body, I who nurtured this body which is filled with flesh, got to attain him in this same body.

When asked “How did that happen?” āḻvār says

**naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambīyō!** – Since you have arrived in tirunaṟaiyūr, I attained you now.

## 7.2.10. Nannir vayal

*nannīr vayal pudai sūḻ naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyaikkannīr māl varait tōḷ kalikanṟi mangaiyar kōnsonnīr sol mālai solluvārgaḷ sūḻ visumbilnannīrmaiyāl magiḻndu nedungālam vāḻvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nal nīr – having beautiful water; vayal – by fertile-fields; pudai – on the sides; sūḻ – surrounded; naṟaiyūr – in the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – mercifully residing; nambiyai – on the lord who is complete; kal – resounding; nīr – waterfalls from the mountain, their; māl – huge; varai – like a mountain; tōḷ – having shoulders; kali – enemies; kanṟi – one who shows anger on; mangaiyar – for the residents of tirumangai region; kōn – mercifully spoken by tirumangai āḻvār, who is the lord; sol – words of praise; nīr – having as nature; sol mālai – these ten pāsurams which are like a garland of words; solluvārgaḷ – those who recite; sūḻ – expansive (and which grants joy); visumbil – in paramapadam; nal – matching the true nature; nīrmaiyāl – by the qualities; magiḻndu – becoming joyful; nedu – end-less; kālam – up to the time; vāḻvār – will remain blissful

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān, who is complete, is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirunaṟaiyūr which is surrounded on the sides by fertile fields having beautiful water. tirumangai āḻvār, who is the lord of the residents of tirumangai region, who shows anger on the enemies, who is having mountain like huge shoulders where the mountain is having waterfalls, mercifully composed these ten pāsurams which are like a garland of words which are having the nature to be words of praise. Those who recite these ten pāsurams, will remain joyful in the expansive paramapadam with qualities matching their true nature and remain blissful forever.

**nannīr …** – Fertile fields having abundance of beautiful water is present everywhere in the surroundings of tirnaṟaiyūr. The lord who is present in such tirunaṟaiyūr and who is complete in auspicious qualities, is being praised.

**kannīr mālvarait tōḷ** – kal – sound. āḻvār who is having the strength of the shoulders which are like mountains with waterfalls having great sound, having the nature of eliminating the enemies, and being the leader of tirumangai region, is the one who sang these pāsurams.

**sonnīr sol mālai …** – Having collection of words, where those who recite these pāsurams will say “What an amazing set of pāsurams!” and praise, as their nature. Those who recite these pāsurams. The benefit for reciting these pāsurams is the recital itself. But on top of that, they will go to paramapadam which is the best among bhōga bhūmi (enjoyable places), and being naturally blissful, through the way matching the ātmā’s svarūpam (true nature), will attain the enjoyment which is said to have no punarāvrutti (return to samsāram).

## 7.3 Sinavil

## 7.3.1. Sinavil

*sinavil sengaṇ arakkar uyir māḷacceṟṟa villi enṟu kaṟṟavar tandammanamuḷ koṇḍu enṟum eppōdum ninṟēttummāmuniyai maram ēḻ eyda maindanainanavil senṟārkkum naṇṇaṟkariyānainān adiyēn naṟaiyūr ninṟa nambiyaikanavil kaṇḍēn inṟu kaṇḍamaiyāl enkaṇṇiṇaigaḷ kaḷippak kaḷittēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sinam – for anger; il – being the abode; sem kaṇ – having reddish eyes; arakkar – rākśasas’; uyir – lives; māḷa – to be destroyed; seṟṟa – one who showed his anger; villi enṟu – saying, oh, one who is having the bow!; kaṟṟavar – wise persons; tam tam – their; manamuḷ – in mind; koṇḍu – meditating; enṟum – at all times; eppōdum – in all situations; ninṟu – remaining firmly; ēttum – one who is praised; mā – great; muniyai – being the one who has gratitude towards devotees; ēḻ maram – seven marāmarams (ebony trees); eyda – one who shot; maindanai – being the strong person; nanavil – in clarity; senṟārkkum – for the wisest persons who conduct themselves; naṇṇaṟku – to attain (to physically see); ariyānai – being very difficult; naṟaiyūr ninṟa – one who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr; nambiyai – pūrṇan (the complete one); adiyēn – I, servitor; kanavil – in my mind; kaṇḍēn – enjoyed; inṟu – now; kaṇḍamaiyāl – due to having external vision; en kaṇ iṇaigaḷ – both of my eyes; kaḷippa – having become joyful (due to that); kaḷittēn – (I too) have become joyful

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Wise persons say “Oh one who is having the bow and showed anger to have the lives of the rākśasas who have anger and reddish eyes, destroyed!”, meditate in their minds, remain firm and praise him at all times and in all situations. He is having great gratitude towards his devotees. He is the strong person who shot the seven marāmarams. Even for the wisest persons who conduct themselves with clarity, he is very difficult to attain. He is the pūrṇan (complete one) who is mercifully residing in tirunaṟaiyūr. I, the servitor, have enjoyed him in my mind. Now, due to having external vision too, both of my eyes have become joyful and in turn I too have become joyful.

**sinavil …** – rākśasas are having great anger, having hatred towards sentient beings for no reason, having reddish eyes which reflect such hatred. Oh, one who is holding the bow which destroyed the lives of such rākśasas! Just as a mother would torment her child without seeing the relationship, bhagavān did not see his common relationship as said in jitantē stōtram “*dēvānām dānavānānca sāmānyam atidaivatam*” (One who is common to both dēvatās and asuras, and who is superior to all), and killed the rākśasas. Since their presence will destroy the world, to preserve his wealth, he destroyed them.

**kaṟṟavar …** – Wise yōgis will have him in their hearts and praise him at all times and in all situations. He would do everything for them yet will remain as if he has not done anything and will think “What can I do for them?” as if he is indebted

**maram ēḻ …** – Even for those who don’t know about his nature, he raises his weapon and makes them believe in him.

**nanavil …** – This is opposite to “*kanavil*” (in dream) and shows the state of awareness. nanavu – clarity. Even for the most knowledgeable person, he is difficult to be directly approached and seen.

**nān adiyēn** … – I, who am a servitor who, unlike those who tried to see him by their own efforts, got to see him by his grace. The complete one who is eternally residing in tirunaṟaiyūr, with auspicious qualities. Instead of seeing him with the help of mind, I enjoyed him as the mind completely fell in line with him.

Having seen him today like this,

**kaṇṇiṇaigaḷ kaḷippak kaḷittēnē** – Instead of having the shortcoming “While the mind fully enjoyed him, eyes did not get to enjoy”, as the eyes saw and enjoyed him, the abode of those eyes, that is, I, got to enjoy as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.8.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/02/thiruvaimozhi-10-8-4-elidhayinavarenru/) “*en kaṇgaḷ kaḷippak* *kaḷidāgiya sindaiyanāyk kaḷikkinṟēn*” (my thirsty eyes are saying “the goal which is difficult to attain, has become easy!” to become joyful, I am enjoying).

## 7.3.2. Tay ninainda

*tāy ninainda kanṟē okka ennaiyumtannaiyē ninaikkac ceydu tān enakkāy ninaindu aruḷ seyyum appanaianṟu ivvaiyagam uṇḍu umiḻndittavāyanai magarak kuḻaik kādanaimaindanai madiḷ kōval idaikaḻiāyinai amararkku ariyēṟṟai enanbanai anṟi ādariyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāyai – (its) mother; ninainda – remembering; kanṟē okka – like a calf; ennaiyum – I who got his favours; tannaiyē – he, the benefactor; ninaikkac ceydu – made me to meditate (further); tān – he who is sarvēśvaran; enakkāy – for me who is ignorant (my well-being); ninaindu – thought; aruḷ seyyum – one who is showering his mercy; appanai – being natural relative; anṟu – during that dangerous time; ivvaiyagam – this world; uṇḍu – consumed (and then); umiḻnditta – let out; vāyanai – one who is having divine mouth; magarak kuḻai – having makara kuṇḍalam (ear-rings); kādanai – having divine ears; maindanai – being eternally youthful; madil – having forts; kōval – in tirukkōvalūr; idai kaḻi – in the divine verandah; āyinai – one who remained (amidst mudalāḻvārs); amararkku – in the middle of nityasūris; ari – like a lion; ēṟṟai – one who is prideful like a bull; en anbanai anṟi – on anyone other than the one who has love towards me; ādariyēn – I will not show my love

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Just as a calf will remember its mother cow, bhagavān, the natural relative, who is the benefactor, made me who got his favours, meditate upon him, and he who is omniscient thought about me who is ignorant and is showering his mercy; he is having the divine mouth which consumed the world during the deluge and let it out subsequently; he is having the divine ears which are decorated with divine makara kuṇḍalam; he is eternally youthful; amidst mudalāḻvārs, he remained in the divine verandah in tirukkōvalūr which is having forts; he remains amidst nityasūris as a lion and a prideful bull; I will not show my love towards anyone other than such bhagavān who has love towards me.

**tāy …** – Just as a calf which remembers its mother, he made me think about him only. The calf thinks about the mother cow not for any other purpose but due to the gratitude of past nursing only; he made me also think about him due to gratitude towards him.

**tān enakkāy ninaindu** – bhagavān thought “Even after doing everything there will be some shortcoming. Hence, why should we place such difficult requirement in him?” and as said in varāha carama ślōkam “*aham smarāmi*” (I will think about such bhakta), and thought about me to eliminate the shortcoming in me of not thinking about him.

**aruḷ seyyum appanai** – Though there is no reason in me, he is the natural relative who showered his mercy fully to me.

**anṟu ivvaiygam uṇḍu umḻinditta vāyanai** – When the world became caught in the deluge of water, bhagavān has the nature to equally help everyone. One who is having the divine lips which protected us by placing in his stomach and letting us out subsequently.

**magarak kuḻai nādanai** … – One who is having such beauty that even in praḷayam one will not fail to notice it.

**maindanai** – one who is having eternal youthfulness.

**madiḷ kōval idai kaḻi āyanai** – One who entered amidst his dear devotees and jostled with them.

**amararrku ari ēṟṟai** – One who is having this aspect of entering the group of his beloved ones and jostling them, as his nature. Being complete in this manner, one who showed love towards me.

**anṟi ādariyēnē** – As he is showering his love upon me, will I support anyone else than him?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.3.3. Vanda nal

*vanda nāḷ vandu en nenjidam koṇḍānmaṟṟōr nenjaṟiyān adiyēnudaiccindaiyāy vandu tenpularkku ennaiccēr kodān idu sikkenap peṟṟēnkondulām poḻil sūḻ kudandait talaikkōvinaik kudamādiya kūttanaiendaiyai endai tandai tammānaiempirānai ettāl maṟakkēnē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

vanda nāḷ – on the day when he first came to accept me; vandu – approached me; en nenju – my heart; idam koṇḍān – acknowledged as his abode; maṟṟu ōr nenju – another person’s heart; aṟiyān – he does not know \[consider\] as his abode; adiyēnudai – my; sindaiyāy vandu – came having my desire (i.e. he voluntarily came with the intent to grant the nitya kainkaryam which I should pray for); then pularkku – on the hands of yama dūtas (messengers of yama) who are present in the southern direction; ennai – me who was pursued and accepted by bhagavān himself; sēr kodān – will not allow me to be caught; idu – this; sikkena – firmly; peṟṟēn – I attained; (hence); ulā – roaming (completely filled); poḻil – by the orchards; sūḻ – filled; kudandait talai – mercifully reclining in tirukkudandai; kōvinai – being the lord; kudam ādiya – performed kudakkūttu (dance with pots); kūttanai – being the one with amazing activities; endaiyai – being my father; endai – for my father; tandai – for my clan which includes my grandfather; tammānai – being the lord; em pirānai – one who is my benefactor; ettāl – with which reason; maṟakkēn – can I forget?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

On the day when he first came to accept me, he approached me and acknowledged my heart as his abode; he does not know another person’s heart as his abode. Having come to me who was pursued and accepted by himself, he will not allow me to be caught by the hands of yama dūtas (messengers of yama) who are present in the southern direction; I attained this firmly. Being the lord who is mercifully reclining in tirukkudandai which is filled with complete orchards, being with amazing activities and who performed kudakkūttu (dance with pots), with which reason can I forget the one who is my benefactor and the lord for my clan which includes me, my father and my grandfather?

**vanda nāḷ …** – bhagavān’s initial acceptance cannot be attributed with any of āḻvār’s previous efforts. Hence it cannot be seen as a return favour from bhagavān and thus it can only be said as “*vanda nāḷ*” (the day he came initially) without any other attributes.

**en nenju idam koṇḍān** – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 5.34 “*āvāsam tvahamiccāmi pratiśtam iha kānanē*” (As I am looking for a place to say, I will live in this forest as you desire), he made my heart as his abode.

**maṟṟu ōr nenju aṟiyān** – He is not even going to tiruvadi (garudāḻvār), tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) et al. As said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.8 “*anandan pālum garudanpālum aidu noydāga vaittu*” (showing less love towards ādiśēśan and garudāḻvār), periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.9 “*ida vagaigaḷ igaḻndittu*” (abandoning all the abodes) and [periya tiruvandādi 68](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/01/periya-thiruvandhadhi-68/) “*kallum kanaikadalum vaigunda vānādum* *pullenṟoḻindanakol*” (tiruvēngada hill, the agitated kśīrābdi, śrīvaikuṇṭam were all ignored like ignoring a blade of grass), bhagavān is not considering that there is any abode other than āḻvār’s divine heart. When asked “In such a case, is he not present in those places?”, just as saubhari took many forms and enjoyed, bhagavān is present everywhere thinking “There is nothing better than āḻvār’s divine heart”.

**adiyēnudaiya …** – He came with the desire I had towards him as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍum*” (should serve fully without leaving anything), and will not show me to the servitors of yama.

**idu sikkenap peṟṟēn** – If this had happened by my vow, there is a possibility of breaking. Since this happened by his vow, it will never break.

**kondulām …** – Mercifully reclining in tirukkudandai which is surrounded by orchards which have bunches of flowers and eternal spring, he manifested his lordship completely.

**kudam ādiya …** – One who fully gave his physical beauty to the covherd people, by dancing with the pots in the four-way junctions.

**endaiyai …** – My father, my clan’s lord.

**empirānai …** – The great benefactor who manifested his svarūpam, rūpam, guṇam, vibhūti etc, to me.

**ettāl maṟakkēnē** – Can I forget him since he helped me in a limited manner? Can I remain patiently thinking about the favours I proffered to him? How can I forget him? \[I can’t forget him\]

## 7.3.4. Urangalal iyanra

*urangaḷāl iyanṟa mannar māḷappāradattu oru tēr aivarkkāyc cenṟuirangi ūrndu avarkku innaruḷ seyyumempirānai vambār punal kāviriarangamāḷi ennāḷi viṇṇāḷiāḻi sūḻ ilangai malangac cenṟusarangaḷ āṇḍa taṇ tāmaraik kaṇṇanukku anṟien manam tāḻndu nillādē*

**Пословный перевод:**

urangaḷālē – by strength; iyanṟa – conducting (the kingdom); mannar – kings such as duryōdana et al; māḷa – to be killed; bāradattu – in the bhārata yuddam; aivarkkāy – for panca pāṇḍavas; senṟu – went; irangi – being softened (in their matters); oru tēr – a chariot; ūrndu – conducted; avarkku – for those panca pāṇḍavas; in – being sweet (natural); aruḷ – mercy; seyyum – did; empirānai – being the benefactor; vambu – fresh; punal – by water; Ar – filled; kāviri – having divine kāviri; arangam āḷi – one who protects śrīrangam; en āḷi – one who rules me; viṇ āḷi – one is the controller of paramapadam; āḻi sūḻ – being surrounded by ocean; ilangai – lankā; malanga – to be tormented; senṟu – reached; sarangaḷ – arrows; āṇḍa – launched; taṇ – cool; tāmarai – like lotus; kaṇṇanukku anṟi – on anyone else’s matter other than the one who has eyes; en manam – my heart; tāḻndu – accepting humility (becoming melted); nillādu – cannot remain

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa went for the sake of panca pāṇḍavas to mahābhārata war to have the kings such as duryōdana et al who were conducting the kingdom by their strength, killed; his heart became softened seeing paāṇḍavas and he conducted a chariot and showered his sweet mercy on them; he is such a benefactor. He protects the śrīrangam which is having the divine kāviri which is filled with fresh water; he rules over me; he also controls paramapadam; he reached lankā which is surrounded by ocean to torment it and launched his arrows. He is having cool lotus-like eyes. My heart will not have any humility towards anyone other than him.

**urangaḷāl …** – Instead of conducting the kingdom with their righteousness, kings such as duryōdana et al are conducting with their strength being possessed by demoniac thought. To kill such kings in mahābhārata war, he placed this single chariot as the opposing force for the enemies. In this manner, for the sake of pāṇḍavas, he troubled himself.

**irangi** – Showing mercy towards them thinking “Alas! They lost their father in their young age; they suffered in the wax-palace; they were tormented in water etc”, he conducted the chariot for them and showed his mercy as if it is his own benefit, instead of helping them as per their request. The benefactor whose favours towards his devotees are boundless.

**vambār …** – One who is having śrīrangam which has the divine kāviri which has perennial flow of water, under his control.

**en āḷi** – My controller.

**viṇ āḷi** – One who owns nitya vibhūti (paramapadam).

**āḻi sūḻ ilangai malangac cenṟu** – For anyone other than sarvēśvaran who is puṇḍarīkākśa (lotus-eyed) and who went to lankā which is well fortified by the ocean and launched arrows to make seven persons wear one person’s clothes, in there.

**en manam tāḻndu nillādē** – My heart will not have humility for anyone other than the one who became the charioteer for his devotees and who favours them by accepting arrows on his divine body.

## 7.3.5. Angu vennaragattu

*āngu vennaragattu aḻundum pōdu anjēl enṟu adiyēnai angē vandutāngu tāmarai anna ponnār adiempirānai umbarkku aṇiyāy ninṟa vēngadattu ariyaip parikīṟiyai veṇṇey uṇḍu uralinidai āppuṇḍatīngarumbinai tēnai nanpālinai anṟien manam sindai seyyādē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āngu – present in the abodes such as pātāḷa etc; ven naragattu – in the cruel hells; aḻundum pōdu – while being drowned (and suffering); angē vandu – came to those places; anjēl enṟu – saying “don’t fear”; adiyēnai – I, who am your servitor; tāngu – one who protects; tāmarai anna – matching a lotus flower; pon Ar – very desirable; adi – one who is having divine feet; empirānai – being my lord; umbarkku – for nityasūris; aṇiyāy ninṟa – one who remains as the decoration; vēngadattu – mercifully present in tiruvēngada mountain; ariyai – being the lion; pari – kēśi who came in the form of a horse; kīṟiyai – one tore the mouth; veṇṇey uṇḍu – (stealing and) eating the butter; ural idai – in between the mortar (with his waist and the mortar); āppuṇḍa – one who was bound; tīm karumbinai – one who is like sweet sugarcane juice; tēnai – one who is sweet like honey; nal pālinai anṟi – anyone other than puruśōttama who is like sweet milk; en manam – my heart; sindai seyyādu – will not think of

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

While I, the servitor, was drowning in the cruel hells which are present in the abodes such as pātāḷa etc, he came to those places and protected me saying “don’t fear”. He is having very desirable divine feet which are like lotus flower. He is my lord. He remains as the decoration for nityasūris. He is mercifully present in tiruvēngada mountain as a lion. He tore the mouth of kēśi, who came in the form of a horse. For eating the butter, he was bound with the mortar. My heart will not think about anyone other than puruśōttama who is like sweet sugarcane juice, sweet like honey and sweet milk.

**āngu ven naragam …** – Instead of relieving me from performing the sins while being engaged in them, after completing those acts, in the cruel hells where suffering is undergone which are not seen while engaging in the acts, he comes there.

**anjēl enṟu …** – Instead of remaining “He has committed the sins and is reaping the results. How does it bother us?” he went there and said “While I am present, should you be a target of the result of your sins? Don’t fear”

**tāngu …** – He protects us with his very desirable, divine feet which are like fresh lotus flower. My lord, whose divine feet can be superficially compared to lotus flower for the expansive nature, freshness, coolness, fragrance etc. But these aspects are not limited in the divine feet as they are in the flower. bhagavān’s lotus feet are very tender and desirable.

**umbarkku aṇi …** – His standing posture in tirumalā appears like an ornament for nityasūris.

**ariyai** – Just as he remains as an ornament for those who love him, he remains invincible for those who hate him.

**pari kīṟiyai** – One who tore the mouth of kēśi.

**veṇṇey …** – He became totally dependent on the food item (butter) which has the physical touch of devotees; having not acquired it directly, tried to steal and eat the same, and being unable to do it perfectly, got caught in the act, bound along with the mortar, got beaten and trying to escape the beating, he became pale and sorrowful. As āḻvār meditated about these aspects again and again, he enjoyed such situation in all manners. This enjoyment is such sweet as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sarvarasa:*” (bhagavān’s divine form is origin of all tastes).

**nal pālinai …** – My heart will not constantly meditate upon anyone other than bhagavān who is so enjoyable.

## 7.3.6. Ettanaip poludagilum

*ettanaip poḻudāgilum enṟumen manattu agalādirukkum pugaḻtattalartta ponnē alarkōngintāḻ poḻil tirumālirunjōlai anggattiyai karumbīnṟa insāṟṟaikkādalāl maṟai nāngum munnōdiyapattanaip paravait tuyilēṟṟai enpaṇbanai anṟip pādal seyyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enṟum – always; ettanaip poḻudāgilum – even a moment; en manattu – from my heart; agalādu – without separating; irukkum – due to mercifully being present; pugaḻ – having fame; tattu – very; alartta – blossomed; pon ēy – desirable like gold; alar – having flowers; kōngin – kōngu trees’; tāḻ – well grown; poḻil – having orchard; tirumālirunjōlai – being mercifully present in tirumālirunjōlai mountain; am – sweet; kattiyai – one who is enjoyable like sugar candy; karumbu – sugar cane; īnṟa – secreting; in – sweet; sāṟṟai – being like the essence; kādalāl – with desire; maṟai nāngum – four vēdams; mun – previously in kriṣṇāvatāram; ōdiya – learnt; pattanai – being a pandit (scholar); paravai – in kśīrābdi; tuyil – mercifully reclining; ēṟṟai – being the best; en paṇbanai anṟi – other than the one who is easily approachable for me; pādal seyyēn – will not sing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is having the fame of always mercifully remaining in my heart without leaving even for a moment; he is mercifully present in tirumālirunjōlai mountain which is having well-grown orchard which is having kōngu trees’ flowers which are blossomed and desirable like gold; he is enjoyable like sweet, sugar candy; he is the sweet essence secreted by sugarcane; he is the paṇḍita who desirously learnt the four vēdams, previously in kriṣṇāvatāram; he is the best one, mercifully reclining on kśīrābdi. Other than the one who is easily approachable for me, I will not sing anyone else.

**ettanai …** – Even if I desire to go towards others seeing some greatness in them, my speech will not cooperate with that.

One who has acquired fame due to not leaving my heart even for a fraction of a moment; he is thinking to be a greater fame than pirātti remaining on his chest saying as in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-10-10-agalagillen-part-1/) “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum*” (I cannot leave even for a fraction of a second). Always, even a fraction of a moment, he will not leave.

**tattu alartta …** – kōngu trees’ flowers which are blossoming and like gold; alternative explanation – blossomed to have the petals well expanded and like gold. One who remains on tirumalai (tirumālirunjōlai mountain) which is having well grown orchards which have kōngu trees having such flowers.

**kattiyai …** – Unlike the sugar candies which are created by hand-pressing which implies that it loses its freshness, being the fresh essence of such sugarcane.

**kādalāl …** – Just as someone who had never learnt vēdam will learn eagerly, the paṇḍita who eagerly learnt four vēdams from sāndīpani. I will not sing anyone else other than such bhagavān who is mercifully reclining on tiruppāṟkadal as the origin for kriṣṇāvatāram (and other avatārams).

## 7.3.7. Pannin inmoli

*paṇṇin inmoḻi yāḻ narambil peṟṟapālaiyāgi ingē pugundu enkaṇṇum nenjum vāyum idangoṇḍānkoṇḍa pin maṟaiyōr manam tannuḷviṇṇuḷār perumānai emmānaivīngu nīr magaram tiḷaikkum kadalvaṇṇan māmaṇi vaṇṇan em aṇṇalvaṇṇamē anṟi vāy uraiyādē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇṇin – in songs; in – pleasant to hear; moḻi – having words; yāḻ – harp’s; narambil – in the strings; peṟṟa – created; pālaiyāgi – being very sweet like the tune named pālai; ingē – in my heart here; pugundu – came and entered; en kaṇṇum – my eyes; nenjum – heart; vāyum – speech; idam kondān – accepted as his abode; koṇḍapin – after accepting in this manner; maṟaiyōr – brāhmaṇas who are vaidikas, their; manam – heart; than uḷ – having as his abode; viṇṇuḷār – for nityasūris; perumān – being the lord; emmān – being my controller; vīngu – growing; nīr – having water; magaram – fish; tiḷaikkum – jumping and playing; kadal vaṇṇan – having complexion of the ocean; mā – best; maṇi – blue gem’s; vaṇṇan – having the nature; em aṇṇal – my lord’s; vaṇṇamē – other than his nature; anṟi – anything else; vāy – my mouth; uraiyādē – will not tell

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being very sweet like the tune named pālai which is created from the string of the harp which has words from the songs which are pleasant to hear, bhagavān entered my heart and accepted my eyes, heart and speech as his abode. After doing so, he is having the heart of the brāhmaṇas who are vaidikas, as his abode, being the lord for nityasūris and being the controller for me, being the one who is having the complexion of the ocean where there is abundance of water and fish which are jumping and playing, being the one who is having the nature of a blue gem. My mouth will not speak about anything else other than my lord’s nature.

**paṇṇinin moḻi yāḻ …** – āḻvār is saying “My mind, speech and body do not know anything else other than bhagavān”.

**paṇṇin …** – The tune named pālai which is created from the strings of harp which has nice sound among the different tunes. bhagavān came and entered as sweet as that tune.

**en kaṇṇum nenjum vāyum idam koṇḍān** – He became the only target of my eyes so that they don’t see anything else; he became the target of my speech so that it does not involve with anything else; he became the target of my heart so that it does not have the opportunity to think about anyone else. In this manner, he became the target of all of my senses.

**maṟaiyōr …** – One who has the heart of brāhmaṇas as his abode and one who remains as the lord of nityasūris as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*“.

**vīngu nīr …** – Having abundant water, the ocean is having many creatures gathering and playing in it; having the complexion of such ocean, having the complexion of priceless blue gem. My speech will not talk about anything else other than the one who made me exist fully for him by showing his such complexion.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.3.8. Ini eppavam

*ini eppāvam vandeydum? solleeremakku immaiyē aruḷ peṟṟamaiyāl adumtuniyait tīrttu inbamē taruginṟadu ōrtōṟṟat tonneṟiyai vaiyam toḻappadummuniyai vānavarāl vaṇangappadummuttinaip pattar tām nugarginṟadu ōrkaniyaik kādal seydu en uḷḷam koṇḍakaḷvanai inṟu kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

immaiyē – in this birth (in this world) itself; aruḷ – (bhagavān’s) mercy; peṟṟamaiyāl – having attained; ini – further; emakku – us; eppāvam – which type of sins (from past and future); vandu eydum – will reach?; solleer – you tell; adum – destroying (the ātmā); tuniyai – karmas which are the hurdles for the goal; tīrttu – eliminating; inbam – pure joy; taruginṟadu – one who is giving; ōr – unique; tōṟṟam – beautiful; tol – ancient; neṟiyai – being the upāya (means); vaiyam – by the people of the world; toḻappadum – being surrendered; muniyai – one who is meditating (upon the results to be granted for those people); vānavarāl – by nityasūris; vaṇangap padum – being surrendered; muttinai – cool like pearl (rejuvenating); pattar tām – by upāsakas (bhakti yōgis) who are mumukśus (liberation seekers); nugarginṟadu – enjoyed; ōr – uniquely sweet; kaniyai – one who is like a fruit; kādal seydu – being desirous; en uḷḷam – my heart; koṇḍa – captured; kaḷvanai – the thief; inṟu – now; kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – have seen you

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

You tell me “Which sins will reach us anymore after having attained bhagavān’s mercy in this birth itself?” bhagavān is eliminating the karmas which are hurdles for the attainment of the goal and destroying the self, and is granting pure joy; he is the unique, ancient means; he is surrendered to, by the people of the world and is meditating (upon the results to be granted for those people); he is surrendered to by nityasūris; he is having a cool, pearl like form; he is enjoyed like a uniquely sweet fruit by the upāsakas who are mumukśus; now I am seeing such bhagavān who desirously captured my heart.

**ini eppāvam …** –  As said in brahma vaivartam-prakruti kaṇḍam 26-90 “***avaśyam anubhōktavyam*** *krutam karma śubhāśubham l* *nābhuktam kśīyatē karma kalpakōti śatairapi* ll´ (The effects of deeds of vice and virtue, carried out by a person, have to be necessarily experienced. The effects cannot be wished away, even after passage of hundreds of crores of *kalpam*), can the sins which are a result of bhagavān’s anger, reach me? Can some of these sins be retained for me saying that they cannot be exhausted without experiencing or saying that these are prārabdam (already started giving results)? \[No\]

What is the reason for saying “*ini*” (after this)?

**immaiyē aruḷ peṟṟamaiyāl** – Since we have got bhagavān’s mercy in this life itself, tell me which sins will come to me?

**adum tuniyai …** – ātmā, who is said in śrī bhagavat gītā 2.24 “***accēdyōýam adāhyōýam*** *aklēdyō’śōśya ēvaca* l *nityas sarvagata*: *stāṇuracalōýam sanātana*: ll” (ātmā, which permeates all through the body, cannot be severed; it cannot be burnt; it cannot be wet; it cannot be dried. Hence, ātmā is permanent, firm, immovable and existing since time immemorial), is destroyed to become as said in taitirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (to be like acit) by tuni. tuni – karmas which are hurdles for the goal. emperumān eliminates all of them. As said in taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli 7 “*ēśahyēvānandayāti*” (he – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – himself makes jīvātmā ecstatic), he makes the ātmā matclessly blissful.

**tōṟṟat tonneṟiyai** – tōṟṟam – beauty. tonmai – greatness. Beautiful, great state. bhagavān is being the stable upāyam for everyone – i.e., a) those who pursue other upāyams also have to depend on him and b) those who pursued him need not look out for anything else. As said in [tirumālai 6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thirumalai-6/) “*aṟam suvarāgi ninṟa*” (one who is standing with darmam (righteousness) as wall) – he need not be created now, he is already present since time immemorial. As said in mahābhāratam vana parvam 71-123 “*yē ca vēda vidō viprā yē cādyātma vidō janā*: l *tē vidanti mahātmānam* ***kriṣṇam darmam sanātanam***  ll” (brāhmaṇas who know vēdams and the elders who know the nature of ātmā know that kriṣṇa symbolises the ancient righteousness). He said about such aspect in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mām*” (I).

**vaiyam toḻappadum …** – Being surrendered to by everyone on the earth; as the svarupam (true nature) of each cētana varies, their ruci (taste) will also vary; one who is meditating about granting such results to each cētana based on their ruci. Also, surrendered to by nityasūris who have no separate desires \[from bhagavān\], and who eliminates their fatigue.

**pattar tām …** – There are mumukśus in this samsāra – those who are having taste towards him. For them, he remains the ripened fruit which can be enjoyed immediately. He is having desire towards me who has no such qualities (of nityasūris and mumukśus) and has fully captured me. He did in a fraction of a moment the act of stealing this ātmā which has been done by me since time immemorial. While I did not expect, I got to see such bhagavān.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.3.9. En seygen

*en seygēn adiyēn? uraiyīr idaṟkuenṟum en manattē irukkum pugaḻtanjaiyāḷiyaip ponpeyarōn nenjamanṟu idandavanait taḻalē puraiminsey vāḷarakkan nagar pāḻ padaccūḻkadal siṟai vaittu imaiyōr toḻumponsey māl varaiyai maṇik kunṟinaianṟi en manam pōṟṟiyennādē*

**Пословный перевод:**

adiyēn – I, who am a paratantra (fully obedient); idaṟku – for his such great favours; en seygēn – what return favour can I do?; uraiyīr – you tell; enṟum – always; en manattē – in my heart only; irukkum – due to residing; pugaḻ – having acquired fame; tanjai āḷiyai – being the controller of tanjai mā maṇik kōyil; pon peyarōn – hiraṇya’s; nenjam – chest; anṟu – previously; idandavanai – one who tore away; taḻalē purai – unapproachable like fire; vinja – having great valour; vāḷ – having the weapon, sword; arakkan – rāvaṇāsura’s; nagar – town; pāḻpada – to become ruins; sūḻ – surrounding (the town); kadal – ocean; siṟai vaittu – building a bridge; imaiyōr – by dēvatās; toḻum – being surrendered to; pon sey – desirable; māl – huge; varaiyai – being like a mountain; maṇi – filled with blue gems; kunṟinai anṟi – anyone other than the one who is having cool form like a mountain; en manam – my heart; pōṟṟi ennādu – will not perform mangaḷāśāsanam saying “Long live!”

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

You tell me “What return favour can be done by me, who is a paratantra, to bhagavān for his such great favours?” He has acquired fame due to residing in my heart only; being the controller of tanjai mā maṇik kōyil, he previously tore away hiraṇya’s chest; being unapproachable like fire, he built a bridge on the ocean surrounding the town of rāvaṇāsura who is having sword, the weapon, to make that town become ruins; he is surrendered to by dēvatās; he is like a huge mountain; he is having a cool form like that of a mountain which is filled with blue gems; my heart will not perform mangaḷāśāsanam saying “Long live!” to anyone other than such bhagavān.

**en seygēn …** – I can’t remain without doing return favour; but I am not seeing what I can do as favour. What can I do?

**adiyēn …** – Since my true nature is to be a paratantra, I don’t have anything in my hand as principal; what can I do?

**uraiyīr** – You, who are on the shore, being neutral (without full engagement with bhagavān), will be able to tell me.

**enṟum …** – Since you \[emperumān\] are constantly residing in my heart, you are having fame. One who stood in tanjāvūr to enter my heart.

**pon peyarōn …** – One who helped me long ago. \[āḻvārs consider bhagavān’s help to others as help to them\]

**taḻalē …** – He remains unreachable by any enemy due to emanating fire, being unconquerable, being ready to help; he built a bridge on the ocean which is like a moat for the lankā of rākśasa \[rāvaṇa\] who acquired the shining sword from a dēvatā \[rudra\].

**imaiyōr …** – brahmā et al. On regaining their abodes, after the rāma-rāvaṇa yuddam, they praised śrīrāma as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 120-13 “*abravīccruṇu mē rāma satyam satya parākrama* l ***bhavān nārāyaṇō dēva*****:**  *śrīmāmścakrāyudō vibhu*: ll” (Oh rāma, the true warrior! Listen to my words: You are the consort of divine mahālakśmi, the one who holds divine disc, and the lord nārāyaṇa who pervades everything and everywhere), as one who remained with radiant form due to that. He remained with a cool complexion thinking “I got to fulfil their desires”. Other than such bhagavān, my heart will not perform mangaḷāśāsanam to anyone saying “*pōṟṟi*” (Long live). My heart will not perform mangaḷāśāsanam to anyone other than the one who is said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-3-vazhatpattu/) “*pāḻāḷāgap padai porudānukku*” (One who took up arms to turn lankā into ruins). āḻvār is saying “I who am a samsāri (materialistic person) got the benefit which is received by the nityasūris. Since I am paratantra, I am unable to see any return favour. What can I do? Please tell me”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.3.10. Todu vindalar

*tōdu viṇḍalar pūmboḻil mangaiyartōnṟal vāḷ kaliyan tiruvālinādan nannaṟaiyūr ninṟa nambi tannalla māmalarc cēvadi senniccūdiyum toḻudum eḻundādiyumtoṇḍargatku avan sonna sol mālaipādal pattivai pādumin toṇḍīr!pāda nummidaip pāvam nillāvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tōdu – petals; viṇḍu – leaving their joints; alar – blossoming; pū – having flowers; poḻil – surrounded by orchards; mangaiyar – for the residents of tirumangai; tōnṟal – being the chief; vāḷ – with the sword; kaliyan – one who destroys the enemies; tiruvāli nādan – one who is the controller of tiruvāli region; avan – that āḻvār; nal – distinguished; naṟaiyūr – in tirunaṟaiyūr; ninṟa – mercifully present; nambi than – one who is complete with auspicious qualities, his; nalla – beautiful; mā – great; malar – very tender like flower; sē – beautiful (easily approachable for everyone); adi – divine feet; senni – on their divine head; sūdiyum – holding; toḻudum – surrendered; eḻundu – stood up; ādiyum – danced; toṇḍargatku – to uplift the devotees; sonna – mercifully spoke; sol mālai – special garland of words; ivai pattu pādal – these ten pāsurams; toṇḍīr – oh those who are having taste in bhagavat viśayam!; pādumin – sing; pāda – as you sing; nummidai – your; pāvam – sins; nillā – will not remain

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār, who is the chief for the residents of tirumangai, which is surrounded by orchards having flowers which are blossoming after the petals leave their joints, who destroys the enemies with his sword and who is the controller of tiruvāli region, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams, which make a special garland of words for uplifting the devotees to hold the beautiful, great, flower-like very tender divine feet of nambi who is complete in all auspicious qualities and is mercifully present in the distinguished tirunaṟaiyūr. Surrender unto him and rise up and dance. Oh, those who are having taste in bhagavat viśayam! Sing these pāsuramss and as you do that, your sins will not remain with you.

**tōdu viṇḍalar …** – Being the chief for the residents of tirumangai which is surrounded by orchards having flowers which are blossoming after the petals leave their joints.

**vāḷ kaliyan …** – Just as prapatti (surrender) is the means to attain bhagavān, the sword in his hand is for the destruction of enemies.

**tiruvāli nādan** – This itself is sufficient for āḻvār’s greatness.

**nannaṟaiyūr …** – Due to having arrived at and standing in tirunaṟaiyūr, he is having completeness of auspicious qualities. Keeping his divine feet, which are incomparably sweet and never check about the good or bad qualities of the one who is surrendering to, as the decoration for their head.

**toḻudum** – Worśipping as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 11.39](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/11-39-and-11-39-5/) “*nama: purastāt*” (Let my obeisances belong to you, in front of you). Due to the bliss of having vorśipped him, the body being restless, would be dancing.

**toṇḍargatku …** – Instead of enjoying it as he knew and leaving it, āḻvār has this for the enjoyment of people of subsequent times. āḻvār has provided a feast for all the śrīvaiṣṇavas as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/07/thiruvaimozhi-9-4-9-kandu-kondu/) “*toṇḍarkku amuduṇṇac col mālaigaḷ sonnēn*” (I did vācika kainkarayam \[servitude in the form of speech\] in the form of a garland of words for the joyful experience of the servitors of the apt lord).

**pādal pattu –** Instead of being a grantam which has 1,25,000 ślōkams (as in mahābhāratam), where we would not know as to where we entered and where we exited, these are only ten pāsurams. Those who are having taste towards bhagavat viśayam should recite these pāsurams.

**pāda nummidai …** – There is reward for eating sugarcane. While singing these pāsurams itself is the goal, on top of that, the sins which are hurdles for attainment of the goal will automatically leave thinking “This place is not apt for us to remain”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4 Kansora

## 7.4.1. Kansora

*kaṇ sōra vengurudi vandiḻiya vendaḻal pōl kūndalāḷaimaṇ sēra mulai uṇḍa māmadalāy! vānavar tam kōvē! enṟuviṇ sērum iḷandingaḷ agadurinju maṇi māda malgu selvattaṇ sēṟai emperumān tāḷ toḻuvār kāṇmin en talai mēlārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vem – having cruel vision; kaṇ – eyes; sōra – to become dizzy and become weak; vem – hot; kurudi – blood; vandu – it came like a flood; iḻiya – to fall from the body, into the ground; vem – having heat; taḻalpōl – reddish like fire; kūndalāḷai – pūtanā, who is having hair; maṇ sēra – (as a dead body) to fall on the ground; mulai uṇḍa – consumed the milk from her bosoms; mā – very; madalāy – oh, one who is youthful!; vānavar tam – for nityasūris; kōvē – oh, lord!; enṟu – praising in this manner; viṇ sērum – reaching the sky; iḷam tingaḷ – young moon’s; agadu – bottom of the stomach; urinju – tearing; maṇi mādam – by mansions which are filled with precious gems; malgum – abundant; selvam – having wealth; taṇ – cool and rejuvenating; sēṟai – mercifully residing in tiruccēṟai; emperumān – lord’s; tāḷ – divine feet; toḻuvār – those who worship; en talai mēlār kāṇmin – see, they step on my head with their divine feet and roam around

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Those who are praising the lord, who is mercifully residing in tiruccēṟai which is having mansions which are filled with precious gems which are reaching the sky and tearing the young moon’s bottom of the stomach, which is having abundant wealth, and is cool and rejuvenating, saying “Oh one who is very youthful and who consumed the milk from the bosoms of pūtanā to make her fall down on the ground after her cruel eyes became dizzy and weak, hot blood came down from her body like a flood and hair looks like reddish hot fire! Oh, lord of nityasūris!” and worship his divine feet! They step on my head with their divine feet and roam around. See that.

**kaṇ sōra …** – pūtanā assumed the guise of mother yaśōdā and approached kriṣṇa; he killed her to have her cruel eyes to weaken.

**vem kurudi …** – Along with the milk from the bosom, her blood came out like flood.

**vem taḻal …** – As her life ended, the decoration she applied also disappeared. His childishness was such that even after pūtanā, who was having fire like reddish hair, fell down to the ground, he was consuming milk from her bosoms.

**vānavar …** – When asked “When pūtanā assumed the guise of his mother and nursed him, who was the one who consumed her milk without seeing that she is a fiend?” āḻvār says “He is the one who is cared for by nityaūris”.

**viṇ sērum …** – The lord who is mercifully present in tiruccēṟai which is incomparably wealthy due to having mansions filled with precious gems and are tall to tear the bottom of the stomach of candra (moon) who is enjoying in svargam (heaven).

**tāḷ toḻuvār …** – bhagavān says to āḻvār “Just as tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) and kaustubam \[a gemstone on his divine chest\], your touch is very enjoyable for me. Bring your head for me to place my feet on it” āḻvār responds “There is no space for your divine feet; there is only enough space for the bhāgavatas who are apt for me”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.2. Amburuva

*amburuva vari nedungaṇ alar magaḷai varai agalattamarndu mallalkomburuva viḷangani mēl iḷanganṟu koṇḍeṟinda kūttar pōlāmvambalarum taṇ sōlai vaṇ sēṟai vān undu kōyil mēyaemperumān tāḷ toḻuvār eppoḻudum en manattē irukkinṟārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

amburuva – beautiful eyebrows; vari – having stripes; nedu – long; kaṇ – having eyes; alar magaḷai – pirātti who was born in the lotus flower; varai – like a mountain; agalattu – in the divine chest; amarndu – making her fit well; mallal – well grown; kombu – branches; uruva – having as form; viḷam kani mēl – on the fruit of wood apple tree (which was possessed by an asura); iḷam kanṟu koṇḍu – having the youthful vatsāsura as the stick; eṟinda – threw; kūttar – one who is having beautiful gait; vambu – fragrance; alarum – spreading; taṇ sōlai – having cool orchard; vaṇ sēṟai – in the beautiful tiruccēṟai; vān undu – pushing the sky (having such height); kōyil – in the divine temple; mēya – one who is eternally residing; emperumān tāḷ toḻuvār – those who worship bhagavān’s lotus feet; eppoḻudum – always; en manattē – in my heart; irukkinṟār – are residing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is making pirātti who is having beautiful eyebrows, long eyes with stripes and was born in lotus flower , fit well in his mountain like divine chest; he is having the beautiful gait after throwing the youthful vatsāsura as the stick on the fruit of wood apple tree which is having well grown branches as its form; he is mercifully present in the beautiful tiruccēṟai which is having cool orchard where fragrance is spreading and where he is eternally residing in the divine temple which is pushing the sky. Those who worship such bhagavān’s lotus feet are always residing in my heart.

**amburuva …** – Having beautiful eyebrows, having divine eyes which are having red and black lines, and are so expansive that even īśvaran, who enjoys them forever, will not be able to completely enjoy them. pirātti is having lotus flower as her abode. Keeping her in his divine chest which looks like a mountain.

**mallal komburuva …** – Ignoring the fact that his divine form is pirātti’s abode, he launched the demon who had come as the calf on the demon who had come as the wood apple tree; even the few steps which he had taken and took the stance of aiming at the target, formed a wonderful gait, and deserved an umbrella to be held, for their attractiveness. mallal – greatness.

**vambu alarum …** – In tiruccēṟai where the rejuvenating orchard is present and which is always in spring season, the divine temple appears to be pushing up the sky, bhagavān is eternally residing. Those who worship those divine feet.

**eppoḻudum en manattē irukkinṟārē** – I don’t see any space for bhagavān who is said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat 6.5.6 “*ātmā vā arē draśtavya*: *śrōtavya: mantavyō*: ***nididyāsitavya***:” (ātmā (here the word ātmā refers to paramātmā, the supreme being) is apt to be heard, to be thought of and to be meditated upon; it is apt to be seen).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.3. Midodi

*mīdōdi vāḷ eyiṟu minnilaga mun vilagum uruvināḷaikādōdu kodi mūkku anṟu udan aṟutta kaittalattā! enṟu ninṟutādōdu vaṇḍalambum taṇ sēṟai emperumān tāḷai ēttipōdōdu punal tūvum puṇṇiyarē viṇṇavaril poliginṟārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mīdu ōdi – growing vertically; vāḷ – having radiance; eyiṟu – tooth; min ilaga – as it shines like lightning; mun – in front, from there (being unable to stand); vilagum – to move away; uruvināḷai – sūrpaṇakā, who is having (scary) form; kādōdu – with her ear; kodi mūkku – nose, which looks like a creeper; anṟu – during rāmāvatāram; udan – at once; aṟutta – severed; kaittalattā – oh, one who is having divine hands!; enṟu – in this manner; ninṟu – remaining firm; tādōdu – along with flower buds; vaṇḍu – beetles; alambum – humming; taṇ sēṟai emperumān – bhagavān who is present in cool tiruccēṟai; tāḷai – divine feet; ētti – praising; pōdōdu – along with flowers; punal – water; tūvum – proffering; puṇṇiyar – fortunate people; viṇṇavaril – more than nityasūris; poliginṟār – more opulent

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Saying “Oh one who is having divine hands which at once severed the ear and creeper like nose of sūrpaṇakā, who is having a form where her tooth is growing vertically upwards and is radiantly shining like lightning and from whom one has to move away instead of standing in front of her!” and remaining firm, the fortunate ones praise the divine feet of bhagavān who is present in the cool tiruccēṟai where beetles, which are having flower buds on them are humming, and proffer flowers and water. They are more opulent than nityasūris.

**mīdōdi …** – Her radiant teeth which are rising vertically and shining.

**min ilaga** – shining like lightning

**mun vilagum …** – Just as one cannot stare at lightning, she is having a form which will scare everyone.

Alternative explanation.

**mīdu …** – As the risen teeth are shining like lightning.

**mun vilagum …** – The form which is roaming around in front.

**kādōdu kodi mūkku …** – Oh, one who severed the limbs which were presented as those of pirātti’s! It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 34.14 “*rāmasya dakśiṇō bāhu:*” (lakśmaṇa is the right hand of śrī rāma).

**tādōdi …** – Praising the divine feet of the one who is mercifully present in tiruccēṟai where beetles which are having flower buds drank the honey and are humming.

**pōdōdu punal tūvum puṇṇiyarē** – Those who are greatly fortunate to worship bhagavān with flowers and water. They are more opulent than nityasūris who worship bhagavān as said in [tiruviruttam 21](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/01/thiruviruththam-21/) “*sūttu nanmālaigaḷ tūyana ēndi*” (Holding the best garlands which are pure). Those who worship bhagavān being in paramapadam cannot be a match for those who worship him being here in samsāram itself.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.4. Teralum

*tērāḷum vāḷ arakkan ten ilangai venjamattup ponṟi vīḻapōrāḷum silai adanāl poru kaṇaigaḷ pōkkuvittāy enṟu nāḷumtārāḷum varai mārban taṇ sēṟai emperumān umbar āḷumpērāḷan pērōdum periyōrai oru kālum pirigilēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēr āḷum – one who can conduct chariot; vāḷ – having sword, the weapon; arakkan – rāvaṇāsura’s; then ilangai – best lankā; vem samattu – in the cruel battle; ponṟi vīḻa – to break down and be destroyed; pōr āḷum – which can conduct the battle; silaiyadanāl – with bow; poru – fighting; kaṇaigaḷ – arrows (which can work on their own); pōkku vittāy – oh, one who launched!; enṟu – saying in this manner; tār āḷum – having tiruttuḻāy garland; varai mārvan – having mountain like divine chest; umbar āḷum – protecting the higher worlds; pērāḷan – having greatness (one who is greater than all); taṇ sēṟai emperumān – the lord who is mercifully residing in tiruccēṟai; pēr – divine names; ōdum – singing; periyōrai – mahātmās \[eminent entities\]; oru kālum – even for a moment; pirigilēn – will not separate

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I will not separate even for a moment from the mahātmās who are praising bhagavān saying “Oh, one who launched fighting arrows with the bow which can conduct the battle to break down and destroy the best lankā of rāvaṇāsura who can conduct a chariot and is having the weapon sword!” and singing the divine names of the lord who is having tiruttuḻāy garland and mountain like divine chest, and the greatness of protecting the higher worlds.

**tēr āḷum …** – Since there are countless members in elephant, horse and soldier groups, only the chariots are counted.

**vāḷ arakkan …** – Even those are not necessary. The sword rāvaṇa has in his hand is sufficient to take care of the enemies.

**then ilangai …** – In the battle, bhagavān broke the town which was difficult to enter for dēvatās.

**pōrāḷum …** – With the bow which conducts the battle

**poru kaṇaigaḷ pōkkuvittāy …** – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam ślōkam 46-22 “*dīpta pāvaka sangkāśai*: *śitai: kāncanabhūśaṇai*: l *na tvāmiccāmyaham draśtum rāmēṇa nihatam śarai*: ll” (I do not wish to see you killed by śrī rāma whose arrows are like burning fire, sharp and decorated with gold), he conducted the arrows, which appear like arrows while launching, but while entering the bodies of the enemies, will appear like fire. Oh one who conducted such arrows! – saying in this manner.

**tār āḷum …** – As said in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 59](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/munram-thiruvandhadhi-59/) “*tāḻum aruvi pōl tār kidappaccūḻum*” (pirātti will surround emperumān’s garland which is hanging off his shoulders like two streams coming down from a mountain), he is wearing a distinguished garland to identify that he is the protector of this world.

**taṇ sēṟai …** – One who is having the apt abode to protect others.

**umbar …** – One who is superior to all and who conducts the higher worlds.

**pērōdum …** – There are mahātmās who have the nature of being unable to sustain themselves without reciting his divine names. Even he himself identifies them as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.13](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-13/) “*mahātmāna:*” (jñānis, the great souls) – they have such fame.

**oru kālum pirigilēnē** – I am unable to separate from them even if I am told “If you separate from them for a moment, you can enjoy them forever”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.5. Vandikkum

*vandikkum maṟṟavarkkum māsudambil vallamaṇar tamakkum allēnmundic cenṟu ari uruvāy iraṇiyanai muraṇ aḻitta mudalvarkkallālsandappū malarc cōlait taṇ sēṟai emperumān tāḷai nāḷumsindippārkku en uḷḷam tēnūṟi eppoḻudum tittikkumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ari uruvāy – being in narasimha form; mundi – in front; senṟu – went; iraṇiyanai – hiraṇyāsuran’s; muraṇ – strength; aḻitta – destroyed; mudalvaṟku allāl – other than the jagat kāraṇa bhūta (cause of the universe); val – debating forcefully; udambil – on the body; māsu – having dirt; amaṇar tamakkum – for jainas; vandikkum – vorśipping their dēvatās; maṟṟavarkkum – bauddas who are different from jainas; allēn – I cannot be together; sandap pū – sandalwood flowers; malar – blossoming; sōlai – surrounded by orchards; taṇ sēṟai emperumān tāḷai – divine feet of bhagavān who is mercifully residing in cool tiruccēṟai; nāḷum – daily; sindippārkku – on the matters of those who meditate; en uḷḷam – my heart; tēn ūṟi – drenched in honey (honey is flooding); eppoḻudum – always; tittikkum – remains sweet

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Other than being together with bhagavān who went as narasimha in front of hiraṇyāsura and destroyed his strength; other than such bhagavān who is the cause of the universe, I will not be together with jainas who forcefully debate and who have dirty bodies, and bauddas who worship their dēvatās and are different from jainas; My heart will be drenched in honey which always remain sweet for those who daily meditate upon the divine feet of bhagavān who is mercifully residing in cool tiruccēṟai which is surrounded by orchards which have blossoming sandalwood flowers.

**vandikkum …** – It appears that even bauddas will say “*vandē*” (I worship).

**māsudambil …** – I will not be together with amaṇas (jainas) who consider that it is to be righteous to avoid eliminating dirt from the body.

**mundi …** – He went in front while the child (prahlādāḻvān) vowed and eliminated hiraṇya’s strength. Other than sarvēśvaran who is the jagat kāraṇa bhūtan who incarnated as narasimha, I will not be together with bāhyas (those who reject vēdam) and kudruśtis (those who misinterpret vēdam).

**sanda …** – When asked “How did you know this?” āḻvār responds – as soon as I hear about śrīvaiṣṇavas, it is pleasant for my heart. In such a case, should I not remain ananyārha (not existing for others) for him? For those who have taste towards bāhyas and kudruśtis, will taste towards bhāgavatas occur?

**sandap pū …** – For those who blissfully meditate upon the divine feet of the leader of the rejuvenating tiruccēṟai which is having orchards which have sandalwood flowers, my heart is drenched in honey and is always sweet. Did this happen just like that?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.6. Pandu enamay

*paṇḍu ēnamāy ulagai anṟu idanda paṇbāḷā enṟu ninṟutoṇḍānēn tiruvadiyē tuṇai allāl tuṇaiyilēn solluginṟēnvaṇḍēndum malarp puṟavil vaṇ sēṟai emperumān adiyār tammaikkaṇḍēnukku idu kāṇīr en nenjum kaṇṇiṇaiyum kaḷikkumāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇḍu – previously; ēnamāy – being mahā varāha (great, wild boar); anṟu – then; ulagai – world, which got attached with the wall of the oval shaped universe; idanda – who dug out; paṇbāḷā – Oh, easily approachable one!; enṟu ninṟu – saying with a firm mind; toṇḍu ānēn – became a servitor (for your highness); tiruvadiyē – (your highness’) divine feet; tuṇai – protection (for me); allāl – other than that; tuṇai ilēn – I am not having anything as my protection; solluginṟēn – I am firmly saying this; vaṇḍu – beetles; ēndum – holding; malar – having flowers; puṟavil – having surroundings; vaṇ – beautiful; sēṟai emperumān – bhagavān residing in tiruccēṟai divyadēśam; adiyār tammai – devotees; kaṇḍēnukku – for me who has seen; idu – in this manner; kaṇ iṇaiyum – pair of eyes; en nenjum – my heart; kaḷikkum āṟu – the way they are rejoicing; kāṇīr – you see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Saying “Oh, easily approachable one, who dug out the world which got attached with the wall of the oval shaped universe, being in the form of mahāvarāha, previously!”, I have become your servitor. I am not having anything other than your divine feet as my protection. I am firmly saying this. You see the way my pair of eyes and my heart are rejoicing in this manner, after having seen the devotees of bhagavān residing in the beautiful tiruccēṟai divyadēśam which is having surroundings having flowers holding beetles.

**paṇḍu ēnamāy …** – Continuously saying “In the past, during the beginning of varāha kalpa \[one day of brahmā is known as kalpa\], being mahāvarāha, bhagavān dug out the earth from the wall of the oval shaped universe. Oh, one who has the simplicity to do that!”, being defeated by that simplicity, I became the servitor for your highness’ divine feet.

**tiruvadiyē tuṇai** – Only your highness’ divine feet are my refuge. I have no other refuge.

**solluginṟēn** – I can vow on that.

How are you firmly saying like this?

**vaṇḍu ēndum …** – As soon as I see the devotees of bhagavān who is mercifully residing in the beautiful tiruccēṟai divyadēśam which is having surroundings which have flowers which always have beetles on them, you see how my heart and pair of eyes are rejoicing. In such a case, do I have any shortcoming?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
