## 7.4.7. Paiviriyum

*paiviriyum variyaravil padukadaluḷ tuyilamarnda paṇbā! enṟummaiviriyum maṇi varai pōl māyavanē! enṟenṟum vaṇḍār neelamseyviriyum taṇ sēṟai emperumān tiruvadiyaic cindittēṟku enaiyaṟivum koṇḍānukku āḷānārkku āḷām en anbu tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pai – hoods; viriyum – expanded; vari – having moles; aravil – on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa); padu – where ratnams (precious gems) manifest; kadaluḷ – in tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi); tuyil amarnda – mercifully reclining; paṇbā – Oh, easily approachable one!; enṟum – saying in this manner; mai viriyum – darkness is spreading; maṇi varai pōl – having divine form which resembles a mountain filled with dark gem; māyavanē – Oh, amazing one!; enṟum – saying in this manner; enṟu – in this manner, repeatedly saying; vaṇḍu – beetles; Ar – filled; neelam – karu neydal flowers (blue water lily); sey – in fertile fields; viriyum – blossoming; taṇ sēṟai emperumān tiruvadiyai – the divine feet of bhagavān who is present in the cool tiruccēṟai divyadēśam; sindittēṟku – I, who am meditating upon; en – my; ai aṟivum – five types of knowledge which are present in five sense organs; koṇḍānukku – for the one who made them to be in his matter; en anbu – my love/affection; āḷ āgum – will be subservient; āḷ ānārkku – for the bhāgavatas who are servitors

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I am repeatedly saying “Oh, easily approachable one, who is mercifully reclining on tiruvanantāḻvān who is having expanded hoods and moles, in tiruppāṟkadal where precious gems manifest!”, “Oh, amazing one, who is having divine form which resembles a mountain filled with dark gem and which is spreading darkness!”. I am meditating upon the divine feet of bhagavān who is present in the cool tiruccēṟai divyadēśam where blue water lily flowers in fertile fields which are filled with beetles, are blossoming. bhagavān made my five types of knowledge which are present in five sense organs to be engaged in his matter. My love/affection will be subservient for the bhāgavatas who are servitors for such bhagavān.

**paiviriyum …** – pai – paṇam – hood. Due to permanent enjoyment of bhagavān, tiruvanantāḻvān has expanded hoods always, has beautiful stripes which make him look beautiful for bhagavān who cannot take his eyes off ādiśēśa and having qualities such as coolness, fragrance and tenderness.

**padu kadaluḷ …** – The ocean where gems manifest; deep ocean.

**tuyil amarnda paṇbā enṟum** – Saying – Oh, one who is having easy approacability to mercifully recline and cannot be woken up even if someone launches arrows at him!

**maiviriyum …** – Saying – Oh amazing one who is having a form which is like a dark mountain spreading darkness!

**vaṇḍār …** – karu neydal flowers which have beetles on them, in the fertile fields, are blossomed everywhere.

**taṇ sēṟai emperumān** – For me who enjoyed the best physical beauty of our lord in the rejuvenating tiruccēṟai.

**en ai aṟivum koṇḍānukku** – All the knowledge known through the sense organs starting with ears, were made to target him. That is, he became the target of the senses. I am not stopping with being the servant for bhagavān who accepted all of my senses. My affection is flowing towards those who become his servitors.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.8. Unnadu

*uṇṇādu vengūṟṟam ōvāda pāvangaḷ sērā mēlaiviṇṇōrum maṇṇōrum vandiṟainjum mendaḷir pōl adiyinānaippaṇṇāra vaṇḍu iyambum paimboḻil sūḻ taṇ sēṟai ammān tannaikkaṇṇārak kaṇḍurugi kaiyārat toḻuvāraik karudungālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mēlai – atop the prakruti maṇḍalam (samsāram, material realm); viṇṇōrum – nityasūris who are residents of paramapadam; maṇṇōrum – those who are residing in this leelā vibhūti which includes earth too; vandu – reached; iṟainjum – to surrender; mel – tender; taḷirpōl – like sprout; adiyinānai – one who is having divine feet; paṇ Ara – to have the songs in harmony; vaṇḍu – beetles; iyambum – singing; pai poḻil – by the vast orchards; sūḻ – pervaded; taṇsēṟai ammān tannai – the lord who is mercifully residing in the cool tiruccēṟai; kaṇ Ara – to fill the eyes; kaṇḍu – worship; urugi – with the heart melting; kai Ara – to fill the hands (to eliminate the shortcoming in the hands); toḻuvārai – bhāgavatas, who worship; karudungāl – meditating; vem – having cruel acts; kūṟṟam – the dēvatā, yama; uṇṇādu – without consuming (without tormenting and destroying); ōvāda – continuously tormenting; pāvangaḷ – sins; sērā – will not come close (to make us reap the results)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

To have the nityasūris who are residents of paramapadam which is atop the prakruti maṇḍalam and those who are residing in this leelā vibhūti which includes earth too, reach and surrender, bhagavān is having divine feet, which are like tender sprout; the lord is mercifully residing in the cool tiruccēṟai, which is pervaded by vast orchards where beetles are singing to have the songs in harmony; vorśipping to the content of their eyes, having their heart melting, those bhāgavatas worship such tiruccēṟai emperumān; cruel yama, the dēvatā, will not consume those who meditate upon such bhāgavatas; the sins which continuously torment, will not come close to them.

**uṇṇādu …** – As one thinks about bhāgavatas with one’s heart, the fear from mrutyu (yama) will go; it is saying that one need not fear for the fear caused by sins.

**uṇṇādu vem kūṟṟam …** – mrutyu who performs cruel acts, will fear to swallow such people even if they fall into its mouth.

**ōvāda pāvangaḷ sērā** – The sins which continuously tormented, will not come close to make one reap the result. What is the reason for these sins not approaching? They have so much affection towards those who enjoy sarvēśvaran who is ubhaya vibhūti nātan \[lord of both nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti\], with all of their faculties. One who is having tender, divine feet which are surrendered to by everyone from ubhaya vibhūti (both material and spiritual realm).

**paṇ Ara …** – The lord of cool tiruccēṟai which is having vast orchard where beetles are humming to be in harmony with the song; seeing him to the eyes’ content, praying due to that affection. iṟainji (praying) is also said to be urugi (melting). While thinking about those who worship to the hands’ content, they will not be consumed by yama and their continuous sins will not come close.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.9. Kallatten

*kaḷḷattēn poyyagattēn ādalāl pōdorugāl kavalai ennumveḷḷattēṟku en kolō? viḷai vayaluḷ karu neelam kaḷainjñar tāḷāltaḷḷat tēn maṇa nāṟum taṇ sēṟai emperumān tāḷai nāḷumuḷḷattē vaippārukku idu kāṇīr en uḷḷam urugumāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viḷai – having crops; vayaluḷ – (grown) in the fertile fields; karu neelam – karu neydal (blue lily) flower; kaḷaijñar – farmers who pluck out the weeds; tāḷāl – with their feet; taḷḷa – as they push away; tēn – honey (which flows from them), its; maṇam nāṟum – fragrance is emanating; taṇsēṟai emperumān tāḷai – the divine feet of bhagavān who is mercifully residing in the cool tiruccēṟai divyadēśam; nāḷum – daily; uḷḷattē – in the heart; vaippārukku – on those bhāgavatas who keep and meditate; en uḷḷam – my heart; urugumāṟu – the way it is breaking down (due to affection); kāṇīr – see; idu – this great benefit; kaḷḷattēn – I, who am a thief who has stolen the ātmā; poy agattēn ādalāl – due to having deceitful heart; pōdu oru kāl – every fraction of a moment (continuously); kavalai ennum – sorrow; veḷḷattēṟku – for me, who is drowned in the great ocean; enkolō – How did I get this? I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is asking “How did I get this great benefit?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is mercifully residing in the cool tiruccēṟai divyadēśam where the fragrance is emanating from the blue lily flowers which are pushed away by the farmers who are plucking out the weeds from the fertile fields which are having crops. See the way my heart is breaking down due to affection towards the bhāgavatas who keep such bhagavān’s divine feet and meditate upon them daily. How did I, who am a thief who has stolen the ātmā \[from bhagavān, claiming it to be owned by me\], who is having deceitful heart and who is always drowned in the great ocean of sorrow, every fraction of a moment, get this great benefit? I don’t know.

**kaḷḷattēn ….** – As said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 42-35 “*yō’nyatā santamātmānam anyatā pratipadyatē* l *kim tēna na krutam pāpam* ***cōrēṇātmāpahāriṇā*** ll” (What sin has not been committed by one who covets ātmā thinking that it belongs to him, while it is the possession of bhagavān?), I have stolen the ātmā since time immemorial. Even that, as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.1.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/05/thiruvaimozhi-5-1-3-ullana-marrulavay/) “*unnaiyum vanjikkum*” (bewilder even you, who are a sarvajña), I concealed that even from my antarātmā (in-dwelling supersoul, you), thinking that he will know if I did not conceal it. Due to doing this, I became drowned in the ocean of forgetfulness, continuously. It is also said as “ocean of sorrow”.

**en kolō** – For such me, how did this benefit come about! How did I get this benefit which is attained by those who surrender oneself to bhagavān, have true love towards him and who always meditate upon him!

**viḷai vayal …** – The blue lily flower which grew as weeds in the fertile fields were pushed away by the farmers. Due to that movement, the honey which was filled in those flowers came out flooding and the place is filled with its fragrance, in the cool tiruccēṟai. For those who always keep that bhagavān’s divine feet in their heart, see how my heart is breaking down; how did I get this benefit!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.10. Puman ser

*pūmāṇ sēr karunguḻalār pōl nadandu vayal ninṟa pedaiyōdu annamtēmāvin inniḻalil kaṇ tuyilum taṇ sēṟai ammān tannaivāmān tēr parakālan kali kanṟi oli mālai koṇḍu toṇḍīr!tūmāṇ sēr ponnadi mēl sūttumin num tuṇaik kaiyāl toḻudu ninṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annam – swan; pū – present in the flower; māṇ – beauty; sēr – present with; karum kuḻalārpōl – like the women who are having dark hair; vayal ninṟa – roaming around in the fertile fields; pedaiyōdum – with the spouse; nadandu – roamed (and then); tēmāvin – mango tree’s; in niḻalil – in the cool shadow; kaṇ tuyilum – sleeping; taṇ sēṟai ammān tannai – on the bhagavān who is mercifully residing in cool tiruccēṟai; vā – coming (fast); mā – where the horses are tied; tēr – having chariot; parakālan – one who defeats enemies; kalikanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; oli – mercifully spoke; mālai – these ten pāsurams which are in the form of a garland; koṇḍu – earning (meditating); toṇḍīr – oh devotees!; tū – pure; māṇ sēr – having beauty; pon – desirable; adi mēl – on bhagavān’s divine feet; num – your; tuṇai kaiyāl – with the hands which are together (in anjali posture); toḻudu ninṟu – being surrendered; sūttumin – decorate \[this garland on his divine feet\]

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is mercifully residing in cool tiruccēṟai where male swan is roaming around along with its spouse, in the fertile fields which appear like the dark hair of women which are decorated with beautiful flowers and then is sleeping under the cool shadow of the mango tree. On such bhagavān, tirumangai āḻvār who defeats the enemies with a chariot tied with horses which are running, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams which are in the form of a garland. Oh devotees! Meditating upon these ten pāsurams, on his pure, beautiful, desirable divine feet, you decorate those divine feet with these pāsurams, performing anjali (joined palms) with your hands and worship him.

**pū māṇ sēr …** – Swans which are in the fertile fields, desiring to walk like the women who are having dark hair which is having beauty acquired by wearing flowers, thinking that if they walk alone they will not get to walk like that, roaming around along with their spouses. Since they could still not walk like those women, they become shy and take shelter of the cool shadow of the mango trees and sleep there.

**vāmān tēr …** – Conducting the chariot with accelerating horses similar to how kriṣṇa conducted arjuna’s chariot and destroyed the enemies, āḻvār too destroys the enemies. Oh devotees who are having taste towards bhagavān! Decorate the divine feet which are opposite to all defects and are desirable, with the tamiḻ garland made of these pāsurams which were mercifully composed with tune by āḻvār. While doing that, you worship with your hands in anjali (joined palms) posture and proffer the garland.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.5 Tandai kalil

## 7.5.1. Tandai kalil

*tandai kālil peruvilangu tāḷ aviḻa naḷḷirutkaṇvanda endai perumānār maruvi ninṟa ūr pōlummundi vānam maḻai poḻiyum mūvāvuruvin maṟaiyāḷarandi mūnṟum anal ōmbum aṇiyār vīdi aḻundūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānam – cloud; mundi – (even) before (the yajña, as its result); maḻai poḻiyum – to pour down as rain; mūvā – having youthfulness which has no old-age symptoms; uruvil – having form; maṟaiyāḷar – best among brāhmaṇas who can conduct vēdam; andi mūnṟum – at three meeting points every day \[dawn, mid-day and dusk\]; anal – in fire; ōmbum – performing hōmam; aṇi Ar – very beautiful; vīdi – having streets; aḻundūr – the divyadēśam named tiruvaḻundūr; tandai – vasudēva, the father, his; kālil – around the feet; peru vilangu – the shackles which were placed for a long time, its; tāḷ – lock; aviḻa – to unlock on its own; naḷ – dense; iruḷ kaṇ – in the darkness; vanda – one who mercifully arrived from kśīrābdi (milk ocean) and incarnated; endai – for me, my father and my clan; perumānār – being the lord; maruvi – desirously; ninṟa – eternally residing; Ur pōlum – is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divyadēśam named tiruvaḻundūr is having best among brāhmaṇas who are having youthful form which has no mix of old-age, who can conduct vēdam and perform hōmam using fire at three meeting points every day, viz dawn, mid-day and dusk, to make the cloud pour down as rain, even before such yajñas. It is having very beautiful streets. This is the eternal abode where the one, who mercifully arrived from kśīrābdi (milk ocean) and incarnated in the dense darkness to make the lock of the shackles which were placed for a long time, around the feet of his father, vasudēva, unlock on its own. He is the lord for me, my father and my clan. Such kriṣṇa’s abode is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam.

**tandai kāl …** – He is having the nature of coming and helping during dangerous times and eliminating that danger. The shackles on śrī vasudēva’s feet had been there for the duration of eight pregnancies (of dēvakip pirātti). He made that go away on its own. He was able to carry kriṣṇa up to tiruvāyppādi (śrī gōkulam).

**naḷ iruḷ kaṇ …** – The lord of my clan who came in the dense darkness and incarnated, to be invisible for those who have been placed as guards by kamsa.

**vanda** – Not just for śrī vasudēva, he came and helped us too.

**maruvi ninṟa** … – Unlike that incarnation in which he left for paramapadam at some point, this abode tiruvaḻundūr is where he is eternally residing to help those who are like śrī vasudēva. The abode where he is present is our goal. āḻvār is telling with great desire that since bhagavān, who is our goal, has arrived here and is residing, this is similar to the ultimate destination, which is paramapadam. This is the same meaning for all of the other pāsurams in this decad.

**mundi vānam …** – The cloud will first pour down the rain. Even before the intent of the brāhmaṇas, the side effects, will happen first.

**mūvā uruvil maṟaiyāḷar** – All of the brāhmaṇas in this abode are youthful agnihōtris. These are the people who get upanayana samskāram etc at the apt ages mentioned in śāstram, and will perform yāgams etc at the apt times.

**andi mūnṟum anal ōmbum …** – They are not performing these activities with the expectation of results; there is no \[specific\] result for nitya anuśtānams (daily mandatory routines); hence this is what is seen in the abode where the streets are beautiful.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.5.2. Parittelunda

*pāritteḻunda padai mannar tammai māḷap pāradattuttēril pāganāy ūrnda dēva dēvan ūr pōlumneeril paṇaitta neduvāḷaikku anjip pōna kuruginangaḷāral kavuḷōdu arugaṇaiyum aṇiyār vayal sūḻ aḻundūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

neeril – in water; paṇaitta – playing joyfully due to overwhelming joy; nedu – huge; vāḷaikku – for the scabbard fish; anji – scared; pōna – ran away; kurugu inangaḷ – the flock of birds named kurugu (crane); Aral – small fish named Aral \[sand-eel\]; kavuḷōdu – holding in the cheek; arugu – (then) in the proximity of the big fish; aṇaiyum – arrived; aṇi Ar – very beautiful; vayal sūḻ – surrounded by fertile fields; aḻundūr – the divyadēśam named tiruvaḻundūr is; pārittu – being eager (to defeat kriṣṇa); eḻunda – came forward; padai – having weapons; mannar tammai – kings such as duryōdana et al; māḷa – to destroy; bāradattu – in mahābhārata battle; tēril – on the chariot (which belongs to arjuna); pāganāy – remaining as the sāraty (kriṣṇa, the charioteer); ūrnda – one who conducted the chariot; dēva dēvan – sarvēśvaran who is the lord of nityasūris, his; Ur pōlum – eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divyadēśam named tiruvaḻundūr is surrounded by beautiful fertile fields where the cranes became scared and ran away seeing the big scabbard fish which is playing and jumping around in the water due to overwhelming joy, and subsequently held the small fish, sand-eel inside their cheeks and came close to the big fish too. sarvēśvaran, who is the lord of nityasūris, became the charioteer for arjuna and conducted the chariot in mahābhārata battle to destroy kings such as duryōdana et al who had come forward eagerly to defeat kriṣṇa. Such kriṣṇa’s abode is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam.

**pārittu …** – They gathered together and came saying “We will capture sāraty today”. These are the same ones who tried to capture him by placing a fake throne, when he went to their place without any weapons.

**padai mannar tammai māḷa** – The kings who have weapons, came holding their weapons in their hands and got killed and were lying at the chariot wheel.

**tammai māḷa** – He gave them that which they were seeking \[they were seeking to kill him and he killed them\].

**tēril pāganāy ūrnda** – If he conducted the chariot as the rati (owner of the chariot), the victory will belong to him. But his intent is – enemies should be destroyed and arjuna should be victorious – hence he remained as the charioteer and conducted the chariot. There was a devotee, who would recite the text while kūrattāḻvān gives kālakśēpam (explanations in a line by line manner), who wanted to learn a particular text from him. But he did not want others to know that he was learning the meanings from āḻvān. āḻvān agreed and was teaching him. He was having the book in his hands and reading the text and āḻvān was teaching him in the western side of śrīrangam in seclusion. At that time, a king arrived there. āḻvān quickly took the manuscripts from that devotee and held it in his hands, pretending that he is learning from that devotee. \[Here āḻvān wanted that devotee to learn, but pretended as if he is learning from that devotee. This is similar to how kriṣṇa helped arjuna become victorious\]

**dēva dēvan Ur pōlum** – What did bhagavān think about himself? He, who is the lord of those who are untouched by the smell of samsāram, made himself subservient to one among the samsāris (materialistic persons)!

**neeril paṇaitta nedu vāḷaikku anjippōna kuruginangaḷ** – The cranes gather in flocks and arrive at the water-bodies/fertile-fields to catch fish which can be held in their mouth. While having such small sand-eel fish inside the cheeks, the cranes will see the big scabbard fish which is joyfully jumping up and down, and think that “it is our food” and come closer. Seeing the large size of the fish, they will fly away with fear due to not knowing “this is in water, it cannot fly” \[it flies away thinking that the jumping fish may catch it\]. But subsequently, it will come back to catch the big fish again.

**aṇiyār vayal sūḻ aḻundūrē** – The cranes went through similar emotions as seen in the mahābhārata war. bhīśma et al, who are great warriors who were thinking “We are famous for our bravery and are known as ‘atirata’, ‘mahārata’ et al. Now we cannot be cowardly for battle” and approached sāraty and then moved away thinking “We cannot be crushed by the wheels of his chariot”.

## 7.5.3. Sembon madil

*sembon madiḷ sūḻ tennilangaikku iṟaivan sirangaḷ aiyiraṇḍumumbar vāḷikku ilakkāga udirtta uravōn ūr pōlumkombil ārnda mādavi mēl kōdi mēynda vaṇḍinangaḷambarāvum kaṇmadavār aimbālaṇaiyum aḻundūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kombil – by the branches; ārnda – filled; mādavi mēl – on the kurukkatti (mādavi) tree; kōdi – pecking with the beak; mēynda – searching for prey; vaṇḍu inangaḷ – swarms of beetles; ambu arāvum – like an arrow which torments (dear ones); kaṇ – having eyes; madavār – women’s; aimbāl – hairs which have five qualities; aṇaiyum – reaching; aḻundūr – the divyadēśam named tiruvaḻundūr; sembon – beautiful like reddish gold; madiḷ sūḻ – surrounded by forts; then – beautiful; ilangaikku – for the city, lankā; iṟaivan – rāvaṇa, who is the lord; ai iraṇḍu sirangaḷaiyum – ten heads; umbar vāḷikku – for brahmāstram; ilakkāga – made as the target; udirtta – severed and made to fall; uravōn – strong cakravartit tirumangan’s; Ur pōlum – is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divyadēśam named tiruvaḻundūr where swarms of beetles which are searching for prey by pecking with the beak on the kurukkatti (mādavi) tree which is filled with branches, are reaching the hairs of women who are having eyes which are like an arrow which torments (dear ones) and have five qualities (like fragrance, honey, softness, density and darkness). Strong cakravartit tirumagan (son of emperor daśarata) made the ten heads of rāvaṇa, who is the lord of the beautiful lankā which is surrounded beautiful reddish gold like forts, as the target for his brahmāstram, severed and made them fall on the ground. Such śrī rāma’s abode is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam.

**sembon …** – The ten heads of rāvaṇa, who was proud thinking “We are in a fortified town. āren’t we the leader of this town?” were knocked down using brahmāstram by the strong cakravartit tirumagan. Such śrī rāma’s abode, tiruvaḻundūr, is as desirable as paramapadam. He severed the evil rāvaṇa’s heads, which were unable to be destroyed by the vajrāyudam etc of indra et al, just with his strength as a human,

**kombil ārnda …** – On the kurukkatti (mādavi) tree which has abundant branches.

**kōdi mēynda vaṇḍinangaḷ** – With its strength, the beetles pecked the sprouts and flowers, and consumed the honey from them.

They thought “We should go to some place else which is darker than those sprouts and flowers, and rest there in the night” and

**ambarāvum …** – They will reach the hair of women who are having eyes which will weaken (defeat) arrows \[in sharpness\] and are having noble qualities. aimbāl – five qualities of hairs.

## 7.5.4. Vellattul

*veḷḷattuḷ ōr ālilai mēl mēvi adiyēn manam pugundu enuḷḷattuḷḷum kaṇṇuḷḷum ninṟār ninṟa ūr pōlumpuḷḷup piḷḷaikku irai tēdip pōna kādal pedaiyōdumaḷḷal seṟuvil kayal nādum aṇiyār vayal sūḻ aḻundūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kādal – having great love; pedaiyōdum – along with the female bird; piḷḷaikku – for its little one; irai tēdi – analysing the food; pōna – going; puḷḷu – bird; aḷḷal – having mud; seṟuvil – in the fertile fields; kayal – fish; nādum – searching; aṇi Ar vayal sūḻ aḻundūr – tiruvaḻundūr, which is surrounded by very beautiful fertile fields; veḷḷattuḷ – in the ocean of deluge; ōr – a; ālilai mēl – on banyan leaf; mēvi – remaining fixed (and then); adiyēn – I, the servitor, my; manam – in the heart; pugundu – entered; en uḷḷattuḷḷum – in my heart; kaṇṇuḷḷum – in my eyes (being the target); ninṟār – (always) being mercifully present; ninṟa – eternally residing; Ur pōlum – is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The divyadēśam named tiruvaḻundūr, where the bird along with its loving female went searching for food for its little one, is searching for fish in the fertile fields which are having mud, and is surrounded by very beautiful fertile fields. In the ocean of deluge, bhagavān remained fixed on the banyan leaf and then entered the heart of me, his servitor, remained as the target of my heart and eyes, and is always mercifully residing. Such bhagavān’s eternal abode is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam.

**veḷattuḷ …** – Mercifully reclining on a freshly appeared banyan leaf on the ocean of deluge.

**adiyēn manam pugundu** – Causing worry as in “He is reclining on the deluge; there is no yaśōdāp pirātti to care for him there; what is going to happen?” As such talk occurred, he entered my heart having such talk as the reason, and then became the target of my eyes to eliminate the thought “He is enjoyable in my heart but not physically enjoyable through my eyes” and became the target of the heart too so that it does not go behind other things.

**ninṟa Ur pōlum** – This abode is like paramapadam where he is visible to the eyes of the residents there.

**puḷḷup piḷḷaikku …** – The bird which was going to find food for its little one, instead of going alone, went with its spouse which is to be identified by its love towards it.

**aḷḷal seṟuvil kayal nādum …** – The bird which will stay away from mud, will roam over such mud, due to the enjoyable nature there. This bird appeared to be similar to mahāvarāha bhagavān who entered the ocean of deluge for the sake of protecting the world.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.5.5. Pagalum iravum

*pagalum iravum tānēyāyp pārum viṇṇum tānēyāynigaril sudarāy iruḷāgi ninṟār ninṟa ūr pōlumtugilin kodiyum tērttugaḷum tunni mādar kūndal vāyagilin pugaiyāl mugil ēykkum aṇiyār vīdi aḻundūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tugilin – hoisted with clothes; tunni – present closely with each other; kodiyum – flags; tēr – while conducting the chariot; tugaḷum – dust (with all of these); mādar – women’s; kūndalvāy – on the hair (added for fragrance); agilin pugaiyāl – by the smoke from agil wood; mugil ēykkum – like cloud; aṇiyār vīdi aḻundūr – tiruvaḻundūr which is having very beautiful streets; pagalum – daytime; iravum – nighttime; tānēyāy – having as his vibhūti (wealth); pārum – earth; viṇṇum – sky; tānēyāy – being the one who is having as his vibhūti; nigar il – matchless; sudarāy – luminous objects; iruḷ – darkness; āgi – being the one who is having as his vibhūti; ninṟār – (always) being mercifully present; ninṟa – eternally residing; Ur pōlum – is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

agil wood was used to add fragrance to the women’s locks which are covered with dust from the riding of chariots which have closely hoisted flags having clothes. Smoke from the fragrant materials as well as dust from chariots creaste a cloud-like smoke on the beautiful streets of the divyadēśam, tiruvaḻundūr. bhagavān is having daytime and nighttime, earth and sky, matchless luminous objects and darkness as his wealth. Such bhagavān’s eternal abode of tiruvaḻundūr is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam.

**pagalum iravum …** – Having what are known as “daytime” and “nighttime” as his wealth.

**pārum viṇṇum tāneyāy** – Having earth and sky as his wealth.

**nigaril sudarāy iruḷāgi ninṟār** – Having darkness and light as his wealth, in this manner, bhagavān who is having the entire creation as his form, has arrived here to manifest his distinguished \[arcā\] form to be enjoyed by all. Such divyadēśam.

**tugilin kodi …** – Flag which is having densely tied clothes, the dust which rose due to the chariots coming into contact with each other, the people of the town will burn agil wood to add fragrance to the women’s hair; that appears like cloud and shows the rainy season. In the rainy season, wind, dust and clouds will all be present. In that, there was new wind created by the swaying of the flags. There was dust from the chariot wheels. The smoke which was created for the women’s hair appear like clouds. Thus, these three together made it look like rainy season in there always. Because of that, no one is able to enjoy the aspects which are specific for different seasons.

## 7.5.6. Edilangu tamarai

*ēdilangu tāmarai pōl sevvāy muṟuval seydaruḷimādu vandu en manam pugundu ninṟār ninṟā ūr pōlumnīdu mādat tanic cūlam pōḻak koṇḍal tuḷi tūvaādalaravattu ārppu ōvā aṇiyār vīdi aḻundūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīdu – tall; mādam – in the mansions; tani – unique; sūlam – peak; pōḻga – as it pierces (the stomach of the cloud); koṇḍal – (due to that) the cloud; tuḷi tūva – pouring rain drops; ādal – dancing women’s; aravattu – caused due to the excited actions; ārppu – great sound; ōvā – not stopping; aṇiyār vīdi aḻundūr – tiruvaḻundūr, which has very beautiful streets; ēdu ilangu – shining by the petals; tāmarai pōl – like a lotus flower; sevvāy – with reddish divine lips; muṟuval seydaruḷi – (first) smiling; mādu vandu – (then) coming close (to me); en manam – (further) in my heart; pugundu – entered; ninṟār – one who is mercifully present like an immovable object; ninṟa – eternally residing; Ur pōlum – is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is the abode which has very beautiful streets where the unique peak atop the tall mansion is piercing the cloud which makes the cloud pouring down rain droplets and the joyful actions of the dancing women causing great sound in a continuous manner. bhagavān first gently smiled with his reddish divine lips which are like a lotus flower shining due to its petals, then came close to me, and entered my heart and is mercifully present like an immovable object. Such bhagavān’s eternal abode of tiruvaḻundūr is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam.

**ēdilangu …** – Mercifully smiling like a shining lotus flower with shining petal. Smiling to show that the rare feat of acquiring me is for his benefit. By that, he caused me the state where I cannot avoid whatever he does, and then, he came close to me and stood, and as I was able to accept that, he entered my heart, and is standing to make us think “Now, there is no other place for him to go”. Such bhagavān is standing in the place to be seen by us with our external eyes.

**nīdu mādam …** – The peak atop the tall mansions, tear the bottom portion of the clouds and cause rain. With this, the tallness of the mansions is highlighted.

**ādal aravattārppōvā** – The tumultuous sound from the joyful reaction while the women are dancing, is continuously heard without a break.

**aṇiyār vīdi …** – The streets which are beautiful due to the continuous dancing sounds.

## 7.5.7. Malaip pugundu

*mālaip pugundu malaraṇai mēl vaigi adiyēn manam pugundu enneelak kaṇgaḷ pani malga ninṟār ninṟa ūr pōlumvēlaik kadal pōl nedu vīdi viṇ tōy sudai veṇmaṇi mādattuālaip pugaiyāl aḻal kadirai maṟaikkum vīdi aḻundūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēlai – having shore; kadal pōl – great, like an ocean; nedu – lengthy; vīdi – in the streets; viṇ – reaching the sky; tōy – spreading; sudai – due to applying limestone paint; veṇ – whitish; maṇi – covered with precious gemstones; mādattu – in the mansions; aḻal – hot; kadirai – (sun’s) rays; ālaip pugaiyāl – by the smoke emitted from the sugarcane factory; maṟaikkum – hiding; vīdi aḻundūr – tiruvaḻundūr, which is having streets; mālai – during the dusk; pugundu – entered; malar aṇai mēl – on the flower bed; vaigi – remaining; adiyēn – (then) in my; manam – heart; pugundu – entered (and then while the talk of separation came about); en – my; neelam – like karuneydal flower (blue Indian water-lily); kaṇgaḷ – from the eyes; pani – tears; malga – overflowing; ninṟār – (seeing that, being unable to leave) one who is mercifully present here; ninṟa – eternally residing; Ur pōlum – is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is the abode which has very beautiful streets which are lengthy and great like an ocean with shores; in those streets, mansions which are reaching up to the sky, which are whitish due to applying limestone paint and are covered with precious gemstones, are present. The sun’s hot rays atop those mansions are hidden by the smoke emitted from the sugarcane factory. During the dusk time, bhagavān entered that abode and remained on the flower bed. Then, he entered my heart and while talk of separation came about, I started crying and tears started overflowing from my karuneydal flower like eyes. Seeing that, he remained here, being unable to leave. Such bhagavān’s eternal abode of tiruvaḻundūr is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam.

**mālaip pugundu** … – Arrived at the time of enjoyment (dusk time), remaining in the flower bed and then left there.

**adiyēn manam pugundu** … – Entered my heart which exists exclusively for him, spoke about leaving, and then saw my teary eyes and suffering, remained here without leaving. The eternal abode of such bhagavān.

**vēlai …** – The greatness of the divine streets is similar to that of the ocean with shores.

**viṇ tōy sudai …** – Being tall, reaching up to svargam (heaven), having applied limestone paint and being whitish due to that, being covered with precious gemstones, the mansion has sun’s hot rays. Those rays along with the streets were covered by the smoke emitted from the sugarcane factory. With this, the closeness of the town and the fertile fields, is highlighted.

## 7.5.8. Vanji marungulidai

*vanji marungulidai nōva maṇandu ninṟa kanavagattu ennenju niṟaiyak kai kūppi ninṟār ninṟa ūr pōlumpanji anna melladi naṟpāvaimārgaḷ ādagattinanjilambin ārppu ōvā aṇiyār vīdi aḻundūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

panji anna – like cotton; mel adi – having tender feet; nal pāvaimārgaḷ – worn by distinguished women; ādagattin – made with gold; am silambin – the beautiful anklets’; ārppu – great sound; ōvā – heard continuously; aṇiyār vīdi aḻundūr – tiruvaḻundūr, which has very beautiful streets; vanji marungul – like a vanji creeper; idai – (my) waist region; nōva – to weaken; maṇandu ninṟa – remaining together (with me); kanavagattu – in the union which is like a dream; en nenju niṟaiya – completely, to have no shortcoming in my heart; kai kūppi – performing an anjali (to make me forgive his offenses); ninṟār – one who is mercifully present; ninṟa – eternally residing; Ur pōlum – is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is the abode which has very beautiful streets where the great sound of the beautiful gold anklets worn by distinguished women who are having cotton like tender feet, is heard continuously. bhagavān remains together with me, to have my vanji creeper like waist region weaken, in the union which is like a dream; he performed anjali to make me forgive his offenses and to have no shortcoming in my heart. Such bhagavān’s eternal abode of tiruvaḻundūr is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam.

**vanji …** – In the union which is like a dream, where he remained united with me to weaken my waist which is having the nature of a vanji creeper.

**en nenjam …** – He entered my heart completely to eliminate any dissatisfaction in my heart as in “I did not get to unite with him in this manner”.

**panji anna …** – The sound from the golden anklets of the women who are having feet which are tender like fresh cotton and are having natural femininity, is continuously present. Such divyadēśam.

## 7.5.9. En aimbulanum

*en aimbulanum eḻilum koṇḍu ingē nerunal eḻundaruḷipponnam kalaigaḷ meliveydap pōna punidar ūr pōlummannu mudunīr aravinda malar mēl varivaṇḍu isai pādaannam pedaiyōdu udanādum aṇiyār vayal sūḻ aḻundūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mannum – where fish etc are living in a dense manner; mudu nīr – present in the ancient pond; aravinda malar mēl – on lotus flower; vari vaṇḍu – beetles which are having stripes; isai pāda – as they are humming; annam – swan; pedaiyōdu udan – being together with its spouse; ādum – dancing; aṇiyār vīdi aḻundūr – tiruvaḻundūr, which has very beautiful streets; nerunal – yesterday; ingē – here, where I am present; eḻundaruḷi – mercifully came; en aimpulanum – knowledge acquired through my five senses; eḻilum – beauty; koṇḍu – abducted; pon – being desirable; am – beautiful; kalaigaḷ – (my) clothes; meliveyda – to loosen and slip away; pōna – one who left me; punidar – the pure one’s; Ur pōlum – is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is the abode which has very beautiful streets where fish etc are living in a dense manner, in the ancient pond where striped beetles are humming, and swan being together with its spouse, is dancing. Yesterday, he mercifully came here, where I am present, abducted the knowledge acquired by me through my five senses and my beauty, and made my desirable, beautiful clothes to loosen and slip away from me, and left me. Such pure bhagavān’s eternal abode of tiruvaḻundūr is eternally desirable as in the case of paramapadam.

**en aimbulanum …** – Abducting the greatness I acquired through my senses such as ear etc and my collective beauty, without my realisation, he mercifully arrived here and made my clothes loosen and slip away from my waist. He is such a pure person. Having abducted everything from me, he is having the purity of not losing any of his aspects. \[āḻvār is being sarcastic that while āḻvār is suffering, bhagavān remains normal as he is detached from everything\]. The abode of such bhagavān.

**mannu mudu nīr …** – The aquatic beings are remaining densely there.

**mudu nīr …** – On the lotus flowers which are present in the ancient ponds with the aged water, swarms of beetles, which are having desirable complexion, drank the honey and hummed as an outlet for their joy. Matching that song, the swan is dancing along with its spouse.

## 7.5.10. Nellil kuvalai

*nellil kuvaḷai kaṇ kātta neeril kumudam vāy kāttaallik kamalam mugam kāttum kaḻani aḻundūr ninṟānaivallip podumbil kuyil kūvum mangai vēndan parakālansollil polinda tamiḻ mālai sollap pāvam nillāvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nellil – grown in-between paddy crops; kuvaḷai – karuneydal (blue lily) flowers; kaṇ – (the women of the town, their) eyes; kātta – show; neeril – grown in water; kumudam – arakku (reddish) āmbal (water-lily) flowers; vāy kātta – show their mouth; alli – having petals; kamalam – lotus; mugam – face; kāttum – showing (shining like their face); kaḻani – having fertile fields; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; ninṟānai – on bhagavān who is mercifully present; valli – creepers’; podumbil – in the bushes; kuyil – cuckoo; kūvum – singing; mangai – for tirumangai; vēndan – being the king; parakālan – āḻvār who is like the deity of death for enemies, his; sollil – by good words; polinda – filled; tamiḻ – done in tamiḻ language; mālai – these ten pāsurams which look like a garland of words; solla – as one recite; pāvam – sins; nillā – will not stay (with them)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is having fertile fields where blue-lily flowers which are grown in-between the paddy crops show the eyes of the women of that town, red-lily flowers which are grown in water show their mouth and lotus flowers with petals show their face. Being the king of tirumangai where cuckoos are singing from the bushes of the creepers, āḻvār who is like the deity of death for enemies, composed ten pāsurams which are filled with good words, which are done in tamiḻ language and which look like a garland of words, on bhagavān who is mercifully present in tiruvaḻundūr. For those who recite these pāsurams, their sins will not stay with them.

**nellil …** – The kuvaḷai (blue-lily) flowers, which sprouted as weeds for paddy crops, show the eyes of the women of the town. The red-lily which sprouted in the water bodies, show their lips.

**allik kamalam …** – Lotus flowers, with many petals, show their face.

**kaḻani aḻundūr ninṟānai** – It will be difficult to differentiate between the fertile fields and the town.

**vallip podumbinil …** – In the bushes where flower-creepers are abundant, cuckoos will sing just like muktātmās sing sāma gānam. āḻvār, who is the king of the residents of such tirumangai, is the vanquiśer of enemies.

**sollil podinda …** – As one recites these tamiḻ garlands which are filled with words.

**pāvam nillāvē** – As one recites these pāsurams which are so enjoyable that even if they cause sins, one cannot avoid singing them, their sins will leave on their own.

## 7.6 Singamaday

## 7.6.1. Singamaday

*singamadāy avuṇan tiṟalāgam mun kīṇḍu ugandasangam idattānait taḻal āḻi valattānaic=sengamalattu ayan anaiyār tennaḻundaiyil manni ninṟaangamalak kaṇṇanai adiyēn kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

singamadāy – assuming the form of narasimha; avuṇan – hiraṇyāsuran’s; tiṟal – strong; āgam – body; mun – when prahlāda vowed; kīṇḍu – tore down; uganda – and having become joyful; sangam – śrī pāncajanyam; idattānai – having in his divine left hand; taḻal – shining; āḻi – śrī sudarśanam; valattānai – having in divine right hand; sem – beautiful; kamalattu – born in the lotus flower from the divine navel; ayan anaiyār – brāhmaṇas who are as good as brahmā (residing); then – beautiful; aḻundaiyil – in tiruvaḻundūr; manni – remaining fixed; ninṟa – one who is eternally residing; am kamalam – like a beautiful lotus flower; kaṇṇan tannai – one who is having divine eyes; adiyēn – I, who am an ananyārha śēśabhūta (exclusive servitor); kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

When prahlāda vowed, bhagavān assumed the form of narasimha and tore down the strong body of hiraṇyāsura and became joyful. He is having śrī pāncajanyam in his divine left hand and śrī sudarśanam in his divine right hand. He is remaining firmly in tiruvaḻundūr where brāhmaṇas, who are as good as brahmā who was born in the lotus flower from his divine navel, reside. He is having beautiful lotus like divine eyes. I, who am an exclusive servitor, got to see him.

**singamadāy …** – Assuming narasimha form; avuṇan – hiraṇyan. His strong body was tore down by bhagavān who came even before prahlāda completed his vow, and became joyful due to eliminating prahlāda’s enemy. bhagavān is the one who eliminates the enemy and also becomes joyful for that. If a small child drinks milk from mother’s bosoms, it is the mother who will be joyful for that.

**sangam idattānai …** – Though he had divine weapons in his hand, he did not know how to accomplish the task using that.

**sengamalam …** – sarvēśvaran, who is puṇḍarīkākśan (lotus-eyed), who is eternally residing in tiruvaḻundūr which is owned by brāhmaṇas, who are as capable as brahmā who could do creation.

**adiyēn kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē** – I, who don’t have the same birth as those who are residents of that town, and who don’t have the nature (bhakti) of śrī prahlādāḻvān, got to see him and enjoy him.

## 7.6.2. Kovanar madiya

*kōvānār madiyak kolaiyār maḻuk koṇḍaruḷummūvā vānavanai muḻunīr vaṇṇanai adiyārkkuā!ā! enṟirangit tennaḻundaiyil manni ninṟadēvādi dēvanai yān kaṇḍu koṇḍu tiḷaittēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōvānār – those who are famously known as kings; madiya – to be killed; kolai Ar – having act of annihilation as the nature; maḻu – the weapon named axe; koṇḍaruḷum – one who is wielding (in his hand); mūvā – not having old-age (etc); vānavanai – being paramapada nātan; muḻu nīr – the ocean which is having abundance of water, its; vaṇṇanai – having complexion; adiyārkku – on those who have exclusive servitude; A A enṟu irangi – showing his mercy saying “alas! alas!”; then – beautiful; aḻundaiyil – in tiruvaḻundūr; manni – remaining fixed; ninṟa – one who is eternally residing; dēvādi dēvanai – one who is the controller of nityasūris; yān – I; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – vorśipping with my eyes; tiḷaittēn – became joyful without any bewilderment

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān wielded the weapon named axe, which has the nature of annihilating others, to kill those who were famously known as kings. He is paramapada nātan who does not have changes such as old-age etc. He is having the complexion of ocean which has abundance of water. He is the controller of nityasūris, who is remaining firmly in tiruvaḻundūr showing his mercy towards those who are exclusive servitors saying “alas! alas!”. I vorśipped him with my eyes and became joyful, without any bewilderment.

**kōvānār madiya** – Those who are the controllers of different places, and being named as kśatriya – to have them killed.

**kolaiyār maḻukkoṇḍaruḷum …** – Having a form which remains the same forever and wielding the axe which remains in tact without needing to be changed even after killing twenty one generations of \[evil\] kśatriyas.

**muḻu nīr vaṇṇanai** – One who is having the complexion of the ocean which is a water body.

**adiyārkku A A enṟu irangi** – Showing his mercy with compassion towards his exclusive servitors, he has arrived and is standing in tiruvaḻundūr.

**dēvādi dēvanai …** – With my eyes, I got to see the lord of nityasūris as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*“, had all my agitation eliminated and became joyful.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.6.3. Udaiyanai

*udaiyānai olinīr ulagangaḷ padaittānaividaiyānōda anṟu viṟalāḻi visaittānaiadaiyār tennilangai aḻittānai aṇiyaḻundūrudaiyānai adiyēn adaindu uyndu pōnēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

udaiyānai – being the lord of all; oli nīr – surrounded by the resounding ocean; ulagangaḷ – the worlds; padaittānai – one who created; vidaiyān – rudran who is having bull as vehicle; ōda – to run away, being defeated; anṟu – during the bāṇāsura yuddam (war); viṟal – strong; āḻi – śrī sudarśanam; visaittānai – one who launched; adaiyār – filled with enemies; then ilangai – lankā, which is in the southern direction; aṇi – being an ornament for earth; aḻundūr – tiruvaḻundūr; udaiyānai – having as his abode; adiyēn – I who am a servitor; adaindu – having surrendered; uyndu pōnēn – became uplifted

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān, who is the supreme lord for all, created the worlds which are surrounded by resounding oceans. He launched the śrī sudarśana, which is strong, during bāṇāsura yuddam, to make rudran, who has bull as the vehicle, runaway from the battlefield, being defeated. He destroyed lankā which is in the southern direction and is filled with enemies. I, who am a servitor, have surrendered unto the one who has tiruvaḻundūr as his abode, became uplifted.

**udaiyānai …** – Being the śēśi (lord) for all the cētanas other than him.

**oli nīr ulagangaḷ padaittānai …** – While everything lay destroyed, the causal lord who created the earth which is surrounded by ocean.

**vidaiyān …** – While those \[dēvatās like rudran\] who were placed as protectors for the world, join forces with the asuras with the intent to harm, bhagavān protects them \[dēvatās\] even at that stage. What did he do to make rudran run away? He launched the tiruvāḻi (sudarśana cakram).

**vidaiyān ōda** – rudra was bewildered, as said in  harivamsam 125-8 “*pāravaśyam samāyāta*: *śuli jrumbhita tējasā* l *pāncajanyasya ghōśēṇa śārngaviśpūrjitēna ca* ll” (Sivan, who is wielding a trident, swooned and fell unconscious, after hearing the trumpeting sound of emperumān’s conch, śrī pāncajanyam, and the sound of emperumān’s bow, śrī śārngam); while he acquired clarity, he said as in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-33-41? “*kriṣṇa kriṣṇa mahābāhō jānē tvām puruśōttamam* l *parēśam paramātmānam anādinidanam param* ll” (Oh kriṣṇa, with huge hands! I know that you alone are the best among all souls, the head of celestial entities, you are the supreme being, the one without a beginning and an end and superior to all).

**adaiyār …** – One who would destroy those who are fully and steadily unfavourable towards him \[and his devotees\].

**aṇiyaḻundūr udaiyānai** – Being the owner of tiruvaḻundūr is greater than being the owner of nitya vibhūti (paramapadam). Since āḻvār has indicated that he is the lord of ubhaya vibhūti (śrīvaikuṇṭam and samsāram) and subsequently/separately identified that he is the owner of the beautiful tiruvaḻundūr, this wealth is superior to the wealth identified first.

**adiyēn …** – I who have no other refuge have attained you. I have changed from the state indicated in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (those who are not knowledgeable about brahmam are as good as acit) to being uplifted and accomplished.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.6.4. Kunral mari

*kunṟāl māri taduttavanaik kula vēḻam anṟuponṟāmai adanukku aruḷ seyda pōrēṟṟaianṟu āvin naṟuney amarnduṇṇa aṇiyaḻundūrninṟānai adiyēn kaṇḍu koṇḍu niṟaindēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kunṟāl – With gōvardana hill; māri – hailstorm; taduttavanai – one who stopped; kulam – born with pedigree; vēḻam – śrī gajēndram; ponṟāmai – to be not killed; anṟu – at that time; adanukku – for that elephant; aruḷ seyda – one who mercifully showered his grace; pōr ēṟṟai – one who is strong in battle; anṟu – during kriṣṇāvatāram; āvin – cow’s; naṟu ney – fresh ghee; amarndu – having desire in his heart; uṇṇa – one who mercifully consumed; aṇi – being an ornament for earth; aḻundūr – tiruvaḻundūr; udaiyānai – having as his abode; adiyēn – I, who am a servitor; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – I got to see; niṟaindēn – became complete

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān stopped the hailstorm with gōvardana hill. He mercifully showered his grace on śrī gajēndram which has a pedigree, to be not killed at that time. He is strong in battle. In that kriṣṇāvatāram, he mercifully consumed the cow’s fresh ghee, having desire in his heart. I, who am a servitor, got to see the one who has tiruvaḻundūr as his abode,and became complete.

**kunṟāl māri taduttavanai** – bhagavān protecting the world when indran, who was appointed as the protector became the one who caused harm, is explained. As indran caused the rain due to being affected by hunger, bhagavān took up the gōvardana hill which can stop it.

**kula vēḻam …** – Being born with a pedigree, being intoxicated, due to its strength, the elephant was roaming around. Without realising the danger ahead, it entered the pond and was caught. Stopping it from getting killed, bhagavān showed his unconditional grace towards it.

**pōr ēṟṟai** – One who is like a male tiger and who can understand the plight of the elephant and protect it.

**anṟu āvin naṟu ney amarnduṇṇa aṇi aḻundūr ninṟānai …** – During kriṣṇāvatāram, he mercifully consumed the cow’s ghee and then stood in tiruvaḻundūr. He is standing in tiruvaḻundūr just as he stood in śrī gōkulam.

**adiyēn …** – Having seen him with my eyes, I, who was incomplete, became complete.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.6.5. Kanjanaik kayndanai

*kanjanaik kāyndānaik kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ ninṟānaivanjanap pēy mulaiyūdu uyir vāy maduttu uṇḍānaisenjol nānmaṟaiyōr tennaḻundaiyil manni ninṟaanjanak kunṟam tannai adiyēn kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kanjanai – on kamsan; kāyndānai – one who showed his anger; kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ – in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai; ninṟānai – one who is mercifully present; vanjanam – mischievous; pēy – pūtanā’s; mulaiyūdu – through the bosom; uyir – her vital air; vāy maduttu – accepting in his mouth; uṇḍānai – one who mercifully consumed (from that bosom); sem sol – filled with words having beauty (of being truthful); nāl maṟaiyōr – brāhmaṇas who have learnt all four vēdams, their; then aḻundaiyil manni ninṟa – remaining firm in the beautiful tiruvaḻundūr; anjanak kunṟam tannai – having a form which resembles a dark mountain; adiyēn kaṇḍu koṇḍhēnē – I, who am a servitor, got to see

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān showed anger on kamsa. He is mercifully residing in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai. He consumed the mischievous pūtanā’s bosom and her vital air through her bosom. He is having a form which resembles a dark mountain and is remaining firm in the beautiful tiruvaḻundūr which belongs to brāhmaṇas who have learnt all four vēdams which are filled with words having beauty. I, who am a servitor, got to see him there.

**kanjanaik kāyndānai** – bhagavān showed anger on kamsa to make him undergo the trouble he wanted to inflict upon bhagavān.

**kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ ninṟānai** – He is remaining in tirukkaṇṇamangai to eliminate the enemies who continue to be present here and protect everyone.

**vanjanam …** – Through the bosom of mischievous pūtanā, he consumed her vital air also.

**sem sol maṟaiyavar …** – He is present with rejuvenating form in tiruvaḻundūr which belongs to brāhmaṇas who are experts in vēdam which speaks the truth. He remains there to eliminate our tāpa trayam (three types of suffering, ādyātmikam, resulting from one’s body and mind, ādi bhaudikam, resulting from other living beings (insects, people et al) and ādi daivikam, resulting from divine or natual forces such as earthquakes, storm etc). I, who am tormented by tāpa trayam, got to see him and eliminated my tāpa trayam.

## 7.6.6. Periyanai

*periyānai amarar talaivaṟkum piramanukkumuriyānai ugandān avanukkum uṇarvadanukkuariyānai aḻundūr maṟaiyōrgaḷ adipaṇiyumkariyānai adiyēn kaṇḍu koṇḍu kaḷittēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

periyānai – being superior to all; amarar talaivaṟkum – for indran who is the controller of dēvatās; piramanukkum – for brahmā; yānai uri – elephant skin; ugandānavanukkum – for rudran who is desirously wearing; uṇarvadanukku – even to know; ariyānai – being very difficult; aḻundūr – present in tiruvaḻundūr; maṟaiyōrgaḷ – best of brāhmaṇas; adi paṇiyum – being available to surrender unto his divine feet; kariyānai – one who is having dark complexion; adiyēn kaṇḍu koṇḍu – I, the servitor, got to see; kaḷittēn – became joyful

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is superior to all. He is very difficult for indran, who is the controller of dēvatās, brahmā and rudran, who is desirously wearing elephant skin, even to know. He is present in tiruvaḻundūr, to be surrendered unto his divine feet by the best of brāhmaṇas. He is having dark complexion. I, the servitor, got to see him and became joyful.

**periyānai** – One who is sarvasmātparan (superior to all).

**amarar talaivaṟkum** – for indran, who is the controller of all the dēvatās.

**piramanukkum** – for brahmā

**uri yānai ugandānavanukkum** – for rudran, who desired elephant skin

**uṇarvadanukku ariyānai** – for these personalities, he is very difficult to even think about him in their hearts.

**aḻundūr …** – One who is having rejuvenating form in tiruvaḻundūr where the brahmāṇas there can surrender unto his divine feet.

**adiyēn kaṇḍu koṇḍu kaḷittēnē** – I, who am an exclusive servitor of bhagavān, got to see him and became joyful.

## 7.6.7. Tiruval marvan

*tiruvāḻ mārvan tannait tisai maṇ nīr eri mudalāuruvāy ninṟavanai oli sērum mārudattaiaruvāy ninṟavanait tennaḻundaiyil manni ninṟakaruvār kaṟpagattaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu kaḷittēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiru – periya pirāttiyār; vāḻ – eternally residing; mārvan tannai – having divine chest; tisai – for the directions; maṇ – earth; nīr – water; eri – fire (and air, ether – for these); mudalāy – being the cause; uruvāy – having (these five elements) as his body; ninṟavanai – one who is mercifully residing; oli sērum mārudattai – having air which has the quality of sound (due to mixing of the five elements); aruvāy ninṟavanai – (for them) being the antarātmā and remaining without form; then aḻundaiyil manni ninṟa – one who is remaining firm in the beautiful tiruvaḻundūr; karu Ar – having garbham (well-rooted); kaṟpagattai – one who is like kalpa tree; kaṇḍu koṇḍu kaḷittēn – I got to see and became joyful

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is having divine chest where periya pirāttiyār is eternally residing. He is having the directions, earth, water, fire, air and ether as his body and is the cause for them. In this manner, he has the five elements as his body and is mercifully present. He is being formless as the antarātmā for air which has the quality of sound (due to mixing of the five elements). He is remaining firm in the beautiful tiruvaḻundūr. He is like a well-rooted kalpa tree. I got to see him and became joyful.

**tiruvāḻ mārvan …** – bhagavān is having divine chest where pirātti who is the cause for the wealth of everyone else other than her, is eagerly present saying as in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-6-10-10-agalagillen-part-5/) “*agalagillēn*” (I will never leave). It is said in śrīrangarāja stavam pūrva śatakam 7 “*īśēśitavya vaiśamya nimnōnnatamidam jagat \| namaś śrīranga nāyakyai yadbrūvibhrama bhēdata: \|\|*” (I worship śrīranga nāyaki whose eyebrow position determines the superiority or inferiority of a person in this world). tisai – directions.

**maṇ nir …** – Being the controller of the five elements which are cause and is having them as subservient as his body.

**oli sērum mārudattai** – Having air which has its own nature which is the sensation of touch and the nature of ākāśam which is sound, as his prakāram (attribute).

In this manner, he creates the dēva (celestial), manuśya (human), tiryak (animal) and stāvara (immovable) entities and then enters in them through an ātmā as said in tatittirīya upaniśat “*tadanupraviśya*” (entered in that). Then, he remains as the cause for them in a way that the words which indicate them will point to him ultimately. He is eternally residing in tiruvaḻundūr.

**karuvār kaṟpagattai** – kalpaka tree which has strong roots. Unlike in svargam where kalpaka tree can stand without support, here bhagavān is like kalpaka tree which stands well-rooted on the earth. Seeing such bhagavān, all my desires were fulfilled and I became joyful.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.6.8. Nilaiyalaga

*nilaiyāḷāga ennai ugandānai nilamagaḷ tanmulaiyāḷ vittaganai mudu nānmaṟai vīdi toṟumalaiyārum kadal pōl muḻangum tennaḻundaiyil manni ninṟakalaiyār soṟporuḷaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu kaḷittēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me; nilai āḷāga – as someone who engages in eternal service; ugandānai – has become joyful; nilamagaḷtan – bhūmip pirātti’s; mulai āḷ – one who can reign over the bosoms; vittaganai – being the amazing one; mudu – ancient (beginningless); nāl maṟai – four vēdams; vīditoṟum – in every street; alai ārum – filled with waves; kadalpōl – like an ocean; muḻangum – resounding; then aḻundaiyil manni ninṟa – remaining firm in the beautiful tiruvaḻundūr; kalai Ar – present in śāstrams; sol – for the words; poruḷai – one who is the meaning; kaṇḍu koṇḍu kaḷittēn – I got to see and became joyful

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān has made me fully focussed on performing eternal service to him and has become joyful. He is the amazing one who can reign over buūmip pirātti’s bosoms. He is remaining firm in the beautiful tiruvaḻundūr where the ancient four vēdams are resounding like an ocean filled with waves, in every street. He is the meaning of the words which are present in śāstrams. I got to see him and became joyful.

**nilaiyāḷāga ennai ugandānai** – Instead of my accepting something from him and leaving as said in “*dēhi mē dadāmi tē*” (I offer you something, you grant me something back), he made me engage in eternal service due to his loving desire towards me. Eternal service is possible to attain only if he desires to grant us and that cannot be attained by tapas (penance) and samādi (deep meditation).

**nila magaḷ …** – He is the amazing lord who can place a horse for an elephant, for śrī bhūmip pirāttiyār’s divine bosoms. \[Placing a horse for an elephant means – to train an elephant in running efficiently, in the olden days, they will make a horse run in front of it and trying to make the elephant catch the horse. ēverytime the elephant gets closer to the horse, the horse will run faster. Similarly, bhagavān is so amazing that he can make bhūmip pirātti’s divine bosoms which are most enjoyable, long for him\]

**mudu nānmaṟai** – mudu nāl maṟai means the vēdam which is beginningless. In every street, the chanting of vēdam is heard like an ocean with agitated waves. Firmly remaining in such beautiful tiruvaḻundūr.

**kalaiyār soṟporuḷai** – Having seen bhagavān who is shown as the goal by all the śāstrams, all my desires got fulfilled and hence I became blissful.

## 7.6.9. Peranai

*pērānaik kudandaip perumānai ilangoḷi sērvārār vanamulaiyāḷ malar mangai nāyaganaiārā innamudait tennaḻundaiyil manni ninṟakārār karumugilaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu kaḷittēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pērānai – one who is present in tiruppērnagar; kudandaip perumānai – being the supreme lord who is mercifully residing in tirukkudandai; ilangu – shining; oḷi sēr – having radiance; vār Ar – having bodice; vana mulaiyāḷ – having beautiful bosoms; malar mangai – for periya pirāttiyār, who resides on the lotus; nāyaganai – the beloved lord; ārā – insatiating; in – sweet; amudai – being like amrutam (nectar); then aḻundaiyil manni ninṟa – remaining firm in the beautiful tiruvaḻundūr; kār Ar – in the rainy season; karu mugilai – one who is rejuvenating like a dark cloud; kaṇḍu koṇḍu kaḷittēn – I got to see and became joyful

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is present in tiruppēr nagar. He is the supreme lord who is mercifully residing in tirukkudandai. He is the beloved lord of periya pirāttiyār who resides on the lotus and who is having beautiful bosoms coverred by śiningly radiant bodice. He is like insatiating sweet nectar. He is rejuvenating like a dark cloud in the rainy season. He is remaining firm in the beautiful tiruvaḻundūr. I got to see him and became joyful.

**pērānai** – He is present in tiruppēr nagar.

**kudandaip perumānai** – Arriving in tirukkudandai and reclining there showing his supremacy.

**ilangoḷi …** – He is the beloved lord of ever-youthful periya pirāttiyār.

**ārā innamudai** – Their togetherness is enjoyable for him.

**then aḻundai …** – While eternally residing in tiruvaḻundūr, he appears in a rejuvenating form like that of a cloud in rainy season.

**kaṇḍu koṇḍu kaḷittēnē** – I got to see him to cool down my eyes and became blissful.

## 7.6.10. Tiral murugan

*tiṟal murugananaiyār tennaḻundaiyil manni ninṟaaṟamudalvan avanai aṇi āliyar kōn maruvārkaṟai neduvēl valavan kalikanṟi sol aiyiraṇḍummuṟai vaḻuvāmai vallār muḻudāḷvar vānulagē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiṟal – in strength; murugan anaiyār – those who are like subrahmaṇya, are eternally residing; then – beautiful; aḻundaiyil – in tiruvaḻundūr; manni ninṟa – one who is remaining firmly and eternally residing; aṟam mudalvan avanai – on the lord who is the basis for all dharma (righteous acts); aṇi – an ornament for samsāra; āliyar – for those who are in tiruvāli; kōn – being the lord; maruvār – enemies’; kaṟai – having blood stains; nedu – lengthy; vēl – the weapon named spear; valavan – one who can wield; kali kanṟi – mercifully spoken by tirumangai āḻvār; sol – divine words; ai iraṇḍum – ten pāsurams; muṟai vāḻuvāmai – without violating the rules; vallār – those who can recite; vān ulagu – paramapadam; muḻudu – completely; āḷvar – will get to protect well

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is remaining firmly and eternally residing in the beautiful tiruvaḻundūr where those who are like subrahmaṇya in strength, are residing. He is the basis for all dharma (righteous acts). On such bhagavān, tirumangai āḻvār, who is the lord of those who are residing in tiruvāli, which is an ornament for this samsāra, who is wielding the weapon named spear which is long and having the blood stain of the enemies, mercifully composed these ten pāsurams which are divine words. Those who are able to recite these pāsurams, without violating the rules, will get to protect the paramapadam in a complete manner.

**tiṟal murugan …** – In strength, the residents of tiruvaḻundūr are not any lesser than subrahmaṇya who is the commander-in-chief of the army of dēvatās.

**aṟu mudalvanavan avanai** – One who is the root cause for dharma. Protecting own citizens, protecting the world of ātmās, protecting the devotees – one who is the root cause for all of these righteous acts.

**aṇiyāliyar …** – The one who is the controller for the residents of tiruvāli which is like an ornament for the samsāram.

**maruvār …** – tirumangai āḻvār who is having the lengthy spear which is stained with blood due to lack of time for washing it after killing the enemies, in his hands, mercifully sang these ten pāsurams with tune. Those who can recite these pāsurams in sequence, will have the whole tripād vibhūti (paramapadam) under their control as said in  [tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-9-10-vidhi-vagai/) “*ānmingaḷ vānagam*” (rule over śrī vaikuṇṭam).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7 Tiruvukkum

## 7.7.1. Tiruvukkum

*tiruvukkum tiruvāgiya selvā! deyvattukku arasē! seyya kaṇṇā!uruvac cenjudar āḻi vallānē! ulaguṇḍa oruvā! tirumārbāoruvaṟkāṟṟi uyyum vagai enṟāl udan ninṟu aivar ennuḷ pugundu oḻiyāduaruvit tinṟida anji ninnadaindēn aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruvāgiya – cause for wealth (for everyone); tiruvukkum – for periya pirāttiyār; selvā – Oh, one who is the embodiment of wealth!; deyvattukku – for nityasūris; arasē – Oh, lord!; seyya kaṇṇā – Oh, one who is having reddish, beautiful eyes!; uruvam – having beautiful form; senjudar – very radiant; āḻi vallānē – Oh, one who is having tiruvāḻi (divine sudarśana chakra) in hand!; ulaguṇḍa – swallowed all the worlds; oruvā – Oh, one who is unique!; tirumārbā – Oh, one who is having periya pirāttiyār in your divine chest!; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; mēl tisai – in the western direction; ninṟa – mercifully residing; ammānē – Oh, lord!; oruvaṟku – for one sense organ; āṟṟi – satisfying the desire; uyyum vagai – to be freed; enṟāl – when I thought about it; aivar – the five sense organs; udan ninṟu – being in close proximity; en uḷ pugundu – entering me; oḻiyādu – without backing out even for a moment; aruvi – tormented; tinṟida – as they close in; anji – became frightened (due to them); nin – your (lotus feet); adaindēn – I surrendered unto

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, one who is the embodiment of wealth for periya pirāttiyār, who is the cause for wealth (for everyone)! Oh, the lord of nityasūris! Oh, one who is having reddish, beautiful eyes! Oh, one who is having very radiant and beautiful tiruvāḻi (divine sudarśana chakra) in hand! Oh, one who is unique in swallowing all the worlds! Oh, one who is having periya pirāttiyār in your divine chest! Oh, lord who is mercifully residing in the western side of tiruvaḻundūr! When I thought about satisfying the desire of one sense organ and be freed, all the five sense organs remained close with me, entered me and remained without leaving, tormented and closed in on me. As that was happening, I became frightened and surrendered unto you.

**tiruvukkum tiruvāgiya selvā** – Oh, one who is the embodiment of wealth for periya pirāttiyār who is the cause for wealth for everyone other than her!

**deyvattukku arasē** … – Oh, one who is the lord of nityasūris as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*“! Oh, sarvēśvara,who is having lotus-eyes! Oh, sarvēśvara who is having very radiant and beautiful tiruvāḻi (divine sudarśana chakra) in hand as a tool to eliminate the enemies! These are identities of supremacy – being laksmīpati, lord of nityasūris and being able to wield the tiruvāḻi.

**ulaguṇḍa oruvā** – One remained as taḷarndār tāvaḷam (refuge for the suffering persons) without discriminating between good and bad qualities of everyone.

**tirumārvā** – Oh, one who is having periya pirāttiyār, who makes you “taḷarndār tāvaḷam”, in your chest!

**oruvaṟku …** – I have ceased to be a servitor of one master. I am not able to just dance according to one master’s orders and be freed.

**udaninṟu …** – The harming entities are standing closer to me than you who are the protector, and are tormenting me. As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-1-1-unnilaviya/) “*uṇṇilāviya*” (remaining inside me), instead of just one or two, my five sense organs are tormenting me assuming the form of a sentient being, by being close to me and are not backing out from such torment.

**aruvit tinṟida …** – Each of them is individually asking me “Feed me, Feed me” tormenting me and closing in on me. Being scared of them, I surrendered unto the divine feet of you, who are the lord of all.

**aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānē** – Should you, who have ventured out to protect us, not do it completely?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.2. Pandar melviral

*pandār melviral nalvaḷait tōḷi pāvai pūmagaḷ tannodum udanēvandāy en manattē manni ninṟāy mālvaṇṇā! maḻai pōl oḷivaṇṇā!candōgā! pauḻiyā! taittiriyā! sāma vēdiyanē! nedumālē!andō! ninnadi anṟi maṟṟaṟiyēn aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pandu Ar – having ball (always); mel – soft; viral – one who is having fingers; nalvaḷai – having beautiful bangles; tōḷi – having shoulders; pāvai – having natural femininity; pū magaḷ tannodum – with periya pirāttiyār; udanē – being together; vandāy – Oh, one who mercifully came!; en manattē – in my heart; manni – remaining fixed; ninṟāy – Oh, one who is mercifully present!; māl vaṇṇā – Oh, one who is having dark divine complexion!; maḻai pōl – (cool) like cloud; oḷi – radiance; vaṇṇā – Oh, one who is having complexion!; candōgā – Oh, one who knows the meaning of cāndōjña upaniśat!; pauḻiyā – Oh, one who knows the meaning of bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat!; taittiriyā – Oh, one who knows the meaning of taittirīya upaniśat!; sāma vēdiyanē – Oh, one who knows the meaning of sāma vēdam!; nedu – having supremacy (which is shown in those vēdams); mālē – Oh, the greatest one!; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; mēl tisai – in the western direction; ninṟa – mercifully residing; ammānē – Oh, lord!; nin – your; adi anṟi – other than your divine feet; maṟṟu – any other refuge; aṟiyēn – I don’t know; andō – alas! (āḻvār is feeling amazed at bhagavān, who has entered his heart)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, one who mercifully came along with periya pirāttiyār, who is having soft fingers which always has a ball, having beautiful bangles, having beautiful shoulders and natural femininity! Oh, one who is mercifully present in my heart, remaining fixed! Oh, one who is having divine dark complexion! Oh, one who is having radiance and complexion like that of a cloud! Oh, one who knows the meaning of cāndōjña upaniśat! Oh, one who knows the meaning of bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat! Oh, one who knows the meaning of taittirīya upaniśat! Oh, one who knows the meaning of sāma vēdam! Oh, the greatest one having supremacy! Oh, lord who is mercifully residing in the western side of tiruvaḻundūr! I don’t know of any refuge other that your divine feet. Alas!

**pandār …** – Even while uniting with sarvēśvaran, she is having a ball in her hand and the fingers which are so tender to even hold that ball.

**nal vaḷait tōḷi** … – You came along with periya pirāttiyār who is having divine shoulders which are decorated with beautiful bangles, having natural femininity and having lotus flower as her residence. As said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.2.10 “*aravindap pāvaiyum tānum*” (bhagavān along with śrī mahālakśmi who is seated on a lotus flower), he came with his paraphernalia and entered my heart.

**en manattē manni ninṟāy** – As I did not reject you, being melted by your arrival in this manner, you entered my heart as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 5.34 “***āvāsam tvahamiccāmi*** *pratiśtam iha kānanē*” (As I am looking for a place to say, I will live in this forest as you desire).

**māl vaṇṇā** – Oh, one who has a dark complexion!

**maḻai pōl oḷi vaṇṇā** – Not just having a dark complexion, but also, you are having a form which is cool like cloud.

**candōgā …** – One who is having omniscience which is required to protect the ones who are suffering. With this, it is said “Oh, one who knows the meaning of the vēdam truthfully!”.

**nedumālē** – Oh one who is having the supremacy which is spoken of by those vēdams.

**andō …** – You cannot remain peacefully thinking that there are others who can protect and they will protect us; I, who am refugeless, have no other refuge than your divine feet.

**aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānē** – Haven’t your highness arrived here to protect those who have no other refuge?

## 7.7.3. Neyyar aliyum

*neyyār āḻiyum sangamum ēndum nīṇḍa tōḷudaiyāy! adiyēnaicceyyāda ulagattidaic ceydāy siṟumaikkum perumaikkum uḷpugundupoyyāl aivar en meykudi ēṟip pōṟṟi vāḻvadaṟku anji ninnadaindēnaiyā! ninnadi anṟi maṟṟaṟiyēn aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

aiyā – Oh, natural relative!; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; mēl tisai – in the western direction; ninṟa – mercifully residing; ammānē – Oh, lord!; nin – your; adi anṟi – other than your divine feet; maṟṟu – any other refuge; aṟiyēn – I don’t know; ney Ar – very sharp; āḻiyum – sudarśana chakra; sangamum – śrī pāncajanyam; ēndum – holding; nīṇḍa – lengthy; tōḷ – shoulders; udaiyāy – Oh, one who is having!; ulagattidai – in this world; adiyēnai – me, the servitor; seyyāda – not done (towards anyone else, the taste and faith towards you); seydāy – Oh, one who created!; siṟumaikkum – to enjoy lowly matters; perumaikkum – to enjoy great matters; poyyāl – by deceit (to be not known by me too); uḷ pugundu – entering me; en mey – in my body; kudiyēṟi – eternally residing (in their apt places); aivar – five senses; pōṟṟi – to praise and follow; vāḻvadaṟku – to live; anji – became scared; nin – your divine feet; adaindēn – I surrendered (considering them to be my refuge)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, natural relative! Oh, lord who is mercifully residing in the western side of tiruvaḻundūr! I don’t know of any refuge other that your divine feet. Alas! Oh, one who is having lengthy shoulders which are holding the very sharp śrī sudarśana and śrī pāncajanya! Oh, one who created the taste and faith in me, the servitor towards you, which is not done towards anyone else in this world! I became scared for the life of praising and following my five senses which have entered me by deceit to enjoy lowly matters and great matters and are eternally residing in my body, and surrendered unto your divine feet.

**neyyār …** – Oh one who is having well sharpened divine weapons! ney – sharpness, Ar – abundance, very sharp tiruvāḻi (divine chakra). Oh, one who is having shoulders which are apt for those weapons!

**adiyēnai –** I who am qualified to remain as a servitor for you.

**ulagattidaic ceyādavaṟṟaic ceydāy** – You made possible what is not done in this world. You placed me in this world which does not think about kainkaryam (service) to your divine feet.

**siṟumaikkum perumaikkum uḷ pugundu** – They \[five senses\] have deceitfully entered into me to be included in the word “I” to acquire lowly pleasures and pleasures which are very difficult to attain.

**pōṟṟi vāḻvadaṟku anji** – Became scared to live the life of praising and following them.

**nin adaindēn** – I approached you, who are a natural relative for me.

**aiyā** – Oh, natural relative! I have no other refuge than your divine feet.

**aḻundūr …** – You have arrived here manifesting your natural relationship.
