## 7.7.4. Parane

*paranē! panjavan pauḻiyan cōḻan pār mannar mannar tām paṇindu ēttumvaranē! mādavanē! madusūdā! maṟṟōr nal tuṇai ninnalāl ilēn kāṇnaranē! nāraṇanē! tirunaṟaiyūr nambī! emperumān! umbarāḷumaranē! ādivarāgam mun ānāy! aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

paranē – Oh, supreme lord!; panjavan – known as panjavan; pauḻiyan – known as pauḻiyan; sōḻan – known famously as cōḻan; mannar – complete with all wealth; pār – (for those) nations; mannar – being kings; tām – themselves (to fulfil their desire); paṇindu – surrendered; ēttum – mercifully present to be praised; varanē – Oh, refuge!; mādavanē – Oh the lord of śrīmahālakśmi!; madusūdā – Oh one who killed the asura named madu!; naranē nāraṇanē – Oh one incarnated as naran and nārāyaṇan (riśis, to acquire devotees)!; tirunaṟaiyūr – one who is mercifully present in tirunaṟaiyūr; nambi – Oh, complete one!; emperumān – Oh one who is natural lord for me!; umbar – dēvatās; āḷum – one who can control (by keeping them under him); aranē – Oh, one who is the antaryāmi of rudran!; mun – in the beginning; ādi varāham ānāy – Oh, one who incarnated as mahā varāham!; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; mēl tisai – in the western direction; ninṟa – mercifully residing; ammānē – Oh, lord!; nin alāl – other than you; nal – one, who is working for the benefit of others only; maṟṟu ōr – any other; tuṇai – protector; ilēn – I am not having

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, supreme lord! Oh, the refuge who is mercifully present to be surrendered unto you and to be praised by kings who are famously known as panjavan, pauḻiyan and cōḻan for their respective nation! Oh, the lord of śrīmahālakśmi! Oh, one who killed the asura named madu! Oh, one incarnated as naran and nārāyaṇan (riśis, to acquire devotees)! Oh, the complete one who is mercifully present in tirunaṟaiyūr! Oh, one who is natural lord for me! Oh, one who is the antaryāmi of rudran who can control dēvatās! Oh, one who incarnated as mahā varāham in the beginning! Oh, the lord who is mercifully residing in the western side of tiruvaḻundūr! I am not having any protector other than you, who is working for the benefit of others only.

**paranē** – Oh, one who is superior to all!

**panjavan …** – There are famous cōḻa kings who are known as “panjavan”, “pauḻiyan” who are kings for different regions and who are opulent; due to their desire, they came and surrendered unto you and got temsleves fulfilled. Oh, the supreme lord who is mercifully present to help them! Oh, one who is refuge for them!

**mādavanē** – Oh, one who is having puruśakāram which will facilitate the fulfilment of their desires!

**madusūdā** – Oh, one who is having the ability to eliminate their enemies!

**maṟṟu ōr nal tuṇai** – I am not having any refuge other than you, who will transform yourself to help those who surrender unto you.

**naranē nāraṇanē** – For the sake of your devotees, oh, you who will perform the penance that will be done by them (such kings) to attain you!

**tirunaṟaiyūr nambi** – Oh, one who is complete in all auspicious qualities and standing in tirunaṟaiyūr!

**emperumān** – Oh, one who manifested your togetherness with pirātti there and made me totally existing for you!

**umbar āḷum aranē** – Oh, one who is remaining as the antaryāmi of rudran to rule over the dēvatās who were born after him! It is said in mahābhāratam āśramavāśika parvam 118-37 “*rudram samāśritā dēvā rudrō brahmāṇamāśrita:* I *brahmā mamāśritō rājan nāham kincidupāśrita:* īī” (Oh king! The celestial entities are taking refuge of rudra; rudra is taking (his father) brahmā’s refuge; brahmā has taken refuge under me; I have not taken refuge under anyone).

**ādi varāham mun ānāy** – Oh, one who incarnated in the beginning of varāha kalpam (one of brahmā’s many days), remained in visibility and protected us directly instead of remaining inside someone else (rudran) and protecting!

**aḻundūr mēl …** – Oh, one who is presently residing in tirunaṟaiyūr by making that (ādi varāha incarnation) as old story!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.5. Vindan vin puga

*viṇḍān viṇ puga venjamattu ariyāyp pariyōn mārvagam paṟṟip piḷandupaṇḍu ānuyya ōr mālvarai ēndum paṇbāḷā! paranē! pavittiranē!kaṇḍēn nān kali yugattadan tanmai karumam āvadum endanakku aṟindēnaṇḍā! ninnadi anṟi maṟṟaṟiyēn aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇḍān – hiraṇyan, the enemy who did not align with him (to die); viṇ puga – to enter vīra svargam (heaven attained by valorous acts); vem samattu – in the cruel battle; ariyāy – having the narasimha form; pariyōn – the stout hiraṇya’s; mārvagam – chest; paṟṟi – held (with his nails); piḷandu – one who tore down; paṇḍu – in kriṣṇāvatāram; An – cows; uyya – to survive; māl – huge; ōr varai – a mountain; ēndum – one who held (as umbrella); paṇbāḷā – Oh, one who is having saulabhyam (easy approacability)!; paranē – Oh, one who is greater than everyone else!; pavittiranē – Oh, one who can turn his devotees to be pure!; aṇḍā – Oh, one who is lord of the universe!; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; mēl tisai – in the western direction; ninṟa – mercifully residing; ammānē – Oh, lord!; nān – I; kaliyugattadan – kali yugam’s; tanmai – nature; kaṇḍēn – have known; enṟanakku – for me; karumamāvadum – acts which are for my well-being; aṟindēn – have determined (when asked “What is that?”); nin – your; adi anṟi – other than your divine feet; maṟṟu – any other refuge; aṟiyēn – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

To have hiraṇyāsura, the enemy who did not align with him, killed and reach vīra svargam, bhagavān assumed the narasimha form in the cruel battle, held the stout hiraṇya’s chest with his nails and tore it down. Oh, one who is having saulabhyam (easy approacability) in holding the huge mountain gōvardana as an umbrella to help the cows survive, in kriṣṇāvatāram! Oh, one who is greater than everyone else! Oh, one who can turn his devotees to be pure! Oh, one who is the lord of the universe! Oh, lord who is mercifully residing in the western side of tiruvaḻundūr! I have known kali yugam’s nature. I have determined the acts which are for my well-being. (That is) I don’t know of any refuge other that your divine feet.

**viṇḍān …** – To make hiraṇyāsura climb and reach vīra svargam.

**vem samattu …** – In the cruel battle, he assumed narasimha form, went and held the chest of hiraṇya, who had body which is stout due to ahankāram and mamakāram, and tore it down to two pieces.

**paṇḍu An uyya** … – With this, it is explained that in narasimhāvatāram, he helped prahlāda who can recognise bhagavān’s help; but the cows and covherd people won’t even have gratitude and yet kriṣṇa helped. Oh, one who lifted up a mountain which was in your hands’ reach to protect cows and covherd people.

**paranē** – Oh, matchless one in protecting your people!

**pavittiranē** – Oh, one who is having the purity to purify the impure persons!

**kaṇḍēn nān kaliyugattadan tanmai** – I have clearly seen the nature of this kali yugam. I have clearly known the nature of this samsāram which causes vaimukhyam (facing away) from you and causes attachment towards worldly matters.

**karumamāvadum enṟanakku aṟindēn** – I have known that surrendering unto your divine feet is good for me.

**aṇḍā** – Oh, the controller of the universe! Alternative explanation – Oh, the controller of covherd people!

**aḻundūr …** – Haven’t you arrived here and stood, to protect the people of the future just like you helped śrī prahlāda, covherd people and cows?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.6. Toya intayir

*tōyā intayir ney amuduṇṇac connār solli nagum parisē peṟṟatāyāl āppuṇḍirundu aḻudēngum tādāḷā! taraiyōrkkum viṇṇōrkkumsēyāy! kirēda tirēda tuvāpara kali yugam ivai nāngum mun ānāy!āyā! ninnadi anṟi maṟṟaṟiyēn aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

sonnār – those who speak as they please; solli – spoke about stealing butter, explicitly; nagum – making fun; parisē – the way (without fearing for the blame, thinking “is it worthy?”); tōyā – not well matured; in tayir – sweet curd; ney – ghee; amuduṇṇa – as you were mercifully eating (at that time); peṟṟa tāyāl – by yaśōdā, who is as loving as dēvaki who gave birth; āppuṇḍu – being bound; irundu – remaining there, without being able to move away; aḻudu – cried (further); ēngum – sobbing continuously; tādāḷā – Oh, the great one!; taraiyōrkkum – for those who are on earth; viṇṇōrkkum – for the residents of higher planets; sēyāy – Oh, one who is difficult to reach!; mun – previously; kirēda tirēda duvāpara kali yugam – kruta yugam, trētā yugam, dvāpara yugam, kali yugam; ivai nāngum ānāy – Oh, one who is the controller for these four yugams!; āyā – Oh, kriṣṇa, the covherd boy!; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; mēl tisai – in the western direction; ninṟa – mercifully residing; ammānē – Oh, lord!; nin – your; adi anṟi – other than your divine feet; maṟṟu – any other refuge; aṟiyēn – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Those who speak as they please, spoke about your stealing butter and made fun of you. Without worrying about the way they did that, you were mercifully eating the sweet curd which is not matured enough and the ghee. At that time, yaśōdā, who is as loving as dēvaki who gave birth to him, bound you. Oh, the great one who remained there crying and sobbing continuously! Oh, one who is difficult to reach for the residents of earth and higher planets! Oh, one who is the controller for these four yugams named kruta yugam, trētā yugam, dvāpara yugam and kali yugam, from the beginning! Oh, kriṣṇa, the covherd boy! Oh, lord who is mercifully residing in the western side of tiruvaḻundūr! I don’t know of any refuge other than your divine feet.

**tōyā in tayir …** – As he was mercifully eating the sweet curd which is not fully matured, and ghee, with great eagerness.

**sonnār …** – Not fearing for the accusations of those who speak as they please, he remained without any shame thinking “If we ate fresh curd, is there anything wrong?” “They don’t need reason to blame me. They will do it all anyway”.

**peṟṟa tāyāl āppuṇḍu** – Being bound by yaśōdāp pirātti.

**aḻudu …** – Being helpless to protest and being unable to leave – having such greatness.

**taraiyōr …** – Oh, one who is far away for those who are present on earth or higher planets, who try to see you with their own effort!

bhagavān asks “Why are you becoming tensed like this? Should I not help at the right time?” āḻvār says

**kirēda tirēda …** – Can you not do as said in śrī bhāgavatam 11.5.38 “*kalau krutayugam tasya*” (kruta yugam appearing in kali yugam)? īsn’t time under your control? I don’t know anything other than your divine feet.

**aḻundūr mēl …** – Haven’t you arrived here and stood for the sake of those who came after kriṣṇāvatāram, to not lose you?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.7. Karuttuk kanjanai

*kaṟuttuk kanjanai anja munindāy! kārvaṇṇā! kadal pōl oḷivaṇṇā!iṟuttittān vidai ēḻum mun venṟāy! endāy! andaram ēḻum mun ānāy!poṟuttuk koṇḍirundāl poṟukkoṇṇāp pōgamē nugarvān pugundu aivaraṟuttut tinṟida anji ninnadaindēn aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kanjanai – on kamsan; kaṟuttu – showed anger; anja – to make him fear; munindāy – Oh, one who mercifully killed him!; kār vaṇṇā – Oh, one who is having a cool form like that of a cloud!; kadal pōl – like an ocean; oḷi vaṇṇā – Oh, one who is having dark radiance and nature of giving protection to others!; vidai – strong; An ēḻum – seven bulls; mun – in kriṣṇāvatāram; iṟuttittu – snapped their body; veṇṟāy – Oh, one who killed and became victorious!; endāy – Oh, my lord!; andaram ēḻum – the seven higher worlds; mun – from the beginning; ānāy – Oh, one who is the controller!; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; mēl tisai – in the western direction; ninṟa – mercifully residing; ammānē – Oh, lord!; aivar – five senses; poṟuttuk koṇḍirundāl – even if I tried to tolerate (the troubles); poṟukkoṇā – being intolerable; bōgamē – worldly pleasures only; nugarvān – to make me enjoy; pugundu – entering me; aṟuttu – tormented; tinṟida – as they are destroying (my true nature, of being your servitor); anji – fearing (that); nin adaindēn – I surrendered unto you

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, one who showed anger on kamsan to make him fear you and mercifully killed him! Oh, one who is having a cool form like that of a cloud! Oh, one who is having dark radiance like that of an ocean and nature of giving protection to others! Oh, one who snapped the body of the seven strong bulls, killed them and became victorious! Oh, my lord! Oh, one who is the controller for the seven higher worlds, from the beginning! Oh, lord who is mercifully residing in the western side of tiruvaḻundūr! Fearing my senses which have entered me to make me enjoy worldly pleasures only, which are intolerable even if I tried to tolerate them, I surrendered unto you.

**kaṟuttuk kanjanai** … – kamsan had evil intentions towards kriṣṇa, who thinks about uplifting everyone; kriṣṇa showed anger on him to make his intentions occur to him; you showed your anger to cause fear in him.

**kār vaṇṇā** – For those who see you, you have a rejuvenating form.

**kadal pōl oḷi vaṇṇā** – Like an ocean, being the protector for all the entities, having a complexion which matches its.

**iṟuttittān vidaiy ēḻum mun venṟāy** – You won over the seven bulls which were like death personified due to being possessed by monsters, by snapping their horns.

**endāy** – You enslaved me by showing such act.

**andaram ēḻum mun ānāy** – Oh, one who owns the seven higher worlds!

**poṟuttuk koṇḍirundāl …** – The five senses force me to enjoy the pleasures causing unbearable pain even if I considered to bear the torment caused by them. Fearing these senses, I surrendered unto your divine feet.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.8. Nediyane

*nediyānē! kadiyār kali nambī! ninnaiyē ninaindu ingu iruppēnaikkadiyār kāḷaiyar aivar pugundu kāval seyda akkāvalaip piḻaittukkudipōndu unnadik kīḻ vandu pugundēn kūṟai sōṟu ivai tandu enakkaruḷiadiyēnaip paṇi āṇḍukoḷ endāy! aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nediyānē – Oh, one who is greater than all!; kadi – being a fort around the earth; Ar kali – on the ocean (mercifully reclining); nambi – Oh, complete one!; endāy – Oh, my lord!; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; mēl tisai – in the western direction; ninṟa – mercifully residing; ammānē – Oh, lord!; ninnaiyē – you only; ninaindu – meditating upon; ingu – in this leelā vibhūti; iruppēnai – I, who am remaining; kadi Ar – strong; kāḷaiyar – having youthfulness (which will not allow a person to retract from harming others); aivar – five senses; pugundu – entering me; kāval seyda – imprisoned me (stopping me from going towards you); akkāvalai – that imprisonment; piḻaittu – escape; un adik kīḻ – beneath your divine feet; kudi pōndu – considering to remain there; vandu – came; pugundēn – entered inside; enakku – for me (who has abandoned worldly pleasures); kūṟai – clothes; sōṟu – food; ivai – these lotus feet; aruḷi – showering your mercy; tandu – granting; adiyēnai – I, who have natural servitude; paṇi āṇḍu koḷ – You should engage me in serving you eternally

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, one who is greater than all! Oh, the complete one who is mercifully reclining on the ocean which is like a fort around the earth! Oh, lord who is mercifully residing in the western side of tiruvaḻundūr! I am remaining in this leelā vibhūti meditating only on you; five senses, which are strong and having youthfulness, have entered me and have imprisoned me; I have escaped that imprisonment and have entered beneath your divine feet considering to remain there. You should mercifully grant me your divine feet which are like clothes and food for me, and I, who have natural servitude, should be engaged in serving you eternally.

**nediyānē** – Oh, supreme lord who is greater than all!

**kadi Ar kali nambi** – Fragrant, fort-like *Ar kali* that is ocean; oh, complete one who is mercifully reclining there!

**ninnaiyē ninaindiruppēnai** … – I, who am having the meditation of those who are remaining in paramapadam; meditating upon you from here in this samsāram itself. The five senses which are youthful to torment others continuously, have imprisoned me.

**akkāvalaip piḻaittuk kudi pōndu unnadik kīḻ vandu pugundēn** – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam ślōkam 17-16 “*sō’ham paruśitastēna dāsavaccāvamānita*: l ***tyaktvā putrāmśca dārāmśca rāghavam śaraṇam gata:*** ll” (I, who am like that, have been rudely treated by rāvaṇa, being treated like a servant; I have left behind my wife and children, and am taking refuge under rāghava), I escaped those senses, and surrendered unto your divine feet.

**kūṟai sōṟu ivai tandu enakku aruḷi** – Granting these divine feet which are like clothes and food. As said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.1.5 “*tōttam illavaḷ*” (Garden, wife etc) and [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-1-unnum-soru/) “*ellām kaṇṇan*” (Everything is kriṣṇa), āḻvār is thinking these divine feet are his clothes and food.

**adiyēnaip paṇi āṇḍu koḷ endāy –** You, who are my apt lord, should engage me in eternal servitude instead of letting me become like a prince who lost the throne.

**aḻundūr …** – Just as you presented yourself in the seashore to be approached by śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān, your highness have arrived and presented yourself here in this divyadēśam, to help me surrender unto you when my relatives abandon me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.9. Kovay aivar

*kōvāy aivar en meykudi ēṟik kūṟai sōṟu ivai tā enṟu kumaittuppōgār nān avaraip poṟukkagilēn punidā! putkodiyāy! nedumālē!tīvāy nāgaṇaiyil tuyilvānē! tirumālē! inic ceyvadonṟu aṟiyēnā! ā! enṟu adiyēṟku iṟai irangāy aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

punidā – Oh, pure one!; putkodiyāy – Oh, one who is having periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) as flag!; nedumālē – Oh, one who is having great infatuation towards devotees!; tī vāy – having a mouth which is spitting fire; nāgu aṇaiyil – on tiruvanantāḻvān, who is the mattress; tuyilvānē – Oh, one who is mercifully reclining!; tirumālē – Oh, śriya:pati (divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi)!; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; mēl tisai – in the western direction; ninṟa – mercifully residing; ammānē – Oh, lord!; aivar – five senses; kōvāy – being my controller (and enslaving me); en mey – in my body; kudiyēṟi – coming to reside; ivai – these lowly; kūṟai – clothes; sōṟu – food; tā enṟu – asking “give”; kumaittu – tormenting (me); pōgār – they are not leaving from here; nān – I, who am your servitor; avarai – the troubles caused by those senses; poṟukkagilēn – I am unable to tolerate; ini – after reaching you as the refuge; seyvadu – to be done for my well-being; onṟu – any other activity; aṟiyēn – I don’t know. Hence; adiyēṟku – for me; A A enṟu – saying “alas! alas!”; iṟai – little bit; irangāy – show your mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, pure one! Oh, one who is having periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) as flag! Oh, one who is having great infatuation towards devotees! Oh, one who is mercifully reclining on tiruvanantāḻvān, who is the mattress and who is having a mouth which is spitting fire! Oh, śriya:pati (divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi)! Oh, lord who is mercifully residing in the western side of tiruvaḻundūr! The five senses, being my controller, came to reside and are asking for lowly things saying “give these clothes, food etc”, are tormenting and not leaving me, who is your servitor. I, who am your servitor, am unable to tolerate the troubles caused by those senses. After reaching, considering you to be the refuge, I don’t know of any other activity to be done for my well-being. Hence, you show your mercy a little bit upon me saying “Alas! Alas!”.

**kōvāy …** – Instead of your being my lord, these five senses have become my controllers and entered my body.

**kūṟai sōṟu ivai …** – They are tormenting me continuously by asking me to give clothes, food etc while I am considering bhagavān’s divine feet as clothes, food etc. I am unable to tolerate their torment.

**punidā** – Oh, one who is having purity to protect me by eliminating my hurdles and doing it as your benefit!

**putkodiyāy** – Oh, one who has hoisted a flag to manifest all these aspects!

**nedumālē** – Oh, one who is greatly infatuated toward devotees!

**tīvāy nāgaṇaiyil tuyilvānē** – Oh, one who is having the nature of being united with your devotees, always! Oh, one who is mercifully reclining on tiruvanantāḻvān who is spitting fire on the enemies, to make others free from fear of danger for you!

**tirumālē** – Reclining on that mattress is to be together with the divine consort, śrī mahālakśmi.

**inic cevadu onṟu aṟiyēn** … – Now, I don’t know what is to be done for my well-being. You should shower your mercy upon me, who is ananyagati (refuge-less) saying “Alas! Alas!”.

**aḻundūr mēl …** – īsn’t this divyadēśam the place where you came to shower your mercy?

## 7.7.10. Annamannu

*anna mannu paimbūmboḻil sūḻnda aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānaikkanni mannu tiṇ tōḷ kali kanṟi āli nādan mangaik kula vēndansonna in tamiḻ nanmaṇikkōvai tūya mālai ivai pattum vallārmanni mannavarāy ulagāṇḍu māna veṇ kudaik kīḻ magiḻvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annam – swans; mannu – eternally residing; pai – vast; pū – having flowers; poḻil – by orchards; sūḻnda – filled; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; mēl tisai – on the western side; ninṟa – mercifully present; ammānai – on the lord; kanni – indestructibility; mannu – remaining fixed (always indestructible); tiṇ – having strength; tōḷ – having shoulders; Ali nādan – being the controller of tiruvāli region; mangai – for the residents of tirumangai; kula vēndan – being the king who is coming in the lineage of rulers there; kali kanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoken; in tamiḻ – being present in the beautiful tamiḻ language; nal – faultless; maṇi – precious stones, their; kōvai – being great like a garland; tūya – being pure without any fault in the poem; mālai – garland of words; ivai pattum – these ten pāsurams; vallār – those who are able to recite; mannavarāy – being the kings; manni – remaining here for a long time; ulagu āṇḍu – protecting the worlds; mānam – huge; veṇ kudaik kīḻ – remaining beneath a whitish umbrella; magiḻvār – be blissful

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is mercifully residing in the western side of tiruvaḻundūr which is filled with orchards which are having expansive flowers and being inhabited by swans permanently; on such bhagavān, tirumangai āḻvār, who is having shoulders which are having indestructible strength and is the controller of tiruvāli, and the king coming in the proper lineage of kings for the residents of tirumangai region, mercifully spoke this decad, which is a pure garland of words in beautiful tamiḻ language and is great, similar to a garland of faultless precious stones. Those who are able to recite these pāsurams, will remain as kings for a long time, protecting the worlds and blissfully remain beneath the whitish umbrella.

**annam mannum** … – Having orchards which are having vast flower where swans are eternally residing. When swans have romantic fight, they can remain in the flower without getting close to each other – such is the vastness of the flowers there.

**aḻundūr mēl tisai ninṟa ammānai** – sarvēśvaran who is greater than all and is standing in the western side of tiruvaḻundūr.

**kanni mannu tiṇ tōḷ …** – āḻvār who is having shoulders which will never lose strength, is the one who controls tiruvāli region and is also the ancient king of the residents of tirumangai region.

**sonna in tamiḻ …** – This garland which is sweet to listen to and which is like a garland of precious stones. Those who are able to recite this decad which has no shortcomings in its poems.

**manni mannavarāy** – Being the king for a long time. They will get to control all the kingdoms and remain under a huge pearl umbrella and will become blissful. An important question is asked here “Why is āḻvār, who feared being subdued by the senses, showing this wealth as the result?” periyavāccān piḷḷai quotes parāśara bhattar’s words “For āḻvār, even that wealth can be used to serve bhāgavatas and hence it will become part of his goal”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8 Sengamalat tirumagalum

## 7.8.1. Sengamalat tirumagalum

*sengamalat tirumagaḷum puviyum sembontiruvadiyin iṇai varuda munivar ēttavangamali tadangadaluḷ anantan ennumvariyaravin aṇait tuyinṟa māyōn kāṇminengumali niṟai pugaḻ nāl vēdam ainduvēḷvigaḷum kēḷvigaḷum iyanṟa tanmaiangamalattu ayan anaiyār payilum selvattuaṇiyaḻundūr ninṟuganda amarar kōvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

engum – in all sentences; mali – having abundance (of being pramāṇam, credible source for knowledge); nāl vēdam – by the four vēdams; aindu vēḷvi – by the panca mahā yajñams; kēḷvigaḷum – (further) important portions which are to be heard; iyanṟa – great; nanmai – having noble nature; am kamalattu – having the beautiful flower on the divine navel as his birth place; ayan anaiyār – brāhmaṇas who are matching brahmā; payilum – due to residing eternally; selvattu – having wealth; aṇi – being an ornament for this leelā vibhūti; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; ugandu ninṟa – one who is joyfully residing there; amarar kō – emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris; sem kamalam – having beautiful lotus flower as her abode; tirumagaḷum – periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi); puviyum – śrī bhūmip pirātti; sem pon – beautiful and desirable; tiruvadiyin iṇai – pair of divine feet; varuda – as they hold; munivar – sages such as sanaka et al; ētta – as they praise; vangam – boats; mali – present abundantly; tadam – vast; kadaluḷ – in the ocean; anantan ennum – known famously as anantan; vari – having stripes; aravin aṇai – on the mattress named tiruvanantāḻvān; tuyinṟa – mercifully reclining; māyōn kāṇmin – behold, he is the sarvēśvaran

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is having the wealth of brāhmaṇas who are as good as brahmā, who is having the beautiful lotus flower in the divine navel as his birth-place, and who are having great nature of being focussed on the a) four vēdams which are having sentences which are filled with being the credible source of true knowledge and are having complete fame due to that, b) panca mahā yajñams and c) important portions which are to be heard. It is an ornament for this leelā vibhūti. emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris and is joyfully residing in such divyadēśam, is having his beautiful, desirable pair of divine feet held (massaged) by periya pirāttiyār, śrī mahālakśmi who is having beautiful lotus flower as her abode and śrī bhūmip pirāttiyār. Sages such as sanaka et al are praising him. In the vast (milk) ocean which is filled with boats, on the striped mattress, which is famously known as tiruvanantāḻvān, such sarvēśvaran is mercifully reclining. Behold that same bhagavān, who is mercifully present in tiruvaḻundūr.

**sengamalat tirumagaḷum** – periya pirāttiyār who makes bhagavān forgive all the mistakes of the devotees.

**puviyum** – śrī bhūmip pirātti who is the teacher for such patience. As both of them massage the divine feet, which are matching each other and are desirable, as sanaka et al remain firm and praise.

**vanga mali tadam kadaluḷ** – The great ocean which has a lot of boats.

**anantan ennum** – Atop the one who is famously known as tiruvanantāḻvān. sarvēśvaran is also said to be anantan since he is beyond limits by time, place and objects; since ādiśēśan has kept such anantan on his lap, ādiśēśan is also known famously as anantan.

**vari aravin aṇait tuyinṟa māyōn kāṇmin** – Like a fire ball, ādiśēśan is having such beautiful stripes that sarvēśvaran cannot take his eyes off ādiśēśan. Behold, it is the same sarvēśvaran, who is mercifully reclining on tiruvanantāḻvān who is having coolness, fragrance etc as his nature, who has arrived here and standing.

**engum mali niṟai pugaḻ …** – The credible nature of vēdam is not in a few portions but every part of vēdam is credible. Hence it is having great fame. Those who are having natural greatness through such four vēdams, panca mahā yajñam (brahma yajña, dēva yajña, pitru yajña, manuśya yajña, bhūta yajña) and whatever has to be learnt through hearing.

**akkamalattu ayan anaiyār** – bhagavān is mercifully standing in tiruvaḻundūr which is having matchless wealth due to the eternal presence of brāhmaṇas who are individually as good as brahmā and who can engage in creation etc. Such bhagavān who granted me this impossible benefit is sarvēśvaran who is known as in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (Lord of nityasūris who have no confusion). āḻvār is saying “Surrender unto him and be uplifted”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.2. Munnivulagaelum

*mun ivvulagēḻum iruḷ maṇḍi uṇṇa munivarodu dānavargaḷ tisaippa vandupannu kalai nāl vēdap poruḷai ellām parimugamāy aruḷiya em paraman kāṇminsennelmali kadirk kavari vīsac cangam avai muralac cengamala malarai ēṟiannam mali pedaiyōdum amarum selvattu aṇiyaḻundūr ninṟuganda amarar kōvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem nel – best paddy crops’; mali kadir – having abundant ears, they; kavari vīsa – as they fan like cāmara; avai – moving around there; sangam – the conces; murala – as they blow; sem – beautiful; kamala malarai – on lotus flower; ēṟi – climbing; annam – swan; mali – very enjoyable; pedaiyōdum – along with its female spouse; amarum – remaining firm and sleeping; selvattu – having wealth; aṇi – being an ornament for this leelā vibhūti; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; ugandu ninṟa – one who is joyfully residing there; amarar kō – Oh, emperumān who is the lord of nityasūris!; mun – in the past; ivvēḻulagum – these seven worlds; iruḷ – ignorance in the form of darkness; maṇḍi – overpowered; uṇṇa – while consuming (i.e. enslaving it); munivarodu – along with sages such as sanaka et al; dānavargaḷ – the rākśasas (demons); tisaippa – becoming bewildered (at that time); vandu – came (bhagavān descending from paramapadam); pannu – vast; kalai – having śāstram; nāl vēdam – the four vēdams, their; poruḷai ellām – all the meanings; pari mugamāy – being hayagrīvan; aruḷiya – one who mercifully instructed; em paraman kāṇmin – he is our leader of all

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is having the wealth of best paddy crops’ abundant ears, which are fanning like cāmaras, the conces remaining there are blowing and the swans climb on the beautiful lotus flowers, firmly remaining there and sleeping along with their female spouse. emperumān is joyfully residing in such tiruvaḻundūr, which is an ornament for the leelā vibhūti. In the past, when ignorance in the form of darkness overpowered the seven worlds and consumed them, the sages such as sanaka et al, rākśasas remained in a bewildered state, bhagavān descended from paramapadam in the form of hayagrīva (horse-headed) and mercifully instructed the meanings of four vēdams which are having vast śāstrams. That same bhagavān is mercifully present in tiruvaḻundūr.

**mun ivvulagu ēḻum iruḷ maṇḍi uṇṇa** – In the past, the darkness expanded and consumed the seven worlds.

**munivarodu tānavargaḷ tisaippa** – Both sātvika (sages, who are remaining in satva guṇam (noble qualties)) and asātvika (demons, who are remaining in rajō and tamō guṇam), without difference, became bewildered. At that time, he incarnated as hayagrīva mūrti and mercifully instructed the meanings of four types of vēdams which have vast śāstrams. That sarvēśvaran is present in tiruvaḻundūr.

**sem nel mali kadirk kavari vīsa** – The heavy ears of the paddy crops are fanning like cāmara \[covry or fly-flapper\].

**sangam avai murala** – The conces which are moving around, are blowing.

**sem kamala malarai ēṟi** – Climbing on the fresh lotus flowers, considering them to be the mattress.

**annam mali pedaiyōdum amarum selvattu** – The swan resting on such lotus flower mattress along with its female spouse which is more enjoyable than it. Having such wealth. Even the birds in this divyadēśam are most enjoyable.

## 7.8.3. Kulattalaiya

*kulattalaiya mada vēḻam poygai pukkukkōḷ mudalai pidikka adaṟku anungi ninṟunilattigaḻum malarc cudarēy sōdī! ennanenjidar tīrttaruḷiya en nimalan kāṇminmalaittigaḻ sandagil kanagamaṇiyum koṇḍuvandundi vayalgaḷ toṟum madaigaḷ pāyaalaittu varum ponni vaḷam perugum selvattuaṇiyaḻundūr ninṟuganda amarar kōvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

malai – in the sahya mountain; tigaḻ – shining; sandu – sandalwood trees; agil – agil \[eaglevood\] logs; kanagam – gold; maṇiyum – precious gemstones; koṇḍu vandu – gathering together and coming; undi – pushing; vayalgaḷ tōṟum – in every fertile field; madaigaḷ – in the channels; pāya – to flow; alaittuvarum – coming with waves which are thrown up; ponni – tirukkāvēri; vaḷam – abundantly; perugum – due to flowing; selvattu – having wealth; aṇi – being an ornament for this leelā vibhūti; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; ugandu ninṟa – one who is joyfully residing there; amarar kō – emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris; kulam – born with good pedigree (among the elephants); talaiya – best; madam – intoxicated; vēḻam – śrī gajēndram; poygai – in the pond; pukku – entered (and while standing there); kōḷ – having strength; mudalai – crocodile; pidikka – as it catches its feet and pulls in; adaṟku – for that crocodile; anungi ninṟu – fearing; nila – moonlight; tigaḻum – making it shine everywhere; malar – expansive; sudar – the radiant moon; ēy – matching; sōdi – Oh, one who is having cool radiance!; enna – as it called (he mercifully arrived there); nenju – present in its mind; idar – sorrow; tīrttu aruḷiya – one who mercifully got rid; en – one who manifested that to me; nimalan kaṇḍīr – behold one who became pure (by that act)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Divine kāvēri river is gathering the sandalwood tree, agil logs, gold and precious gemstones which are shining in the sahya mountain and pushing them into the fertile fields flowing through the channels, with rising waves. tiruvaḻundūr is having the wealth due to the abundantly flowing divine kāvēri. It is an ornament for this leelā vibhūti. emperumān is the lord of nityasūris and is joyfully residing in such divyadēśam. śrī gajēndrāḻvān, who is the chief among elephants, having best pedigree and is intoxicated, entered the pond. At that time, the strong crocodile caught śrī gajēndrāḻvān’s feet and pulled it in. śrī gajēndrāḻvān called out saying “Oh one who is having cool radiance of the radiant moon which is expansive due to the moonlight which makes it shine everywhere!”. bhagavān mercifully arrived there and mercifully got rid of its mental agony. Behold that bhagavān, who manifested such vision to me and became pure due to that.

**kulattalaiya mada vēḻam** – Being the chief among elephants, having the best pedigree, being intoxicated, the elephant which is roaming around freely, without realising what is coming, entered into the habitat which is not natural for it, and got caught by the cruel crocodile.

**kōḷ mudalai pidikka** – Being cursed, the crocodile was waiting for a remedy thinking “When will the elephant become trapped by me?” Caught by such crocodile.

**adaṟku anungi ninṟu** – Became frightened of that, remaining actionless when the crocodile was in full action.

**nilat tigaḻum malarc cudarēy sōdi enna** – Moon which is having expansion due to the spread of moonlight. śrī gajēndrāḻvān requested bhagavān to appear with the coolness/mercy of such moon.

**nenju idar tīrttu aruḷiya en nimalan kāṇmin** – Accepting the flower held by śrī gajēndrāḻvān, before it loses its freshness, at his lotus feet and thus mercifully eliminated its mental agony. Behold one who manifested his purity of having the nature of eliminating the obstacles for his devotees and fulfilling their desires.

**malait tigaḻ sandu agil kanaga maṇiyum koṇḍu** – Gathering the sandalwood tree, agil logs, gold and precious gemstones which are shining in the sahya mountain.

**vandu undi …** – Just as a person who cannot tolerate the weight will drop heavy objects, ponni (kāvēri) is flowing into every fertile field through the channels. Having such great wealth of having constant flow of the river kāvēri along with precious objects. Just as he \[emperumān\] would go to places where people are suffering and protect them, this river too would flow wherever it is required.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.4. Silambu mudal

*silambu mudal kalan aṇindōr sengal kunṟamtigaḻndadenat tiruvuruvam panṟi āgiilangu puvi madandai tanai idandu pulgieyiṟṟidai vaittaruḷiya em īsan kāṇminpulambu siṟai vaṇḍolippap pūgam tokkappoḻilgaḷ toṟum kuyil kūva mayilgaḷ ālaalambu tiraip punal pudai sūḻndu aḻagār selvattuaṇiyaḻundūr ninṟuganda amarar kōvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pulambu – shining beautifully; siṟai – having wings; vaṇḍu – beetles; olippa – as they are humming; pūgam – areca trees; tokka – dense; poḻilgaḷ toṟum – in all the orchards; kuyil – cuckoos; kūva – as they coo; mayilgaḷ – the peacocks; Ala – as they dance; alambu – swaying; tirai – having waves; punal – water; pudai – in the surroundings; sūḻndu – having pervaded; aḻagu Ar – having abundant beauty; selvattu – having wealth; aṇi – being an ornament for this leelā vibhūti; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; ugandu ninṟa – one who is joyfully residing there; amarar kō – emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris; ōr – unique; sem kal – having reddish precious gemstones; kunṟam – mēru mountain; tigaḻndadu ena – shining like; silambu mudal – anklets etc; kalan – ornaments; aṇindu – wearing; tiruvuruvam – having beautiful form; panṟiyāgi – incarnated as mahā varāham; ilangu – shining; puvi madandai tanai – śrī bhūmippirātti; idandu – digging out (from the wall of the oval shaped universe); pulgi – united with her; eyiṟu idai – in between the tusks; vaittu aruḷiya – one who mercifully placed and climbed up; em – for us (due to that); īsan kāṇmin – behold the sarvēśvaran who controls us

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is having the wealth of orchards where beetles, which have shining, beautiful wings are humming and areca trees are densely present. Cuckoos are cooing and peacocks are dancing. Water, which is having swaying waves, are pervading the surroundings. In this manner, the town is abundantly beautiful. emperumān is the lord of nityasūris and is joyfully residing in such divyadēśam. He incarnated as mahā varāham, who is having beautiful form which is decorated with ornaments such as anklets etc which look like mēru mountain which is having unique, reddish precious gemstones. He dug out the shining śrī bhūmip pirātti from the wall of the oval shaped universe and placed her in between his tusks and mercifully climbed up. Because of this, he is the sarvēśvaran who controls all of us. Behold that same bhagavān, who is mercifully present in tiruvaḻundūr.

**silambu mudal kalan aṇindu** – Being decorated with many ornaments such as anklets etc, one who is having varāha form, like a shining mēru mountain.

**ilangu puvi …** – Climbing up with the earth, digging it up from the wall of the oval shaped universe where the earth was stuck, embracing śrī bhūmip pirātti who is the controlling dēvatā for the earth and mercifully having that earth on his divine tusk like blue gem embossed there. Showing that act, he enslaved me. Such bhagavān.

**pulambu siṟai vaṇḍu olippa** – Beetles, which have beautiful wings, are humming due to being drunk with honey.

**pūgam tokkap poḻilgaḷ toṟum kuyilgaḷ kūva** – In the orchards which have densely populated areca trees, where cuckoos are cooing, like muktātmās sing sāma gānam.

**mayilgaḷ Ala** – As the peacocks dance according to the songs of the cuckoos.

**alambu tiraip punal pudai sūḻndu aḻagār selvattu** … – The water which is coming with swaying waves, is spreading in all the surroundings. In tiruvaḻundūr which is having such wealth and is like an ornament for the samsāra vibhūti (material world).

## 7.8.5. Sinamevum

*sinamēvum adal ariyin uruvamāgittiṟal mēvum iraṇiyanadu āgam kīṇḍumanamēvu vanjanaiyāl vanda pēyccimāḷa uyir vavviya em māyōn kāṇmininamēvu varivaḷaikkai ēndum kōvaiēyvāya maragadam pōl kiḷiyin insolanamēvu nadai madavār payilum selvattuaṇiyaḻundūr ninṟuganda amarar kōvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

inam mēvum – arranged well, in rows; vari – beautiful; vaḷai kai – with hands having bangles; ēndum – held; kōvai ēy – like kōvai fruit; vāya – having mouth; maragadam pōl – having complexion similar to emerald green; kiḷiyin – parrots’; in sol – having sweet words; anam mēvum – like swan; nadai – having beautiful gait; madavār – women; payilum – eternally residing; selvattu – having wealth; aṇi – being an ornament for this leelā vibhūti; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; ugandu ninṟa – one who is joyfully residing there; amarar kō – emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris; mēvum sinam – having great anger; adal – having strength; ariyin uruvam āgi – having narasimha form; tiṟal mēvum – very strong; āgam – body; kīṇḍu – one who tore; manam mēvum – fixed in the mind; vanjanaiyāl – by deceit; vanda – came (to kill); pēycci – pūtanā; māḷa – to be killed; uyir – her vital air; vavviya – being the one who consumed; em – (that amazing act) for me (one who manifested); māyōn kāṇmin – behold, he is the same amazing lord

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is having the wealth of being the eternal abode of women, who are having rows of bangles decorated in their hands, who are having sweet speech of parrots which have kōvai (a reddish) fruit like mouth and complexion similar to emerald green, and who are having the beautiful gait matching that of a swan. It is an ornament for this leelā vibhūti. emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris and is joyfully residing in such divyadēśam, is having the narasimha form with great anger and strength, and tore the very strong body of hiraṇya. He consumed the vital air of pūtanā, who is having deceit in her mind, to kill her. He is the amazing lord who manifested such amazing acts to me. Behold that same bhagavān, who is mercifully present in tiruvaḻundūr.

**sinam mēvum adal ariyin uruvam āgi** – As hiraṇya charged on towards prahlāda, the child, with great anger, being unable to tolerate that, bhagavān assumed the form of narasimha which appeared to be made of anger and which is not easily approachable.

**tiṟal mēvum iraṇiyanadu āgam kīṇḍu** – Tearing hiraṇya’s body, which is very strong to make even narasimha bhagavān to step back.

**manam mēvum …** – Instead of acquiring compassion in the heart on seeing the age of kriṣṇa which will make (even an evil) one to say “My bad! Why should we kill this child?”, she is having deceit which is firmly placed in her heart. To make such pūtanā die, he mercifully consumed her vital airs through her bosom. Such amazing lord has arrived and is standing here.

**inam mēvum …** – Being held by the hands which have beautiful bangles, being similar to parrrots in having kōvai fruit like reddish lips, having emerald green like complexion, having the sweet speech of the parrot. The speech of the women who teach and the parrots (which are trained) cannot be differentiated. Having matcless wealth due to the women who are having swan like gait, residing densely.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.6. Vanavar tam

*vānavar tam tuyar tīra vandu tōnṟimāṇuruvāy mūvadi māvaliyai vēṇḍittānamara ēḻulagum aḷanda venṟittani mudal sakkarap padai en talaivan kāṇmintēnamarum poḻil taḻuvum eḻil koḷ vīdicceḻumāda māḷigaigaḷ kūdandōṟumāna tol sīr maṟaiyāḷar payilum selvattuaṇiyaḻundūr ninṟuganda amarar kōvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēn – honey; amarum – continuously flowing; poḻil – in the orchards; taḻuvum – being surrounded; eḻil koḷ – being very beautiful; vīdi – in the streets; seḻu – beautiful; mādam – in the maṇḍapams; māḷigaigaḷ – in the palaces; kūdam tōṟum – in the homes; Ana – being filled with noble qualities; tol sīr – having ancient (indestructible) fame; maṟaiyāḷar – brāhmaṇas, who are engaged in learning/reciting vēdams; payilum – densely residing; selvattu – having wealth; aṇi – being an ornament for this leelā vibhūti; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; ugandu ninṟa – one who is joyfully residing there; amarar kō – emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris; vānavar tam – dēvatās’; tuyar tīra – to eliminate the sorrows; tān – He (who is omnipresent and has no unfulfilled desires); māṇ uruvāy – having vāmana form; vandu tōnṟi – came and incarnated; māvaliyai – from mahābali; mūvadi – three steps; vēṇḍi – begged (as he got it); ēḻulagum – seven worlds; amara – to remain (at his divine feet); aḷandu – one who scaled; venṟi – victorious; tani – unique; mudal – primary (among weapons); sakkaram – sudarśana chakra; padai – one who is having as weapon; en talaivan – my lord; kāṇmin – behold, he is the same sarvēśvaran

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is having the wealth of brāhmaṇas who are engaged in learning/reciting vēdams and are densely residing in the beautiful mandapams, palaces, homes and streets which are very beautiful due to being surrounded by orchards where honey is continuously flowing. emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris and is joyfully residing in such divyadēśam, came and incarnated in the form of a vāmana \[dwarf\] to eliminate the sorrows of the dēvatas. He begged for three steps from such mahābali and took over all the seven worlds under his divine feet. He is having the victorious, unique and primary weapon, sudarśana cakram. Behold that same bhagavān, who is mercifully present in tiruvaḻundūr.

**vānavar tam tuyar tīra** – bhagavān came and incarnated for the sake of dēvatās who would say “I am īśvara” immediately after getting help from bhagavān, instead of those who are totally surrendered to him and who remain knowing nothing but him and remain as said in [tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci 10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppalliyezhuchchi-10-kadimalar/) “*todai otta tuḷavamum kūdaiyum polindu tōnṟiya*” (manifesting the shining shoulders which carry the flower-basket that contains properly prepared tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garlands).

**māṇ uruvāy** – Having a form which reflects expertise in begging as in “If I don’t get by begging from him, I will not survive”, thinking that he does not have three steps of land, thinking that mahābali is the one who is having that, bhagavān accepted through pouring of water from mahābali’s hand and grew to have the seven worlds under his divine feet.

**venṟit tani mudal cakkarap padai** – Having tiruvāḻi (divine chakra) which is victorious, unique and the primary among all the weapons as the tool, he is my lord. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.5.17 “*trivikrama: kramākrānta trailōkyas spuratāyuda:*” (the weapons rose when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) set out to measure the worlds), he is the one who is having divine weapons. “*jitam bhagavatā jagat*” (bhagavān won over the universe).

**tēn amarum poḻil taḻuvum eḻil koḷ vīdi** – The streets which are surrounded by orchards where honey is continuously flowing.

**seḻu mādam …** – Beautiful mansions, palaces, homes, halls and other spacious places – everywhere.

**Ana tol sīr …** – Having the wealth due to the dense population of brāhmaṇas who are abundantly endowed with knowledge and in turn humility and ancient fame. tiruvaḻundūr is their divyadēśam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.7. Pandanainda

*pandaṇainda melviralāḷ sīdaikkāgippagalavan mīdiyangāda ilangai vēndanandamil tiṇkaram sirangaḷ puraṇḍu vīḻaadu kaṇaiyāl eyduganda ammān kāṇminsendamiḻum vadagalaiyum tigaḻnda nāvartisaimuganē anaiyavargaḷ semmai mikkaandaṇar tam āgudiyin pugaiyār selvattuaṇiyaḻundūr ninṟuganda amarar kōvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem tamiḻum – beautiful drāvida vēdam (which can easily reveal its meaning); vada kalaiyum – samskruta vēdam; tigaḻnda – shining; nāvar – having tongue; tisaimuganē – as good as brahmā; anaiyavargaḷ – having greatness; mikka semmai – having very distinguished nature; andaṇar tam – brāhmaṇas’; āgudiyin – arising from the āhuti (offering, in yajña); pugai Ar – smoke filled; selvattu – having wealth; aṇi – being an ornament for this leelā vibhūti; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; ugandu ninṟa – one who is joyfully residing there; amarar kō – emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris; pandu aṇainda – being together with the ball; mel – tender; viralāḷ – having fingers; sīdaikkāgi – for the sake of sītāp pirātti; pagalavan – sun; mīdu – atop; iyangāda – cannot roam (having such fort); ilangai – of lankā; vēndan – rāvaṇa, the king, his; andam il – limitless; tiṇ – strong; karam – arms; sirangaḷ – heads; puraṇḍu vīḻa – to sever and fall down; adu kaṇaiyāl – with the arrows which can kill; eydu uganda – shot (and killed) and became joyful; ammān kāṇmin – behold, he is the sarvēśvaran

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is having the wealth of being filled with smoke rising from the āhuti (offering) given by brāhmaṇas, who are having greatness which is as good as brahmā’s greatness, having very distinguished nature and having tongue which is shining with drāvida vēdam and samskruta vēdam. emperumān is the lord of nityasūris and is joyfully residing in such divyadēśam. He is the sarvēśvaran who shot the arrows which can kill, aiming at the limitless and strong arms and heads of rāvaṇa, the king of lankā where sun cannot roam atop the place. emperumān severed such rāvaṇa’s hands and heads, which fell off, and killed him for the sake of sītāp pirātti who is having tender fingers, which are always attached with a play ball. He became joyful doing that. Behold that same bhagavān, who is mercifully present in tiruvaḻundūr.

**pandu aṇainda …** – For the sake of the union with periya pirāttiyār who is so youthful to hold on to the ball even in the presence of sarvēśvaran and who is having fingers which are very tender to even hold that ball. The reason for their separation, rāvaṇa, who is the ruler of lankā which is fortified to limit the movement of moon and sun. His,

**andam il …** – They \[heads\] are limitless since they keep coming back even after severing. To have the strong shoulders and heads break apart and fall off, shooting him with a killer arrow and killed him, sarvēśvaran enjoyed the bliss which is to be had by the followers thinking “Our enemy is eliminated; the devotees have regained their abodes”. Such sarvēśvaran.

**sem tamiḻ …**

**sem tamiḻum** – tamiḻ which can directly show the meanings.

**vada kalaiyum** … – samskrutam. Those who are having the tongue where these are shining.

**tisaimuganē anaiyavargaḷ** – The abode of brāhmaṇas who are individually capable to engage in creation like brahmā.

**semmai …** – tiruvaḻundūr which is an ornament for this world, which is having the smoke from the hōma (fire sacrifice) of very distinguished brāmaṇas and beautiful wealth.

## 7.8.8. Kumbamigu

*kumbamigu mada vēḻam kulaiyak kombupaṟittu maḻa vidai adarttuk kuravai kōttuvambaviḻum malark kuḻalāḷ āycci vaittatayir veṇṇey uṇḍuganda māyōn kāṇminsembavaḷa maragadam nanmuttam kāttattigaḻ pūgam kadali pala vaḷam mikku engumambon madiḷ poḻil pudai sūḻndu aḻagār selvattuaṇiyaḻundūr ninṟuganda amarar kōvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem pavaḷam – reddish coral (fruits in areca trees); maragadam – emerald green (their unripen fruits); nal muttam – good pearls (their flowers); kātta – showing; pūgam – by arecas; tigaḻ – shining; pala – many; kadali – bananas; vaḷam – abundance; engum – everywhere; mikku – being great; am pon – very desirable; madiḷ – having forts; poḻil – by orchards; pudai – in the surroundings; sūḻndu – being surrounded; aḻagu Ar – very beautiful; selvattu – having wealth; aṇi – being an ornament for this leelā vibhūti; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; ugandu ninṟa – one who is joyfully residing there; amarar kō – emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris; migu kumbam – having huge head; madam – exultant; vēḻam – kuvalayāpeedam; kulaiya – to be destroyed; kombu – its tusks; paṟittu – plucked; maḻam – youthful; vidai – bulls; adarttu – crushed; kuravai – in rāsa krīdā; kōttu – holding hands (with the women); vambu – fragrance; aviḻum – spreading; malar – flowers’; kuḻalāḷ – having locks; āycci – yaśōdāp pirātti; vaitta – preserved; tayir – curd; veṇṇey – butter; uṇḍu – mercifully consumed; uganda – became joyful; māyōn kāṇmin – behold, he is the amazing lord

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is having the wealth of the great beauty of being surrounded by greatly fortified orchards in the surroundings, having the shine of areca trees which can show reddish coral in the fruits, emerald green in the unripen fruits and good pearls in the flowers and having abundance of plantains everywhere. emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris and is joyfully residing in such divyadēśam, is the one who plucked the tusks of exultant and large headed elephant, kuvalayāpeedam, to have it destroyed; he held the hands of the women in rāsa krīdā and mercifully consumed the curd and butter which were preserved by yaśōdāp pirātti who is having locks which are decorated with flower which spread fragrance. Behold that same bhagavān, who is mercifully present in tiruvaḻundūr.

**kumbam migu mada vēḻam** – Having a head which is wounded due to fighting with elephants and rocks, the extultant kuvalayāpeedam was knocked down like a small wall by plucking its tusks effortlessly.

**maḻa vidai adarttu** – Youthful by age, the seven bulls which are saying “Show me! Show me!” and were looking like mrtyu (Death personified) were killed.

**kuravai kōttu** – Placing himself in the middle of rāsa krīdā of women, and holding their hands.

**vambu aviḻum …** – One who eliminated the enemies personally, due to being unable to sustain without the food items which are directly prepared by his devotees; he mercifully consumed the curd and butter which were preserved by yaśōdāp pirātti who is having locks which are decorated with very fragrant flowers. He is the amazing lord who remains as if he has attained impossible goal, due to enjoying those curd and butter.

**sem pavaḷa maragada nanmuttam kātta** – In the areca trees there, the swathes show the pearls, the unripen fruits show the emerald and the ripen fruits show the coral. Thus, the place has all three of these beautiful aspects enjoyable at once, and having acquired beauty by the abundance of plantains and is desirable. tiruvaḻundūr which is having fortified orchards, is the abode of such bhagavān.

## 7.8.9. Uderu kanjanodu

*ūdēṟu kanjanodu mallum villumoṇ kariyum uruḷsagadum udaiyac ceṟṟanīdēṟu peruvalit tōḷudaiya venṟinilavu pugaḻ nēmi angai nediyōn kāṇminsēdēṟu poḻil taḻuvum eḻil koḷ vīdittiruviḻavil maṇi aṇinda tiṇṇai tōṟumādēṟu malark kuḻalār payilum selvattuaṇiyaḻundūr ninṟuganda amarar kōvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sēdu ēṟu – being very youthful; poḻil – by the orchards; taḻuvum – pervaded everywhere; eḻil koḷ – having beauty; vīdi – in the divine streets; tiruviḻavil – in the utsavams; maṇi – by precious gemstones; aṇinda – decorated; tiṇṇai tōṟum – in every pial \[a raisaed platform at the frontyard of houses\]; ādu ēṟu – being very fragrant; malar – decorated by flowers; kuḻalār – women, who have locks; payilum – residing densely; selvattu – having wealth; aṇi – being an ornament for this leelā vibhūti; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; ugandu ninṟa – one who is joyfully residing there; amarar kō – emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris; ūdu ēṟu – climbed up on the middle (of the raised platform); kanjanodu – with kamsan; mallum – the group of wrestlers such as cāṇūra et al; villum – the bow; oḷ – beautiful (strong); kariyum – kuvalayāpeedam; uruḷ – rolling forward; sagadum – śakatāsuran; udaiya – to break; seṟṟa – one who destroyed (them); nīdu ēṟu – growing more and more; peru vali – having great strength; tōḷ udaiya – having shoulders; venṟi – victory; nilavu – due to being present (always); pugaḻ – having fame; nēmi – tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); am kai – holding in his beautiful divine hand; nediyōn – he is the sarvēśvaran

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tiruvaḻundūr is having the wealth of densely residing women, who have locks which are decorated with very fragrant flowers, the pials which are decorated the precious stones during utsavams (festivals) in the beautiful divine streets, and is being pervaded by orchards which are very youthful. emperumān, who is the lord of nityasūris and is joyfully residing in such divyadēśam, broke and destroyed kamsan, who had climbed up to the middle of the raised platform, the group of wrestlers such as cāṇūra et al, the bow, the strong kuvalayāpeedam and śakatāsuran who was rolling forward. He is having shoulders whose strength is ever-growing and is holding the divine chakra which is having ever-growing fame due to continuous victory. He is the supreme lord who is greater than all. Behold that same bhagavān, who is mercifully present in tiruvaḻundūr.

**ūdēṟu kanjanaodu** – kamsan who climbed up and stood on a raised platform due to his fear, along with the group of wrestlers who were placed for his protection.

**villum** – The bow which was placed as the main aspect of the bow festival.

**oṇkariyum** – kuvalayāpeedam which was placed there to kill kriṣṇa. kamsan was thinking to cry saying “The elephant killed kriṣṇa”.

**uruḷ sagadam** – The cart wheel which was possessed by a demon, aimed to attack kriṣṇa who was still in cradle stage.

**udaiyac ceṟṟa** – āḻvār is able to clearly visualise these acts as if the enemies were killed at once. Such is āḻvār’s expansive knowledge.

**nīdēṟu peruvalit tōḷudaiya …** – Having shoulders which become strong as days go by and having in his hand the divine chakra which is having the fame of being victorious always. Such sarvēśvaran is in this divyadēśam.

**sēdēṟu poḻil …** – Being surrounded by very youthful orchards, in the divine streets which are very beautiful due to that, in every pial which is having precious gemstones embossed in there during divine festive days, women who have locks which are decorated with very fragrant flowers, are present densely. In tiruvaḻundūr which is having wealth based on such aspects. ādu – fragrance. Locks decorated with very fragrant flowers.

## 7.8.10. Panriyay minagi

*panṟiyāy mīnāgi ariyāyp pāraippadaittuk kāttu uṇḍu umiḻnda paraman tannaianṟu amararkku adi padiyum ayanum sēyumadi paṇiya aṇiyaḻundūr ninṟa kōvaikanṟi neduvēl valavan āli nādankalikanṟi oli seyda inbap pādalonṟinodu nāngum ōraindum vallārolikadal sūḻ ulagāḷum umbar tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

panṟiyāy – as mahāvarāham (wild boar); mīnāy – as matsyam (fish); ariyāy – incarnating as narasmiham (lion-man) too; pārai – earth; padaittu – created; kāttu – protected; uṇḍu – consumed (during deluge); umiḻnda – let out (during creation); paraman tannai – being supreme lord; anṟu – at that time; amararkku – for dēvatās; adi padiyum – indran, who is the king; ayanum – brahmā; sēyum – rudran (his son); adi paṇiya – to fall at his feet and surrender; aṇi – being an ornament for samsāram; aḻundūr – in tiruvaḻundūr; ninṟa – one who is mercifully residing with joy; kōvai – on sarvēśvaran, who is the lord of nityasūris; kanṟi – stained; nedu – lengthy; vēl – spear, the weapon; valavan – one who can hold; Ali nādan – the leader of tiruvāli region; kali kanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; oli seyda – mercifully spoken to have \[beautiful\] tune; inbam – sweet; onṟinodu – with one pāsuram; nāngum – four pāsurams; ōr aindum – (subsequently) another five pāsurams; pādal – thus, these ten pāsurams; vallār – those who can recite; oli – resounding; kadal sūḻ – surrounded by ocean; ulagu – worlds; āḷum – capable of ruling over; umbar tām – will become dēvatās

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is greater than all and incarnated as mahāvarāham, matsyam and narasihmam, and created the earth, protected it, consumed it during deluge, and let it out during creation. sarvēśvaran, who is the lord of nityasūris, is mercifully residing with joy in tiruvaḻundūr, which is an ornament for this samsāram. indran who is the king of dēvatās, brahmā and his son rudran fell at his feet and surrendered to him then. On such sarvēśvaran, tirumangai āḻvār, who can wield the stained and lengthy spear and who is the leader of the tiruvāli region, mercifully spoke the ten sweet pāsurams which are made of one plus four plus five pāsurams, with tune. Those who are able to recite these pāsurams will become dēvatās who can rule over the worlds which are surrounded by the resounding ocean.

**panṟiyāy …** – If protecting the devotees is the task to be done, he would do it without caring for him.

**pārai …** – Creating the earth. In the form of mahāvarāham etc

**kāttu …**– Protecting the earth. Again, as the deluge occurs, he protects the earth by keeping it in his stomach. Subsequently, lets it out. In this manner, while protecting in every aspect, if we count him, there is none to be counted along, since he is greater than everyone.

**anṟu amararkku …** – The abode where even brahmā et al, who are prideful, can come and surrender unto him and fulfil their desires. indran who is the controller of all dēvatās, brahmā, who has a distinguished birth than all others and his son, rudran.

**adi paṇiya** – To surrender unto his divine feet. The supreme lord who is mercifully standing in tiruvaḻundūr.

**kanṟi nedu vēl …** – There is no time to remove the stains after killing the enemies. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 100.12 “*ālikantamivākāsam avaśtabhya* ***mahaddanu****:*” (One who is tightly holding the great bow which reaches up to the sky), he is wielding in his hand, the lengthy spear which cannot be held and controlled by anyone. āḻvār, who is owning tiruvāli region, composed these ten sweet pāsurams, which are having tune. Those who can recite these pāsurams. They are to be enjoyed in groups as said in “*onṟinodu nāngum ōr aindum*” \[First pāsuram talks about kśīrābdi, four pāsurams (2nd, 4th, 5th and 10th) about incarnations in animal form and five pāsurams (3rd, 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th) talk about incarnations in celestial and human forms\]. For those who can recite these pāsurams, there is no shortcoming in attaining the post such as brahmā \[all of the dēvatās are positions held by different ātmās at different times\]. Our ācāryas mercifully explain “Since tirumangai āḻvār is able to engage wealth in bhagavān’s purpose, he encouraged acquiring wealth”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9 Kallam manam

## 7.9.1. Kallam manam

*kaḷḷam manam viḷḷum vagai karudik kaḻal toḻuvīrveḷḷam mudu paravait tirai viriyak karai engumteḷḷum maṇi tigaḻum siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattuuḷḷum enadu uḷḷattuḷum uṟaivārai uḷḷīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaḷḷam – Having deceit of stealing the ātmā; manam – heart; viḷḷum vagai – the way to escape (such stealing of ātmā); karudi – desiring; kaḻal – (sarvēśvaran’s) divine feet; toḻuvīr – Oh, those who are desirous to surrender!; mudu – ancient; paravai – present in the ocean; tirai – caused by the waves; veḷḷam – the flood; karai engum – on the shores; viriya – as it spreads; teḷḷum – pushed out (by those tides); maṇi – precious gems; tigaḻum – shining; siṟupuliyūr – having the divine name siṟupuliyūr; salasayanattu uḷḷum – bhagavān who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water) is reclining in this divyadēśam and; enadu – my; uḷḷattuḷḷum – in heart; uṟaivārai – one who is eternally residing; uḷḷīr – meditate upon \[him\]

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, those who are desirous to have a change of deceit in heart and surrender unto sarvēśvaran’s divine feet! sarvēśVaran who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is eternally residing in a reclining posture in this divyadēśam having the divine name siṟupuliyūr where shining, precious gems are pushed out by the flood on the shores of the ocean, the spreading of which is caused by the waves which are present in the ocean, and \[is also residing\] my heart.

**kaḷḷam manam viḷḷum vagai** – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 109.34 “*yatāhi cōras satatāhi budda:*” (Just as a thief should be driven out, one who rejects vēdam should also be driven out), those who deny the meanings of vēdam are thieves; further, there are some who steal the self (ātmā) which is bhagavān’s possession. Having the heart which deceives in this manner, desiring to have a change of state, oh, those who are eager to surrender unto his divine feet!

**veḷḷam mudu paravait tirai viriya** – As the waves of the ancient ocean spread everywhere on its shores.

**teḷḷum maṇi tigaḻum** – As the ocean breached the shores naturally, the precious gems are shining there.

**siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattuḷḷum enaduḷḷattuḷḷum uṟaivārai uḷḷīrē** – bhagavān has equal love towards ugandaruḷina nilangaḷ (divyadēśams which are dear to him) and āḻvār’s heart. Because of this, for those who desire to approach, both these places are desirable. “salasayanan” means jalaśayana, which is his divine name. Because this town is inhabited by jalaśayana, the abode came to be known as salasayanam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.2. Teruvil tiri

*teruvil tiri siṟu nōnbiyar senjōṟṟodu kanjimaruvip pirindavar vāymoḻi madiyādu vandadaivīr!tiruvil poli maṟaiyōr siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattuuruvak kuṟaḷadigaḷ adi uṇarmin uṇarvīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

teruvil – in every street; tiri – those who roam around; siṟu – very lowly; nōnbiyar – having vratam (vow); sem sōṟṟodu – (beautiful) (with curd etc) with rice; kanji – (drinkable) porridge; maruvi – desiring and consuming; pirindavar – jainas et al who are different from sātvika (noble) people; vāy moḻi – the words spoken by their mouth; madiyādu – without supporting; vandu – leaving them; adaivīr – Oh, those who are eager to surrender!; tiruvil – by wealth; poli – opulent; maṟaiyōr – where brāhmaṇas are residing; siṟupuliyūr – having the divine name siṟupuliyūr; salasayanattu – bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is reclining in this divyadēśam; uruva – having beautiful form; kuṟaḷ – vāmana; adigaḷ – lord’s; adi – divine feet; uṇarvīr – if you desire to meditate upon; uṇarmin – do that

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, those who are eager to surrender, leaving aside jainas et al who are different from sātvika (noble) people, who roam around in every street, disregarding their words and having very lowly vratam of consuming rice and porridge! If you desire to meditate upon bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), who is reclining in this divyadēśam having the divine name siṟupuliyūr, where brāhmaṇas, who are opulent due to their wealth, are residing, and if you desire to meditate upon the divine feet of vāmana who is having a beautiful form, do that.

**teruvil tiri siṟu nōnbiyar** – Having a form which is not apt for public, they are roaming in the streets, and having avaidika (non-vaidika) deeds.

**senjōṟṟodu kanji maruvip pirindvar vāy moḻi madiyādu vandadaivīr** – As said in [periya tirumoḻi 2.1.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/07/periya-thirumozhi-2-1-7/) “*taṇ tayirināl tiraḷai midaṟṟidai* *nerukkuvār*” (pushing handful of rice mixed with the best curd), they would consume porridge that does not bring any confusion in their minds. In this manner, they are having avaidika conduct and are roaming around being away from vaidika rules. Oh, those are discarding such words and are eagerly surrendering!

**tiruvil poli maṟaiyōr** – Where very opulent brāhmaṇas are residing…

**siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattu** – Meditate upon the divine feet of vāmana, who is sarvēśvara who is having a divine form which is beautiful and is desirable for anyone who sees it. Oh those who are trying to meditate in this manner!

**uṇarvīr** – Oh those who are meditating! The verb is to be understood as in “Abandon the words from the mouth of those jainas et al who are roaming around in the streets desiring for rice and porridge. Try to surrender unto bhagavān who is in siṟupuliyūrc calasayanam. Understand the divine feet of trivikrama”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.3. Paraiyum vinai

*paṟaiyum vinai toḻudu uymin nīr paṇiyum siṟu toṇḍīraṟaiyum punal orupāl vayal orupāl poḻil orupālsiṟai vaṇḍinam aṟaiyum siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattuuṟaiyum iṟai adi alladu onṟu iṟaiyum aṟiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vinai – sins; paṟaiyum – will fly away; nīr – you; toḻudu – surrendering unto (him); uymin – be uplifted; siṟu – in lowly matters; toṇḍīr – oh, those who are desirous!; paṇiyum – (abandoning those) try to surrender unto him; oru pāl – on one side; punal – water; aṟaiyum – throwing up waves; oru pāl – on another side; vayal – having fertile fields; oru pāl – on yet another side; poḻil – having orchards; siṟai – having wings; vaṇḍu inam – swarms of beetles; aṟaiyum – are humming; siṟupuliyūr – having the divine name siṟupuliyūr; salasayanattu uḷḷum – bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is reclining in this divyadēśam; uṟaiyum – firmly residing; iṟai – lord’s; adi alladu – other than the divine feet; onṟu – anything else; iṟaiyum – even a little bit; aṟiyēn – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**Have you not seen how we are \[having eliminated the deceit in our heart\]? You also try to be like that.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, those who are desirous in lowly matters! You surrender unto him and your sins will fly away; I don’t know even a little bit about anything other than the divine feet of the lord who is firmly residing in the divyadēśam, which is having the divine name siṟupuliyūr, where bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is reclining; on one side of the divyadēśam the water is throwing up waves; on the other side, it is having fertile fields; on yet another side, the swarms of beetles, having wings are humming, in the orchards.

**paṟaiyum vinai** – All the sins committed by you since time immemorial will fly away. Surrender unto him and be uplifted.

**paṇiyum siṟu toṇḍīr** – You, who are are bound by inapt aspects, should fall at his feet and surrender unto him. Alternative explanation. Oh, you who desire to become confidential servitors! **paṇimin** – Surrender unto him.

**aṟaiyum …** – That town siṟupuliyūr is being hit by flood water on one side, having orchards on another side and fertile fields on yet another side. bhagavān is eternally residing in siṟupuliyūrc calasayanam, where winged beetles are humming in all these three places. I don’t know anything other than such sarvēśvaran’s divine feet, even if it is something to be abandoned.

## 7.9.4. Vanar madi

*vānār madi podiyum sadai maḻuvāḷiyodu orupāltānāgiya talaivan avan amararkku adipadiyāmtēnār poḻil taḻuvum siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattuānāyanadu adiyalladu onṟaṟiyēn adiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oru pāl – (residing) in one part of his divine body; vān – in the sky; Ar – pervaded; madi – candran (moon); podiyum – submerged; sadai – having matted hair; maḻuvāḷiyodu – with rudran who is having axe; amararkku adipadi – dēvēndran; tān āgiya – having them as his wealth, to be included in the word “tān” (him); talaivanām – being the lord of all; avan – being famously known as suśeela (simple), him; tēn Ar – having abundant honey; poḻil – by orchards; taḻuvum – filled with; siṟupuliyūr – having the divine name siṟupuliyūr; salasayanattu – bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is reclining in this divyadēśam; ānāyanadu – kriṣṇa, who is mercifully present, his; adi alladu – other than the divine feet; onṟu – anything else; adiyēn – I, the servitor; aṟiyēn – do not know (as protection/refuge)

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is thinking “Since they consider me as trustworthy, they will obey my words” and announces his state to them and tells “You also try to get him to eliminate your hurdles by him, just like I did”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

rudran is having an axe, is residing in one part of bhagavān’s divine body and is having matted hair where candran, who has pervaded the sky, is submerged; bhagavān is having such rudran and dēvēndran as his wealth, such that the word “tān” (him, bhagavān) will include those entities. He is the lord of all and is famously known as suśeela (simple). Such bhagavān who is jalaśāyi, is reclining in this divyadēśam which is having the divine name siṟupuliyūr, and is filled with orchards which are having abundant honey. I, the servitor, do not know anything else other than the divine feet of kriṣṇa, who is mercifully present in such divyadēśam.

**vānār madi …** – candran, who appears to pervade the vast sky is held by rudran in his matted hair; that rudran is having an axe to kill anyone irrespective of whether the person is his own father or others; bhagavān is greater than all, who has abundant simplicity to give a place for such rudran, in his divine body.

**avan amararkku adipadiyām** – indran, who is the leader of dēvatās. bhagavān has such greatness that when he says “I” that includes rudran, indran et al.

**tēn Ar poḻil ….** – Being surrounded by orchards where honey never stops flowing.

**siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattu ānāyan** – Instead of having to feel upset that kriṣṇāvatāram is concluded, bhagavān is reclining here with the same qualities as in such kriṣṇāvatāram such that those who came after kriṣṇāvatāram too could enjoy him. I do not know anything other than such kriṣṇa’s divine feet. The reason for that is – I am his exclusive servitor.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.5. Nanda nedunaragattidai

*nandā nedunaragattidai naṇugā vagai nāḷumendāy! ena imaiyōr toḻudēttum idam eṟi nīrccendāmarai malarum siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattu andāmarai adiyāy! unadadiyēṟku aruḷ puriyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

imaiyōr – dēvatās; nāḷum – daily; endāy ena – saying “Oh, my lord!”; toḻudu – surrendering unto you; ēttum – praising; idam – being the abode; eṟi nīr – in vaterbodies where waves are agitating; sendāmarai – reddish lotus flower; malarum – blossoming; siṟupuliyūr – having the divine name siṟupuliyūr; salasayanattu – bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is reclining in this divyadēśam; am – beautiful; tāmarai adiyāy – Oh, one who is having lotus like divine feet!; nandā – imperishable; nedu – long-lasting; naragattidai – in the samsāram which is as bad as hell; naṇugā vagai – to not reach (to not be born anymore); unadu adiyēṟku – in the matters related to me, your servitor; aruḷāy – shower your mercy

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is reclining in this divyadēśam which is having the divine name siṟupuliyūr, where reddish lotus flowers are blossoming in vaterbodies where waves are agitating, and the abode where dēvatās are surrendering unto you and praising daily, saying “Oh, my lord!”. Oh, one who is having beautiful, lotus-like divine feet! Shower your mercy in the matters related to me, your servitor, to not reach this imperishable, long-lasting samsāram which is as bad as hell.

**nandā nedu naragattidai** – To not make enter this samsāram which is a long-lasting hell where there is no break.

**nāḷum …** – The abode where brahmā et al remain eternally, saying “My lord”, surrendering unto him and praising him.

**eṟi nīr …** – In siṟupuliyūrc calasayanam, in the ponds which are having abundant water, the lotus flowers are blossoming due to the dense water, there.

**am tāmarai adiyāy** – Oh, one who is having divine feet which resembles fresh lotus flower!

**unadu adiyēṟku aruḷ puriyē** – Let others be in whatever way; you should mercifully shower your mercy upon me who has no refuge other than you.

## 7.9.6. Mulu neelamum

*muḻu neelamum alar āmbalum aravindamum viravikkaḻunīrodu madavār avar kaṇvāy mugamalarumseḻunīr vayal taḻuvum siṟupuliyūrc calasayanamtoḻunīrmai adu udaiyār adi toḻuvār tuyar ilarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

muḻu neelamum – fully bluish coloured flower (without mix of other colours); alar – blossoming; āmbalum – arakku āmbal (water-lily); aravindamum – lotus flower; kaḻunīrodu – along with sengaḻunīr flower \[red water-lily); viravi – being together; madavāravar – women’s (those who are residing there); kaṇ – like the eyes; vāy – like the lips; mugam – like the face; alarum – blossoming; seḻu – abundant; nīr – water; vayal – fertile fields; taḻuvum – surrounding; siṟupuliyūr – having the divine name siṟupuliyūr; salasayanattu – bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is reclining in this divyadēśam; toḻumadu – surrendering; nīrmai udaiyār – those who have it as their nature; adi – their divine feet; toḻuvār – those who surrender unto; tuyar ilar – will not have any sorrows

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The abundant water is surrounding the fertile fields in siṟupuliyūrc calasayanam, where fully bluish coloured flower, the blossoming water lily, lotus flower along with the sengaḻunīr flower being together looks like the shining eyes, lips and the faces of the women of that town. Those who surrender unto the divine feet of those who are naturally surrendered unto bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi, will not have any sorrows.

**muḻu neelamum …** – Fully black coloured flower, red water lily, lotus flower and water lily flower being together show the eyes, lips and faces of the women who reside in that town.

**seḻunīr vayal taḻuvum …** – Beautiful water is surrounding the fertile fields in siṟupuliyūr. The sorrows will not remain for those who are vorśipping the divine feet of those who are naturally vorśipping jalaśāyi bhagavān there. They will go away on their own.
