## 7.9.7. Seyongu

*sēyōngu taṇ tirumālirunjōlai malai uṟaiyummāyā! enakkuraiyāy idu maṟai nānginuḷāyō? tīyōmbugai maṟaiyōr siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattuāyō? unadadiyār manattāyō? aṟiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sēy ōngu – very tall; taṇ – cool; tirumālirunjōlai malai – in tirumālirunjōlai hill; uṟaiyum – remaining firm; māyā – Oh, amazing lord!; nāngu maṟaiyin – In the four vēdams; uḷāyō – are you present?; tī – three types of fire; ōmbugai – naturally nurturing it through hōmams; maṟaiyōr – where brāhmaṇas are residing; siṟupuliyūr – having the divine name siṟupuliyūr; salasayanattu – bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is reclining in this divyadēśam; āyō – are you present?; unadu – for you; adiyār – bhāgavatas, who are servitors; manattāyō – are you residing in their heart?; aṟiyēn – I am not knowing; idu – the answer for this question; enakku – for me; uraiyāy – you should mercifully give

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, amazing lord who is remaining firm in tirumālirunjōlai hill which is very tall and cool! Are you present in the four vēdams? Are you present in the divine abode siṟupuliyūr where bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi, is reclining and where brāhmaṇas, who are naturally nurturing the three types of fire through hōmams (fire sacrifice), are residing? Are you present in the hearts of those bhāgavatas, who are your servitors? I am not knowing the answer for this question. You should mercifully answer me.

**sēyōngu …** – sēy can be considered as the name of the kśētrapālan (guard for the abode) \[who is rudra’s son, skanda and others\] and here it is indicating him. Alternatively, sēy indicates distance and hence implies very tall hill. The amazing one who is standing in such divine hill.

**enakku uraiyāy idu** – You should mercifully give me the answer for this.

**maṟai nāngin uḷāyō** – Are you present in the four vēdams which completely speak about you?

**tī ōmbugai** … – Are you present in the siṟupuliyūrc calasayanam where brāhmaṇas are fully engaged in fire sacrifices?

**unadu adiyār …** – Are you present in the hearts of those who are exclusively focused on your divine feet? I am not knowing this. You have to mercifully explain this in the manner which will make me understand it.

By this, it is explained that just as saubhari assumed multiple forms, bhagavān is present in all of these places, completely, without any shortcoming, and he manifested that to āḻvār.

## 7.9.8. Maiyar vari neelam

*maiyār vari neelam malark kaṇṇār manam vittittu uyvān una kaḻalē toḻudu eḻuvēn kiḷi madavār sevvāy moḻi payilum siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattu aivāy aravaṇai mēl uṟai amalā! aruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kiḷi – parrots; madavār – women’s; sevvāy – spoken from reddish mouth; moḻi – words; payilum – learning; siṟupuliyūr – having the divine name siṟupuliyūr; salasayanattu – bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is reclining in this divyadēśam; aivāy – having five mouths; aravu aṇai mēl – on the mattress known as tiruvanantāḻvān; uṟai – remaining fixed; amalā – Oh, very pure one!; mai Ar – decorated with black pigment; vari – having stripes; neela malar – like karuneydal \[purple water-lily\] flower; kaṇṇār – on women, having eyes; manam vittu – abandoning the desire; uyvān – to be uplifted; una kaḻalē – your divine feet only; toḻudu eḻuvēn – will surrender and be uplifted; aruḷāy – you should shower your mercy for that

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Parrots are learning the words which emanate from the women’s reddish mouth in this divyadēśam named siṟupuliyūr where bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is reclining. Oh, very pure one who is remaining fixed on the mattress known as tiruvanantāḻvān who is having five mouths! Abandoning the desire on women, who are having eyes which are decorated with black pigment, having stripes and are like karuneydal flower, with the intent to be uplifted, I will surrender unto your divine feet only and be uplifted. You should shower your mercy for that.

**maiyār vari neelam …** – Abandoning the desire on women who are having their eyes which resemble karuneydal (dark purple) flower, being well decorated by black pigment, having reddish and blackish stripes, I will surrender unto your divine feet, to be uplifted.

**toḻudu eḻuvēn** – I will surrender.

**kiḷi madavār sevvāy moḻi payilum …** – In the divyadēśam siṟupuliyūr where parrot-like women are having parrot-like speech. There, tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) is having five heads to let out his happiness acquired through enjoying bhagavān and is having coolness etc as his nature. Oh, one who is mercifully reclining on him and engaged in protection without any expectation! You should shower your mercy upon me. Also said as the parrots are learning from the reddish mouth of the women there.

The pāsuram should be arranged as in – “*kiḷi madavār sevvāy moḻi payilum siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattu vāyaravaṇaimēl uṟai amalā – maiyār vari neela malarkkaṇṇār manam vittittu ! uyvān una kaḻalē toḻudeḻuvēn; aruḷāy*“. sevvāy – being straight.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.9. Karuma mugil uruva

*karumā mugil uruvā! kanal uruvā! punal uruvā! perumāl varai uruvā! piṟa uruvā! ninaduruvā! tirumāmagaḷ maruvum siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattu arumā kadal amudē! unadu adiyē saraṇāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karu mā – (for devotees) blackish and big; mugil uruvā – Oh, one who is having cloud like form!; kanal uruvā – (for non-devotees) Oh, one who is having fire like form!; punal uruvā – Oh, one who is having water like easily approachable form for all!; perumāl – very big; varai uruvā – Oh, one who is having inconceivable mountain like form!; piṟa uruvā – Oh, one who is having another different form!; ninadu uruvā – Oh, one who is having a special form!; tiru mā magaḷ maruvum – where periya pirāttiyār is eternally residing; siṟupuliyūr – having the divine name siṟupuliyūr; salasayanattu – bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi (one who reclines on water), is reclining in this divyadēśam; aru – difficult to attain; mā kadal – came out of kśīrābdi (milk ocean); amudē – Oh, one who is incomparably enjoyable like the nectar!; unadu adiyē – your divine feet only; saraṇām – are my goal

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, one who is having blackish and big cloud like form! Oh, one who is having fire like form! Oh, one who is having water like easily approachable form for all! Oh, one who is having inconceivable, huge mountain like form! Oh, one who is having another different form! Oh, one who is having a special form! Oh, one who is incomparably enjoyable like the nectar which came out of kśīrābdi (milk ocean) which is the origin of periya pirāttiyār and is difficult to attain and who is jalaśāyi, reclining in this divyadēśam which is having the divine name siṟupuliyūr! Your divine feet are my only goal.

**karu mā mugil uruvā** – Oh, one who is having rejuvenating big cloud like form which will eliminate all the sufferings of the devotees just on seeing you!

**kanal uruvā** – Oh, one who is having an invincible form which cannot be approached by non-devotees!

**punal uruvā** – Oh, one who is having water like easily approachable form for all!

**perumāl varai uruvā** – Oh, one who is having inconceivable form!

**piṟa uruvā** – Oh, one who is having many more countless forms which are not listed here!

**ninadu uruvā** – Apart from having the entire existence as your form, oh, one who is having distinguished forms!

**tiru mā magaḷ maruvum** – Where periya pirāttiyār is eternally residing,

**aru mā kadal amudē** – Being very enjoyable like the nectar which was brought out with great difficulty from the huge ocean, oh, one who is mercifully reclining in siṟupuliyūr divyadēśam as jalaśāyi, along with periya pirāttiyār!

**unadu adiyē saraṇāmē** – I have no other goal than the lotus feet of yours, the śriya:pati.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.10. Sirar

*sīrār nedumaṟugil siṟupuliyūrc calasayanattu ērār mugilvaṇṇan tanai imaiyōr perumānaik kārār vayal mangaikkiṟai kaliyan oli mālai pārār ivai paravit toḻap pāvam payilāvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sīr Ar – having opulence; nedu – lengthy; maṟugil – having divine streets; siṟupuliyūr – having the divine name siṟupuliyūr; salasayanattu – mercifully present in the divyadēśam named salasayanam, where bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi, is mercifully reclining; ēr Ar – very beautiful; mugil vaṇṇan tannai – having cloud like form; imaiyōr perumānai – on sarvēśvaran who is the lord of nityasūris; kār Ar – blackish; vayal – having fertile fields; mangaikku – for the residents of tirumangai region; iṟai – lord; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; oli – mercifully spoke; ivai mālai – these pāsurams which are in the form of a garland; pārār – residents of earth; paravi – reciting; toḻa – as they surrender unto him; pāvam – sin; payilā – will not approach (them)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran is the lord of nityasūris, who is having very beautiful cloud like form and is mercifully present in the divyadēśam named siṟupuliyūrc calasayanam. bhagavān, who is jalaśāyi, is mercifully reclining in this place, which is having opulent and lengthy divine streets. tirumangai āḻvār, the lord of the residents of tirumangai region, which is having blackish fertile fields, mercifully spoke on such sarvēśvaran, these pāsurams which are in the form of a garland. As the residents of earth recite these and surrender unto such bhagavān, no sin will approach them.

**sīr Ar …** – In siṟupuliyūrc calasayanam which is having lengthy streets which reveal its opulence, bhagavān is mercifully reclining with a beautiful cloud like form.

**imaiyōr perumānai** – When asked “Who is mercifully reclining there?” he is none other than the one who is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipadi*” (the lord of nityasūris who are faultless).

**kār Ar vayal mangaikku iṟai** – Explaining that the clouds are always roaming in this town; or the fertile fields are blackish in colour (implying well-grown crops). āḻvār, who is the controller of such tirumangai region, mercifully spoke these pāsurams with tune.

**pārār ivai paravit toḻa pāvam nillāvē** – Even though these people are present in the place (samsāra) where there is scope for acquiring sin, as they recite these pāsurams and surrender unto him, the sins will go away saying “This is not the place for us”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10 Perumburak kadalai

## 7.10.1. Perumburak kadalai

*perumbuṟakkadalai adalēṟṟinaip peṇṇai āṇai eṇṇil munivarkkaruḷtarum tavattai muttin tiraḷ kōvaiyaip pattar āviyai nittilattottinai arumbinai alarai adiyēn manattāsaiyai amudam podi insuvaik karumbinaik kaniyaic cenṟu nādik kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

puṟam – present outside all oceans; perum kadalai – one who is like inconceivable ocean; adal – prideful/strong; ēṟṟinai – one who is having the gait of a bull; peṇṇai – being āśrita paratantra (submissive towards devotees) like a woman; āṇai – being svatantra (independent) like a man; eṇ il – having countless penance; munivarkku – for yōgis; aruḷ tarum – granting the result of the penance; tavattai – one who is an embodiment of tapas (i.e, being omniscient); tiraḷ – gathered together; muttin kōvaiyai – enjoyable like a pearl necklace; pattar – for the devotees; āviyai – one who is like the prāṇan (vital air) which sustains; nittilam – pearl’s; tottinai – being a protector like a bunch of; arumbinai – having childhood like that of a sprout; alarai – having adulthood like a blossomed flower; adiyēn – I, the servitor, my; manattu āsaiyai – target of heart’s desire; amudin – nectar’s; podi – being fed with (like spraying the nectar as water); in suvai – being incomparably sweet; karumbinai – one who is enjoyable like sugarcane juice; kaniyai – sarvēśvaran who is like a fruit which is immediately enjoyable; nādic cenṟu – went to, seeking him; kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ – in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai; kaṇḍukoṇḍēn – I saw him

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I, the servitor went to the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai for sarvēśvaran who is like an inconceivable ocean, which is outside all the other oceans, who is having the prideful/strong gait of a bull, who is āśrita paratantra (submissive towards devotees) like a woman and svatantra (independent) like a man, who is an embodiment of tapas, granting the result for the penance of the yogis who are having countless penances, who is enjoyable like a pearl necklace which is gathered together, who is like the prāṇan (vital air) which sustains for his devotees, who is like a protector like a bunch of pearls, who is having childhood like that of a sprout and adulthood like a blossomed flower, who is the target of my heart’s desire where I am his servitor, who is enjoyable like sugarcane juice which is incomparably sweet due to being nourished by nectar as water and who is like a fruit which is immediately enjoyable. I saw him there.

**perum puṟak kadalai** – One who is inconceivable like an ocean which has all (many) entities in it and protects those. One who is like a huge ocean which is outside all the oceans.

**adal ēṟṟinai** – One who is having the prideful gait due to having everything in him and protecting everything other than him by having those in him.

**peṇṇai** – When asked “If that is the case, is he unapproachable for everyone?” he is present as paratantra (obedient).

When asked “Does he only have pāratantryam?”

**āṇai** – One who has uncontrollable freedom.

**eṇ il munivarkku aruḷ tarum tavattai** – For the yōgis who have countless tapas (penance), he is the tapas which can grant the result of their tapas.

**muttin tiraḷ kōvaiyai** – One who is like a pearl necklace, made from a collectioin of pearls, which removes fatigue as soon as it is seen and could be adorned on the body.

**pattar āviyai** – One who is very rare such that those who care for him cannot live without serving him.

**nittilat tottinai** – One who is like treasure trove of pearls, which comforts us that we will also get a share of it. nittilam – pearl, beauty. Collection of beauty.

**arumbinai alarai** – One who is having both childhood and adulthood simultaneously. as said in “*yuvākumāra:*” (youth and adolescent).

**adiyēn manattu āsaiyai** – Though I am enjoying him always, I am having this desire as if I have never enjoyed him in the past.

**amudam podi in suvaik karumbinai** – One who is like incomparably sweet sugarcane, as if it was nourished with nectar as water.

**kaniyai** – One who is well ripened fruit, to consume as it is.

**senṟu nādik kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē** – Just as the one who gets to eat where he felt hungry, I got to see and enjoyed him in the place where desire was born in me to see him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.2. Meynnalat tavattai

*meynnalat tavattait tivattait tarum meyyaip poyyinaik kaiyil ōr sangudai mainiṟakkadalaik kadal vaṇṇanai mālai ālilaip paḷḷi koḷ māyanai nennalaip pagalai iṟṟai nāḷinai nāḷaiyāy varum tingaḷai āṇḍinai kannalaik karumbinidait tēṟalaik kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mey – truth (matching one’s true nature); nalam – beautiful (in the form of love); tavattai – being the target of tapas in the form of bhakti yōgam; tivattai – paramapadam; tarum – granting; meyyai – being the target of trustworthy prapatti (surrender); poyyinai – being non-existent (unseen) (for those who don’t surrender); kaiyil – holding in his divine hand; ōr sangu udai – having a matchless śrī pāncajanyam; mai niṟam – having the complexion of anjanam (black pigment); kadalai – like an ocean (which is of a different species); kadal vaṇṇanai – one who is having the nature of the ocean (that is, being a protector); mālai – being greater than all; ālilai – on banyan leaf; paḷḷi koḷ – one who is mercifully resting (during praḷaya (deluge)); māyanai – being an amazing person; nennalaip pagalai – one who gives bliss based on past experience, as if enjoyed in the day-time of previous day; iṟṟai nāḷinai – one who gives bliss for the present time, as if being enjoyed today; nāḷaiyāy – one who will give bliss in the future, as if enjoyed tomorrow; varum – coming (in this manner in different times); tingaḷai – every month; āṇḍinai – one who gives bliss every year (which is a collection of months); kannalai – one who is sweet like sugar; karumbin idai – formed in the sugarcane; tēṟalai – one who is immediately enjoyable like the juice; kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍukoṇḍēn – I got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I got to see bhagavān in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai, who is the target of tapas in the form of bhakti yōgam which is truthful and beautiful; he is the target of trustworthy prapatti (surrender) which grants paramapadam; he is non-existent for those who don’t surrender; he is like an ocean having the complexion of anjanam (black pigment) and is holding a matchless śrī pāncajanyam in his divine hand; he is having the nature of the ocean (that is, being a protector); being greater than all, he is an amazing person resting on a banyan leaf (during deluge); he gives bliss based on past experience as if enjoyed in the day-time of previous day; he gives bliss for the present time, as if being enjoyed today; he will give bliss in the future, as if enjoyed tomorrow; he is coming and giving bliss every month and year; he is sweet like sugar; he is immediately enjoyable like the juice formed in the sugarcane.

**mey nalat tavattai** – bhakti \[yōgam\] which matches one’s true nature, the means to attain bhagavān who is desirable, and is in the form of affection.

**tivattait tarum meyyai** – prapatti.

**poyyinai** – For those who lack either one of these bhakti and prapatti, one whose aspects remain unknown.

**kaiyil ōr …** – One who has the sight to behold for those who have either one of bhakti or prapatti. Unlike the ocean which keeps and protects everything which is seen, he is black pigment coloured ocean, who is having śrī pāncajanyam in his hand.

**kadal vaṇṇanai** – One who is having the nature of an ocean which protects everything inside it with the help of its waves which are like the hands, by ensuring that the strong entities do not abuse the weak entities.

**mālai** – Greater than all.

**ālilai …** – One who is having agatita gatanā sāmartyam (ability to unite contrasting aspects). The amazing personality who consumed all the worlds in a small form and mercifully rested on a fresh banyan leaf.

**nennalaip pagalai** – Just as the bliss recollected on the next day after getting one’s desire fulfilled, he can be sustained thinking “What a beautiful experience we had during the daytime yesterday”.

**iṟṟai nāḷinai** – The present day when we get experience.

**nāḷaiyāy varum tingaḷai** – Not having any break for such experience, he is like the next day where one will think “We will have the same experience tomorrow also”, and not just stopping there, it continues to months.

**āṇḍinai** – One who is like the year which contains many such months. Now, that year, will also multiply further.

**kannalai** – one who is incomparably enjoyable

**karumbin idait tēṟalai** – Not having to press into juice and enjoy, he is present as the juice of the sugarcane.

**kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ …** – Such bhagavān is seen in tirukkaṇṇamangai.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.3. Engalukku

*engaḷukku aruḷ seyginṟa īsanai vāsavār kuḻalāḷ malai mangai tanpanganaip pangil vaittu ugandān tannaip pānmaiyaip pani māmadiyam tavaḻ mangulaic cudarai vada māmalai ucciyai nacci nām vaṇangappadumkangulaip pagalaic cenṟu nādik kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

engaḷukku – to us who are having no other refuge; aruḷ seyginṟa – giving his mercy; īsanai – being sarvēśvaran; vāsam vār – spreading fragrance; kuḻalāḷ – having hair; malai mangai – pārvati who is the daughter of himālaya mountain; than panganai – rudra who is having her on one side of his body; pangil – in a portion of his divine form; vaittu – placed; ugandān tannai – one who became happy; pānmaiyai – one who is having (such simplicity) as his nature; pani – cool; mā – vast; madi – moon’s; am tavaḻ – having beautiful movement; mangulai – being the controller of the sky; sudarai – being the antaryāmi (in-dwelling super-soul) of sun; vada – present in the norter direction; mā – vast; malai – tiruvēngada mountain’s; ucciyai – (one who is mercifully present) on the peak of; nacci – desired; nām – by us; vaṇangappadum – surrendered; kangulai – being the controller of night; pagalai – being the controller of day; senṟu nādi – went searching for; kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍukoṇḍēn – I got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I went searching for bhagavān and got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai; he is sarvēśvaran giving his mercy to us who are having no other refuge; he became happy by placing rudra in a portion of his divine form, where rudra who is having pārvati on one side of his body, who is the daughter of himālaya mountain and whose hair is spreading fragrance; he is having such simplicity as his nature; he is the controller of the sky which is having the cool, vast moon’s beautiful movement; he is the antaryāmi (in-dwelling super-soul) of sun; he is mercifully present on the vast tiruvēngada mountain’s peak, which is in the northern direction; he is the controller of night and day, is desired by us and surrendered to by us.

**engaḷukku aruḷ seyginṟa īsanai** – sarvēśvaran who is giving his causeless mercy to us who have no other refuge.

**vāsavār …** – Unlike us, rudran is having to share his body with pārvati and is considering himself to be īśvara; bhagavān is having joy of simplicity due to having such rudra on one side of his divine body and is considering that to be benefit for himself.

**pānmaiyai** – He is having this simplicity as his permanent nature, unlike an accidental quality such as a worm unknowingly writing a letter as part of its crawling.

**pani mā madi am tavaḻ mangulai** – One, who is the sky which has the cool and complete moon’s movement.

**sudarai** – The sun which can eliminate the humidity using its rays.

**vada mā malai ucciyai** – Unlike these common forms, bhagavān is firmly standing on that tirumalā with a distinguished form.

**nacci nām vaṇangappadum kangulai** – One who is the enjoyable time who is surrendered to by those who are eagerly seeking him.

**pagalai** – One who is the daytime, which is favourable to gather wealth for nightly enjoyment.

## 7.10.4. Pey mulait talai

*pēy mulait talai nanjuṇḍa piḷḷaiyait teḷḷiyār vaṇangappadum dēvanai māyanai madiḷ kōval idaikaḻi maindanai anṟi andaṇar sindaiyuḷīsanai ilangum sudarc cōdiyai endaiyai enakku eyppinil vaippinaik kāsinai maṇiyaic cenṟu nādik kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pēy – pūtanā’s; mulaittalam – present in the place of the bosom; nanju – poison; uṇḍa – mercifully consumed; piḷḷaiyai – being a child; teḷḷiyār – by very wise persons; vaṇangappadum – being surrendered to; dēvanai – shining (due to that); māyanai – being amazing; madiḷ – surrounded by prākārams (forts); kōval – in tirukkōvalūr; idai kaḻi – in divine verandah (where he is mercifully present along with mudalāḻvārs); maindanai – being youthful person; anṟi – further; andaṇar – śrīvaiṣṇavas’; sindaiyuḷ – in their hearts (being present); īsanai – being the one who can control (them); ilangum – shining (to be not touched by their defects); sudar – radiant; sōdiyai – having a effulgent form; endaiyai – being my lord; enakku – for me; eyppinil – in dire situations; vaippinai – being a saviour, like wealth; kāsinai – being desirable like gold; maṇiyai – being the very best, like precious gem; senṟu nādi – went searching for; kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍukoṇḍēn – I got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I went searching for bhagavān and got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai; being a child, he mercifully consumed the poison which was present in pūtanā’s bosom; he is surrendered to by very wise persons; due to that, he is shining; he is amazing; he is the youthful person who was mercifully present along with mudalāḻvārs in the divine verandah in tirukkōvalūr which is surrounded by forts; further, he is being present in the hearts of śrīvaiṣṇavas and controls them; he is shining and having a radiantly effulgent form; he is my lord; he is my saviour, in dire situations, like wealth; he is desirable, like gold; he is the very best, like precious gem.

**pēy mulai …** – Mercifully consuming the poison in pūtanā’s bosom, he remained as an infant who does not know the effect of such act.

**teḷḷiyār vaṇangap padum dēvanai** – Being surrendered to, not just by ignorant people, but by very wise persons. He is shining due to that.

**māyanai –** Amazing entity.

**madiḷ kōval idai kaḻi maindanai** – One who is eternally youthful and who jostled with his dear devotees where it was already cramped.

**anṟi andaṇar sindaiyuḷ īsanai** – Further, entering the hearts of his devotees, he controls them to follow him.

**ilangum sudarc cōdiyai** – Though he is present in their physical bodies and souls, he remains untouched by the defects which come about based on the nature of the body and soul \[body transforms and keeps changing; ātmā’s knowledge expands and shrinks\].

**endaiyai** – One who enslaved me by showing this nature.

**enakku eyppinil vaippinai** – One who is like the wealth which can be spent during difficult times for my survival.

**kāsinai** – He is desirable like gold.

**maṇiyai** – One who is like precious gem, which can be obtained by melting that gold. Seeking him.

## 7.10.5. Errinai

*ēṟṟinai imayattuḷ em īsanai immaiyai maṟumaikku marundinai āṟṟalai aṇḍattu appuṟattu uyttidumaiyanaik kaiyil āḻi onṟēndiyakūṟṟinai kurumā maṇikkunṟinai ninṟavūr ninṟa nittilat tottinaik kāṟṟinaip punalaic cenṟu nādik kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēṟṟinai – being prideful like an ox; imayattuḷ – one who is mercifully residing in himavān (tiruppiridi); em īsanai – being our lord; immaiyai – being the one who grants worldly benefits; maṟumaikku – for higher benefits; marundinai – being the means, like medicine; āṟṟalai – being strong; aṇḍattu appuṟattu – outside the oval shaped universe (up to paramapadam); uyttidum – one who can conduct (the devotees); aiyanai – being the natural relative; kaiyil – in his divine hand; onṟu āḻi – having distinguished sudarśana āḻvān; ēndiya – holding; kūṟṟinai – causing fear like the deity of death (for non-devotees); kuru – best; mā maṇi – made with blue gems; kunṟinai – being very beautiful like a mountain; ninṟa Ur – in tiruninṟavūr; ninṟa – mercifully residing; nittilam tottinai – having a cool form like that of a collection of pearls; kāṟṟinai – being like wind, which causes joy; punalai – one who is like water which sustains; senṟu nādi – went searching for; kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍukoṇḍēn – I got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I went searching for bhagavān and got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai; he is prideful like an ox; he is our lord who is mercifully residing in himavān (tiruppiridi); he is the one who grants worldly benefits and is the means like medicine for higher benefits; he is strong; he is the natural relative who can conduct his devotees outside the oval shaped universe (up to paramapadam); in his divine hand, he is having distinguished sudarśana āḻvān and causing fear like the deity of death (for non-devotees); he is very beautiful like a mountain made of the best blue gems; he is mercifully residing in tiruninṟavūr and is having a cool form like that of a collection of pearls; he is like wind which causes joy; he is like water which sustains.

**ēṟṟinai** – One who is prideful due to his joyful experience.

**imayattuḷ em īsanai** – One who attracted me by showing his presence in tiruppiridi in himavān (himalayas).

**immaiyai maṟumaikku marundinai** – One who is the means for worldly benefits and higher benefits.

**āṟṟalai** – When asked “How can a single entity grant all benefits?” the answer is – “He is omnipotent who is not having any shortcoming”.

**aṇḍattu appuṟattu uyttidum aiyanai** – When asked “What is he going to do with this omnipotence?” the answer is – He can conduct these ātmās up to paramapadam.

When asked “Why should he do that for the ātmās?” āḻvār says

**aiyanai** – He is naturally related to all the ātmās \[as the father, sustainer, protector etc\].

**kaiyil āḻi onṟu ēndiya kūṟṟinai** – When he hands over an ātmā to ātivāhikas (those who can cross-over from one lōka to another) and conducts the ātmā, if anyone questions that, he is having the weapon to cut them into two pieces. For the enemies, he is like the deity of death.

**kuru mā maṇik kunṟinai** – One who is having the form like that of a mountain made of precious blue gem. When he takes these ātmās to paramapadam, this is how bhagavān’s form looks like \[shining like a blue gem\].

**ninṟavūr ninṟa nittilat tottinai** – One who is having a rejuvenating form like that of a collection of pearls and is mercifully standing in tiruninṟavūr for those who cannot go up to parampadam.

**kāṟṟinai** – One who is joyful, due to being touched by wind.

**punalai** – One who is the sustainer. Seeking him …

## 7.10.6. Tuppanai

*tuppanait turangam padac cīṟiyatōnṟalaic cudar vān kalan peydadōrseppinait tirumangai maṇāḷanait tēvanait tigaḻum pavaḷattoḷioppanai ulagēḻinai ūḻiyaiāḻi ēndiya kaiyanai andaṇarkaṟpinai kaḻunīr malarum vayal kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuppanai – being capable (strong); turangam – the demon named kēśi; pada – to be destroyed; sīṟiya – one who mercifully showed anger on him; tōnṟalai – being beautiful; sudar – being radiant; vān – priceless; kalan – ornaments; peydadu – to be placed; ōr – distinguished; seppinai – like a copper container; tirumangai – for periya pirāttiyār; maṇāḷanai – being the beloved lord; dēvanai – being radiant (due to that); tigaḻum – shining; pavaḷattu – coral’s; oḷi oppanai – one who is similar to radiance (being desirable); ulagu ēḻinai – being the controller of the seven worlds; ūḻiyai – being the controller of time; āḻi ēndiya – holding divine chakra; kaiyanai – having divine hand; andaṇar – by brāhmaṇas; kaṟpinai – one who is studied/recited; kaḻu nīr – the sengaḻunīr flower; malarum – blossoming; vayal – having fertile fields; kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍukoṇḍēn – I got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I got to see bhagavān in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai which is having fertile fields where the sengaḻunīr flowers are blossoming; he is capable; he is the beautiful one who mercifully showed anger on kēśi, the demon and destroyed him; he is like a distinguished copper container where raidant, priceless ornaments are placed; he is the beloved lord of periya pirāttiyār and is radiant due to that; he is similar to the radiance of shining corals; he is the controller of the seven worlds; he is the controller of time; he is holding the divine chakra in his divine hand; he is studied/recited by brāhmaṇas.

**tuppanai** – One who is having the ability to complete the tasks which he desired.

**turangam padac cīṟiya tōnṟalai** – The young boy who showed anger to tear the mouth of kēśi.

**sudar vān kalan peydadu ōr seppinai** – he is like a distinguished copper container where raidant, priceless ornaments are placed.

When asked “Which is the sudar vān kalan (radiant, priceless ornament)?” āḻvar says

**tirumangai maṇāḷanait tēvanai** – One whose divine form is shining with the turmeric paste, saffron paste, sandalwood paste and their fragrance, in the togetherness of pirātti and himself.

**tigaḻum pavaḷattu oḷi oppanai** – One who is desirable for all, in all manners.

**ulagu ēḻinai** – One who is present as bhōjña (enjoyment), bhōgōpakaraṇa (the tools for enjoyment) and bhōgastāna (the abode of enjoyment).

**ūḻiyai –** One who remains as time, when only time remains (after praḷayam).

**āḻi ēndiya kaiyavanai** – One who is having the divine hand which is holding the eternal, divine weapons. Implies that he has an eternal, divine, auspicious form.

**andaṇar kaṟpinai** – One who is having the will which resembles brāhmaṇas’ discipline. Also said as the one who is learnt/recited by brāhmaṇas.

**kaḻunīr malarum vayal** – Having fertile fields where flowers such as sengaḻunīr blossom.

## 7.10.7. Tiruttanai

*tiruttanait tisai nānmugan tandaiyait tēva dēvanai mūvaril munniyaviruttanai viḷangum sudarc cōdiyai viṇṇai maṇṇinaik kaṇṇudal kūdiyaaruttanai ariyaip pari kīṟiyaappanai appil ār aḻalāy ninṟakaruttanaik kaḷi vaṇḍaṟaiyum poḻil kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruttanai – being satisfied (in joy, being complete); tisai – the controller of the people who are in different directions; nānmugan – for brahmā; tandaiyai – being the father; dēva dēvanai – being the dēva who is surrendered to by dēvatās; mūvaril – among the three primary dēvatās viz brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra (for the two other dēvatās); munniya – being the chief; viruttanai – being the lord (the controller); viḷangum – shining; sudar – radiant; sōdiyai – having luminous divine form; viṇṇai – being the controller of svargam (heaven); maṇṇinai – being the controller of bhūmi (earth); kaṇ nudal – rudran who is having an eye on his forehead; kūdiya – remaining together; aruttanai – being the one who has half of his body given; ariyai – being strong like narasimha; pari kīṟiya – tore and put down kēśi; appanai – being benefactor; appil ōr – present in water; aḻalāy ninṟa – being like patapāgni (fire which is formed in the middle of the ocean and which is the resting place for all entities); karuttanai – sarvēśvaran, who is the lord of all; kaḷi – drunk; vaṇḍu – beetles; aṟaiyum – humming; poḻil – having orchards; kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍukoṇḍēn – I got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I went searching for bhagavān and got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai which is having orchards where drunk beetles are humming; he is satisfied’; he is the father of brahmā, who is the controller of the people in different directions; he is the dēva who is surrendered to by dēvatās; he is the lord and chief among the three primary dēvatās viz brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra (for the two other dēvatās); he is having a shining, radiant, luminous divine form; he is the controller of svargam (heaven) and bhūmi (earth); he is the one who has half of his body given to rudran who has an eye on his forehead and being together with him; he is strong like narasimha; he is the benefactor who tore and put down kēśi; he is like patapāgni which is present in water; he is sarvēśvaran who is the lord of all.

**tiruttanai** – Due to self-enjoyment, he is eternally satisfied.

**tisai nānmugan tandaiyai** – Being the father of brahmā who is greater than everyone in samsāram.

**dēva dēvanai** – Not just for brahmā, but he is the refuge for all the dēvatās.

**mūvaril munniya viruttanai** – One who remains clearly as the lord among the three dēvatās (brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra) and not just brahmā.

**viruttanai** – vrudda – elder, The chief.

**viḷangum sudarc cōdiyai** – One who is having distinguished divine form beyond having the viṣṇu form amongst trimūrtis (three primary dēvatās).

**viṇṇai** – One who is the \[controller of\] svargam etc which are enjoyable abodes.

**maṇṇinai** – One who is the \[controller of\] karma bhūmi where the means are pursued to attain such enjoyable abodes.

**kaṇ nudal kūdiya aruttanai** – One who is having the half which hosts rudra who has an eye in the forehead.

**aruttan** – arda bhāgan (one who has granted half his body to rudra).

**ariyai** – One who eliminates enemies.

**pari kīṟiya appanai** – Benefactor who has virōdi nirasanam (elimination of enemies) as a natural quality.

**appil aḻalāy ninṟa karuttanai** – Just as the patapāmukāgni (fire in the middle of ocean) will make the water rest on it and evaporate it, he is having the ability to make all the entities rest on him.

**kaḷi vaṇḍu aṟaiyum** – I saw such bhagavān in tirukkaṇṇamangai which has orchards filled with drunk beetles which are humming.

## 7.10.8. Venjinak kalirrai

*venjinak kaḷiṟṟai viḷangāy vīḻak kanṟu vīsiya īsanai pēy magaḷtunja nanju suvaittuṇḍa tōnṟalait tōnṟal vāḷarakkan kedat tōnṟiyananjinai amudattinai nādanai naccuvār ucci mēl niṟkum nambiyai kanjanait tunja vanjitta vanjanaik kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vem sinam – having very cruel anger; kaḷiṟṟai – beautiful like an elephant; viḷangāy – monster, as a wood apple; vīḻa – to fall down and be destroyed; kanṟu – monster, who came as a calf; vīsiya – threw; īsanai – being the lord; pēy magaḷ – pūtanā; tunja – to be killed; nanju – poison (which was in her bosom); suvaittu – sucked; uṇḍa – mercifully consumed; tōnṟalai – being a child; tōnṟal – being famous (as the enemy); vāḷ arakkan – the demon rāvaṇa, who is having the weapon, sword; keda – to be killed; tōnṟiya – mercifully incarnated; nanjinai – being like a poison; amudattinai – being enjoyable like nectar (for devotees); nādanai – being the lord of all; naccuvār – those who desire him, their; ucci mēl – on the heads; niṟkum – mercifully present; nambiyai – being the complete one; kanjanai – kamsan; tunja – to have him killed; vanjitta – one who cheated (and killed); vanjanai – the cheater; kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍukoṇḍēn – I got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

I got to see bhagavān in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai; he is beautiful like an elephant having very cruel anger; he is the lord who threw the monster who came as a calf on the monster who came as a wood apple to fall down and be destroyed; being a child, he sucked and mercifully consumed the poison from pūtanā to have her killed; he mercifully incarnated as poison to kill the famous demon rāvaṇa, who was having the weapon, sword; he is enjoyable like nectar (for devotees); he is the lord of all; he is the complete one who is mercifully present on the heads of those who desire him; he is the cheater who cheated to have kamsan killed.

**venjinak kaḷiṟṟai** – One who is beautiful like an intoxicated elephant which is having cruel anger.

**viḷangāy …** – The two monsters who came in the form of a calf and a wood apple were killed by using them against each other – one who is capable of doing that.

**pēy magaḷ …** – The young child who happily consumed the poison of pūtanā to kill her.

**tōnṟal …** – The deity of death who incarnated to kill rāvaṇa who was famously known as enemy in all the worlds and was wielding a weapon.

**amudattinai** – For the favourable ones, his presence itself is like nectar.

**naccuvār ucci mēl niṟkum nambiyai** – One who stands atop the heads of those who have even the slightest desire towards him and who remains complete by thinking that it is his own benefit to do so.

**kanjanai …** – Eliminating kamsan’s evil thought with himself; the one who deceives those who are unfavourable. I saw him in tirukkaṇṇamangai.

paṇṇinai – sweet like a song; paṇṇil – in that song; ninṟadu – very distinguished and being the essence; pānmaiyai – being very enjoyable like the nature of; pāluḷ – like milk and that which is inside; neyyinai – being like ghee; māl uruvāy ninṟa – being naturally very vast; viṇṇinai – being the controller of paramapadam; viḷangum sudar – very radiant; sōdiyai – having a luminous form; vēḷviyai – being the controller of fire sacrifices; viḷakkin oḷi tannai – self-illuminous like the flame of the lamp; maṇṇinai – being the sustainer like earth; malaiyai – being immovable like a mountain; alai nīrinai – being iśta viniyōga arha (at the disposal of others) like water, which is hit by waves; māmadiyai – being the one who gives great knowledge; maṟaiyōr tangaḷ – for the brāhmaṇas, who recite vēdam; kaṇṇinai – being the eye which reveals the knowledge; kaṇgaḷ āraḷavum – to fill the eyes; ninṟu – remaining firm; kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍukoṇḍēn – I got to see him in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Remaining firm, to have my eyes filled, I got to see bhagavān in the divyadēśam named tirukkaṇṇamangai; he is sweet like a song; he is very enjoyable like the nature of being very distinguished and being the essence of that song; he is like milk and ghee which is inside that milk; he is the controller of paramapadam which is naturally very vast; he is having a very radiant, luminous form; he is the controller of fire sacrifices; he is self-illuminous like the flame of the lamp; he is the sustainer like earth; he is immovable like a mountain; he is *iśta viniyōga arha* (at the disposal of others) like water, which is hit by waves; he is the one who gives great knowledge; for the brāhmaṇas who recite vēdam, he is like the eye which reveals the knowledge.

**paṇṇinai** – As said in “*ya ādyas svādunām*” (Best among sweet words), one who is sweet like a song.

**paṇṇil ninṟadu ōr pānmaiyai** – One who is incomparably sweet like the music of the song which will attract everyone, without any difference.

**pāluḷ neyyinai** – One who is a pursuable aspect in both the essence (ghee) and the residue (milk).

**māl uruvāy ninṟa viṇṇinai** – One who is having nitya vibhūti which is vast enough to be known as “*tripād vibhūti*“.

**viḷangum sudarc cōdiyai** – One who is standing there with limitlessly radiant, divine auspicious form.

**vēḷviyai** – One who remains as the karmas, which are means to reach that abode.

**viḷakkin oḷi tannai** – One who has natural radiance.

**maṇṇinai** – One who forgets all the mistakes committed by everyone. One who gives space to remain on him, even to those who commit mistakes.

**malaiyai** – One whose such nature cannot be shaken by anyone.

**alai nīrinai** – One who remains to be channeled anywhere and used for different purposes.

**mālai** – One who is an embodiment of love towards his devotees.

**māmadiyai** – As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 10.10](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/10-10/) “*dadāmi buddiyōgam tam*” (I bestow them the knowledge to attain me), one who can grant the buddi yōgam to attain him.

**maṟaiyōr tangaḷ kaṇṇinai** – One who remains as the vision for those who have learnt vēdam, to not see anything other than him.

**kaṇgaḷ āravum ninṟu** – To eliminate the dryness of the withered eyes due to not seeing him, I got to see him remaining firm.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.10. Kannamangaiyul

*kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍēn enṟu kādalāl kalikanṟi urai seyda vaṇṇa oṇ tamiḻ onbadōdu onṟivai vallarāy uraippār madiyam tavaḻ viṇṇil viṇṇavarāy magiḻveyduvar meymmai sollil veṇsangam onṟēndiyakaṇṇa! nindanakkum kuṟippāgilkaṟkalām kaviyin poruḷ tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇamangai uḷ – in tirukkaṇṇamangai; kaṇḍu koṇḍēn enṟu – saying “I got to see”; kalikanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; kādalāl – with love; urai seyda – mercifully spoke; vaṇṇam – having music, which is an attribute of song; oṇ tamiḻ – present in beautiful tamiḻ language; onbadōdu onṟu – the ten pāsurams; ivai vallavarāy – being able to learn these ten pāsurams; uraippār – those who are able to recite; madi tavaḻ – where moon is roaming; am viṇṇil – going to the beautiful (most enjoyable) heaven; viṇṇavarāy – being dēvatās; magiḻvu eyduvar – will become joyful; meymmai sollil – if we were to speak about the real benefit; veṇ sangam onṟu – śrī pāncajanyam, which is white and distinguished; ēndiya – holding; kaṇṇa – Oh, the supreme lord!; kuṟippāgil – if it is agreeable to your divine heart; kaviyin poruḷ – the meanings of these pāsurams; ninṟanakkum – even for you, who are omniscient; kaṟkalām – they are apt to be learnt

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Saying “I got to see bhagavān in tirukkaṇṇamangai”, tirumangai āḻvār mercifully spoke with love these ten pāsurams having music which is an attribute of song, which are present in beautiful tamiḻ language; those who are able to learn and recite these pāsurams will become joyful, going to the beautiful heaven where moon is roaming and becoming dēvatās. Oh, the supreme lord, who is holding śrī pāncajanyam which is white and distinguished! If we were to speak about the real benefit and if it is agreeable to your divine heart, even for you, who are omniscient, the meanings of these pāsurams are apt to be learnt.

**kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍēn enṟu** – Saying “I got to see bhagavān, who is seen after reaching the special abode of paramapdam, right here in this samsāram, in tirukkaṇṇamangai”.

**kādalāl kali kanṟi urai seyda** – Mercifully spoken by āḻvār due to overwhelming love.

**vaṇṇa oṇ tamiḻ onbadōdu onṟu ivai** – These ten pāsurams, which are having music and are beautiful.

**vallarāy uraippār** – Considering the difficulty in reciting the pāsurams fully in sequence, for those who would like to recite, āḻvār is saying “If anyone is able to recite”.

**madiyam tavaḻ viṇṇil viṇṇavarāy magiḻveyduvar** – They will enter the higher worlds and enjoy the enjoyable aspects in there fully.

**meymmai sollil** – If we were to explain the nature of the meanings of these pāsurams.

**veṇ sangam …** – Oh supreme lord, who is holding śri pāncajanyam, which highlights your aiśvaryam (opulence/control), in your divine hand! Even for you, if you have the desire in learning these meanings, the meanings are so potent that you have to learn it as my śiśya (disciple).

**kuṟippāgil** – If it is agreeable to your divine heart.

**kaṟkalām** – It will not be possible if you remain prideful as naturally omniscient; you can learn if you study under me. For bhagavān who remained humble and studied under vasiśta, sāndīpani, is there anything wrong to study under tirumangai āḻvār?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## Eighth Centum

## 8.1 Seruvarai

## 8.1.2. Seruvarai

*seruvarai mun āsaṟutta silai anṟō?kaittalattadu enginṟāḷāl poruvarai mun pōr tolaitta ponnāḻi maṟṟoru kai enginṟāḷāl oruvaraiyum ninnoppār oppilā ennappā! enginṟāḷāl karuvarai pōl ninṟānaik kaṇṇapurattu ammānaik kaṇḍāḷ kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

seruvarai – enemies who are set to fight; mun – in the past; āsaṟutta – destroyed; silai anṟō – isn’t it this bow?; kaittalattadu – present in the divine hand; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; poru – fighting; varai – mountains; munbu – in the past; ōr – at a time; tulaitta – destroyed; pon – beautiful; āḻi – tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); maṟṟu oru kai – present in the other hand; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; oruvaraiyum – any one; nin – for you; oppār – not a match (Hence); oppilā – matchless; en appā – Oh my lord!; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; karu – blackish; varaipōl – like a black mountain; ninṟānai – standing (to be easily visible to our eyes); enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; kaṇṇa purattu – mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; ammānai – the lord, śaurirājan; kaṇḍāḷ kolō – did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship him?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter, parakāla nāyaki is saying “īsn’t it this bow which is present in his divine hand which destroyed enemies who were set to fight, in the past? In his other divine hand, the divine chakra which destroyed the fighting mountains in the past at a particular time, is present. Since there is none who matches you, you are matchless, oh, my lord! Did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship the lord, śaurirājan who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram?

**seruvarai mun āsaṟutta silai anṟō kaittalattadu enginṟāḷāl** – Should you not give me, who has seen you once, the eternal experience? parakāla nāyaki is saying “Is the reason for not doing so, due to not having the weapon in your hand to eliminate the obstacles? \[No – you have it\] āren’t you having śrī śārngam which was used to destroy rāvaṇa et al, who were obstacles for your union with pirātti? Will it not be a tool to accept me? Is that the obstacle for my goal? It is remaining without helping me in this manner”. *seruvar* – those who fight. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 51.55 “*trātum na śaktā yudi rāma vadyam*” (If śrī rāma decides to kill someone, no one can save that person) – no one can fight him in a war and win over him – one can win over him only by atoning for the mistake and surrendering unto him.  śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36-11 “*dvidā bhajyēyam apyēvam na namēyam* . .” (Even if I am broken into two pieces, I will not bend before anyone) – those who remained fully in an inimical state. Those people.

**āsaṟutta** – Eliminated the wars. Those evil people who roamed around thinking “When will we have someone to fight with us?” were eliminated so that they cannot go anywhere and say “We are your enemies” – such bow was in his divine hand. Do I have to remain relaxed since he has placed it elsewhere and has to bring it over? While it is in his hand, why should I suffer in separation? Is he holding it in his hand for beauty? parakāla nāyaki asks “Should he not use it to destroy the enemies?” iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 23.30 “*na danur bhūśaṇāya mē*” (I am not having this bow as a decoration). lakśmaṇa is asking “While it looks like it is present for decoration superficially, did you think that it will not be useful for my valour?” When the enemies were increasing and marching \[towards the town/temple\], piḷḷai tirukkaṇṇapurattu araiyar pleaded in front of bhagavān “*seruvarai mun āsaṟutta silaiyanṟō kaittalattadu*“, śaurip perumāḷ mercifully said that he will finish the enemies immediately.

**poru varai …** – parakāla nāyaki says – Should I remain relaxed thinking “If this hand is having bow, the other hand is free”? ōr should I remain relaxed thinking “He will only eliminate the hurdles occurred for his beloved consorts”? Would he not eliminate my sorrows, while he eliminated the sorrows of the world? Is he not having the beautiful divine chakra in his other hand, which destroyed the mountains which would fly with wings, in the past?

It is said that in the past, all of the mountains would have wings and fly around and land in particular places causing destruction there. Just as iḷaiya perumāḷ would eliminate perumāḷ’s obstacles, bhagavān incarnated as upēndra mūrti, as the younger brother of indra and used his divine chakra to sever their wings.

**pon āḻi** – That divine chakra, which was adding to his beauty, was used to sever the wings of the strong mountains. Alternatively, *poruvarai* indicates kuvalayāpeedam. This could be talking about that incident where kriṣṇa punched its cheeks with his hand decorated by ring \[which is also known as tiruvāḻi\]. It is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-10-6-nugarchchi-urumo/) “*pugarc chem mugatta kaḷiṟatta pon āḻik kai en ammān*” (my lord, is having divine hands with attractive divine ring, which was used to destroy the elephant having incomparable radiance and reddish face). Due to certain persons’ \[his parents’\] request, he hid the divine chakra, but usually he will never be without the divine chakra in his hand. Even in incarnations where he hid himself completely as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 120-11 “*abravīt tridaśaśrēśtān rāmō darmabhrutām vara*: l ***ātmānam mānuśam manyē*** *rāmam daśaratātmajam* ll” (śrī rāma, the most supreme among noble people, addressing the distinguished celestial entities said “I consider myself as rāma, a human entity, the son of daśarata”), periya tiruvadi came and performed his duties \[though the quote is from śrī rāmāyaṇam, the incident of garudāḻvār coming is in kriṣṇāvatāram\]. Though he tries to hide it, the divine chakra will automatically climb his hand as said in mahābhāratam bhīśma parvam – “*sudarśanam cititamātramāśu tasyāgrahastam svayamārurōha*” (As soon as he \[kriṣṇa\] thought about him, sudarśana at once seated himself on the hand of kriṣṇa).

**oruvaraiyum …** – Oh, one who has no match for your valour, even if there is a match for other qualities! When he holds śrī śārngam and tiruvāḻi, it will be visible that he is the superior lord. Since you have no match, oh, one who is incomparable!

**en appā** – Oh, one who is naturally related in all manners, so that we need not withdraw from you, thinking you are superior to all! These people would not like everyone in this world who holds onto weapons. She is saying “Oh, one who is naturally related to me!” With the divine weapons in his hand, are his favours limited? His acts reveal that he is our natural relative.

**karu varai pōl ninṟānai** – He came and stood here even before she called out. To bestow himself, he arrives first and waits for the opportunity.

**karu varai** – When he is seen, he appears \[pleasant\] like a black mountain.

**ninṟānai** – He will give himself fully – there will be shortcoming in those who come and accept him – that is how he is standing there.

**kaṇṇapurattu ammānai** – Being present like a black mountain is seen in śrīvaikuṇṭam also. Unlike there, here in tirukkaṇṇapuram, he is present as sarvēśvaran, yet, in an easily attainable manner.

**kaṇḍāḷ kolō** – Not stopping with just hearing about him, it appears that she has seen him.

**kaṇḍāḷ** – Not only is he waiting for an opportunity to accept her, she also got to be favourable towards him. Looks like she has opened her eyes to see his physical beauty and the standing posture which reveals his generosity.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.3. Tunnu mamani

*tunnu māmaṇi mudi mēl tuḻāy alangal tōnṟumāl enginṟāḷāl minnumā maṇi magara kuṇḍalangaḷ vil vīsum enginṟāḷāl ponnin māmaṇi āram aṇiyāgattu ilangumāl enginṟāḷāl kannimāmadiḷ pudai sūḻ kaṇṇapurattu ammānaik kaṇḍāḷ kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

tunnu – dense; mā – best; maṇi – by precious gemstones (decorated); mudimēl – on the divine crown (worn); tuḻāy alangal – divine tuḷasi garland; tōnṟumāl – appearing; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; minnu – shining; mā – best; maṇi – embossed with precious gemstones; magara kuṇḍalangaḷ – divine makara kuṇḍalams (earrings); vil – radiance; vīsum – spreading; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; ponnil – made of gold; mā – best; maṇi – embossed with precious gemstones; āram – necklace; aṇi – being an ornament (for that ornament); āgattu – in his divine chest; ilangumāl – is shining; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; kanni – imperishable; mā – having greatness of being indestructible by anyone; madiḷ – by the divine fort; pudai – in the surrounding; sūḻ – surrounded; kaṇṇa purattu – mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; ammānai – the lord, śaurirājan; kaṇḍāḷ kolō – did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship him?

**Перевод:**

**parakāla nāyaki tells her divine mother “Even if you say ‘You should not have this much of love. Whatever you may do, you have to follow our good instructions’, the beauty of his ornaments, is standing in front of my eyes. Should I listen to your words, or should I be engaged in his physical beauty which is made visible to me?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter parakāla nāyaki is saying “Divine tuḷasi garland is appearing on his divine crown, which is decorated densely with the shining, best, precious gemstones; the divine makara kuṇḍalams (earrings), embossed with precious gemstones are emanating the radiance; the golden necklace, which has the best precious gemstones embossed in it, is shining in the divine chest which is like an ornament for ornaments”. Did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship the lord, śaurirājan who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram where the surrounding areas are surrounded by the imperishable divine fort which is having greatness of being indestructible by anyone?

**tunnu** – parakāla nāyaki says “While the divine tuḷasi which is worn on the divine crown, which is decorated densely with priceless precious stones, is seen, will I hear your words?” The divine crown and the divine tuḷasi which is placed on the divine crown, reveal his lordship. Just as the enemies’ necks were only visible to arjuna, only the divine tuḷasi garland is visible for her.

**minnum …** – She says “The divine earrings pulled her heart from the divine garland. The earrings’ radiance was appearing to be a lamp which shows the beauty acquired by him from these aspects. The divine earrings which are embossed with shining, priceless precious stones, made the other radiance to subside and the radiance of the earrings spread over all of his divine form”.

**ponnin …** – She says “The golden necklace, which is embossed with precious stones, is shining in his divine chest which appears like an ornament to that ornament”.

**aṇi āgattu ilangum** – It is shining in the divine heart where pirātti is mercifully present. The divine chest for which, the ornament is extraneous. She is saying “In the divine chest which is like an ornament for the ornament and should be checked for druśti (evil eyes) by performing ālatti (a ritual involving lit camphor), the divine ornaments and śrī kaustubha jewel are shining”.

**kanni …** – It looks like that the one entity, who is well protected, is known exclusively by her. It looks like that she has seen the bhagavān, who is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram, which is surrounded by the fort which can protect according to the greatness of the one who is inside and which cannot be destroyed by anyone.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.4. Taraya tan tulaba

*tārāya taṇ tuḷaba vaṇḍuḻuda varai mārban enginṟāḷālpōrānaik kombositta putpāgan en ammān enginṟāḷālārānum kāṇmingaḷ ambavaḷam vāy avanukku enginṟāḷālkār vānam ninṟadirum kaṇṇapurattu ammānaik kaṇḍāḷ kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

tār – blossomed; āya – good; taṇ – cool; tuḷabam – in the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland (present in); vaṇḍu – beetle; uḻuda – moving around; varai – like a mountain (strong); mārban – one who has divine chest; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; pōr – battle-ready; ānai – elephant’s (kuvalayāpeedam); kombu – tusks; ositta – one who plucked; puḷ – climbing on periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); pāgan – one who conducts; en – for me; ammān – the lord; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; ārānum – any of you (who stops me by giving good instructions); kāṇmingaḷ – see; avanukku – for such emperumān; am – beautiful; pavaḷam – like a coral; vāy – his divine lips are present; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; kār – blackish; vānam – cloud; ninṟu – residing eternally; adirum – roaring; kaṇṇa purattu – mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; ammānai – the lord, śaurirājan; kaṇḍāḷ kolō – did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship him?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter is saying “bhagavān is having mountain like divine chest where a beetle is moving around in the blossomed, cool tiruttuḻāy garland; he plucked the tusks of the elephant, kuvalayāpeedam which was battle-ready and is the lord who conducts periya tiuvadi (garudāḻvār) for me; any of you, who is trying to stop me by giving good instructions, should see the coral like beautiful divine lips, which are present for such emperumān”; did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship the lord, śaurirājan who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram where the blackish cloud is present eternally and roaring?

**tārāya …** – The beetle, which is present on the well blossomed, fresh, cool tiruttuḻāy garland, is moving around on the divine chest which seems to be the dune formed by the overflowing honey from that tiruttuḻāy garland. The divine chest is so slushy that my bosoms can be taken and planted there; parakāla nāyaki desires to embrace that chest, still unable to do it, but a beetle gets to be there.

**pōr ānai …** – Effortlessly plucked the battle-ready kuvalayāpeedam’s tusk and made me totally exist for him – says parakāla nāyaki. She is like one among the girls who are mentioned in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-20-54 which says “***sakhya: paśyata*** *kriṣṇasya mukhamatyaruṇēkśaṇam* l *vikāsiśāradarambhōjamavaśyāya jalōkśitam* l *paribhūya stitam janma saphalam kriyatām druśa*: ll” (Oh friends! Look at the eyes of kriṣṇa which have won over \[the beauty of\] lotus of autumn season, which has been sprinkled with dew. Make use of having been provided with eyes). Manifesting his presence on periya tiruvadi, he made sure that I don’t live for myself \[but for him\].

**ārānum kāṇmingaḷ** – You, who are giving good instructions and trying to withdraw me from him, also see. For those who have seen his divine lips which resemble a beautiful coral, was it possible to leave him?

**kārvānam …** – The cloud in the rainy season will be roaring. Reminding what is said in “*ōgha mēghasvana:*” (thunder-cloud filled with water). As said in “*mēghōdaya:*” (rising cloud), the lord of tirukkaṇṇapuram which is always having rainy season where the sky is always roaring.

**kaṇḍāḷ kolō** – Not just returning on hearing, it looks like she remained there, seen him and enjoyed.

## 8.1.5. Adittalamum

*adittalamum tāmaraiyē angaigaḷum pangayamē enginṟāḷāl mudittalamum poṟpūṇum en nenjattu uḷ agalādu enginṟāḷāl vadittadangaṇ malaravaḷō varai āgattu uḷ iruppāḷ enginṟāḷāl kadikkamalam kaḷḷugukkum kaṇṇapurattu ammānaik kaṇḍāḷ kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

adi – divine feet’s; talamum – place; tāmaraiyē – is enjoyable like lotus; am – beautiful; kaigaḷum – divine hands; pangayamē – are also looking like lotus; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; mudi – the divine crown’s; talamum – place (to be decorated on it); poṟpūṇum – divine ornament; en – my; nenjattu – heart’s; uḷ – from the inside; agalādu – not separating; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; vadi – sharp; tadam – expansive; kaṇmalar – having flower-like divine eyes; avaḷō – that periya pirāttiyār; varai – expansive like mountain; āgattu – (emperumān’s) divine chest’s; uḷ – in the middle; iruppāḷ – residing; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; kaḷ – honey; ugukkum – shedding; kadi – fragrant; kamalam – lotus flowers present; kaṇṇa purattu – mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; ammānai – the lord, śaurirājan; kaṇḍāḷ kolō – did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship him?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter, parakāla nāyaki is saying “His divine feet are enjoyable like lotus and divine hands are also looking like lotus; the divine ornament on his divine crown is not separating from the inside of my heart; that periya pirāttiyār who is having sharp, expansivfe flower-like divine eyes is residing in the centre of his mountain-like expansive divine chest”; did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship the lord, śaurirājan, who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram where fragrant lotus flowers, which are shedding honey, are present?

**adittalam …** – Our goal \[divine feet\] is incomparably enjoyable.

**angaigaḷum pangayamē** – The divine hands which will lift up those who fall at those divine feet, are also like lotus – says parakāla nāyaki.

**mudittalam …** – Being withered by the embrace, when one looks up, the divine crown confirms that this is the apt entity and the divine ornament which decorates such divine crown, are not leaving my heart – she says. The mothers will say that you should listen to our words where we say “Whatever it is, you should not have so much love” and hold them in your heart. For that, she responds saying “Your words will impact my heart only when these aspects of bhagavān leave my heart”.

**vadittadam kaṇ …** – The ornament for his divine chest appears to be periya pirāttiyār. While the one who unites us is present close to you, what can I say as the reason and leave? When my hold for you is standing close to you, what shortcoming can I identify and move away? Just as one glance will knock a person down, my lady lord who is having eyes which can handle unlimited enjoyers, is the one who is present on his divine chest. Alternatively – should I remain patiently thinking that he is not well learnt in romance? Is there no enjoyability? Is he not the apt lord? Is the one who unites us not present? What can I say as the reason to leave \[None\]?

**kadikkamalam …** – Very fragrant flower sheds honey. It sheds honey since there was too much honey which is not useful for the beetles and since the flower was unable to hold so much honey. In that town, the beetles which stay on the lotus flower cannot fully drink the honey from that flower \[i.e. there is so much extra\].

**kaṇṇapurattu ammānaik kaṇḍāḷ kolō** – In that town, the objects are much more enjoyable than the ability of the enjoyers to enjoy them. In that manner, it appears that parakāla nāyaki is speaking after enjoying the incomparably enjoyable lord.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.6. Per ayiram udaiya

*pēr āyiram udaiya pērāḷan pērāḷan enginṟāḷāl ērār kanamagara kuṇḍalattan eṇ tōḷan enginṟāḷāl nīrār maḻai mugilē nīḷ varaiyē okkumāl enginṟāḷāl kārār vayal maruvum kaṇṇapurattu ammānaik kaṇḍāḷ kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

āyiram – thousand; pēr – divine names; udaiya – due to having; pērāḷan – having greatness; pērāḷan – the great personality; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; ēr – beauty; Ar – filled; kana – made of precious gemstones; magara kuṇḍalattan – one who is wearing śrī makara kuṇḍalam (earring); eṇ tōḷan – having eight divine shoulders; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; nīr – by water; Ar – filled; maḻai mugilē – dark cloud; nīḷ – vast; varaiyē – dark mountain; okkumāl – emperumān who resembles; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; kār – darkness; Ar – filled; vayal – by crops; maruvum – surrounded; kaṇṇa purattu – mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; ammānai – the lord, śaurirājan; kaṇḍāḷ kolō – did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship him?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter, parakāla nāyaki is saying “He is the great personality having the greatness due to having thousand divine names; he is wearing śrī makara kuṇḍalam (earring) which is made of precious gemstones filled with beauty; he is having eight divine shoulders; he is resembling a dark cloud filled with water and a vast dark mountain”; did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship the lord, śaurirājan who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is surrounded by crops which are filled with darkness \[i.e. ready for harvest\].

**pēr āyiram …** – One who is having thousand divine names which explain his qualities and leelās \[divine activities\].

**pērāḷan** – As said in mahābhāratam “*dēvō nāma sahasravān*” (The shining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has thousand names), [tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/06/thiruvaimozhi-9-3-1-orayiramay/) “*pēr āyiram koṇḍadōr pīdudaiyan* *– nārāyaṇan*” (nārāyaṇan is the one who is having the greatness of having thousand names) and [mudal tiruvandādi 8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/munram-thiruvandhadhi-8/) “*nāmam pala solli nārāyanā enṟu*” (reciting many divine names \[of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] and the divine name nārāyaṇa which is his most important name), as said in “*pāl pasu udaiyavan*” (one who has milking cow), he is having the greatness of having thousand divine names as said in periya tirumoḻi 10.8.4 “*nāmam palavum udai nāraṇan*” (one who has many divine names).

**pērāḷan** – Greatness got added to great personality. She is saying “Because these divine names belonged to him, they became shining”. Alternatively – pērāḷan reflects his true nature – further, his qualities became inconceivable due to those divine names etc.

Alternatively,

**pērāḷan pērāḷan** – She is saying “Great personality! Great personality!”.

**ērār …** – She is speaking about the true nature of bhagavān who is indicated by these divine names. She is reminded of his beauty which she enjoyed previously. She says “Being the one who is having divine makara kuṇḍalams which are made of very beautiful precious gemstones, and one who is having eight shoulders where they \[the earrings\] are swaying and touching”.

**eṇ tōḷan** – Just as he held the five divine weapons while having four shoulders only, just as he churned the ocean with four shoulders which appeared as thousand shoulders for him, she is saying that he has eight shoulders while he only has four shoulders.

**nīrār maḻai mugil …** – The simile needs to be well decorated to explain bhagavān’s divine form so that it is comparable to some extent. She is saying that he is having a divine form which resembles a cloud which has absorbed water fully and a dark mountain. It indicates both aspects – rejuvenating, inconceivable.

**kārār vayal …** – Since there are well-matured crops everywhere, the fertile field is dark. Just as muktātmās will always remain aged twenty five years, and matching the colour of bhagavān who is residing inside the town, the town is as said in periya tirumoḻi 10.1.1 “*karunel sūḻ kaṇṇamangaiyuḷ kāṇḍumē*” (Seen in tirukkaṇṇamangai which is surrounded by dark crops). In this manner, the fields are always dark and ready for harvest.

**kaṇṇapuram …** – Looks like she has seen his divine form.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.7. Sevvaratta

*sevvaratta udai ādai adan mēl ōr sivaḷigaikkaccu enginṟāḷāl avvaratta adi iṇaiyum angaigaḷum pangayamē enginṟāḷāl maivaḷarkkum maṇi uruvam maragadamō! maḻai mugilō! enginṟāḷālkaivaḷarkkum aḻalāḷar kaṇṇapurattu ammānaik kaṇḍāḷ kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem – reddish; varatta – best; udai – worn; ādai – divine garment; adan mēl – atop that pītāmbaram; ōr – unique; sivaḷigaik kaccu – golden pleat; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; avvaratta – similarly reddish; adi iṇaiyum – two divine feet; am – beautiful; kaigaḷum – divine hands; pangayamē – lotus only; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; mai – black colour; vaḷarkkum – nurturing; maṇi – like a black gemstone; uruvum – divine form; maradagamō – is it emerald?; maḻai mugilō – is it a dark cloud?; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; kai – with his hands; vaḷarkkum – nurtured (through hōmam); aḻalāḷar – where those, who are having fire, are residing; kaṇṇa purattu – mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; ammānai – the lord, śaurirājan; kaṇḍāḷ kolō – did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship him?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter, parakāla nāyaki is saying “He is wearing reddish divine garment in the best way and is having golden pleats on that pītāmbaram; similarly his pair of divine feet and beautiful divine hands are lotus only; is his divine form which is like a black precious gemstone which nurtures black colour, an emerald stone or dark cloud?” Did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship the lord, śaurirājan who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram where those who are having fire, which was nurtured by his own hands, are residing.

**sevvaratta udai ādai** – She is speaking out revealing how she was won over by his dressing sense. If he wears the divine pītāmbaram, it would appear as if it flowered out of his divine waist as said in “*kauśēya puśpita katītatam*” (the silk garment in the waist appears to have blossomed from the waist)

**sevvaratta udai ādai …** – Through both sevva (red) and ratta (blood), red is only indicated. The same word may be repeated or a synonym for the word may follow. This is said as *mīmisai* (repetition) and implies the stronger impact of the meaning. Also, it can be seen as sivanda (reddish), varatta (best); thus, very reddish garment which is worn. Further atop, sivaḷigaik kaccu – the kaccam (folds) which are worn; also said as golden folds. Similarly, reddish divine feet and divine hands are also lotus only due to their expanse and other qualities.

**mai vaḷarkkum …** – Everything is dark in his case. Like a black gemstone which nurtures black colour as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.6.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/09/thiruvaimozhi-7-6-6-vandheydhumaru-ariyen/) “*malgu neelac cudar taḻaippa*” (bluish gem with well spread, abundant bluish radiance).

**kai vaḷarkkum …** – In this town, no one would submit dakśiṇai (offering) to perform hōmam. Since he is having fire which was nurtured by him, everything starting with his divine garment appears reddish for her.

## 8.1.8. Korrap pul

*koṟṟap puḷ onṟēṟi manṟūdē varuginṟān enginṟāḷāl veṟṟip pōr indiraṟkum indiranē okkumāl enginṟāḷāl peṟṟakkāl avan āgam peṇ piṟandōm uyyōmō! enginṟāḷāl kaṟṟa nūl maṟaiyāḷar kaṇṇapurattu ammānaik kaṇḍāḷ kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

koṟṟa – Victorious (due to helping devotees); onṟu – unique; puḷ – periya tiruvadi; ēṟi – remaining seated; manṟu ūdē – in a common/public place; varuginṟān – he is coming; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; veṟṟip pōr – just for engagement in battle; indirarkkum – for king nahuśa et al who are spoken as indra in this world; indiranē – dēvēndra, who is the indran; okkumāl – to be matching; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; avan – that emperumān’s; āgam – in the divine chest; peṟṟakkāl – if we get to embrace; peṇ – as woman; piṟandōm – we who are born; uyyōmō – will we not be uplifted?; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; kaṟṟa – learnt; nūl – śāstrams; maṟai – vēdams; āḷar – where those who are having are residing; kaṇṇa purattu – mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; ammānai – the lord, śaurirājan; kaṇḍāḷ kolō – did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship him?

**Перевод:**

**While narrating this, nampiḷḷai, who had heard this pāsuram mercifully explained, said “As piḷḷai amudanār was explaining the introduction for this decad, he cleverly narrated how the kings would climb their palanquin and roam around in the private quarters and streets. Since we were young at that time, we could not comprehend those explanations. We analysed what is the connection between this decad and the activities of the kings. Now, we have understood that it is this (what is explained in this pāsuram)”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter, parakāla nāyaki is saying “bhagavān is remaining seated on the victorious, unique periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) and coming to a common/public place; he is matching dēvēndran who is the indran for king nahuśa et al who are spoken of as indra in this world just for their engagement in battles; will we, who are born as women, not be uplifted if we get to embrace that emperumān’s divine chest?” Did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship the lord, śaurirājan who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram, where, those who have learnt vēdams and other śāstrams, are residing?

**koṟṟap puḷ …** – bhagavān, who is common for all and who is the unique benefactor, climbed his vehicle and arrived at the place which is common/public for all, just as those who go and feed water in a pot to thirsty people, wherever they are. She is saying “I don’t know who is going to capture him? Who is going to attack him?” She is thinking that he should come without anyone else’s knowledge and enter into her eyes and remain there.

Next, she is saying “If he sets out to come here, he has no obstacles”.

**veṟṟip pōr …** – When it comes to battles in wars, he is as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 3.40 “*vīryē sākśāt śaśipatē:*” (In valour, he is like indra). For indran \[valorous kings\], there is another indran – that is, mahēndran. One who became crowned through killing of vrutrāsura et al. She is saying that bhagavān matches such indran.

**peṟṟakkāl …** – If we get to embrace his divine chest. As said in  śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 40-5 “***sruśtatvam vanavāsāya*** – *pramādam mākārśī:*” (you were sired by me only to follow śrī rāma to the forest – don’t look at his beauty and miss out on serving him), if we get to embrace him, we will live, otherwise we will perish as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (considered as non-sentient). Such us, will be uplifted by such an embrace. In that divyadēśam, there is no one who steals manuscripts and studies them; there is no one who learns by studying books on his own; they are all well-learnt in śāstrams and vēdams by hearing from an ācārya and repeating that. While she is speaking about one who is fully spoken of in vēdam coming there and what is said in “*yam indramāhu:*” (He is said to be indran), should she not have seen him at all?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
