## 8.1.9. Vandamarum

*vaṇḍamarum vanamālai maṇi mudi mēl maṇa nāṟum enginṟāḷāl uṇḍu ivar pāl anbu enakkenṟu oru kālum pirigilēn enginṟāḷāl paṇḍu ivaraik kaṇḍu aṟivadu evvūril? yām enṟē payilginṟāḷāl kaṇḍavar tam manam vaḻangum kaṇṇapurattu ammānaik kaṇḍāḷ kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu – beetles; amarum – spread over; vanamālai – tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; maṇi – embossed with precious gemstones; mudi mēl – on the divine crown; maṇam nāṟum – specially emanating fragrance; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; ivar pāl – towards him; enakku – for me; anbu – desire; uṇḍu – is there; enṟu – saying this; oru kālum – ever; pirigilēn – will not separate; enginṟāḷāl – she is saying; paṇḍu – previous; yām – us; ivarai – this lord; evvūril – in which divyadēśam; kaṇḍu – seeing to the full satisfaction of eyes; aṟivadu – known; enṟē – saying; payilginṟāḷ – repeatedly saying; Al – alas! (trouble); kaṇḍavar – those who have vorśipped śaurirājan; tam – their; manam – heart; vaḻangum – beautiful to give fully; kaṇṇa purattu – mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; ammānai – the lord, śaurirājan; kaṇḍāḷ kolō – did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship him?

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter, parakāla nāyaki is saying “tiruttuḻāy garland which is having beetles spread over it and is on the divine crown embossed with precious gemstones, is specially emanating fragrance; I am having desire towards him and I will never separate from him”. She is repeatedly saying “In which divyadēśam had we seen this lord to the full satisfaction of our eyes and known him?” Alas! Did she see to the satisfaction of her eyes and worship the lord, śaurirājan who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram and who is so beautiful that those who vorśipped him will give their heart fully to him?

**vaṇḍu amarum …** – The tuḷasi will emit fragrance a little bit less while being on the plant, and will emit double the fragrance upon climbing the divine crown. The beetles are present on the tuḷasi just as fragrance rests on it.

**uṇḍu ivar …** – She, who would prove with certainty that she has no love towards him when told that she has, is now saying “I have love towards him”. What is implied by this? She is saying “I have completely abandoned you \[her friends and mothers\]and said this”.

**paṇḍu …** – On the first day when he is seen, he would be seen with the natural lordship and mercy in his face and will make one think “His face looks familiar; where did we see him?”; after becoming well familiar with him, he will make one think “We have not seen him anywhere at all”. It is implied that he is nitya apūrva viśayam (one who remains fresh forever). When asked “Does the sentence show both the meanings?”, nanjīyar mercifully explains “See the usage of payilginṟāḷāl (speaking – present tense). She will always be saying the same thing. Hence the meaning should be in these two ways only”. When asked “Since her words are in this manner, should it be that she has entered the town and seen him?”, her words appear to be those of a person who has had her heart captured; had her heart not captured by him, she would not say these words in front of her mother. Those who have come and seen him, will hand over their hearts to him fully.

## 8.1.10. Mavalarum

*māvaḷarum mennōkki mādarāḷ māyavanaik kaṇḍāḷ enṟu kāvaḷarum kadipoḻil sūḻ kaṇṇapurattu ammānaik kaliyan sonna pāvaḷarum tamiḻ mālai panniya nūl ivai aindum aindum vallār pūvaḷarum kaṟpagam sēr ponnulagil mannavarāy pugaḻ takkōrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā – like a deer; vaḷarum – expansive; men – soft; nōkki – having eyes; mādarāḷ – woman; māyavanai – being the amazing personality; kā – like a flower garden; vaḷarum – spreading on its own; kadi – fragrant; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; kaṇṇapurattu – mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; ammānai – śaurirājan, who is the lord; kaṇḍāḷ – vorśipped with her eyes to their full satisfaction; enṟu – on that matter; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; pā – meter of the poem; vaḷarum – nurturing; nūl – by the literature known as śāstram; panniya – elaborated; tamiḻ mālai – in the form of a tamiḻ garland; ivai aindum aindum – these ten pāsurams; vallār – those who can learn/recite; pū – flowers; vaḷarum – growing; kaṟpagam – kaṟpaga trees; sēr – present; pon ulagil – in paramapadam; mannavarāy – as lords (by nityasūris); pugaḻ – to be glorified; takkōrē – will be the goal

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār mercifully spoke ten pāsurams in the mood of a woman, who has the soft and expansive eyes like those of a deer, towards śaurirājan, who is an amazing personality and the lord who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is surrounded by fragrant gardens which are like a flower garden spreading fragrance, on seeing such bhagavān to the full satisfaction of her eyes; these ten pāsurams are in the form of a tamiḻ garland where the meter of the poem is nurturing and is elaborated by the literature known as śāstram; those who are able to learn/recite these pāsurams will be glorified by nityasūris as their lords in paramapadam where kaṟpaga trees, having well blossomed flowers, are present, and will be the goal for such nityasūris.

**mā vaḷarum …** – The divine mother said that she cannot be withdrawn. The mother said “Like that of a deer, she saw with her expansive, soft eyes, the amazing personality, matching the beauty of her eyes”.

**kā vaḷarum kadi poḻil …** – Fragrance in garden flooded everywhere on the earth. poḻil – earth. The gardens were grown on their own but looked like they were made by someone. The gardens which surround the town look like that.

**pā vaḷarum …**– Not having any shortcoming in poetic meter, i.e. being complete in poetic rules. kaṟpaga tree is usually identified along with higher worlds. In paramapadam, as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-9-6-velviyul-maduththalum/) “*āṇmingaḷ*” (should rule over), being the controllers, those who learnt these pāsurams will be the goal for the nityasūris.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2 Telliyir

## 8.2.1. Telliyir

*teḷḷiyīr! dēvarkkum dēvar tiruttakkīr! veḷḷiyīr! veyya viḻu nidi vaṇṇar ō!tuḷḷu nīrk kaṇṇapuram toḻudāḷ ivaḷkaḷviyō! kai vaḷai koḷvadu takkadē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

teḷḷiyīr – being wise; dēvarkkum – for nityasūris; dēvar – being the controller; tiru – for periya pirāttiyār; takkīr – being a match; veḷḷiyīr – being pure; veyya – molten; viḻu nidi – like pure gold; vaṇṇar – (for you) having physical beauty; kai – present in (my daughter’s) hand; vaḷai – bangle; koḷvadu – snatching; takkadō – is it apt?; ivaḷ – this girl; nīr – (non-sentient) water; tuḷḷum – joyfully residing; kaṇṇapuram – tirukkaṇṇapuram; toḻudāḷ – performed an anjali; kaḷviyō – is she deceitful?; O – How amazing is this!

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Is it apt for you, who are wise, who are the controller for nityasūris, who are a match for periya pirāttiyār, who are pure, who are having physical beauty like that of pure molten gold, to snatch the bangle which is present in my daughter’s hand? Is she, who performed an anjali towards tirukkaṇṇapuram where even insentient water is joyfully residing, deceitful? \[No. You are deceitful\] How amazing is this!

**teḷḷiyīr …** – When she asked “Is it apt to snatch my bangle?” śaurip perumāḷ asked “What is not apt in my snatching your bangle?” She is telling further as to how it is inapt to snatch her bangle.

**teḷḷiyīr** – teḷḷimai – being wise. āren’t you well capable of knowing the different aspects? perumāḷ (śrī rāma) is said to be as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 1.18 “*lōkē puruśa sārajña: puruśāntara kōvida:*” (śrī rāma could grasp the essence of men and more skilled than others). Similarly, when you see individuals in this world you can estimate them as in “He is like this; his knowledge is this much”. Should you, who are like that, not understand the state of women? Does snatching the bangle from hand look apt for your omniscience?

Let that be.

**dēvarkkum dēvar** – As said in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 4.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/07/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-4-1/) “*teḷḷīyār palar kai toḻum dēvanār*” (emperumān is being vorśipped by many nityasūris, who have clear knowledge, in paramapadam, through *anjali*), you, who are the controller of nityasūris who have acquired knowledge without any difficulty, are snatching the bangle from the hand of a helpless girl. Is this apt for your supremacy? As said in sāma vēdam “*nādātum dēvāvaramarhanti*“, even inferior dēvatās in this world will grant boons for humans while being present in front of them, to be seen. nityasūris are such that they are like gods and those dēvatās are like humans \[seeking something\]. It is said in puruśa sūktam 18 “*yatra pūrvē sādyā santi dēvā*:” (He is the lord of nityasūris, who have been there since time immemorial). Your highness is such that you can fulfil their expectations as well. She is asking “If those inferior dēvatās are granting the desires of their followers, should you take away or grant us what we need?” When perumāḷ left from śrī ayōdyā and mercifully arrived at śrungibhērapuram, śrī guhap perumāḷ submitted honey from the mountains and fruits from the forest as offerings. Seeing that, perumāḷ told him “We did not take birth to accept from others; we took birth to give to others”; thus, is it apt for you to give or accept others’ possessions – she asks.

Let your supremacy be set aside.

**tirut takkīr** – Your highness is matching pirātti, who is said in śrī sūktam “*asyēśānā jagatō viṣṇupatni*” (one who is the lord of the worlds and the divine consort of viṣṇu) and śrī sūktam “*īśvarīm sarvabhūtānām*” (the lord of all creatures). There are three types of cētanas in the world – nityar (eternally free souls), muktar (liberated souls) and mumukśus (souls who are seeking liberation); samsāris are identified as non-existing as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (as good as non-sentient). In that, pirātti is greater than nityasūris and is comparable to your highness. She is matching you, as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*alarmēl mangai*” (the youthful pirātti who is seated atop the lotus flower) and  śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16-5 “*tulya śeelavayōvruttām tulyābhijanalakśaṇām* l *rāghavō’rhati vaidēhim tam cēyamasitēkśaṇā* ll” (for vaidēhi who has (with śrī rāma) matching qualities, age and conduct, śrī rāma is well suited; with her well-matched lineage and characteristics, this black-eyed sītā is also well suited to him). Still, a salute to your being a lover. Even while you are having a dear consort on your chest, is it apt to snatch away the bangle from a helpless girl’s hand?

**veḷḷiyīr** – Let your being a lover remain. āren’t you the opposite of all defects? īsn’t it a defect to snatch away the bangle from the hand of a girl? Alternative explantion. You are naturally pure. Is it apt for your purity to steal others’ possession? As said in “*yōrtē śucissahi śucirna mrutvāri śuciśśuci:*“, purity means purity of the self and not just purity caused by soil and water. Another explanation. “*veṇmai*” (being white) indicates ārjavam (honesty). With respect to the harmonious nature of mind, speech and body, what is the match between your words of “I won’t separate; even if I separate, I cannot sustain myself” and your action of abandonment?

**veyya viḻu nidi vaṇṇar** – Let your svarūpam remain. She is saying “Having such form, is it possible for you to refrain from giving? Would you not always grant this form to those who desire for it?” veyya – molten. viḻunidi – pure gold; with this, she is saying as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-2-katturaikkil/) “*sutturaitta nanpon un tirumēni oḷi ovvādu*” (even pure gold which has been melted in fire and polished on a grinding stone will not match your divine complexion). veyya correlates to sutturaitta. viḻunidi correlates to nanpon. Alternative explanation. “*vaṇṇam*” indicates nature, implying he has the nature of gold. In this case, she is saying “Will he snatch away others’ possession instead of being owned by others?” She is speaking about bhagavān’s nature as herself; but while speaking about her daughter’s nature, she is speaking in her daughter’s words; she is saying “What a nature he is having? \[Inferior\] What a nature she is having? \[Superior\] What a mismatch?”

As she \[mother\] called out in this manner, śaurip perumāḷ ,who is prideful due to being the lord of nityasūris as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” thought “A woman is calling out. What is the reason for that?” and came out of his sannidi entrance and asked her “Come! Why are you calling me?” She asks him “*kaivaḷai koḷvadu takkadē?*” (Is it apt to snatch away the bangle from the hand?) He responds “You have told yourself ‘*tiruttakkīr*‘ about me; only if your daughter has śrī mahālakśmi’s nature, it is inapt for me to snatch the bangle from her hand”. She asks “What is śrī mahālakśmi’s nature?” śaurip perumāḷ stands firm and responds:

She remains, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 39-30 ‘*śaraistu sankulām krutvā lankām parabalārdana*: l *mām nayēd yadi kākutstas* ***tat tasya sadruśam bhavēt*** ll’ (If śrī rāmapirān, who annihilates the strength of his enemies, bewilders lankā with his arrows and takes me with him, it will be apt for him) for the attainment of her goal. But parakāla nāyaki thinks that she has to put in the effort to attain her goal. Further, you identified my nature to be “*viḻu nidi vaṇṇar*“. Instead of accepting from such a wealthy person as he gives, isn’t pursuing oneself, the activity of those who are ātmāpahāri (those who steal ātmā, i.e., those who consider themselves to be independent)? Thus, it is apt for me to snatch away her bangle.

**tuḷḷu nīr kaṇṇapuram toḻudāḷivaḷ kaḷviyō? O** – She is proclaiming “Cruel act! Cruel act!” Since this divyadēśam is a rejuvenating abode, she performed an anjali. Should she be thrown under elephant’s feet for that?

**tuḷḷu nīr** – In this divyadēśam, where, even water, which is non-sentient is joyfully residing, should she be blamed for performing anjali to manifest that consciousness?

**kaṇṇapuram toḻudāḷ** – Did she worship paramapadanātan? Did she worship vyūha forms? Did she worship \[vibhava\] avatārams? Did she not worship you in the town where you are standing in arcāvatāram?

**toḻudāḷ** – Did you not identify her as an ātmāpahāri? Does performing an anjali considered as an act of an ātmāpahāri? āren’t those who do not worship him remain as said in  śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36-11 “*na namēyam* . .” (Even if I am broken into two pieces, I will not bend before anyone)? Her true nature is as said in yajur brāhmaṇam 3.7 “*yasyāsmi*” (the one for whom I am a servitor). īsn’t your true nature as said in jitantā stōtram “*bhaktānām … na tē rūpam*” (Your form etc are present for the sake of your devotees only). She performed the anjali to manifest that she is your possession. āren’t you the ātmāpahāri, having snatched away her possession? The mother is saying – in this manner, you have only done svarṇāpahāram (stealing gold), ātmāpahāram (stealing the self) and paramātmāpahāram (stealing bhagavān), previously.

**ivaḷ kaḷviyō** – She is saying “Is my daughter a cheat? āren’t you the cheat?”

**kaivaḷai koḷvadu takkadē** – Child, just as a person will sever the hands of someone who is saluting with those same hands, is there anyone who will snatch way the ornaments while performing anjali? īsn’t it apt to remove the bangles (ornaments) which were previously highlighted in [periya tirumoḻi 8.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2026/02/periya-thirumozhi-8-1-1-part-1/) “*silaiyilangu ponnāḻi*” (The bow, radiant and desirable chakra), decorate them on her hands and enjoying that?

**takkadē** – Even lowly male-lovers will give some gifts to their female-lovers and accept some gifts. For you, who is the ultimate lover, is it apt to snatch away from her? īsn’t it apt for parakāla nāyaki’s hands to be similar to śrī mahālakśmi’s hand as said in [tiruccanda viruttam 57](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2023/11/thiruchchandha-viruththam-57/) “*sangu tangu munkai nangai*” (The complete woman who has bangles in her forearm). She is saying “This is not apt”. She is saying as in jitantā stōtram “*na tē rūpam*” (Your form is not for your sake).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.2. Neenila murrattu

*neeṇilā muṟṟattu ninṟu ivaḷ nōkkināḷ kāṇumō! kaṇṇapuram enṟu kāttināḷ pāṇanār tiṇṇam irukka ini ivaḷnāṇumō? nanṟu nanṟu naṟaiyūrarkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivaḷ – this girl; nīḷ nilā muṟṟattu – in the third floor; ninṟu – being present; nōkkināḷ – saw the world (then); kaṇṇapuram – tirukkaṇṇapuram; kāṇumō – see; enṟu – saying that; kāttināḷ – she showed; pāṇanār – ācāryas who sing; tiṇṇam – being firm; irukka – while remaining; ini – while being continuously instructed; ivaḷ – this girl; nāṇumō – will she withdraw?; naṟaiyūrarkkē – the lord of tirunaṟaiyūr, his objective; nanṟu nanṟu – attained well

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Remaining on the third floor, this girl (my daughter, parakāla nāyaki) saw the world and said “See tirukkaṇṇapuram” and showed that; will she withdraw while being continuously instructed by ācāryas, who sing, are remaining firm? The lord of tirunaṟaiyūr, has attained his objective, well \[i.e. made her remain for him fully\].

**nīḷ nilā …** – It was said in the previous pāsuram – If she abandoned the vow as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36-11 “*na namēyam* . .” (Even if I am broken into two pieces, I will not bend before anyone) and as said in bhāratvāja samhitai “*anjali*: *paramāmudrā kśipram dēva prasādinī*” (anjali, which makes emperumān happy quickly, is an eminent identity), highlighting that there is no more argument, she performs an anjali, is that a fault? śaurip perumāḷ, who heard this, said “Can you put the blame on me? Can you not control your daughter? For women, among the noble qualities such as ‘nāṇ, madam, accam, payirppu’ (shyness, humility, fear, modesty), isn’t shyness the primary quality? When your daughter does not have it, should you not control her?” The mother says “Due to the way she speaks and due to the fault in her togetherness \[with tirunaṟaiyūr nambi\], is there any possibility to control her? Finally, tirunaṟaiyūr nambi’s goal is accomplished as he made her blabber from the beginning”.

**nīḷ nilā muṟṟattu ninṟivaḷ nōkkināḷ** – The mother placed her daughter parakāla nāyaki in the third-floor thinking “If we place her in a secluded place where people are not seen, she will withdraw from emperumān”.

**nīḷ nilā muṟṟam** – The nilā muṟṟam (penthouse which gets plenty of moon light) which is so tall that the voices of people will not be heard. For a mumukśu (liberation seeker), in the place where there is connection with body etc (and bodily relatives), while he has restrictions and fear, when worldly pleasures are observed, there is scope for engaging in such pleasures. That is due to being bound in the body. To remedy that, it is said that such mumukśu will remain in a secluded place. Similarly, since she (mother) is fully situated the first half \[of dvaya mahā mantram or carama ślōkam\], considering her daughter has acquired this great love towards emperumān due to samsarga dōśam (the fault of the union with bhagavān), she placed her daughter in the third-floor.

**ninṟu ivaḷ nōkkināḷ** – As the daughter saw the nilā muṟṟam, she said this looked like the place where emperumān came as said in [periya tirumoḻi 8.1.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2026/03/periya-thirumozhi-8-1-8/) “*koṟṟap puḷ onṟēṟi manṟūdē varuginṟān*” (bhagavān is remaining seated on the victorious, unique periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) and coming to a common/public place), made me totally existing for him and enjoyed union with me; she then stood up and sustained herself from the state mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-2-4-itta-kal/) “*itta kāl itta kaiyaḷāy irukkum*” (My daughter’s leg and hand remain \[unmoved\] wherever they were placed). This is similar to how one remains disturbed on seeing worldly plesaures before acquiring true knowledge through instructions from an ācārya and how one remains fearless and sustains oneself after engaging in apt matters (related to bhagavān) as said in taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli 6 “*ata sō’bhayagatō bhavati*” (one becomes fearless about samsāram).

**ivaḷ nōkkināḷ** – Not just that, she became capable to see the world as well \[That is, she was able to understand the bhāgavatas of this world to be the means and goal\].

**kāṇumō kaṇṇapuram enṟu kāttināḷ** – As she glanced around, tirukkaṇṇapuram became target of her eyes; while many other places are there, should tirukkaṇṇapuram be seen by her? Since śaurip perumāḷ is her beloved lord and since she is focussed \[on her goal\], she saw tirukkaṇṇapuram. When many kings came to marry draupadi during her svayamvaram (where a bride chooses her future husband), the challenge placed in front of them was to shoot the neck of the target \[a fish\]. While others said “I saw its feet; I saw its stomach and so on”, arjuna said “I saw its neck”. That is because he was focussed and eagerly wanted to marry her.

**kāṇumō kaṇṇapuram enṟu kāttināḷ** – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.2.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/05/thiruvaimozhi-5-2-2-kandom-kandom/) “*toṇḍīr elleerum vārīr*” (Oh those who are favourable towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and bhāgavatas! All of you, please come), she is telling everyone in her vicinity to see tirukkaṇṇāpuram. She is telling even her mother who is stopping her saying “You should not have so much love”. She is not of the nature to enjoy any good thing alone.

**kaṇṇapuram enṟu kāttināḷ** – The mother showed bhagavān as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-5-5-kuzhaiyum-val/) “*pirān irundamai kāttinīr*” (you showed the merciful presence of our benefactor); she is showing his abode. This is the greatness of a sacciśya (true disciple) over his sadācārya (true preceptor). ācāryan will show that your means and goal are the divine feet of īśvaran; the true disciple remains thinking “āren’t you the one who established these two principles? Hence your divine feet are my means and goal”.

Alternative explanation.

**kāṇumō kaṇṇapuram enṟu kāttināḷ** – She started saying “See tirukkaṇṇapuram. Perform an anjali” but could not fisniś the statement and conveyed the message through sign language.

Another explanation. She is saying “*kāṇumō*“. Will you see?

Another explanation. She is upset thinking “īsn’t the purpose of our eyes to see tirukkaṇṇapuram? Is there anyone who avoids that?” A devotee named vadamaduraip piṟandān magan was once in front of kōyilāḻvār (śrīranga vimānam) and was performing some japam with his eyes closed; bhattar who came to worship bhagavān at that time became upset and said “When the śrīranga vimānam is in full view of the eyes, why is he closing his eyes? Should he not make use of the eyes properly?”. Within a month or two, he lost his eyesight.

This is how she speaks and acts.

**pāṇanār …** – The mother is speaking about the love her daughter has acquired through the union with emperumān.

**pāṇanār** – When the hero separates, to eliminate the anger and unite with him again, a singer will be sent; the singer too will eliminate the anger in the hearts of both the hero and heroine and unite them, by speaking sweet words. Here, the singer is the ācārya (preceptor) who eliminates the anger which came about in the cētana (ātmā) due to svātantrya (independence), instills the knowledge about servitude and unites him with bhagavān. She is saying “pāṇanār” since she has heard from her daughter who said in [periya tirumoḻi 7.4.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2025/10/periya-thirumozhi-7-4-4/) “*pērāḷan pērōdum periyōr*” (mahātmās who are praising bhagavān). There is no specific restriction on who can teach whom. It is only required for a person to be fixated on bhagavān \[to be known as ācārya\] as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat 1.2.12 “*samitpāṇiś śrōtriyam brahmaniśtam*” (Approach with samit (firewood) in hands, the one who is well learned in śāstram and is fixated on bhagavān).

**tiṇṇam irukka** – As they remain unśakeable.

**ini ivaḷ nāṇumō** – Even if the mother is giving unpalatable advice continuously, is there any scope for her to withdraw from bhagavān?

**ini ivaḷ nāṇumō** – She will neither withdraw due to the love she acquired through the union nor due to the natural love. I who am telling her, “This is not apt for you”, will only end up withdrawing from my act of giving instructions, due to becoming ashamed. She won’t withdraw. Even if I am her ācārya (teacher), if she is not a sat prakruti (good natured – i.e. obedient), she is not withdrawing \[due to excessive love\]. Both ācārya and śiśya should be apt to accomplish the goal.

**nanṟu nanṟu naṟaiyūrarkkē** – Her goal is also not attained; śaurip perumāḷ’s goal is also not attained; but in the beginning it was tirunaṟaiyūr nambi who made her pick up madal (a process to unite with the loved one) and made her disobedient; his goal was accomplished well.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.3. Aruvi sor vengadam

*aruvi sōr vēngadam nīrmalai enṟu vāyveruvināḷ meyyam vinavi irukkinṟāḷ perugu sīrk kaṇṇapuram enṟu pēsināḷurugināḷ uḷ melindāḷ idu en kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

aruvi – the waterfalls from mountain; sōr – flowing; vēngadam – saying tiruvēngadam; nīrmalai – tiruneermalai; enṟu – saying; vāy veruvināḷ – speaking without thinking; meyyam – saying tirumeyyam; vinavi – hearing; irukkinṟāḷ – she remains; perugu – (like river) flowing; sīr – having wealth (of qualities in completion); kaṇṇapuram enṟu – saying tirukkaṇṇapuram; pēsināḷ – she is speaking; urugināḷ – melting (as water); uḷ – in the heart; melindāḷ – she is suffering; idu en kolō – alas; what a suffering!

**Перевод:**

**In the previous pāsuram, she said “ini ivaḷ nāṇumō” (Will she withdraw now?). That lajjai (shyness) will occur only if she sustains herself; the mother is saying “Whatever pampering we do to her, we are not seeing any results. How is this going to end for her?”. One who is suffering due to the heat/suffering, will naturally surrender unto one who remains in water, who can eliminate that heat/suffering; parakāla nāyaki is not of the nature to surrender unto him \[in vyūha form, in the milk ocean\]; only sanaka et al (the four kumāras) who are as good as muktātmās, surrender unto him; she surrenders unto arcāvatāra form only. In that, she is enlisting a few divyadēśams which are rejuvenating for her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter, parakāla nāyaki, is speaking without thinking, saying “tiruvēngdam where the water-falls from the mountain is flowing, tirneermalai”; she is asking “tirumeyyam” and remaining; she is saying “tirukkaṇṇapuram which is having wealth like a flowing river”; she is melting; she is suffering in her heart; alas! What a suffering!

**aruvi sōr vēngadam** – Since the source of the water remains perennial, the water-falls also remains perennial. It is a rejuvenating abode as said in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 8.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/09/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-8-1/) “*teṇṇīrpāy vēngadam*” (tiruvēngadam where clear streams are flowing).

**neer malai** – In tiruvēngadam, the water-falls is on the flow. Unlike that, in tiruneermalai, there is water surrounding everywhere, there is a divine mountain amidst the water and he is mercifully reclining in the middle of the mountain.

**enṟu vāy veruvināḷ** – Since her heart was stolen \[by bhagavān\], she spoke without thinking.

**meyyam vinavi irukkinṟāḷ** – She would ask “Did the abode not get the name tirummeyyam since this is where he truly remained for his devotees and helped them?”. There would be no one who would respond to her. She remains as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 16-1-3 “*stabdōsi*” (you are standing as if you are without emotions \[as if in a shock\]).

**perugu nīr kaṇṇapuram enṟu pēsināḷ** – Unlike the other divyadēśams where there is sufficient wealth, tirukkaṇṇapuram is having greatly growing wealth like a flowing river. She is constantly uttering that tirukkaṇṇapuram.

**kaṇṇapuram enṟu pēsināḷ urugināḷ** – She is not melting after speaking. Even while speaking, she is melting.

**uḷ melindāḷ** – The ātmā which is said in śrī bhagavat gītā 2.24 “***accēdyōýam adāhyōýam*** *aklēdyō’śōśya ēvaca* l *nityas sarvagata*: *stāṇuracalōýam sanātana*: ll” (ātmā, which permeates all through the body, cannot be severed; it cannot be burnt; it cannot be wet; it cannot be dried. Hence, ātmā is permanent, firm, immovable and existing since time immemorial), has withered as it is. Alternative explanation – the body melts only when the heart melts; she is saying that the heart has melted.

**idu en kolō** – Sin is the reason for her suffering. As said in “*maturā nāma nagarī puṇyā pāpaharī śubhā*” (the town maturā is pious, removes sins and auspicious), as one speaks about the abode where the faultless lord resides, the sins will be eliminated and enjoyment will occur – says śāstram. The mother is saying “It is my sin that it is not occurring for my daughter”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.4. Unnum nal illai

*uṇṇum nāḷ illai uṟakkamum tān illai peṇmaiyum sāla niṟaindilaḷ pēdai tān kaṇṇanūr kaṇṇapuram toḻum kārkkadalvaṇṇar mēl eṇṇam ivatku idu en kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṇṇum nāḷ – (for her) days to eat; illai – not there; uṟakkamum tān – sleep too; illai – not there; peṇmaiyum – (her) femininity; sāla – very; niṟaindilaḷ – not complete; pēdai tān – (even now) she is a young girl; kaṇṇan – where kriṣṇa is mercifully present; kaṇṇapuram – known as tirukkaṇṇāpuram; Ur – the divyadēśam; toḻum – she is vorśipping; ivatku – for her; kār – dark; kadal – like an ocean; vaṇṇarmēl – on kriṣṇa who has physical beauty; eṇṇam – has her thoughts; idu en kolō – How amazing is this!

**Перевод:**

**When asked “The suffering she goes through as said in ‘Speaking incoherently, asking, speaking, melting’ is only when she sustains herself; how is that?” the mother responds “She is not sustaining herself”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter has no time to eat; she does not sleep either; she has still not become a well matured woman; she is a young girl; she is vorśipping the divyadēśam which is known as tirukkaṇṇapuram where kriṣṇa is mercifully present; she has her thoughts on kriṣṇa who has physical beauty like that of a dark ocean. How amazing is this!

**uṇṇum nāḷ illai uṟakkamum tān illai** – The mother is saying “It appears that her previous states can be considered as good sitautions, when we see her situation now”. Whatever was mentioned previously can occur only if she eats and sleeps properly.

**uṇṇum nāḷ illai** – She remained fasting. Instead of saying “*ūṇillai*” (no food), she has said “*uṇṇum nāḷ illai*” (no time for food). vālmeeki riśi has written that when sītāp pirātti was living in separation and was fasting, dēvēndran came and offered her food which is filled with nectar without the knowledge of rākśasas and rākśasis (demoniac men and women), and she mercifully consumed it. The mother is saying that there is no such day for parakāla nāyaki.

**uṟakkamum tān illai** – A day is made of daytime and night-time; in that, if she has no engagement in eating which is an activity done in the daytime, does she at least have sleep which is an activity done in the night-time? The mother is saying “that is also not there”. Instead of saying “*uṟakkamillai*” (no sleep), she is saying “*uṟakkamum tān illai*” (even, there is no sleep). This is because, sleep is required compulsorily, and she is saying that it is not there. When perumāḷ (śrī rāma) was mercifully present in the forest, he was about to go to sleep. At that time, he mercifully told iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) “My dependent, maitili (sītāp pirātti) has come along with me; you should abandon your sleep, laziness, and fatigue acquired through the travel so far, and protect us without anything happening to us by your lethargy in protecting us”. At that time, he responded as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 56.3 “*jahau nidrānca tandrim ca prasaktam ca pariśramam*” (Being woken up by perumāḷ, iḷaiya perumāḷ abandoned his sleep, laziness and fatigue from the travel). She is unlike lakśmaṇa who had sleep and gave it up subsequently. She did not have the aspect of sleep at all.

**peṇmaiyum sāla niṟaindilaḷ pēdai tān** – If one has experience in uniting with one’s husband, one can avoid eating and sleeping. But she has not yet reached that stage.

**peṇmai** – strītvam (femininity). She has not experienced femininity even a little bit.

Alternative explanation.

**peṇmaiyum sāla niṟaindilaḷ** – She only knows about the taste of union with her husband; but has not experienced it fully.

When asked “She is complete in femininity as a pēriḷam peṇ (well matured woman, in her thirty plus age); is she at least in the stage of mangai (teen age)?”. The mother responds

**pēdai tān** – She is very young (just 5 years old).

**kaṇṇan Ur …** – Would she not need dāraka (sustenance), pōśaka (nourishment) for her age? How are they present?

**kaṇṇapuram toḻum** – This is her sustenance.

When asked “How is it that vorśipping someone sustains that person?” the mother responds

**kaṇṇan Ur** – kriṣṇa, who is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-1-unnum-soru/) “*ellām kaṇṇan*” (Everything is kriṣṇa), is the one who is present inside the divyadēśam; the residents of śvētadvīpam \[a place in and around kśīrābdi\] remain as said in mahābhāratam śānti parvam 344.45 “*baddānjaliputā* *hruśtā*” (They are always performing anjali joyfully). They remain in anjali posture always as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.1.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruvaimozhi-2-1-7-thorrom-madanenjam/) “*tōṟṟōm*” (We have lost) and in jitantā stōtram 1 “*jitam*” (Victory to you). Only if he disappears, their anjali posture will be discarded. For such devotees, all their limbs remain intact by such anjali.

**kārkkadal vaṇṇar mēl eṇṇam** – She is desiring to embrace kriṣṇa who is standing inside that divyadēśam like a stagnated ocean. Since she vorśipped his abode, her eating stopped. Since she desired his divine form, her sleeping also stopped.

**peṇmaiyum sāla niṟaindilaḷ, pēdai tān, eṇṇam ivatku idu** – She has attained the state of those who are accomplished in yōgam (upāsanam/bhakti yōgam). How amazing! – says the mother.

**en kolō** – The mother is saying – We have not seen this state in the sages who are accomplished in yōgam. We have not seen this in āḻvār \[nammāḻvār\] who visualised kriṣṇa and enjoyed him. We have not seen this in sītāp pirātti who enjoyed with śrī rāma for twenty five years without separating even for a moment, by being together the whole sixty nāḻigai (24 minutes) of every day, and subsequently was able to remain in separation for ten months. This is parakāla nāyaki’s age \[5 years\]; these are her sustenance and nourishment. How amazing is this!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.5. Kannanur

*kaṇṇanūr kaṇṇapuram toḻum kārigai peṇmaiyum tannudai uṇmai uraikkinṟāḷ veṇṇey uṇḍu āppuṇḍa vaṇṇam viḷambināl vaṇṇamum ponniṟam āvadu oḻiyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa’s; Ur – abode; kaṇṇapuram – tirukkaṇṇapuram; toḻum – due to vorśipping; kārigai – beautiful (girl); tannudai – her; peṇmaiyum – femininity; uṇmai – truth; uraikkinṟāḷ – speaking; veṇṇey – butter; uṇḍu – (stole and) mercifully consumed; āppuṇḍa – bound; vaṇṇam – (his) nature; viḷambināl – if spoken; pon niṟa mādu – having golden complexion; vāṇṇamum – bodily beauty; oḻiyumē – is being lost

**Перевод:**

**In the previous pāsuram, the mother said “peṇmaiyum sāla niṟaindilaḷ” (She has not matured enough into a woman). When asked “Let that happen over time. But is she at least having the femininity for that?” the mother is saying “Even that is not there”. When asked “How did you come to know?” the mother is saying “The moment she thinks about him, all her faculties (mind, speech and body) are changing; what femininity is present in her?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

My daughter, who is having the beauty acquired by vorśipping tirukkaṇṇapuram which is kriṣṇa’s abode, is speaking about her femininity and truth; if the nature of kriṣṇa, who is stealing and mercifully eating butter and got bound due to that, is spoken, she is even losing the beauty of her body which is having golden complexion.

**kaṇṇanūr kaṇṇapuram toḻum** – She is repeating what was said previously. She is saying “Did I not say previously? Instead of stopping with vorśipping him, she goes beyond and worships his abode. What femininity is she having!”

**kaṇṇanūr kaṇṇapuram** – The abodes such as śrī maturā, tiruvāyppādi, śrīmat dvārakā appear similar to the assembly in paramapadam as said in [tiruviruttam 47](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/02/thiruviruththam-47/) “*kaṇṇan viṇṇūr*” (kriṣṇa’s abode, śrīvaikuṇṭam). Just as in dāra niyati (principle with respect to wife, where śrī rāma had one wife and kriṣṇa had many wives), \[in the case of abodes also\] cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma, son of the emperor), was born and raised in a single place; kriṣṇa is quite opposite to that. The nature of the town (maturā) is so dangerous that he had to leave the place as soon as he was born. After leaving those abodes and entering tirukkaṇṇapuram, he would think this to be his abode.

**toḻum** – Just as that abode is the primary identity for him, vorśipping him is the primary identity for her. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 4-42 “prājñalim prahvamāsīnam” (one who stood humbly with joined palms), when perumāḷ (śrī rāma) was leaving his private quarters, iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) who was in the second gate, was performing anjali above his head and was with a bent back, standing to be seen by perumāḷ. Similarly, parakāla nāyaki is having anjali posture with her hands. kārigai indicates beauty. If her beauty was seen by him, then he would pursue her with hands in anjali posture, falling head over heels. For her, who has the roles reversed now, what femininity is there! With this, her bodily actions are highlighted.

**peṇmai …** – Speaking about her speech.

**peṇmaiyum tannudai uṇmai uraikkinṟāḷ** – peṇmai – strītvam – femininity. That is – even in dire situations, even for the closest friend, the emotions will be hidden. That friend will look at her actions and determine “This is probably what she is going through”; in such case, she is revealing that to me, who is her mother. What femininity she is having! – says the mother.

**tannudai uṇmai uraikkinṟāḷ** – The thoughts which are happening in her heart; alternative explanation, uṇmai – sadbhāvam – true state. She is speaking about that. [śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 86.1](https://granthams.koyil.org/2025/11/16/sri-ramayana-thani-slokam-23-english/) “*ācacakśē’ta sadbhāvam lakśmaṇasya mahātmana:* I *bharatāyāpramēyāya guhō gahanagōcara:* īī” (guhap perumāḷ, who lives in the forest,  spoke to bharatāḻvān, whose qualities of goodness are incomprehensible, about mahātmā iḷaiya perumāḷ’s virtues). After hearing that bharatāḻvān is coming, śrī guhap perumāḷ started listing out the activities of iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa). He remained with anger, thinking “Why should I tell what I will do when he comes? I have the boats. I have the weapons. I will see how he and his people cross over the river to the other side”. Subsequently, sumantran et al came and told “bharatāḻvān’s nature is also the same as iḷaiya perumāḷ’s nature. You should see him”. He then went and saw bharatāḻvān and became amazed thinking “What an amazing nature he has!” and thought “What can we give him \[matching his greatness?” and concluded that it is apt to speak about iḷaiya perumāḷ’s glories to him and started telling the same.

[śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 86.1](https://granthams.koyil.org/2025/11/16/sri-ramayana-thani-slokam-23-english/) “*ācacakśē’ta sadbhāvam lakśmaṇasya mahātmana:* I *bharatāyāpramēyāya guhō gahanagōcara:* īī” (guhap perumāḷ, who lives in the forest,  spoke to bharatāḻvān, whose qualities of goodness are incomprehensible, about mahātmā iḷaiya perumāḷ’s virtues) is explained here.

- **ācacakśēta sadbhāvam** – sadbhāvam – noble people’s conduct. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*saccabda: sāduvācaka:*” (the word sat indicates a noble person) and śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*sādava: kśīṇadōśāstu*” (sādus are those whose faults have been eliminated). As said in these, sattukkaḷ are those whose faults have been eliminated already.
- **bhāvam** – ācāram (conduct). One is known as artavān (wealthy), abhijātan (person of great heritage), vidvān (wise), based on their conduct only. Similarly, iḷaiya perumāḷ’s conduct is very noble. guhap perumāḷ started speaking about iḷaiya perumāḷ’s conduct as in “He will cut the grass to make a bed for perumāḷ’s merciful reclining, make the bed, fetching some lotus leaves and water in those leaves and washing perumāḷ’s divine feet, again fetching water and offering it to perumāḷ to mercifully drink the same; remaining water is offered to pirātti, making them rest, having arrow and bow in his hand and protecting perumāḷ, doubting even us”.
- **lakśmaṇasya mahātmana:** – He started fetching the water of an ocean with his hands \[iḷaiya perumāḷ’s glories were as big as an ocean\].
- **lakśmaṇasya mahātmana: sadbhāvam apramēyāya bharatāya – ācacakśē** – He started explaining the greatness of a salt-pan to an ocean.
- **bharatāya apramēyāya ācacakśē** – \[bharata’s greatness being inconceivable is highlighted here by comparing him with iḷaiya perumāḷ’s words and actions\] If one is a servitor, would one say “I will serve you” \[instead of actually just doing it\]; let that be aside; after vowing that he will do everything ordered by śrī rāma as in [śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25](https://granthams.koyil.org/2025/10/06/sri-ramayana-thani-slokam-17-english/) “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (I will do everything), when śrī rāma told lakśmaṇa “You remain in the kingdom”, lakśmaṇa refused and followed śrī rāma – is this an act of a servitor? The real act of a servitor is to follow the lord’s instructions – if the lord ordered to enter into fire, one should do it; even better than that if asked to remain in the kingdom, he should do that; if he ordered to follow him, he should do that.
- **guha:** – Alas! guhap perumāḷ who has seen perumāḷ just for once is now telling bharatāḻvān, who has served perumāḷ for a long time. There is no restriction that only such and such person can instruct such and such person; the speaker should be learned – that is the only requirement.
- **gahana gōcara:** – Sage vālmeeki is praising guhap perumāḷ as in “Look at this person who moved with trees and branches, is speaking about the nature of iḷaiya perumāḷ”. Alternatively – it can be said that guhap perumāḷ who became sorrowful and buried his head in the bushes, has now become enlivened, seeing bharatāḻvān.

**veṇṇey uṇḍu …** – Is she only speaking out with her mouth? She is revealing through all her faculties. What a femininity she is having! – says the mother. In the [previous pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2026/03/periya-thirumozhi-8-2-4/), she desired to embrace the divine form as mentioned in “*kārkkadal vaṇṇar mēl eṇṇam*” (my thoughts are on the one who has dark ocean like complexion) and is remaining as said in [periya tirumoḻi 8.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2026/02/periya-thirumozhi-8-1-1-part-1/) “*mulaiyilangu pūm payalai munbōda*” (beautiful paleness of her bosom is going in front). When others say “He is such that, he desires for yasōdāp pirātti’s possession which is butter, and if he does not get it, he will engage in stealing that and even got caught red-handed in that as said in periya tirumoḻi 11.5.5 ‘*kattuṇḍān kāṇ*‘ (see he got caught)'”, as soon as my daughter hears these leelās, she will say “Oh! I am glad that he is someone who desires for the possession of a woman and would not let it go when he does not get it and will try to steal the same. And finally, he gets caught, to be bound by her. We got a person who is very easily approachable for us” and is having the desire to embrace such divine form and became happy. She is saying that we have no more shortcoming since bhagavān, who is avāpta samasta kāman (one who has no unfulfilled desires) is desiring for a woman’s possession; one who is omnipotent, engages in stealing; and he becomes so easily approachable that he gets caught stealing and becomes bound; how simple he is.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.6. Vadavarai

*vadavarai ninṟum vandu inṟu kaṇapuram idavagai koḷvadu yām enṟu pēsināḷ madavaral mādar en pēdai ivarkku ivaḷkadavaden? kaṇ tuyil inṟu ivar koḷḷavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yām – We (I); vada – in the northern direction; varai ninṟum – from tirumalā; vandu – arrived; inṟu – today; kaṇapuram – tirukkaṇṇapuram; idavagai – as the abode; koḷvadu – to have (we have arrived); enṟu – in this manner; pēsināḷ – she said; madavaral – being obedient; pēdai – being childish; en – my; mādar – daughter; ivaḷ – she; ivarkku – for this emperumān; kadavaden – what relationship has she got, to do anything?; ivar – this emperumān; inṟu – today (her); kaṇ tuyil – sleep; koḷḷavē – what is the purpose of taking away?

**Перевод:**

**In the previous pāsuram, you said “tannudai uṇmai uraikkinṟāḷ” (speaking about the truth), “veṇṇey uṇḍu āppuṇḍa vaṇṇam viḷambināl vaṇṇamum ponniṟamāvadoḻiyum” (if the nature of kriṣṇa, who is stealing and mercifully eating butter and got bound due to that, is spoken, she is even losing the beauty of her body which is having golden complexion). In that what is “uṇmai” and how did you lose your ponniṟam? – For these questions, she is giving the explanation here. She said “kaṇṇan Ur” (kriṣṇa’s abode) in the previous pāsuram; all of the girls of that tiruvāyppādi (śrī gōkulam) which is the abode of kriṣṇa, were saying as in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-18-22 “gurūṇāmagratō vaktum kim pravīśi na na: kśamam l gurava: kim kariśyanti dagdānām virahāgnitā ll” (Are you saying that we cannot reveal this matter in the presence of elders? What can our elders do to us when we are being burnt by the fire of separation?) indicating “What are these elders planning to do to us? Will they pour a pot of water over us who are burning in the fire of separation?”; they left their relatives fully, and arrived at the banks of yamunā to enjoy kriṣṇa; they did not see kriṣṇa there; they then performed anukāram (acting out kriṣṇa leelās) – one girl said “I will walk nicely; you hold an umbrella honouring my walk”; śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.13.27 “duśta kāḷiya tistāttara” – one gōpikā said “Look kāḷiya! I am climbing on you to dance” – in this manner they performed anukāram. parakāla nāyaki too is considering tirukkaṇṇapuram as tiruvāyppādi, śaurip perumāḷ to be kriṣṇa, herself to be that śaurip perumāḷ and performs anukāram, speaking in this manner. As said in cāndōjña upaniśat “sarvam kalvidam brahma” (everything is \[a form of\] brahmam), bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “aham brahmāsmi” (I am \[a form of\] brahmam), she considers herself to be him and him to be herself. This is parakāla nāyaki’s vaidika lōkāyata matam (materialism based on vēdam) \[Note: In lōkāyata, there is no specific concept of ātmā and everything is seen from a materialistic view point; in vaidika matam, everything is seen in a combination of ātmā, paramātmā and matter. Here, parakāla nāyaki is just seeing paramātmā everywhere, even in place of her own self\]. There are others \[other āḻvārs\] who have performed anukāram. She is unlike parānkuśa nāyaki (nammāḻvār in feminine form) who held on to bhagavān who is jagat kāraṇa rūpi (one who is the cause of entire creation) as in tiruvāimoḻi 5.6 “kadal jñālam seydēnum yānē ennum” (She says that she is the one who created the universe). She performs anukāram of arcāvatāra rūpi (one who is in arcā form). She is so attached to arcāvatāram that she will say “Other than the experience acquired from arcā form, all other experiences from different forms of bhagavān can be fed to dog”. āppān tiruvaḻundūr araiyar and āḻvār tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar recited and meditated upon this pāsuram and said “We are unable to understand the aptness of this pāsuram” and came to parāśara bhattar and asked “How is this pāsuram explained?”; bhattar mercifully explained to them “The mother is speaking about the anukāram performed by her daughter, parakāla nāyaki”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

When some persons who are ārūda yōgis (those who reached the highest stage of yōga) arrive, they will be asked “*yō bhavān yan nimittam vā yatāgamana kāraṇam*” (Who are you? For what purpose have you come here?) saying “Who are you? Where did you come from?”. Similarly, when asked “Where did you come from? Why did you come?” she says “I have come from such and such abode; this is the reason why I have come”

My daughter spoke in this manner “We have come from tirumalā in the northern direction and arrived today in tirukkaṇṇapuram to have it as our abode” Being obedient and childish, what relationship does my daughter have with this emperumān, to do anything for him? What is the purpose of this emperumān in taking away her sleep today?

**vada varai ninṟum vandu** – Coming from the tirumalā (sacred hill) which is in the northern direction. She is not like nammāḻvār who starts from śrīvaikuṇṭam as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.7.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/02/thiruvaimozhi-10-7-8-thirumalirunjolai-malaiye/) “*tirumāl vaigundamē taṇ tiruvēngadamē*” (paramapadam where he is residing as śriya:pati as said in “*śriyāsārdam*“, invigorating periya tirumalai). She starts from arcāvatāram \[tirumalā\]. tirumalā is the abode where the poles were planted for all arcāvatāra forms.

When asked “What is the purpose of your visit?” She says

**inṟu kaṇapuram idavagai koḷvadu yām** – I have come to tirukkaṇṇapuram to reside here permanently. This is the purpose of my arrival. This is how my truth is.

**enṟu pēsināḷ** – Previously, she said “*uraikkinṟāḷ*” (she spoke). That is repeated by the mother as “*pēsināḷ*“.

**mada varal …** – Is she like the girls of tiruvāyppādi? \[That is\] Being those who blabber, like those who throw accusations and performed anukāram? Is she not the one who acts according to the words of the relatives? \[i.e. very obedient\]

**madavaral mādar** – Obedient girl.

**en pēdai** – Is it that she is obedient towards the relatives? īsn’t she of the nature that she does not know anything beyond my \[her mother’s\] instructions?

**pēdai** – If she is in her youth, she may disobey my words; she is in the stage where she cannot differentiate between her father and her husband.

**ivarkku** – For kriṣṇa who has enjoyed with those girls and remaining shrewd and crowned

**ivaḷ** – She, who desires to grow.

**kadavaden** – What is the aptness in taking away her sleep like a person, who has given a loan based on a security, forces repayment?

**kaṇ tuyil inṟu ivar koḷḷavē** – He can take it away if she is also blabbering like them; what is the benefit of taking away her sleep – asks the mother. Previously, she said “*vaṇṇamum ponniṟamāvadoḻiyum*“; when asked “What is that golden complexion? What is her natural complexion?” The response is – as said in śruti (vēdam), as in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*ya ātmani tiśtan ātmanō’ntara:*” (One who is present inside the ātmā; one who controls the ātmā) and in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*yasya ātmā śarīram*” (For whom (brahmam), the ātmā is a body), body being subservient to ātmā, knowledge about ātmā who is śēśa (subservient) and bhagavān who is śēśi (lord), the bliss which is attained by such knowledge – thus, the natural complexion is the knowledge of being a servitor and the bliss derived by that; golden (pale) complexion is – considering the body in which the ātmā has entered to be the ātmā itself as in “*dēvō’ham, manuśyō’ham*” (I am a dēva, I am a manuśya) and assuming the attributes which are said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*durgā’jñānamalādarmā:*” (difficulty, ignorance, impurity and unrighteousness).

The aspects which are difficult to attain even for those who have reached the highest stage of yōga, is attained by her who is just desirous. The mother is saying “How amazing is this!”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.7. Taranga nir

*taranga nīr pēsilum taṇ madi kāyinum irangumō? ettanai nāḷ irundu eḷgināḷ? turangam vāy kīṇḍu ugandānadu tonmaiyūr arangamē enbadu ivaḷ tanakku āsaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tarangam – having rising tides; nīr – the ocean; pēsinum – even if it roars; taṇ – cool; madi – moon; kāyinum – even if it pours fire (this girl); irangumō – will she weaken?; ettanai nāḷ – for a long time; irundu – from these; eḷgināḷ – suffered; turangam – kēśi who was in the form of a horse; vāy – mouth; kīṇḍu – tore (by that); ugandān adu – for kriṣṇa, who became joyful; tonmai – ancient; Ur – temple; arangamē enbadu – that it is śrīrangam; ivaḷ tanakku – for her; āsaiyē – remains the desire

**Перевод:**

**You said “ivarkku ivaḷ kavadu en” indicating “Is there any aptness in him taking away her sleep?” Are there no exchanges between him and her? She remains saying “kārkkadal vaṇṇar mēl eṇṇam” (thoughts are on the one who has dark ocean’s complexion), “kaṇṇapuram toḻum” (worships tirukkaṇṇapuram), “kaṇṇapuram enṟu pēsināḷ” (she says tirukkaṇṇapuram) and as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.5.11 “sindaiyālum sollālum seygaiyinālum” (by mind, words and actions) on śaurip perumāḷ only; can we say that there is no aptness between them? \[No\] Let that be aside. Is your daughter capable of handling these sufferings? The mother is asking “Will these weaken her?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Will she weaken even if the ocean which has rising tides roar and the cool moon shines? For a long time, she remained in such a situation and suffered. She only desires for śrīrangam which is the ancient abode of kriṣṇa, who became joyful tearing the mouth of kēśi who was in the form of a horse.

**taranga nīr pēsilnm taṇ madi kāyinum irangumō** – After waking up from sleep, she opened her eyes and saw. The place where those who are separated from their lovers will go is the seashore. Hence, she was tormented by the roar of the ocean which reminds her about the shoulder which eagerly embraced her when they were sitting on the seashore and conversing, and reminds her about his lowly romantic talks such as “adiyēn, kudiyēn” (servitor) during their union, and the coolness which was derived by the comforting embrace. If these aspects such as the roar of the ocean and the coolness of the moon torment her, will she weaken? \[No\]

**taranga nīr pēsinum** – Even if the ocean which has rising tides, roars.

**taṇ madi kāyinum** – īsn’t the moon born from that ocean.? Just as bhagavān, who is the well-wisher of all entities, has become harmful towards her, even if the moon who causes coolness for everyone, is pouring fire. If bhagavān’s nature is \[cruel\] like this, we need not talk about the nature of his followers \[like moon etc\]. It is said “*yacceelasvāmy tacceelāprakruti:*” (the dependants of the lord are like him only).

**irangumō** – She said “Will she weaken?”

When asked “What is the reason for her not becoming weak?”

**ettanai nāḷ irundu eḷgināḷ** – Will she, who got beaten up by these previously and became stiff, suffer?” eḷgudal – suffering. When a clamp (a kind of instrument named vidunagam in tamiḻ) is mounted, the one who is not used to it, will suffer. But the one who got used to it, will remain indifferent about it.

**turangam …** – When said “If she is suffering in this manner, should you not find a remedy for it? You are her mother and hence you should do it. Tell us about that remedy” parakāla nāyaki’s mother says “I am the one who knows her remedy”.

**arangamē enbadu ivaḷ tanakku āsaiyē** – She desires to say “*tiruvarangam*“, “*tiruvarangam*“. If that is the case, what is stopping her from saying that? That is because, since she is a noble person who will break down if we speak about him, her relatives will silence her.

**āsaiyē** – If she tries hard and starts telling, they will remain close and say “*vāy, vāy*” (Watch out your mouth). He is the same kriṣṇa who is present in tirukkaṇṇāpuram.

When asked “Is there any difference between that kriṣṇa and śrī ranganāta?”

**turangam vāy kīṇḍu ugandānadu tonmai Ur** – As said in nārasimha purāṇam “*kēśava: klēśa nāśana:*” (one who eliminates our sorrows), did he not kill kēśi, who was the hurdle for his enjoyment? As he enjoyed along with the girls in śrī brindāvanam, bhagavān did not think “Let me eliminate these enemies who came and do something good for the gōpas and gōpikās”; instead he thought “I eliminated the hurdle for my enjoyment” and became joyful.

**tonmai Ur** – Ancient temple. Just as old as tiruvāyppādi and having connection with purāṇams. tirukkaṇṇapuram is similar to śrī dvāravatī (dvārakā) where people inhabited newly in the middle of the ocean; the town is reminded as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.10.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-10-1-malai-nanni/) “*vēlai mōdum madiḷ*” (the fort which is banged by the tides) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.10.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-10-2-kal-avizhum/) “*veḷḷi ēynda madiḷ*” (sliver fort) and reminds the moon and ocean which tormented her; will he still be considered as the one who killed kēśi if he fails to shut the ocean’s mouth? While pacifying the moon who poured fire, as he was suffering from the curse of dakśa prajāpati, bhagavān helped the moon by making him take a dip in chandra puśkariṇi and eliminated the moon’s suffering.

**arangamē enbadu ivaḷ tanakku āsaiyē** – She said tirukkaṇṇapuram. In her natural form as parakālan, she will talk about śrīrangam; that is kaṇṇanūr; this is śrīrangam. This is the abode which is ruled by a woman (sītāp pirātti) who says in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed). For those who have attained true knowledge without any confusion and are said as in “*ārūda yōgar*” (one who is in advanced state), the mūla prakruti, is indicated by the creation of water as said in manu smruti “*apa Eva sasarjātau*” (he first created the ocean); the next stage of that mūla prakruti is śabda et al. Unless these primordial matter and enjoyments derived from that viz śabda (sound), sparśa (touch), rūpa (form), rasa (taste) and ganda (smell), are eliminated, the enjoyment will not be complete. Here ocean is compared to matter and the moon who is born from the ocean represents the sense enjoyments.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.8. Tondellam

*toṇḍellām ninnadiyē toḻudu uyyumākaṇḍu tān kaṇapuram toḻap pōyināḷvaṇḍulām kōdai en pēdai maṇi niṟamkoṇḍu tān kōyinmai seyvadu takkadē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

toṇḍu ellām – all the bhāgavatas; nin – your highness’; adiyē – divyadēśam (divine abode); toḻudu – performed anjali; uyyumā – and be uplifted; kaṇḍu – saw; tān – she too; kaṇṇapuram – tirukkaṇṇapuram; toḻa – to worship; pōyināḷ – went; vaṇḍu – beetles; ulām – roaming; kōdai – having hair; en – my; pēdai – young daughter’s; maṇi – like a precious gem; niṟam – complexion; koṇḍudān – usurped; kōyinmai – injustice; seyvadu – doing; takkadē – is it apt (for you)?

**Перевод:**

**As the mother said in the first pāsuram “veḷḷiyīr, toḻuda ivaḷ kaivaḷai koḷvadu takkadē” (Is it apt for you to take away the bangles of this girl who vorśipped you?), śaurip perumāḷ admitted his mistake saying “It is not apt for me to take away the bangles from her hand, after she vorśipped me. I have done a mistake”. Subsequently the mother said in the sixth pāsuram “ivarkkivaḷ kadavaden kaṇḍuyil inṟivar koḷḷa” (Being obedient and childish, what relationship does my daughter have with this emperumān to do anything for him? What is the purpose of this emperumān taking away her sleep today?) and in the seventh pāsuram “arangamē enbadu ivaḷ tanakkāsaiyē” (She desires for śrīrangam only) and those were heard by śaurip perumāḷ.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

\[A question arises – some of these interactions were with her neighbours. How did he know about what was discussed?\]

He remains as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 13.13](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/13-13/) “*sarvataśśruti mallōkē*” (That pure ātmā can perform all activities of hands and feet, eyes, head and face and ears everywhere; it is pervading all entities in the world). As the mother said this, he angrily said “We thought of giving the bangle; but now, why would I do that? If it is possible for you to get it, why don’t you do it?” and further said “You said that your daughter desires śrīrangam only; you said I don’t have any relationship with her; in such a case, why is she coming to my town? Did we invite her? Should she not go to the place which is desirable for her?” The mother responded, saying “There is no doubt about it. She desires śrirangam only. Her thoughts are also on that only. She just observed what the people of the town were doing and repeated the same thing to accomplish her goal”. In this manner she was waiting to see how bhagavān protects. Her desire is as said in “*kārkkadal vaṇṇar mēl eṇṇam*” (one who is having divine form which has the complexion of dark ocean). It is said in [tirunedundāṇḍagam 24](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/10/thirunedunthandakam-24/) “*ilangolineerp perumpauvam maṇḍiyuṇḍa* *peruvayiṟṟa karumugilē oppar vaṇṇam*” (Like a dark cloud which consumed the ocean water which has light and sound, from the bottom, to leave out the sand only), periya perumāḷ is having the form which resembles a dark cloud which drank the water from the ocean. Hence it is clear that her thoughts are on śrīrangam only.

My daughter, parakāla nāyaki saw all the bhāagvatas (devotees) performing anjali towards your highness’ divyadēśam and she also went to worship tirukkaṇṇapuram; is it apt for you to do injustice to my childish daughter who is having hair where beetles are roaming around, by usurping her complexion which resembles that of a precious gem?

**toṇḍu ellām** – She is saying “Everyone”. toṇḍar – bhagavān’s devotees. They may be ārtar (those who are suffering), ātma prāpti kāmar (those who desire to enjoy the self eternally) and bhagavat prāpti kāmar (those who desire to serve bhagavān eternally). There is no difference among them with respect to the relationship and the surrender. The difference is in the result they expect. Hence, she is saying “ellām” (everyone). Will “toṇḍellām” indicate devotees? It is similar to “*mancā: krōśanti*” (Bed is crying) \[which implies the children on the bed are crying\].

**toḻudu uyyumā kaṇḍu** – Seeing that those who seek any of the four puruśārtams (dharma, arta, kāma, mōkśa) surrender unto your divine feet and get their desires fulfilled.

**toḻudu** – anjali is a physical action as said in mahābhāratam śānti parvam 344.45 “*baddānjaliputā* *hruśtā*” (They are always performing anjali, joyfully).

**kaṇṇapuram toḻap pōyināḷ** – For us too, though we can go to śrīrangam right here, she went saying that she wants to worship tirukkaṇṇapuram.

**nin adiyē toḻudu** – She is not vorśipping you but is vorśipping your tirukkaṇṇapuram. īsn’t it said “*yatōpāsanam tatā palam*” (based on the intent of the worship, the result will be bestowed). Those who seek wealth, will surrender to the bhagavān with opulence. Those who seek self enjoyment will surrender unto bhagavān with purity. Those who seek bhagavat kainkaryam will surrender unto bhagavān with qualities as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*sōśnutē sarvān kāmān*” (will enjoy all the qualities of bhagavān). Since she is desirous of the divyadēśam, she worships it. Whosoever bhagavān with a specific aspect is vorśipped, will lead to bhagavān with that particular aspect. Those gōpikās who desired kriṣṇa went and surrendered to kāmadēva who is the son of kriṣṇa. udaiyavar (rāmānuja) served \[dēvap\] perumāḷ (varadarāja bhagavān) by bringing tirumanjanam (water for tiruvārādanam) for a long period and surrendered unto him and only then resided in kōyil (śrīrangam). Unlike those who are mentioned in “*toṇḍellām*“, she does not have different means and goal. Considering the entity, which is the means to be the same entity, as the goal, she sings the glories of divyadēśams as said in tirunendāṇḍagam “*tānuganda Ur ellām than tāḷ pādi*” (singing the glories of divine feet of emperumān who liked many abodes). Even when āḻvār says “*oruvarkkuriyēnō*” (will I exist for anyone else?), it is only with respect to other sādanams (upāyams) \[not for showing more affection towards divyadēśam than bhagavān himself\].

**tān pōyināḷ** – Only if she can remain without any transformation, could she go, like those who can worship without any transformation; will those who lost their complexion while going to worship, be able to go there?

**pōyināḷ** – Did those, who are born in śrī mitilā (sītāp pirātti), kuṇḍinapura (rukmiṇip pirātti) ever go \[leaving bhagavān\]? We only saw them coming to bhagavān’s town.

**pōyināḷ** – She is saying “You have not seen the one who walked as said in [periya tirumoḻi 3.7.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2022/09/periya-thirumozhi-3-7-5/) ‘*vēyana tōḷ visiṟip pedai annamena nadandu*‘ (swaying her bamboo like shoulders like a female swan, she, who is having beautiful creeper like waist, is walking behind him)”

When such parakāla nāyaki goes to tirukkaṇṇapuram, isn’t it apt for him to bestow rūpa sāmyam (having similar form), just like his? The mother is asking “Just as someone is robbed in a headless state in a secluded place, should he take away her complexion also?”

**vaṇḍu ulām kōdai en pēdai** – She is of the \[young\] age where if she ties her hair and decorates it with flowers, the beetles will fly into it, and hence she will go inside her home.

**toṇḍellām** – Just as all the devotees will take shelter of his divine feet \[or divine abode\], in his divyadēśam, all the beetles will take shelter of her hair. This is the beauty of her decoration.

**en pēdai** – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 73.26 “*mama sutā*” (my daughter), the mother is saying that her daughter has a great heritage.

**pēdai** – mugdai – child.

**maṇi niṟam koṇḍu tān** – śaurip perumāḷ asks “Your daughter is not a child; her interactions are beyond experts \[in romance\]. What is wrong in taking away her complexion?” The mother says – Should you not give your complexion as said in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 47](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-47/) “*nanmaṇi vaṇṇan*” ([sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (lord of all) who has the form of a blue coloured good gemstone); let that be aside; isn’t she a child who lacks knowledge about her true self? But should you also lack knowledge about your true self?

**koṇḍu tān** – It is natural to desire for her decoration (complexion) when it is seen; it is not wrong; but if you take it, isn’t it apt for you to give her too?

**kōyinmai seyvadu takkadē** – Should you do what is done by those who have no rāja nīti (royal morality)? īsn’t it the duty of the king to rescue what was lost? If the king himself robs, is it royal morality? The mother is saying “īsn’t it apt to carry her to the apt abode and enjoy her?” But śaurip perumāḷ thinks “If we had taken her to the apt abode when she vorśipped him in the beginning, should my devotees and I lose out?” \[If he had granted what āḻvār wanted in the beginning itself, he would not have composed these beautiful pāsurams which help the devotees and bhagavān himself\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.9. Mulleyiru

*muḷḷeyiṟu ēyndila kūḻai mudi kodā teḷḷiyaḷ enbadōr tēsilaḷ en seygēn? kaḷḷaviḻ sōlaik kaṇapuram kai toḻumpiḷḷaiyaip piḷḷai enṟeṇṇap peṟuvarē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

eyiṟu – (for her) teeth’s; muḷ – roots; ēyndila – not grown; kūḻai – (her) hair; mudi – to tie; kodā – is not allowing; (further); teḷḷiyaḷ – one with clarity; enbadu – to say that; ōr – any; tēsilaḷ – she is not having the radiance; en seygēn – (on her) what can I do?; kaḷ – honey; aviḻ – flowing; sōlai – having orchards; kaṇapuram – tirukkaṇṇapuram; toḻum – vorśipping (such); piḷḷaiyai – child; piḷḷai enṟu – as one’s own child; eṇṇa – to consider; peṟuvar – will they get to do it?

**Перевод:**

**In the previous pāsuram, the mother said “en pēdai maṇi niṟam koṇḍudān kōyinmai seyvadu takkadē” (is it apt for you to do injustice to my childish daughter by usurping her complexion which resembles that of a precious gem?), asking “Should you take away the complexion of childish daughter just robbing in a headless state?”. Hearing this, śaurip perumāḷ said “Can you order me? Can you order me who is the controller of everyone as said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat ‘sarvasya vaśī – sarvasya īśāna:‘?”. He further asks “You said she is your daughter and is obedient towards you as said in ‘madavaral mādar en pēdai’. Could you not control her? Why are you trying to control me?”. The mother is responding “This is her age. This is her mood. Hence, is she under my control?” While this is her state, the mother of another girl (parānkuśa nāyaki) who experienced in the same manner as parakāla nāyaki, is speaking on behalf of her daughter.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

[tiruviruttam pāsuram 60](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/02/thiruviruththam-60/) is explained here.

*mulaiyō muḻumuṟṟum pōndila moy pūnguḻal kuṟiya*  
*kalaiyō araiyillai nāvō kuḻaṟum* *kadal maṇṇellām*  
*vilaiyō ena miḷirum kaṇ ivaḷ paramē perumān*  
*malaiyō tiruvēngadam enṟu kaṟkinṟa vāsagamē*

**mulaiyō …** – While she is in such a state, how immersed she is! She said that it was unlimited.

**mulaiyō muḻu muṟṟum pōndila** – Bosoms are just starting to grow. They are not well grown. This is her age.

**tiruvēngadam enṟu kaṟkinṟa vāsagamē** – She kept talking about tirumalā. This is how immersed she was.

**ivaḷ paramē** – It is beyond her age/ability. parakāla nāyaki is not as grown as parānkuśa nāyaki. Even in the engagement, she was only engaged with him through her speech. But, for parakāla nāyaki, even physical engagement is present. Also with respect to tirumalā, it is similar to paramapadam in the sense that it is impossible to reach for crippled ones and blind ones, and the path to tirumalā is very steep, similar to arcirādi mārgam. But tirukkaṇṇapuram is not that difficult to attain. tirukkaṇṇapuram is easily attainable for everyone and enjoyable as they are. Hence parakāla nāyaki’s ability is in this manner and the limit of engagement is in this manner. Hence the mother is saying in public “Who can control parakāla nāyaki, my daughter?”.

For my daughter, the roots of the teeth have not yet grown; her hair is not allowing us to tie it; further, she is not having any radiance to say that she is the one with clarity; what can I do? Will anyone get to consider one’s child who is vorśipping tirukkaṇṇapuram which is having orchards where honey is flovig, as one’s own child?

**muḷ eyiṟu ēyndila** – eyiṟu – tooth; muḷḷeyiṟu – root of the tooth; the tooth is not grown.

**kūḻai mudi kodā** – If we try to gather her hair and tie it together, it will not co-operate.

**teḷḷiyaḷ enbadu ōr tēsilaḷ** – Even if she is present in this manner, still she is not having the ability to make her beloved lord starve for ten or twenty times. She is not having the radiance to mesmerise the omniscient lord.

**en seygēn** – Previously she spoke about her daughter’s childish nature and subsequently about her daughter’s greatness, and now says “What can I do?”.

**en seygēn** – Will it be possible to control her? ōr, will it be possible to follow her?

**kaḷ aviḻ …** – We cannot control her if we look at her previous state \[of childishness\]. If we look at her subsequent state \[of her vorśipping tirukkaṇṇapuram\], we can follow her – says the mother. How did she determine that we can follow her? She is saying that isn’t my daughter, who is having such great nature, great?

**kaḷ aviḻ sōlai kaṇṇapuram** – The abode where there is spring eternally. The abode which is having an orchard where the flowers have blossomed and are shedding a lot of honey.

**kaṇapuram kai toḻum piḷḷai** – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.27 “*bālyāt prabruti susnigda*:” \[lakśmaṇa was very friendly with śrī rāma right from his childhood\], iḷaiya perumāḷ was so friendly that immediately after his birth he had to be placed near the divine feet of śrī rāma in the cradle. Even such iḷaiya perumāḷ did worship only him as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 4.42 “*prānjalim prahvamāsīnam*” (lakśmaṇa who has joined palms and is seated). parakāla nāyaki is the one who worships his divine abode \[which is greater\].

**piḷḷaiyai** – One who is having such a huge greatness.

**piḷḷai enṟu eṇṇap peṟuvarē** – Can such a great person be controlled by her mother just because she was born from her?

**eṇṇap peṟuvarē** – Can anyone consider? If she considers as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*hari samsmaraṇam param*” (Remembering viṣṇu is the best among atonements), she must atone for that. The ślōkam is shown here – “*krutē pāpē’nutāpōvai yasya pumsa: prajāyatē \| prāyaścittantu tasyaikam hari samsmaraṇam param \|\|*” (If a person feels genuine remorse for the sins he committed, the best atonement is to perfectly remember hari \[and seek forgiveness from him\]). *krutē pāpē* – If a person commits a sin knowingly. *anutāpa:* – Subsequently, if he shows remorse thinking “We did a mistake; what will happen if the supreme lord comes to know about it?”, he is qualified to do atonement. *yasya pumsa: prajāyatē* – Everyone is qualified for this. Let it be anyone. *prāyaścittantu tasyaikam hari samsmaraṇam param* – It is sufficient to think about bhagavān who can remove all the sins, just once. *param* – It is said that this is the best among all the atonements.

It is written in mahābhāratam, āraṇya parvam – When periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) was mercifully flying, he decided to rest on the peak of a mountain; a woman was living on the peak and was speaking about bhagavān’s auspicious qualities; he thought with dismay “Though she is a woman, she has great taste in devotion towards bhagavān; it is unfortunate that she is not residing in a holy abode of bhagavān”; subsequently, in the morning, when he set out to fly, his wings fell down and he could not get up. \[The intent to show this incident here is – we should not think about a person who is devoted to bhagavān, to be inferior based on any of their aspects\].

With this, the following principe is revealed – even if someone is eager in bhagavat viśayam a little bit, we should not think about that person’s previous state and think inferior about that person. He should be accepted as he is and we should glorify such person. raikva samvādam “*durācarōpi sarvāśī krutagnō nāstika: purā \| samāśrayēdādidēvam śraddayā śaraṇam yadi \| nirdōśam vidditam jantum prabhavāat paramātmana: \|\|*” (Even if one has bad conduct, eats anything, remains ungrateful and remains as an atheist, if surrenders to bhagavān with faith, no defects will be observed in him by the greatness of bhagavān \[to whom he has surrendered\])”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.3 Karai edutta

## 8.3.1. Karai edutta

*karai edutta surisangum kanapavaḷattu eḻukodiyum tirai eduttu varupunal sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapurattu uṟaiyum virai edutta tuḻāy alangal viṟal varait tōḷ pudai peyara varai edutta perumānukku iḻandēn en varivaḷaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karai – roar; edutta – having; suri – curved; sangum – conces; kanam – dense; pavaḷattu – coral’s; eḻu – having growth; kodiyum – creepers; tirai – waves; eduttu – carrying; varum – coming; punal – with water; sūḻ – surrounded; tirukkaṇṇapurattu – in tirukkaṇṇapuram; uṟaiyum – eternally residing; virai – fragrance; edutta – having; tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy’s; alangal – having garland; viṟal – strong; varai – like a mountain; tōḷ – divine shoulders; pudai peyara – to sway; varai – gōvardana mountain; edutta – one who lifted, his; perumānukku – for the great benefactor, sarvēśvaran; en – my; vari – beautiful; vaḷai – bangle; iḻandēnē – I have lost

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is eternally residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram, which is surrounded by water which is coming along with waves, which are carrying creepers which have densely grown corals and curved, roaring conces. His strong, mountain like shoulders are decorated with fragrant tirutuḻāy garland; to have those shoulders swaying, the great benefactor, sarvēśvaran lifted up the gōvardana mountain. I have lost my beautiful bangle to such sarvēśvaran.

**karai edutta** – Roar is said as “karai”. This roar could indicate – a) as the conces climb atop the waves in groups, those who are on the banks would say “How big is each of those conces!” b) alternatively, the conch will naturally make noise, that is said here.

**kana …** – The creeper of the densely grown coral. The waves are bringing about the abundance of water. Being eternally present in such tirukkaṇṇapuram.

**virai …** – He stood having his shoulders sway and held gōvardana mountain to eliminate the sufferings which came about for the herds and herd-folk. I lost my beautiful bangle to the āpatsakan (friend in need) who is savēśvaran, who is having divine shoulders which are having very fragrant tiruttuḻāy garland, great strength and are like mountains.
