## 8.3.2. Ariviravu

*ariviravu mugil kaṇattāl agil pugaiyāl varaiyōdum terivariya maṇimādat tirukkaṇṇapurattu uṟaiyum vari aravin aṇait tuyinṟu maḻai madatta siṟu taṟu kaṇ kari veruva marupposittāṟku iḻandēn en kanavaḷaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ari – black colour; viravum – spreading; mugil – clouds’; kaṇattāl – by the group; agil pugaiyāl – by the smoke from agil (eaglevood) (present in that town); varaiyodum – with the mountain; terivu – knowledge that they are different; ariya – difficult (to acquire); maṇi – filled with gemstones; mādam – having homes; tirukkaṇṇapurattuṟaiyum – one, who is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram; vari – having stripes; aravin – known as tiruvantāḻvān; aṇai – on the mattress; tuyinṟu – reclining; maḻai – like rain; madatta – having exultation fluid; siṟu – small; taṟu kaṇ – having eyes (which appear cruel); kari – kuvalayāpeedam; veruva – to fear; marupposittārkku – for the one who effortless broke the tusks; en – my; kana – heavy; vaḷai iḻandēnē – lost the bangle

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is mercifully reclining on the mattress known as tiruvanantāḻvān who is having stripes, and is residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is having homes which are decorated with precious gemstones and are difficult to be differentiated from a mountain, due to the group of clouds which are black in colour in there and the smoke from agil (eaglevood); I lost my heavy bangle for such lord who effortlessly broke the tusks of kuvalayāpeedam to cause fear in it which is having exultation fluid like streams of rain flowing and small, cruel eyes.

**ari viravu mugil kaṇattāl** – By the group of dark clouds which have black colour spread everywhere, and the fragrant smoke which are caused by the residents of the town, darkness surrounds. Because of that darkness, we are unable to differentiate between the home and the mountain; one, who is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is having mansions filled with gemstones.

**vari …** – Mercifully reclined on such tiruvanantāḻvān who is having many stripes, having good fragrance, coolness and tenderness, as the mattress. kuvalayāpeedam is having small eyes matching its species instead of large eyes matching its physical size. The stream of exultation fluid coming down from those eyes looks like stream of rainwater. To cause fear in it, kriṣṇa effortlessly broke its tusks. I lost my bangle for such an act.

## 8.3.3. Tungama

*tungamā maṇimāda nedumugattin sūligai pōmtingaḷ māmugil tuṇikkum tirukkaṇṇapurattu uṟaiyumpaingaṇmāl vidai adarttup panimadi kōḷ viduttugandasengaṇmāl ammānukku iḻandēn en seṟivaḷaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tunga – best; mā – priceless; maṇi – having gemstones; mādam – having mansions; nedu – tall; mugattil – present on peak; sūligai – lightning-rod; pōm – moving around (in the sky); tingaḷ – moon; mā – having huge form; mugil – clouds; tuṇikkum – tearing; tirukkaṇṇapurattuṟaiyum – mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram; paingaṇ – having greenish eyes; māl – having huge form; vidai – bulls; adarttu – killed; pani – causing coolness; madi – moon’s; kōḷ – decay; viduttu – eliminated (due to that); uganda – being joyful; sem kaṇ – being puṇḍarīkākśa (having lotus-eyes); māl – having great love; ammānukku – for sarvēśvaran; en – my; seṟi – being irremovable ever; vaḷai iḻandēnē – lost my bangle

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is having mansions with best, priceless gemstones and lightning-rod present on tall peak of those mansions which tear into the moon and clouds which are moving around in the sky. He killed the bulls which are having greenish eyes and huge form. He eliminated the decay of the moon which causes coolness and became joyful due to that. For such sarvēśvaran, who is puṇḍarīkākśa and has great love, I lost my irremovable bangle.

**tungam …** – The lightning-rod which is present on the tall mansions which are having priceless gemstones embossed on them.

**tingaḷ …** – Mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram where the rod will tear the bottom portion of the belly of the moon and the huge clouds.

**paingaṇ māl …** – sarvēśvaran killed the bulls which were having greenish eyes and huge forms, and eliminated the decay acquired by the moon who causes coolness, and considered these acts to be a favour for himself. I lost my irremovable bangle to such sarvēśvaran who is puṇḍarīkākśan.

## 8.3.4. Kanamaruvu

*kaṇamaruvu mayil agavu kadipoḻil sūḻ nedumaṟugiltiṇamaruvu kanamadiḷ sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapurattu uṟaiyummaṇamaruvu tōḷ āycci ārkkap pōy uralōdumpuṇar marudam iṟa nadandāṟku iḻandēn en ponvaḷaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇam – muster (group); maruvum – abundantly present; mayil – peacocks; agavum – dancing; kadi – fragrant; poḻil – with orchards; sūḻ – surrounded; nedu – lengthy; maṟugil – having divine streets; tiṇam – by firmness; maruvum – having; kanam – strong; madiḷ – by fort; sūḻ – surrounded; tirukkaṇṇapurattuṟaiyum – mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram; maṇam – by fragrant materials; maruvum – pervaded; tōḷ – having divine shoulders; āycci – mother yaśōdā; ārkka – as she binds (immediately); uralōdum – with the mortar; pōy – went; puṇar – remaining together; marudam – maruda trees; iṟa – to break and fall down; nadandāṟku – for emperumān who walked; en – my; pon – best; vaḷai iḻandēnē – lost my bangle

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is surrounded by fragrant orchards where abundant muster of peacocks is dancing, is having lengthy divine streets and is surrounded by strong forts which have firmness. For that emperumān, who was bound along with a mortar by mother yaśōdā who has divine shoulders which are pervaded by fragrant materials and who immediately went along with it through the maruda trees which were remaining together to make them break and fall down, I lost my best bangle.

**kaṇam …** – The muster of peacocks which is in abundance out of joy, dance. The orchard is very fragrant. There are lengthy divine streets. The forts are so strong that they remain as protection. Mercifully residing in such tirukkaṇṇapuram.

**maṇam …** – Due to the affection towards her son kriṣṇa, she always decorates her shoulders with fragrant materials \[so that it is pleasant for kriṣṇa\]. kriṣṇa was bound by the likes of such mother yaśōdā and hence instead of cutting it off, he dragged the mortar along. When enemies like bhagadatta shoot arrows, he shows his divine chest and stands in front of them. For the acts such as binding him with the mortar, of those who are affectionate towards him, he cannot react adversely. Hence, he drags the mortar along through the two maruda trees which remained as one \[with a small gap\] to make them break and fall down. For such childish kriṣṇa, I lost my best bangle.

## 8.3.5. Vay edutta

*vāy edutta mandirattāl andaṇar tam seytoḻilgaḷtī eduttu maṟai vaḷarkkum tirukkaṇṇapurattu uṟaiyumtāy edutta siṟukōlukku uḷaindōdit tayir uṇḍavāy tudaitta maindanukku iḻandēn en varivaḷaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāy edutta – recited in a loud meter; mandirattāl – by mantrams; andaṇar – brāhmaṇas; tam – for them; sey toḻilgaḷ – the deeds which are to be done; tī – with fires; eduttu – (make them) shine; maṟai – the order of vēdam; vaḷarkkum – nurturing; tirukkaṇṇapurattuṟaiyum – mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram; tāy – yaśōdāp pirātti, the mother; edutta – lifted in her hand; siṟu – small; kōlukku – for the stick; uḷaindu – feared; ōdi – ran away; tayir – curd; uṇḍa – mercifully consumed; vāy – all over the mouth; tudaitta – smearing; maindanukku – for the lord; en – my; vari – best; vaḷai iḻaṇḍhēnē – lost my bangle

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram where brāhmaṇas are performing their deeds which are to be done, making it shine with the fires and the loud recital of vēda mantrams and nurturing the order of vēdam. yaśōdāp pirātti, the mother, took a small stick in her hand and kriṣṇa became scared and ran away. He mercifully consumed curd and smeared it on his mouth. I lost my best bangle to such a lord.

**vāy edutta mandirattāl** – bhagavān is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram where brāhmaṇas are performing their deeds which are to be done, making it shine with the fires and the loud recital of vēda mantrams and nurturing the order of vēdam.

**tāy …** – He \[kriṣṇa\] stole and mercifully consumed the butter and milk which have had physical contact with the touch of favourable persons, devotees. yaśōdāp pirātti, due to the difficulty by which they \[buttter and milk\] were gathered, picked up a stick in her hand. Without realising “She is the mother, she is just scaring me”, he became scared and ran away; thinking they will say “You stole”, to avoid that accusation, he smeared the butter on his mouth and face. For such loser, I became a loser.

## 8.3.6. Madal edutta

*madal edutta nedundāḻai marungellām vaḷar pavaḷamtidal eduttuc cudar imaikkum tirukkaṇṇapurattu uṟaiyumadal adarttu anṟu iraṇiyanai muraṇaḻiya aṇiyugirāludal edutta perumānukku iḻandēn en oḷivaḷaiyē*

madal – flaps; edutta – taken; nedum – lengthy; tāḻai – having tāḻai (fragrant screw pine trees); marungellām – all the sides; vaḷar – flourishing; pavaḷam – coral; tidal – on the sand dunes; eduttu – spread; sudar – with radiance; imaikkum – shining; tirukkaṇṇapurattuṟaiyum – mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram; adal – in the battle; adarttu – confronted; anṟu – at that time; iraṇiyanai – hiraṇya’s; muṟaṇ – strength; aḻiya – to be destroyed; aṇi – beautiful; ugirāl – with his nails; udal – his body; edutta – who tore; perumānukku – for sarvēśvaran; en – my; oḷi – shining; vaḷai iḻandēnē – lost my bangle

**No specific introduction.**

sarvēśvaran is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram which has lengthy tāḻai (screw pine) trees which are with flaps, flourishing on all sides and is shining with radiance of the corals on the sand dunes. sarvēśvaran confronted hiraṇyan in the battle at that time and tore his body with beautiful nails to have the strength destroyed. I have lost my shining bangle for such bhagavān.

**madal …** – sarvēśvaran is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram where the lengthy screw pine trees, having the well grown flaps, are present on all sides. The coral is spreading all over the sand dunes to cover them and is making the place shine.

**adal …** – Confronting hiraṇya in the battle, he destroyed hiraṇya’s strength and tore hiraṇya’s body with his nails, while his divine consorts were witnessing. In this manner, he established his īśvaratvam (control). For such person, I lost my bangle, while thinking that he helped a person (prahlādāḻvān) who was at my age \[to become disappointed\].

## 8.4 Vinnavar tangal

## 8.4.1. Vinnavar tangal

*viṇṇavar tangaḷ perumān tirumārvanmaṇṇavar ellām vaṇangum malipugaḻ sērkaṇṇapurattu emperumān kadir mudi mēlvaṇṇa naṟunduḻāy vandūdāy kōl tumbī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōl tumbi – Oh dragaonfly which is residing on a pole!; viṇṇavar tangaḷ – for nityasūris; perumān – being the controller; tiru – periya pirāttiyār; mārvan – being the one who holds on the divine chest; maṇṇavar ellām – all the residents of leelā vibhūti (samsāram – this world); vaṇangum – to worship; mali – abundant; pugaḻ – qualities such as śeelam (simplicity); sēr – one who has; kaṇṇapurattu – mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram; emperumān – sarvēśvaran’s; kadir – shining; mudi mēl – on the divine crown; vaṇṇam – colour; naṟum – fragrance (having); tuḻāy – on tiruttuḻāy (remaining there and carrying the fragrance from it); vandu – coming here; ūdāy – should blow it to me

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, dragaonfly which is residing on a pole! sarvēśvaran is the controller of nityasūris; he holds periya pirāttiyār on his divine chest; to be vorśipped by all the residents of leelā vibhūti (samsāram – this world), he is having abundant qualities such as simplicity; he is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram. You should bring the fragrance from the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) which is having \[beautiful\] color and fragrance, on his divine crown, and carry that with you, to here and blow it on me.

**viṇṇavar tangaḷ perumān tirumārvan** – īsn’t bhagavān the target of enjoyment of nityasūris and his divine consorts? This is the neem drink (medicinal drink) I am asking you to drink. As said in [tiruviruttam 21](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2021/01/thiruviruththam-21/) “*sūttu nanmālaigaḷ tūyana ēndi*” (Carrying the best garlands), nityasūris are serving him and he is accepting their service along with pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi).

**maṇṇavar ellām vaṇangum** – Just as everyone in nitya vibhūti is qualified, here in leelā vibhūti also, he comes and stands as if everyone is qualified. Just as there is no unqualified persons in nitya vibhūti, here in leelā vibhūti, there is no one qualfied and inferior. Still, he comes and stands here, as if they are qualified.

**mali pugaḻ sēr** – śeela guṇam (the quality of simplicity) should be understood through satkāryavādam (This concept is – When the effect is truth (an observable entity), the cause should also be truth (an observable entity). That is, since simplicity is present in arcāvatāram (deity form), it should be available in paramapadam also). In paramapadam, we can only understand through pramāṇam (śāstram). Here, in samsāram, since he is present in arcāvatāram making himself visible to even the lowliest persons, his simplicity is obvious here only.

**kadir mudi mēl** – On the tivuvabhiśēkam (divine crown) which is radiant due to being the lord of both nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti

**vaṇṇa naṟum tuḻāy** – Sitting on the fresh and fragrant tiruttuḻāy and carrying the fragrance from there to here, and blow it on me.

**kōl tumbi** – You who can drink the honey which was placed on poles and branches, are told to “Go and enjoy the entity who is known in cāndōjña upaniśat as ‘*sarvarasa:*‘ (the abode of all taste)”

## 8.4.2. Veda mudalvan

*vēda mudalvan viḷangu purinūlan pādam paravip palarum paṇindētti kādanmai seyyum kaṇṇapurattu emperumān tādu naṟunduḻāy tāḻndūdāy kōl tumbī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēda mudalvan – having the prominence of being revealed in vēdam; viḷangu – shining (in his divine form); puri nūlan – one who is having śrī yajñōpavītam (sacred thread); palarum – everyone; pādam – his divine feet; paravi – speak expansively; paṇindu – worship; ētti – praise (due to that); kādanmai – friendliness; seyyum – apt to show; kaṇṇapurattu emperumān – emperumān, who is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram; tādu – having pollens; naṟum – fragrant; tuḻāy – in the tiruttḻāy; tāḻndu – immerse; ūdāy kōl tumbi – Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Blow on me

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān, who is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram, is having the prominence of being revealed in vēdam; he is having śrī yajñōpavītam (sacred thread) which is shining on his divine form; he is spoken of expansively, vorśipped, praised and is apt to be friendly with everyone. Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Immerse in the tiruttuḻāy which is having pollens and fragrance, and blow its fragrance on me.

**vēda mudalvan** – Am I speaking about the one who is spoken of by men, based on their own prefereneces? It is not speaking about the one who is spoken of by āgamam etc \[ancillary literature\]. But he is having the prominence of being exclusively and completely spoken of by unautored, faultless vēdam

**viḷangu puri nūlan** – As said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*hiraṇmaya: puruśa:*” (The lord has a golden form), he is having a beautiful form and a śrī yajñōpavītam which is shining on it.

**pādam …** – Praising the divine feet incoherently, falling at those feet, everyone praises and shows their friendliness. I am asking you to pursue the one who is said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*ātmāvā arē draśtavya: śrōtavya: mantavya:* ***nididyāsitvya****:”* (Oh maitrēya! bhagavān is to be heard, contemplated and meditated upon, and seen).

**tādu …** – You should immerse into the tiruttuḻāy which is well blossomed and fresh, and then come here and blow on me.

## 8.4.3. Vinda malar

*viṇḍa malar ellām ūdi nī en peṟudi? aṇḍa mudalvan amarargaḷ ellārum kaṇḍu vaṇangum kaṇṇapurattu emperumān vaṇḍu naṟunduḻāy vandūdāy kōl tumbī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇḍa – blossomed; malar ellām – in all the flowers; ūdi – roaming around; nī – you; en – what (happiness); peṟudi – did you get? (Thus); aṇḍa – for the oval shaped universe; mudalvan – being the controller; amarargaḷ – dēvatās; ellārum – all of them; kaṇḍu – seeing to the satisfaction of their eyes; vaṇangum – one who is surrendered unto; kaṇṇapurattu emperumān – emperumān, who is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram; vaṇḍu – beetles (are present); naṟum – very fragrant; tuḻāy – (carrying the fragrance of) tiruttuḻāy; vandu ūdāy kōl tumbi – Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Come here and blow on me

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

What happiness did you get by roaming around on all the blossomed flowers? emperumān, who is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram, is the controller for the oval shaped universe; he is seen to the satisfaction of their eyes by all of the dēvatās and is surrendered unto. Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Carrying the fragrance of the very fragrant tiruttuḻāy which has beetles present all over, come here and blow on me.

**viṇḍu …** – Your journey is similar to that of those who enter any gate which is open. Even if you wait for the petals to open and the flower to blossom, the honey from the other flowers will overflow and what is present in this flower too is very little and temporary; even such honey is not there to start with. Whatever we get is also very little; is there anyone who tries so much for very little?

**aṇḍa mudalvan** – Controller of the oval shaped universe.

**amarargaḷ …** – One who is standing in tirukkaṇṇapuram to be surrendered to by all of those celestial beings who consider themselves to be the refuge, after giving up their pride.

**vandu** – Would you not like to be similar to other beetles \[which are enjoying bhagavān’s tiruttuḻāy\]?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.4.4. Nir maliginradu

*nīr maliginṟadōr mīnāy ōr āmaiyumāysīr maliginṟadōr singa uruvāgikkār mali vaṇṇan kaṇṇapurattu emperumān tār mali taṇ tuḻāy tāḻndūdāy kōl tumbī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīr – in the ocean; maliginṟadu – pervaded; ōr – unique; mīnāy – as matsyāvatāram; ōr – unique; āmaiyumāy – as kūrmāvatāram; sīr – wealth of valour; maliginṟadu – complete; ōr – unique; singa – narasimha’s; uruvāgi – having the form; kār – by beauty; mali – filled; vaṇṇan – having divine form; kaṇṇapurattu emperumān – emperumān, who is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram; tār – in the garland; mali – fully spread; taṇ – cool; tuḻāy – in the fragrance of tiruttuḻāy; tāḻndu ūdāy kōltumbi – Oh, dragonfly who is present on a pole! Immerse in it and and blow that fragrance on me

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, who is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram is having the divine forms which are filled with beauty in the unique matsyāvatāram and unique kūrmāvatāram which pervade the ocean, unique narasimhāvatāram which is complete with the wealth of valour. Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Immerse in the garland which is spread with cool tiruttuḻāy and its fragrance, and blow that fragrance on me.

**nīr maliginṟadu ōr mīnāy ōr āmaiyumāy** – Being a fish in the ocean as if the ocean’s eyes are covered. It is said in periya tirumoḻi 11.4.1 “*alaikadalneer kuḻamba*” (To agitate the ocean which has waves). The greatness of the form is such that the water in the ocean gets agitated and gathers together. Unlike the fish, being a tortoise which can inhabit both water and land.

**sīr maliginṟadu ōr singa uruvāgi** – Being narasihma who has no shortcoming in the wealth of valour. Am I asking \[all of\] you to surrender unto the form which was assumed by bhagavān for the sake of an unfavourable one? \[These forms were taken to destroy unfavourable ones\]

**kār …** – I am asking \[all of\] you to surrender unto the one who is standing with a divine form which is eagerly approachable by everyone, in tirukkaṇṇapuram.

**tār mali …** – Immerse in the tiruttuḻāy which rejuvenates the earth.

## 8.4.5. Erar malar

*ērār malar ellām ūdi nī en peṟudi?pārār ulagam paravap perungadaluḷkār āmaiyāna kaṇṇapurattu emperumāntārār naṟunduḻāy tāḻndūdāy kōl tumbī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēr – by beauty; Ar – filled; malar ellām – in all the flowers; ūdi – roamed; nī – you; en – what benefit; peṟudi – did you get?; pār – on earth; Ar – present abundantly; ulagam – all the worlds; parava – to spread; perum – vast; kadaluḷ – in the ocean; kārāmaiyāna – being the huge tortoise; kaṇṇapurattu emperumān – emperumān, who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; tār – in the garland; Ar – filled; naṟum – fragrant; tuḻāy – in tiruttuḻāy; tāḻndu – immerse; ūdāy kōl tumbi – Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Blow on me

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

What benefit did you get by roaming around all the flowers filled with beauty? emperumān, who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram, appeared as the huge tortoise in the vast ocean which spreads over all the worlds which are abundantly present on earth. Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Immerse in such emperumān’s garland which is having fragrant tiruttuḻāy and blow its fragrance on me.

**ērār malar ellām ūdi** – Your desire is not limited to one flower fully. You are just getting bewildered looking at the complexion/form. Wherever you went and searched for honey, I have never heard that you ever got to protect yourself.

**pārār ulagam parava** – To spread all over the worlds, which are fragrant..

**perum kadaluḷ kār āmaiyāna** – āḻvār is reminded by what was spoken in previous pāsurams.

**kār āmai** – Huge tortoise.

**tār Ar …** – Immerse in the tiruttuḻāy which is fragrant on earth.

## 8.4.6. Marvil tiruvan

*mārvil tiruvan valanēndu cakkarattanpāraip piḷanda paraman paranjōdikāril tigaḻ kāyā vaṇṇan kadir mudi mēltāril naṟunduḻāy tāḻndūdāy kōl tumbī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

mārvil – on his divine chest; tiruvan – one who is having periya pirāttiyār; valan – on the right divine hand; ēndum – held; cakkarattan – one who is having tiruvāḻi (sudarśana cakram); pārai – earth (from the wall of the oval shaped universe); piḷanda – one who broke (due to that); paraman – having eminence; param jōdi – being the supreme light; kāril – being the abode of black colour; tigaḻ – shining; kāyā – like a kāyām pū; vaṇṇan – emperumān who is having beautiful form, his; kadir – shining; mudi mēl – on the tiruvabhiśēkam (divine crown); tāril – present in the garland; naṟum – fragrant; tuḻāy – in tiruttuḻāy; tāḻndu – immerse; ūdāy kōl tumbi – Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Blow on me

**Перевод:**

**She is saying – if you go there (to bhagavān), there is pirātti who will make bhagavān look at youi and acknowledge you. He is the vanquiśer of enemies; he always helps us in dangerous times. He is such beautiful that we cannot abandon him even if he does not help us. Hence you go to him and then come here and blow the fragrance on me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram, is having periya pirāttiyār on his divine chest, is holding the divine chakra on his right divine hand, broke the earth from the wall of the oval shaped universe and is having eminence due to that. He is having a supremely radiant form and is having a beautiful form which has the complexion similar to a kāyām pū (a dark coloured flower) which is the abode of black colour. Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Immerse in such emperumān’s garland, which is present on his shining, divine crown and is having fragrant tiruttuḻāy, and blow its fragrance on me.

**mārvil tiruvan** – periya pirāttiyār will mercifully remain on his divine chest and when out of his freewill, finds fault in the ātmās and angrily abandons them, she will pacify him using her noble qualities and unite the ātmās with him.

**valan ēndu cakkarattan** – He is not holding the divine chakra in his hand based on her instructions. He is as said in [periya tiruvandādi 87](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/periya-thiruvandhadhi-87/) “*eppōdum kai kaḻalā nēmiyān*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), from whose hands the divine disc will not separate at any time).

**pāraip piḷanda paraman** – Earth, which entered into the wall of the oval shaped universe and lost its shape, was not abandoned by bhagavān. Instead, he assumed a form which is apt to dig out the earth from there, rescued earth and came out. In this manner, if one were to start counting those who protect, there will be none, who could be counted, after him.

**param jōdi** – One who is the ultimate goal for everyone.

**kāril tigaḻ kāyā vaṇṇan** – Even if he is not the goal, his beauty is such that he cannot be abandoned. The darkness is fully said to be the greatness of his form (and the flower). The fragrance is fully said to be the greatness for him.

**kadir …** – You should immerse in the fresh tiruttuḻāy on his divine crown which reveals his supremacy over everyone, and come here to blow that fragrance on me.

## 8.4.7. Vamanan karki

*vāmanan kaṟki madusūdan mādavantār mannu dāsaradiyāya tadamārvankāman tan tādai kaṇṇapurattu emperumāntāma naṟunduḻāy tāḻndūdāy kōl tumbī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāmanan – one, who performed vāmanāvatāram; kaṟki – one, who has vowed to perform kalki avatāram; madusūdan – one, who killed the monster named madu; tār – by the garland (which is revealing his protection); mannu – well-fitting; dāsaradiyāy – as dāśarati, the son of emperor daśarata; mādavan – being the divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi; tadam – vast; mārvan – having divine chest; kāman than – for manmata too; tādai – being the father; kaṇṇapurattu emperumān – emperumān, who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; dāmam – as the garland; naṟum – fragrant; tuḻāy – in tiruttuḻāy; tāḻndu – immerse; ūdāy kōl tumbi – Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Blow on me

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān, who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram, performed vāmanāvatāram; he has vowed to perform kalki avatāram; he killed the monster named madu; he is present with well-fitting garland as dāśarati, the son of emperor daśarata; he is the divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi and is having a vast divine chest; he is the father of manmata (cupid) too. Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Immerse in the fragrant tiruttuḻāy, which has taken the shape of a garland on such emperumān’s and blow its fragrance on me.

**vāmanan** – One who comes as a seeker to attain his own possession.

**kaṟki** – One who has vowed to torment the enemies.

**madusūdan** – One who forcefully fetched the vēdams and gave them to brahmā.

**mādavan** – Being śrīya:pati, which is the cause for these noble qualities.

**tār …** – Since he is donning a distinguished garland revealing his protection, we can force him to help us.

**kāman than tādai** – He is father even for manmata, who torments the world with his beauty.

**dāma …** – You should immerse in the fragrant tiruttuḻāy which has shaped into a garland, come here and blow that fragrance on me.

## 8.4.8. Neela malargal

*neela malargaḷ nedunīr vayal marungil sāla malar ellām ūdādē vāḷarakkarkālan kaṇṇapurattu emperumān kadir mudi mēl kōla naṟunduḻāy koṇḍūdāy kōl tumbī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nedu – abundant; nīr – having a lot of water; vayal – present in fertile fields; neela – blue coloured; malargaḷ – in flowers; marungil – in the surroundings (of such fertile field); sāla – lot of; malar ellām – in all the flowers; ūdādē – don’t roam around; vāḷ – having sword, the weapon; arakkar – for rākśasas; kālan – death; kaṇṇapurattu emperumān – emperumān, who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; kadir – shining; mudimēl – present on the divine crown; kōlam – beautiful; naṟum – fragrant; tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy’s fragrance; koṇḍu – bringing it here; ūdāy kōl tumbī – Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Blow on me

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Don’t roam around in all the abundant flowers which are present in the surroundings of the fertile fields which are having abundance of water and the blue coloured flowers in the fertile fields themselves. emperumān, who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram, is death personified for rākśasas who are having the weapon, sword. Bringing the fragrance of the beautiful, fragrant tiruttuḻāy which is present on the shining divine crown of such emperumān, blow it on me.

**neela …** – The blue coloured flowers which were grown in the fertile fields which have abundant water. All of the flowers which are present in the surroundings of that fertile field.

**ūdādē** – Don’t roam around even for insignificant benefit. There is scope for doubt only making one think “If there are flowers, would there not be honey?”

**vāḷarkkar kālan** – bhagavān is death personified for the armed rākśasas. You should bring the fragrance from the beautiful tiruttuḻāy on the shining divine crown of the sarvēśvaran who has arrived in tirukkaṇṇapuyram, and blow it on me.

## 8.4.9. Nandan madalai

*nandan madalai nilamangai nal tuṇaivan anda mudalvan amarargaḷ tam perumān kandam kamaḻ kāyā vaṇṇan kadir mudi mēl kondu naṟunduḻāy koṇḍūdāy kōl tumbī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nandan – śrī nandagōpa’s; madalai – being the divine son; nilamangai – for śrī bhūdēvi; nal – good; tuṇaivan – being the protector; andam – for samhāram (annihilation); mudalvan – being the controller; amarargaḷ tam – for nityasūris; emperumān – being the lord; kandam – fragrance; kamaḻ – spreading; kāyā – like a kāyām pū; vaṇṇan – emperumān who is having divine complexion, his; kadir – shining; mudimēl – on the divine crown; kondu – as a bundle; naṟum – fragrant; tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy’s fragrance; koṇḍu – bringing here; ūdāy kōl tumbi – Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Blow on me

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

emperumān is the divine son of śrī nandagōpar; he is the good protector of śrī bhudēvi; he is the controller of samhāram (annihilation); he is the lord for nityasūris; he is having the divine complexion of a kāyām pu which is spreading its fragrance. Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! Bring the fragrance from the bundle of fragrant tiruttuḻāy on the shining divine crown of such emperumān and blow it on me.

**nandan …** – Am I asking you to go to a place which is unreachable for us? \[kriṣṇāvatāram is in the past\]

**nandan madalai** – One who became easily approachable by taking birth as the divine son of śrī nandagōpar.

**nila mangai nal tuṇaivan** – He took birth as kriṣṇa to eliminate the burden on earth.

**anda mudalvan** – He is the annihilator of all and creator of all.

**amarargaḷ tam perumān** – He is\`as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*ayaravaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (the lord of nityasūris who are free from bewilderment).

**kandam …** – One who is having the divine complexion of a fragrant kāyām pū. Only the complexion can be compared with the kāyā flower \[in all other aspects, he is beyond comparison with that flower\]. He has the greatness as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sarvaganda:*” (the abode of all fragrances). The tiruttuḻāy is present as a bundle and is fragrant.

## 8.4.10. Vandamarum

*vaṇḍamarum sōlai vayalāli nal nādan kaṇḍa sīr venṟik kaliyan oli mālai koṇḍal niṟavaṇṇan kaṇṇapurattānai toṇḍarōm pāda ninaindūdāy kōl tumbī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōl tumbī – Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole!; toṇḍarōm – We, the servitors; vaṇḍu – beetles; amarum – residing; sōlai – having orchards; vayal – having fertile fields; Ali – known as tiruvāli; nal – good; nādan – being the controller of that region; kaṇḍa – be seen (with eyes); sīr – having wealth; venṟi – one who vanquished the enemies; kaliyan – tirumangai āḻvār; oli – mercifully spoke in a famous way; mālai – in the form of a garland (with these ten pāsurams); koṇḍal – cloud’s; niṟam – like the complexion; vaṇṇan – having a form (which is rejuvenating); kaṇṇapurattānai – sarvēśvaran, who is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram; pāda – to sing; ninaindu – keeping in your heart; ūdāy – you should blow on us

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

tirumangai āḻvār is the controller of the good region named tiruvāli which is having orchards where beetles are residing and which has fertile fields; he has wealth which can be seen with eyes; he has vanquished his enemies; he mercifully composed in a famous way, these ten pāsurams in the form of a garland for the emperumān who is having cloud-like complexion and is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram. Oh, dragonfly which is present on a pole! You keep it in your heart that we, the servitors of bhagavān sing him, and that you should blow \[his fragrance\] on us.

In the end,

**vaṇḍu …** – Beetles, having drunk honey, are humming in the orchards. āḻvār is the controller of tiruvāli which is having such orchards and fertile fields. āḻvār is having unlimited wealth which are not just heard from authentic texts but can also be seen. He has vanquished the enemies. He has sung these pāsurams which are in the form a garland. To have us, the servitors, sing with these pāsurams, sarvēśvaran who has arrived here in tirukkaṇṇapuram with a rejuvenating form, you should keep in your heart, inform him, make him acknowledge us and try to eliminate our worries; as āḻvār becomes pacified, everyone will become pacified.

## 8.5 Tandai kalil

## 8.5.1. Tandai kalil

*tandai kālil vilangaṟa vandu tōnṟiya tōnṟal pin tamiyēn tansindai pōyiṟṟut tiruvaruḷ avanidaip peṟumaḷavu irundēnaiandi kāvalan amuduṟu pasungadir avai suda adanōdumanda mārudam vanamulai tadavandu vali seyvadu oḻiyādē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tandai – vasudēva, the father, his; kālil – present on feet; vilangu – shackle; aṟa – to break and fall down; vandu – mercifully came; tōnṟiya – incarnated; tōnṟal pin – behind kriṣṇa, who was childish; tamiyēn than – me, who is alone (being separated from him), my; sindai – mind; pōyiṟṟu – has gone; avanidai – from him; tiruvaruḷ – mercy; peṟum – to get; aḷavu irundēnai – me, who was waiting; andi kāvalan – moon’s; amuduṟu – abundant with nectar; pasum – fresh; avai – those; kadir – rays; suda – as they burn; adanōdu – with that; manda mārudam – soft, southerly breeze; vanam – beautiful; mulai tadam – on my bosom; vandu – entered and touched; oḻiyādē – continuously; vali seyvadu – tormenting me

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

sarvēśvaran mercifully came and incarnated as childish kriṣṇa to eliminate the shackles from the feet of his father, vasudēva. While I am being alone in separation from him, my heart went behind such kriṣṇa. I am waiting to get his mercy. The rays of moon which are fresh due to the moon’s nectar, is burning me. Along with that, the soft, southerly breeze entered my bosoms and touched them, and is continuously tormenting me.

**tandai …** – One who eliminates the shackles caused by others, is not eliminating the shackles caused by him \[to me\]. Meditating upon the nature of childish kriṣṇa who came and incarnated to make the shackles on śrī vasudēva’s feet break and fall down, my heart which is alone, in separation from him, thought “Since he comes and helps during dangers, will he not come and help us who are having more love than such father, vasudēva?” and went behind him.

**tiruvaruḷ avanidaip peṟum aḷavu irundēnai** – I was waiting for his mercy, when my heart was not helping me, as said in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 19](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/munram-thiruvandhadhi-19/) “*aruḷādoḻiyumē*” (Will he not shower his mercy?). Not only did I not get the result of his mercy, only enmity resulted.

**andi kāvalan …** – Just as the guardian for a town steals, moon, who is the controller of night, his.

**amuduṟu pasum kadir avai suda** – If poison torments, we can do remedy using nectar. If nectar torments, there is no remedy for that. The nectarean rays are burning as if fire was thrown at us.

**adanōdu manda mārudam** – That was sufficient for the severity of the torment. Along with that, the southerly breeze, which roams around moderately, has appeared.

**vana mulai tadam vandu** – Wherever his hand touches, the breeze entered all those places and touched.

**vali seyvadu oḻiyādē** – That southerly breeze could think “If we torment her too much, should we not stop at some point” and withdraw due to mercy; instead of doing that, it is continuously tormenting me. Even for rāvaṇa’s evil acts, there was a limit. We are not seeing any limit for this breeze’s torments.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.5.2. Mari makkadal

*māri mākkadal vaḷai vaṇaṟku iḷaiyavan varai purai tirumārbil tārin āsaiyil pōyina nenjamum tāḻndadōr tuṇai kāṇēn ūrum tunjiṟṟu ulagamum tuyinṟadu oḷiyavan visumbiyangum tērum pōyiṟṟut tisaigaḷum maṟaindana seyvadonṟu aṟiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māri – one who is like a cloud; mā – vast; kadal – one who is like an ocean; vaḷai – like a conch; vaṇarkku – for baladēva who is having complexion; iḷaiyavan – kriṣṇa, who is the younger brother, his; varai purai – like a mountain; tirumārvil – on the divine chest; tārin – for the garland; āsaiyil – due to the desire; pōyina – left; nenjamum – heart; tāḻndadu – remained (with him); ōr tuṇai – a companion; kāṇēn – I am not seeing; ūrum – residents of the town; tunjiṟṟu – have slept; ulagamum – the worlds; tuyinṟadu – have slept; oḷiyavan – sun; visumbu – in the sky; iyangum – faded away; tērum – (his) chariot; pōyiṟṟu – disappeared; tisaigaḷum – directions; maṟaindana – became void; seyvadu – to be done; onṟu – anything; aṟiyēnē – I am not knowing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Due to its desire towards the garland on the mountain-like divine chest of kriṣṇa, who is like a cloud, vast ocean and is the younger brother of baladēva who is having conch like complexion, my heart which went there, remained with him; I am not knowing any companion; the residents of the town have slept; the worlds have slept; sun in the sky has faded away; his chariot has disappeared; the directions have become void; I am not knowing as to what is to be done.

**māri …** – While there is no other protector, he is having a form which cannot be left without embracing. One, who is having a form which resembles a cloud and an ocean.

**vaḷai vaṇarkku iḷaiyavan** – Being born as the younger brother of baladēva, he is as enjoyable as his physical beauty for us. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.24.20 “*sāntvayāmāsa tā rāma: kṛiṣhṇasyātimanōharai: \| sandēśai: ślakṣṇamadurai: sapraśrayamanulbaṇai: \|\|*” (balarāma consoled the gōpikās and gave them kriṣṇa’s divine message which was soft and sweet. He was humble and free from arrogance, towards the gōpikās) – balarāma would console the heart which was wounded by kriṣṇa’s misciefs and unite her with krishna. She is calling out as done by sītāp pirātti in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 28.8 “*hārāma hālakśmaṇa*” (Oh śrī rāma! Oh lakśmaṇa!).

**varai …** – Had it gone there for a particular purpose, it can return with that purpose accomplished. Since the heart went there desiring to attain garland on his divine chest, which appears like waterfalls coming down from the divine chest, instead of returning, with great love, it stayed there.

**ōr tuṇai kāṇēn** – The heart which went there did not return; the nāyakan (hero) has abandoned me and left; now, who will be the companion?

When asked “Are you not living in a town?” she says

**ūrum tunjiṟṟu** – They don’t have their heart taken away; hence there is no shortcoming for them to sleep at night. Hence those who disturb us \[heart\] and who advise us \[townspeople\], both of them are not there.

**ulagamum tuyinṟadu** – Along with the town, all the worlds too, went to sleep.

**oḷiyavan …** – Sun, who pacifies us, also left. Did he leave since there is no place for him to roam around? Even if he left, at least if the chariot, which he rides, is visible to me, will I not survive?

**tisaigaḷum maṟaindana** – Only by sun’s presence, we can identify the directions. Even those directions have disappeared.

**seyvadu onṟu aṟiyēnē** – There is no outsider. Lost the heart. nāyakan has not arrived. Now, what can be done?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.5.3. Ayan mayame

*āyan māyamē anṟi maṟṟu en kaiyil vaḷaigaḷum iṟai nillā pēyin āruyir uṇḍidum piḷḷai nam peṇ uyirkku irangumō? tūya māmadik kadir sudat tuṇai illai iṇaimulai vēginṟadāl āyan vēyinukku aḻiginṟadu uḷḷamum anjel enbār ilaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āyan – kriṣṇa’s; māyamē anṟi – other than the misciefs; maṟṟu – other; en – what?; kaiyil – present on hand; vaḷaigaḷum – bangles; iṟai – even for a moment; nillā – not remaining; pēyinār – pūtanā’s; uyir – life; uṇḍidum – consumed; piḷḷai – kriṣṇa, the child; nam – our; peṇ – girl’s; uyirkku – for the life; irangumō – will he feel sad?; tūya – blemiśless; mā – huge; madi – moon’s; kadir – rays; suda – as they burn; tuṇai – (to eliminate that) companion; illai – not having; iṇai – remaining together; mulai – bosoms; vēginṟadu – are being burnt; Al – alas!; āyan – kriṣṇa’s; vēyinukku – for the flute; uḷḷamum – (her) heart; aḻiginṟadu – being destroyed; anjelenbār – those who would say “Don’t fear”; illaiyē – not there

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

**Note: This pāsuram can be seen as being spoken by parakāla nāyaki’s well-wishers on seeing her state in the past two pāsurams.**

For our girl, what else other than kriṣṇa’s misciefs is present? Her bangles are not remaining on her hand even for a moment. Will kriṣṇa, the child who consumed pūtanā’s life feel sad for our girl’s \[my\] life? She is not having a companion, while the blemiśless, moon’s rays are burning her. Her bosoms, which are remaining together, are being burnt; alas! Her heart is being destroyed for kriṣṇa’s flute. Those who would say “Don’t fear” are not there.

**āyan …** – When kriṣṇa went away he said “I will not separate from you; even if I did, I will not survive” and left. Unlike that these bangles quickly slipped out. This is as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.29 “*śaitilyamupayāntyāśu karēśu valayānyapi*” (When kriṣṇa left us, our bangles also slipped away). *āśu śaitilyam upayānti* – I observed that they immediately slipped away. Hope it is not the time when those, who are in our hands \[reach\], leave us!

**iṟai nillā** – They won’t stay even for a moment. After he left, they did not stay even for one moment.

**pēy …** – Will the one, who planned to get caught by pūtanā and thus torment us, show his mercy now? From the beginning, he set out to torment the women.

**tūya mā madik kadir suda** – As the blemiśless moon’s rays blow fire and burn.

**tuṇai illai iṇai mulai vēginṟadāl** – There was no one who could extinguish the fire. It burnt as it saw/desired.

**āyan …** – The covherd boy’s flute appeared to destroy the heart which was saying “He is still not coming, even at this stage of suffering”. She will not be immersed in the flute played by brāhmaṇas.

**anjal enbārillaiyē** – No one who can say as in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mā śuca:*” (Don’t grieve), is present.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.5.4. Kayangol

*kayangoḷ puṇ talaik kaḷiṟundu vendiṟal kaḻal mannar perum pōril mayanga veṇsangam vāy vaitta maindanum vandilan maṟikadal nīr tayangu veṇ tirait tivalai nuṇpani enum taḻal mugandu iḷamulai mēliyangu mārudam vilangil en āviyai enakkenap peṟalāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kayam koḷ – pus is continuously oozing; puṇ – wound; talai – having on head; kaḷiṟu – elephants; undu – being able to conduct; vem – cruel; tiṟal – strong; kaḻal – having valourous anklets; mannar – kings’; perum – great; pōril – in the battle; mayanga – to be bewildered; veṇ – whitish; sangam – śrī pāncajanyam; vāy vaitta – keeping on mouth (and blew); maindanum – youthful kriṣṇa also; vandilan – has not come; maṟi – agitated with waves; kadal – ocean’s; nīr – in the water; tayangum – swaying and coming; veṇ – whitish; tirai – caused by the waves; tivalai – collection of water; nuṇ – subtle; paniyenum – known as “mist”; taḻal – fire; mugandu – fetching; iḷa – youthful; mulaimēl – on my bosom; iyangum – blowing; mārudam – southerly breeze; vilangil – if withdraws; en – my; āviyai – life; enakkena – for me; peṟalām – can attain

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa, who kept the whitish śrī pāncajanyam and blew it to bewilder the kings who have cruel strength and valourous anklets and are able to conduct elephants which have pus oozing out of their heads, in their great war, has not come. The southerly breeze is fetching the subtle collection of water which is known as “mist” and which are caused by the whitish waves coming from the agitated ocean. This mist feels like fire and is blown on my youthful bosom. Only if it withdraws, could I preserve my life.

**kayam koḷ …** – The kings are able to control as they wish, the elephants which are always exultant and are hence poked by the mahout with the hook ,causing wounds which are constantly letting out pus. They \[the kings\] are very strong and are having valourous anklets. To have them bewilder in the battle, kriṣṇa placed the śrī pāncajanyam on his divine lips and blew it as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.19](https://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-19/) “*sa gōśō dārtarāśtrāṇām* …” (The sound of the conces blown together that filled the sky and the entire earth, broke the hearts of the sons of drutarāśtra) and destroyed the enemies. Such kriṣṇa is not coming; he, who is the protector, has not helped me in this dire situation; I can remain alive only if the entity which harms, withdraws.

**maṟi kadal …** – In the agitated ocean, the waves are swaying and coming on the water. That causes the subtle mist to form and appears like fire. Fetching that, the southerly breeze blows that on my bosom which cannot tolerate the separation.

**vilangil** – If the breeze thinks at some point that “This is harming a woman. Should I do it?” and withdraws… Our state is such that the one who causes harm should become the protector. sītāp pirātti said “rāvaṇa! Can’t you unite me with perumāḷ?” Only then, I will be alive.

## 8.5.5. Elu mamaram

*ēḻu māmaram tuḷai padac cilai vaḷaittu ilangaiyai malanguvittaāḻiyān namakku aruḷiya aruḷodum pagal ellai kaḻiginṟadāltōḻi! nām idaṟken seydum? tuṇai illai sudar padu mudu neeril āḻa āḻginṟa āviyai aduvadōr andi vandu adaiginṟadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēḻu – seven; mā – huge; maram – sāla vrukśam (ebony trees); tuḷaipada – to pierce through them; silai – bow; vaḷaitta – one who drew; ilangaiyai – lankā; malanguvitta – one who caused bewilderment; āḻiyān – cakravartit tirumagan,who is wearing a ring; namakku – for us; aruḷiya – showered mercy; aruḷodum – with the grace; pagal ellai – the end of daytime; kaḻiginṟadu – leaving; Al – alas!; tōḻi – Oh friend!; nām – we; idaṟku – for this; en seydum – what will \[we\] do?; tuṇai – companion; illai – not present; sudar – sun too; padum – the place where he is seen; mudu nīril – in the ocean; āḻa – immersed (and disappeared); vāḻginṟa – having the desire to live; āviyai – prāṇa (the vital air); aduvadu – which destroys; ōr – unique; andi – sandyā (dusk time); vandu – came; adaiginṟadē – is appearing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

cakravartit tirumagan\`, who is wearing a ring, drew his bow to pierce through the seven huge ebony trees, caused bewilderment to lankā; his grace, which was mercifully given by him and the end of the daytime are leaving; alas! Oh friend! What can we do for this? There is no companion for us. The sun too immersed into the ocean where he was seen and disappeared. The sandyā (dusk time) which will destroy the prāṇan which is having the desire to live, has come and is appearing.

**ēḻu mā maram tuḷai pada** – He is the one who performs acts to make others have faith in him; but he is not helping me, who has faith in him and desires for him.

**ilangai …** – He made the residents of lankā to become so bewildered that seven people will end up sharing one person’s clothes.

**āḻiyān** – It appears that the only ornament which escaped kaikēyi’s boon, is that ring in his hand.

**namakku aruḷiya** – Along with the grace he mercifully gave us, the daytime which is a reflection of his grace, also left. Just as the grace leaves, light will also go.

**tōḻi nām idaṟku en seydum** – Should both of us, who are helpless, protect ourselves?

**tuṇai illai** – If bhagavān were there, he could save us \[but he is also not present\].

**sudar padu mudu nīr …** – The sun immersed into the ocean where he appeared and set; having lost the sun, who is the pacifier, the prāṇans (vital airs) had the desire to live. At that time, the unique sandyā arrived and set out to destroy those vital airs.

## 8.5.6. Muriyum ven tirai

*muriyum veṇ tirai mudukayam tīppada muḻangu aḻal eri ambin varikoḷ venjilai vaḷaivitta maindanum vandilan en seygēn? eriyum vengadir tuyinṟadu pāviyēn iṇai nedungaṇ tuyilākariya nāḻigai ūḻiyin periyana kaziyumāṟu aṟiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

muriyum – tumultuous; veṇ – whitish; tirai – having waves; mudu kayam – the ancient ocean; tīppada – to burn; muḻangu – sounding; aḻal – fire; eri – blowing; ambin – having arrow; vari koḷ – beautiful; vem silai – cruel bow; vaḷaivitta – one, who drew; maindanum – the strong cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma, the son of the emperor); vandilan – is not coming; en seygēn – what can I do?; eriyum – shining; vem kadir – hot sun; tuyinṟadu – has set; pāviyēn – me, the sinner, my; iṇai – matching each other; nedum – expansive; kaṇ – eyes; tuyilā – are not sleeping; ūḻiyil – than kalpa (brahmā’s day\|); periyana – bigger; kariya – blackish; nāḻigai – the unit \[of time\] named nāḻigai (24 minutes) (of the night); kaḻiyumāṟu – the way to spend; aṟiyēnē – I am not seeing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The strong cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma, the son of the emperor) who drew his beautiful yet cruel bow, which is having arrow that is blowing resounding fire to burn the ancient ocean having tumultuous whitish waves, is not coming; what can I do? The shining hot sun has set; I, the sinner, am having vast eyes which are matching with each other and are not sleeping. I am not seeing the way to spend the blackish unit named nāḻigai (24 minutes) of the night, which is more than the duration of a brahmā’s day, kalpa.

**muriyum …** – There is the ocean which is ancient water body that is having tumultuously roaming whitish water (waves). That,

**tīppada** – To burn. vikrama cōḻa dēvar would say “Is this some kind of a haystack!”

**muḻangu** – Blowing fire to make noise. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam ślōkam 46.22 “***dīpta pāvaka sankāśai*****:** *śitai: kāncanabhūśaṇai*: l *na tvāmiccāmyaham draśtum rāmēṇa nihatam śarai*: ll” (I do not wish to see you killed by śrī rāma, whose arrows are like burning fire, sharp and decorated with gold), having beautiful bow which is having beautiful arrow which is blowing fire. śrī rāma, who is having such strength, is not coming.

**eriyum vem kadir tuyinṟadu** – Sun, who,due to his brightness, makes others see the objects and brings them peace, has set; serving īśvara (śrīman nārāyaṇa) fully, at some point, he also set out to sleep.

**pāviyēn iṇai nedum kaṇ tuyilā** – If sun, who gives sight to the entire world, can sleep, why can’t I do it?

**kariya** – Since the night, which is not liked by her, is dark in colour, she is asking “Is the nāḻigai which is night’s part, also has dark complexion?” Alternatively – “Very cruel nāḻigai”. Another explanation – that sandyā kālam is a very dark time.

**kaḻiyumāṟu aṟiyēn** – I don’t know how it will be exhausted ever. We have heard that in the past, some kalpas were destroyed. But now even the nāḻigai is not withdrawing.

## 8.5.7. Kalanga makkadal

*kalanga mākkadal kadaindadaittu ilangaiyar kōnadu varai āgammalanga venjamattu adusaram turanda em adigaḷum vārānāl ilangu vengadir iḷamadi adanodum vidai maṇi adum āyanvilangal vēyinadu ōsaiyumāy ini viḷaivadonṟu aṟiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā – vast; kadal – ocean; kalanga – to become agitated (that); kadaindu – churned it; adaittu – building a bridge; ialangaiyar – residents of lankā, their; kōnadu – rāvaṇa, the king, his; varai – strong like a mountain; āgam – chest; malanga – to throb; vem samattu – in the battle; adu saram – deadly arrow; tuṟanda – launched; em adigaḷum – our lord of all; vāran – not coming; Al – alas!; ilangu – shining; vem – burning; kadir – having rays; iḷa madi adanōdum – with the young moon; vidai – bull’s; maṇi – sound of the bell (tied to its neck); adum – killing (me); āyan – kriṣṇa, the covherd boy; vilangal – present on the mountain; vēyinadu – flute made with bamboo, its; ōsaiyum – sound being created; āy – is tormenting me; ini – further; viḷaivadu – effect; onṟu – anything; ariyēnē – I am not knowing

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

To agitate the vast ocean, bhagavān, who is the lord of all, churned it and built a bridge; he launched the deadly arrow to kill the king of rākśasas, rāvaṇan, to have his mountain-like vast chest throbbing.; he is not coming. Alas! Along with the young moon which is having shining rays which are burning, the bell which is hung on the bull’s neck, is killing me. The sound of the flute, made by bamboos which grew from the mountain, which is from kriṣṇa, the covherd boy himself, is tormenting me. I am not aware of any effects.

**kalanga …** – For the sake of pirātti, emperumān churned the ocean which cannot be comprehended by anyone, to have the bottom sand come up; he built a bridge on the ocean for her sake; the lord of all, who launched the deadly arrow to pierce the mountain like strong chest of rāvaṇa, the king of lankā, has not come.

**ilangu …** – Along with the young moon which is shining with the rays which are burning, the sound of the bell on the bull’s neck, is killing me. These are sufficient enough to torment anyone. Further,

**āyan …** – The flute which is having great origin and is in the covherd boy’s hand, is killing me.

**ini viḷaivadu onṟu aṟiyēnē** – If I die, he will not be alive; if he is gone, the nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti which are taken care of by him, cannot exist; hence, I don’t know how this will end.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.5.8. Muludu ivvaiyagam

*muḻudu ivvaiyagam muṟai keda maṟaidalum munivanum muniveydi maḻuvināl mannar āruyir vavviya maindanum vārānāl oḻugu nuṇpanikku odungiya pēdaiyai adanga anjiṟai kōlittaḻuvu naḷḷiruḷ tanimaiyin kadiyadōr koduvinai aṟiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivvaiyagam – this world; muḻudu – fully; muṟai – order; keda – to be violated; maṟaidalum – since lost; munivanum – jamadagni bhagavān; muniveyda – since showed anger (having that as the reason); maḻuvināl – with the axe; mannar – kings’; Ar uyir – dear life; vavviya – one who got rid of; maindanum – śrī paraśurāma bhagavān; vārān – not coming; oḻugu – flowing; nuṇ – intolerable; panikku – for the mist; odungiya – shriveled; pēdaiyai – female bird; adanga – to subdue (the birds); am – beautiful; siṟai – wings’; kōli – bottom portion; taḻuvum – embrace; naḷ iruḷ – amidst pitch dark times; tanimaiyil – more than remaining separated; kadiyadu – cruel; ōr – a type of; koduvinai – cruel sin; aṟiyēnē – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Since the whole world lost its order and since jamadagni bhagavān became angry, śrī paraśurāmāḻvān eliminated the dear life of the kings with his axe; such śrī paraśurāmāḻaān is not coming. I don’t know of any cruel type of sin than remaining alone in the pitch darkness when the overflowing mist causes the female bird to shrivel and the male bird embraces in the bottom portion of its wings, to subdue it,

**muḻudu …** – The system of kśatriyas ruling under the guidance of brāhmaṇas, became lost; due to that jamadagni became angry; having that as the reason, the strong śrī paraśurāmāḻvān severed with his axe for twenty-one generations, the kśatriyas , who were the reason for this. Such śrī paraśurāmāḻvān is not coming. Since the system of kśatriyas collapsed and since his father was insulted, śrī paraśurāmāḻvān gathered the kings and severed them.

**oḻugu …** – The female bird became shriveled due to the mist coming inside their nest; at that time, the male bird will spread its wings and embrace the female bird in protection. Other than remaining separate, at this time.

**kodiyadōr kaduvinai aṟiyēnē** – As said in brahma vaivartam prakruti kāṇḍam 26.70 “***avaśyam anubhōktavyam*** *krutam karma śubhāśubham \| nābhuktam kśīyatē karma kōti śatairapi \|\|”* (The karma which was performed in the form of good and bad deeds, has to be experienced. Even after passing one hundred crore days of brahmā, such karma will not be exhausted without experiencing it), I am not aware of any cruel sin which cannot be exhausted in any way other than experiencing the result. That is, there is no higher suffering which is to be experienced after reaching the narakam (hell), than the current experience.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.5.9. Kananjey

*kananjey māmadiḷ kaṇapurattavanodum kanavinil avan tanda mananjey inbam vandu uḷ puga veḷgi en vaḷai nega irundēnai sinanjey mālvidaic ciṟu maṇi ōsai en sindaiyaic cinduvikkum anandal anṟilin arikural pāviyēn āviyai aduginṟadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kanam – heavily; sey – made; mā – huge; madiḷ – having fort; kaṇapurattavanodum – with the one, who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram; kanavinil – to be like a dream; avan – that lord; tanda – gave; manam sey – occurred in the heart; inbam – joy; uḷ – inside; vandu – came; puga – as it enters (by that); veḷgi – became immersed; en – my; vaḷai – bangle on the hand; nega – to slip out; irundēnai – me, who was present; seṟu – affecting; sinam sey – angry; māl – having huge form; vidai – bull’s; maṇi – bell’s; ōsai – the sound; en – my; sindaiyai – mind; sinduvikkum – breaks down; anandal – having slumber; anṟilin – anṟil (nightingale); ari – tormenting, faltering; kural – speech; pāviyēn – me, who has committed sins, my; āviyai – prāṇan (life); aduginṟadē – hurting

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is having huge forts which are made in a heavy manner. The dream-like joy in heart which was given by him came and entered me. Becoming immersed in that, I remained in a state where the bangle on my hand would slip out. The sound of the bell of the angry, huge bull is breaking my heart down and tormenting me; I have committed sins and the slumbering nightingale’s tormenting, faltering speech is hurting my life.

**kanam sey …** – The bhagavān who is mercifully present in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is having strong fort, which is a protective layer, gave the dream-like union.

**manam sey inbam** – Experienced only in the heart and nothing is felt externally. As such experience entered my heart, I became immersed in it, and due to that I remained in a state where the bangle slipped out.

**sinam …** – The sound of the bell on the neck of the angry, huge bull, looks superficial for the eyes but has the ability to finish (those who are suffering in separation) and is breaking my heart.

**anandal …** – The slumbering nightingale’s faltered speech.

**pāviyēn āviyai aduginṟadē** – It is causing to destroy me who has committed great sin, where everything torments me.

## 8.5.10. Varkol

*vārkoḷ menmulai madandaiyar tadangadal vaṇṇanait tāḷ nayandu ārvattāl avar pulambiya pulambalai aṟindu mun urai seyda kārkoḷ paimboḻil mangaiyar kāvalan kalikanṟi oli vallār ērkoḷ vaikunda mānagar pukku imaiyavarodum kūduvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vār koḷ – having corset; men – soft; mulai – having bosoms; madandaiyar – girls; tadam – vast; kadal – ocean-like; vaṇṇan – emperumān who is having complexion in his divine form, his; tāḷai – divine feet; nayandu – desired; ārvattāl – due to overwhelming desire; avar – their; pulambiya – calling out; pulambal – lament; aṟindu – thinking about it in the same way; mun – first; urai seyda – called out; kār koḷ – having the movement of clouds; pūmpoḻil – having flower orchards; mangaiyar – for the residents of tirumangai region; kāvalan – being the protector; kali kanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; oli – to have tune (mercifully composed this tirumoḻi); vallār – those who are able to recite; ēr koḷ – beautiful; vaigunda mānagar – in the nityavibhūti (śrīvaikuṇṭam); pukku – enter; imaiyavarōdum – along with nityasūris; kūduvarē – will get the result (which ensures no return to samsāra)

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān is having vast ocean-like complexion in his divine form. The girls who are having soft bosoms, which are decorated with corset, desired for such bhagavān’s divine feet and due to that overwhelming desire, called out for him and lamented. tirumangai āḻvār, who is the protector of the residents of tirumangai region, which is having flower orchards which are having movement of clouds, at first understood such calling out, and lamented in the same way in this decad which has tune. Those who are able to recite these pāsurams will enter the beautiful nityavibhūti, and will get the result to remain along with nityasūris, eternally.

**vār koḷ …** – The girls of tiruvāyppādi (śrī gōkulam) who are aptly young, desired for kriṣṇa’s divine feet and since they did not attain the same, out of overwhelming desire, lamented. Thinking about such calling out, āḻvār also called out in the same manner.

**kār koḷ …** – For the residents of tirumangai which is having vast orchards which are having constant movement of clouds, āḻvār is the protector. He mercifully composed this decad with tune. Those who can recite this decad.

**ēr koḷ …** – Eliminating such lamentation in separation, uniting with the nityasūris in the nitya vibhūti, one will let out sounds as in taittirīya upaniśat bruguvalli “*aham annam aham annam*” (I am his food (enjoyment), I am his food (enjoyment)) revealing the joy, and will never have to return to samsāram.

## 8.6 Tondir uyyum

## 8.6.1. Tondir uyyum

*toṇḍīr! uyyum vagai kaṇḍēn tuḷangā arakkar tuḷanga muntiṇ tōḷ nimirac cilai vaḷaiyac ciṟidē muninda tirumārbanvaṇḍār kūndal malarmangai vadikkaṇ madandai mānōkkamkaṇḍān kaṇḍu koṇḍu uganda kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

toṇḍīr – Oh servitors of bhagavān! (I); uyyum – for ujjīvanam (to be uplifted); vagai – a means; kaṇḍēn – have seen; mun – previously; tuḷangā – fearless; arakkar – rākśasas \[demons\]; tuḷanga – to be scared; tiṇ – strong; tōḷ – divine shoulder; nimira – to raise; silai – bow; vaḷaiya – to draw; siṟidē – (in this world) a few rākśasas; muninda – on who vanquished (caused by that); tiru – veera lakshmi (the wealth of valour); mārvan – on who is having on his divine chest; vaṇḍu – by beetles; Ar – filled; kūndal – having hair; malar mangai – with periya pirāttiyār; vadi – appearing like a sharp sword; kaṇ – having divine eyes; madandai – with śrī bhūmip pirātti; mā – great (to protect the world); nōkkam – sankalpam (divine vow); kaṇḍān – emperumān who did; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – seeing (this to be a secluded abode); uganda – mercifully became joyful; kaṇṇapuram – tirukkaṇṇapuram; nām – us; toḻudumē – will worship

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh servitors of bhagavān! I have found a means to be uplifted; bhagavān is having veera lakshmi (wealth of valour) on his divine chest due to destroying a few rākśasas who were fearless previously, to become scared, to have his strong shoulder raise and to draw his bow; such emperumān has identified tirukkaṇṇapuram to be the abode and became joyful having taken the great vow, remaining along with periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi) who is having hair which is filled with beetles and śrī bhūmip pirātti who is having sword-like sharp divine eyes. Let us worship such tirukkaṇṇapuram.

**toṇḍīr** – Oh those who are eager to engage in kainkaryams as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍum*” (We should engage in continuous kainkaryam)!

**uyyum vagai kaṇḍēn** – Leaving the state mentioned in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva sa bhavati*” (become as good as insentient), I have found a way to surrender unto him and be uplifted. When asked “What is that way?” āḻvār says “*kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudum*” (Let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram).

**tuḷangā arakkar tuḷanga** – Previously these rākśasas would not know anything abour fear. To have that whole clan fear.

**tiṇ tōḷ …** – To have the shoulder which is unśakeable on hearing about the enemies, raise and to draw his bow.

**siṟidē muninda** – Instead of destroying the entire world, he showed anger only towards the rākśasa clan. If the one who created everything with his sankalpam (vow) shows his anger, the entire universe will be destroyed \[Yet, he did not destroy everyone\].

**tirumārban** – One who has the divine chest which is the abode for veeraśrī.

**vaṇḍār …** – We got to serve in that union of bhagavān along with his consorts.

**vaṇḍār kūndal malar mangai** – periya pirāttiyār who will mesmerise bhagavān with her hair, so that he does not have scope to analyse the faults of those who worship him.

**vadik kaṇ madandai** – śrī bhūmip pirātti, who can flatten him just with his glance, without having the need for such beautiful hair.

**mā nōkkam kaṇḍāy** – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/04/thiruvaimozhi-4-9-10-kandu-kettu/) “*oṇḍodiyāḷ  tirumagaḷum nīyumē nilā niṟpak* *kaṇḍa sadi*r” (after seeing the togetherness of you and the one who is having distinguished forearms with ornaments like bangles, the best among women, who is known as śrī due to being the collection of all wealth, and determined the best means), bhagavān determined that for the protection of the people “I should remain together with my divine consorts” .

**kaṇḍu koṇḍu …** – He mercifully became joyful thinking that tirukkaṇṇapuram is the secluded abode for our union. Let us worship that abode.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.6.2. Porunda arakkar

*porundā arakkar venjamattup ponṟa anṟu puḷḷūrndu perum tōḷ māli talai puraḷap pērnda arakkar tennilangai irundār tammai udan koṇḍu angu eḻilār pilattup pukkoḷippakarum tāḷ silai kaikkoṇḍānūr kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

porundā – not matching; arakkar – rākśasas; venjamattu – in the battle; ponṟa – to be destroyed; anṟu – at that time; puḷ ūrndu – riding the tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); perum – huge; tōḷ – having strong shoulders; māli – māli’s \[a demon\]; talai – head; puraḷa – to roll; pērnda – other; arakkar – rākśasas; then – in the southern direction; ilangai – in the town of lankā; irundār tammai – the rākśasas who were present; udan koṇḍu – gathering them; angu – from there; eḻil – by beauty; Ar – pervaded; pilattu – in the pātāḷam; pukku – entered; oḷippa – to hide; karundāḷ – very strong; silai – bow; kai – in the divine hand; koṇḍān – one who held; Ur – town; kaṇṇapuram toḻudumē – let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

bhagavān rode on garudāḻvār when the rākśasas, who did not align with his thoughts, engaged in a battle to destroy them. He held his very strong bow in his divine hand to make the head of māli, who has huge shoulder strength, roll on the ground. Through this, he made the rākśasas to gather the other rākśasas from the town of lankā, which is in the southern direction, to enter the pātāḷa which is pervaded by beauty and hide there. Let us worship such lord’s divine abode known as tirukkaṇṇapuram.

**porundā …** – Even if bhagvān remained fully favourable towards them, the rākśasa clan was firm on non-alignment; to have them killed in the battle, bhagavān rode garudāḻvār, made the head of māli, who has huge shoulder strength, roll on the ground; he also made the other rākśasas take along the rākśasas of lankā which remain as an ant-hill, filled with evil people always, and enter into the pātāḷa which is an enjoyable abode and hide there. He did that by holding his very strong bow in his divine hands. Let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram, which is the abode of such lord.

## 8.6.3. Valli idaiyal

*valli idaiyāḷ poruttāga madiḷ nīr ilangaiyār kōvai allal seydu venjamattuḷ āṟṟal migutta āṟṟalān vallāḷ arakkar kulap pāvai vāda muni tan vēḷviyaik kalvic cilaiyāl kāttānūr kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

valli – creeper-like; idaiyāḷ – pirātti who is having waist, her; poruttāga – for her sake; nīr – having the ocean as a moat; madiḷ – having fort; ilangaiyār – for the rākśasas residing in lankā; kōvai – rāvaṇa, who is the controller; allal seydu – tormented; venjamattuḷ – in the battle; āṟṟal – by strength; migutta – greater; āṟṟalān – being the eminent person; vallāḷ – having great masculinity; arakkar – rākśasas’; kulap pāvai – tātaki, from that clan; vāda – to be destroyed; muni than – viśvāmitra’s; vēḷviyai – yajña; kalvi – in the learning stage of military subject; silaiyāl – with the bow; kāttān – emperumān, who protected, his; Ur – divine abode; kaṇṇapuram nām toḻuḻudumē – let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram

**Перевод:**

**śrī rāmāvatāram which was spoken about in the previous pāsuram, is again appearing in āḻvār’s mind – that is explained here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

For the sake of sītāp pirātti, who is having creeper-like waist, emperumān tormented rāvaṇa who is the controller of the rākśasas who were residing in the fortified lankā which is having the ocean as a moat, and was eminent in the battle, by his strength; while he was in the learning stage of military subject, with his bow, he protected viśvāmitra’s yajña by destroying tātaki who is from the clan of rākśasas who were having great masculinity; let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram, which is his divine abode.

**valli …** – For the sake of sītāp pirātti; rāvaṇa who is thinking “Am I not the controller of the residents of lankā which is having ocean as a moat, having fort?”

**allal seydu** – Destroying his chariot, breaking his bow, making him flee the battle-field showing his back and insulting him in these ways are being spoken here. One who is having the strength of the bow, where he could say in the battle “You leave now and come back tomorrow” \[when rāvaṇa was beaten well\].

**āṟṟal migutta** – Eminent personality with great strength; instead of killing the enemy who was cornered, he said to him “You leave now and come back tomorrow”. I will not be satisfied by killing you when you are weakened. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāndam 59.144, śrī rāma tells rāvaṇa “*gaccānujānāmi raṇārtitas tvam praviśya rātrincararāja! lankām* I ***āśvāsya*** *niryāhi ratīca danvī tadā bhalam drakśyasi mē ratastata:* īī” (Oh, king of demons! You have become tired in the battlefield. Go back! I allow you to go. Go to your place, recoup your strength and come back with your chariot and your bow. Sitting on your chariot, you will see my strength), when rāvaṇa became weak, śrī rāma pacified him just like he would pacify someone in his own army becoming weak and told him to recoup and return on the next day.

**val āḷ …** – This deed was performed even before getting matured.

**val āḷ arakkar kulap pāvai vāda** – To finish the one who is the desirable star of rākśasa clan which is having strong masculinity.

**muni …** – He protected the yajña of the sage, viśvāmitra, with the bow which he had even before defeating śrī paraśurāmāḻvān and getting his viṣṇu danus from him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.6.4. Mallai munnir

*mallai munnīr adarpada varivenjilai kāl vaḷaivittukkollai vilangu paṇi seyyak kodiyōn ilangai pugaluṟṟuttollai marangaḷ pugappeydu tuvalai nimirndu vān aṇavak kallāl kadalai adaittānūr kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kodiyōn – Cruel rāvaṇa’s; ilangai – lankā’s; pugal – entering; uṟṟu – having that intent; mallai – abundant; munnīr – ocean, having three types of water (river water, ground water and rain water); adarpada – to worship; vari – having (beautiful) stripes; vem – cruel; silai kāl – the bow; vaḷaivittu – drew; kollai – roaming around on the \[tree\] branches in the forests; vilangu – monkeys; paṇi – kainkaryam (service); seyya – to perform; tollai – ancient; marangaḷ – trees; puga – to fall (being uprooted); peydu – to push them into (the ocean); tuvalai – water drops; nimirndu – rise; vān – in the sky; aṇava – to touch; kallāl – by rocks; kadalai – ocean; adaittān – for cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma, divine son of the emperor) who built / bound; Ur – abode; kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē – let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

śrī rāma, the divine son of emperor daśarata, was having the intent to enter the cruel rāvaṇa’s lankā; to make the ocean which is having abundant water from three sources namely rain, ground and river, worship, he drew his beautiful, striped bow and with the help of monkeys which are roaming around on the \[tree\] branches in the forests, by making the ancient trees fall and be pushed into the water and to have the water droplets rise and touch the sky, built the bridge with rocks. Let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram, which is the abode of such emperumān.

**mallai munnīr adarpada** – mallai means abundance. To have the ocean which is a water body having three types of water, worship; to have the ocean which is glorified as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19-31 “*apramēyō mahōdadi*” (this ocean, which cannot be measured), worship.

**vari vem silai kāl vaḷaivittu** – Having beautiful stripes, drawing the cruel bow which will make the enemies scared by the way it is held.

**kollai vilangu paṇi seyya** – With the service done by the monkeys which are not used to battles and are constantly roaming around the \[tree\] branches; the kainkaryam which is done by garudāḻvār, ādiśēśa et al who are untouched by the smell of samsāra, is done by the monkeys which don’t know the difference between right and left hands.

**kodiyōn ilangai pugal uṟṟu** – Thinking about the cruel act of rāvaṇa, in his divine heart, āḻvār is saying cruel rāvaṇa. His cruelty is such that he could not tolerate the father and mother remaining together.

Should be read as “*ilangai pugal uṟṟu mallai munnīr adarpada varivenjilaikāl vaḷaivittuk kollai vilangu paṇi seyyak kallāl kadalai adaittānūr*“.

**tollai marangaḷ pugap peydu** – Uprooting ancient trees which were never touched, and making those trees enter into the ocean.

**tuvalai nimirndu vān aṇava** – The abode of cakravartit tirumagan who built the bridge with the rocks which will usually drown in the water and as a result the water droplets rise and fill the sky.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.6.5. Amaiyagi

*āmaiyāgi ariyāgi annamāgi andaṇar tamōmamāgi ūḻiyāgi uvari sūḻnda nedum puṇariccēmamadiḷ sūḻ ilangaik kōn siramum karamum tuṇittu munkāmaṟpayandān karudumūr kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āmaiyāgi – being in the form of kūrma (tortoise); ariyāgi – being in the form of narasimha (human-lion); annamāgi – being in the form of a hamsa (swan); andaṇartam – brāhmaṇas’; ōmamāgi – being in the form of yajña; ūḻiyāgi – being in the form of time; nedum – vast; uvari – salty; puṇari – by ocean; sūḻnda – surrounded; sēmam – protection; madiḷ – by the fort; sūḻ – surrounded; ilangai – for lankā; kōn – rāvaṇa, who is the king, his; siramum – heads; karamum – shoulders; tuṇittu – being in the form of cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma, son of emperor daśarata) who severed; mun – previously; kāman payandān – kriṣṇa who is the father of kāman (cupid); karudum – desirously residing; Ur – divyadēśam; kaṇṇapuram nām toḻdumē – let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Being in the form of tortoise, half human and half lion, swan, the fire sacrifices done by brāhmaṇas, time, cakravartit tirumangan (śrī rāma, son of emperor daśarata) who severed the heads and shoulders of rāvaṇa, the king of lankā which is surrounded by the fort which is a protection and is surrounded by the salty ocean, tirukkaṇṇapuram is the abode which is desirously inhabited by kriṣṇa who previously gave birth to cupid. Let us worship this divine abode.

**āmai …** – He is of the nature that when he has to protect his devotees, he will not care about himself and protect them.

**āmaiyāgi** – Being in the form of kūrmam.

**ariyāgi** – Being hayagrīva \[head of horse and torso of human\]; also said to be narasimha.

**annamāgi** … – Being in the form of hamsa to redeem the vēda cakśus (vēdam, the eyes which let us see the truth). He is the one who accepts the havis offered by brāhmaṇas in yajñas. Being the time where only time remains. He is the one who is present when no one else is present.

**uvari …** – Being surrounded by the salty ocean which is having high tides, lankā, which is having forts which cannot be penetrated by anyone, is having rāvaṇa as the controller. śrī rāma killed such rāvaṇa playfully by severing his heads and shoulders.

**mun …** – kriṣṇa, who is the father of kāman who torments the world with his beauty, desirously resides in this abode. When recited as “ulagu”, it implies the world which is surrounded by huge ocean.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
