## 8.6.6. Varundadiru

*varundādiru nī madanenjē! nam mēl vinaigaḷ vārā muntirundā arakkar tennilangaic cendī uṇṇac civandu oru nāḷ perum tōḷ vāṇaṟku aruḷ purindu pinnai maṇāḷanāgi munkarum tāḷ kaḷiṟonṟu osittānūr kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mada nenjē – Oh noble mind!; nī – you; varundādu – without grieving; iru – should remain; nam mēl – on us; vinaigaḷ – sins; vārā – will not come; mun – previously; tirundā – not reforming; arakkar – rākśasas’; then ilangai – lankā which is in the southern direction; sem – reddish; tī – fire having flames; uṇṇa – to consume; sivandu – angry; oru nāḷ – once; perum – abundant; tōḷ – having shoulders; vāṇaṟku – for bāṇāsura; aruḷ – mercy; purindu – one who showers; pinnai – for nappinnaip pirātti; maṇāḷanāgi – being the beloved; mun – in the front portion; karum – blackish; tāḷ – having feet; kaḷiṟu onṟu – an elephant named kuvalayāpeedam; osittān – kriṣṇa who killed, his; Ur – divyadēśam; kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē – let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh noble mind! You remain without worrying; sins will not come towards us; as śrī rāma, bhagavān previously showed his anger to make the fire with flames, consume lankā which is in the southern direction and is the abode of rākśasas who were not reforming; once, he showed his mercy on bāṇāsuran who had abundant shoulders; he is the beloved lord of nappinnaip pirātti; he killed the elephant named kuvalayāpeedam which was having blackish feet in the front portion; let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram which is such lord’s abode.

**varundādiru nī** – Instead of thinking about the past activities “What will we do?” and worrying, try to remain fearless.

**mada nenjē** – Oh humble mind! Oh mind which is seeing only you, and not seeing bhagavān’s greatness!

When asked “After accumulating so many sins, how can we remain without worries?” āḻvār says

**nam mēl vinaigaḷ vārā** – Can they come close to us saying “Weren’t these done by us?”? [mudal tiruvandādi 64](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-64/) “*nayavēn piṟar poruḷai naḷḷēn kīḻārōdu* *uyavēn uyarndavarōdu allāl viyavēn* *tirumālai alladu deyvam enṟu ēttēn* *varumāṟu en enmēl vinai*” (I will not desire the ātmā, which is the possession of distinguished [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), as mine; I will not move closely with samsāris (dwellers of materialistic realm who think that ātmās are their own); I will not speak to anyone other than śrīvaiṣṇavas (who are servitors of emperumān); I will not respect as deity anyone other than śrī mahālakśmi’s consort; how will sins come on me?). [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 27](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/munram-thiruvandhadhi-27/) “*ārē tuyaruḻandār tunbuṟṟār āṇḍaiyār*  
*kārē malinda karum kadalai nērē* *kadaindānaik kāraṇanai neeraṇaimēl paḷḷi* *adaindānai nāḷum adaindu*” (After attaining the one who stood in the forefront and churned the dark ocean which is full of clouds, one who is the cause for all the worlds and one who is reclining on tiruppāṟkadal (on ādiśēśan), who suffered even for one day? Where are those who experienced sorrow (like that)?). These pāsurams should be recited to understand the meaning shown here.

When asked “Where did we see him pursue on his own and eliminate the sins?” āḻvār says,

**mun …** – Did pirātti put in any effort to eliminate her hurdles? As strong as the hurdles, his nature is such that, he will ensure that they are eliminated. The lankā, which is the abode of rākśasas, who would not listen to the advice of mālyavān et al.

**sem tī uṇṇa** – Due to the fear towards rāvaṇa, the fire would be pale, roaming around only to facilitate cooking of food; to make such fire become blazing and consume.

**sivandu** – showed his anger.

**perum tōḷ vāṇaṟku aruḷ purindu** – Severing the thousand shoulders of bāṇan who was prideful that he had many shoulders, still bhagavān left two shoulders for him to remain, so that he can conduct his life. He is the beloved lord of nappinnaip pirātti and he effortlessly killed kuvalayāpeedam which has strong feet which are blackish in the front portion. Such kriṣṇa’s divine abode.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.6.7. Ilaiyar malar

*ilaiyār malarp pūm poygai vāy mudalai tannāl adarppuṇḍu kolaiyār vēḻam nadukkuṟṟuk kulaiya adanukku aruḷ purindān alainīr ilangait tasakkirīvaṟku iḷaiyōṟku arasai aruḷi munkalaimāc cilaiyāl eydānūr kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kolai Ar – intoxicated; vēḻam – elephant; ilai – by leaves; Ar – filled; malar – blossomed; pūm – having flowers; poygaivāy – in the pond (entered and by the one which is present there); mudalai tannāl – by a crocodile; adarppuṇḍu – being tormented; nadukkuṟṟu – shivering; kulaiya – when it became still without any activity; adanukku – towards that elephant; aruḷ purindān – one who showed mercy; alai – tides (which are thrown up); nīr – surrounded by water; ilangai – (king) for the town of lanka; tasakkirīvaṟku – for the ten headed rāvaṇa; iḷaiyōṟku – for vibhīśaṇāḻvān who is the younger brother; arasai – (giving the) kingdom of lankā; aruḷi – one who blessed; mun – before (that); kalai – mystical deer; mā – big; silaiyāl – by the bow; eydān – emperumān who killed, his; Ur – divyadēśam; kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē – let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

The intoxicated elephant which entered the pond, which was filled with leaves and blossomed flowers, was tormented by a crocodile, was shivering and remained still without any activity; emperumān showed his mercy on that elephant; he blessed vibhīśaṇāḻvān who was the younger brother of ten-headed rāvaṇa, the kingdom of lankā which was surrounded by ocean with tides; previously, he killed the mystical deer with his big bow; let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram which is the abode of such emperumān.

**ilai …** – In the beautiful pond which is filled with leaves and spread with blossomed flowers, the intoxicated elephant, which was roaming around, entered an unnatural habitat, without realising what is coming and was tormented by an amphibian entity, and remained still without any activity; only the crocodile was acting; due to that, the elephant was shivering and became weak; at that time, bhagavān came and helped the elephant.

**alai nīr …** – Though rāvaṇa’s enmity would affect his brother too, bhagavān, without seeing that aspect, gave rāvaṇa’s younger brother, the lankā kingdom; even before that, he killed the mystical deer, which was arranged as a result of rāvaṇa’s enmity.

## 8.6.8. Malay maname

*mālāy manamē! arum tuyaril varundādiru nī vali mikkakālār marudum kāysinatta kaḻudum kadamāk kaḻudaiyummālār vidaiyum mada kariyum mallar uyirum madivittu kālāl sagadam pāyndānūr kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mālāy – being crazy; manamē – oh mind!; nī – You; arum – cannot exhaust (enjoying); tuyaril – in sorrows; varundādu – without worrying; iru – remain; mikka – abundant; vali – having strength; kālār – well rooted; marudum – maruda trees; kāy sinatta – very angry; kaḻudum – pūtanā, the ghost; kadam – angry; mā – horse; kaḻudaiyum – the donkey; mālār – having huge form; vidaiyum – bulls; mada – intoxicated; kariyum – kuvalayāpeedam; mallar – wrestlers’ (cāṇūra et al); uyirum – vital air; madivittu – one who destroyed; kālāl – by the divine feet; sagadam – śakatāsuran; pāyndān – kriṣṇa, who vanquished (to turn him into smithereens), his; Ur – divine abode; kaṇṇāpuram nām toḻudumē – let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

Oh, crazy mind! You remain without grieving in sorrows which cannot be exhausted. Let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram which is the abode of kriṣṇa, who destroyed well rooted maruda trees which are having abundant strength, very angry pūtanā, the ghost, angry horse, donkey, bulls which are having huge form, intoxicated kuvalayāpeedam, the vital air of the wrestlers, and who vanquished śakatāsura with his divine feet.

**mālāy …** – Oh, mind which has gone crazy thinking “What will we do meditating upon past sins”! Don’t worry about the sorrows which cannot be exhausted by experiencing the results; of the sins.

When the mind asks “How can we remain without grieving?” āḻvār says

**vali …** – īsn’t this his state? The very strong maruda trees which were well rooted, very angry pūtanā, angry horse, donkey, the bulls which have huge forms, intoxicated elephant, the vital air of the wrestlers who jump around like mountains – h vanquished all of these; due to the delay in mother yaśōdā’s arrival to feed bosom milk to him, he angrily lifted his feet and made sreśkatāsutra become smithereens.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.6.9. Kunral mari

*kunṟāl māri paḻudākkik kodiyēr idaiyāḷ poruttāgavan tāḷ vidai ēḻu anṟu adartta vānōr perumān māmāyan senṟān tūdu panjavarkkāyt tirigāṟcagadam sinam aḻittukkanṟāl viḷangāy eṟindānūr kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kunṟāl – With gōvardana mountain; māri – hailstorm; paḻudākki – one who made it ineffective; kodi – like a creeper; ēr – having beauty; idaiyāḷ poruttāga – for the sake of nappinnaip pirātti, who has the waist region; van – strong; tāḷ – having feet; ēḻu – seven; vidai – bulls; anṟu – at that time; adartta – one who destroyed; vānōr – to be cared by nityasūris; perumān – having supremacy; mā māyan – having amazing activities; panjavarkkāy – for panca pāṇḍavas; tūdu – as the dūta (messenger); senṟān – one who went (to duryōdana); tiri – rolling; kāl – having feet; sagadam – śakatāsuran’s; sinam – anger; aḻittu – one who eliminated; kanṟāl – with dēnukāsuran; viḷangāy – the asuran who stood as the wood apple; eṟindān – kriṣṇa who threw and killed, his; Ur – divyadēśam; kaṇṇapuram nām toḻudumē – let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa made the hailstorm ineffective with the help of gōvardana mountain; for the sake of nappinaip pirātti who is having creeper-like beautiful waist region, he killed seven bulls which had strong feet, during that time; he has the greatness of being cared for, by nityasūris; he has amazing activities; he went as a messenger for the sake of the five pāṇḍavas towards duryōdana; he eliminated the anger of śakatāsura who had rolling feet; he killed the asuran who remained as the wood apple by throwing dēnukāsuran; let us worship tirukkaṇṇapuram which is the divine abode of such kriṣṇa.

**kunṟāl …** – kriṣṇa made the hailstorm ineffective by lifting up the gōvardana mountain; for the sake of nappinaip pirātti who is having creeper-like beautiful waist region, he killed seven bulls which had strong feet.

**vānōr perumān** – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (lord of nityasūris who are free from any confusion), one who is having the greatness of being cared for by nityasūris, he placed himself at the feet of these bulls, without caring for himself.

**māmāyan** – One who has amazing activities.

**panjavarkkāy …** – Instead of caring for himself, he went as a messenger for pāṇḍavas, wearing a palm-leaf on his neck, to duryōdanan.

**tiri …** – Eliminating the anger of śakatāsuran who was having rolling feet; killed both the asuras who hatched amongst themselves a plan to kill kriṣṇa and came, by launching one on the other.

## 8.6.10. Karumamugil

*karumāmugil tōy nedumādak kaṇṇapurattu em adigaḷai tirumāmagaḷāl aruḷ māri seḻunīr āli vaḷanādanmaruvār puyaṟkaik kalikanṟi mangai vēndan oli vallār irumānilattukku arasāgi imaiyōr iṟainja vāḻvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karu – being black; mā – huge; mugil – dark clouds; tōy – to remain; nedu – tall; mādam – having mansions; kaṇṇapurattu – mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram; em adigaḷai – on my lord kriṣṇa; tiru mā magaḷāl – due to receiving the mercy of periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi); aruḷ māri – having the divine name, aruḷ māri; seḻu – abundant; nīr – having water; Ali vaḷa nādan – having the tiruvāli region; maruvār – complete (present in rainy season); puyal – like a cloud (always able to give fully); kai – having divine hands; mangai – for tirumangai; vēndan – the king; kali kanṟi – tirumangai āḻvār; oli – this tirumoḻi (decad) which is mercifully composed with tune; vallār – those who are able to recite; iru mā nilattu – for bhūlōkam and svarga lōkam; arasāgi – being the king (and then); imaiyōr – nityasūris; iṟainja – to worship their divine feet; vāḻvārē – will live

**Перевод:**

**No specific introduction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

kriṣṇa, my lord, is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram which has tall mansions, to have the blackish, huge, dark clouds remain on them; tirumangai āḻvār is known as aruḷ māri (merciful cloud) due to being the recipient of periya pirāttiyar’s mercy; he has the tiruvāli region which is having abundant water; he is having divine hands which are like complete cloud (which will always give rain) and is the king of tirumangai region; such āḻvār mercifully composed this decad with tune on such kriṣṇa; those who are able to recite these will remain the king of bhūlōkam and svarga lōkam and will live where they have the nityasūris worship their divine feet.

**karu mā mugil …** – kriṣṇa, who is mercifully residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram, which has mansions which are the resting places for the clouds which have absorbed the water and risen, is praised in this decad. Since āḻvār was the target of periya pirāttiyār’s complete glance, he is having “aruḷ māri” as his divine name. He is the owner of tiruvāli which has abundant water. Only if there is a cloud which is eternal and pours down without any restriction always, that can be compared to his divine hand. For āḻvār who is constantly giving, a cloud which occasionally appears and pours down in a particular place, cannot be a match. Those who are well versed in this decad which has tune and is mercifully composed by āḻvār who is the king of tirumangai region.

**iru mā nilattukku arasāgi** – As said in viṣṇu darmam “***bhaumam manōratam svarjñam*** *svargivandyanca yatpadam\| dadāti dāyinām nityam apavargapradō hari:*” (bhagavān who is liberation giver, bestows worldly pleasures, pleasures in celestial worlds and paramapadam which is desired by the residents of celestial worlds, for those who meditate upon him), getting all these decorations.

**imaiyōr iṟainja vāḻvārē** – Not stopping with that, they will enter paramapadam and will get the benefit of having the nityasūris fall at their feet as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/03/thiruvaimozhi-10-9-10-vidhi-vagai/) “*padiyinil pānginil pādangaḷ kaḻuvinar*” (cleansed the divine feet of such śrīvaiṣṇavas, in an honourable manner, in their respective abode).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
